The countdown to Expo 2020 Dubai
Dubai Chamber to host African Business Forum at Expo 2020 Dubai
A survey conducted by the Dubai Chamber with participants in previous sessions of the World Africa Business Forum, including dignitaries, investors, trade and investment leaders and experts, revealed that agriculture is the most promising area for investment in the African continent.
During the questionnaire, the participants ’ ideas, attitudes and views on the various aspects of investment and its prospects in the continent were identified.
He concluded that cash investment is the preferred form of FDI, and that Ghana and Nigeria are the preferred destinations for investment in the African continent, due to growth potential and investment opportunities.
The results of the survey provide important data for participants in the sixth edition of the forum, which will be organized by the Dubai Chamber and Expo 2020 Dubai during the exhibition from 13 to 14 October.
This year ’ s edition of the Forum will be organized under the theme “Trade Leads the Future of Economic Transformations ”, which is characterized by radical and fundamental changes that keep pace with the current stage, and at the same time reflects the keenness of the Chamber to achieve a qualitative shift in form and content, which enhances the Forum ’ s status and leading role in publicizing the commercial opportunities available in Africa.
Dubai Chamber, the official business integration partner of Expo 2020 Dubai, will play a pivotal role in stimulating partnerships with the global business community during the six months of the event.
The Forum ’ s program consists of three sections: the Forum ’ s Insights program, the Global Africa Business Forum ’ s networking program, which specializes in bilateral business meetings between investors and businessmen and investors from both sides to discuss opportunities for cooperation and potential partnerships, and the Expert Center, which provides a fast and reliable investment information platform on African countries.

Hana Al Hammadi (Abu Dhabi)
She grew up in a socially cohesive family, adhering to the traditions and heritage of the UAE between educated parents, who had a profound impact on her and all her brothers to continue her education. From childhood, she felt a sense of loyalty and gratitude to the homeland. She loved the sea and considered herself captive to it. That passion within her for art and beauty.
Professional Excellence
Engineer Hessa Al Malik, Advisor to the Minister for Maritime Transport at the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure, President of the Association of Women in the Maritime Sector (EMA), and the first regional ambassador to the Maritime Global Club of Informa Markets in the Middle East, oversees all the preparatory work and activities of the Maritime Administration in the UAE in relation to the mandatory audit system on member countries in the International Maritime Area. She graduated from the UAE University School of Architecture in 2000, which was the year of the construction boom and real estate development, where most of the real estate development companies and major projects originated in the country.
Ambition
“By virtue of my academic specialization, the Ministry of Works was at that time the best place to work, so I started my career as a field engineer responsible for supervising achievement in the work sites, and this was the first step in my life where I entered a male-dominated work field. At that time, it was not uncommon for women to be in such positions, but the great support I received from my family in the first place and my managers in the second. ” It pushed me to continue my career and move up the career ladder.
Accomplishments
Engineer Hessa feels proud when she oversaw the completion of a set of distinctive and detailed government buildings.
“I am proud of my contribution to the Cultural Center in Ras Al Khaimah, and the details of the design and implementation of theatres, as well as the building of the General Directorate of Ras Al Khaimah Police, and other projects. I was assigned to supervise the UAE ’ s comprehensive plan for urban development in remote areas, which is a qualitative leap and an important milestone in my career, especially with my master ’ s degree in planning. ”“ Because it allowed me to demonstrate my qualitative and specialized abilities and skills in the first place, and it allowed me to deal with infrastructure development projects across the country, and I am proud of the exceptional success I achieved with my team in completing this project. ”
She explained: “Thanks to all these achievements, I was appointed responsible for the planning and development of federal roads in the country, and I continued my path to success, and focused heavily on the adoption of digital technologies, ” stressing:“ I am proud to win the project, which I supervised with my team distinguished “linking federal roads on a unified electronic system ”. in the management of road assets worldwide.
We have also been able to link all federal entities in the country with the Federal Geographic Information System, which constitutes the largest spatial database enhanced by the detailed data of the federal government, which enabled the government at all levels to replan its resources and make decisions related to the organization of its work. ”
Captive of the sea
The success stations did not stop there, but was transferred to continue working in the Federal Transport Authority Land and Maritime to be the executive director of the maritime transport sector, explaining in this regard: « I quickly became attached to the sea and fell captive to his love, and I did not feel how the years passed, and we are achieving achievement after achievement, the most important of which is the successful nomination to the Executive Office of the International Maritime Organization, in (category B), This will contribute to the empowerment of the maritime sector for the coming years, in addition to a long list of projects that we have launched in terms of the development of maritime infrastructure in the country, which is among the best of its kind in the world, making the UAE one of the top 10 maritime centers in the world. ”
Other Talents
Despite the concerns and challenges faced by the engineer, she loves beauty, art and creativity, her house at first sight is a center of artistic hobbies and talents, loves perfumes, and has launched a special brand in this field, and then comes her love of reading, in all literary and historical fields beside scientific.
Motherhood and work
The love of giving in the life of engineer Hessa was not only in her field of work, but there was her family who did not spare her support, especially « her husband » was the first supporter and encouragement of her success, and says about it: « The challenge of professional success and my role as a mother of three daughters are the most precious thing I have in life.
Be the first supporter and supporter of my success as a mother, and second as a professional leader on the career side. ”
Coronavirus crisis
During the Corona crisis, Hessa ’ s work did not stop, but it was necessary to maintain the continuity of maritime operations in the country ’ s ports. At a time when we face the spread of the pandemic a major challenge, the global landscape of the shipping sector was greatly confused, and the movement of global trade and supply chain was almost completely paralyzed.
“In the UAE, we were able to devise creative solutions that allowed us to overcome this crisis, and we are proud to be the first country in the world to allow the change of crews, helping thousands of sailors stranded on their ships at sea.
The UAE has also been a haven for thousands of tourists stranded on oceanic cruise ships, allowing them to leave for their home countries in a process that involved all government agencies involved in the country.
A message to the UAE
Hessa Al Malik sends a message to every Emirati woman: We are living today in a time of empowerment of Emirati women, a commitment imposed by the leadership of the state, and devoted to all its capabilities and governmental and private facilities, so, Emirati women must not miss this historic opportunity, and everyone must turn with enthusiasm and perseverance to achieve excellence and success.
Best Manager
Eng. Hessa Al Malik is proud to have been named the best executive director in the UAE in 2019 and to have been awarded the Prime Minister ’ s Medal for the best Assistant Undersecretary and Executive Director as part of the Mohammed bin Rashid Award for Excellence in Government Performance in its fifth cycle.
Ambitions for the future
Hessa Al Malik ’ s ambitions without borders feel that the field is still open to opportunities for the development of the maritime sector, so she looks forward to actively contributing to the preparation of the fifty, and building the elements of the UAE ’ s blue economy full of employment and investment opportunities for citizens.

Many medical studies have confirmed not to overtake vitamins or supplements, in order to avoid their adverse results and numerous health risks.
As a result of the spread of the coronavirus, vitamins and minerals are the most commonly used dietary supplements, due to their important results in increasing energy levels, reducing weight, improving health and protecting against infection.
Despite this, studies have proven that taking vitamins and minerals has serious medical risks, as the risk arises through harm to the body due to the cumulative toxicity of many products taken at once, and experts have identified three main risks associated with taking vitamins:
Drug Interaction:
Various drug interactions interfere with vitamin supplements to backfire and cause serious consequences, including cognitive impairment and delirium, and experts have also warned against drug interference with some natural herbal supplements containing active substances.
Side effects:
Experts warn that the use of dietary supplements and vitamins may cause some side effects:
Vitamin A: Possible side effects include impaired liver function and vision loss.
Group B vitamins: Redness and burning of the skin, low blood pressure may occur.
Vitamin C: Causes an increased risk of kidney stones.
Vitamin D: Its overdose causes nausea, itchy skin, headaches, as well as the deposition of excess calcium in the liver, kidneys, lungs, heart and blood vessels, which increases the risk of heart attacks and coma.
Vitamin K: leads to the breakdown of red blood cells and the development of anemia.
Delay in effective treatment:
Taking some vitamins, supplements and vitamins causes interference with the diagnosis of some diseases and the start of the correct treatment, which poses a great risk and allows the exacerbation of the disease, so it is necessary to tell the doctor what we are taking other medicines and vitamins.
Experts point out that excessive consumption of fat-soluble vitamins leads to greater damage than water-soluble ones, due to the fact that the former accumulate in the tissues of the body, while the latter exits the body through sweating and urine.

Can technology help writers write?
• Bernd Debusman Jr.
• Reporter of Economic and Business Affairs
The famous American author Mark Twain was strongly frowned upon by those who thought it was possible for someone to learn how to write a novel.
One of his famous sayings on the subject is: “He who is not born with the queen of writing a novel will inevitably have a hard time trying to write a novel. ”
“If a person doesn ’ t have a clear idea of their story, that necessarily means that, in fact, they don ’ t have a story, ” he said.
British writer Stephen Fry has another way of framing the idea: Successful authors are those who know how difficult it is to write a book.
About 2.2 million books are published each year worldwide, according to the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), which monitors and counts books.
This figure includes both fictional novels and non-fictional works.
For most of these authors, the writing process has remained relatively unchanged since Twain was at the peak of his glory and giving in the late 19th century.
The process begins by outlining the plot and ideas, and then gradually decoding, developing and refining them over time.
But these days, the effectiveness of technology is growing in making the life of an author a little easier.
For Michael Green, an American statistician and data scientist turned novelist, the need to use technology to simplify the writing process and make it seamless came when he was in the middle of writing his first book.
After writing 500 pages of a complex story, he reached a point where he felt the process was becoming difficult to manage: “In the midst of editing, I reached a point where I started to feel like I had a lot of plots and characters. ”
“I had all these documents about the deeper aspects of the world I was working on creating.
I was worried about being able to track all the leads.
That ’ s the point where I turned again to my data science methodology to solve a complex, complex problem that has so many aspects and details. ”
The end result was that Green created Lynit, a digital platform that helps authors visualize, plan, and weave together the different elements, such as characters, plot aspects, themes, and major events, that make up the story.
The app is now in its experimental phase, and is being tested by a number of writers.
It is currently free, and enables users to draw and update complex digital templates or story maps.
Greene says many novelists start their work with more than just a general idea of a particular plot or character.
He says the process of adding Lynette to this initial idea is simple and easy.
“When a new idea shines in the mind of an author who wants to insert it into the story, he is able to insert it into a natural framework.
They are building a vision. ”
“They develop the story by adding one part after another, and as new ideas emerge, they make changes and adjustments, perhaps by creating new nodes (or interactions), or new relationships. ”
Technology is increasingly being harnessed once a writer has published his book to help authors connect with their readers.
This can be through the simple use of social media, as some writers welcome lengthy chats with their audience.
But there are other ways, where authors can turn to specialized companies such as Chicago-based Hiitide.
Its website and app allow writers to participate in live paid Q & A sessions with their readers.
Authors of self-help and self-development books can create and earn money through educational courses.
Ivan Shay, CEO of Hiitide, says the courses are “copies of writing workshops about a particular book. ”
“It helps you better understand the material and integrate its principles into everyday life. ”
As an example, he points to Ryan Holliday ’ s book The Obstacle is the Way: The Immortal Art of Turning Attempts into Triumphs, which draws its inspiration largely from Stoic Philosophy (an ancient Greek philosophical school that essentially holds that emotions are caused by errors in judging things and that a wise man does not suffer from such feelings).
“Users not only learn about Stoicism through the Hightide cycle, they can identify the virtues they want to embody and then follow them on a daily basis, ” Shay says.
“They can also participate in a Q & A seminar with author Ryan Holliday about his book. ”
Another tech company, California-based Crazy Maple Studios, says it ’ s helping authors revive their books.
Instead of giving readers just words in lines, its four apps, Chapters Scream, Spotlight and Kiss, add animations, music, sound effects and even games to digital books, enabling the reader to decide what the character does.
Joy Jia, the company ’ s founder and CEO, said: “The digital revolution and the emergence of digital readers (who rely on reading across digital devices) have brought about the first major transformation of the publishing industry. ”
Jia suggests that authors are more likely to employ technology as a result of the need to compete in a world where readers have many choices about how to spend their free time.
But experts still warn against over-reliance on technologies meant to help writers.
“Technology can be distracting, especially if you ’ re one step away from social media, or you ’ ve been trapped searching for a topic for too long, ” says Melissa Huffman, a trainer and ghost author.
“Five quick minutes you intended to take as a break can sometimes turn into hours of wasted writing time.
One of the tips I ’ m going to give on technology is to find work that fits your personality and writing styles, and then use it. ”
“But authors can sometimes fall into the trap of trying everything in the hope that they will find the magic tool, which can actually turn out to be another distraction. ”
But Michael Green believes that technology will take a more prominent place when it glitters the new generation of tech-oriented writers.
“What I ’ m seeing in Generation 21 and even younger writers is that they ’ re looking for technology to give them direction, they ’ re simply seeing it as a tool to learn and grow, rather than as work and extra effort, ” he says.

Did the Lebanese turn to alternative medicine?
CAIRO (Reuters) - Since 2020, the Lebanese have been suffering from the crisis of cutting off medicines from pharmacies, and the search for medicines has become a daily habit, despite the decision of the Lebanese Minister of Health, Hamad Hassan, to lift subsidies on medicines that cost less than 12,000 pounds.
The Minister of Health kept the prices of medicines for chronic and incurable diseases, children ’ s milk, vaccines and psychological and neurological diseases, to increase the prices of most medicines between 4 and 6 times.
The nightmare of Lebanese lives has increased as the Lebanese Pharmaceutical Importers Syndicate warned a few days ago of a potentially catastrophic shortage of essential medicines amid the country ’ s ongoing economic crisis.
The syndicate said that imports have been almost completely stopped for a month, but as is known, the Lebanese are always looking for an alternative, has he returned with this crisis to knocking on the doors of perfumers, and treatment by herbs and natural formulations?
Kamal said Omar Houla, about 30%, in the perfume shop "Mecca", which he runs, attributing this to "not only the loss of medicines from pharmacies, but also the high price."
As for the most sought herbs, he said: "Those related to the treatment of depression, they are at the top of the list, as well as herbs for chronic diseases such as diabetes, pressure and cholesterol prevalent among the Lebanese, where there are special mixtures for each of them," stressing that "we have nothing to do with heart disease at all and very young children."
On the preventive herbs, Omar, who studied as "therapeutic nutrition and Chinese medicine", explained that these herbs are very important for the prevention of diseases, especially the calgan plant and the Indian premium. "
On the effectiveness of herbs on human health, he said: "Certainly replace ordinary drugs and more, but after the availability of two conditions, the patient's faith in this treatment, and perseverance," stressing that "herbs do not show side problems when taken unlike chemical drugs."
For his part, Attar Kamal Yahya Shehal, who inherited the profession father by grandfather, since 4 grandparents, and has 3 branches in northern Lebanon, including in the old market of Attarine, that "this profession was originally a refuge for people to be treated, but today medicine has advanced a lot, and there is a specialization for every disease."
He explained: "Herbs do not replace medicine in many cases, if a patient suffers from a large rise in blood pressure can not be prescribed herb, but he needs a hospital, but if the rise in pressure is simple can take some herbs such as basil for example to help reduce pressure."
He advised to see the doctor and consult him.
On the role of herbs, he continued: "It is often preventive and needs a long time, that is, it is not for the treatment of emergency cases, but is considered a dietary supplement," he continued, asking: "What can herbs do if a person, for example, suffers from appendicitis or more severe?", pointing out that "some people make mistakes when they think that herbs replace medicine."
As for the herbs required today, he said: "Those for strengthening immunity such as black seed, as well as the original honey is very useful for immunity, and there is a mixture of herbs such as chamomile blossom and marshmallow beneficial for the chest and cough, and propolis bees for inflammation."
As for whether he fears for his profession of extinction, he said: "Everything in life progresses and develops and we must keep pace with scientific progress, so I directed my children to the correct scientific path of the profession, I have a son who graduated from the Faculty of Pharmacy, and a son who graduated from the Faculty of Medicine specializing in hematology."
He concluded by stressing: "As for herbs, the patient must deal with them with caution because they may be suitable for some and harmful at the same time for others, and behind the non-specialists, which may cause more harm than benefit."
As for the Lebanese opinion of the alternative option, Fada al-Shami, 35, an employee of a clothing store, said that "the herbs were used by our ancestors and had a very positive effect, but because of the development of medicine, it was natural to turn to the world of medicines for the speed of its result."
She added: "In light of the economic crisis and the crisis of medicine that we suffer from in Lebanon, we returned to alternative treatment for many uses, including stomach and chest pains," explaining: "We have perfume shops in Tripoli with competent, they offer us distinctive mixtures that we feel benefit from, even if the treatment takes time to show the result."
Sherine Ghalaini (32 years old, housewife and mother of three) considered that "the crisis that Lebanon is going through has led some to resort to herbs without scientific studies proving its effectiveness, especially with regard to chronic diseases such as sugar and pressure, and whether it has side effects, as some patients resort to it because of the lack of basic drugs, as the sick saying is related to air ropes."

Study: Walking 30 minutes a day may reduce risk of stroke death
In a new study conducted at the University of Calgary, Canada, researchers found that people who walked or landscaped for at least three to four hours a week, or cycled for at least two to three hours a week, or the equivalent after a stroke, may have a 54% reduced risk of death from any cause. In general this amount of movement or sport, the risk of death decreased by 80%.
The study showed that 895 people of the sample with an average age of 72 had a previous stroke and 97,805 people with an average age of 63 did not have a stroke, and the average weekly physical activity was assessed through questions about activities such as walking, running, gardening, weight training, cycling and swimming.
The team followed participants for an average of four and a half years, and after accounting for other factors that could affect their risk of death, such as age and smoking, the researchers found that 25% of people who had previous strokes died of any cause, compared to 6% of people who did not have a stroke.
Data show that in the stroke group, 15% of people who exercised at least three to four hours of walking per week died while following, compared to 33% of those who did not exercise that minimum.
In the group of people who had never had a stroke before, 4% of people who practiced this amount died, compared to 8% who did not.
The team of researchers found that the biggest reduction in mortality came among people who had a previous stroke and were younger than 75 years old.
In that group, 11% of those who did at least minimal exercise died, compared to 29% of those who did not, and people with a previous stroke under the age of 75 who achieved minimal physical activity were about 80% less likely to die than those who did not.
The study indicated that people over the age of 75 who exercised the minimum did not receive the lower benefit but were 32% less likely to die.
These findings suggest that getting minimal physical activity may reduce long-term mortality from any cause in stroke survivors.
The team says doctors should especially emphasize this to younger stroke survivors, who may get the biggest health benefits from just walking for thirty minutes each day.

Disney Plus reaches 116 million subscribers and exceeds all expectations
Disney Plus was able to surpass all expectations in the fourth quarter and reach 116 million subscribers by the end of July, after adding 12.4 million new subscribers in the third fiscal quarter of Disney, which saw its revenue grow by 46% compared to the same period in 2020.
This rise in the number of subscribers comes despite the increase in the value of the subscription by one dollar during the last period, where analysts' expectations were limited to the arrival of the service to 112.8 million subscribers only.
Disney Plus was able to reach these numbers despite not being released worldwide, as it was launched at the end of the year in Western Europe, while it will be launched in the summer of 2022 in Eastern Europe, and it does not operate in a large part of the Asian, Latin and African continent.
It is noteworthy that the existence of a large library of classic and modern Disney movies contributed to a great acceptance among users, and the introduction of new and exclusive films directly on the platform contributed to the participation of users to follow these films in conjunction with their launch in the cinema, especially the films of superheroes and Star Wars series and three-dimensional animated films developed by Pixar Studios.
Disney-owned Hulu, on the other hand, was able to make a profit after a long time, and saw growth in the number of users and revenues in the last fiscal quarter.

The Arab Investment Guarantee Corporation (AIGC) revealed that it had acquired 14.6% of the total cumulative foreign direct investment (FDI) to Arab countries at a value of $132.5 billion by the end of 2020.
According to the Investment Climate in the Arab Countries Report 2021, Egypt came in second place as the largest recipient of foreign direct investment in the Arab countries, according to UNCTAD statistics, with inflows of $5.9 billion, representing 14.5% of the total inflows to the region in 2020.
According to the data of the report issued by a research team headed by Ahmed Al-Dabaa, head of research and publishing at the Foundation, Egypt ranked seventh with foreign direct investment inflows of $327 million in 2020, and ranked eighth in the Arab world in terms of foreign direct investment balances issued with $8.5 billion by the end of 2020.
With regard to the acquisitions and mergers witnessed by the Egyptian market during the year 2020, the report pointed out that the buying and selling operations amounted to a total of 917 million dollars.
In terms of foreign direct investment projects, Egypt received the entry of 43 new projects, representing 7% of the number of projects received by the region during 2020, at an investment cost of $1.4 billion, which provided more than 6,000 jobs representing 11.3% of the Arab total during the year.
With regard to inter-Arab investment, Egypt received 19 projects, representing 17.3% of the Arab total, while 5 Egyptian companies implemented 6 projects in Arab countries.
The Arab Investment Climate Report for 2021 showed that Egypt ’ s ranking improved by 5 places in the Business Performance Environment Index for 2020 as a result of its improved ranking sub-indicators for starting the project, obtaining electricity 21 places, dealing with cases of default 17 places, paying taxes, protecting minority investors 4 centers and trading across borders one center in contrast to the stability and decline of the ranking in the rest of the sub-indicators.
The report attributed this improvement to Egypt ’ s implementation of four basic reforms in the business performance environment, the most important of which is facilitating the start of commercial activity by eliminating the requirement of obtaining a certificate of no ambiguity and improving the work of the single window.
Improving the procedures for obtaining electricity through the application of automated systems to monitor and report power outages, in addition to enhancing the protection of minority investors by requiring the approval of shareholders when issuing new shares, as well as facilitating the payment of taxes through the application of an electronic system for the filing and payment of corporate income tax and value added tax.
Egypt ranked second in the Arab world and 53 globally in the Foreign Direct Investment Regulatory Restrictions Index for 2020, and settled on the Arab average in the Governance Index, which measures the control of corruption, government effectiveness, political stability, absence of violence and terrorism, organizational quality, rules of law, political participation and accountability. 2020.
In terms of risk assessment indicators, Egypt has maintained a better ranking than the Arab average in the Fitch Political, Economic and Operational Risk Index, and around the Arab average in the Coface and EllerHermes Risk Index.
Despite the repercussions of the new pandemic, Egypt achieved the only positive growth in the region at a rate of 3.5%, bringing the gross domestic product (GDP) to $362 billion and the purchasing power parity (PPP) to $1292.5 billion.
Egypt has also achieved a great leap in its Arab ranking in terms of average GDP per capita in terms of purchasing power parity for the year 2020, ranking seventh after the six Gulf Cooperation Council countries.
At the level of external performance indicators, the ratio of foreign currency reserves coverage for the number of months of imports rose to 7.8 months to rank seventh in the Arab world, and the performance of the current account improved with relative stability in oil and gas production and exports, and the ratio of external debt to GDP stabilized at safe borders by 34.5%.
The report urged Egypt and the countries of the region to give priority to improving the investment climate and business environment in the coming period, especially in light of the political, economic and security challenges and the negative impact of the spread of the new Coronavirus and the accompanying closure measures, especially with the escalation of competition to attract investors on the one hand and the decline of the activity of multinational companies.
The report called on Egypt and the Arab countries to consider the improvement of the investment climate as a dynamic, continuous and multifaceted process linked to competing countries and changes in the factors of attracting investment.
He called for the identification of a higher authority to implement the plan with the participation of various investment related bodies, specialists and regional and international expertise to meet the challenges of investment, political, institutional, economic, legislative and procedural related to infrastructure, facilities and production elements, including land, attached production sites, trained professional cadres, technology and modern management systems.
The report believes that the integrated marketing of the country as a destination for investment, trade, technology transfer, tourism, human resources, knowledge and business in general, is a crucial element in conjunction with direct and continuous communication and interaction with investors, especially multinational companies.
The report stressed the need to evaluate and adjust the results of the plan based on measuring the impact of foreign investments on value added, export, employment and technology transfer, while monitoring the negative effects on the environment, excessive consumption of resources and other repercussions.

New Scientific Breakthrough Promises Massive Increase in Processor Power
Researchers in Japan have made a discovery that could open up opportunities to combine classical and quantum computing techniques in new ways, leading to a massive increase in processing power.
+ A -A
Source: Amr Zanati - Eram News
Researchers in Japan have made a discovery that could open up opportunities to combine classical and quantum computing techniques in new ways, leading to a massive increase in processing power.
The team, led by Professor Takahiro Matsumoto of Nagoya City University, was investigating a concept called quantum entanglement, where the interaction between multiple particles is so that they can only be described in relation to each other.
Historically, scientists have found it difficult to manufacture quantum entanglement (which is fundamental to quantum computing) due to numerous engineering and logistical challenges.
Proton entanglement was previously observed in molecular hydrogen and plays an important role in a variety of scientific disciplines, however, entanglement was found only in gas or liquid phases, Matsumoto explained.
"Now, we have discovered quantum entanglement on a hard surface, which could lay the foundation for future quantum technologies."
According to the paper, the integration of a proton qubit (a fundamental unit of quantum information) with modern silicon technology “could lead to an organic union of classical and quantum computing platforms. ”
This could allow systems with far more qubits (10 ^ 6) than is currently possible (10 ^ 2) and thus significantly boost processing speeds across supercomputing applications.
On the importance of his team ’ s discovery, Matsumoto explained that “the new generation of quantum computers can create new opportunities across a wide range of disciplines and use cases. ”
"Quantum computers can handle complex problems that are almost impossible to solve using conventional supercomputers."
“The discovery could be a game changer in quantum computing in terms of data storage, processing and transmission, potentially leading to a paradigm shift in pharmaceuticals, data security and many other areas. ”
Quantum computers are machines that explicitly use quantum physics to increase computational speeds beyond the capabilities of conventional computers.
Experts agree that the next revolution in informatics will be driven by quantum computing, which will provide an enormous ability to process information and accomplish tasks that the most powerful conventional computers cannot do.

American scientists have discovered that intermittent fasting, which is now widespread, has many health benefits, in addition to weight loss.
According to Cell Reports, a diet that restricts eating at certain hours is of interest to people seeking to reduce and control their weight, so most previous studies focus on this issue.
But scientists at the Salk Institute for Biological Research in California decided to conduct experiments on laboratory mice to determine the effect of intermittent fasting on body functions.
The results of these experiments have shown that intermittent fasting helps with type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, liver cancer and even infectious diseases, including COVID-19.
Prof Satchidananda Banda, head of the research team, said: "The main result of the clinical tests is weight reduction.
"But we have discovered that intermittent fasting is beneficial not only for metabolic diseases, but also for increasing insulin resistance and resistance to infectious diseases."
According to him, glucose intolerance, the first step of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and liver cancer, is one of the few cancers whose incidence and mortality have risen, rather than declined over the past 25-30 years.
This trend makes the search for simple ways to combat glucose intolerance a major scientific research priority.
The experiments involved feeding the mice with foods rich in fat and sugar, but for nine hours a day they were deprived of food.
The researchers coordinated the eating schedules with the mice ’ s lifestyle – sleeping during the day and looking for food at night.
During these experiments, the researchers were conducting an analysis of the chemical composition of the liver and the level of glucose in the blood, assessing muscle mass and testing performance, endurance and survival in case of sepsis.
The researchers discovered that intermittent fasting protects against fatty liver disease regardless of age and gender.
Glucose tolerance tests performed on mice after 16 hours of fasting showed that intermittent fasting keeps blood sugar levels low and provides a quicker return to normal after disturbances.
Intermittent fasting, therefore, can be a free and convenient way to prevent or treat diabetes and metabolic syndrome.
The researchers also found that intermittent fasting can protect against death from sepsis, for example in intensive care units, which is especially important during a pandemic.

People with incurable genetic diseases such as Parkinson's disease, sickle cell anemia and cystic fibrosis can get a lifeline using a new technique.
The new technique, dubbed the Swiss Army Knife, is an evolution in the technology known as the CRISPR gene editing procedure, first developed in 2012 and described as one of the most powerful medical tools in history.
The technique works by cutting out specific sections of DNA.
Experts agree that there is huge potential in CRISPR as an effective treatment, and the CRISPR gene editing system is usually associated with Cas9 (an enzyme derived from bacteria that cuts and replaces defective genes), but there is a problem that its efficiency is somewhat constrained by its relatively large size, making it difficult for the mechanism to squeeze cells and start working.
Scientists at Stamford University have now developed a CRISPR tool called CasMINI, using a protein close to Cas9, but much smaller than it, that should be able to enter human cells more easily.
The team created a tiny enzyme called Cas14, which is half the size of Cas9.
But Cas14 doesn ’ t work in mammals, so Stamford ’ s team genetically manipulated the enzyme to fix this problem and named it CasMINI.
Dr Lee (Stanley) Key, from the research team at Stamford who worked on the project, said: “There have been previous efforts to improve CRISPR ’ s performance.
This is a crucial step forward for CRISPR genome engineering applications.
The work presents the smallest CRISPR to date, according to our knowledge, as a genome-editing technique. ”
“If people sometimes think of Cas9 as molecular scissors, here we made a Swiss knife that has multiple functions.
It ’ s not big, but it ’ s miniature portable for ease of use. ”
In their experiments, the researchers noted that CasMINI can delete, activate, and modify genetic code just like its larger counterparts.
Its smaller size means it should be easier to deliver to human cells and the human body, making it a potential tool for treating various diseases, including eye diseases, organ degeneration, cancer treatment and genetic diseases in general.
CRISPR is known to be a serious game-changer in the medical field.
That ’ s why Professors Emmanuel Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna, who were involved in the discovery of Cas9, won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry last year for their work in the field.
But until now, CRISPR ’ s use in humans has been very limited by a small set of studies.
Some people are concerned about the potential long-term effects of this type of technology, with safety and ethical implications being a particular concern.
There have been some examples of illegal use of CRISPR, such as the infamous scientist He Jiankui, who used CRISPR on twin embryos of girls in an attempt to make them resistant to HIV.

Russian scientists, from the research and production company Initium-Pharm and the Engelhardt Institute of Molecular Biology of the Russian Academy of Sciences, are among the first in the world to demonstrate the ability of Siberian fir to initiate the process of autophagy in the human body (purification of cellular debris), which contributes to an increase in the expected average youth stage.
According to the study, published by scientists in the international scientific journal Aging, experiments conducted by the authors of this work in 2021 proved that Siberian fir terpenes are able to quickly and safely release autophagy in human cells.
Scientists say they have begun searching for terpenes found in the roots and trunk of a coniferous plant known as Siberian fir, some of which live for 4,000 years.
Scientists believe that terpenes, as it turned out during the research, lead to autophagy, since the cells of the old tree are no different from the cells of the young plant.
Anastasia Lipatova, a researcher at the Cell Reproduction Laboratory of the Engelhardt Institute of Molecular Biology, told Sputnik: "We conducted a multi-mixtures study of the complex effect of terpenes on the cell, collected data on changes in the expression of 20,000 genes and quantitative analysis of protein (total body protein molecules - editor), highlighting the mechanism behind the biological effects of terpenes in Siberian fir."
During the experiments, it was possible to discover that autophagy in human lung tissue cells begins even when terpenes are used in low concentrations.
Vanya Maganova, head of research projects at Initium-Pharm, said in an interview with Sputnik: “Thanks to terpenes, the process of intensive autophagy in the studied human cells began within 24 hours.
We have seen how autophagy recycles the dysfunctional material of cells, thus maintaining energy balance.
This prevents the accumulation of harmful substances in the cell, including viruses. ”
"Therefore, it is easier for the body to recover from various infectious diseases, including after infection with coronavirus and influenza."
According to Maganova, in order to completely "regenerate" the cells of the body with the help of autophagy, you do not need to engage in exhausting training and fasting - it is enough to add a little terpenes to your diet.
“We are about to discover the ‘ Elixir of Youth ’, which can significantly increase a person ’ s lifespan. ”
The researchers noted that autophagy is genetically disrupted in most cells, and their normal cleansing processes are in a "dormant" state.
Therefore, scientists around the world are actively looking for ways to "awaken" this process, and are developing ways to activate autophagy in the cells of the human body.
Some scientists believe that stress leads to autophagy in cells.
For example, fasting or intense sports training can be a source of such stress, but these methods of stimulating autophagy have very serious drawbacks.
First, there has been no long-term scientific research on the benefits of fasting in the world.
Secondly, fasting does not comply with the principles of a healthy diet and can cause depression, fatigue and reduced sexual activity.
Thirdly, fasting and intense physical activity are prohibited for people with diabetes, cardiovascular disease and various injuries.
The term "autophagy" was coined by Belgian biochemist Christian de Duff, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1974 for the discovery of this process.
Japanese scientist Yoshinori Osumi continued his research and described the mechanism of autophagy.
For this, in 2016, the world also received the Nobel Prize.

Benefits and harms of seafood
Published 17 September 2021 - 06: 30
Benefits and harms of seafood
Seafood is an essential part of the diets of many people around the world, and eating it has been linked to a variety of health benefits.
Seafood is divided into several types including fish, crustaceans such as shrimp, mollusks such as oysters, and sea lobsters such as sea urchins, and through this article we will talk about the benefits and harm of seafood to the body in general.
Benefits of Seafood
Extremely nutritious
Seafood is a concentrated source of many essential nutrients, rich in protein, vitamins and minerals such as vitamin B12, selenium and zinc, and 85 grams of cooked shellfish provide more than 3,500% of the daily value of vitamin B12, 99% of the daily value of selenium, 21% of the daily value of zinc, and 13% of the daily need for iron.
Eating seafood can therefore cover common nutritional gaps, especially in people who follow a low-nutrient diet and those who eat less than optimal levels of nutrients, and young women, the elderly, and pregnant and lactating women may be most at risk of low levels.
An essential source of omega-3 acids
Seafood is an essential food source of omega-3 fatty acids, EPA and DHA, and each of these acids shares many aspects of health, including neuronal function and inflammation regulation.
According to research, diets rich in seafood significantly benefit the health of the nervous system and cardiovascular system, and scientists believe that this is mainly due to the seafood content of EPA and DHA.
Reduce the risk of disease
Because seafood is rich in nutrients, including proteins, vitamins, minerals, and anti-inflammatory omega-3 fatty acids, it may offer protection from many health conditions.
A 2020 review of 34 studies found that higher fish consumption reduced the risk of coronary heart disease, heart attack, heart failure, stroke, depression and liver cancer.
Damage to seafood
Fried seafood is harmful to health
Frying any food whether it is chicken, potatoes or fish leads to unfavorable changes in food, including the formation of harmful compounds, and frying fish generally creates compounds called heterocyclic amines, acrolein, aldehydes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, all of which are known to contribute to the development of diseases such as cancer, and may have negative effects on heart health as well.
Some seafood is high in mercury.
Certain types of seafood contain a high percentage of heavy metal mercury, and the levels of mercury in seafood depend on several factors including the age and size of the fish and the water in which the fish live.
In fact, mercury is easily absorbed by the body, and this can cause health problems if too much of it accumulates in tissues, for example, exposure to high levels of mercury in the womb may lead to cognitive problems in children, and high levels of mercury may increase the risk of high blood pressure and heart attacks, and may also negatively affect the immune system.
Fish that contain the highest percentage of mercury, certain types of tuna, swordfish, tilefish, king mackerel, and in fact tuna is the most important food source of mercury in the world, where the body absorbs mercury more easily than raw tuna, so if you eat tuna regularly should be careful of the risks of mercury accumulation.
Environmental and Ethical Issues
The demand for seafood has led to overfishing and the destruction of marine environments around the world, and the target species cannot reproduce fast enough, resulting in a serious global problem, as marine ecosystems are neatly balanced, and drastically reducing the number of one species can lead to catastrophic effects on other species.
Therefore, experts fear that poor fishing management and irresponsible methods used to buy seafood and overfishing around the world could lead to a collapse of fisheries and a global food crisis.
It can be helped by reducing seafood consumption, buying only sustainably fished seafood, and avoiding eating overfished species.

LONDON (Reuters) - Royal Dutch Shell plans to start mass-producing low-carbon jet fuel by 2025 in a bid to encourage the world ’ s airlines to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
Aviation, which accounts for 3% of the world ’ s carbon emissions, is one of the toughest sectors to tackle due to a lack of alternative technologies to jet engines.
Shell, one of the world ’ s largest oil traders, said it aims to produce 2 million tonnes of what is known as sustainable aviation fuel by 2025, a tenfold increase from today ’ s total global production.
Shell said sustainable aviation fuel produced from waste cooking oils, plants and animal fats could cut up to 80 percent of air traffic emissions.
Shell said on Monday it wants green jet fuel to account for 10 percent of its global jet fuel sales by 2030.
Environmentally friendly jet fuel can be blended with ordinary jet fuel with little need to change aircraft engines.
Jefferies Investment Bank said sustainable aviation fuel accounted for less than 1 percent of global jet fuel demand today, which stood at around 330 million tonnes in 2019.
The growth of the market is facing many obstacles, primarily due to the cost of sustainable aviation fuel, which is currently eight times higher than the cost of regular aviation fuel and limited availability of raw materials.
Shell said it wanted other companies to follow suit.
Shell president Anna Masculo told Reuters: “We also expect other companies to add it to their production plants. ”
The United States said last week it wanted to cut greenhouse gas emissions from aircraft by 20 percent by the end of the decade by dramatically boosting the use of sustainable aviation fuel.

Over the past nine decades, the kings of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia have been keen to achieve achievements and successes at various levels, until the Kingdom has become one of the most important countries in the world, both regionally and internationally, and during the last decade has achieved unprecedented qualitative leaps at the political, economic and social levels.
The celebrations of Saudi Arabia ’ s 91st National Day this year come in light of an unprecedented cultural boom witnessed by the Kingdom, where significant strides have been made in the process of comprehensive economic development through a series of projects, programs and strategies of economic diversification, support to non-oil sectors, and the establishment of modern and sophisticated industrial entities.
During the last decade, the Kingdom hosted a number of international, Arab and Islamic summits. Saudi Arabia was visited by leaders and leaders of major countries of the world, led by US President Donald Trump, who visited Riyadh in May 2017, in his first official foreign visit since taking office.: The Saudi-American summit, the US-Gulf summit, and the US-Arab and Islamic summit, and the leaders of 55 Arab and Islamic countries participated in the three summits.
Saudi Arabia has achieved many other foreign policy successes, including the announcement of the establishment of the Council of Arab and African States bordering the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden in early 2020, which includes Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Egypt, Sudan, Djibouti, Somalia and Yemen.
In a historic precedent that is the first of its kind in the history of the Arab region, Saudi Arabia assumed the presidency of the G20 on December 1, 2019, thus becoming the first Arab country to lead the largest international group, whose countries account for 75 percent of global trade volume and 80 percent of global economic output.
During the Saudi presidency of the G20, King Salman chaired a virtual extraordinary summit of G20 leaders hosted by Riyadh in March 2020 to coordinate international efforts in the field of combating the Corona pandemic and reducing its humanitarian and economic impact, with the participation of US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Road Map
As a result of these reforms, Saudi Arabia has been ranked by the World Bank among the top 20 reformers in the world, and the second among the top high-income countries and G20 countries in terms of implementing reforms to improve the business climate.
Saudi Vision 2030, which was launched on April 25, 2016, is at the top of the development programs adopted by the Kingdom. It is a road map towards comprehensive future national development, and aims to reduce the Kingdom ’ s dependence on oil and diversify its sources of income through a package of economic reforms unprecedented in the Kingdom ’ s history.

In a precedent witnessed by Saudi Arabia for the first time, the trend began to approve the general budget of the state by supporting and developing the national economy, without relying mainly on oil as the sole source of national income, which observers ranked among the most important achievements in the history of the Kingdom.

The economic achievements achieved by Saudi Arabia in the recent period, including reducing the budget deficit by 48 percent, increasing the number of licenses granted to foreign investments by 130 percent, and moving to develop a city for the automotive industry in order to attract investments, increase exports and create jobs, and repair more than 4 million square meters of road networks.
Agricultural renaissance

International universities, and provide jobs for scholarships after their return.

The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development confirmed on Wednesday that the proportion of women in middle and senior management positions increased by 30% in the public and private sectors during the past year 2020.
The indicators showed that the percentage of Saudi women in the civil service increased to 41.02% by the end of the same year, as the Ministry confirmed that the steps of women accelerated towards empowerment thanks to the issuance of many decisions, legislations and regulations that enhance their status in society, including the initiative to empower women in the civil service and assume senior structural leadership positions in government agencies through a range of supporting projects.
The National Platform for Women Leaders serves as a tool that enables various entities to communicate and nominate women leaders for leadership positions, boards of directors or official delegations in international forums based on precise criteria. The project aims to focus on three axes: the enabling environment, the institutional level, and the community or individual level. The Civil Service will expand employment options for both working women and men, by identifying jobs that can be exercised in this manner.
The initiatives to empower women to enter the labour market aim to reduce inequalities in employment conditions and opportunities through incentives and support the creation of a supportive and inclusive environment to facilitate women's entry into the labour market. They also include raising awareness of policies related to women in the labour market; designing training programmes to enable women to enter the labour market; and launching awareness campaigns to support them.
It also includes the promotion of women's career development, the identification of potential career advancement tools for women and the analysis of the feasibility and impact of the tools, as well as the development of regulatory legislation that supports women's work in the labour market, with a view to developing legislation, regulations and regulations that enhance the development of the physical work environment and resolve obstacles that hinder women's work.
The initiative aims to increase the proportion of women in middle and senior leadership positions to achieve the objectives of increasing women's participation in the labor market by training women cadres in various sectors, whether in the public or private sectors.
The initiative aims to increase employment opportunities for Saudi men and women, especially those living in less developed regions with limited education, in addition to promoting economic growth and diversity in employment opportunities across different segments of society, through the development of comprehensive flexible work laws (hourly) and motivating employers to provide flexible work contracts.

By French writer Pierre Bayard, translated into Arabic by Ghassan Lotfi, and the title of the book itself is enough to raise more questions, so why should we talk about books we have not read?
What is the need for false pretenses to read?

The author of the book Pierre Bayard, professor of literature at the University of Paris and psychoanalyst, and has many controversial books in which he embodies his unique vision of things, a man navigating in reading and literature and a writer at the same time, how to bother to write a book in which he advises not to overread, but he calls not to read originally, where the writer to abandon the idea of sanctifying books, and demolishes some beliefs related to talk about adventure It invites us not to feel guilty for not reading all the books in our libraries, and even more so it invites us to talk about those books that we have not read in the first place, regardless of any purpose or justification, because it believes that it is an excellent opportunity to discover the creative self within each of us.
He demands the liberation of the reader from the text of the writer and the removal of the weight of the words of others from his shoulders, because in short he is looking for that power to create the text of each reader to become a writer in turn, the goal is to free the possibilities in each individual knowing that few will become writers.
And to write after you are just a reader is liberation and an act that requires a lot of courage, while excessive reading may deprive you of the possibility of being an authentic writer, because when you read only without expressing your opinion, you remain a follower of the writer, and this reminds me of the style of writing practical research and academic writing where the strength of your research lies by quoting the above to be the master of the situation. Community Library
In his call not to overread, the writer elaborates on the idea that there is no need at all to read the book in order to have an accurate idea of its content and be able to talk about it, and explains that there is no book isolated from other books, each book is an element of a group called the collective library, which must not necessarily be known to evaluate or estimate this element specifically, and we must go beyond the individuality of the book. When you review the collection of books that you have already read and discover that you have forgotten parts of them and this is normal, does this mean that you have read the book that you forgot to read a briefing?
In order to be able to talk about books we have not read shamelessly, we must free ourselves from that tyrannical image, the image of the whole culture which the family and the school institutions have imparted to us, and which throughout our lives we seek to identify with, in vain, the truth directed to others is less important than the truth of the ego, which is only reached by the liberation from the yoke of necessity that compels us to appear to people as a culture. That torments us deep down and prevents us from remaining who we really are, ” he asserts that reading is a rubber term with no clear, explicit meaning, and explains the difference between reading and not reading and not reading.

Pierre Bayard warns in his book from falling into the trap of drowning in the books of others, the writer is a simple man who exercises his authority in the flow of ideas and feelings, and may not be completely neutral, but writes because he wishes to express his opinion and idea even if he is not familiar with the whole subject he writes about, and is not better than the reader in any way, he only possessed the tools that made him able to write his vision and experience and science, Prisoners of the text and we have the decision to accept this flow of thought, analyze it, and perhaps reject it.

Betrayal of Memory
One of the fundamental questions in Pierre Bayard ’ s book is: Do books that have already been read and fallen out of our memory still count in the list of books read?

Personally, more than once you found me browsing through a book and finding a comment on one of the footnotes of the book or notes in my handwriting that prove my passing one day, but I do not remember who wrote anything at all at that moment!

All of this leads us to the most important question: what is culture?
Does it resemble the stereotype imposed by family and school institutions, with which we always and in vain seek to identify ourselves?
The subject is thorny and large and this article may not be enough to talk about it, but it is necessary to work to desecrate books and evoke the real self in everything we read without the need to pretend or resemble the usual stereotype, and most importantly not to fabricate culture and remain who we really are and continue to stroll between books and pick the most beautiful fruits, and that reading for fun is the most important thing that books can give us Reading books that we haven ’ t read is the beginning of creative creativity.

LONDON, United Kingdom (CNN Business) -- More than 50 aviation, oil and other companies, including Delta, BP and Boeing, have pledged to replace 10% of the world's jet fuel supply with sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) by 2030.
The move is the boldest in terms of addressing the environmental impact of aviation traffic, and requires a significant increase in the production of this type of fuel, which currently accounts for only 0.1% of the jet fuel used in commercial aviation.
Sustainable jet fuel is a type of biofuel that reduces greenhouse gas emissions by 80% compared to conventional jet fuel.
It is seen as a pillar in efforts to reduce rapidly rising carbon emissions in the aviation sector.
This type of fuel is produced from recycled foods and agricultural waste, such as cooking oil.
Since electric and hydrogen powered aircraft will not be available for at least another decade, even for short flights, "this type of fuel is one of the most important keys to decarbonization in the aviation sector," said Matthew Merullo, an aviation policy officer at the European environmental group Transport & Environment.
Countries around the world, including the Gulf states, consider tackling climate change a priority.
The oil-rich Gulf states are investing in renewables to diversify their economy away from oil.
The UAE, for example, has announced in its Energy Strategy 2050 that it aims to reduce carbon emissions from electricity production by 70%.

A recent study revealed that working from home has environmental benefits and can save the planet, at a time when many companies around the world are preparing to return their employees to work from their offices, after the spread of vaccines for the new coronavirus.
Employees who work remotely four days a week can reduce nitrogen dioxide levels by as much as 10 percent, the study said.
Researchers from the Institute of Environmental Science and Technology of the Autonomous University of Barcelona found that after testing for remote work two, three or four days a week, nitrogen dioxide levels dropped by 4, 8 and 10 percent, respectively.
In their study, published in Urban Sustainability, they found that if 40 percent of service sector employees worked remotely four days a week, it would not only reduce nitrogen dioxide levels by 10 percent, but also reduce traffic emissions by 15 percent.
The authors of the study also noted that the duration of work-related travel would be reduced by rates of 12.5%, 25% and 37.5%, if working remotely two, three or four days a week, respectively.
They also found that online education would reduce the use of private vehicles by 20 percent, and shopping would decrease by 30 percent.
The researchers based their findings on mobility and air quality data obtained in Barcelona during the coronavirus shutdown last year.
The authors of the study advise prioritizing remote work, promoting it as an effective contribution to reducing urban air pollution in the long term and peak pollution in the short term.
As the lead author of the study, Alba Badiaa, suggests resorting to the option of working remotely 4 days a week during periods of heavy pollution, because it is simply based on maximizing remote work and reducing work-related travel and shopping.
The findings of the new study are supported by another study published by NASA in June, which found that global NOx levels have fallen by 15 percent since June 2020, the peak of COVID-19.

Solutions to prevent carbon emissions
There is no reason for delay in deterring climate change and environmental damage, especially by tackling carbon emissions. In some sectors, decarbonisation will improve the consumer ’ s situation and boost the economy. In 10 years, for example, the cost of owning and using a car will be significantly lower for drivers in Europe, as electric cars are more efficient than petrol or diesel cars.
For some “hard-to-mitigate ” industries, decarbonisation will be costly. Shipping rates could increase by 50% or more when container ships burn ammonia or methanol instead of heavy fuel oil.
Also, wholesale steel prices could rise by about 30% if producers use hydrogen as a reducing agent instead of coke, or add carbon capture and storage to existing processes.
Carbon pricing is necessary to allow non-carbon producing companies to compete effectively with those that adopt older, high-emission technology, and the impact on end consumers will be minimal.
If the price of a ton of steel increases by 30%, the price of a car will increase by less than 1%.
Even a 100% increase in sea freight rates would have an impact of less than 1% on the price of jeans made in Bangladesh and bought in Berlin or New York.
For aviation, another sector whose emissions are difficult to cut, electric motors could offer shorter, carbon-neutral, guilt-free journeys, and are cheaper than the ones currently in use.
But because batteries are too heavy to power long-distance electric flights, decarbonization will require sustainable aviation fuel instead of the conventional fuel used today to power aircraft engines.
Whether biofuel or synthetic, it will almost certainly carry a cost premium, which large-scale innovation can reduce over time, but never eliminate.
Thus, free markets, volunteerism and innovation will not be enough to decarbonize aviation; public policy is also required.
One option is to make biofuels or synthetic fuels less expensive, and there is a strong case for public financial support for technology development.
But a permanent subsidy that allows the airline industry to avoid the costs of its carbon pollution would not be acceptable.
Closing the cost gap will therefore require either a carbon tax on conventional aviation fuel, or fuel use authorizations that require airlines to use an ever-increasing proportion of sustainable aviation fuel.
But if this is the cost of decarbonizing the aviation industry, we must tell consumers frankly while putting higher prices in the right context.
Higher cost tickets will not significantly reduce consumer living standards, as air travel accounts for only about 3% of total UK consumer spending.
At the same time, many people who travel on low-cost land transport will earn more than they lose when they travel on expensive planes.
Increased costs for the aviation industry will also not have a top-down distribution effect.

Many people are keen to maintain the integrity and strength of bones by getting adequate amounts of calcium, but many are unaware of some foods, which negatively affect bone health.
The American medical website WebMed, in a report, pointed to the need to reduce these foods, in addition to avoiding habits that reduce the strength of bones.
Smoke.
When a person inhales cigarette smoke regularly, the body can ’ t easily form new healthy bone tissue, and the longer you smoke, the worse it gets.
Smokers are more likely to break bones and take longer to heal, but if you quit, you can reduce these risks and improve the health of your bones, although it can take a few years.
Too much salt.
The higher the amount of salt in food negatively affects bone health, as the more salt you eat, the more calcium your body gets rid of, which leads to weak bones, and foods such as bread, cheese, chips and cold meat contain the highest percentage of salt.
Excess of some drinks.
Eating too much carbonated drinks like cola can impair bone health.
Some studies have linked osteoporosis to both the caffeine and phosphorus found in these drinks.
Other experts have suggested that harm occurs when you choose to consume soda instead of milk or other calcium-containing beverages.
Too much coffee or tea can steal calcium from your bones.
MEDICAL RECIPES
Some medications, especially if you have to take them for a long time, can have a negative effect on your bones.
Some anti-seizure medications and glucocorticoids, such as prednisone and cortisone, can cause bone loss.
Thinness
A low body weight, with a mass index of 18.5 or less, means there is a higher chance of fractures and bone loss.
If you have small bones, do weight-bearing exercises, and ask your doctor “if you need more calcium in your diet. ”
Long distance bike riding
When you pedal on a bike when you ’ re going to work or when you ride it for hours on the weekend, your heart and lungs become stronger.
But your bones?
Not so much.
Since it is not a weight-bearing activity, riding a bike does not increase the density of your bones, unlike walking, running, and hiking.
If you ’ re a cycling enthusiast, you ’ ll want to add some time in the weight room to your routine and mix it with activities like tennis, hiking, dancing, and swimming (water resistance helps your bones).

Five major European airports emit almost as much carbon as the whole of Sweden
Conversation
By: Euronews
These European airports are doubling CO2 emissions in the atmosphere - Christophe Ena / AP
Text size Aa Aa
A study published by the Centre for Airport Carbon Emissions Tracking shows that the carbon dioxide emissions from five of Europe ’ s largest airports combined are comparable to Sweden ’ s overall emissions.
According to figures released Tuesday by The Airport Tracker, the total emissions from London Heathrow, Paris Charles de Gaulle, Frankfurt, Amsterdam and Madrid Barajas airports are 53 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.
Sweden in 2020 emitted about 45.4 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, less than the year before.
Airport Tracker, which tracks airports that emit the most carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, is a tool that shows emissions from aircraft departing from airports around the world.
Airplanes have a role in reducing CO2 emissions using wind, and studies published in January revealed that airlines could significantly reduce their fuel consumption and CO2 emissions if the planes they use become more efficient at flying and facing the wind.
Scientists at the University of Reading said in a study published at the time that commercial flights between New York and London during the winter of 2019-2020 could have used up to 16% less fuel if pilots had fully benefited from the air currents and strong winds.
Since many flights from these airports (London Heathrow, Paris Charles de Gaulle, Frankfurt, Amsterdam and Madrid Barajas) have destinations outside Europe, they are exempt from EU and UK cap-and-trade schemes, which only apply to domestic flights in the EU.
For example, 80 percent of emissions from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport come from long-haul flights, while smaller airports, such as Krakow, Poland, are largely short-haul.
Smaller airports are taxed more than larger ones with longer flights and higher emissions.
“Unlike cars or power plants, most flight emissions are released outside Europe ’ s borders, which means that the bulk of emissions from European airports are blatantly overlooked, ” said Jo Darden, director of aviation at T & E.
"We can now see the alarming extent of emissions from airports and it is clear that the aviation industry is not doing enough to reduce pollution," she said.
ACI ’ s Airport Carbon Program is the only institutionalized international airport carbon management program that recognizes efforts to manage and reduce carbon emissions at airports, and is implemented at a consistent pace at airports around the world.
Some airports around the world are adopting many green initiatives and programs, in line with a commitment to reduce carbon emissions, which are part of the green development strategy, where they resort to strict control of electricity and water consumption, as well as implement an integrated waste management system aimed at achieving zero.
The aviation industry added more than 1 billion metric tons of CO2 emissions to the atmosphere in 2019, while emissions have since declined due to the coronavirus pandemic and the disruption it caused to airlines and air traffic around the world, but this is likely to be temporary and could rise again over time.

Dr. Rania Al-Mashat, Minister of International Cooperation, said that the operationalization of the African Free Trade Agreement is an important factor for the sustainable growth and recovery of the continent.
She pointed out that there are three main factors that must be worked on in the continent to move forward towards benefiting from the Continental Free Trade Agreement and enhancing joint action between the countries of the continent, namely stimulating the participation of the private sector and facilitating the infrastructure of decisions and regulatory legislation, as well as encouraging e-commerce.
This came during the participation of the Minister of International Cooperation in a panel discussion entitled “Africa in the Era of the New Trade War ” at the summit of the African CEO Forum, held from 28 to 30 September, with the participation of a number of high-level speakers, including the Prime Minister of Mauritania, Mr. Mohamed Ould Bilal Massoud, and the Executive Director of the International Finance Corporation, Mr. Mokhtar Diop.
She added that the world has taken many protectionist decisions before the Corona pandemic, which in turn affected the movement of international trade, and then the pandemic came at the beginning of 2020 to impose more restrictions on the movement of international trade, causing increased cost of international trade, harm to consumers and higher prices, as well as reduced competition and productivity in both developing and developed countries.
She pointed out that the epidemic contributed to changing many global systems, norms and rules, and highlighted new challenges, including climate change, the world ’ s need for equality, and the dangers of migration, which requires concerted global efforts and collective action to address these challenges.
Al-Mashat said that the economic repercussions of the epidemic are still unclear and the exact extent of its impact is not known, as the International Monetary Fund predicted that the global economy will shrink by 5.2% this year due to the negative effects of the epidemic.
The African Free Trade Area, the largest in the world, could open new horizons for the African economy and serve as a model for multilateral cooperation and international trade, with exports between the continent accounting for 16.6% of total world exports in 2017, compared to 68% in Europe and 59% in Asia. This points to the huge untapped potential.
“The establishment of the African Free Trade Area (AFTA), aimed at improving the economies of the continent, which is home to 1.3 billion people with a GDP of $3.4 trillion, could be a driving force for sustainable recovery, inclusive growth and overcoming the challenges of the Coronavirus pandemic on the continent, ” she said.
Al-Mashat pointed out that the World Bank report, which expected the African Free Trade Area to contribute to lifting 68 million citizens of the continent out of poverty, living on less than $5.5 a day, enhancing the competitiveness of economies, stimulating productivity, achieving sustainable and inclusive growth, as well as lifting about 30 million African citizens out of extreme poverty.
During the workshop on the Continental Free Trade Agreement, which was attended by government officials from Nigeria, Cameroon and Namibia, the Forum stressed the importance of the free trade agreement and the imperative of enhancing the role of e-commerce, as well as South-South and triangular cooperation to support sustainable development in the continent. continent of Africa.

Ultimately, this would promote inclusive economic recovery, benefiting youth, women and small and medium-sized enterprises engaged in e-commerce.

Carbon footprint
According to a press release published on the official website of the University of Georgia on October 14, sustainability research specialist Dr. Bonnet Doividi believes that “if we can secure the supply of raw materials and provide appropriate economic incentives for supply operations, it is likely that we will produce sustainable aviation fuel from the mustard plant grown in the southern United States. ”

Competitive price supported by political trends
Developed and tested a few years ago, the first jet flight based on pure biofuel derived from Brasica Carinata was successfully launched in 2012, but the cost was much higher than traditional jet fuel.
In their new study, researchers did not aim to demonstrate that sustainable fuels are viable, but to estimate the cost-effectiveness of sustainable fuels and reduce emissions.
