An expert has suggested that super-robots, designed so that they are indistinguishable from people and with thinking skills far superior to that of humans, are likely to become a reality within two decades.
Janet Adams, head of operations at SingularityNET, warned that there are currently no safeguards against the threat of these machines being deployed as soldiers – with new laws governing humanity ’ s relationship to artificial intelligence (AI) sure to become an increasing necessity in the years to come.
She was speaking after SingularityNET unveiled Grace, a new robotic nursing assistant, at the 14th General Artificial Intelligence (AGI) Conference, for what was only the robot ’ s second public engagement.
Grace was designed by SingularityNET founder, Dr. Ben Gurtzel, to look and behave like a human being who is also capable of solving complex problems.
It provides an indication of what kind of things will come from general AI — defined as the virtual ability of a machine to learn any intellectual task a human can do.
But Adams told Express it was pointless to compare human and technological development.
“Technology is advancing dramatically every month, while biological evolution has done little in the last 100,000 years.
And there ’ s a difference more important than speed — biological evolution is driven by survival, while technological development seems to be moving forward relentlessly, pursuing a broader set of goals than just survival — goals like learning and creating more and more, and also — if we make things right — beneficial goals like maximizing human well-being and all other emotions. ”
“The technological singularity we ’ re talking about is a moment in the future when technological change becomes so rapid — and so far-reaching — that it breaks our assumptions about the human condition.
He gave people different dates for when they expect this to happen, 2040 to 2050 is probably a common guess, but who knows?
Dr. Gortzel suggested that the singularity could come much sooner. "
“Robots with human-like appearance and behavior will be a very likely outcome of technological uniqueness, but this may not be a fundamental advance like the ability to think and learn beyond humans. ”
Adams acknowledged that HBO ’ s science fiction series Westworld, with its focus on robots in a futuristic amusement park that begins to develop self-awareness, touches on many of these topics.
“The main lesson we ’ re learning from Westworld is that if we want AI robots to treat us at the human level in a meaningful way, we ’ re likely to treat them beneficially.
“This is not exactly a surprising or advanced conclusion — the most likely path to meaningful AI is to anchor sophisticated AI minds in the early stages of mutual empathy, assistance, love and co-creation with humans. ”
Adams pointed out that such rapid technological developments will inevitably force humanity to ask itself some research questions in the future.
“The day an AI or robot declares itself self-aware and shouts that it wants equal rights, it will be hard for most humans to ignore that harshly.
Legal, economic and cultural systems will need to adapt radically and quickly to accommodate the new realities that various individual technologies have opened up on the horizon.
Eventually, the new rules will be set by humans and artificial intelligence working together. ”
Adams stressed that there are currently no guarantees about the ways in which advanced technology will be used increasingly, raising some disturbing possibilities.
“It would be great to say that this technology can ’ t be used maliciously, but life isn ’ t that easy.
As human beings and as a society, we have to be vigilant, we will have to make ethical choices about how to nurture these powerful new minds. ”
Regardless, it is clear that the advanced technology that supports the development of robots is here to stay.
Adams said: “Robots will play an increasing role in our daily lives, as part of the continuous progress and penetration of artificial intelligence.
In a decade or two, AI will be as surrounding our daily lives as electric power – with a subtle combination of general AI and narrow AI systems helping us in every aspect of our daily routine.
“Human-like robots will play a role where deep emotional connection is important, such as education and healthcare, but the overall activity of the AI matrix will bypass any given device or interface. ”
“It will be very important that this pervasive AI matrix is controlled and directed in a democratic and decentralized way, rather than a single government or company.
This is the primary goal of the SingularityNET project – using blockchain to create a decentralized infrastructure for global AI systems, including those that operate human robots. ”

Artificial intelligence beats humans in mind games
Artificial intelligence is similar to human intelligence in terms of its ability to learn through play, but it is superior in terms of time, experiences that may take a human to gain years, artificial intelligence can gain within a day.
Artificial Intelligence Succeeds in Deception and Perfects Multiplayer Poker
In mid-2019, the artificial intelligence program Pluribus played with five professional players in a poker game called Texas Holdem – No Limit, the most popular form of poker in the world.
Bloribus beat them all, and it was the first time that artificial intelligence beat the best professional human players in a complex six-player game.
BlueRebus was developed in collaboration between Facebook ’ s Artificial Intelligence Lab and Carnegie Mellon University.
Poker is one of the most difficult games, and is radically different from a game such as chess, where the opponent's cards remain closed, and there is no perfect move, but may sometimes require maneuvers that suggest the player has cards other than those he actually owns.
Poker belongs to the category of "missing information" games, so there is no accurate strategy that starts from the analysis of all possible movements of the opponent, hence its importance because it resembles a lot of real world situations, and therefore its techniques can have many practical uses, such as pricing products and steering self-driving cars during busy traffic.
On this occasion, the cover of the August 30, 2019 issue of "Science" magazine, "Artificial intelligence succeeds in deception and mastery of multiplayer poker."
The last stop of the human mind.
The superiority of computers over humans in mind games dates back to 1997 when they defeated the world chess champion.
When IBM began developing a computer capable of playing chess professionally, Gary Kasparov, then world chess champion, stated, “No computer can beat me. ”
In 1997, IBM ’ s Deep Blue supercomputer defeated him.
This was the first defeat of the human mind to a machine in a complex game, where the total number of possibilities in one game is 1 and to the right is 123 zeros (the average number of moves per game per party is 37).
The cover of Newsweek's May 5, 1997 issue was "The Last Stand of the Human Mind."
Watson is on the line.
IBM not only developed an automated system to defeat the world chess champion, but also developed another system to defeat the champions of the cultural games.
In 2011, artificial intelligence made headlines when IBM ’ s Watson beat two contestants on the popular TV show Jeopardy, especially since one of the contestants, Ken Kennings, held the record for the number of times he won the show (74 consecutive victories).
It took Watson five years to prepare for the task, including four years to learn English, one year to read and memorize everything published on Wikipedia and a few thousand other books.
MBC Saudi Arabia has prepared and presented an Arabic version of the program under the name of "The Stake".
Google is on the line.
In 2017, AlphaGo, an artificial-intelligence-based program designed by Google ’ s DeepMind, beat the world champion KG in China ’ s Go.
Go is an ancient and very complex Chinese game, which is more like chess, but more difficult for computers, as the total number of possibilities is 1 and to the right is 360 zeros (the average number of moves per game is 150), more than the number of atoms in the known universe.
From learning by training with data to learning by self-training across rules
AlphaGo has defeated the world champion after training on hundreds of thousands of human gaming data.
The new version, AlphaGo Zero, did not use any human data; after providing the program with the rules of the game, he trained himself by playing millions of games with himself and within a few days of training crushed the original AlphaGo program.
This breakthrough in artificial intelligence technology was made by the DeepMind team.
David Silver, Principal Researcher at DeepMind and Professor at University College London, said: “By not using human data or human experience, we have already removed the limitations that artificial intelligence had to use human knowledge.
Artificial intelligence is able to create knowledge of itself from the first principles. ”
Is artificial intelligence superior to humans?
To answer this question, we must distinguish between the two types of artificial intelligence.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is divided into two types; Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) and Artificial Narrow Intelligence (ANI).
When a computer can learn a single individual mental task (such as playing chess), it is called limited artificial intelligence (ANI), and general artificial intelligence (AGI) means that the computer has the ability to learn any mental task that a human can perform at a level not lower than his own.
A third type is Artificial Super Intelligence (ASI), although its birth was unexpected several decades ago.
The best test for machine intelligence is still the Turing Test, invented by English mathematician Alan Turing in 1950.
Three computers are used in this test that are isolated from each other.
The first is operated by a human who asks a set of pre-prepared questions, the second is used by a human to answer the questions, and the third is used by a computer program designed to answer the same questions.
The computer assigned to the answer successfully passes this exam, if the questioner cannot determine whether the answer he received was provided by the computer or by a human.
According to Alan Turing, “A computer deserves to be called intelligent if it can trick a human into thinking that it is a human being, not a machine. ”
The term “artificial intelligence ” was coined by American computer scientist John McCarthy in 1956 when he invited a group of researchers from a variety of disciplines to a summer workshop to discuss machine thinking.
According to the types of intelligence referred to, we are still in the stage of limited artificial intelligence, when is the intelligence of the machine expected to reach the level of human intelligence?
Raymond Kurzweil, an American computer scientist, says that “2029 is the right date when I expect AI to pass the Turing test and thus achieve human levels of intelligence, ” but most expert surveys suggest that this could happen between 2040 and 2050.

Sustainability as the basis for the eradication of hunger
In 2015, 193 countries met within the framework of the United Nations and pledged to end global hunger by 2030 as part of the Sustainable Development Agenda.
With less than a decade left, the odds of achieving that goal seem slim.
Clearly, improving these prospects requires governments and the private sector to simultaneously address the global food and environmental crises.
Food insecurity has increased in recent years as a result of conflict and climate change, as well as the 2019 Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic and the accompanying global economic crisis.
Today, as many as 811 million people suffer from hunger, including an additional 132 million people who were classified as malnourished during the pandemic, and another 3 billion people who are too poor to afford a healthy diet.
The fight against hunger has traditionally focused on producing more food – but this has come at a high environmental cost.
Agriculture consumes 70% of the world ’ s fresh water and 40% of its land.
Agriculture has contributed to the imminent extinction of about 1 million species.
Food production also generates 30% of greenhouse-gas emissions, the main cause of deforestation in the Amazon.
Policymakers seeking to eradicate hunger today face an extremely difficult dilemma: preventing billions of people from going hungry while saving the planet.
For example, fertilizer subsidies may increase crop yields and reduce hunger, but they may also lead to overuse of nitrogen, thus damaging the soil.
Similarly, livestock farming and rice farming emit methane, a greenhouse gas stronger than carbon dioxide.
The most effective way to reduce methane emissions is to tax them.
But this would cause food prices to rise, affecting poor consumers ’ access to food, and threatening the livelihoods of farmers and ranchers.
Therefore, countries need to establish an optimal level of environmental pollution that does not reduce agricultural productivity or undermine the social and economic well-being of the poor.
We need a solution that feeds most mouths without endangering the planet.
Reaching a workable plan requires looking at diets holistically – a major departure from the current, isolated approach.
To avoid any unintended consequences, it is critical to quantify any data swaps.
Turning data-driven strategies into action on the ground also requires concerted efforts to boost public and private investment.
No single intervention will solve the problem of hunger.
But studies suggest that a combination of key measures aimed at increasing farm productivity and reducing food loss and waste could reduce the number of people chronically hungry by 314 million in the next decade, and provide 568 million people with healthy diets.
Expanding national safety nets across countries, including school feeding programmes, could provide an additional 2.4 billion people with access to a healthy diet by 2030.
Another study shows how a series of low-cost initiatives could end hunger for 500 million people by 2030 while also reducing greenhouse-gas emissions in line with the goals of the 2015 Paris climate agreement.
These include agricultural research and development projects to produce food more efficiently, information services that provide farmers with weather forecasts and crop prices, literacy programs for women – who account for nearly half of small farmers in developing countries – and expanded social protection.
All this can be achieved if rich countries double their food security assistance to $26 billion a year until 2030, and the poorest countries maintain their annual investments at $19 billion.
Automation can help manage trade-offs between food production and environmental protection.
For example, equipment called AgBots, which are similar to small farm vehicles, can recognize and remove weeds.
Because they don ’ t use expensive chemical herbicides, they can help reduce the cost of weeding by 90% and protect the soil from potentially harmful chemicals.
Similarly, artificial intelligence technologies and cloud solutions can detect pest infested areas using drone imaging.
The data collected can help guide and inform decisions by farmers regarding irrigation, agriculture and fertilization, and indicate the best time of year for the sale of a particular crop.
Governments must now work with the private sector to make high-tech precision farming systems available at lower costs, especially to small farmers.
The good news is that private companies are increasingly keen to promote sustainability – including through “blended finance ” schemes that combine initial investment by governments or multilateral financial institutions with subsequent trade finance.
This approach can effectively reduce the risk of private financing and encourage investment in improving food systems.
For example, the governments of the United States and the Netherlands are working with German coffee company Neumann Café Group and three European banks to provide a $25 million loan to smallholder farmers in Colombia, Kenya, Honduras, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Peru and Uganda to promote sustainable coffee production.
Banks initially rejected the proposal because small farmers are usually excluded from financial services, leaving them unable to prove their creditworthiness and turning them into a high-risk category in the eyes of commercial lenders.
But banks signed on to the scheme after the Dutch government and Neumann Café Group agreed to cover the first 10 percent of the losses if the initiative did not work, with the US government absorbing 40 percent of the remaining losses.
Critics will argue that countries should be individually responsible for reversing rising levels of hunger through domestic policies.
While this may be true, other problems such as greenhouse-gas emissions cannot be addressed by a single country or region and need to be addressed and funded globally.
Saving the planet should not necessarily come at the expense of feeding the poor, and vice versa.
If governments properly organize their efforts, there is still a chance to eradicate poverty by 2030.
* Chief Economist of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.

Researchers from the University of Arizona divided the 238 volunteer participants into groups equally between men and women, asking them to complete a series of math problems in return for a reward and studying gender differences in competition.
Sharing Gains
Participants were given the opportunity to choose a guaranteed prize for getting a correct result, a larger prize if they were the best performers, or a larger prize with the option of sharing the winnings with the losers.
60% of the participants chose the opportunity to compete while sharing their gains with the losers, while only 35% decided to compete if they won the lottery.
In contrast, 51% of men chose the winner-take-all option, compared to 52.5% of men who chose to win a bigger prize for better performance.
Expressionist
Researcher Mary Rigdon, assistant director at the University of Arizona Research Center, says the purpose of the study was to explore the "relatively new theory" that women are less competitive and less willing to take risks than men.
Wage gap
The study is part of a broader series of work on how market structure, information and incentives affect behavior, particularly around gender.
Professor Rigdon and her colleague Alessandra Cassar, a professor of economics at the University of San Francisco, also worked side-by-side to examine the gender pay gap.
Professor Rigdon said: “If we want to close the gender pay gap, we have to understand its causes, as well as the solutions and remedies required for it. ”
Expressionist
2% less pay

Why Are Solar Storms Worrying Scientists?
Earth is bracing for the cannibalistic solar storm, which has been preceded by other storms that have affected communications and power grids in several countries.
Why is this particular storm causing so much anxiety among scientists and what effects it could have on Earth?
Power grid operators in several countries have received warnings against the backdrop of the upcoming solar storm
Over the past few days, Earth has been hit by a large magnetic storm, which occurred as a result of a series of explosions that occurred on the surface of the Sun on Monday and Tuesday (November 1 and 2).
These eruptions are associated with the appearance of sunspots, magnetic storms that erupt on the surface of the Sun.
Both sunspots and solar activity occur in a cycle of about 11 years, and storms this week are symptoms of the current phase of the sun in that cycle.
“Over the past several years, we have had very little solar activity, but now it ’ s escalating and we ’ re moving very quickly to the next solar cycle limit, which we expect in 2025, ” Bill Murtaugh, program coordinator at NOAA ’ s Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC), told Profound Space.
Murtaugh said: “We are seeing more activity than expected with this rise in solar cycle activity which has increased our interest. ”
As this week ’ s storms have shown, solar activity doesn ’ t just affect the Sun: when those storms approach Earth, solar eruptions can cause a range of phenomena called “space weather ” with effects ranging from interesting auroral displays to satellite damage.
The "cannibal" storm.
The geomagnetic storm originated this week as a result of explosions in the solar corona, referred to as CMEs, bubbles that scientists resemble as if the sun burps occasionally.
“These explosions are a billion-ton cloud of plasma gas with magnetic fields, so it ’ s safe to say that the Sun launched a massive magnet into space 150 million kilometers from Earth, ” Murtaugh said.
But the Earth has its own magnetic field, and the magnetic fields that overlap in space often have bad effects.
Murtaugh says of the arrival of CME explosions to Earth: "The two magnets will come together (solar and terrestrial) and this will create this geomagnetic storm."
Sometimes, these violent solar storms can grow on their way through space to multiply their impact.
The geomagnetic storm originated this week as a result of a series of explosions that merged as solar storms moved faster than their predecessors.
Solar storms appear on the planet through the aurora borealis phenomenon.
The strength of such a solar storm depends on both the size of the cannibalistic storm CME and the distance between the storm's magnetic fields and Earth.
Scientists believe that the solar storm will be large enough to interfere with the Earth ’ s magnetic field, compounding the effects of this interference.
Scientists are monitoring the movement of the cannibal solar storm through space through a space shuttle called DSCOVR launched by the Deep Space Climate Observatory (NOAA), which hovers 1 million miles (1.5 million kilometers) from Earth in the direction of the Sun.
“We won ’ t know the magnetic structure of that massive solar storm until the DSCOVR spacecraft hits, at which point, the cannibalistic storm will hit Earth in 20 or 30 minutes, so the geomagnetic storm that it will cause is very imminent.
Space weather.
On the ground!
Geomagnetic storms are not just an interesting phenomenon, as these events can interfere with the planet ’ s critical infrastructure, including power grids, navigation satellites and aircraft radio communications in remote areas.
That ’ s why the Space Weather Forecasting Center was created where Martagh and his colleagues monitor space weather to alert operators of this infrastructure to the possibility of problems or service malfunctions.
Solar storms cause communications to stop and disrupt the GPS tracking system
For this week ’ s storm, warnings have already been issued to all power grid operators in several countries.
According to the Frankfurter Rundschau website, this type of solar storm is expected to cause widespread disruptions to power and communications networks.
When a solar storm hits Earth, it means that the amount of energy emitted by the Sun has increased sharply to reach Earth in the form of X-rays and ultraviolet rays.
This radiation in turn increases the ionization of the upper layers of the atmosphere – affecting shortwave propagation as well as GPS positioning accuracy.
In 1989, a solar storm caused a 12-hour power outage across the Canadian province of Quebec as the United States dealt with a number of power plant losses, according to NASA.
One of the largest known solar storms is Carrington, which broke out in 1859 and caused widespread disruption of telegraph systems in the world, so that auroras could be seen from the Hawaiian Islands, according to NASA.
Unfortunately, space weather is more difficult to predict than weather on Earth.
This is because scientists are still working to understand how the sun actually works.
Murtaugh noted that NASA ’ s Parker Solar Probe and the European-American Orbital Solar Missions all produce data that will help scientists address these mysteries, but it doesn ’ t make forecasting any easier at the moment.

Riham, a 24-year-old who lives with her parents and five younger siblings, has chosen a shop, most of whose customers are women, to ease parents' fears of mixing with men.
“I felt guilty when I asked my father for anything.
But since I started working, I am proud to be able to help my family. ”
Every day, thousands of women across the country go out to work, something that would not have come to mind just a few years ago, but has now become a norm under reforms led by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to modernize the kingdom.
It highlights its progress on women ’ s issues, but does not allow political parties or elections to take place.
There are currently no women in the Saudi cabinet or in any senior advisory roles.
The Shura Council has only 30 women among its 150 members.
However, women now make up 33% of the total workforce, nearly double the proportion five years ago.
Women of different age groups and educational levels are now accepting jobs that were previously restricted to Saudi men and expatriate workers in restaurants, supermarkets, accounting firms and graphic designers.
As part of the reforms, women have been allowed to drive since 2018.
But Reham al-Ahmad, who earns 4,500 riyals ($1,200) a month, cannot afford driving lessons, aside from the price of a car.
“I spend about a third of my salary on a taxi, ” she said, adding that she was saving money to buy a car.
“But I ’ m really happy that I have a job where I get a private income at the end of the day.
I never thought it was possible for me. ”
A small number of women have long worked in Saudi Arabia, but their jobs have traditionally been in the government sector of teaching and medical care, following strict gender segregation rules in place, but with the easing of restrictions on mixing genders, driving cars and some aspects of male guardianship, companies have started hiring more women.
This is especially true in the retail and hospitality sectors, where a 2011 plan to replace cheaper expatriate workers with nationals was launched to tackle unemployment among Saudis, which now stands at 11 percent.
Economist Jennifer Beck said, “Many of the jobs held by women have traditionally been held by non-Saudis. ”
The new laws have made it easier for women to work in jobs that require direct interaction with customers.
Her research shows that the number of Saudi women in the private sector jumped to 935,508 in 2021 from 56,000 in 2010, and continues to rise.
In Unaizah, a city in the Qassim region at the heart of a conservative society, trends are changing, and more women are working, though some are wary of turning against tradition.
Ghada al-Salman, 33, after graduating from university, struggled to find work in Qassim, where unemployment among women is about 18 percent, three times the rate of unemployment among men.
It turned to the bakery industry, eventually opening three stores with 45 employees.
More recently, at the Dates Festival, she promoted the production of her bakery, Rose Raben Bakery (Pink Ribbon), one of the few women-owned businesses in Qassim.
She said, “If it weren ’ t for my parents, I wouldn ’ t have been able to do any of this. ”
“Most parents here still don ’ t approve of their daughters working all day with men, even if they are bosses and even if they wear the niqab, ” she said.
She wears face coverings and a long black cloak like most women in public places in Unaizah, but faces reproach from older conservatives.
A man in his 60s complained about the speed of social change, and he relishes eating one of her cupcakes.
The man, who asked not to be named, said the government “tells us that women should work, but it ’ s against our tradition. ”
Others believe that these changes are long overdue.
Rana al-Turki, 45, joined her father ’ s oil and gas company in 2000, and was one of the first women to work at the company, working for years in a gender-neutral office.
Rana al-Turki, who is now the owner and one of the directors of Rawabi Holding, said: “At the time, the men were not even polite.
No one would say good morning or ride the elevator with me, and they couldn ’ t even stand standing with me in one room. ”
He added: “Thank God things have changed.
In my day, we were even afraid to ask for a salary.
But girls these days come in and negotiate hard.
They know their value. ”
Yet the gender pay gap in Saudi Arabia stands at 49 percent, according to research by the non-governmental Al-Nahda Association.
“Social trends continue to govern women ’ s entry into the labor market, ” said Hala al-Dosari, a Saudi women ’ s rights expert who works in the United States, noting that most new jobs for women are poorly paid.
Although laws to prevent harassment and discrimination were in place, women continued to be harassed and denied their rights.
Economist Jennifer Beck said some employers still ask women for their guardian ’ s permission to work, despite recent reforms that give women more control over their lives.
An employer at one of the biggest companies told Reuters he preferred to hire women because they worked harder than men and earned half the pay.
Nearly 400 companies interviewed by Peak ’ s research group said Saudi women were paid less than men, and a third said women were more productive than men.
But for many Saudi women, these are only growing troubles.
Ghada al-Salman, the owner of the bakery, said: “Young women ask me all the time how they can achieve what I have achieved.
10 years ago, it was impossible.
Now the future is yours. ”

The reform efforts and legislation undertaken in recent years in accordance with the Kingdom ’ s Vision 2030 have reflected the objectives of empowering women by overcoming some obstacles related to freedom of movement, work, education, obtaining travel documents and completing many government transactions.
The Saudi Ministry of Justice has given women the ability to document company incorporation contracts, agency issuance and dissolution, mortgage, real estate emptying, debt declarations and repayment, and other necessary transactions.

Another example of a Saudi female entrepreneur who managed to cover the Saudi market with a pure national industry, for products that are ISO and UNIDO certified, and also contributed to the employment of a large number of Saudi girls in this project.

The Kingdom, through the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development, has launched a number of projects supporting women, such as the National Platform for Women Leaders, which serves as a tool to enable entities to communicate and nominate women leaders for leadership and military positions, boards of directors or official delegations in international forums based on smart search criteria among female applicants.
There is also a leadership training and mentoring initiative to enrich the knowledge of Saudi women leaders, among other initiatives.
The total number of establishments owned by Saudi businesswomen during the first half of 2021 amounted to more than 450 establishments funded by SR 432 million, thus increasing the percentage of benefiting businesswomen to 124%, compared to the same period in 2020.
One of the great historical achievements for the empowerment of Saudi women is the crowning of Riyadh as the “Capital of Arab Women ” in 2020, coinciding with its chairmanship of the 39th session of the Arab Women ’ s Committee, which highlighted the national will to support women ’ s gains in all fields, including increasing women ’ s economic participation and effective presence in administrative positions.
One of the fruits of the vision on women ’ s empowerment is that the Kingdom has made significant progress in four global indicators on women ’ s empowerment, including achieving first place in “achieving gender equality in enrollment in higher education ” based on the results of the“ Gender Gap ” index issued by the World Economic Forum.
In addition, the Kingdom achieved the largest improvement in the Women, Business and Law Index, a jump of 150.7% from 2017, according to the results of the World Bank ’ s Women, Business and the Law Index released in February 2021.
The Kingdom also advanced 33 places in the index of “equal pay between women and men in similar jobs, ” according to the report issued by the World Economic Forum.
With regard to equality between men and women and the fight against discrimination in employment, the labour system does not differentiate between women and men in terms of rights and duties. There is also no discrimination in remuneration when the value and quality of work is equal.
There is full equality between men and women in the job-search subsidy, as well as in the support for training and employment, there is equality in terms of the amount of support for training costs, remuneration or duration of support, as well as in the retirement age for men and women.
The Kingdom's regulations also guarantee all citizens the right to education free of charge without any discrimination, and equal access to higher education scholarship programmes.
Saudi women have proven that they have a leading role in building the economic renaissance through sustainable participation, being a key partner in building and strengthening the country ’ s capabilities and achieving sustainable economic development.

The Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research (KISR), in cooperation with the Kuwait Foundation for the Advancement of Sciences (KFAS) and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), completed a study project to investigate the impact of ocean acidification and ocean surface warming on the growth and abundance of local shrimp.

The sea and some phytoplankton species, but that does not mean that this is a positive thing because the increased growth of these organisms can disrupt the food chain, biodiversity and ecosystem mechanisms and construction.

Study shows the impact of household chores on the health of older adults
A new scientific study has confirmed that housework, from cleaning, dusting and washing floors, carpets and windows, may promote the health of older people.
According to the Guardian, regular physical activity “improves physical and mental health, reduces the risk and effects of chronic diseases, and reduces the chances of sudden falls, immobility and mortality among older people. ”
The study, published in the journal BMJ Open, was conducted on 240 participants aged 65 to 90 living in Yishon, Singapore.
The researchers, from the Geriatrics Research Institute of Singapore, asked participants to complete tests related to cognitive function, as well as do some activities to assess their physical abilities, such as standing and sitting as quickly as possible.
Participants were then asked how much household work they did, including light household chores (such as flossing) and heavy household chores (such as cleaning floors and washing windows).
The team found that cognitive scores and attention scores were 14 per cent higher for older adults who did large amounts of strenuous housework – an average of 131 minutes per week – than for those who did not do such work at all.
Elderly people who did strenuous household chores were able to perform standing and sitting exercises faster than others, and the researchers also confirmed that they were less likely to fall.
The team also found that cognitive scores were 5 per cent higher for older adults who reported high levels of light housework, averaging 902 minutes per week.

Study: Homework Improves Physical Health and Increases Cognition for Seniors
Wednesday ، 24 November 2021 10: 00 AM
Benefits of Housework for Seniors
Written by Fatima Khalil
Leave a comment and read the comments of the readers.
A new study by the University of Singapore revealed that housework may be the key to staying healthy in old age, these include vacuuming, washing and ironing, and the researchers explained that people over the age of 65 who spend a lot of time in housework have better physical strength, improve their mental intelligence and have greater protection from the risk of falling.
The researchers interviewed nearly 500 participants, aged between 21 and 90, about the frequency of routines and other types of physical activity and were given a score of "housework intensity."
Light housework was defined as washing dishes, dust, making beds, washing, ironing, arranging and cooking meals, and heavy housework included cleaning windows, changing bedding, vacuuming, washing the floor, and manual labor.
The study found that the combination of light and heavy household chores was "associated with higher cognitive function" among people over the age of 65, but not in younger adults.
Retirees who engaged in more strenuous housework scored 14 percent higher in attention span, while those who regularly performed light tasks scored 12 percent better on memory tests.
Meanwhile, those who regularly perform the most physically demanding jobs around the house can stand up more quickly.
They also had better balance and coordination scores, suggesting that housework could help protect people from falling into old age — a common cause of hospitalization.
Lead author Professor Xiu Liangwei told the British Medical Journal: “After adjusting to other types of regular physical activity, the results showed that housework was associated with sharper mental abilities and better physical ability but only among the older age group. ”
He explained that the combination of light and heavy household chores is associated with higher cognitive function of the brain, specifically in the areas of attention and memory, among the elderly.

Technologies that blossomed in the Corona Pandemic and will stay with us forever
The coronavirus pandemic, which has ravaged the world and continues to have repercussions, has forced people, businesses and society at large to adapt quickly to a new and uncertain reality, a reality that has changed our usual way of dealing with things, isolating us from people and the natural life to which we are accustomed.
Interestingly, recent technological innovations have stepped up to fill this void, as many technical advances have been made in the fields of medicine (such as vaccine development via technology using digital twins), virtual communication, e-learning, artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT) and e-commerce.
None of these technologies are entirely new, but the rapid pace of their adoption, especially in the healthcare and education sectors – which are usually very slow to adopt new technologies – was unexpected, and what usually took many years to adopt, happened within a few months as digital connectivity suddenly became the focal point of our daily lives.
Now, some 20 months into the epidemic, it is clear that many of these technologies are likely to stay with us for many years to come, perhaps forever.
Digital Home Work Desks
A recent survey by the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) of UK businesses found that 75% of them have adopted new technologies and technological innovations to improve their productivity since the start of the epidemic, most notably working online from home. More than 65% of respondents still work from home at least part of the time, and 25% work from home most of the time.
Interestingly, the majority of people who work from a home office report that they are happy with this new way of working, according to businesstech, which published the survey results.
The pandemic has led to the collapse of many companies and cost cuts in many others, so people around the world have developed multiple and diverse income streams, all based on working from home, to compensate for salary cuts or to find new work instead of lost ones.
For employers, they have reaped benefits such as reduced office rent, bills, insurance and maintenance costs, as well as increased employee productivity.
Sixty per cent of business owners are happy to reduce their office space, while 43 per cent believe that by 2030 there will be no need for offices at all, and there is no doubt that the future of work will be remote and the digital home office is here to stay.
Telemedicine
The health sector has long been slow to adopt new technologies, however, the pandemic has changed this forever, as industry leaders have recognized the value of technologies such as telemedicine and the use of robots to limit the spread of the virus.
There are hundreds of ways in which technology is changing the way health care is delivered and managed, for organizations the biggest challenge is prioritization, and for individuals, the biggest challenge is accessible personal health care that puts them in control of the future of their existence in this life, as digitalhealth recently reported.
In countries and cities where the 5G network is available, patients, paramedics and medical experts communicate remotely in real time.
This collaboration between doctors and paramedics, using high-speed 5G technology, has enabled healthcare professionals to diagnose and treat patients remotely when they cannot reach the hospital.
During the epidemic, access to health services was limited so that hospitals could focus on treating those infected with the coronavirus, and this forced health care providers to adopt alternative methods of consultation and services via video conferencing, telephone consultations via the Internet, e-mail or smartphone applications, research found that these virtual services were particularly valuable for older people.
The pandemic has created many changes in the world ’ s healthcare industry, changes that remain and will forever change the future of medicine.
E-Learning
During the pandemic, schools and universities closed, and millions of students around the world were sent home.
Suddenly students and parents had to adapt to digital distance learning using tools such as video conferencing, language learning applications, e-learning platforms and programs, and virtual education, and educational institutions from schools and universities made great efforts to ensure that students had access to the Internet and the technology needed to promote inclusion and digital learning.
The COVID-19 pandemic has forced schools and universities around the world, which have been slow to adopt technology, to change in a very short period of time, and with the pandemic now coming to an end, many universities around the world have decided to adopt a “blended learning ” approach (online and live teaching) for the future. A report on the future of digital education.
Contactless transactions
In the business world, the pandemic has promoted contactless transactions to reduce the spread of the virus through direct communication, and the most important technologies that have become popular are contactless payment, express shopping (without cashiers), online shopping, and biometric check-in for travel and accommodation.
All the major online companies reported a significant increase in business during the epidemic, and in fact, these safe and convenient innovations have evolved due to the increased power of data processing with better image sensors, smarter artificial intelligence, and much faster communication networks, and these methods of contactless dealing in various fields will certainly increase in the future with the steady development of technology.
Artificial Intelligence
We are currently living at the beginning of an era of artificial intelligence that has accelerated dramatically due to the epidemic, and more and more companies are using artificial intelligence to develop themselves, and re-modernize their business models in order to achieve long-term success.
During the epidemic, many companies have replaced people with artificial intelligence to limit the spread of the virus, and artificial intelligence has been widely used in many countries, not only to predict the spread of the virus, but also to monitor, predict and manage healthcare resources.
In the future, AI will move from a technology enabler to a technology driver, and thus, AI will become an essential part of all business strategies to achieve long-term value.
Innovations will remain
At the height of the pandemic, many businesses could have stopped working, the entire education process would have been disrupted, with a fatal shortage of healthcare, and in fact, life would have been disrupted without innovative and sophisticated technological solutions, and it is now clear that most of these innovative technologies will be an essential part of our future.

Lymantria dispar dispar and Malacasoma disstria maggot infestations occur at least every 5 years in temperate forests, feeding on many leaves, so much so that researchers have found that reduced leaf loss due to feeding on them and increased larval droppings dramatically change the way the larvae feed on them. Nutrients, especially carbon and nitrogen, circulate between land and lakes.
In new research, published in the journal Nature Communications on Nov. 3, researchers found that nitrogen-rich waste, called ferase, can drift into the lake and act as a fertilizer for microbes, which then enables them to release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere as they metabolize the waste.
Changing the chemistry of water
The report, by a research team led by John Gunn, Canada ’ s research chair on stressed water systems at Laurentian University in Ontario, and published on The Conversation on November 16, states that in years of insect infestation, large amounts of waste may help grow bacteria that emit greenhouse gases in lakes, which overpower salt. The lake is responsible for removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
These insects are basically small machines that convert carbon-rich leaves into nitrogen-rich feces, and then the feces fall into the lakes instead of the leaves, which dramatically changes the chemistry of the water, and the researchers believe will increase the extent to which the lakes are a source of greenhouse gases.
With climate change in the temperate zone of the world, insect numbers are expected to increase and move north, this puts northern forests at increased risk of future outbreaks of these insects, which may cause the release of greater amounts of carbon dioxide from nearby lakes.
Where's the good news?
While the effects of insect foliar erosion appear to be increasing in frequency and severity, the lake's water across the Canadian Shield (Laurentian Plateau) is also undergoing a process called water flushing due to the buildup of dissolved organic carbon (which is similar to tea) in the lake's water.
This deterioration in lake water transparency is due to many factors — including climate change, recovery from acid rain and logging — and the 32-year observational study showed that the spread of the leaf-eating larva can effectively offset year-long carbon accumulation in nearby lakes, significantly improving water transparency.
In years when leaf-eating insects do not infect, carbon and nitrogen usually enter the lakes from the decomposing leaves, usually peaking in terms of quantity in the fall.
In the years of the outbreak, researchers found that nearby freshwater lakes, especially those surrounded by leaf-falling forests, had dissolved carbon — or “forest tea ” — one-third less in the water because hungry larvae effectively blocked the flow of carbon into the lake.
The lasting benefits of these voracious insects become apparent when invasive insects encounter already strained trees, such as the stunted birch forest surrounding the huge metal smelters in Sadbury, Ontario, Canada, where this 80,000-hectare industrial zone is experiencing a remarkable natural self-recovery, due to a 98% reduction in acid and metal particulate emissions from the source that was the world ’ s largest source of sulfur pollution in the 1970s.

That ’ s why knowledgeable farmers regularly try to stop extracting nutrients from the soil, plowing a nutrient-rich fodder crop like alfalfa, to rebuild the soil.

Enemies of vaccine and conspiracy fantasies?
Scientists Explain the Relationship (Video)
For ages, belief in conspiracy theories has been on the rise, and claims have spread and varied widely.
After chemtrails, the idea that governments release chemicals into the environment via aircraft to control populations, came the perennial conspiracy theories of adding fluoride to public water supplies to create a docile population vulnerable to communist takeover.
In the wake of the coronavirus epidemic, the idea that the world is run by devils or aliens or that the coronavirus is spread by 5G technology has become mainstream, as have attempts by some to prove that the virus does not exist at all, and that the vaccine is a way to control or monitor people.
To many people, these claims seem strange and funny, and it is very difficult to understand why anyone believes them, yet recent surveys have shown that a large percentage of people are willing to believe these and other conspiracies.
In a March research by Ipsos, supported by the British Embassy in Montenegro and UNICEF, four in 10 (43%) believed there was a global conspiracy to hide the harm caused by the vaccine so that pharmaceutical companies could continue to make profits around the world.
In this regard, Dr. Ahmed Al Awadhi, from the Royal British College of Psychiatrists and director of the Do Not Grieve Centre in London, revealed a range of factors explaining the cognitive processes of this situation.
Al-Awadi explained to the program with Al-Hakim that “conspiracy theories have always been a way of thinking that people resort to in times of crisis, when things are not clear for self-defense. ”
For example, we can all be prone to seeing imaginary patterns (like a face in the clouds), but for conspiracy theorists this probability rises dramatically, meaning they ’ re likely to see clear connections between disparate events that the rest of us don ’ t notice.
To be sure, many conspiracy theories make claims that are factually incorrect or based on fundamentally flawed logic, but unfortunately, theorists are not only more likely to see illusory connections, they are also less likely to receive the advice or critical thinking skills needed to help them see glaring gaps in their erroneous theories, creating fertile ground for unfounded beliefs.
Al-Awadhi pointed to a strong element of conspiracy theory: a person ’ s sense of being part of a community, which helps meet some people ’ s need to feel special.
The most important question is how does the scientific community deal with conspiracies?
Perhaps the best solution in such situations is to try to help people discover conspiracy theories early on, which is the on-going battle with tech companies to get them to remove conspiratorial content, which YouTube has done since 2018.
The worst strategy for dealing with conspiracy theories is to walk away from rhetoric and mock those who might believe in conspiracies.
Ultimately, the message should be that it is scientists who have the tools to find the truth.

Is it time to work less in the Gulf?
Wael Mahdi
Posted in: Last Updated:
It was a big shock to those in the UAE or abroad after the announcement that working days from Sunday to Thursday will be changed to Monday to Friday for government institutions, with working hours changed to four and a half days instead of five days, apparently taking into account the religious and social specificity of Friday.
Although this trend is not new, many countries are moving in and trying to reduce working hours or days, we mention here Scotland, which began to test this model this year, Iceland, which has already implemented it between 2015 and 2019, as well as Spain and other countries that announced their experience of this system to see the results.
Steps like this may increase the happiness of citizens, as people are happy to work fewer hours as long as their income remains constant, may increase the attractiveness of countries or cities, and in other cases may significantly help integrate cities such as Dubai and Abu Dhabi into the global system further.
The quest to make cities global – in other words, to increase their connectivity to the global system – has become a goal for many legislators around the world, and more recently in the Middle East, following Saudi Arabia ’ s push to make Riyadh a global destination.
But the universality of cities is complex and cannot be attributed to certain organizational and administrative matters, such as reducing working hours or turning working days into the universally recognized week.
The competitiveness of cities is important, but it does not come without costs, as some decisions that increase the attractiveness of cities to foreigners may not increase it for the citizens of countries or companies operating in them.
For example, reducing working hours in government agencies and keeping it the same in the private sector will reduce the attractiveness of the private sector in the eyes of job seekers, which is not in line with many of the economic plans of the majority of countries in the region that want the private sector to generate more jobs.
If operating companies are affected by such decisions, it is not unlikely that they will decide to move to other cities.
The other thing is that the speed of regulatory decisions does not make companies comfortable; the corporate system and the mechanism of work can be subject to significant changes without consulting employers.
Therefore, we note that countries and cities globally are cautious in this matter, and may require a public referendum or experiment on a small scale and examine the results and their impact on the conduct of business.
Iceland has noted that productivity has increased as working days have been shortened, and this has been an important observation, but do we expect the results to be similar in developing or Middle Eastern countries?
Personally, I don ’ t think reducing working hours and days is economically feasible for countries in the Middle East, where the government sector operates less efficiently and productively than the private sector, so cutting makes it worse for me.
The countries of the region have not reached the level of economic maturity, which is the stage that the economy enters after years of large and rapid growth rates of between 10 and 20%; the region has not reached this level of economic growth, so it is better to redouble efforts until we reach an advanced stage after which we can think of working fewer hours.
A decision such as reducing or increasing working hours should be a purely business decision borne by companies because they can determine its feasibility.
The more companies improve their work environment, the more attractive they are.

Opinion by Princess Lamia bint Majid bin Saud Al Saud: International Human Rights Day..
Equality is the foundation of the rise and progress of nations

This article is written by Princess Lamia bint Majid bin Saud Al Saud, Secretary General of Alwaleed Philanthropies. The views expressed below are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect CNN ’ s view.
Every year on 10 December, the world celebrates International Human Rights Day, a reminder to all of us of the need to provide equal opportunities for all regardless of people ’ s gender, race, religion and other different backgrounds.
The fundamental principle of International Human Rights Day is the equality of rights from fundamental human rights to equal access to cultural and social perceptions, opinions and ideas for all without exception.
Although significant progress has been made in creating a prosperous environment with equal opportunities and rights for both men and women, we still have a long way to go to achieve full gender equality.
In light of the great change taking place in the world at various levels, we now have a unique opportunity to shape the future that everyone deserves by working to activate a social and economic response that will support and empower women and youth around the world.
As such, the global community has responsibilities and duties to pave the way for solutions based on solid strategic dimensions that combat all forms of discrimination that have marginalized many of the world ’ s most vulnerable communities and individuals.
Therefore, we must commit ourselves to the need to look at the current and future needs of people from a social, cultural and economic perspective.
We must all work with international human rights actors and alert human rights specialists to the importance of their interaction with and understanding of human rights mechanisms and build the capacity to interact with them to ensure the development of a general framework that meets such needs and rights.
Women ’ s rights and their importance in the development of nations
Many institutions at the local and global level have adopted an agenda and plans that recognize the need for equal rights and empowerment of women because of its importance in the development of nations.
If we want to talk about the status of women ’ s rights in the Arab world, we are witnessing an increasing and noticeable trend in changing society ’ s perception of women ’ s rights at all levels.
Here, I would like to offer a vivid example of this trend, which is reflected in the Kingdom ’ s Vision 2030, which includes the need for Saudi women to participate fully at all levels, invest their energies, provide a suitable environment, provide services that facilitate them to carry out their national duties, increase women ’ s participation in the labor market, and reduce the gender gap in order to achieve economic balance.
The observer of the reality of Arab and Saudi women in particular during the past period, notes that there are participatory efforts at the local and international levels to change the perception that prevailed in the past for women, where many roles and professions were limited to men.
We at Alwaleed Philanthropies, through our cooperation with various government institutions within the Kingdom and international institutions, have sought from the beginning to change the societal perception of women ’ s work based on our firm belief in the importance of empowering and supporting women in all sectors.
In order to achieve this, we have initiated fruitful cooperation and partnerships with various parties, including the Human Rights Commission, with which we have launched a series of training programs to raise the level of legal awareness and enhance the protection of the rights of women and youth in Saudi Arabia.
Various human rights bodies and institutions should promote women ’ s economic independence inside and outside the Kingdom.
As part of our contribution to the economic independence and social and cultural empowerment of women, and through our partnership with the National Crafts and Handicrafts Program of the Saudi Commission for Tourism and National Heritage and the Turquoise Mountain Foundation, we have successfully supported women and youth artisans by providing a variety of business opportunities to sell their products to 5-star hotels.
I would also like to point out here that legal work in Saudi Arabia was previously limited to men and not women, and as part of our role in promoting women ’ s empowerment, we launched in 2014 a legal initiative “Waya ’ ea ” which aims to educate women about their legal rights.
In 2020, Alwaleed Philanthropies signed a memorandum of cooperation with the Human Rights Commission for the empowerment of women and youth, building indicators to support the rights of persons with disabilities, women and children in accordance with international conventions, in addition to supporting and empowering the abused women in the Kingdom psychologically, socially and economically.
Access to equal opportunities
The COVID-19 pandemic has created extraordinary challenges across all sectors of life, and has had a greater impact on women by reducing direct education opportunities, economic impact, limited employment opportunities, access to resources, health and well-being in general.
During the next recovery period, women may be at risk of being forced to agree to precarious working conditions that do not provide them with adequate social protection.
Women from disadvantaged and low-income communities will be the most vulnerable group to these risks.
In order to avoid further challenges of economic crises in the future, we must work together to provide equitable opportunities for the most vulnerable and work to change gender-discriminatory environments to reach their economic potential.
When speaking of Saudi Arabia, which had a large gap in the number of female workers versus male workers in some sectors, it has already made great strides in this area.
In 2021, the Saudi General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT) reported that the overall unemployment rate for Saudis (males and females aged 15 and over) decreased to 11.7% in the first quarter of 2021 compared to 12.6% in the fourth quarter of 2020.
This comes in line with the Kingdom ’ s efforts to develop the skills of citizens by providing learning opportunities by supporting innovation, entrepreneurship culture and the Saudi workforce as part of Vision 2030.
Thus, the female participation rate of the total labor force increased to 33.8%.
Support for the most disadvantaged
Violence against women is a problem that exists in different societies around the world.
According to studies, 35% of women worldwide experience some form of violence.
Unfortunately, this percentage worsened during the pandemic.
First, we need to ensure that women have access to the resources available to enhance their access to help and seek legal advice.
Second, we must work with relevant bodies to combat the misconceptions and unrealistic causes associated with violence against women.
By doing so, this trend will encourage more women to seek help and create a catalyst for real change among society.
In conclusion, I would like to refer to the problem of refugees and people displaced by conflicts, wars and natural disasters around the world, especially women and children, where we must provide them with educational and economic opportunities in order to live a better future.
Together, we can build bridges to a more tolerant and welcoming world.

7 Types of Fish to Eat and 7 to Avoid
Fish has a high nutritional value; it contains many important elements such as omega-3 acids and unsaturated fats, which help in the prevention of many diseases.
Despite these benefits, experts recommend avoiding some fish species because of their potential harm to human health or because their catch is inconsistent with environmental fishing standards.
In a report published in Health Digest, author Allie Arcuri lists the best nutritionally available fish and other species to avoid.
First, fish that you are advised to avoid
Farmed salmon (farmed salmon)
Experts often recommend avoiding farmed salmon, as it feeds very differently from sea salmon.
Farmed salmon contain 3 times more fat per 4 grams than sea salmon, because the farmed feeds on high-fat diets in order to double its size.
Worse still, most of those fats come from omega-6 fatty acids, the type recommended for moderation.
Farmed salmon also have higher levels of contaminants, as they live in enclosed spaces.
2. Tilapia
Tilapia live in fresh water, and although it is a favorite meal for many, it carries some health risks depending on the country in which it originates.
Compared to other fish, tilapia does not provide a high nutritional value, due to its high content of omega-6 and very low percentage of omega-3 fatty acids, which help control cholesterol and heart disease.
Atlantic flatfish (Atlantic flatfish)
Much of the flounder caught today has been proven to contain contaminants.
In the 1980s, research showed that about 75 percent of fish caught in Boston had signs of liver disease and cancerous tissue.
The larger the fish, the more heavy metals they contain, taking years to fully mature and absorbing more mercury than other fish.
Caviar (caviar)
Caviar are eggs extracted from the butterflies of some types of fish, such as sturgeon, but did you know that fishermen extract these fish to cut their butterflies, and then throw them to die in the sea?
Such fishing contravenes established environmental standards.
The Shark (Shark)
Because sharks are predators at the top of the food chain, they eat whatever harmful fish and plastics they encounter, so sharks are usually full of toxins, including mercury, arsenic and lead.
Shark fishing is also devastating to the environment, killing 100 million sharks each year, according to National Geographic.
6. Orange roughy
Orange ruby fish contains a high amount of mercury, its constant intake can lead to dysfunction of the nervous system, and its consumption can harm the pregnant woman.
Regardless of the health risk posed by eating these fish, overfishing can harm the food chain.
The Eel (Eel)
The Monterey Bay Seafood Control Center explains that eels (known as eels) are on the seafood list to avoid due to sustainability issues related to their catch.
Several environmental organizations are working to find sustainable ways to raise these fish, under the threat of extinction of species of eel.
Most eels are classified as high mercury fish, according to the Environmental Defense Fund.
Second: The fish that you are advised to eat
Wild Caught Alaskan Salmon (Wild Caught Alaskan Salmon)
This type of salmon is the best choice, as it contains less fat than farmed salmon, and provides plenty of minerals and other essential nutrients, including iron and calcium.
Some studies have shown that wild salmon has a healthy omega-3 and omega-6 content, partly due to the lower amount of fat in this fish overall.
2) Rainbow trout
Rainbow trout is a healthy and sustainable marine food; from a nutritional point of view, this type of fish is rich in omega-3 acids, as well as containing selenium, potassium, vitamin B12 and vitamin B6, in addition to containing a high percentage of proteins.
Atlantic mackerel (Atlantic mackerel)
Atlantic mackerel is a healthy and environmentally friendly choice; it contains very little mercury.
The equipment used to catch mackerel is less harmful to the environment, helping to maintain the reproduction and sustainable consumption of these fish.
According to Eating Well, every 3 ounces of Atlantic mackerel contains about 20 grams of lean protein, with a high content of omega-3 fatty acids.
The same serving provides nearly three times the recommended daily intake of vitamin B12.
The herring (herring)
Herring contains vitamin D and selenium (a rare mineral that promotes fertility and cognitive function), as well as lean proteins, and low amounts of mercury.
Pregnant women are recommended to eat these fish, as research has revealed that omega-3 acids help in the development of the brain of the fetus.
Sable fish (sablefish)
Sable is a nutritious and delicious oily fish that has many health benefits.
According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, American sable fish is a good choice in the seafood world because its catch is regulated.
Sable fish contains more omega-3 than other low-fat fish.
Catfish (Catfish)
In addition to the nutritional benefits, these fish absorb less pollutants and heavy metals than other large, long-lived fish.
According to the Food and Drug Administration, swordfish, for example, contain 40 times as much mercury as catfish.
About 3.5 ounces of catfish contain about 3 grams of fat and 18 grams of protein.
The catfish also contains selenium, phosphorus, potassium, thiamine and vitamin B12.
Pacific wild-caught sardines
Pacific sardines are one of the best fish to eat, as they are small fish that reproduce quickly.
Because their life cycle is relatively short, they do not contain a high content of heavy metals compared to other fish.
In terms of its nutritional value, Pacific sardines contain an abundant amount of vitamin D, as well as omega-3, and a high percentage of calcium.

Is it safe to follow a keto diet with intermittent fasting?
I know the answer.
Thursday ، 23 December 2021 02: 18 PM
Is it okay to combine intermittent fasting with keto diet
I wrote Marwa Haridi.
Leave a comment and read the comments of the readers.
Ketogenic diet and intermittent fasting are two popular dietary methods for losing kilograms at the moment, the first is about adding more fat to the diet and reducing carbohydrates, while the latter stresses the need to manage the eating pattern without restricting any food group, both are proven methods of weight loss, but both rely on different methods, but is it acceptable to combine both systems for rapid weight loss?
This is illustrated by the Times of India report.
What is the ketogenic diet?
The keto system focuses on consuming fewer calories and increasing fat consumption, as it forces the body to enter the ketosis phase, where it begins to produce ketones from fat deposited in the liver, to be used by the body as the main source of energy in the absence of carbohydrates, and over time, the body begins to burn stored fat for energy, which ultimately leads to weight loss.
The only thing to consider is the quality of fat you eat when following this diet, as there are two basic types of fat, healthy and unhealthy, and in this diet you need to include more good fats and exclude bad fats.
What is Intermittent Fasting?
Intermittent fasting is not a diet, it is an eating pattern in which fasting alternates with eating, and in which no food group has to be restricted, it is only about eating clean and consuming all the calories during a specific period of the day.
Staying in a state of fasting gives your body a chance to focus on tasks other than digesting food, and this helps increase metabolism, reduce the risk of chronic diseases and eventually get rid of excess kilograms.
There are different methods of intermittent fasting such as the 5: 2 method, the 16: 8 method, the alternate day fasting method and others, and the method to be followed depends on your fitness goal, stamina and health status.
Is it safe to follow both at the same time?
Because keto is about restricting food intake while intermittent fasting is not about restricting time periods, it may not seem harmful to combine them, but in scientific terms, combining the two can do more harm than good, both systems have advantages and disadvantages, and combining them may double their risk especially for novice people and those with certain health conditions.
Beside that, keto is a restricted diet and following it for a long time may lead to nutrient deficiencies and kidney problems unlike intermittent fasting, and when you combine the two, you may put excessive stress on your body, causing health conditions such as mood swings, constipation, irritability and fatigue.
As the combination of the two systems may not be effective with everyone, each of us has a different body nature from the other, so of course, our journey to lose weight will be unique and different from the others, no two people are the same, so it is not necessary that the combination of intermittent fasting and keto diet will help you lose weight effectively.

“Studies in Scientific Literature. ”
A book that explores the features of science fiction in Arabic works
Science fiction literature has witnessed a wide presence in Arab creative writings despite its emergence and prosperity in the Western world, and despite its creative popularity, it has not received sufficient critical attention. Based on this idea, the Syrian writer and critic Ahmed Ali Mohammed observes the features and features of science fiction in Arabic literature, both ancient and modern, in his book "Studies in Science Literature", recently published in the series of studies by the Arab Writers Union.
The Syrian researcher believes that the Arab criticism has overlooked the literature of science fiction, citing a number of arguments such as the immaturity of this type of writing in the Arab world, and the disregard of his writers for the features of literary writing, as well as the lack of scientific knowledge, which the writer considers weak, especially with the presence of remarkable writings in this field succeeded in setting a firm foot and overcome many shortcomings.
Leadership in scientific literature
Ali points out that the philosophical messages of Avicenna and Ibn Tufayl can be considered as the beginning of the link in ancient Arabic literature between literature and science, as the Arab heritage includes philosophical messages written in successive times that represented the basis of literary thinking based on science fiction, the most prominent of these messages: "The message of Hayy bin Yaqzan" by Avicenna.
Shahabuddeen al-Sahrawardi ’ s “Strange Alienation ” message is inspired by the story of the neighborhood of Ben Yaqzan, and Ibn al-Nafees ’ s“ Perfect Letter ” in which he followed the example of his predecessors.
The author says of the relevance of these letters to science fiction: "These letters draw a narrative basis based on the facts of science, elaborate on the imagination based on thought and knowledge, and depict part of the knowledge of their owners.
The most prominent aspect of these letters is the narrative imager related to the facts of science and the perceptions of philosophy, which confirms the existence of seeds of scientific literature in the Arabs. ”
Science Fiction Poetry
The writer points out that science fiction literature has been associated with narrative forms, was raised with the French writer Jules Verne, who published the first story in science fiction literature in 1863 entitled "Five Weeks in a Balloon" and then wrote another story entitled "Journey to the Hollow of the Earth" and then continued productions, including the novel "Time Machine" by George Wells and others.
Science fiction poetry is rare, including the poem "The Asteroid" by Russian poet Nikolai Glazkov, translated by Al-Azhar University professor Ahmed Shafiq al-Khatib, a poem based on the achievements of science fiction literature in terms of prediction, foresight and time travel.
Criticism of scientific literature
Some of the works of Tawfiq al-Hakim include The Year of One Million (1953), which is dominated by philosophical consideration of life, nature and the universe, and his play Journey to Tomorrow (1958), which involves a forward-looking view of the future related to man ’ s struggle with time, as well as his play “Food for Every Mouth ”." In which he talks about the problem of food that people will suffer from in the future, and his play "The Prayer of Angels", which deals with the impact of science on the happiness of humanity and the provision of its needs.
Political fiction literature
The writer monitors the branches of science fiction literature that not only addressed the problems of the environment, pollution, space and planets, but touched the problems of politics, society and economy through the literature of political fiction, which includes under its banner the literature of utopia and dystopia.
There are a number of writings concerned with depicting Utopia, which means a utopia without trace of corruption, evil or injustice, the most prominent of these writings is Thomas Moore ’ s “Utopia ”, which depicts an ideal world critical of the political, religious and social conditions of his time.
The literature of dystopia comes in contrast to utopia, but they belong under the name of political fiction, which is a branch of science fiction literature, as each deals with political life by storytelling accompanied by fiction, and dystopia means the literature of the corrupt city or the world of bitter reality that depicts a society full of corruption and highlights the phenomena of destruction, murder and destruction and transformation of human beings. A feuding.
The author mentions a number of Western and Arabic writings that have emerged in the field of dystopia, including George Orwell ’ s 1984, Aldous Huxley ’ s Brave New World, and Ray Bradbury ’ s Fahrenheit 451.
At the level of Arabic writings, a number of works can be observed such as the novel "The Front" by Izz al-Din Issa, the novel "The Tale of the Last Arab" by Wassini al-Araj, "Frankenstein in Baghdad" by Ahmed Saadawi, "The Second War of the Dog" by Ibrahim Nasrallah, "Mercury" by Mohammed Rabie, "The Line" by Basma Abdul Aziz, and "Novelist of the First City" by Omar Hazek. And "Orwell in the Southern Suburbs" by Fawzi Thebian.
Literary Studies
In his book, the Syrian critic offers critical readings in a number of works under the banner of science fiction literature, including the novel "Hala al-Nour" by Mohammed al-Ashri, seeking to stand on the aesthetic trend, especially with the departure of literary criticism from the study of the aesthetic aspects of science fiction literature, observing the methods of the novelist mixing the facts of science with the world mythical heritage.
The book provides another analysis of the collection “Behind the Dark Walls ” by the Syrian writer Taleb Omran, which falls within the literature of dystopia, because the stories depict worlds in which savagery, destruction, murder and destruction prevail, and on the other hand it monitors the Syrian storyteller ’ s interest in the method of scientific storytelling and its reliance on astronomical knowledge and geographical information.
The writer also analyzes the elements and features of fantasy in some of the works of Ahmed Khaled Tawfik as one of the most prominent writers in this field, explaining that science fiction is different from fantasy or wonder in the contemporary novel in that it starts from the modern scientific output, and depends on scientific knowledge specialized, while fantasy completely degenerates from logic and depends on the imagination and does not find a trace of laws we know in reality and depends on mythological and form It is in harmony not with the outside world but with its own world according to which it takes place.
