Egyptian startups reap the largest number of investment deals in Africa
Egypt ranked first on the African continent in terms of the number of investment and financing deals in Egyptian startups during 2021, according to the report "Venture Investment in Egypt" issued recently by the platform "Magnit" specialized in data financing startups, in cooperation with the Information Technology Industry Development Authority.
The report pointed out that the Egyptian companies succeeded in raising financing deals worth $491 million through 147 deals concluded during 2021, representing a new record for the volume of investment capital in the startup sector in Egypt, with an annual growth rate of 168% compared to last year.
The report also stated that Egypt ranked third in terms of the total value of investments in startups in the African continent, with its startups accounting for 18% of the total capital invested in the continent during 2021.
The report also compared the performance of startups in the Middle East and North Africa in the same year, with Egypt ranked second in terms of the number of investment deals directed to startups in the region, accounting for 24% of the total number of deals in the region, while Egypt ranked third in terms of the total value of investments in startups in the Middle East and North Africa.
The report highlighted the indicators of the recovery of the startup sector in Egypt from the repercussions of the pandemic, which contributed to the decline in the number of deals in 2020, and then Egypt to witness a growth during 2021 in the number of deals, which reached 26%, as well as an increase in the number of investors to reach 124 investors, which is also unprecedented.
The Egyptian state pays attention to the innovation-based entrepreneurship sector, and the boom witnessed by the technology startups sector in Egypt is a result of the spread of entrepreneurial and innovative thinking among young people in the Egyptian society, in light of the growth of the number and quality of investors, and the expansion of the network of co-working spaces, creative communities, technology incubators and innovation centers in Egypt throughout the country.
The strategy is based on four main pillars: enhancing the business environment of startups and developing their growth factors, facilitating access to finance and investments, developing technical skills and increasing the number of professionals to facilitate access to them, creating a climate conducive to the growth of innovation and entrepreneurship, and facilitating the penetration of global markets through an international promotion and marketing plan.
The report highlights Egypt ’ s position as a leading ecosystem for startups in the Middle East and Africa, and its record rise in the volume of investments, which confirms the market maturity witnessed by the country.
Egypt achieved a record number of investors, growing by 68% year-on-year, reflecting the growing interest and attraction of foreign investors from across the region and international markets.
The report identified the proportion of foreign investors (investors from outside the MENA region) in Egyptian startups at 51% and 63 investors, while the proportion of foreign investors (non-Egyptian investors from within and outside the region) in Egyptian startups at 77%, which is the highest in the region, reflecting the confidence of foreign investors and global venture capital funds in the Egyptian entrepreneurship and technology startups climate.
Fintech led the deal activity, accounting for 17% of the total number of deals in Egypt in 2021, in line with the general approach in the Middle East and North Africa.
The fintech sector accounted for the largest share of 18% of the total number of VC investment deals in the past year.
The transportation and logistics sector accounted for more than a third, about 36% of the total capital invested in Egypt ’ s start-ups in 2021.
The financial technology sector recorded 25 deals, e-commerce 23 deals, transport and logistics 15 deals, healthcare 12 deals and food and beverage 11 deals, the highest sectors for the number of deals concluded in 2021 respectively.
Sectors ranked in terms of investment value as follows: transportation and logistics $177 million, e-commerce $96 million, fintech $60 million, retail $42 million, and food and beverage $38 million.

Which European countries have implemented a system of four days a week with employees keeping their salaries?
Conversation
By: Euronews
Which European countries have implemented a four-day working week with employees retaining their salaries - Copyright Frank Cilius / AP
When the Coronavirus epidemic spread across Europe, many organizations adopted more flexible work plans through telecommuting, and other countries were quick to consider reducing working days, in order to give employees the flexibility to combine work and family life, by conducting experiments and studies that go hand in hand with the demands of the labor market and to motivate employees to be more productive in their workplace.
What do advocates say about working four days a week?
Advocates of the idea of working four days a week, an important way to enable employees to focus on their family and private lives, considering that employee comfort contributes to improving the quality of work and achieving satisfaction.
Trade unions across Europe have called on governments to work four days a week.
Which European countries have adopted a four-day working week or are planning to adopt it?
Belgium
In Belgium, workers will soon be able to work four days a week instead of the current five, provided the 38-hour working week does not change.
Last month, the country ’ s coalition government agreed that the new “labor market ” deal would include a series of measures that would provide more flexibility for employees to do their jobs.
Employees who want to work four days will be given the possibility to work more hours a day in exchange for an extra day off during the week.
In this case, the weekly rest days are limited to three days.
Belgian Prime Minister Alexandre De Croo hopes the measure will help “make the Belgian labor market more flexible, where employees will be able to reconcile their family and professional lives ” and explained that the new model should create a more dynamic economy.
"The goal is to give individuals and companies more freedom to arrange their work times," he said, adding that "if we compare our country to other countries, we will see that we are often less dynamic."
Sweden
In Sweden, a four-day work week with full pay was tested in 2015.
The proposal was to try out six-hour workdays instead of eight hours while keeping the salary the same, but not everyone was thrilled with the idea of spending money on the aforementioned experiment.
Even left-wing parties believe that implementing this plan on a large scale would be too costly for the state treasury.
But positive results were observed within the orthopaedic unit of a university hospital, which turned 80 nurses and doctors to work six hours a day and hired new staff to make up for the remaining time.
The response of the medical staff was positive, but the experiment also faced much criticism, however, some companies, such as automaker Toyota, chose to keep reduced working hours for workers.
Germany
The average working week in Germany is 34.2 hours.
Most jobs in Germany require working seven or eight hours a day, five days a week.
Last year, IG Metall, the country ’ s largest trade union, called for fewer work weeks, arguing that it would help keep jobs and avoid layoffs.
According to a survey by the Forsa survey institute, 71% of workers in Germany would like to apply the option of working four days a week.
SPAIN
In March 2021, the Spanish government approved the launch of a pilot project for companies interested in implementing the four-day (32-hour) week.
Earlier last year, Spain ’ s left-wing Mas Pais party announced that the government had accepted its proposal to test the idea, and has held talks since then.
Party leader Enigo Erijón said the debate on the four-day week had begun, adding: “It ’ s an idea whose time has come. ”
“Spain is one of the countries where workers work more hours than the average in Europe. ”
The pilot phase is set to last at least one year, but it is not yet clear when it will begin.
United Kingdom
In the UK, a six-month pilot programme was launched in January, where companies are looking at the impact of shorter working hours on the productivity of companies and the well-being of their workers, as well as the impact on the environment and gender equality.
So far, about 30 companies have signed up for the program, which starts in June this year and is overseen by researchers at the universities of Cambridge and Oxford.
Under the reform, employees will be allowed to work up to 9.5 hours a day, that is, from 9 a.m. to 6: 30 p.m., meaning the employees involved will be able to work four days a week and keep the salary the same without the slightest change.
Scotland
In Scotland, the experience associated with working four days a week is set to begin in 2023.
The government cited a recent survey conducted by the Public Policy Research Institute (IPPR) in Scotland, which showed that 80 per cent of people who responded to and participated in the survey gave very positive impressions of the initiative.
Respondents said the program would significantly boost their health and happiness.
Some Scottish companies have already started working four days a week, with Glasgow ’ s UPAC Group recently saying its employees will soon start working four days a week with the same salary and benefits after running a “successful pilot program, ” company officials said.
Iceland
Icelandic and British think tanks say the world ’ s biggest weekly workday reduction experiment has been a huge success.
More than 2,500 Icelanders participated in the experiment, which reduced their weekly working hours to between 35 and 36 hours (four days of weekly work) between 2015 and 2019 without reducing their salaries.
The researchers said the experiment improved workers' productivity and well-being, or at least kept it at normal levels at work five days a week.
According to the results of the study, approximately 90 per cent of the working population now perform their jobs on reduced hours.
The researchers found decreased levels of worker stress and burnout, and reported improvements in work-life balance conditions.

Avocado reduces the risk of heart disease
New research has found that eating two or more servings of avocados a week can reduce the risk of heart disease by a fifth.
The research, published in the Journal of the American Heart Association, followed the diets of 68,000 women and 41,000 men every four years for 30 years.
During the study, 9,185 heart attacks and 5,290 strokes were recorded.
Researchers identified a link between people ’ s intake of healthy fats and heart health, and found that those who ate avocado more frequently reduced their risk of coronary heart disease by 21 percent, compared to those who didn ’ t.
In addition, the research showed that replacing half a daily serving of margarine, butter, eggs, yogurt, cheese, or processed meat with a similar amount of avocado reduced the risk of heart disease by 16 – 22%.
Avocado contains dietary fiber, minerals and vitamins, such as vitamin C, E and K.
Dr Lorena Pacheco, who led the research, said: “Our research provides additional evidence that eating a quantity of trans fats from natural sources can improve diet quality, an important component in preventing cardiovascular disease.

127 new defendants arrested in corruption cases in ministries
The Saudi Anti-Corruption and Control Authority (Nazaha) has arrested 127 people accused of financial and administrative corruption in a number of government ministries, as part of an ongoing anti-corruption campaign.
+ A -A
Source: Erm News
The Saudi Anti-Corruption and Control Authority (Nazaha) has arrested 127 people accused of financial and administrative corruption in a number of government ministries, as part of an ongoing anti-corruption campaign in conjunction with the implementation of a comprehensive development plan that requires spending and investing billions of dollars.
The government authority said in a statement on Thursday that "the detainees belong to the Ministries of Defense, Justice, Interior, National Guard, Health, Education, Housing, Municipal and Rural Affairs, in addition to the General Authority of Civil Aviation."
Nazaha pointed out that the detainees, a number of whom were released on bail, are accused of crimes of financial and administrative corruption, most notably bribery and the exploitation of functional influence, fraud and money laundering.
She pointed out that she investigated 258 people during more than 5 thousand rounds of surveillance, during the month of March, before stopping 127 people.
This is the second statement of the Anti-Corruption Commission in two weeks, as “Nazaha ” has been publishing monthly or less than monthly data, the results of its investigations and prosecution of corruption cases and those involved in it, amid the support of senior leaders of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for the Commission, which has not worked with the same momentum since its establishment in 2011.
The commission ’ s statements detail corruption cases involving judges, officers, businessmen and senior government officials, including employees of the same “integrity ” in some cases.
Riyadh has tightened its anti-corruption measures since the launch of Vision 2030 in 2016, a giant development plan aimed at diversifying the economy, providing jobs and housing for Saudis, improving the quality of life and attracting foreign investment to implement large industrial, tourism and entertainment projects.
The head of the anti-corruption body, Mazen al-Kahmos, meets every month with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who oversees the implementation of Vision 2030.
Since then, Nazaha ’ s investigations have revealed the involvement of many convicts in million-dollar corruption cases, many of which involve awarding large government projects to private companies in exchange for million-dollar bribes.
In 2017, Prince Mohammed bin Salman headed a special anti-corruption committee and arrested a number of ministers, princes and businessmen on billion-dollar corruption charges, before the unprecedented campaign ended with settlements in which Riyadh received large sums of money from the detainees.

Thank you for reading about the 5 best exercises for seniors.

Exercise is essential for people of all age groups, and exercising regularly even for 15 minutes a day improves mood, strengthens bones and reduces the risk of chronic diseases, and even for the elderly, exercise can help reduce the risk of osteoporosis, manage the level of blood pressure, maintain balance and improve mood.
5 Best Exercises for Seniors
Walking..
Walking is a low-impact exercise that helps you burn a good amount of calories It ’ s an easy way to control weight and improve your mood.
The best is that a person can perform this activity at any time of the day, a moderate walking session for 30 minutes a day can keep you healthy and fit.
Yoga...
Yoga increases flexibility and range of motion and improves mood It is an excellent activity for older people with joint pain and balance problems.
Even chair yoga is an excellent alternative for older people.
Along with yoga, meditation can help keep the mind calm, increase concentration levels, and reduce stress levels.
Swimming...
Swimming is an excellent exercise if done regularly and for a long period of time, as swimming helps to build endurance, muscle strength and cardiovascular fitness.
It is a low-impact activity that targets your entire body muscles.
Swimming in the summer is the best activity as it helps to relax and overcome the heat.
Aerobic exercises.
One of the most common health problems for older adults is joint pain and weak knees that make it difficult for them to perform most of the exercises or activities.
Aerobic exercises put less pressure on the joints and are an excellent choice for older people Some aerobic exercises that older people may try include water jogging, leg lifting, pressure exercises in stagnant water, arm rolls, and flutter kicks.
Body weight exercises.
Simple body weight exercises such as squatting, lengthening the leg while sitting and lifting the toes are easy body weight exercises that older people can do.
These exercises do not put too much pressure on the joints, but they help burn a lot of calories, and bodyweight exercises can help strengthen muscles, strengthen the body and build muscle mass.

US-Saudi relations are no longer the same as they were during the last millennium, as the decline of the United States ’ need for Saudi oil has led to a new political reality, on the basis of which Washington has engineered its relations with the countries of the region in general and Saudi Arabia in particular.
The Saudi sphinx turned its head from here, and Riyadh was fighting fiercely to regain its place in America.
Later, Saudi oil became an Asian need, and Riyadh worked to bridge relations with Moscow and Beijing.

Speaking about Saudi-American and Saudi-Asian relations, Al-Ittihad Center for Research and Development interviewed Dr. Fuad Ibrahim, a member of the leading committee of the opposition in the Arabian Peninsula.
The first axis: Saudi-American relations
The author and political researcher dr.
Ibrahim spoke about the decline in the volume of US imports of Saudi oil due to the high volume of US production, especially shale oil, which the United States accelerated the pace of production, becoming today the largest oil producer in the world, followed by Russia and Saudi Arabia.
Ibrahim then went on to say that this is not enough for the United States, which produces about 12.5 million barrels a day, because its daily consumption is about 20 million barrels, and therefore it needs to import.
Here, Washington compensated for this shortage from countries other than Saudi Arabia, such as Canada, Mexico and others, so the volume of US imports from Saudi Arabia decreased.
But despite this, Saudi Arabia is still an active player in the oil market, and is required to cover the shortage, as well as Riyadh has always played this role, especially during the Cold War, when Saudi Arabia declared that it was ready to compensate for any shortage in the oil market, as well as it represents the main player in the Organization "OPEC" because it produces a third of the production of "OPEC", 10 million to 30 million. At a stable level of production, according to the equation of supply and demand in order to pressure prices, Riyadh here is like the regulator of the global oil market.

Then these funds entered the daily American capitalist cycle, because Saudi money is mainly located inside American banks, and so we note in 2008 when the real estate credit crisis in the United States, the funds of the Gulf countries deposited, which amounted to almost 6 trillion dollars, of which 3 trillion Saudi Arabia in addressing the crisis, Saudi Arabia has huge funds in American banks, as well as buying treasury bonds, Saudi Arabia comes second country after China directly in this purchase Bonds.

Also on the issue of the relationship with Iran, Obama advised them to partner, and warned them that Washington cannot fight proxy wars, which are costly in vain.

Its purpose is to keep Washington as the patron of the Saudi regime in the region.
The New Economic Inheritance of American Companies

In other words, bin Salman wanted to enter the United States with all its weight to protect him and to be a lever for his safe arrival to the Saudi throne, but what happened was that after the failure of Trump and the arrival of Biden, the crown prince felt dangerous, especially after the systematic destruction of the interior and the family.
It is clear that Biden is hesitant in this matter, not morally, but because he committed himself before the public to hold accountable those who committed the crime of Saudi journalist Jamal Khashafji.
Despite all this, Mohammed bin Salman is still betting on the American, according to Ibrahim.
The "oil for protection" equation no longer exists
Over time, however, Saudi-American relations have changed because the components of the “oil for protection ” equation no longer exist today.
The main reason, according to Ibrahim, is that the United States no longer desperately needs Saudi oil; on the contrary, this oil is needed by China, Japan and other countries.
But for Washington, it is different because it can get oil from other countries such as Venezuela, Iran and others.
Also, oil today is no longer the monopoly of a country or region, as well as Washington is accelerating the pace of shale oil production, and will at some point reach self-sufficiency, and therefore the main element in this equation is missing, and other elements must be available in order to maintain Saudi-American relations.
For the United States, Saudi Arabia is still a sought-after market, a consumer country, and as one American ambassador put it, the United States covers Saudi Arabia ’ s needle-to-tank needs.
As long as there is high purchasing power, Saudi Arabia will remain a permanent customer of Washington.
Asked whether the United States would continue to protect Saudi Arabia if it achieved self-sufficiency in oil, Ibrahim said it would protect Saudi Arabia as a market and customer, not as a strategic ally.
Ibrahim explains that there is a strategic factor that brings the two parties together, as Saudi Arabia is located on three strategic straits, namely Bab al-Mandab, Hormuz and the Red Sea, which are strategic waterways for Washington, but if the geopolitical situation of the region changes, for example, if Yemen achieves its new status by being completely independent of Saudi, Emirati and foreign influence, Sanaa will play an important role in the next phase. As a result, even if there is a tension between Saudi Arabia and the United States or between Saudi Arabia and China, this region will remain economically viable.
But it will not be at the same level as it was in the previous US strategic plan, especially since the US administration has other challenges that Americans always talk about in their reports, namely the fear of the rise of China, which is now the second economic power after the United States.
Thus, the American fear is that China will reach a stage where it will be the master of the world economy.
The second axis: Saudi-Asian relations
Relationship with Russia
The political researcher described Saudi-Russian relations as highly ambiguous, and the main factor that keeps them going so far is oil.
In his opinion, there are differences between Riyadh and Moscow on many issues, but on the oil issue, it is different because there is a common interest.
Although at an earlier stage, relations between the two sides were tense but continued thanks to the oil file.
Since 2003, the oil countries have sought to maintain a certain level of production, knowing that Moscow is not a member of OPEC, but shares with Riyadh this goal, since the two countries depend mainly on oil and its derivatives, so there is a common need, knowing that there is a clash between the two countries in other files.
The political researcher explains that the American understands that Riyadh and Moscow are close in the oil file, but with limits, the two sides have previously sought to form a kind of lobby, and the understanding should have happened in Qatar, and then ended up with a decision by the United States.
But the two sides always try to maintain this relationship because it provides them with stable incomes and also saves them from unforeseen risks.
The political researcher here does not miss to mention that the Iranian knot was at one time a contributing factor to the Saudi-Russian rapprochement, but Saudi Arabia reached the conviction after years of attempts to convince the Russians to abandon the alliance with Iran, that the Russian is not interested in reducing the level of this relationship, so in the visit of Saudi King Salman bin Abdul Aziz to Russia in 2019, the Russian was clear that the issue of the relationship with Iran is out of discussion.
Bandar bin Sultan, the former secretary of the Saudi National Security Council, and Mohammed bin Salman have tried to compensate the Russians for any potential interests with Iran, but the Iranians ’ position has been to stick to this relationship as it is beyond direct interests, because there are strategic dimensions to the two countries.
It is not in the interest of the Russian to lose its relationship with Iran, especially after he tried this partner in a citizen that could have been abandoned by the Iranian, but the latter did not do so.
The Russians discovered this in Syria, and in the oil file, as Iran could have exploited the vacuum created in light of the Russian-Ukrainian war, because it needs additional revenues now, in addition to the issue of the war on terrorism, Tehran provided a lot of assistance to Moscow affected by terrorists, especially in Syria or in Chechnya and the former Soviet republics, according to the researcher.
Relationship with China
As for Saudi relations with China, Ibrahim believes that there is currently no infrastructure for a deep relationship between Saudi Arabia and China, for this relationship to rise to the level of strategic partnership needs an infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, and the latter is an American institution that does not have elements that serve a strategic partnership with China.
Infrastructure, according to the researcher, means companies and institutions in Saudi Arabia, which were built according to American specifications and standards, such as military cities designed according to American directives, as well as oil and commercial companies.
Also vital sectors that serve as a source of presence for Saudi Arabia, and the intention is not to talk about clothes and electricity imported by Saudi Arabia from China, which does not make Beijing a strategic partner for Riyadh.
The political opponent dates back to the days of the former King Abdullah bin Abdul Aziz, and he mentions that Salman bin Abdul Aziz went to visit Moscow and Beijing, then the comment of the Americans in the sense that whatever the Saudis go they will return to the United States, because they know that Saudi Arabia is an American founding country.
Therefore, even the military deals that Riyadh had with Moscow were canceled by an American decision, so that the United States would remain in control of the Saudi market, while Riyadh would not dare to take any action that could threaten American interests.
According to the researcher, if Washington imposed on Saudi Arabia the same economic sanctions it imposes on Iran and Russia, for a period of only two weeks, and seized the Saudi money as it did with the Russian money, we will all see to what level the Saudi riyal will collapse, because its presence is linked to the dollar.
To sum up, for the United States, this region is national security, and China knows its borders well, as it withdraws directly at a time when the interests of Washington or Europe could be harmed.
In Lebanon, for example, China told a delegation of presidential representatives that it was willing to invest approximately $12 billion to $13 billion, subject to U.S. approval.
In Syria, the United States is still blocking reconstruction, while China, Russia and Iran are ready.
The Third Theme: The Saudi Economy
The researcher who specializes in Saudi affairs confirms that Saudi Arabia is still mainly dependent on oil as a source of income, still accounting for about 80 percent.
It is true that it has declined as a result of the creation of a new source of income, the taxes imposed on the people, bringing the state ’ s income to more than 200 Saudi riyals annually.
The researcher points out that there are other but few sources of income, such as the revenues of Hajj and Umrah, which amount to about 30 billion riyals annually, but the main source of income is oil.
Decline in services and higher taxes
In contrast, taxes on the people have risen, as the gap between the poor and the rich has widened dramatically, today the middle class has been greatly eroded in Saudi Arabia, and people are struggling to secure the minimum of basic needs, especially as we note the complaints of the people about the high prices of goods and services.
So, according to Ibrahim, we have not seen any significant progress on the living situation of the people that has changed since April 2016 when Vision 2030 was announced until today.
He pointed out that we hear about festivals, celebrations and productive projects that do not exist, especially those related to addressing poverty, unemployment, services and much of what concerns people ’ s daily lives, and this is what concerns us when they talk about a change in the economic reality, not recreational projects such as the construction of the Neom project and tourist cities.
Vision 2030: Projects that don ’ t exist
The citizen in Saudi Arabia today asks himself what Mohammed bin Salman has achieved from these projects, says the researcher and adds, as he pays high taxes, still unable to secure the required level of decent living for his family, also finances fictitious projects, and is responsible for paying bills unrelated to them, especially Vision 2030 projects or in relation to invisible services, as well as corruption, which is declared to fight but no trace.
Ibrahim summarizes Vision 2030 in the following phrase: “I hear a noise, but I don ’ t see flour, ” as we hear a lot of projects that don ’ t exist on the ground.
For example, the Saudi authorities announced that the rate of “Saudization ” will increase, as there are 13 million workers in Saudi Arabia, including 10 million foreigners, 2 million males and 1 million females.
But in reality, the percentage of Saudi workers remained the same.
Knowing that Mohammed bin Salman has already said that he will raise the rate of employment and reduce unemployment to 7 percent, noting that the figures in the media are completely unrealistic, so that the General Authority for Statistics in Saudi Arabia lies a lot of the announced figures.
Moreover, there are millions below the poverty line for whom the Saudi authorities have given nothing.
Housing crisis
The same is true of the housing crisis that the Saudi regime has promoted, but it remains the same: most people live in rented houses, as the ownership rate is very low, at only 28 percent previously.
Moreover, Mohammed bin Salman displaced hundreds of thousands of families after demolishing neighborhoods in Jeddah, Mecca and other cities without compensating the residents.
Moreover, the basic files that concern the daily life of the individual have not been treated as if they were designed for other purposes such as the construction of tourism projects.
Private sector
As for the role of the private sector, the political opponent points out that it previously played a role somewhat parallel to the public sector, Mohammed bin Salman came and destroyed this sector, as if he wanted to impose himself as an alternative.
This happened in stages, first when he confiscated the money of many merchants, and when he took over most of the company ’ s property and commercial revenues, and embarked on projects that weakened others, the crown prince came to dominate the public and private sectors.
At the end of his speech, the researcher concludes: “Vision 2030 transformed the country into a personal property after it was a family property. ”
If Washington achieves this, the protection of the Saudi regime will not be among its priorities, then Riyadh in its natural size will face alone neighboring countries and be forced to live with them, it will also be forced to understand with the opposition inside and respond to its demands.

Africa adapts to renewable energy
T + T - normal size
Africa is one of the most vulnerable regions to the effects of climate change, although it is responsible for less carbon emissions than the big rich countries.
There are many opportunities that countries in Africa can invest in order to reduce the effects of the climate crisis and open wider prospects for economic development, most importantly renewable energy projects, which can be a key pillar of a successful energy strategy for Africa.
The African continent is rich in renewable energy resources, yet there are significant disparities in the capacity of its countries in this sector, including the volume of investments being made.
While the volume of global investments in the renewable energy sector shows a remarkable decline in Africa, many countries in Africa have in recent years specifically recognized the importance of moving faster than ever before and urgently necessary to utilize renewable energy sources as tools to reduce the effects of climate change as well as to achieve economic development, which threatens to increase investment rates in the sector in the future.
In this context, the recent climate report issued by the United Nations through the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), talked about the potential of the countries of the continent, which, if employed optimally, would reduce the severe effects of climate change, support economic development and lift millions out of poverty through renewable energy projects.
This April ’ s climate report points to the need for more renewable energy programs, such as Kenya ’ s Lake Turkana wind farm, which was launched in 2019.
It is estimated that this project accounts for 18% of the country ’ s energy production.
Africa ’ s total investment in the sector over the past two decades has reached nearly $60 billion, accounting for just 2 percent of the $2.8 trillion global investment in renewable energy over the past 20 years, according to a recent report by the Associated Press this month.
In 2020, 9% of all energy generated in Africa came from renewable sources, with a strong (6.8%) reliance on hydropower.
However, the PwC (Multinational Professional Services Network) report indicates that progress has been made in this area.
The current phase is witnessing a relative boom in renewable energy projects on the African continent, with many African countries increasing efforts to use more renewable energy such as solar and wind, and moving away from dependence on fossil fuels.
Several countries, including Kenya, Tanzania, Morocco, Egypt, Ethiopia and South Africa, have taken the lead in adopting large-scale clean energy policies, supporting the global trend to adapt the energy mix to develop sustainability.
Key factors
The deputy of the Egyptian Scientific Foundation for Training, Professor of Finance and Investment, Dr. Mustafa Badra, said that the African continent is a continent rich in wealth and renewable and clean energy sources, in addition to the availability of manpower, which adds to it the advantage of expanding renewable energy projects if the necessary political will and funding are available.
In statements to Al-Bayan, Badra identifies three key factors that will contribute to the development of the renewable energy sector in the continent and the transformation in this framework, especially as the continent “is still in its first phase or step in this transformation in the hope of catching up with the world. ”
The first factor, according to Badra, is the availability of political will, starting with the adoption of broader economic policies for a green transition based on clean energy.
The second factor is related to financial support, in light of the cost of transformation and projects and with the lack of investments facing the continent ’ s countries in this sector.
The third factor or challenge relates to the availability of technological infrastructure.
At the same time, the economist talks about the reasons for the disparity witnessed by African countries in the file of renewable energy, pointing to the challenges witnessed by some countries, including conflicts, internal conflicts and security disturbances imposed on the scene in some of those countries, as well as the economic conditions, the spread of poverty and political instability among the variables witnessed by the countries of the continent.
The economist pointed to the Egyptian experience in this context as one of the experiences that attaches great importance to renewable energy, which is reflected in many projects carried out by the state and its interest in the political leadership in the green economy, as well as its call for international financial institutions to help and finance Africa in this important sector and enter with large investments.
Cairo aims to increase the share of renewable energy in the electricity mix to 42% by 2035.
The near future
A recent report from the World Economic Forum stressed that “growth in the near future is driven by solar and wind projects in Egypt, Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco and Ethiopia. ”
According to the report, North Africa is currently the continent ’ s leading region in terms of renewable energy capacity and is likely to remain in this position when capacity currently under construction is taken into account, while Central Africa will see the largest increase when all projects under construction are completed, with capacity set to more than double.
On the other hand, West Africa has very little new capacity on the doors.
From 2019 to 2020, solar and wind power increased by 13% and 11% respectively, while hydropower increased by 25%.
Africa ’ s total installed renewable energy capacity has grown by more than 24 gigawatts since 2013.
Looking ahead, projections to 2050 point to an increase of 27.3 exajoules (EJ) compared to the current 1.8 exajoules, according to a report by the World Economic Forum.

Dust storms.
sources and danger.
|
At the beginning of this year's spring season, the incidence of dust storms increased significantly.
Their frequency varies from year to year, but generally increases in the transitional periods between seasons, especially spring and autumn, for many reasons, some natural and others of a human nature, that is, by man.
Dust storms are fast winds that transport dust and plankton, causing a lack of visibility at short distances.
Despite the great controversy over the causes of dust or dust storms and the fact that the camel bears full responsibility for their occurrence, as stated in one of the videos circulated on social media, the reasons are not limited to the poor camel alone, even if it is one of the reasons!
The causes of dust storms are many, including: (1) Desertification as a result of drought resulting from low rainfall.
(2) Desertification due to human activities associated with overgrazing as a result of increasing numbers of camels and sheep on pasture capacity.
(3) Extensive agricultural activities, especially ploughing the land and leaving it exposed for long periods.
(4) Soil movement as a result of development and military actions and absurd car tracks in deserts that led to the breaking and dismantling of the soil and the destruction of vegetation cover.
(5) The reduction of the surface groundwater table, which led to the drying of the soil and thus the impact on the vegetation cover.
Globally, sub-Saharan Africa is the main contributor to Earth ’ s dust storms, which travel to the Americas via the Atlantic Ocean via tropical east winds.
But the Fertile Crescent has also become a source of dust, due to the halving of agricultural production as a result of climate change.
Iraq is one of the sources of dust storms as a result of the decline of the level of rivers, which led to the drought of the marshes and lakes in Iraq and Iran, and add to the list of sources open deserts of the Kingdom, which suffer environmental degradation as a result of human tampering of unfair grazing and wood and the like.
Dust storms are one of the factors responsible for increased allergic reactions, asthma attacks and chronic breathing problems, as well as blood vessels and heart disease.
Dust storms are also carriers of microorganisms, including bacteria, fungi, germs and viruses that cause certain diseases.
Besides, dust storms have economic effects, they adversely affect agricultural production by transporting agricultural pests, reducing photosynthetic activity, destroying crops, as well as affecting infrastructure, by reducing visibility, disrupting energy and air and road transport systems, burying railways, as well as contributing to the deterioration of the performance of solar panels, as well as damaging residential property.
There is no doubt that dust storms and their increased frequency are a warning sign that requires a rapid response through a review of environmental regulations, the need to raise the environmental awareness of the population, the organization of grazing seasons based on the identification of the pastoral capacity of each region, as well as innovative solutions to mitigate desertification that benefit from tremendous technical progress.
Finally, it follows from the above that the problem is not country-specific, but a regional problem that requires concerted efforts.
The Green Middle East initiative by Prince Mohammed bin Salman is designed to design innovative solutions to address climate change and promote environmental sustainability through a number of projects, including: planting 50 billion trees across the Middle East region and reclaiming 200 million hectares of degraded land through afforestation, which contributes to a 2.5 per cent reduction in global carbon emissions.

A poll conducted by Edelman, an American consulting and public relations firm, found high levels of trust in Saudi society in the kingdom ’ s key institutions: government, business, NGOs and the media.

Edelman has international credibility and has been surveying the confidence index in 28 countries for nearly 22 years.

A new study says a home video game may help stroke sufferers rehabilitate their weakened limbs.
They can be relied upon to minimize a visit to a physical therapy clinic.
Lin Gauthier, from the University of Massachusetts, said: “Recovery Rapids is for stroke patients, and when players, for example, paddle in the river and avoid rocks, they need to use the arm affected by the stroke, and when playing cards, they need to use the injured fingers. ”
According to Freewell Health, the research team followed 167 patients in the physiotherapy phase after a stroke.
The patients were divided into 4 groups for 3 weeks.
The first group (self-play) received 5 hours of traditional physical therapy that focused on making behavioral changes.
They also played the game at home alone.
The second group (telematics) received 5 hours of behavioral therapy and games at home, as well as telemedicine visits that focused on the behavior.
The third group (traditional care) received 5 hours of traditional physical rehabilitation that focused on motor skills.
The fourth group (restraining) received 35 hours of restraining motion therapy, which traditionally involves restraining the limb that was not affected by the stroke, forcing the patient to use the affected limb.
RESULTS
The researchers found that the self-play group and the remote play group made meaningful gains in motor activity in their arm.
In fact, they were better than those seen in the traditional group.
The tele-gaming group achieved gains similar to those seen in the “constraint ” group, yet self-gaming was not as effective as therapy induced by restraints.
After six months, most patients appeared to have retained the gains they had made in treatment.
The study found that this game works in combination with a physical therapist to improve rehabilitation outcomes, while reducing visits to a physical therapy clinic.
Gauthier said: "The patient was the driver of his own treatment and independently participated in motor practice through technology.
After that he would meet periodically with the therapist who worked as a coach to a greater degree. ”

UAE participates in setting global standards for fair, accountable and understandable systems
Artificial intelligence.
Scientific Maturity with Moral Dilemmas
T + T - normal size
With the increasing use of artificial intelligence technologies in vital sectors that directly affect our lives, such as health, education, mobility, agriculture and even arts and space, experts believe that it is possible to develop a super artificial intelligence that reaches the point of controlling the emotions and motivations of people and thus their reality.
Will we be the ones who shape the reality and future of artificial intelligence systems or vice versa?
The more pressing question is, can we ensure that artificial intelligence is harnessed as a moral responsibility to improve human lives?
The rapid progress of artificial intelligence in recent years has led groups of experts to call for the need to develop safeguards to protect humanity from the dangers of artificial intelligence.
Given the gravity of the issue, many government bodies, civic organizations, private companies, think tanks, and research groups are working to develop principles governing AI trends such as the Barcelona Declaration, the Montreal Declaration, the Google Principles, and the Microsoft Principles.
One such organization is the Future of Life Institute, a nonprofit research and outreach organization founded in Boston in 2014 to monitor existential threats to humanity.
The institute was founded by MIT cosmologist Max Tegmark, Skype co-founder Jan Tallinn and DeepMind research scientist Victoria Krakow.
The institute worked with AI researchers and developers as well as scientists from many disciplines to create the 23 guidelines now referred to as the Asilomar Principles, which aim for AI technologies to develop reliably, safely and comprehensively.
A recent study by the Future of Life Institute suggests that AI is unlikely to show human emotions such as love or hate, and that there is no reason to expect AI to automatically deliberate good or evil.
But experts at the institute suggest two scenarios in which AI could become an imminent threat: The first scenario is that humans program AI to do something destructive, such as “autonomous ” or autonomous weapons — AI systems programmed to kill and capable of easily causing mass casualties in the wrong person ’ s hands.
Moreover, an AI arms race could inadvertently lead to an AI war that also leads to heavy casualties.
To avoid “losing ” to the other side, these weapons can be designed to be extremely difficult to stop, and humans can easily lose control in that situation.
This risk exists even with “narrow ” — or limited — AI, but it grows with increasing levels of AI and autonomy.
The other scary scenario is that the AI is programmed to do something useful, but it may develop a destructive way to achieve its goal, which can happen when we fail to fully align the AI goals with our goals, which is very difficult.
For example, if you ask a smart, obedient car to take you to the airport as soon as possible, you may arrive “as soon as possible, ” but you will be chased by police helicopters and probably passed out at speed.
The car didn ’ t do “what it wanted, ” which was to arrive at least safely, but it did literally what you asked.
If a super-intelligent system is tasked with an ambitious geoengineering project, it could cause havoc in our ecosystem as a side effect, and human attempts to stop it are seen as a “threat ” to be met.
Benefit
His Excellency Omar bin Sultan Al Olama, Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Teleworking Applications, said: “The UAE government attaches great importance to ensuring the optimal use of AI solutions and capabilities, and adopts within its future directions to make the most of this advanced technology, with full commitment to employ it with high ethical responsibility centered on people and community service. ”
To achieve this, the UAE government, through the UAE Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain Council, has formed a dedicated subcommittee to ensure effective governance and regulation of AI technology.
Among the initiatives related to the ethics of artificial intelligence applications worked on by the Council is the self-assessment tool for artificial intelligence applications, which was launched at the level of the Government of Dubai, and is being developed and launched at the level of the federal government.
Principles
He added: “This assessment is based on four basic principles: inclusion: It means that the benefits of artificial intelligence include all members of society, and that governance systems apply to this technology globally, while respecting the dignity, rights and privacy of individuals.
Humanity: AI should be beneficial to humanity and consistent with human values, both in the short term and in the long term.
And safety: AI systems should be safe, and be harnessed in the service of humanity.
AI systems must be fair, transparent, accountable and understandable.
In addition to these principles and standards, the UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain, represented by its subcommittee of artificial intelligence experts in the country, participates in the development and formulation of global standards, through the World Organization for Standards, with a group of experts. ”
He pointed out that the committee is currently working on the development of technical standards for artificial intelligence, including the standards of "explainable artificial intelligence", which is one of the most important technical topics that allow to verify the compatibility of models of artificial intelligence with the basic principles of its use.
The committee has played an important role in the development of these standards, and it is expected that they will be adopted in the country once approved by the technical committee of the World Organization for Standards, to control and ensure the optimal employment of artificial intelligence applications.
Data protection
As for the data used to train artificial intelligence models, which is one of the most important possible elements of these applications, the UAE has issued the “Personal Data Protection Law ”, which aims to protect the data of individuals available to companies from the uses that violate privacy in the training of artificial intelligence models and other uses.
The Office of Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Telework Applications, in collaboration with Oxford University, is working to train the employees of ministries and federal and local government agencies through the “Artificial Intelligence Program ” to develop the ability of trainees to analyze the security and ethical risks that may result from the wrong adoption of artificial intelligence technologies.
Rules.
Ghassan Abu Ajamiya, director of strategic planning at the Emirates Alliance for Technical Solutions, said: “Science at the beginning is simple, but with the development of these sciences, including artificial intelligence, societies need laws and legislation to regulate its transactions, and what happened in our digital life is that developments are faster than legislation, and giant companies began to impose their way of dealing with data. ”
Abu Ajima pointed out that most of those companies and owners of platforms that contain millions of data are American companies, so the European Union began its journey to address these trends by issuing a few days ago the Digital Services Law, which aims to get rid of harmful or toxic content on the Internet, and under this decision will be responsible for their algorithms, disclosure in all transparency, and required to assess the risks in content and mitigate it to protect users. Prevent the rapid spread of misinformation, combat hate speech, and avoid putting unsafe products on the market.
About a month earlier, the Digital Markets Act was announced, with the aim of reducing the broad dominance of companies in the digital economy, and the beginning of the union with the laws was when the data privacy protection system was issued in 2018.
He added: “There is no doubt that the set of decisions issued by the European Union can serve as a platform to help draw up a legal framework for legislation that can be built on and adapted according to the values and ethics that suit each country or region, and this will undoubtedly contribute to improving how user data is used and reduce its exploitation by IT giants that own major social media platforms. ”
A proactive step
Mohamed Amin, senior vice president of Dell Technologies in the Middle East, said many companies today rely on AI technologies to get accurate and quick answers to difficult issues they may face.
He added: “Today, we rely more and more on artificial intelligence models to make different decisions, whether about approving bank loan applications or helping customers decide on their next holiday destination, this technology is able to calculate the smallest details and differences.
So we need to make sure that AI systems are ethical and incorruptible, and that people are able to understand how decisions are made through this technology.
There is no doubt that artificial intelligence has the ability to calculate huge amounts of data and improve decision-making processes, but we cannot lose sight of the fact that the decisions made by AI systems affect the lives of humans, they are a machine that can currently use big data to create better information than humans, but they do not understand the context, have no emotions or ethics, and are unable to think outside the box.
When there are no clear checks and balances in the functioning of these systems, they can negatively affect the diversity of our ideas and our excellence, by treating us as a homogeneous group, and providing only structured content that does not respect our differences.
Artificial intelligence has been described as the most important technology under development today.
However, we need to place it under the proper supervision of governments and regulators, who will be instrumental in helping companies deal with the ethical side and shortcomings of these systems.
Challenges
“The ethical challenges of AI are not limited to regulating the collection and circulation of personal data, but rather to putting in place controls to prevent the employment of AI to make decisions or to subject, compel or influence certain people or their decisions through the processing of their personal data, whether without their consent or in a way that may prejudice or affect their rights, ” said lawyer Mujahed Sebai.
He added: "Many legal and ethical questions related to the use of artificial intelligence are also raised about the mechanism of making decisions or correcting them if they are wrong or determining who is responsible for them, especially in the event of damage, whether material or moral, and may take biased decisions or lead to injustice or discrimination in all its forms or to monopolize the huge data that may be collected about people or institutions."
“To deal with these challenges, all stakeholders, from governments to individuals, must work together to identify the direct or long-term effects of AI, to develop strategies and systems to ensure that it is employed through a humane approach that respects the human principles and values on which our societies and the rights of individuals are based, without negatively affecting or reprogramming those values, especially by outsiders, whether for political, economic or security considerations. ”

Scientists warn of what could lead to a “mass extinction ” of marine life that“ rivals ” the severity of the Great Death!
The Libyan Observatory Newspaper
A new study has revealed that greenhouse gas emissions could lead to mass extinctions of marine life to levels not seen since before the dinosaurs.
Researchers in New Jersey modeled the future extinction risk of marine life in all of the world's oceans under different projected climate scenarios.
If emissions are not curbed, the loss of marine species due to global warming and oxygen depletion could reverse the “Great Death, ” the most serious extinction event on Earth, by about 2100, they say.
The Great Death, known as the deadliest extinction on Earth, saw the loss of 95% of all marine species when it occurred about 250 million years ago.
It can also match other major extinction events in Earth's history, including the mass extinction at the end of the Cretaceous that killed the dinosaurs 66 million years ago.
According to the researchers, tropical waters will face the greatest loss of biodiversity, while polar species are more at risk of extinction.
On a more positive note, experts say reversing greenhouse gas emissions could reduce the risk of extinction by more than 70 percent.
Lead author Justin Penn, at Princeton University ’ s Department of Earth Sciences, said: “The bright side is that the future is not written in stone.
The scale of the extinction we have discovered depends heavily on the amount of carbon dioxide [CO2] we release going forward.
“There is still enough time to reverse the trajectory of CO2 emissions and prevent the magnitude of warming that could cause this mass extinction. ”
The Great Death marks a period when life on Earth has never been so close to extinction without recovery, either before or after.
When carbon dioxide dissolves in the oceans, it becomes extremely acidic and the level of oxygen in the water drops, killing marine life.
Scientists have long debated theories of the cause of extinction ranging from meteorite impact to volcanoes, which could have caused climatic and environmental changes that make the Earth uninhabitable.
But in the event of the next mass extinction, history will directly blame anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions.
For the study, Ben and co-author Curtis Deutsch, also based at Princeton, combined existing data on marine species with climate change models to predict how changes in habitat conditions will affect their survival.
The experts compared their model to the size of the “Big Five, ” five historical mass extinctions recorded in the fossil record, among them the“ Great Death. ”
The researchers say that with global temperatures rising “as usual, ” marine life is likely to be subjected to a mass extinction that could potentially rival the size and severity of the Great Death.
Since the Great Death is the deadliest extinction event on Earth, the next marine extinction is likely to surpass the other four species.
Among the events, they found a common pattern – as the ocean warms and oxygen availability decreases, there is a clear decline in the abundance of marine life.
Water temperature and oxygen availability are key factors that will change as the climate warms due to human activity.
Warm water is not only a risk factor for species adapted to cold climates; it also contains less oxygen than cold water, slowing ocean circulation further and reducing the supply of oxygen at depth.
Paradoxically, the metabolic rates of the species increase as the water warms, and therefore the demand for oxygen rises as the supply decreases.
“Once the oxygen supply is less than what a species needs, we expect to see significant species losses, ” he said.
Experts say marine animals have physiological mechanisms that allow them to adapt to environmental changes, but only to a certain extent.
The researchers found that polar species are more likely to become extinct globally if climate warming occurs because they will not have suitable habitats to move to.
Tropical marine species are likely to be better off because they have traits that allow them to cope with warm, low-oxygen waters in the tropics.
To determine the relative importance of climate in the occurrence of extinctions, the team also compared future extinction risks from climate warming with data from the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) on current threats to various marine animals.
They found that climate change currently affects 45% of marine species at risk of extinction, but is only the fifth most important stressor after overfishing, transport, urban development and pollution.
However, Ben said climate change could soon overcome all these stressors in importance.
"Extreme warming will lead to climate-induced extinctions, which, towards the end of the century, will compete with all current human pressures combined," he said.
The study, “Avoiding mass extinction of oceans due to climate warming, ” was published in the journal Science.

The World Health Organization is interested in alternative medicine.
Mohamed Ismail - Cairo - DPA -
Many people use traditional medicine – but what do these methods really do?
A new WHO centre intends to explore this.
The center is based in India, a country where alternative medicine is so important that it even has its own ministry – which specializes in Ayurveda, Yoga, Physiotherapy, Greek Medicine, Master and Homeopathy.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the opening of the centre in Jamnagar in mid-April, saying: “India ’ s traditional medicine system is not just a cure.
It ’ s a comprehensive science of life. ”
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the Indian government is supporting the centre with US $250 million (230 million euros).
WHO President Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said: “The center aims to be an engine of innovation, moving towards an agenda of evidence, data and sustainability in traditional medicine, ” adding that the center would connect traditional medicine practitioners around the world and help set standards for research.
Traditional medicine is a broad field.
According to the World Health Organization ’ s statement for the center, 80% of the world ’ s population uses traditional medicine, which includes among other things acupuncture, Ayurvedic medicine and herbal blends.
Traditional medicine is also represented in modern science.
According to the World Health Organization, about 40% of all drugs approved today are derived from natural substances.
The discovery of aspirin, for example, is based on ancient recipes made from the bark of the willow tree.
The research for artemisinin for use in the fight against malaria, for which the Nobel Prize was awarded in 2015, began with the study of ancient texts of Chinese medicine.
George Rochmeyer of Cochrane, an international network that provides the scientific basis for decisions in the health field, said it makes sense at least to take a closer look at treatment methods that have been developed over centuries, to verify the reasonableness of these methods, and to conduct clinical studies on them in case of doubt.
Cochrane reviews are systematic reviews that collect all scientific evidence on a specific issue from medicine or other health sciences.
However, Rochmeyer also stressed that besides the examples of traditional methods cited by the WHO, which form the basis of currently developed treatments, there are likely many other examples where traditional methods of careful review have proven ineffective or even dangerous, such as phlebotomy, noting that spending too much money on studies to review a therapeutic practice is always a matter of discretion.
Rochmeyer stated that there are many Cochrane reviews about the use of traditional methods such as acupuncture in certain cases, but: “From my personal experience at Cochrane, I would say that I have not come across many reviews that have shown really compelling evidence for traditional therapeutic practice. ”
This is often due to the fact that when searching for these treatments we find only a few often-poorly conducted studies that cannot prove or disprove any benefit from them – which brings us back to the question of whether the already limited research funds should be invested in a scientifically unreasonable procedure – for example, homeopathy.
Professor Emeritus Edzard Ernst, a longtime professor of alternative medicine at the University of Exeter, noted that while it was necessary to wait and see who would lead the center and what it would do, the WHO press release was full of exaggerations.
The World Health Organization says it also wants to use new technologies at the new center for the study of traditional medicine — via artificial intelligence and big data, for example.
The center is expected to focus on providing a reliable evidence base for policy and standards of traditional medicine practices and products.
In addition, the center is supposed to help countries integrate these practices into their health systems.

Heart Rhythm Case Reports, an official journal of the Heart Rhythm Society, has published a research report on the negative effects of natural herbal supplements.
Dr Elise Baclantes, in the Department of Cardiology, University Hospital Geneva, said: “More and more people are taking herbal supplements for their potential benefits.
However, their “normal ” nature can be misleading, as these preparations can have serious adverse side effects on their own or if combined with other supplements or medications, their use should not be underestimated, and dosage recommendations should always be respected. ”
The study looked at a 56-year-old woman who was admitted to the emergency department after developing dizziness and fainting without warning was diagnosed with a life-threatening heart rhythm disorder after an electrocardiogram showed short cycles of the Torsad de Pointe, rapid heartbeat originating in the ventricles, and a remarkably long QT interval, meaning that the heart ’ s electrical system takes longer than usual to recharge between beats.
Doctors were able to identify the cause of this condition as the herbal supplements she was taking to help her cope with the stressful work-life balance.
Having started a regimen of six times the recommended dose of hemp oil four months ago and recently added berberine to the mix, all supplements were discontinued during her hospital stay, leading to a gradual decrease in her QT interval until normalized five days later.
In her three-month follow-up, she did not report any new episodes of dizziness or fainting, and her electrocardiogram remained within the normal range, with no other causative factors, her return to normal strongly proved that the diagnosis linked the supplements to the arrhythmia.
According to experts, the popularity of herbal supplements has grown rapidly in recent years, especially those containing cannabidiol, which is available without a prescription, and CBD or cannabidiol has been shown to have anti-inflammatory, anti-epileptic, analgesic, anxiolytic, antipsychotic and immunological properties.
It is supplied as raw materials or as ready-to-use products (such as cosmetics, tobacco substitutes and scented oils), and does not contain the tetrahydrocannabinol that causes the psychoactive effect of cannabis.
Therefore, it is not subject to examination by drug regulatory bodies.
Berberine, found in the roots and stem bark of many medicinal plants, is frequently used in traditional Chinese medicine and Ayurveda to treat infections, diarrhea, type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol and high blood pressure.
Dr. Baklantis points out that the preparation of herbal supplements is widely seen as harmless, largely unregulated, natural substances.
"The exact composition can vary greatly from distributor to distributor, and the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic properties of these substances are not well known.
As a result, it is not always possible to anticipate its negative consequences. ”

According to TikTok ’ s announcement, Branded Mission is the industry ’ s first advertising solution that enables advertisers to collect authentic content from TikTok creators, convert high-performance videos into ads, and improve brand affinity with media exposure.

Finally, Branded Mission now has more opportunities to discover trends within the TikTok platform and interact with its vast ecosystem of creators of various creativity and talents.
However, TikTok creators must be at least 18 years old and have more than 1,000 followers to be eligible to participate in Branded Mission.

In addition, each Branded Mission page will display a potential earning opportunity so that creators can decide if they want to participate in one or not.

The keto diet is undoubtedly useful in getting rid of kilograms and accumulated fat, as it negatively affects health and shows a range of signs and symptoms experienced by the body during the diet phase from hair loss to insomnia.
The keto diet is one of the most popular diets around the world, it depends mainly on proteins without eating carbohydrates completely, helps in losing weight significantly and quickly, but it has many health harms, and has warned many nutritionists.
Here ’ s what the keto system is, the complications of following the keto system and the side effects of its followers
What is the keto system?
The keto diet is a low-carb, high-fat, and medium-protein diet, the main focus of this diet is to reduce carbohydrate intake and make the body use more fat to produce energy.
When you consume low carbs the body begins to use fat to produce energy to perform your daily functions, once the body consumes all the fat it consumes per day, it begins to burn stored fat in the body which actually helps in weight loss.
The process of burning fat to produce energy instead of carbohydrates is known as ketosis, and the transition from burning carbohydrates to burning fat leads to the development of keto flu.
Keto Diet
Commenting on the above, Dr. Nahla Abdel Wahab, a nutrition consultant, said that the keto diet system works to convert the burning of sugars to fat, explaining that it serves as a treatment for some cases and not a lifestyle.
Nahla Abdel Wahab added that the keto diet system relies on the reduction of a large proportion of foods in daily meals, including vegetables.
The nutrition consultant pointed out that the keto diet depends on 95% of healthy fats, 20% of protein, and a small percentage of sugars.
She added that the missing nutrients "keto diet" are sometimes replaced by supplements, which is not desirable for the body.
She pointed out that the keto diet lasts for six months, and allows some foods that are not allowed by any other diet, such as mayonnaise and protein.
Complications of Keto Diet System
Jamal Shaaban, former Dean of the Heart Institute, said that keto is a diet based on causing a physiological inversion in the body and converting the energy substance used to fat instead of glucose.
Jamal Shaaban added in his post through his official account on the social networking site "Facebook", saying "The attractiveness of keto gives you impressive initial results in terms of rapid reduction in weight, but the harm of keto is great in the short and long term and has warned the American Heart Association recently, as it may raise harmful cholesterol and lead to the hardening of the coronary arteries."
On the other side according to Health24.
The most prominent harms of the keto diet on health are as follows:
1. Harmful to kidney health
Prevents carbohydrate intake and relies on protein intake which makes urine more acidic and it negatively affects the functioning of the kidneys,

Sand and dust storms threaten societies and economies in the Middle East
Fishermen sail in the Shatt al-Arab waterway during a sandstorm in Basra, Iraq.

By: Euronews
Sand and dust storms in the countries of the Middle East are slowly affecting the health of the population and the economies of the region, yet they are ignored, according to the Israeli newspaper Haaretz.
In countries such as Syria, Iraq, Iran and other Gulf states, the average temperature rises to more than 30 degrees Celsius, and in Baghdad, for example, heavy dust and sand filled the atmosphere of the Iraqi capital last week, adding a pale orange color to the city.
Sand and dust storms usually hit Iraq during the spring, but the phenomenon has been increasing in frequency and severity in recent years and is expected to worsen in the coming years.
These storms cause health problems and high economic costs in the hundreds of millions of dollars, as the storms forced 1,000 Iraqis to enter hospitals because of respiratory problems, and the authorities forced residents to stay in their homes, and closed several airports.
Experts point to a close relationship between these storms and respiratory problems, some heart disease and conjunctivitis.
According to the World Bank, the global cost of dust and sand storms increased by 63% between 1990 and 2013 to reach about $3.6 trillion, according to a report issued in 2019, which indicated that the global cost of this natural disaster may exceed 123%, worth up to $141 billion.
According to Haaretz, these figures reflect the losses from premature deaths due to exposure to dust, as more than ten thousand premature deaths were recorded in Iraq in 2013 and this cost the Iraqi economy $15 billion, equivalent to 2.9% of GDP.
In addition, there are direct costs of the natural phenomenon such as the closure of airports, the loss of agricultural crops and the interruption of production, which, according to the World Bank, is estimated at about $13 billion, bringing the total costs in the Middle East and North Africa to exceed $150 billion annually.
Climate change is only one factor for such dangerous weather events, experts say, although the impacts of the climate crisis will be greater in the future because it causes desertification and drought.
Sand and dust storms are exacerbated by human activity and erosion, such as leaving the soil unprotected after the harvest, and farmers abandoning their fields due to war, creating vast areas that drive the wind to pick up dust easily to carry it high.
Lakes such as Lake Aral between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan and Lake Urmia in Iran are drying up, dam construction projects are draining river streams, and the flow of water in the Tigris and Euphrates is declining.
Scientists believe that the phenomenon of "ocean Nina" (the stage of sea temperature decline, opposite El Nino) is contributing to sand and dust storms in the Middle East, where measures have been taken to combat the phenomenon, Saudi Arabia has pledged to plant 10 billion trees and another 40 billion in the region to combat desertification and storms, and the UAE launched an alarm system in 2016, to counter major storms.
