« Money » monitors the forecasts of economic analysts for foreign investment flows in the current year
A number of them predicted it would reach $10 billion.
Samar Al-Sayed
Praying for Mahmood
6: 59 AM, Wednesday, 27 Jul 22
Wael Ziadeh: The Russian-Ukrainian war is an opportunity for the Egyptian stock exchange to attract more capital
Esraa Ahmed: Clean energy, infrastructure and digital financial services are the most attractive sectors
Hani Geneina: Companies should be encouraged to reinvest their profits instead of transferring them to parent entities abroad
Naaman Khaled: Most of the money will come from Gulf markets
The Egyptian government aims to increase foreign direct investment flows, especially the Gulf, in the local market in the coming period, in light of the repercussions of the Russian-Ukrainian war on the global and local economies, and a number of analysts and macroeconomic experts estimated the value of these investments to reach $10 billion, driven by various factors, including the decline in the stock prices of companies on the stock exchange, and the exchange rate of the pound against the dollar.
The latest report issued by UNCTAD in June on the volume of foreign investment flows in 15 African countries last year showed that Egypt ranked second in the list, recording the volume of flows about 5.122 billion dollars compared to 5.852 billion in 2020 compared to 9.010 billion in 2019.
South Africa came first last year with a 1,235% jump in investment inflows of $40.889 billion compared to $3.062 billion in 2020 and $5.125 billion in 2019.
Wael Ziadeh, founder and CEO of Zela Capital, said that the Russian-Ukrainian war had negatively affected foreign direct investment flows in the world, while inter-state assistance had increased to counter the negative consequences of the war.
He explained to Al-Mal that these negative effects included the exit of investment flows from some emerging countries, which led to the impact of their trade balance, especially as their imports of food and oil more than their exports, for example Turkey and many European countries, as well as Sri Lanka.
On the other hand, the war represents a positive area for these countries, especially in activating the stock market sector, he said, adding that in this context, the Egyptian Exchange has opportunities to attract more foreign investments in the coming period.
He predicted that Egypt will take no more than six months to recover its trade balance once the war is over, as the prices of petroleum products and food will fall rapidly, as they rose rapidly after the outbreak of the war.
The objectives of the Egyptian government published in July 2021 in the second and final review report of the Credit Standby Arrangement Program signed with the International Monetary Fund, amounting to about $5.4 billion, indicated that the percentage of net foreign direct investments of GDP will rise to 2.5% in the current fiscal year compared to 2% in the last fiscal year, adding that it recorded 1.4% in the fiscal year 2021 / 2020, 2% in 2019 and 2.6% in 2019. / 2018.
These targets pointed out that the proportion of net foreign direct investment will jump to 3% of GDP in the fiscal year 2025 / 2024 compared to 2.9% in 2023 / 2024.
The government also expected in the report to increase the volume of foreign direct investment flows in the local market to about 11.7 billion in the current fiscal year against 8.6 billion dollars in the last fiscal year 2022 / 2021 to rise to 14.9 billion in the next fiscal year (2023 / 2024) and 16.5 billion in 2025 / 2024.
According to the Central Bank of Egypt ’ s forecasts issued in its statistical bulletin for May, the proportion of net foreign direct investment in GDP declined to about 1.3% in the fiscal year 2020 / 2021 compared to 2% in the fiscal year 2019 / 2020, adding that it was 2.7% in the fiscal year 2018 / 2019 and 3.1% in the year 2017 / 2018.
Economist Hani Geneina predicted that the value of net foreign direct investments in the local market will exceed 10 billion dollars in the coming period, due to several different factors, including the decline in the prices of shares of companies in the stock exchange and the exchange rate of the pound against the dollar.
However, Egypt was the second largest recipient of foreign direct investment in the African continent, he said, adding that recent pledges from Gulf countries to invest about $22 billion in various sectors will boost foreign direct investment in the future.
The number of new green projects in Egypt has more than tripled to $5.6 billion, according to the UNCTAD report, pointing out that for example, the UAE real estate company Reportage announced a real estate project worth $1.5 billion.
According to the report, the volume of foreign direct investment flows to North Africa declined by 5% to $9.3 billion last year.
Geneina told Al-Mal that the flows of foreign direct investments to the markets are divided into three types, the first is the acquisition of one company on another by more than 10%, pointing out that this investment happened last fiscal year, such as the acquisition of the UAE Holding “ADQ ” on several Egyptian companies, pointing out the importance of this type of investment, but it is not very useful in the list of foreign investments.
This type of rapid investment is encouraged by the decline in both stock prices on the stock exchange and the exchange rate of the pound against the dollar, as well as the recent government stimulus measures that included the implementation of the state ownership document.
The document of state ownership announced by the government in mid-June revealed the most prominent sectors that will witness the stabilization or reduction of government investments (while allowing the participation of the private sector), a number of activities in the transport, education, mining, real estate, electricity, telecommunications and sports sectors.
Geneina said that the second type of flows is the reinvestment of a foreign company present in the market for its profits again, pointing out that this type is classified in the balance of payments as foreign direct investments.
He added that the most prominent local sectors that will go to this type of investment is oil and gas, due to the high value of its profits achieved last fiscal year, and will therefore reinvest its large financial surpluses during the current fiscal year.
He pointed out that the third type of investment is the most difficult, which is the establishment of a new company or project from the beginning, and the employment of new workers, pointing out that for example, Dana Gas announced that it will expand its operations implemented in the local market.
This area is likely to witness an increase during the current fiscal year, especially in the oil and gas sectors and related sectors, namely petrochemicals and fertilizers, especially by Gulf investments in light of the features announced recently by the government, namely the state ownership document, the gold license, as well as the large financial surpluses they have, which motivates them to invest in the local market.
In mid-May, Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly announced a number of concessions on the industrial sector, most notably the issuance of the golden license for some projects, pointing out that it will be granted once and include three areas as a start, namely green hydrogen, electric car manufacturing and infrastructure, seawater desalination projects and renewable energy.
Geneina stressed the importance of the government encouraging foreign companies to reinvest their profits in the local market instead of transferring them to parent companies abroad by providing incentives to urge them to take this step.
According to the latest UNCTAD report, Mozambique ranked third in the list of foreign investment flows to 15 African countries last year, and its inflows rose by 68% to $5.102 billion compared to $3.035 billion in 2020, while it recorded 2.212 billion in 2019.
Nigeria ranked fourth on the list, attracting inflows of 4.844 billion over the past year, an increase of 103 percent from the previous year, the data added, adding that it recorded 2.385 billion in 2020 and 2.305 billion in 2019.
Ethiopia followed in fifth place, and foreign direct investment inflows increased last year by 79% to $4.259 billion compared to $2.381 billion in 2020.
In the sixth place came « Congo » with the volume of flows of $3.691 billion, a decline of 8% from its value in 2020, and recorded 4.016 billion dollars, followed by Ghana in the seventh place in the list and increased flows by 39% to reach 2.614 billion dollars during 2021 compared to 1.876 billion in 2020.
According to data from the UNCTAD list, foreign direct investment flows in Senegal jumped by 21% to 2.232 billion against 1.846 billion dollars in the previous comparison period.
According to the report, the value of flows to Morocco increased by 52% last year to $2.153 billion, and a major international financing deal was announced there, a $20 billion construction project for a 3,800km transmission line to the UK with a capacity of 3.6 gigawatts, sponsored by English company Xlinks.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo ranked 10th on the list, with investments up 14% to $1.870 billion compared to $1.647 billion in 2020.
Gabon came in eleventh place, with direct investment flows falling by 5% last year to record 1.635 billion dollars compared to 1.717 billion in 2020, followed by Uganda, with flows rising by 31% to 1.142 billion dollars compared to 874 million in 2020.
Tanzania ranked 13th, with foreign investment up 35 percent in 2021 to $922 million compared to $685 million in 2020.
According to the bulletin, investment flows in Algeria decreased by 24% last year to $870 million compared to $1.143 million in 2020, pointing to the decline of investments in Tunisia to $660 million compared to $652 million in 2020 to be ranked 15th.
Esraa Ahmed, a macro-economic analyst at the investment bank “Ahly Pharos ”, agrees with Geneina ’ s opinion as she expects the volume of net foreign direct investment in Egypt to rise to about $10 billion during the current fiscal year (2022 / 2023), up from levels that will not exceed $7 billion in the fiscal year ending 2021 / 2022.
She added that this rise is driven by the Gulf investment flows that have been announced recently, and the acquisition deals that we see are witnessing activity during the current period.
There are other factors that may prevent net foreign direct investment from rising to larger numbers in the near future due to the continuation of the war in Ukraine and its repercussions on the global economy.
According to Ahmed, these factors are the economic situation of the European Union, which is an important partner for Egypt in terms of trade and investment, in addition to the general reluctance globally to risk starting new projects, and the prevailing outlook for emerging markets and the risks of their currencies.
On the sectors that may witness foreign inflows during the coming period, she said that the most prominent of them are clean energy, new infrastructure driven by the expansion of the state in this field, in addition to digital financial services, and some branches of manufacturing industries.
For his part, Numan Khalid, a macro-economic analyst at Arqaam Capital, said that the current circumstances in the world prevent the possibility of predicting the volume of foreign direct investment flows in the local market during the coming period.
He added that most of the investments come from the Gulf market, especially from Saudi Arabia and the UAE, pointing out that these two countries have benefited greatly from the recent increases in oil prices, and thus have a great financial solvency through which to invest in surrounding countries, especially in Egypt, which is one of their target markets.
He pointed out that health, hotels, real estate and the financial sector will witness an increase in the volume of investment flows to them during the coming period.
During his participation in the Qatar Economic Forum last June, the Minister of Finance, Mohamed Maait, looked forward to increasing the volume of Gulf investments with the transformation of their deposits in Egypt into real investments that benefit from the promising development opportunities available in various fields.

Will America be like the weather in the Middle East soon?
New analytical results have revealed a major shift in 16 American cities where temperatures will become equivalent to the weather experienced in the Middle East, according to the British newspaper The Guardian, Monday, August 1, 2022.
The heatwaves have put about a third of the American population in front of new weather, with temperatures rising to 46 degrees Celsius in some areas of the Great Plains.
Cities have hit record temperatures, from Boston, Massachusetts, where the temperature reached 37 degrees Celsius, to Portland, Oregon, where the temperature reached 38.9 degrees Celsius on Tuesday, July 26.
But global warming could plunge many places in the United States into the kind of extreme weather that was previously impossible, leading to long-term climate change that is now common in areas far south of the country, or even similar to areas separated by ocean waters from the United States.
America is like the weather in the Middle East.
An analysis of temperature trends by the nonprofit Climate Central found that summer temperatures in 2100 for many U.S. cities would on average be equivalent to the weather in some 437 miles south of the country.
Temperatures in Washington, D.C., will be similar to those in Austin, Texas, while Boston will be more like Philadelphia, and temperatures in Billings, Montana will be equivalent to those in El Paso, Texas.
Some cities in the United States can change their climate to become like cities in other countries: Los Angeles, for example, will become the Mexican city of Tuxpan.
Summer in Austin could be similar to the current climate in Dubai, Phoenix could be similar to what Saudi Arabia is witnessing now, and Las Vegas will be similar to Kuwait.
Peter Gerrard, a spokesman for Climate Central, a research organization made up of climate scientists and science communicators, said: “The real risk is that heatwaves that are now transient extreme temperatures will start to last longer.
Heat waves of this type will become normal and the risks will be more present.
There will be people who have never needed air conditioners before, facing these conditions.
It can quickly turn from an uncomfortable situation to a dangerous one. ”
The researchers collected temperature data between 1990 and 2020 to arrive at today ’ s “normal ” temperatures and looked at the temperature forecasts for 20 different cities this century under different climate change scenarios.
Many analysts predict that rising temperatures will be held back below 3.6 ° C due to increased use of renewable energy, but Gerrard said even lower warming levels would cause changes to normal weather conditions in U.S. cities.
“Regardless of the scenario, this will be a near-term challenge almost everywhere.
“Reducing emissions will reduce rising temperatures and give governments and cities more time to take steps to keep people safe. ”

Life after COVID-19: Which countries ignore the telecommuting approach and why?
Conversation
By: Euronews
Many companies have come to see remote work as an effective method, turning many of their jobs into fully or partially remote jobs.
Copyright by AP Photo
Two and a half years ago, with the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic and the resulting health crisis escalating, the business world took a new direction dictated by stringent health measures: teleworking.
But as life has almost completely normalized and precautionary measures have been lifted, the question of telecommuting has become urgent: Do companies keep the telecommuting approach or return their employees to their offices?
Many companies have come to see remote work as an effective method, turning many of their jobs into fully or partially remote jobs.
According to a recent study from Indeed, global job listings featuring remote jobs have risen since the start of the epidemic, nearly tripling from just 2.5 percent in January 2020 to nearly 7.5 percent in September 2021.
Spain, Ireland and the United Kingdom were some of the countries with the largest increases, and the United States followed a similar trend.
The proportion of remote jobs has jumped from less than 4% of all high-paying jobs before the epidemic to about 9% at the end of 2020, and to more than 15% today in North America.
Data scientists at the job site Ladders believe that remote work will survive.
Despite these figures and data showing a large adoption of telework and hybrid work in many parts of the world, it seems that some countries did not like the idea and did not adapt to it, for cultural, legal or technical reasons.
Czech Republic: A legal crisis
The Czech Republic has not adopted the idea of working remotely despite its technological development, which is no less than that of its European peers.
The reason is simply legal, as the law does not specify whether a teleworker is a regular employee or not, so companies prefer to avoid working remotely due to legal uncertainty.
According to a survey conducted by Ipsos, 51% of Czech employees surveyed were interested in permanent remote work, and 59% were partially interested in remote work.
France: Lagging behind
France is not doing well in terms of remote work.
According to a study conducted jointly with Ifop and the Jean Juris Foundation, only 34% of French people worked remotely regularly during the epidemic, compared with 61% in Germany, 56% in Italy and 50% in Britain.
The amount of time the French worked remotely was also lower than their European neighbors: 11% worked from home four to five days a week, compared to 30% of Italians.
These low numbers can be explained by the extreme disparity between senior management – where the majority of those can work remotely – and other professional social groups, who largely continue to go to their workplaces.
Age has also been another reason for these disparities: older workers are less comfortable with digital technology than the new generation.
The French are known for their reluctance to change, so the situation may not change anytime soon.
A culture of “presence ” — being in the office despite illness — is still firmly rooted in the minds of the older generation.
When asked if they wanted fewer or more remote working days, French respondents said they wanted fewer remote working days, compared to their European neighbors.
Japan: A Strong Culture of "Presence"
Japan, just like France, is another country where a culture of “presence ” is rooted.
Many Japanese fear job stagnation if they don ’ t work long hours in the office, and forcing these workers to resort to remote work due to the health crisis has turned out to be a disaster.
While most employees say working from home has made them more efficient than they were in the office, Japanese employees are 20 percent less productive, according to a 2020 study by economist Toshihiro Okubo.
Japan also has a high social work structure, which makes it difficult to work remotely: employees prefer to work in teams and conduct evaluations collectively, while in the case of remote work, employees are assigned individual responsibilities and evaluated individually.
Mentoring and dialogue are core values of the Japanese work system, with senior employees supervising their younger colleagues, and informal conversations between employees foster communication within teams, which is not available in remote work.
Another reason why the Japanese telecommuting approach is not preferred is the lack of access to personal computers for many employees; in Japan one of the lowest rates of access to personal computers according to the OECD.
In addition, home offices are much less common than in the West, due to the small average size of apartments in cities and the high prices of large houses.
China: a difficult transition
Although China was the first country to resort to telecommuting because it was the first country to deal with the coronavirus, the transition was relatively difficult for the Chinese workforce.
At the start of the epidemic, 40 percent of Chinese workers were forced to work from home, an unexpected cultural shift in a country deeply attached to a culture of presence and hierarchy, according to consulting firm Bloomberg.
Once the state started shutdowns, the use of digital technologies — including artificial intelligence, location tracking, facial recognition, and so on — increased to contain the spread of the outbreak.
Some companies began to tighten their grip on their employees even as they worked remotely, recording their attendance daily with their managers and announcing their locations and whether they showed any symptoms of the virus.
Chinese communist history and culture may also explain the country ’ s difficulty in embracing telework, where employees have to negotiate agreements collectively.
Developing Countries: Weakness of the Internet
The epidemic has highlighted the technological disparity between nations of the world and highlighted it as an obstacle to a successful transition to telecommuting.
Not surprisingly, developing countries are the most vulnerable, but many have taken positions that go against their Internet resilience.
For example, Mexico and Brazil were more resilient than Indonesia or India, according to economic consultants Bhaskar Chakravorti and Ravi Shankar Chaturvedi.
Angola has also emerged as the world ’ s least telecommuting country, with just 0.70 out of every 100 people in the country having fixed-line broadband access in 2020, compared to 36.41 in the United States, according to the World Bank.

5 exercises to relieve discomfort
Dr. Deepak Ravindran, head of pain medicine at the Royal Berkshire Hospital in Reading, has spent more than two decades specializing in the management of acute and chronic pain.
In specific cases such as chronic pain, the research actually proves that mental body techniques can be effective compared to traditional techniques such as medications and surgery.
These mental practices may not fully cure the individual ’ s pain but they can certainly help.
In some cases it is more effective than traditional medical interventions.
"We now understand neuroplasticity, which is the ability of the brain and nerves to be plastic and rewire themselves in a way that can overcome pain."
"Alongside this, we recognise the role and contribution of lifestyle and personality driven by genes, and may indeed combine with environmental factors that can stimulate a particular gene in undesirable ways."
The doctor shared 5 practical tips on how you can begin to control pain:
• Activate your internal security system by breathing 3-4-5
Breathing is one of the most reliable and easily controlled ways to activate the safety system (parasympathetic apparatus).
When we can breathe longer than we breathe, the safety system can activate more predictably and provide the mind with reassurance that everything is safe.
A simple way to incorporate the breathing technique is the 3-4-5 method where you can breathe for three seconds, hold your breath for four seconds, and then exhale for five seconds.
Even practicing this for two to five minutes will help you take 10 to 20 breaths which can often help calm the nervous system considerably.
Another method that is easy to start with is the 5-5-5 method which requires 5 seconds of breathing, five seconds of waiting, and then five seconds of exhalation.
• Focus on a word, phrase or thing
One approach to trying to relax is to focus on a word, stage, or thing — a response that Howard ’ s cardiologist and professor of the mental body Herbert Benson wrote about.
This aims to achieve a state of focused flow or awareness of ourselves using a repetitive word, phrase, or action.
The use of Christian swimming pools or Hindu "jap mala" are examples of object focus.
This allows the nerves of our brain to move from the so-called virtual network to a different set of neural circuits called flow circuits.
This can then help relax the nervous system and thus reduce physical pain.
• Try yoga or tai chi
Both yoga and tai chi, also known as mind-body techniques, are becoming increasingly popular now, exercises are already in the mainstream with general practitioners and hospital doctors recommending tasks for different situations and age groups.
There are also studies that suggest that yoga and tai chi can benefit and cause pain relief.
Both exercises embrace the concept that pain can be present in both mind and body and relieve slow rhythmic movements, and yoga and tai chi can help control breathing as well as tighten and improve unconditioned muscles.
There are many videos and apps that can help you get started, while gyms and local health care centers may also have classes available.
• Exercise vigilance
Try to adopt a negative, non-judgmental, empathic attitude toward your thoughts as this is the essence of mindfulness-based stress reduction.
This technique has a very good evidence base for managing chronic pain using mind / body methods.
There is now good scientific evidence to suggest that when people are well-awakened meditators, there are positive changes in their nerves, the practice based on mindfulness shouldn ’ t be just about meditation.
It can be any physical activity that patients feel safe and like doing – be it eating, running, running, or going to the gym.
Be selective in the language you use.
Even when thinking.
Evidence has shown that the type of language we use can be very powerful in shaping our thoughts, and therefore our behaviors and actions, this is important because the language we use and the stories we tell can cause unsafe thoughts and actions, which can trigger activation of our immune system.
Writing down your positive thoughts at the beginning of the day with some points you are grateful for are also examples of positive thinking that can change the way you think and reduce pain.
Ultimately, many mental body techniques are used to relieve pain and all of them now benefit from the principle of neuroplasticity.
The growing success of these techniques shows that these can be safe and sustainable long-term strategies to overcome pain and in some cases become pain-free.

Do you dream of trading in your current job with a shiny new job abroad?
You're certainly not the only one.
The COVID-19 pandemic has led many people to rethink their relationship to work, including exactly where they want to stay.
With the exit of strict restrictions and closures related to the epidemic, many workers in Europe and the United States are still considering leaving jobs that do not meet their needs or provide a good work-life balance.
If you ’ re like one in five recently polled respondents by PwC who say they ’ re likely to change employers in the next 12 months, the new salary “calculator ” could be useful.
The tool, created by insurance company William Russell, shows how average salaries vary for different jobs across 38 OECD countries, and the company used data from Glassdoor to find the average salary for each OECD country for 36 different jobs, then converted those salaries into US dollars and British pounds.
Hourly rates have been converted into annual pay based on 37.5 hours worked per week.
How much will you earn as a digital nomad?
Using a calculator, a web developer who wants to be based in Europe can see that they will get more money in Switzerland ($88,496) or Denmark ($70,763), compared to France ($43,757) or the Netherlands ($40,531), in stark contrast to Greece ($13,492) or Portugal ($15,557).
The calculator confirms salaries for a wide range of occupations, including nurses, doctors, graphic designers, and accountants (though data is not available for each job in each country).
Salaries vary widely between countries, but so does the cost of living.
Switzerland and Denmark may pay salaries at the end of the scale, but both countries are among the 10 most expensive countries in terms of cost of living, based on the OECD cost of living index.
Besides calculating salaries a list of the most expensive and least expensive countries is included, based on this indicator.
Switzerland, Iceland, Norway, Israel and Australia are the top 5 countries with the highest cost of living while Turkey, Colombia, Mexico, Poland and Hungary are listed as the most expensive.

Fish deaths threaten livestock.
Environmental Disasters and ‘ Painful ’ Economic Impacts
2022-08-16 | 07: 04
2,499 Views
Report: Alsumaria News
No year or period passes without the announcement of the crisis of fish deaths in the southern provinces, which has an economic, environmental and social impact on all regions of Iraq, in addition to threatening the livelihoods of many Iraqis in light of the difficulty of obtaining a profession at the present time, as fishermen in the areas of the Iraqi marshes never imagined that they will abandon a profession inherited from their parents and grandparents.
Occasionally, Iraqi media and social media platforms have circulated hundreds of videos from many riverine areas of Iraq, showing the death of millions of fish floating on water bodies and inside productive pools in central and southern Iraq.
According to environmental activist Abulhasan al-Masafri, "Lake Razzaza in the province of Karbala has witnessed during the past period large deaths of fish without any government signal and interest in the incident."
He added that "the deaths in the lake occurred because of the low levels of water in it, and the high temperatures that lead to the evaporation of water and high salt concentrations," pointing out that "all these factors made the lake unsuitable environment."
The phenomenon of the death of fish in Iraqi waters, especially the marshes in the south, returns to the forefront from time to time, for reasons attributed by specialists to reckless fishing through the dumping of toxic substances by some fishermen as well as the most prominent reason, which is drought.
A member of the Association of Management of National Fish Lakes in Diyala, Mustafa Khalidi, revealed a comprehensive stop for all fish lakes.
Al-Khalidi said in an interview that "Diyala used to include 30-40 native fish lakes near the main and even sub-river streams, and it depends to a large extent on the permanence of the water, in order to feed them continuously throughout the year."
He added that "all fish lakes have now stopped working because of the severe drought crisis and the decline of water, in addition to the existence of strict instructions to prevent the existence of lakes at the current time because of the limited availability of water."
He pointed out that "the lakes were feeding the markets with more than 100 tons of fish per week," stressing that "only fish breeding cages remain in large rivers, including the Tigris is still engaged in fish production at the moment."
Approximate statistics indicate that the number of people working in these lakes, directly and indirectly, reaches more than 1,500 people, which threatens to stop their livelihoods.
For his part, environmental activist in the province of Dhi Qar, Raad al-Asadi, said that "large quantities of fish have been killed in the Ishaqi River, which is the southernmost of the province of Dhi Qar, which is one of the most prominent rivers that feed the central marshes in Chabaish."
He stressed that "the river is close to the stations that feed the areas of the east and Kassra in the Chabaish and Cheetahs, and therefore the death of fish is the beginning of the spread of diseases dangerous to the environment in the areas it feeds, because of the high salinity."
Two months ago, an official in the Basra Agriculture Directorate, Shaker Abdul Razak, said that 90 percent of the tilapia fish had died.
He explained that the cause of pollution is the dumping of waste in the river, pointing out that the solution for the Directorate is to pump water in the riverbed to remove pollution.
The Basra Agriculture Directorate vowed legal procedures for those who pollute the river.
The director of agriculture of the province Hadi Hussein Qassem, said that "the Directorate formed a working team of the fish department at the moment of receipt of information on mortality."
He added that "the dead fish are considered alien to the visual environment and undesirable to the consumer," explaining that the analysis of the samples showed "the poor quality of water in this river due to the dumping of heavy and sunken water and the waste of shops and some residential neighborhoods, which led to a decrease in the proportion of oxygen in the water."
More than three million people live in the province of Basra, and the population of the province depends on some government stations and more than 200 private civil stations to secure drinking water, and according to them, the water of the province is salty and not suitable for drinking or agriculture.
According to international standards, the salinity of drinking water should not exceed 500 degrees of the standard "TDS", while the salinity in Basra water exceeds the specified number.
The vice president of the Fish Breeders Association in Iraq, Akram al-Mashhadani, says that "more than 75% of fish breeders have abandoned this profession, due to the spread of the virus (Koi herpes) in lakes and rivers, which caused the death of large numbers of these riches with the expansion of the circle of infection and danger as time progresses."
Koi runaway (KHV), a viral disease also known as interstitial nephritis in carp fish or gill necrosis virus, is a killer with an estimated 100% eradication rate among this species of fish.
Since 2008, the fishing profession has flourished after the introduction of carp, through the American Development Organization.
Mashhadani adds that "the virus began to spread in 2018 in the Tigris River and then moved to lakes and river basins, at a time when the production capacity of fish farming was about 900 thousand tons, but it is decreasing by 20% each year since the virus."
He pointed out that with a number of lake owners, they met with officials in the Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation and the General Secretariat of the Council of Ministers, in order to receive government support to eliminate the virus.
“But none of those rounds came up with solutions and we were given the vaccine to the private sector, which is very difficult because it ’ s more than a million dollars in price with few suppliers of such vaccines, ” Mashhadani continued.
On October 26, 2018, a massive fish mortality in Iraq killed millions of cultured carp in the Middle Euphrates region, creating concern in the country.
There was widespread fear that fish deaths were due to mysterious pollution that could also poison people, while fish farmers suffered financial losses due to fish deaths, which affected their livelihoods.
Mashhadani pointed out that "there are other aspects added to the viral disease that affects fish, which is the scarcity of water and the high prices of feed for fish farming."
He calls on the competent authorities to legislate laws concerning fish farming, especially since most of the regulations adopted in Iraq date back to 1972, when fishing was confined to the high seas.
Most of the lakes for fish farming are distributed at the outskirts of the northern capital Baghdad, extending towards the city of Samarra, numbering more than three thousand sites, most of which are not officially licensed.
In turn, says the adviser of the former parliamentary agriculture committee, Adel al-Mukhtar, "fish farming can be classified into four types, the first is fish farming in lakes and river cages and is the most famous and approved by the Ministry of Agriculture."
“This section suffers from the deadly virus, water scarcity, high feed prices and lack of marketing, so it must be eliminated because it puts a great strain on our water reserves and is dangerous for these diseases to spread to the rest of the rivers, ” he added.
He stressed that "the volume of water used by those lakes allocated for fish farming reaches about one billion and a quarter of a billion cubic meters, in light of the futility of the continuation of this profession and the investment of fodder in filling the lack of nutrition for poultry and livestock."
He continued: "This wealth can be compensated through many alternatives at lower cost and more affordable prices for the quantities of water, including the adoption of water bodies such as Tharthar, Habbaniya, Razzazah, marshes and others, which is the second section of fish farming."
The third type is fishing at the Faw marine area in the far south of Iraq, according to the mukhtar, adding that "there are about 1500 boats out of service, each of these boats can return within 10 days by about half a ton of fish."
He pointed out that "most of the fishermen in that region are subjected to humiliation, beatings and arrest by the Iranian authorities, which prevent them from practicing this profession, despite the fact that there is an agreement to regulate fishing in territorial waters."
The fourth type is "located on the high oceans" according to the chosen one.
According to the strategic plan of the Ministry of Agriculture in 2014, the area allocated to fish lakes should not exceed 31 thousand dunums for two decades, but the current area is more than 60 thousand dunums.
At the end of his speech, Mukhtar stressed that "the solution to eliminate the deadly virus, is to stop the breeding of fish of the first type for at least five years."
A few days ago, Undersecretary of the Ministry of Agriculture Mahdi al-Jubouri said in a statement to the official agency that "the rise in fish prices came because of seasonal injuries and also increased demand with the scarcity of the product in some periods, which led to raising prices, in addition to rising prices of vaccines, medicines and feed."
He added that "the budget of the Ministry of Agriculture within the emergency support law for food security will support fish feed, which will reduce the cost of production and reduce prices in the coming days."

The goal is to achieve non-discrimination in positions of leadership and decision-making.
Equality between men and women.
A long road to equality of opportunity
Women and girls represent half of the world ’ s population, and therefore half of its potential.
Gender equality, besides being a fundamental human right, is essential to achieving peace in societies and unlocking society ’ s full potential.
Moreover, the empowerment of women has been shown to stimulate productivity and economic growth, according to the United Nations report and vision.
Unfortunately, there is still a long way to go to achieve full equality of rights and opportunities for men and women, as UN-Women warns.
It is therefore crucial to end multiple forms of gender violence and to ensure equal access to quality education, health, economic resources and political participation for women, girls, men and boys.
Equal access to jobs, leadership and decision-making at all levels was also essential.
Achieving gender equality and empowering women and girls is the unfinished business of our time and the greatest challenge to human rights in our world.
United Nations and women
United Nations support for women's rights began with the international framework enunciated in the Charter of the United Nations.
Among the purposes of the United Nations proclaimed in Article 1 of the Charter of the United Nations is "to achieve international cooperation... to promote and encourage respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms for all without distinction as to sex, language or religion."
In the first year of the United Nations, the Economic and Social Council established the Commission on the Status of Women as the main global policymaking body exclusively concerned with the achievement of gender equality and the advancement of women.
One of its first achievements was to ensure gender-neutral language in the draft Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
Women 's rights
Gender equality became part of international human rights law under the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on 10 December 1948.
That landmark document in the history of human rights recognized that “all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights ” and that“ everyone is entitled to all the rights and freedoms set forth in this Declaration, without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, birth or other status. ”
As the international women's movement began to gain momentum during the 1970s, the General Assembly proclaimed 1975 as the International Women's Year and organized the first World Conference on Women, held in Mexico.
Subsequently, at the invitation of the Conference, it proclaimed the years 1976-1985 as the United Nations Decade for Women and established the Voluntary Fund for the Decade.
In 1979, the General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, often described as the International Bill of Women's Rights.
The Convention, in its 30 articles, explicitly defines discrimination against women and sets out a programme of national action to end such discrimination.
The Convention targets culture and tradition as influential forces in shaping gender roles and family relations, and is the first human rights treaty to affirm women ’ s reproductive rights.
Five years after the Mexico Conference, the Second World Conference on Women was held in Copenhagen in 1980.
The Programme of Action of the Conference called for stronger national measures to ensure women's ownership and control of their property, as well as improvements in women's rights with regard to inheritance, child custody and loss of nationality.
In 1985, the World Conference to Review and Appraise the Achievements of the United Nations Decade for Women: Equality, Development and Peace was held in Nairobi.
The conference came at a time when the movement for gender equality had gained global recognition and 15,000 NGO representatives participated in a parallel NGO forum.
The Nairobi Forward-looking Strategies 2000 were adopted by 157 participating Governments.
This paved the way for the Conference to publicize all issues as women's issues.
Beijing Conference on Women
The Fourth World Conference on Women, held in Beijing in 1995, went a step further than the Nairobi Conference.
The Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action affirmed women's rights as human rights and committed to specific actions to ensure respect for those rights.
Commission on the Status of Women
The Commission on the Status of Women is a major intergovernmental body dedicated exclusively to the promotion of gender equality and the empowerment of women.
The Commission on the Status of Women plays a key role in promoting women's rights, documenting the realities of women's lives around the world and shaping global norms in gender equality and women's empowerment.
Women 's Organization
On 2 July 2010, the United Nations General Assembly unanimously established a single United Nations body mandated to accelerate progress in achieving gender equality and the empowerment of women.
The new United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN-Women) integrates four international agencies and offices: the United Nations Development Fund for Women (UNIFEM), the Division for the Advancement of Women, the Office of the Special Adviser on Gender Issues and the International Research and Training Institute for the Advancement of Women (INSTRAW).
Equality and empowerment
The United Nations is now focusing on its recently developed global development agenda, which is made up of 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
Women play a critical role in each of these goals, with many of these goals specifically recognizing the issue of women ’ s equality and empowerment both in the goal, and also as part of the solution.
Goal 5, “Achieve gender equality and empower women and girls ” is known as the stand-alone goal, because it is dedicated to achieving these goals.
To ensure women ’ s rights around the world, profound legal and legislative changes are needed.
While 143 countries guaranteed equality between men and women in their constitutions by 2014, 52 have yet to do so.
Glaring gender disparities persist in the economic and political spheres.
While some progress has been made over the decades, women still earn 20 percent less than men in the labor market globally.
As of 2021, only 25 percent of all national parliamentarians are female, a slow rise from 11.3 percent in 1995.
Elimination of violence against women
The United Nations system continues to pay special attention to the issue of violence against women.
The 1993 General Assembly Declaration on the Elimination of Violence against Women set out “a clear and comprehensive definition of violence against women and a clear statement of the rights that should be applied to ensure the elimination of violence against women in all its forms ” and represented“ a commitment by States to shoulder their responsibilities and by the international community as a whole to strive to eliminate violence against women. ”

CAIRO (Reuters) - CNN reported on Tuesday that an increasing number of American citizens have moved their residence to Mexico due to high prices in the United States, which has a positive impact on some but a negative impact on others of the local population.

According to State Department data, 1.6 million Americans live in Mexico officially, while the number of Americans who received tourist visas between January and May this year, regardless of whether they left or not, reached 5.3 million.
That is one million more than the number recorded during the same period in 2019, according to the Mexican government.
Mexico City real estate broker Adita Noriko told CNN she receives dozens of calls from U.S. clients every week to inquire about moving to Mexico City.
Most of them live mainly in New York and Los Angeles, she said, adding that most of them escape the cost of living by taking advantage of the currency difference.
According to Noriko, 70% of her customers are American.
According to the US Department of Tourism, tourism revenue from American travelers in the first five months of 2022 reached $11.5 billion, close to that achieved before the pandemic.
In neighborhoods such as Rome and Condesa, the city center has many contemporary restaurants and cafes aimed at English speakers.
Mexican citizen Bustos Corosby says foreigners do not seek to speak Spanish and wait for locals to learn English for them, making many citizens angry.
In one of those neighborhoods, someone hung a sign in English that said, "Please leave, we don't want you here."
But the most powerful reason for this anger is that many landlords have become motivated to expel local tenants and shop owners so that they can renovate their buildings and convert them into apartments in line with the demand of these foreigners or because they can no longer pay the rent, which has increased due to the greater purchasing power of these American expatriates.
One of the victims is 54-year-old Sandra Ortiz, who lost her restaurant, along with her four siblings, which her parents founded 55 years ago as a bakery, after the owner of the property, consisting of a ground floor and four floors in the neighborhood of Rome, fired her in February after a long legal battle.
She and two of her sisters now work as dishwashers in a suburb of the Mexican capital.

Although he is not sure he wants to stay in Mexico in the long term, he is starting to feel like home.

Women break into construction sector to fill labour shortages
Bloomberg: The number of construction workers in the United States exceeded 1 million in May last year, for the first time since data collection began in 1964, and the share of women among workers in the sector reached its highest level at 14.1 percent last month.
About a third of construction workers in the United States are Hispanic, according to BLS.
Cerato herself got to know the industry at an early age through her Mexican immigrant father, saying, “I used to go out to work with him, and I never saw anyone like me, so it never occurred to me that it could be a viable career path. ”
The presence of another Latina as a mentor made a big difference, she said, adding: “That ’ s why our representation is important. ”
One of the women is Andy Dirkschneider, who negotiates millions of dollars in loans to buy land for her family ’ s homebuilder, but sometimes vendors call her “petite ” and ask to speak to the man in charge.
Dirkschneider, 32, who heads Brookline Homes in Charlotte, said: “I tell them I ’ m the man in charge.
A young blonde girl doing this job confuses everyone.
It ’ s frustrating, but it can ’ t be allowed to. ”
Dirkschneider and thousands of women like her are breaking through the walls of the professions.
It is not brittle, it is concrete.
The field of construction has always been a world for men, from handicrafts such as construction and carpentry to the offices of developers and executive companies.
The accelerating wave of retirement of the 1960s and 1970s generation has exacerbated the industry ’ s chronic labor shortage.
Construction jobs totaled 440,000 in April, the highest in Bureau of Labor Statistics records that began in 2001.
Aryan Higuish, a senior researcher and fellow at the Women ’ s Policy Research Institute, said there is room for growth, because the construction sector ’ s historical dependence on men now risks constraining its growth.
The institute estimates that about a third of women in the industry work in deals, and their share across sectors such as painting and carpentry is still as small as a tenth, though Higuish believes it will continue to grow.
This is partly because of the need for labor and because states and local administrations want to see more diversity in companies when they are awarded contracts.
Patrice Haley, of the diversity leadership team at construction giant DPR, said: “In this industry, we can ’ t dismiss people on the basis of gender.
“A lot of veterans are retiring, and we can ’ t leave any of the doors closed. ”
One of the temptations for women in the industry, Haley said, was to see what they were building right in front of their eyes, and she had started working in the industry in a manual job that required wearing a helmet and toe boots.
She said, "I can say I worked on this and built that."
There ’ s also the temptation to pay better than many other jobs that don ’ t require a college degree: In 2021, the average salary of an electrician was $59,000 and $98,500 for a construction manager, according to U.S. Department of Labor data.
Taqiya Wallace, 35, works for a large energy company in tracking construction project documents.
But she dreams of getting a license as a general contractor to start working on her own.
In June, I began studying building skills in a 16-week curriculum organized by Goodwill Industries in South Piedmont, Charlotte, where I learned to read blueprints and handle equipment.
If all goes according to plan, she will finish training with four industry certifications.
Although Goodwill does not target women, its organizers say a group of 15 people who completed training last year were all women, about half of whom went on to work in industry jobs.
Wallace, who was the first to receive a college degree in her family, sees getting a contractor ’ s license and hanging a sign for her company as a way to build the wealth she can bequeath to her family.
She said, “I want to be able to tell them this is our legacy. ”
Harassment and discrimination
Despite these encouraging trends, the sector still has a long way to go.
About a quarter of respondents to a survey of 2,635 workers conducted by the Women ’ s Policy Research Institute last year said they had experienced sexual harassment or repeated harassment on the basis of sex.
Half of those surveyed said that their lack of equal treatment by men was frequent or persistent.
Jenny Parker stood at a construction site in High Point, North Carolina, on a very hot day in July, grabbing a paper cup with an iced drink as she looked at her sawdust, paint and sweat stained shirt and said, "I love this.
It took me 10 years to get here. ”
Parker, who spent nine years in the Marine Corps, was upset by the managerial jobs she worked so she could pay her bills while raising her daughter, so she started working hard in real estate.
She signed up for training in building skills so she could repair the rental housing she owned.
At High Point, Parker received hands-on training in building house structures, performing stone work, and installing roofs.
She said she was able to work in partnership with the men on the team, but there were tensions at times, adding: “To be female in a male environment you have to prove yourself and work twice as hard, ” noting that some men do not accept instructions from a woman.
She said, “It ’ s a mindset that men should overcome. ”
Nicole Goulsby, owner of Red Ladder Residential, a construction company in Raleigh, North Carolina, recalls that when she started running worksites, some men ignored her when she addressed them.
She said her experience of bias faded when she distributed her signed paychecks, and she now notes that there are more women on the crews she contracts, whether they ride boards or paint.
Golsby explained that women build relationships easily and are more attentive to details, making them suitable for her field of work.
Nicknamed “Becky Nicky, ” Golsby said,“ I see things that no one else sees, and that ’ s why I do my job well. ”
The construction industry is also attracting more minority women.
An analysis by the Women ’ s Policy Research Institute found that the number of female construction apprentices between 2016 and 2019 nearly doubled, while Latinas recorded the largest increase of any race.
If we look at Ferridiana Cerato who graduated from college in 2020 with a double major in history and Spanish without being able to find any job that would enable her to benefit from her education well, she decided to try construction management.
Cerato took courses and received some certificates, including a certificate in welding.
She is now a project engineer in Indianapolis.
The job requires toughness, the 24-year-old says, with a lot of conversational “that doesn ’ t conform to HR rules ” and dealing with cynicism at times.
Cerato is one of three women in a team of nine managers and the only Latina among them.

The cardiovascular system is an important part of the body and one of the essential elements of fitness and overall health.
The reason for this is the need to pump oxygen throughout the body to vital organs including those that make up the concerned cardiovascular system such as the lungs and heart.
Moreover, the more oxygen that can be pumped into the body ’ s control center, the brain, the healthier the organ will be in the long run.
Exercise is part of a range of tools available to someone to help improve cardiovascular health.
According to a 2015 study, frequent sauna use was associated with a lower risk of a fatal heart attack.
Moreover, a subsequent study in 2018 found that bathing in a sauna three to seven times a week can reduce the likelihood of fatal cardiovascular events.
A new study, published this time in the American Journal of Physiology by the University of Jyväskylä in Finland, compared the effect of sauna bathing with exercise and exercise alone.
For research purposes, the study recruited 48 men and women between the ages of 30 and 64, each with at least one risk factor for cardiovascular disease such as obesity, smoking, or a related cardiovascular condition such as high cholesterol and high blood pressure.
After completing the study, it was found that the group that combined exercise and sauna bathing had a higher degree of cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), one that was measured by maximum oxygen absorption.
Moreover, this group also experienced lower blood pressure and lower cholesterol levels compared to the other two groups.
Lead author of the study, Errik Lee, said: “What we know from the literature is that the post-workout period is what ’ s known as the ‘ window of opportunity ’, where there is improved insulin sensitivity and diminished blood lipid levels (below 60-90 minutes).
This presents itself as an ideal opportunity for paired interventions such as heat therapy and, in this case, sauna bathing.
In addition, during the post-exercise period, vasogenesis factors rise and therefore changing blood flow or oxygen delivery after exercise can have an additional or synergistic effect on the vasogenesis signals generated by exercise alone, although this has not yet been demonstrated experimentally in humans.
What this means is that sauna bathing used the post-workout period to act as a cure for the heart.
Meanwhile, Professor Christopher Minson of the University of Oregon added, “Some of these changes are likely to be manifested by a greater response to heat shock protein (HSP) in the [exercise and sauna group] versus the exercise group alone.
HSPs are known to have many beneficial effects on blood vessel health, endothelial function, and heart function when regulated. ”

Replacing animal fats with unsaturated vegetable fats reduces the risk of dying from heart disease by 24-26 percent.
She adds, avocados also contain silicon, boron and nickel elements, which help improve metabolism.
She says, “Avocado is distinguished in that, in addition to unsaturated fatty acids, it contains natural antioxidants, vitamins and dietary fiber.
Together, these substances help to absorb each other and enhance their positive effect in the body. ”
She points out, that there are no contraindications to eating avocados, except for individual sensitization of the fruit.

While the Middle East was looking to Western governments where young people assume leadership positions and their energies explode in order to elevate their homelands, no one expected to see a similar experience in our Arab countries soon, before circumstances gave us a chance to see the experience of Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Wednesday turned 37, the youngest crown prince in Saudi Arabia ’ s history.
On April 29, 2015, the royal order was issued to choose Prince Mohammed bin Salman as crown prince, amid a state of regional and international surprise at the unprecedented and “previous ” step, and amid anticipation of what this young man might do, the question was:“ Is he qualified to carry out the duties of this heavy position in such a great country? ”
The obvious truth is that Prince Mohammed bin Salman did more than this question and answer it, but it was an answer to a question that did not occur to him, a question about the revolution to change the face of the Kingdom and lead it towards the future.
How did the young prince change the face of the kingdom?
Prince Mohammed bin Salman has shown since his tenure the Kingdom ’ s era an open mentality that flushed the dust of reactionary and extremist thought about the Kingdom, a task that was not imagined that anyone would dare, the challenge of the common mistake is the task of misery, where he will not forgive you your sanity and will not protect you from doubt and denigrating, but the steadfast leader does not turn and go his way for the sake of his people.
Prince Mohammed bin Salman made history when his reign saw Saudi women allowed to drive and enter sports stadiums and then established the Entertainment Authority.
His views have always been clear in categorical terms, when he described “religious extremism ” as an outsider in Saudi society, and that there is no place to waste women ’ s rights according to misconceptions about Islam, as the kingdom under King Salman bin Abdulaziz abolished the guardianship system for women in 2016.
Prince Mohammed bin Salman told The Atlantic: “Before 1979 there were more flexible social customs, and there were no guardianship laws in Saudi Arabia. ”
He refers to a series of disparate pieces of legislation that have not taken the status of law since the late 1970s that have limited the rights of Saudi women as minors in need of a guardian.
Bin Salman was aware of a real understanding of the change he is leading, aware of the challenge and aware of the essence of Islam, where he described those who oppose the project of “Islamic awakening ” and the mixing of the sexes in work as“ extremism, ” saying: “These extremists are contrary to what the Prophet and the adult caliphs were like, ” and hinted at the imminence of allowing Saudi women not to wear the“ black cloak. ” It is a legal text that requires the abaya to be black or the veil to be black. ”

The launch of the "Macatna" project to valorize the Tunisian food heritage in four pilot areas
The project "Our Food Heritage" was launched today in four pilot areas in Zaghouan, Mahdia, Tozeur and Tobruka-Ain Drahm, with the support of the German Technical Cooperation Program and the European Union.
The six-month Maklatna project aims to promote Tunisia ’ s food heritage as part of the development of sustainable tourism, diversification and enrichment of the Tunisian tourism product, as well as boosting the Tunisian tourism sector.
The project targets about 80 beneficiaries working in tourism units, rural residences, guest houses and tourist restaurants who will receive theoretical and practical training courses.
The “Maklatna ” project will culminate in the organization of a tourist promotional event on March 18, 2023, during the presentation of the most important products of Tunisian food heritage in the four regions.
Zuhair Samoud, director of the studies office, which is implementing the project, told Watt that the selection of the four bodies was based on balance, taking into account the specificity of each region.
In this regard, he pointed out that the particularities of desert tourism (Tozeur), beach tourism (Mahdia) and forest and mountain tourism (Zaghouan and Tabarka Ain Darham) were taken into account.
He stressed the importance of betting on alternative tourism as an area capable of providing added tourism value to Tunisia, especially in terms of diversifying tourism supply.
Samoud said that the project will contribute to bringing together professionals to work in a participatory comparison aimed at promoting the Tunisian food heritage.
The project will also have positive results on the tourism sector as a whole through the possibility of attracting a new category of foreign tourists wishing to search different food habits and traditions.
For his part, the Director of Alternative Tourism at the German Technical Cooperation Agency, José Fröling, revealed to Watt that a sum of 19 million euros has been identified for alternative tourism projects in Tunisia distributed over four axes during the period 2019 / 2024.
He considered that the development of the Tunisian food heritage is part of a new tourism dynamic in Tunisia to diversify the tourism product, saying that another project will be announced soon is the food heritage tracts in Tunisia within the framework of the promotion of the alternative tourism sector.
On the other hand, he explained that the food heritage and its richness can be a crucial element for taking the decision to travel to a particular country, pointing out that Tunisia has the potential and energies in this area.
Fritz Jung, in charge of economic cooperation and development at the German embassy in Tunis, said Tunisia has an important food heritage that can be used as an element to promote Tunisian tourism and diversify the country's tourism offer.

UAE allows virtual work residence permit
Thank you for following the news of the UAE allows to obtain a virtual work residence permit on the site Gulf Dot and now with full details
Bassam Mohammed - Abu Dhabi on Monday 12 September 2022 04: 53 PM - Follow - Nagham Hassan
The UAE made it possible to obtain a virtual work residence permit, the first of its kind in the region.
Under this permit, a foreigner can enter the country on his personal sponsorship and stay there for one year and practice his virtual job in accordance with the conditions and regulations issued with the visa.
The program benefits foreign individuals, professionals from outside the country, entrepreneurs, start-ups and SMEs, who meet the criteria for joining the program.
If the application is approved, the beneficiary can bring his / her family to stay on the basis of an application submitted to the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs in Dubai.
The applicant is required to hold a passport valid for at least 6 months, with valid health insurance covering the entire duration of their stay in Dubai.
If you are an employee, you must provide proof of employment with your current employer, a one-year employment contract, a certificate of last salary of at least $5,000 per month, and a bank statement for the last three months.
If you are an owner of the company (employer) you must also provide proof of ownership of the company for one year or more, proof of a monthly income of at least $5,000, and a bank statement for the last three months.
The annual program costs US $287, plus health insurance valid in the UAE, and an application fee per person.
This program allows people to use all services related to residence and work in Dubai, including, for example, telecommunications, opening bank accounts, education and others.

The UAE government has announced a new step for all expatriates wishing to enter the country, namely the issuance of a virtual work residence permit, which is the first permit that is allowed to be issued. This allows a foreigner to enter the country without a sponsor on his personal sponsorship, in addition to staying on the UAE territory for a full year. Virtual work in the UAE.
Virtual Work Residence Permit in UAE
A new paragraph has been announced within the Executive Regulations of the Law of Entry and Residence of Foreigners, to be implemented as of October 1, which will grant any foreigner to stay in the UAE territory for a year in which he guarantees himself throughout that period.
According to the regulation issued by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security, this permit will grant the foreigner a full residence permit for virtual work without a guarantor or as he is called (host) for a period of one year, in which renewal is allowed, if he practices work outside the country remotely.
The foreign worker can use all the services available while living and working in the UAE, in addition to obtaining many privileges such as opening bank accounts, education, and the possibility to practice normal life in the city, which hosts more than 200 nationalities.
Conditions for obtaining a virtual work residence permit in the UAE
The Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security has announced the need to meet some conditions so that a foreign worker can obtain a permit in the UAE, such as:
• Submit an application for the permit proving that he works for an entity outside the UAE.
• Provide a certificate of the last salary received that is at least USD 5,000 per month, or its equivalent in other foreign currencies.
• Submit a bank statement for the last three months prior to the application.
• If the applicant is the owner of a company must provide proof of ownership of the company for a year or more.
• If the applicant is a worker, proof of employment must be submitted to the current employer, in addition to providing a valid employment contract for one year.
How to Apply for a Virtual Work Residence Permit in the UAE
Immediately after the announcement of the possibility of obtaining a virtual work residence permit in the UAE, and its advantages that obviate the need for the sponsor, the questions about how to apply for a virtual work residence visa increased.
You will go directly to the website of the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Security of the official outlets.
The first three steps are to add the name in Arabic and English as in the passport, and the applicant ’ s data, namely:
The first step is to
• Add mobile number.

• The department from which the visa is to be issued.
• Then add all personal information of the beneficiary, such as previous nationality, current nationality, employer, monthly income in dollars, gender, date of birth, country of birth.
• Then add the city of birth in Arabic, passport number, passport type, place of issuance of travel document in Arabic and English.
• Country of issue, date of issue, date of expiry, religion and denomination.
• Enter the mother ’ s name in Arabic and English, the reason for the visit, and e-mail.
• Then add the address inside and outside the entry in detail.
• Step 2: Attach documents and papers.
• Step 3: - Review the application after completing the verification step.
• Thus, you have completed the steps of issuing a virtual work residence visa in the UAE.
UAE Virtual Work Residence Permit Fees
• In principle, the work permit can be renewed again, provided that the application is applied again, while the fee for the virtual work residence permit in the UAE for one year is estimated at 287 USD, in addition to the health insurance valid in the UAE, and the application fee is also added for each person.

Survey: Saudi youth are optimistic about the future, driven by Vision 2030
Almost half (43%) of young people in the Kingdom say they prefer to work in the private sector while a third (34%) tend to work in government jobs
Posted in: Last Updated:
As Saudi Arabia prepares to celebrate its 92nd National Day, on September 23, under the slogan “We Have a Home, ” a high percentage of young Saudis have expressed confidence that the Kingdom is moving in the right direction and that their days ahead are better.
This was one of the findings of the 14th annual ASDA ’ A BCW Arab Youth Survey, the most comprehensive survey of its kind for the Arab world ’ s largest population of more than 200 million young men and women.
ASDA ’ A BCW, a PR consultancy, in collaboration with ADS Research and Consulting, conducted 3,400 interviews with young Arabs aged 18-24 in 50 cities across 17 Arab countries from May 13 to June 16.
The sample of participants was evenly distributed between the sexes.
In Saudi Arabia, almost all young people surveyed (99%) expressed confidence that Vision 2030 will ensure a strong economy for the Kingdom, and a similar percentage (97%) believe their next days are better.
Ninety-seven percent of young Saudis also believe the kingdom ’ s economy is heading in the right direction, while nine in ten respondents believe they will have a better life than their parents.
98% of young Saudi men and women believe that their leadership cares about their views and that their government has the right policies to address their problems such as quality education, job creation and economic growth.
Mile for the private sector
Recent government reforms to the private sector are very popular among Saudi youth, with 96% of them saying they support measures that stimulate private sector participation in the national economy.
93% of respondents said they strongly support reforms that encourage citizens to play a greater role in the business sector.
More young Saudi men and women today say they prefer business over government jobs (43% vs. 34%), while a quarter (23%) say they prefer to work independently or with their families.
Women in the labour market
In the face of Western stereotypes about Saudi Arabia, more than two-thirds of young Saudis (68%) say men and women have equal rights, and 61% say they also have equal employment opportunities.
96% believe that a greater presence of women in the labor market will benefit the Kingdom.
Social Media Generation
Young Saudis are among the most prominent users of social media.
According to the survey, their most popular platforms are WhatsApp (98%), Snapchat (84%), YouTube (83%), Twitter (73%), TikTok (60%) and Facebook (55%).
TikTok usage has nearly tripled over the past three years, from 24% of young Saudis who said they use it daily in 2020 to 60% today.
Snapchat, Instagram and Twitter have also risen in popularity, while Facebook ’ s daily usage rate has dropped from 82% in 2020 to 55% currently, according to the survey.
Rapid growth in online shopping
The number of Saudis who shop online has doubled over the past five years, according to the survey, from 58% who said they buy products and services via websites and social media at least once a month in 2018, to almost all respondents who said they currently shop online.
The most purchased products and services online included clothing (69%), cosmetics / personal care products (33%), food (31%), electronic devices (22%), and groceries (17%).
Arab youth at a crossroads
The results of the 14th annual ASDA ’ A BCW Arab Youth Survey are grouped under six main themes: my identity, livelihoods, attitudes, global citizenship, lifestyle and future aspirations.
Its findings revealed a generation trying to start a new era, at a crossroads between preserving its values and culture and embracing new modern values.
Commenting on the survey findings, Sunil John, president of BCW MENA and founder of ASDA ’ A BCW, said: “The survey provided more important insights into the ideas of young Arab men and women across the region and the problems that decision makers need to address to ensure that their potential is maximized. ”
John added: “We at ASDA ’ A BCW believe that to better understand the Arab world, we must first understand the feelings and thoughts of the Arab youth who make up the largest segment of the Arab population.
This year ’ s survey shows a generation of young Arab men and women who want to start a new era away from the divisions of the past. ”
“The survey results in Saudi Arabia are very promising, indicating that young Saudis, both men and women, are fully aligned with the country ’ s reform agenda and optimistic about their future. ”
