Parents ’ guide to their children ’ s interaction with TikTok
Did your child ever come back from school and immediately grab your phone (or his phone!)
Browsing TikTok immediately?
Did you warn him more than once to turn off those annoying clips while he was eating at the table?
Did you walk into his room expecting to find him asleep, but you saw him lying on the bed, the radiant phone light on his face, and when you asked him why he was up late, he told you he was surfing TikTok?
Maybe dear parent, whether you are a mother or a mother, you personally love TikTok, an application that is really fun and entertaining and new, but you know that it absorbs your time and attention and focus and your whole day, or that you do not know it at all, but you have fears because you do not know something that obsesses your child in this way and do not know what to do.
In this guide, take your hand in the corridors of this application, introduce you to what is happening inside, and the most appropriate ways to protect your child from it based on the advice and recommendations of psychologists.
How did TikTok start?
Launched at the beginning of 2016 as "Musical" in China, then acquired by the company "Byte Dance Technology" Chinese at the end of 2017 and named TikTok, and within a short time spread the application spread wildfire, exceeding the number of download billion on Android devices, and is about to complete the billion also on the Apple Store.
According to statistics, its users watch about a billion videos every day.
It is one of the most widespread and influential applications for the younger generation that has abandoned Facebook and Twitter and found in TikTok a space for creative play and communication and a mix of dance, quick information and visually entertaining tales.
In China, 80% of TikTok users are teenagers, and in the United States, 30% of all users are under the age of 19 (1) (2).
How does it work?
TikTok is a very simple application, whether as a viewer or a content maker; once you open you find a page called "For You Page" (or "For You"), which is similar on TikTok Timeline on Facebook, Instagram and Twitter applications, but shows random clips that the user does not follow its publishers.
The app ’ s algorithm studies the user ’ s preferences and displays a different variation on this page. If the user interacts by liking, commenting, sharing, or even watching a full clip, the TikTok algorithm takes notes and continues to display similar clips.
The app is designed in a way that allows the user to scroll up to view more videos constantly, and no matter how fast you browse, there ’ s never an end to that page, and there ’ s no room for duplicate content either.
What is the content of the clips?
In general, TikTok is also filled with information about almost everything, similar to YouTube but faster and lighter.
One of the disadvantages of TikTok is the instability of the terms of use, although it is a platform that targets and attracts young people mainly, applies its terms very randomly, may prohibit sexual content scientifically, but does not block the appearance of pure pornographic clips; which is dangerous for the child who controls the algorithm what he sees.
At first, the app limited users to recording a clip of no more than three minutes, then extended it to 10 minutes.
The content of TikTok is hugely diverse, and its interruptions are overwhelming in an incalculable way, but most of the content is limited to several categories: dance clips, usually short and simple dances to popular or popular songs, sometimes involving reserved movements adapted from famous movies or written by a TikTok user, and sometimes its source remains unknown.
Lip sync clips, where TikTok is the most popular content because it is prepared easily and without the need for any innovation, as the user repeats a few sentences from a song or from famous movies or TV shows in a comedic way.
Memes are also spread on the app, which are short and quick phrases placed in the text at the top of the clip or a video that explains a particular situation sarcastically.
TikTok features a feature called duet – later added by Instagram – in which the user paired his clip with another clip via the stitch option, which is a new clip or has already been posted on the app.
The use of this feature varies, the user may silently show his reactions to the original clip, may sing, may add a comment.
There are also challenges, but they are not a specific type, or specific content, but there are challenges that everyone tries to create their own version of, whether it is a dance or a specific idea such as the idea of ​ ​ the Arabian night, which has spread overwhelmingly in the past months.
Why did TikTok get so popular in such a short time?
To help your child resist the ubiquitous application, we need to understand the psychology based on it.
In general, companies based on social media platforms build immersive communities, the goal of which is to attract the attention of the user for as long as possible, and away from conspiracy theories, but “you are the product if you do not pay to buy the product offered, ” nothing is free, user focus is the commodity that competes for access to social media.
As a result of the long periods spent on these platforms, companies daily gain deeper insights and detailed knowledge of their users ’ personalities and psychology, and then use them for more precise targeting.

What are the potential risks of using TikTok?
• Poor concentration of the child:
It ’ s not just TikTok that weakens a child ’ s concentration, but it ’ s the most dangerous because they rely mainly on extremely short clips, perhaps watching 50 clips in less than 10 minutes, and end up not remembering one of them.
Also, if the child has shared clips of it, his or her focus will be on tracking the views and likes he or she gets.
Creating Healthy Habits:
If strict rules are not established for the use of electronic devices, the child may cling to the phone even at the table without any respect or pay attention to her etiquette, also, which is the biggest problem, will not feel hunger.
The child drowns in the application to a degree that the world around him forgets, as the brain sends signals to the body to alert him that he is hungry, but if the child is busy with something fun and attention-grabbing in this way, he will not notice his hunger in the first place, and this may lead to many other medical problems.
• Low or no interaction with the family:
These devices and apps consume a child ’ s energy, making them unable or unwilling to talk to their surroundings or even their parents.
A child may agree, and even like, to have their parents participate in a lot of activities before they discover TikTok, but after falling into this trap all they will want is your consent to watch TikTok non-stop.
Even on the weekend, instead of playing, you ’ ll see your child sitting very attentively in his room all the time with the phone in his hand.
He changed his view of himself:
Spending too much time with friends online rather than living in reality can isolate the child from the outside world, and this is very damaging to him, because at this stage his consciousness is formed about himself and everything around him.
There are also some clips on TikTok of children who are very beautiful or have unique talents that may lead the child to question his abilities and shape.
According to a report by the American Society of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgeons (ASPS) in 2020, nearly half a million plastic surgeries were performed on adolescents aged 13 to 19.
• Being bullied, harassed or tolerated:
TikTok, like many platforms, is always on the table, but the idea that the policies of TikTok make it easy and quick to spread, it is very easy to create fake accounts without real name, pictures or even posts, and since most clips do not exceed the minute, it is easy for any bully to watch a large amount of content and ridicule them in a short time.
Some content is actually provocative in order to attract more commentators and increase the percentage of its appearance on the TikTok homepage, a young child may feel after reading these comments that it is normal to ridicule everything that we disagree with, whether in its form, manner of speech or ideas.
If a child posts content that he or she makes himself or herself, it is possible to be harassed or harassed, as it has been noted that some users target the content of children mainly.
• False or misleading information:
Information is spread from various people on TikTok, specialists and non-specialists or even the prosecutor of jurisdiction.
There are no clear policies that point to the misinformation that spreads on the application, there are a lot of clips that show people who have gained fame in one way or another and then began to provide psychological advice that is not based on research or opinions from experts, based only on the experience of the famous life.
What can I do to protect my child from TikTok damage?
• First: Prohibit children under 15 years of age
Difficult, I know.
As soon as the child sees his peers talking about him, he will want to participate in it immediately.
The problem is not only that his concentration will weaken at a formative and pivotal stage in his life, but the danger is that your child may watch content that does not suit his age at all, even in its simplest form there are semi-pornographic dances, not to mention clips that are full of vulgar words, and songs of a sexual nature that do not suit children at all. On songs that the child likes, or certain hashtags (hashtags) added by everyone in order to increase the rate of arrival.
Therefore, it is better to prevent the child from using it and replace it with a different activity.
Also, because the design is designed in a way that literally endless flipping without repeating the content, the fear stems from absorbing the child ’ s concentration for long hours without feeling it (3).
Second, protect their privacy.
What if we can't stop him?
It 's okay, you just have to focus with him and adjust the settings of the application to protect your child, first we turn the account from visible to everyone to a personal account, when you first create an account on TikTok that is public and open to everyone, means that anyone can access your child' s account and view and comment on it, and also the possibility of his content appearing in the "for you" page, and also send messages to him.
So, first, change the account settings from public to private, not only to protect its content, but also so that the account does not appear in the case of search by strangers, and also to avoid any unwanted followers, because in the case of private accounts the user has to approve or reject follow-up requests.
You should also check the validity of the year of birth that your child enters in the application, because it restricts certain features depending on age, for example, as part of its policy to prevent publication for those under 15 years of age.
• Third: Reduce the time of use
Controlling the time of use will prevent potential addiction, it may be difficult to prevent it directly from using it, but you can reduce it gradually daily until you reach a reasonable time, preferably not before bedtime.

His discussion will open you calmly and take his opinion on the decision to approach a step into the world of your daughter or son, the desire to share this world and not limit it.
By linking your account to his account you will be able to do all the past through you and not through his account, and there are no secret codes, but you will be able to convert his account to a private account, limit the follow-up suggestions that appear to him, prevent the arrival of any messages except from friends, and also control who can see his content or comment on it.
First you have to download the app and create an account on TikTok, open the profile shown in the previous photos, press the three lines until you reach Settings and Privacy, scroll down until you reach “Family Pairing ” if the app is English, and follow the instructions in the photos until you reach the QR code, then you will be able to adjust all your child ’ s account settings as you like., including the time of use of the application and limiting the access of content to others and privacy settings.
Your child can cancel this link, but the app will notify you and give you 48 hours before you cancel it with all the settings you ’ ve set, so discussing it with your child is essential to continue to protect your child and to maintain understanding between you (3) (4).

Study warns of “keto diet ”: heart disease and strokes

A study has warned that following the keto diet may increase the risk of heart disease and other deadly cardiovascular diseases.
This comes at a time when the diet has become low-carb in recent years, and is widely applied among those wishing to lose weight.
Canadian researchers, tracking 1,500 people for more than a decade, have found that the keto diet may raise levels of “bad ” cholesterol.
The results showed that people who followed a high-fat, low-carb diet were more likely to develop cardiovascular diseases, such as clogged arteries, heart attacks and strokes, than their peers.
The research team attributes the cause to high levels of bad cholesterol that cause fatty deposits to build up in the artery walls, which can lead to narrowing or blockage, according to the Daily Mail.
Dr Yulia Iatan, a doctor at the University of British Columbia ’ s Center for Heart and Lung Innovation, who led the study, said: “Among participants on a low-calorie, high-fat diet (similar to the keto diet), we found that those with the highest LDL cholesterol levels were the most at risk for cardiovascular disease.
“Our findings suggest that people considering a keto diet should be aware that doing so may lead to increased levels of LDL cholesterol.

Those wishing to follow this diet are advised to consult a doctor.
While dieting, it is recommended to monitor their cholesterol levels, and they should try to address other risk factors for heart disease or stroke, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, lack of physical activity and smoking.
But one of the main limitations of the 12-year study was that participants were asked about their diets only once.
There was no way to verify whether they had adhered to the same diet throughout those years.
The study, led by researchers from the University of British Columbia, was based on data from 70,687 people in the Kingdom ’ s Biobank database who had data on their daily caloric intake and cholesterol levels taken once, including 305 participants who followed a keto diet.
The system included getting more than 45 percent of daily calories from fat and less than a quarter from carbohydrates, matching them with 1,220 people whose diets didn ’ t match the system.
About three-quarters of the female participants, with an average age of 54, were overweight.
Taking into account factors such as diabetes, high blood pressure, smoking and obesity.

Risk of heart attacks and strokes
During the study, about 9.8 percent of people in the keto diet group had a serious heart problem, which included heart attacks, strokes, and an artery blockage that needed a stent procedure.
In contrast, only 3 percent of people who ate the standard diet, 4, experienced serious heart events during the same period.
The researchers also found higher levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol — or bad cholesterol — and polypoprotein B, a protein that helps carry fat and cholesterol through the body in the keto group.
The study was presented at the American College of Cardiology ’ s annual scientific session alongside the World Cardiology Congress in New Orleans, USA, on Sunday.
Bad cholesterol in the body
The body naturally produces “bad ” cholesterol, or low-density lipoprotein, but eating diets rich in saturated and trans fats causes the body to produce more low-density lipoprotein.
Harmful cholesterol contributes to the accumulation of inflamed fatty deposits known as plaques in the arteries, which increases the risk of a heart attack or stroke.
The other type of cholesterol — high-density lipoprotein — absorbs cholesterol in the arteries and returns it to the liver, then expels it from the body.
That ’ s why I call it “good ” cholesterol.
The keto diet involves getting 60 to 80 percent of your daily calories from fat, including cheese, avocado and fatty fish, and 20 to 30 percent from protein.
Followers try to consume as little carbs as possible, which means less bread, rice and potatoes, among other sources.
Carbohydrates are the main source of energy used by the body when exercising or moving on a daily basis, and their lack pushes the body to a state called “ketosis ” where it begins to break down fat for energy.
The idea is to take advantage of stubborn fat stores, accelerate weight loss and help with mental clarity, but there are conflicting results about how effective this is.

A new step by bin Salman to “change identity ”?
Is Saudi Arabia moving towards more identity modernization?
A new project in the capital Riyadh mimics the shape of the Kaaba, in a context that is witnessing a shift from the Saudi leadership towards easing the historical and religious dimension.
The giant cube in the middle of the new square project has nothing to do with the Kaaba in Mecca, although there is a similarity in the geometry.
A huge project announced by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman under the name of "Square Project" in the capital Riyadh, with a width, height and length of 400 meters, which will be in the center of Riyadh, with the aim of developing the largest "Downtown", where the Saudi leadership plans to be the largest city center in the world.
The project includes "an innovative museum, a university specializing in technology and design, a multi-use theater and areas for live and entertainment shows," the Saudi Press Agency announced a few days ago, and is scheduled to be completed in 2030.
The project resembles the Kaaba in its geometric form, which has left a great controversy on social media sites.
Bruno Schmidt Fuerherd, a political analyst from Cambridge University, told DW that “in the Saudi public sphere, religion is increasingly being replaced by culture, ” denying that cube-shaped architecture is something specific to the Kaaba.
Change Date of Incorporation
This new square is not the only change in Saudi Arabia; it has been preceded by other steps that confirm a trend towards modernizing the country.
For the first time, the anniversary of the founding of the Saudi state was celebrated last year, and the occasion was designated on February 22 of each year, known as "Foundation Day", in addition to the Saudi National Day celebrated on September 23 of each year, and dates back to the occasion of the unification of Saudi Arabia in 1932.
The most important thing in establishing the "Foundation Day" is to change the date of the founding of the country from 1744 to 1727.
The year 1744 is linked to the agreement between the ruling Al Saud family and the cleric Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, the leader of the so-called Wahhabi Islam, who remained in control of Saudi Arabia for decades.
The agreement includes Abdul Wahab's support for the House of Saud in power, from a religious point of view, while the ruling family financially supports the Wahhabi family and allows it to have authority over education and public morals, and even laws were the same Wahhabi.
In 1727, it is related to the rise to power of Mohammed bin Saud as the founder of the first Saudi state, after his control of the Emirate of Diriyah north of Riyadh.
“The new interpretation of the birth of the state clearly underestimates the role of religion, ” says Schmidt Feuerhard, highlighting that“ the goal is a national campaign to celebrate non-religious holidays. ”
Earlier this month, Saudi Arabia declared Flag Day, a day officially celebrated for the first time on March 11, 2023, which dates back to the day the current Saudi flag was approved by King Abdulaziz.
The royal decree referred to the Testimony of Tawhid as symbolizing "the message of peace and Islam" while the sword symbolizes "strength, nobility, wisdom and prestige".
The Saudi Ministry of Islamic Affairs also announced major changes to the rules of the month of Ramadan, including urging not to bring children to mosques, prohibiting collection of donations inside mosques, not to be absent from work except for the utmost necessity, taking into account the conditions of people in Taraweeh prayers and supplications, and prohibiting the use of cameras in mosques.
Change in a general context
These changes have generally been accepted by a large number of Saudis, and Schmidt Fuerherd points to several explanations for the phenomenon, including sending tens of thousands of Saudis abroad with full government funding, that have made them receptive to these cultural changes in the country.
Education and job creation for Saudi youth have also become priorities for the kingdom, a key part of Vision 2030, announced by the crown prince during his rise in politics, since he was crown prince ’ s deputy.
Since 2016, Mohammed bin Salman has announced a series of decisions to change the face of the conservative kingdom.
This included diversifying the economy by not making it focused on oil, modernizing the country ’ s infrastructure, creating a recreational policy that allowed the establishment of music festivals and the opening of cinemas, and the largest beneficiaries are the women of the Kingdom, which eased restrictions on them, including allowing driving and Hajj and Umrah without a mahram, and mixing became normal, as well as abolishing the Commission for the Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice.
Mohammed bin Salman wants to modernize Saudi society without guaranteeing political freedoms
Freedom is not guaranteed!
Activist Loujain al-Hathloul spent three years in prison for defending women ’ s rights. Last year, 34-year-old Salma al-Shehab was sentenced to 34 years in prison for liking or tweeting about human rights in the kingdom. Noura bint Saeed al-Qahtani was sentenced to 45 years in prison. For the same reason.
“While there are more social freedoms, the state wants to remain the owner of change. ”
Schmidt Feuerherd says, “So any form of political activity is thwarted, and critics and opponents are portrayed as traitors to the nation. ”

Ways to Slow Down Brain Aging with Age
Monday ، 13 March 2023 02: 00 PM
Alzheimer 's disease
Written by Fatima Khalil
Leave a comment and read the comments of the readers.
There are ways you can slow down the aging of the brain as you age, as your brain is also affected by aging, that ’ s why we hear about many people developing dementia, Alzheimer ’ s and other mental health problems, so we present in this report ways to slow down the aging of the brain, according to the site “Health. ”
Ageing and its effects on the brain
Aging is a natural process that affects our bodies, including the brain It causes certain parts of the brain to contract, especially those that are important for learning and other complex mental activities.
In some areas of the brain, the connection between nerve cells may not be as effective, and therefore blood flow in the brain may decrease.
Progressive aging also leads to increased inflammation and cell loss due to cell death affecting a person ’ s ability to remember names and find words.
Ways to slow down the aging process in the brain
1.
Exercise regularly
Aerobic exercise for 30 to 60 minutes several times a week has been shown to reduce the risk of dementia, increase blood flow in the brain and promote cell growth.
2.
Good sleep.
Good sleep is crucial, so try to get at least 7 to 8 hours of uninterrupted sleep each night.
A restful sleep enhances the consolidation of memories and removes toxins and abnormal proteins.
If your sleep is interrupted, you may have sleep apnea.
It is important to see a sleep specialist if you suffer from lack of sleep and daytime fatigue.
3.
Dietary system
A healthy diet rich in whole grains, unsaturated or healthy fats, nuts and fish may reduce the risk of Alzheimer ’ s disease.
Try to get oils such as extra virgin olive oil rich in omega-3 fatty acids.
4.
Stay mentally active.
Your brain is like a muscle in many ways, so keeping it active slows down aging.
Retirement from active work should not translate into intellectual inactivity Continue to engage in cognitive stimulation tasks such as reading, problem-solving tasks and puzzles rather than just watching TV.
5.
SOCIAL COMMUNICATION
Being social is one of the most important human needs.
It meets our need for love and bonding, promotes brain health, and reduces the risk of depression and anxiety.
6.
Healthy weight and heart protection
Strokes are like heart attacks to the brain that increase the risk of early dementia.
Protect yourself by maintaining a healthy weight, and make sure your blood glucose and blood pressure are well controlled.
7.
Auxiliary devices such as hearing aids
Hearing loss and progressive fall are part of aging There is often resistance to seeking help from devices such as hearing aids, glasses, dentures and walkers in the elderly This leads to limited mobility, decreased social communication, poor appetite and increased risk of falls, all of which aggravate the appearance and development of cognitive function.

Anadolu News Agency

Greece continues to close historic Ottoman mosques (Anatolia)
Greece continues its policy of closing historic Ottoman mosques to worshippers, most notably those of the Sultans, which it has turned into warehouses and a museum, in violation of the principle of reciprocity with Turkey regarding the use of religious buildings.
Both the faculty member of the Department of History at the Turkish University of Thrace, Dr. Sabri Jan Sinau, and the faculty member of the Faculty of Architecture at the Turkish University of Marmara, Dr. Nawal Konouk, told Anadolu Agency that "Greece deliberately keeps the historical Ottoman mosques on Saqz Island (Chios) closed to worshippers."
Museum for displaying antiquities
Snau added that after the Greek takeover of the island in 1912, the Majidiyeh mosque on Saqez was converted into a museum to display antiquities from the Byzantine era.
On the current status of the mosque, Sinau explained that it has undergone restoration work at various periods to change its architectural and historical character, and that Christian artifacts and models of Jewish and Muslim tombstones are currently on display.
A faculty member at the Department of History at the Turkish University of Thrace reported that the Ottoman Empire archives of 1894 indicated that the island contained 9 mosques, 2 schools, 3 tekaya, 98 churches, 1 monastery, 2 synagogues, 2 baths and 18 streams of water.
Explaining the difference between Greece and Turkey, he pointed out that while Greece continues to close the mosque, Turkey has not imposed any restrictions on the Greek Orthodox Patriarch Bartholomew, who has continued to lead mass throughout the country, including in the Turkish state of Izmir near the Greek island of Saqez.
As a member of the European Union, Greece should be more concerned with human rights principles and related issues.
All EU member states affirm freedom of religion and belief and equality before the law, regardless of religious or sectarian affiliation, and undoubtedly these principles also apply to places of worship.
Although it is not a member of the European Union, Turkey, he added, adheres to the rules on freedom of religion and belief.
Today, non-Muslims can pray freely in their religious institutions across Turkey.
While Christians can come to churches in Turkey and pray there, Muslims cannot pray in the Majidiya Mosque or other mosques in Greece.
Sinau stressed that Greece does not follow a policy consistent with the principle of reciprocity regarding Ottoman monuments and places of worship within its borders.
He explained that in the past 20 years, we have opened about 84 Greek Orthodox churches in Edirne, Gesme (Izmir), Ordu, Gemlik and other Turkish states and regions, while Greece continues to close many mosques dating back to the Ottoman era, foremost of which is the Majidiya Mosque in Saqz, the Sulaymaniyah Mosque in Rhodes.
Mosques of Sultans.
Warehouses
Criticizing Greece ’ s approach to Ottoman antiquities, Nawal Konouq said Greek authorities were using historic buildings from the Ottoman era for their own ends.
She explained: We have four mosques in Saqz known as the Sultans Mosques.
One such mosque is used today as a warehouse where electrical appliances are repaired.
Not only that, according to Konouk, the mosque was converted into a museum after Greece occupied the island, and an Ottoman and Orkhanid mosques used as warehouses for excavation equipment owned by the Directorate of Antiquities.
She stressed that Greece follows a policy of ignoring Ottoman Turkish monuments, although the country still contains more than 8,500 historical Ottoman buildings.
The Greek authorities are using negligence as a means of destroying Ottoman historical buildings and resorting to restoration to change the historical and religious character of those buildings.

António Pedro, Acting Executive Secretary of the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, called on African countries affected by multiple crises to implement and invest in people-centred strategies to mobilize financial resources and accelerate the recovery of the continental economy.

MANAMA (Reuters) - After seven years of estrangement, Iran announced a Chinese-sponsored agreement to resume political and diplomatic relations between the two countries after they were severed after Iranian protesters stormed the Riyadh embassy in Tehran in January 2016, in response to Saudi Arabia ’ s execution of Saudi citizen Nimr al-Nimr, a prominent Shiite cleric and pro-Iranian in the kingdom.
Under the auspices of China, the two sides agreed to resume diplomatic relations and reopen their embassies and representations within a maximum of two months.
It also included their emphasis on respect for the sovereignty of States and non-interference in their internal affairs.
They also agreed that the foreign ministers of the two countries will hold a meeting to activate this and arrange the exchange of ambassadors and discuss ways to strengthen relations between them, and they also agreed to activate the security cooperation agreement between them and the general agreement for cooperation in the field of economy and trade.
Following the announcement, several countries welcomed the agreement — such as Qatar, Turkey, Oman, the UAE, Iraq, Lebanon, Jordan and Egypt, as well as the United Nations, among others — but attention in Yemen was focused on the impact the agreement could have.
In this analysis, YShabab Net highlights the motives of Saudi Arabia and Iran for an agreement between them, and the extent to which each country needs an agreement, given the range of factors that affect each party, and the impact of the agreement on the Yemeni file in the near future.
Saudi Motives:
There are many Saudi reasons that prompted Riyadh to sign an agreement to restore relations with Iran, after years of estrangement, the most important of which are related to the internal structure of the ruling family, regional and international relations, and others related to the war in Yemen.
Progress in securing the transition of government
During the years of the war in Yemen, specifically in the first three years, the ruling family exploited the war in Yemen to secure the transition of power in Saudi Arabia to the third generation, namely the descendants of the founder Abdulaziz Al Saud, where King Salman worked to remove his brother Muqrin from the crown prince, then removed his nephew Mohammed bin Nayef, and appointed his son Crown Prince, and recently appointed him as Prime Minister. The establishment of a series of security agencies that work to ensure the transition of government without disputes.
Vision 2030
Prince Mohammed bin Salman announced an ambitious economic development vision to build the Kingdom ’ s economy, away from oil revenues, aimed at diversifying investments, attracting international companies to the Kingdom, improving job opportunities for Saudis, and achieving vast economic leaps for the Kingdom, which will be possible only under lasting peace in the region.
Saudi Arabia ’ s Improved Relations with Iran ’ s Perimeter Countries
Compared to Saudi Arabia ’ s relations with a number of important regional countries surrounding Iran, from 2020 until today, and the previous period, we find that Saudi Arabia has rebuilt its relations from tension and conflict to reconciliation and improvement, such as its relations with Pakistan, Turkey, Oman, Qatar, Azerbaijan, and even China and Russia.
There is also the United States, whose President Biden had pledged to abandon Saudi Arabia and then returned to it in mid-2022.
Most of those countries had better relations with Iran before 2020, but now they have better relations with Riyadh, enabling Saudi Arabia to be in a good position even during negotiations with Iran.
American withdrawal from the region
The American factor is one of the most important determinants of foreign and domestic policy of any country in the region, and the United States began many years ago a strategic trend to withdraw from the Middle East and divide influence, between Iran and Saudi Arabia, and this trend strengthened with the advent of the Obama administration in 2009, and continued its approach Donald Trump, and Biden continued the path of Obama.
Many believe the drone and missile attacks on Abqaiq and Khurais, where Aramco's largest headquarters are located, have left Saudi Arabia deeply disappointed with the U.S. commitment, in place since the 1940s, to protect Gulf oil.

On the military level, Houthi and non-Houthi missile and drone attacks targeting the Kingdom led to the reduction of Saudi Arabia ’ s stockpile of anti-missile and drone weapons, especially as it coincided in mid-2021 with the US withdrawal of a number of air defense systems from Saudi Arabia and the region.
Saudi conflict with the UAE in Yemen
Saudi Arabia used the UAE in Yemen to lead the Arab coalition to support legitimacy in its war against the Houthi militia, but soon Abu Dhabi began to turn to rival Riyadh instead of ally or follower, and the conflict between the two parties plunged them into conflicts that undermined the government in Yemen, and resulted in a series of conflicts between the two countries.

The “digital nomads ” are often young people, who work using digital sites, and do not want to work from a fixed location in a particular country, but move from one country to another, combining work and tourism.

Attracting through the granting of visas
Countries such as Namibia, Ecuador, Belize, Malaysia and Albania have recently issued visas to attract digital nomads.
In Europe, Malta, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Greece and Hungary followed suit.
Countries ’ motivations range from wanting to compensate for the loss of tourists during the outbreak to accepting the positive side of hybrid methods of work, while others want to attract workers to compensate for their lack of skilled labor and their aging populations.
All of this helps to accept digital nomads, who are no longer seen by countries as job dropouts, but as pioneers of a new way of life.
Digital nomads see themselves as part of an international community, sharing tips and experiences on the best places to live and work online.

When a person has superficial and scant information, they often tend to exaggerate their cognitive abilities, called the Dunning – Kruger effect, or cognitive bias for the unqualified.
In April 1995, the American MacArthur Wheeler robbed two banks in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and in both cases he was not wearing a mask to hide his features, but was smiling and waving for surveillance cameras, not interested in revealing his identity!
The arrest warrant did not take long, and it turned out that he was under the false impression that he could hide his features by simply smearing his face with lemon juice, because he believed that it worked as a secret or invisible ink, and would make his features or the whole of his head invisible.

* * *
Wheeler ’ s belief in the powerful effect of lemon juice caught the attention of psychology professor David Dunning, of Cornell University, and he hired Justin Krueger, one of his distinguished students, to help him conduct a series of studies and field experiments on large sectors of people in several American cities, to try to find a relationship between intellectual competence and self-confidence.
What they found, over and over again, through scattered samples of humans, especially those with very little knowledge, in general, that they tend to claim and believe that they are experts on many topics, and understand a lot, so the researchers called the phenomenon, "the Daning-Kruger effect," meaning in short; the less familiar people think they are the most informed and understood!

We must remember that these people already believe that they know too much, but their knowledge is in fact much less, and this prompts them to claim science, and even boast about it!

World Today – Two small countries driving strong growth in Africa ’ s private wealth
You are now following the news of two small countries driving strong growth in Africa's private wealth from the World News section and now we leave you with the full details
MOHAMMED, Abu Dhabi, March 4, 2023 09: 22 PM – Rwanda and Mauritius combined account for less than 5 percent of Nigeria ’ s GDP, but the two small countries are driving strong growth in private wealth in Africa which is expected to rise to $3 trillion by 2031 from the current 2.1 trillion.
According to Henley Global Consulting ’ s Africa Private Wealth Report, Africa ’ s smaller and better-regulated economies are fast becoming centres of wealth and home to more millionaires on the continent.
Private wealth in Mauritius is expected to grow by 80 percent over the next 10 years, compared with 60 percent for Rwanda.
Great for Mauritius.
The number of high net worth individuals in Mauritius will reach more than 8,000 by 2031, making it one of the fastest attracting markets for high net worth individuals in the world, along with Australia, New Zealand, Switzerland and Malta.
In 2022, Mauritius became the first African country in terms of per capita wealth, due to the significant growth in the number of wealthy people who have flocked to it in recent years, taking advantage of the easy environment to do business, with Mauritius ranked 13th globally in the latest World Bank report on the indicators of the business environment; and ranked by the New World Index as the safest country in Africa.
Adult Retreat
As small countries attract more wealth, countries that have historically been the epicenter of private wealth in Africa are experiencing a steady exodus of millionaires.
Over the past 10 years, about 4,500 people with more than $1 million have left South Africa.
Although South Africa remains a major bastion of wealth in Africa, with a strong market for luxury real estate and wealth management services, it has faced significant economic and security challenges in recent years.
Of the 2,668 billionaires in the world, 15 are born in South Africa, but only 5 still live there.
Nigeria, Africa ’ s largest economy, has seen a sharp decline in total wealth, having suffered in recent years from high unemployment, corruption and over-reliance on oil exports.
Positive outlook
The outlook for private wealth on the continent is largely positive, as African countries have become less reliant on extractive industries, and business conditions continue to improve in many countries.
On the other hand, rapid population growth is a magnet for financiers looking for larger consumer markets.
Khaya Munzima, editor-in-chief specializing in economic affairs at the South African Broadcasting Corporation, believes that the continent has a lot of potential that helps to grow private wealth, especially in the central sectors that include agriculture, mining, information and communications technology, real estate and others.
“Africa is the second largest continent in the world with a population of 1.2 billion people, which is important for consumer activities that attract private wealth. ”
“The global economy is so interconnected that it is undeniable that the impact of the Russian conflict in Ukraine has been enormous on Africa, and there is an urgent need to pay more attention to the development of the financial sector, which is a key pillar of private capital. ”
Challenging the business environment
For experts, the African countries best able to improve the business environment will be the most profitable for the most part.
The World Bank estimates that of the 35 least business-friendly countries in the world, 27 are in Africa.
In this context, experts point to several challenges that hinder financial flows to many African countries, including corruption, bribery and extortion, as well as security and political instability.
Investment consultant Khea Sithol says some African countries are treating foreign firms as tools to absorb the crises they face.
“They stalk and blackmail foreign companies when they feel they need more money, hard currency, or more taxes to run parts of the country. ”
The economic system in many African countries poses a real challenge to the wealthy, as the legal framework governing investment relations is linked to the survival or demise of power in a highly volatile political environment.
Important indicators
136,000 people in Africa have assets of more than $1 million, of whom about 7,000 have assets of more than $10 million and 305 have assets of more than $100 million.
21 individuals in Africa have net assets of more than $1 billion, most of whose investments are in real estate, mining, telecommunications, luxury goods trading and agriculture.
39,000 South Africans own $651 billion in South Africa, of which $370 billion is concentrated in Johannesburg and Cape Town, the two richest cities in Africa.
• 27% decline in private wealth in Nigeria over the past 10 years, and 10,000 private Nigerians currently own about $228 billion.

A warm meal heals your worries and improves your health.
Why should you eat with your family during Ramadan?
Introduction to Translation
The family does not meet for one basic meal a day like in Ramadan, and the main reason behind this is the fixed time of Iftar as opposed to the normal daily meals, but there are also reasons for celebration. For most people, Ramadan is not only a month of worship and closeness to God, but also an occasion of celebration, in which people exchange visits and exchange congratulations.
All of this reminds us of a great “grace ” that we may not pay attention to, which is eating together, gathered in love and joy, which is very important, as Cody Delstrati of the Atlantic explains in this article, which we found to be very important in reminding ourselves of that important habit, which we should not leave after Ramadan.
Translation text
After my mother ’ s death and my brother ’ s departure to study in New Zealand, a new wind blew through my life, and the first thing I felt radically different about was the dining table.
My dad and I started eating separately.
Sometimes we would go out to dinner with friends, sometimes we would eat sandwiches in front of computers, or pizza slices while watching movies.
There were days when we rarely saw each other, but a few weeks before I was ready to leave home and go to university, my father stepped downstairs and said, “You know what?
I think we should start eating together even if there ’ s no one else in the house, and if your mother were here, she would want to. ”
Of course, it wasn ’ t perfect, the meals we prepared weren ’ t amazing, and those times gave us a deep longing for my mother and brother.
However, there was a new and special impulse deep within me about this time that I had dedicated to my father.
My time with my father was a form of medicine or a therapeutic potion, an excuse to shake our hearts and reflect on our days and recent events, and our simple and ordinary conversations about baseball or television often led us to serious discussions about politics, death, memories and loss in our lives.
Although eating together was a simple act that required only 45 minutes of daily life free from the distractions and pressures of life, this act, as simple as it was, has always had a profound impact on me and one of the happiest parts of my day.
It is sad to witness how things have turned out in our time, for example, in American society (or in any society) rarely meet for a meal that they share with the family.
Food in a hurry.
The average person eats one in five meals in their car, one in four people eats at least one fast food every day, and most American families report sharing only one meal every five days.
It is a pity that most people miss what can be considered valuable and valuable time with the family, as stopping eating together leads to a passion and severe consequences both physically and psychologically.
An analysis by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), using data from nearly three-quarters of the world ’ s countries, found that students who do not regularly share meals with their parents are more likely to miss school.
The International Student Assessment Program (PISA), a test conducted by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) to assess the performance of 15-year-olds in schools, showed that the average absenteeism rate worldwide was close to 15%, while the average absenteeism rate rose to about 30% when students reported that they often did not share meals with their families.
This brings us to the most important question: how do we eat better?
And we ’ re not talking from a nutritional perspective just as much as we ’ re talking from a psychological perspective as well.
One study presented at the European Conference on Obesity in Bulgaria showed that children who did not have dinner with their parents at least twice a week were 40% more likely to be overweight than their peers who enjoyed regular meals with their family.
Another study by the National Center for Addiction and Drug Abuse at Columbia University found that children who eat meals with their parents five or more days a week have fewer problems with drugs and alcohol, eat healthier, show greater academic superiority, and feel closer to their parents than their peers who have fewer meals with their parents.
There are two main reasons for these dire consequences associated with not eating meals with our family: the first is that when we eat out, especially in cheap fast food stores, or other places where most children go, we are not inclined to eat healthy meals, writes Michael Pollan, one of the most famous nutrition writers around the world, in his latest book, Cooked: A Natural History of the Transformation. Cooked: A Natural History of Transformation).
Pollan points out in his book that the meals we eat outside are almost all less healthy than home-cooked foods and often high in fat, salt and calories.
The other reason is that the idea of eating alone is an experience that may make you feel alienated or isolated. The dining table plays a role in uniting individuals and gathering them in one place to communicate, and sharing food with those we love is an acceptable reason to join a company that humanizes our unity and dissipates the brutality of our days by sharing news and conversations with them. Put their work aside and take time out of their day to enjoy a company that eases the stress of their days, because we rarely allow ourselves to enjoy anything at the expense of productivity.
In France, for example, it is acceptable to eat alone, but not in haste.
Eating or chewing food feverishly in public places, such as the metro, can attract arrows of disagreeable glances, so employees are given at least an hour to eat lunch.
In many Mexican cities, for example, people gather with friends and family in parks or city squares to eat together, and the same happens in Cambodia (located in Southeast Asia), where villagers brush colorful mats or rugs to share meals with loved ones in a banqueting atmosphere.
In her book Eating Together, Alice Jolier argues that eating together can radically change people ’ s views, because it eases people ’ s feelings of inequality, for example, with diners looking at others of different races, genders, and socioeconomic backgrounds with a more egalitarian eye than they might in other social contexts.
But not eating with the family or not eating slowly was not the common theme: in 1950, Elizabeth David became known as one of the most important American chefs whose recipes are considered moving (such as the famous American cook Alice Waters and David Leibovitz, the best-selling cookbook of our time), and published a book on Mediterranean food.
In this book, Elizabeth argued that great food is simple food, and the best food is not necessarily food served by fancy or trendy restaurants; on the contrary, the simple basic meal you enjoy in the company of your loved ones is the best meal ever.
In one of the most striking passages, she wrote: "Under the shade of the lemon grove, I cut a slice of bread and sprinkled it with some of the most attractive and strongly flavored olive oil, then emptied into my belly a glass of my favorite drink, and I remembered at this moment what the British novelist Norman Douglas said when he wrote that everyone who helped us expand our understanding by giving meaning to everything that surrounds us deserves our gratitude. forever".
But Elizabeth ’ s equation for our physical and psychological well-being was a straightforward one: all you have to do is simply eat and share with others, but for families who spend a lot of money on fast food and groceries, the simplicity Elizabeth pointed out is not easily attainable.
In America, for example, spending time joining the family and having a nice meal with them seems like more of a show-off.
American painter Norman Rockwell ’ s painting of the family wrapped around the dinner table is no longer as close to the middle class as it is to the bourgeoisie.
Crisis of the Age
Many families can ’ t afford for a parent to miss work by staying home and spending the day cleaning and grilling meat and potatoes for their spouse and children. Most parents don ’ t have time to cook, many don ’ t cook, and the idea that you should spend more money and time buying products from stores instead of replacing them with a box full of ready-made Chinese meals may seem unwieldy and leave an impression....
It ’ s understandable, of course, that you want to save time and money, and that ’ s exactly why small stores stop working as soon as Walmart (an American multinational retail company, a chain of stores, supermarkets, and department stores) comes along.
But what we may not realize in such a case is that the store owner will not suffer or face problems as much as the consumer who relies on unhealthy and fast meals will suffer.
How, then, can we adopt a better way of eating our food not only from a nutritional perspective, but also from a psychological perspective?
François de la Rochefoucauld, a 17th-century French writer, once wrote, “Eating is a necessity, but eating it intelligently is an art. ”
If we discuss the meaning of “intelligence ” in the context of food, we will discover that it is a controversial issue.
There are those who are obsessed with food, eating it only if it is organic, with a vague desire to “originate ” the cooking process, a category known in the United States as“ foodies ” and in France as “Le Fooding ”. Satisfy them.
But all of this was no closer to the term “intelligence ” referred to by the French writer De La Rochefoucauld.
Perhaps what LaRochefoucauld meant by “eating smart ” was that all one needed was to eat in the company of others.
Although eating healthy would be a good option, fast food can also be sufficient and very satisfying psychologically as long as you eat it in the family or with roommates or friends.
We often set aside time despite our busy schedules to go to the cinema or the gym, while distancing ourselves from having meals with the family on the pretext that there is not enough time for them.
But perhaps if we stop treating mealtime as just a date in our busy schedules, instead seeing it as an opportunity to de-stress and reconnect with those we love, it could help our children improve their school performance, and a healthy meal at home will also help us reach a slim figure or look better, not to mention reduce the likelihood of drug and alcohol use.
Eating together can guide children ’ s lives by building a better relationship with their parents, and the same goes for adults.
The night before I left home to continue my studies, I went with my father to our favorite restaurant in my hometown of Sichuan, a restaurant where we always order the same food, but even after 60 years of enjoying life on the planet and eating countless dinners there, my father still finds it difficult to use chopsticks properly.
So I offered him a hand and began to explain to him, holding the chopsticks, how necessary it was to hold one of them well, while moving the other stick to pick up the food.

Study: Intermittent fasting protects against type 2 diabetes
Contact – Editorial Team:
Having been shown to have many potential health benefits, from weight loss to longevity, a recent study has found a new benefit of intermittent fasting.
According to the study, conducted by researchers from the University of Adelaide, Australia, intermittent fasting may outperform low-calorie diets when it comes to preventing type 2 diabetes in people at high risk.
Intermittent fasting and low-calorie diet
The researchers compared the time-restricted intermittent fasting regime with a low-calorie diet in more than 200 people to see which had a greater impact on the risk of type 2 diabetes.
The time-restricted eating group in the study was allowed to eat only between 8 a.m. and 12 p.m. on fasting days three days a week, and ate normally for the other four days.
Also read:
Which is better for weight loss: calorie counting or intermittent fasting?
A study answered
They showed greater improvement in blood sugar metabolism for at least six months, compared to people who followed a low-calorie diet.
Interestingly, people in both groups lost the same amount of weight during the study period.
Study author Xiao Tong Tong, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Adelaide, Australia, said: “Our study suggests that meal timing and fasting tips expand the health benefits of a calorie-restricted diet, regardless of weight loss, and this may be influential in clinical practice. ”
The researchers examined blood sugar after eating.
If blood levels are too high, this indicates a higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes, the form of disease most associated with obesity.
Also read:
Study: Intermittent fasting may eliminate need for diabetes medications
Fasting Timing
Previous studies have suggested that eating early improves health, but no study has looked at the timing of ideal fasting.
“Our study findings add to the body ’ s growing evidence regarding meal timing with prolonged fasting is key to improving postprandial glucose metabolism in adults at risk for type 2 diabetes. ”
Participants were allowed to change to a weight maintenance plan after six months or stick to their initial diet.
More low-calorie people stayed on their plan, and the benefits first measured in the fasting group disappeared after 18 months.
Tong pointed out that not everyone can, or should, experience intermittent fasting.
He warned against following the fasting diet for each of the following:
- Pregnant women.
-People with eating disorders or diabetes
People who take glucose-lowering medications.
People with any underlying health conditions should check with their doctors before trying a fasting diet.
Maintain order for a long time
Christa Faraday, a professor of nutrition at the University of Illinois at Chicago, said this is one of the longest and largest intermittent fasting studies to date.
Faraday, who was not involved in the study, added: "Blood glucose control was better in the time-restricted eating group versus calorie restriction after six months, but these benefits were no longer observed by the end of the study at 18 months."
“It ’ s very difficult to maintain this in the long run because people don ’ t like to skip dinner with their family / friends for several days a week, ” Faraday said.
Participants stopped following the diet after the first six months of the study.
“The long-term viability of this eating pattern doesn ’ t seem to be that great, ” she said.
Faraday explained that the most common forms of time-restricted eating include eating between 12pm and 8pm and not counting calories.
“This intervention is easy to follow, because people don ’ t have to track calories and still allow individuals to participate in social eating every evening. ”

Recent research has revealed that fasting, whether intermittent or consecutive for several hours, has health and psychological benefits for humans, in addition to the religious and cultural reasons for which they fast, according to the website Business Insider.
Dr. Andrew Wang, professor of immunobiology at Yale University School of Medicine, explained that fasting is not eating food or drinks for a certain period, and there are many different types of fasting, consecutive fasting for several hours and intermittent fasting.
Benefits of fasting for mental and physical health:
Fasting relieves inflammation
One of the most important benefits of fasting is that it reduces inflammation, which is the body ’ s natural response to infection and there are several ways to reduce inflammation in the body by fasting:
When your body is fasting, it cannot convert glucose from food into energy, and instead, your body must rely on an alternative energy source called ketone bodies, which comes from fatty acids.
Your body produces fewer free radicals when you burn ketones, which helps reduce inflammation.
Fasting strengthens cognitive performance
With age, our organs are prone to chronic inflammation, and chronic inflammation can contribute to cognitive decline and possible dementia due to plaque buildup in the brain.
Fasting helps counter this by reducing inflammation.
Studies have confirmed that fasting can prevent the development of Alzheimer ’ s disease in animals.
Research has also revealed that intermittent fasting can slow cognitive decline and improve Alzheimer ’ s disease symptoms in mice.
Fasting regulates blood sugar levels
Fasting may also regulate blood sugar levels, which is important to protect against diseases such as type 2 diabetes.
Blood sugar increases when you eat, so it naturally decreases when you fast.
However, your body will prevent your blood sugar from dropping too much by making glucose itself.
This keeps blood sugar at healthy levels.
Fasting improves heart health
Research has suggested that fasting promotes heart health by reducing inflammation and protecting against diabetes, both of which are risk factors for heart attacks and strokes.
Fasting helps to lose weight
Fasting helps you lose weight by limiting the number of calories you eat.
Intermittent fasting, in particular, helps with weight loss by keeping blood sugar levels low in the evening when they are less active.
In the same context, Dr. Wang warned certain categories of fasting of various types, including pregnant women, those who breastfeed their children, diabetics, and thyroid patients.

Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk has once again sounded the alarm about the dangers of artificial intelligence to humanity, claiming that the popular chatbot ChatGPT is biased towards liberalism, and he plans to counter it with a robot that “seeks truth. ”
In an exclusive interview with Fox News, which aired at dawn on Tuesday, Musk said he would establish an artificial intelligence company called TruthGPT.
The interview with the CEO of Twitter, Tesla and other major tech companies discussed why he created an alternative to the artificial intelligence-based chatbot that he helped fund initially, and other concerns about how the robot could affect the freedom to use information.
In the interview, Musk said, “I ’ m going to create something called Truth JBT, or the ultimate truth-seeking AI that tries to understand the nature of the universe. ”
“I think this may be the best route to safety in the sense that AI, which is interested in understanding the universe, is unlikely to eliminate humans because we are an interesting part of the universe. ”
The Fox News presenter pointed out in the interview that Musk co-founded OpenAI to “control ” it, but unfortunately, it wasn ’ t done that way, as Musk said that Microsoft had become, sort of, controlling OpenAI.
Musk warned that artificial intelligence could have a catastrophic impact on the entire existence of humanity if not managed properly.
AI is more dangerous than poorly managed aircraft design or poor car production, he said, meaning it has potential, no matter how small but not trivial, that threatens to destroy civilization.
He even tweeted over the weekend that he had used his only meeting with former U.S. President Barack Obama to warn of the dangers surrounding AI capabilities and called for regulation.
“I ’ ve seen it happen a long time ago since GPT-1, and that ’ s why I ’ ve tried to warn the public for years, ” he said.
"The only meeting I had with Obama as president was not to invite Tesla or SpaceX, but to encourage regulation of artificial intelligence."

Researchers calculated the value a community gets from a shared but hidden underwater resource, and found it to be far higher than we ever expected.
Kelp forests have always done so much for humanity, working all the time out of sight beneath the waves.
Advertisement
It hugs a third of our coasts, providing food and shelter for many coastal seafood.
In doing so, these vibrant ocean jungles helped bold human migrations like the Southern Colonization of the Americas 20,000 years ago.
We also eat kelp itself, use it to fertilize crops, add it to medicines and skin care, and inhale the oxygen it produces.
However, kelp forests are in catastrophic decline, and we don ’ t fully understand how much we ’ re losing, let alone its value.
So a team of researchers made an estimate of the services provided by kelp ecosystems.
Aaron Eiger, a marine ecologist at the University of New South Wales, said: “For the first time, we have the numbers that demonstrate the significant commercial value of our global kelp forests.
We found 740 million people living within 50 kilometers of the kelp forest.
So these systems have an important role to play in supporting these people ’ s livelihoods and vice versa. ”
Eiger and his colleagues used 1,354 fish and invertebrate surveys across six different types of kelp forests in eight different ocean regions.
They also took measurements of nutrient use from carbon to phosphorus.
The average economic value of kelp forests contributing to fisheries production is US $29,851 and 904 kilograms per hectare per year, the team reports.
Surprisingly, only 50 of the 193 animal species identified contributed the bulk of the value to fisheries, especially invertebrates such as lobsters and hedgehogs.
These ocean "trees" not only provide habitat for thousands of marine species, but they also play a major role in global nutrient cycles as well.
Seaweed is a type of algae, not plants, but just like plants, photosynthesis puts energy into the networks of life that protect it, removes carbon dioxide from its environment and produces oxygen in the process.
Removing carbon dioxide, in turn, raises pH levels and oxygen supplies in immediate areas – helping to mitigate the local effects of ocean acidification.
Kelps algae devour other nutrients, such as nitrogen and phosphorus, to fuel their rapid growth, with some species able to add up to 50 cm of height per day.
Previous research has found that kelp forests are more productive in terms of growth than intensively cultivated crops such as rice and wheat.
While kelp ’ s absorption of carbon may not be as impressive as its removal of nitrogen, it is still equivalent to wild forests and seagrass.
The team concludes that "these kelp forests produce an estimated US $500 billion annually globally."
This is three times more than previous best estimates and is just a basic metric that has yet to take into account other important contributions to the economy.
There were also many other services that we didn ’ t evaluate, including tourism, educational experiences, and kelp as a food source, so we expect the actual value of the world ’ s kelp forests to be higher. ”
Kelps also has amazing potential as a sustainable biofuel and helps protect our coasts from erosion.
But like much of the world around us, kelp forests struggle.
In the past few decades, about a third of all kelp forests have suffered heavy losses.
A combination of heatwaves and predatory invasive sea urchins has seen a 95 percent drop in kelp off the coast of California since 2014.
Australian kelp forests have been listed as endangered after similarly severe degradation.
They also suffer from pollution from human activities, and as these floating forests deteriorate, so do crabs, fish, and all the other life forms that depend on their existence.
“Putting the dollar value on these systems is an exercise to help us understand one measure of their immense value.
It is important to remember that these forests also have intrinsic, historical, cultural and social value in their own right. ”
The researchers hope their findings will attract some much-needed attention to this long-neglected ecosystem.

The story of an American businessman who tries to reduce his biological age and maintain his youth always
• Lara Livington
• ClickTV-BBC Introduction
Death is the inevitable end for all humans, but more and more experts believe that what we feel in our later years as we age (a symptom of aging and associated diseases) may change.
These experts are currently talking about “health spans, ” that is, increasing the number of years we feel healthy during our lives.
Life expectancy may have doubled in the last 150 years, but many of us have witnessed the deterioration in the health of many of our loved ones as they age.
To avoid this fate, a new industry is emerging, heralding a long-term revolution and technologies that they say lead to longer lives but are also healthier.
Working with those in the field thrives, they describe supplements as being able to fight cell degradation in humans, as well as all sorts of hot and cold treatments that try to help us reduce inflammation and disease risk in our bodies.
So I decided to take a trip to the New Domain Center in California, unsure whether I had just reached a fund-raising organization, or whether we had already reached the highest ranks of progress in medicine.
Tech entrepreneur Brian Johnson is spending millions of dollars a year hoping to reduce his biological age — making his body look younger than his actual chronological age of 45.

There is a good reason for any of us to do so.
Age is the most risk factor for disease, whether it is cancer, type 2 diabetes, heart disease, or dementia, so if it is possible to delay aging as a whole, it may delay the risk of these conditions developing.
For him, it ’ s a sport.
In Johnson ’ s luxurious home on the beach of Venice, the bedroom has been converted into a clinic where he spends long hours.
He wakes up at 5 a.m. and eats his first meal an hour later, followed by a second meal, and his last at 11 a.m.
In addition to this, he takes 54 medically selected pills, a combination of supplements and over-the-counter medications, all of which were planned based on the results of medical tests.
All his days are spent practicing hard sports, monitoring his condition and taking various treatments.
He told me that his entire skin laser treatment reduced the age of his skin by 22 years, the largest age reduction in any part of his body.
The aesthetics of the body are only a small part of all that, with Johnson reminding me that “our skin is our largest organ. ”
Johnson was logical and friendly.
I left his house and I want to be like him (a little).
Maybe I am already like him, I run 5 kilometers a day, try to avoid sugar, use measuring and tracking devices for fun.
My colleagues considered Johnson not to be happy, so it is clear that his life does not suit everyone.
While his routine might seem harsh, every conversation was focused on lifestyle.
Eric Verdin, chief executive of the Buck Institute for Aging Research, says: “Lifestyle is responsible for about 93 percent of your longevity — only about 7 percent are genetic factors. ”
“Based on the data (if we live healthy), I would expect most people to live up to 95 years healthy, ” Verdin told me.
So there are 15 to 17 (extra) years of healthy living that we are all waiting for. ”
The big question now, which Verdin and others are investigating, is what does a healthy lifestyle mean?
Take a push-up exercise for example, should it be a daily outing or participating in a gym class regularly?
The same applies to healthy eating.
Is fasting just as important as avoiding sugar?
What about a good night's sleep?
You can't underestimate the sleep mania I've come across.
I met many people who set their alarm devices not to wake up in the morning, but to remind them to sleep on time for a full eight hours.
Well, we each have our own way of organizing it at a different level.
Verdin practices what he preaches, and his regimen consists of “a lot of exercise, some fasting, good sleep, a lot of social contact, and a little alcohol. ”
But what about his advice to others?
“Try to spend at least 14 of 24 hours without eating any calories as this has a profound effect on your metabolism, ” Verdin says.
But there is a difference about how healthy this is for some women.
Tracking our bodies better as they age may be helpful.
Health risks can be reported in advance and any new drugs can be used in a timely manner.
It was interesting to see that all longevity science workers wear more than one body state tracking device, usually a smartwatch (a more convenient way to sleep I can tell you, these people are obsessed with prioritizing sleep).
For my part, I found that healthy tracking of the state of the body is beneficial.
I ’ m not diabetic, but I ’ m fascinated by the results of the ongoing glucose monitoring devices I ’ ve worn for a while.
The assumption is that progress in longevity will be made, albeit less dramatically than some might hope.
Experts suggest that a drug may appear that will initially make a difference for a year or two, and then gradually increase the years with the next generation of the drug, and so the progress continues.
But along with this progress will come practical and moral dilemmas.
One of the fundamental questions is whether aging can be defined as a disease.
This may make it easier for regulators to approve drugs, but there is a risk that people over a certain age may be labeled as “sick. ”
The cost of these treatments may or may not be an issue (for advanced medical systems), depending on what it looks like.
At the same time, a healthy lifestyle is likely to increase lifespan by a few more years, so we may need to work longer.
During the research assignment on the subject of longevity, my expectations were overturned.
I ’ ve seen sensational headlines, talking about tech billionaires hanging out on their yachts, discussing dreams of saving the world, going into space, or “curing ” aging.
But actually that wasn ’ t what I saw.
Rich people have been donating money to medical research for years.
This is just a new generation of wealth, a potential new specialty of medicine.
Plus it's really interesting and affects all of us.
But for now, extending your period of good health requires hard work.
As Silicon Valley-based journalist Danny Fortson put it: “Exercise is hard, magic pills are easy, and that ’ s why everyone is so excited to get the pills. ”
So I came home more determined than ever to live my life healthy, sleep better, exercise without excuse, eat well, and cherish social connections (yes, this was a recipe for longevity).
With a little luck I could have the time to take advantage of any scientific breakthroughs.

New York Abu Dhabi: 200 students from 24 countries participate in the International Hackathon to benefit the community
The 11th edition of the annual International Hackathon to Benefit the Community in the Arab World, hosted by New York University Abu Dhabi from April 27 to 30, attracts more than 200 students from 24 countries.
The competition focuses on the concept of sustainability as the main theme and aims to develop innovative solutions using quantum computing technologies to address challenges related to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.
The Hackathon covers a number of different sectors, including health, education, film, music, business and science. In its current edition, the competition features world-renowned computer science professors, successful startup founders, technology specialists and venture capitalists at NYU Abu Dhabi to guide teams of talented computer science students from around the world, mostly from the Arab world, to create web and smartphone applications. Serving the community.
Participating students have an exceptional opportunity to gain basic practices in quantum computing and hardware technologies as well as software development, under the guidance of 51 world-leading experts in the industry and academia.
The competition also allows students to discover quantum computing solutions for a wide range of challenging projects, from machine learning and artificial intelligence, to complex physical simulations, chemistry, computer science, healthcare and sports, to online gaming, security and social science concepts and artworks created using quantum computing technologies.
The competition provides clear insights into all stages of starting a tech startup, opening doors for future global project collaborations, startup launches and academic research, while experts from world-leading institutions such as MIT, the Federal Institute of Technology and Stanford University supervise and guide participants.
The annual International Hackathon is held to benefit the community with the support of leading quantum computing technology experts from the industry and academia around the world, including the Center for Quantum Systems and Topography at NYU Abu Dhabi, the Institute of Technological Innovation, the Geneva Foundation for Science and Diplomacy, the Quantum Center at the Federal Institute of Technology Zurich, the Institute of Quantum Science and Technology at the University of Calgary, MIT IQU Hack, and QWorld. From global business companies, including IBM Global, QPride and NIW.
Professor Sana Odeh, Faculty Member and Professor of Computer Science at New York University Abu Dhabi and Chair of the Organizing Committee, said: “The theme of the Hackathon 2023 to solve difficult problems related to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals using quantum computing is a testament to our commitment to contribute to sustainable growth in the country, the region and around the world and to ensure a sustainable future. at the Conference of the States Parties COP28".
“The level of partnerships and experts participating this year reflects the global standing of the event, and in addition to our new role in the University Climate Network at the COP, we are confident that the International Hackathon provides a unique opportunity to collaborate with young climate leaders to showcase the potential of technology and quantum computing to solve sustainability challenges. ”
“The event provided a unique platform for former participants to embark on their different career paths, with some receiving scholarships and others getting jobs or launching their own startups. ”
