Avocado: Between Environmental Impacts and Global Market Controllers
In the Mexican state of Michoacán, which produces about 80% of the world ’ s avocado, avocado cultivation has depleted local water supplies and caused severe environmental damage, with studies showing that avocado cultivation has led to deforestation, soil erosion and chemical contamination of water sources.
(Getty)
In recent years, the avocado industry has become a staple in many diets around the world, and its popularity has increased greatly due to the multiple health benefits.
However, the demand for this fruit has led to harmful environmental effects and the emergence of a mafia that controls the production and distribution of avocados in some countries.
A Chilean study published recently said that avocado cultivation has caused severe water shortages, as well as in Peru, where large farmers have dominated the avocado market since the 1990s, where cultivation requires huge amounts of water, the production of one kilogram of avocado, consumes about 1,000 liters of water, much more than other crops such as tomatoes or oranges.
According to a report by the Water Footprint Network, the production of one kilogram of tomatoes requires about 300 liters of water, and the high water use of avocado production has led to water scarcity and depletion of aquifers in some areas.
In the Mexican state of Michoacán, which produces about 80% of the world ’ s avocado, avocado cultivation has depleted local water supplies and caused severe environmental damage, with studies showing that avocado cultivation has led to deforestation, soil erosion and chemical contamination of water sources.
According to the report, moving avocados from the production site to the market also has a significant impact on the climate, as avocados are grown mainly in developing countries, and are exported to developed countries such as the United States, Europe and Japan, and the transport of avocados over long distances contributes to greenhouse gas emissions harmful to the environment. Approximately 5.4 kg of carbon dioxide emissions per kg of avocado.
Avocado production has also led to the emergence of a mafia that controls the production and distribution of avocados in some countries, where the avocado mafia operates mainly in Mexico, where it controls the production and export of avocados, and this mafia, according to media reports, consists of criminal organizations that use violence and intimidation to control the production and distribution of avocados, and often extort money from farmers. The avocado mafia uses violence to eliminate competitors and dominate the export market, as studies have shown that these gangs are responsible for deforestation, land grabbing and violence against indigenous communities in Mexico.
According to dozens of studies published in recent years, avocado cultivation also has negative effects on local communities. In some areas, demand for avocados has led to land grabbing, community displacement, labor exploitation, and avocado cultivation in the Mexican state of Michoacán has led to the displacement of indigenous communities and the exploitation of often paid migrant workers. Some studies have shown that the expansion of avocado cultivation has displaced traditional crops, leading to food insecurity and loss of biodiversity.
According to the study, governments around the world can take various measures to mitigate the impact of this agriculture on the climate, and one way is to promote sustainable avocado farming practices that reduce water use and reduce the use of chemicals. Protect the environment, provide financial incentives to farmers and enact laws that will deter illegal and criminal practices in these countries.

The temperature of the oceans is sounding the alarm on the planet Earth.
By the end of March, the surface temperature of the world's oceans was higher than anything seen in the 40 years that satellites were measuring.
Scientists said the records were “off the charts, ” and as the heat refused to fade for more than a month, the Earth became“ uncharted territory. ”
A new disaster.
The temperature on the surface of the ocean – as it is on land – is being raised by global warming but could jump from year to year as weather systems emerge and fall again.
At a depth of 2 kilometers below sea level, this contrast can ’ t be seen almost anywhere.
The temperature rise there has been on the rise for decades, thanks to the burning of fossil fuels.
Dr Paul Durack, a research scientist specialising in ocean measurements and modelling at the US Department of Energy ’ s Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, said: “The ocean ’ s ability to retain heat is enormous.
“The ocean captures more than 90% of the energy imbalance we create due to human-induced climate change. ”
The ocean is much less reflective than Earth and absorbs more direct energy from sunlight, but as greenhouse gases trap more energy that is reflected back — allowing less escape into space — the ocean is trying to balance itself with the heat in the atmosphere above.
A technical planner in a chapter of the UN ’ s latest climate assessment laid out unfathomable heat gains.
Between 1971 and 2018, the ocean gained 396 zetajoules of heat.
A study conducted in January found that the ocean increased by 10 marriages in 2022 from the previous year – enough heat to boil 700 million boilers every second.
Compared to the ocean, according to a study conducted in January, the atmosphere has retained about 2 percent of the excess heat caused by global warming since 2006.
To understand what is happening beneath the surface of the ocean, far from seeing satellites, scientists are looking at a vast network of thousands of thermometers on buoys, ships, underwater gliders and permanent moorings.

Later this year, Apple will enable iPhone and tablet users with cognitive disabilities to deal more easily and independently with Assistive Access by launching a feature that makes speech impaired from speaking through its apps or voice calls on its devices.
It is expected that the new feature will enable individuals who do not speak in writing to speak during calls and conversations using Live Speech; people at risk of losing their ability to speak can also use their personal voice to create a composite sound similar to them to communicate with family and friends.
Advertising material
For users who are blind or have poor vision, Magnifier mode offers Point and Speak, which identifies text that users point to and read aloud to help them interact with physical objects such as home appliances, Apple announced on Tuesday.
The iPhone and iPad will learn the user ’ s voice after training the device for just 15 minutes.
The Live Speech feature will then use Composite Audio to read a user ’ s written text aloud during phone calls, FaceTime conversations, and even in-person conversations.
People will also be able to save commonly used phrases to use during live conversations.
This feature is one of several that aim to make Apple devices more inclusive for people with impairments in cognition, vision, hearing and movement.
Apple has said that people who may experience situations where they lose their voices over time, such as ALS (ALS), could benefit more from the tools.
Apple ’ s senior director of global access policies and initiatives, Sarah Herlinger, said in a blog post: “Accessibility is part of everything we do at Apple. ”
“These groundbreaking features are designed with feedback from members of disability communities at every step of their development, to support a diverse range of users and help people connect in new ways. ”
The new features are due to be rolled out later this year.
While these tools have the potential to meet a real need, they also come at a time when advances in AI have raised alarms about bad actors using convincing fake audio and video – known as “deep fakes ” – to defraud or mislead the public.
In a blog post, Apple said the Personal Voice feature uses “machine learning on the device to keep users ’ information private and secure. ”
Other tech companies have experimented with using artificial intelligence to replicate sound.
Last year, Amazon said it was updating its Alexa system that would allow the technology to imitate any sound, even if a family member is deceased.
(The feature has not yet been launched.)
In addition to voice features, Apple announced Assistive Access, which combines some of the most popular iOS apps, such as FaceTime, Messages, Camera, Photos, Music, and Phone, into a single call app.
Apple is also updating its Magnifier app for the blind.
It will now include detection mode to help people better interact with physical objects.
The update will allow someone, for example, to hold an iPhone camera in front of the microwave and move their finger through the keyboard while the app labels and advertise the text on the microwave buttons.

Overfishing – African fishermen are paying the price for their wrong practices
African fishermen in countries bordering the Atlantic Ocean are suffering from a shortage of fish, while overfishing has become a major problem due to harmful fishing practices and large fishing operations in international waters.
Overfishing is threatening the livelihoods of fishermen off the coast of Africa.
The sight of a fishnet coming out of the sea full of fish is often drooled by any fisherman, but it has become rare in African countries bordering the Atlantic, where harmful fishing practices and overfishing have for years destroyed fish stocks and marine life.
Fishermen face many difficulties in fishing, whether to earn a living or feed their families, while large global fishing vessels are forced to resort to innovative and often destructive methods to maintain their marine activity, but these methods are not sustainable, which poses a threat to the marine environment, especially as the phenomenon of climate change worsens.
The crisis was the focus of a panel discussion held on the sidelines of the Ministerial Conference on Fisheries Cooperation among African States bordering the Atlantic Ocean (ATLAFCO) in Rabat, where attendees tried to explore new ways to balance fishing and biodiversity conservation.
The reality for African fishermen seems bleak, with many, including Burton, a fisherman in Benin, stressing the lack of fish.
Burton, who has been fishing in the Bay of Benin for more than 30 years, said: “Once, I could trap fish in the net ten minutes after putting underwater water lamps.
Mr Burton, 50, said fishing had been a lucrative business in the past, but that had changed in recent years.
Miserable measures.
He said the crisis has been exacerbated by large foreign fishing boats fishing for the fish that are supposed to be the day of his comrades who go out at sea on boats and small boats, but competition with large ships seems impossible.
The suffering of Benin fisherman Burton appears to be frequent in other African countries bordering the Atlantic, where years of overfishing have reduced fish catches by almost half over the past 15 years.
Similar to large fishing operations on the high seas, fishermen in countries such as Ghana are looking for innovative ways to catch and keep fish, but many fishermen resort to dangerous practices such as poisoning fish and using dynamite to kill fish at night.
Fishing was a lucrative activity in Ghana, but now fishermen cannot earn a living.
“I ’ ve seen fishermen in Ghana use chemicals like soap powder while others use heavy means like dynamite where they can catch fish using these techniques, ” Burton said.
Hunters have some responsibility.
Experts confirm that these practices inflict heavy losses on the environment as well as being contrary to the law, while these methods have become common amid the efforts of fishermen to secure their livelihood, especially with the failure of governments to work on this problem.
As a result, fishers have become part of the problem as a result of their harmful fishing practices.
Rodrigue Bilibe, a researcher at the Africa Regional Centre for Excellence in Coastal Resilience at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana, said the use of dynamite and chemicals "damages the marine and aquatic environment and exacerbates the crisis".
He added in an interview with DW that these practices “contribute to the destruction of coral reefs which hinders the marine ecological balance of coral reefs and eliminates the entire food chain.
Even if the authorities curb these illegal practices, fishermen continue to find new ways to destroy the seabed.
They are still developing other harmful practices to capture what remains of the fish from the seafloor. ”
Although there is a fact that dwindling fish populations are enough evidence of the disastrous impact of harmful fishing practices, Pelepi said fishermen still do not understand the seriousness of the issue and are flouting the rules.
According to the United Nations, fishing is the source of livelihood for about 2.7 million people in Ghana, accounting for 10% of the total population, while fish and seafood are the source of 60% of the protein consumed in the country.
In the face of these figures, the problem of fish shortage is a serious nutritional problem.
A vicious circle.
Participants at the Rabat symposium agreed on the need to find solutions to estimates that the damage caused by this problem in the coastal West African countries alone is estimated to be at least $2.3 billion annually.
Abdelnaji Lamarish, head of cooperation and information systems at TLAFCO, said improving monitoring mechanisms is an important step to start assessing and addressing the problem, adding that African countries should “fight harmful and illegal fishing methods. ”
Amadou Tall, head of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) programme, highlighted another issue: identifying harmful methods among fishermen is less difficult than identifying the latest fishing methods by global vessels in international waters.
Illegal and unauthorized fishing activities are the main problem because they are responsible for 26 million tons of fish caught annually, he said, adding that such practices occur on the high seas, which means that they are impossible to control since they fall outside the jurisdiction of coastal States.
He stressed that although illegal fishing activities take place on the high seas, they do much damage to coasts as coastal populations bear the brunt of illegal overfishing practices.
Fishermen are caught in a vicious cycle as they try to stay active, even through harmful fishing practices, while fish in the Atlantic waters off the coast of West Africa do not feed.

African Bank Meetings: Focus on Attracting External Finance and Crucial Institutional Reform in Africa
President of the African Union Commission, Moussa Fakih, during a speech at the opening of the 58th Annual Meetings of the African Development Bank (AfDB) in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, stressed the importance of these meetings focusing on ways to attract external financing for the implementation of green investments in the continent.
He stressed the need for member states to take specific reforms to reduce investment risks by preventing all manifestations of corruption and embezzlement of public funds and reviewing the inappropriate tax base and illegal financing.
During these meetings, which will be held from May 22 to 26, 2023, under the theme "Mobilizing private investment for climate and green growth in Africa", with the attendance of about 4,000 participants from 81 countries, Fakih said that the failure of African countries to implement these critical reforms will lead to the emergence of an amorphous business climate that lacks competitiveness.
In this regard, he called for the lifting of financial restrictions that hinder the advancement of development in Africa, urging financiers to take concrete and specific decisions for the benefit of the peoples of the continent and avoid successive promises.
He pointed out that the African continent is subject to unfair tax charges as it is a high-risk region, and is often subjected to downgrade by international agencies, which negatively affects the confidence of foreign investors in this market.
The Chairperson of the African Union Commission expressed the hope that these annual meetings will not be another occasion to discuss the often-delayed financing of Africa, noting the importance of the talks to focus on ways to find optimal financing mechanisms and achieve win-win partnership.
For his part, the Governor of the Bank of Egypt and the Chairman of the Board of Governors of the African Development Bank Group, Hassan Abdullah, spoke about the important financing gap facing the African countries to reduce the effects of climate change, pointing out that the volume of domestic and international financial financing allocated to this in Africa did not exceed 12 percent of the total financing required in 2020, equivalent to about $30 billion.
He pointed out that climate change has led to increasing economic pressures on the continent and widening funding gaps due to the decline in the volume of international aid, the heavy debt burden and the increasing costs of social precaution, which hindered the implementation of development plans of African governments.
Climate change has also reduced the water resources of 75 to 250 million people in Africa and halved the rate of agricultural production based on rainwater, he said.
In the same context, the Governor of the Central Bank of Egypt called for the need to encourage the private sector to provide investments for the benefit of the climate and strengthen the partnership between the public and private sectors.
He praised the importance of the role of the African Development Bank in enhancing the confidence of private investors.
Abdullah said that the convening of the African Bank meetings for 2023 coincides with the emergence of many challenges for African countries, such as the disruption of the performance of the financial sector, increasing inflationary and geopolitical pressures, as well as the repercussions of the COVID-19 crisis.
For his part, the President of the Arab Republic of Egypt, Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, called on multilateral financial institutions to reconsider the criteria and conditions that qualify countries to obtain soft loans to become available to low- and middle-income countries, especially in light of the high cost of borrowing and increased debt service burdens and its negative repercussions on the budget of these countries.
Al-Sisi said that climate changes have cast a shadow on all countries of the world and have further affected the least developed countries through the frequency of drought, the expansion of desertification and the reduction of the rate of agricultural production.
Drought-related risks in Africa alone have led to losses of more than $70 billion and a 43 percent decline in agricultural production growth.

Rising prices and declining water resources.
Morocco ’ s Green Plan Criticisms, Calls for Climate Change Alternatives
Rabat – More than 10 years after the launch of the Green Morocco Plan, controversy has been raised over its results in conjunction with the rise in the prices of agricultural products such as vegetables, meat, poultry and eggs in recent months.
While the government says agricultural production has increased over the past decade, agricultural exports have tripled, the agricultural trade deficit has narrowed, and job opportunities have risen in villages, critics say the scheme has failed to achieve food security by marginalizing domestic market needs, focusing on exports and reducing subsistence crops, while others accuse it of draining water resources for promoting water-depleting crops such as avocados, melons and watermelons. Others, at a time when the country is suffering from water scarcity, and a number of villages live in the summer in the impact of thirst crises.
Positive results and criticism
Moroccan Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch defended the Green Morocco Plan to parliamentarians during his recent attendance at the monthly accountability session on food sovereignty.
Akhannouch, who was agriculture minister for 14 years and oversaw the development and implementation of the plan, said the accusations were far from the truth given the positive results achieved in the agricultural sector over the past decade.
According to the data presented by the Prime Minister to the deputies of the parliament, the green plan contributed to doubling the agricultural GDP to exceed the ceiling of 127 billion dirhams (about 13 billion dollars) in 2021, and doubling exports three times, while being able to create more than 50 million additional working days with an employment rate of 75% in rural areas.
According to the same source, the coverage of basic consumption needs of red meat, poultry, eggs, vegetables, fruits and milk during the period between 2008 and 2020 reached between 98 and 100%, and the efforts made to reduce the deficit of the agricultural trade balance, where the coverage of imports by agricultural exports went from 49% in 2008 to 65% in 2020.
According to the Moroccan Prime Minister, the recent instability of the agricultural price system is due to what he called the “exceptional and transient periods ” witnessed by the Kingdom, which directly affected the productivity of agricultural crops.
These are the consequences of the health crisis, which directly affected the balance in the animal sector, especially red meat and milk, and then drought and climate fluctuations.
On the other hand, critics of the Green Morocco Plan, especially the opposition parliamentary groups, believe that the plan focused on an export-oriented agricultural pattern at the expense of the consumption-oriented one, and reduced subsistence agriculture, which became a threat to food security.
They added that the agricultural strategies in place for years have contributed to the deepening of the water crisis, denouncing the promotion of water-depleting crops while the Kingdom is living under water stress with successive drought years.
Environmental groups have repeatedly warned against these crops, which have turned cities and villages, especially in the southeast, into thirsty areas.
Between Export and Domestic Market
The director of the government work observatory, Mohammed Jadri, believes that the green plan has achieved important achievements, but it has witnessed a number of shortcomings and negatives.
He explained to Al Jazeera Net that the scheme contributed significantly to achieving self-sufficiency of red and white meat, eggs, vegetables and fruits, and created jobs in the rural environment, and contributed to the introduction of hard currency, but it could not reduce dependence abroad in terms of fertilizers, feed, energy cost and mitigation of vulnerability to climate fluctuations.
For his part, Badr Zaher Azraq, professor of economics at Hassan II University, believes that the scheme has succeeded in achieving a number of its objectives, especially with regard to increasing cultivated areas, whether in grains, vegetables, acids and fruits, diversifying the crop map, and raising the added value of agriculture as a result of the high volume and value of exports, especially in 2022.
According to data from the Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, for the first time, exports of agricultural and marine food products exceeded the threshold of 80 billion dirhams in 2022 (about 8 billion dollars), which represents an increase of about 20% compared to 2021.
Fresh fruit and vegetable exports reached 2.3 million tons in 2022 at an annual growth rate of 10%, while red fruit exports grew by 20% to 132,000 tons.
However, Azraq points out that large farmers have upset the balances that have been in place for years with the emergence of new export destinations.
He pointed out that the government agreed with the major farmers on the basis of exporting part of the products to Europe and keeping part of them in the internal market to avoid any shortage, but the emergence of new export destinations, especially in the African continent, prompted the major farmers to export their products to it instead of selling them in the internal market in search of greater profit.
Azraq adds that the objectives set by the Green Plan regarding improving the conditions of small farmers, raising their purchasing power and establishing a middle peasant class were not achieved, but the benefit remained limited to large farmers, which calls for a review of the directions of this plan.
Correction of errors
The Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries has developed a new plan called the "Green Generation", which is the result of a set of achievements of the Green Morocco Plan, and aims by 2030 to strengthen the agricultural middle class, sustain agricultural development and double agricultural GDP and exports.
Mohammed Jadri believes that the green generation emphasizes the importance of human capital and the need to use scientific research in order to develop national crops, in addition to moving away from crops that drain water such as red melons, strawberries and avocados.
He points out that the bet today should be to return to subsistence agriculture and increase the areas cultivated with cereals, barley, maize, beets, sugar cane and oily plants, which are essential for the local consumer.
Bader Azraq stresses the need for the Green Generation Plan to build on the successes of the Green Morocco Plan, taking into account the failures to correct and overcome them to achieve food and water security, and to achieve the goal of contributing agriculture to the economy in a sustainable and stable manner.
He believes that the Kingdom is aware today of the importance of correcting mistakes, which is reflected in public policies and public investment trends, part of which has been allocated to the water sector and the agricultural sector.
Azraq calls for the provision of strategic stocks of wheat and barley in the rainy years to meet the needs and avoid high prices in the dry years, and stresses the need to transform the agricultural sector from a sector that exports agricultural raw materials to a sector that engages in the industrial scene, especially manufacturing and food industries; which will raise the value of agricultural exports and make a qualitative leap in the sector.
Will agriculture continue to be the backbone of the economy?
In light of climate change and successive years of drought, the question arises about the dependence of the Moroccan economy on agriculture, although this trend is strategic with the state of water stress in the Kingdom and the sharp decline in its water resources?
Azraq believes that dependence on the agricultural sector is dependent on a relatively fragile sector because of its link to international contexts and also to climatic disturbances, and points out that the successive years of drought have had a significant impact on growth rates in the last two years, as well as on a number of sectors related to agriculture.
He said that Morocco is aware of this situation, so it has been trying hard for two decades now and has become more accelerated in order to raise the productivity of a number of industrial sectors, such as the automotive, aircraft and technology industries and opening up to other industries such as the pharmaceutical and defense industries.
For Mohamed Djadri, continued investment in the agricultural sector is an urgent necessity for Morocco, because it is necessary to achieve self-sufficiency in red and white meat, eggs, vegetables and fruits, regardless of the changes in the international markets, but he believes that it is necessary to break with the past, work to provide fertilizers and feed locally, continue investing in renewable energies in order to reduce the energy cost for farmers, solve the water stress problem through water treatment. the construction of more seawater desalination plants and the construction of small and medium dams.

Saudi Arabia and Canada agree to restore diplomatic ties
Canadian Foreign Minister Melanie Jolie announced that the two countries will appoint ambassadors to each other.
Ottawa has named Jean-Philippe Lanto as its envoy to Riyadh.
Bin Salman (Gettyimages)
Saudi Arabia and Canada announced on Wednesday an agreement to restore their diplomatic relations and to close a dispute that erupted in 2018, including the expulsion of representatives and the suspension of commercial dealings, after Ottawa condemned Riyadh on the basis of its human rights record.
The kingdom ’ s foreign ministry said the agreement was mainly due to talks held by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Bangkok in November 2022.
"With the desire of both sides to restore diplomatic relations between the two countries on the basis of mutual respect and common interests, it has been decided to restore the level of diplomatic relations with Canada to the status quo ante," it said in a statement.
The Canadian Foreign Ministry confirmed the agreement on the return of relations to the previous one.
Canadian Foreign Minister Melanie Jolie announced that the two countries would appoint ambassadors to each other.
Ottawa has named Jean-Philippe Lanto as its envoy to Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia did not specify who it chose to represent.
Riyadh announced in August 2018 that it had asked the Canadian ambassador to leave, recalled its ambassador in Ottawa, and froze business dealings with Canada because of what it considered “interference ” by the latter in its internal affairs.
The move followed a strong demand by Ottawa for Riyadh ’ s immediate release of civil society activists arrested by Saudi authorities as part of a wave of arrests at the time.
Saudi Arabia reiterated its rejection of diktats and any interference in its internal affairs.
Canada said it was "deeply concerned" by the move, but said it would "always stand up for the protection of human rights, especially women's rights and freedom of expression around the world".
Trudeau's government "will not hesitate to promote these values and we believe that this dialogue is essential to international diplomacy," she said.
The move to expel the ambassador entailed measures such as Saudi Arabia halting its student scholarship programs to Canada, while Arab countries took positions supporting the kingdom in the crisis.
The re-establishment of ties comes in the context of a series of recent diplomatic moves by Riyadh, which analysts believe reflect the ambitions of Saudi Arabia, especially the de facto ruler of the kingdom, Prince Mohammed bin Salman, to strengthen its presence on the world stage.
One of the most notable moves in recent months has been the signing of a Chinese-sponsored deal to resume ties with Iran ’ s main regional rival after years of estrangement.
Riyadh also restored diplomatic relations with the Syrian regime after they were severed following the outbreak of the conflict in Syria in 2011, and welcomed President Bashar al-Assad to the Arab summit it hosted in Jeddah last week.
The summit itself saw the surprise participation of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, whose country has been facing a large-scale invasion of Russia since early last year.
Riyadh has also opened channels of communication with the Houthi rebels in a bid to end the war it is leading against them in Yemen.
Saudi Arabia hosts representatives of both sides in the Sudanese conflict and, in cooperation with the United States, announced their agreement to a seven-day truce that officially began on Monday night.
Analysts say Riyadh ’ s agenda is clear: to reduce unrest abroad and engage in economic and social reforms at home, especially Vision 2030, which is mainly aimed at diversifying sources of income and reducing dependence on oil revenues.
Despite a series of sweeping reforms spearheaded by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the kingdom ’ s human rights record continues to draw international criticism and from rights groups.
The kingdom has long been criticised for its high execution rates.
The Saudi authorities say that the defendants have exhausted all stages of litigation, stressing that "the government of the Kingdom is keen to establish security, achieve justice and implement the provisions of God in all those who encroach on the safe."
In 2022, 147 people were executed, more than double the 69 executions in 2021, according to an AFP tally.

Turmeric: scientific research on its benefits
- Alzheimer 's disease
There is not enough clinical data to say that turmeric is beneficial for Alzheimer ’ s patients.
You may be interested to learn about ways to prevent Alzheimer ’ s.
- Cancer.
The research is very active in this area and awaits the results of several clinical trials.
But researchers believe that the antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects of curcumin may play a role in preventing and treating cancer.
In vitro studies already indicate that curcumin inhibits the proliferation of cancer cells by acting at various points in their development and promotes the production of enzymes that help the body get rid of cancer cells.
According to epidemiological data, the prevalence of many cancers (colon, breast, prostate and lung) is lower in Asian countries, where much turmeric is consumed.
In addition, several studies in animals exposed to carcinogens indicate that curcumin can prevent many types of cancer (lung, colon, stomach, liver, skin, breast, esophagus, lymphoma, leukemia).
When used alone or in combination with chemotherapy, curcumin (8 g daily) has, in a few cases, stabilized the development of pancreatic cancer.
This effect has also been observed in patients with colorectal cancer.
- Peptic ulcer
Laboratory and animal studies indicate that turmeric has protective effects on the gastric mucosa and can destroy or inhibit the bacterium Helicobacter pylori, which is responsible for most stomach and duodenal ulcers.
- Chronic inflammatory diseases
In India and China, turmeric has been used for a very long time for its anti-inflammatory properties.
Laboratory and animal trials have shown positive results for the treatment of ulcerative colitis, rheumatoid arthritis and pancreatitis.
In humans, the data is still incomplete and we will have to wait for the results of several ongoing clinical trials to get a more accurate idea of its effectiveness.
- Arthritis
Compared to traditional anti-inflammatory drugs, curcumin (1200 mg daily) has been shown to be as effective as phenylbutazone in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.
As for turmeric, doses of 2 grams per day for 6 weeks produced effects similar to ibuprofen (800 mg per day) in people with osteoporosis.
You may be interested in a natural treatment for osteoporosis.
- Inflammatory bowel diseases
Standard turmeric extract has been used successfully in people with irritable bowel syndrome.
The two doses, equivalent to 72 mg and 144 mg of curcumin per day, were tested, reducing symptoms and improving patient comfort.
Other experiments are underway in America.
- Cardiovascular diseases
Only one study has been done so far to assess whether physical exercise, along with turmeric consumption (150 mg per day in postmenopausal women with left ventricular dysfunction), is appropriate.
The results suggest that turmeric combined with physical exercise significantly reduced body mass, body mass index as well as aortic blood pressure.
Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.
- Gingivitis
A randomized study has shown that turmeric mouthwash reduces bacterial contamination as effectively as the mouthwash available in pharmacies.
- Diabetes
Two studies reported a possible protective effect of turmeric at the onset of diabetes.
- High blood lipids
Animal studies suggest that turmeric lowers cholesterol levels, especially the harmful LDL cholesterol.
- Digestive disorders
Committee E and WHO recognize the effectiveness of turmeric root in the treatment of indigestion, that is, digestive disorders, such as stomach pain, nausea, loss of appetite or a feeling of heaviness.

NASA's CPEX-CV mission answers now with details
NASA ’ s CPEX-CV mission in September 2022 collected extensive data on the early stages of hurricane formation off the northwest coast of Africa, providing insight into how dust, moisture, clouds and the ocean interact to influence storm evolution.
When dust from Africa ’ s Sahel-Saharan regions mixes with tropical clouds, it creates what is known as a “disturbance ” of rain in the eastern Atlantic. [1] These disturbances are hurricanes in their smallest form, and as they travel across the ocean, they can dissipate or turn into powerful storms.
To study these small storms, a group of NASA scientists in September 2022 spent months on a flight off the northwest coast of Africa aboard NASA ’ s DC-8 research plane, each day the team took off from Cabo Verde, an island nation off the west coast of Africa, recording nearly 100 hours as the mission, known as the Cabo Verde Thermal Operations Experiment (CPEX-CV), released its data publicly in 1. April.
The CPEX-CV team worked from September 1 to 30, 2022, using the latest remote sensors, radars, radiometers and projectors – lightweight 11-inch tubes with a parachute dropped from the aircraft to measure wind, temperature and humidity.
Will McCarty, a CPEX program scientist based at NASA headquarters in Washington, D.C., said: “Coupled with the global image provided by satellites, this data provides finer details that can only be measured by an aircraft equipped with instruments, ” according to scitechdaily.
These observations provide a window into how dust, moisture, clouds, and the ocean interact to either build or prevent the intensification of rainstorms that are likely to turn into hurricanes, this data, open and publicly available, will benefit researchers and weather forecasters, especially those in the atmospheric science community, according to Amin Nahrer, a research scientist based at NASA ’ s Langley Research Center in Virginia.
"This can be considered discovery data, which will inevitably help answer questions that have not yet been asked in the coming years," said Nahrir.
Once the aircraft was above the clouds, the onboard remote sensors captured detailed profiles of desert dust, wind speed and direction, temperature, humidity, convection structure and rain within clouds. Together, these measurements provide a comprehensive, multidimensional view of what is in the air over the Northeast Atlantic Ocean, highlighting how these variables impact. Weather systems in childhood.
Several times in the campaign, the DC-8 flew through the Transtropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), an area where the northeast and southeast trade winds meet together, ITCZ sailors are known as “calm ” because of its windy weather, and Nahrir said some of the world ’ s most remote oceans make up the international trade zone.
"What struck me most was my ability to look out the window and see how the clouds have changed as far as the eye can see from the faint swollen clouds to cloud streets to convection systems, and you can see the evolution of convection systems all in one shot."
“Nine science projects and 10 hardware and support teams were funded under this campaign, so these investigators helped plan the mission, and now they ’ re going to return this data to their local institutions to see what they can do, ” McCarty said.

Global Warning: Artificial Intelligence Threatens Extinction of Humanity
2023 / 05 / 30 | 22: 13 - Source: Baghdad Today
(News of the Day) - Baghdad Today - Follow
A group of scientists and technology experts on Tuesday issued a new statement on what they called the dangers posed by artificial intelligence, calling for the need to confront them as the world faces crises such as epidemics and nuclear wars.
“Mitigating the risk of human extinction from artificial intelligence should be a global priority with other risks such as pandemics and nuclear war. ”
Notable signatories to the statement include Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, who is responsible for the program “Chat GBT ”, Jeffrey Hinton, a computer scientist known as the father of artificial intelligence, Kevin Scott, chief technology officer at Microsoft, and others.
The statement focuses on growing concerns about the threat of artificial intelligence, with experts in the technology saying that the world is still far from developing the types of artificial intelligence that reach the limits of science fiction.
But with increased investment and ongoing debate over the AI industry, there have been calls for the technology to be regulated before disasters strike.
Concerns are growing about AI systems that may override human intelligence or get out of control with the emergence of a new generation of high-powered AI chatbots such as Chat GBT.
More than 1,000 researchers and technology experts, including Twitter and Tesla owner Elon Musk, signed a letter earlier this year calling for a six-month moratorium on the development of artificial intelligence systems, which could pose significant risks to society and humanity.
Dan Hendricks, director of the Center for Artificial Intelligence Safety, said in a tweet Tuesday that this statement will not hinder society from facing other forms of AI-induced risks such as bias or misinformation.
Hendricks compared the statement to warnings by nuclear scientists about what they had already made.
Countries around the world have begun to take steps to draft regulations and rules related to the development of artificial intelligence technology, and the European Union announced the “artificial intelligence ” law expected to be passed later this year.
Hinton, the spiritual father of artificial intelligence, told The New York Times that applications like the chatbot “can indeed turn into a tool for spreading misinformation, and may very soon pose a threat to jobs and to humanity as a whole. ”
President Joe Biden has previously urged Congress to pass laws that would place stricter restrictions on the tech sector.
The White House has urged new steps to “promote responsible American innovation in artificial intelligence, ” including a $140 million fund to expand research on artificial intelligence and a rating system to work with big companies to“ correct ” some of the controversies around artificial intelligence.
OpenAI launched the chatbot in November and has been popular with users, but there have been significant privacy concerns, political bias, or other security concerns related to the software.

BEIRUT – Cutting carbs and feeding the body fat is a common dietary strategy called the keto diet.
Intermittent fasting based on eating during limited hours is also an effective system, so some tend to mix the two systems with the aim of rapid weight loss.
Some experts, including Professor Jason Fong, author of The Obesity Code, recommend using the keto system as a basis for intermittent fasting, and said that this combination targets fat areas and is therefore useful in case of suffering from localized obesity.
What is the keto diet?
Photo by Freepik
Research shows that scientists originally designed a keto diet in the 1920s to help control seizures in children with epilepsy.
Keto is based on eating 3 to 4 grams (g) of fat per 1 gram of carbohydrates and protein.
The keto that many use for weight loss today is a little different in that it is high in fat, medium in protein, and low in carbs.
Fat makes up about 80 percent of your daily calories, and aim to consume between 20 grams and 50 grams of net carbs depending on your personal needs.
The list of keto diet foods is devoid of most carbohydrates, even healthy foods such as fiber-rich whole grains and most fruits, with priority given to fats, such as avocado and olive oil.
The idea in the keto diet is that it pushes the body towards burning fat for energy called this ketogenic state or keto.
Instead of relying on glucose and carbohydrates.
What do you think about learning more about the 5 types of cheese allowed and forbidden in the keto diet
How does intermittent fasting work?
Photo by Freepik
Intermittent fasting is a diet based on time and not the type of food, the day is divided into fasting hours and eating hours, and there are more than one plan but the months between them are to stop eating within 16 hours while eating is allowed in the remaining 8 hours of the day.
Intermittent fasting diet plays an important role in the treatment of obesity and insulin resistance (the hallmark of type 2 diabetes) and is also effective in cases of localized obesity.
Experts recommend eating between 1200 and 1800 calories between 8 am and 4 pm, or at any time you choose, and some prefer to adopt another diet during the hours of eating and to be keto to be doubly effective.
Why mixing intermittent fasting with keto has become popular for weight loss?
Photo by Freepik
A keto diet with intermittent fasting can help you lose weight in the short term, although every diet is very restrictive, so it ’ s definitely not a one-size-fits-all method.
The keto diet increases the levels of ketones in the body.
During fasting times, ketones also increase.
The brain will rely less on glucose for energy when it is in the state of dietary ketosis.
Therefore, the transition to a fasting state (ketogenic) eventually becomes smooth after eating a low carbohydrate or ketogenic intake for a few weeks.
Who should try the keto diet with intermittent fasting?
Photo by AdobeStock
Anyone who has been on the keto regimen for more than two weeks and wants to add intermittent fasting can do so — but only after seeing a doctor.
It may not be suitable for people who follow the keto diet as part of a diabetes treatment plan.
Asking these patients not to eat for a long time can be dangerous.
Also, if you have chronic kidney disease, have a history of eating disorders, are undergoing active cancer treatment, or are pregnant or breastfeeding, it is not advisable to follow these two diets together.

Is the African continent emerging from the trap of external debt?, a question that is frequently asked in the economic circles and its discussions have become a fatty substance on the table of analysts and experts, especially since the prospects for the ability of African countries to bear debt are still unclear, according to statements recently made by Andrew Dabalin, chief economist for the Africa region at the World Bank.
According to the World Bank, nearly half of sub-Saharan Africa ’ s countries are in default or at high risk of default this year, while inflation is expected to be double-digit across much of the continent with a growth rate of 3.1 percent in 2023.
The debt of African countries is estimated at $1 trillion in 2022, doubling five times since 2000, 66 percent of the debt is concentrated in nine countries, led by South Africa, while 22 countries are unable to meet their financial obligations to creditors, according to the International Monetary Fund, which pointed out that debt installments of about $100 billion annually strained the budgets of many countries and cut more than 15 percent of GDP.
Domestic resource gap
The main reason for resorting to external debt and borrowing is the gap between the investment rate required to achieve the target growth rate and the domestic savings rate, pointing to the expansion of the public debt of Africa, where the debt levels in middle-income countries reached unprecedented levels in modern history, as global debt rose to 28 percent of GDP in 2020. Increased government spending in response to the coronavirus outbreak and loss of revenue due to economic recession.
Stifling investment and undermining growth
Of the total external debt of the African continent, for example, South Africa owns 15 percent, Egypt 13 percent, Angola 7 percent, Morocco and Sudan 6 percent each, while Tunisia, Kenya and Zambia each own 4 percent. Public finances in highly leveraged countries such as Angola, Sudan, Tunisia, and Zambia ranked uncomfortably high in a longer list of countries including Cameroon, Chad, Djibouti, Ghana, Mauritania, Mozambique, and Senegal.
“The heavy debt burden on public finances will continue to undermine the ability to channel funds into economic and social development projects and undermine the resilience to external shocks. ”
But what is the level of external debt that has a negative impact on economic growth?
“External debt can be beneficial if it reduces liquidity constraints, provides an additional source of financing for development and meets the needs of the necessary infrastructure for growth, but external debt affects growth by reducing capital accumulation, which leads investors to lower their expectations of returns due to their expectation of higher tax rates, and also constrains African economic growth by reducing the productivity of production elements because African countries are less willing to adopt more expensive policies. ” Finally, economic growth is negatively affected indirectly through the impact on public spending on social services, education and health, in addition to weak exports, weak savings mobilization, and high inflation as African countries begin to pay off their external debt service.
Safe Limits of External Debt
A high external debt stock can have a negative impact on economic growth through a negative impact on private investment due to the expectation that governments may increase taxes in the future to service debt, so foreign and domestic investors will refrain from investing in debtor countries, leading to lower economic growth, according to Dr. El Shennawi, who explained that the safe limit for external debt is 150 percent of GDP. If the state wants more hedging, the safe limits of debt can be considered to be in the range of 100 percent.
Economic expert Dr. El Shennawi proposes a scenario to get rid of Africa ’ s external debt trap according to four axes:
Public debt is unavoidable
It is not possible to imagine a situation in which any state or government can run its operations without debt, and in estimating this inevitability, the questions that must be asked while seeking to dismantle this structure are, where does religion come from, how is it used, and what are the terms associated with it?
The source of the use and justification of religion are therefore crucial considerations.
• Capital controls
The ultimate goal of the Bretton Woods institutions was, and remains, to protect the interests of international companies by ensuring that African economies offer investor-friendly environments, that African economies are characterized by low wages and consistently low labor costs, and that African economies do not maintain capital controls, so that capital inflows and outflows remain easy.
It also does so by anchoring export-oriented growth strategies even in economies that are unable to produce and export adequately, exacerbating their balance of payments.
• Debt crisis cannot be avoided without focusing on growth
As long as policymakers put the importance of growth aside, we must forget Africa ’ s ability to emerge from the debt crisis.
Yet despite this fact, “neoliberalism ” (an ideological ideology based on economic liberalism) systematically creates a framework that makes it impossible for African governments to focus on growth.
Dismantling the neoliberal model
The focus of neoliberal policy reforms is inappropriate for Africa because of the same initial arguments that African governments have used in order to pursue mixed economies — economies in which the government plays a leading role, not only as a arbiter but also in facilitating and even leading the expansion of productive capacities.
Desperate move to restore macroeconomics
Economist Ali Hamoudi told Sky News Arabia: “African countries have faced financial difficulties for many years, and with the accumulation of debt on some African economies due to increased borrowing amid unexpected domestic expenditures, African countries resorted to default on their external debt or threatened to default in a desperate move to restore macroeconomic and debt sustainability.
As an example in 2021, six countries – Chad, Eritrea, Mozambique, the Republic of Congo, South Sudan and Zimbabwe – were classified as having distressed debt as African governments issued a record $7.5 billion in sovereign bonds, 10 times more than in 2016, and the IMF changed Zambia and Ethiopia ’ s ratings from moderate to high risk.
This year, with rising global inflation, rising borrowing rates, and a strong dollar, paying off debt and generating money has become more difficult, making the situation very complicated in a number of countries such as Ghana, Malawi, Zambia, Tunisia and Egypt, according to Hamoudi.
Economist Hamoudi adds: “I am not surprised to see some African countries default on their external debt, most of these African countries have high debt ratios relative to GDP, and spend a larger proportion of their revenues on debt service financing, which is not sustainable, and it is expected that they will reach a point of imbalance that will make it impossible to pay their debts. ”

Less seats and more passengers
PARIS (AFP) - Ticket prices are likely to continue to rise in the long term despite the recent drop in oil prices, aviation experts say.
In 2022, the gradual return of travel demand, following the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions, prompted several regions of the world to raise ticket prices.
But this year, as airlines seek to restore pre-COVID-19 passenger numbers, price volatility has peaked.
In France in April, travelers had to pay an average of 32.6% more than they did four years ago for the same flight.
The increase was up to 51% for flights from France to the Asia-Pacific region.
In the United States, the travel ticket price index published by the Federal Reserve in Saint-Louis shows an increase of 11% between April 2019 and April 2023.
These increases are occurring despite the stabilization of kerosene prices, which peaked after the start of the Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The International Air Transport Association estimates that prices will fall this year to $98.5 per barrel, compared to $135.5 per barrel last year.
Fuel accounts for between 25% and 30% of airline costs and usually has a significant impact on ticket prices.
However, the price decline is long overdue.
In addition to fuel, “labor costs and other costs associated with the supply chain […]
They ’ re getting higher or rising, ” says Air Transport Association chief economist Mary Owens Thomsen.
“Companies need to find a way to cover these costs or they will start losing money again, ” she said this weekend in Istanbul at the General Assembly of her foundation of 300 air carriers around the world, while they are barely returning to the safety zone and have to pay off huge debts from the period of the COVID-19 crisis.
– Deficiency and inflation –
Vic Krishnan, an aviation expert at the McKinsey Strategic Consulting Center, said the key issue was not “oil prices, but rather the lack of enough seats on planes with a large number of passengers. ”
Although their order books are sometimes complete until the end of the decade, aircraft manufacturers struggle to meet their delivery goals due to the lack of parts or materials at their suppliers.
There is also the issue of “the cost of labor and many companies have had to negotiate higher wages for pilots and crew, ” according to Jeffrey Weston, a consultant at Pine & Company.
That ’ s also the case for operations companies on the ground, which had to “pay significantly higher salaries out of the COVID-19 crisis ” for couriers and mechanics, he said.
Pascal Faber, an aviation expert at Alex Partners, said: “There are not many factors that can reduce ticket prices.
Carlos Munoz, president of Spain ’ s low-cost airline Polotia, said: “With my peers, we all have the same impression, demand is still very strong despite macroeconomic headwinds. ”
But while the aviation industry will have to invest trillions of dollars to try to decarbonize by 2050 in new aircraft and renewable fuel, Mary Owens Thomsen sees no respite for consumers.
“Costs will rise until we reach commercially viable solutions that are mass-produced, ” she says.

It is often seen as an attractive funding source for companies and sovereigns looking to diversify their funding and access low-cost capital.

Fundraising in Egypt also marks the first time an African country has reached this lucrative market.

Mohammed bin Salman ’ s change to the kingdom ’ s image is happening quickly and the danger lies in the time to reach the core
Middle East
Publish
11 minutes read
Analysis by Nick Robertson, CNN's Middle East Newsletter.
To subscribe to the newsletter (click here)
LONDON, United Kingdom (CNN) -- Saudi Arabia has made headlines recently, this time to try to find its place in the world of sports.
She's spending a lot of money.
In an announcement that shocked the world of sports last Tuesday, the US-based PGA Tour Golf Association announced a merger with its Saudi-backed rival LIV Golf and the Dubai-sponsored DP World Tour (formerly known as the European Tour), ending a dispute that dominated male pro golf last year.
News of the partnership has become the talk in several capitals and stadiums around the world.
Meanwhile, the Saudi Professional League welcomed the winner of the Golden Ball French player Karim Benzema, to catch up with his teammate who previously joined the Saudi league Portuguese football star Cristiano Ronaldo, who is said to earn $200 million a season.
Perhaps the last time many people showed so much interest in the kingdom was in 2018 when journalist Jamal Khashoggi was killed by Saudi government agents in the Saudi consulate in Istanbul.
The golf coup of that partnership may have been the sporting achievement so far of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
He has already secured a spot on the F1 circuit, hosted all boxing matches as well as organising a series of global and regional music events to impress local audiences who considered all this far from reality for them.
None of this was possible before Mohammed bin Salman came to power.
The speed and scale of his changes have earned him popularity among many of the country ’ s youth, which is as unexpected as it is rare in Saudi history.
Fame in sport is built on moments of brilliance.
Unlike politics where it is slowly won.
Decisions can usually take years to mature and yield benefits, but for Mohammed bin Salman it is different.
He's in a hurry.
In fact, he consolidated his power by shaking up the old guard in 2017, many of whom were potential contenders for power.
More than 200 members of the royal family and businessmen were detained at the Ritz Hotel in Riyadh that year over allegations of corruption.
The result is that once vibrant and vocal members of the royal family with strong royal assets have much less influence today and little chance of gaining it.
Arguably among some of Mohammed bin Salman ’ s Western partners, he is still seen as a potentially dangerous interlocutor.
For them, he is seen as responsible for sending the team that killed, sliced and burned Khashoggi, who has been critical of Mohammed bin Salman ’ s high-speed reforms.
Mohammed bin Salman has denied any personal involvement in Khashoggi ’ s killing but has taken full responsibility as the country ’ s leader.
Khashoggi ’ s killing has tarnished Mohammed bin Salman ’ s reputation and may have derailed his father King Salman ’ s ambitions for him to modernize the kingdom.
In 2015, when King Salman came to the throne, the nation was fossilized, its royal office and bureaucracy were arrogant and rigid, and according to the accounts of many Saudis “very corrupt. ”
The conservative religious police took control of the streets and women were banned from driving.
The country has been stuck in a cultural time crisis since its rulers panicked when Muslim extremists stormed the Grand Mosque in 1979, members of the royal family feared for their future and pacified Islamists by giving conservative clerics a huge role in running the kingdom.
A different regional player
By the time King Salman came to power, the 21st century was passing through Saudi Arabia without the benefit of it.
The larger and more powerful Gulf kingdom was culturally different, decades behind its neighbors in business and development, woefully below its capabilities.
That was until King Salman empowered Mohammed bin Salman, not his eldest son, but his chosen son to fix it.
The LIV Golf Championship is the latest example, not only of his intention to do so, but of what he went through before achieving it.
Since coming to power, he has banished the religious police almost overnight, shrinking the space for religion in public life and replacing it with a new kind of Saudi nationalism.
Women were allowed to go to football stadiums with men, and national day parties were held outdoors in the streets with music and dance, unheard of before the Mohammed bin Salman era.
The changes didn ’ t stop there, emancipation allowed unmarried men and women to sit together in cafes, work in the same office, and shop in stores together.
New neighborhoods have sprung up in Riyadh to meet a new lifestyle.
Extremely modern office complexes dotted with fountains and palm trees sprang up, and roadside cafes, which looked like Dubai, lured young people out of their homes.
Mohammed bin Salman is the architect of a new and freer lifestyle for many, but those who skip it and ask on social media skeptical of his decisions risk their disappearance.
Even the few who were released after international pressure, such as Loujain al-Hathloul, have been released from prison, but cannot leave the country and have been warned to keep their thoughts to themselves or risk going back to prison.
But despite the rough edges, there is a soft force at work.
Saudi Arabia recently started to build an extravagant football league with expensive European stars.
Mohammed bin Salman wants the world to take him just as seriously as many of his fellow citizens seem to be doing now.
Chinese President Xi Jinping has become an increasingly close geostrategic partner, and Russian President Vladimir Putin is benefiting at least for now, with Mohammed bin Salman cutting oil production, ignoring U.S. concerns that high oil prices are helping Moscow pay for its war in Ukraine.
The crown prince has also embarked on a regional and international diplomatic track aimed at making the kingdom a bigger player on the world stage.
Saudi Arabia has led efforts to bring Syria out of isolation and has tried to mediate conflicts such as those in Sudan and even in Ukraine.
Mohammed bin Salman has begun mending ties with his former foes, from Turkey and the regime of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad to Houthi rebels in Yemen and even arch-foe Iran.
The prevailing idea is that he needs to ensure stability in order for his economic plans to succeed.
In terms of oil, it has made Saudi Arabia a bolder player.
Having been quick to respond to U.S. calls to open faucets and lower prices, the kingdom is now ignoring those requests, risking damage to its decades-old partnership with Washington.
The message is that Saudi interests come first.
These interests are to bring as many oil dollars as possible to the kingdom so that it does not fall into a budget deficit or see its mega projects fail.
What's best for his people?
Like Putin and Xi, Mohammed bin Salman wants what he believes is best for his people, meaning that the old model of affordable energy access in exchange for Western security guarantees that have moved Saudi Arabia to a cultural dead end is no longer an option.
Perception is everything.
America ’ s shift to Asia, its failure in 2011 to side with deposed allies during the Arab Spring, and now its support for Ukraine and what most Gulf Arabs see as misguided Western hegemony reeling from failed wars in Iraq and Afghanistan all help sharpen Mohammed bin Salman ’ s paths toward new relationships where he also has some support.
The United States wants to increase oil production, support Ukraine, and normalize relations with Israel.
But it ’ s on the streets of Riyadh and Jeddah where Mohammed bin Salman ’ s biggest potential challenges lie.
The clock is approaching Vision 2030, a bold and tumultuous reimagining of city life powered by non-oil industries.
It is not only a new way of living, but also securing the work necessary to meet the needs of the country ’ s huge young population.
Two-thirds of Saudis are under 35 and have finally been able, in part thanks to Mohammed bin Salman, to taste what their contemporaries have enjoyed in the outside world for years.
Saudi officials say Vision 2030 for a new city on the Red Sea and another mega project — the New Square — in the capital Riyadh may not even partially materialize, but it aims to inspire the country and investors.
These are great adventures to keep people at work, so they are happy in their lives and less likely to challenge Mohammed bin Salman ’ s autocratic rule.
Plans of this magnitude are often realized over generations rather than the lifetime of a generation already living and yearning for a meaningful future.
Mohammed bin Salman, in a hurry, is attaching stability to a combination of ambition and an antidote to the people.
The process of changing the image is in full swing, but the longer it takes to get to the core, the greater the risk of failure.

Global Concerns About Artificial Intelligence
Artificial intelligence is the intelligence demonstrated by machines and programs that mimic human mental abilities and modes of operation.
Artificial intelligence algorithms are designed to make decisions, often using data in real time and at incredible speed.
They are unlike passive machines that can only respond mechanically or predetermined.
Using sensors, digital data or remote inputs, they collect and store information from a variety of different sources, immediately analyze the material, and act on the insights derived from that data.
The current anger around the world over artificial intelligence is unprecedented, as it is uniquely troubling.
The ultimate benefits of AI will be many, but its risks may outweigh its positive benefits.

While AI produces many other challenges, influential U.S. actors are now putting forward the theory of “possible adaptation. ”
To this end, prominent tech figures have suggested stopping the development of the next generation (such as OpenAI ’ s ChatGPT or Google Bard).

In their view, if the United States pauses or even slows down the development of this technology, while China does not, then Beijing will overtake Washington in the race of the Second Cold War to dominate the world.
But America ’ s technocrats have another view: The answer to this question begins with examining his hypothesis that an intense struggle against China is a foregone conclusion, a kind of unchanging geopolitical law.
It follows, therefore, that the AI challenge must take a back seat to this reality.
These experts ’ vision stems from a question: Isn ’ t it possible that at least the AI challenge is so important that, not the Second Cold War, it should be the organizing principle of U.S. foreign policy?

“My only hope, ” Hinton says, is that the two countries“ realize we ’ re all in the same boat, ” so they have to work together to keep AI under control.
Hinton cited the nuclear arms control agreements between the United States and the Soviet Union as a precedent.
Drafting a treaty and verifying parties ’ compliance is easier than in the case of artificial intelligence.
History shows that nuclear weapons can be curtailed even in the atmosphere of the cold war.

The existence of this world, according to them, suggests that a return to it is possible, even if it will require a sustained effort and a reordering of foreign policy priorities on both sides.

Oil spills are one of the most destructive forms of pollution, and occur when oil is released as a result of accidents during drilling, shipping and illegal dumping, and these events release large quantities of petroleum hydrocarbons, causing immediate and long-term damage to marine life.
Industrial activities release heavy metals such as mercury, lead and cadmium into marine environments, and these toxic substances accumulate in organisms through bioaccumulation and biomagnification, leading to severe health effects.
For example, mercury poisoning from contaminated seafood poses significant risks to human health and the survival of marine mammals.
The proliferation of plastic waste has also become a global environmental crisis, with plastics entering marine ecosystems through improper disposal and inappropriate waste management practices, and studies have shown that marine organisms often mistake plastic debris for food, leading to ingestion and entanglement.
This can lead to internal injuries, suffocation, and starvation, affecting both large marine animals and microorganisms.
The fragmentation of the larger plastic elements results in the formation of small plastic particles less than 5 mm in size, and according to researchers, these particles have infiltrated into the marine food chains, which affected a wide range of species, from organisms that feed filtration to the top predators, and proved studies published results during the past years, that microplastics can cause physical harm, hinder the success of reproduction, and disrupt Physiological processes in marine organisms.
Human activities, such as shipping, seismic exploration and military exercises, contribute to underwater noise pollution, where excessive noise interferes with the communication, feeding, mating and navigation capabilities of marine organisms, and scientific studies have linked noise pollution to responses to stress, hearing loss, behavior change, and reduced reproductive success in various marine species. Especially the discharge of hot water from power plants and industrial facilities, in thermal pollution in marine environments.
High water temperatures can adversely affect the survival, growth and reproduction of marine organisms, especially those that adapt to certain temperature ranges.
Coral bleaching, caused by rising sea surface temperatures, has become a major concern, leading to the loss of biodiversity in coral reef ecosystems.

Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are two closely related concepts that are revolutionizing various industries.
Artificial intelligence refers to the development of intelligent systems that can simulate human cognitive functions, while machine learning focuses on algorithms that enable systems to learn from data and improve their performance over time.
Artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms analyze vast amounts of data, recognize patterns, and make predictions without being explicitly programmed.
They use statistical techniques and mathematical models to process information and extract valuable insights.
From natural language processing and image recognition to recommendation systems and autonomous vehicles, artificial intelligence and machine learning have diverse applications.
By training models with relevant data, these techniques can make accurate predictions and perform complex tasks.
However, it is critical to address ethical concerns, biases and transparency to ensure responsible use.
The continuous advancement of artificial intelligence and machine learning opens up exciting possibilities for innovation, making it essential to understand the underlying principles and potential impact.

"Short term"!

Do you want to lose weight quickly?
Follow the fast of water – in which people consume nothing but water for several days.
It may help, but it ’ s not clear how long you ’ ll keep it, according to researchers from the University of Illinois at Chicago, who note that the metabolic benefits of water fasting, such as lowering blood pressure and improving cholesterol, seem to disappear soon after the fast ends.
Christa Faraday, professor of kinesiology and nutrition, who led the research published in Nutrition Reviews, and an expert on intermittent fasting, said: “There don ’ t seem to be any serious adverse effects for people who do water fasting or similar fasting as people consume very few calories a day.
My general conclusion is that you can try it, but it seems to require a lot of work, and all these metabolic benefits disappear. ”
However, Faraday stressed that no one should fast more than five days without medical supervision.
The new study is a review of eight studies on water fasting or Buschinger fasting, a medically supervised fasting common in Europe where people consume only a tiny amount of juice and soup a day.
The researchers found that fasting stimulated significant weight loss in the short term.
People who fasted for five days lost about 4% to 6% of their weight.
Also, those who fasted for seven to ten days lost about 2% to 10%, and those who fasted for 15 to 20 days lost 7% to 10%.
Despite this, people regained all that they had lost in water fasting for five days within three months.
Some of the studies involved participants with type 1 and type 2 diabetes, who did not experience any adverse effects of fasting, although they were closely monitored and their insulin doses were adjusted during fasting.
Faraday said the most common side effects of this prolonged fasting were similar to those caused by intermittent fasting, such as headaches, insomnia and hunger.
In addition, there were no serious adverse effects in studies, such as metabolic acidosis or death.
Faraday noted that participants in this prolonged fasting lost about two-thirds of their weight from muscle mass and one-third from fat mass.
This is the opposite of what happens most often during weight loss, where more fat is lost than muscle.
Faraday said it makes sense for this extreme fasting to have this result, because “your body needs a steady intake of protein.
If he doesn ’ t have it, he derives it from the muscles. ”
She added that she would encourage someone hoping to lose weight to try intermittent fasting instead of water fasting, “because there ’ s a lot of data showing that it can help with weight management. ”

But analysts said China ’ s development of artificial intelligence lags far behind its Western counterparts in several sectors, although there was one area where Beijing was ahead of Washington: regulation of artificial intelligence.
Chinese authorities have been very proactive about regulating some uses of AI, especially those that allow the general public to create their own content, and compliance has become a major obstacle for companies in the country.
Some Chinese companies have gone so far as to set their own rules, and Duane, the Chinese version of TikTok, requires the classification of content created by artificial intelligence, and that anyone posting on the platform register their real identities.
As the use of AI spreads, regulators in Washington and around the world are trying to figure out how to manage potential threats to privacy, employment, intellectual property, and even human existence itself.
Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer urged Congress last month to adopt “comprehensive ” regulations on the artificial intelligence industry.
But there are also concerns that putting up firewalls on technology in the United States will hand over leadership in the sector to Chinese companies.
Chinese companies have been investing in artificial intelligence for years — from putting surveillance cameras on city streets to using facial recognition technology to monitor the use of napkins in public toilets — and have long been at the forefront of surveillance technology.
But when it comes to other types of AI, Chinese companies lag behind their international counterparts, in part because the Chinese government tightly controls information and communications.
Instead of focusing on AI technology that lets the general public create unique content, such as chatbots and image generators, Chinese companies have focused on technologies with obvious commercial uses, such as surveillance technology.
As a result, in other areas of AI, such as large language models that support chatbots, Chinese companies have had to take advantage of models developed outside of China.
In a recent study, it was found that most of the large language models developed in China were about two years behind those developed in the US, a gap that would be difficult to close even if US companies had to adapt to regulation.
The gap also makes it harder for Chinese companies to attract the world ’ s best engineering talent, and many would prefer to work for companies that have the resources and flexibility to experiment in leading research areas.
While lawmakers in Washington argue about how to regulate artificial intelligence in a way that limits potential harm, they have the opportunity to achieve what Beijing has not achieved, which is to find a way to put firewalls on the technology without restricting its future development.
