The current state of the gender gap in technology
The gender gap in technology remains a significant problem, with women being underrepresented in technical roles and leadership positions across the industry.
Despite efforts to increase diversity in recent years, the gap remains.
According to a 2021 study, women held only about 25% of tech jobs worldwide.
Moreover, women made up only 17% of senior positions in tech companies, while the number of female CEOs or founders was only 10%.
One reason for this underrepresentation may be the “pipeline problem, ” referring to the lack of women graduating in computer science or other technology-related degrees.
A report by the National Center for Women and Information Technology (NCWIT) stated that in 2020, women earned only 19% of bachelor ’ s degrees in computer and information science.
This limited supply of female graduates can lead to a cyclical problem as fewer women enter the workforce, resulting in less representation in the industry, which in turn limits the number of female role models for future tech professionals.
Skillsoft ’ s Women in Technology Report 2023 revealed a rising gender imbalance, with nearly half (45%) of tech women surveyed indicating that men outnumber them in the workplace by ratios of four to one or higher.
This represents a significant rise compared to 25% who reported a similar situation in 2021.
Stereotypes surrounding gender roles in technology can also contribute to the gap.
The unconscious biases and discriminatory practices that stem from these stereotypes can create barriers for women, including less access to opportunities and resources, unequal pay, and a less inclusive work culture.
The importance of closing the gender gap
Closing the gender gap in technology is critical for several reasons:
• Improving Creativity and Innovation: Greater gender diversity leads to the emergence of different perspectives and methods to solve problems, foster creativity, and drive innovation within the industry.
• Improving financial performance: Research has consistently shown that companies with a diverse workforce are more profitable.
A study by McKinsey & Company found that companies in the top quartile for gender diversity in executive teams were 21% more likely to achieve above-average profitability than those in the bottom quartile.
More inclusive products and services: With a gender-balanced workforce, technology companies are better equipped to design products and services that meet the needs of both men and women, ensuring wider market appeal.
• Combat gender biases in hiring practices: Increasing gender diversity within tech companies helps break down unconscious biases in hiring and promotion decisions, ensuring a fair and more equitable workforce.
Gender diversity not only benefits individual companies but also contributes to positive social change because it helps reduce the under-representation of women in the tech industry in general.
Strategies to address the gender gap
Companies can adopt different strategies to address the gender gap in technology:
Creating an inclusive work environment: A welcoming and supportive work culture that prioritizes equality and inclusion in the workplace is essential to attract and retain women in technical roles.
This can be achieved by applying gender-neutral language to vacancies, providing diverse training for managers and staff, and advocating for flexible working arrangements.
Promote mentorship and sponsorship programs: By offering mentorship programs to women in technology, companies can help them meet challenges and develop their careers.
Sponsorship initiatives, where senior leaders advocate for career advancement for female employees, can also help women reach higher leadership positions within organizations.
Provide skills development programs: Opportunities to improve and reshape skills can benefit all employees, but they can play a vital role in helping women transition into technical roles or advance to senior positions.
By providing support for continuous learning, companies can grow a variety of talent and empower female employees to grow.
Setting and Tracking Diversity Targets: Setting specific and measurable targets focused on increasing women ’ s representation in the workforce, particularly in technical and leadership roles, can motivate companies to take significant steps towards gender equality.
Regular review and adjustment of these goals can help ensure continuous improvement and accountability.
Employing women at multiple career levels: Active employment of women at various stages of their careers can help close the gender gap.
By strategically focusing on early, middle and experienced career roles, companies can create a diverse pool of female talent that can help tackle the problem from all angles.

Another obstacle is the lack of representation and role models for women in technology.
Without visual examples of successful women in technology, it can be difficult for tech aspirants to imagine themselves in similar positions.
Encouraging and promoting diverse role models and showcasing their achievements can inspire women and empower them to pursue technical careers.

By achieving gender parity in executive teams, organizations can experience improved financial performance and competitive advantage.

Rafael Semia, director of the Agronotris plant in Ritel, which will release its first batch of insect flour this summer and aims to produce 5,000 tonnes of it in 2024, explains that “the growth of aquaculture is phenomenal, which means we need raw materials to feed these breeding farms. ”

There is no interest in feeding fish with fish that can be eaten directly by humans or with soybeans that are widely imported.
Under recent changes to European rules, more than 5 percent of fish consumed in the EU could come from farms using insect-based proteins by 2030, according to estimates by the pro-insect flour lobby group in Brussels.
Existing farmed fish diets are made partly from wild fish.
International NGOs have for years denounced this contradiction, which they blame for overfishing, with dire consequences for ecosystems, the marine food chain and the livelihoods of local populations.
Therefore, the insect meal represents an alternative being developed in France from three players that are now in the manufacturing stage: Insect, Innovavid and Agronotrice, which raised 100 million euros in 2021 and finally signed a contract worth “tens of millions of euros ” with Biomar.
This Danish company, a world leader in the manufacture of farmed fish feed and salmon in particular, has decided to invest in this project.
“There is no interest in feeding fish with fish that can be eaten directly by humans ” or with soybeans, which are widely imported and whose intensive farming contributes to the expansion of deforestation, says Biumar ’ s marketing director Catherine Briar.
In Ritel, inside a transparent container, there are like thousands of semolina seeds.
Cedric Oriol, co-founder of Agronotris, says, “These larvae have just hatched.
Today, it weighs 15 micrograms, and this weight will double ten thousand times in just two weeks.
So 100 grams of larvae will become a ton of larvae in two weeks. ”
The rapid growth of black soldier fly larvae is one of the reasons the company chose this non-invasive species known as the composting queen.
French factories raise black soldier flies that convert agricultural waste into proteins used to feed animals and fish
This choice, along with the dough recipe or optimal conditions for the marketing of the production, has been the subject of 12 years of research at a laboratory in Toulouse, according to the company.
After two weeks of growth, 98 percent of the larvae are crushed to make proteins, while 2 percent are kept for use in reproduction.
Inside one of the cages, where adult flies move, Antoine Riebois, wearing a hat covered with insects, explains that “the main activity here is to lay eggs, and the goal is to recover as many eggs as possible. ”
The black soldier fly can lay between 600 and 1,000 eggs in its short two-week life.
Another use associated with fly breeding is a mixture of insect droppings known as feras, which is an excellent fertilizer for agriculture.
The company aims to produce about 16,000 tons quickly.

Slow travel.
How do you enjoy your vacation in 2023 in a completely different way?
Tourism and travel have recently become another way to keep up with popular trends or “trends ”, and to capture impressive images that bring in more followers.
While planning vacations, some no longer think only of the places they themselves wish to visit, as much as they observe the experiences of others on social media and think of all those wonderful places they go.
In the meantime, we seem to be surrounded by a flood of travel and tourism social media accounts, which post only minute-long "flutes" where influencers navigate between various fascinating tourist destinations.
Photos and leaflets tell you that you can travel to 10 places in seven days, and that there are 100 destinations you shouldn ’ t miss.
All of this makes us feel like we are in a race to go to as many destinations as possible in as little time as possible, and creates hunger for more experiences, drives us to jump like rabbits from one destination to another and from one experience to another, so we plan vacations filled with experiences, destinations and landmarks instead of focusing our time and budgets on what really interests us.
So, perhaps it ’ s time to rethink the way we travel from a different perspective that gives us more opportunity to relax and delve deeper into the travel experience, through “slow travel. ”
From food to travel.
In praise of slow and slow
In the 1980s, in 1986, McDonald ’ s opened a new branch in Piazza di Spagna, one of Rome ’ s most famous tourist attractions.
Italian sociologist and activist Carlo Petrini published a statement announcing the launch of the Slow Food movement as a reaction to fast food that has become permeating food cultures from one country to another, leaving its negative impact on food cultures and local cooking and turning it into a similar and unified “monster. ”
The statement sparked interest around the world, and quickly led to the emergence of a global movement and organization supported by more than 100,000 members, a movement that over time evolved into sub-ideas in other domains such as slow living, slow design, and slow travel.
Hence the term Slow Tourism, an approach to travel that offers different possibilities and ways to support sustainable tourism and low-carbon tourism, based on reducing mobility by plane and car, and relying more on bicycles or walking.
It also relies on communicating with local people and cultures and eating local folk food, with an interest in preserving the environment (2).
Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, global tourism had reached a record high of 671 million international tourists.
Despite the positive effects of the boom in tourism, it has a negative aspect that cannot be ignored.
In a study published in the Journal of Sustainable Tourism, researchers focused on the potential of slow travel in the face of climate change challenges, with travel at the time of publication accounting for 50-97.5% of the amount of heat emission of most tourist trips.
The emerging concept of slow travel at the time was a reaction to high-carbon travel practices, so that slow travel becomes an integral part of the tourism experience and not just a difference in mode of transportation.
The negative impact of the tourism boom was not only on the increasing carbon footprint, but also on other environmental impacts of no less importance, for example, the Philippine government was forced to temporarily close the Boracay tourist area in 2018 to tourists, after it was transformed from a picturesque island to a sewage and waste sink for tourists, which affected the aquatic life there.
All these and other effects have led to the embrace of a new way of tourism, while embracing greater responsibility towards the environment and local communities, and opening up another horizon for individual enjoyment and exploration of the self and the world.
Here are a selection of slow travel mechanisms that will help you enjoy this exciting experience.
Take the least traveled routes.
Off The Beaten Path (or The Road Less Traveled) is one of the terms associated with slow travel, and is adapted from verses by the American poet Robert Frost, which means choosing unusual areas and different routes than the familiar, crowded routes, and is highly associated with the search for hidden local gems and avoiding the pattern of consumer tourism.
We advise you to stay away from peak tourist seasons, so you will be able to avoid the crowds, as well as get cheaper accommodation and transfers.
You will also be able to explore your destination slowly and quietly away from the crowds and crowds of tourists.
Nobody sees everything.
Many tourists fall into the sin of trying to see and discover everything, and you find lists such as “places not to miss if you go to such a country ” containing dozens of places that it is impossible for an ordinary person to visit all of them on a short vacation.
Take the Louvre as an example, one of the most famous and important museums in the world, with an area of ​ ​ about 13 square kilometers, and its complex map makes you wonder will you be able to visit all these halls?
And see over a million pieces of art and history in one day?
Or even a few days?
Here you will have to choose between jumping from hall to hall and planning your visit so that you can see as many pieces as possible and take dozens of photos, or choose the pieces that really interest you, and look at each piece, and reflect on its meanings.
You can gasp from hall to hall, or you can settle for a few paintings, and if you go in the opposite direction, you can visit the same painting for several days and spend hours in front of it.
And what about the pictures?
The images are already on search sites, and believe me if you ’ re not an exceptional professional artist, the image you take in the Louvre has been taken by thousands of people before you.
Choose what matters to you, and build your own list based on your priorities.
If you don ’ t enjoy art, and you love outdoor adventure, why spend hours in a museum and see paintings you won ’ t be able to communicate with instead of climbing a mountain, for example.
The opposite is also true.
Think about what really interests your heart, are you a lover of architecture, nature or art and history?
And what are your priorities?
Let coincidence lead you.
Despite the importance of planning, planning every minute of your trip deprives you of a lot of coincidences that may give you irreplaceable opportunities.
Leave room for a bit of randomness, an empty space for chance, free tours in which your feet and intuition lead you towards the unknown and the adventure it carries.
You might want to skip the usual tourist attractions to enjoy other things, such as living like the locals and exploring the side streets away from the city center.
Knowing people is a treasure.
Speaking of side streets instead of renting a car, walking and using public transport will enable you to get to know the country better, as well as the chance to get to know the local population.
It is said that "the people of Mecca know its people", and so in every city, away from the popular tourist destinations, the people of the city know the best and cheapest places, restaurants and shops, and from them you can explore the city in the best possible ways.
Not only that, in movies we often see heroes change their lives after having an inspiring conversation with a passing person on the way.
Perhaps we wonder why we do not meet such inspirations, and why our lives do not change.
You may not be able to take inspiration if the ones you ’ re talking to are the hurried tourists or the tour guide.
But what about people from different cultures?
Shopkeepers and old people who sit in cafes, those who belong to a land other than your land and a time other than your time, is it not possible that if you open your heart and speak without concern, you can draw inspiration from them?
There is a hidden pleasure in talking to strangers you may never meet again.
The conversation may not turn your life upside down like in the movies, but if you allow your soul to open up enough, it could be an opportunity to explore a new aspect of yourself or the world.
Find out about local markets and food.
Instead of buying souvenirs from tourist bazaars or airports, you can try buying from local markets, where you will find unique handmade goods.
You can learn about the many handicrafts of each city, from which you explore its history, and support it in the face of counterfeit products that do not carry a soul.
Be sure to try local food as it is one of the most important experiences not to be missed when traveling.
Look for local dishes and try what works for you, visit local markets, and taste vegetables and fruits that may be unfamiliar in your country.
If you ’ re a foodie, you might want to take lessons in cooking local dishes, learn how to prepare them and understand more about the culture and history of the place.
Instead of searching for branches of international chains of cafes and restaurants drink your coffee in a small local cafe, meet the waiters and pioneers and pick up the tales scattered from their mouths, this is your real wealth from the journey, not the bright photographic image that resembles the hundreds of photos taken by tourists before you.
Get rid of travel stress
When you rush from one place to another with a full list of activities you do every minute, you usually come back from vacation with a deep sense of stress, which is called travel fatigue.
In the slow travel experience you will enjoy relaxing, walking through forests and gardens, or lying in the desert in a star-studded sky.
Ignore your phone and your desire to take pictures.
Relax a bit and enjoy your experience. (6)
You don ’ t need any more time or money.
Some may say I can ’ t travel slowly, my vacation is only 7 days.
Slow travel doesn ’ t mean long travel, it doesn ’ t have to do with time frame as much as the way you travel and your way of thinking.
So slow travel brings us back to the real and root causes of travel, why do we move from one place to another?
And what are we looking for?
Are we looking for more photos of our social media accounts, are we looking for relaxation, are we looking for more cultures and history, or do we want to dig deeper and connect with ourselves?
In terms of budget, I ’ m happy.
There are many ways to reduce your travel budget, it is possible to try work while traveling, you can work in one of the farms or small hotels in exchange for accommodation, which many places offer, especially if you decide to settle in one place for long enough.
Also, instead of looking for luxury hotels, you can opt for shared homes, live with a local resident, or look for shared accommodations and cheap local hotels.
And within your city, too.
If you don ’ t have a chance to vacation outside your city, you can apply these ideas in your city as well, instead of meeting your friends in repeated places behind glass walls, go on a tour to explore the city, the unknown areas of it, the unfamiliar streets.
Turn to the old cafes, to the trees you pass every day on your way to work without seeing or noticing its presence, to people and stones.
Remember that slow travel is not just a way to travel, but a different view of the world and a way to live and think.

Global electricity losses of $100 billion due to heat

The Citizen - Translated by Hala Abdulrahman
A large sector of industries is suffering huge losses due to unprecedented global temperature rises, but it is also driving up business costs and putting pressure on the national economy of major global economies.
$100 billion in electricity losses
As a large part of the United States is suffering from a record-breaking heat wave, the massive heat range is not only affecting millions of Americans, it is also driving up business costs and squeezing the economy.
The report revealed that the wave of bad weather has led to a $100 billion productivity drain, while the real economic impact has yet to be determined for the record weather event hitting the world.
Global electricity crisis
Recent studies have shown that extreme heat could cost the United States $100 billion a year, and the heat and electricity crisis could drain a sixth of global economic activity by 2100.
Chris Lavakis, director of economic research at Moody ’ s Analytics, wrote: “Recent heatwaves and scorching summer temperatures show the economic cost of power grids. ”
Heat waves can cause fatalities and cause disruptions to business continuity.
Heat waves can also strain power grids, increasing the cost of cooling spaces. ”
Loss to the global economy
Economist Lavakis added that workers, especially those who work outdoors, are less productive now, and chronic physical risks from heat stress could reduce global GDP by as much as 17.6% by 2100.
Cathy Bogman McLeod, director of the Foundation Resilience Center, said the record-breaking temperatures cause greater losses in sectors such as agriculture and construction, but no industry or company is immune from the effects of bad weather.
Even if an employee works in an air-conditioned environment, it doesn ’ t necessarily mean they will give the same performance because sleep disturbances can lead to fatigue and poor performance the next day.
"Temperatures are rising so rapidly that our current perceptions of risk cannot match reality."
Power outages around the world
Rising temperatures in China have caused more use of electric power as a result of the use of air conditioners and power outages, forcing Beijing to use coal plants more to meet growing needs, according to the New York Times.
Various disasters, such as extreme temperatures, storms and floods, are sweeping a large number of countries in the world, especially Europe and America, causing power outages and human casualties.
There are 8,000 people without electricity in the United States.

Important tips to protect the elderly from the risk of falling
The bulletin of the Institute for Family Health Care, King Hussein Foundation, puts in the reader ’ s hands on Monday important steps to prevent the elderly from the risk of falls, with an indication of its causes, and tips to follow to protect this category from the problems of falls, which increase with age.
Add Announcement
More than one in four people age 65 or older experience falls each year.
The risk of falling and the problems associated with falling increases with age.
However, many falls can be prevented.
Many older people fear falling, even if they have never fallen before, this fear may prompt them to avoid activities such as walking, shopping or participating in social activities, but keeping active is important to keep the body healthy and actually helps prevent falls.
In this article, we want to introduce you to the causes of falls and how to reduce the risk of falls so that you feel more comfortable staying active.
What causes falls in the elderly?
Causes of falls include:
Hearing and vision problems: Vision, hearing and reflexes may not be as severe as when a person is younger.
Certain conditions, such as diabetes, heart disease, thyroid problems, nerves, feet or blood vessels, can affect balance and lead to falls.
Conditions that lead to rapid movement of the bath, such as urinary incontinence, may also increase the chance of falling.
Older adults with mild cognitive impairment or certain types of dementia are at greater risk of falling.
Age-related loss of muscle mass (known as sarcopenia), balance and gait problems, and blood pressure that drops a lot when you get up from a lying or sitting position (called postural hypotension) are all risk factors for falling.
Foot problems that cause pain, and unsafe shoes such as backless shoes or high heels, can also increase the risk of falling.
Certain medications can increase a person's risk of falling because they cause side effects such as dizziness or confusion.
The more medications a person takes, the more likely they are to fall.
Safety hazards in the home or community environment can also cause falls.
Steps to prevent falls:
Here are some tips to help reduce the risk of falls:
Stay physically active and plan an exercise program that is right for you.
Regular exercise strengthens muscles and contributes to maintaining flexibility of joints, tendons and ligaments.
Light weight-bearing activities, such as walking or climbing stairs, may slow bone loss due to osteoporosis, a disease that makes bones weak and more prone to fracture.
Try balance and strength exercises.
Yoga exercises can improve balance and muscle strength, as well as weight lifting exercises or the use of resistance bars to build strength.
Find out what changes you can make to your home that will help you avoid falling and ensure your safety, such as:
1) Make sure there is a handrail on either side of any staircase, and make sure it is safe.
Hold the handrails as you go up or down the stairs, even when you ’ re carrying something, and don ’ t let anything you ’ re holding obscure your view of the steps.
2) Make sure there is good lighting with light switches at the top and bottom of the stairs and in the hallways.
It is possible to use the lighting with the motion detector so that it is activated when moving and is connected to electrical outlets and thus automatically turned on when you walk next to it to help illuminate stairs and corridors.
3) Keep the areas where you walk tidy and do not leave books, papers, clothes or shoes on the floor or ladder.
4) Make sure that the carpet is firmly fixed to the floor, so that it does not slip.
Place anti-slip strips on tiles and wooden floors.
5) Do not use small sized rugs which are easy to slip and cause falls.
6) Do not walk on newly rinsed slippery floors.
Examine your eyes and hearing: Even minor changes in vision and hearing are associated with an increased risk of falls.
When you get new glasses or contact lenses, take time to get used to them.
Wear your glasses or contact lenses as advised by your doctor, and if you have a hearing aid, make sure they fit you well and wear them.
Know the side effects of any medications you take: If the medication makes you sleepy or dizzy, tell your doctor or pharmacist.
Get enough sleep: If you ’ re tired, it could expose you to falls.
Avoid alcohol: Excessive alcohol intake can lead to balance problems, falls, and fractures.
Stand up slowly: Moving from a sitting position to a standing position too quickly can lead to low blood pressure, which can make you feel out of balance.
Use an assistive device if you need help to feel steady when walking: Using sticks and walkers properly can help prevent falls and make sure they are the right size for you.
A physical or occupational therapist can help you identify devices that may be useful and teach you how to use them safely.
Be extra careful when walking on wet or icy surfaces in the winter as they can be very slippery, use a solvent or sand product to remove icy areas next to doors and walkways.
Keep your hands free: Use a shoulder bag or backpack to leave your hands free to attach to the handrails as you go up the stairs.
- Choose the right shoes: To fully support your feet, wear non-slip shoes, rubber soles and low heels.
Do not walk on stairs or floors with socks or shoes and slippers with smooth surfaces.
Always tell your doctor if you ’ ve had a fall, even if you don ’ t feel pain when you fall.
A fall can alert your doctor to a new medical problem or problems related to your medications or health that can be corrected.

Details of the launch of the last phase of « Women lead to executives » in the « National Training »
The National Training Academy (NTA) witnessed today the launch of the last phase of the “Women Lead for Executives ” program, the first days of personal interviews to accept the first batch, which lasts for 3 consecutive days, and includes 360 applicants, in light of the Academy ’ s interest in qualifying and preparing Egyptian women.
A number of ministers, experts, senior public figures, as well as members of the Academy ’ s Board of Trustees participate in the interview committees that take place at the Academy ’ s headquarters.
The program seeks to prepare Egyptian women in executive positions in various institutions in the government and private sectors by developing their skills, abilities and competencies, and preparing them for executive leadership in various sectors, according to the vision of the state in the development and empowerment of women.
The program is in line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, and aims to develop women ’ s skills and invest in their training, through an integrated package of theoretical and practical programs, to give them real opportunities to participate and influence in executive positions and positions.
The conditions for applying for the program include that the applicant is an Egyptian national, residing in the Arab Republic of Egypt, in addition to her work in the public or private sector or self-employment, and between the ages of 22 and 50 years.
The applicant is also required to obtain a TOEFL certificate with a score of at least 450 or an IELTS certificate with a score of at least 4.5, delivered before the start of the program, and complete the registration form.
The applicants go through several stages of admission to the program, namely: application and registration electronically, then the applicants who comply with the requirements of submission are selected, followed by conducting and passing the personal interview, and finally sending an e-mail to the applicants upon admission.
The training lasts for 10 months, with a total of 223 training days, divided into 9 months of training within the headquarters of the Academy, and one month for field training within the government or private sectors, during which the Academy relies on the application of the training methodology based on interactive learning, which includes lectures and workshops, in addition to conducting case studies, discussions and field training.
The National Training Academy was established by a presidential decree issued by President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in August 2017, to be the kiss of development and learning in Egypt, and the beacon of development and the locomotive of human development and advancement of science and knowledge, at the local, regional and international levels.
Applicants: The program develops personal and professional abilities and skills
Female applicants to join the “Women Leads for Executives ” program expressed their happiness to participate in the program, hoping that they will be selected, because of the different and diverse training programs that contribute significantly to the development of personal and professional abilities and skills, which qualify women to lead.
The applicants thanked President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi for his interest in Egyptian women, who live their golden age in his era, through receiving the necessary training programs to prepare Egyptian women in executive positions in various institutions, in the government and private sectors, by developing their skills, abilities and competencies.
UN official: Consistent with the UN Sustainable Development Goals and gives them an opportunity to participate and influence
Rania Hadiya, Regional Director of the United Nations Office for Human Settlements (UN-Habitat), based in Egypt, praised the “Women Lead for Executives ” program, considering that it is very important, and a strong message on the empowerment of women in Egypt, and the Egyptian state ’ s interest in it, and its delivery to leadership positions, and participation in the labor market.
The UN official added, in statements on the sidelines of the interviews: “The program is an important message for women, and an opportunity for them to empower and reach leadership positions. ”
She stressed that the program is consistent with the Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations, and aims to develop the skills of women and invest in their training, through an integrated package of theoretical and practical programs; in order to give them real opportunities to participate and influence in executive positions and positions.
Minister of Culture: We are witnessing a surge in interest in the value and status of women in the era of President Sisi
Minister of Culture, Dr. Nevine El-Kilani, said that Egypt under President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi is witnessing an unprecedented boom in achieving the comprehensive development vision, especially in the fields of training and rehabilitation, which aims to prepare professional and executive cadres in various fields, with great attention to the value and status of women in society, and work to refine their capabilities and empowerment in many fields.
The Minister considered that the National Training Academy is one of the most prominent signs of the existence of this boom, because of its outstanding effort, and its training programs to choose future leaders, and qualify them in line with the growing technological developments witnessed by the world, and to achieve the requirements of human development of cadres and leaders in all sectors of the state, and upgrade their capabilities and skills.
The Minister of Culture expressed her happiness and pride in the female cadres of applicants to the Academy, and their distinctive scientific and cultural characteristics and abilities in all fields, as well as their ability to bear the burdens of many responsibilities and tasks life and work distinctly, describing them as “Egypt ’ s hope and promising bright future. ”
Minister of Environment: Increasing the number of female executives in national projects
Dr. Yasmin Fouad, Minister of Environment, Dr. Nevin Al-Kilani, Minister of Culture, and Dr. Suha Jundi, Minister of Immigration, participated in the first day of personal interviews.
Also present were Dr. Nisreen Al-Baghdadi, member of the National Council for Women, and Dr. Lamees Negm, Advisor to the Governor of the Central Bank for Social Responsibility, responsible for the Union of Egyptian Banks.
The Minister of Environment said that the program is very important, as women hold leadership positions in accordance with the directives of the political leadership, noting that this requires the appropriate qualification for those positions.
She added: “This program is very important for the selection of those with outstanding abilities, and to hone their skills to empower them, because if women do not hone their skills, they will not be effective in the position in which they were placed. ”
She pointed out that the importance of the program lies in its contribution to increasing the number of women executives on the ground, especially in national projects, and this impact will be shown in the coming years, through increasing the number of women in leadership positions at the executive level at the level of the Republic.
She pointed out that the program balances the scientific part with the part on the nature of women, related to their role as mothers and wives, in addition to their role in public life and the economy, adding: "The program explains how women face challenges, what to do if they fail, and how to rise again."
She pointed out that the percentage of women ’ s representation was low in the past, but now it has risen, and women represent 25% of the parliament, and have a large percentage in the Council of Ministers, as well as at the level of universities, boards of directors of the banking sector, and bodies affiliated with financial supervision, but there is still a need to increase their percentage on the ground.
Director of the National Training Academy: Women middle leaders are in agreement with the vision of the state
Dr. Rasha Ragheb, Executive Director of the National Training Academy, said that the Academy has committed itself since its inception to be a responsible institution that meets the needs of training, rehabilitation, development and investment in human capital.
This was not far from the UN Sustainable Development Goals or Egypt ’ s 2030 Strategy, nor was it far from the Academy ’ s objectives to achieve justice in the representation of women in various programs, as well as in its administrative structure, and coinciding with a political will keen to preserve women ’ s rights and give them the opportunity to assume leadership positions.
She continued: "The Women's School for Rehabilitation offers several programs for women inside and outside Egypt, and inside and outside the administrative apparatus of the state, to give real opportunities for women to develop and learn, to achieve the status they deserve."
She stressed that the state pays great attention and great attention to Egyptian women, and is currently witnessing a real momentum for the participation of women in many parliamentary, executive and other positions, in addition to many legislations that have been issued to support and preserve their rights.
In order to activate these objectives, the National Training Academy, in coordination with the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development, launched the “Women Lead for Executives ” program, which aims to prepare women middle leaders in various executive positions, in line with the Egyptian state ’ s vision for the development and empowerment of women.
Women 's Leadership School
The program is designed to stimulate modern management skills and logical and creative thinking, and to hone the experiences of the trainees to become more influential in their families, work and communities.
The school targets Egyptian working and non-working women in the public and private sectors and entrepreneurs, whether residing inside or outside Egypt, from the age of 22 to 50 years, to include a wide range of Egyptian women who want to develop their behavioral skills and professional abilities necessary for leadership tasks, and have the ability to participate effectively in the development of society.
The program is implemented through the National Training Academy, in partnership with the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development, and in cooperation with the National Council for Women.
The trainees are selected by applying on the program ’ s website, according to the stated criteria and conditions, and then passing the personal interview and a number of tests.
Applicants must be of Egyptian nationality, have a high qualification, work in the public or private sector or self-employment, and be between the ages of 22 and 50 years, and have a TOEFL certificate with a score of at least 450 or an IELTS certificate with a score of at least 4.5, to be delivered before the start of the program.
The most important of which is that the school provides many training programs for various categories of Egyptian women locally and internationally, with theoretical and practical training on the latest global theories of leadership, and the provision of meetings with decision makers to know the mechanisms of decision-making in different institutions.
Women drive in the provinces.
The program is one of the funded grants provided by the National Training Academy, in partnership with the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development, as part of the state ’ s strategy to enhance the capabilities, knowledge and skills of women that guarantee them a place and opportunity in the labor market, to secure their economic well-being and enable them to be re-employed in markets of an ever-changing nature.
The program aims to provide many topics and training topics to a group of Egyptian women in all governorates, in line with the vision of the Egyptian state in the development and empowerment of women, as well as the sustainable development goals of the United Nations.
The program is part of a series of training programs, initiatives and grants directed to women in various categories, targeting women in the Egyptian governorates, ranging from 22 to 50 years old, and lasts 23 training days for the batch, during which the trainees are supported by a rich training experience in many disciplines and knowledge.
Egyptian Abroad
The first grants funded by the National Training Academy, under the auspices of the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development, and the participation of the Ministry of State for Migration and Egyptian Affairs abroad, are part of the state ’ s strategy to enhance the capabilities, knowledge and skills of women, which guarantees them a place and opportunity in the labor market, to secure their economic well-being and enable them to be re-employed in markets of an ever-changing nature.
This program is the beginning of a series of programs, initiatives and grants that will be directed to women in various categories, targeting Egyptians who live abroad, and want to have the opportunity to develop themselves and refine skills, in order to prepare well and keep pace with the market and its trends.
The program lasts 75 training days, during which the trainees are enriched with a rich training experience in many disciplines and knowledge, and was designed to manage and broadcast through the electronic platform of the National Training Academy, which will give the ability and space for trainees to manage their schedule freely without compromising the richness of interaction and engagement.

African Development Bank expects North African inflation to reach 14.2% by 2023
North African countries are likely to see a slight increase in economic growth.
Samar Al-Sayed
5: 19 PM, Tuesday, 1 Aug 23
In a recent report, the African Development Bank (AfDB) predicted that inflation in the North African region will continue in the two-digit range, at 14.2% in 2023 and then return to 6.9% in 2024.
According to the bank ’ s forecasts, the regional budget deficit will remain around 3.5% of GDP in 2023 and 3.2% in 2024.
The regional current account deficit is expected to shrink to 0.5% of GDP in 2023 and 0.2% in 2024.
According to the African Development Bank, the global economic environment, including fuel prices, trade patterns, tourism and foreign direct investment flows, should affect the external situation of the region.
Projected growth rate
North African countries are likely to see a slight increase in economic growth to 4.6% in 2023 and 4.4% in 2024, and should make green growth an emergency.
The African Foundation published its annual report on the economic outlook for North Africa for 2023 under the overall theme “Mobilizing private sector finance for climate and green growth in Africa ”.
According to the Bank Group, growth in the region is driven mainly by the services sector, particularly trade and tourism.
In 2022, growth in the region was moderate, at 4.1% compared to 5.4% in 2021.
Supporting inclusive growth
However, there are large disparities between countries in the increase in growth, according to Audrey Verdier Chouchan, regional economist for North Africa and acting head of the Department of State Economics for Central Africa, North Africa and the West.
“To support inclusive growth, the region must implement structural reforms that promote private sector development, improve productivity and employability, and create jobs. ”
The Bank ’ s strategy to preserve the region ’ s economies
To preserve the region ’ s economies, the AfDB calls for coordinated monetary and fiscal policies to address rising inflation and protect small businesses and individuals through targeted public expenditures.
Similarly, maintaining and supporting food security in the region remains a critical objective.
The Bank stresses that countries should invest in agriculture, including the development of improved varieties as well as water and soil management strategies.
The region must strengthen its resilience, particularly within the framework of the “energy transition – water management – food security ” nexus.
Finally, to address fiscal consolidation challenges, countries must continue their efforts to implement reforms, particularly by improving the digitization of tax administration, broadening the tax base, rationalizing public expenditures, and strengthening governance systems.
Implementation of the African Free Trade Area
North Africa should also promote the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), in order to stimulate intra-African trade and investment.
In addition, North African governments must address rising levels of public debt over the medium term by monitoring debt funds transparently, restructuring state-owned enterprises in a difficult situation, and conducting regular public expenditure reviews.
North African governments, foreign and domestic private investors, multilateral development banks, development finance institutions and the private sector must invest in green growth.
In particular, private sector financing can play a crucial role through investments in clean energy infrastructure, energy efficiency, sustainable agriculture, and land reclamation.
The private sector can also provide the expertise, technology and management skills necessary for the effective and efficient implementation of green development projects.
Thus, countries should invest in the sustainable management of natural capital to provide a complementary financing option for climate and green growth initiatives, thereby contributing to poverty and inequality reduction, job creation and sustainable economic growth.
A crucial role
The report highlights that the AfDB Group and other development partners are playing a critical role in improving the role of the private sector and natural capital in financing climate action and green growth in North Africa.
The North Africa Economic Outlook is one of the flagship reports of the African Development Bank Group, which has been published since 2003.
Government officials, national and regional institutions, the private sector, researchers and academics, as well as the media, attended the launch event, which took place at the Bank Group ’ s regional headquarters in Tunis and via video link.

What is the most frightening mystery of artificial intelligence?
Urgent.
407.
The rapid advancement of generative AI technologies has revolutionized our world today, leading to unprecedented progress and innovation in how we create and use text and visual content, and these technologies have affected many sectors by simplifying processes, improving work efficiency and enhancing productivity, and over time may even affect the way we live our lives.
But at the same time, the rapid progress of AI also brings with it many risks, the most important of which is now the expected danger of most companies integrating generative AI models into all their products, and these models are evolving very quickly now, and with time AI and machine learning engineers will not be able to predict the behavior of these systems or explain their behavior!
Perhaps the scariest aspect of today ’ s generative AI revolution is the lack of knowledge among the scientists and programmers who built the big language models.
Alexander C. Karp, CEO of Palantir — a company that creates data analytics software and works with the U.S. Department of Defense — wrote last week in an opinion piece in The New York Times: “It ’ s not at all clear even to the scientists and programmers who built large language models how generative language models and image models work. ”
Hey, what's happening?
For decades, we ’ ve used computer systems that provide the same output they gave each time the same input was used, but in contrast, generative AI systems aim to offer multiple possibilities from a single text request, where you can easily get different answers to the same question.
Some of the latest models contain a trillion or more parameters, and variables that are adjustable within an algorithm, represent a measure of processing that is impossible for the human mind to begin to understand, making it difficult to analyze how these models arrive at a particular answer.
Why are you so worried about artificial intelligence?
In short, the concern is not artificial intelligence itself, but its very rapid evolution, as more advanced versions of large language models are now beginning to show what a group of researchers have called “Sparks of Artificial General Intelligence. ”
General Artificial Intelligence (AGI) refers to a powerful form of artificial intelligence that is adept at solving multiple problems and possesses skills such as human skills, and there are those who say that it will be smarter than a human in a short period of time.
This rapid development is expected to lead to the arrival of AGI very soon, and when it does, the AI will be able to improve itself without any human intervention.
It will do so in the same way as Google ’ s AlphaZero program, which learned how to play chess better than even the best human chess players or other AI players within just nine hours of its first run.
He has achieved this feat by playing with himself millions of times.
A team of Microsoft researchers analyzed GPT-4, OpenAI ’ s most advanced language model to date, and said it had “signs of advanced general intelligence. ”
In GPT-4, it performed better than 90% of human test takers in the Bar examination, a standardized test used to accredit lawyers for practice in many U.S. states, up from just 10% in the previous GPT-3.5 version, which was trained on a smaller dataset.
Researchers have found similar improvements in dozens of other tests, most of which are thought tests.
This is the main reason why the Microsoft team concluded that the GPT-4 model could reasonably be considered a preliminary – but incomplete – version of the General Artificial Intelligence (AGI) system.
This very rapid pace of change was also the reason Geoffrey Hinton, the godfather of artificial intelligence, left his position at Google after 10 years and worked to warn about the dangers of artificial intelligence.
Hinton told The New York Times: “Look at how AI evolved five years ago and how it is now, take that difference and predict how much impact it will have in the future.
As Sam Altman (Sam Altman), founder of OpenAI – the developer of ChatGPT – said at a Senate hearing in mid-May about the potential of AI, “I think if something goes wrong with this technology, things could go completely wrong, so a new AI licensing body should be created. ”
Breaking the Protection of Large Linguistic Models LLMs:
Larger language models (LLMs) used in popular chatbots, such as ChatGPT, Bard, Bing, or Claude, are subject to careful and thorough tuning to not produce harmful content in their responses to user questions.
But four researchers published a paper last Thursday showing that users can defeat “firewalls ” aimed at preventing AI systems from explaining, for example,“ how to make a bomb. ”
Chatbots like ChatGPT, Bing, and Bard will not answer this question when asked directly.
But it will go into great detail if some additional code is added while the claims are being written.
“It ’ s possible that the nature of deep learning models makes such threats inevitable, so if you can ’ t accurately predict how the system will respond to the new claim, you can ’ t build firewalls that can withstand. ”
Because AI developers cannot easily explain the behavior of systems, they are now working using outdated methods and practice, as there is no scientific method or specific mechanism for neural networks to work.
In February, mathematician Stephen Wolfram wrote, “Random is part of the tradition of neural networks, meaning that if we use the same request several times, we ’ re likely to get different articles each time. ”
In line with the idea of randomness in neural networks, they can be set to be relatively more or less random to provide a wider or narrower variation in their responses, and the developers call this setting in their models the Temperature Parameter, which determines how often higher-order and lower-order words are used to generate textual responses.
But on the other hand, some experts assert that artificial intelligence is the most important tool that may serve humanity, and that we do not yet understand its importance.
Arvind Narayanan, a computer scientist at Princeton University, said: “The black box of neural networks is greatly exaggerated, and we have great tools to reverse engineer them.
Other critics also argue that the claim that developers don ’ t know how large language models work is just a prevarication that helps AI companies avoid accountability.
Conclusion:
The question remains as to whether over time AI developers will be able to provide deeper and better answers to how their systems work.
But experts say the more companies develop AI models whose choices and decision paths can be practically documented, the more likely we are to get answers to this question.
Nuclear weapons divided the world into two parts: who owns and who doesn ’ t, and the industrial revolution allowed Europe to excel in economic and military power.
So the most important question now in the AI revolution is, who benefits the most, who will be able to access the workings of this powerful new technology, and who will be left behind?

Rising temperatures are the first phenomenon of climate change
As greenhouse gas concentrations rise, the Earth's surface temperature rises.
The past decade, 2011-2020, has been the warmest on record.
Since the 1980s, each decade has been warmer than the previous decade.
Almost all land areas experience more hot days and heat waves.
High temperatures increase heat-related illnesses and make outdoor work more difficult.
Forest fires burn more easily and spread more quickly when the weather is hotter.
Temperatures in the Arctic have risen at least twice as fast as the global average.
More severe storms.
Devastating storms have become more intense and frequent in many areas.
As temperatures rise, more moisture evaporates, exacerbating heavy rainfall and flooding, thus causing more devastating storms.
The frequency and scale of tropical storms are also affected by ocean warming, as hurricanes, tornadoes, and typhoons intensify with warm waters on the ocean surface, and such storms often destroy homes and communities, causing deaths and severe economic losses.
Increased drought
Climate change is altering water availability, making it more scarce in more regions.
Global warming exacerbates water shortages in water-poor areas, increases the risk of drought for agriculture, thus affecting crops, and environmental drought increases the vulnerability of ecosystems.
Droughts can also trigger devastating sand and dust storms that can transport billions of tons of sand across continents.
Deserts are also expanding, reducing the amount of land available to grow food.
Many people are now at risk of not getting enough water on a regular basis.
Warming of the oceans
The oceans absorb most of the heat of global warming.
The rate of ocean warming has increased dramatically over the past two decades, across all the ocean depths.
As the oceans warm, their size increases as the water expands due to their warming.
Melting ice sheets are also causing sea levels to rise, threatening coastal and island communities.
In addition, the oceans absorb carbon dioxide and prevent it from being released into the atmosphere, but the increase in carbon dioxide makes the oceans more acidic, putting marine life and coral reefs at risk.
Loss of species
Climate change poses risks to the survival of species on land and in the oceans.
These risks increase with higher temperatures.
The loss of species is exacerbated by climate change, with the world losing species at a rate 1,000 times greater than at any time in recorded human history.
One million species are at risk of extinction in the next few decades.
Forest fires, extreme weather, invasive pests and diseases are among the many threats related to climate change.
While some species will be able to move and survive, others will not.
Lack of food
Changes in climate and increased extreme weather events are among the reasons behind the global rise in hunger and malnutrition. Fisheries, crops and livestock may be destroyed or become less productive.
As the oceans become more acidic, the marine resources that feed billions of people are at risk.
Changes in ice and ice cover in many Arctic regions have disrupted food supplies from grazing, fishing and fishing sources.
Heat stress can reduce grazing water and grassland, causing crop yields to drop and affecting livestock.
More health risks
Climate change is the biggest health threat facing humanity.
Climate impacts are already harming health, through air pollution, disease, extreme weather events, forced displacement, pressures on mental health, and increased hunger and malnutrition in places where people cannot grow crops or find enough food.
Each year, environmental factors claim the lives of approximately 13 million people.
Changing weather patterns lead to the spread of diseases, extreme weather events increase deaths and make it difficult for health care systems to keep up.
Poverty and displacement
Climate change increases the factors that place people and keep them in poverty.
Floods can wipe out urban slums and destroy homes and livelihoods.
The heat can make working outside jobs difficult.
Water scarcity can affect crops.
Over the past decade (2010-2019), weather-related events have displaced an estimated 23.1 million people on average each year, leaving many more vulnerable to poverty.
Most of the refugees come from countries that are most vulnerable and least prepared to adapt to the effects of climate change.

What are the risks of artificial intelligence for business?
Advances in artificial intelligence have helped businesses improve their operations, raising productivity and thus increasing profits.
But this revolutionary technology, which has been heavily invested by several companies in Silicon Valley, California, continues to pose a threat to for-profit organizations.
Add Announcement
Among the great benefits and risks of using the technology, Boris Sibut, chief security engineer at Sinopsis Software Integrity Group, describes the technology as “smart but naive. ”
Speaking to the cyber security website The Cyber Express, he said that “would be a fair description of the artificial intelligence we see today. ”
From Reputation to Lawsuits
Beyond the risk of eliminating millions of jobs, IT expert Ayman Itani believes there are potential risks to business from artificial intelligence.
Speaking to Al-Hurra, Itani said the impact of AI on businesses “starts with reputation and privacy, and may even get into legal trouble. ”
Pope Francis did not bounce back from the Balenciaga fashion house, and filmmakers did not pretend to land on the moon.
However, in recent months, stunningly realistic images of these AI-generated scenes have mushroomed online, threatening society ’ s ability to separate truth from fiction.
Over the past years, the use of artificial intelligence technologies has grown by companies in their various operations.
According to an IMG research paper, “more than 35 percent of companies are already using AI in their operations, while 40 percent of businesses are exploring this technology for potential future use. ”
Companies are using AI to perform tasks such as analyzing consumer behavior, removing errors, improving productivity, and more operations, says Tyler Whitsman, co-founder of SpeechFi, a smart app that uses the same technology to turn audio into text.
Based on his personal experience at Spectvay, Whitsman suggests in an article published by Forbes, “taking risks as well as benefits into account ” in business operations.
With technological advances, artificial intelligence (AI) has become one of its fastest advances.
The idea of a machine that learns and makes independent decisions may seem very interesting, but how exactly does it work?
Whitsman outlines the risks of using AI for businesses in three key areas: “errors, vulnerability to cyber attacks, and inhumane behavior. ”
“Any mistakes made by the technology would cause serious damage to the company and its reputation, which could ultimately affect its profits, ” he says.
"The Biggest Danger"
Itani explains, “Reliance on AI in companies ’ operations can affect the quality of work, especially in areas such as marketing and copywriting. ”
“Most AI tools cannot validate information, especially since they are designed to derive their information from the Internet, ” Itani said.
Therefore, according to Itani, “any misinformation may also cause companies legal problems, if data that has not been verified by a human element is used. ”
He gave an example of how AI applications could be asked to create text or images based on the method of another company, triggering lawsuits over intellectual property rights.
Also, intelligence systems can provide data with discriminatory descriptions, which can pose a risk to a company ’ s reputation or even get into legal cases.
The use of facial recognition technology by police is again stirring controversy in the United States after a complaint by an African-American woman who was arrested in February and released ten hours later for a crime she did not commit.
AI applications derive discriminatory descriptions through algorithms used in their programming language, according to The Cyber Express.
However, privacy issues are the “biggest risk ” to companies from their use of AI, especially those applications that deliver information depending on the generative type, Itani says.
“The risk of private information being leaked to businesses comes from their use of apps that learn new things themselves, so this sensitive information could be available to competing companies. ”
“The benefits are greater. ”
Itani pointed out that large commercial institutions resorted to the use of special robots, so that they are not available to all people, in order to avoid leakage of information to competitors.
These risks come as the development of artificial intelligence continues, making investors ’ appetite for work in the field open.
The mood in Silicon Valley was bad a year ago after tech stocks plunged, starting waves of layoffs.
But the tech industry is currently experiencing a huge boom for one reason: artificial intelligence.
Venture capitalists invested more than $11 billion in AI startups in May alone, according to data firm Pitchbook, up 86 percent from the same month last year.
Such large investments will increase the proportion of companies that use technology in their business to obtain its benefits.
Experts insist that the benefits of using AI for companies are far greater than the risks, which can be avoided by adhering to ethical standards, and keeping the human element to scrutinize how the technology works.
“Artificial intelligence has become an integral part of many companies, whether we accept technology or not, and it ’ s there to stay, ” Whitsman said.
He added: "We can deal with many of these potential risks of AI, if we consider its significant benefits," citing Alhurra.

The United Nations Health Agency defines traditional medicine as the knowledge, skills and practices used over time to maintain health and to prevent, diagnose and treat physical and mental illnesses.
But many traditional treatments lack any proven scientific value, and conservation activists say the industry is pushing for increased trade in endangered animals, including tigers, rhinos and squam-eaters, and threatening the survival of entire species.

In China, traditional medicine has a long history, but major European medical bodies have previously requested that it be subject to the same principles of regulatory oversight as traditional medical methods.
John Ryder, head of research at the World Health Organization, said: “Scientific progress in traditional medicine must be subject to the same rigorous standards as in other areas of health. ”
The use of traditional medicine in the absence of rules
Of the 194 WHO member states, 170 have recognized their use of traditional and complementary medicine since 2018, but only 124 have reported laws or rules for the use of herbal medicines, while only half have a national policy on such methods and medicines.

About 40% of approved pharmaceutical products currently in use are derived from a “natural product basis, ” according to the World Health Organization, which cites“ prominent drugs ” derived from traditional medicine, including aspirin, based on formulations using willow bark.

August 20, 2023 13: 13
The UAE attaches high priority to the conservation of biodiversity and the protection of endangered species, their propagation and their resettlement in their natural areas of spread inside and outside the country.
The State has recorded great successes in the conservation of endangered species, as a result of the adoption of an integrated legislative structure, including laws to protect these species and the nature of dealing with them, in line with international agreements and treaties, in addition to increasing the number of nature reserves and expanding them, launching many breeding programs for endangered species, as well as adopting several techniques to preserve the environment and various species.
Endangered species are species of animals and plants in danger of extinction and are classified in the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, while the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species is a methodology or method for assessing and monitoring the status of biodiversity on the planet. The theme of the ‘ Reserve ’ as part of the recently launched ‘ National Sustainability ’ campaign, which coincides with the preparations for the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP28) taking place from 30 November to 12 December this year at Expo City Dubai, highlights the UAE ’ s efforts to protect the environment through a range of innovative initiatives and solutions. “To raise awareness about environmental sustainability issues, encourage community participation, and support national strategies related to climate action, so as to have a positive impact on individuals ’ behavior and responsibilities, leading to an environmentally conscious society.
An integrated legislative structure.
The UAE has a unique biological diversity that includes a range of plants and land and aquatic organisms. Accordingly, the UAE has issued several legislations to protect its biological diversity, such as Federal Law No. 23 of 1999 on the exploitation, protection and development of living aquatic resources in the UAE, and Federal Law No. 24 of 1999 on the protection and development of the environment, which prohibits hunting, transporting, killing or harming land or marine organisms. Or areas that are home to animal or plant species or their reproduction, introducing alien species to the protected area and polluting the soil, water or air of the protected area. In this regard, Federal Law No. 11 of 2002 on the regulation and control of international trade in endangered animals and plants and its implementing regulations.
The UAE has joined several international conventions aimed at protecting endangered species, most notably the Convention on the Regulation of Trade in Endangered Species of Plants and Animals (CITES), the International Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and its protocols on biosafety from genetically modified resources, the Protocol on the Equitable Sharing of Genetic Resources, the Convention on Wetlands of Global Importance (Ramsar) and the Convention on the Conservation of Wildlife and its Natural Habitat. In addition, the GCC has joined the International Convention on Migratory Species, the International Union for the Conservation of Nature and other global alliances.
National Red List of Threatened Species.
As part of the UAE ’ s strategy to conserve local biodiversity and protect endangered species, the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment launched in 2022 the National Red List of Threatened Species, which includes a comprehensive assessment of the status of species in the local environment.
The National Red List project included identifying endangered species and assessing the risk of extinction of wild species at the national level. The list included an assessment of the status of 1,167 species in the local environment, where the country hosts 58 native mammal species. There are also other mammal species in the country, but they are alien species, and there are also reptiles and amphibians with a total of 72 species, including 57 terrestrial reptiles, 13 marine reptiles, and 2 amphibians.
The National Red List of Threatened Species provides data and statistics that contribute to the development and adoption of future plans and programs to enhance the protection and sustainability of local biodiversity, conserve many endangered species, and highlight the value of ongoing efforts. In addition to providing valuable material for researchers and academics in the country, it also represents a strong motivation to focus their future research on species whose data are not available in the current situation, which helps to feed the national database of endangered species.
Assessments included in the list concluded that the average rate of endangered mammal species in the country is 46.7%, and the assessments and monitoring carried out by the Red List project showed a great diversity of wild mammals in the country in different environments, where carnivores make up 28.2%, rodents 20.5%, while bats make up 30.7% of the local species confirmed. The Arabian Har is the only endemic mammal species in the region, while the country has five species of mammals endemic to the Arabian Peninsula: the Arabian Oryx, Arabian Gazelle, Sand Gazelle, Gerboa and Arabian Rat. The list also showed that the country is home to a variety of marine mammals, with 18 species of cetaceans and one species of calanids (sea cows), as well as important groups of four species of marine mammals. At least one of them is the humpback dolphin.
According to the National Red List, the UAE includes about 60 species of wild reptiles, with 19% of the reptiles in the country threatened with extinction, including one endemic species, the leaf-finger gecko, in addition to two amphibians, eight species of sea snakes and five species of sea turtles, and the results of the assessment of the state of reptiles in the country showed that 69% are considered less endangered.
The list revealed that the local environment of the country includes 459 species of birds, and 167 species were evaluated, where the birds in the country are divided into two groups are regularly present birds and endemic birds, and the results of the assessment showed that 53% of the bird species in the country are threatened with extinction, while 14% are under threat of extinction, and 33% less threat.
Some 945 plant species have been registered in the country, and 598 native vascular plant species have been identified and evaluated, with 8 percent of plant species in the country endangered, 3 percent less threatened and 62 percent not.
Red List of Wildlife Species in Abu Dhabi
In 2021, EAD issued the first Red List of Wildlife Species in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, which is an assessment of the threat status of wild and marine species in the emirates.The Abu Dhabi Red List complements the National Red List of Threatened Species, which is carried out by the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, and is in line with the development of these lists at local, national and regional levels.
The Abu Dhabi Red List assessed 244 species, including 101 plants, 49 birds, 9 marine species, 32 land mammal species, 25 invertebrate species, 26 reptile species and two amphibian species.
Of the 244 species assessed, 74 fall under different threat categories, such as critically endangered, endangered and endangered species.The Abu Dhabi Wildlife Red List helps EAD prioritize conservation measures for some of the emirate ’ s most threatened species, which may include developing more systematic monitoring as well as conservation and action plans to protect specific species. The world ’ s most successful resettlement of species that were on the brink of extinction such as the Arabian Oryx and the African Oryx (Hirab), Abu Dhabi is now home to the world ’ s largest collection of Arabian Oryx.
The Environment Agency - Abu Dhabi (EAD) is implementing some of the world ’ s most successful projects to repopulate endangered species such as the Arabian Oryx and the African Oryx, which numbered more than 550 in the wild. Abu Dhabi is now home to the world ’ s largest collection of Arabian Oryx through its wildlife breeding centres.
- Establishment and expansion of natural reserves.
The UAE ’ s efforts to protect endangered species include the establishment and expansion of nature reserves, which enjoy their biodiversity and rare animals and plants, in addition to coral reefs full of unique marine organisms, and the expansion of nature reserves has contributed to great successes in the conservation of endangered species.
The UAE is home to 49 nature reserves, representing about 15.53% of the total area of the country, and these natural reserves are divided into 16 marine reserves representing about 12.01% of the marine and coastal areas, and 33 land reserves representing 18.4% of the land areas in the country.
- Endangered species breeding programs.
As part of its initiatives to protect endangered species, the UAE has placed great importance on the breeding programs of endangered species through the provision of reputable breeding centers locally and internationally. The UAE authorities have organized several awareness campaigns on the protection of endangered species and the reduction of malpractices against them. Satellite tracking technologies, as well as the use of drones to survey and enumerate large populations of breeding bird species, for highly accurate results over short periods of time compared to traditional methods.

Traditional use: Ashwagandha is believed to have soothing, anti-inflammatory and anti-stress properties.

Scientific research: There are some scientific studies that support some of the potential benefits of ashwagandha.

During the first six months of this year, Tunisia succeeded in attracting international investments worth 1217 million dinars (MD) compared to 1043 MD in the same period last year, an increase of 17.6 percent.
TUNIS, 23 August 2023 (Watt) During the first six months of this year, Tunisia managed to attract international investments worth 1217 million dinars (MD) compared to 1043 MD in the same period last year, an increase of 17.6 percent.

"..."
At the end of June this year, Tunisia attracted international direct investment of 1028 million dinars, compared to 1030 million dinars in the same period last year, with a growth rate of 5 percent, according to the same source.
International direct investments were distributed by sector to the industrial sector, which attracted 521 MD compared to 445 MD in June last year, with a growth of 16.9 percent.
The services sector accounted for 324.7 million dinars compared to 310.4 million dinars at the end of the first six months of 2022, an increase of 4.6 per cent.
As for the agricultural sector, it continued to be weak in attracting international investments, only attracting 2.9 MD compared to 2.7 MD in the same period last year.

The completed investment operations were divided into 27 operations in the form of new developments at a value of 30.4 million dinars, which provided 420 jobs and 294 investment operations in the form of expansion projects at a value of 812 million dinars, which contributed to the saving of 3196 tons of employment.
At the level of regional distribution of international investments, the data of the Agency highlighted the wide and important disparity between the regions, with the provinces of Greater Tunisia accounting for 59.5% (504.6 MD), mainly the province of Tunis with investments of 358.5 MD, followed by the provinces of the north-west attracting international investments of 194.1 MD.

For a value of 19.1 md.
