New Study Shows Impact of Emotional Communication on Consumer Behaviors
11.
In a world where process trumps emotion, the concept of “emotional entertainment ” is emerging as a new way of presenting content and helping individuals rekindle their creativity.
TikTok is a leading digital space to this end, and can be described as the best platform for building strong emotional connections with users.
Building genuine connections with users and triggering positive emotions in them of joy, happiness and inspiration is a huge challenge today, especially with the difficulty of finding innovative ideas that are new in today ’ s world.
This challenge is even greater for brands and marketers, so that emotional communication has become the key to reaching customer loyalty and shaping customer behaviors.
Tailoring content to the resonance of the target audience and fueling various types of emotions in them, from sympathy and nostalgia to inspiration and hope, has become the ideal way for brands to leave unforgettable impressions.
Leading research firms IPSOS and MediaProber have conducted a first-of-its-kind study to uncover the significant impact of consumers ’ emotional response to content on digital social media platforms, examining the impact of emotional entertainment on business outcomes in the UAE, and also drawing on data from a 2021 study conducted by APSOS and Neurons in the Middle East, North Africa and Turkey (MENA) region., sheds light on why users are interested in TikTok content.
To understand the scientific reason behind emotional communication, Ipsos and MediaProper have used innovative research techniques to identify moments when emotional communication peaks while using digital media platforms.
The research revealed that users experienced these moments while browsing major digital platforms about five times in a 30-minute session, while the positive emotions of TikTok users increased by 1.2 times compared to other digital platforms.
TikTok ’ s leadership in attracting attention is evident, with platform users spending 92% of their time using it compared to 8% watching TV (the percentage of time using TikTok versus TV – when given the choice between the two in a natural multi-screen environment).
The content of short videos is of interest to TikTok users, and attracts their attention as they watch videos (generated by users as well as ads) 1.6 times more than other digital platforms.
The chilling effect of the content lasts longer than the immediate reaction, which improves the mood of users even long after using the platform.
TikTok was the only platform that improved the mood of users by 2.6 times higher than other digital platforms, cementing its position as a source of positivity and inspiration.
Bruno Ribeiro, Global Head of Research and Insights at MediaProper, said: “This groundbreaking and first-of-its-kind marketing study examined the impact of emotional moments on user experience and online content sharing, while identifying business opportunities for brands to connect audiences. ”
Ribeiro added: “We looked at participants ’ varying psychological and physiological data through TikTok and other digital channels to identify moments of emotional connection.
The results revealed that high-impact clips are an integral part of a business strategy that aims to enhance user experience, content satisfaction and brand impact. ”
Emotionally impactful content is tuned by users and includes a great mix of original content, positive style, real people and music, giving the content an authentic touch and pushing to engage users effortlessly in the platform ’ s trends, elevating the mood of its followers and thus enhancing emotional resonance, leaving a lasting impact on viewers.
Ramesh Redicar, Head of Brand Tracking at Ipsos, MENA, commented: “This scientific research on emotional entertainment demonstrates the profound impact that emotion-related content can have on digital users, particularly on TikTok.
The effect goes beyond entertainment and engagement to prompt users to take action.
This type of content not only enhances the overall evaluation of the platform, but also improves the mood of users, and therefore, they are more likely to remember and interact with ads and create greater links with brands. ”
Emotional communication in TikTok is highly correlated with consumer behavior.
A research study conducted by Ipsos on the purchasing motivation of brands in the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Turkey in 2022 showed that emotional impact with content drove 68% of shoppers to shop on TikTok.
Brands can leverage the power of the emotional entertainment effect to leave more lasting impressions, boost product loyalty and drive purchase.
With users consuming so much content, TikTok is twice as likely to remember ads as other platforms.
A 2023 study revealed that users who experience moments of emotional connection are 1.5 times more likely to purchase a product or service across digital platforms, especially via TikTok, where emotional communication is stronger in TikTok, making users more open to experiencing the product or service, and buying it.
These findings highlight the tremendous potential that TikTok offers brands seeking to build genuine, emotional and sustainable connections with their audience.
By leveraging the power of emotional entertainment, brands can drive buying and leverage the overall impact of their TikTok marketing efforts.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has issued a $7.5 billion loan tranche for Argentina in a deal that took four months to negotiate.

Due to severe drought and political errors, Argentina has failed to make the agreed budget adjustments, the IMF said.
However, it was possible to agree on new targets such as increasing central bank reserves and more fiscal discipline.
The Buenos Aires Economy Ministry must pass more than half of the newly disbursed money to other creditors, La Nación reported.
In order to meet its interest obligations to the Fund, Argentina recently received several temporary loans from China and Qatar and from the Latin American Development Bank.
South America ’ s second-largest economy is mired in a severe economic and financial crisis.
Argentina suffers from a bloated state apparatus, low industrial productivity and a large parallel economy that deprives the state of much of its tax revenue.
The national currency, the peso, continues to fall against the US dollar, and debt is constantly increasing.
Inflation has risen to 115%.

Warnings about the dangers of artificial intelligence
Message Net- Agencies
The UK Parliament ’ s Science, Innovation and Technology Committee has warned of the potential threat artificial intelligence poses to human lives.
The committee demanded that the risks of artificial intelligence be the focus of any future government regulation and that controls be put in place for the use of this technology, according to the British network "Sky News".
Members of the UK Parliament ’ s Science and Technology Committee have called on Prime Minister Rishi Sonak to address the challenges posed by artificial intelligence ahead of the UK hosting the world ’ s first global summit on artificial intelligence.
The committee identified 12 challenges posed by artificial intelligence, noting the need to address these challenges during the summit and reach a common approach among countries to reduce the risks of modern technology.
According to the committee, the threats included:
An existential threat.
The committee recalls that some experts have warned of the significant threat to human life posed by artificial intelligence, so it is necessary to enact regulations that provide protection for national security.
Bias
The British Commission believes that artificial intelligence can reinforce existing biases in society or introduce new biases.
Privacy Policy
Sensitive information belonging to individuals or companies can be used to train AI models.
Misrepresentation.
The panel warned that ChatGPT models could produce distorted material about a person ’ s behavior and personal views.
DATA
The committee said training the most powerful AI tools would require a huge amount of data.
Computing power
According to committee members, developing the most powerful AI tools requires enormous computing power.
Transparency
AI models struggle to explain why they broadcast a particular result, or where they come from information.
PROPERTY RIGHTS
Generative models, whether text, images, audio or video, typically make use of existing content, which must be protected so as not to undermine the creative industries, the committee said.
Responsibility
If AI tools are used to harm, the policy should determine whether developers or service providers are responsible or not, according to the committee.
JOBS
The UK Science and Technology Commission has asked politicians to anticipate the potential impact that the adoption of AI will have on existing jobs.
Openness
She called for the computer code behind AI models to be made openly available, to allow for more reliable regulation and to promote transparency and innovation.
International coordination
The Committee stressed that the development of any organization must be an international task, and the November summit should welcome as many participating countries as possible.
In June, British Prime Minister Rishi Sonak announced during a visit to Washington that London would host the first global AI summit this year.
Sonak said countries should make sure that AI is developed and used in a safe way, especially as it has amazing potential to change lives for the better.
The Secretary-General of the United Nations, António Guterres, has called for the establishment of controls rooted in human rights, transparency and accountability, in the development and use of artificial intelligence for the common good.

Millions of dollars pledged to boost Africa ’ s carbon stocks at climate summit
An initiative to boost the production of carbon credits in Africa to 19-fold by 2030 drew pledges of hundreds of millions of dollars on Monday as Kenyan President William Ruto opened the continent ’ s first climate summit.
In one of the most anticipated deals, investors from the UAE committed to buy $450 million worth of carbon credits from the African Carbon Markets Initiative launched at the COP27 summit in Egypt last year.
“Green growth should be seen not only as a climate imperative, but also as a source of billions of dollars of economic opportunities that Africa and the world are poised to take advantage of, ” he told delegates.
African leaders are promoting market-based financing instruments, such as carbon credits or offsets that can be obtained from projects that reduce emissions, usually in developing countries, such as planting trees or switching to cleaner fuels.
Companies can buy carbon credits to offset emissions they cannot reduce from their own operations to help meet climate goals.
One balance is equivalent to saving or avoiding one tonne of carbon dioxide.
Organisers of the three-day summit in Nairobi say they aim to present Africa as a destination for climate investment rather than a victim of floods, drought and famine.
African governments see carbon credits and other market-based financing instruments as critical to mobilizing financing, which has been slow to arrive from donors in the rich world.
The carbon offset market was worth about $2 billion in 2021, and Shell and the Boston Consulting Group predicted in January that it could reach between $10 billion and $40 billion by 2030.
A number of speakers at the summit said they saw little progress toward accelerating climate finance because investors still saw the continent as too risky.
Africa has received only about 12 percent of the money it needs to deal with climate impacts, according to a report released last year by the non-profit Climate Policy Initiative.
Bogolo Kinwendo, a former UN climate adviser and trade minister in Botswana, said: “No African country has succeeded in attracting climate finance. ”
Kevin Kariuki, vice president of the African Development Bank, told Reuters the agreements announced on Monday were “very welcome ” but not enough.
At the United Nations climate summit in Dubai at the end of November, African countries will press for an expansion of the International Monetary Fund ’ s Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), which could unleash $500 billion in climate finance that could be raised fivefold, he said.
More than 20 heads of state and government are expected to attend the summit in Kenya from Tuesday.
The leaders plan to issue a declaration outlining Africa ’ s position ahead of the UN climate conference later this month and COP28.
The UAE presents itself as a leader in climate finance in Africa.
Hassan Ghazali, investment manager at the UAE Independent Accelerators for Climate Change, made a $450 million commitment by the UAE Carbon Alliance, an alliance of private sector players.
Many African activists oppose the summit ’ s approach to climate finance, and about 500 people staged a protest march in downtown Nairobi on Monday.
They argue that carbon credits are an excuse for wealthier nations and companies to continue their polluting business and that they should instead pay off their “climate debt ” through direct compensation and debt relief.
Sultan Al Jaber, president of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP28), said carbon markets are an important tool, but the lack of generally agreed standards “undermines their integrity and diminishes their value. ”
A working paper from the Debt Relief for a Green and Inclusive Recovery Project found that sub-Saharan African countries face an annual debt service cost that is almost identical to their climate finance needs.

Quantum programming
Quantum programming is an emerging field in the field of computer programming that focuses on the development of algorithms and software for quantum computers.
To harness the unparalleled computational power of quantum computing systems, quantum programming combines the principles of quantum mechanics, linear algebra, and computer science to solve complex problems that are beyond the reach of classical computing architectures.
Quantum programming languages and frameworks are designed to handle qubits and facilitate the processing of quantum information, enabling revolutionary advances in areas such as cryptography, optimization, and simulation.
Unlike classical bits, which can be either 0 or 1, quantum bits can exist in multiple states simultaneously due to a phenomenon known as superposition.
This property, along with entanglement, which allows correlation between qubits in discrete quantum states, enables quantum computers to simultaneously process vast amounts of data and perform a large number of calculations in parallel.
As a result, quantum programming has the potential to radically transform many industries, from pharmaceuticals and finance to artificial intelligence and cybersecurity.
In the context of programming models, quantum programming represents a distinct shift from classical deterministic and probability methods.
While traditional programming languages are designed for classical computers with binary logic gates, quantum programming languages use quantum logic gates and quantum circuits to manipulate qubit states and perform quantum operations.
These specialized languages are designed to exploit the unique characteristics of quantum computing, thus enabling developers to encrypt quantum algorithms more naturally and effectively.
Some notable examples of quantum programming languages and frameworks include Q # (a specific domain language from Microsoft), Qiskit (IBM ’ s Open Source Quantum Software Development Group), and Cirq (Google ’ s Open Source Python Framework).
These tools have been developed to facilitate the creation of quantum software that can run on both simulators and actual quantum devices, allowing programmers and researchers to explore and refine quantum algorithms without needing a deep understanding of fundamental physics.
The advent of quantum programming has also led to the emergence of classical quantum hybrid approaches, where classical and quantum computing resources are combined to solve specific problems.
A notable example is the Quantitative Approximate Optimization (QAOA) algorithm, which involves running iterative optimizations on a quantum processor followed by evaluation and modification on a classical processor.
This technology can efficiently address harmonic optimization issues, which are commonly encountered in real-world applications such as scheduling and resource allocation.

Moreover, many online courses and tutorials cater to beginners and experienced developers alike, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to harness the power of quantum computing.
In short, quantum programming is a rapidly evolving field that seeks to unlock the extraordinary potential of quantum computing through the development of algorithms, languages, and software designed for quantum computers.

Effat Sherif writes: Promises and dangers of temporary online freelancing in developing countries
(MENAFN- Al-BoNews) Decent work for all is the surest way out of extreme poverty, as well as promoting shared prosperity for all.
As new technologies transform global economies, we must expand our thinking about jobs in developing countries.
The temporary online freelancing economy, through digital platforms that match available labor with customer-driven tasks, accounts for up to 12% of the global labor market.
In developing countries, online freelancing platforms open up unique avenues for employment, as well as offering great potential to young people, women and people in remote areas who may have been excluded from traditional labor markets.
Besides, temporary online freelancing provides a necessary source of income in times of shock and transition, helps build digital skills for younger workers and provides flexible earning opportunities for all.
Moreover, temporary online freelancing platforms also provide a cost-effective source of talent for small and emerging businesses, thus supporting businesses to maintain productivity and flexibility, and adapt to rapid shifts in market demand.
In line with the growth of the digital economy and the spirit of innovation around the world, the demand for online free labor in low- and middle-income countries is rising and moving at a faster pace than in industrialized countries.
In Sub-Saharan Africa, for example, job ads posted on a large digital labor platform increased by 130 percent, while in North America, their growth rate did not exceed 14 percent from 2016 to 2020.
Interestingly, among middle-income countries, the lower tier of these countries contributes more to the demand for temporary free labor online than the upper tier of these countries, mainly because of the needs of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
Interestingly, the impact of temporary online freelancing in emerging economies is largely poorly understood and more attention is needed to identify the potential of this type of work.
What are the best policies to maximize the benefits of online freelancing in developing economies?
And what regulations and controls are needed to protect free labor online?
What role do local and regional freelance platforms play?
A new World Bank report, “Work Without Borders: The Promises and Dangers of Temporary Online Freelancing, ” tracks temporary online employment worldwide, including those working across local platforms or using languages other than English, and this employment is often overlooked in most research.
The global prevalence of temporary self-employment online is much greater than previous estimates, and as many as 435 million people perform this work as secondary work.
Nearly 3 billion people globally did not use the internet in 2022, mostly in developing countries.
To address this challenge, the World Bank is working with governments and the private sector to bridge this gap.
This includes policy reforms, public and private financing, and smart support programs for specific segments of the population to stimulate the deployment of digital infrastructure in rural areas and increase the affordability and use of high-speed Internet services and digital devices.
In addition, building digital skills is very important.
In Bangladesh, Malaysia and Kosovo, governments offer online entrepreneurship training specifically to support young people, women and the poorest 40% of the population.
The vast majority of temporary online freelancers, like most informal workers in developing countries, face risks such as income instability, difficult working conditions, and limited ability to save.
Such employment does not enjoy social protection, especially in low-income countries.
More than 90% of the workforce are not covered by social insurance and therefore are not subject to labour regulations.
As outlined in the World Bank's social protection system, Governments should pursue innovative ways to extend coverage to informal and self-employed workers, including temporary self-employment via the Internet.
Digital technology can provide new types of solutions, and online freelance platforms can help increase the visibility of online employment, supporting the government ’ s efforts to expand the social protection umbrella.
Many countries are taking steps in this direction and are working with platforms to encourage workers to register and participate in social insurance.
For example, the government in Malaysia has teamed up with a temporary online freelancing platform to offer a corresponding 5% contribution to the temporary online freelancing market for those who subscribe to the government ’ s retirement savings program.
In addition, it is necessary to design more modern forms of collective bargaining for informal labor such as temporary free labor online.
Evaluations by the public of employers, companies and platforms, or the use of social media to aggregate disparate labor groups, are examples of the use of technology to create new models and solutions.
Although more women participate in the temporary online freelancing economy than in the general labour market, mainly because of the flexibility of working online, the gender pay gap persists.
For example, in some online freelance platforms in developing countries, women earn less than men – in Argentina, women earn 68% less than their male counterparts.
Although temporary online freelancing is still a new and rapidly evolving form of work, it has taken root in low- and middle-income countries and even offers a possible escape from poverty, linking employment to employment globally.
It also provides an opportunity for a growing group of motivated young people to learn and expand digital skills with the aim of earning from work, as well as being a practical option for women facing significant constraints in traditional labour markets.
This work has become a flexible source of talent that entrepreneurs and companies need to grow their businesses, thus creating more jobs.
By focusing on expanding digital connectivity, building digital skills and supporting efforts to expand social protection coverage, we can increase the number of people who thrive in the new online world of work.

7 Exercises Necessary for Perfect Balance
Balance is your ability to coordinate and control your body ’ s center of gravity – in everyday life you have to deal with this all the time!
For example, your balance ensures that you can walk without falling.
(Illustrated - Gettyimages)
Although it may not occur to you, you need a good balance to do almost everything, including walking, getting up from a chair and bending over to tie your shoes.
Balance training involves doing muscle-strengthening exercises that help keep you upright, including your legs and torso as these types of exercises can improve stability and help prevent falls.
And while there are intense balancing exercises like some very challenging yoga poses, others are as simple as standing on one leg for a few seconds.
If you have a problem with this, you can use equipment that forces your body to stabilize, such as a semi-circular stability ball.
Meaning of Balance
Balance is your ability to coordinate and control your body ’ s center of gravity – in everyday life you have to deal with this all the time!
For example, your balance ensures that you can walk without falling, that you can sit up straight, and that you can jump over a hole without falling.
Your body uses different systems: your eyes (the visual system) help you see the space around you, your inner ear (the vestibular system) records rotating movements and accelerations, and the receptors in your joints and muscles and the pressure receptors in your skin (together the stimulus receptor system) transmit changes in your posture.
All the stimuli your body receives through these systems come together in your central nervous system, and your brain in turn sends the message to your muscles that adapt immediately to prevent you from falling; all this has to happen at lightning speed and that ’ s what it should be, as our bodies have to adapt constantly as we move.
With the help of balanced training, you can teach your muscles to respond more quickly to brain messages as this allows you to improve fine motor and coordination skills.
Areas targeted by balance
• Middle: Yes, balance exercises target this area, you need strong core muscles to achieve good balance, many stability exercises work to exercise the abdominal muscles and other core muscles.
• Forearms: No, balance exercises do not target these ends, most balance exercises revolve around balance on your feet.
Legs: Yes, the legs are definitely areas where balance is targeted, and exercises in which you balance on one leg and then squat or lean forward also work to exercise the leg muscles.
Buttock: Yes, the same balance exercises that work on the legs also work to strengthen the buttocks.
Back: Another area targeted by balance exercises, where your core muscles include some of your back muscles.
Good balance depends on:
Sensory information from your eyes (visual system), muscles, tendons, joints (stimulation inputs), and balance organs in the inner ear (vestibular system).
The brain stem understands all of this sensory information combined with other parts of the brain.
Movement of your eyes to keep things stable in your vision and maintain your balance.
What are the benefits of balance training?
The benefits of balance training are great, for example:
• You can improve your posture and you can stand or sit better.
• Train your deep muscles, especially the muscles in the torso and around the spine.
• Reduce back wear and less muscle pain due to poor posture.
Prevent injuries during exercise and in daily life because your body is not constantly out of balance, causing muscle strain.
• Ability to perform movements more efficiently and smoothly.
A positive effect on how your body feels and your performance improves as you make faster progress.
• Improve the motor coordination of the body.
How often do you have to do this type of training?
You have to aim to do balance workouts one to two times a week, this applies to beginners all the way to advanced athletes, and it is very important that professionals improve their stability as well.
Simple exercises to get the perfect balance:
Tai Chi (Tai Chi)
Studies show that tai chi, a gentle exercise often called “movement meditation, ” can help you reduce falls if you ’ re older and have balance problems, a skilled teacher can show you slow and precise movements that help you not only achieve more stability but also boost your overall health and mood as well.
Standing on one leg (one-legged stand)
Start by installing yourself on the back of the chair or any other sturdy handle.
Raise one foot to approximately calf level and hold for 10 seconds.
• Repeat this 10-15 times and then move on to the other leg.
As time goes on and your balance improves you may be able to continue in this situation without fixating yourself on any purpose.
Weight Shifts (Weight Shifts)
Stand with your feet spaced by the width of your hip.
Slowly lean forward horizontally on one leg to bear all your weight while lifting the other leg off the ground.
• Wait for up to 30 seconds, then move to the other side.
You can do the same exercise while standing straight and raising one leg forward or left / right.
• Yoga and Pilates
To maintain your balance, you need muscles that can hold you while standing, walking, or doing other movements. These muscles are known as your “core muscles. ” Yoga and Pilates involve movements that help you stretch and strengthen these muscles, but first consult your doctor before starting and to learn the movements correctly it is a good idea to join a nearby class taught by a certified instructor.
Heel-to-Toe Walk
Walk slowly in a straight line.
• Touch your heel to the opposite toe as you progress.
Walk about 20 steps using the wall for support if you feel unsteady.
Back Leg Raises (Back Leg Raises)
To build up the lower back and buttocks, try raising your back leg while standing upright.
Hold a chair and lift one of your legs back without bending your knee or pointing your toe.
• Keep the leg on the floor slightly bent.
• Hold position for 5 seconds.
Do this 10-15 times with the first leg before moving on to the other leg.
• Squats (squats)
To strengthen the muscles of your legs and pelvis, do a squat exercise.
Stand up straight, make your feet slightly wider than your hips while pointing your toes forward.
Bend your knees and send your ass back, and slowly descend as if you were sitting.
Place your weight on your heels and arms in front of you or on your thighs.
Raise yourself once and repeat 10 times.
To get a better idea of how strong your balance is while standing, lift one foot and see how long you can keep it there, or test your balance as you move and try to walk as if you were on a tightrope for 10 steps and see how it goes, you ’ ve probably noticed that one side is much stronger and more coordinated than the other.

The researchers used data from more than 300 tidal gauges around the world to conduct trend analyses and estimate future extreme sea levels under two carbon emission scenarios set by the International Panel on Climate Change: if carbon dioxide emissions continue to rise until the end of the century, and if carbon dioxide emissions peak by 2040 and then fall, and in both scenarios, they found that the level of carbon dioxide is rising. Previous studies relied on consistent estimates of extreme sea levels to predict flooding for 100 years, but this study used non-static methods and found that the shift in extreme sea levels would not be uniform at many tidal measurement sites.

Opinions about the feasibility of Egypt ’ s return to expand the granting of tax exemptions to attract new investments varied between those who considered it a departure from the approach of economic reform that began in 2016 based on the recommendations of the International Monetary Fund, and those who believe it is necessary to attract local investments, while tax experts agreed that the target is the local investor in light of an international agreement with a minimum tax on multinational companies.
The government approved a stimulus package targeting strategic industries with the aim of deepening the industry, including tax exemption, with the exception of value-added tax, up to five years, and the possibility of extending the exemption for a similar period, provided that they achieve specific targets, according to the size of external investment and the controls determined by the Council of Ministers.

Al-Kilani: The continued imposition of “value added ” on projects is important for the governance of the tax community
He explained that these exemptions contribute to increasing tax evasion rates locally, and that the International Fund recommends the need to limit the payment of more exemptions.
According to Egypt ’ s program documents with the IMF, the government has pledged to publish a comprehensive annual report on tax expenditures, detailing and estimating tax exemptions, including those provided to companies in free economic zones, all state-owned enterprises, as well as public sector companies, the public business sector, joint ventures and partnerships.
Sherif El-Kilani, CEO of Ernst & Young Egypt, said that the directives related to tax exemptions are encouraging for local investment while attracting foreign investment requires the addition of several factors, including the stability of the tax policy, ease of issuing licenses, and the possibility of transferring profits abroad, with a focus on the availability of trained workers.
He explained that the continued imposition of value added tax on these projects aims to increase the governance and accounting of the tax community.
Abdulla Al Adly, Principal Tax Partner at Moore Egypt Tax and Financial Advisory, said that according to the multilateral agreement, tax exemptions do not encourage international investment, which means that their impact on exemptions is limited only to local investment.

Khaled Abu Zahra, senior tax partner, told MMC Egypt and the Gulf that according to the multilateral agreement, the source countries in which companies operate give up their tax rights through the application of more exemptions that transfer those revenues externally to the countries of residence.

How to Use Personal Voice Feature in iOS 17
Apple ’ s iOS 17 update contains new features useful for people with hearing or speech problems, including: Personal Voice, one of the iPhone ’ s accessibility features.
Personal Voice is a feature that uses machine learning to create a copy of your voice with voice samples that you record, and this feature works with another new accessibility feature in iOS 17 called Live Speech to convert text to voice.
With personal voice and direct speech, you can write messages in FaceTime, or make a call, and what you want will be said verbally in a voice similar to yours.
First, how to set up a personal voice feature:
Before you start using the Personal Voice feature, you should know that setting it up takes some time, as it takes 15 to 20 minutes to add samples of your voice, as well as several hours to process the voice, so make sure you have enough time to set up before you start, then follow these steps:
1.
Go to Settings and then select Accessibility.
2.
Click Personal Voice in the Speech section, and then click Create a Personal Voice.
3.
A screen will appear with instructions to guide you on how to get started, you will be asked to record 150 phrases aloud in a quiet place, you should speak normally and hold your device between 6 and 12 inches away.
While recording audio samples, you will be asked to read 150 phrases that include a set of questions and data that contain historical facts and random excerpts.
The importance of variation in phrases lies in capturing the full range of your voice in different contexts and tones, which is why you need to provide multiple audio samples.
This step will take 15 to 20 minutes, depending on your downtime and reading speed.
You can pause while recording phrases, or save and close them, allowing you to go back to the setup process again.
4.
After you ’ ve finished recording all the phrases, click continue and the phone starts setting up your personal voice.
At this point, your iPhone should be locked and connected to the charger, and the lock screen will show that your personal voice is being processed and you will receive a notification when it is ready.
This process will take a few hours to complete, so start setting up the feature before bedtime, and leave your phone during bedtime to complete the personal audio setup.
Second: How to use the personal voice feature:
Once the Personal Voice feature is set up, start using it by adding your voice to the Live Speech voice collection, and to do so, follow these steps:
1.
Go to Settings, then Accessibility, then Live Speech.
2.
Turn on the Live Speech option, and in the Voices section of the same page, your personal voice will be one of the options available in the Sounds menu, click Personal Voice to choose your voice.
3.
To use this feature at any time you will need to activate the Live Speech feature, you can do this by clicking three times on the side play button, and a window will appear at the bottom of the screen asking you to write a message.
4.
When you type the message and press the input button, you ’ ll hear a copy of your voice created by artificial intelligence.
You can do this at any time to test the feature, when you ’ re using FaceTime or during a phone call.

A recent study by North Carolina State University sheds light on why some freshwater insects suffer in salt water.
The research suggests that a lack of metabolic responses to increased salinity could be a contributing factor.
Salinity refers to the concentration of salts in the aquatic environment, exceeding only sodium.
Freshwater habitats are becoming saltier due to various factors such as road salt, agricultural runoff, coal and natural gas extraction, drought, and sea-level rise.
These changes in salinity affect the diversity of organisms, including freshwater insects that act as indicators of ecosystem health.
Aquatic animals, including insects and crustaceans, must maintain a water-salt balance within their bodies, a process called osmotic regulation.
Ideally, these animals will thrive in an environment where their external salinity levels correspond to their internal levels, reducing the energy needed for osmotic regulation.
However, the study found that high salinity is often associated with increased ion absorption rates in freshwater insects, leading to delayed growth or death.
The researchers hypothesized that freshwater insects devote a lot of energy to osmotic regulation in saltier environments, causing them to struggle to grow or thrive.
To test this hypothesis, the researchers measured the metabolic rates of crustaceans, insects and snails in different salinity conditions.
They found that while the metabolic rates of crustaceans and snails increased in attenuated environments, the metabolic rates of insects remained constant regardless of salinity.
In addition, the team found that calcium was the main driver of increased metabolism in non-insects with low salinity, as these animals worked harder to transport calcium ions.
On the other hand, insects had a higher calcium ion transport rate in saltier environments, although their metabolic rates did not rise.
This suggests that insects have a lower demand for calcium and may use resources that can be used for growth and development to counter over-absorption of ions in saltier environments.
The study challenges the idea that freshwater insects thrive in environments close to their internal salinity.
Instead, low demand for calcium allows them to grow in diluted environments typically dominated by insects.
Conversely, low calcium appears to put pressure on crustaceans and snails.
Further research will investigate whether these physiological differences stem from the origin of organisms or their use of calcium in exoskeletons and shells.
In conclusion, the study highlights the potential costs of a consistent metabolism of freshwater insects in salt water.
The findings provide a better understanding of how changes in salinity affect aquatic ecosystems and can help guide conservation efforts.
Source: North Carolina State University.

Quantum physicists at Trinity College Dublin have achieved a significant breakthrough by simulating superdiffusion in a system of interacting quantum particles on a quantum computer.
This achievement, made possible through a collaboration with IBM Dublin, opens up new avenues for research in condensed matter physics and materials science.
The team used a 27-qubit quantum computer located at the IBM lab in New York but programmed remotely from Dublin.
Quantum computing, a booming field, is showing promising results for both commercial applications and basic research.
Through simulations, the researchers aim to gain insights into quantum transfer calculations, which are difficult to solve on classical computers.
Quantum simulation allows scientists to study the dynamics of complex quantum systems with interacting components.
The advantage of using a quantum computer for this simulation is that the quantum system itself is described by a wave function, eliminating the need to significantly increase classical resources.
This makes quantum simulation an attractive way to study quantum dynamics.
In this particular study, the team focused on simulating spin chains, which serve as models for understanding magnetism in more complex materials.
They investigated the long-term behavior of spin excitation and noted the super-propagation, which is characterized by faster transmission as the size of the system increases.
The researchers were able to verify the existence of the Cardar-Parisi-Jang equation, which describes the random growth of surfaces, in the quantum dynamics of the simulated system.
Programming quantum computers comes with its own set of challenges.
One of the big challenges is dealing with errors and disruptions caused by noise and environmental factors.
Reducing program uptime is critical to mitigating the impact of these disruptions on results.
This achievement by quantum physicists at Trinity College Dublin underscores the potential of quantum computing in furthering our understanding of fundamental physics and facilitating future technological advances.
As quantum simulation becomes more widespread, Trinity ’ s Quantum Alliance, in partnership with IBM and other industry collaborators, is well positioned to drive further innovation in the field.

How did artificial intelligence enter the war in Sudan?
A campaign using artificial intelligence to impersonate Sudan ’ s former president, Omar al-Bashir, has generated hundreds of thousands of views on TikTok, adding online confusion to a country ravaged by civil war.
An anonymous account has been publishing what it says are “leaked recordings ” of the former president since late August.
The channel posted dozens of clips — but the sound is fake.
Bashir, accused of war crimes and ousted by the military in 2019, has not appeared in public for a year and is believed to be suffering from a serious illness.
He denies accusations of war crimes.
The uncertainty surrounding his whereabouts adds further uncertainty to a country in crisis after fighting broke out in April between the army, now in charge, and rival Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia.
Experts say such campaigns are important because they show how new tools can quickly and cheaply spread fake content on social media.
Hani Farid, a researcher in digital forensics at the University of California in the United States, says: “Democratizing (freedom) access to cutting-edge audio and video processing technology is what worries me most. ”
“Sophisticated actors have been able to distort reality for decades, but now the average person with little or no technical expertise can create fake content quickly and easily. ”
The recordings are posted on the Voice of Sudan channel.
The publications appear to be a mix of old clips from press conferences during the coup attempts, news reports and several “leaked recordings ” attributed to Bashir.
Posts often look like they ’ re taken from a meeting or phone conversation, and they seem as cluttered as you might expect from a lousy phone line.
To verify its authenticity, we first consulted a team of experts on Sudan in the BBC ’ s media monitoring section.
Ibrahim Haithar told us that these recordings are unlikely to be recent.
“The voice sounds like Bashir, but he has been very ill over the past few years and I doubt he will be able to speak that clearly. ”
That doesn't mean it's not him.
We ’ ve also investigated other possible explanations, but this isn ’ t an old clip showing up again, and it ’ s unlikely to be the work of someone who knows how to mimic the voice.
The most definitive guide came from users on X, formerly Twitter.
They identified Bashir ’ s first recordings published in August 2023.
It appears to show the former president criticizing Sudan ’ s army chief, General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.
Bashir ’ s recording matched a live broadcast on Facebook, broadcast two days earlier by a well-known Sudanese political commentator, known as al-Ansrafi.
He is believed to be living in the United States but has never shown his face on camera.
Recording and streaming don ’ t look exactly the same, but the scripts are the same, and when you play both clips together, they play perfectly synchronously.
Mr Farid points out that comparing sound waves shows similar patterns of speech and silence.
Evidence suggests that the voice-switching software was used to mimic Bashir ’ s speech.
The program is a powerful tool that allows you to download a sound clip, which can be changed to a different sound.
After further research, something came up.
We found at least four other Bashir recordings taken from the blogger ’ s own live stream.
But there is no evidence of his involvement.
TikTok ’ s account is purely political and requires deep knowledge of what is happening in Sudan, but the identity of the beneficiary of this campaign remains open to debate.
One consistent narrative is criticism of the army chief, General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.
The motive may have been to deceive the public into believing that Bashir appeared to play a role in the war.
Or perhaps the channel is trying to legitimize a particular political point of view, using the voice of the former leader.
Voice of Sudan denies misleading public opinion and says it does not belong to any group.
We contacted the account, and we received a textual response saying: “I want to communicate my voice and explain the reality my country is going through in my style. ”
Henry Ajder, whose BBC 4 series deals with the evolution of artificial media, says an attempt on this scale to impersonate Bashir can be seen as “important to the region ” and has the potential to deceive the masses.
AI experts have long been concerned that fake videos and audio will lead to a wave of misinformation, potentially provoking unrest and disrupting elections.
Mohammed Suleiman, a researcher at Northeastern University ’ s Civic Artificial Intelligence Lab, said: “What ’ s worrying is that these recordings can also create an environment where many people don ’ t believe even real recordings. ”
As we ’ ve seen in this example, people have to wonder if a recording seems reasonable before sharing it.
Checking whether it ’ s released by a trusted source is vital, but voice verification is difficult, especially when content is circulating on messaging apps. It ’ s even more difficult during a period of social unrest, such as the one currently in Sudan.
The technique of creating algorithms trained to detect artificial sound is still in very early stages of development, while the technique of imitating sounds is already very advanced.
After the BBC contacted TikTok, the account was blocked.

Medical advice for the prevention of osteoporosis..
Months of symptoms
Dr. Eleonora Arsenieva said the effects of osteoporosis can be devastating, but the disease is treatable and preventable, a large number of fractures associated with osteoporosis occur each year, and millions of deaths occur each month as a result of a hip fracture.
What is Osteoporosis?
Osteoporosis is when bones gradually become more brittle, and the right combination of lifestyle changes, dietary changes, and exercise can stop the progression of bone loss and in some cases increase bone density.
And while prevention is really the best course of action, there are important steps that can help you if you already have the disease, Dr. Eleonora Arsenieva tells MedicForum.
Symptoms of osteoporosis
In the early stages of bone loss, there are usually no symptoms however, if your bones are damaged, you may experience the following signs of osteoporosis:
Back pain caused by the destruction or fracture of the vertebrae.
Gradual loss of height.
The flabby posture.
A bone fracture that occurs more easily.
Hormone levels
One of the strongest risk factors is low estrogen levels in postmenopausal women.
Treatment of prostate cancer in men and breast cancer in women can accelerate bone loss, and hyperthyroidism, or overproduction of thyroid hormones, can also cause bone loss.
Doctor ’ s Tips for Preventing and Even Reversing Osteoporosis
Getting enough calcium and vitamin D is an important part of preventing osteoporosis and other related diseases by promoting bone growth and bone health.
Eating lots of fruits and vegetables will not only benefit the health of your bones, but your overall health as bones can be strengthened through exercise, so it is recommended to exercise for at least two and a half hours a week to improve their strength.
Osteoporosis prevention and bone health can be improved at any age you don ’ t think it ’ s too late and talk to your doctor for advice on how to improve your bone health.

A new study by Indian and German scientists has found that aerosols are causing the Himalayas to heat up dramatically, with serious implications for climate change and monsoon patterns in the region.
The study, which included ground observations, satellite data and model simulations, highlighted the high aerosol radiative forcing efficiency (ARFE) over the Indian Ganges Plains (IGP) and Himalayan foothills.
The average ARFE was found to be 2-4 times higher in this region compared to other contaminated sites in South and East Asia.
Aerosols are fine solid particles or liquid droplets suspended in the atmosphere, which can be of natural or man-made origin.
The researchers noted that aerosol-induced warming observed at high altitudes of the Himalayas increases air temperatures, accelerates the retreat of glaciers, and affects the hydrological cycle and precipitation patterns.
The study confirmed that these changes have significant consequences for the summer monsoon in Asia and the melting of snow ice.
The Himalayan region, including the Hindu Kush-Himalaya-Tibet Plateau (HKHTP), is home to the largest ice mass outside the Antarctic and Arctic polar regions.
The observed retreat of glaciers in this region is influenced by atmospheric warming caused by aerosols and the deposition of light-absorbing carbon aerosols on snow and ice.
The researchers warned that this rapid retreat of glaciers would have negative impacts on water supplies in South and East Asia, affecting the regional hydrological cycle.
The study highlights the need for further research and understanding of the impact of aerosols on the Himalayan climate and the larger impacts on climate change and water resources in the region.

How does Egyptian Petroleum turn cooking oil into jet fuel?
The aviation industry is one of the sectors that contribute significantly to carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, which makes it responsible for a large part of these challenges, and with the advancement of technology and research and development there has been an innovative solution to this problem through the production and use of jet fuel from used cooking oil.
How to produce jet fuel from used cooking oil
Production and Technology:
The process of producing jet fuel from used cooking oil involves several basic steps. First, used cooking oil is collected and assembled from various sources, such as restaurants and food factories, and then purified and filtered well to remove solids and impurities.
This can include chemical reactions with adjuvants or the application of analysis and conversion processes, with the aim of converting the oil into a sustainable aviation fuel that meets international standards of quality and safety.
Fuel Output:
The final product is aviation fuel that can be used in aircraft engines, this fuel is similar to diesel in terms of its chemical and physical properties, it can be stored and transported using the already existing infrastructure of traditional aviation fuel, without the need for major modifications in aircraft or in aviation airports.
Environmental and economic benefits:
The use of aviation fuel derived from used cooking oil carries many benefits, from an environmental point of view, reduces CO2 emissions and other harmful emissions produced by the aviation industry, in addition, helps reduce dependence on fossil fuels and minimizes the depletion of natural resources.
Economically, the production and use of jet fuel from used cooking oil can provide lower operating costs for airlines, can be less expensive for consumers, and can encourage investment in this technology and promote the airline industry ’ s transition towards sustainability.
Developments and challenges:
Researchers and engineers are working to develop production processes and improve the quality of used jet fuel, however, the industry also faces challenges, such as ensuring the quality and safety of fuel and complying with local and international legislation and regulations.

YouTube is developing an artificial intelligence tool to use the voices of musicians
YouTube is developing an artificial intelligence tool that will allow content makers to record audio using the voices of famous musicians.
The video streaming giant has reached out to music companies for the rights to songs it can use to train the new AI tool.
The companies have yet to sign any deal, although discussions between the two sides continue.

YouTube must figure out how to legally use this new technology.

YouTube presents itself as a partner in the use of generative AI technology, having developed over the past year a lot of generative AI tools, although it is currently unknown if it can legally provide content makers with AI voice transcription tools without raising many copyright lawsuits.

The amount of dust in the world's air worsened in 2022, according to the United Nations World Meteorological Organization.
The organization called for more research on the relationship between climate change and increasing sandstorm hotspots.
The rise in dust is attributed to increased emissions from areas such as West Central Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, the Iranian Plateau, and northwest China.
WMO President Petteri Taalas stressed that human activities affect sandstorms and dust storms.
Higher temperatures, drought and increased evaporation lead to lower soil moisture, which, together with poor land management, contributes to more frequent sand and dust storms.
The annual WMO report analyses the occurrence and risks of dust storms and highlights their impact on society.
The report revealed that the global average annual dust surface concentrations in 2022 were slightly higher than in 2021.
In 2021, the figure was 13.5 micrograms per cubic meter, while in 2022 it rose to 13.8 micrograms per cubic meter.
The Baudeli region of Chad recorded the highest estimated annual average surface dust concentration, ranging from 900 to 1,200 micrograms per cubic meter.
In the southern hemisphere, central Australia and the west coast of South Africa recorded the highest concentrations, ranging from 200 to 300 micrograms per cubic metre.
Dust storms have far-reaching effects, contributing to the dark sky and damaging air quality.
Nearly 2,000 million tons of dust enter the atmosphere each year, affecting economies, ecosystems, weather and climate, even in areas thousands of kilometers away, the report said.
While natural processes play a role, poor water and land management also contributes significantly.
The bulletin highlighted three major incidents in 2022, including an “exceptional dust outbreak ” from North Africa over Spain and Portugal, which exceeded EU air quality regulations.
Another severe dust storm occurred in the Middle East, resulting in reduced visibility across the region.
In addition, a dust storm on farmland in the eastern United States affected agricultural activities.
Taalas stressed the importance of addressing the effects of sand and dust storms on health, transport and agriculture.
The publication called for more research on the relationship between dust storms and climate change, as this region remains largely unexplored.
The World Meteorological Organization aims to establish early warning systems for weather disasters around the world within four years to mitigate the worsening effects of climate change, including dust storms.

The underwater world is often seen as a silent and quiet place.
However, this idea cannot be further from the truth.
Contrary to popular belief, the ocean is teeming with sounds, ranging from the painful songs of humpback whales to the complex communication networks of different fish species.
In fact, sound travels faster and farther in water than in air, making it a staple of marine life.
It is fascinating to think about how our understanding of the oceans and their inhabitants has evolved over time.
In 1943, French engineer Émile Gagnon and naval lieutenant Jacques Cousteau invented the underwater breathing device (SCUBA), which revolutionized our ability to explore the depths of the sea.
Through his groundbreaking television documentaries, Cousteau has played a crucial role in promoting and illuminating the wonders of ocean life, as David Attenborough does today.
Throughout history, we have wrongly viewed the ocean as a silent world.
Our ears, attuned to airborne vibrations, struggle to perceive the underwater acoustic scene.
Cousteau himself believed that the voice was absent in the depths.
However, we now know that the ocean is a symphony of sounds, in which marine organisms use complex sounds to communicate, navigate, and hunt.
But as with many environmental challenges, human activity has upset this delicate balance.
Noise pollution from sources such as ship engines, wind turbine installations and offshore drills has been increasing steadily since the Industrial Revolution.
The constant tinnitus of underwater noise has forced marine animals, such as whales, to shout louder to be heard amid dissonance.
Unfortunately, a new study from Utrecht University brings more disturbing news.
The researchers found that warming oceans, due to climate change, is exacerbating the problem of underwater noise pollution.
Warmer, more acidic waters enhance sound transmission through the water, making the ocean more noisy.
Climate change will also stratify the North Atlantic, creating an “acoustic channel ” that allows noise to travel further.
The impact of this increased underwater noise pollution is significant and far-reaching.
Marine life relies on sound for survival, from finding mates to locating food and avoiding predators.
Disturbing acoustic landscapes can disrupt these vital processes, leading to a low population and ecosystem imbalance.
To protect the acoustic sensitive environment of the oceans, it is essential to reduce man-made sources of underwater noise and mitigate the effects of climate change.
More stringent regulations on shipping, construction activities and naval exercises could help reduce the impact.
In addition, advocacy for sustainable practices and conservation of marine habitats is essential to maintaining the natural acoustic landscape of our oceans.
So, the next time you contemplate the breadth of the ocean, remember that beneath its seemingly calm surface is a world full of vitality and sound – a world that we must strive to protect for the sake of all its inhabitants.
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Q: How was the underwater respirator (SCUBA) invented?
A: The underwater respirator (Scuba) was invented in 1943 by French engineer Émile Gagnon and naval lieutenant Jacques Cousteau.
Q: How has our understanding of the acoustic landscape of the oceans changed over time?
A: At first, the ocean was thought to be silent.
However, we now know that the underwater world is full of a variety of sounds, from whale songs to ways of communication between different fish species.
Q: How does underwater noise pollution affect marine life?
A: Noise pollution disrupts vital communications and navigation processes for marine animals, leading to a potential reduction in their numbers and ecosystem imbalance.
Q: How does climate change contribute to underwater noise pollution?
A: Rising ocean temperature and increasing acidity, due to climate change, enhance the transmission of sound through water, making the underwater acoustic scene louder and more disturbing.
Q: What can be done to mitigate underwater noise pollution?
A: Implementing stricter regulations on man-made underwater noise sources and taking steps to address climate change can help mitigate the impact of underwater noise pollution on marine life.

Quantum computing.
Is it time to get serious about it?
The old joke that quantum computing is the technology of the future — and will remain so forever — is no longer funny.
The engineering challenges of building a quantum computer powerful enough to fulfill its extraordinary theoretical promise remain enormous.
But early prototypes are evolving rapidly and the future may come faster than expected.
Every data-rich body should start thinking about how to move into a quantum world, as the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology is set to release encryption standards for the post-quantum era next year.
Quantum computers, which exploit the frightening behavior of subatomic physics, operate differently from conventional computers, expanding the range of possible solutions to many problems.
Some companies are exploring the potential of hybrid methods, combining the current capabilities of primitive quantum computers and their classical counterparts to improve port logistics, airline schedules, grocery delivery, and TV ad programming, for example.
Alan Baratz, CEO of DWave, an American quantum computing company, said: “Quantum has become real today.
But serious threats to quantum computing may emerge faster than its potential.
Security experts warn of the dangers of QDay, when a quantum computer may be able to hack into the RSA encryption system, widely used by tech companies, banks and governments in their data.
Earlier this month, the heads of the intelligence agency Five Eyes, which included the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, warned of the dangers of China ’ s activities in quantum computing, artificial intelligence and synthetic biology.
Ken McCallum, director general of MI5, said: “If you ’ re close to the latest technologies, you may not be interested in geopolitics, but geopolitics is interested in you. ”
Since 1994, when mathematician Peter Shore wrote an algorithm that could run on an as-yet-uninvented quantum computer to hack the RSA system, security experts have been concerned about the world ’ s digital secrets.
It may take another decade (or more) before we have a quantum computer stable enough to run Shore ’ s algorithm, but we can never be sure when that day will come.
However, this is one of those rare technological fields, when the solution anticipates the problem.
Since 2016, the US National Institute has been ordering and evaluating anti-cryptography.
Four approved standards will be released next year, which will then be replaced by other agencies around the world.
According to Ilham Kashefi, chief scientist at the UK ’ s National Centre for Quantum Computing, it would be “very worrying ” if any organisation held sensitive data that was not really prepared for the threat posed by QDay.
Speaking at the Ceftaid summit earlier this month, she said: “You should be very concerned. ”
One concern, Kashefi said, is that adversaries can harness data today and decrypt it later when quantum computers have evolved.
That may not matter if the old data hacked are daily supermarket sales records.
But it will be different if the data contains health records or sensitive personal information.
Switching from one crypto system to another across thousands of organizations will take years to implement.
That ’ s why internet experts are urging companies to start thinking now about how to adopt the NIST crypto standard.
The transition to a quantum resistant world would be a win-win for some cybersecurity companies.
That ’ s what BQ Shield, an Oxford-based startup that recently held an expert conference to examine whether NIST ’ s mathematical drafts can work in the “bad ” hardware world.
The good news, according to Ali al-Qafarani, founder of BQ Shield, is that it can.
He said to me, “Is there a perfect security solution at all?
He never exists.
"But my personal view is that these schemes are very secure, powerful and very difficult to penetrate, whether on a classical or quantum computer."
When I spoke with Shore earlier this year, he predicted that the quantum computer needed to run his algorithm might still be several decades away.
But in the meantime, he composed a poem to explain the quantum puzzle:
"If the computers you are building are quantitative,
Spies from all factions will want it.
All our symbols will fail.
They'll read all of our e-mails.
Until we get quantum cryptography, and scare them with its power. ”

The ethical and legal features of manipulating music sounds using artificial intelligence
(MENAFN- Al-Bayan)
Today, we live in the era of digital technology, where modern technologies are playing an increasingly important role in the music industry, and one of the technologies, which have significantly affected this industry are artificial intelligence techniques, which enable producers and musicians to modify the sounds of songs in advanced ways, yet these technologies raise multiple issues in terms of legal and ethical responsibility.
The problem of modifying song sounds using AI software is legally complex.
This adjustment can include changing sounds, removing errors, adjusting times, and more.
If these technologies are used without permission from artists or song rights holders, it can be a violation of intellectual property rights.
Often these works require licenses and legal agreements with artists, and rights holders.
Legally, the assessment of liability depends on several factors.
First of all, it is necessary to verify the existence of specific licenses and agreements, which allow for the modification of votes.
If there is a written agreement that allows for this type of amendment, the legal liability is greatly reduced, however, if AI technologies are used to modify votes without explicit permission or authorization, this can lead to infringement of intellectual property rights, exposing the responsible party to legal accountability.
Some countries have adopted strict legislation to protect the rights of artists and owners of intellectual property rights.
For example in the United States such cases are considered under copyright and trademark laws, and sometimes penalties for intellectual property rights violations can be harsh, including significant financial compensation.
On the other hand, there are ethical aspects related to the proper use of AI techniques in modifying the sounds of songs, and artists and producers should consider the extent to which these modifications affect the quality of songs and their resonance to the audience, and the increasing manipulation of sounds may lead to loss of originality, and human communication in music.
In conclusion there must be a balance between the use of technology and legal and ethical responsibility in the music industry.
Producers and artists should abide by applicable laws and regulations, and tread carefully with AI technologies, to ensure that intellectual property rights are respected and the quality and authenticity of music is preserved.
In the end, the parties concerned must tread cautiously and transparently on this issue.

The Arctic region is currently undergoing rapid and significant changes, with acidification and warming occurring at alarming rates.
These shifts raise concerns about the resilience of marine communities in the face of such environmental shifts.
Marine zooplankton, especially copepods, play a crucial role in the Arctic food web.
However, differences in environmental conditions can disrupt zooplankton populations, leading to adverse consequences for the entire ecosystem.
Recent research has focused on understanding the extent to which copepods in early life are exposed to environmental stressors, as they represent a critical bottleneck in the copepods life cycle.
A study by Espinel Velasco et al.
(2023) Explore the responses of 4-day-old Kalanos Hyperborius Lenobli to acidification (pH 7.5 and 8.1) and warming (0 and 3 ° C), both individually and collectively.
The study revealed that the larvae 'breathing rates increased significantly when exposed to a combination of acidification and warming.
Surprisingly, exposure to these stressors individually did not produce the same effect.
Surprisingly, the researchers did not find any noticeable differences in fat content and fatty acid composition in the larvae across various experimental treatments.
Wax esters, which make up about 75% of the fat reserve, and high amounts of long-chain fatty acids 20: 1 and 22: 1, necessary for copepods to reproduce, have been detected in all treatments.
By highlighting the sensitivity of larvae to the combined effects of acidification and warming, this study aligns with a growing body of evidence from relevant research.
It highlights the potential impacts of global change on Arctic copepod populations and stresses the importance of understanding early life stage responses to environmental stressors.
Questions and Answers:
Q: What are zooplankton?
A: Zooplankton refers to small, often microscopic, organisms that drift into the ocean or other bodies of water and serve as one of the main sources of food for many marine species.
Q: What is the role of copepods in the Arctic food web?
A: Copepods, especially calanotic copepods such as Calanus Hyperboreus, are a critical component of the Arctic food web.
They serve as a vital link between primary producers (such as phytoplankton) and higher trophic levels, serving as a food source for various marine species.
Q: What is acidification?
A: Acidification refers to the process of increasing acidity (lowering pH) in seawater due to the absorption of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
This occurs as a result of human activities, such as the burning of fossil fuels.
Q: How does global warming affect marine ecosystems?
A: Ocean warming can have various impacts on marine ecosystems, including changes in species distribution, changing reproductive cycles, and potential disruptions to the delicate balance of food webs.

Biden issues executive order setting safety, security and transparency standards for artificial intelligence systems
US President Joe Biden
Published on: Tuesday 31 October 2023 - 8: 08 AM | Last updated on Tuesday 31 October 2023 - 8: 08 AM
US President Joe Biden on Monday issued an executive order setting out safety, security and transparency standards for artificial intelligence systems, requiring companies developing them to share details of systems safety tests with the US government.
Companies that train in artificial intelligence through so-called foundational models, which may pose risks to national security and public health depending on how they are deployed, must disclose safety results to U.S. agencies.
Foundational models refer to AI systems that absorb large amounts of data and can then be deployed in a variety of applications.
Many AI systems that use natural language processing, and those that propose the creation of new chemical compounds, use foundational models.
The National Institute of Standards and Technology will set a standard for the types of safety tests that companies must perform before releasing AI systems.
The Department of Homeland Security will then apply these standards to systems used in critical infrastructure sectors and establish a safety and security board on artificial intelligence.
The Biden order uses the authority the president has under the Defense Production Act, which presidents routinely use to oversee U.S. companies for the purpose of national security.
Former President Donald Trump used the law during the COVID-19 pandemic to control exports of medical goods and boost production of vital supplies.

First Global Summit to Discuss the Risks of Artificial Intelligence
Here are the details of Day 1.
The first Global AI Safety Summit, hosted by the United Kingdom, kicked off on Wednesday, November 1, and will continue until Thursday, November 2, when political leaders, executives from major technology companies and AI experts will gather to examine the risks posed by the rapid development of this revolutionary technology.
The UK government chose the venue for the summit in Bletchley Park, northwest of London, a highly symbolic centre that saw the development of the first computer system, where German military codes were decoded during World War II.
The summit aims to achieve a common understanding of the risks associated with AI, lay the foundations for advanced international cooperation to ensure its safety, identify measures that individual organizations should take to increase the safety of AI use, and focus on collaboration in AI safety research, such as evaluating language models, developing new standards, and reviewing how to ensure its safe development, with the aim of maximizing benefits globally.
Michelle Donilan, the UK Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, delivered a speech on the first day stressing that the risks posed by AI are serious and fundamental, and it is important that we work together, across sectors and countries alike, to identify these risks, noting that the summit is an opportunity to make sure we have the right people with the right experience gathered around the table to discuss how to mitigate these risks going forward.
“Artificial intelligence is an extraordinary force for good in our society, with limitless opportunities to grow the global economy and deliver better public services.
Artificial Intelligence and the Arab World:
Saudi Arabia and the UAE are major players in the AI market in the Arab region, so both countries are participating in the AI Safety Summit.
The summit is currently attended by His Excellency Omar Sultan Al Olama, UAE Minister of Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Teleworking Applications, and His Excellency Dr. Abdullah bin Sharaf Al Ghamdi, President of the Saudi Commission for Data and Artificial Intelligence (SADaya).
Musk: AI Safety Summit Aims to Establish Regulatory Framework for AI
US billionaire Elon Musk, who is also attending the summit, said: “What we ’ re really aiming for here is to create a supervisory framework so that there is at least a third-party referee, an independent referee, who can monitor what leading AI companies are doing, and at least sound the alarm if there are concerns. ”
Musk said he doesn't necessarily know what the fair rules are, but you need to start understanding the nature of things before you can supervise.
Musk ’ s comments came after Britain published a declaration signed by 28 countries and the European Union, which outlined a two-pronged agenda focused on identifying and understanding AI risks on a scientific basis and building coordinated policies between countries to mitigate them.
“I think there ’ s a big concern among AI workers that governments will rush to set the rules before they know what to do, ” he said.
China, US and EU agree to work together:

Coral reefs, often referred to as “sea rainforests, ” are not only stunningly beautiful but also play a crucial role in supporting marine ecosystems and providing habitat for countless species.
However, the devastating effects of climate change, including rising ocean temperatures, have caused mass bleaching events that threaten the existence of these sensitive ecosystems.
However, the recent discovery by researchers at the University of Melbourne and the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) offers a glimmer of hope for the world ’ s dying coral reefs.
Traditionally, corals rely on a symbiotic relationship with microalgae called Zooxanthellae.
These small algae supply the corals with energy, while the corals provide them with structural shelter and vital nutrients.
However, when the water temperature rises beyond a certain point, the corals expel the microalgae, leading to bleaching, starvation, and eventually death.
In an effort to combat this phenomenon, the research team initiated a pilot project entitled "Assisted Evolution".
They have successfully developed a strain of microalgae, known as Cladocopium proliferum, to withstand high temperatures.
By exposing microalgae to elevated temperatures over a decade, the researchers enhanced their heat tolerance.
Through laboratory experiments, the team recently introduced these "refractory" microalgae into chemically bleached adult coral fragments.
Surprisingly, microalgae not only maintained coexistence with corals, but also facilitated faster recovery from bleaching while enhancing the corals ’ heat tolerance.
Remarkably, this positive effect has been observed in adult corals, not just in larvae and juveniles, suggesting that it could be applied more widely.
While the immediate effects of this breakthrough are promising, researchers warn that it is not an independent solution.
Dr. Wing Yan Chan emphasizes the long-term stability and potential benefits of symbiosis between thermogenic microalgae and corals.
However, Professor Madeleine Van Oben emphasizes that without strong action on climate change, these efforts will not be enough to save coral reefs.
However, the discovery of "heat-resistant" microalgae paves the way for innovative techniques for coral restoration.
This research can be replicated globally by leveraging local microalgal cultures, providing a beacon of hope for coral reef conservation.
While time is critical, with the frequency and intensity of marine heatwaves expected to increase, supporting coral reefs is vital to the preservation of marine ecosystems, industries and cultural heritage.
Questions and Answers
1.
What is microalgae?
Microalgae are microscopic organisms that photosynthesize, similar to plants.
They are found in various aquatic environments and play a crucial role in marine ecosystems.
2.
What is coral bleaching?
Coral bleaching occurs when corals expel the colored algae that live symbiotically within them, causing them to turn white or pale.
This expulsion usually occurs when corals are exposed to stressful environmental conditions, such as high water temperatures.
3.
How does climate change affect coral reefs?
Climate change, especially rising ocean temperatures, poses a major threat to coral reefs.
High water temperatures can trigger mass bleaching processes, disrupting the microsymbiotic relationship between corals and microalgae.
In addition, climate change is leading to ocean acidification, further undermining the public health and resilience of coral reefs.
