Fifty-year-old fisherman Salem Haidar sits idle on the beach of the coastal city of Al-Khums, looking at the state of the sea after witnessing fellow fishermen using explosive fingers to catch fish, placing in front of him fishing nets that had been torn apart by explosives for weeks and not a single fish was caught.
Libya ’ s coastline stretches 1,770 kilometers along the Mediterranean Sea, containing several coastal cities and towns including Al Khoms, Misrata, Sirte and Benghazi.
Today, Libya ’ s waters are facing increasing danger, with rich seas impoverished by over-fishing, especially by illegal means.
Salem learned to fish from his father and spent more than half his life living from the bounties of the city sea.
“Those were times when the sea water was pure, untainted, and its fish were plentiful enough to feed everyone, ” he says, recalling those days.
Fishing with dynamite threatens Libyan coasts
“A decade ago, the harvest was enough to sustain us, but in recent years, it has fallen dramatically because of the overfishing that happens every season.
Today we find huge numbers of fish floating dormant above sea level. ”
Overfishing operations were widespread among fishermen because of the lack of effective control over the violators, whom Salem described as “weak souls ” saying:“ Previously, there were laws and strict control imposed on us to the extent that we were obliged to use a certain type of nets and a certain amount of fish we catch each season to avoid a shortage of fish and maintain them, contrary to what is happening today. ”
All these factors combine today to be a burden for the fishermen who grew up on the banks of the sea and knew no profession other than fishing, and their eyes look miserable and prolong the sight of the water polluted by the saboteurs.
Fisherman Salah al-Taeb, 48, says that dynamite fishing has spread so widely among fishermen in the area that those close to it may think that an artillery war is going on at sea.
In an attempt to hide the sound of explosions, the perpetrators throw explosives at the moment the planes cross over them, and the sound gets lost with the roar so that the security authorities do not detect them.
The penitent fisherman is one of those who were greatly affected by the dynamite catch, until he saw the same death years ago when he was fishing at sea.
On that day, fishermen threw a package of dynamite near him, and he lost consciousness, and he stayed in the hospital for three months, where fishermen threw the fingers of dynamite where he was submerged after they thought the movement and the air bubbles rising that indicated the presence of a crop of fish.
Bombing is also a dangerous practice for the owners, as a fisherman was killed or lost a limb as a result of dynamite detonation.
Safety of Fishermen
The marine environment is threatened by incalculable dangers.
Its fish and plant resources are depleted day by day as a result of overfishing, especially by illegal methods, some of which amount to a felony.
Despite the efforts of the fishermen ’ s union to report to the competent security services the presence of fishermen using explosives in fishing operations, it seems that these fishermen evade sanctions on a continuous basis, which negatively affects attempts to reduce this phenomenon.
Fish Market in Tripoli
Khalil al-Shibel, a member of the Fishermen ’ s Syndicate, is deeply concerned about the devastating effects of dynamite fishing on the seafloor, especially in areas extending from the coast of the oil crescent to the coastal city of Khums.
He points out that these areas have seen significant damage to their natural habitat, which has lasted for millions of years.
In particular, he points to the loss of sponges, which play an important role in cleaning seawater, and the loss of large areas covered with seaweed.
Dynamite kills all fish species, large and small, indiscriminately.
The cub reveals that the detonation is sometimes carried out at distances of up to 100 or 150 meters, where the fish lay eggs, and the seeds and small and large fish die.
What is even more regrettable is that fishermen only get about 10 percent of the dead fish, most of which sink to the bottom and float very little, and they come in the morning to collect and sell it to citizens without talking about the serious health risks of consuming fish caught with explosives.
The cub says, "Thanks to dynamite, there are no more fish in our sea.
Most species have disappeared, for decades we have been seeing species that we no longer see today.
Libya ’ s fishing law, which has been in place since the 1960s, needs to be updated to ensure sanctions are effective and deter violators.
This modernization comes as a result of the proliferation of weapons and the presence of vehicles, including desert four-wheel drive vehicles, that enable fishermen to reach distant and vast areas of the natural wealth that exists in particular.
The law on land and sea fishing in force in Libya since 1989 on the regulation of the exploitation of marine wealth stipulates that "the use of explosive substances for fishing in marine waters by means of explosives, toxic substances, drugs or substances harmful to public health or by any other means harmful to marine organisms without discrimination is strictly prohibited.
Because this law is no longer compatible with the requirements of the times and the current reality.
Environmental expert Ibrahim al-Rubaie proposed a law to protect the marine environment, as it is no longer a violation, but is considered a criminal offense.
Al-Rubaie says that most countries, especially the countries of the Mediterranean basin, have enacted modern laws that punish these crimes, and some have even doubled the punishment, such as in Egypt, Greece and Jordan, while in Libya it still does not exceed the penalty of a misdemeanor.
Fish shows are varied in the capital Tripoli
The environmental expert pointed out that since the beginning of last summer, Libya has lost thousands of tons of fisheries, and in addition to environmental damage, the fishing with explosives kills and injures dozens annually, but the authorities do not provide any statistics on this matter.
He adds that there is a sharp decline in the number of fish, especially species such as parrotfish, rabbit fish and eels, which are important fish for the ecosystem.
Even fish that are supposed to be abundant, such as mullet and sardines, have become rare.
This case points to a critical threat to these species, many of which are on the brink of extinction.
In an interview with DW from the capital Tripoli, he adds that there are many threats looming for the marine environment, which are not only fishing with explosives, but also solid waste that affects a large part of marine life, as well as sewage that is pumped directly into the sea in the Libyan capital Tripoli until the beaches are no longer suitable for swimming.
Environmental impacts and marine resources at risk
One of the most prominent effects of explosives on marine plants is that TNT galatina explosions raise water pressure, resulting in a sudden increase in water temperature, and this interaction between water nitrate and phosphate forms a toxic substance.
The damage extends to the killing of many non-fish organisms, significantly affecting the marine ecosystem.
These effects continue to cause the fracturing of benthic rocks and the uprooting and destruction of marine plants.
DW could not obtain further clarification from the Ministry of Marine Resources in the Interim National Unity Government, as officials declined to comment on the matter.
Fish Market in Tripoli, Libya
Some seven years ago, religious institutions issued a fatwa prohibiting the use of explosives in fishing at sea because of the harm it causes to the environment and human beings.
However, that opinion seems to have had little effect.
The deteriorating situation and abuses on Libyan shores are unlikely to change any time soon.
This is due to the ongoing conflicts and wars that have plagued Libyan territory for years, which have distracted the authorities from focusing on what is going on at sea, and until the situation changes, the “gelatinization ” will continue to crush marine life, unchecked.

Sudaya Releases Report on Generative Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models
A series of forums were held in the universities of the Kingdom to enhance the knowledge of professors and students
The Saudi Commission for Data and Artificial Intelligence (SADaya) has issued a report on generative artificial intelligence and large language models in a step aimed at raising the level of awareness of these technologies, as part of its interest in enhancing community awareness of data and artificial intelligence technologies as the national reference in the Kingdom of organization, development and business.
SADaya has launched a series of generative artificial intelligence (AI) forums at universities in the Kingdom in order to enhance the knowledge of the field of AI among university professors and students.
The developments of generative artificial intelligence technologies have become the most intense in the world as one of the transformations of the 21st century in the fields of advanced technologies that penetrated its uses in various fields, including (the field of education), in which these technologies contributed to the improvement of teaching and learning methods through more advanced technical tools that emerged from the generative artificial intelligence and adopted its method the world 's finest universities amid the assurances of many specialists that these tools The importance of human thinking will not be negated by employing its use as only an advanced robotic assistant to the human mind.
Experts define generative artificial intelligence as a type of artificial intelligence technology that aims to generate new content, whether in the form of text, images, videos or otherwise. Unlike traditional artificial intelligence, generative intelligence is characterized by the ability to generate diverse and unlimited results with training data, and opens the door to unprecedented possibilities in several areas such as machine translation, text and image production. The machine can generate unique and creative content without any imitation or reproduction.
Generative AI is likely to make educational institutions around the world redraw their learning objectives and assessment methods to align them with AI capabilities and their focus on critical thinking, analysis and information auditing skills is a high priority in the educational process. These technologies provide innovative solutions to enhance the learning experience by finding harmony between the pillars of the educational process triangle (student, teacher and educational management). Its function in various use cases according to the educational context and work to regulate its use according to specific guidelines.
Many education experts in the world expected to adopt the use of AI as a key element in the systems of educational institutions, so some educational institutions in higher and public education began to formulate policies for the use of AI in education, where a recent UNESCO study of more than 450 schools and universities in the world showed that less than 10% of this sample have established policies or official guidelines on the use of AI applications.
When using these technologies, the principles of ethics of artificial intelligence, approved by the countries of the world in a document issued by UNESCO in 2020, should be taken into account with the growing demand for generative artificial intelligence technologies, but controls have been established that emphasize the importance of: respect for the dignity of all individuals and take into account their privacy, support justice, equality of opportunity and inclusiveness with the prevention of abuse Using these techniques in a way that may harm the student, teacher and educational administration or negatively affect the educational process.
Stanford University has launched a website that includes the university ’ s policies and guidelines on the impact of AI tools on the principle of academic integrity and provides clear guidance to both professors and students on how to use these tools responsibly and ethically in the academic environment. These principles focus on encouraging the conscious use of AI in line with maintaining academic integrity in the educational process. Similar experiences in general education have been applied in Japan, Australia and New Zealand.
Generative AI relies on advanced technologies such as Deep Neural Networks and Large Language Models that allow you to learn complex patterns from huge data collected from books, websites and social networking sites. Although these technologies are not new, recent developments in the design of generative AI models, computing infrastructure and the ability to collect large amounts of training data have increased the capabilities of AI. He has made tremendous progress in recent years.
On the other hand, education experts stressed the importance of the human mind in the educational process, considering that AGI is just a digital assistant for students who are diligent in their studies by shortening time, simplifying scientific concepts and translation, evaluating academic progress and identifying areas that need more focus, and opening new horizons for the development of teaching and supporting the teacher in various tasks such as: increasing student participation or customizing learning to facilitate the selection of appropriate techniques for each educational use.
Educational departments can take advantage of AI to improve institutional performance, raise the quality of academic results, and automate some administrative tasks to save time and effort. Educational departments also play a key role in setting policies and controls that regulate the optimal and ethical handling of AI tools.
Generative AI has many uses in education, including but not limited to: producing rich and diverse content through multi-species data, including: text (summarizing and answering questions), images (generating image from text, image processing and image resolution enhancement), videos (generating video from text or image and video optimization), and speech (generating speech from text, speech recognition, and speech modification). Concerns include: the inaccuracy of some information, the presence of biases in models, the possibility of infringement of intellectual property rights, as well as the weakness of arithmetic and logic compared to the capabilities of the human mind.
In order to obtain the required results from the tools of generative artificial intelligence, the user must learn the engineering prompt, which is the process of drafting the instructions and questions provided for the tools of generative artificial intelligence to obtain the best desired results. Choosing the right words and determining the correct context for the task. Learning the methods of order engineering is very important as it is formulated accurately and clearly helps the tools of artificial intelligence generative to understand the requirement better and by generation. - High quality.
Throughout history, artificial intelligence in education has passed through four stages, the first stage between 1960 and 1974, in which language processing programs such as ELIZA and SCHOLAR appeared, and the second stage between 1975 and 1990, in which the foundations of intelligent education systems were developed.
The third stage was between the years 1990 - 2010, in which the Internet appeared, which had a role in the spread of e-learning and distance learning using artificial intelligence techniques, and in the fourth stage, which began in 2010 and still so far, appeared in the development of chatbots and machine learning techniques and deep learning.
Many AI experts warn of the potential risks if the application and regulation of generative artificial intelligence in education is delayed scientifically and with applicable regulatory legislation, most notably: increasing the digital divide between developed and developing countries, as developed countries will be able to benefit from this technology to improve the quality of their education while developing countries remain in the region. In addition to this delay, educational institutions lose the competitive advantage in education at the global level, which affects the quality of education and the ability of students to meet the requirements of the future labor market.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, welcomed the participants in the International Conference on Women in Islam Status and Empowerment, which is now being held in Jeddah. India Leads Change in Collaboration with Africa
(MENAFN- Al-Borsa News) Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has raised his country ’ s flag in Africa recently, seeking to strengthen trade and investment relations with the continent ’ s countries.
Modi began his speech at the G20 summit in New Delhi last September, announcing that the African Union would become a permanent member of the group, which would strengthen the voice of the global South.
The move followed a decision by India and the four other current BRICS members the month before the summit to admit Egypt and Ethiopia, along with four other countries, into their ranks.
These examples illustrate how India is playing an increasingly active role in international diplomacy on behalf of Africa and the Global South.
At the same time, New Delhi ’ s growing trade and investment ties with Africa illustrate how channelling funds towards the global South can not only reap financial benefits, but also drive real systemic change in environmental, governance and social issues.
Trade relations between India and Africa go back centuries, when Indian traders traveled to the eastern coast of the continent in search of precious metals and gems.
These days, India is a key driver behind the growing global recognition of Africa ’ s strategic importance.
Modi, in particular, is using the platform offered by his position to promote a better understanding of the investment opportunities Africa offers to foreign investors.
Africa has a large working-age population, a growing middle class, and a wealth of raw materials including gold, diamonds, petroleum and minerals.
As the race to secure minerals for a green energy transition gains momentum, Africa ’ s strategic importance to the global economy is rapidly being redefined, with increasing initiatives coming from the United States, Europe and China, as well as India.
For its part, India is exporting food, beverages, petroleum products, medicines, machinery and vehicles to Africa.
In fact, India has become the largest supplier of passenger cars to South Africa, with automakers in South Korea and Japan assembling vehicles in India for export afterwards.
This model is likely to be scaled up to other African countries where the middle classes seek affordable transportation for their families.
India has also become one of Africa ’ s top five investors over the past decade, with about $74 billion flowing into the continent, attracted by rich supplies of crude oil, grains and nuts.
There are still many potential areas for further collaboration and innovation in Africa and India, especially in agriculture, where a major transformation is taking place.
Agriculture accounts for about 57% of Africa ’ s jobs, and new start-ups and established companies alike are radically changing the market by offering innovative solutions that address challenges across the agricultural value chain, from creating dashboards to connecting farmers in need to financing with potential investors to digitizing trade documents to reduce the burden of paperwork on farmers.
There is ample scope for India to contribute to modernizing Africa ’ s agricultural infrastructure, increasing the efficiency of the agricultural supply chain and improving productivity.
India and Africa can work together to strengthen their agribusiness ties by channelling money into agricultural technology, which will enhance global food security, and India can have the opportunity to drive sustainable agricultural practices in Africa through its investments.
The shift to clean energy in Africa is now the focus of attention, with renewable energy becoming an emerging hub for trade between India and Africa.
India is already investing heavily in renewables and is the world ’ s third largest producer of renewable energy.
At the same time, Indian investors can support the transition towards renewable energy in Africa by financing solar, wind and hydropower projects across the continent.
By leveraging its long-standing trade relationships, India can help drive real systemic change and contribute to the achievement of global net zero emissions targets.
India and other Asian countries have already shown interest in using their technologies, skills and capabilities to actively participate in Africa ’ s green energy transition by bidding for engineering, construction and management contracts for renewable energy projects.
As the global order continues to shift, investors and businesses must head to the global South if they want to stay ahead of the curve and support international growth.
India and Africa have built the foundation for a strong and long-term business relationship, and it is time to channel investments in a strategic way to foster collaboration, innovation and shared growth between India and Africa.

Exploring the Future of Global Assistive Robotics (2023-2028): Mobility, Applications and Type Shifts
The field of assistive robotics has seen remarkable developments in recent years, revolutionizing the lives of individuals with disabilities and the elderly.
These robots are designed to provide assistance and support in various tasks, from mobility assistance to housework.
As we look to the future, the potential for further transformation and innovation in this area is enormous.
Mobility Shifts:
Mobility is one of the key areas where assistive robots are expected to undergo major transformations.
Traditional mobility aids such as wheelchairs and walkers are enhanced by the use of robotic technologies, allowing greater autonomy and freedom of movement.
For example, robotic exoskeletons can provide individuals with disabilities in the lower extremities the ability to walk again.
In addition, self-driving motorized wheelchairs are being developed to navigate complex environments and provide a smoother mobility experience.
Application Shifts:
Assisted robots are also expanding their applications beyond the healthcare sector.
These robots are increasingly being used in industries such as manufacturing, logistics and even entertainment.
In manufacturing, cooperative robots, or collaborative robots, work alongside human workers to perform repetitive tasks, reducing physical stress and increasing productivity.
In logistics, robots are used to help meet orders and manage warehouses.
Furthermore, assistive robots are being developed for entertainment purposes, providing companionship and emotional support to individuals.
Type Transfers:
The types of assistive robots themselves are also evolving.
While humanoid robots have been the focus of much attention, there is a growing trend towards more specialized robots designed for specific tasks.
For example, robotic prostheses are becoming more advanced, mimicking natural limb movements and providing a greater range of motion.
In addition, robotic escorts are being developed to provide social interaction and emotional support to individuals who may feel isolated or alone.
Questions and Answers:
Q: What are assistive robots?
A: Assisted robotics refers to the use of robotic technologies to provide assistance and support to individuals with disabilities or the elderly.
Q: How do assistive robots transform mobility?
A: Assisted robots improve mobility aids such as wheelchairs and walkers using robotic technologies.
They also develop robotic exoskeletons and autonomous wheelchairs to provide greater autonomy and freedom of movement.
Q: What are the new applications for robotics?
A: Assistive robots are expanding their applications beyond healthcare to include industries such as manufacturing, logistics and entertainment.
Robots are used in manufacturing to collaborate with human workers, in logistics to meet demands, and in entertainment to provide companionship.
Q: How are the types of assistive robots changing?
A: Although humanoid robots have been prominent, there is a shift towards specialized robots designed for specific tasks.
Robotic and companion prosthetics are becoming more advanced, providing natural limb movements and emotional support, respectively.
In conclusion, the future of global robotics holds enormous potential for transformation.
With advances in mobility, applications and types of robotics, individuals with disabilities and older adults can look forward to increased independence, improved quality of life and enhanced support in various aspects of their daily lives.

Many healthy habits can profoundly affect your overall health, from eating enough vegetables to getting enough and good sleep every day.
According to Eating Well, steps can be taken to keep the body at its best, including exercise and physical activity, provided you commit to doing it for at least 30 minutes a day.
Health Benefits of Exercising Regularly
Regular exercise is a powerful tool for maintaining a healthy lifestyle.
Incorporating active physical movement into everyday habits is an important way to maintain overall health, including:
1.
Reduce the risk of cognitive decline
One of the important benefits of regular exercise is its positive effect on cognitive performance.
According to a small 2021 study published in Alzheimer ’ s Disease, exercise — such as walking and cycling — can help reduce cognitive decline.
Some research has also shown that increased physical activity may help prevent about 3% of all dementia cases, according to a 2021 review in Nutrients.
2.
Reduce blood pressure
Regular exercise plays a pivotal role in maintaining heart health.
Increased heart rate promotes better blood circulation, which helps reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease.
It also helps keep blood pressure levels within the normal range, thus reducing pressure on the heart, according to a 2020 review in the American Heart Association.
According to a 2020 review published in the American journal Physiology-Heart and Circulatory Physiology, frequent physical activity can also help lower cholesterol levels while increasing HDL cholesterol.
3.
Supporting bone health
Exercise also helps maintain and improve bone health.
According to a 2022 review published in the journal Frontiers in Endocrinology, weight-bearing and resistance exercises, such as running, jumping or lifting weights, stimulate bone growth and strengthening.
They help increase bone density and reduce the risk of osteoporosis and fractures later in life.
Exercise improves balance and coordination, reducing the likelihood of falls that can lead to bone injuries, according to a 2021 article in the journal Medical Clinics of North America.
4.
Improving the quality of sleep
Regular exercise helps to improve sleep quality.
Physical activity can contribute to a more restful and calmer sleep by helping to fall asleep faster and deepening sleep.
According to a 2018 review in the journal Sleep Medicine Reviews, an increase in body temperature during exercise is thought to improve sleep quality by helping it fall during sleep.
A person can also feel more alert during the day.
5.
Increased energy levels
Regular exercise promotes natural and sustainable energy, as blood flow increases in the body, ensuring that important nutrients and oxygen reach cells efficiently.
This process helps convert nutrients into usable energy, boosting stamina and reducing feelings of fatigue, according to a 2021 analytical study published in the journal Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation.
Regular physical activity also helps improve metabolic function, leading to more consistent energy levels throughout the day.
6.
Boosting Mood
Scientific research has shown that exercise may help support mental health by improving mood.
According to a 2021 article in the journal Biomolecules, exercise triggers the release of endorphins, often referred to as the “happiness hormone, ” which can lead to feelings of happiness and euphoria.
Regular physical activity can relieve symptoms of depression and anxiety by promoting relaxation and enhancing the body ’ s ability to cope with stress.
Precautionary reserves and potential risks
Despite the many health benefits of regular exercise, there are potential risks one should be aware of – especially those who exercise recently or who have pre-existing medical conditions.
Potential risks
Injuries: High-impact exercises can lead to injuries such as sprains, strains, and fractures.
Over-training: Exercising without adequate rest can lead to over-training syndrome, which is characterized by decreased performance, increased resting heart rate and persistent muscle pain.
Heart problems: Although rare, intense exercise can sometimes lead to heart problems in individuals with undiagnosed heart disease.
Precautions
Medical clearance: Before starting an exercise program, individuals with chronic health conditions or those over the age of 45 must obtain a medical clearance that includes approval for specific exercise and a certain intensity.
Progressive progression: Start with low-intensity exercise and gradually increase the duration and intensity to reduce the risk of injury.
Warm-up and sedation: Warm-up and sedation procedures should be combined to prepare the body for exercise and help recover after exercise.
• Hydration and nutrition: Consuming enough fluids and nutrients is critical to conserving energy during exercise and promoting recovery afterwards.

8 Secrets That Make You Younger
Your biological age is an indicator of your health, and it is more accurate than your chronological age in determining how well your organs are and how strong your muscles and bones are, and it can be reduced by following certain tips, and this makes you younger regardless of your chronological age.
First, we need to understand the difference between the terms chronological age and biological age.
Chronological age is the period of time from the moment a person is born.
In contrast, biological age is the amount of aging of the body ’ s cells.
The biological age and chronological age are usually the same, but in different cases, for example, the chronological age of a person may be 30 years, but he is a smoker and his lung suffers from damage as a result of tobacco and then his biological age is 50.
In contrast, a chronological person may be 60 years old, but they take care of their health and strong muscles and bones, making their biological age 40.
The chronological age cannot be changed, but the biological age can be changed so that we become younger by following healthy habits.
Scientists at Sweden ’ s Karolinska Institute have found that people with a biological age five years higher than their chronological age have a 40 percent higher risk of dementia or stroke, according to a report in The Independent.
Sarah Haag, associate professor of molecular epidemiology at the Karolinska Institute and co-author of the study, said: “If you compare your body ’ s current performance with people your age, does it work better or worse?
“If it ’ s worse, your biological age will be less than your chronological age, and vice versa, and any reduction in your biological age is good for your long-term health. ”
How can biological age be known?
Dr Richard Seo, director of gerontology research at King ’ s College London, says that at the moment only truly accurate reading is available in research studies.
One way in which biological age can be measured is by using blood biomarkers, molecules that indicate normal or abnormal processes occurring in the body, and these include blood lipids, sugar, pressure, lung function, and body mass index.
If you have measurements of height, weight, cholesterol, and blood pressure, they help you estimate your biological age. The more you weigh, the higher your pressure, and your cholesterol, the more your biological age is, and your body ages faster.
Noor Markarem, an assistant professor of epidemiology at Columbia University ’ s Melman School of Public Health, says the strongest indicator of biological aging ever is a higher body mass index (BMI).
She co-authored a new paper presented at the Scientific Sessions of the American Heart Association 2023, which identified eight key lifestyle habits that, if adhered to over time, could reduce a person ’ s biological age by up to six years.
Here are some tips to reduce your biological age:
1) Less by a quarter
Earlier this year, a first-of-its-kind study was published in the Lancet Medical Journal, which looked at the effects of eating less on biological age.
The two-year study, which involved 200 people aged 21 to 50, found that those who ate about 25 percent less than they normally ate reduced their biological age and improved their cardiovascular status.
If you are reducing your calories, choose foods that are rich in nutrients and low in calories.
Here, a healthy diet rich in fruits and vegetables, lean proteins, unrefined starchy carbohydrates, low sugar, red meat and processed foods is recommended.
Stop eating after 8 p.m.
“If I could give any advice to reduce your biological age, time-restricted nutrition (intermittent fasting) would be when you reduce the number of hours you eat each day, ” says Sarah Haag.
“It ’ s a way to reduce the time it takes your body to metabolize and digest, ” says Sarah,“ and this keeps your blood sugar stable, and healthy blood sugar is a sign of biological aging.
There are many different ways of time-restricted feeding, such as stopping eating at 8 p.m. and starting again at 8 a.m. (Form 12: 12), stopping at 7 p.m. and starting again at 9 a.m. (14: 10) or fasting for 16 hours.
Use of dental floss at night
Inflammation is one of the pathways that leads to accelerated biological aging, especially in the mouth.
Inflammation is the immune system ’ s way of removing harmful substances, and when immune cells become overactive more damage occurs, says Siu, “The bacteria in the mouth known as the oral microbiome affect biological aging. ”
"If your gums are bleeding, bacteria can pass through the blood vessels in your mouth, increase inflammation in the brain and lead to accelerated brain aging."
One of the main signs of gum disease is bleeding gums, and several studies have linked gum disease to increased biological aging.
“If you keep your mouth clean and flossing twice a day it could positively affect your biological age, ” he says, and if that ’ s difficult, try flossing only at night.
A study published in the Journal of Aging Research found that three oral habits were associated with increased longevity: brushing at night, flossing at night, and regular visits to the dentist (2-3 times a year).
Walk faster for 10 minutes a day
Walking faster in everyday life at speeds (more than 3-4 miles per hour) leads to a lower biological lifespan.
But don ’ t worry if you can ’ t walk fast all the time, brisk walking for 10 minutes a day is associated with longer life expectancy.
5. Eat the Mediterranean diet
A study by the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health published in September this year found that adults who followed a polyphenol-rich diet for 18 months received a nine-month reduction in their biological age.
Polyphenols are nutrients found in plant foods, such as vegetables, berries, dark chocolate, and green tea.
Here comes the Mediterranean diet at the forefront in terms of containing polyphenols, as studies link it to a lower risk of heart and circulatory disease and associated risk factors, such as type 2 diabetes, obesity, high blood pressure and high cholesterol.
6- Treatment of depression
“Depression actually accelerates biological aging, ” says Seo, and research conducted by King ’ s College London earlier this year found that people with depression, anxiety or bipolar disorder were biologically older than their chronological age.
Depression leads to changes in sleep patterns, exercise, what we eat, and levels of sun exposure, so recognize the early signs of depression and develop small lifestyle interventions to address them, such as reducing social media use or not using your phone late at night, as this reduces the quality of your sleep, which can expose you to depression.
7. Reduce sitting
Research found that those who engaged in 150 minutes of moderate physical activity or 75 minutes of vigorous physical activity per week had lower biological age.
However, any physical activity is beneficial, meaning that a little exercise is better than no exercise.
If you can ’ t go to the gym but walk around, cycle or walk more, it will reduce your biological age over time.
8- Commit to bedtime
Who doesn't like to lie down on weekends?
The bad news is that if your sleep and wake times on vacation differ from your weekday sleep and wake times by more than 30 minutes, you are likely inadvertently increasing your biological age.
“Differences between week and weekend in sleep timing and duration have been linked to an increased risk of various diseases. ”
Going to sleep and waking up at the same time or within a 30-minute range can reduce the risk of many chronic diseases and reduce biological age.
"The recommendation is to sleep at least 7 hours, but not more than 9 hours because that can affect the risk of disease," she says.

DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (CNN) -- It was no easy task to see the small Elektra Trainer from a distance.
Despite its bright orange hull, the small two-seater plane was like a small dark spot in cloudy skies that grew darker over time.
The electric plane's engines ensured near-silent approach and provided no clues as to its location.
Suddenly, the E-Flight Challenge team queued up to watch the battery-powered plane land gracefully on the island of Norderney, off the northwest coast of Germany.
The landing was a few minutes before sunset on August 29, marking the end of the E-Flight Challenge 2023, which pitted the battery-powered Elektra Trainer against a sports car from Lucid Motors Air, which is also electric.
The plane and car had left earlier that day from Gellenhausen, a grass airport about 300 kilometres (186 miles) south of Frankfurt-M-Main, in a race to first reach the island.
The purpose of this adventure, created by a group of electric mobility enthusiasts, was to showcase the growing capabilities of this promising and rapidly evolving technology.
It's a long way from electric flight.
The E-Flight Challenge was inspired by the early days of flying.
From Louis Blerio ’ s jump across the English Channel in 1909, to Charles Lindbergh ’ s famous solo crossing across the Atlantic in 1927.
The history of aviation is mostly made against the backdrop of competitive challenges accomplished by brave pioneers.
A century later, this spirit of discovery has reached the field of electric aviation, which is still a small sector of the industry seeking to expand its capabilities.
As electric cars become prevalent across the planet, making up the largest segment of car sales in countries such as Norway, it ’ s the opposite of electric aviation.
Power requirements are quite different even for the smallest aircraft compared to cars.
Current battery technology has not yet reached the energy density levels required to power larger aircraft of smaller classes on a short flight.
The Elektra Trainer used by the E-Flight Challenge can carry no more than two people.
Batteries currently available in the market are not enough in terms of energy.
The addition of larger battery packs does not pull on the aircraft, as this increases the weight significantly, leading to a serious weakening of performance.
Even Swedish startup Heart Aerospace, one of the most ambitious electric jet developers, which has received orders and investments from United Airlines and other prominent industry players, announced in 2022 that it will abandon pure electric propulsion for the aircraft it is developing.
This was in order to adopt a hybrid electric approach that would allow it to develop an aircraft with a capacity of up to 30 seats, which is still small compared to industry standards.
Technology hasn ’ t reached that level yet.
Italian aircraft manufacturer Tecnam, which partnered with Rolls-Royce and Norwegian regional airline Widerøe as part of an electric aircraft project in 2021, announced the suspension of its electric aircraft project this summer, after three years of research, arguing that battery technology is not mature enough.
But a slew of recent announcements, this time from battery developers, provide strong reasons for hope.
China ’ s CATL, the world ’ s leading battery technology company, announced in April 2023 that it had developed a battery with a capacity of 500 Wh per kilogram, marking a significant step forward. This capacity is almost double what is currently available on the market, at around 270 Wh per kilogram.
A few days later, another announcement was made by Cuberg, a subsidiary of Swedish battery giant Northvolt, about advancing the development of a new generation of lithium-metal batteries that were shown in the test to deliver 380 Wh / kg, an increase of 40%.
But switching larger aircraft to electricity, such as the Airbus A320 and Boeing 737 that make most of today ’ s flights, remains a distant prospect.
Looking to the future
One company that is eagerly awaiting the arrival of electric jets, is Berlin-based private airline Air2E, which has supported E-Flight Challange.
Its founder and CEO, Norbert Wierle, likes to make a comparison to the early years of electric cars.
“Before Tesla became a household name as it is now, I launched a roadster that wasn ’ t quite as successful, but that paved the way and showed that great electric cars can be made, ” he said.
Whirl hopes that if electric jets achieve cost reductions, they will also be able to absorb some of the net of road traffic.
This is the assumption that some entrepreneurs are building on the business cases of new regional air carriers powered by electric power.
The day before the flying car.
In this context, the E-Flight Challenge was an illustration of the challenges of electric flight, but of what might be promising in the future as well.
While the aircraft would be able to continue on a relatively straight path across land and sea to Norderney, the land team relied on Lucid Air ’ s declared range of 500 miles, and the absence of speed limits on long stretches of the German motorway.
The range was to be, quite unexpectedly, the Achilles heel of the aircraft team.
But the Elektra Trainer had to stop almost halfway, spending two and a half hours on the ground to recharge its batteries at Orlinghausen Airport.
In the end, I lost the race.
Once the car reached the ferry terminal on the northern coast of Germany and was ready to sail to the island, the game was over.
The Lucid Motors team flew to Norderney Airport at 6.13pm.
Local time, seven hours after departure, the plane arrived about an hour later.

One of the first commentators on the news of Millie ’ s election was Donald Trump, who wrote on his social media platform, Truth Social: “I ’ m proud of you.
It will change your country and make Argentina great again. ”
U.S. Secretary of State Anthony Blinken issued a statement on Monday saying the election was “a testament to Argentina ’ s electoral and democratic institutions, ” noting that Washington“ looks forward to working with President-elect Milley and his government on shared priorities. ”
Man of Economics and Music
Milley, 53, describes himself as a “chaotic capitalist, ” and the economist only entered politics two years ago.
His victory comes at a time when Argentina is trying to solve the problem of inflation, which has reached 143 percent, one of the highest in the world, poverty afflicting about 40 percent of the population, as well as the debt crisis and the devaluation of the local currency.
Videos of Milly went viral after he was sure to win the election in a state of great joy.
According to the Guardian, Millie “suffered as a child due to the mistreatment of his parents, as well as bullying at school during the 1980s. ”
Argentina ’ s president-elect loves music, has previously been a lead singer for a band and has always loved Bob Marley and Verdi.
Milley gained fame during his television appearance as an economic analyst, where he often talked about suffering due to inflation, as well as talking live about sexual topics.
The Guardian report noted that Millie ’ s character “was always meant to attract attention, which helped him enter the world of politics. ”
His friends and foes alike likened him to Trump and also to Brazil ’ s former and right-wing president, Jair Bolsonaro, whom he called “Trump Argentina. ”
"The lesser of two evils."
Mili was elected to Argentina ’ s parliament in 2021 for La Libertad Avanza, before taking office amid voter anger over corruption and mismanagement following the country ’ s worst economic crisis in two decades.
According to AFP, some Argentines described the vote as the choice of "the lesser of two evils", between fear of the painful economic solutions proposed by Mili and anger at the economic crisis.
Milley pledged to find a solution to the economic crisis in the country, beginning with the closure of the central bank and the disposal of the local currency (peso) and dollarization of the economy and reduce spending and get rid of the "parasitic class", which met with the approval of voters despite the difficulty of these measures.
But some experts believe that Milley "will retreat from his hard-line policies and will be forced to moderate as he takes the reins next month, because of the difficulty he may face in implementing his plans, with his party holding 38 seats in the upper legislative chamber of the country, out of 257 seats, while in the Senate it has 8 seats out of 72."
During his campaign, he made promises similar to what Trump has long talked about for America, and said he would “make Argentina great again, ” the slogan for Trump ’ s campaign,“ Make America great again. ”
“Today the end of decadence begins, and the reconstruction of Argentina begins, ” Argentina ’ s president-elect said on Sunday, warning that there would be“ no half-solutions. ”
Addressing thousands of supporters at his campaign headquarters in Buenos Aires, Milley said: “The poor class model is over, and today we are adopting the model of freedom to once again become a world power.
Today the way politics were practiced ends, and another way begins. ”
Milley will assume the presidency on December 10, succeeding President Alberto Fernandez.

ICAO Conference kicks off in Dubai with government delegations from 90 countries
UAE looks to the future of aviation globally with low carbon fuel
T + T - normal size
Under the patronage of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, Dubai witnessed yesterday the launch of the third International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Conference on Aviation and Alternative Fuels, with a large international presence of more than 1,000 participants from around the world, including more than 40 ministers, government delegations from more than 90 countries, more than 30 relevant international and regional organizations. Aviation, fuel production companies and aircraft manufacturers.
Sessions
The conference will run from 20 to 24 November and will include a high-level ministerial session followed by several sessions of government delegations from ICAO member states, with representatives from airlines, fuel production companies and related organizations participating as observers, to discuss 5 key items over 17 sessions, focusing on clean energy production and policies to support the transition to low-carbon, sustainable fuels and other types of fuels. Clean fuels (such as hydrogen), as well as ways to support countries to build their capacity to produce clean energy for aviation, financing mechanisms, and a review of ICAO ’ s ambitious long-term goal of zero carbon emissions by 2050.
Climate Neutrality
The first edition of the conference was launched in 2009 in Brazil, followed by the second in Mexico in 2017, and the world is looking forward to the third special and sensitive edition, as it comes immediately after the ICAO General Assembly resolution 41 of 2022 on the goal of climate neutrality 2050, and aims to achieve an international consensus on the need to invest in the development and production of low-carbon alternative fuels for aircraft. Low carbon in the aviation sector.
A crucial role
His Excellency Suhail bin Mohammed Al Mazrouei, Minister of Energy and Infrastructure, said: “The aviation industry plays a crucial role in supporting international efforts to reduce carbon emissions, and the UAE is exerting intensive efforts to develop the national regulatory environment for the production of sustainable aviation fuel in line with our national ambitions to promote a clean energy transition and serve our efforts to achieve climate neutrality by 2050.
He added that the UAE is taking a balanced approach to exploring future opportunities for sustainable jet fuel and improving the carbon intensity of hydrocarbon-based jet fuel, which is one of the axes of the rapid energy transition towards clean energy.
The conference is an ideal platform to catalyse international efforts to shift towards clean energy in the aviation sector, serving the ambitious goal of achieving net zero carbon emissions in the aviation sector by 2050.
Challenges
His Excellency Abdullah bin Tawq Al Marri, Minister of Economy and Chairman of the General Authority of Civil Aviation, said that the unprecedented development challenges facing the world today as a result of the repercussions of climate change left us no other option to shift towards a low-carbon economic model, pointing out that in light of the international efforts to find a realistic approach to this transformation capable of keeping pace with development and economic needs. Pillars of inclusive and sustainable economic growth globally.
In his opening speech, he stressed that the issue of climate change is now on the list of priorities of the wise leadership in the UAE, and the country is making serious efforts to accelerate the transition towards a new low-carbon economic model, and the aviation sector is one of the most important axes of this model.
He explained that the UAE was one of the first countries to adopt sustainability and environmental impact in the aviation sector, and participated in all negotiations led by the International Civil Aviation Organization, and ratified all international resolutions that serve this direction, and was one of the first countries to announce its commitment in 2016 to implement the « Corsia » plan for carbon compensation in international air transport.
The UAE has also launched a national road map for sustainable aviation fuel, setting an ambitious target to achieve an annual production of 700 million litres of sustainable aviation fuel by 2030, which will reduce up to 4.8 million tonnes of CO2 emissions, and the industry has committed to reaching zero carbon emissions by 2050.
He added that the government commitment has been accompanied by parallel efforts by the private sector in the country, where our national companies invest heavily in research and development activities, strengthening infrastructure, and developing international partnerships to support sustainable fuel production and uses.
He pointed out that this large international gathering of senior officials and representatives of the global aviation community at the third ICAO Aviation and Alternative Fuels Conference will be a turning point in the future of the aviation and travel industry, and will take us to a new stage in the production of aviation fuel, more sustainable and low emissions, and contribute significantly to achieving climate neutrality and achieving our commitment in the General Assembly resolution 41 of 2022 to reach zero carbon emissions by 2050.
An opportunity.
Salvatore Shaketano, Chairman of the ICAO Council, said: “The conference represents a crucial opportunity for countries to show a strong and leading position in addressing international aviation emissions solutions, which is being held just days before the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP28), also here in the UAE.
Developing a strong and ambitious global framework will serve our joint efforts and commitment to decarbonize the sector.
Ambitious goal
In a recorded speech to the conference, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said: “Let me begin by saluting last year ’ s resolution of the ICAO General Assembly on adopting the ambitious global goal of zero carbon emissions by 2050. Achieving this ambitious goal will be a huge task for the aviation sector, which contributes 2% of total carbon emissions.
He added: “A zero-emission aviation sector requires a global shift towards clean energy, which requires new economic policies and laws that support this shift and are capable of creating economic opportunities and attracting investments, and we look forward to the global framework that will emerge from this conference to support the shift towards alternative fuels for aviation, which will be a decisive step towards a more prosperous and sustainable future for this vital sector. ”
Holding this conference just days before COP28 makes it the right time to turn this global ambition into realistic and actionable plans, find the path to zero carbon emissions by 2050 and build a better and more sustainable future for all of us.
Ban Ki-moon, former Secretary-General of the United Nations, also participated in the conference through a recorded speech in which he stressed that the civil aviation sector has made significant progress in the field of environmental protection, especially after the Paris climate agreement in 2015.
ICAO ’ s landmark decision in 2016 on Corsia, a plan to offset and reduce carbon emissions in the aviation sector, is the only global market-based action to reduce carbon emissions that has seen a broad international response.
In addition, the ICAO General Assembly ’ s decision last year to commit to the ambitious long-term global goal of zero carbon emissions in aviation by 2050 highlights the shared aspiration of ICAO member states to make real progress in this area and heralds the beginning of a new chapter in aviation sustainability.
The time had come to turn that ambition into reality.
“There is significant progress in developing solutions to produce low carbon and sustainable fuels, ” he said, calling for enhanced cooperation between governments, airlines, fuel companies, manufacturers and financing institutions to continue this progress towards ambitious targets.
Correct course.
In a keynote speech, Ambassador Majid Al Suwaidi, Director General and Special Representative of the UAE Presidency of COP28, stressed that the current indicators confirm that the world is not on track to achieve the climate goals of the Paris Agreement, but we still have time to change course, if we consider this challenge as a common opportunity for cooperation.
He explained that the presidency of COP28 has developed an action plan consisting of four main axes: accelerating the achievement of an orderly, just and responsible transition in the energy sector, developing climate finance mechanisms, focusing on the preservation of human beings and life and improving livelihoods, and supporting all these pillars of full inclusion.
He stressed that the transformation in energy has become a vital requirement for all sectors and economic industries, and the current transformation of the aviation sector towards low-carbon and sustainable fuels is a development necessity to support the objectives of climate action.
No country, company or individual can meet the challenge of this magnitude alone, and no one should be left behind.
He pointed out that coordination, cooperation and partnerships among countries is the basis, pointing to the existing partnership between the UAE and the United States to accelerate clean energy, which provides an example of the type of partnerships required, and transport is one of the main axes in this partnership.
The conference was attended by Saif Mohammed Al Suwaidi, Director General of the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA), Juan Carlos Salazar, Secretary General of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and a number of senior officials and important figures in the aviation, energy and investment sectors.

UAE aims to produce 700 million litres of sustainable aviation fuel per year
Part of the conference (Photo: Ashraf Al-Amra)
November 22, 2023 00: 47
Mustafa Abdul Azim (Dubai)
The UAE aims to produce 700 million liters of sustainable aviation fuel annually by 2030 as part of its national road map to reduce aviation carbon emissions, according to a working paper submitted by the UAE to the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) at its third Aviation and Alternative Fuels Conference.
The paper, a copy of which was obtained by Etihad, said that the UAE has intensified efforts to reduce carbon emissions through increased operational efficiency and the use of sustainable, low-carbon aviation fuel.
Saif Al Suwaidi, Director General of the General Authority of Civil Aviation, said on the sidelines of the second day of the third ICAO Aviation and Alternative Fuels Conference, hosted by the UAE, that the UAE will become one of the main centers in the world for the production of alternative fuels and low carbon as well as sustainable fuels, stressing that the UAE has many prominent investments in these fuels.
Al Suwaidi added that the UAE ’ s hosting of the ICAO Aviation and Alternative Fuel Conference, with the participation of more than 1,000 participants, 40 ministers and government delegations from more than 90 countries, more than 30 international and regional organizations, and heads of aviation and fuel companies around the world, reflects the confidence of the international aviation sector in the UAE and its potential to host exceptional events.
He stressed that the conference is a turning point in the course of international aviation activities and aviation fuel in particular, especially as it aims to reach an international consensus under the umbrella of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) on the mechanisms of transition towards a balanced system of aviation fuel production and the sustainability of the growth of the aviation sector, and come up with understandings a few days before the Conference of the Parties (COP28).
He stressed that the international aviation community is a reliable and responsible society and attaches the highest priority to environmental issues, pointing out that the main goal of the conference is to bring the concerned parties from all countries of the world to reach a unified position on the rationalization of the use of fossil fuels and put forward alternatives and solutions, including the expansion of the use of sustainable aviation fuel. alternative fuel.
The UAE was one of the first countries to adopt sustainability and environmental impact in the aviation sector, and participated in all negotiations led by the International Civil Aviation Organization, and ratified all international resolutions that serve this direction, and was one of the first countries to announce its commitment in 2016 to implement the Corsia plan for carbon offsetting in international air transport.
The UAE has also launched a national sustainable aviation fuel roadmap, setting an ambitious target to achieve an annual production of 700 million litres of sustainable aviation fuel by 2030, which will contribute to reducing up to 4.8 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions, and the industry has committed to reaching zero carbon emissions by 2050.
Positive indicators
The sessions of the second day of the Alternative Aviation Conference witnessed positive indications of the interest of the Member States of the Organization to reach a strong, ambitious and comprehensive global framework that takes into account the interests of all and bridges the gaps, emphasizing equal opportunities for all and adopting socially and economically acceptable measures to develop and deploy the use of sustainable aviation fuel and alternative fuels.
According to the ICAO Secretariat Working Paper, national initiatives and action plans that enable countries to identify their activities to reduce CO2 emissions have increased significantly in the past period, with some 142 countries submitting their plans to ICAO, which include the definition of a cleaner energy and fuel sustainability guidelines document in a coherent manner.
Investments of the sector
The paper pointed to the need for the aviation sector to invest up to $3.2 trillion over the 30 years to 2050 to reach net zero emissions in the aviation sector, noting the great interest of the private sector and energy producers in this transition to cleaner energy, and their interest in developing policies governing sustainable aviation fuel so that confidence in this fuel can be built.
The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) said agreeing on a clear path to increase sustainable aviation fuel production would send a strong message about key opportunities for financing the energy transition in the sector.
The third ICAO Conference on Alternative Aviation Fuel (CAAF / 3), seeks to create a global framework for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), low carbon aviation fuel (LCAF) and other clean energy, which is critical for the aviation sector to reach its goal of net zero by 2050.
As ICAO member states deliberate this week to reach a consensus on a global mechanism to increase production of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), some developing countries have concerns about the economic impact of these initiatives and the technical know-how needed to implement them.
According to the International Air Transport Association (IATA), sustainable aviation fuels can reduce more than 60% of aviation emissions globally by 2050, while the rest can be addressed through improved efficiency through technology, processes and the use of hydrogen-powered aircraft, provided countries have effective support policies in place.

MOHAMMED - Abu Dhabi on Saturday 25 November 2023 02: 24 PM - With the ongoing environmental changes and transformations of the planet, the impact of climate change on the agriculture sector, which is the backbone of the stability of human life, is clearly visible.
This requires understanding the implications of the agricultural map and how nature ’ s shifting scales and weather fluctuations affect planting times and harvests.
Rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and natural disasters such as droughts and floods.
All of this poses challenges to the agricultural map, as rising temperatures can degrade soil quality, exacerbate desertification, and reduce the amount of arable land.
Similarly, poor rains, droughts, floods and violent storms significantly affect crops and agricultural resources by degrading agricultural productivity or destroying crops and contaminating the soil.
To overcome these challenges, the agricultural map needs to adapt to climate change, through actions to improve water resources management, develop modern irrigation techniques to deal with water shortages, and focus on agricultural research to develop drought-resistant and high-temperature crops that help adapt to climate change and achieve agricultural sustainability.
Specific effects
To understand the impact of climate change on the agricultural map, specialists reviewed some of the different aspects of agriculture that can have this impact, from planting dates to agricultural production levels, as follows:
Changes in planting times: Higher temperatures and changes in rainfall patterns can affect crop planting times.
The need to adapt planting dates to climate change may increase.
• Change in harvest seasons: Climate change can affect harvest dates and cause fluctuations in the quality and quantity of harvested crops.
Changes in rainfall distribution: Changes in rainfall distribution can affect soil quality and water availability, leading to a change in plant varieties that can be grown in different areas.
Increased extreme weather events: Increased weather extremes, such as floods or droughts, can lead to crop loss and deteriorating agricultural conditions.
Rising temperatures: Higher temperatures can lead to a change in agricultural genius and crop ripening times.
Impact on ecosystems: Climate change can affect the ecological balance in agricultural areas, affecting the availability of vital resources for farms.
• Change in the spread of diseases and pests: Climate change can increase the spread of certain diseases and pests that may affect crops.
Need for Adaptive Plant Varieties: Climate change may require the development and use of plant varieties that are adapted to changing growing conditions.
Impact on crop distribution: Climate change may lead to a change in crop distribution, with some areas becoming less suitable for some crops and others becoming more suitable.
• Pressures on water resources: Climate change may have impacts on the availability of water for irrigation, putting pressure on agriculture in areas that rely heavily on water.
• The need for sustainable agriculture: Climate change highlights the importance of improving sustainability in agriculture, including the use of water conservation techniques and the application of more sustainable agricultural practices.
Climate change and its new challenges require continued adaptation and innovation in the agriculture sector, including the use of new technologies, better scheduling, and improved agricultural sustainability to balance food production needs with environmental conservation.
Adaptation and mitigation
Professor of Environmental Studies, Dr. Abdul Masih Samaan, explains in private statements to Eqtisad Dot Al-Khaleej, the impact of climate change on the agricultural map, that it is divided into two parts:
1.
The first is related to rising temperatures, which have now reached an above-average increase of 1.4 ° C (according to the World Meteorological Organization), and this has repercussions on the agricultural crop, and the water that irrigates the crop, if water is reduced, this means that all crops will be reduced as a result of water scarcity.
In addition, if there are floods in some places, this also negatively affects the implants by wasting them.
2.
The second is that each crop has a certain temperature during its growth cycle, and as temperatures rise, this means that almost all agricultural crops will reduce their productivity by 5% to 30% such as maize, wheat and rice, except for the only crop that may survive this, cotton because it needs high temperatures, the rest of the crops will be affected by high temperatures.
Professor of Environmental Studies, refers to the efforts of adaptation and mitigation in the agricultural sector, and among the mechanisms of adaptation is the creation of a different agricultural cycle; the farmer naturally knows the seasons of cultivation of each crop, if there is a change in temperature in the time to be cultivated, he must think of a new agricultural cycle.
He stresses that research is now moving to identify and study patterns of agricultural cycle modification, with the search for varieties that tolerate high temperature and lack of water; for example, it is known that rice needs a lot of water and in light of the scarcity of water, genetic engineering research to search for alternative types that bear high heat with lack of water. The product is an existing trend, and may reach a lower cost with future development.
To overcome the lack of water, he shows that there are two solutions; the first is desalination of sea water, and the second is sewage treatment, pointing out that some developed countries have reached the purification of wastewater by 100%, where they extracted sterile water and ozone treatment and completely pure, but in the Arab world there is a reservation on the use of this water for drinking but can be used in the cultivation of wood trees forests to improve the climate.
Planting trees
He points out that with the increase of trees, the proportion of oxygen increases and the proportion of carbon dioxide, the main cause of the phenomenon of climate change, and therefore whenever we plant forests, this was very useful for the climate, especially since with the high temperatures now there are fires in forests such as Amazon, Australia and others; add to this the erosion of forests in Africa because of the injustice on trees to use their wood for agriculture or export for hard currency and so on.
According to the professor of environmental studies, solving the climate problem requires the concerted efforts of many, the first and most important of which is the expansion of new and renewable energies.
However, Samaan also warns that there are two triangles (economy, politics and environment), and these three sides of the equation; the improvement of the environment will of course affect politics and the economy, so what he called the "terrible equation" here is how to reconcile the three, by reconciling the policies of countries working on many strategic axes and forms and how to develop the economy at lower cost under the high cost of clean energy such as solar and green hydrogen. in order to preserve the environment.
Developing countries need to invest $1.7 trillion in renewable energy annually, according to the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD).
The United Nations has warned that there is little hope of achieving any climate targets by 2030 unless there is massive investment in clean energy in developing countries.
• International investment in renewable energy has almost tripled since the Paris climate agreement was concluded in 2015, but most of that increase has been in developed countries, according to UNCTAD.
Challenges and Solutions
Dr. Wafiq Naseer, a member of the Global Parliament for the Environment, explained in an exclusive statement to Eqtisad Dot Al-Khaleej that climate changes affect harvests and agriculture significantly, as high temperatures and lack of rainfall can reduce agricultural productivity and deteriorate crop quality.
In addition, climate change can cause the emergence of new pests and diseases that affect different crops.
He adds that climate change also affects the timing of crop planting, so higher temperatures can reduce the duration of crop growth and change planting dates.
Naseer states that the main challenges facing agriculture due to climate change are:
Lack of water: Lack of rain can lead to a lack of water available for irrigation, affecting crop growth and quality.
Increased temperatures: Increased temperatures can worsen crop quality and reduce agricultural productivity.
• The emergence of new pests and diseases: Climate change can lead to new pests and diseases affecting crops.
To overcome these challenges, Naseer points out that some actions can be taken such as:
• Agricultural sustainability strategies: Promote the use of sustainable agricultural practices that preserve biodiversity, improve soil quality and reduce the use of harmful chemicals.
• Smart irrigation: The use of smart irrigation technologies that improve water use efficiency and reduce waste.
• Agricultural diversity: Promoting agricultural diversity and growing crops adapted to climate change.
• Modern technologies: The use of modern technologies such as organic agriculture, precision agriculture and climate control to improve crop quality and increase agricultural productivity.
