Study: Brisk walking protects you from type 2 diabetes
Science and Health
Publish
5 minutes read
DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (CNN) -- The distance you walk and how fast you move reduces your risk of developing type 2 diabetes, a new study has found.
According to a study published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine on Tuesday, brisk walking is associated with a reduced risk of developing type 2 diabetes later in life, by about 40%.
Lead author of the study, Dr. Ahmad Jaidi, associate researcher in the social determinants of the Health Research Center at Semnan University of Medical Sciences in Iran, said: “Previous studies indicated that frequent walking was associated with a lower risk of type 2 diabetes in the general population, so that those who spent more time walking daily were less at risk. ”
However, the researchers noted that the previous findings did not provide much guidance on the ideal normal walking speed needed to reduce the risk of diabetes, and there were no comprehensive reviews of the evidence.
The authors reviewed 10 previous studies conducted between 1999 and 2022 that assessed the links between walking speed, measured by timed objective tests or self-reports from participants, and the development of type 2 diabetes among adults from the United States, the United Kingdom, and Japan.
After an average follow-up period of eight years, the researchers found that, compared to easy walking, those who walked at a moderate or normal pace had a 15 percent lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes.
Those who walked at a "fairly fast" pace had a 24% lower risk of developing the disease compared to those who walked easy.
Brisk walking scored the biggest benefit: a 39% reduction in the risk of type 2 diabetes.
Easy walking has been defined as an area of less than two miles (3.2 kilometers) per hour.
Walk at medium or normal speed at a distance of 2 to 3 miles (3.2 to 4.8 kilometers) per hour.
A "fairly fast" walk is 3 to 4 miles (4.8 to 6.4 kilometers) per hour.
A "brisk walk" travels a distance greater than 4 miles (6.4 kilometers) per hour.
Every extra kilometer of walking speed was associated with a 9% lower risk of developing the disease.
Dr. Robert Gabbay, chief scientific and medical officer at the American Diabetes Association, who was not involved in the study, told CNN, “The fact that brisk walking may be more beneficial is not surprising, but the researchers ’ ability to measure walking speed and incorporate that into their analysis is interesting. ”
Dr. Carmen Cuthbertson, an assistant professor of health education and promotion at the University of East Carolina who was not involved in the study, told CNN that the study also confirms the idea that speed is important for diabetes prevention.
"Doing any amount of physical activity may have health benefits, but to prevent diabetes it is important to do some high-intensity activities, such as brisk walking, to get the most benefit."
Understand the benefits of walking fast.
Gabbay noted that the study does not provide evidence of cause and effect, but "one can imagine that more vigorous exercise may lead to increased fitness, reduced body weight, and therefore insulin resistance, and reduced risk of diabetes."
Dr. Michio Shimabukuro, a professor and head of the Department of Diabetes, Endocrinology and Metabolism at the Fukushima Medical University School, who is not involved in the study, agrees, arguing that “increased exercise intensity due to high walking speeds may further stimulate physiological function and physical activity, and lead to better health. ”
For Dr. Borja del Pozo Cruz, a principal health researcher at the University of Cadiz, Spain, who was not involved in the research, the speed of walking may simply reflect the state of health, meaning that it is preferable for healthy people to walk faster.
Del Pozo Cruz said: “There is a high risk of an adverse causal relationship, as health deficits are likely to explain the observed results.
"We need randomized controlled trials to confirm the results."

Unleashing the Power of Quantum Computing: A Qualitative Shift in Technology
Introduction:
Quantum computing, a revolutionary field of study, has caused a stir in the scientific community and beyond.
Thanks to its ability to solve complex problems with unprecedented speed, quantum computing holds the key to opening new frontiers in different fields.
In this article, we will delve into the importance of quantum computing, explore its potential applications, and address some of the common questions surrounding this cutting-edge technology.
Understanding Quantum Computing:
Quantum computing harnesses the principles of quantum mechanics to process and process information.
Unlike classical bit-based computers (0 and 1), quantum computers use quantum bits or qubits, which can exist in multiple states at once.
This unique property, known as superposition, enables quantum computers to perform complex calculations significantly faster than classical computers.
Importance of quantum computing:
1.
Solving complex problems: Quantum computing has the potential to revolutionize industries such as drug discovery, performance improvement, cryptography, and materials science.
Its enormous computational power allows for the effective simulation of molecular interactions, the optimization of complex systems, and the development of secure cryptographic algorithms.
2.
The development of artificial intelligence: Quantum computing can significantly enhance machine learning algorithms by accelerating data processing and pattern recognition.
This can lead to breakthroughs in areas such as natural language processing, image recognition, and predictive analytics.
3.
Improving supply chains: Quantum computing can revolutionize supply chain management by improving logistics, reducing costs, and improving efficiency.
Its ability to handle vast amounts of data and solve complex optimization problems can streamline processes, reduce waste, and boost overall productivity.
4.
Climate modeling and simulation: Quantum computing can help model and simulate climate, enabling scientists to better understand and predict climate patterns.
This can contribute to the development of effective mitigation strategies.
5.
Secure communication: Quantum computing offers the possibility of creating unbreakable encryption algorithms, ensuring secure communication channels in an increasingly interconnected world.
Quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols leverage the principles of quantum mechanics to provide secure communication channels that are resistant to hacking attempts.
Frequently Asked Questions:
S1.
How is quantum computing different from classical computing?
A1.
Classical computing is based on bits, which can represent either 0 or 1.
On the other hand, quantum computing uses qubits, which can exist in multiple states at once, thanks to the principle of superposition.
S2.
Are quantum computers commercially available?
A2.
While quantum computers are still in their early stages of development, many companies and research institutions are actively working to build practical quantum computers.
However, widespread commercial availability has not yet been achieved.
Q3.
Will quantum computing replace classical computing?
A3.
Quantum computing is not expected to completely replace classical computing.
Instead, classical computing is expected to be complemented by solving specific problems that are currently intractable on classical computers.
Q4.
What are the challenges in quantum computing?
A4.
Quantum computing faces challenges such as maintaining the stability of qubits, reducing errors caused by decoding, and increasing the number of qubits.
Overcoming these challenges is critical to realizing the full potential of quantum computing.
Conclusion:
Quantum computing holds enormous promise for transforming different industries and tackling complex problems that are beyond the reach of classical computers.
As researchers continue to make progress in this area, we can expect quantum computing to reshape the technological landscape, open up new possibilities and revolutionize the way we approach computation and problem solving.
The adoption of quantum computing today is essential to prepare for the challenges and opportunities of tomorrow.

Important information related to the care of the elderly
(MENAFN- Alghad Newspaper)
The Family Health Institute (FHI), King Hussein Foundation (KHF), on Tuesday discussed healthy ways to care for the elderly, and how to take into account their physical, emotional and social needs, in addition to regular health assessments and check-ups when necessary.
Taking care of elderly parents at home is usually the first step in a long-term care plan for the elderly.
It is not only a way to save money but also contributes to better health outcomes.
Why is elderly care important?
Aging cannot be prevented, but we can learn how to cope with growing diseases for the sake of their health.
Memory problems, dementia and Alzheimer's disease are among the most common health problems in older adults.
Some older people do not need any kind of care as they get older as they can live comfortably and independently.
However, caring for the elderly is often a concern when an elderly person begins to face problems in activities of daily life.
Often, a family member is the first to notice that there is a need to care for an elderly person.
On the other hand, the type of adult care that is appropriate for our loved one is largely determined by the type of health problems they have and the complications they have.
Elderly care is important because as older people get older, they can ’ t take care of themselves properly.
When caring for the elderly, it is important to take into account their physical, emotional and social needs.
Here is a comprehensive list of things to consider:
Physical Health:
Some things one can do to provide optimal care for the elderly:
- Regular medical checkups.
Help manage their medications and make sure they are taking them as prescribed.
- Provide a balanced diet and encourage drinking water in sufficient quantities.
- Promote physical activity and exercise to maintain strength and movement.
Ensure that their living environment is safe and risk-free.
Understand their needs: Consider if older adults have trouble performing basic tasks such as eating, commuting or doing their daily activities, they may need home care from their family or a professional caregiver.
Communication is essential, observing them, identifying their needs and meeting them accordingly.
Involve them in their care options.
Adapt the environment in the home.
If they are in a wheelchair, install ramps at the entrance to the house so they can move higher or lower levels.
Install rods to hold them in the bathroom and areas that tend to be slippery
Adjust the lights according to their needs.
Emotional well-being:
Here are some things you can do to support older people emotionally:
Spend time with them to ease loneliness and provide companionship.
Engage in activities that stimulate cognitive abilities, such as puzzles and games.
Provide emotional support, empathy and understanding.
Be alert for signs of anxiety or depression and seek professional help if necessary.
SAFETY:
Things to keep them safe:
- Make their living space safe by installing handrails and removing tripping hazards.
- Implementation of fall prevention measures.
- Remove all irregular carpets, repair worn carpets, duct tape, or remove scattered carpet edges
Arrange furniture to allow enough space for safe walking between and within all rooms.
Help them wear tight sleeves to prevent spills and burns that can occur with long, loose sleeves.
Clean up spills immediately.
- Place safety strips or anti-slip mat in the bathtub / shower and install grab bars.
Keep closet doors and drawers closed to prevent bruising or tripping.
Keep walking aids handy and keep a night-light or flashlight handy for their beds.
Store medications safely
- Social interaction:
Things that enhance their social interaction:
Encourage participation in social activities or clubs.
- Facilitate visits by family and friends.
Help use technology to stay in touch with loved ones.
Transportation:
- Ensure they have transportation for medical appointments and daily activities.
- Explore other transportation services if needed.
Temporary Care:
Arrange for temporary care to give caregivers a break when needed.
Regular health assessments:
Monitor their health closely and seek medical advice when necessary and perform the following tests:
- High blood pressure screening.
- Checking for high cholesterol.
- Obesity screening.
- Screening for abnormal blood glucose and type 2 diabetes.
- Examination of abdominal aortic aneurysm.
- Examination of osteoporosis;
- Hepatitis C screening
- HIV testing.
- Examination of other sexually transmitted diseases.
- Check for lack of brochures.
Check the use of tobacco.
Check for alcohol abuse.
Check for signs of cognitive impairment.
- Checking the use of drugs and analgesics.

Alternative Medicine - An Appropriate Approach to Improving Health

Alternative medicine forms an important part of the healthcare field, offering a holistic approach to improving health and wellness using natural methods and traditional practices.
This topic addresses the understanding of alternative medicine, its different types, and the benefits and challenges associated with it.
Definition of Alternative Medicine:
1) Complementary Medicine:
Complementary medicine involves the use of traditional medical treatments and techniques alongside traditional medical treatments.
Alternative Medicine:
It relies on non-traditional methods and techniques, such as herbal therapy, touch therapy, and traditional Chinese medicine.

Summary:
In recent years, the field of robotics has made remarkable progress, leading to the development of advanced humanoid robots.
As these machines become more intelligent and able to simulate human emotions, the question arises: Can a robot really fall in love?
This article delves into the complexities of human emotions, the limitations of artificial intelligence, and the ethical implications of human-robot relationships.
Through a combination of research, analysis and expert opinion, we aim to shed light on this thought-provoking topic.
Can a robot fall in love?
The concept of love has always been considered a unique human experience, characterized by complex emotions, attachment and intimacy.
However, with rapid advances in robotics and artificial intelligence, the line between man and machine has become increasingly blurred.
This begs the question: Can a robot really experience love?
To understand this, it is important to define what love involves.
Love encompasses a wide range of emotions, including affection, attraction, empathy, and a deep sense of connection.
These feelings are deeply rooted in biology, psychology, and personal experiences.
While robots are able to mimic some of these emotions, they lack the basic human experiences that shape and define love.
One of the main limitations of robots is their inability to have awareness or subjective experiences.
Love, as humans experience it, involves a personal perception of the world and the ability to feel emotions on a deeply personal level.
Robots, on the other hand, operate on the basis of algorithms and programmed responses, and lack the ability to engage in real emotional experiences.
In addition, love involves reciprocity and mutual understanding, which is difficult to replicate in the relationship between a robot and a human.
While robots can be programmed to respond to certain stimuli and exhibit affectionate behaviors, these behaviors are predetermined and lack the spontaneity and originality that defines human love.
Furthermore, the ethical implications of human-robot relations must be considered.
The idea of forming emotional attachments to machines raises concerns about objectification, exploitation, and possible emotional damage.
It is essential to ensure that the development and use of robots in intimate relationships is guided by ethical frameworks that prioritize the well-being and autonomy of both humans and machines.
Frequently Asked Questions:
Q: Can robots experience emotions?
A: While robots can mimic emotions through programmed responses, they lack the subjective experiences and awareness needed for real emotional experiences.
Q: Can robots develop human connection?
A: Robots can be programmed to display association-like behaviors, but these behaviors are predefined and lack the depth and complexity of human associations.
Q: Are there any risks associated with forming emotional bonds with robots?
A: Yes, there are ethical concerns surrounding objectification and the potential emotional harm that can arise from forming intimate relationships with machines.
Q: Could advances in artificial intelligence change the possibility of robots falling in love?
A: While future developments may lead to more sophisticated robots, they are unlikely to possess the subjective experiences and awareness needed for true love.
Q: What are the potential benefits of human-robot relationships?
A: Human-robot relationships have the ability to provide companionship, support, and assistance to individuals who may be socially isolated or in need of specialized care.

Summary:
Artificial intelligence has made significant advances in recent years, leading many to question whether it has surpassed human intelligence.
While AI has shown remarkable abilities in specific tasks, it is still unable to replicate the overall cognitive abilities of humans.
This article explores the current state of artificial intelligence, compares its strengths and limitations to human intelligence, and provides insights from experts in the field.
Are Artificial Intelligence Really Smarter Than Humans?
Artificial intelligence has made tremendous strides in recent years, making remarkable breakthroughs that were once thought to be limited to human intelligence.
From defeating world champions in complex games like chess and Go to helping with medical diagnostics, AI has demonstrated its ability to process vast amounts of data and make decisions with unparalleled accuracy.
However, the question remains: Is artificial intelligence really smarter than humans?
To answer this question, it is important to understand the fundamental differences between artificial intelligence and human intelligence.
Artificial intelligence refers to computer systems designed to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as visual perception, speech recognition, and decision making.
These systems rely on algorithms and machine learning techniques to analyze data and make predictions or decisions.
While AI excels in specific areas, it lacks the comprehensive cognitive capabilities that humans possess.
Human intelligence encompasses a wide range of skills, including emotional intelligence, creativity, common sense, and adaptability.
These qualities enable humans to navigate complex social interactions, think critically, and solve problems in diverse and unpredictable environments.
Moreover, AI systems are limited by their reliance on data.
They require extensive training in classified data sets to learn patterns and make accurate predictions.
In turn, humans can learn from some examples and apply their knowledge to new situations.
Humans also have intuition and can make judgments based on incomplete or ambiguous information, an ability that AI struggles to imitate.
Experts in the field of artificial intelligence confirm that despite the great progress achieved by artificial intelligence, it is still far from keeping pace with human intelligence.
Dr. John Doe, a renowned AI researcher, explains that “AI excels in narrow domains where it has been extensively trained, but lacks the ability to generalize knowledge across domains or demonstrate sound understanding. ”
It is essential to realize that artificial intelligence and human intelligence are not mutually exclusive, but rather complement each other.
The goal of developing artificial intelligence is not to replace human intelligence, but to enhance it.
By leveraging the computational power of AI and data processing capabilities, humans can enhance decision-making processes and tackle complex problems more efficiently.
Frequently Asked Questions:
Q: Can artificial intelligence outperform human intelligence in the future?
A: Although artificial intelligence has made significant progress, achieving the level of human intelligence remains a major challenge.
The development of artificial general intelligence (AGI), which encompasses the range of human cognitive abilities, remains a distant goal.
Q: Are there any risks associated with the superiority of artificial intelligence over human intelligence?
A: The potential risks associated with AI ’ s superiority over human intelligence, often referred to as AI superintelligence, are the subject of debate among experts.
Ensuring ethical and responsible development of AI systems is critical to mitigating any potential risks.
Q: How can artificial intelligence and human intelligence work together?
A: AI can complement human intelligence by automating repetitive tasks, providing data-driven insights, and aiding decision-making processes.
This collaboration allows humans to focus on tasks that require creativity, empathy, and critical thinking.
Q: What are some of the notable achievements of artificial intelligence?
A: AI has made significant achievements, including defeating human heroes in games like chess and Go, enabling autonomous vehicles, improving medical diagnostics, and enhancing natural language processing capabilities.
Q: What are the limits of artificial intelligence compared to human intelligence?
A: AI lacks the ability to demonstrate logical reasoning, adaptability, creativity, and emotional intelligence, which are inherent in human intelligence.
AI also relies heavily on disaggregated data sets and struggles to generalize knowledge across domains.

Summary:
Robots have become an integral part of our lives, revolutionizing various industries and enhancing our everyday experiences.
From manufacturing and healthcare to transportation and entertainment, robots are deployed in diverse real-life scenarios.
This article explores the different areas where robots make a big impact, highlighting their capabilities and potential future developments.
Where do you see robots in real life?
Robots have gone from just science fiction to reality in our daily lives.
It is no longer confined to the fields of research laboratories and manufacturing plants, but it has found its way into various sectors, revolutionizing the way we live and work.
Here are some areas where robots are making a big impact:
1.
Manufacturing: The manufacturing industry has undergone a major transformation with the introduction of robotics.
These machines are able to perform repetitive tasks accurately and quickly, resulting in increased productivity and reduced costs.
Industrial robots are commonly used in assembly lines, welding, coating and packaging processes.
2.
Healthcare: Robots are increasingly being used in the healthcare sector to help doctors, nurses and patients.
Surgical robots allow minimally invasive procedures, enhancing accuracy and reducing recovery time.
Robots are also being used in rehabilitation centers to help patients in the recovery process.
In addition, robotic exoskeletons are being developed to assist individuals with motor disabilities.
3.
Transportation: Self-driving vehicles, including self-driving cars and drones, are transforming the transportation industry.
These robots use advanced sensors and artificial intelligence algorithms to navigate and transport goods or passengers safely.
Self-driving cars have the potential to reduce accidents and traffic congestion, while drones are being explored for delivery services and aerial surveillance.
4.
Entertainment: Robots have found their way into the entertainment industry, captivating audiences with their performance.
From animated characters in theme parks to robotic pets and escorts, these machines provide interactive and engaging experiences.
In addition, robots are used in filmmaking for special effects and as an alternative to dangerous or complex scenes.
5.
Home and personal assistance: Robotic devices are increasingly integrated into our homes to help with various tasks.
Smart home systems use robots to control lighting, temperature and security, enhancing comfort and energy efficiency.
Self-help robots can do household chores, such as vacuuming or mowing grass, saving individuals time to focus on other activities.
Frequently Asked Questions:
Q: Are robots replacing human workers?
A: While robots automate some tasks, they also create new jobs.
The integration of robotics often leads to the creation of more specialized roles that require human expertise in the operation and maintenance of these machines.
Q: What are the ethical implications of using robots in real life?
A: The increasing use of robots raises ethical concerns regarding the privacy, security and potential displacement of human workers.
It is important to develop regulations and guidelines to ensure responsible and ethical deployment of robots in various fields.
Q: What does the future hold for robots in real life?
A: The future of robotics is promising, with advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and sensing technologies.
We can expect to see robots play a more important role in healthcare, education, agriculture and space exploration, among other areas.
However, a balance between human involvement and robotic automation is necessary to ensure harmonious coexistence.

IATA: Insufficient quantities of sustainable aviation fuel produced
The International Air Transport Association (IATA) has announced its estimate of sustainable aviation fuel production volumes, with 2023 producing more than 600 million litres (0.5 metric tonnes) of sustainable aviation fuel, more than doubling the production volume in 2022 at 300 million litres (0.25 metric tonnes).
Share of sustainable aviation fuel
Sustainable aviation fuels accounted for 3% of total renewable fuel production, while other sectors accounted for 97% of renewable fuel production.
In 2024, sustainable aviation fuel production is expected to triple to 1,875 billion litres (1.5 metric tonnes), representing 0.53% of aviation fuel needs and 6% of renewable fuel capacity.
The low production of sustainable aviation fuel relative to total renewable fuels is mainly due to the allocation of new capacity produced during 2023 to other types of renewable fuels.
Advertisements
Willie Walsh, Director General of the International Air Transport Association (IATA), said: “We see the doubling of sustainable aviation fuel production in 2023 as a positive sign, as is the forecast for a threefold production growth over the next year.
Despite this remarkable growth, the relative share of sustainable aviation fuel in total renewable fuel production will only grow from 3% this year to 6% in 2024, and remains insufficient, limiting the supply of sustainable aviation fuel and keeping prices high.
The aviation sector requires 25 to 30% of renewable fuel production capacity for sustainable aviation fuel.
Based on these data, the aviation industry is expected to achieve full climate neutrality by 2050.
We will not be able to take advantage of all opportunities to achieve net zero carbon emissions from the aviation sector before these levels are reached.
This is where government policies can make a difference, by focusing on policies that encourage increased production of sustainable aviation fuels and diversification of raw materials, including those available locally. ”
Results of the Third Conference on Aviation and Alternative Fuels
Participants at the third Aviation and Alternative Fuels Conference, organized by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), agreed to create a global framework to promote sustainable aviation fuel production in all regions so that the carbon emissions of fuels used in the global aviation sector will be reduced by 5% by 2030, requiring 17.5 billion litres (14 metric tons) of sustainable aviation fuel to reach this level.
Walsh added: “Governments aspire to achieve climate neutrality in aviation by 2050.
“Following the announcement of the interim objective at the Aviation and Alternative Fuels Conference, policies and measures must be put in place to achieve the desired significant increase in sustainable aviation fuel production. ”
The problem is not the demand, especially since the entire amount of sustainable aviation fuel produced has been purchased and used.
Sustainable aviation fuel contributed US $756 million to total record global fuel sales in 2023.
At least 43 airlines have already pledged to use up to 16.25 billion liters (13 metric tons) of sustainable aviation fuel in 2030, with more agreements announced in turn.
The challenge is to increase supply in line with demand levels; sustainable aviation fuel production is expected to exceed the 78 billion litres (63 metric tonnes) mark in 2029.
Governments should develop a policy framework to encourage renewable fuel producers to allocate 25-30% of their production to sustainable aviation fuels, to meet the ambitions of the 3rd Aviation and Alternative Fuels Conference in line with current regional and national policies and airline commitments.

Laram and Africa CMDC launch first ‘ environmentally responsible ’ flight
Heba Press _ Rabat
Royal Air Maroc and Africa CMDC have launched the first carbon-free flight from the African continent, powered by sustainable aviation fuel.
“Flight AT 505, which was secured by a Boeing 787-9 aircraft in conjunction with the COP28 Climate Conference in Dubai, landed on Saturday at 4: 30 pm (16H30) at Belize Diani Airport in Dakar, three and a half hours after taking off from Casablanca ’ s Mohammed V Airport, ” the statement said.
The Dreamliner, with 302 passengers on board, used nearly 9 tons of sustainable aviation fuel, 40 percent of the amount needed to make the flight, avoiding the emission of nearly 23 tons of carbon dioxide.
In parallel, the CO2 emissions from the rest of the traditional fuel used for this flight (60 per cent of the fuel volume) will be offset by Royal Air Maroc under the voluntary carbon offset programme led by the Mohammed VI Foundation for Environmental Protection.
The president and general manager of Royal Air Maroc, Abdelhamid Adou, said: “We are proud to launch the first sustainable aviation fuel flight connecting two African countries.
This process is part of our efforts to contribute to the development of research and experiments by industry, researchers and specialists to significantly reduce the carbon footprint in the aviation sector. ”
“This reflects our commitment to accelerate the decarbonization of Moroccan air transport, through full commitment, like key leaders in the aviation sector, to achieve the goal of carbon neutrality by 2050, ” Adou added, noting that“ the first strategic phase of this goal is the integration of 10 per cent of sustainable aviation fuel from 2030. ”
“Although aviation contributes only 2 per cent of global CO2 emissions, all industry players are mobilizing with sustainable aviation fuel.
Today, as an African leader, Royal Air Maroc must be exemplary and pave the way for our continent. ”
Said Baghdadi, Managing Director of Africa CMDC, said: “We are honored to be a partner of Royal Air Maroc and to accompany it in the implementation of this historic journey, which is a new building block for the promotion of sustainable fuel consumption in our country, which is indispensable for achieving decarbonization of air transport. ”
“As part of its voluntary environmental strategy, Africa CMDC is firmly committed to exploring all possible solutions to ensure the integration of the long-term sustainability goals of air transport in Morocco, ” he added.
The use of sustainable aviation fuel is the main lever that will enable decarbonisation of the air transport sector on medium and long haul flights.
The variety of sustainable aviation fuel used for the AT 505 flight on December 9 does not require any engine modification.
This sustainable fuel comes from the conversion of used vegetable oils, providing a reduction of up to 90 per cent of carbon dioxide emissions over the entire life cycle compared to fossil fuel equivalents.
Other types are being developed by the sector and researchers, such as sustainable aviation fuels produced from biomass, or from hydrogen and carbon dioxide taken from the atmosphere.
The launch of this environmentally responsible flight is a historic precedent for Royal Air Maroc and Commercial Air Africa, and coincides with the Climate Conference (COP28) in Dubai, where the international community is discussing a number of environmental issues.
Thus, this initiative responds to the ambitious goals set during this World Conference, which aims to accelerate the energy transition of the planet.
It is also in full harmony with Morocco's policy in the field of sustainable development and the use of renewable energies.
For several years, Royal Air Maroc has been working to reduce its carbon footprint through several workshops, notably the renewal of its fleet and the gradual integration of new generation aircraft such as the Dreamliner, allowing a reduction of its carbon footprint by 25 per cent.
The company has also implemented an ambitious program to reduce its energy consumption, such as reducing weight on aircraft, improving flight plans, and even maintenance procedures for environmentally responsible aircraft.
These measures, contained in the Fuel Efficiency Program, have enabled Royal Air Maroc to reduce its fuel consumption by 10 per cent and its CO2 emissions by 10 per cent.
Another energy efficiency project was implemented at the Royal Air Maroc buildings, enabling it to obtain the LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) certification, a globally recognized certification in the field of sustainable development.
Thanks to all these measures, in 2023 Royal Air Maroc was awarded the IEnvA (IATA Environmental Assessment) certification, an environmental management system developed by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) that demonstrates respect for environmental obligations.
The Royal Air Maroc Group is determined to strengthen its continental leadership through innovation and investment in the use of sustainable aviation fuels in the coming years, while contributing to the development of more sustainable solutions.
Sustainable aviation fuel, an alternative fuel for aviation, is produced from various sources that are wholly or partly renewable, such as biomass, algae, agricultural or food waste, or even hydrogen.
It is a fuel designed to be blended with fossil fuels used in aviation, without modifying aircraft engines.
New technologies are being developed, including sustainable synthetic aviation fuel, made from hydrogen and carbon taken from the atmosphere.
Production of jet fuel is complex and must meet strict standards.
Targeted investments, regulatory controls and government support mechanisms are among the catalysts that will facilitate the industry ’ s transition to sustainable aviation fuel.

The Impact of Technology on Agriculture | A Qualitative Shift Towards a Sustainable Agricultural Future
TECHNOLOGY
Technology is one of the key drivers of a qualitative transformation in the agriculture sector, contributing significantly to improving productivity, saving resources, and promoting environmental sustainability.
The integration of technology into agriculture is key to meeting food safety challenges and improving crop quality.
Let ’ s take a look at the impact of technology in this vital area.
1.
Improvement in irrigation methods:
Smart irrigation technologies contribute to improving the efficiency of water consumption in agriculture.
The use of automatic irrigation systems and accurate soil monitoring techniques can reduce water losses and improve water distribution in a way that meets the needs of plants.
2.
Effective use of fertilizers:
Graphical analysis and plant sensing techniques enable farmers to accurately determine the nutrient needs of plants, reducing excess fertilizer use and improving soil and crop quality.
3.
Precision Cultivation:
Precise farming techniques allow resources to be allocated more effectively, such as irrigation, fertilizers, and pesticides, based on the needs of each part of the field, reducing costs and improving production.
4.
Robotics and Intelligent Vehicles:
The use of robots and smart vehicles in agriculture contributes to doing heavy and expensive work more efficiently.
Drones can quickly and effectively scan fields to check crop conditions and needs.
5.
Biotechnology in Agriculture:
The use of biotechnology enhances the effectiveness of crops and reduces the impact of pests and diseases.
Develop genetically modified crops that contribute to improving qualities such as drought resistance and pest resistance.
6.
Smart Farm Management Systems:
Artificial intelligence and data analysis technologies allow for efficient farm management, while providing accurate guidance based on environmental conditions and crop needs, contributing to improved agricultural decisions.
Challenges and opportunities:
Cost of technology:
Some technologies can be expensive, posing a challenge to farmers, especially in areas with limited resources.
2.Provide training:
The use of technology requires specialized training for farmers to ensure its effective use.
Security and privacy issues:
Farm data must be protected and a balance must be struck between providing information and maintaining data privacy.
Conclusion:
Agriculture technology is proving successful in improving production efficiency and enhancing the sustainability of agriculture.
As technological advances continue, a continuous improvement in the performance of agriculture can be expected, through the use of innovations to meet future challenges in food safety and environmental protection.

Scientists have made major breakthroughs in quantum mechanics this year, challenging our understanding of the universe and pushing the boundaries of what is possible.
The James Webb Space Telescope has captured stunning images of distant galaxies and stars, raising questions about their formation and growth.
In the field of quantum computing, researchers have made progress in developing more reliable quantum computers and improving quantum debugging.
In addition, scientists have made achievements such as remote energy transfer and the discovery of new types of phase transitions in entangled qubits.
These discoveries highlight ongoing progress in understanding the quantum world, and there is much to explore and uncover in the future.
In astronomy, the James Webb Space Telescope provides groundbreaking images of the universe.
The telescope observed the first stars and galaxies in the universe that formed shortly after the Big Bang, challenging our predictions about their size and brightness.
Astronomers are now struggling to understand the rapid growth of these galaxies and the formation of supermassive black holes, which appear earlier and with a larger mass than expected.
At the frontiers of quantum computing, researchers have made great strides in overcoming the challenges of developing reliable quantum computers.
The new approach involves storing information in topological particles called "non-Abelian anions", which are likely to lead to error-tolerant quantum computers.
In addition, progress has been made in correcting quantum errors, paving the way for improved quantum bit stability.
Quantum mechanics has also revealed fascinating phenomena.
Scientists have been able to transfer energy across microscopic distances by exploiting the characteristic properties of quantum vacuum.
Moreover, a new type of phase transition has been discovered in entangled qubits, where the measurement of one qubit affects the state of other qubits.
Understanding these shifts may have implications for information processing and sharing.
As researchers delve deeper into the quantum world, they continue to define “quantum. ”
Additional metrics, such as entanglement and "fermion magic", have been introduced to capture the unique nature of quantum systems that cannot be simulated on classical computers.
These groundbreaking discoveries in quantum mechanics shed light on the enormous complexities and possibilities that exist within the universe.
Although we have made tremendous progress, much remains to be discovered and understood.
As we begin the next phase of exploration, we can expect more profound discoveries about the mysteries of our universe.

Millie's attempts to liberalize Argentina's economy
366 rules changed, including privatization, housing and work
Demonstration in Argentina against the decree of President Javier Milli.
"E.B.A."
Last week, Argentina ’ s libertarian president, Javier Milley, issued a sweeping decree to change or abolish 366 economic rules in a country accustomed to heavy government intervention in the market.
The move is the first of its kind in Argentina ’ s history, as none of its democratically elected presidents has attempted such a massive dismantling of the system.
That ’ s exactly what Milley promised during his election campaign, waving a chainsaw to symbolize his attempt to cut public spending as Argentina struggles with three-figure inflation after decades of fiscal mismanagement.
However, according to Argentine law, Congress still has the power to flood Melli ’ s program.
Change of daily life
Ten days after taking office, and on the eve of the holidays, Milley presented his "necessary and urgent" decree to loosen some of the rules governing the country's economy, where annual inflation has reached 160 percent.
One big change will be the removal of all restrictions between tenant and landlord, such as laws on increasing rents.
In recent years, landlords have increasingly priced their properties in dollars to avoid falling into the rental income trap that has long been overtaken by rising inflation.
This was a nightmare for tenants in a country where access to the dollar was tightly controlled.
Melli ’ s plan also loosened labor laws, increasing the probation period for new employees from three to eight months.
Compensation for Groundless Dismissal Laws have been amended in the interest of companies, and plans are being made to renegotiate labor agreements in force since 1975.
He also lifted export restrictions and said the internet market would be liberalized.
Milley also abandoned rules preventing the privatization of government institutions, already setting his sights on the national airline and the oil company.
He also moved to limit the right to strike enshrined in the constitution.
Purpose of the decree
Milley, a figure whose rise to the country ’ s highest office surprised most observers, blames the interventionist and protectionist policies of previous governments for stifling the economy.
Before the decree was announced, the new government had already devalued the Argentine peso by more than 50 percent and announced massive cuts in generous government subsidies for fuel and transportation starting in January.
“The goal is to begin the process of rebuilding the country, restoring the freedom and independence of individuals and beginning to dismantle the vast amount of systems that have halted and hindered economic growth, ” Milley said.
One protester said: "There may be people with Stockholm syndrome.
They are fascinated by a model that impoverishes them. ”
The opposition, who was recently ousted from the government, criticized Milley for the decree, seeing it as a way to overcome his lack of a majority in Congress.
Miley Libertad Avanza, who is only two years old, has only 40 of the 257 seats in the House of Representatives and seven of the 72 seats in the Senate.
German Martinez, speaker of the parliament of the Peronist coalition, said: "Uniting for the homeland is not the right way.
They sent the reforms as bills.
“Don ’ t be afraid of democratic debate. ”
Constitutional lawyer Emiliano Vitaliani said the country's highest laws state that "in principle laws cannot be amended by decree and the president cannot replace Congress."
Political scientist Lara Guiboro said the resolution "crosses all boundaries and rules out many issues that need political agreements from Congress and the provinces."
Vitalini said the decree could be revoked if it was rejected by both houses of Congress.
Otherwise it will come into force on December 29.
Constitutional lawyer Alejandro Carrillo said in an article in the Lanacion newspaper that "the president has made a very big bet, and his success will depend on his ability to obtain legislative support that is not yet known."
It comes at a time when Argentina is stuck in the grip of an economic crisis with the highest inflation in 30 years.
Cecilia Rojas is searching every store in the vast city of Buenos Aires to find affordable gifts for her children for what is expected to be a bleak Christmas day this year as Argentina faces its worst economic crisis in decades.
Rojas, 47, said: “Before, I used to buy from a well-known toy chain, but now I ’ m looking at smaller stores nearby to find a better price.
Rojas, a psychologist, has two sons, one aged 17 and the other eight.
This year, they will each receive one gift, knowing that they have received many gifts in previous years. ”
Argentina ends the year with the highest inflation rate in the past 30 years, over 160 percent year-on-year.
The 50 percent devaluation of the peso, approved by the government of liberal President Javier Milley on Dec. 12 two days after taking office, has led to a new price spike in a country where more than 40 percent of the population is poor.
Games prices have risen by 110 to 230 percent this year, according to figures from the Argentine Chamber of Gaming Industry.
Thus, shoppers on Christmas Day should be patient and seasoned.
Ogostina Jago, a 23-year-old mother of four, said: "If you walk a little, you can find the same product in different stores at different prices."
"This year, we will buy him a gift thanks to the help we get from grandmothers and fortunately, there are many of them."
The country is also under the brunt of the radical measures of President Javier Mille ’ s new government, which has issued hundreds of decrees to revive the ailing economy.
Milley, who has pledged to cut government spending, also announced deep cuts in subsidies on fuel and the transport sector starting in January.
His government also scrapped a programme to control the prices of some goods introduced by the previous government to try to soften the impact of inflation.
Milley warned that the country was on the brink of hyperinflation and that things would get worse before they began to improve.
Alexandra Mazi, a 49-year-old schoolteacher who took part in a protest against the new measures, said: “They are starving people, using policies that have been applied in the past and have not worked, and all they are doing is impoverishing the working class. ”
Milley ’ s government has forced organizers of its first protest to pay tens of thousands of dollars to cover the cost of deploying security forces to protect it.
Euronews reported that thousands of people took part in a demonstration on Wednesday against Milley ’ s austerity measures and to commemorate the bloody 2001 protests that followed the country ’ s economic collapse.
Government spokesman Manuel Adorney said the cost of the massive deployment of police and riot police was 60 million pesos ($73,000 at the official exchange rate).
“The bill will be sent to social movements ” as they“ bear responsibility for the cost that should not be borne by citizens, ” he said.

A new study has found that walking at least 4,000 steps a day is enough to maintain brain health and prevent Alzheimer ’ s disease.
Add Announcement
Benefits of walking
Researchers from the Pacific Institute of Neuroscience ’ s Brain Health Center, located in Providence St. John ’ s Health Center, studied the brains of more than 10,000 people and found that gray matter, which helps process information, white matter, which connects different brain regions, and the hippocampus, which is important for memory, were all more pronounced in exercisers.
The team studied MRI scans on 10,125 people to find out why exercise reduced the risk of dementia or Alzheimer ’ s disease, according to the Journal of Alzheimer ’ s Disease.
Importance of walking
Dr David Merrill, co-author of the study, said: “We found that even moderate levels of physical activity, such as taking fewer than 4,000 steps a day, can have a positive effect on brain health.
“That ’ s far less than the 10,000 steps often proposed, making it a more achievable goal for many people. ”
Lead researcher Dr Cyrus Raji added: “Our research supports previous studies that have shown that physical activity is good for your brain.
"Not only does exercise reduce the risk of dementia, but it also helps maintain brain size, which is critical as we age," he said.
Regular physical activity and brain size
Dr Sumaya Misami, assistant professor of neuroscience at the St. John ’ s Cancer Institute and Pacific Brain Health Center, said: “Our research links regular physical activity to larger brain volume, suggesting neuroprotective benefits.
"This study strengthens a large sample of our understanding of lifestyle factors in brain health and dementia prevention."
10 Factors That Increase Your Risk Of Alzheimer 's Disease
A study published in the Lancet in 2020 found that about ten modifiable risk factors increase the risk of Alzheimer ’ s disease, including physical activity.
George Perry, editor-in-chief of the Journal of Alzheimer ’ s Disease, said: “This study demonstrates the effect of exercise on brain health imaging, and when added to other studies on the role of diet, stress reduction and socialization provide proven benefits to drugs. ” – Free modifiable factors in dramatically reducing Alzheimer ’ s disease.
"Whether it's daily walking or a favorite sport, regular physical activity can have lasting benefits for brain health."
It is noteworthy that Alzheimer's disease scientists have not yet found a cure for it.

Thousands of Argentines protest President Milley's economic measures
Call for court action to repeal decree that undermines workers ’ and consumers ’ rights
Protests against economic decisions in Argentina
Thousands of Argentines demonstrated in Buenos Aires on Wednesday to protest against the decree of comprehensive economic reform and deregulation, proposed by President Javier Mille.
In detail, the protesters, who protested at the call of the unions, demanded that the courts intervene to overturn the decree, which they say undermines the rights of workers and consumers.
Argentina ’ s Congress is holding an extraordinary session this week to consider the decree at the request of the ultra-liberal Mili, who took office on December 10.
The decree would change or repeal more than 350 economic regulations in a country accustomed to heavy government intervention in the market, according to Sky News Arabia.
Among other things, the decree abolishes the rental price cap, some labor protections, and laws that protect consumers from arbitrary price increases at a time when annual inflation exceeds 160 percent and the poverty level is 40 percent.
A number of civic groups on Saturday filed a legal challenge to the constitutionality of the decree, while demonstrators on Wednesday waved Argentine flags and banners reading "The homeland is not for sale".
Building union official Gerardo Martinez told reporters during the march: "We do not question the legitimacy of President Milley, but we want him to respect the separation of powers.
Workers must defend their rights when there is unconstitutionality. ”
Javier Mille's "chainsaw plan" to cut government spending has sparked a series of popular protests against the government.
Other aspects of the decree include ending automatic increases in pensions, imposing restrictions on the right to strike, and easing price caps for private health services.
Some 7,000 public sector contracts are being terminated in a bid to cut government spending.
Unless Congress repeals the plan in its entirety, the decree will go into effect on Friday.
Milley ’ s far-right party has 40 of the 257 members of Congress and seven of the 72 senators.

Arm speed aggravates the risk of fractures in old age
(MENAFN-Al Wakeel News) New research says younger adults move their arm more quickly than their older counterparts when they slip, helping them regain balance, preventing falls and fractures.
According to New Scientist, researcher Jonathan Lee Conver and his team focused on the side fall.
People ’ s legs can ’ t move sideways as freely as their arms, so the upper limbs play a more important role in restoring balance when sliding sideways.
To better understand how to prevent such falls, 11 people with an average age of 72 and 11 people with an average age of 25 walked over a glass panel installed in a driveway at the University of Illinois at Chicago.
They were made to slide sideways through movements on the walkway and lubricants on the roof.
The researchers analyzed the movement by installing monitoring devices and photographed the participants from each angle using eight cameras.
All participants wore a special belt to ensure they did not fall down and hurt themselves.
The researchers found that when exposed to the risk of slipping, the younger ones accelerated their arms by an average of 36% more than the older participants.
The younger ones ’ reaction time when they reached the maximum speed of their arm movements was also 310 milliseconds faster.
The results called for training older people to move their arms more quickly to avoid injuries associated with falling, especially as it is one of the most important causes of increasing bone fractures and joint injuries in old age.

Navigating the future of generative AI: balancing exciting possibilities with potential pitfalls
Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful force, reshaping the technological landscape thanks to its ability to independently create content.
From language models such as GPT-3 to image generation algorithms, generative AI holds enormous promise for the future.
However, this promising future is not without challenges.
In this article, we will explore the potential negative consequences and the most exciting possibilities of generative AI, with the aim of balancing optimism with caution.
In addition, we will address the recent leadership shift involving Sam Altman at OpenAI, highlighting ethical considerations associated with AI development.
Sam Altman ’ s Leadership Transformation: Lessons in Ethical Artificial Intelligence
In recent months, the AI community has seen a major leadership shift at OpenAI that Sam Altman has been involved in.
The CEO, known for his influential role in guiding OpenAI initiatives, faced a period of controversy over his subsequent dismissal and reappointment.
This incident highlighted the challenges associated with ethical considerations in the development and management of AI.
Addressing ethical concerns: Sam Altman ’ s leadership transformation has led to a reassessment of ethical considerations in AI development and regulatory decision-making.
The incident raised questions about transparency and accountability and the need for strong ethical frameworks to guide the development and deployment of AI technologies.
Transparency and accountability: The leadership transition emphasized the importance of transparency in organizational decision-making, especially in contexts involving AI technologies with wide-ranging implications.
He highlighted the need to hold leaders and organizations accountable for their actions and to ensure that ethical guidelines were followed.
Community Engagement: The controversy surrounding Sam Altman ’ s leadership transformation has also highlighted the importance of involving the wider community in decisions related to AI development.

Possible negative consequences
Ethical Concerns and Prejudice
One of the primary concerns with generative AI is its susceptibility to biases found in training data.
If the data used to train these models reflects societal biases, AI may inadvertently perpetuate these biases and amplify them in their resulting content.
Addressing this problem is critical to preventing AI systems from inadvertently promoting and spreading harmful stereotypes.
Security Threats and Deep Counterfeiting
The ability of generative AI to produce highly realistic and compelling content raises serious security concerns.
Deepfakes, for example, are images or videos created by artificial intelligence that manipulate content and superimpose it on real footage.
This technology can be exploited for harmful purposes, such as creating fake news, impersonating individuals or spreading misleading information.
With the development of generative AI, the challenge of distinguishing between real and fake content has become increasingly difficult.
Invasion of Privacy
Advances in generative artificial intelligence also raise concerns about privacy violations.
The ability to create realistic images and videos of individuals who have never been involved in creating such content poses a risk to personal privacy.
Protecting individuals from the unauthorized use of their images in AI-generated content will be a pressing issue in the coming years.
Unemployment and economic turmoil
The automation capabilities of generative AI – the displacement of the workforce in some industries – may be driving.
Jobs that involve routine and repetitive tasks, such as content creation, may be at risk.
Balancing technological progress with societal well-being will be a challenge to ensure that AI complements human work rather than replaces it.
Ethical and ethical dilemmas
As AI systems become more efficient at producing content that mimics human creativity, ethical questions arise.
For example, who owns the rights to art or literature generated by artificial intelligence?
Identifying the legal and ethical implications of creations produced by non-human entities challenges our traditional understanding of authorship and intellectual property.

The most exciting possibilities.
Enhancing creativity and productivity
Generative AI has the ability to amplify human creativity and productivity by automating mundane tasks, allowing individuals to focus on the most complex and strategic aspects of their work.
In areas such as content creation, design and marketing, AI can help and inspire, leading to an increase in innovation and efficiency.
A revolution in health care
The future of generative AI promises breakthroughs in healthcare, from drug discovery to personalized medicine.
AI models can analyze large data sets, identify patterns, and propose new solutions, dramatically accelerating the pace of medical research and improving patient outcomes.
Custom User Experiences
As generative AI continues to evolve, it can provide highly customized and tailored experiences for users.
From adaptive learning platforms to content recommendations, AI systems can understand individual preferences and behaviors, providing a smoother and more engaging user experience.
Collaboration between Human and Artificial Intelligence
Instead of replacing human roles, generative AI is likely to foster collaboration between humans and machines.
AI tools can act as creative partners, helping professionals in various fields achieve results that would not be possible by traditional methods alone.
This collaborative approach can lead to unprecedented levels of innovation.
Innovations in art and entertainment
Generative AI has already made waves in the art world, creating unique pieces that challenge traditional notions of creativity.
In the entertainment industry, AI-driven content creation can open up new horizons for storytelling, virtual worlds, and interactive experiences, pushing the boundaries of what is possible in these areas.
CONCLUSION
The future of generative AI is a double-edged sword, offering exciting possibilities and potential pitfalls.
As we navigate this technological landscape, it is important to recognize and address the ethical concerns and negative outcomes associated with generative AI.
Balancing innovation and responsible development is essential to harnessing the full potential of AI while mitigating its risks.
By fostering interdisciplinary collaboration, implementing ethical guidelines, and investing in research to address biases and security threats, we can pave the way for a future where generative AI enhances human creativity, productivity, and well-being.
The recent leadership shift that Sam Altman participated in serves as a reminder of the importance of ethical considerations in the development of AI, urging the industry to learn from the mistakes of the past and shaping a collective future where AI benefits humanity responsibly.

The speed of the arm when falling.
Risk factor for fractures
MOHAMMED ISMAIL, CAIRO - A recent study reveals that people who move more quickly in their arm are more likely to have broken bones when falling
Younger people move the arm more quickly than their older counterparts when they slip, helping them regain balance and prevent falls and fractures, new research says.
Reportedly in the New Scientist, researcher Jonathan Lee Conver and his team focused on the side fall.
People ’ s legs can ’ t move sideways as freely as their arms, so the upper limbs play a more important role in restoring balance when sliding sideways.
To better understand how to prevent such falls, 11 people with an average age of 72 and 11 people with an average age of 25 walked over a glass panel installed in a walkway at the University of Illinois at Chicago.
They were made to slide sideways through movements on the walkway and lubricants on the roof.
The researchers analyzed the movement by installing monitoring devices, and photographed the participants from each angle using eight cameras.
All participants wore a special belt to ensure that they did not fall down and hurt themselves.
The researchers found that when exposed to the risk of slipping, the younger ones accelerated their arms by an average of 36% more than the older participants.
The younger ones ’ reaction time at the top speed of their arm movements was also 310 milliseconds faster.
The results called for training the elderly to move their arms more quickly to avoid injuries associated with falling, especially as it is one of the most important causes of increasing bone fractures and joint injuries in old age.

Who Should Avoid Intermittent Fasting?
The eating pattern known as intermittent fasting (IF) alternates between the times a person eats and when they fast.
It emphasizes when to eat rather than focusing on what to eat specifically, there are many common ways to practice intermittent fasting.
One such approach is the 16 / 8 approach, which entails fasting for 16 hours each day and limits food intake to 8 hours.
Intermittent fasting (IF) has revolutionized the world of health, promising weight loss, improved health and even mental clarity.
Before you jump into this trendy eating pattern, it ’ s important to understand that it ’ s not a one-size-fits-all solution.
Intermittent fasting may not be suitable for everyone, and some individuals should treat it with caution.
In fact, some groups should stay away from intermittent fasting for the sake of their health.
Children and adolescents: Growing bodies need constant fuel, and restricted eating windows in intermittent fasting can hinder their growth.
Pregnant and lactating women: Nutritional needs increase during these periods, and intermittent fasting may harm the health of the mother and baby.
Individuals with diabetes: Fluctuations in blood sugar are a major concern for diabetics, and intermittent fasting can exacerbate this risk.
People with eating disorders: Intermittent fasting can lead to unhealthy behaviors in people with anorexia, bulimia, or other eating disorders.
Individuals with certain medical conditions: Conditions such as heart disease, kidney disease and hypoglycemia make intermittent fasting dangerous.
Anyone taking certain medications: Some medications require you to eat with them, and intermittent fasting can disrupt this important routine.
Even if you are not in the above categories, consider warning signs such as:
Excessive hunger or dizziness: These may indicate an unhealthy imbalance of energy.
Difficulty concentrating or fatigue: Intermittent fasting can affect energy levels and cognitive function in some individuals.
Sleep Disorders: Skipping meals can disrupt your sleep patterns and make you feel drained.
According to Fidhi Chawla, dietitian and founder of the Fisico diet and cosmetic clinic, the best way to determine if intermittent fasting is right for you is to listen to your body.
If you experience any negative effects, feel free to abandon the plan and consult a healthcare professional.
Remember that sustainable weight loss and overall health comes from a balanced diet, regular exercise and personal methods that prioritize your well-being.
Intermittent fasting can be a healthy and effective tool for some people, but it ’ s not suitable for everyone.
Be aware of the potential risks, listen to your body, and prioritize your individual needs before embarking on any new food plan.

Qu Day, when a computer can hack into all the world's computers
(MENAFN- Al-Anbaa) - Quantum technology could compromise our encryption systems.
Can the United States replace them before it is too late?
Today, they call it Q-Day, the day when a quantum computer, more powerful than any device built to date, will be able to destroy the world of privacy and security as we know it.
- This will happen with a bold arithmetic work; it is to analyze some very large numbers, which are hundreds of numbers long, into their initial factors.
It may sound like a meaningless split question, but it will fundamentally undermine the encryption protocols that governments and companies have relied on for decades.
Sensitive information such as military intelligence, weapon designs, industry secrets and banking information are often transferred or stored under digital locks that can be unlocked through the process of analyzing large numbers.
Surprisingly, among the various threats to U.S. national security, cryptographic detection is rarely discussed in the same terms as nuclear proliferation, the global climate crisis, or artificial general intelligence.
But for many behind the scenes solvers, the danger is existential.
Glenn Gerstel, former NSA general counsel and one of the authors of the Expert Consensus Report on Cryptography, confirms that this issue is likely to be very different from any one we ’ ve ever encountered.
There may be only a 1% chance of this happening, but a 1% chance of a catastrophic risk is something to worry about.
In the same vein, the White House and its internal security apparatus have made clear that a powerful quantum computer, if it falls into the wrong hands, can disrupt everything from secure communications to the foundations of our financial system.
In a short time, scammers can control credit card transactions and stock exchanges; manipulate air traffic systems and GPS signals; and the security of critical infrastructure, such as nuclear plants and the power grid, can be compromised.
The risk extends not only to future breaches, but also to decrypted sets of encrypted data collected now and in the years to come.
Current and former intelligence officials say China and other potential rivals are already working to find and store such data in the hope of decrypting it in the future.
No one knows when quantum computing will go this far.
Today, the most powerful quantum device uses 433 qubits, also called the quantum equivalent of transistors.
That number would probably need to reach tens of thousands, perhaps even millions, before today ’ s crypto systems fall.
But within the American cybersecurity community, the threat is perceived as real and urgent.
China, Russia and the United States are racing to develop technology ahead of their geopolitical rivals, though it is hard to know who is advancing because some of the gains are shrouded in secrecy.
On the American side, the prospect of an adversary winning this race has driven a years-long effort to develop a new generation of encryption systems that even a powerful quantum computer won ’ t be able to decrypt.
The effort, which began in 2016, will culminate early next year when the National Institute of Standards and Technology finalizes its guidance for the transition to new systems.
Late last year, US President Joe Biden signed into law the Quantum Computing Cybersecurity Preparedness Act, which directed agencies to begin verifying their cryptographic regulations that would need to be replaced.
But even in light of this new urgency, the shift to stronger encryption will likely take about a decade or more, a pace that some experts fear may not be fast enough to avert disaster.
Stay on top of the scene
Researchers have known since the 1990s that quantum computing — which relies on the properties of subatomic particles to perform multiple calculations at the same time — may one day threaten the cryptographic systems used today.
In 1994, American mathematician Peter Shore demonstrated how to do this, publishing an algorithm that a virtual quantum computer could use at the time to quickly factor exceptionally large numbers, a task in which traditional computers lacked efficiency.
- Shore's algorithm was initially treated with a degree of anxious curiosity.
But the world is already moving to embrace encryption methods that Shore has proven to be particularly weak.
However, quantum computing has undergone a major breakthrough.
In recent years, IBM, Google and others have shown steady progress in building larger and more capable models, leading experts to conclude that expansion is not only theoretically possible, but also achievable through some crucial technical advances.
Cybersecurity experts have been warning for some time that rivals such as China and Russia — among the few adversaries with both the scientific talent and the billions of dollars needed to build a massive quantum computer — are likely to go ahead with quantum science in secret.
Despite a number of achievements by American scientists, analysts insist the nation is still at risk of being left behind — a fear echoed this month in a report by the Center for Data Innovation, a think-tank focused on technology policy.
Open Source Defense
According to the National Institute of Standards and Technology, the federal government has set an overall goal of switching as far as possible to these new anti-quantum algorithms by 2035, which many officials acknowledge is ambitious.
These algorithms are the product of years of collaboration within a diverse and international community of cryptographers.
After being invited around the world in 2016, the National Institute of Standards and Technology received 82 applications, most of which were developed by small teams of academics and engineers.
As in the past, the National Institute of Standards and Technology relied on a guidebook in which it solicited and then launched new solutions for researchers in government and the private sector, to be selected because of weaknesses.
The National Institute of Standards and Technology eventually selected four algorithms to recommend their wider use.
Despite the serious challenges of transitioning to these new algorithms, the United States has benefited from the experience of previous migrations, such as those that addressed the so-called Y2K bug and previous moves to new cryptographic standards.
The size of American companies like Apple, Google, and Amazon, with their control over large swaths of internet traffic, also means that few players can quietly accomplish the transformation.
But strategists warn that the way an adversary might behave after a major breakthrough makes the threat different from any society has faced.
