Human and high-tech era
January 11, 2024 01: 15
Alfahm Muhammad
There is no doubt that philosophy is the mirror of its time, for a philosopher cannot think outside the fundamental issues posed by his reality.
This is exactly the case for Nick Bostrom, a Swedish philosopher born in 1973, where all the issues that concern him express the concerns and problems that afflict the human mind at the turn of the third millennium: the challenges of artificial intelligence, the weakness of contemporary civilization, existential dangers, and the improvement of human capabilities through technology.
In short, what matters to Bostrom is the totality of issues that question the fate of man in the high-tech era.
Perhaps that is why he is credited with founding the Institute for the Future of Man, part of the University of Oxford to which he belongs.
He also oversees the Oxford Martin Program, on the effects of future technology on human civilization.
Nick Bostrom has written hundreds of articles and published works including Entropy Bias 2002, Human Improvement 2009, and Artificial Superintelligence 2014, the latter of which is considered one of the best sellers in the world according to the New York Times.
In 2015, Foreign Policy named the author as one of the top 100 global thinkers.
Existential risks
Nick Bostrom talks about existential dangers, which are the sum total of the dangers that result from human activity and its scientific and technological development.
In his joint book with Serbian astronomer and philosopher Milan Serkovic, “Global Catastrophic Risks. ”
The author attempts to identify a bundle of dangers that may threaten the survival of human civilization.
Throughout his history, man has known many natural hazards with devastating effects, such as volcanoes, epidemic diseases, the collision of Earth with space asteroids, or what we are currently experiencing from global warming.
But what the authors mean by existential dangers is something entirely different.
It is about the sum total of activities of a human nature, such as those associated with the applications of biotechnology, or the dangers of artificial intelligence, or also nanotechnology and its amazing applications.
In other words, Nick Bostrom considers that existential dangers are those that carry the potential for mass destruction of humanity, or at least can radically hinder the possibility of development and civilizational development.
Such risks will be more likely to occur in the future, given the cultural and cognitive complexity we have reached.
If the human race has so far survived natural hazards such as asteroid collisions, diseases, earthquakes and volcanoes...
Other existential risks are very likely to be more difficult.
Super Artificial Intelligence
One of the dangers that haunt modern humans is the threats associated with the development of artificial intelligence.
This is what Bostrom explores in his book, “Superintelligence, ” where he asserts that artificial intelligence with the ability to self-learn can pose a real threat to human intelligence.
We are talking about an intelligence that can greatly surpass the natural intelligence of man, in all the abilities that it performs, such as remembering, analyzing, calculating, solving problems, and others.
This superiority may be promising and positive in many areas, so that artificial intelligence can overcome human weakness, such as forgetfulness, lack of attention or good incompetence.
But what if this intelligence decides to remove man, and even surpass him altogether?
Such a dangerous possibility is what Bostrom ’ s book focuses on, wondering whether we can control this disturbing intelligence, for in his eyes we will be: “In the face of the effects of the explosion of intelligence, we humans are like little children playing with a bomb! ”
Weakness of contemporary civilization
Another fundamental thesis in Nick Bostrom ’ s line of thought is what he calls the “weak world hypothesis. ”
Suppose, for example, that there is a large jar full of balls, some white, representing all the inventions and knowledge useful to mankind, and some gray, which is the sum total of discoveries that, despite their benefits, have had some negative effects.
Here Nick Bostrom assumes that there is a deadly black ball that we have not yet extracted.
It is a technological invention that could lead to the final collapse of human civilization.
And in the author ’ s view we have not yet reached such a ball, and that is not because of our wisdom, from his point of view, but only because of luck and chance, which means that we may eventually face this ominous ball at the bottom of the jar.
The hypothesis of a weak world, then, means that we live close to the danger, which invariably haunts us with the possibility of a party reaching such a deadly invention!
In the author ’ s view, this always means that oversight of such research must be strengthened, and a kind of global prevention established.
Of course, the black sphere could be nuclear weapons, as could uncontrolled global warming.
In the first case, it may be done by any extremist, or any scientist who is dissatisfied with civilization!
It could also be due to human error in pressing a button or in a runaway experiment.
In the second case, we will all contribute in one way or another to the extraction of this ball.
For example, all motorists who raise the temperature of the Earth are involved, in some way, in global warming.
Improving human capacity
From the weakness of civilization to the weakness of man.
This weakness has been thought through by philosophers under various headings such as the fragility and vulnerability of the human condition, as well as the idea of finality and death.
But thanks to the technological advances we are making today, we can overcome this weakness.
This, however, is what Nick Bostrom puts forward in his joint book with the Roman philosopher Julian Savulescu, published in 2009, entitled “Human Enhancement ”: it is true that the improvement and promotion of man has always been mediated by education and cognitive and moral formation, but in recent years this has become a self-contained discipline supervised by biomedical sciences.
What this means is that biotechnological applications are being harnessed to upgrade human physical abilities.
Medicine no longer intervenes here only to repair natural imbalances, such as in the case of disease, but also to give man abilities that sometimes exceed what is normal.
“Reinforcement of man ”, then, is intended to bring about a smallpox change in human nature, changes that could lead to the birth of a new human species, so to speak.
There is a debate between conservatism, which defends the inviolability of the human body, and transhumanism, which demands that we take advantage of what these vital applications give us.
Boundaries of science
There is no doubt that some uncontrolled techniques can pose serious problems related to the moral, psychological and societal aspects, and may even affect the spiritual and mental aspects of the human being.
Such medical interventions in the human body, as a complex biological system, can be counterproductive.
Should we set limits at which science stops, or should we proceed so unexpectedly, indifferent to such strong fears and anxieties?
Bostrom replies, “When we go in the wrong direction, the last thing we need is progress. ”

That ’ s better than nothing, but the fees are a fraction of what many experts say is fair value.
A recent study by researchers from Columbia University, the University of Houston and Bratel Group, a consulting firm, estimated that if Google gave American publishers 50 percent of the value their news content created, they would spend between $10 billion and $12 billion a year.
In fact, the New York Times — one of the biggest news publishers — only gets $100 million over three years.
An asymmetrical relationship.
“Now, artificial intelligence is poised to make that asymmetric relationship look good.
When you ask a question on a chatbot like OpenAI ’ s ChatGPT or Google ’ s Bard, you ’ re not sent to the creator ’ s website.
You are given the answer directly.
Users stay in the walled garden of any big tech company that owns an AI platform. ”
The fact that AI has been trained on the same copyrighted content it aims to bypass makes matters worse.
It ’ s not just traditional content creators who are worried.
Brands are now creating virtual social media influencers using AI, so they don ’ t have to pay $1,000 or so for every post that some real influencers charge.
The strikes of Hollywood actors and writers last year were also revolving around this context, as more and more creative managerial functions will be carried out by software.
Artificial intelligence may represent the "ultimate" and perhaps inevitable "reversal of the starting point of the World Wide Web, which was about helping users easily find and navigate many of the original web pages that emerged with the spread of the Internet.
It ’ s all about extracting user data and interest and selling it back to us in ways that lead to lower and lower input costs and higher and higher platform margins.
Impact of Artificial Intelligence
Ahmed Banafa, an academic advisor at San Jose State University in California, told Sky News Arabia that the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on content creators is multifaceted, reshaping the landscape of content production, user engagement, and search engine optimization.
As AI technologies continue to evolve, content creators find themselves at the intersection of human creativity and machine intelligence.
Accelerated production processes:
The impact of AI on content production is profound, especially in terms of accelerating processes.
Content creation often involves labor-intensive tasks, such as research, data analysis, and drafting.
AI-powered tools can streamline these processes, automate routine tasks, and allow content creators to focus on the most strategic and creative aspects.
Natural language processing algorithms, for example, can help create coherent and context-relevant text.
Creators can take advantage of these tools to automate repetitive writing tasks, save time for reflection and create more accurate content.
Improved user experience:
Understanding user behavior is central to creating content that resonates.
Artificial intelligence empowers content creators with the ability to analyze large sets of data, revealing insights about user preferences, engagement patterns, and content consumption habits.
By harnessing this information, content creators can tailor their content to meet the specific needs and expectations of their audience.
Personalization becomes a key element in enhancing the user experience.
AI algorithms can dynamically recommend content based on individual preferences, resulting in increased user satisfaction and long-term engagement.
This personalized approach not only preserves existing audiences, but also attracts new audiences by delivering relevant and compelling content.
Enhanced Search Engine Optimization (SEO) Strategies:
Search engine optimization also remains the cornerstone of content visibility.
Artificial intelligence plays a crucial role in optimizing content for search engines.
Machine learning algorithms can analyze search trends, identify high-value keywords, and recommend content edits to improve search rankings.
Moreover, AI-based tools can assess the competitiveness of keywords, helping content creators target niche topics that are less competitive but garner significant audience attention.
This strategic approach enhances the discoverability of content, ensuring that it reaches the target audience through organic research.
Automatically create content:
The ability of AI to automatically create content is a quantum leap in the content creation landscape, and while it raises concerns about job displacement, it also provides opportunities for content creators to creatively leverage these capabilities.
Automated content creation tools powered by artificial intelligence can also help create drafts, generate ideas, and even produce basic designs.
Creators can use these created outputs as a foundation, and add their unique insights, creativity, and human touch to improve and elevate the final outputs.
It identifies a range of "resistance" or "recruitment" strategies for AI, as follows:
Developing Planning and Creativity Skills: Content creators must constantly hone their planning and creative skills to stay ahead of AI capabilities.
While AI can help with certain tasks, strategic thinking and imaginative aspects of content creation remain distinctly human.
Interactive learning with technology: The adoption of AI involves a continuous learning process.
Content creators should actively interact with AI technologies, attend workshops, and explore new tools to understand their functions and effectively integrate them into their workflow.
Continuous improvement in content quality: Quality content remains critical.
Content creators should leverage AI analytics to gain insight into audience preferences, and design content to meet evolving expectations.
This iterative process ensures that the quality of the content remains high and aligned with the interests of the audience.
Strategic use of artificial intelligence as an analytical tool: Artificial intelligence is a powerful analytical tool.
Content creators can harness their abilities to analyze audience data, identify emerging trends, and make data-informed decisions.
This strategic approach ensures that the content remains relevant and resonates with the target audience.
Innovation in form and content: Innovation becomes a competitive advantage.
Content creators must experiment with diverse formats, storytelling techniques, and multimedia elements to attract audiences.
AI can be collaborative in experimentation, providing insights on emerging content trends.
Future considerations and ethical dimensions
As the synergy between AI and content creation evolves, ethical considerations come to the fore, as content makers must address questions about transparency, accountability and responsible use of AI.
Ethical AI practices include ensuring fairness, avoiding bias, and communicating transparently when AI is involved in content creation.
In addition, the evolving role of AI requires ongoing dialogue on copyright, property and attribution, as AI tools contribute significantly to the content creation process, defining the boundaries of intellectual property and recognizing the collaborative nature of human AI content creation becomes critical.
Banafe says the relationship between AI and content creators is dynamic, posing challenges and opportunities.
Artificial intelligence accelerates processes, enhances user experiences, optimizes search engine optimization strategies, and automates the content creation process.
Content makers, in turn, need to strike a balance between embracing AI capabilities and preserving the unique qualities of human creativity.
Strategic adaptation, continuous learning and ethical considerations are critical as content creators navigate this evolving landscape.
The future of the content industry lies in the harmonious collaboration between human ingenuity and artificial intelligence, opening up new possibilities and forming a dynamic and engaging digital ecosystem.

The dangers of consuming dietary supplements in a large amount.
Dr. Abdulrahman Shams, a nutritionist, said that consuming supplements in large quantities can pose health risks.
Risks of consuming dietary supplements in a large amount
Shams explained through special statements to Echo El Balad, some of the risks that can result from consuming dietary supplements in excess quantities:
Vitamin and mineral toxicity: Some vitamins and minerals if taken in excess may be toxic to the body.
For example, consuming large amounts of vitamin A can lead to vitamin A poisoning and cause symptoms such as headache, dizziness, nausea and vomiting.
Drug interactions: Some supplements may interact with other medications taken, consuming excessive amounts of some supplements with medications may lead to unwanted interactions and side effects.
Increased risk of diseases: In some cases, consuming supplements in large quantities may increase the risk of certain diseases.
For example, consuming excessive amounts of antioxidants such as vitamin E and vitamin C may increase the risk of cardiovascular disease.
Negative effects on the digestive system: Some supplements in large quantities can irritate the digestive system and cause symptoms such as nausea, diarrhea, and bloating.
Fungal poisoning: Some supplements that contain natural ingredients such as mushrooms can be toxic if consumed in excess quantities or if unsafe types of mushrooms are used.
It is crucial that you follow the guidelines and recommended dosages for dietary supplement use and consult with a dietitian or doctor if you intend to take large amounts of them, dietary supplements should be used as a supplement to a healthy diet and not a substitute for it, and you should choose supplements from reliable and approved sources.

New rules come into effect for visiting Hagia Sophia mosque in Turkey
DBA
Published on: Tuesday 16 January 2024 - 1: 54 PM | Last updated on Tuesday 16 January 2024 - 1: 54 PM
The project for the Hagia Sophia mosque was closest to the heart of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan – but it was also the project that drew international criticism.
In the summer of 2020, Erdogan restored Hagia Sophia to be a mosque after it was originally a church, converted into an Ottoman mosque, converted into a museum.
At the time, Erdogan assured citizens that entry fees would be abolished, adding that the cultural edifice would remain open to everyone – Muslims or non-Muslims alike.
There will be another major change from January 15, with access to the Hagia Sophia restricted and visitors will have to pay fees again.
Turkish Tourism Minister Mehmet Nuri Arsoy hopes this will improve coexistence between religious and tourist visitors.
Arsoy said recently that tourist visitors are making noise and disrupting calm and prayer.
Until recently, visitors and worshippers were allowed to enter the interior of Hagia Sophia together, with barriers and signs keeping a certain distance between them.
However, from now on, worshippers and tourists will be introduced through different entrances.
Although worshippers can use the same entrances as before, tourists will be guided through an upstairs hallway.
According to Arsoy, tour guides will not be allowed to accompany visitors through the corridors, and earphones will be used instead.
“Our priority there is prayer, ” Arsoy said, noting that the building is a world cultural heritage site and should therefore remain open to all visitors around the world.
Zuleiha Duman, 29, who returned to Istanbul from Germany to see Hagia Sophia after it was converted into a mosque, said she found it taking away.
Welcoming the new rules, she said: “As long as the entrance fee isn ’ t too high, I think it ’ s acceptable. ”
“Why shouldn ’ t Turkey and the government take advantage of this place?
These funds can be channeled to preserve more religious places. ”
Hagia Sophia has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of Istanbul ’ s history since 1985.
Built by Emperor Justinian, Hagia Sophia was the largest place of worship in Christianity for nearly a thousand years, it was the main church during the Byzantine Empire, and from the seventh century, the emperor was crowned inside.
After the Ottomans entered Constantinople (now Istanbul) in 1453, the Hagia Sophia was converted into a mosque.
On the orders of the founder of the Turkish Republic Mustafa Kemal Ataturk, the building was converted into a museum in 1934 until the summer of 2020.
Hagia Sophia is as symbolically important to Orthodox Christians around the world as St. Peter ’ s Basilica is to Catholics.
After the building was converted into a mosque, criticism poured in from the Greek Orthodox Church.
The UNESCO Foundation also criticized the decision without consultation.
For Erdogan, turning the place into a mosque was his “childhood dream, ” as he himself said, and pleasing to religious voters.
A few external changes were made at the time, for example, a green carpet was placed above the marble floor.
It seems clear that all these things did not detract from the popularity of this teacher.
According to official statistics, some 13.6 million people visited the Hagia Sophia landmark in 2022, not all of them from Europe.
The number of visitors from Indonesia in particular has risen, Hagia Sophia Imam Binyamin Topoglu told Turkey ’ s Anadolu news agency in 2023.
The amount of the fees has not yet been determined.
Tourism Minister Ersoy says the proceeds will be spent on cultural assets, for excavation or preservation of monuments such as the Hagia Sophia.

IMF: Artificial intelligence will affect 40% of jobs worldwide
A-A.
A new study by the International Monetary Fund has warned that artificial intelligence could soon affect 40 percent of jobs worldwide.
Add Announcement
In advanced economies, the impact is expected to be more pronounced, with 60 percent of employees affected.
Effects of Artificial Intelligence
The IMF warns that even when the effects of AI are positive, computer automation is likely to lead to wealth inequality.
High-paying occupations will see wages increase with the use of artificial intelligence, while low-paying roles are at high risk of wage cuts and layoffs.
Some have compared the explosive development of artificial intelligence over the past few years to the industrial revolution for its ability to affect employment.
Unlike the invention of the steam engine, artificial intelligence threatens to replace highly skilled intellectual labor.
Kristalina Georgieva, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund and co-author of the study, said: “We are on the brink of a technological revolution that can spur productivity, boost global growth, and raise incomes worldwide.
However, it can replace jobs and deepen inequality. ”
The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Employment
Previous studies on the impact of AI on employment have focused on the extent to which a job is “exposed ” to AI.
The new study divides jobs into three categories:
Jobs that are not exposed to artificial intelligence
Jobs that are exposed to artificial intelligence but will be helped
Jobs that are vulnerable and will not be helped by artificial intelligence.
For example, clerical workers such as secretaries and staff are very likely to be replaced by AI because most of their work can be done by machines.
Judges will also be heavily exposed to AI, because much of the text analysis involved in their work can be automated.
AI is likely to make judges more productive rather than replace them.
Accountants, consultants, psychologists
The study found that accountants, consultants and psychologists were among the professions most likely to give up in favor of artificial intelligence.
Athletes, roof builders, and steel installers are the least at risk from artificial intelligence.
According to the IMF, these differences are likely to lead to increased wealth inequality.
“We may see a polarization between income groups, with workers who can harness AI seeing an increase in their productivity and wages — and those who can ’ t afford to be left behind, ” Georgieva said.
The study warned that occupations with high exposure are likely to experience lower wages and job losses.
Jobs with high exposure and integration will see their wages increase as they become more productive with AI.
Increasing the wage gap
Because jobs that make the most of AI are already higher-paying, this is likely to increase the pay gap between the best and the worst in society.
“In most scenarios, AI is likely to exacerbate overall inequality, a worrying trend that policymakers must proactively address to prevent technology from further fuelling social tensions. ”
The study also found that women and those with a college education will be positively affected by artificial intelligence.
This will have repercussions on the international arena, where the economies most capable of harnessing artificial intelligence will see rapid growth, while the poor countries will decline.
The report found that only 26 percent of jobs in low-income countries are vulnerable to AI because of the high proportion of people working in manual labor and agriculture.
In India, for example, more than two-thirds of jobs will not be affected by artificial intelligence.
While this means that residents are unlikely to lose their jobs due to computer automation, it also means that the effects of automation on boosting the economy are likely to be limited.
Singapore and the United States in the lead
In the IMF ’ s ranking of a country ’ s readiness for AI – a measure of how well a country ’ s policies set it up to make the most of AI – Singapore and the United States lead.
Britain is in fifth place, slightly behind Japan and Germany, while India and other emerging economies lag behind.
“It is critical that countries establish comprehensive social safety nets and provide retraining programs for vulnerable workers.
By doing so, we can make the shift to AI more inclusive, protect livelihoods and reduce inequality. ”

The British Standards Authority has published an international standard, the first of its kind, on how to safely manage artificial intelligence, according to a report by the German news agency DPA.

Where is the water crisis in Morocco?
Ismael Azzam
January 19, 2024
Weak rainfall and drained underground reservoirs.
The water situation in Morocco has reached a critical level, and the state is announcing urgent strategies to meet the challenge.
Does it work?
https: / / p.dw.com / p / 4bNCW
The water crisis in Morocco has been part of the public debate for years, since it was confirmed that the kingdom is suffering from a major problem that threatens agriculture and even drinking water.
The successive years of drought, the depletion of underground reservoirs in several regions, and the lack of significant progress in alternative water projects are the main pillars of a crisis that Moroccans fear will turn for the worse.
The Kingdom recorded a deficit in rainfall during the current agricultural season by 70% compared to the average, while the percentage of filling dams decreased to 23.2% compared to 31.5%, while the per capita share of water resources decreased from "2560 cubic meters annually in 1960 to 620 cubic meters in 2020," according to data of the Ministry of Equipment and Water.
But even last season, conditions were catastrophic, with the kingdom experiencing a drought unprecedented in four decades.
Morocco relies heavily on dams, a strategy for coping with dry seasons, but their succession has significantly reduced the filling rate.
“The water situation in Morocco is very serious and there is no exaggeration in this description, the water scarcity is obvious, ” Jawad al-Kharraz, Executive Director of the Regional Center for Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency (RCREEE), told DW Arabia, stressing that the weak filling of dams and the continuation of drought are raising alarm, especially with regard to water cuts to the population, as well as the situation of Moroccan farmers.
In some parts of Morocco, there are interruptions in the supply of water to the population, an option that Moroccan media reports indicate is deliberate in order to push the population to more rationalize water, especially in areas where there is a great pressure on water resources.
Areas in central and southern Morocco suffer greatly from the drinking water crisis, including Agadir al-Kabir, which was affected by a significant decline in the water of dams amid a complete scarcity of rainfall, as well as the region of Daraa Tafilalt, which several reports warned that it is threatened by a crisis of thirst.
Many experts point out that the crisis is caused by climatic fluctuations, especially high temperature, as some areas witness a hot climate throughout the year, successive years of drought, as well as population growth, and the lack of rational use, especially in the field of irrigation.
Disorders contributed to the situation.
While surface water has declined due to drought, groundwater is subject to significant depletion as a result of its use to provide drinking water, or for intensive agricultural activity, especially some crops that drain water.
Official reports indicate that 88 percent of water in the kingdom is used for watering.
Jawad El Kharraz highlights that Morocco has important laws and strategic plans in water governance, but the problem is also that they are not implemented, giving the example of “licensing large farmers who have exploited vast lands and overused groundwater ”, as well as supporting the application of the law on the“ water mattress contract ” which obliges farmers to manage groundwater reservoirs.
The Economic, Social and Environmental Council (ECOSOC), an advisory body, has warned in a publication that water is being overconsumed and wasted despite its scarcity in Morocco.
He pointed out that there is a weakness in the effectiveness of control mechanisms, and the resort of some cities to use drinking water to water green spaces and tourism projects, despite the suffering of residents in other areas of thirst, pointing also to the continuation of crops that consume water abundantly.
A working session to study the crisis
The fact that King Mohammed VI chaired a working session on the water crisis earlier this week underscores the extent of the challenge the kingdom is facing.
One of the objectives of the meeting was to put forward the emergency plan to deliver water to areas threatened by the risk of water scarcity.
The measures included "filling existing dams, wells and desalination plants", "restricting the use of irrigation water and reducing the flow of distribution whenever the situation requires it," as well as speeding up strategic workshops such as dams and projects linking water basins, and the use of treated wastewater, according to a Royal Court statement.
Morocco announced several measures, within the framework of a program from 2020 to 2027, to ensure access to drinking water and irrigation to a number of areas, such as the Rabat-Salé axis, which benefited from the transfer of surplus water from the Sebou River basin to the Bouregreg River basin, as well as the start of the operation of desalination plants in the cities of Agadir and Safi.
Jawad al-Kharaz, who is also a board member of the European Desalination Association, believes that all these measures are very important and needed, but the need for greater measures is urgent, pointing out that the model of exporting agricultural products that consume water in abundance, such as avocados, red melons and tomatoes, which transport “virtual water ” abroad, which is economically profitable in the short term for companies, but destructive for the environment.
The expert also calls for investment, whether public or private, in the provision of non-conventional water, whether wastewater, or desalination, which is no longer as expensive as it used to be, especially with the trend to make it sustainable using renewable energies.
It is also proposed to seek global funding for new projects, enact new legislation to deter waste and reduce the environmental impact of desalination, and support scientific research in universities on the sustainability of agriculture and water.

That's why, now with the details.
CAIRO (Reuters) - Britain ’ s Supreme Court says artificial intelligence cannot be mentioned in a patent as the inventor of a new idea or product, in a ruling that raises existential questions about our relationship with machines that are becoming smarter than ever.
Lord Kitchin, issuing the ruling, said: "We conclude that the 'inventor' must be a natural person, only man can invent an invention."
The case was first heard in 2018 by Imagination Engines founder Stephen Thaler, who sought patents to name his artificial intelligence device DABUS as the inventor.
Thaler has applied to various courts to list DABUS as the inventor of a food container that robots can easily hold, and a flashing warning light designed to attract attention during emergencies.
Both the European Patent Office (EPO) and the UK Intellectual Property Office (UKIPO) rejected the application, on the grounds that the inventor identified in the application must be a human – not a machine, and the UK Supreme Court upheld the decision, the first time a case of this kind has been heard in the highest court of any country.
When asked how he felt about judgment, Thaler said, “DABUS, a conscious artificial being, actually invented new inventions. ”
“Unfortunately, no one wanted to commit to delving deeper into the technology itself and instead, belief and prejudice prevailed at the community level, ” TheNextWeb reported.
Thaler is part of the Artificial Inventor Project, a team of researchers and lawyers who seek intellectual property rights for outputs generated by artificial intelligence in the absence of a traditional human inventor or author.
They argue that granting patent rights to AI systems would encourage companies to invest in the development of AI systems, as they would be more confident in their ability to patent the results.
While authorities in the United States, Europe and the United Kingdom have barely welcomed the idea, Dalos has surprisingly secured patent rights in both South Africa and Australia, provoking significant backlash.
According to some experts, issuing patent rights to machines may not be as ridiculous as some portray them.
Johann Lianyag, a partner at law firm Linklaters, told Bloomberg that given how quickly AI capabilities are expanding, the problem “may need to be addressed again in the future. ”
“If the UK government is serious about its aspiration to establish itself as an AI superpower, legislative intervention may be necessary to allow patent eligibility for inventions created independently by AI systems, ” she said.

Amr Sobhi writes: Women and sustainable development of the aviation industry
The aviation and aerospace industry is among the most important and innovative fields in the world, however, it is also one of the most male-dominated fields, with women constituting only a small percentage of professional roles in this sector.
This lack of diversity is a big problem, as women are not usually given the same opportunities as men to succeed in the industry.
Given this issue, industry leaders must take steps to combat gender inequality in aerospace and aviation to promote inclusiveness and equal opportunities for women.
While this year ’ s International Women ’ s Day theme of embracing equality has made industry leaders around the world reassess their engagement and retention strategies for the day, it ’ s important to ensure that your organization has a culture of inclusion and belonging throughout the year.
Highlight the importance of an inclusive workplace culture, and in research statistics on workers in the work environment by international organizations indicate that employees will leave their job if they feel they do not belong to their workplace, 72% of them consider that employer values and purpose are very important to understand the gender difference in work in general and performance in particular.
How big is the problem?
As women ’ s rights have made great strides in recent decades, industry leaders sometimes unconsciously assume that women are equally represented in the workplace (in numbers only) or, at least, similar to the number of male employees.
However, the problem of gender inequality and imbalances in practice for women in professional roles in the aviation and aerospace industry is one of the biggest challenges facing the aviation workforce.
Very few women hold senior leadership positions in the aviation and aerospace industry, for example, less than 6% of the UK ’ s 16,000 pilots are women.
In addition, the International Federation of Airline Pilots (IFALPA) reported in January 2020 that out of 185,143 airline pilots in the world, only 9,746 were women (5.26%), and 2,630 were pilots (1.42%).
Unfortunately, this percentage has decreased since January 2020 due to the negative impact of the redundancy policies caused by COVID-19.
According to the International Federation of Aviation Pilots (IFALPA) in January 2020 there were 185,143 aviation pilots in the world, of which 9,746 were women (5.26%) and 2630 were pilots (1.42%) (IFALPA 2021).
This percentage has since declined as aircraft have been negatively affected by redundancy policies due to COVID-19, resulting in a decline in U.S. aircraft numbers from 5.1% to 4.1%.
There may also be talk about the extent to which women air traffic controllers employ air traffic service providers around the world, as the number of female air traffic controllers is lower than that of male air traffic controllers.
Empowering women in aviation and space
The aviation and aerospace industry has traditionally been male-dominated, but there is hope that this will change in the coming years.
Industry leaders are increasingly seeking employment services to find talented women and encourage them to join the industry.
Women make invaluable contributions to the aerospace industry, bringing unique skills and perspectives that can help the industry grow and develop.
Therefore, strategic decision makers must take steps to ensure the promotion and empowerment of women in this sector.
So, the question becomes: How can you empower women in this area?
1. Effectively promote gender diversity and diversity in the workplace.
The aerospace industry is short and focused skills, which means employers must look for innovative ways to make women work.
Employers sometimes stumble when trying to develop strategies to effectively increase gender diversity, and it is not uncommon for an employer to struggle to uncover where they are wrong.
Here are some key pointers on how employers can successfully promote diversity — specifically, gender diversity — in the workplace to foster an equal environment.
2. Stay flexible
One way to encourage diversity in your workplace is to provide flexible working arrangements, which allow employees to work more flexibly and manage their own time.
A report on gender equality in the workplace for 2022 by a European study centre found that 60% of women in the survey cited work-life balance as having a significant impact on their careers.
Working women often have other commitments in life, from family to hobbies to personal projects, and a flexible work schedule and employer understanding is a tremendous addition to many women seeking employment in the industry.
3. Pledges to diversity
Employers in the sector must also commit to increasing diversity and inclusion in the workplace.
Prioritizing diversity and promoting an inclusive environment for women is essential to show potential employees that your organization values diversity and pushes for equal opportunities for women.
Diversity pledges can be made by identifying and signing documents that are committed to diversity and by implementing programs and initiatives that promote diversity, such as orientation programs, diversity training, and unconscious bias awareness training.
4. Change initiatives
Employers in the sector must address gender-based wage disparities and other problems that make it difficult for women to advance in the industry.
One of the best ways you can achieve this goal is through inclusive change initiatives, which can be done by committing yourself to changes such as pay transparency and job rotation based on gender.
In addition, employers must put in place policies to ensure that women are given fair and equal opportunities for career advancement.
5. Blind CV Applications
Finally, CV applications effectively ensure that candidates are evaluated solely on the basis of their skills and experience rather than gender or any other irrelevant criteria.
This process can help reduce the risk of unconscious bias, a common issue in the aviation and aerospace industry.
Blind CV applications and digital automation through the use of innovative online applications can also help ensure that hiring decisions are fair and objective.
By removing any personal information, such as name and gender, from the application, the job application can only focus on the candidate ’ s skills and experience to ensure that the most suitable candidate is selected for aviation jobs, regardless of gender.
5. Creating a guiding human development plan
Creating a mentoring scheme is a great way to help women survive and advance their careers in the aviation and aerospace industry.
INNOVATION STEERING PLATFORM is a mentoring platform designed for women by women working in the aerospace industry.
The mentoring scheme provides a practical way to promote gender equality for individuals, organisations and the entire sector.
With innovative solutions, your organization can focus more on attracting and retaining female employees in the best way.
How do organizations support women in aviation and aerospace?
Leaders of international organizations and developed governments are keen to support employers in addressing this gender imbalance and increasing the number of women in the aviation and aerospace industry.
It does this by acquiring talented female candidates to support the sector, and by helping to create attractive and diverse workplace environments.
In addition, organizations and governments are prioritizing unique ways in which employers can attract more women into the workplace and create a more diverse and inclusive environment.
Provide tailor-made employment solutions to attract more women to aviation and aerospace roles.

Dr. Mohamed Abdel Razek, head of the Central Department of Tourism and Resorts in Alexandria, said that the climate changes caused the melting of snow as a result of thermal emissions, which caused the rise of sea waves in the seas and oceans to about one meter and two centimeters, which increased the speed of sea currents and the occurrence of shorelines.
On Saturday, during the meeting of the National Environment Day at the National Museum of Alexandria, Abdel Razek said that to reduce these effects by scientific methods, submersible barriers of 25-30 centimeters should be placed inside the sea to reduce the strength and height of the waves and break their intensity, as well as by feeding the beaches with sand.
He pointed out that marine pollution negatively affected 45% of marine mammals and 21% of seabirds, and caused the extinction of some marine organisms, including sea turtles, which were feeding on jellyfish, and thus resulted in the spread of jellyfish on the beach.
He stressed that environmental pollution of sea water is all that harms marine life, explaining the types of pollution, including plastic pollution that occurs as a result of the presence of plastic bags and bottles, pointing out that once it drifts to the sea, fish feed on it, which is an important food source for humans.
He continued, there is also marine light pollution and the occurrence of artificial light and search and exploration, which affected fish living in the dark, and caused their migration, as well as the audio pollution that occurs as a result of boat engines and submarines, which affected whales living on sound waves.
He added that pollution can be reduced through awareness campaigns to change the behavior of beachgoers, separating rain pipes from sewage pipes, not draining the latter into the sea, not leaking oil materials transported through ships, and reducing the dumping of hazardous materials and ship waste.

Millie is facing the minefield of the economy, politics and society of Argentina
Argentina ’ s president-elect Javier Milley ’ s sweeping reform package overcame the first parliamentary hurdle, winning public approval on the third day of debate in the House of Representatives, while the initiative, which included economic, social and political areas, sparked strong protests from the opposition and the Argentine street.
Argentina has been embroiled in a long-running conflict with severe economic crises that have led its citizens to turn their attention to Mili, who won a resounding victory in last October ’ s election.
As a result of public discontent over decades of economic instability, with annual inflation surpassing the 200 percent threshold and poverty levels rising to 40 percent, Milley embarked on a “bold path to redefining Argentina ’ s future. ”
Massive opposition.
Tens of thousands took to the streets in defiance of Milley ’ s austerity measures, which included cuts to the balance sheet.
The demonstrations disrupted parliamentary debates, leading to confrontations between law enforcement forces and protesters.
Police fired rubber bullets and tear gas, and sprayed protesters with water cannons, with reports of injuries and arrests among protesters.
The leftist opposition withdrew from parliament, denouncing what it saw as a severe police crackdown on protesters.
Opposition MP Mariano del Canio told the AP that "we can't work this way", stressing that protesters should be heard before they return to the hearing after a period of suspension.
Parliamentary manoeuvres
In a strategic move to bolster his program, Milley secured IMF approval to disburse nearly $4.7 billion to Argentina.
The package of reforms, dubbed Omnibus, spans across different sectors, from electoral and cultural reforms to privatization, penal code amendments, and changes to the status of football clubs.
The House of Representatives, by 144 votes to 109, granted general approval, paving the way for the next phase of negotiations in the Senate.
The bill ’ s 664 clauses, which sum up the complex fabric of Melli ’ s reforms, will be subject to close scrutiny and possible amendments.
Although the House of Representatives has generally approved Melli ’ s reform bill, negotiations are on the horizon.
The complex details of the bill, which include economic, administrative, criminal and environmental areas, will be subject to strict scrutiny, according to a pro-plan parliamentary description.
Lawmakers, some of whom have expressed reservations about specific articles on privatizing state companies and delegating legislative powers to the president, are due to participate in detailed discussions.
Milley ’ s challenge is not just to overcome ideological differences, but to build consensus within a fragmented political landscape.
The upcoming recess will provide a break before crucial negotiations resume, marking a pivotal stage in Milley ’ s ambitious agenda for his program.
Millie's presidency is at a crossroads.
Milley ’ s presidency, marked by libertarian principles and capitalist ideals, faces the complex challenge of balancing economic liberalization with societal expectations.
Austerity measures and privatization plans were not without opposition, leading to protests and even a general strike.
The president ’ s swift measures, including a 50 percent devaluation of the peso, cuts in subsidies, and deep cuts in ministries, reflect his confrontational approach to tackling the government ’ s budget deficit and fighting inflation.
However, these actions have aroused resentment, as protesters have questioned the potential impact on the most vulnerable groups in society.
The course of Melli's reforms will shape the country's economic and social landscape.
Experts say that the fine line between government initiatives, parliamentary negotiations and street reactions highlights the multifaceted nature of Argentina ’ s current socio-political reality.
As Argentina grapples with historic economic challenges, observers expect Milley ’ s presidency to be a decisive chapter, with the split between economic liberalization and social welfare taking center stage with every decision that resonates in the corridors of power and crowded streets.

Consuming spices in large quantities leads to a sudden rise in blood pressure, reduces blood clotting and increases the risk of heavy bleeding.
Ginger also contains a small amount of oxalate – oxalic acid salts.
They are harmful to people with bowel and kidney diseases, especially those with urolithiasis with an increased risk of oxalate stones.

6 Herbs That May Increase Heart Disease Risk
Millions of people around the world are taking herbal remedies for multiple reasons, including high cholesterol levels and depression, and despite popular belief that they are safe, some of these products may lead to dangerous interactions in people taking prescription drugs to treat cardiovascular problems.
Add Announcement
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has indicated that dietary supplements are not subject to the same levels of control as drugs, meaning that the efficacy of standard ingredients and doses has not yet been proven, increasing the risk of drug interactions.
According to the National Center for Integrative and Complementary Health, there are several herbal supplements that should be avoided for those taking specific medications, highlighting the need for caution when using herbal remedies in conjunction with medical medications.
Among the herbs that you should stay away from or reduce as much as possible in case you suffer from heart disease we find:
Risk of heart disease..
Green Tea
Green tea, extracted from the leaves of Camellia sinensis, is widely consumed around the world in various forms such as beverages, capsules and extracts, for its various health benefits; for its ability to help lose weight, enhance mental alertness, reduce cholesterol levels in the blood, as well as its potential role in preventing cancer.
However, consuming green tea may carry some risks, especially for people taking certain medications.
Studies, including those published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology, show that green tea may negatively affect the effectiveness of certain drugs because of its vitamin K content, which is known to reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulant drugs such as warfarin.
In addition, the caffeine found in green tea can interfere with beta inhibitors, drugs commonly used to treat high blood pressure and heart rhythm disorders.
Care should also be taken when taking green tea in conjunction with adosine, which is used to treat irregular heart rhythm disorders, because of the potential for interaction between the two.
It is essential for people taking any of these medications or suffering from certain health conditions to consult their health care providers before including green tea in their diet or treatment, to ensure that any adverse drug interactions are avoided and their health and safety are maintained.
Consumption of garlic
According to the American site "health", garlic is part of the onion family, sold in the markets in the form of oil, extract or grain, in addition to its natural form.
According to the National Center for Integrative and Complementary Health (NCCIH), garlic is known as a treatment that contributes to lowering levels of total cholesterol and LDL cholesterol, as well as blood pressure.
Healthy individuals, as well as those with high levels of LDL cholesterol and triglycerides, may benefit from eating garlic to improve heart health.
However, patients using anticoagulant or antiplatelet drugs should stay away from taking "tetragonal G", which includes garlic, ginkgo biloba, grape seeds, and green tea.
People with low blood pressure are also advised not to use garlic because of its ability to lower blood pressure.
Garlic ’ s anticoagulant properties may increase the likelihood of bleeding, especially in people taking aspirin and warfarin, a drug used to reduce blood clotting and often prescribed to patients with heart rhythm problems, heart attacks or heart valve swaps.
These recommendations emphasize the utmost importance of caution when using garlic as a dietary supplement, especially for people taking certain medications, to prevent the risks of drug interactions.
Ginger and Heart Disease
Throughout the ages, ginger has been used in traditional medicine to treat many health problems, especially those related to the digestive system, such as nausea, diarrhea, and stomach pain.
Not only has it been used to relieve joint and muscle pain, making it an important ingredient in a wide range of medical treatments and supplements.
However, scientific research shows increasing interest in the effect of ginger on the clotting process, especially for people taking drugs such as warfarin, an anticoagulant, or aspirin, which is used to prevent the formation of blood clots.
Studies show that ginger may increase the risk of bleeding through its effect on blood clotting, which requires additional studies to understand this effect more deeply.
Given these considerations, people who take ginger as a supplement, especially if they are also using warfarin or aspirin, are strongly advised to consult with their health care providers before continuing to use it.
This precautionary approach aims to avoid the potential risks of drug interactions that may lead to an increased risk of bleeding, and to ensure that ginger is used in a safe and effective manner, in line with an individual ’ s overall health condition.
Licorice Juice
Licorice root, which is extracted from the licorice plant and usually taken as a dried extract in the form of capsules, has multiple medical uses including the treatment of peptic ulcers, various stomach problems, bronchitis, throat infections, and viral infections.
Licorice is known for its various health benefits, but some groups should exercise caution when using it.
According to the National Center for Integrative and Complementary Health (NCCIH), the potential effects of licorice on the body ’ s potassium levels and blood pressure are a concern, especially for people with high blood pressure or who have heart or kidney problems.
These effects can exacerbate or complicate their health problems.
In addition, licorice root is likely to affect the effectiveness and safety of certain medications, such as ACE inhibitors, drugs used to lower blood pressure, and diuretics used to regulate blood pressure.
Consult with your doctor or health care provider before starting licorice root supplements, especially for people taking these types of medications, to avoid adverse drug interactions and ensure safe and effective use.
Herbs...
Aloe Vera and its supplements
Aloe vera is known to be used as an ointment or lotion. Aloe vera (aloe vera) is also used orally to treat serious health conditions such as arthritis, epilepsy, diabetes, and asthma.
However, aloe vera can cause low potassium levels in the blood, which can lead to heart rhythm problems.
Low potassium levels may also lead to complications for heart patients taking digoxin to treat heart rhythm disorders or congestive heart failure.
Furthermore, alovera "has the potential to increase bleeding if anti-platelet analgesics such as aspirin and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are used at the same time," according to a study published in the journal EPMA in January 2019.
This information suggests that caution should be exercised when using aloe vera, especially if you are taking medications that may interact with it and cause additional health risks.

After the majority of medicines ran out of pharmacies, Palestinians in the Gaza Strip resorted to alternatives to treat some of their diseases, such as herbs.
Herbs, or so-called medicine or alternative treatment, have become popular among the population, many of whom are unable to get treatment from pharmacies and hospitals, either because they are shut down and out of service due to Israeli bombing or because many medicines are directed to treat war wounded.
Semi-empty pharmacies
Mohammed al-Sawyer, who lives with his family in the southern Gaza Strip town of Rafah after being displaced from Gaza City, says he began searching for a mixture of herbs to treat intestinal spasms and constipation, which he began to suffer from more than a month ago, after failing to get treatment in pharmacies.
Al-Sawyer told Sky News Arabia: "I was taking a treatment for more than 5 years for constipation, but I did not find it after I searched for it in all the pharmacies of the city," pointing out that he found an alternative treatment in a pharmacy, but does not have any effectiveness in the face of what he suffers.
As for the treatment in the hospital, Sawyer said: "I cannot go to hospitals that are full of patients and wounded around the clock, and in light of the continued Israeli shelling on the city of Rafah, so I did not find an alternative except some herbal remedies."
In turn, pharmacist Khaled Odeh told Sky News Arabia that the majority of pharmacies in Rafah have become empty of the most basic types of medicines, including painkillers and antibiotics, due to the population density in the city, which includes about 1.4 million Palestinians.
According to Odeh, most pharmacies only open their doors to sell some health items to women and children if available, and some cosmetics, of which quantities are still present in the sector.
Growing interest in herbs.
As a specialist in the field, Dr. Nasser Hassanein, an Indian herbal expert and director of the Rafah Herbal Medicine Center, confirms that there is an increasing demand in the Gaza Strip for alternative medicine or herbal treatment, and this demand has become more noticeable during the ongoing war on the Strip.
Hassanein added to Sky News Arabia that "he found a need for his center more with the continuation of the war, which prompted him to activate communication electronically through groups on the application of WhatsApp, to answer as much as possible of the inquiries of those in need of treatment without receiving any payment."
Electronic communication also helped the Palestinian herbalist to increase his expertise by expanding his contacts with specialists in the same field.
Hassanein said: “I have collaborated with experienced herbalists in Yemen, Iraq and Jordan who volunteered for free to answer queries about some of the most common diseases and symptoms among Palestinians in the Gaza Strip. ”
Among these diseases, which have been particularly linked to the war, Hassanein explains, are those related to the digestive system, and caused by the types of canned food that increased dependence, because of its preservatives, after the traditional cooking dishes fresh consisting of meat, fish, fruits and vegetables became scarce amid displacement or high price.
Hundreds of thousands of Palestinians have been displaced from cities in the northern and central Gaza Strip under Israeli shelling of homes there, which has continued since the outbreak of the war on October 7.
Doctors are trying to search for recipes of available herbs that are easy to obtain, Hassanein said, pointing out that “types of herbs are no longer available in Rafah because they were cultivated on agricultural land in the center and east of the Strip, and it is now difficult for farmers to reach them because of their proximity to the border and the presence of Israeli army vehicles that fire on farmers constantly. ”
Hassanein continued: "We are forced to give alternative herbs from the available, even if they are less efficient, and we rely on what we know is available to the perfumers in the city."
According to the pharmacist Odeh, "herbal treatment or alternative medicine needs to be monitored by competent authorities, especially since this type of herbs often does not take into account the differences between pathological conditions and the extent of symptoms that can cause them."

An anti-aging and anti-wrinkle herb and a safe alternative to retinol
Retinol is commonly used in skincare formulations and is seen as the ideal ingredient for correcting and treating common skin problems, but it is accompanied by many complications and side reactions, especially for those with sensitive skin, such as skin dryness, inflammation, itching, flaking and redness. It is also prohibited to use it in pregnancy and lactation.
More recently, with the spread of the term "clean beauty", Bakocchiol has gained great popularity in the field of skin care, as a natural and light alternative to the skin, as it has the same properties as retinol, but without any significant side effects to date.
What is bakuchiol?
It is a natural ingredient, extracted from the seeds and leaves of the Babchi plant that grows in India, and is a purple herb commonly used in ancient medical practices such as ancient Indian medicine (Ayurveda) and traditional Chinese medicine for centuries, according to its anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties.
Since 2007, many brands have sought to produce it in the form of serums and creams to combat wrinkles and skin aging, many of which combine Bakocchiol with other plants such as rosehip, Swiss Alpine flowers and seaweed, so it is an ideal choice for women who prefer plant products.
Safe during pregnancy and lactation
Today ’ s website quotes dermatologist Benjamin Barrankin as saying that Bakuchiol stimulates skin cell turnover by getting rid of dead skin cells and getting smooth, radiant and firm skin. It also works to repair signs of aging and reduce fine lines and skin pigmentation. According to Barrankin, Bakuchiol is a safe choice during pregnancy and lactation, as a natural ingredient.
However, Barrankin advises caution when using any new product, he explains, “Bakocchiol can be started 3 nights during the first week, and if you don ’ t feel irritated and itchy after a few weeks, you can use it daily morning and evening on clean skin before moisturizer or any other preparations. ”
Benefits of Bakocchiol
Limited studies show that Bakocchiol has the same benefits as retinol, and Vanessa Thomas, a member of the American Society of Cosmetic Chemists, lists the benefits with regular use as follows:
Uniformity of skin tone: It has antioxidant properties that neutralize free radical damage and protect the skin from contaminants, promoting uniformity of skin tone and reducing hyperpigmentation. Its antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties help rid the skin of faulty bacteria.
• Enhance collagen production: Improves skin elasticity, reduces the appearance of wrinkles and fine lines.
• Fight acne and its effects, and get a fresher skin.
• Suitable for all skin types: whether oily, dry, sensitive or mixed skin, Bakocchiol does not cause skin dryness or irritation.
Bakocchiol or Retinol?
In 2018, a buzz about Bakocchiol erupted after the British Journal of Dermatology published a small study looking at comparing the properties of Bakocchiol and Retinol, conducted over a 12-week period, and concluded that both Bakocchiol and Retinol were instrumental in erasing fine lines and treating hyperpigmentation and photoaging caused by prolonged sun exposure, after retinol results were difficult to obtain from any Another component, the study also indicated that retinol user participants were more likely to have dry, flaky and inflamed skin.
Early studies also show that most skin types tolerate bacochiol better than retinol, making it safer for people with sensitive skin, rosacea or atopic dermatitis, according to a study published in the Journal of Medicines in Dermatology 2020.
Based on early studies, Bakuchiol appears to have the same benefits as retinol, and there are no studies yet that reflect any unwanted side effects, she said, noting that the use of Bakuchiol in ancient medicine is of interest to consumers, although so far it does not have the same evidence and scientific support as retinol, which has been studied for decades in trials involving hundreds of human participants....
According to Li, Pacocheol does not interact with other active ingredients in your skincare routine, and can be combined with other ingredients aimed at improving skin texture and fighting wrinkles and pigmentation such as alpha hydroxy acids and ascorbic acid, unlike retinol, which should not be used with facial exfoliators and benzoyl peroxide.
How to use Bakocchiol?
A report on the Everyday Health website mentions a set of tips before including Bacochole in your daily skincare routine, including:
• Wash and dry your face gently and apply Bakocchiol before moisturizing. If your skin is sensitive or prone to dryness, apply a layer of moisturizer before distributing Bakocchiol.
Start with small amounts on the face and neck and gradually increase them to prevent any possible complications.
It can be used twice daily, day and night, unlike retinol, which loses its effectiveness in daylight.
Apply sunscreen in the morning as a last step to protect the skin, as it stimulates the regeneration of skin cells.
• If more than one product is used at the same time, thicker products can be started with thicker products.

Deal Details
Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly announced in a press conference an investment of about $35 billion to develop Ras al-Hikma, close to Marsa Matrouh, to become a tourist destination, free zone and other investment, residential, commercial and recreational spaces.
Madbouly said his government would allocate about 170 million meters (more than 40,000 acres) for the project, expecting investments of up to $150 billion over the life of the project, without specifying the extent.
Madbouly said that his government signed a contract with Abu Dhabi Holding Company (ADQ) and that an Egyptian joint stock company named Ras al-Hikma will be established between the Egyptian government and the company, for the Egyptian company to implement the project.
Madbouly confirmed that within a week there will be a cash advance for the deal of $10 billion, and that the UAE has waived its deposit with the Central Bank of Egypt of $11 billion in favor of the deal, of which $5 billion will be transferred to the Egyptian pound with the delivery of the first batch to Abu Dhabi Holding Company.
The second installment will be in two months, of which $14 billion in cash will enter Egypt, in addition to the remaining part of the UAE deposit of $6 billion, all of which will be transferred to the benefit of the executing company of the project.
Abu Dhabi Holding Company (ADQ) said on its website that it had acquired the rights to develop the Ras al-Hikma project for $24 billion and that the Egyptian government would retain a 35 percent stake in the Ras al-Hikma project and its revenues, which is expected to start work in early 2025.
The company confirmed that its total investments in Egypt will amount to $35 billion and that the UAE deposit funds of $11 billion will be used to invest in key projects across Egypt to support economic growth.
He predicted that the number of tourists to Egypt would increase by 8 million annually after the completion of the project.
A political project with an economic character
Some argue that a project of this size indicates that the investment agreements are "political agreements of an economic nature", in terms of the time limit of $24 billion to enter the country of two months, although the project will start in early 2025, according to a statement by Abu Dhabi Holding Company (ADQ) on its website.
Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly credited the completion of the deal on these terms to the political leadership of the two countries.
Abu Dhabi Holding Company (ADQ) has been actively investing in Egypt for some time, acquiring a 40.5 percent stake in Icon Group, the hospitality arm of Talaat Mustafa Holding Group (TMG) through a capital increase.
ICON owns a range of historic hotels in Egypt, according to the company ’ s website.
Hisham Talaat Mostafa appeared with the Egyptian prime minister with the president of the United Arab Emirates in Abu Dhabi in early February, what some saw as “preparation for the Ras al-Hikma deal. ”
In April 2022, ADQ acquired stakes in Commercial International Bank (CIB), one of Egypt ’ s largest private banks, Fawry, and Alexandria Container and Cargo Handling.
In addition to Misr Fertilizers Production Company (MOPCO) and Abu Qir Fertilizers and Chemical Industries, two of the country ’ s main industrial companies, Amun Pharmaceuticals Company, one of the largest companies in the manufacture of medicines, was acquired.
Dr. Rashad Abdo, professor of economics at Cairo University, says that some of these acquisitions have not been announced terms, and the value of some of them has not been announced, and does the contract give the right to sell to others?
Even if they are a threat to national security, for example, the historic hotels owned by Icon.
Abdo said that some of these companies, which were acquired from the Emirati company, were generating profits and even dollars to the Egyptian currency market, but these sales scared everyone, according to his description.
Abdo added that people say that there is a group of economists "led the country to what it is now suffering, which forced them to sell the assets of the state, which is deducted from the right of future generations."
Fears of the Cape of Wisdom deal
Some fear investing in Ras al-Hikma has to do with land and claims to sell an entire city, critics say, and the suggestion that recent acquisitions from the UAE are raising concerns about the country ’ s economic future, such as not putting all eggs in one basket, critics say.
Dr. Hisham Ibrahim, a professor of economics at Cairo University, told the BBC that "the company that will implement the project is an Egyptian joint stock company, and the government holds 35 percent of it is Egyptian land located inside the country, and the investment itself is inside the country, so there is no need to worry."
Ibrahim added that the state, when dealing with large projects and real estate in particular, such as the New Alamein and the administrative capital, was heavily exhausted, and criticized: Why does the state do this and exhaust itself with this volume of investment?
But Egypt in the Ras al-Hikma project “changes direction and gives the private sector the opportunity to set up and rotate the project and it contributes in part, ” he said.
Ibrahim adds that the Egyptian companies will be the ones who will do the whole project, whether they are contracting companies, suppliers and workers, and they are “pure Egyptian ”.
Dr. Rashad Abdo said that he is relieved that the Ras al-Hikma project is a partnership and not a sale, it is true that the allocated spaces are very large, according to his description, but in the end the government holds 35 percent and the partnership has the advantage of serving the current and future generations.
Return on the Egyptian Citizen
Dr. Rashad Abdo pointed out that the deal will enter dollars that will increase the foreign reserves in the country, and the dollar will be available to import important production inputs and strategic goods, and meet the needs of importers and goods in customs.
It invalidates the argument that importers say, even temporarily, that they buy dollars on the black market for 70 pounds, which affects prices.
But the calm that may affect the exchange market will reflect on prices.
Dr. Hisham Ibrahim confirms that prices will decline, but not only with this project, but in addition to the agreement with the International Monetary Fund, which guarantees the entry of foreign exchange, prices will calm even slightly.
Ibrahim said that the turmoil in the exchange market, which affects the food, drink, real estate, cars and gold market, all this will calm down relatively with the provision of foreign exchange and the stability of the exchange market to some extent.
Rashad Abdo believes that the Egyptian government should be wise in spending these amounts, according to the economics professor, and take strong measures in the Egyptian market to control prices after the availability of foreign exchange.
Experts believe that the structural problems in the Egyptian economy remain as long as the state does not expand production, which can export surpluses, and not export what is on the table of Egyptians, which ensures foreign exchange income for the stability of the Egyptian market.

Humpback whales are threatened by climate change and food shortages
29 Feb 2024
Although threatened by commercial fishing, the effects of climate change are threatening the existence of humpback whales in the northern Pacific, according to a recently published study.
https: / / p.dw.com / p / 4d1FS
A study published in the Royal Society of Science found that the effects of climate change threaten the existence of humpback whales in the North Pacific, although this mammal has always been threatened by commercial fishing, but has been better off in the past.
Between 2012 and 2021, the number of humpback whales in the North Pacific dropped by 20 percent to 26,600 from 33,000, according to the largest data set of large marine mammals studied by 75 scientists.
The number of a subgroup of whales that spent the winter in Hawaii fell by 34 percent.
With other threats such as ship collisions and noise pollution, their future is no longer assured, scientists have warned, calling for greater consideration of climate change in conservation efforts.
Lead author Ted Chesman, a whale biologist and PhD student at Australia ’ s Southern Cross University, said about 7,000 whales had died of starvation.
CLICK - Can Artificial Intelligence Protect Species?
Changes in the marine ecosystem
Although the fluctuation of species numbers is a natural issue, such a large number decline in long-lived species portends a major disturbance of the oceans.
Between 2014 and 2016, the strongest and longest sea heat wave ever recorded swept the Northeast Pacific, leading to changes in the marine ecosystem and in the availability of prey for large whales.
"Not only have whale prey populations declined," Chesman said, but the populations of puffins, sea lions and seals have declined, adding that "the ocean at high temperatures produces less food" due to the decline or migration of phytoplankton that form the basis of the oceanic food chain.
In 2016, the United States began removing the majority of humpback whale populations from its list of endangered species, similar to the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), which in 2008 downgraded their status from “endangered ” to“ non-threatened. ”
But climate change seems to be changing the status quo.
In 2022, another study showed that rising ocean temperatures had driven humpback whales away from their traditional breeding grounds.

Study: A diet that mimics the effect of fasting can prolong life for years
2020-03-02T16: 26: 48 + 00: 00
Scientists always warn of diets and their impact on human health and age, but in a recent study published by the British Daily Mail, citing the journal Nature Communications revealed that a diet that mimics the effect of fasting without starving the soul can prolong biological life for years.
Researchers found that people who followed a fasting diet (FMD) for 15 days reduced their biological lifespan by more than two and a half years on average.
Tests also showed it reduced the risk of diabetes, heart disease and stroke, based on biomarkers in the blood of those who followed it.
Less than 1000 calories
A fasting simulation diet involves eating less than about 1,000 calories — consisting of low-fat foods, soups, energy drinks, and supplements.
It is said to trick the body into thinking it is fasting, releasing enzymes and other chemicals into the body associated with longevity.
Professor Walter Longo, a biologist from the University of Southern California, Los Angeles, who developed the diet and lead author of the study, said: "This is the first study of its kind to show that a food-based intervention that does not require chronic changes in diet or other lifestyles can make people biologically younger."
The diet used in the study included three five-day cycles on a fasting simulation system.
The first day saw participants eat 1,100 calories, while in the second to fifth days they ate about 720 calories per day.
Their diet during these days also consists of healthy snacks and tea.
Ingredients of the diet
The diet consists of 34% carbohydrates, 10% protein and 56% fat for the first day, then 7% carbohydrates, 9% protein and 44% fat for the other days.
Participants then received their usual diets for 25 days.
Men and women up to 70 years
Both groups include men and women between the ages of 18 and 70.
Three months later, the researchers analyzed blood samples from the participants, showing that participants in the fasting simulation group had lower risk factors for diabetes, including lower insulin resistance and lower blood sugar levels.
Biological age
The chronological age is how long a person lives, while biological age is the age of cells and tissues.
It is an important measure because it shows how susceptible a person is to diseases.
Amazing Benefits
MRI scans also showed a reduction in belly fat and liver fat, which is associated with a lower risk of metabolic syndrome, meaning a lower risk of heart disease, stroke and diabetes.
Fasting simulation cycles also appear to have increased the lymphocyte to spinal cord ratio in participants, an indicator of a more youthful immune system.
The researchers believe that the fasting simulation diet has "regenerative effects on the immune system."
In previous studies in mice, a diet that mimics fasting caused "blood image regeneration."
Autophagy of "bad" cells
The body has what are known as “nutrient sensing ” pathways, which control autophagy, a type of“ housekeeping ” of body cells.
It constantly occurs in the body and removes unwanted by-products of cellular processes.
The more autophagy occurs, the better you feel and the lower your risk of future health problems.
Fasting simulation diet accelerates the process of autophagy, thus eliminating more by-products and "bad" cells in the body that cause disease and aging.
The diet is supposed to mimic the effects of water fasting only while still delivering essential nutrients.
Water-only fasting is when a person drinks only water for a period of time and does not eat any other foods or drinks, which is how some people lose weight or lower blood pressure.
