Does Ashwagandha Really Help You Sleep?
(MENAFN- Alghad Newspaper) Ashwagandha has become popular among prominent celebrities and social media users, especially on TikTok for many reasons, most notably their claim that it improves sleep, reduces anxiety, strengthens memory and even muscle mass.
But does this magic herb really help you sleep?
To answer that we have to know that Ashwaganda is far from being a new treatment and has been used to treat a variety of ailments for thousands of years in countries like India, a traditional healing system from South Asia.
Those who use ashwagandha to help sleep may benefit from its known sedative qualities, as studies on mice have identified the chemical compound called triethylene glycol.
The compound may be responsible for promoting sleep as well as affecting GABA receptors, the same receptors that many sedatives and anti-seizure drugs target, according to a report in The Washington Post.
A meta-analysis of five randomized human trials also found that ashwagandha led to a modest improvement in total sleep time, up to about 25 minutes compared to a placebo.
This also led to a marked improvement in sleep efficiency and quality, according to the participants ’ assessment.
But while ashwagandha may sufficiently induce sleep, it should not be seen as a long-term solution.
Side effects
In parallel, some of the more common reasons why people are interested in this herb are a bit of stress and anxiety, but studies looking at this have indicated that the results are few and even mixed.
Chetty Barrick, associate director of integrative health at Weill Cornell Medical School, advised using the herb for a limited time, noting that patients taking higher doses often report intestinal side effects such as nausea or diarrhea, and serious liver injuries are associated with higher doses.
Darshan Mehta, medical and educational director of the Usher Center for Integrative Health at Brigham and Women ’ s Hospital and Harvard Medical School, explained that Ashwagandha is safe, but said the blemishes in Ashwagandha products are a real concern.
He added that heavy metals have been found in some products in the past, and there have been several reports of Ashwaganda-related liver injury, which sometimes ends in hospitalization and acute liver failure, which may have been linked to these issues.
Who should avoid it?
It is indicated that there are those who should avoid ashwagandha such as pregnant or lactating women and also should not mix the herb with drugs that can be analgesic (such as gabapentin or benzodiazepines).
As well as people who suffer from symptoms such as stomach upset and nausea after eating ashwagandha, it is best to avoid them, since ashwagandha belongs to the family of aubergines, which some people do not tolerate well and other examples include aubergines, aubergines, sweet peppers and tomatoes.

Sara Al Olama: Amazon provides a supportive environment for women to feel safe and do their best in the workplace
T + T - normal size
March 8 is International Women ’ s Day and is an important occasion for Sara Al Ulama, Amazon Channel Team Leader, to celebrate the achievements of women who believe in their abilities and chart their own path, and to inspire Sarah, who believes that unconscious bias in the global workplace can be an obstacle for women to achieve their ambitious goals.
According to the UN ’ s 2023 report, there are fundamental and strong prejudices against women in nearly 9 out of 10 men and women.
Sarah calls for an increase in the number of women in senior leadership positions, with the aim of inspiring young women.
She also talks about Amazon ’ s efforts to support female employees in the company from taking on leadership roles and achieving further growth and success in this path, and explains how Amazon enables female employees to feel safe and provide full support to provide the best in the workplace.
What does International Women ’ s Day represent to you?
For me, International Women ’ s Day is more than a celebration; I see it as a special occasion to highlight the strides we have made in empowering women against prejudice, the achievements we have made so far in breaking down barriers to their advancement, and the distance we still have to travel and the milestones we need to reach in terms of women ’ s empowerment.
On a personal level, I consider this day to be an occasion to recognize the potential of women, their determination to persevere and achieve their goals and their continuous quest to overcome the obstacles they face every day. I also see this day as a platform through which we call to strengthen our collective efforts to challenge discrimination against women and continue to build a world where gender equality is the norm.
Tell us about your position at Amazon and why you chose to pursue a career in the logistics industry.
As Amazon ’ s channel team leader, the nature of my tasks necessitates assistance in the various operations and support areas of the terminal.
This includes coordinating with delivery service providers and point of contact teams to ensure the best possible customer experience.
After returning from my studies in the US and joining the Amazon Logistics team, I started working in a field that is a daily challenge for me, as the logistics sector is a dynamic and evolving field that requires constant innovation and adaptation.
What interests me most is the diversity of the stores every day, and the opportunity to work with specialist teams ranging from health and safety professionals to reliability, maintenance engineering and training and professional development departments.
In a fast-paced work environment, with many tasks and diverse work styles, each day is a unique experience that drives me to learn and grow continuously.
It is also important to highlight the emerging opportunities for women in the logistics sector, especially in light of the long-term dominance of men in the sector.
With the expansion of the e-commerce landscape and the transition of the logistics sector from a traditional to a more important place thanks to the modern digital economy, this transformation has been a paradigm shift and heralds a future in which women have more opportunities to build prestigious jobs and contribute to the growth and development of this sector.
How has Amazon supported you in your career growth and advancement?
Amazon has played a pivotal role in helping me grow and advance my career, providing me with opportunities for continuous learning, mentorship and support programs to address new challenges.
As a participant in the Amazon Future Leaders Program, I received special support that was pivotal to me as an Emirati working at Amazon, ensuring a clear path for my future and career development.
The culture here is based on the premise that every opinion matters and every observation counts and needs to be taken into consideration, which is an incentive for creativity, innovation and initiative to make decisions with confidence and responsibility, which are key factors to help me expand my skill set and advance my career.
Amazon ’ s diverse work environment, which welcomes everyone equally, makes us all feel valued and empowered to deliver our best in the workplace, supporting the company ’ s vision goals that see our diverse backgrounds as a source of strength and innovation.
How important are government policies in providing job opportunities for women and creating the right environment for women to succeed and prosper?
The UAE ’ s wise leadership believes that gender balance is not just about empowerment in the workplace, but is an important driver of progress and prosperity for the country at all levels.
National strategies and policies, such as the UAE Gender Balance Council Strategy 2026 and the National Policy for the Empowerment of Women 2031, contribute to providing an enabling environment for women of all levels of education and experience to access many opportunities in the field of employment, enabling them to contribute effectively to the country ’ s path towards sustainable development and innovation.
By overcoming gender barriers in the workplace, we open up a wealth of resources and potential that lead to greater achievement, the opportunity to gain more diverse perspectives and thus a successful journey led by collective efforts.
What change do you aspire to see that will increase women ’ s participation in the UAE labor market?
I look forward to a future where the number of women in leadership is not just numbers, but the embodiment of active participation that sets a standard for excellence.
I aspire to see a work environment in which women are encouraged to take up positions in the top leadership of companies and organizations, and women's perspectives and opinions form an indispensable part of the decision-making process.
This paradigm shift requires not only confronting the feelings and attitudes of prejudice we may have about our abilities, but also getting rid of those feelings and attitudes, we need a cultural transformation process in which we witness women supporting women, encouraging them to succeed as a success for all women, and working together to eliminate any form of gender bias.
As the country continues to support and nurture a new generation of women leaders, I hope to see more women in senior and traditionally male-dominated positions, more gender-balanced work environments, and continue to invest in training and mentorship programs that support and encourage women, while giving them equal opportunities to move beyond traditional roles to courageously and confidently reach leadership positions, as Amazon has done for me.
On International Women ’ s Day, what is your advice for women, is there a special message for them on their day?
I recently read that studies indicate that 41% of women do not defend themselves, and this motivates me to send a message to all women on International Women ’ s Day that women trust themselves and their ability, have the courage to make bold decisions, and not allow anyone to question their competence and potential.

International report reveals high demand for travel in January 2024
The International Air Transport Association (IATA) released its latest travel report, which included global passenger demand data for January 2024, signaling a strong start to the year.
According to the report, total demand, measured by passenger revenue per kilometre, increased by 16.6%; total capacity, measured by available seats per kilometre (ASK), increased by 14.1%; load factor was 79.9% (+ 1.7 points); international demand increased by 20.8%; capacity increased by 20.9% and load factor remained at 79.7% (+ 0.0 points) while domestic demand increased by 10.4%; 4.6% and load factor 80.2% (+ 4.2 points).
Willie Walsh, Director General of IATA, said: “2024 is off to a strong start despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty, and as governments look to build prosperity in their economies in the busiest election year ever, it is critical that they view aviation as a catalyst for growth.
“We will address governments for policies that help aviation reduce costs, improve efficiency and make progress toward net CO2 emissions by 2050. ”
International Passenger Markets: Airlines in the Middle East
Airlines in the Middle East recorded a 16.2% increase in travel traffic in January 2024 compared to a year ago.
Capacity increased by 15.7% and load factor increased by 0.4 percentage points to 79.9%.
African Airlines
African airlines saw an 18.5% increase in travel traffic in January 2024 compared to last year.
Capacity in January increased by 19.2%, reducing the load factor by 0.4 percentage points to 73.3%, the lowest among regions.
Asia and the Pacific
Airlines in the Asia-Pacific region saw a 45.4% increase in travel traffic in January 2024 compared to January 2023, continuing the rapid recovery in the region after the lifting of epidemic restrictions, capacity increased by 48.1% and load factor decreased by 1.5 percentage points to 82.6%. The exceptionally strong growth rate was attributed to China, which was in the early stages of lifting travel restrictions due to the coronavirus (COVID-19) in January 2023. The recovery of major international routes to and from the Asia-Pacific region is lagging, but routes like Central Asia have surpassed pre-epidemic levels.
China continues to drive domestic demand growth, seeing strong demand for travel on the occasion of the Lunar New Year, and this likely led to increased traffic in February as well, and Chinese airlines have responded by increasing their capacity, especially through the deployment of wide-body aircraft.
European Airlines
European airline traffic in January 2024 increased by 10.8% compared to January 2023.
Capacity increased by 10.7%, load factor increased by 0.1 percentage point to 77.3%, and routes between Europe and North America rebounded particularly strongly after the epidemic and were 6.5% higher than in January 2020.
Airlines in America
North American airlines saw traffic increase by 12.3% in January 2024 compared to 2023, capacity increased by 13.7%, and load factor decreased by 1.0 percentage points to 79.4%.
Latin American airline traffic increased by 17.9% compared to the same month in 2023, and capacity in January increased by 13.2%, pushing the load factor up 3.4 percentage points to 86%, the highest among regions.

Fasting has come under new scrutiny in scientific research, and a recent study by researchers from Queen Mary University of London and the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences has shed light on the complex mechanisms of fasting and its impact on the human body.
The study, published by Newsweek, followed 12 healthy volunteers through strict water-based fasting for seven days.
This period of calorie restriction provided researchers with a unique opportunity to observe the body ’ s response to prolonged fasting.
The volunteers were closely monitored, paying particular attention to changes in blood biomarkers, providing valuable insights into the physiological adaptations that occur during fasting.

Benefits beyond weight loss
One of the most important findings of the study was that the body switched from glucose to fat as a primary fuel source during the first days of fasting.
This metabolic shift confirms the body ’ s remarkable ability to adapt to periods of nutrient scarcity.
Over the course of the fasting, participants showed an average weight loss of 5.7 kilograms, including fat mass and lean mass.
The study ’ s findings extended beyond just metabolic changes, as researchers identified distinct changes in blood protein markers on the third day of fasting, demonstrating a comprehensive systemic response.
Notably, these changes involved proteins important for the structural integrity of brain cells, suggesting potential cognitive benefits associated with fasting.
Claudia Langenberg, director of the Queen Mary University Research Institute for Microhealth (PHURI), confirmed the pioneering nature of these findings, saying: “For the first time, we are able to see what is happening at the molecular level throughout the body when we fast. ”
If followed under medical supervision, fasting can be an effective weight loss intervention and may lead to additional health benefits beyond simply restricting calories.

The spread of artificial intelligence and easy access to tools capable of altering the truth have led to the emergence of one of the most shocking and disturbing digital manipulation techniques, “deepfake. ”
Deep fakes make it possible to create fake videos, photos and sounds that show individuals saying or doing things they never said or did, and although the most popular version until recently was video, deep fakes are gaining importance day by day.
A historical overview
The first major program to bring the potential of deep voice counterfeiting to the general public was Adobe Voco in 2016, which used artificial intelligence to mimic a person ’ s voice from a short recording.

At present, we can find many applications and tools online that use this technology to create fake sounds, where Microsoft has launched an artificial intelligence model called VALL-E that can imitate the human voice with a recording of only three seconds.
Deep sonic falsification
Deep voice falsification aims to create an audio model capable of replicating the actual speaker ’ s voice, but the model must be trained through the speaker ’ s audio recordings, in order to be ready to generate an artificial sound similar to that of the original person.
expressiontelegraph.co.uk
Deep learning and natural language processing techniques are used to analyze the unique patterns and characteristics of sound, some of which include pitch, speed, rhythm and tone, and artificial intelligence uses recordings to deliver an original sound, creating a new audio recording that mimics the speaker ’ s voice to a full degree.
How to Create Deep Audio Counterfeiting
Fake deep voice is created using AI-powered text to speech technology, and this can be done with just a few minutes of recorded speech to train an AI speech model, which can read any text with the target voice.
expressionveritonevoice.com
The original recorded sound must be of sufficient quality to sample the unique characteristics of the speaker ’ s voice, after which AI algorithms analyze the patterns and characteristics of the original sound and learn to mimic them.
This can be done with male and female voices and adaptation to the identity of the speaker, the result is a fake voice recording that mimics the voice of the original person, and in addition to generating speech, these instruments can simulate sounds such as breathing and mouth movements.
Initiatives to combat voice counterfeiting
There are initiatives aimed at combating this increasingly prevalent voice counterfeiting, and some technologies can detect these counterfeit products, such as voice biometrics, an authentication method that uses a person ’ s unique voice pattern to verify their identity.

Spectroscopy can also be used, consisting of analyzing acoustic signals to detect unique sound patterns that are difficult to replicate in deep fakes.
There are also tools that can detect the digital traces present in deep voice fakes, because the latter fails to accurately simulate all the variables of the actual voice recording, and therefore, deep fakes may contain breaks in sound or background noise that differ from those expected in the original sound.

(CNN) -- A new report commissioned by the State Department paints a worrying picture of the "catastrophic" national security risks posed by rapidly evolving artificial intelligence and warns the federal government is running out of time to avert disaster.
The findings were based on interviews with more than 200 people over more than a year, including senior executives from leading AI companies, cybersecurity researchers, weapons of mass destruction experts, and national security officials within the government.
The report, released this week by AI Gladstone, categorically suggests that more advanced AI systems could, in the worst case scenario, “pose an extinction-level threat to the human race. ”
The US State Department did not respond to a request for comment.
The warning in the report is another reminder that while the potential of AI continues to captivate investors and the public, there are real risks as well.
Jeremy Harris, CEO and co-founder of Gladstone AI, told CNN on Tuesday: “Artificial intelligence is already an economically transformative technology.
It can allow us to cure diseases, make scientific discoveries, and overcome challenges we once thought insurmountable. ”
"But it could also bring serious risks, including catastrophic risks, that we should be aware of."
“A growing body of evidence – including empirical research and analysis published at the world ’ s most important AI conferences – suggests that above a certain threshold of capability, AI systems are likely to become out of control. ”
White House spokeswoman Robin Patterson said President Joe Biden ’ s executive order on AI was “the most significant action any government in the world has taken to deliver on the promise and manage AI risk. ”
“The President and Vice President will continue to work with our international partners and urge Congress to pass bipartisan legislation to manage the risks associated with these emerging technologies, ” Paterson said.
A clear and urgent need to intervene
Researchers warn of two major dangers posed by large-scale artificial intelligence.
First, Gladstone AI said the most advanced AI systems could be armed to cause irreparable damage.
Second, there are particular concerns within AI labs that they may at some point “lose control ” over the very systems they are developing, with“ potentially devastating consequences for global security. ”
"The rise of artificial intelligence and artificial general intelligence has the potential to destabilize global security in ways reminiscent of the introduction of nuclear weapons," the report said, adding that there is a risk of an AI "arms race", conflict and "deadly accidents the size of weapons of mass destruction."
The Gladstone AI report calls for radical new steps aimed at countering this threat, including the launch of a new AI agency, the imposition of “emergency ” regulatory safeguards and restrictions on how much computer power can be used to train AI models.
The authors wrote in the report: "There is a clear and urgent need for the intervention of the United States government."
The report notes that although the work was produced for the State Department, its views “do not reflect the views ” of the agency or the U.S. government in general.
A government notice issued in 2022 by the State Department ’ s Nonproliferation and Disarmament Fund Office shows that the government is offering to pay up to $250,000 for an assessment of “proliferation and security risks ” associated with advanced AI.
Safety Concerns
Harris, Gladstone ’ s executive director of artificial intelligence, said his team ’ s “unprecedented level of access ” to public and private officials had led to startling conclusions.
Gladstone AI said it spoke to technical and leadership teams from chat owner OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Facebook parent company Meta and Anthropic.
In a video posted on Gladstone AI ’ s website announcing the report, Harris said: “Along the way, we ’ ve learned some disturbing things.
Behind the scenes, the safety and security situation in advanced AI seems largely inadequate compared to the national security risks that AI may soon pose somewhat. ”
The Gladstone AI report said competitive pressures were driving companies to accelerate AI development “at the expense of safety and security, ” increasing the likelihood that more advanced AI systems would be“ stolen ” and “weaponized ” against the United States.
The findings add to a growing list of warnings about the existential risks posed by AI — including from even some of the industry ’ s most powerful figures.
Nearly a year ago, Jeffrey Hinton, known as the “godfather of artificial intelligence, ” quit his job at Google and sounded the alarm about the technology he helped develop.
Hinton said there is a 10% chance that artificial intelligence will lead to human extinction within the next three decades.
Hinton and dozens of AI industry leaders, academics and others signed a statement in June saying that “mitigating the extinction risk of AI must be a global priority. ”
Business leaders are increasingly concerned about these risks – even as they invest billions of dollars in AI.
Last year, 42% of CEOs surveyed at last year ’ s Yale CEO Summit said AI has the potential to destroy humanity five to ten years from now.

Some employees at AI companies share similar concerns privately, according to Gladstone AI.
“An individual at one of the well-known AI labs expressed the view that if a specific next-generation model of AI were launched without access restrictions, it would be ‘ very bad ’, because the model ’ s potentially convincing ability could ‘ break democracy ’ if leveraged in areas such as election interference or voter manipulation, ” the report said.
Gladstone said she had asked AI experts in some labs to share their personal estimates privately about the likelihood that an AI incident could lead to “irreversible global effects ” in 2024.
Estimates ranged from 4 percent to as much as 20 percent, according to the report, which notes that the estimates were informal and likely to be heavily biased.
One of the biggest surprises is how quickly artificial intelligence is evolving — specifically artificial general intelligence (AGI), a hypothetical form of artificial intelligence that has a human-like or even superhuman learning ability.

Gladstone AI points out that disagreements over AI timelines make it difficult to develop policies and safeguards, and there is a risk of a slowdown in regulation as technology evolves.

Is humanity dying or reaching beyond humanity?
(MENAFN- Alghad Newspaper) Investigations Department - (Independent Arabia) 20 / 1 / 2024
The question of the Swedish philosopher Niklas Boström opens up a wide range of debate about the artificial mind and the human brain, and can science alone be a way to change human life in the centuries to come?
* * *
“Humanity lives through existential dangers posed by events that will either destroy the intelligent life that was created on Earth, or radically reduce its potential. ”
This phrase sounds alarming, not just alarming, and is one of the brainchild of this Swedish philosopher known for his in-depth readings and writings, particularly on the relationship between man and artificial intelligent machines for the rest of this century.
It is no longer a secret that traditional artificial intelligence, and thus super artificial intelligence, has become one of the existential fears that worry scientists and scholars, philosophers and thinkers, and all those who deal with "post-futuristic" ideas, all of them assert that it is very possible that this new arrival will turn on humans, despite the facilities provided to them, on humanity at a certain moment in time, to turn its victories into breakdowns, Her uncle to hell.
This is what the Swedish-born philosopher predicted, and his predictions were shared by more than 11,000 people in 2015.
This has called for increased public and private awareness around the world about this threat, the risk of which is still underestimated.
Scientists estimate that artificial intelligence could cause the extinction of humanity before the end of this decade at about 10 percent of its probability during the rest of the century.
Who is Nicholas Bostrom of this vision, and why is he one of the brightest global minds to raise his voice, warning humanity of the great horror coming from afar, and that the story of Frankenstein is reincarnated?
Nicholas Bostrom.
The Young Philosopher
It is customary for a philosopher to be a man of age, of great experience.
Becoming a philosopher in one ’ s forties – and perhaps earlier – reveals an unusual and enormously progressive mindset, capable of questioning and sometimes challenging icons and postulates.
Born in Helsingborg, Sweden, on March 10, 1973, Nicholas Bostrom received his secondary education and earned a bachelor's degree in philosophy, mathematics and artificial intelligence from the University of Gothenburg.
He also holds a master ’ s degree in philosophy and physics from Stockholm University, the country ’ s largest university.
He then went on to study a master ’ s degree in “custodial neuroscience ” at King ’ s College London, and then earned a PhD in philosophy from the London School of Economics.
His thesis was supervised by Professor Colin Hawson.
He then held a training position at Yale University from 2000 to 2002.
Bostrom took an early interest in the entropy principle.
Dismantling this principle is notoriously complicated, but in simple words he was able to define a standard for measuring the randomness or order of the universe around us using specific measures of matter.
This principle was an entry point for Bostrom to study the dangers to civilization and humans on Earth, in line with his concerns about humanism, reinforcement ethics, and the dangers of superintelligence.
Bostrom founded the Oxford Martin program to see how modern technology will affect human life in the future.
He is currently the Director and Founder of the Institute for the Future of Humanity at the University of Oxford.
From 2009 to 2015, Bostrom was listed on Foreign Policy ’ s World ’ s 100 Best Thinkers list.
* * *
In his writings, Bostrom brings us to the idea that what many people fail to realize today is that technology will not only change our surroundings or the influence of our actions – as evidenced by the age of smartphones, which has been accompanied by phenomena of “euphoria ” and isolation from society on the one hand, and drift behind new passions and fashions on the other hand. It is time sooner or later for technology to act on us physically and mentally, opening the door to changes and consequences that many would not think of.
Bostrom ’ s books are among the most important in the science of AI futurism, including “Superintelligence: Pathways, Dangers, and Strategies, ” which he published in 2014 and was the highest-selling book on the New York Times list.
Elon Musk and Bill Gates recommended reading this work for its extreme importance.
Artificial Intelligence
And Bostrom's fears.
Since 2016, Bostrom ’ s voice has been rising, warning that by 2075, all evidence suggests that the evolution of artificial inventions could bring them to the point where they use their power to destroy the human race.
The Swedish philosopher asserts that such dangerous ideas today are mere fantasies that we are accustomed to in science fiction films.
But some scientists, like Stephen Hawking, contend that the rapid development of technology makes those ideas seem more realistic.
Will artificial intelligence dominate the human mind in the foreseeable future?
Bostrom and other scientists maintain that in 2022, AI was equivalent to 10 percent of human mental capacity, but by 2040, it will reach 50 percent.
By 2075, it will reach 90%.
This explains Bostrom ’ s concern that the machines would use their powers against their inventors — that is, the magic would turn on the magician.
In this sense, the concerns justifying AI as an existential threat are manifested by the possibility that humans will no longer be able to control its trajectories once it appears.
Artificial intelligence could intentionally, or possibly unintentionally, destroy humanity or trap humans in a perpetual corrupt world.
It may be used by individuals or institutions that are not well-intentioned, seeking to enslave the rest of humanity or worse.
To his credit, Bostrom was, and still is, the first to move the level of talk and thinking from the stage of artificial intelligence and the appreciation of gains and fears to the world of what he called “superintelligence ” or“ superintelligence. ”
Bostrom believes that we are now spectators of a world we no longer understand, where technological transformations are no longer waiting for us to catch up with them or try to realize their consequences in our lives.
Therefore, our feelings about its inevitable consequences will not go beyond surprise and immediate fascination, then shock and anxiety when planning and utilizing AI is much earlier.
What is this “superintelligence ”, and how can it change the life of humanity today, as well as in its immediate future?
Brilliant intelligence.
And beyond the human mind.
Bostrom opens up a wide range of debate about this kind of intelligence in his highly qualitative book, "Superfanity.
A brief guide to the future ", he argues that it is the" super-intelligent mind ", sometimes called" super-intelligence ", that has the potential to radically outperform the best human minds in almost every field, including scientific creativity, general wisdom, and social skills.
Bostrom sometimes distinguishes between a weak, powerful superintelligence.
Weak superintelligence is what you get if you manage to run a human brain exponentially, as if you were activating it on a fast computer.
If the rate of lift speed is 1,000 times the speed of the biological brain, it will perceive reality as being slowed by 1,000 times.
He would think in a certain period of time with ideas more than a thousand times his biological counterpart.
Superintelligence refers to a mind that is not only faster than the speed of the human brain, but qualitatively smarter.
Similarly, there may be types of intelligence that are inaccessible even to very fast human brains given their current capabilities.
Does Bostrom go to the possibility of changing these realities, and thus modifying the shape of the next world?
It seems so in word and deed.
He suggests that something as simple as increasing the size or connectivity of our neural networks may give us some of these capabilities, and other improvements may require a complete reorganization of cognitive engineering or the addition of new cognitive layers on top of the old ones.
When can we see this kind of superintelligence?
Many, but not all, ‘ superhuman ’ expect this ‘ superintelligence ’ to emerge during the first half of the 21st century, and this requires two things: hardware and software.
The implications of intelligence
The Overwhelming of Humanity
The immediate philosophical question that emerges from the talk of superintelligence seems to be: “What are the consequences of this intelligence on the paths of humanity in its present and future? ”
According to Bostrom, it is clear that the arrival of “superintelligence ” will deal a devastating blow to human-centered visions of the world.
However, its practical implications will have more important effects than its philosophical implications.
The creation of "super intelligence" may be the last invention humans need as super-intelligent devices can take care of further scientific and technical development.
It will do so in a much more efficient way than humans.
Bio-humanism would not then be the smartest form of life on Earth.
Here, we see how the prospect of “superintelligence ” raises many big issues and concerns that we must think deeply about before they actually develop.
The more important question is: What can we do to maximize the chances of benefiting from access to “super intelligence ” rather than enabling it to harm us?
The range of expertise needed to address this issue extends far beyond the community of AI researchers.
Indeed, neuroscientists, economists, cognitive scientists, computer scientists, philosophers, ethicists, sociologists, science writers, military strategists, politicians, legislators, and many more — should put their ideas together if we are to deal wisely with what may be the most important task our species must tackle.
Does it mean, in any case, that reaching the stage of “super intelligence ” is already achievable?
It is hard to believe that many “meta-humanists ” would like to become super-intelligent themselves.
This is clearly a distant and uncertain goal, but it may become achievable — either by upgrading minds and subsequent improvement, or gradually improving our biological brains with futuristic activation drugs — cognitive enhancement drugs, cognitive technologies, and IT tools such as wearable computers, smart media, information sorting systems, visualization software, neural interfaces, or brain implants.
Humanity and challenges
What – Above – Humanity
One of the points that distinguishes Bostrom in terms of adequately illuminating it is the issue of "superhumanism", a thought-provoking term that has never been raised before...
What does he mean by that?
According to his various writings, it can be said that the superhuman current means a way of thinking about the future, based on the assumption that the human species in its present form does not represent the end of our evolution, but only a relatively early stage, and formally defines it as the intellectual and cultural movement that confirms the possibility – and desire – of radically improving the human condition through practical rationality, especially through the development and creation of large-scale techniques to eliminate aging. To enhance the intellectual, material and psychological capabilities of the human being significantly. ”
"Super-humanism" can be seen as an extension of, and partly derived from, humanism.
Humanists believe that humans matter, and individuals matter.
We may not be perfect, but we can make things better by promoting rational thinking, freedom, tolerance, democracy, and concern for our fellow human beings.
Supporters of superhumanism support this, and they also emphasize what we are willing to turn into.
Just as we use rational means to improve the human condition and the outside world, we can also use them to improve ourselves, that is, human beings.
In doing so, we are not limited to traditional humanistic methods, such as education and cultural development.
We can also use technical means that will eventually enable us to go beyond what some people imagine when they think of “man. ”
Bostrom ’ s philosophy is clearly expressed in his talk about what makes us human.
It is not just our form, or our current biological details, that do not show what is valuable in us, but the role played by our aspirations, goals, experiences, and the kinds of lives we live.
For the super-humanists, and Bostrom on top, progress happens when more people gain a greater ability to shape themselves, their lives, and the places where they relate to others, according to their deepest values.
Super-humanism values autonomy: the ability of individuals and their right to plan and choose their own lives.
Is the relationship between meta-humanism and contemporary technologies imperative?
There are, of course, some people who, for any number of reasons, choose to give up the opportunity to use technology to improve themselves.
The superhumanists seek to create a world in which individuals of independent will can choose to remain without technical enhancement, or be strengthened, while their choices are respected.
Techniques and Expectations
A forward-looking vision
Is Nicholas Bostrom a man who only talks about artificial intelligence?
His interests certainly outweigh one part of the human landscape, so to speak.
This is because, in addition to his interest in the idea of intelligent and superior minds in particular, he remains very interested in the idea of man and his development at all levels, technically and biologically.
It therefore pays great attention to issues of the quality of biotechnology, genetic engineering and stem cells, in addition to cloning.
In his talk, for example, about biotechnology, which opens a wide door for the human body to escape from the diseases of the present age and the new diseases and epidemics that are not visible in the present days, he says that biotechnology is the application of techniques and methods based on biological sciences.
This includes various projects such as fermentation, human insulin manufacturing, interferon, human growth hormone, medical diagnostics, cell cloning and reproductive cloning, crop genetic modification, biotransformation of organic waste and the use of genetically modified bacteria to clean up oil spills, stem cell research and much more.
Genetic engineering is the field of biotechnology that deals with the directed change of genetic material.
Bostrom argues that the potential medical benefits of biotechnology are too numerous to be counted.
Researchers work on all common diseases with varying degrees of success.
Progress is not only in the development of drugs and diagnostics, but also in the creation of better research tools and methodologies, which in turn accelerates progress.
Looking at the long-term outlook, we must calculate the impact of improvements in the research process.
The Human Genome Project was completed earlier than expected, mostly because initial estimates underestimated how much hardware technology had improved over the course of the project.
Bostrom advises that the world should not prepare to dramatize every new improvement, but rather act on the premise that “don ’ t fight the facts, deal with them. ”
Did Bostrom seek to revive some of the science of the ancient Egyptians, particularly the science of embalming?
If he approached the region with accountability, did he follow the ways of the former, or did he offer different arguments and explanations in his vision of the superhuman of the moment?
About future freezing embalming
Freezing embalming is an experimental medical procedure that seeks to save lives by placing people who cannot be treated with current medical procedures and are legally dead, in tanks under low heat, in the hope that technological advances can revive them.
Bostrom says that for embalming to work today, it is not necessary that we be able to revive patients embalmed by freezing, but all we need is to be able to preserve the possible technologies that are being developed in the future, and one day we will be able to repair the freeze damage and reverse the original cause of the cessation of life.
More than half of the complete freezing procedure cannot be identified today, and the other half cannot be implemented in the future.
Is this talk practically applicable?
What is certain, according to the Swedish philosopher, is that what we now know relates to the possibility of stabilizing the patient ’ s condition by cooling it in liquid nitrogen (-196 ° C).
A great deal of cell damage occurs as a result of the freezing process.
These injuries can be minimized by following the suspension procedure, which provides for the immobilized body to be saturated with cryoprotectors.
The formation of completely destroyed ice crystals can even be bypassed in a process known as “vitrification, ” in which the patient ’ s body is transformed into a type of glass.
This may seem like an unlikely cure, but the purpose of embalming is to preserve the structure of life rather than the processes of life, because life processes can be restarted in principle, as long as the information encoded in the structural properties of the body, especially the brain, is adequately preserved.
Once frozen, the patient can be stored for thousands of years without any further tissue degradation.
Improving the present or planning for the future?
Perhaps the last question we can conclude this quick reading in the mind of Nicholas Bostrom, the famous Swedish philosopher: “Shouldn ’ t we focus on current problems such as improving the condition of the poor, rather than on planning for the distant future? ”
Bostrom stresses that we have to do both, that is, do this and don ’ t leave that one.
Bostrom believes that many of the technologies and trends discussed by “meta-human ” are already a reality. Biotechnology and information technology have changed large sectors of our economies, and the importance of meta-human ethics is reflected in contemporary issues such as stem cell research, genetically modified crops, human gene therapy, embryo screening, end-of-life decisions, enhanced medicine, information markets, and research funding priorities.
The importance of superhuman ideas is likely to increase as opportunities for human betterment spread.
Is Bostrom a philosopher or scientist, forward-thinking thinker or visionary dreamer?
Maybe it's all this and more.
He is a prolific man who cherishes classification.

Due to it being a slower metabolic process for energy production and the possibility of lowering blood sugar levels.
Studies have shown that ketones can provide an alternative source of energy to maintain brain function and prevent age-related neurodegenerative disorders and cognitive decline.
Increasing ketones through supplementation or diet has been shown to improve cognition in adults with mild cognitive decline and those at risk of developing Alzheimer's disease.
Biological clock synchronization: Eating at times that don ’ t match our body ’ s natural circadian rhythms can disrupt how our organs function.
Studies of shift workers suggest that this may make us more susceptible to chronic diseases.
Time-restricted eating is when you eat your meals within six to ten hours during the day when you are most active.
Time-restricted eating causes changes in gene expression in tissues and helps the body during rest and activity.
A 2021 study of 883 adults in Italy indicated that those who restricted their eating to 10 hours a day were less likely to develop cognitive impairment than those who ate without time restrictions.
Intermittent fasting may provide protection for the brain by improving mitochondrial function (a cellular organelle responsible for cell energy production), metabolism and reducing oxidants.
The main role of mitochondria is the production of energy which is essential for brain health.
Many age-related diseases are closely related to the imbalance between energy supply and demand, and this is likely due to mitochondrial dysfunction during aging.
Rodent studies suggest that alternate day fasting or reducing calories by up to 40% may protect or improve mitochondrial function in the brain.
Intestinal and brain axis: The gut and brain communicate with each other through the body ’ s nervous systems.
The brain can affect gut feeling, and the gut can affect mood, cognition, and mental health.
In mice, intermittent fasting showed signs of improving brain health by increasing survival and the formation of neurons in the hippocampal brain region, which are involved in memory, learning and emotion.
There is no clear evidence of the effects of intermittent fasting on cognition in healthy adults.
However, a 2022 study interviewed 411 older adults and found that a lower frequency of meals (less than three meals a day) was associated with lower evidence of Alzheimer ’ s disease in brain imaging.
Some research has suggested that calorie restriction may have a protective effect against Alzheimer ’ s disease by reducing oxidative stress and inflammation and promoting vascular health.
The expert advises that if you are considering intermittent fasting, it is best to seek advice from a health professional such as a dietitian who can provide guidance on the regulation of fasting periods, meal timing and nutrient intake.

With overcrowded seats, limited legroom and a lack of free drinks, global air travel is becoming uncomfortable for many passengers as airlines race to cut carbon emissions.
As the global aviation industry is about to recover from the COVID-19 fallout, reducing emissions remains the industry ’ s number one challenge.
The low-cost and luxury travel model that made aviation affordable for most people has become an unlikely factor to reduce pollution.
This may be due to airlines ’ obsession with reducing weight to save fuel by installing light seats, abandoning first and business class, and not providing blankets and drinks, resulting in a significant increase in carbon emissions.
The five lowest carbon emitters in the world belong to the budget aviation category, led by Wizz Air from its headquarters in Hungary.
In contrast, companies including Delta Air Lines, Cathay Pacific and British Airways are estimated to emit twice as much as their economic counterparts for every person on board, according to the Washington Post service.
With 2050, the industry ’ s deadline to reach carbon neutrality, emissions data suggests that airlines need to tighten more seat space and cut air services to make aviation more sustainable.
Without comprehensive reforms, the aviation sector will not be able to cut emissions by the middle of the century, with its share of emissions expected to rise significantly, while other sectors seek to reduce carbon by 22% by 2050, from the current 2%, according to the International Energy Agency.
Airlines that do not take enough action to reduce carbon emissions are subject to stricter fines and regulations.
In Europe, fuel tariffs have already been introduced to activate systems that drive greener aviation.
First and Business Class seats result in a more carbon footprint for occupants, as they have more space than Economy Class seats.
For example, the average carbon passenger between Hong Kong and Singapore on an Airbus 350 is estimated to be 170 kg of carbon emissions, while the average carbon passenger for the same business class passenger is estimated to be 682 kg, according to the IATA Carbon Accounting Unit.
Economical airlines have taken a variety of routes, both to achieve their carbon emissions reduction target and to carry more passengers.
While in 2009 Ryanair adopted the idea of straight seats, to stand on them rather than sit down, to provide as many seats as possible, Cebu Air Philippines reduced the number of toilets and kitchens on its Airbus A330 to a record 460 seats.
Economical airlines may be fuel efficient, but they have increased passenger traffic due to low ticket prices.
These airlines are responsible for more than 90% of the growth in fuel consumption and carbon emissions between 2005 and 2019.
Unfortunately, fuel efficiency improvements have not kept pace with the significant increase in passenger numbers, according to the International Clean Transport Council.
Airlines, governments and regulators should make more use of the fuel efficiency embraced by budget airlines, taking into account emissions from increased demand.
It is also essential to consume as little fuel as possible, as the aviation sector ’ s plans to shift towards sustainable fuels do not look in the near future.
The current production capacity of this type of fuel is only 1% of global aviation fuel requirements, while the number of passengers is expected to double to more than 8 billion in two decades, compared to 2019.
Demand for premium business and economy class seats has risen, in relative terms due to high savings and a lack of travel during the epidemic.
But the potential need for more austerity at more than 30,000 feet raises questions about the longevity and affordability of luxury air travel.

Learn about the ‘ most prominent ’ patterns of online fraud and identity fraud
A new study on online fraud based on impersonation and identity fraud has revealed a 10-fold increase in detected deep fraud based on artificial intelligence (AI) between 2022 and 2023.
Add Announcement
The study, prepared by the platform "Sumsub", presented a comprehensive analysis of fraud based on identity fraud, classified by regions around the world and according to the areas of work targeted, and pointed in its report to the most prominent methods and patterns adopted to impersonate and falsify identity.
Sumsub is an identity verification platform that helps businesses monitor fraud around the world and contributes to raising people ’ s awareness of identity theft and identity theft fraud.
Using the term “identity fraud ” to refer to the unauthorized use of personal data or fake identity for malicious purposes, the report analyzed trends, patterns and changes in“ identity fraud ” over the years of monitoring, with data from more than 2 million fraud attempts from 224 countries and regions around the world, covering 28 industries. Identity fraud.
The report says that in the past three years, the fraud landscape has evolved with the development of new technologies.
Based on the results of the study, it is clear that there is a marked upward trend in the rates of identity fraud, where the rate showed a significant increase, doubling from 1.1 percent, in 2021, to 2 percent, in 2023.
The most common types of fraud
In 2023, patterns of identity fraud continued to shift towards more complex and sophisticated technologies, according to the report, the five most prominent types of fraud were:
False identities and counterfeiting
The report shows that the ID card is the most vulnerable document to be exploited in frauds, accounting for nearly 75 percent of all fraudulent activity involving documents.
Then came the passport, then the driver ’ s license and then the residence permit.
The study showed that in 2023, fraudsters increasingly targeted developed countries in the process of falsifying documents, with the proportion of forged identities in these countries rising by an average of 163 percent, while the proportion of forged passports increased by 147 percent.
Documents linked to advanced economies have become new targets for scammers and are often forged and used, the report warns, because they are more credible and reliable.
Organizations and individuals must resort to enhanced verification of documents, even those that appear reliable and credible.
The UAE passport is the most falsified identity document of 2023, with one in four passports falsified, while the Brazilian driver ’ s license was the least falsified in the world, and the Ethiopian driver ’ s license has seen the fastest growth in falsification cases in the world.
Although some forgeries still use basic techniques such as printed images, there has been a notable rise in the prevalence of deep falsification of documents and identities altogether.
The study adds that technological advances have given scammers access to sophisticated tools and techniques to create fake documents, much like original documents.
Andrew Novoselski, head of product at Sumsub, said the fraud has evolved with the adoption of remote operations, especially in financial services, travel and transportation, where there is no longer direct contact with a live person, attracting scammers.
It has also become easier to create new identities, as one person can have 100 or 1,000 different identities online.
Deep fakes.
Deep fake technology remains a major threat in the field of identity fraud, as the widespread accessibility of this technology has enabled criminals to falsify audio, photos and video in a very realistic way in easier and less expensive ways, deceiving individuals and fraud prevention systems.
According to Pavel Goldman Kalaidin, head of artificial intelligence and machine learning at Sumsub, scammers can, depending on their skills, try to trick the system in several ways, ranging from simply wearing a gag to creating a complex deep fake technique, which uses machine learning to either create a fake character or impersonate an existing character using processed photos and videos, as well as scandalising and misleading celebrities.
He adds that deep fake voices are being used extensively to deceive people and hack into their accounts, where, for example, a journalist succeeded in entering his own bank account using a replica of his voice using artificial intelligence.
Seizure of accounts
The study says that despite efforts to strengthen security measures, account seizures have grown steadily.
Internal platform statistics showed global account hijackings increased 155 percent in 2023.
The continuing threat of account takeovers can be attributed to several key factors:
Technological advancements allow more sophisticated techniques for offenders to hack user credentials, including phishing attacks and advanced malware.
Exploiting human vulnerabilities: Fraudsters manipulate trust and use psychological tactics to trick individuals into inadvertently providing their account information.
This human characteristic makes it difficult to detect and prevent this type of fraud.
Exploiting vulnerabilities in the digital ecosystem: Fraudsters are becoming more adept at targeting and exploiting vulnerabilities within digital ecosystems.
By taking advantage of vulnerabilities in one platform, they can gain unauthorized access to other platforms.
To prevent account takeovers, companies need to deploy advanced anti-fraud systems.
These systems include continuous monitoring of user behavior and real-time alerts, along with actions such as biometric authentication, device intelligence, and more.
Money laundering networks
Money laundering was among the most common complex fraud schemes, according to the study, recruiting “seemingly innocent ” individuals who were used to transfer illegally obtained funds and conceal their origin.
Forced verification
The report describes “forced verification ” as an emerging trend in scams, in which individuals are manipulated to undergo verification for the benefit of fraudsters.
While forced verification is not currently widespread, experts are increasingly concerned about its potential impact.
According to internal platform statistics, forced verification rose from 0.31 percent to 3.52 percent of total fraud cases globally in 2023.
The study published indications of trying to perform short-form verification, most notably: the presence of suspicious voices during a verification call, such as background conversations or repetitive sounds, and unusual behavior, such as using a phone or other external devices during verification.
In order to avoid forced verification, the study recommends first deploying AI-based fraud detection systems with voice recognition technologies that can identify flaws.
Second, it advises training staff on signs of forced verification and providing them with guidance on how to deal with such situations.
Results by country
The countries most vulnerable to identity fraud are Bangladesh, where fraud accounted for 5.44 percent of the total number of checks conducted by the platform, followed by Pakistan 4.59 percent, Latvia 4.05 percent, Hong Kong 3.33 percent and Tanzania 3.31 percent.
While Bangladesh and Pakistan have continued to top the list since 2021 despite declining rates, Latvian and Hong Kong ’ s rates of identity fraud more than doubled compared to 2022.
The Middle East and Africa (MEA) region saw a 450 per cent increase in deepfake technology, with the UAE topping the list of countries in the region with 2,200 such frauds, due to its strong online presence, technological advances and rapid growth associated with the business environment.
This is followed by Algeria (1000 cases), Saudi Arabia (700), Morocco (580), Lebanon, Jordan, Iran and Israel (500 cases), Turkey (480), Kuwait (400), Egypt (300), Somalia (200), Yemen, Tunisia, Libya and Qatar (100 cases).
Among African countries, South Africa (19.7 percent) and Nigeria (11.5 percent) faced the highest number of deepfakes attacks.
For its part, the United States saw a significant rise in identity-related fraud rates from 1.04 percent in 2021 to 2.30 percent in 2022, and then recorded a decline later in 2023, settling at 1.68 percent.
Canada showed a more gradual increase, moving from 0.56 percent in 2021 to 1.16 percent in 2023.
The report says U.S. advances in artificial intelligence and digital manipulation technology have led to a rise in fraud involving fake videos and images.
The wide spread of high-quality media content and the popularity of social media platforms in the United States also contribute to the spread of deepfakes fraud.
Identity fraud rates in Europe have shown diverse patterns in the past three years, with Latvia, Estonia and Ukraine experiencing a marked increase in identity fraud rates.
In contrast, countries such as Malta, Portugal and Switzerland have maintained relatively lower fraud rates over the past three years, all remaining below one percent in 2023.
Deep fake attacks posed significant challenges for Spain, the UK and Germany, each of which accounted for more than 10 percent of the total cases in the region.
According to the study, the average growth of scams across Europe is + 780 percent, due to the attractiveness of these economically advanced countries to scammers, as well as their advanced digital infrastructure and large online presence.
Deep counterfeiting technology in the Asia-Pacific region has increased by 1,530 percent.
Vietnam and Japan are leaders in the number of attacks, far outpacing other countries, as Japan is known for using deepfake technology in entertainment, which may allow fraudsters to exploit this technology in other areas, according to the report.
In the Latin American region, identity-related fraud rates increased in all the countries analyzed in 2023.
This is due to several factors, according to the study, including increased digitization of transactions, social and economic imbalances, and informal economies.
The problem is compounded by the ability of some fraudsters to forge documents in Portuguese and Spanish, increasing the risk of identity fraud in Latin American countries.
Brazil has the highest number of deep fakes in Latin America, accounting for nearly half of all reported incidents.
Most of the cases are related to the sectors of digital currencies, financial technology and electronic games.
Average growth across the region is + 410 percent.
Sectors that are more vulnerable to fraud
Identity fraud tends to target unregulated industries more frequently.
This is primarily due to a lack of strict regulations and verification requirements, which makes it easier for fraudsters to exploit vulnerabilities.
As for the top five areas of business experiencing identity scams, they are:
The online media sector, which includes news sites, streaming services, social media platforms and digital advertising, saw the largest rise in identity-related fraud (four times), rising from 1.56 percent to 4.27 percent between 2021 and 2023.
Large audiences create an environment vulnerable to fraudulent activities such as fake accounts, manipulation of participation and dissemination of misinformation.
Professional services 3.14 percent
-Healthcare 2.41 percent, where it saw a big jump in 2023, with the rate of fraud from not reporting any cases of fraud rising in 2021.
In transportation, the figure was 2.03 percent.
Video games were 1.82 percent, up from a peak of 3.1 percent in 2022, but fell the following year.
Conversely, sectors such as e-learning have remained relatively stable, even declining over the years.
In the context of deep counterfeiting, the cryptocurrency sector has emerged at the forefront, followed by financial technology, as the nature of the sector ’ s digitization, the potential for significant financial gains and ongoing regulatory challenges create vulnerabilities that fraudsters exploit.
The report quoted fraud and financial crime expert, Luke Raven, as saying that cooperation between different sectors is necessary to effectively combat fraud, adding that there is a need to go beyond traditional partnerships between sectors, as breaking down information barriers and sharing information between different participants enhances prevention, detection and response to fraud.
This could lead to better identification of fraud trends, tracking of illicit transactions and technology development.
Artificial Intelligence: Friend or Enemy?
AI has revolutionized the fight against fraud, but it comes with its own set of challenges.
While AI can be a powerful weapon in preventing fraud, it can also be exploited by fraudsters who use it to their advantage.
Artificial intelligence is a powerful defensive weapon against the rising tide of identity fraud.
As fraud methods evolve and become increasingly complex, AI-powered fraud prevention solutions have become an indispensable tool for organizations and individuals alike.
Machine learning models can analyze huge data sets, identify unusual patterns and discrepancies that may indicate fraudulent activity, and can employ natural language processing algorithms to detect phishing messages, protecting users.
AI systems can even verify identities using biometric data, reducing the risk of unauthorized access.
It is important to harness the potential of AI while keeping one step ahead of those who seek to exploit it.
Expectations for 2024
The study presented the platform ’ s expectations of what may be witnessed in 2024 in the world of fraud, where it expected that the technology of deep counterfeiting will become more advanced and difficult to detect, and that the control of accounts and the transfer of funds will escalate.
Account purchases and money transfers are expected to continue to proliferate, as fraudsters will find innovative ways to exploit these methods, requiring more robust countermeasures and regulatory responses.
In terms of preventive measures, the platform expected strict rules to be imposed on social networks, and the acquisition of identity data from global storage to local authorities, which would enhance data security, privacy and local control over sensitive personal information.
Stricter regulations may also push for electronic identification (eID) or video identity verification with automated processes, which will provide improved ways to confirm individual identities.
Web3 technologies and decentralized solutions could gain wider adoption, according to the study, providing better security and control of personal data in a decentralized digital environment.
The report also predicted that there would be an increased focus on undocumented identity verification and the adoption of alternative methods of identity verification, providing diverse and robust options for confirming identities.
The identity verification and fraud prevention market is also likely to see consolidation, as key players collaborate to deliver more comprehensive solutions.
Network analysis will become necessary to effectively combat fraud, allowing organizations to detect patterns and complex communications that point to fraudulent activities.
General advice
In order to prevent corporate identity fraud, the study recommends:
Implement Know Your Customer (KYC) protocols: enforce robust procedures when listing new customers, regularly update and authenticate customer data, and invest in technology to identify fake videos and audio using deep fakes.
Secure data storage: By using encryption for sensitive data, updating databases and maintaining regular backups, as well as limiting access to sensitive information.
Implement robust authentication methods via two-factor authentication to access company systems, and regularly update and strengthen password policies.
Regular training and awareness programs, through educating employees about the latest fraud techniques, and conducting regular cybersecurity trainings.
Monitor transactions in real time to monitor suspicious activities, and set up alerts for unusual patterns.
Verify vendors by making sure they follow strict security protocols, and regularly review their security procedures.
Update security systems by keeping all software, especially security software, up to date, and addressing system vulnerabilities on a regular basis.
Implement a response plan for potential breaches and regularly train staff on it.
Implement physical security by ensuring secure access controls to the company ’ s premises and the use of surveillance systems such as CCTV cameras.
Conduct regular security audits and review and update security policies as needed.
Encourage staff to report suspicious activities and establish an anonymous reporting system if necessary.
Advice for staff:
Protect personal information and do not share personal details on public platforms.
Regularly review and clean social media profiles.
Beware of unsolicited communications, especially those requesting personal information, and always ensure the identity of the applicant.
Use strong and unique passwords for all accounts, and install and update antivirus software regularly.
Learn how to detect fake videos, audio clips and deep fakes properties
Protect important paper documents in a safe place and shred unnecessary documents containing personal details.
Monitor and search personal accounts for suspicious activities
Avoid using unsafe public Wi-Fi networks.
-Caution with emails for suspicious links, attachments and phishing
-View the latest fraud schemes and follow up the cyber security training provided by the company.

Pollution of the seas: a disaster threatening the planet
From the inspiration of the series Light and the Happy Planet
During the events of the children's animated series Noor and the Happy Planet, the heroes discussed the danger of pollution of the seas by petroleum substances and how this affects marine life.
The Constitution lists the most important information on the issue of marine pollution.
Seas and oceans cover more than 70% of the Earth ’ s surface and are a vital part of our planet ’ s ecosystem.
But, unfortunately, the seas today face a serious threat: pollution.
What is marine pollution?
The term "marine pollution" refers to the introduction of harmful substances into the marine environment, which adversely affects the health of the seas and the organisms that inhabit them.
Types of marine pollution:
Plastic waste pollution: Plastic waste is one of the most common types of pollution, posing a serious threat to marine life.

Study bears surprising result: Intermittent fasting increases risk of death from heart disease
A recent study has found that people who follow an intermittent fasting regimen may be at a higher risk of heart-related death.
The study, led by Dr. Victor Waines Chung, professor of epidemiology and biostatistics at Shanghai University, was presented at the American Heart Association ’ s Epidemiology and Prevention – Lifestyle and Cardiovascular Health Sessions March 18-21.
The researchers analyzed data from more than 20,000 adults across the United States.
The scientists found that those who ate only 8 hours of the day (i.e. fasted 16 hours a day) following a specific eating schedule were 91% more likely to die from cardiovascular disease than those who followed a normal schedule.
This finding is unexpected, as previous studies have found that intermittent fasting improves blood pressure, blood glucose levels and cholesterol.
Intermittent fasting
Intermittent fasting is an eating pattern that moves between fasting and eating periods.
There are several methods of intermittent fasting, but the most common ones include the 16 / 8 method, which involves fasting for 16 hours a day and restricting the period of eating to 8 hours, and the 5: 2 method, which involves eating normally for 5 hours during weekdays and restricting calorie intake to 500-600 calories for two non-consecutive days.
“Restricting daily eating time for a short period, such as eight hours a day, has gained popularity in recent years as a way to lose weight and improve heart health, ” Chung said.
The Jiao Tong University School of Medicine in Shanghai, China, said in a statement: "The long-term health effects of time-restricted eating, including the risk of death from any cause or cardiovascular disease, are unknown."
The researchers found that for people with cardiovascular disease, eating 8 to 10 hours a day increased the risk of death from heart disease or stroke by 66 percent, and that intermittent fasting did not reduce the overall risk of death from any disease.
The researchers also found that people with cancer who ate more than 16 hours a day had a lower risk of death.
"We were surprised to discover that people who followed a specific 8-hour eating schedule were more likely to die from cardiovascular disease," Chung said.
"It shows that compared to the typical eating time range of 12 to 16 hours per day, shorter eating time was not associated with living longer."
“It is important for patients, especially those with heart disease or cancer, to be aware of the association between eating for 8 hours and an increased risk of death from cardiovascular disease.
"Our findings encourage a more cautious and personalized approach to dietary recommendations."
"Although the study identified an association between an eight-hour window of food intake and cardiovascular death, this does not mean that time-restricted food intake causes cardiovascular death."
Some of the limitations in this study include the fact that people self-reported their dietary schedule, which means that this data may be affected by a patient ’ s memory.
The analysis also did not include factors such as the duration of food intake, or even the cause of death.
Beware of results
The research study has not yet been published, so it is too early to judge the credibility of the findings.
However, be cautious about the results, and do not jump to general conclusions that intermittent fasting is harmful to health, as the majority of current studies confirm its benefits.
Duane Mellor, a dietitian lecturer at Aston Medical School, Aston University, who was not involved in the study, said: "It is impossible to determine whether how a person restricts time to eat is associated with the risk of health outcomes as suggested by the study, because it is unclear, given that the data is so limited based on two days of diet recall, why they do it."
Mellor explained: “They were probably restricting the time they were eating.
Perhaps some people do it for health reasons, while others are due to stressful work environments or poverty, which are risk factors for death from cardiovascular disease. ”
"We have to be very careful not to make worrisome headlines and stories based on such limited information.
“Perhaps what you eat and your overall lifestyle is more important than if you ate all your food in less than 8 hours over two days a year. ”
Baptiste Laurent, associate professor of medical statistics at the University of California, Los Angeles, who was not involved in the study, said: "The results presented in the summary of this conference are very astounding and suggest that those who follow a time-restricted diet may have twice the risk of dying from cardiovascular disease.
This would challenge the commonly perceived health benefits of this common diet. ”
The information available was very limited.
The full research has not yet been published, and these results are too brief to draw any conclusion: for example, it is not clear if the reported results take into account the fundamental difference between the comparison groups: if people on this diet tend to be older, or more at risk of cardiovascular disease, then it would be understandable that intermittent fasting is associated with an increased risk of death.

Blinken called on governments to “collaborate with the private sector, civil society, international, regional and academic organizations, research institutions, technical communities and all other stakeholders to build this approach. ”

Dust storms from the Sahara desert spread invisible allergens around the world
Science and Technology
Copy Link https: / / en.rt.com / x903
Many blame pollen when the allergy season begins, but there are “invisible travelers ” coming from the Sahara and Sahel region, who may be the cause of this allergy.
The huge dust plumes, which originate thousands of miles away in sub-Saharan Africa, travel by dust storms around the world every summer, carrying a mix of pollutants and potential pathogens across continents.
Dr. Shankar Chilam, a professor at Texas A & M University, led the task of understanding the biological movers within dust storms.
He and his team are working to identify microbes, specifically bacteria and fungi, that migrate with dust and explore their potential impact on human health.
Dr. Chillam ’ s research uniquely addresses how desert dust storms introduced these microbes into North America.
Dr Chillam and his team analysed samples of desert dust that arrived in Houston in 2018, measuring minerals, bacteria and fungi to check for any links.
Surprisingly, their findings revealed strong links between microbial biodiversity and specific elements, especially calcium.
While these elements occur naturally in the Sahara Desert, they are also found in local North American environments.
Identifying the exact source and payload of the dust remains a challenge that scientists continue to face.
Perhaps the most surprising discovery is that even seemingly lifeless dust clouds are full of biological activity.
High-tech DNA analysis allowed the team to create a reservoir of bacteria and fungi, even if the microbes themselves were not active.
Surprisingly, they found traces of several pathogens known to cause disease in humans, according to the World Health Organization.
Dr Daniel Spalink, an assistant professor at Texas A & M University, warns: “This doesn ’ t tell us whether they will be able to infect us and make us sick, but at least the DNA of many pathogenic bacteria and fungi has been identified in African dust. ”
Climate change is changing weather patterns globally.
This shift affects the behavior of dust storms, leading to differences in their frequency and severity.
The dust storm in the Sahara travels far beyond the borders of North America, affecting global ecosystems in profound ways.
The dust, which originates from the vast Sahara desert, is released on transcontinental journeys that affect climate, ocean biology and ecosystems far from its source.
As it travels across oceans and continents, desert dust reflects sunlight back into space, cooling the Earth ’ s surface.
This natural phenomenon acts as a counterbalance to the greenhouse effects of greenhouse gases, illustrating how desert dust can affect global temperatures.
Dust also carries microorganisms and nutrients, such as phosphorus, which fertilises remote ecosystems, from the Amazon rainforest to the Caribbean Sea, demonstrating complex nutrient cycles in nature.
Ocean biology also benefits from nutrient-rich dust.
When desert dust settles on ocean waters, it provides essential minerals that stimulate the growth of phytoplankton that form the basis of the oceanic food chain and support a variety of marine life.
Thus, the flow of food from the Sahara could boost marine productivity, affecting fish populations and the global fishing industry.
But the effect of desert dust is not always beneficial, and in ecosystems unusual for the flow of foreign particles and nutrients, the dust can disrupt local environments.For example, excessive dust deposition can strangle corals, block sunlight and hinder photosynthesis.
Moreover, the health effects of desert dust extend across continents, where dust not only carries nutrients but also contaminants and pathogens that can affect air quality and public health.
Communities in the path of these dust plumes may face increased respiratory problems, allergies and diseases, highlighting the need for surveillance and global health preparedness.
