Superfood for those over 50 years old
(MENAFN- Al-Bayan)
With age, some changes occur in the body so that some of the activities we once enjoyed become very challenging, and eating a balanced diet is one of the best things you can do to prolong your life and stay as healthy and energetic as possible after you ’ re over 50.
These foods will make you look young in your golden years.
Beans.
As we approach 50, your risk of developing problems like type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol increases, adding beans to your daily diet is a great way to reduce that risk.
Just 3 ⁄ 4 cups of beans or lentils each day reduces bad cholesterol (LDL) by up to 5%.
Beans can also improve blood sugar levels in people who already have diabetes.
One thing to remember is that if you choose canned beans, it ’ s best to wash them thoroughly before eating them because canned foods are high in sodium.
Oatmeal
The risk of heart disease is very close when men reach the age of 45 and women reach the age of 55.
Therefore, the more cholesterol-lowering foods in your diet, the better.
Oats are great for this purpose because of a type of soluble fiber called beta-glucan.
Soluble fiber binds to cholesterol during digestion and allows it to pass out of the body, rather than stay in the arteries.
Aim for at least 3 grams of beta-glucan daily to reduce total and LDL cholesterol levels by 5-10%.
It has been found that people who eat a lot of oats have a lower risk of premature death than others.
Apples.
Apples are a great nutrient because they reduce the risk of diabetes by helping to regulate blood sugar levels as one apple contains on average 5 grams of fiber, which can lower cholesterol.
Apples also contain a substance called quercetin, which is known for its ability to lower blood pressure.
It is also a reliable source of vitamin C, potassium and antioxidants.
NUTS
Studies have shown that eating an ounce of nuts per day reduces the risk of heart attack and stroke by 28%.
It doesn ’ t have to be a problem nut; whatever you prefer will do, including peanuts.
Leafy greens
Recent research has found that people who eat a lot of leafy vegetables such as spinach or cabbage compare in cognitive ability with 11 years younger people who rarely eat these foods.
Blueberries
Berries are high in certain phytochemicals that are thought to increase blood flow to the brain while reducing inflammation at the same time.
The result is a slower age-related memory decline and a lower risk of Alzheimer ’ s disease.
Berries are also great overall due to their high fiber content and range of vitamins and minerals and if you can ’ t get fresh berries all year round, the freezer can be just as good.
Yoghurt
Yogurt (especially Greek varieties) can be a great source of muscle strength as body mass tends to decrease with age, and studies suggest that the distribution of daily protein intake throughout the day can slow down this process.

Secrets of Successful Intermittent Fasting

Intermittent fasting is one of the most popular diets in recent years, which helps in weight loss, reduces the risk of type 2 diabetes and boosts the intestinal microbiome.
Add Announcement
Rob Hobson, a nutritionist, said: “Some of the strongest research on fasting revolves around the possibility of reducing insulin resistance and reducing the risk of type 2 diabetes.
Other potential benefits include reducing oxidative stress and inflammation in the body, which increases the risk of aging and disease; lowering cholesterol and blood pressure; and protecting brain health.
But Hobson cautioned that “you can ’ t eat what you want with intermittent fasting if you want to lose weight.
You have to eat balanced meals during the feeding period. ”
How can you get all the benefits of fasting without the downsides, and who should avoid intermittent fasting altogether?
Hobson replied that intermittent fasting works on the following:
Reduces your appetite
You might expect fasting to make you feel hungry, but it has been shown to affect hormones that help regulate appetite.
Fasting initially leads to increased levels of the hunger hormone ghrelin, but over time, and with regular fasting, levels can be adjusted.
This may lead to lower levels of hunger in general.
Fasting can help improve sensitivity to leptin, the “fullness ” hormone, and thus maintain satiety for longer, which may help maintain weight.
Eat the right calories on fasting days
If you follow the 5: 2 diet, it can be difficult to maintain fasting days, especially if you ’ re not sure what to cook in the range of 600 or 800 calories a day.
But getting energy from unhealthy sources such as fast-digesting carbohydrates, white bread and sweat sweets will only increase hunger and cause blood sugar imbalances.
So, he advised planning your fast day snacks — and meals on “normal ” days — to include protein, fiber, and healthy fats so that you feel full between meals.
This will also ensure that you get enough micronutrients necessary for good health.
Anger due to hunger.
At first, increased hunger due to fasting can cause feelings of anger.
Fluctuations in blood sugar levels can also affect mood, and low blood sugar can lead to irritability and mood swings.
Fasting also triggers a stress response that leads to an increase in the hormone cortisol, so during long periods of fasting this may increase feelings of anxiety in some people.
But the good news is that the body will adapt to fasting, so over time these side effects can subside, the Daily Mail reports.
Not exercising at the usual pace
Exercise is particularly associated with intermittent fasting or calorie restriction, as energy levels drop dramatically on fasting days.
Start with a low intensity and then slowly increase it until you reach the point where you feel comfortable.
This will help reduce the risk of injury.
If you feel dizzy, dizzy or weak at any time, stop exercising.
Ask yourself if you need breakfast or even adopt another fasting method?
Drinking too much water.
Drinking water increases hydration levels in your body, so fasting days need to be replaced with more fluids than usual.
It is very important that the body remains well hydrated during exercise, and if the workouts are intense, and you feel a lot sweating, add electrolytes to the water to help replenish lost minerals.
Strength Exercises
Strength training is recommended at the end of the fasting period, so if you follow 16: 8 and eat between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m., finish your weightlifting session before 8 a.m.
Make sure you eat enough protein (about 20-25g) after exercise so you can help your body build more muscle.
Cardio exercises at the beginning of fasting
If you do a cardio exercise (running, cycling, swimming, or aerobics), try scheduling it right after your eating period is over.
Therefore, for those who follow at 16: 8, and end at 4 pm, it will be from late afternoon onwards.
You can also plan your last meal around carbohydrates to ensure that muscle glycogen stores, the body ’ s energy source, are full to fuel your workout.
Is intermittent fasting suitable for everyone?
Fasting is not suitable for children and young adolescents because they are at a stage when the body is still developing, especially the bones.
It may seem logical for overweight children and adolescents to lose weight by fasting, but this may lead to nutrient deficiencies and not help them develop healthy eating behaviors.
Fasting is also not recommended for anyone with increased nutritional needs such as during pregnancy or when recovering from illness.
Long-term fasting may affect nutrient intake, and even more so if someone excludes food groups as well.
Although there is no "bad" time to fast globally, some women may find fasting more difficult or less beneficial during the second half of the cycle, which is called the "luteal phase".
During this phase – between ovulation and the beginning of the menstrual cycle – some women experience increased hunger and cravings for food due to increased energy demand.
Progesterone levels rise, which may slightly increase metabolism and lead to an increased need for calories.
Fasting can also exacerbate PMS symptoms such as mood swings, fatigue, and discomfort, making it a less ideal time to restrict food intake.

Five tips for getting young:

Matcha Tea to Improve Health

The effect of extending life is due in particular to the components in it.

Resveratrol - a regenerative plant compound
"Resveratrol" (Resveratrol) is also a secondary plant compound found in the peels of red grapes, and therefore is also found in grape juice as it is found in blueberries, cranberries and cocoa.

Therefore, he swears to eat this plant compound.

Adequate exercise
The fifth factor that helps slow down the aging process, according to Sinclair, is exercise.

How to protect yourself from it.
You should be careful when receiving emergency phone calls, especially when you are asked to transfer money, or provide sensitive information, even if the voice is like the voice of your relatives or friends, in the age of artificial intelligence, counterfeiting surrounds people in all their matters.
Recently, a type of fraud has spread by artificial intelligence applications called "fraud counterfeiting" or "voice manipulation", but you can survive it if you pay attention to these developments, and follow the advice given by two experts in cybersecurity and information technology for the site "Sky News Arabia".
OpenAI, a specialist in generative artificial intelligence, and the creator of the popular chat program “Chat GBT, ” last March, offered a tool for voice cloning that will be limited in use to avoid fraud.
The tool, called Voice Engine, is able to reproduce a person ’ s voice through a 15-second audio sample, according to an OpenAI statement that touched on the results of a small-scale test.
“We recognize that the ability to generate human-like voices is a high-risk step, especially in this election year, ” the statement said, adding that“ we are working with U.S. and international partners from governments, media, entertainment, education, civil society and other sectors, and taking their observations into account. ”
Manipulation and loss of confidence
According to cybersecurity and information technology expert Mohammed Khleif, it has become “very easy ” to use artificial intelligence to make phone calls with sounds that sound familiar to people, and this is called“ voice counterfeiting ” or “voice manipulation. ”
On how this fake sound is made, Khalif says it is done with artificial intelligence programs to imitate known or taken sounds from social media.
One of the perils of using this counterfeiting is to defraud victims in urgent financial requests by deluding them that the caller is known to them, explains Khalif, who warns that such uses may lose confidence in the digital world, negatively affecting the pace of digital transformation.
Cybersecurity and information technology expert Tamer Mohammed calls for caution in the communications we receive, saying that “phone communications by artificial intelligence have spread very widely, and there are applications that implement them without the need for the fraudster to have experience. ”
It is worth mentioning that the frauds reached the most famous figures in the world, including that an adviser working in the presidential campaign of a rival in the Democratic Party of the US President, Joe Biden, invented during the presidential primaries, an automated program that impersonated Biden, and called the fake voice voters not to vote in the New Hampshire elections.
The voices of celebrities such as English artist Stephen Fry and London Mayor Sadiq Khan have also been cloned and attributed to them statements that caused them inconvenience or embarrassment, and one of the executives, who was not named, was exposed to fraud that caused him to transfer $243,000 to the fraudster after receiving a fake phone call, according to the British newspaper “Daily Mail ”.
How do we protect ourselves from fraud?
To counter this new threat, Mohammed Khalif and Tamer Mohammed offer these tips when receiving phone calls, or listening to voices without seeing them:
Always question the authenticity of the communication, even if the sound is familiar, especially when it seems urgent.
Try to communicate with the person who is supposed to be calling through a different means of communication that you check.
Be careful to provide personal information or financial statements during a call that you did not initiate yourself.
- Do not access the link of an account or an unknown website; because through it the phone is hacked, uses voice recordings and knows the voice of the person.
- Not to agree to the terms of any program without checking them and knowing the application well.

Saudi Arabia revisits economic projects "away from arrogance"
RIYADH (Reuters) - Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed al-Jadaan ’ s remarks on Sunday marked a clear official Saudi recognition of the difficulty of implementing the Vision 2030 launched by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in 2016, a comprehensive development plan aimed at diversifying the oil-dependent economy and attracting foreign investment.
While analysts said the decision came too late — especially as reports years ago pointed to many difficulties in implementing the vision, including financial and operational — Jadaan ’ s remarks reflected an awareness of the challenges away from “arrogance ”, arrogance and stubbornness.
Analysts say the move, which comes eight years after the launch of Vision 2030, is an unequivocal acknowledgement that there is too much optimism about the vision, as well as too many of its goals.
Saudi Arabia ’ s finance minister said on Sunday the kingdom would adjust its Vision 2030 plan to transform its economy as needed, reducing the size of some projects and speeding up the pace of others.
Riyadh ’ s decision reflects an acknowledgement that there is too much optimism about Vision 2030, and many of its goals have been ambitious.
In a speech delivered at the World Economic Forum ’ s special meeting under the theme “International Cooperation, Growth and Energy for Development, ” Jadaan said the Kingdom is focused on ensuring the quality of future economic growth and recognizes that the challenges it faces require flexibility.
He said, “There are challenges.
We don ’ t have vanity, we ’ re going to change course, we ’ re going to adapt, we ’ re going to expand some projects, we ’ re going to reduce some projects, we ’ re going to speed up some projects. ”
Saudi Arabia is accelerating efforts to diversify its economy away from oil as part of a vision to develop sectors such as tourism and industry, expand the private sector and create jobs.
Non-oil activities significantly outperformed the expansion of the oil sector during the past year, registering growth of 4.4 percent, while the economy contracted by 0.8 percent on the back of oil production cuts and lower prices.
The International Monetary Fund said in its latest regional outlook report, on the back of continued production cuts, that Saudi Arabia ’ s economy is expected to grow 2.6 percent this year, a downward revision from October ’ s forecast of 4 percent growth.
Non-oil activity growth in the medium term is expected to exceed 5 percent annually, Jadaan said in February, yet the kingdom is likely to continue to rely on oil and gas revenues to drive investments in order to expand non-oil activities.
On Sunday, he reaffirmed the role of the expanded private sector in the implementation of Vision 2030.
“Vision 2030 is about empowering the private sector.
The role of the government is to put in place policies to enable the private sector without doing business on its own. ”
The International Monetary Fund forecasts that the Arab world ’ s largest economy needs oil to rise to $96.2 in order not to run a 2024 budget deficit.
Al-Jadaan ’ s statements did not surprise the Saudi and Gulf circles; they came after leaks published by Bloomberg about the Kingdom ’ s keenness to review projects in the vision, perhaps the most prominent of which is the NEOM project.
In an earlier report by Bloomberg, the agency said Saudi Arabia had scaled back its ambitions for the NEOM project, the largest of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman ’ s plans.
Saudi authorities had planned to have 1.5 million people living in The Line, the futuristic $500 billion city with parallel, mirrored skyscrapers stretching 170 kilometers between mountainous and desert terrain, by 2030.
But now Saudi officials expect the project to accommodate fewer than 300,000 residents by the same date, according to a person familiar with the matter.
The source, who asked not to be identified, said officials expect to complete only 2.4 km of the project by 2030.
The Saudi government has found itself shouldering the bulk of the spending on mega-projects, and as a result at least one contractor has fired a number of workers it employs at the site, according to a document seen by Bloomberg.
Observers view the decision to reduce the NEOM project positively, pointing out that due to financial and economic factors, the implementation of the plan was never possible as initially presented.
They point out that the amount of wealth the Saudis generate from oil is not enough to fund NEOM, Vision 2030 ’ s most ambitious project.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Monday officially opened the Kari Mosque in Istanbul ’ s Byzantine Museum and Monastery of Khora, four years after the church dedicated a mosque to Muslims.

7 Essential Things to Keep Your Heart Healthy

Exercise is one of the best things a person can do for the heart because it helps reduce risk factors for heart disease, including obesity, high blood pressure, and stress.
Add Announcement
The Health Service recommends that every week an adult should do at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity, such as brisk walking or water aerobics, or 75 minutes of high-intensity exercise, such as running.
But exercise isn ’ t the only way that ’ s good for the heart — cardiologist Dr Josiah Wamill offers the most important tips for keeping your heart healthy.
SOCIAL ACTIVITIES
Dr Wamil told The Sun that social activities “help reduce loneliness and social isolation, which have been linked to an increased risk of heart disease. ”
"These social connections can lead to lower blood pressure and lower stress levels, both of which are good for heart health."
According to her, “studies show that people with strong social connections and those who pursue hobbies and have a strong purpose to live may live longer and healthier lives. ”
Strong social relationships are common in the Blue Zones, which have large numbers of people up to 100 years old.

Meditation
Mental alertness is associated with mental health, but there is evidence that it can be a measure of the power the heart uses to pump blood around the body.

Dr Wamil says: “High-quality studies have proven that meditation can improve cardiovascular health.

Plant Care
If they don ’ t want to run or ride a bike, taking care of your plants is beneficial for cardiovascular health.
“Gardening is a physically attractive hobby and can improve cardiovascular health by increasing activity, which is known to reduce the risk of heart disease, ” says the cardiologist.
Cutting grass, planting seeds, digging, weeding and other green activities improve balance, muscle strength and fitness.
One study of 146,000 people over 65 found that those working in plant care had a lower risk of heart attack, stroke, high blood pressure and other negative health outcomes.
And that's not the only benefit.
Dr Wamil says it promotes relaxation and stress reduction, which further contributes to heart health and reduces the risk of strokes and heart attacks.
Diversification of meals
Experts say 30 different plant foods should be eaten throughout the week, which include fruits, vegetables, herbs, and legumes such as lentils, nuts, and seeds.

European Law for the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
The regulation of AI is crucial for a number of reasons, and is primarily about ethical, safety and social considerations.
The rapid advancement of AI technologies poses potential risks that require careful oversight and governance.
It reflects concerns about the ethical, legal and social implications of AI technologies and the European push for a law to regulate the use of AI.
Add Announcement
The EU ’ s approach to regulating AI is based on principles aimed at ensuring the development and deployment of AI systems in a responsible and human-centred manner.
The EU emphasizes the development of artificial intelligence that is in line with human values and rights.
The new regulations aim to promote the ethical use of AI, ensure that AI systems respect fundamental rights such as privacy and non-discrimination, and disseminate them in ways that benefit individuals and society.
European regulations also seek to promote transparency and accountability in AI systems.
The goal is to avoid a “black box ” of artificial intelligence, where decision-making processes are ambiguous.
Thus, the EU recognizes the importance of ensuring the safety and reliability of AI systems, especially in critical areas such as healthcare, transportation and manufacturing.
The law sets standards for risk assessment, testing and verification to reduce the potential harm caused by faulty or unsafe AI applications.
Privacy and data protection is another issue that makes the EU highly focused on data protection and privacy.
Artificial intelligence often relies on comprehensive data sets, and regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) set out guidelines for the legal and ethical processing of personal data.
AI developers must abide by these regulations to protect the privacy of individuals.
Furthermore, European regulations regarding AI emphasize the importance of human supervision and control of AI systems.
Even as AI grows in governance, the EU is seeking to ensure that humans remain in control, especially in critical decision-making processes.
This approach aims to prevent the delegation of authority in decision-making in favor of artificial intelligence.
The EU also aims to promote innovation and competitiveness while maintaining high ethical standards.
A unified regulatory framework can create an equal playing field for companies operating in the EU and contribute to the EU ’ s global leadership in AI governance.
A unified regulatory approach across the EU provides legal certainty for businesses and citizens.
Standardization helps avoid fragmentation and incoherent interpretations of AI-related regulations, creating a more predictable environment for the development and use of AI technologies.
The EU Council is expected to formally approve AI legislation by May 2024.
It will be fully effective 24 months after its entry into force, and it concerns the “Regulation for Determining the Uniform Rules on Artificial Intelligence (AI Law) ”.
It ranks AI systems based on their risk levels and includes provisions on transparency, accountability, non-discrimination and human stewardship.
The regulations, once adopted, will apply to artificial intelligence systems used in various sectors.
Given the impact of new European regulations on innovation and humanitarianism, it is a complex and evolving issue.
The aim of these regulations is to strike a balance between promoting AI innovation and ensuring that it is developed and used ethically and responsibly to protect human rights and public safety.
The regulations aim to encourage innovation in artificial intelligence while setting clear ethical limits.
The EU aims to create an environment in which innovative AI solutions can flourish without compromising core values.
It is hoped that clear rules and guidelines will encourage companies and individuals to adopt AI solutions, so that there are safeguards that protect against misuse and ensure responsible practices.
The EU ’ s efforts to regulate AI also make it a global leader in AI governance.
This law may impact and set a standard for other regions, contributing to the creation of international standards for ethical AI.
While large companies may have the resources to adapt to regulatory requirements, smaller entities may face challenges.
It is essential to reconcile encouraging innovation with not placing a disproportionate burden on small players.
The overall goal is to exploit the benefits of artificial intelligence while preserving its benefits to humans, and the regulations reflect a commitment to develop artificial intelligence in a responsible and human-centered manner.
Continuous assessment and adaptation to legal regulations will be necessary to strike a balance between innovation and ethical considerations.
In conclusion, AI regulation is necessary to ensure its ethical use, to prevent the harm it can cause to humanity, and to address the social challenges associated with its deployment.
A well-thought-out and comprehensive regulatory framework necessary to exploit the benefits of AI while minimizing its risks and protecting the well-being of individuals and communities is a necessity to think about.

Ocean temperatures are reaching record highs, indicating that warming is accelerating beyond expectations, and many parts of the world, from polar ice shelves to coastal cities, will be affected.
The oceans are a huge battery; they absorb large amounts of heat and then release it slowly.
Now, our oceans absorb more than 90 percent of the heat trapped in the Earth ’ s atmosphere by increasing greenhouse gas emissions.
Recently, however, ocean temperatures have increased dramatically.
Since March 2023, ocean surface temperatures around the world have hit record highs every day compared to the same day in previous years.
On 47 of those days, there was a significant difference between the new temperatures and those observed on the same days in previous years since humanity became familiar with satellite monitoring technology, according to data from the European Union ’ s Copernicus Climate Change Monitoring Service.
In February 2024, average global air temperatures exceeded 1.5 degrees Celsius.
Last year, ocean temperatures in parts of the world were close to what would be expected if global air temperatures were 3 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels – meaning ocean temperatures are rising faster than expected.
This rapid pace of ocean warming is puzzling scientists who wonder why.
Hilly Fowler, a professor of the effects of climate change at Newcastle University in the UK, said: “The jump in ocean temperatures over the past year is a huge leap.
The fact that we can ’ t absorb this leap is becoming clearer by the day, but that it brings terror. ”
What is clear, however, is the effects of that jump in ocean temperatures on both humans and ecosystems.
In the summer of 2023, water temperatures were observed off the coast of Florida, hotter than hot tub water.
Coral reefs are now experiencing their fourth "bleaching" on the planet.
Beyond that, there are other effects that aren ’ t being addressed as much: from the loss of oxygen in the deep sea to the increasing intensity of rain in the sky — all evidence that these unprecedented degrees of ocean heat are destabilizing the planet.
What is causing the oceans to warm at such an unprecedented rate?
There are two main reasons for this rise in ocean temperatures over the past year, according to Michael McFadden, a researcher with the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
The first is the steady rise in greenhouse gas concentrations.
The second reason is the activity of the El Nino phenomenon in 2023, which saw the surface of the waters warming more than usual in the equatorial Pacific, which in turn led to increased evaporation rates – and the transfer of large amounts of heat to the atmosphere.
Besides these two reasons, there are other, less obvious reasons that have played a role in ocean temperatures rising over the past year at such a pace.
According to Michael McFadden, the eruption of the Tonga Honga volcano in the Pacific Ocean in early 2022 released unprecedented amounts of water vapor, which in turn trapped large amounts of heat in the atmosphere.
In 2020, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) asked commercial ships to switch to low-sulphur fuels.
This has helped reduce sulphur dioxide emissions from global shipping.
Sulfur dioxide mainly contributes to the expulsion of heat into space away from the atmosphere, and if sulphur dioxide decreases, global warming increases.
But even when these factors and causes are factored in, their combined effects do not explain how hot the oceans have warmed over the past year, McFadden said, pointing to parts of the North Atlantic, for example, that are currently experiencing “extraordinary ” warming, for reasons that are not yet understood.
Despite this lack of understanding, the effects of this unprecedented rise in ocean temperatures are evident around the world.
Tornadoes on the way.
Heavy rains and hurricanes are among the most prominent effects.
As the sea surface warms, the amount of evaporated moisture increases, explains researcher Healy Fowler.
At the same time, global warming is also contributing to the warming of the atmosphere.
Warmer air also has the ability to retain more moisture.
So when it rains, there's a lot of moisture.
With every one degree of warming, the likelihood of rainfall and higher humidity increases by 7 percent, according to Healy Fowler.
The speed at which storm systems condense in 2023 was staggering for meteorologists.
Fowler said: "We think this is the result of ocean warming, which in turn has accelerated the intensification of small storms into massive systems.
But the exact mechanism by which this process took place is still beyond our comprehension. ”
Active hurricanes are among the worrisome forecasts for 2024.
El Nino is also expected to turn into La Nina, which favors intense and frequent storms in the North Atlantic off the coast of Africa.
As water surface temperatures rise at record levels, storms are getting stronger, resulting in the most active hurricane season ever.
A sailor choking.
Below the surface too, the effects of warming can be severe.
From Australia to Tanzania, “coral bleaching ” is becoming more common, says Anna Kiros, a marine ecologist and climate change scientist at Plymouth Marine Laboratory in the UK.
Unlike many marine organisms, such as fish, corals cannot move if the temperature increases.
With so much of the deep sea warming, the result is “terrifying. ”
Warming ocean waters deprive marine life of oxygen as well as nutrients essential for life.
Oxygen is less soluble in hotter water, which is why surface water gets hotter before deep water, and surface water becomes less dense, making it impossible to mix with deep water. In the absence of this mixing, nutrients deposited on or near the bottom struggle to find their way into surface water where microorganisms such as phytoplankton, which form the base of the food web, need them.
Similarly, oxygen in surface water cannot make its way into deeper layers of ocean water.
As a result of this lack of oxygen, there are more bottlenecks and therefore more deaths of organisms at this bottom.
Rising sea levels
Beaches, too, cannot escape the consequences of ocean warming; as ocean temperatures rise and the density of that water decreases, more space is created for them and sea levels rise as a result.
Warming water also contributes to melting ice in Antarctica and Greenland (located between the Arctic Ocean and the Atlantic Ocean).
Over the past 140 years, sea levels around the world have risen by an average of 21 to 24 centimeters (8 to 9 inches).
According to William Sweet, a researcher with the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, sea levels are on track to rise by an average of 6-7 inches (15-18 centimeters) by 2050.

A solar storm hits the earth.
Does it affect humans?
On March 25, 2024, the U.S. Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) warned that a powerful magnetic solar storm was approaching Earth, classified as G4, the most severe category on the geomagnetic effects scale.
What are magnetic solar storms?
Magnetic solar storms are caused by massive emissions of energy from the sun, including solar wind and solar flares, and when these emissions collide with Earth magnets, disruptions affect various aspects of life on our planet.
Effects of solar storm
On human health: Solar storms may affect people with cardiovascular disease, which can cause chest pain and heart rhythm disturbances.
It can also cause insomnia, headaches, dizziness and joint pain.
On technology: Powerful solar storms can cause interruptions in satellites and wireless communications, and disrupt air and marine navigation systems.
On the environment: Solar storms may cause auroras in unusual areas, such as Europe and Asia.
Methods of protection
There is no sure way to prevent solar storms, but some steps can be taken to mitigate their effects:
Follow space weather warnings: It is important to follow space weather warnings from competent authorities, such as the US Space Weather Forecasting Center (SWPC).
Protection of electronic systems: Electronic systems must be protected by lightning protection devices and the installation of protection programs.
Prepare for power outages: It is important to store food, water and medicines in emergency situations, as well as having a backup power supply.

It may help lower high blood pressure in the short term.
A pilot study published in June 2018 in the Journal of Nutrition and Healthy Aging found that a 16: 8 ratio significantly lowered systolic blood pressure in the study ’ s 23 participants.
The systolic blood pressure is the highest number in the blood pressure reading and indicates the strength of the heart against the artery walls each time it beats.
3.
Reduce Inflammation
Animal studies suggest that both intermittent fasting and general calorie restriction can reduce inflammation levels, although clinical trials are few and far between.
4.
Lower Cholesterol
Various forms of intermittent fasting, including alternate day fasting and 5: 2, can help lower LDL (“bad ”) cholesterol, among other signs of heart health, such as blood pressure.
Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol can increase the risk of heart disease or stroke, according to the CDC.
The researchers also noted that IF reduced the presence of triglycerides, which are fats in the blood that can lead to stroke, heart attack or heart disease, according to the Mayo Clinic.
5.
Better outcomes for stroke survivors
Healthy cholesterol levels and low blood pressure play a key role in helping reduce the risk of stroke.
But that's not the only potential benefit associated with stroke from intermittent fasting.
6.
Enhance brain function
Intermittent fasting improves sharpness of mind and concentration.
There is some early research to support this idea: A study published in November 2021 in Molecular Psychiatry found that fasting every day may boost memory.
7.
Protection from cancer
A fasting diet may reduce the risk of cancer by slowing the ability of cancer cells to adapt and spread and improving the effects of cancer treatment, people undergoing cancer treatment before making changes to their diet.

Microsoft President Brad Smith said the technology firm ’ s high-profile deal with UAE-backed artificial intelligence firm G42 could eventually involve the transfer of advanced chips and tools, a move a senior Republican congressman warned could have implications for national security.
In an interview with Reuters this week, Smith said the sales agreement, much of which is being published for the first time in this report, could progress to the second phase involving the export of critical components of AI technology such as model weights, the crown jewel of AI systems that determine how powerful they are.
Smith said there was no specific timetable for the second phase.
U.S. officials say AI systems could pose national security risks, for example by facilitating the engineering of chemical, biological and nuclear weapons.
In October, the Biden administration asked makers of the largest AI systems to share details with the U.S. government.
To move forward, the deal will require approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce.
Microsoft executives said the agreement included safeguards to protect Microsoft's technology and prevent its use by Chinese entities to train artificial intelligence systems.
But these measures have not been made public, and some U.S. lawmakers question whether they are enough.
Some lawmakers are concerned about the blackout in negotiations between two private companies over terms and guarantees for the transfer of U.S. technology.
Republican Michael McCall, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told Reuters: “Despite the significant national security implications, Congress has yet to receive a comprehensive executive briefing on this agreement.
“I am concerned that there are not enough means to protect sensitive U.S.-origin technology from Chinese espionage given [the Chinese Communist Party ’ s] interests in the UAE. ”
The Commerce Department is already requesting notifications and, in many areas, export licenses to send AI chips abroad.
But the Microsoft and G42 deal highlights loopholes in U.S. laws as regulators scramble to keep up with fast-evolving technology.
Currently, for example, there is no regulation restricting the export of AI models, although McCall and a bipartisan group of lawmakers this week introduced legislation that would give U.S. officials clearer authority to do so.
Microsoft executives said the company welcomed the discussion about a new legal framework governing the transfer of artificial intelligence technology, and that the deal with the G42 binds the UAE company to US regulations as it evolves.
“Basically, what we ’ re focused on is trying to ensure that American technology can move around the world safely and securely, ” Smith said.

BEIJING (Reuters) - China ’ s commercial aircraft company COMAC is looking to Saudi Arabia as a springboard for its ambition to expand internationally as it steps up its efforts to sell aircraft abroad and enter the passenger jet market dominated by Western manufacturers.
Dongfeng He, chairman of state-owned COMAC, visited Saudi Arabia for the first time this week after welcoming a Saudi delegation to the company ’ s facilities in Shanghai in February amid a marked uptick in economic ties between the two countries.

The company, founded in 2008, is looking for international customers in a bid to compete with commercial aircraft giants Airbus and Boeing.

During the company ’ s president ’ s visit to Riyadh, the Saudi group that owns low-cost airline Flyadeal said it had invited COMAC to set up an assembly line in Jeddah, confirming to Reuters a report in the UAE-based newspaper The National.

However, following this diet intermittently, with periods of rest, did not produce any infections associated with cell aging as opposed to continuing it.
These findings point to important clinical effects, confirming the positive benefits of the keto diet, but should be enhanced by including planned breaks for maximum benefit.
Lead author of the study, David Gaius, assistant dean of research and professor of radiation oncology at the University of Texas Health Sciences Center at San Antonio, said: “Let ’ s keep in mind that 13 million Americans use the keto diet, and we say you need to take breaks from this diet or there could be long-term consequences. ”
The keto diet is a high-fat, low-carb diet, which stimulates the body to produce ketones, chemicals produced by the liver when fat is broken down, which are later used as an alternative source of energy.
Although this diet is beneficial in some health conditions and is very popular for weight loss, several infections have been reported.
“Since cellular aging is a major cause of organ disease, the results of this study have important clinical implications for understanding ketogenic diet use, as with other diets, you need to take a break from keto. ”

China Returns to Africa After Pandemic, Redoubles Mining Efforts
A Reuters analysis of lending, investment and trade data found a rebound in China ’ s economic cooperation program after its decline during the COVID-19 pandemic, with a focus on Africa.
Chinese leaders point to unprecedented two-way trade and billions of dollars earmarked for new construction projects as signs of their commitment to supporting the continent ’ s development and promoting “win-win ” cooperation.
But the data reveal even greater complexity in a relationship that remains largely focused on extractive activities and has not yet lived up to some of Beijing ’ s theses on the Belt and Road Initiative, President Xi Jinping ’ s strategy to build an infrastructure network connecting China to the world.
While China ’ s new investment in Africa increased by 114 percent last year, according to the Griffith Asia Institute at Griffith University in Australia, it has focused on minerals essential to the global energy transition and China ’ s plans to revive its struggling economy.
Those minerals, as well as oil, dominated intra-regional trade.
Africa ’ s trade deficit with China has ballooned as efforts to boost other imports from the continent, including agricultural products and manufactured goods, have stalled.
China ’ s sovereign lending, which has been Africa ’ s main source of infrastructure finance, has fallen to its lowest level in two decades, and public-private partnerships, which China has called the world ’ s new preferred investment vehicle, have not flourished.
The result is a relationship dominated by imports of African raw materials more than China aspires to.
Analysts say it resembles economic relations between Europe and the continent during the colonial era.
China rejects this analysis.
In response to questions from Reuters, China ’ s foreign ministry wrote: “Africa has the right, ability and reason to develop its foreign relations and choose its partners. ”
"China's practical support for Africa's modernization path in line with its own characteristics is welcomed by an increasing number of African countries," she said.
China ’ s investment in Africa through the Belt and Road Initiative has grown rapidly in the two decades before the COVID-19 pandemic.
Chinese companies have been building ports, hydroelectric power stations and railways across the continent with sovereign loans.
Annual lending commitments peaked at $28.4 billion in 2016, according to Boston University's Global China Initiative.
But many projects have proved unprofitable.
China cut lending allocations at a time when some governments were struggling to repay loans.
The pandemic then forced China to shut down, leading to a decline in Chinese construction projects in Africa.
A recovery in sovereign lending is not expected.
Asked about the decline in lending to African infrastructure, Chinese officials pointed out that trade generated by the Belt and Road Initiative is boosting Africa's wealth and development.
Two-way trade hit a record $282 billion last year, according to Chinese customs data.
At the same time, however, the value of Africa ’ s exports to China fell by about 7%, mainly due to lower oil prices and its trade deficit widened by 46%.
Chinese officials have sought to allay the fears of some African leaders.
At a summit in Johannesburg in August, Xi said Beijing would launch initiatives to boost the continent's industrialization and agricultural modernization, sectors African policymakers see as key to bridging trade gaps, diversifying their economies and creating jobs.
China has pledged to increase agricultural imports from Africa.

Intermittent fasting is forbidden for 4 people.
The first is pregnant.
Intermittent fasting is a dietary pattern that focuses more on the timing of food intake than the quality of food consumed, and is beginning to gain wide popularity as a diet among many to lose weight, it is based on alternating periods of eating and fasting.
Types of Intermittent Fasting
According to Onlymyhealth, it is necessary to understand intermittent fasting well and know that it is not suitable for everyone, there are several common methods of intermittent fasting, including:
Method 16 / 8
It includes fasting for 16 hours and eating during an 8-hour period.
Method 5: 2
It involves eating normally for five days a week, and restricting calories to 500-600 calories on the other two days.
Fasting method for a full 24 hours
Fasting is done for 24 hours once or twice a week.
People banned from intermittent fasting
There are categories of people who are advised to avoid intermittent fasting for health reasons, and they are:
Pregnant or lactating women
It may adversely affect the intake of necessary nutrients and the production of milk, affecting the health of the mother and child.
People with eating disorders
Intermittent fasting may exacerbate disturbed eating behaviors, especially in individuals who have a history of eating disorders such as bulimia or anorexia.
People with specific medical conditions
Such as diabetics or those with low blood pressure or other chronic health conditions.
These conditions require eating regularly to keep blood sugar levels and blood pressure within normal levels.
Children and adolescents
Children and young people need consistent nutrition to support growth and development.
Intermittent fasting can limit the nutrients necessary for their proper growth.
On the other hand, if you are considering intermittent fasting, it is important to consult your doctor, especially if you have any underlying health condition.
Your doctor can advise on whether this regimen is right for you and how to apply it safely.
Benefits of Intermittent Fasting
Although intermittent fasting is not suitable for everyone, it may carry health benefits for some people, such as:
Losing weight
It can help reduce calories and improve metabolism.
Improve blood sugar levels
It may help improve insulin sensitivity and reduce the risk of type 2 diabetes.
Improve heart health
It can reduce risk factors associated with heart disease such as cholesterol levels.
Promote brain health
It may help improve brain function and reduce the risk of Alzheimer ’ s disease.
In general, intermittent fasting can be an effective diet for weight loss and improved overall health, but not for everyone.
It is important to consider your individual health condition and consult your doctor before starting this diet to ensure maximum benefits are achieved without any health risks.

Avocado is a nutritious fruit that may not be suitable for everyone
Although an avocado is an overall healthy fruit, avocado consumption should be limited in six cases, VnExpress reports.
According to Dr. Huynh Tan Fu of Ho Chi Minh City University Hospital of Medicine and Pharmacy HCMC, avocado is rich in nutrients, as it is a good source of carbohydrates, protein, potassium, fiber, vitamin B, vitamin E, vitamin C and vitamin K. So, avocado fruit can help improve eyesight, cardiovascular and digestive system, as well as prevent osteoporosis and cancers.
But these benefits do not necessarily mean that everyone can eat as much fruit as they want, as Dr. Fu has identified six categories that recommend avoiding or limiting avocado intake, as follows:
1.
Breastfeeding mothers
Consuming too much avocado leads to a decrease in milk production for nursing mothers.
Therefore, it is recommended to limit the intake of avocados.
2.
Patients with bowel problems
Eating avocado can lead to indigestion, bloating and diarrhea in patients with bowel problems.
To avoid these problems, experts advise people with bowel problems to eat only half an avocado a day.
3.
Allergy to avocado
People who are prone to allergies experience symptoms that include nausea, headaches or suffocation after eating avocado, as an allergic reaction in their bodies.
4.
Liver Patients
Avocado contains a high amount of collagen, which may damage liver cells if not fully digested.
Thus, it is necessary for those with liver problems to limit the consumption of avocado.
5.
Medication Users
Certain types of medications, such as anticoagulants or NSAIDs, lose their effects when taken with and interacting with avocados.
Avocado can also increase the likelihood of side effects for those taking cholesterol-lowering medications.
People undergoing drug therapy should consult their doctors if they want to eat avocado.
6.
Excessive Obesity
Avocados are high in fat, so eating too much of them can lead to uncontrollable weight gain.
Therefore, it is advisable to reduce the amount of avocado in daily meals if the person is aiming to shed some excess weight or is suffering from excessive obesity.

Indicators confirm that sustainable aviation fuel will meet 0.53% of the global fuel demand in 2024, which will cost $3.75 billion, which represents an additional $2.4 billion to the cost of purchasing the same amount of aviation fuel, and the carbon dioxide emissions from the industry in 2024 is expected to reach 935 million tons from the consumption of 99 billion gallons of fuel.

Mabra announces the drafting of eight guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence in the field of public relations and media communication
Unveiling the first framework for the use of artificial intelligence in the public relations and communication sector
The Middle East Public Relations Association (MBRA), the leading public relations and communication body in the Middle East, has unveiled the first guidance document that includes a set of guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of public relations and media communication.
Through a joint collaboration between Mabra ’ s Artificial Intelligence Department and the ChatGBT platform, Mabra has developed eight guiding principles as a guiding framework for the effective and ethical use of AI for its members and others working in the field.
These principles, based on regional and global standards, form a frame of reference that helps to responsibly integrate AI into daily content production processes, along with other guidelines, policies and references.
Margaret Flanagan, co-founder of Tales & Heads and chairman of Mabra ’ s Artificial Intelligence Committee, stressed the importance of the new framework, saying:
“By formulating this framework, we are looking to promote the responsible use of AI in public relations, protect the outputs of this important field in the region, and lay the foundations of a unified methodology for the use of AI tools in various organizations, while raising awareness of the ethical and legal implications of such technologies. ”
“We believe that our responsibilities go beyond the organizations we work with, to include relevant media professionals and the wider public, especially as the continuous development of AI and the rapid change in regulations for its use prompt us to continue to develop the practical guidance and updates needed to ensure that these technologies are used responsibly and effectively. ”
Mabra ’ s Artificial Intelligence Committee includes professionals such as Ibrahim Al Mutawa, Co-Founder and Managing Director of Jumar PR; Tala Abu Taha, PR Manager at Viola Communications; Andrea Gesdal, Independent Communications Consultant; Natasha Hatheral Shaw, Founder and CEO of TishTash; and Henry Jenkins, Senior Vice President and Head of Business Marketing at First Abu Dhabi Bank Professor Dalia Mahmoud, European University of Applied Sciences; Joseph Nalore, Head of Communication Control, School of Communication, Murdoch University Dubai; Kirsty O ’ Connor, Regional Director of Innovation, Hill & Knowlton; Nada Shelton, Senior Vice President of Communication, Mubadala Group; Enka Steever, Professor of Practice, Zayed University, School of Communication and Media Sciences; and Denise Graemin, Director of Operations Qatar for Advertising and Advertising.
The guidelines issued include:
1.
Integrity and transparency: referring to the use of AI every time it is used in public relations and media communications to ensure trust.
This involves having a prior dialogue with customers or line managers to inform them about the reliance on AI platforms and how they are being used.
That doesn ’ t mean you have to go back to them every time, as specific standards for the use of AI can be agreed upon.
When you are asked directly whether you have used AI in a particular project, you have to be honest and transparent.
If you are asked not to use artificial intelligence in a particular project, you must abide by these instructions.
We recommend best practice recommendations, such as the University of Cambridge recommendations on the optimal use of text, audio and video AI tools.
It is necessary to keep abreast of the legal materials on this subject in order to keep up with the constant change of the proposed bills in the definition of intellectual property and the fair use of creative content.
2.
Responsibility and credibility: It is essential that the PR and media communications industry be honest about the use of AI in content sent to the media.
Transparency in the use of AI is not limited to customers and co-workers, but includes content that is shared with the media.
Photos, videos and audio clips that will be sent to the media when created using AI should always be clearly marked.
It is preferable that the entire textual content of the media be written by the staff or at least with their explicit intervention.
If artificial intelligence is used, a signal should be clearly placed.
Concerns are growing today about misinformation and misinformation leading to a decline in trust in the media.
Content created using artificial intelligence further erodes this trust.
It is the responsibility of public relations and media communication experts to provide the media with content that does not compromise the reputation of the media or reduce its credibility to the target audience.
Therefore, a plan must be developed to address any problem or crisis that arises as a result of providing the media with content created by artificial intelligence.
3.
Respect privacy: Ensure that all AI tools used follow privacy laws and use copyrighted content.
Always remember that the data you provide with AI tools, including files, order form and your account information, is saved and used as a standard procedure by the companies that manage the AI tools.
Therefore, it is important to know the privacy settings and what data you can hand over to an AI tool and which data should not be shared to ensure the integrity of the information.
It is common knowledge that the public relations and media communications sector deals with a lot of sensitive information about customers and companies, including government institutions and companies listed on the stock exchange.
To reduce risk, data and files that are not confidential or that are already available to the public can be entered.
You should also familiarize yourself with and adhere to data security protocols and non-disclosure agreements regarding the use of AI for your customers or organization.
4.
Using artificial intelligence correctly: Ensure the accuracy and accuracy of the content issued by the artificial intelligence before sharing it to avoid spreading false information.
Reference should be made to reliable sources to verify the facts, such as scientific reference studies, a known third party or a reliable media outlet.
Look for original sources and research findings whenever possible instead of using unreliable references.
AI is known to compose facts, figures and even links to non-existent research and media stories, so do not assume the validity of the information it provides, and it is necessary to ensure that our sector does not contribute to the dissemination of false information.
When dealing with content in Arabic, remember that AI tools work with a much smaller content base compared to English.
So you ’ ll need more human intervention and editing and additional fact-checking.
5.
Fairness: Attention should be paid to cultural considerations or unfair biases in AI programs and content to ensure inclusiveness and fairness.
Machine learning programs have proven to adopt and amplify some biased human ideas, which means that AI-generated content may be misleading or contribute to amplifying stereotypes.
Therefore, the texts, images and audio generated by artificial intelligence should always be reviewed very carefully.
Using well-thought-out request formats can help to get more comprehensive content.
Because there are so many biases within current technologies, it is our responsibility to review the results and make sure they represent our customers, organizations, cultures and communities.
It is our duty to think about people whose voices are not being embraced in AI content while referencing other sources and drawing on their expertise.
6.
Create real content: AI can be used to help get work done, but remember that it is human creativity and strong relationships that ensure effective communication.
Remember that the ability of AI is limited to relying on existing sources and references, not innovation.
Although detailed demand formulas may help control the type of outcome, machines connect information in a different way than humans, they do not use the senses of sight, smell and taste and have no emotions.
Better text or better image is what drives us to feel differently, and no one can do it so far better than creative people.
7.
Thinking about people: The use of AI may affect society, so make sure you use it to help people and not just serve your goals.
Encourage your team and everyone in the industry to use AI fairly and responsibly.
The use of artificial intelligence is leading to huge consequences that cannot be known or predicted at the moment.
These consequences range from the possibility that a person may lose some jobs, create new jobs, or cause more inclusiveness or more segregation.
These consequences can only be known in due course.
All we can do now is consciously use AI technologies, including practical steps such as not holding customers accountable for work done by AI as a human substitute, and using the skills of editors, content writers, designers and photographers in cases where these skills add irreplaceable value, including work we send to the media.
These conscious practices also involve using artificial intelligence to help us make better decisions rather than trusting technology to make those decisions entirely.
8.
Keep learning and evolving: Keeping abreast of the latest changes in the PR and media communications sector as a result of the use of artificial intelligence, and being prepared to adapt and use this technology optimally.
As AI continues to evolve, laws and regulations governing its use in various markets and sectors are evolving.
We will often see more changes in the future because of the tremendous technological development and our reliance on these developments in new ways.
We are also likely to see more controversy over intellectual property and copyright, such as the New York Times lawsuit against Microsoft, which could have major repercussions on the media, public relations and media communications sector, as well as growing concerns about the use of artificial intelligence to spread misinformation.
It is our responsibility to follow up and ensure that we use artificial intelligence ethically and legally.

Africa does not benefit from mineral boom despite expensive technology
Africa does not benefit from mineral boom despite expensive technology
Technology is increasingly impacting the way people live around the world, creating opportunities in some cases and posing new challenges in others.
Any particular technology, through its individual components and materials, can be traced back to its origins, making the question of the source of those components and materials important.
Technology, economies, livelihoods and modern weapons rely on important minerals such as magnesium, cobalt, lithium or even copper, the majority of which are found in Africa.
As Africa is home to 30 percent of the world ’ s known important minerals, the continent is at the forefront of talks.
Alexander Tripp, associate director of the Atlantic Council ’ s Africa Center, argues in a report published by the institute that at present, African countries are not getting their fair share of the benefits of the important mineral boom and the hustle caused by the development of modern technologies.
For that to happen, Africa will need to invest more in its capacity to refine or add value to minerals within the continent, and such investment could fuel a long-awaited development push.
Unless African countries can break their history of acting only as a supplier of minerals, they will be left behind.
Africa is home to many important mineral reserves, but it is not home to an industry that adds value to minerals.
While Africa has some capacity to process and refine some minerals, significant value-added strides in this sector are still lacking.
Africa will therefore not reap the benefits of the important mineral boom associated with mineral extraction, as concrete action towards the long-awaited value chain development and investment goal on the continent remains elusive.
The African Union and many African nations have long recognized the continent's need to tap its mineral wealth, rather than provide minerals to the rest of the world for others to process and then reap economic benefits.
In 2009, the African Union released its African Mining Vision, which highlighted the importance of the value-added industry.
In 2019, the African Union released the African Commodity Strategy, which calls for transforming Africa from a mere raw material supplier to a continent integrated into global value chains.
The African Union has established an African Mineral Development Centre to coordinate and oversee the implementation of the African Mining Vision.
Since its establishment in 2016, however, the Centre has not been ratified by a sufficient number of Member States, meaning it has not been fully operational.
Metals are important.
Africa is home to many important mineral reserves, but not home to an industry that adds value to minerals.
The global market for lithium battery recycling alone was worth $6.5 billion in 2022 and is expected to reach $35 billion by 2031.
On the public investment side, the United States has published funding and regulatory incentives for battery recycling.
The European Union has adopted a regulation setting out the target percentages for the recovery of vital metals from batteries.
Part of the regulation includes the introduction of a new “battery passport, ” a digital record that accompanies each battery and includes information about its history and components to ensure responsible recycling.
Besides efforts to increase battery recycling, there are also ongoing initiatives to develop batteries that do not rely on rare earth elements.
Private investment in battery replacement research and alternative materials is on the rise, and with it is also likely that the economic benefits of today ’ s important mineral boom will outweigh Africa.
Today, the world needs what Africa needs, but that may not be the case tomorrow.
INVESTMENT
If Africa is to truly benefit from the boom and momentum of important minerals, it will need support in developing its ability to add value to its minerals.
The Lobito Corridor project is the cornerstone of U.S. public investment in Africa ’ s mining sector today, which is looking to stretch more than 1,000 miles of railways to help transport vital minerals from Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo to a port in Angola.
Some experts see U.S. and EU investment as an attempt to counter China, amid concerns about Beijing ’ s dominant position in the region ’ s vital metals market.
Ideally, investing in Africa ’ s vital minerals sector would support the continent ’ s ability to add value to minerals before shipping.
But efforts are needed beyond limited U.S. and European investment compared to China, which ultimately aims to help transport and export important minerals.
The relationship between Africa ’ s natural mineral wealth and the continent ’ s strategic importance to the United States is not new.
The United States has sought to acquire minerals vital to Africa, for its geopolitical goals.
The uranium used in the atomic bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in Japan is known to have come from the Shinkolubwe mine in the Congo.
Tripp believes that intense competition over mineral extraction, national security and supply chains will transcend Africa unless the opportunity is seized.
The Africa Centre task force aims to bring together stakeholders from the United States, Europe and Africa, including representatives of the financial sector, development institutions and government.
The group will meet regularly to explore the role and potential of African minerals in critical supply chains, strategies to further engage African states and suppliers, and ways to mobilize the private sector.
The task force will host public talks on topics ranging from the need for (and how best to facilitate) private investment to domestic African policymaking.
The team hopes to contribute to building a new business model and development through strategic and win-win partnerships.
If Africa is to truly benefit from the boom and momentum of important minerals, it will need support in developing its ability to add value to its minerals.
Unless African countries can break their history of acting only as a supplier of minerals, they will be left behind.

Research shows that dust storms coming from the Sahara Desert can severely damage solar energy production.
So, what can be done to better manage this problem?
Climate Now reports from Andalusia on efforts to beat the dust.
Announcement
On this month ’ s episode of Climate Now, we set out to southern Spain to report on the growing problem of Sahara dust, which has a significant impact on solar power generation.
Our visit to southern Spain comes as the Copernicus Climate Change Authority announced that we have seen the highest ever recorded temperature for May 2024, registering a temperature rise of 0.65 ° C above the 1991-2020 average.
This is the 12th consecutive month with the highest recorded temperature for the month in question.
In May 2024, we witnessed extreme weather conditions in many areas.
Floods in Brazil have displaced more than half a million people, temperatures in the Delhi region of India hit 49.9 degrees Celsius, its highest recorded to date, and Finland issued a heatwave warning of temperatures rising to more than 27 degrees Celsius.
In Europe, heavy rains led to flooding in southwestern Germany, Belgium, and northern Italy.
Massive losses in solar power generation due to Sahara dust
The dust of the Sahara Desert in Europe is famous for turning its skies orange, which reduces air quality and leaves a fine layer of dust on the roofs of homes and cars.
On the other hand, it causes another growing problem known as “dirty ” solar cells.
At Gianni University in Andalusia, we met with Dr. Eduardo Fernández and Professor Florencia Almonacid, who were among the authors of a recent paper that found that the severe dirt on the panels in March 2022 reduced solar capacity by up to 80 percent.
Dr Fernandez told Euronews: “It felt like we were on Mars where everything turned red. ”
March 2022 saw extreme weather, but even small amounts of dust could reduce the amount of sunlight reaching solar cells by 15%, and with the rapid growth of solar energy in Europe, losses from dirt could account for billions of euros a year.
Therefore, the research team at Jian University is using photovoltaic laboratories to find solutions.
Some scientists focus on developing dust-resistant layers, while others look at how dust accumulates with different weather conditions, such as high and low temperatures, and low rainfall.
There are many variables that need to be taken into account.
For example, dust grains may be of different sizes or colors, and can affect how well solar panel installations perform.
Even design elements make a difference, such as whether a painting is frameless or has a solid lip around its tip.
Professor Almonacid says that Sahara dust is particularly problematic: "Sahara dust particles are very fine.
It ’ s especially hard to clean. ”
The Cost and Benefit Dilemma of Solar Panel Cleaning
Renewable energy company Sonnedix faces the grime challenge every day, monitoring production from each solar power generation site and carefully calculating when cleaning PV panels is commercially feasible.
The cost of cleaning is considerable – around €400-500 per megawatt – so there are difficult choices to make depending on how the power plant is priced.
Joanne Fernandez, chief operating officer of the company, told Euronews: “As you generate electricity, every kilowatt-hour is important for the plant ’ s revenue, so this dust weather has a big impact. ”
He is now working with meteorologists to help plan cleaning sessions according to dirt weather conditions, and the amount of rainfall, as light spray may increase the soiling of the panels, and heavy rain may wash them away for free.
“Severe dust storms coming from the Sahara desert could actually lead to a significant reduction in production within the network, and this could cause a significant problem for the network operator, ” he explains.
“So forecasting, forecasting, and the ability to proactively manage the network is the most important, ” he says.
Announcement
Have dust storms from the Sahara increased due to climate change?
The recent increase in dust storms coming from the Sahara desert could be the result of natural climate variability, or it could be caused by something else.
A spokesman for the Copernicus Meteorological Authority told Euronews: “Although the arrival of dust plumes from the Sahara to Europe is not unusual, there has been an increase in the intensity and frequency of such weather conditions in recent years, and may be attributed to changes in atmospheric circulation patterns. ”
There is some speculation that these changes in atmospheric air circulation patterns are linked to climate change.
Dust expert Dr. Eduardo Fernandez says: “Scientists are always cautious about drawing conclusions, and that should be the case, right? ”
“But what we ’ re seeing is that there ’ s been a dramatic increase in extreme weather conditions, not just in terms of slabs getting dirty, but also in terms of rainfall and wind blowing.
“We are recording more dust storms coming from the Sahara, and they are increasingly penetrating into larger areas in northern Europe, and there is, of course, suspicion that global warming is the cause, ” he concludes.

The study showed that social factors can make exercise more difficult for some people than others, and found that young teens who exercise a lot may not be so when they get older.
Study author and epidemiologist Kirsten Pepins Domingo of the University of California, San Francisco explained that adolescents and those in their early 20s may be physically active but these patterns change with age.
Several studies have shown that exercise lowers blood pressure, but the new research suggests that “maintaining physical activity during adulthood — at levels higher than previously recommended — may be particularly important for preventing high blood pressure, ” Domingo says.
High blood pressure is a serious condition that affects hundreds of millions of people worldwide, can lead to heart attacks or strokes, and is a risk factor for dementia later in life.
According to the World Health Organization, more than one in four men and one in five women suffer from high blood pressure, but most people with high blood pressure do not know they have it, which is why it is called the “silent killer ”.
In the new study, more than 5,100 adults were recruited, and their health was tracked over three decades through physical assessments and questionnaires about their exercise habits and smoking status.
In each clinical evaluation, blood pressure was measured three times, one minute apart, and to analyze the data, participants were grouped into four categories, by race and gender.
Across the board, levels of physical activity declined from age 18 to 40, with high rates of hypertension and decreased physical activity over subsequent decades.
According to the researchers, this suggests that youth is an important window of intervention to prevent high blood pressure in middle age through health promotion programs designed to promote exercise.
Lead author Jason Nagata, an expert at the University of California, San Francisco, said: “Nearly half of the participants in adulthood had suboptimal levels of physical activity, which was significantly associated with the onset of high blood pressure, suggesting that we need to raise minimum standards of physical activity. ”
When researchers looked at people who exercised five hours of moderate exercise per week during early adulthood, twice the current recommended minimum for adults, they found that this level of activity significantly reduced the risk of high blood pressure, especially if people continued exercising after they were older.
In their paper, the researchers wrote: “Achieving at least twice the current minimum adult physical activity guidelines may be more beneficial for preventing high blood pressure than simply meeting the minimum guidelines. ”
“This may be particularly the case after high school when opportunities for physical activity diminish as young people transition to college, the workforce, parenthood, and leisure time erodes, ” Nagata said.

Generative AI technology is impressive thanks to its ability to produce new and innovative content, but it also carries risks and challenges that require effective management.
Risks associated with the use of generative artificial intelligence
Abuse:
Cyber attacks and fraud: Generative AI is used to create deep fakes that are used for fraud, identity theft, and election manipulation.
Deceptive Campaigns: Fraudsters can use artificial intelligence to create misleading campaigns, resulting in the dissemination of incorrect or harmful information.
Incorrect information (hallucinations):
Inaccurate outputs: AI may produce false or misleading information, causing legal or reputational problems.
For example, OpenAI was sued for providing ChatGPT with false information.
Post content without validation:
• The spread of fake news: AI-generated content can spread quickly without being validated, causing economic and social damage.
For example, a fake video of a Tesla car crash or a fake photo of a Pentagon explosion.
How to reduce the risks of generative artificial intelligence
Mitigating the risks of abuse:
Develop principles and guidelines:
• Organizations should develop clear policies for the use of generative AI that align with the organization ’ s ethical values to ensure no harm is caused.
Watermark the content:
• All AI-generated content should have clear watermarks, which helps verify the source of the content and reduce the spread of fake content.
Creating a control environment in artificial intelligence:
• Organizations can develop their own large language models (LLMs), allowing them to control privacy and ensuring models are trained on unbiased datasets.
Mitigating the risks associated with publishing fake content:
Awareness in the field of artificial intelligence:
Companies should provide training programs to raise awareness of the responsible use of AI, and define clear policies on when and how the technology can be used.
Validation of outputs:
Specialized systems should be developed to validate content published online, reducing the risk of publishing fake content and enhancing public confidence in available information.
Generative AI holds great potential for improving productivity and innovation, but it requires careful risk management.
By establishing clear policies, validating content, and educating employees, organizations can make the most of this technology while minimizing potential risks.
