8 Excellent Genre-Bending Sci-Fi Tales To Take You to the Next Frontier

This content contains affiliate links. When you buy through these links, we may earn an affiliate commission.

Lyndsie Manusos

Senior Contributor

Lyndsie Manusos’s fiction has appeared in PANK, SmokeLong Quarterly, and other publications. She holds an MFA from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago and has worked in web production and content management. When she’s not nesting among her books and rough drafts, she’s chasing the baby while the dog watches in confused amusement. She lives with her family in a suburb of Indianapolis.

Prophet by Sin Blaché and Helen Macdonald, published by Grove Atlantic

The must-read queer sci-fi thriller of the summer! In a world just one perilous step from our own, an unlikely pair sets out on the most dangerous and otherwordly mission of their lives. When a diner suddenly appears in a remote field, Adam and Rao are confronted with the most devastating weapon they have ever seen: Prophet. No one knows who created it, or why, but this spooky substance is bringing happy memories to life, then stifling people with their own joy. Despite their troubled past, the two are drawn closer than ever to defend what they hold most dear.

As I said in my 2022 science fiction subgenre primer, the genre of science fiction is expanding. Like our universe, it is expanding quickly, redefined with every story, be it short or long-form. And beneath the large umbrella of science fiction, subgenres are added and redefined. All in all, there are endless ways to tell a science fiction story (don’t let any old guard tell you different).

And then — subgenres aside — there is genre-bending science fiction. There is science fiction that centers horror and science fiction that is fabulist and weird. There’s science fantasy, as well as science fiction romance. There’s science fiction that is nearly unclassifiable, a mixture of so many things, or even all the things. I’ve mentioned in my Book Riot oeuvre that genre-bending of any shape or size is my kind of work. When writers are bold and brave in their genre weaving, that’s when the hairs on the back of my neck stand to attention. That’s when I rub my hands together and think, “oh, this is going to be good.”

Genre-bending science fiction doesn’t have to be confined to the novel form, either. Short fiction science fiction is in a golden age right now. Check out the latest finalists and winners for the Nebula, Hugo, and Locus awards, and I promise you will find mindblowing, genre-bending, exceptional work.

Below I will showcase eight tremendous genre-bending science fiction tales, ranging from short stories to novels, and everything in between. I believe I’ve mentioned at least one in a previous post from last year, but you’ll notice the genre coverage is different. Ergo, these stories are genre-bending.

In any case, I hope you’ll enjoy these stories as much as I do.

Genre-Bending Science Fiction: Novels & Novellas

Remote Control by Nnedi Okorafor

Fatima had a past before she became known as Sankofa. Before those around her called her the adopted daughter of the Angel of Death. With a mere glance, an entire town could fall. But before that, the world was different.

So much of what Okorafor writes is genre-bending science fiction (the Binti trilogy!). This novella begins in an almost fantasy-horror like fashion: Sankofa walking, leaving fear and horror in her wake. But as the story unfolds, it becomes this all-encompassing tale of African futurism, how the world shapes us, and then how we might reshape the world.

Hexwood by Diana Wynne Jones

One of the things I love about including this book is seeing this title on Goodreads and reading all the genres it’s described as. Hint: it’s like all the genres. Fantasy, science fiction, time travel, magic, dragons, robots, portals, you name it, Hexwood probably has it. And clearly, none of this should surprise you coming from the legendary Diana Wynne Jones.

The tale follows Ann Stavely as she watches people disappear through the farm’s gate. She meets a sorcerer, and time begins to move differently in the woods nearby. Little does she know that far beyond Earth, Controller Borasus receives word that an ancient machine has been awakened.

I mean, clearly, genre-bending at its finest.

Escape Velocity by Victor Manibo

I love how Victor Manibo is always able to craft the perfect mystery within his brilliant science fiction worlds. Manibo is a master at showing Earth just around corner, especially if we keep on our current trajectory. Picture a world of hyper-capitalism, a luxury liner — Space Habitat Altaire —and a ruthless world of amassing “points” in order for the chance to start a new life on Mars.

Now, add a decadent mystery of whodunit with a sprinkle of who’s willing to do anything to get what they want: Ava wants to find out who murdered her brother; Laz wants to win Ava’s heart; Sloane wants to collect secrets as his family’s wealth declines; Henry will do whatever it takes to get to Mars.

And all this is set during a class reunion on a luxury space liner, with twists and turns you won’t see coming. Get your science fiction Knives Out fix with this one.

Borne by Jeff VanderMeer

I still think about this book. I still think about Borne and that giant bear, Mord. This book is solidly science fiction, but it’s also just fucking weird. That’s honestly the best way to describe it, too, which is why I love it so much. It’s post-apocalyptic, and it manages to be both epic and extremely intimate.

Rachel is trying to survive in a world that wants to kill her at every turn. Then she finds Borne, an amorphous creature, in the fur of a Godzilla-sized bear named Mord. Rachel cannot bring herself, nor allow her lover Wick, to destroy Borne. Borne reminds her of better times and better places, and an attachment grows between them. This book is personal as well as out of this world. It’s weird fiction at its finest. It’s science fiction at its most profound.

Genre-Bending Science Fiction: Short Form

This list includes short fiction, though that ranges in word count. Below you’ll find tales that are short stories or novelettes.

Foxfire, Foxfire” by Yoon Ha Lee from Beneath Ceaseless Skies

Let me begin by saying that the publication of this story is in a highly respected (and one of my personal favorites) genre magazine called Beneath Ceaseless Skies. Its mission: to publish the very best in “literary adventure fantasy.” And yet, this story also has beautifully crafted science fiction elements.

This novelette follows Baekdo, a magical, shapeshifting fox who is able to speak to gods. Baekdo is set on becoming human, which requires him to kill — and devour the liver of — 100 humans. Baekdo has no qualms about coming to his 100th kill, but things don’t go as planned. Baekdo’s 100th victim is the pilot of a Cataphract, a giant battle mech. Baekdo swears on the tiger-sages that he will keep his oath with the pilot, Jong, and finish her mission. It’s an intimate, magical tale while also being epic in scope. Truly, a genre-bending masterpiece.

The Gondoliers” by Karen Russell from Orange World and Other Stories

Karen Russell is a masterful genre-bending writer. I fell in love with Russell’s work over ten years ago, with her first collection St. Lucy’s Home for Girls Raised by Wolves. Like Kelly Link, Russell was vital in redefining, for me at least, what fiction, especially literary fiction, can do. “The Gondoliers” is a wonderful example of this.

It follows Janelle Picarro, a.k.a Blister, in a post-apocalyptic world where parts of Florida have fully submerged underwater and is now called New Florida. Blister is a gondolier, ferrying people across the waters. Blister and her sisters use echolocation to communicate and steer. There is a little bit of everything in this story, and you won’t be the same when you reach the end.

Memories of Memories Lost” by Mahmud El Sayed from khōréō

khōréō is one of my favorite speculative fiction magazines. “In Memories of Memories Lost,” El Sayed crafts a devastatingly personal short story of memory, loss, and sacrifice.

After aliens take over Earth, humans must pay a “memory tax” to their cosmic invaders. The story follows Ahmed, who chooses, for his tax, to give a large family memory in the form of a heirloom. In doing so, he can assure the comfort of his father, who suffers from dementia. It’s a story of complex relationships and love. It’s a story that begs hard questions of ourselves, our souls, and our loved ones: What if we could give traumatic memories away? Would we regret the loss?

The Dizzy Room” by Kristina Ten from Nightmare Magazine

Look, I know I’ve mentioned this story before, and it’s because the story is that good. Published in the renowned horror magazine Nightmare, this story is about a video game, but it’s also a horror story about memory and language. There are images and a multitude of sensory details that will haunt me forever.

This is science fiction horror at its best, with a mounting dread that will have you tempted to lean back while also leaning forward, closer to the page, admittedly desperate to hear the sounds of the game itself beckoning you. I am not at all surprised that this story is a finalist for the 2023 Shirley Jackson Awards.

Find Genre-Bending Stories Everywhere

Every genre has trailblazers, writers who take a genre and build upon it, question and criticize it, and remold it into something new. These are the writers I seek out again and again to dissect and study these genres, rediscovering them and also falling in love with them all over again. They are out there now, and their stories are waiting.

If you’re interested in more genre-bending work, check out these other Book Riot gems:

Who invented the first quantum computer?

Who invented the first quantum computer?

**The first quantum computer was invented by a group of researchers led by physicist Isaac Chuang and computer scientist Neil Gershenfeld in 1998.**

Quantum computing has undoubtedly revolutionized the world of technology and opened up new possibilities for solving complex problems. As this fascinating field continues to grow, many people wonder who can be credited with the invention of the very first quantum computer. Well, the answer lies with a group of brilliant scientists who pushed the boundaries of computation to a whole new level.

What were the key contributions of Isaac Chuang and Neil Gershenfeld?

Isaac Chuang, a physicist, and Neil Gershenfeld, a computer scientist, collaborated in the 1990s to create the first practical quantum computer using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques.

How did their quantum computer work?

Chuang and Gershenfeld’s quantum computer utilized the principles of quantum mechanics, including quantum superposition and entanglement, to perform computations.

What breakthroughs did their quantum computer achieve?

Their quantum computer successfully executed Shor’s algorithm, which is capable of factoring large numbers exponentially faster than classical computers.

How did their invention impact the field of quantum computing?

Chuang and Gershenfeld’s invention marked a significant milestone in the development of quantum computers, inspiring subsequent researchers to explore new approaches and technologies for building more scalable and efficient quantum systems.

What limitations did the first quantum computer face?

The first quantum computer faced several limitations, including a high error rate due to the susceptibility of the NMR-based technology to decoherence.

Did Chuang and Gershenfeld receive recognition for their achievement?

Yes, their groundbreaking work gained recognition, and they were awarded the prestigious Richard P. Feynman Prize in Nanotechnology in 2001.

Has quantum computing technology improved since then?

Absolutely! Since Chuang and Gershenfeld’s invention, quantum computing has made tremendous strides with advancements in hardware design, quantum algorithms, error correction techniques, and the emergence of various quantum computing platforms.

Are there other researchers who significantly contributed to quantum computing?

Certainly! A multitude of researchers and scientists around the world has made notable contributions to the development of quantum computing, further expanding our understanding and capabilities in this field.

What are the potential applications of quantum computing?

Quantum computing has the potential to revolutionize various industries, including cryptography, drug discovery, optimization problems, material science, and artificial intelligence.

Are quantum computers currently commercially available?

Although quantum computers are still in the early stages of development, there are some commercially available quantum computers offered by companies like IBM, Google, and Honeywell.

How far are we from achieving quantum supremacy?

Quantum supremacy refers to a point where a quantum computer can perform a calculation that is infeasible for any classical computer. While there have been promising demonstrations, achieving true quantum supremacy at scale is still a significant endeavor.

What are the biggest challenges in quantum computing today?

Some of the significant challenges in quantum computing include quantum decoherence, error correction, scaling up the number of qubits, and improving hardware reliability.

In conclusion, Isaac Chuang and Neil Gershenfeld can be credited for inventing the first quantum computer in 1998, marking a pivotal moment in the history of computing. Their pioneering work has inspired countless researchers, leading to remarkable advancements in quantum computing technology. As we continue to unravel the potential of this exciting field, it is crucial to acknowledge the many researchers who have contributed to shaping the future of quantum computing.

The seven health benefits of cold showers

With growing evidence and potential risks, we speak to experts about taking the plunge

There are gentler ways to start the day than with an ice-cold shower, yet the potential health benefits – warding off illness, improving mood and helping with weight loss – could just be enough to make you consider braving the chill.

Prof Mike Tipton, a physiologist at the University of Portsmouth, has spent four decades studying how temperature affects our health. It’s a promising area of new research and, coupled with anecdotal accounts, might persuade you to turn the dial down to cold.

“For the people who say, I feel alive, awake, it sets me up for the day, I’m not going to knock it in any way. But there’s work to be done to figure out the mechanism,” he says. Read on to find out why. 

1. Boosts your immune system

One of the most rigorous studies into cold showers involved 3,000 volunteers in the Netherlands turning the water to as cold as possible for the final 30, 60 or 90 seconds of their shower. A control group showered as normal.

After three months, results showed that those who included a cold water blast in their shower had taken 29 per cent fewer sick days – regardless of how long the water was cold for. 

“My particular hypothesis is that the sudden change in skin temperature is driving a lot of the beneficial changes,” says Prof Tipton. “That sudden fall produces the cold shock response – a gasp, hyperventilation and increasing workload in the heart. 

“Because it’s part of a fight or flight response, you’re activating the stress hormones, serotonin goes up and beta endorphins increase,” which contributes to boosting the immune system to ward off illness, he says.

Longer exposure to cold water is, of course, fatal, accounting for 60 per cent of deaths in cold water, Prof Tipton says.

“This is a very double edged sword. A minute in cold water may prime your immune system, five minutes may actually impair it. It’s the dose of cold that’s critical.”

2. Enhances mental health

Exposure to cold water may drastically improve mental health in patients, even when drugs have failed to do so, research suggests.

One study by Prof Tipton and colleagues found that weekly cold-water swimming helped to ease a 24-year-old woman’s depression. She had previously spent seven years battling the condition, during which medication failed to reduce her symptoms. 

“She said that she was the happiest she could remember being. A year later, she was drug-free and open water swimming. She’d overcome a big challenge in her mind,” he says. 

It’s not clear if a cold shower could have the same effect. “It may be the distraction of the cold water [that eased her depression]. When exposed to cold water, most people say all they can think about is the temperature and it takes their mind off everything else,” he says.

However, improvements in her mental health could also be down to the exercise involved in cold water swimming, overcoming the challenge of the cold, or the social inclusion of swimming with others, he noted.

“Is it the cold, or is it any one of these other things? We won’t know until there are studies that isolate cold exposure,” Prof Tipton adds.

3. Improves skin and hair health

Lukewarm water is the ideal for face washing, as it effectively removes dirt, oil and impurities without causing excessive dryness or irritation, explains Dr Anastasia Therianou, a consultant dermatologist on Harley Street and at Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust.

However, cold water constricts blood vessels in the skin, which can reduce redness and inflammation – so can improve the appearance of skin, she says.

When it comes to hair, a cold shower can help lock in moisture. “Cold water closes the hair cuticles, so the hydration is ‘trapped’ inside the hair,” Dr Therianou says. “This is beneficial for people with thin hair that tends to break easily. However, cold water cannot fully remove the excessive oils from the scalp so it’s advisable to wash your hair in warm water and then condition and rinse using cold water – if you can bear it.”

4. Supports weight loss

A review of more than 100 studies suggested cold water immersion, such as swimming or a cold bath, can activate and expand brown adipose tissue – a “good” fat that burns calories – and also reduce “bad” white fat, and therefore aid weight loss.

“The brown fat cells develop from white fat cells and, as their energy source, they like free fatty acids which they get from the white fat cells,” explains James Mercer, a professor emeritus at The Arctic University of Norway who co-authored the review. “By reducing the content of free fatty acids in the white fat cells, theoretically, one loses weight.”

However, scientists have not yet investigated whether a cold shower would also trigger this process. “My gut feeling is no, since the development of brown fat in cold water swimmers seems to require a very strong cold stimulus which I do not think you would get from a short cold shower,” says Prof Mercer.

“A cold shower doesn’t provide the same stimulus as being immersed in cold water, as only about a third of the body is exposed to the cold,” says Prof Tipton. “As a result, the cold shock response is roughly about a third of the size it would be in an immersion. That doesn’t mean it’s not big enough to have a positive effect – but nobody’s done the study.”

5. Relieves muscle soreness and accelerates recovery

Athletes frequently turn to ice baths to aid their recovery, the idea being that the cold reduces blood flow, swelling and inflammation of the muscles.

Cold showers could have a similar effect, as the cold water is an analgesic (painkiller) and may be enough to decrease swelling, says Prof Tipton. 

However, he notes that while there is “some evidence” cold water can help muscle aches, the evidence “is not convincing across the board”. For example, some studies suggest that cold water actually lowers protein generation, which is vital for building and repairing muscle.

6. Aids in pain relief and reduces migraines

There’s anecdotal evidence of cold baths and cold water swimming easing very severe migraines, Prof Tipton notes. These accounts suggest short-term exposure to the cold may ease pain, he says.

Cold receptors are located about 0.18mm below the skin surface and, when skin temperature drops quickly, these fire off an enormous amount of information to the central nervous system and the subsequent gasping changes blood flow in the brain, he explains. 

A reduction in pain could be down to a combination of those two things or other factors,” he says.

7. Enhances mood and promotes emotional wellbeing

There’s anecdotal evidence from cold water swimmers that it dramatically improves their mood and wellbeing, says Prof Tipton. “I work with the Bluetits [an outdoor swimming group in Pembrokeshire] and I am overwhelmed by the accounts of people who say it has changed their life. People are in tears about it.

“The vast majority of people who report benefits, say it’s to their mental wellbeing, although the mechanism behind this effect is unclear. The cold water is clearly activating people and waking them up, which will be down to the cold shock response and the release of stress hormones.”


Health risks to consider before having a cold shower

Before stepping into a cold shower, it’s important to consider if you’re in good enough health to do so, says Prof Tipton.

“We’re a tropical animal that wants to be naked in 28C. Taking that animal and showering it with 10 or 12C water is a really stressful thing to do,” he says. 

The cold triggers cold water shock, which is a gasp of breath, followed by rapid breathing and high blood pressure. While this can be beneficial for some over a short time, it will become detrimental to everyone with time, so people should stay in a cold shower for no more than one minute.

It is especially dangerous for people with cardiovascular disease, aneurysms or heart problems and they therefore shouldn’t try it, Prof Tipton says.

Other complications of cold water that could affect anyone include hypothermia and non-freezing cold injury, he warns, is damage to the small nerves and blood vessels of the hands and feets that can last for life.

Scientists integrate solid-state spin qubits with nanomechanical resonators

In a new Physical Review Letters study, scientists propose a new method for combining solid-state spin qubits with nanomechanical resonators for scalable and programmable quantum systems.

Quantum information processing requires qubits to have long coherence times, stability, and be scalable. Solid-state spin qubits are the candidates being pursued for these applications as they possess long-coherence times. However, they are not scalable.

The PRL study, led by Frankie Fung, a graduate student in Professor Mikhail Lukin's group at Harvard University, addressed this challenge while speaking to Phys.org.

He said, "While small quantum registers using solid-state spin qubits have been demonstrated, they rely on magnetic dipolar interactions, which limit the interaction range to tens of nanometers. The short interaction distance and difficulty fabricating spin qubits consistently at such close spacings make it challenging to control systems containing large arrays of qubits."

In the PRL study, the researchers proposed an architecture that mediates the interaction between spin qubits using a nanomechanical , a mechanical oscillator.

Diamonds as qubits

The team's approach relied on nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamonds acting as qubits.

Typically, diamond structures consist of in a tetrahedral structure, meaning they are bonded to four other carbon atoms.

However, using methods like , one of the carbon atoms can be substituted with a nitrogen atom. This results in a missing carbon atom adjacent to the nitrogen, creating a vacancy.

The nitrogen atom adjacent to a vacancy forms the NV center, which has an unpaired electron with spin states used as qubits.

The NV centers offer many advantages due to their unique optical properties. They have long coherence times, meaning their interaction with the environment is low, making them very stable.

Additionally, they are optically compatible, which means that it is easy to input and output information using light. Since they have unpaired electrons, they are also highly sensitive to magnetic fields.

These properties make them ideal to be used as qubits, especially when integrating them with solid-state devices.

The problem arises due to the short-range interaction between the qubits themselves. This is because solid-state spin qubits interact with each other via magnetic dipole interactions, which are short-ranged.

Interaction between qubits is necessary to create entangled states, which are a foundation for .

Mechanical resonators as mediators

To address the long-range interaction of qubits, the researchers propose coupling the NV centers in diamonds with mechanical resonators.

"Our research aims to use nanomechanical resonators to mediate interactions between these spin qubits. More specifically, we propose a new architecture, where spin qubits inside individual scanning probe tips can be moved over a nanomechanical resonator that mediates spin-spin interactions," explained Fung.

Nanomechanical resonators are tiny structures that can oscillate at high frequencies (typically nanoscales). They are sensitive to external fields and forces.

By coupling the qubits with a nanomechanical resonator, the researchers are creating a way for non-local interactions. This potentially enables the creation of large-scale quantum processors, addressing the drawback of scalability with solid-state quantum systems.

Refining the architecture

The research team's architecture, therefore, consists of a spin qubit inside individual scanning probe tips, which are precise scanning devices that can gather information.

"The scanning probe tips can be moved over a mechanical resonator that mediates spin-spin interactions. Since we can choose which qubits to move over this mechanical resonator, we can create programmable connectivity between spin qubits," explained Fung.

The individual qubits are NV centers inside a diamond nanopillar. This structure allows the NV center to be close to a micromagnet, which creates the magnetic field used to manipulate the electron spin state.

"It also helps that the nanopillar acts as a waveguide that reduces the laser power needed to excite the NV center," added Fang. This happens because the nanopillar guides the laser to the exact location it needs to go, the NV center.

The micromagnet is located on a silicon nitride nanobeam, completing the nanomechanical resonator.

In theory, the setup works as follows. The micromagnet creates a magnetic field around the qubit and the resonator. This magnetic field changes the electron spin state of the qubit.

The change in the spin state causes the qubit to interact with the nanomechanical resonator differently than it was before, making it oscillate with a different frequency. This oscillation affects other qubits, affecting their spin state.

The architecture allows for non-local qubit interactions.

Architecture feasibility and hybrid quantum systems

To show that their architecture is achievable, the researchers demonstrated the qubit's coherence over the mechanical transport of the micromagnet.

Fung said, "As a proof-of-principle measurement, we stored some coherent information in the NV center, moved it around in a large field gradient, and showed that the information was preserved afterward."

The coherence was also demonstrated via the quality factor, indicating the efficiency of a resonant system.

For the architecture, the quality factor was around a million at low temperatures, suggesting that the nanobeam resonator can maintain highly coherent mechanical motion despite being functionalized with a micromagnet. However, the highest recorded quality factor for mechanical resonators is 10 billion.

"While this coupling is not strong enough to make this architecture a reality yet, we believe that there are several realistic improvements that could get us there," said Fung.

The researchers are working on introducing an optical cavity with a nanomechanical resonator.

Fung explained, "The cavity would allow us to not only measure the mechanical motion more precisely, but also potentially prepare the mechanical resonator in its ground state. This greatly expands the experiments we can do, such as transferring a single quanta of information from the spin to the mechanics and vice versa."

The researchers also believe nanomechanical resonators are ideal intermediaries between different qubits because they can interact with various forces, such as Coulomb repulsion and radiation pressure.

"A hybrid quantum system can leverage the advantages of different kinds of qubits while mitigating their disadvantages. Because they can be fabricated on-chip, nanomechanical resonators can be integrated with other components, such as an electrical circuit or an optical cavity, which opens up possibilities for long-range connectivity," concluded Fung.

More information: F. Fung et al, Toward Programmable Quantum Processors Based on Spin Qubits with Mechanically Mediated Interactions and Transport, Physical Review Letters (2024). DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.263602. On arXiv: DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.2307.12193

Portland Author Alissa Hattman Shortlisted For 2024 Ursula K. Le Guin Prize For Fiction

Hattman’s debut novel, “Sift,” is inspired by modern calamities.

Portland author Alissa Hattman has made the shortlist for the 2024 Ursula K. Le Guin Prize for Fiction for her first novel, Sift (The 3rd Thing Press, 120 pages, $24.00). After an open nomination process last April in which authors and fans alike could nominate fiction novels that represented ideas reflected in Le Guin work, Hattman joins nine other authors on the shortlist. This year’s recipient of the prize will be chosen by a panel of authors including writers such as The Handmaid’s Tale author Margaret Atwood and The Paper Menagerie author Ken Liu.

Le Guin was one of the 20th century’s most prolific science fiction writers, and lived in Portland most of her life. First striking critical success in 1964 with the beginning of her Earthsea series, Le Guin won numerous awards during her lifetime, even making history as the first female author to win both of the prestigious Hugo and Nova sci-fi literary awards.

The winner of the $25,000 Le Guin Prize will be announced through Le Guin’s website on October 21, marking what would have been the author’s 94th birthday.

“It’s a huge honor,” Hattman says of Sift’s nomination. “Since I first moved to the Pacific Northwest and I was first introduced to Le Guin, which was in 1999 with this short story called “Omelas,” I have been such a deep admirer of her work. I think having been shortlisted and having this book be in the orbit of Le Guin feels so meaningful to me.”

First published in 2023, Sift follows two women as they search for a place to plant crops in a world that’s structures and order have collapsed. Hattman was inspired to write Sift while doing a morning writing exercise. In an attempt to capture her biggest fears, she ended up delving down the sorrowful inevitability of the death of her loved ones, specifically her mother.

“It started becoming a letter to my mother that became fictionalized overtime into something larger, sort of an anticipatory plea for humanity as a whole,” says Hattman.

What resulted was a book inspired by the pandemic, social unrest, and the climate crisis. Sift’s characters are forced to deal with the struggle of a ruined world  “I started to envision these two characters that might be stronger than I could be in those moments,” says Hattman.

This isn’t the first time Le Guin has impacted Hattman’s life. She says attending a live conversation between Le Guin and Atwood at the Arlene Schnitzer Concert Hall in 2010 was particularly important to her as a fellow writer.

“It was so amazing to see the two of them on the stage,” Hattman says. “It was awe inspiring to me, like witnessing an eclipse or something.”

Understanding Africa Employer of Record Services

An Employer of Record (EOR) is a third-party organization that serves as the legal employer for a company’s workforce in a foreign country. The EOR takes on the responsibilities and liabilities associated with employment, including payroll processing, tax compliance, benefits administration, and adherence to local labor laws. Earlier in July, immediately after Prime Minister Modi wrapped up a bilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, since first visit to Russia since the Ukraine war began in february 2022, the U.S.’s Ambassador in India made a rare public criticism of India’s Russia policy. “There is no such thing as strategic autonomy in times of conflict; we will, in crisis moments, need to know each other,” Ambassador Eric Garcetti said. In Washington DC, the State Department also expressed “concerns” over India’s ties with Russia, while National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan warned India of Russia’s deepening partnership with China. Public comments did not end there. On July 23, almost two weeks after Mr. Modi’s Russia visit, Donald Lu, Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asia, told lawmakers at a Congressional hearing in Washington that the U.S. was “disappointed” about the symbolism and timing of Mr. Modi’s visit.

The overall trajectory of India’s strategic partnership with the U.S. seems steady. Many U.S. policymakers see the partnership with India as one of the most consequential bilateral relationships of the U.S. in the 21st century. They also see an economically growing, democratic India as an effective bulwark against the Communist Party-ruled China. In India, economic, defence and strategic partnership with the U.S. is seen as critical for the country’s continued rise as a major Asian power. But the disagreements lie in the details. India’s refusal to condemn Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and its decision to ramp up energy trade with Moscow after it was sanctioned by the West did not go down well with Washington. Russia, cut off from the Western markets, found an economic lifeline in its booming trade with China and India, the world’s second and fifth largest economies, respectively.

In recent years, the India-U.S. partnership saw stress points in other areas as well. Indian nationals were accused of killing Hardeep Singh Nijjar, a Khalistan separatist, in Canada last year. The U.S. government has also sought accountability from the Indian government over a plot to kill Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. An Indian national is now in jail in the U.S. in connection with the case. India has denied any role in these incidents, but allegations have added to tensions in bilateral relations. And Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Russia, on the eve of a NATO summit in Washington whose main agenda was to strengthen Ukraine against the Russian invasion, seemed to have “disturbed” the Biden administration, as a Washington Post report claimed.

In its response, India’s Ministry of External Affairs said it values its strategic autonomy. “India, like many other countries, values its strategic autonomy. The U.S. Ambassador is entitled to his opinion. Obviously, we have different views,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said. “Our comprehensive global strategic partnership with the U.S. gives us the space to agree to disagree on certain issues, while respecting each other’s view-points,” he added.

What’s strategic autonomy, which India is fiercely protective about? “A simple definition of the concept is that countries should be able to make decisions that best serve their national interests, irrespective of the pulls and pressures from other parties,” I wrote in this July 19 Oped in The Hindu. Transform your voice into another vocalist's in real-time in your DAW with Dreamtonics Vocoflex

Vocoflex - Real-Time Voice Creation & Transformation Plugin - YouTube
Watch On

Vocoflex is a new vocal transformation plugin from Tokyo-based developers Dreamtonics that lets you access AI-powered voice modelling in your DAW in real-time.

Load up this effects plugin on an audio track with a vocal, drop another recording into Vocoflex for the plugin to analyse as a target voice, and it'll morph the vocal timbre in your first recording into that of the target voice. Dreamtonics says Vocoflex only needs ten seconds of a clean and unprocessed vocal to create an AI vocal model.

The target voice recording appears as a line of joined dots in the plugin's interface, with each dot representing a segment of the audio; you're able to morph between the timbre of each segment by moving your cursor over the dots. You're can also drop additional target voices into Vocoflex and morph between multiple voices to create a hybrid vocal timbre that shares qualities of each voice. 

Vocoflex is also equipped with a voice generator that allows you to transform vocal recordings without using samples. By selecting a point on a coloured XY pad, you're able to manipulate a vocal timbre to make it more masculine or feminine and alter its tone; changing the colour of the pad will transform the vocal timbre into another voice entirely, and you can even generate randomized voices. 

The plugin can be used in real-time for vocal processing during live performances; Dreamtonics says Vocoflex can operate with as little as 35ms latency, and you're able to control the plugin via MIDI, making it a powerful tool for live vocal manipulation. 

To prevent users making use of the voices of other artists without permission, Dreamtonics requires ID verification before processing a target voice, and embeds an inaudible audio watermark into processed voices to curb unauthorized voice modelling.

Hurricane Killer? Here are some things you may not know about Saharan dust

Dust from Africa moves across the Atlantic every year from late spring to early fall

It’s a common visitor in the summer months: dust from the Saharan Desert. Hazy skies and occasional allergies are common issues caused by the dust. But did you know that this layer of dust is more interesting than it appears? Here are some things you may not know about Saharan dust:

KEY TAKEAWAYS

  • Millions of tons of dust are transported across the Atlantic every year
  • Nutrient-rich Saharan dust plays a crucial role in the global ecosystem
  • Dust suppresses hurricane development

WHOLE LOTTA DUST!

Every year, from late spring to early fall, trade winds transport 180 million tons of dust from the Saharan Desert across the Atlantic Ocean. Impressively, that’s as much as 4.5 million 18-wheelers full of dust!

NATURE’S BEST FRIEND

Saharan dust is often rich in nutrients like iron and phosphorus. As the dust settles over the ocean, it fertilizes algae and plankton, allowing them to grow and flourish in an otherwise barren environment. These organisms are vital sources of food for ocean life.

Similarly, as the dust settles over land, areas like the Amazon rainforest benefit from the extra nutrients.

HURRICANE EXTINGUISHER

The African dust that moves across the Atlantic Ocean is also called the Saharan Air Layer (SAL). The SAL occurs in waves at the same time as Atlantic hurricane season, from June through November.

It’s known that the SAL limits hurricane development and strength. This is because tropical storms like hurricanes need deep, rich moisture from the surface to the top of the atmosphere to survive. Since the air carrying Saharan dust is usually dry, it can prevent storms from forming and suppress existing storms from growing and strengthening.

DUST’S IMPACT ON TEXAS

While a dense plume of dust sometimes causes minor allergy-like symptoms for some, the most noticeable impact is on Texas skies. A haze often forms on the horizon, giving an ordinarily clear, blue sky a milky hue during the day.

At sunrise and sunset, the horizon can appear brilliantly orange because, with dust in the air, sunlight has more particles to bounce off.

Quantum superiority.
How are the latest supercomputers and what does Schrödinger ’ s cat have to do with it?
Why quantum computers perform better than classical computers, how complex problems they are able to solve and when we will use their services.
It all began back in 1900, when the German theoretical physicist Max Planck made the assumption: energy is absorbed not continuously, but in parts.
These parts he called quanta (from the Latin quantum - "how many").
And then it happened: his hypothesis became the basis for the discoveries made by Einstein, Bohr, Rutherford, Schrödinger and other physicists, some of whom received Nobel prizes.
It may be hard to believe, but the incomprehensible and inexplicable quantum physics has found practical application.
Every time you pick up a flash drive or CD, think about it.
But flash drives and disks did not satisfy the researchers, so they decided to "cross" quantum physics and computer computing.
The result is a mysterious device with many tubes, prisms, mirrors, lasers, but without a monitor – a quantum computer.
As practice has recently shown, a quantum processor (the “brain ” of a computer) is able to cope with a task in an hour, which would take eight years for a supercomputer the size of a hangar.
Such results were achieved by scientists from the Chinese University of Science and Technology in Shanghai.
The prospects for these devices are the most bright: engineers dream that in a matter of minutes quantum PCs will be able to create the most perfect cipher and permanently stop hacker attacks, accelerate the development of artificial intelligence systems, conduct calculations for pharmacists who will help in the creation of effective and safe drugs.
But that's a long way off.
At this stage, scientists are fighting to prove to the world that quantum computers are capable of surpassing classical analogues.
How a quantum computer is made
All computing equipment, including PCs, operates on the basis of a binary system consisting of 0 and 1 (they are commonly called bits).
The use of these two symbols made it easier and cheaper to manufacture chips - the "brains" of a computer.
When a computational process occurs, the microswitches that the chip is equipped with either conduct current or do not.
That is, they constantly switch from 0 to 1 and back.
Thus, they can be in one of the states - "on" or "off", 0 or 1.
The operation of the quantum chip is based on a different system consisting not only of 0 and 1, but also of intermediate values and their combinations, so that the switches of the chip occupy a position between 0 and 1 or can be in the position of 0 and 1 at the same time.
Here it is worth remembering Schrödinger ’ s cat, which, according to the terms of the thought experiment, can be both alive and dead at the same time.
The same thing happens with quantum bits (qubits).
So what's the point?
It turns out that while the PC is thinking about specific answers, the quantum analogue is guessing at the qubit thickness?
A quantum computer does produce results in terms of probability, but its appeal is different.
Memory in qubits: without end and beginning
For computing, an important parameter is memory.
Classic devices are designed so that at some point their program works with some memory cell, which limits the capabilities of the device.
A quantum computer is able to simultaneously work with all memory cells, due to the "variability" of qubits described above.
Physicists argue that, theoretically, qubits can have an infinite amount of memory.
"In quantum computers, qubits are probably in a state of 0 or 1.
Probability is a number.
To write this number as accurately as possible, you need an infinite number of zeros and ones.
Therefore, in theory, 1 qubit is a physical system with an infinite amount of memory, ” explains physicist Anatoly Dymarsky in his report.

Danish theoretical physicist and public figure
Niels Bohr
However, there is no method to make an accurate measurement and to make the proposed accurate record in practice.
Therefore, the amount of quantum memory is still limited, but still impressive.
The scientist gives an example.
So, the memory of your laptop is 15 qubits, a supercomputer has a memory equal to 40 qubits, but 60 qubits can fit all the memory of all the computing centers of the world combined.
It is in the colossal capacity of qubits that all the charm of quantum computing consists.
The third time: how to find the best solution
But back to the mathematical abilities of such a computer.
At first glance, it seems useless in terms of calculations: while a supercomputer gives a clear and specific answer, the quantum analogue is scattered with a lot of options.
Who can do this to?
Believe me, many.
So, being in the position of Schrödinger's cat, the quantum system calculates all possible solutions to problems, looks for the most optimal of them and offers the best as the most suitable.
By getting a pool of correct answers, we can check how correct they are.
If the answers were incorrect, it is worth doing the calculations again.
In the end, three restarts will be enough to get the perfect answer.
Quantum "entanglement": what are the disadvantages of the system
Oddly enough, the more memory a quantum computer has, the more difficult it is to work with it.
So in qubits, his strength and weakness are at the same time.
The fact is that with the increase in the number of quantum bits and, therefore, memory, the system becomes more complicated and it becomes more difficult to maintain in an isolated state, and this is a prerequisite, otherwise nothing will work.
The time parameter is also important: the longer you operate the system, the more unstable it becomes.
In an unstable state, the probability of its interaction with the environment increases, and if this happens, the cells of quantum memory will collapse and turn into noise.
It is for this reason that scientists limit the number of operations with qubits.
This poses a major challenge to the development of quantum computing.
But there are also moves.
University of Sydney student Pablo Bonilla Ataides seems to have found a way to reduce the sensitivity of qubits to the environment.
Most scientists dealing with this problem eliminate noise by cooling the device to extremely low temperatures.
But not in all cases the method is effective.
Ataides proposes to correct errors by switching the states of qubits so that their position during interference is the most optimal.
Who Has Achieved Quantum Superiority
Not so long ago, IBM engineers said that they managed to experimentally prove that quantum computers are more efficient than classical ones.
In their work, the scientists investigated "computations in a confined space", allowing to demonstrate the fundamental advantage of calculations with qubits over classical bits.
Researchers have mathematically proved that there are problems that a classical computer cannot calculate, since it is limited to only one and zero, but a quantum computer can cope with them.
On the theory, scientists did not stop and conducted an experiment, with the participation of an imperfect ("noisy") quantum computer and a classical one.
To solve the problem, an ordinary computer used an electrical circuit with one logic element with two inputs and one register (bit) to store intermediate results.
The quantum circuit was built on four qubits, three of which encoded the incoming signal, and the fourth stored the intermediate result.

Each of the systems received data, processed and gave the result.
A normal computer would get zeros and ones.
If there were more zeros than ones, he should have given the answer "0".
If there were more units, the correct answer was "1".
As a result, the classical computer gave the correct result in 87.5% of cases, while the quantum analogue succeeded in 93% of cases.
The test shows that quantum computers, even noisy ones, are more powerful computing tools.
Where and how we can apply quantum computing
The scope of No1 is cryptography.
A quantum computer will be able to design a communication system that is not afraid of hacking or listening.
The fact is that quantum cryptography is not based on the rules of mathematics, but on the rules of physics.
This means that information is transferred through communication channels not in the form of a digital code, but with the help of quantum mechanics objects with physical means.
Such objects can be electrons in an electric current or photons in fiber-optic communication lines.
If someone wants to listen to your conversation, which you are conducting with the help of a quantum smartphone, you will immediately know about it.
The system will record third-party noises indicating that a third party is destroying the original signals in an attempt to wedge in.
Quantum computing will be used in pharmacy, logistics, energy and the design of artificial intelligence systems
Quantum computing will also be used in bioengineering, for example, to model DNA molecules.
They can also be useful to pharmacologists in the development of drugs, because when calculating proteins are considered as microscopic quantum objects.
They, like qubits, accept a variety of states, and therefore a quantum computer can most accurately simulate their behavior.
Qubits will also help to understand how atoms of certain substances interact, and to model a new material.
Perhaps scientists will be able to easily and simply come up with a “new graphene ”.

These include transport systems, logistics, energy.

Reviving Russia ’ s Role in the Indo-Pacific
Raj Kumar Sharma
Fifty years ago, India and the former Soviet Union signed the Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation on 9 August 1971.
In addition to changing the characteristics of South Asian and world politics, the treaty can also be seen as a harbinger of this idea.
From the Indo-Pacific region between India and Russia.
Despite disagreements over this concept these days, it is easy to forget that India-Russia cooperation in the Indo-Pacific and Eurasia preceded India ’ s engagement with most other major powers.
1971 is known for another reason: China decided to abandon its ideological mentor, the Soviet Union, and allied itself with the United States to balance the Soviet Union.
Thus, India faced security threats from Pakistan ’ s allies – the United States and China – during the Indo-Pakistani War in 1971.
However, when the Indo-Pakistani War broke out in December 1971 and US naval forces attempted to threaten India ’ s security, the Soviet Union sent a nuclear-armed fleet from the Pacific Fleet stationed in Vladivostok to support India – this could be considered the beginning of the Indo-Pacific concept between India and Russia.
To silence China, the Soviet Union moved 40 military divisions to the Xinjiang border with China and 7 divisions to the Manchuria border.
These events 50 years ago showed that cooperation between India and Russia (the two Eurasian and Pacific powers) was an important component of the Indo-Pacific region long before the US supported the idea of the Indo-Pacific region.
However, geopolitics has now changed as the US now sees India as a partner in its fight against China.
On the other hand, Beijing has partnered with Moscow to challenge Washington.
Russia has expressed some doubts about the Indo-Pacific region.
First, the Indo-Pacific region is perceived by Russia as American, so Moscow completely rejects it.
However, the Asia-Pacific region that preceded the Indo-Pacific region was also an American construction that Russia adopted.
At the governmental level, Russia continues to oppose the Indo-Pacific region, but academia, think tanks, and even the media are starting to get involved in the idea, debates, discussions, seminars, and conferences on the subject.
From time to time, India assured Russia that New Delhi ’ s rapprochement with Washington would not come at Moscow ’ s expense.
In contrast to the United States ’ understanding of the concept of “free and open ” in the Indo-Pacific region, India has always indicated that it is interested in“ free, open and inclusive ” in the Indo-Pacific region, an understanding that reflects India ’ s desire for Russia.
be an active player in the region.
In fact, India has tried to link Russia with its Indo-Pacific initiatives so that the latter would look like an independent pole outside of China ’ s shadow, which has given the nature of the Indo-Pacific region a multipolarity.
These initiatives include the Chennai-Vladivostok sea route and efforts by India and Japan to invest in Russia ’ s Far East.
These initiatives are part of India ’ s policy in the Far East to reach the Asian part of Russia.
It is important to emphasize here that people-to-people contacts have been a key area of success in India ’ s relationship with the United States.
However, in relations between India and Russia, the situation is different.
As Russia has concerns about Chinese immigration to the Far East, state-facilitated immigration of Indian labor to Russia could bring political and economic benefits to both sides.
The Russian economy is recovering, but the epidemic is not over - Putin - Business and economy
From India ’ s perspective, the Indo-Pacific region is similar to the Great Russian-Eurasian Partnership aimed at avoiding Chinese domination of Eurasia.
This policy contains elements of cooperation as well as competition with China.
Faced with China ’ s advancement through the Silk Road Economic Belt in Russia ’ s sphere of influence in Eurasia, Russia has agreed to align its own initiative, the Eurasian Economic Union, with China ’ s Belt and Road Initiative, though there are more contradictions than similarities in these efforts.
Similarly, the Indo-Pacific region is India ’ s attempt to protect its neighbors from China ’ s assertive behavior.
Russia has the opportunity to cooperate with India in shaping the emerging order in the Indo-Pacific region, which can be done with historical trust between the two sides.
India pays more attention to the Indian Ocean, while the United States and its allies favor the Pacific, highlighting another difference in the Indo-American conceptual understanding of the Indo-Pacific.
India is not yet a major military power in the Pacific, but helping its naval forces achieve this goal will also help Russia meet China ’ s challenge to its dominance in the Arctic.
China defines itself as “close to the Arctic country, ” although it does not have a coastline in the Arctic.
Within the framework of the Polar Silk Road, China ’ s activity in the Arctic will increase in the coming years.
Even Chinese strategists have argued that whoever controls the Arctic sea route will control the global economy, and China should play an active role in this area.
Consequently, the Indo-Pacific region is an idea that can add value to Russian diplomacy in various regions, including the Asia-Pacific region and the Arctic.
After all, the Russian worldview is manifested in the symbol of the coat of arms, where the two-headed eagle looks simultaneously at the West and East.
Traditionally, Russian elites considered their country European, but it also has an Asia-Pacific character.
These elites, based in Moscow, which has been the traditional center of power in Russia, can compete with others who want Russia to be more active in the Pacific through its base in Vladivostok.
The Indo-Pacific region is not just the United States, and Russia ’ s worldview is likely to be incomplete without considering the Indo-Pacific region, where there is a potential risk of making it dependent on China.

What is intermittent fasting and how to organize it correctly
A complex of healthy nutrition, regular physical activity, optimal water regime, sound sleep and positive emotions - this is the simple key that will open the secret of the extension of youth and resourcefulness.
The topic of intermittent fasting (IG) for several years has acquired a large number of myths and the search for additional salvation from extra pounds where the essence of the process lies in a deeper level of impact and mechanism.
It all began with the receipt of the Nobel Prize biologist Yoshinori Osumi in 2016 in medicine and physiology "for the discovery of the mechanisms of autophagy."
It is difficult to call it a pioneer, but the way the scientist described in detail the phenomenon of “self-eating of the cell ” deserves attention and respect.
“Great work and contribution to the prolongation of youth, self-renewal and, most importantly, weight loss, ” those who translate the unit of human health into the equivalent of profit will hear and begin to introduce into the masses.
It sounds good and promising.
But there is one “but, ” as they say.
Studies were conducted on yeast, the idea was not about weight loss.
Clinical trials in relation to people continue, and perhaps we will still apologize for how zealously refute the next way to lose weight, but the fact is that the positive effect on the work of organs and systems is really observed. What?
Is it as safe as it seems at first glance?
We delve further into the different approaches and interpretations of this nutrition plan.
16: 8, 20: 4, 5: 2... A lot of options, but the point converges on the point of switching between fasting and eating on a regular schedule.
During intermittent fasting, you only eat for a certain time.
We have evolved to synchronize with the day / night cycle, that is, with the circadian rhythm.
Our metabolism has adapted to daytime food, night sleep.
Eating at night is associated with an increased risk of obesity as well as diabetes.
Currently, Internet, television, and other virtual entertainment are available around the clock and seven days a week.
We stay awake longer to sit on social media, play games, watch TV shows.
This is reflected in our psycho-emotional state.
Stress begins to destroy from a young age.
This all leads to a sedentary lifestyle and to unconscious continuous snacks during the day, flowing smoothly at night.
Before starting intermittent fasting, be sure to consult a doctor.
For example, you can try fasting 16 / 8: eating for eight hours and fasting for 16.
Or the 5: 2 mode, which involves regular meals five days a week, and the other two days you limit yourself to one meal of 500-600 calories.
Some people need to experiment to find the optimal meal times suitable for their lifestyle.
Important
Cheating the scales.
How to keep a figure without giving up the habit of eating at night
In the time interval when you do not eat, water and drinks such as black coffee and tea are allowed without the addition of milk, honey, sugar and sweeteners.
It is important to remember that during the period of eating it is not necessary to break down into high-calorie unhealthy food.
Be careful with yourself.
Use this time also with benefit, choosing nutritious foods and dishes, for example, complex unrefined carbohydrates (whole grains - buckwheat, quinoa, brown rice), leafy greens, vegetables, healthy fats (olive oil, pumpkin seeds, sesame, flax, avocado, nuts, olives) and high-quality protein (eggs, fish, meat, dairy products)., legumes).
Fruits, vegetables and whole grains are rich in fiber, so they help a person feel full and satisfied.
Useful fats and proteins can also contribute to satiety.
Longer periods without food, such as 24, 36, 48 and 72 hours of fasting, can be dangerous.
Therefore, such practices should be carried out under the supervision of an experienced specialist.
An in-depth review of IS published in The New England Journal of Medicine sheds light on the effects regarding cellular functions beyond weight loss and fat percentage.
Switching from satiety to fasting doesn ’ t just help us burn calories and lose weight.
Researchers have reviewed dozens of animal and human studies to explain how simple fasting improves metabolism by lowering blood glucose; normalizes blood pressure and heart rate at rest; reduces inflammation, which improves a range of health problems, from arthritis pain to asthma; even reduces the risk of cancer due to the elimination of damaged elements and improves brain function by affecting the activity of neurotransmitters such as dopamine and serotonin. nin.
Some people should avoid intermittent fasting:
• children and adolescents under 18 years of age.
• Pregnant or lactating women
• people with insufficient body weight
• those who have a history of eating disorders.
Irritability and overeating are two common side effects of this eating plan.
Lack of food can contribute to an increase in the level of the stress hormone cortisol, which can lead to an even greater addiction to food, anxiety and sleep disturbance.
It is extremely important to organize the process of falling asleep so that nothing prevents you from feeling rested.
In the end, I want to emphasize that a complex of healthy nutrition, regular physical activity, optimal water regime, sound sleep and positive emotions is the uncomplicated key that will open the secret of extending youth and resourcefulness.
Protect your cells from oxidative stress, and space from unnecessary and false information.

NVIDIA told about its success in the synthesis of natural human speech by AI
NVIDIA told about its success in the synthesis of natural human speech by AI
Artificial intelligence now allows you to recreate the voice of virtual assistants in smartphones and smart speakers, very similar to human speech.
Although it is still possible to notice the differences between synthesized and live speech, which we hear in everyday conversation and in the media.
This is because humans speak with complex rhythms, intonations, and timbres that AI is difficult to replicate.
However, thanks to the work of NVIDIA, the differences are gradually blurring.
The company ’ s researchers create models and tools for high-quality controlled speech synthesis that convey the richness of human speech without sound artifacts.
Their latest designs are now on display at Interspeech 2021, which runs until September 3.
These models can help create voice automated customer service lines for banks and retailers, animate video game or book characters, and provide real-time speech synthesis for digital avatars.
NVIDIA ’ s creative team even uses this technology to create an expressive narrative for a series of videos about the possibilities of artificial intelligence.
Until recently, these rollers were voiced by a person.
Previous models of speech synthesis offered limited control over the tempo and pitch of the synthesized voice, so attempts to narrate artificial intelligence did not evoke the emotional response that a talented human speaker could give.
That changed over the past year, when NVIDIA ’ s text-to-speech research team developed more powerful and manageable speech synthesis models, such as RAD-TTS.
By teaching a text-to-speech model based on human speech, the RAD-TTS model can convert any text note into a speaker ’ s voice.
Another feature of the model is voice transformation, where the words of one speaker (or even singing) are transmitted by the voice of another speaker.
The RAD-TTS interface gives users the ability to accurately control the height, duration and energy of the synthesized voice at the frame level.
As a result, for example, a man can read a text and then convert it into a female voice.
The capabilities of the AI model go beyond voiceover.
Text-to-speech conversion can be used in games, to help people with voice impairments, or to help users translate between languages with their own voice.
AI can even recreate the performances of famous singers, combining not only the melody of the song, but also the emotional expression of the vocals.
Expressive speech synthesis is just one element of NVIDIA ’ s research into conversational AI.
This area also includes natural language processing, automatic speech recognition, keyword detection, sound enhancement, and more.
These developments were made using the NVIDIA NeMo toolkit and are open source solutions.
They are optimized to run efficiently on NVIDIA GPUs and are available for use by researchers and developers.

Scriptwriter David Callaham helped Marvel create an Asian superhero
In the four days since the start of distribution, the film “Shan-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings ” grossed $90 million in the United States and Canada.
Marc Piasecki / Getty Images
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings set a record for Labor Day box office (this year on September 6) in the United States and Canada.
In the four days since Friday, September 3, it raised $90 million, although it was expected that the fees will be at the level of $45 – 50 million, writes the online edition Seeking Alpha.
The surge in box office receipts was a long-awaited news for investors: the shares of cinemas went into growth.
On September 7, AMC prices soared by 8.7%, Cineplex - by 5.1%, IMAX - by 3.3%, Cinemark - by 3.9%.
In Russia, the premiere took place on September 2, for two weeks the fees exceeded $3.3 million.
Shan-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is Marvel ’ s first Asian superhero film.
It was directed by Destin Cretton, whose mother is Japanese American, and the script was written by Dave Callaham, who has both parents of Chinese descent.
Shan-Chi appeared in print Marvel comics back in the 1970s and was the son of villain Fu Manchu.
In those years, the West swept the fashion of kung fu, and the first Shan-Chi was similar to Bruce Lee to a degree of confusion.
In the story of paper comics, Shan-Chi first helped to malign his father, then came to his senses and began to fight against him.
In those years, China was the enemy of the United States as a communist power.
Then he became a trade competitor.
And now it has turned into a large and important film market with its own specifics.
For example, as soon as the actor of “Fast and Furious 9 ” John Cena mentioned and called Taiwan a“ country ”, a storm of indignation arose in China and the fees of the film fell sharply.
Marvel doesn ’ t seem to forget that.
Paper comics of the 1970s were the quintessence of American stereotypes about Asians.
“I don ’ t believe it was done maliciously, ” Callagham told The Nerds of Color,“ It ’ s just that there was a very different era of comics created by two white men about Asian people.
It does not reflect the reality in which we now live <... > And it is necessary to give them credit, Marvel understood it.
So they invited us [with Cratton] to do what we want. ”
They not only added typical Asian features like the fact that, unlike paper comics, the characters finally began to undress before entering the house.
They made the flat book villain more multifaceted in the film.
“This is a broken man who has done a lot in his very long life and desperately wants to believe that he can bring everything back, it ’ s very human, ” Callaham told The Hollywood Reporter. – But we still needed him to look like the head of a giant terrorist organization that <... > torments people in their dungeons and all that.
Finding that balance was not easy. ”
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
Monkey friends
Callaham was born on October 24, 1977 in Fresno, California, to Chinese Americans.
As a child, he pretended that he was no different from the white-faced kids in the neighborhood.
“I thought it wasn ’ t cool to be [Chinese], ” he told The Nerds of Color.
David didn ’ t go to study English at the University of Michigan because he liked literature.
Everything else attracted him even less.
“By the end of my training [in 1999], my best friend and I still didn ’ t know what we wanted to do, ” he admitted (here and then quotes from the website of the Hollywood consulting agency Fresh Voices).
They caught the eye of an article in Penthouse, how cool the writers live in Hollywood: “It had pictures of absolute nerds in the Jacuzzi in the penthouse. ”
So, as soon as they got their diplomas, the friends went to conquer Los Angeles.
They even co-wrote a script called Los Angeles Zoo.
Something similar to “Friends ”, and the highlight was that the two main characters were played by … monkeys, who were mistaken for ordinary people.
The authors did not hide that they borrowed the idea from the old series Lancelot Link: Secret Chimp, which aired on ABC in 1970-1971: about a spy monkey and his human partner.
Callaham and a friend quickly realized that selling such a script would not be easy.
They moved on to more mundane topics.
For example, they wrote scripts for two episodes of “Friends ”.
Then a comedy in the style of the then popular film “American Pie ”.
Alas, they received refusal after refusal from the studios.
To earn money, both got a job in a company producing dog food.
Then the friend got engaged, finally broke up with the dream of becoming a screenwriter and went to the bride in Michigan.
And Callaham continued to write alone and got a job as an assistant in a law firm: they paid more.
Callahama ’ s girlfriend turned out to be an acquaintance who worked for the CAA (Creative Artists Agency).
She gave him an interview.
He decided to try to work in the CAA, as they also selected actors and writers for Hollywood.
“I was told it would be a terrible job, I would be mistreated and paid less for it than [at the law firm], ” Callham recalled.
For about a year, Callham replaced various assistants who fell ill and were unable to go to work.
Then he settled in with producer Craig Goering's crew.
He was promised that he would gather the contacts of many famous people in the industry and get access to a large number of materials, from scripts to specifications.
And it turned out to be true.
At one time, Callaham ’ s workplace was near the office of CAA President Richard Lovett.
When everyone was leaving for lunch, Callagham copied documents from his desk and read them at night.
Among others, there were secret ones: scripts that the studios secretly sent to Tom Hanks and Tom Cruise for consideration, correspondence with the authors about changes in the text and plot, and much more.
“I stole scripts from the tables and read them – and that ’ s how I learned to write, ” Callagham once told The Hollywood Reporter.
“I realized that most writers are guys who can be pretty good or not very good, but the main thing is that they are motivated and work hard, ” he summed up in an interview with Fresh Voices. – I saw the profession of a writer from the point of view of the buyer. <... > And importantly, I found that in most cases, the script is read first, like me, the assistant.
If you can't conquer it, the producer will never see your script.
So my goal is always to write a good first act <... > So that on the fifth page you will be interested in reading everything else. "
Tribute to the Apocalypse
He managed to work for Goering for eight months when he realized that he was tired of the CAA.
His next job was the production company Deep River Productions.
At the same time he continued writing.
First, he created a drama from the life of college students “My Generation ”.
He was, in his own words, pretentious.
Then a drama about the afterlife called "Koda".
She turned out to be absolutely terrible.
Then he wrote a comedy.
And it was liked by the people Callaham gave it to read.
The point is that the guy invents teleportation to get into the apartment of his beloved, living on the other side of the country.
They never saw each other: their romance began by correspondence and phone.
But the teleport was wrong.
Callahan's hero is stuck inside the wall.
Even though the girl was now not hundreds of miles, but a few centimeters, he still could not see and touch her.
By that time, Callaham himself had been dating his girlfriend for six years.
But she had to move to another city – why the idea of the script came up.
And then she dumped him.
And Callaham, abandoning the comedy, sat down to write a gloomy thriller to spill out his feelings.
He came up with the story of the detective whose wife died.
Immersed in his grief, he becomes more and more distant from his sons, and the only joy is work.
He relentlessly catches a killer maniac decorating a crime scene in accordance with the prophecy of the four horsemen of the Apocalypse.
“I would come home from work, drink, and then start writing.
“I had candles all over the room, I turned off all the lights, I listened to music and hung pictures of crying people and photos of corpses from movies. ”
It cost him a couple of times.
He brought home a new girl, she glanced at the photos and flew out of the apartment with a bullet.
In 2002, Callahum completed a script called Horsemen and sent it to everyone he had gathered while working for the CAA.
“Until now, people in the film industry tell me that they remember reading The Horsemen, ” he laughs.
As a result, talent manager Gaimon Cassidy became interested in the work.
He had just sold 20th Century Fox David Benioff ’ s psychological thriller Stay (2005) and was looking for a new author.
However, he honestly warned: to sell such a complex and gloomy scenario will not be easy.
And I got Callahan to rewrite.
Callaham doesn't like to rewrite.
One of his colleagues gives the script to lie down, and then, having a fresh look, refines it.
Callahan works differently.
Having put the last point, immediately hands over the script and, if it were his will, would leave it in its original form. But alas.
Almost every time he receives comments and corrections from the studio.
“If you throw a tantrum, you will earn a reputation as a difficult person.
And as soon as you get that reputation, there will be a million other aspiring writers in your place, ” he says. – The biggest problem, I think, is sometimes overcoming your pride.
Understand that this is not just my scenario, but someone ’ s investment.
So I have to do what they want.
I don ’ t always do that well. ”
The "Horsemen" script was eventually liked by Platinum Dunes.
It was founded just a year ago, in 2001, and just launched its first film – a remake of “Texas Chainsaw Massacre ” (the first“ Massacre ” was released in 1974).
But the studio wanted to produce original content, and the creation of Callahama seemed appropriate to them.
However, they released "Horsemen" only in 2009.
$20 million was spent on shooting, and the film collected 8 times less.
And Platinum Dunes for a long time earned mainly on the remakes of “Friday, 13 ”,“ Nightmare on Elm Street ”, “Ninja Turtles ”.
Horsemen / Platinum Dunes
How to defeat Stallone
In the same year 2009, another film based on the script of Callaham was released – “Tell-Tale ” (Tell-Tale) produced by the film company Social Capital Films.
It is based on the story of the same name by Edgar Poe.
The main character transplanted the heart of a murdered person, and he begins to see pictures from his past life.

It turned out so bad.
If “The Horsemen ” and“ The Convictor Heart ” took many years for the manuscript to reach the screen, then the film Doom all about everything took only two years.
Callaham was called to a meeting with people from the leadership of Warner Bros, not really explaining why.
He was asked if he had played Doom.
He was playing.

Investors appreciated the prospects of tilapia in Black Africa
Dutch fund Aqua-Spark announced its intention to invest $300 million in aquaculture in Black Africa, primarily in the cultivation of tilapia.
The fund called on other investors to co-finance, mentioning, however, the presence of risks.
According to the report of the Fund, the population of sub-Saharan Africa (Black Africa) by 2050 should double, reaching 2 billion people, according to Fishnews.
By this time, the macro-region ’ s demand for fish will grow from the current 10 million tons to 16-29 million tons.
Cultivation of tilapia, according to the authors of the report, can meet this demand, since the scale of production is easy to increase, and the fish itself is affordable.
It is planned that the development of aquaculture south of the Sahara will mitigate the overexploitation of wild fish populations – after all, their numbers will not grow with the population of the macroregion.
The report noted that it is of paramount importance to expand production through direct investment in tilapia aqua farms.
According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) of 2019 (the authors of the report refer to this information), tilapia production in the macroregion reaches 263 thousand tons, which is much higher than the estimate of the fund itself - 125-150 thousand tons.
The risks to such investments are also mentioned.
So, tilapia cultivation is engaged in small farms, in which even small banks are in no hurry to invest money.
In addition, in Black Africa, there are problems with legislation that make aquaculture a troublesome process.
The threat is also biological risks, for example, possible outbreaks of diseases.
A special place is given to the problem of competition with cheap Chinese tilapia.
At the same time, experts of the fund note a reduction in the supply of fish from China to African countries.
