Scientists have confirmed the popular myth about the benefits of a cold shower
Researchers believe that such water treatments not only strengthen the immune system, but can even improve brain function.
Scientists are gaining more and more evidence that a cold shower has a positive effect on health.
This is reported by Science Alert.
Cold shower for medical purposes first began to be used in the early 19th century.
Then doctors used it in psychiatric hospitals to “cool the hot inflamed brain. ”
As early as the mid-19th century, Victorians realized that warm showers could also be used for personal hygiene.
Thus, the shower became part of the daily ritual of self-care.
But the practice of pouring cold water anywhere has not disappeared, and it seems that recently its popularity is only growing.
Scientists from the Netherlands conducted a large study in which participants took a daily cold shower for a month.
The group of more than 3,000 people was divided into four subgroups.
In the first group, people took a cold shower for 30 seconds, in the second - 60 seconds, and in the third - 90 seconds.
The fourth group was a control group, in which the participants enjoyed the usual warm shower every morning.
After three months of observations, scientists found that people who took a cold shower, the number of sick leave decreased by 29%.
Interestingly, the duration of cold water procedures did not affect the health of people.
Scientists do not yet know how this mechanism works, but some studies show that cold showers have something to do with boosting the immune system.
A study by Czech scientists showed that young people immersed in cold water three times a week for six weeks strengthened their immune system.
Of course, more research is needed for more specific findings, experts say.
It is known that cold water activates the sympathetic nervous system, the one that is responsible for the “fight or flight ” reaction (the body ’ s reaction to a dangerous, stressful event).
When this condition is activated during a cold shower, the level of the hormone norepinephrine increases in the body.
It is he who causes a rapid heartbeat and increases blood pressure.
There is also evidence that bathing in cold water improves blood circulation.
When people immerse themselves in cold water, blood flow to the skin decreases.
After that, the body should warm up and the flow of blood to the surface of the skin increases dramatically.
Scientists who studied the benefits of a cold shower after training found that after three weeks of such procedures, blood flow to the muscle improved.
There is also evidence that a cold shower helps people lose weight.
The study showed that immersion in water at a temperature of 14 ° C increases metabolism.
In addition to the physical benefits, a cold shower can also be beneficial in a psychological sense.
Immersion in cold water increases mental activity due to the stimulation of the same fight-or-flight response.
Scientists have found that in older people, washing with cold water improved brain function.
But before jumping into cold water, it is worth remembering that such stressful procedures do not work for everyone.
Because the sudden flow of cold water is so shocking to the body, it can be dangerous for people with heart disease and can cause a heart attack or heart rhythm disturbance.

The Ministry of Finance proposed to change the taxation system of citizens in Russia
The Ministry of Finance of Russia proposed to make adjustments to the taxation of citizens, according to “Izvestia ” with reference to the annex to the“ Main directions of budget, tax and customs tariff policy for 2022 and the planning period of 2023 and 2024 ”.
The first change concerns people working remotely in other countries for Russian companies.
They may be required to pay income tax (NDFL).
Now there is no such norm, said Levon Hayrapetyan, head of the direction “Tax Policy ” of the CSR.
At the same time, the Ministry of Finance wants to establish a limit on the amount of compensation payments that employers make to remote employees for the organization of labor.
Now companies reimburse remote workers for the costs of the necessary equipment, materials and other things.
According to the new proposals, such costs of organizations will not be subject to personal income tax if the amount does not exceed a certain threshold, Hayrapetyan noted.
Also, the Ministry of Finance proposes to change the approach to taxation of bookmakers.
Now if you win less than 15,000 rubles, the Russians have to pay personal income tax from the amount received.
The authorities want to shift responsibility to gambling establishments, regardless of the amount of revenues.
Another measure concerns the strengthening of control over the use of maternity capital.
The Ministry of Finance came up with the idea to oblige the Pension Fund of Russia (PFR) to provide tax information about the owners of the relevant certificates, who disposed of the allocated funds, and about the amounts used.
It is assumed that this will automate the supervision of the legality of the provision of property tax deductions, which are not provided for in the case of the purchase of real estate with the funds of the parent capital.
In addition, now liquidated or bankrupt banks can not transfer information on the interest paid to depositors.
The Ministry of Finance proposes to impose the need to provide this information to the Federal Tax Service (FTS) on the Deposit Insurance Agency (DIA).
Some of the changes that are proposed to be implemented are related to the reduction of the tax burden.
For example, the Ministry of Finance intends to endow the owners of shares of companies received as a gift or inheritance, upon leaving the company or upon liquidation of the organization, to reduce the taxable income by the amount with which the contribution was paid when it was acquired by the donor or testator.
The Ministry also wants to expand the list of recipients of tax deductions.
One of the proposals is to increase to 24 years the age limit for full-time students of children of taxpayers who claim to receive a social deduction.
At the same time, the standard tax deduction can be available to persons who are in the care of children or recognized incapable citizens.
The Ministry of Finance proposes to allow people when acquiring property rights to refuse a tax deduction and reduce the amount of taxable income by the amount of actually incurred expenses.
With a fixed amount of tax deduction, the new option will be limited only to the amount of income from the sale of the property.
Finally, the department came up with the idea of adjusting the procedure for accounting for expenses when families with children sell housing purchased under state support programs.
It is assumed that it will be made in proportion to the share of each family member in the ownership of the dwelling.

Gastronomic tour in Bashkiria: the republic took first place in the ranking with unusual dishes in the country
Travelers are very fond of beshbarmak and "kazy"
"Zur-belish" personifies the familiarity and hospitality of the Bashkir people
Photo: Rustem AKHUNOV
Many travelers are very fond of gastrotours - tasting local dishes.
This fashionable word immediately evokes thoughts about abroad, however, you can go on a gastrotour around Russia!
There are many regions in which delicious and unusual dishes are prepared.
For example, the global marketplace for road trips BlaBlaCar made its rating from five regions of Russia with unusual national cuisine.
Bashkiria took first place in it.
We will tell you who was bypassed by the region, what dishes tourists loved, what delicious can still be tried and where.
FOUR REGIONS
The first place in the ranking experts assigned to Bashkiria, but it is followed by the Irkutsk region, the Republic of Tatarstan, the Novosibirsk region and the Republic of Adygea.
In Irkutsk, tourists are very fond of Baikal omul, the tenderness of which makes dishes with this fish not only unusual, but also incredibly tasty.
Residents of the region prepare omul in different ways: smoked and salted, boiled from it to the ear and eaten in the form of sagudai.
“Sagudai ” literally translates from the Enetz language as“ eating raw fish ”.
Today, this dish of the indigenous peoples of the North is valued as an excellent snack.
In Tatarstan, every visitor likes to drink fragrant tea with local desserts - this is chak-chak, kak-tosh and absolutely magical talkysh kaleve.
Previously, only very wealthy Tatars could afford this, but now it is all on the shelves of shops and in cafes.
In Novosibirsk, tourists remember Siberian fish and meat of wild animals - bear, elk, beaver.
Bright accents in dishes are manifested by white mushrooms, berries and fern, which Siberians add to dumplings and warm salads, and also salted for the winter.
In Adygea, everyone should taste a hearty outlandish soup with chestnuts, beans, fragrant roast and spicy greens and, of course, local Adygea cheese.
IN BASHKIRIA – BESHBARMAK AND “KAZY ”
Bashkir dishes instantly conquered travelers with flavors and aromas.
Nobody was indifferent to the king of Bashkir cuisine Beshbarmak.
The dish consists of three parts, each part is served in a separate plate: boiled meat (horse meat or beef) with homemade noodles, broth, sour cream korot.
The name of the dish translates as “five fingers ” because beshbarmak is eaten with hands, sipping broth with a deep spoon.
Also, the guests of the region remembered the meat delicacy "kaza" - a homemade sausage made of horse meat, cooked from a fatty part with fragrant spices.
After a hearty meal, you can drink Bashkir tea with herbs and enjoy desserts - everyone should taste the puffy Bashkir donuts of baursaki, which melt in his mouth.
With a gift you can take away from Bashkiria delicious Bashkir honey, which is known throughout the country and even abroad.
The people of the region are particularly proud of them.
WHERE TO EAT?
From mastic to confectionery sculpted Bashkir as a decoration of cakes
Photo: Rustem AKHUNOV
Bashkir cuisine is also called nomadic cuisine.
It is simple and nourishing.
Perhaps not a single traveler who came to Bashkiria will leave here without visiting the capital.
It is here that there are several restaurants and cafes where you can try Bashkir cuisine.
National Bashkir cuisine has become an integral part of the menu of most Ufa restaurants.
We will tell you where to try real zur balish, elesh, beshbarmak or kabyrgu.
In the restaurant "Duslyk" rich Bashkir menu.
Meat eaters will be happy - here you can taste "Bashkir assorted" from horse brisket, dried smoked balyk, homemade sausages.
Here they prepare the most delicious elesh, shurpa of sterlet, tukmas of poultry with a spool, beshbarmak with rich broth.
"Cheap and angry" - we are talking about the well-known throughout the republic "Pyshka".
Here you can find delicious Bashkir pastries at affordable prices.
The main idea of the Pyshka network is to position Zur-belish as a new culinary attraction of the region.
Here you can taste "Zur-belish", which personifies the familiarity and hospitality of our people.
It's a big pie with potatoes and meat.
Bashkirs prepare it for holidays, important events and eat together with a large family.
Ashkhan of Bashkir national cuisine "Zur Neneyka" is an ode of love for its people, its traditions and culture.
It is famous for the abundance of Bashkir dishes, delicious ayran is also served here.
Restaurant "Azyk-Tulek" is located in the heart of Ufa and is famous for both modern and local dishes.
There is a high level of service, experienced chefs and a beautiful interior.
From the "Bashkir" here you can order a meat platter - on a plate will carry dried kazylyk, boiled kazylyk, dried goose, withers of horse meat, boiled smoked tongue.
Horse tartar is the hallmark of the restaurant, you won ’ t find it anywhere else.
From the first courses, you can order elesh - Bashkir soup with horse meat, it is covered with puff pastry and served with sour cream, tukmas with chicken - chicken broth with homemade noodles.
The menu of hot dishes will please you with bishbarmak, horse meat rib, ossobuco - horse meat drumstick stewed in red wine with herbs.
Of course, you will enjoy the abundance of pastries!
You can taste kystybyy (tortilla with stuffing) with potatoes or millet, tortilla sabantuy, in the filling of which pounded potatoes, lard and kazylyk, uchpochmak - triangular pie with meat and potatoes, zur balish of lamb, vak balish of horse meat.
KUMYS, HONEY AND SHORT
From Bashkiria, tourists take away such delicacies as koumiss - a drink made from mare's milk, honey and short.
It is better to buy it at fairs or proven stores, otherwise it is easy to run into a fake.
Honey is good in every district of Bashkiria - beekeepers approach their business with love and all responsibility.
The most unusual honey can be tasted in the Burzyan district in the Shulgan-Tash Natural Park - bead honey is mined here.
Bashkiria, by the way, is the only place in Europe where beekeeping has been preserved - the extraction of wild honey, which has useful and medicinal properties.
Bortev honey – wild bee honey is mined in Burzyana
Photo by Elvina APARINA
TABLE ETIQUETTE BASHKIR
Bashkir food is hearty, tasty, meat and the most important difference is that it has a minimum of additives.
Bashkirs honor their traditions and prepare national dishes for the holidays and today.
No Bashkir feast is complete without kaza, bishbarmak, chak-chak, koumiss and honey.
Also, nomadic people have several rules of etiquette at the table:
- Food is served immediately upon arrival of the guest;
- The owner touches the food first;
- An odd number of cakes are served on the table, but certainly not less than guests;
- As soon as the guest ceases to eat, the owner also ceases to eat;
- Drink and eat only with the right hand;
- If the guest is hungry and there is not enough food, the host eats as little as possible to satisfy the guest as much as possible;
- From the common dish, food is taken worse, others leave the best;
- With a knife, freshly baked bread is not cut, they do not bite off the whole cake;
- During meals with the owner observe the peace, try to be cheerful and cheerful;
At the end of the meal, they pray for the well-being of the owner.

At the same time, 70 percent of specialists would like to get the right to remote not only from other regions, but also from other countries.
The mood of the “white collar ” found the international recruitment company Hays.
The study "Relocation of employees" (available to "WG") involved about a thousand HR-managers and hired professionals.
Only 22 percent of employers plan to introduce permanent office visits for all employees.
Most will agree if people don't show up every day.
According to the survey, in half of the companies remotely from other cities work up to 20 percent of the staff (in half of cases this is a very small proportion of specialists, no more than five percent).
As a rule, this opportunity is received by any person who is released by his immediate supervisor.
A quarter of employers provide remote access to IT specialists, 15 percent - to top management, another 13 - to marketers, PR specialists, advertisers and employees of digital departments.
At the same time, in a third of organizations, the salary of people “released ” to the regions is tied not to the level of income in the central office, but to indicators in the territory where a person actually works.

Every fifth respondent employee reported that in his company it is possible to work remotely from any city of Russia by agreement with the management.
About the same number said that they can even allow removal from another country - in the normal mode or as an exception.

Another 17 percent said that such an opportunity would be a significant bonus.
Women dream about it more often than men.
"At the moment, remote work from another country is not regulated by Russian legislation, - said Lilia Gazina, a leading lawyer at Hays. - This is a" gray zone "for both employers and employees.
For example, the letter of the Ministry of Labor dated July 27, 2016 No. 17-3 / B-292 says that federal laws and other normative legal acts of the Russian Federation containing labor law norms are valid only in Russia.
According to the lawyer, it is not possible for the employer to provide safe working conditions for remote workers working outside Russia.
“Although this letter is aimed primarily at foreign citizens, ” said Lilia Gazina,“ restrictions may apply to employees with Russian citizenship who decide to work from another country. ”
When working from abroad, the norms of information security provided by the company may be violated.
There are also nuances on labor protection and tax obligations.
"Both employers and employees should be very attentive to the design of such labor relations, - added Gazina. - And provide for all possible controversial issues in order to protect themselves and ensure effective interaction."
The most likely to appreciate "remote", including from other countries, people aged 55 + and 25-28 years.
For respondents under 24 years of age, the possibility of remote work is not so significant, only a third of specialists in this group called it fundamentally important.

In the UAE, fraudsters using a deepfake voice deceived a bank employee and stole $35 million
The employee was unable to distinguish the fake voice from the real one.
The criminals robbed a bank in the UAE, posing as a director of a large company: they forged his voice with the help of artificial intelligence technologies and convinced a bank employee to transfer money to fraudulent accounts.
This is stated in court documents.
The incident occurred in January 2020, but details have only been made public now.
Then the head of one of the branches of the bank (the name is not disclosed) answered the call, and the caller introduced himself as a director of a large company with whom the head of the branch recently spoke.
The fraudster told the employee that the company was entering into a major $35 million deal and convinced him to transfer that amount to the firm ’ s allegedly new accounts.
The employee did not suspect anything, since the director ’ s voice was no different from the real one.
Also, for credibility, the fraudster sent the employee fake emails of the company and attracted a lawyer.
The investigation found out that the criminal used deepfake technology to clone the speech and voice of the director.
A total of 17 people participated in the fraudulent scheme.
The stolen money was transferred to many bank accounts scattered around the world.
Two of them are open in the US Centennial Bank, so the UAE law enforcement agencies asked for help from the US.

The cause of the extinction of mammoths
Scientists have found that mammoths died out due to climate change
Photo: Stanislav Krasilnikov / TASS
An international team of researchers found that the cause of the extinction of mammoths in Siberia was primarily a sharp climate change, not human activity.
The article is published in the journal Nature.
Woolly mammoths became extinct only about four thousand years ago.
They were not only the main source of meat of ancient people – the latter made from their bones the basis for dwellings, from their tusks made harpoons and even musical instruments.
Therefore, there is a widespread theory that the main cause of extinction was humans.
Researchers from the Institute of Earth Sciences of St. Petersburg State University together with colleagues from the UK, Denmark, China, Norway and the United States decided to restore the appearance of the tundrosteppe, which was inhabited by mammoths.
To do this, they using the shotgun method — obtaining from a random massive sample of cloned fragments of the original sequence — analyzed the DNA of ancient plants and animals collected from 535 different places in the Arctic, where the mammoth lived, over 20 years.
They also analyzed the DNA of more than 1,500 modern plants and animals.
Researchers were able to map the distribution of populations of mammoths and other representatives of the megafauna of the tundrosteppe.
They saw that over time their populations and genetic diversity became smaller and smaller — making survival increasingly difficult.
With the end of the Pleistocene about 12 thousand years ago and the accompanying retreat of glaciers and the formation of rivers, lakes and marshes, vegetation has decreased in volume, and it has become insufficient to maintain the previous level of populations.
As the climate warms, trees and swamp plants have taken the place of former mammoth pastures.
“We have shown that climate change, in particular rainfall, has directly led to changes in vegetation.
According to our models, people did not have any influence on them [mammoths], ” said the first author of the work, a researcher at the University of Cambridge Yuchen Wang.
However, the extinction of mammoths was influenced not only by the warming of the climate itself.
“His speed was the last nail in the lid of the coffin – they (megafauna tundrosteppe – approx.
“Tape.ru ”) could not adapt quickly enough, when the landscape radically changed and food was not enough, ” said the head of the scientific group, Professor of Copenhagen and Cambridge universities Eske Willerslev.

It would seem that mammoths existed for millions of years and survived several ice ages.

But as soon as they encountered humans, they began to die out.
Finally, we were able to prove that the problem was not only climate change, but also the speed of these changes.
This was the last nail in the coffin – the mammoths could not adapt quickly enough when the landscape changed dramatically and food became scarce.
- says the author of the study Eske Willerslev, a professor at the University of Cambridge and director of the Center for Geogenetics of the Lundbeck Foundation at the University of Copenhagen.
The team, led by Prof. Willerslev, sequenced the DNA of plant, animal, and their fossilized excrement, coprolites.
The selection of these samples lasted about 20 years and allowed us to fully understand why the majestic animals died out.
After the end of the last cooling, the glaciers began to melt.
The environment quickly became quite humid, leading to a chain change in flora.
Typical mamut habitats and pastures became increasingly swampy and vegetation changed accordingly.
As a result, there is simply no food left typical for animals.

Will the US punish India for Russian air defense systems
Senators asked Biden not to impose sanctions against India for the purchase of S-400
In the United States, they fear the possible imposition of sanctions against India for the purchase of Russian S-400 air defense systems.
Two US senators urged Joe Biden to abandon the application of the law against New Delhi, because of which only a few years ago the US imposed restrictive measures against Turkey.
The experts interviewed by Gazeta.Ru are confident that the White House will fulfill this demand, since the pressure on India contradicts the anti-China strategy of the United States.
However, experts do not rule out that Washington will still try to influence Russian-Indian cooperation in the military sphere.
Republican Senator John Cornyn and his Democrat colleague Mark Warner sent a letter to US President Joe Biden urging him not to impose sanctions against India under the CAATSA (Countering America ’ s Adversaries Through Sanctions) Act.
Possible restrictive measures against New Delhi are related to the purchase of weapons from Moscow, including a major contract for five S-400 anti-aircraft missile systems, the delivery of which should begin before the end of 2021.
“We are concerned that the upcoming transfer of these systems will trigger sanctions under the Countering America ’ s Adversaries Through Sanctions Act, which was enacted to hold Russia accountable for its malign behavior, ” the senators wrote.
In their opinion, Washington ’ s concern about the Russian-Indian contact is understandable, but in recent years, India has allegedly reduced the number of transactions for the purchase of Russian weapons.
“In this regard, we urge you (Mr. Biden) to grant India exemption from CAATSA in connection with the planned purchase of S-400 Triumph anti-aircraft missile systems, ” the authors of the letter emphasize.
Waiting for sanctions against India
The US has consistently threatened India with sanctions for the purchase of Russian S-400 air defense systems, but New Delhi refuses to break the contract with Moscow, pointing to the need to protect its borders, including against the background of the strengthening of China and confrontation with Pakistan.
There is no certainty that Washington will indeed impose restrictive measures against New Delhi.
On the one hand, the United States has already resorted to sanctions pressure on its allies through CAATSA, thereby reacting to their purchase of Russian weapons.
Turkey signed a contract with Russia for only one set of S-400, which led to a protracted US-Turkish conflict, the introduction of personal and economic restrictive measures against representatives of the Turkish military-industrial complex.
Moreover, Ankara lost the program of production and purchase of the latest American F-35 fighters, but did not abandon the Russian air defense systems.
According to Dmitry Suslov, Deputy Director of the Faculty of World Economy and World Politics at the Higher School of Economics, India is unlikely to see a repeat of the Turkish scenario, since the situation here is completely different.
“Ankara is an ally of the United States and a member of NATO, but New Delhi is not.
India is a welcome partner for Washington, but not an ally.
New Delhi makes it clear that it will not become an ally of the United States.
The White House will not impose sanctions on India.
This is due to Washington ’ s desire to strengthen relations with India and involve New Delhi in a coalition to contain China in Asia, ” the expert explained.
India is a key participant in all American plans to counter China, Suslov continued.
In fact, without this country, any attempts by the US to contain China are doomed to failure, and the Biden administration is well aware of the central role of New Delhi.
“Washington, even at the level of symbolism, emphasizes the main role of India in countering China, in particular, this is manifested in the concept of the Indo-Pacific region.
It was in order to engage New Delhi and emphasize its status that the US renamed the Asia-Pacific region to the Indo-Pacific region for itself.
The Biden administration fully follows this terminology and logic, so the probability of imposing sanctions against India is zero – it would be detrimental to a much more strategically important direction of American foreign policy, ” the expert added.
At the same time, the efforts of the Americans to build allied relations with India are unlikely to interfere with Russian-Indian cooperation.
Professor of the Department of Oriental Studies of MGIMO, Doctor of Historical Sciences Sergei Lunev believes that the United States will not be able to force India to abandon military cooperation with Moscow.
“India will not refuse to cooperate with Russia, because New Delhi pursues a policy of balancing and maneuvering.
Strengthening relations with the United States, including in the military-political sphere, India does not want to become a military-political ally of Washington.
New Delhi needs freedom of hands in this regard, hence we can proceed in relation to cooperation with Moscow, ” the expert said.
What the US will do to India
Military-technical cooperation between Russia and India has a long history.
The interaction between the two states began during the existence of the USSR and quite fruitfully continues to this day.
This worries the US, as evidenced by the consistent pressure on New Delhi from the White House and the Pentagon over the purchase of S-400.
From the point of view of Dmitry Suslov from the HSE, the United States really does not like Russian-Indian military cooperation, although the Americans understand that New Delhi is not going to give up its independence.
"India will not become the new Japan and will not be a military ally or satellite of the United States.
And any attempts to pressure or impose restrictive measures will only weaken US-Indian cooperation.
Therefore, the best way to somehow weaken Russian-Indian cooperation, from the point of view of the Biden administration, is not to put pressure on India, but as if allowing it to cooperate with Russia, to increase its own interaction with New Delhi, ” the expert said.
According to Suslov, the United States expects to naturally weaken the interaction between India and Russia by strengthening the US-Indian relations on an anti-Chinese basis, given India ’ s concern over the strengthening of China.
That is, US-Indian cooperation will compete against Russian-Indian cooperation as US-India relations strengthen, as well as mutual discontent between Moscow and New Delhi over China increases.
Because India expresses great concern and dissatisfaction with how deeply Russian-Chinese relations are developing, including in the military sphere, ” the expert said.
At the same time, Sergey Lunev from MGIMO believes that it is not so easy to reduce Russian-Indian cooperation, given India ’ s dependence on arms supplies from Russia.
According to him, Moscow ranks first among the military-political partners of New Delhi in terms of arms supplies.
“Russian-Indian cooperation in this regard is so significant that all the main tanks in India are Russian-made, and the aircraft are mainly Soviet, the same applies to the Navy of the country.
That is, in addition to the fact that New Delhi pursues a policy of military maneuvering and balancing, it should take into account its certain dependence on Moscow for arms supplies.
The United States will not be able to change the position of India, at least in the foreseeable future, ” the expert concluded.

China unveils fastest quantum computer in history
Spread the love
China ’ s new quantum computer is a million times more powerful than Google ’ s machine.
It may be the fastest in the world.
Competition between Washington and Beijing in the field of quantum technologies is growing.
Physicists in China claim to have built a quantum computer whose speed and performance exceeds the American counterpart of Google.
The article is published by the peer-reviewed journals Physical Review Letters and Science Bulletin.
A supercomputer called Jiuzhang 2 can solve in one millisecond a task that the fastest conventional machine would take 30 trillion years to complete.
Also, scientists told about the Zuchongzhi 2 - this is an improved version of the previous machine, it was built three months ago.
Pan Jianwei, lead author of the new study, said that Zuchongzhi 2, a programmable superconducting quantum computer with 66 qubits, is 10 million times faster than Google ’ s 55-qubit Sycamore.
At the same time, the Jiuzhang 2 has fewer applications, but it can work at an incredible speed - 100 sextillion times faster than ordinary computers.
But while the characteristics of these new machines hint at a computational revolution, they won ’ t hit the market anytime soon.
So far, both computers can only work in a special environment and only for hyper-specific tasks.
And, even with extreme caution, they still make a lot of mistakes.
Chinese scientists said they plan to fix the situation in the next 4-5 years.

The head of SOTSPROF Vostretsov spoke about the ineffectiveness of the seven-hour working day in Russia
The idea of switching to a seven-hour working day was criticized by the chairman of the association of trade unions SOTSPROF Sergey Vostretsov.
He believes that this will be an ineffective measure.
The corresponding proposal was previously made by a member of the State Duma Committee on Labor, Social Policy and Veterans Affairs Svetlana Bessarab.
In her opinion, the transition to a seven-hour week can improve the situation with the demographics in the country.
According to Vostretsov, this idea is extremely unsuccessful.
He believes that the option of switching to a four-day working week, which was previously proposed by the deputy chairman of the Security Council of the Russian Federation Dmitry Medvedev, is more appropriate.
“In my opinion, reducing the working day to seven hours is unlikely to give an increase in the birth rate.
In general, I think this idea is pretty pointless.
I am much closer to the proposal of Dmitry Medvedev about a four-day working week, so that people can really feel that they have an additional day off, ” said Vostretsov in an interview with the Federal news Agency.
In addition, the head of SOTSPROF believes that this hour will be simply wasted on the road.
This is especially true for residents of large cities.
Vostretsov added that employees who are ready to switch to a four-day work and at the same time work more intensively should be given this opportunity.
The politician believes that this will be a good incentive for people not to portray activities, but to really work.
Vostretsov previously positively assessed the idea of ​ ​ introducing additional days of rest in Russia.
He believes that it is necessary to postpone all holidays to weekends, thereby making a working week of four days long.

Prevention of heart disease: how to protect pensioners themselves
18 0 01.11.2021, 08: 09 | News, Society
Sports can significantly improve the health of people in adulthood.
Scientists from France conducted a study according to which exercise in adulthood helps people with heart disease to improve their health, reports Novoe Vremya.
A couple of weeks ago, a group of scientists published a study according to which excessive amounts of physical activity can negatively affect the work of the brain.
But, as for the work of the heart - here everything can be the opposite.
Recently, researchers from the French University of Burgundy said that sports can significantly improve the health of people in adulthood who have heart problems.
"Aging is associated with several factors, such as increased inflammation or oxidative stress, that predispose people to cardiovascular disease.
As a result, older patients tend to be less fit than younger patients, and their physical condition worsens more quickly after cardiovascular disease, "the study authors write.
The researchers analyzed data on 733 patients who had undergone cardiac rehabilitation programs in the past few years.
Patients were divided into three age groups: up to 65 years, from 65 to 80 years and over 80 years.
It turned out that people who exercised for several weeks not only improved their health, but also reduced levels of anxiety and depression.
Most progress was seen in people under 65.
"These improvements will undoubtedly have a big positive impact on patients' independence and quality of life, and can help both doctors and patients understand how beneficial exercise rehabilitation can be."
According to experts from the British Health Council, there are several types of light physical activity that can best help you protect your heart in old age.
You can start with a little physical activity:
- slow walking on the street;
- house cleaning;
- regular movement around the house.
Moderate physical activity includes:
- cycling;
- water aerobics;
- dancing;
- table tennis.

Cave lions in Europe and mammoths in the United States.
Scientists have told what the Earth would be without Homo sapiens
The researchers say that in general, the planet could be an exciting place, which would be inhabited by representatives of megafauna.
Scientists believe that without humans, the Earth would be a more wild and fertile place, in which giants such as ostrich moa birds with a height of 3.6 meters still lived.
They lived in New Zealand for millions of years, but disappeared 750 years after their land was invaded by man, writes LiveScience.
The vanished giant moas and eagles of Haast, whose wingspan was 2.6 meters or more, are a small example of how human activity has changed the planet.
The survival of such large animals is crucial in thinking about what the Earth would be like without humans, as such giants have a crucial influence on landscapes.
Senior lecturer in zoology at the University of Gothenburg in Sweden, Seren Forby, says humans have played a crucial role in the extinction of many large mammals.
Forby led the study, published in the journal Diversity and Distributions.
It said that without humans, the Earth would resemble an ecoregion in East Africa, the Serengeti, teeming with life.
In such a scenario, extinct animals, along with elephants, rhinos and lions, would live throughout Europe.
For example, the African lions (Panthera leo) would still be replaced by cave lions (Panthera spelaea), a larger species that lived in Europe about 12,000 years ago.
At the same time, America would be home to larger relatives of elephants and bears, as well as unique species such as the glyptodon – car-sized armadillos and giant sloths.
“In a world without humans, there would be a lot more different species of large mammals, as well as a much more open habitat, ” says Forby.
Elephants or other species of large animals do not tolerate obstacles in their search for food.
In such cases, the territory acquires a less wooded appearance.
The world would be brighter
During the last Pleistocene Ice Age (2.6 million to 11,700 years ago), the Earth was rich in megafauna.
Much of it went extinct after the end of this ice age or millennia later.
A 2021 study from the journal Nature found that climate change had wiped out woolly mammoths as well as other Arctic megafauna, but humans also put additional pressure on these species by hunting them.
Christopher Doughty, an ecologist at the University of Northern Arizona, modeled how large animals, among other things, affected ecosystems by moving seeds and nutrients during eating and defecating.
The expert found that the movement of elements such as phosphorus, calcium and magnesium, which play a crucial role in life, decreased by almost 90% along with the disappearance of megafauna.
The researcher emphasizes that without human intervention, all the necessary elements would be evenly distributed throughout the landscape.
Thus, the soil would be more fertile and productive.
Agriculture and zoning make land less fertile compared to systems in the wild.
Such increased fertility means that the Earth would be much richer in crops and colors, the planet would definitely be brighter without humans.
Without humans, the climate would be different.
Human induced global warming is known to have raised the average temperature by 1 degree Celsius since the early 20th century.
Consequently, the weather on the planet would be cooler without humanity.
A 2016 study in the journal Nature found that current warming delayed the onset of the ice age by at least 100,000 years.
But this should not have happened for another 50,000 years, so it is unlikely that without humans there would be another ice age on Earth right now.
People are inevitable
Modern humans (Homo sapiens) were not always the only hominins on the planet.
The disappearance of Homo sapiens could open up new perspectives for Neanderthals.
There is no single answer to the question of why the Neanderthals died out about 40 thousand years ago.
There were probably several reasons for their disappearance, and Homo sapiens are the main suspects.
Professor Chris Stringer from the Natural History Museum in London believes that the competition between Neanderthals and humans was one of the reasons for the disappearance of the former.
“If Homo sapiens hadn ’ t come to Europe about 45,000 or 50,000 years ago, I think Neanderthals and their descendants would still have lived on Earth, ” Stringer says.
The expert notes that Neanderthals led a complex life in Europe, they faced climate change, were a small group with low genetic diversity.
“Neanderthals probably were already in distress when modern humans came to their lands, and this factor could be the last, ” the expert notes.
But humans could have influenced the survival of more than just Neanderthals.
At least there is another relative of Homo sapiens who shared land with humans and Neanderthals: the Denisovans.
This line is closer to Neanderthals than to modern humans in terms of genes and appearance.
Judging by a number of studies, people interbred with Denisovans, because modern people continue to find the DNA of Denisovans.
It is assumed that Denisovans had a wider range of habitat than Neanderthals.
They may also have more genetic diversity than Neanderthals.
"Perhaps the Denisovans were even better species for survival than the Neanderthals," Stringer said.
In general, Denisovans and Neanderthals could pave the way similar to H. sapiens, moving from hunting and gathering to the development of agriculture.
"There is no obvious reason why Neanderthals or Denisovans would not have evolved if they had the time to do so," he said.

IBM showed what the quantum computers of the future will look like (video)
The new electronics and cooling system will allow to launch large-scale quantum computing as early as 2023.
IBM has announced a next-generation integrated quantum computing system called IBM Quantum System Two.
Details are described on the official website.
According to the developers, the platform is designed to work with future quantum processors with 433 and 1121 qubits.
It is based on the principle of modularity, when functional parts are combined into complete blocks.
This approach allows you to change the capabilities of the machine, increasing the number or power of computing modules designed for certain tasks.
The IBM Quantum System Two prototype is expected to be launched in 2023.
In the meantime, the company has shown what the future hall with quantum computers will look like.
In the video, you can see that the processors want to place in huge luminous blocks, most of which will be hidden at the lower level, probably cryogenic installations.
There will be a lot of free space between the equipment to move employees.
As IBM notes, due to the increase in the number of qubits in processors, high flexibility of the control equipment and resources for scaling are needed - the ability of the machine to cope with increasing workload.
These include tools that allow users to control qubits, as well as cryogenic cooling systems that maintain a very low temperature so that particles exhibit their quantum properties.
The design of the IBM Quantum System Two will receive advanced scalable electronics to control qubits, as well as cables and cooling elements of higher density.
The engineers, in collaboration with Bluefors, have developed a new cryogenic platform that will allow the most efficient use of space for auxiliary equipment and larger processors and provide specialists with convenient access for maintenance.
Thanks to the new design, the working space of the cooling unit was expanded and it became possible to connect several quantum processors.
“IBM ’ s Quantum System Two offers a glimpse into the future of the quantum computing data center, where the modularity and flexibility of the system infrastructure will be key to continuous scaling, ” said Jay Gambetta, IBM ’ s vice president of quantum computing.
In 2019, IBM launched the world ’ s first integrated quantum computing system called IBM Quantum System One.
Over the past three years, the company has made it the foundation for its cloud services in the US, Germany and Japan.
In addition, on November 16, IBM partnered with Yonsei University in Seoul to deploy the country ’ s first Quantum System One in South Korea.
Earlier, IBM created a new 127 qubit Eagle quantum processor.
According to the developers, no classical computer is able to keep up with it in performance.
According to IBM CEO Arvind Krishna, to solve the same problems, an electronic machine needs to use more bits than there are atoms on Earth.
At the same time, quantum computers will not be able to solve any problem and require complex equipment to work.

According to him, both sides are interested in substantive filling and making the visit successful.
The Russian Foreign Ministry stressed that Russia and India have a similar vision of the model of the emerging more just and equitable polycentric world order.
“Our countries demonstrate the identity or proximity of positions on the most important issues of peace and security, advocate compliance with the norms of international law, strengthen the collective principles of interstate communication, adhere to the principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of sovereign states and respect for the cultural and civilizational identity of peoples, ” the Russian Foreign Ministry added.

Why does Russia have an alliance with India?
Russian defense and foreign ministers Sergei Shoigu and Sergei Lavrov arrived in India this morning, followed by President Vladimir Putin.
Why do Moscow need these visits and an alliance with New Delhi in general?
Before independence, India was a British colony.
After World War II, when the Cold War broke out between the USSR and the United States, India opted for neutrality.
Along with Egypt and Cuba, it joined the Non-Aligned Movement.
At the same time, relations with the USSR among the Hindus were quite close.
Suffice it to say that the Soviet Union provided significant military assistance to India under Khrushchev during the Indo-Chinese conflict – despite the fact that China was a communist country and Moscow ’ s ally in the Cold War.
In the same 60s, Moscow supported New Delhi in a dispute with Pakistan over Kashmir.
Moreover, it was with the participation of the Chairman of the Council of Ministers Kosygin that the Second Indo-Pakistani War was stopped.
On January 10, 1966, the declaration on the cessation of hostilities was signed in Tashkent.
Today, India is trying to follow the same course of non-alignment.
However, as then, geopolitical realities – the ongoing rivalry with China and Pakistan – are forcing Hindus to look for strong allies.
In this sense, India has a small choice: the United States, the European Union and Russia.
Europe could be a support, but traditionally tries not to get involved in the battle of the Titans.
Even in the U.S.-Russia standoff, Europeans are calling for a lessening of passions, and by the way, they recently challenged U.S. intelligence findings about an alleged Russian invasion.
The EU has close economic ties with China, plus the EU is a very heterogeneous structure.
France is now resentful of the Anglo-Saxons because of the anti-Chinese AUKUS, and Germany is very modest in foreign policy.
As for the US itself, this would be a very convenient option for India.
The United States is now actively opposing China, both economically and through military alliances.
India participates in the QUAD alliance and, together with the United States, Japan and Australia, conducts naval exercises in the Indian Ocean.
The last of them, in October, became the largest in 40 years.
Only the whole snag of the alliance with Washington for New Delhi is that the Americans demand complete submission.
The United States literally forbids India to buy S-400 air defense systems from Russia, threatens it with sanctions, as it was with Turkey.
In such a situation, Russia is, if not the only, then at least a unique partner for India.
Yes, unlike the United States, it will not oppose China, but at the same time, Russia sells India weapons that help maintain the balance of power in Asia.
We are also taking steps to reduce escalation.
For example, it is thanks to Russian efforts that India and China are now full members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.
Is it possible to imagine joint military exercises between the Hindus and the Chinese under the auspices of the Pentagon?
Of course not.
But almost such exercises took place this year: in September, 200 Indian military personnel, as well as Chinese and Pakistani observers, participated in the Russian-Belarusian Zapad-2021 maneuvers.
In addition, Russia is trying to bring China and India closer economically.
Within the framework of the BRICS format, there is a joint pool of reserve currencies that helps strengthen the financial sovereignty of the five countries.
In short, Russia is strengthening India ’ s defenses and working to reduce its conflict with China.
Separately, it is also worth mentioning the North-South project, which leads from Russia to India and vice versa, which will strengthen trade opportunities and macro-regional importance of both countries.
Thus, today ’ s visit of Putin, Lavrov and Shoigu to India is extremely important.
Relations with India need to be strengthened.
This increases our role in Asia, strengthens our cards to the United States and, in the good sense of the word, allows us to balance a growing China.
After all, an alliance with India is good money.
For 30 years on the supply of aircraft, tanks and "Kalashnikovs" the Russian budget was replenished by $60 billion.

India may become the first foreign buyer of the new S-500 air defense system, but deliveries will begin only after meeting the needs of the Russian army, Deputy Prime Minister Yuri Borisov said.
“After we supply these weapons to our native army in the right amount, India will probably be the first on the list if it expresses a desire to buy these modern means, ” Borisov said on the air of the RBK-TV channel.
India is one of the main buyers of Russian weapons.
The volume of the portfolio of arms orders of India from Russia is about $15 billion, and in total since 1991, India has ordered weapons worth about $70 billion, reported the Federal Service for Military-Technical Cooperation (FSMTC) of the Russian Federation.
It was officially reported that in early October 2018, a contract was signed on the sidelines of Russian-Indian negotiations at the highest level for the supply of S-400 Triumph air defense systems to India (Almaz-Antey Concern).
Under the contract with a total value of $5.43 billion, India will receive five regimental sets of S-400.
In November, the head of the FSMTC Dmitry Shugaev told Interfax that Russia began supplying India with the first batch of S-400 systems.

Diets to prolong life: encouraging myths and sobering facts
Scientists figured out what ’ s wrong with intermittent fasting, keto, and other dietary restriction regimes.
Published by Reminder.
The history of research on the effects of diets on aging began more than 100 years ago.
The first work, published back in the 1900s, showed that laboratory mice, after reducing their diet, began to age more slowly and live longer.
From this, it was concluded that calorie restriction is a key factor in slowing aging.
It not only increases the life expectancy of rodents, but also slows the development of diseases and functional disorders.
Numerous studies of the late XX century picked up and popularized this idea.
The most popular diets are still based on calorie restriction, refusal of certain macronutrients or reduction of meal time.
This prompted a team of scientists from the University of Washington to figure out whether such approaches to nutrition really have a scientific basis.
And most importantly, do they work for people?
What diets can prolong life
In their review, the researchers analyzed different types of diets — with calorie restriction and without.
Calorie Restricted Diets
• Limit daily calorie intake by 20-50%.
The ratio of proteins, fats and carbohydrates remains unchanged.
• Limit the daily intake of calories, but only by reducing fats and carbohydrates in the diet.
Protein consumption remains unchanged.
• Periodic fasting.
Between the periods of eating should pass at least a day.
In studies of intermittent fasting, laboratory mice were fed three times a week.
• Diets that mimic fasting.
Periods of low-calorie keto-diet for 3-4 days alternate with a three-day restoration of the total caloric content of food.
• Ketogenic diet.
Reducing the intake of carbohydrates (in studies in mice - up to 1% of the total caloric content) to stimulate ketosis - a condition in which fats become the main source of energy instead of glucose: from them the liver synthesizes ketone bodies.
Diets without calorie restriction
• Restriction of protein intake.
• Limit the consumption of amino acids - methionine, tryptophan and amino acids with branched side chains.
There are many of them in food proteins: meat, fish, legumes, eggs and so on.
• Intermittent fasting.
Limit food consumption over time.
A popular pattern is 16: 8: 8 hours of eating followed by 16 hours of fasting.
• Periodic fasting with preservation of caloric content.
Daily fasting is compensated by increased calorie intake during the period when you can eat.
Animal studies
In studies on rodents, diets really increase life expectancy, and at the same time improve metabolic health: restore the balance of glucose and insulin, inhibit the development of metabolic and age-related diseases.
Most of these effects are associated with a decrease in caloric intake.
The authors of the review noticed that in popular studies, rodents consumed fewer calories, even when this was not part of the scientists ’ plans.
For example, in a study of the effect of intermittent fasting, in which scientists trained mice to eat a daily calorie intake for 12 hours, the rodents still consumed less food than their counterparts in the control group.
It is believed that diets that limit the intake of protein and amino acids work by slowing down the growth processes.
The lack of protein leads to a deficiency of growth hormones, so in mice on a low-protein diet, sexual development first slows down, and then the aging of the body.
But even here the effect is often associated with the fact that on a low-protein diet, experimental animals simply eat less.
In mice that are restricted access to protein food, but retain the total caloric content of the diet, life expectancy increases by only 15% - against 50% with an overall reduction in calories.
So the less you eat, the longer you live?
It's not that simple.
There is scientific evidence that refutes the conclusions about the “rejuvenating ” effect of calorie reduction even for rodents (1, 2).
Not to mention primates: one of two long-term studies found that low-calorie diets had no long-term effect on the lifespan of rhesus monkeys (1, 2).
Probably, the effect of reducing calories depends on many factors that are simply not taken into account in the experiments, from gender to genetics.
Studies involving people
They, for obvious reasons, are many times less than experiments with rodents.
But they expose at least one important idea: restrictive diets are uniquely beneficial for those already suffering from obesity and / or metabolic disorders.
As for healthy people, everything is ambiguous.
For some, diets work, although they have little effect.
It doesn ’ t work for someone.
And sometimes even harm your health.
For example, in one study, intermittent fasting led to impaired glucose metabolism in healthy subjects.
Why do life extension diets affect humans and mice differently?
There may be several reasons.
Rodents may be more sensitive to interventions in the usual diet.
Laboratory mice are bred specifically for research: they reach sexual maturity faster and begin to multiply earlier.
Calorie deficiency in their case immediately affects growth hormones and other biological indicators of aging.
Laboratory tests are performed under sterile conditions.
Mice are kept in rooms in which there are practically no pathogenic bacteria.
For rodents, they simulate a regular change of day and night, so their circadian rhythms are never disturbed.
And the temperature of the environment is usually kept below that which is comfortable for mice, so they have to spend a lot of energy on thermoregulation.
People live in completely different conditions – and this can affect the effects of diet changes.
We have a calorie deficit often weakens the immune system and reduces the recovery ability of the body, which negates the possible benefits of diets.
Strict diets are difficult to adhere to, and few people manage to do it for a long time.
Usually, a restrictive diet is alternated with the usual diet, which can lead to dangerous weight fluctuations.
It is proved that such jumps are fraught with hypertension, kidney and heart diseases.
But the key may be the genetic factor.
Studies on animals with a more diverse genetic background - wild rodents and fruit flies - have shown that in individuals with a certain genotype, diets may not prolong, but, on the contrary, shorten life.
On the question of whether there is reliable evidence that diets to prolong life actually prolong people ’ s lives, the authors of the review answer: no.
But there is hope: new methods of monitoring the aging process are being developed.
Thanks to them, scientists will soon be able to conduct experiments that will show how changes in nutrition actually affect age-related processes in humans.

According to the plan, on July 24, the first prayer will be held in Hagia Sophia in Turkey, after it was decided to convert the building of the Orthodox church into a mosque.
The leaders of many Muslim countries are invited to take part in it.
Erdogan ’ s invitation came from Qatar and Azerbaijan.
The remaining heads of state have not yet responded to the Turkish president.
Remind me!
The Turkish government decided to change the status of the architectural monument and the Orthodox Church of St. Sophia and convert the room into a mosque.
The Pope said that this situation causes him grief.
The Patriarch of Ecumenical and Constantinople, who recently received a great number of churches on the territory of Ukraine, and did not demand the transfer of the museum to the Diocese of Constantinople in a timely manner, said that the creation of a mosque in the museum building can be negatively met in the Orthodox world.
It is expected that the first prayer in the new mosque will be attended by about 1000-1500 people.
All quarantine conditions will be met, participants in prayer will be given masks, and disinfectants will be placed everywhere in the cathedral so that people can treat their hands and their prayer mats.
During the prayer, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan will also be present in the cathedral, along with Turkish ministers, leaders of the ruling Justice and Development Party.
As previously reported, all the frescoes and mosaics at the time of prayer will be covered with curtains.
On July 10, a Turkish court ruled that the decision to convert the mosque into a museum in 1934 was illegal.
Erdogan immediately signed a decree on assigning Hagia Sophia the status of a mosque.
The move has sparked international criticism and concern, including from Greece, the United States and Russia, as well as UNESCO and Pope Francis.
Turkey insists that the status of the architectural monument is its internal affair.

The economy of Turkey is not in the best condition, but Erdogan was again able to win the Hagia Sophia.

"Stop looking at the crystal ball": in the world of work, you need to adopt new rules of the game
What to expect in 2022 from the world of work?
At the moment, it is difficult to predict something, and experts point out that with the beginning of the third year of the pandemic, workers still have to face unprecedented difficulties.
Moreover, the return to full-time work begins to seem more and more unreal, reports BBC Worklife.
Two years ago, when the pandemic began, many businesses began to organize work remotely.
The idea was - "so far remotely, but then everything will return to the rolled rails."
But the spread of the omicron strain delayed the plans of millions of workers to return to the workplace.
In addition, the activities of enterprises and the labor market have so adapted to the “new reality ” that a return to“ normal work before the pandemic ” seems increasingly unrealistic.
However, we still don ’ t know what or how will affect the way we work.
Last year, on January 5, people hoped that 2021 would bring some stability or strengthen the hybrid model of work.
Somewhere it worked, but somewhere it did not, as there were new variants of the virus, as a result of which it is too early to talk about stability.
The situation often changes and it is difficult to find a point of reference that would allow us to say where we will be in 12 months.
Experts who study the labor market and employment have found several trends that have already been outlined quite clearly.
This can be considered topical issues in the world of work this year, which will determine its future.
Shortened work weeks may be relevant
The call for shorter working weeks and a more concentrated work schedule is gaining ground in the world.
Many companies and even governments are already experimenting with various alternative work schedules.
We need to change the way we work and the way we work.
The standard 40-hour working week “from 9 to 5 ” was introduced back in the days of the Industrial Revolution about 200 years ago.
This was the last time the work schedule changed.
It is no longer effective in the long run, as our work has become more intense, thanks to new video conferencing technologies and the Internet, ” says Abigail Marks, a professor at the Newcastle University School of Business.
“Those in business and politics should take into account all aspects of how not to overload workers, while at the same time thinking about maintaining or increasing productivity.
This decision often comes in the form of a four-day work week.
Work that is concentrated in a shorter period of time and more free time is good news for the mental health of workers and the balance between personal and work life, ” says the professor.
Although it looks that this idea in 2022 may receive even greater support, this model of work, unfortunately, will not suit all workers.
Marx recalls that switching to a four-day working week may be convenient for individual office workers, but not for all workers.
“A four-day work week may be the privilege of a limited group of white-collar workers.
Such a change in labor policy will not affect low-paid labor in any way.
You also need to take into account the specifics of the work: in the field of IT and many other services, a four-day work week is virtually impossible, ” says Marx.
Therefore, she points out that in 2022, the main challenge will be finding a middle ground between those workers who can enjoy an elastic work schedule and those who do not.
“This way we can come to a fragmented labor market.
As long as various office workers and important officials can enjoy fewer hours of work, for others, especially health care workers, this will not even be possible in theory, ” says the expert.
Different benefits as the main way to attract employees
In 2021, there were not enough workers around the world.
This problem is not going anywhere, and in 2022 it will also create new problems.
According to Allison Sullivan, manager of corporate communications at Glasdoor, this is because "the factors that create this problem will not disappear as the pandemic and the growing demand for food delivery continue to be around."
This means that employers will be forced to change tactics when hiring new employees, as well as have to think about how to keep those who are already working.
The methods that helped before the pandemic are no longer going to help.
Associate Professor Anthony Klot of the University of Texas pointed out that this year a popular trend was a personal approach to each potential and actual employee.
"In 2022, we will see employers pay more attention to the interests of employees to improve relationships with those who are already working, as well as attract new professionals," Klot said.
This is not only the basis of good business performance – elasticity and employee care is becoming a major advantage, and more and more workers expect this from their employers.
Sullivan argues that workers will also become more demanding, so the employer must be willing to provide everything necessary to ensure a comfortable working environment.
As a result, companies will have to develop "personalized tactics of personnel organization.
Instead of a one-size-fits-all program, companies will have to take care to give each employee an individual approach, ” says Klot.
Sullivan points out that a personalized approach can be expressed in salary increases, or, for example, in helping with loan repayment, or extended maternity leave.
Another important nuance is to determine the mental health of an employee as a priority.
After all, burnout last year was a major problem for many companies, and more people are leaving their jobs, or thinking about it.
“Even bastions of career and work like Wall Street are beginning to act and changing the culture of work, focusing more on workers than just performance, ” says Klot.
Employees will not return to the same office.
When some (not all) workers finally return to work in the office - this year, or later, it will have to be concluded that the "new normal" office will not be like the one we have seen before.
Nicholas Bloom, a professor of economics at Stanford University, points out that companies will adapt jobs to all the requirements of hybrid labor, taking into account how people actually want to work.
Bloom, who has been studying the future of office work for many years, points out that the days that all employees will be in the office will be rare.
When they do, it will be unusual and even uncomfortable.
He pointed out that he had heard “horror stories about employees who have to go to an office where there is an unusual silence. ”
In other words, such work in the office, as before the pandemic, will remain in the past.
More and more companies are introducing a hybrid model in their work, where individual employees are sent to the office and the rest remain at home.
Under this model, offices are also adjusted, where everything is now equipped so that it is possible to comply with all the requirements of epidemiological safety.
"Separate meeting rooms, small soundproofed rooms for video calls, as well as free choice of workplace.
Employees no longer like being in the crowd.
Therefore, offices adapt to this by providing employees with a convenient and accessible environment where there is enough space to meet colleagues in person, ” Bloom said.
Another important thing is the need for office space itself.
Experts point out that the need for offices will not disappear, and their area will not change.
Although it is expected that the number of hours worked on site will still be 30% less than before the pandemic, companies are not going to reduce the area of ​ ​ their offices.
“While the hybrid model, where we work both remotely and on-site, will be relevant, the office will remain an integral part of the job. It ’ s impossible to imagine a job without a specific base, ” says Bloom.
The Road to the Unknown Continues
Although man by nature tries to make predictions and hope for the best, much is still almost unclear.
The main thing is that we don't know - what exactly we don't know.
At the beginning of the pandemic, many analysts predicted that a return to office work would largely happen by the summer of 2021, when vaccines became publicly available.
However, this deadline continues to be pushed back to the future.
Delta- and omicron strains of the coronavirus cause concerns about public health, so plans to return to the office continue to be delayed.
“What we ’ ve learned over the past two years is to stop looking at the crystal ball, ” said Canina Blanchard, a professor at the University of Western Ontario.
There are things that give hope for a return to “normal life before the pandemic, ” such as vaccines, coronavirus medications, and a short period of self-isolation.
But we know that there are many unknowns in the future (a good example is the omicron, which unexpectedly changed the plans of many companies).
We also do not know what to expect from the future, as everything can change in an instant.
Therefore, with forecasts and hopes for 2022, you need to be careful.
Especially when it comes to returning to “normal life. ”
It is very possible that the "new normal" situation is the rules of the game that we must accept.
“What we clearly know is that in 2022, as in the previous two years, the most important thing will be health and its preservation.
Life will still be very chaotic and even abnormal, "Blanchard said.

Do you think the supporters of a flat earth in the shape of a bagel drew this idea from the Old Testament?
As if not so!
It was presented to them by Dr. Rosenpenis in 2008.
On the Flat Earth Theory forum, he jokingly offered a rationale for his theory, writing:
"I used advanced scaled astrophysical professional academic software to create a model of the geoponchik, the most delicious celestial body of our planet Earth, covered with sugar icing."
In short, the doctor “joked ”, and those present were happy to believe that our world has the shape of a massive donut with a giant hole in the middle.
It is not known how the "hypothesis" grew legs, but it widely diverged among supporters of the flat Earth.
To know, the poor people experienced a lack of scientificness in their own worldview.
At the same forum, but already in 2012, another flat-earth proponent named Varaug added to the idea of more science-like.
He seriously argued that our planet is a ring or, to use scientific terminology, a torus.
Say, we can not see the hole in the middle due to the fact that the light bends, following the curve of the torus and making the hole “invisible ”:
“I have a theory that the Earth actually has the shape of a torus (bagel).
But the light is warping, so we can't see it. "
Explaining why no one has ever fallen into this hole, the “theorist ” asks other forum participants to imagine the Earth in the form of a“ donut with jam ”, in the direction of which gravity acts.
According to him, day and night still exist because the Earth in the form of a donut makes a revolution every 24 hours, and the hole is at an angle of 90 degrees to the Sun.
A flat Earth proponent suggests that the torus shape was formed as a result of the gravitational attraction of rocks, dust and pieces of cosmic matter to an orbit without a central focus.
This actually created a ring-shaped planet orbiting the void.
Scientists have disproved this theory, explaining that the Sun could not rise and set as it does if the Earth had a gaping hole in the middle, and we could not see day and night as now.
Oxford professor Dr. Anders Sandberg points out that on a donut shaped Earth, the clouds would be three times higher and pushed by stronger winds.
Well, people living near the hole would see “double seasons ” when summer is replaced by winter and vice versa.

A convinced libertarian, Doctor of Economics, a follower of the Austrian school, a member of the Argentine Congress from the Freedom, Forward! coalition, during the 2021 election campaign, he promised voters to abandon the parliamentary salary, which currently amounts to 205,000 Argentine pesos (due to the gap in quotations of the official and unofficial dollar exchange rate, in rubles this amount can be from 73 to 140 thousand).
The newly minted deputy kept his promise - on January 12, his first salary will be raffled in the "lottery".
On a specially created site "My Word" has already left more than 250 thousand applications for participation in the draw.
To date, the counter has recorded a million two hundred thousand visits.
A special correspondent of the FAN international editorial office in Argentina tells about the eccentric initiative of the newly minted parliamentarian.
“Let it all be decided by chance. ”
The only requirement for those who want to participate in the drawing of the deputy salary is to be over 18 years old and not to be legal entities.
Sufficiency, political beliefs, gender, profession - all this does not matter.
People simply upload their passport data and get a certain number that will participate in the draw.
“I refused the idea of targeted donation, because it is too common political ploy, ” Milei said at a meeting with Argentine media. – I believe that it is immoral to manage in this way with state (that is, not belonging to me) money.
It goes against my philosophy of life.
Let everything be decided by chance, and my participation in this will be as neutral and detached as possible. ”
The recording will be open until 10 am on January 12.
And at 19.00, at the next open lesson of the “popular economy ” – which Javier Miley is going to hold right on the beach in the resort town of Mar del Plata – the winner will be announced in the presence of a notary.
All his subsequent salaries, the deputy promises to play in the same way.
Miley at the point of attack
Javier Miley claims to be an anarchocapitalist and a supporter of minarchism (Political ideology, which involves the involvement of the state only for the protection of life, property and contractual relations. – Note FAN).
The son of a housewife and a bus driver, he came into politics from academia and the “elite ” stratum of Argentine economists — with experience in the Association of Private Pension Funds (AFJP), the Argentine branch of HSBC Holdings plc, the WEF and private financial institutions.
In the parliamentary elections of 2021, Milei ran for deputy in the capital district and scored 17.04% of the vote.
This is a very significant result for an independent candidate who began his political career almost before the elections and, as he himself says, “completely by accident ” – as a result of a skirmish with a representative of the ruling party during a round table on one of the Argentine TV channels.
Milea ’ s harsh statements (as well as the leather jacket in which he went to meetings with voters and debates with opponents) quickly made him very popular among young people and those Argentines who are tired of traditional politics and its predictable discourse.
Milea ’ s “fan club ” was not frightened by the abundance of numbers in his speeches, nor by the eccentric candidate ’ s love for complex concepts, which he generously subdued with obscene expressions; nor by the promise to“ burn the Central Bank ” (perhaps this is his only election promise that has not yet been fulfilled).
“In my first month in Congress, I managed to do what I told my constituents.
On December 9 (this is officially recorded), I stopped working in the private business in order to completely exclude possible interference with my parliamentary activities.
I voted against subsidies.
He opposed a new tax on private property, precisely because he promised not to vote for creating new taxes or raising old ones.
He signed the draft law on the reduction of VAT.
And now I will play my salary – because I also promised, ” Milei said.
From Love to Hate
Although Miley and his Freedom Forward party are formally in opposition to the ruling Frente de Todos coalition, the opposition Juntos por el Cambio party does not always share the position of an eccentric economist, especially on key issues.
So, his decision to refuse the deputy salary caused indignation from another deputy - Sabrina Ahmechet, who also represents the capital district in the lower house of the Argentine parliament.
“What does he live on and how is he going to pay the bills? ” asked Sabrina indignantly on Twitter, and immediately clarifies his position.
After all, if not, then only the rich will be engaged in politics, as was mostly the case in the 19th century. ”
Another parliamentary lady, Patricia Bulrich, who heads the coalition “Together for Change ”, Javier Miley clearly favors.
One way or another, the more active the polemics, the more brightly the figure at the center of the discussion is highlighted.
And the more political capital that Miley will surely find where to invest in the medium and long term.

Scientists have found a plant that reduces blood sugar by 29%
Scientists have found a plant that reduces blood sugar levels by 29 percent, and also significantly reduces cravings for sweets.
We are talking about jimnema sylvester or jimnema forest - woody shrubs from the forests of India, Africa and Australia.
Its leaves were used in ancient Indian medicine.
According to the medical portal Verywell Health, recent Western studies show that jimnema can reduce blood sugar levels in people with type 2 diabetes.
“Amazingly, jimnema can make sweet foods taste less sweet, so you ’ ll end up wanting to eat less of them.
The herb is well known for its ability to reduce fat accumulation and promote weight loss due to its enzyme inhibiting properties, "the authors report.
And the Daily Express newspaper writes that people with type 2 diabetes who consumed 400 mg of extract from the leaves of jimnema daily for 18-20 months, fasting blood sugar decreased by 29 percent.
One study also found that, thanks to the powerful antioxidant activity of jimnema, it can help prevent organ damage often seen in diabetes.
At the same time, scientists warn that people taking diabetes medications or using insulin should not simultaneously take jimnem without the supervision of a doctor.
