Who needs to be hungry?
What is therapeutic starvation?
We deal with the doctor.
Get a charge of vivacity, increase working capacity, lose extra pounds - and all this with the help of therapeutic fasting?
That sounds tempting.
This is how the effects of adherents of this diet are often described.
But who and when is it really useful and what do doctors think about it?
Candidate of Medical Sciences, Doctor of Clinical Laboratory Diagnostics CITILAB
A healthy body does not need special “cleansing ”, it knows how to do it on its own.
What is “healthy obesity ”?
Doctors have not yet reached a consensus.
4 scientific evidence that sport is good for mental health
What is therapeutic starvation?
The basis of therapeutic fasting is the voluntary refusal of food (and sometimes water) for a certain time.
The method belongs to the field of alternative medicine, promises the renewal and purification of the body.
According to this theory, during a stressful period (with abstinence from food), the digestive system goes into recovery and purification mode.
But what's really going on?
Irina: After a week of fasting, ketone bodies (metabolic products) accumulate in the body - they are normally few.
They are formed from adipose tissue when there is no necessary energy, namely from carbohydrates.
An increase in their number can cause feelings of lightness and euphoria, which is called ketone euphoria.
Photo: unsplash.com / @ giancescon
Many adherents of fasting are sure that at this moment detoxification occurs, the body removes toxins and toxins - from this there is a feeling of lightness.
In fact, slag (if we are talking about the human body, and not waste in chemical production) is a myth.
A healthy body does not need special “cleansing ”, it knows how to do it on its own.
To do this, we have the liver, kidneys, bile and urinary system - they help to remove from the body all the waste products of metabolism.
What happens to your body if you starve?
By depriving the body of food, in particular, glucose, we abandon the main source of energy.
The reserves of this organic compound in the body are enough for 12-16 hours, after which the processes of “energy production ” from other sources are launched.
One-day fasting can pass without consequences, but a longer one will harm the body.
The first changes occur on the third day and are localized in the gastrointestinal tract.
Instead of hydrochloric acid, unsaturated fatty acids enter the stomach, this creates an imaginary feeling of saturation.
Further, the synthesis of amino acids is activated.
Irina: The intestinal microflora suffers, the beneficial bacteria eventually die.
The acid-base balance shifts towards acidification.
The body lacks nutrients, vitamins, minerals.
Such deficits will not manifest in a day or two without food, because we know how to store vital substances.
However, with a longer abstinence from food, the body will begin to deplete.
Photo: unsplash.com / @ jexm
This is observed even with strict diets, not to mention the complete rejection of food.
Especially dangerous is starvation, implying the rejection of water.
It literally threatens life.
Even short-term dehydration can have long-term negative effects.
Who should not starve?
In these cases, it is strictly contraindicated to starve:
• oncological diseases;
• problems with the digestive tract;
• gastritis and peptic ulcers;
• any diseases of the central and peripheral nervous system;
• lack of body weight;
• tuberculosis and HIV infection;
• arrhythmia and other diseases of the cardiovascular system;
• autoimmune pathology;
• predisposition to the formation of blood clots;
• chronic diseases of the liver and kidneys, especially with the development of insufficiency of the function of these organs;
• diabetes mellitus.
Obesity can occur even at a normal weight.
How it works
What happens to the body when we are hungry?
Answered by Doctor
Who then benefits from therapeutic starvation?
There are times when hunger may be necessary.
Therapeutic fasting is not a diet, not a way to "cleanse the body of toxins", but a medical method necessary in a limited number of situations.
Such fasting should take place according to the doctor's prescription and under his supervision.
In what cases is temporary abstinence from food applied?
Photo: istockphoto.com
• When preparing for surgery or examination as prescribed by a doctor.
In some mental disorders, for example, the acute phase of an attack of schizophrenia (carried out under strict medical supervision).
Irina: Lack of food, not to mention water, leads to a deterioration in the supply of oxygen to the heart, which, in turn, can lead to heart failure.
Prolonged fasting introduces the body into a ketoacidotic coma, which can lead to death.
Fasting can also aggravate concomitant diseases and generally harm the body.
Therefore, this method can be applied only by appointment of a specialist.

Residents of Belgium were allowed to ask the employer to switch to a four-day working week
Author:
Oleg Panfilovich
Date:
The Belgian authorities have allowed workers to submit a request to their employers to switch to a four-day week with pay.
This is reported by The Guardian.
The introduction of a four-day work week is part of Belgium ’ s labour reform.
According to Belgian Prime Minister Alexander de Cros, only about 71% of Belgians under the age of 64 have a permanent job.
This is 10% less than in neighboring Germany and the Netherlands.
Companies may reject an employee ’ s request for a four-day work week, but then employers will have to justify their response in writing.
In addition, companies with 20 or more employees may allow employees not to respond to calls, emails, or messages from 23: 00 to 05: 00.
“Switching to a four-day work week will give employees and companies more freedom in organizing their working hours, ” de Cro said.
He also noted that the new rules will allow you to work an unequal number of hours from week to week - one more and the other less.
• In the UK, a test project with a four-day working week will be launched from June.
About 30 companies will participate.
• The results of two large studies, which took place in Iceland from 2015 to 2019, showed the effectiveness of a four-day work week.
The four-year study involved 3,000 Icelanders (1% of the country ’ s workforce).
They were transferred to a 36-hour working week without a pay cut.
They worked according to the standard schedule (from 09: 00 to 17: 00), and some on night shifts.
The studies mainly involved civil servants from various fields, from teachers to doctors.
• The results showed that people became happier and more productive.
In addition, stress and burnout became less, and the employees and managers themselves noted the establishment of a balance of work and rest.

Artificial intelligence developed by the Israelis is able to duplicate films with the voices of the original
Israeli startup Deepdub has developed a service for translating video content into new languages using machine learning algorithms.
The company uses neural networks to generate the speech of original actors from movies, TV shows, games and advertising.
AI processes voices and then translates them into a new language, preserving the timbre, rhythm, intonation and other important voice nuances in the work of a professional artist.
Deepdub promises to solve the main problems of industries related to voiceover and duplication.
According to Aberdeen, an average of five minutes of storytelling takes an hour to work in a recording studio.
And if the dubbing actor wants to match the original track as much as possible, the time spent on dubbing can increase by another two times.
At the same time, the cost of such services is a significant part of the budget for filmmakers and video game developers - a minute of duplication of one person per language on average costs about $75 for a simple video.
The startup aims to create a one-stop solution for content makers who want to go international or reduce their own costs for translators.
Using synthetic voices based on the original voice patterns of the actors, the startup duplicates movies, games and advertising in the post-production phase.
According to the developers, in addition to reducing costs, dubbing with the help of neural networks gives another advantage - AI reproduces the voice of the original, so the viewer will always watch the film in the form in which it was conceived by the director and performed by the actor. "Our artificial intelligence models allow you to reproduce the characteristics of the voice, using no more than three minutes of original voice data.
The AI-generated voice in the target language can be reproduced at any level of expressiveness, including crying, screaming, talking with food in the mouth, and more — even if the original voice data did not contain this information, ” said Deepdub co-founder Nir Krakowski.
Additionally, Deepdub ’ s algorithms track facial expressions and lip movements of actors.
Thus, the output of the audio track of the startup fully corresponds to how the voice actors work.
The current version of the platform supports six languages, and the startup plans to add six more before the end of next year.
In the long term, the company also intends to take its algorithms to the next level – to teach AI to duplicate voices in real time.
Among the famous works of Deepdub Krasowski mentioned the English-language thriller “Every time I die ” 2019.
The startup dubbed the film into Spanish and Portuguese.
According to the developers, this is one of the first cases when a full-fledged film with synthesized voices was released in the world.
Recently, Deepdub raised $20 million in the series A round. The company will direct the funds received to improve its technologies.

Ever since Russia began to draw troops to the border with Ukraine, the government in Kiev has been frantically trying to enlist the support of the international community.
For the most part, the authorities of the former Soviet republic turn to their partners in the EU and North America.
Thus, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy held meetings with British Prime Minister Boris Johnson, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Olaf Scholz.
Narendra Modi
Ivan Shilov © IA REGNUM
He regularly talks on the phone with US President Joe Biden.
In turn, the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine Dmytro Kuleba held a conference with US Secretary of State Anthony Blinken, and also attended the December meeting of NATO ministers, where Russia ’ s capacity building was discussed.
In a December article for Foreign Affairs, Kuleba urged the West to more actively and persistently support Kiev.
But on February 3, Kuleba made a direct appeal to India, a country in another part of the world, Manjari Chatterjee Miller, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, wrote in an article published on February 22 in Foreign Affairs.
The Ukrainian Foreign Minister noted that if India had unequivocally told the Kremlin that it considers Russia ’ s actions “unacceptable, ” such a step would have been“ a very strong signal of support for [Ukraine] and would have changed a lot. ”
His appeal is not meaningless.
India is an important player on the world stage and has strong ties with both Moscow and Washington.
If New Delhi were to criticize Russia, it would at least demonstrate that the crisis over Ukraine worries countries outside the West.
Such a move would signal India ’ s strong support for democracy and would demonstrate New Delhi ’ s optimism about the future of the India-US partnership.
And that would represent a stark contrast to China, which has been meticulously silent about Ukraine.
Joe Biden and Narendra Modi
The White House
Nevertheless, for India, the crisis is a very complex situation, and any action it takes against Ukraine carries considerable risk.
If it criticizes Moscow, India will alienate an important historical friend and, even worse, bring Russia closer to China, which India considers its biggest external threat.
If it supports Moscow, New Delhi will spoil its relations with the United States, a new but very valuable strategic partner.
If it says nothing, India may evoke rejection by both countries, which may then view it as a fickle and unreliable partner.
This state of affairs highlights an increasingly acute dilemma for New Delhi.
India is a state that could eventually become a great power in an increasingly multipolar world, and as disputes between countries become more complex (and perhaps more frequent), such states will need New Delhi ’ s support.
India may not like this: the country has long avoided alliances and prefers to focus on its own development, while maintaining friendly relations with major international players.
But international politics is not always favorable to those who seek to remain aloof without ideological justification.
During the Cold War, India was not officially part of any alliance, refusing to get involved in the confrontation of superpowers.
Because of this position, the country sometimes became unpopular — especially in the United States — but many recognized that its foundation lay in moral ideology.
India was a country recently freed from colonialism, and it refused to be a pawn in the imperialist policies of a superpower.
In the post-Cold War world, India has begun to talk about maintaining “strategic autonomy, ” but this is only the old idea of non-alignment, only wrapped in a new package and motivated by economic and military interests rather than moral principles, and therefore it has not attracted the same degree of understanding.
India does not need to get involved in every conflict.
But it and other emerging powers will have to recognize that as the world becomes more multipolar, it becomes increasingly difficult to avoid compromises.
In the case of Ukraine, this means that India must seize the initiative.
New Delhi and Moscow have maintained friendly relations for decades, and the former can use the accumulated goodwill to quietly pressure Russian President Vladimir Putin to find a diplomatic solution to the crisis without harming his reputation.
Such a move may not be natural for India, but ending a full-scale war is crucial to India ’ s global standing.
Vladimir Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Russian-Indian talks in New Delhi.
October 5, 2018
Kremlin.ru
Russia has already deployed military forces to Ukraine ’ s two separatist regions for “peacekeeping purposes. ”
If the crisis escalates into a Russian invasion, New Delhi will lose a lot both economically — oil and gas markets will experience an unprecedented jump in prices — and politically.
In India ’ s ideal world, the United States and Russia would balance against China, which would be impossible if they were in conflict.
During the last Ukrainian crisis, India unconditionally sided with Russia.
Although much of the world has condemned Moscow ’ s “annexation ” of Crimea, New Delhi has spoken out against Western sanctions against Russia.
Shivshankar Menon, then India ’ s national security adviser, stressed that Moscow had “legitimate interests ” in Ukraine and that“ annexation ” was an “internal matter. ”
India ’ s foreign ministry said it would oppose “unilateral measures ” such as sanctions against the Russian government in response to the Kremlin ’ s actions.
Putin warmly thanked India for this strong support, and then responded in kind.
In 2020, India annulled the special autonomous status of Kashmir, which caused a wide transnational reaction.
But Moscow refused to condemn the act, using language that echoes Menon ’ s previous description of Ukraine.
"This is a sovereign decision of the Indian government," Russian Ambassador to India Nikolai Kudashev said.
Shivshankar Menon
Sebastian Zwez
But this crisis seems larger than the previous one, and India ’ s relations with Washington have deepened in the meantime.
In 2020, the United States provided information and equipment to the Indian military in its border confrontation with China.
When New Delhi organized a diplomatic boycott of the 2022 Olympics, Washington offered public support.
(Beijing made a soldier involved in attacks on the Indian military a torchbearer.)
The two countries now regularly coordinate their actions in the field of regional security within the framework of the Quadripartite Security Dialogue, which makes it much more costly for New Delhi to openly support Moscow in the confrontation over Ukraine.
In an effort to avoid a crisis, India ’ s Foreign Ministry called for a “peaceful settlement ” and stressed the need for“ sustained diplomatic efforts ” to resolve the situation.
But this is an understatement that is unlikely to please both Russia and the United States.
This, of course, will not please Ukraine, where about 20 thousand citizens of India live.
India ’ s efforts to remain silent may also lead Moscow to believe that New Delhi supports it, which the government would like to prevent.
When India abstained from voting on January 31 in the UN Security Council to discuss the crisis, the Russian ambassador thanked India, as well as China, for their support.
Instead, India can help resolve the crisis by quietly pressuring the Kremlin to move toward a settlement.
This means that India must stress the long-term consequences of the absence of a diplomatic settlement.
Russian-Indian relations are not one-sided — the former also benefits from supporting the latter — and New Delhi should make it clear to Moscow that Russia cannot count on India ’ s support for an invasion of Ukraine.
India should also remind Russia that it is also interested in balancing against China, especially in Central Asia, where both Moscow and Beijing have economic interests and want to create a sphere of influence.
India could point out that a military confrontation would make it harder for Russia to compete with Beijing, isolating Moscow from other potential partners.
The invasion may also force the government of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, which many international observers have repeatedly described as authoritarian, to move to an even closer partnership with the United States to defend its commitment to democracy and the Quartet.
Narendra Modi and Joe Biden.
September 25, 2021, Washington
The White House
It will be an unpleasant conversation for India.
But it is worth it, both for New Delhi and for the whole world.
India is the only major power that can rely on decades of friendship to put pressure on Moscow to tell it the bitter truth.
This means that New Delhi has a unique opportunity not only to strengthen its geopolitical position, but also to prevent a deeply destabilizing and bloody conflict.
An alternative for India trying to avoid a crisis in order to preserve “strategic autonomy ” is no good.
Instead of promoting New Delhi ’ s interests or strengthening its global status, silence will portray India as an opportunist and self-serving partner who does not deserve broader cooperation or support.

20 + facts about the fairy tale about Snow White, after reading which you involuntarily think: “And it is definitely for children? ”
In 2023, a remake of Snow White will be released on the big screens.
It, like the legendary cartoon of 1937, is being prepared by Disney.
Few people know that the studio ’ s products are different from the original Grimm fairy tale.
For example, the prince did not kiss Snow White, it was dropped and thereby saved by his servants, and his stepmother was destroyed not by dwarves, but by dancing shoes.
We at AdMe.ru studied the legendary story and came to the conclusion that the story of Snow White can seriously captivate not only children, but also adults.
Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs was published by the Grimm brothers in 1812.
The tale is considered to be pure fiction, but recent research indicates that this story could have happened in real life.
One of the prototypes of Snow White is Maria Sophia von Ertal, born on June 15, 1729 in the Bavarian town of Lore am Main.
Maria Sophia ’ s father, a large landowner, married again after the death of his wife.
Maria Sophia left her home, the castle of Lore, because she could not stand the mistreatment of her stepmother.
She went blind and spent the rest of her life in a convent.
Maria Sophia lived 71 years and was never married.
• Dwarves that appeared in the fairy tale could be associated with the mining town of Bieberhemund: very low miners worked in the tunnels, who, by the way, wore bright hoods.
A glass coffin is a possible reference to the famous glass factory of the region.
In the castle of the Maria Sophia family, a mirror was stored, which was famous for its extremely smooth surface.
It was called the “talking mirror ” because it“ always spoke the truth. ”
Today, the mirror is kept in the museum in which the castle was turned.
Another prototype of Snow White is called the German Countess Margarita von Waldeck.
The exceptional beauty of the girl became the object of envy of her stepmother Katharina von Harzfeld.
When Marguerite was 16 years old, her father and stepmother sent her in search of a profitable party at the royal court of Brussels.
She and the future king of Spain Philip II fell in love with each other, but the Prince ’ s entourage hoped to find a more promising party for him.
Therefore, when in 1554 the life of Marguerite was suddenly interrupted, it was believed that either the Spanish authorities or the stepmother, who later became the main and only villain in this story, could be involved.
• This story and fairy tale has other coincidences.
The German region, the birthplace of Margarita, was a copper deposit.
Simple people started working on it from childhood.
Close mines did not allow workers to straighten in full growth, and the youngest of them - to grow, they remained low.
• The fairy tale of the Brothers Grimm is also filled with unjoking passions and details with deep meaning.
Children, they are likely to say nothing, but adults will be interested in re-reading the story.
• There are many symbols in the story.
For example, a magic mirror is endowed with a magical meaning, a poisoned apple refers to the Bible, and 7 dwarves can symbolize 7 days of the week.
• Pushkin wrote his work based on the Russian folk tale.
But a similar story with similar characters has many peoples.
A Scottish folk tale tells the story of the king ’ s wife, who learns that her daughter is prettier, from a trout floating in a stream.
Greek - about 3 sisters: the older ones chase the younger one into the forest because she is more beautiful than them.
There she meets 12 months and lives with them as a sister.
And in the Italian fairy tale tells about the owner of the hotel, who constantly asks guests who is the most beautiful in this world.
And when one of them points to her daughter, the poor girl is driven into the woods.
• Interest in the story described by the Grimm brothers has always been there.
In 1912, a Broadway play was staged based on the fairy tale, and in the 1930s, a cartoon was created at Disney Studios.
• In the 1930s, animation was created by sequential changes of individual images.
For 1 second of animation in "Snow White" required from 12 to 24 drawings.
The animators manually drew each movement and facial expression of the character.
The cartoon differed from the fairy tale one important thing: the dwarves acquired individual features.
For example, Dopi did not have a beard, he wore clothes that were large to him - so the multipliers made him younger than the rest of the dwarves.
At one time, he was very popular - there were rumors that Disney even considered creating a series of short films about him.
Walt Disney presents the audience dwarves, 1937.
The plot of the cartoon is an adaptation of the original story recorded by the Brothers Grimm.
For example, a prince does not kiss a sleeping Snow White.
He decides to take the crystal coffin to his father.
On the way, the coffin is accidentally overturned, a piece of poisoned apple falls out of Snow White's throat, and she comes to life.
In the end, the mirror suddenly tells the stepmother that someone prettier than her has reappeared, and that someone is the prince ’ s bride.
Then the queen goes to the wedding, where the prince recognizes her, forces her stepmother to put on hot shoes and dance in them until she gives up her breath.
The story of Snow White is interesting and in demand today.
In 2023, Disney is preparing to release a remake of Snow White, starring Rachel Zegler and Gal Gadot.

Who in the East will be wrapped in the Ukrainian flag, and who will not.
Western media about the reaction of Israel, India and the Arab world to the war in Ukraine
March 11, 16: 47
This material is available in Ukrainian
Residents of Tel Aviv participate in a rally in support of Ukraine on the third day of the Russian invasion, February 26, 2022 (Photo: Ronen Zvulun / REUTERS)
While India refrains from direct criticism of the Kremlin, and the Arab world, under pressure from the West, takes a tougher stance towards Russia, Israel is trying on its role as a mediator.
Publications of the foreign press in the review of NV.
In the early morning of March 5, a plane with a high-ranking delegation secretly flew from Tel Aviv to Moscow.
Despite the Sabbath, when the Torah instructs all Jews to refrain from work, except in situations where there is a threat to life, the passengers of this aircraft worked, writes the British news Agency BBC.
Among them were Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and Housing Minister Zeev Elkin, who was born in Kharkiv and has long served as a Russian translator for Israeli leaders.
Bennett is the first foreign leader to meet Vladimir Putin face to face since his invasion of Ukraine began.
What are the chances that he could mediate the worst crisis between Russia and the West since the Cold War?
So far, Israel ’ s response to the war in Ukraine has been mixed.
This country did not join the powerful Western sanctions against Russia and did not support the UN Security Council resolution against Moscow.
However, Israeli Foreign Minister Yair Lapid condemned the Russian attack, and Israel eventually joined the UN General Assembly resolution demanding the withdrawal of Russian troops from Ukraine.
Israel has strong ties with both Russia and Ukraine.
However, it is unlikely that this country will be able to be an influential arbiter who tries to persuade each of the parties to make concessions, writes the BBC.
Rather, it would be suited to the role of a transmitter of messages from one to the other of the unequal parties to the conflict.
But how effective is it?
Moreover, as some observers note, “only a fool can trust Vladimir Putin now. ”
Some Israeli officials still believe that their country can serve as a “bridge ” between Moscow and the West.
Israel sees itself as a card that must remain on the table and can be played by the West if necessary.
In Ukraine, however, they gratefully perceive Israel ’ s attempts to “end the war ”, but do not hide a certain disappointment.
“We have good diplomatic relations, but I do not feel that he [Benet] is wrapped in our flag, ” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said after a conversation with the Israeli Prime Minister.
Since the beginning of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, a lot of criticism has been voiced against India because of its refusal to publicly condemn the aggressor.
However, certain signs indicate that the leadership of this country does not approve of Moscow ’ s actions, writes the British edition The Guardian.
In particular, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in the latest of several recent telephone conversations with Russian dictator Vladimir Putin, called on the head of the Kremlin to direct talks with the Ukrainian president to “greatly contribute to the ongoing peace efforts. ”
When there were numerous votes in the UN Security Council against Russia ’ s actions, India abstained.
And in her statements, she spoke bluntly about the need for dialogue, diplomacy and respect for territorial integrity, never appealing directly to Russia.
For many, this looks like Putin ’ s approval, but experts in Indian diplomatic history and traditions note that not everything is so clear.
“India ’ s discontent with Moscow is evident from the way they treat Ukrainians, from the statements it makes at the UN and its repeated calls for de-escalation of violence, ” Avinash Palivala, deputy director of the South Asia Institute at the University of London ’ s School of Oriental and African Studies, told The Guardian.
The war in Ukraine has put India in a difficult position, because it sees important partners in both Russia and the United States.
As a result, she now has to “walk the diplomatic rope. ”
With Russia, India is united by historical friendship and arms imports: from 60% to 80% of Indian defense systems come from the Russian Federation.
In addition, India sees Moscow as an important counterweight to Beijing ’ s growing strength.
While the volume of trade with India, which does not include weapons, the United States significantly exceeds Russia: $100 billion against $9 billion.
In addition, the rapprochement of Russia with China is alarming in Delhi.
What real consequences the war in Ukraine will have for India is still unknown, says Tanvi Madan, director of the Indian Project at the Brookings Institution in Washington.
“But there are likely to be difficult decisions ahead of [India], ” he concludes.
Meanwhile, the Arab world is reacting in its own way to the events in Ukraine.
When the West quickly united against the aggressor, the Arab countries paused.
Its purpose was to give a certain signal to Washington, notes the American magazine Time.
On February 25, Saudi Arabia abstained during the UN Security Council vote for the first resolution against the invasion of Ukraine.
Three days later, the Arab League, which includes 22 countries, issued a statement in which it did not condemn the Russian invasion and almost did not express support for the Ukrainians.
However, a few days later, the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, one of the most influential Arab states, joined the condemning resolution of the UN General Assembly.
Why did it take that time?
After all, among the countries of the region, only one directly supports Putin, and this is Syria under the leadership of Bashar al-Assad.
But other states, while prioritizing relations with the West, are not hostile to Moscow.
They see Russia as a significant global power influencing their region, flirting with which can help them improve their own positions in relations with the West.
That is why in the early days of Russia ’ s invasion of Ukraine, it was noticeable that the Arab states wanted to leave their opportunities as open as possible, and not push Moscow away if it really wasn ’ t necessary, Time analyzes.
That all changed when the West made it clear that the war in Ukraine was not a case where “neutrality ” would be acceptable.
This does not mean that the tensions between the Arab states and the West are over.
So, the actual ruler of Saudi Arabia, Mohammed bin Salman, who is condemned in Washington because of his likely order to kill journalist Jamal Khashoggi, will certainly try to get concessions from US President Joe Biden, suggests the publication.
In particular, he will try to gain recognition of his status as the de facto ruler.
However, as a result of the war in Ukraine, relations between the Arab world and the West are changing.
“The Russian invasion has called into question some of the basic foundations of this relationship, and it remains to be seen what the new ones will be. ”

08: 19 24.03.2022
Russia ’ s military operation in Ukraine provoked the expected harsh reaction of the West.
The United States, the European Union (EU) and the United Kingdom adopted several packages of sanctions, including against the financial, energy, transport and technological sectors of the Russian economy.
Following the restriction of the work of Visa and MasterCard payment systems, many foreign companies announced a partial or complete cessation of activities in Russia.
However, not all states supported the sanctions campaign.
Moreover, China and India have already started talking about expanding cooperation with Russia.
"Lenta.ru" understood why the "Asian giants" decided to support the northern neighbor and what they hope to get in return.
Friendship without barriers
Russia has been developing friendly relations with China for almost a decade since Chinese President Xi Jinping took over as chairman of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) in 2013.
Back in 2019, he said that “over the past 70 years, China-Russia relations have reached an unprecedented high level, ” and described relations with Russian President Vladimir Putin as deeply personal friendship.
In early February, Putin, at the invitation of Xi Jinping, attended the opening of the Winter Olympics in Beijing.
The visit was the occasion for full-scale negotiations, as a result of which the parties signed a package of intergovernmental, interdepartmental and commercial documents, as well as agreed to increase the volume of bilateral trade to $250 billion.
Friendship between the two states has no borders, there are no forbidden zones in cooperation, the strengthening of bilateral strategic cooperation is not directed against third countries, is not subject to the influence of a changing international environment and situational changes in third countries.
After Putin announced the start of a special operation in Ukraine on February 24, the Chinese authorities did not condemn the actions of the Kremlin and did not call the operation “invasion ”.
However, Xi Jinping called on Russia and Ukraine to sit down at the negotiating table to de-escalate the situation and said that China stands for respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states.
Recently, the situation in eastern Ukraine has changed dramatically and attracts increased attention of the international community.
Xi Jinping
General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China
Nevertheless, after the introduction of Western sanctions against Russia, the official representative of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) of the PRC Zhao Lijian said about the harm of economic restrictions in the settlement of the crisis.
He pointed out that the sanctions imposed created new problems leading to mutual loss and multiple economic losses.
She refrained from condemning Russia ’ s operation in Ukraine when voting in the UN Security Council and India.
The Chinese government continues to be neutral – like China ’ s political leadership, it calls for a cessation of hostilities and a return to diplomatic dialogue, avoiding criticism of Russia ’ s actions.
Special attention to the crisis in Ukraine was drawn by the death of a 22-year-old Indian student in Kharkov.
The incident caused indignation in Indian society, which turned into a demand for the authorities to take immediate measures to organize the evacuation of more than 20,000 Indians who are in Ukraine.
Narendra Modi and Vladimir Putin
Narendra Modi and Vladimir Putin
Photo: Mikhail Klimentyev / RIA Novosti
Later, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a telephone conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin and discussed the issue of the export of Indian citizens from Ukraine.
Putin assured that all instructions were given to the military, and they are doing everything possible to ensure the safe removal of foreigners from the combat zone and their return to their homeland.
The prompt reaction of the Russian authorities and the promise to investigate the death of the student allowed to smooth out the possible consequences and maintain friendly relations with the Indian side.
Not the last role, however, was played by the pragmatic attitude of official Delhi: Western sanctions and their attempts to isolate Russia economically open up new attractive short-term and long-term prospects not only for China, but also for India.
The Asian Giants
Today, China is Russia ’ s key economic partner.
The growth of trade in ten years was about 165 percent.
Trade turnover in 2021 increased by 35.9 percent and amounted to $146 billion compared to 2020.
The plans of Russia and China are to increase it to 200 billion by 2024.
However, there is a significant imbalance in the economic relations between the two countries.
While China accounted for about 18 percent of total trade with Russia, Russia ’ s share of Chinese trade was just over two percent.
Under sanctions and a ban from Western countries on the supply of a number of high-tech goods to Russia (microelectronics, marine and navigation equipment), military and dual-use products, aircraft and spare parts, goods for use in the aviation and space industry, equipment and technologies for oil refining, as well as reducing demand for Russian energy resources, this imbalance will increase.
Photo by Shizuo Kambayashi / AP
According to Vasily Kashin, director of the Center for Comprehensive European and International Studies at the Higher School of Economics, the restrictions imposed on Russia will make China our country ’ s main trading partner for decades to come, which will inevitably affect coordination in the military and political spheres.
“Everything will be pretty clear here.
The situation, in which we will depend on one China, will require some policy adjustments from us, ” the expert believes.
It is impossible to say that we will be a "junior partner", but we will have to take into account the interests of China to a much greater extent than before, and this will be expressed in some joint actions in the military sphere - most likely, in the region of Northeast Asia.
Vasily Kashin
Director of CKEMI NRU HSE
In such circumstances, the partnership with India, guided by its own aspirations, which on a global and regional scale often do not contradict the interests of Russia, becomes especially significant for Russia.
For both Moscow and New Delhi, bilateral Russian-Indian relations have an independent value.
Today, India is a leading importer of fertilizers, oil and vegetable oil, and the Russian side is one of the main suppliers of these goods.
In addition to hydrocarbons and fertilizers, the Indian side buys from Russia products of the military-industrial complex and nuclear energy.
In turn, India exports to Russia pharmaceutical, agricultural and other goods.

However, trade between the states is significantly inferior to Russian-Chinese cooperation.
Last year, it amounted to about $12 billion, which was a record figure in the entire history of trade relations between India and Russia.
Nevertheless, Putin and Modi during the meeting in New Delhi within the framework of the Russian-Indian summit "Russia - India: Partnership for Peace, Progress and Prosperity" assessed the volume of bilateral trade as "not corresponding to the potential of strategic partnership" and stated the need to intensify efforts to increase mutual trade to achieve the target of 30 billion by 2025.
Not canceled this desire and new sanctions, which significantly complicated for India the system of payments with Russia.
Russia ’ s disconnection from SWIFT paralyzed about $500 million for goods already sent to Russia.
As reported by The Hindu newspaper, the Indian government has already ordered the creation of a group to study the impact of Western sanctions against Russia on the Indian economy.
It included representatives of the Ministries of Food and Consumer Affairs, Fertilizer, Trade, Foreign Affairs, Oil and Natural Gas.
According to Alexei Kupriyanov, a senior researcher at IMEMO RAS, Russia previously played the role of a mediator in relations between India and China, at the same time a mediator of such a force that helped to find mutual understanding between states in the event that relations were deadlocked.
Now objective circumstances make possible the scenario of closer rapprochement between Russia and China.
The Indians are extremely concerned that, as a result of Western sanctions, Russia may even closer to China, and are trying to prevent this.
That is why they do not plan to curtail further cooperation with Russia - because it will only push Russia into the Chinese arms
Alexey Kupriyanov
Senior Researcher, IMEMO RAS
Ignoring threats
Despite the attractiveness of the voids that have formed in the Russian economic space, both Beijing and New Delhi have close trade relations with Washington.
Thus, the United States is the third largest trading partner of China after ASEAN and the EU (if you evaluate not by individual countries, but by macro-regions).
755.6
billion dollars was the trade turnover between China and the United States in 2021
More extensive economic ties allow the United States to require India and China to comply with the sanctions regime against Russia, since both countries depend on foreign technologies, on Western intellectual property, on the supply of components and developments of European and American companies.
The White House is already considering the possibility of imposing sanctions against India because of the import of Russian weapons and the position regarding the special operation of Russia in Ukraine.
India is now a really important security partner for the United States, and we appreciate that.
I hope that the leadership of India will decide that it is time to distance itself from Russia
Donald Lou
Assistant Secretary of State
According to Vasily Kashin, director of the HSE CCEMI, the abuse by the American side of its role in world finance can cause a negative reaction from the Indian authorities, who "very strictly protect the independence of their foreign policy."
India does not see itself as a "junior partner" of the United States, who is told who to be friends with and with whom not.
Attempts at harsh and brutal pressure will cause an extremely negative reaction
Vasily Kashin
Director of CKEMI NRU HSE
Jen Psaki
Jen Psaki
Photo by Patrick Semansky / AP
Similar threats are being made against China.
White House spokeswoman Jen Psaki promised China “significant consequences ” from the United States for violating sanctions against Russia because of the situation in Ukraine.
However, the Chinese government has repeatedly stated that it does not accept unilateral economic pressure and the application of the principle of extraterritoriality.
When considering the issue of Ukraine and relations with Russia, the American side must strictly and accurately take into account the concerns of China and prevent the infringement of the rights and interests of the Chinese side.
Zhao Lijian
official representative of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China
Kashin noted that imposing sanctions on China is an order of magnitude more dangerous than imposing sanctions on Russia.
He explained that the Chinese economy controls many key production chains and is a key market for many American businesses, which will require much more careful sanctions pressure on China.
The British newspaper The Guardian, citing sources, reports that the Chinese authorities have already decided to send economic assistance to Russia against the background of a special operation in Ukraine.
The source stressed that Beijing is serious about cooperation with Moscow, since such an initiative allegedly comes from Xi Jinping, who with Putin “shares the opinion of the United States as a despot. ”
Photo by Bikas Das / AP
It does not want to refuse cooperation with Russia and India.
Thus, countries are considering the possibility of switching to trade settlements in rubles and rupees.
The new mechanism will allow Indian exporters to receive payment for their goods in national currency instead of dollars and euros.
It is planned that the Russian bank for this purpose should open an account in the Indian, and the Indian - in the Russian.
* * *
Attempts to exert economic pressure on countries actually translate the confrontation into a political plane.
The economic well-being of the state becomes the subject of bargaining, which has to be sacrificed as a sign of political loyalty to this or that bloc of countries.
Both China and India consider themselves exclusively independent players in the international space.
The authorities of these countries do not want to obey the political will of the United States, to lose the benefit of cooperation with Russia and consider offensive instructions dictating how and on what conditions to build relations with other states.
Russia will remain a strategic partner for both China and India.
However, in the face of Russia ’ s loss of other alternatives, cooperation will be disproportionate.
The Russian side is more likely to retain its role as a mediator in India-China relations.
India is not interested in the loss of a supplier of goods of the military-industrial complex and in the rapid rapprochement of Russia with China.
China, in turn, is not interested in breaking the Russian-Indian cooperation in order to prevent India from rapprochement with the United States.

The Ministry of figures opposed the ban on the emigration of IT-specialists
20
The Ministry of Digital Development of the Russian Federation opposed legislative restrictions on movement for employees of the IT sector.
The corresponding message was published on March 25 on the website of the Ministry of Statistics.
The statement said that such measures could have a destructive impact on the industry as a whole, and noted the creation of comfortable conditions as the only way to retain staff.
“The Ministry of Digital Affairs of Russia does not support any legislative restrictions related to the movement of IT personnel and their employment.
Such measures can lead to an increase in the outflow of specialists and have a destructive effect on the industry as a whole, ” the ministry said.
The Ministry believes that domestic personnel are valued in the world market, so they need to provide decent working conditions, and not impede their movement or employment.
Earlier, RBC reported that the company of Yevgeny Prigozhin “Concord ” has developed a bill that assumes control over the movement of IT specialists and the ability to impose a restriction on their travel abroad.

The Incredible Treasure (Willie Winky, 2022)
A series about two friends – very similar, but completely different.
From the first story, the reader learned how the couple first met and how they got used to each other, and the second tells about their new adventures.
In many countries, as one of the first books for self-reading, traditionally children are offered a series about Kwaka and Toad Arnold Lobel.
The books of Amy Timberlake (winner of the Newbury Prize and a number of others) are perfect for being the next on this path.
Beautiful illustrations by John Klassen, charming characters, fascinating plot - kind and cheerful, devoid of gross moralizing books for senior preschool and primary school age.
Is it possible to make friends with someone who at first sight did not like you at all?
And what happens when your neighbor leads a completely different life than you used to?
Instead of loneliness and neatly laid out in boxes of stones and minerals - crowds of chickens and joint breakfasts.
Is it okay to accept it?
It is much better to learn how to enjoy it!
Christian McKay Hydiker, Scary Stories for Little Foxes.
"Scary stories for little foxes.
The Big City » (Wonder books, 2022)
Children love scary stories.
Children ’ s mystical folklore about the black hand is passed down from generation to generation.
Christian Hydikker uses the childish craving for the creepy and mysterious, and creates images of little curious foxes, going at night to the road for stories, from which their tails turn white.
Their mother warned them of this.
Since the white tip on the tail is a sign of adult foxes, the process of growing up is shown through these horror stories.
Listening to dangerous adventures, foxes gain life experience, which insures them from making their own mistakes.
“Scary stories for little foxes ” are books about family and folklore traditions, adventures, the ability to cope with their fear and emerge victorious from the most confusing situations.
Mark Hartzman, The Big Book of Mars.
A Million Facts from the Pharaohs to the Mask ” (Alpina.Deti, 2022)
"Once upon a time, the planet Mars was a beautiful place where wonderful intelligent beings lived.
The Martians, who ranged in height from 10 to 12 feet (3.05 to 3.66 m), feverishly dug canals to irrigate their arid planet, and desperately tried to make contact with us earthlings.
It is hard to imagine, but this idea of ​ ​ Mars was widely used only a hundred years ago.
The theory that Mars is not just inhabited, but inhabited by intelligent beings, gave rise to a lot of attempts to establish contact with them.
For example, not someone, but Nikola Tesla himself was going to “call ” the Martians.
But interest in the planet arose much earlier.
The ancient Babylonians named the days of the week according to the number of visible celestial bodies.
Aristotle studied Mars and believed that it was closer to the moon, Chinese astronomers called it a fire star and believed that it brings misfortune.
Many science fiction writers wrote about the war of earthlings with Martians, and the colonization of Mars occupies the minds of mankind to this day.
Mark Hartzman has collected the most interesting stories about the red planet from the past and the present.
It is recommended for reading not only for children, but also for adults - many facts will surprise even them.
Finbar Hawkins "The Witch" (Alpina Publisher, 2022)
The book about England of the XVII century is no longer the Middle Ages, but the witch hunt is still in full swing.
Here love and sorrow walk hand in hand, and people are moved by anger and revenge.
The main character of this story - red-haired Evie - is jealous of the younger sister Dill to her mother and lives an almost ordinary life.
But when witch hunters brutally kill her mother and take her sister, Evie is ready to do anything to get revenge on them and save Dill.
A wave of contradictory feelings boils in the girl: love, grief, annoyance, anger that the mother was a witch, and the witches are bad, and because of this they are now left alone.
The author does not spare the reader's feelings - this is a terrible and cruel book, but precisely because it is true.
It is a book about fanaticism and bestiality, embracing people in the name of an idea they believe in, about guilt and remorse, which embraces too late – when nothing can be changed.
Or is it possible?
It turns out that sometimes in order to change something, you first need to change yourself.
Except... that's the hardest part.
To change and remember that even to fight with kindness in the soul – and in the name of good.

The food supplement market is not as tightly regulated as the drug market.

A dietary supplement includes everything from vitamins and minerals to plant and biosimilar foods.
However, for the most part, people use a “supplement ” to refer to a single vitamin or mineral preparation or multivitamin.
The evidence for the benefits of taking dietary supplements is mixed at best.
However, evidence linking dietary supplements to health problems is accumulating.
Harvard Health provides an overview of studies linking high doses of vitamin supplements to a number of health problems.
The health authority shall preface its assessment with the following words:
"Most supplements are safe to take, but there are exceptions."
It says:
High doses of beta-carotene are associated with an increased risk of lung cancer in smokers.
• Supplemental calcium and vitamin D may increase the risk of kidney stones
• High doses of vitamin E can lead to stroke caused by brain hemorrhage
• Vitamin K can interfere with the anticoagulant effect of blood thinning drugs.
• Taking large amounts of vitamin B6 for a year or longer has been associated with nerve damage, which can lead to impaired body movements.
It is important to note that supplements may play an important role for some high-risk groups.

According to him, for certain types and areas of business, the transition to a four-day period will mean a direct reduction in profits.
“My opinion is that the market itself will come to optimization where it is possible, artificial restrictions or, conversely, imposition will only harm, ” the politician said.
The parliamentarian noted that a normal balance between work and free time is quite possible, this was shown by the coronavirus pandemic.
In his opinion, in the conditions of technical improvement and with the introduction of artificial intelligence, part of the usual labor costs will be gradually shifted to equipment and technologies.
And this will allow you to free up time for “investing in yourself and your intelligence. ”
“There is a digital revolution going on in the world today.
Enterprises require less physical strength and more mental strength.
Man is transformed from a worker to a machine operator.

Initiative 2019
Dmitry Medvedev spoke publicly about the possible transition to a four-day working week for the first time, speaking at the 108th session of the International Labour Organization in Geneva in early June 2019.
Then Medvedev held the post of Prime Minister of the Russian Federation.
“Employers will have to take more and more into account the interests of their employees.
It is very likely that the future lies in a four-day work week...
The constant pursuit of success turns into systemic fatigue, chronic stress.
Sometimes people just burn up at work.

Already on October 1 of the same year, the Ministry of Labor of Russia sent a report to the government on the introduction of a four-day working week in the future.
"This issue requires further study...
During the discussion, it was revealed that a sharp mandatory reduction in the length of the working week carries risks, but at the same time has positive aspects.
So, reducing the length of the working week can, for example, lead to an increase in labor costs, as well as the cost of production, ” the Ministry of Labor said on its website.
The Ministry noted that during the discussion of the four-day working week with authorities, employers and trade unions, it was proposed to consider the topic “at the site of the Russian Tripartite Commission for the Regulation of Social and Labor Relations ” (RTK).
It was also planned to establish a working group on working hours and flexible forms of employment within RTC.
“At the same time, reducing the length of working time while maintaining the level of remuneration can contribute to the protection of the employee ’ s health, increasing the efficiency of work and professional capacity for work, personal and professional development, a more harmonious combination of family and work responsibilities, and the release of time for sports, culture, and recreation, ” the ministry said.
“He ’ s completely crazy, isn ’ t he? ”
In January this year, in an interview with RIA Novosti, Deputy Chairman of the Security Council Dmitry Medvedev said that the four-day working week should be moved as the economic prerequisites matured.
“The four-day work week — for some reason, when I said this at the ILO session, there was such a state of shock, as if it were some kind of revelation.

Someone applauded, said: “That ’ s right, you need to work less! ”
Someone said, “He ’ s crazy, isn ’ t he?
And so the money is not enough, and four days if you work, you will receive less ” and so on, — said Medvedev.
He noted that for the first time this was talked about in the 1960s.
“In many countries, such a system has been introduced as a pilot.
In some cases, it has already been implemented and, in fact, legally.
The question is the economic preparedness to work four days a week.
We all understand that a person must recover, that three days off is better than two, you will agree.
But this can not be done just by a stroke of a pen, ” explained the deputy chairman of the Security Council of the Russian Federation.
He added that “60 years ago ” in Russia there was a six-day working week, which today“ seems nonsense ”.
Two days off is totally natural.
Three days off is normal.
But it is necessary to mature all the prerequisites necessary for this.
They are beginning to appear, ” the official said.
In modern Russia, there are already several companies that have transferred their employees to a four-day working week.
So, entrepreneur Sergei Polonsky told KP.ru that the four-day period was introduced in Mirax Group more than 10 years ago.
“Working hard at a large company is stressful.

During this time, people only have time to do some household chores, children or elderly relatives to work out, and there is no time left for themselves: go to the gym, steam in the bath, just lie on the couch with a book - so that the brain reboots.
The head should rest — otherwise it will not be visited by any interesting ideas, ” — said the businessman.
He noted that productivity did not fall: in four days, employees began to do what they had done in five days.

Weekend outfit: when should the Russians rest
2022-04-29 16: 24: 12
Voice-over text
Highlight the main
INCLUDING
off
According to surveys, 40% of Russians are ready for the long May holidays to abandon the long New Year holidays, 60% would like to rest longer in the winter.
How to determine how many days off workers need to recover and at what time of the year — figured out “Izvestia ”.
When Russians want to rest
The service “Rabota.ru ” interviewed in April 3 thousand users of the portal from all regions of Russia to find out how they relate to the May holidays.
It turned out that 14% of respondents are going to extend their weekend, taking a vacation between the May holidays.
72% decided not to do so, and the rest at the time of the survey did not decide on plans for three working days between May 1 and 9.
At the same time, 68% of the study participants would like the May holidays to continue from May 1 to May 10 without a break, only 32% were against.
40% of respondents would agree to abandon the long New Year holidays in favor of long May holidays, 60% would like to leave everything as it is.
Photo: TASS / Kirill Kukhmar
A similar survey was conducted by SuperJob.
The results are similar: of the 1,600 representatives of the economically active population with permanent jobs interviewed, 13% of all districts of the country reported that they would take a vacation between the May holidays.
At the same time, Russians with an income of more than 80 thousand rubles want to extend their vacation on holidays, and more often men than women.
According to SuperJob, similar results are obtained annually - last year, 13% of working citizens also reported a desire to take a few days of vacation between the May holidays.
On the question of whether it is worth exchanging long winter holidays for other vacation options, SuperJob interviewed its users at the end of December 2021 - when the leader of the LDPR Vladimir Zhirinovsky proposed to cancel the fixed New Year holidays and add these weekends to the vacations of Russians.
Then the initiative to refuse the New Year holidays was supported by about the same 38% of Russians.
Moreover, the right to rest in January was more often defended by people older than 45 years.
Why extend the May holidays
One of the latest proposals for the May holidays came in early April from the Deputy speaker of the state Duma Vladislav Davankov, who called for the extension of the May holidays in 2022 from 1 to 10 may, as it “will help people prepare food for the fall ”, so that“ food security was in order this fall. ”
He recalled that last year the May holidays were extended due to the pandemic.
At the same time, the deputy said that it is not proposed to constantly make the weekend in May long, since entrepreneurs have problems in this regard.
Later, Davankov said that he received a response from the government on his initiative - at the federal level, the proposal was not supported, but allowed each region to prolong the holidays independently.
This proposal was listened to only in the Republic of Adygea - the local Ministry of Labor reported that the days off will be from May 1 to 5 and from May 7 to 10.
There was only one working day, May 6.
This is explained by the fact that the republican non-working holidays of Uraza Bayram and the Day of Remembrance of the Dead (Radonitsa) (May 2 and 3) coincided with federal holidays, so they were moved to May 4 and 5.
Photo: Izvestia / Dmitry Korotaev
But in general, legislators and regions reacted negatively to the idea of additional days off.
Thus, the Chairman of the State Duma Committee on labor Yaroslav Nilov said that the additional weekend will be a serious burden on the Russian economy.
Other deputies pointed out that not for all regions May is the time to sow fields, but there are supporters of this approach to the May holidays.
How many weekends do people need?
Associate Professor of the Department of Labor and Social Policy of the Institute of Public Service and Management (IGSU) of the RANEPA Konstantin Dobromyslov notes that according to tradition, weekends in May in Russia are considered more important, since at this time there is a sowing season.
“But to make a decision, it is necessary to conduct political and economic studies aimed at studying the impact of holidays on the country ’ s economy, ” he told Izvestia.
He believes that it is not necessary to specifically review the number of holidays, and the practice of postponing weekends allows us to form a “normal cycle of the state ’ s life, depending on economic, political, epidemiological and other situations. ”
— Discussing a possible reduction or increase in the number of holidays, of course, you need to proceed from socio-economic expediency, — said Dobromyslov. — Russia is not resting in a single impulse — we have continuous production, watches, transport, medical services, commercial enterprises, entertainment industry, museums, theaters.
These areas continue to work regardless of holidays and weekends, thanks to which a certain economic balance is created: while one part of the population rests, the other gets the opportunity to earn money.
Photo: TASS / Sergey Savostyanov
He believes that in the light of the discussion on the reduction of the working week, the issue of January and May holidays is not relevant at all - the duration of these holidays should be determined annually depending on the current situation.
Sociologist Sergei Talanov also agrees that any decisions should be made on the basis of scientific and economic research.
– It is necessary to take into account, and sociological surveys show that the majority of our working citizens are more important than high incomes, and not long weekends, – he said in an interview with Izvestia. – If we talk about the New Year and May holidays, then rest from December 31 to January 7 and from May 1 to May 3, and then May 9 – this is quite enough to restore your strength and not particularly break your usual working rhythm.
Deputy Head of the Federal Center for Mediation, Chairman of the All-Russian Trade Union of Mediators Vladimir Kuznetsov believes that the motives for changing the number of holidays can be purely economic.
“To illustrate, we can cite the example of India: there, public holidays cost a billion rupees (about $25 million) — 21 official plus an additional 9-10 in each state, ” he told Izvestia.
Vladimir Kuznetsov points out that approaches to this issue in different countries really differ greatly, and cites the opinion of the Malaysian political economist Charles Santiago, who noted that a large number of official non-working days for the majority of the population of Malaysia is “a welcome and often the only opportunity to take a break from hard work. ”
Photo: TASS / Anatoly Zhdanov
Those businessmen who complain about the excessive number of holidays, Santiago believes, should understand that “rested workers are also an increase in labor productivity.
And in the long term – an undoubted benefit for the economy of the country as a whole, ” — quotes Kuznetsov. — Consequently, the approach to determining the number of holidays can be due to both national characteristics and the economic structure of a particular state, and speaking of Russia, it can be noted that it is still advisable to maintain the current number of holidays in the year.
Elena Heifetz, a leading analyst in the Economics and Social Development section of the CSR, notes that there are 14 non-working holidays in Russia, and this figure is significantly higher than in more economically developed countries: in Germany — 13, in the UK — 9, in the United States — 10.
— The exception is Japan, where the number of public non-working days is 15, but it must be taken into account that these days are compensation for a small paid vacation, which is 10 days, — she told “Izvestia ”. — In Russia, the duration of annual paid vacation is 28 calendar days, and for certain categories — more.
How Holidays Affect the Economy
“It is obvious that lengthening the May holidays without reducing winter or other holidays is not feasible in the current economic situation, ” says Elena Heifetz. – On average, one non-working day costs the country about 200 billion rubles, so it is impractical to increase the burden on the economy.
At the same time, she says, the postponement of winter holidays to May can be considered as a reasonable decision due to the fact that most Russian citizens take leave on May 4-8.
— It is impossible to say unequivocally that the day off / holiday is a loss for the economy, — believe in the Accounts Chamber. — For many sectors, weekends are, on the contrary, the most favorable time.
For example, for cafes and restaurants, hotels.
For some sectors, there is not much difference between holidays and working days – for example, in enterprises with a continuous production cycle.
Photo: TASS / Gavriil Grigorov
The department told Izvestia that it did not conduct relevant studies, but in general, in accordance with the principles of evidence-based policy, studies confirming the effectiveness of the transfer are needed to resolve the issue of changing the structure of weekends.
Such data could show whether post-holiday productivity gains offset economic losses by fewer working days.
The Department of International and Regional Cooperation of the Accounts Chamber reported that attempts to study the problem of the impact of holidays on the country's economy were carried out in other countries.
At the same time, it is stipulated that this issue in fact remains insufficiently studied in world practice.
— Existing studies do not allow to draw an unambiguous conclusion about the positive or negative economic effect, — noted in the Department. — The results of such studies are often contradictory.
For example, in 2015, PricewaterhouseCoopers Australia (PWC) assessed how the introduction of two days off in Victoria — Easter Sunday and Friday before the Australian Football League Grand Final — would affect the economic development of the state.
Production losses or economic costs were estimated at 717-898 million Australian dollars (about $628 million).
Also, the introduction of non-working days led to an increase in salary payments in the amount of 252 million to 286 million Australian dollars per year ($179 – 203 million) for those who were forced to work on holidays.
But this fact did not have a negative impact on the state economy, since it meant only the redistribution of funds from employer to employee.
On the other hand, positive factors were noted that can partially compensate for economic losses.
Annual in-state tourism spending increased by AUD $17 – 51 million ($12 – 35 million), as well as spending on sports events by AUD $7 – 49 million ($5 – 35 million).
Such a less obvious aspect as the individual benefit of citizens from additional free time was also analyzed.
The value of this time is calculated in the range of 50 to 100% of average earnings and, according to PWC, amounted to 156 – 312 million Australian dollars ($110 – 221 million).
Photo: TASS / Sergey Malgavko
An attempt to assess the impact of holidays on the UK economy in 2020 was made by the BBC.
It was concluded that the positive effect will extend mainly to the sphere of trade, tourism and leisure - one day off contributes to the growth of income of small shops in the country by an average of 253 pounds sterling.
In 2019, two additional holidays increased the profits of small and medium-sized businesses in the UK by £118 million.
However, the overall extent of the losses of the British economy was not analyzed.
The Department of International and Regional Cooperation of the Accounts Chamber indicates that the experience of individual foreign companies in introducing a four-day working week may be relevant in the context of studying this problem.
So, in 2019, Microsoft tested such a working mode in the framework of the “Summer competition Work-Life Choice Challenge 2019 ” in Japan.
On Fridays, employees were given a weekend without a pay cut, and it turned out that the productivity of one employee increased by almost 40%.
However, the company said that a number of other factors contributed to this.
There were other positive effects of the four-day week – a 23% reduction in energy consumption, a reduction in print volumes by almost 60%, a reduction in the duration of workshops by almost 50% – from 1 hour to 30 minutes.
- Analysis of the experience of foreign countries shows that the introduction of additional non-working days leads to financial losses on the scale of the national economy, - noted in the Accounts Chamber. - Nevertheless, part of the losses is compensated by increasing costs of citizens.
As a result, there is an increase in some sectors of the economy - mainly the sphere of recreation and tourism.
It would be possible to assess the need for long vacations from the point of view of medicine – when is it more useful to rest?
But even here everything is not clear, says the doctor-therapist, endocrinologist, cardiologist, deputy chief physician of the clinic "Mprofico" Alexey Zhito.
- Someone likes winter holidays and can spend them qualitatively, - he told "Izvestia". - And others, for example, in the May holidays is simply bad - because of allergies, it would be convenient for them to change the place at the time of flowering and fly away from their allergens.
Zhito emphasizes that 10 days is a good time to have a good rest and gain strength, but a lot here depends on each person individually.

From the conflict in Ukraine, India ’ s geopolitical opportunities have narrowed – The Hindu
22: 49 17.05.2022
The Russian-Ukrainian conflict has significantly reduced the geopolitical opportunities of India, writes the newspaper The Hindu.
The author of the material notes that New Delhi should be wary of the increased influence of the PRC in South Asia.
Happymon Jacob
The main concern is what to do with China, which is trying to rally the entire region under its influence.
The short-lived confrontation between Russia and Ukraine, as New Delhi had hoped, resulted in a full-scale conflict with no end in sight, and its long-term consequences are very vague.
As for India, the diplomatic rush is over, and as the conflict drags on, its geopolitical options are shrinking.
Fewer opportunities
For several weeks in late March and early April, the conflict in Ukraine seemed to open up a range of geopolitical opportunities.
Loud visits to New Delhi, pleas of world leaders to support their positions and political equilibrism on the part of India - it seemed that the country was in the center of attention of the whole world.
However, instead of expanding New Delhi ’ s strategic capabilities in its region, the conflict in Ukraine threatens, on the contrary, to narrow the options available to India – for at least three reasons.
First, Russia, a key strategic partner, is no longer available to India as a balancer.
In the third month of the special operation in Ukraine, Moscow is perhaps even more dependent on India than vice versa.
Second, Russia ’ s sudden fall from the Asian equilibrium has only strengthened China ’ s influence.
Whatever the global balance of power may be at the end of the conflict, the regional balance will irrevocably shift in favor of Beijing.
Third, given that the US and its Western partners are now more interested in the Ukrainian theater of operations, their attention to China has already suffered – and with it the entire Indo-Pacific region.
These factors will automatically limit India ’ s regional geopolitical capabilities.
The main dilemma for India today is not whether to continue to engage with Russia or not.
Further cooperation in the short and medium term is beyond doubt.
However, due to the Russian adventure, New Delhi has new reasons for anxiety and reflection.
The Growing Chinese Challenge
The main headache of New Delhi is still the solution to the Chinese problem.
Of course, the Chinese challenge as such is not connected with the Ukrainian crisis, but, as a result, it has only become more complicated.
The conflict in Ukraine has breathed new life into the US-led global military-political coalition, but it will inevitably weaken American influence in South Asia.
Although this process began long before the outbreak of hostilities, it will only accelerate in the future, especially given that Washington ’ s concern with European theater will further reduce its interest in South Asia.
The main benefit of reducing the American and Western presence in the region will be China - it will actually be carte blanche.
Thus, Moscow is no longer available to New Delhi from the point of view of regional interests, and the US ability to help India achieve favorable geopolitical results is also reduced.
Thus, New Delhi is not so much concerned about how to please both sides of the conflict, but what to do with China, which is rapidly consolidating the entire region under its influence.
How is India working in this direction?
Take the recent visit of Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi to New Delhi.
It was noted that the Indian counterpart Subramanyam Jaishankar and the national security adviser Ajit Doval convinced Wang that the normalization of diplomatic and political relations is possible only after the withdrawal of troops from the Indian side of the line of de facto control (LFK).
But Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’ s decision to attend the BRICS summit in China threatens to soften New Delhi ’ s harsh stance toward Beijing.
In other words, the harsh tone of Jaishankar and Doval in response to Wang ’ s proposal for normalization may be weakened by Modi ’ s presence at the BRICS summit, even if virtual.
But how could New Delhi, whose geopolitical choice in the region due to the fighting in Ukraine has been severely limited, leave the Chinese diplomatic initiative unheeded?
Engaging Chinese-Russian ties
While there is no doubt that, in the long run, a conflict-weary and weakened Russia will become China ’ s junior partner, India now has the opportunity to influence Moscow to persuade Beijing to abandon the irredentism of exercise therapy.
Imagine that option.
If the Chinese side, taking advantage of the general distraction to Ukraine, takes steps along the exercise therapy, India will have to turn to the West and the United States for support (political, diplomatic, intelligence, and so on).
This will always be at the expense of Russia ’ s interests.
Therefore, it makes sense for Moscow to ask Beijing to refrain from such steps until the end of hostilities.
Wang ’ s visit to New Delhi and his request for India to return to the status quo may indicate that Beijing is also seeking to resolve conflicts along the exercise track.
Although China may have other reasons to “normalize ” relations with India (for example, to give the impression that Beijing unites all of South Asia under its leadership, as long as the West and the United States are occupied with Ukraine), it is important for Russia that its main Asian friends - China and India - do not conflict.
At least until the fighting ends.
While this may well help deal with Chinese aggression along exercise therapy in the short term, the outcome will depend on how China views its own relationship with Russia and its relationship with India.
That is the challenge for New Delhi.
If China stabilizes exercise therapy with the participation of Russia, it will expect that India will let the events in the Indo-Pacific down on the brakes - and it cannot afford it.
Keeping Calm in Kashmir
India ’ s continental strategy in the northwest – particularly Afghanistan and Central Asia – will also be complicated by the conflict in Ukraine.
At first glance, it may seem that the situation favors India.
Consider the following.
The Line of Control (LK) with Pakistan has been quiet for more than a year, and violence in Kashmir has decreased.
The main reason for the current lull is that Pakistan was initially busy consolidating its successes as a result of the Taliban ’ s return to Afghanistan (the Taliban is a terrorist organization banned in Russia, approx.
And now it has unpleasant consequences.
Moreover, New Delhi ’ s presence in Afghanistan has disappeared as such.
So, roughly speaking, calm in Kashmir and along the LC can be called the price for India ’ s withdrawal from Afghanistan.
From the outside, this may seem like a good deal.
But in the long run this is not the case.
If New Delhi signs, the deal implies not only abandoning strategic interests in Afghanistan, but also reducing participation in the whole of Central Asia - against the background of feverish raids into the region by China, right on the margins of the Russian sphere of influence.
In the future, the situation will worsen, including due to the Ukrainian conflict.
If Moscow had not gotten involved in the fighting in Ukraine, it would have repelled Beijing ’ s attempts to seize its backyard (in a sense, China is doing the same economically with Russia as NATO is doing militarily).
During the December summit, India and Russia decided on a number of initiatives on Central Asia and Afghanistan.
But they are unlikely to revive in the near future – most likely, the countries will give up their positions to China and Pakistan.
The combination of geopolitical consequences from the untimely withdrawal of American troops from Afghanistan, the conflict between Russia and Ukraine and the rapid expansion of Chinese influence shows how sharply the geopolitical choice of New Delhi has narrowed.
