Air-drip study reveals a surprisingly large role of desert dust in the formation of cirrus clouds
, 2: 45 pm
Each year, several billion metric tons of mineral dust are released into the atmosphere from arid regions of the world, making dust one of the most common types of aerosol particles in the atmosphere.
Now, scientists are learning that tiny bits of dust from the hottest and driest parts of the Earth are a surprisingly big driver in the formation of thin ice clouds known as cirrus clouds in the cold, high-altitude atmospheres.
Although scientists know that desert dust particles can sow certain clouds, the extent of this relationship has been a long-standing question.
A new study, based on the largest aerial sampling mission in history, sheds light on the role of dust in the climate system.
"The dust-initiated cirrus clouds are remarkably numerous, accounting for 34 to 71 percent of all cirrus clouds outside the tropics," explained lead author Carl Froyd, a CIRES scientist at NOAA's Laboratory of Chemical Sciences.
“Perhaps even more surprising, we found that while the Sahara Desert is by far the world ’ s largest source of dust emissions, deserts in Central Asia are often more important sources of cirrus cloud formation. ”
Analysis of atmospheric measurements collected over distant oceans during NASA ’ s three-year atmospheric tomography (ATom) mission shows that dust plays a dominant role in the formation of cirrus clouds in both the northern and southern hemispheres, and that some deserts are far more efficient than others when it comes to creating clouds.
To investigate the role of wind-blown dust in creating cirrus clouds, Froyd and colleagues deployed a purpose-built single-particle mass spectrometer, known as PALMS, on NASA ’ s DC-8 research aircraft during the ATom project to measure the chemical composition of aerosol particles in a distant atmosphere.
ATom flights circled the globe four times between 2016 and 2018, flying long transects down the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans and across the Arctic and Southern Oceans.
During the flight, the PALMS instrument continuously absorbed atmospheric particles, one by one, using a laser to evaporate each of them into their individual components before they were sent to a mass spectrometer to detect their chemical signatures.
Mineral dust is just one of the many types of aerosols that this powerful tool is able to identify.
The researchers encountered continental dust at almost every altitude and latitude selected by the aircraft, including over the Southern Ocean, the distant Pacific Ocean, and Antarctica.
The dust levels present in the cirrus formations of the upper troposphere were quite low, far below what could be observed by the satellite, but were ubiquitous.
Even at low concentrations, dust has been found to play a large role in controlling cloud properties.
Despite the small amounts of dust aerosols measured in the upper troposphere, dust is still common enough to stimulate cirrus cloud formation throughout all seasons outside the tropics, including the Southern Hemisphere.
The simulation results also showed that the meteorological environment along the winds of desert regions was more important for the formation of cirrus than just the amount of dust emitted.
The Sahara Desert, for example, accounts for 60% of global dust emissions, but only a small fraction of that dust is transported vertically to the cold temperatures of the upper troposphere, where it can sow tiny ice crystals that make up cirrus clouds.
In contrast, dry convection and the Asian summer monsoon help lift dust from Central Asia more efficiently.
The ability to properly model the abundance of dust and the formation of ribbed cirrus formations in the models is important for understanding the role of cirrus clouds in climate.
Clouds strongly influence the balance of solar radiation, which regulates surface temperature, but clouds and cloud formation remain a poorly understood aspect of the climate system.
Unlike the plump white clouds we see at lower altitudes that reflect sunlight, high-altitude cirrus clouds have a net warming effect on our climate, trapping heat that would otherwise escape into space.
The surprisingly large role of mineral dust in controlling the formation of cirrus compounds on a global scale establishes the critical role of dust in the Earth's climate system.
“With climate change, deserts are changing around the world, and dust emissions are changing with them.
These new findings help to focus our attention on the most important deserts in terms of formation of cirrus compounds, ” added Froyd.
"These results are a startling message to the aerosol and cloud science community that we need to improve our dust handling and cloud formation in climate models to more accurately predict current and future climate."

Quantum computing devices use such phenomena of quantum physics as entanglement and superposition, which allows quantum bits (qubits) to be in two states - both 0 and 1 - at the same time, thereby solving problems that are inaccessible to classical computers and supercomputers.
However, in physics, there are also extended versions of qubits - qubits, capable of taking more than two states: 0, 1, 2, and others.
"A group of scientists from the Russian Quantum Center (RCC) has received a patent for the physical implementation of a quantum computer based on kudites - quantum systems capable of simultaneously being in more than two states," the report said.

In the near future, the researchers also plan to apply for international registration.
Research in the field of the use of kudites for quantum computing has been conducted by a group of scientists from the RCC over the past few years.
Obtaining a patent will allow the team in the future to consolidate the exclusive right to the architecture of the created processor.
Its peculiarity lies in the combination of two approaches to increasing the power of a quantum computer.

Starting from February 24, interesting metamorphoses occur with my LJ rating (trifle, but unpleasant).
LiveJournal, apparently, defined me as an “unreliable ” user – and therefore he is just monotonically declining.
Of course, the principle of forming LiveJournal ratings has always remained a terrible military and commercial secret, but the general principle could be caught: if you are read a lot, your posts have a lot of comments and likes, the rating increases; if you read a little, there are no comments, or you do not write anything at all, the rating decreases.
It's kind of simple.
But with the beginning of the war, LiveJournal not only introduced censorship and canceled anonymous names, but also, it seems, revised the principle of rating.
Now the “unreliable ” users ratings simply decline no matter what.
I noticed it back in April – when on one of the posts (about AvtoVAZ) there was almost a record attendance – 75 thousand per day, about 1000 comments – and the rating, as if nothing had happened, continued to decline.
I am almost certain that the LJ algorithm has a restriction, according to which it by default believes that “Shoemaker writes nothing ”; accordingly, every day my personal rating gradually dries up, although I still have, even in conditions of censorship and general militaristic insanity, extremely“ fruitful ” posts.
All this is understandable – LJ, while he was “in the shadows ” and outside the attention of the“ ideologists ” of the regime, lovingly debugged his mechanisms of work and brought them almost to perfection, but when censors and censorship came, it breaks everything down in a few months, since the mechanisms were made with an emphasis on the objectivity of measurements, and no objectivity of ideology is needed.
I just don ’ t understand why it ’ s so half-hearted.
With other "unreliable" treated much cooler.
Kungurov was simply squeezed out of LiveJournal, Nikonov was squeezed out, Mitrich ’ s rating was simply halved in one fell swoop, Alex Rozoff was driven somewhere in the end of the first rating hundred (although his posts are read and discussed in the same way, if not more than before the sad Free Date) – and my rating is just slowly and sadly “blown away ” (about minus 8 thousand points), and almost ceased to include posts in the Top.
The only thing is that I ’ m treated about the same as El Murid: he ’ s also “slowly and sadly ” losing in the rankings, although his posts are read almost more than mine (but since we have the same rate of fall in the“ they write nothing ” mode, I can ’ t fall lower than him).
These are the ratings quirks.

How to pay the salary of an employee abroad.
What to do with taxes
If an employee works remotely from abroad, there are nuances in its registration, payment of personal income tax and insurance premiums.
We tell you how to be an employer whose employees have left the country or are going to do so.
What contract can be concluded with an employee who is abroad
The Ministry of Labor noted several times that it is impossible to conclude an employment contract with a remote employee who is outside of Russia.
For example, in letters dated 07.08.2015 No 17-3 / B-410 and dated 16.01.2017 No 14-2 / OOG-245.
Officials explain their position by the fact that the norms of labor legislation are valid only on the territory of the Russian Federation.
Therefore, the employer will not be able to provide safe working conditions.
The Ministry of Labor recommends in such cases to conclude a contract of a civil law nature (GPH).
At the same time, the TC does not directly prohibit the conclusion of an employment contract with a remote employee who is abroad.
This is indicated, for example, by the AU of the North Caucasus District in the judgment of 24.12.2020 in the case No A20-4914 / 2019.
Therefore, theoretically, the employer can choose any option, but it is necessary to take into account the risks associated with the inspection of labor inspection.
How to pay personal income tax from payments to an employee who is abroad
When calculating the personal income tax, two factors must be taken into account:
1.
Place of work, which is determined by the terms of the contract (letter of the Ministry of Finance from 14.04.2021 No 03-04-06 / 27827).
If the place of work is located abroad, then all payments to the employee are considered income from sources outside the Russian Federation (para. 6 para.
3, Art. 208 of the Tax Code).
2.
Status of tax resident of the Russian Federation.
A tax resident is a person who has spent more than 183 days in the territory of the Russian Federation for 12 months in a row (paragraph 2 of Article 207 of the Tax Code).
There are exceptions for treatment, training, etc.
What kind of citizenship does not matter.
Tax residents of the Russian Federation must pay personal income tax on all their income, and non-residents - only on income received in the territory of the Russian Federation (Article 209 of the Tax Code).
A tax resident of the Russian Federation must independently calculate and pay tax received outside the Russian Federation (subpara. 3 para.
1 of Art. 228 of the Tax Code).
Payment of personal income tax from the income of an employee who is abroad
* standard personal income tax rates for incomes not exceeding 5 million rubles per year are indicated.
How to pay insurance premiums if the employee is abroad
For the calculation of insurance premiums are important:
1.
Nationality of the employee.
All citizens of the Russian Federation, as well as foreigners temporarily residing or staying in the territory of the Russian Federation, are considered insured persons for pension, medical and social insurance in terms of sick leave and maternity benefits (paragraph 1 of Article 7 of the Law of 15.12.2001 No. 167-FZ, paragraph 1).
1 Art. 10 of the law of 29.11.2010 No 326-FZ, p.
1 Art. 2 of the law of 29.12.2006 No 255-FZ).
Insurance against accidents at work applies to all citizens of the Russian Federation and foreigners, regardless of their place of residence (paragraph 2 of Art. 5 of the law of 24.07.1998 No. 125-FZ).
2.
Type of contract.
All types of insurance premiums must be paid under employment contracts.
There is no need to charge contributions for temporary disability insurance under GPC contracts.
Accident contributions are accrued only if it is specified in the contract itself.
Thus, if the employee left, but remained a citizen of Russia, nothing changes for him in terms of contributions.
If he became a citizen of another state, only mandatory contributions for accident insurance under the labor contract remain.
What should the employer do if the employee has left or plans to go abroad
1.
Reissue the contract.
In this case, the employer has two options: to leave the current employment contract, adding to it the provisions on remote work, or to issue a new contract of the state farm.
The GPH contract is more profitable for the employer: you do not need to pay insurance premiums to the FSS and the likelihood of conflicts with the labor inspectorate is reduced.
However, the employee may not agree to this.
If it is not possible to agree, you can use Article 312.8 of the Labor Code, according to which the employer has the right to terminate the employment contract if the remote employee has moved and after that he cannot perform labor duties under the previous conditions.
What exactly makes the performance of labor duties after moving impossible is not deciphered in the law.
The court practice on the application of Article 312.8 of the TC has not yet developed.
It can be, for example, a significant change in time zones.
2.
Determine the procedure for payment of NDFL.
The procedure depends on what place of work is specified in the contract.
Place of work is the territory of a foreign state.
In this case, the employer should not withhold personal income tax from the moment of moving.
If an employee spends less than 183 calendar days abroad in the first calendar year, he will have to submit a declaration and pay personal income tax at a rate of 13% at the end of the year.
The employer does not have to do anything.
If the employee spends more than 183 days abroad in the first calendar year, then:
1.
The employee does not have to file a declaration and pay personal income tax on all income after moving.
2.
The employer must recalculate at the rate of 30% of personal income tax from all income that he paid to the employee from the beginning of the current year and until the date of moving (letter of the Ministry of Finance of the Russian Federation dated 15.03.2017 No 03-04-06 / 14804).
Unpaid tax must be withheld from current payments in favor of the employee until the end of the year.
No more than 20% can be withheld from each payment.
If the employer does not have time to keep everything in the current year, he must notify the tax authorities before March 1 of the next year.
Then the Federal Tax Service will send a notification to the employee and he will have to pay the tax himself before December 1 (p.
Art. 226 of the Tax Code of the Russian Federation, p.
6 Art. 228 of the Tax Code of the Russian Federation).
Starting from the second year of the employee ’ s stay abroad, the employee and the employer will have no obligation to pay personal income tax.
Place of work — territory of the Russian Federation.
In this case, the employer must withhold personal income tax at a rate of 13% from all payments until the employee has lived abroad for more than 183 days.
It is necessary to check the status of a tax resident at each payment (letter of the Ministry of Finance of the Russian Federation dated 01.09.2016 No 03-04-05 / 51258).
To confirm the time of stay abroad, you can use, for example, a copy of the passport page with a mark on crossing the border.
If the employee lives abroad for more than 183 days already in the first year of stay, then the tax on all payments from the rate of 13% for the first year must be recalculated at the rate of 30% and withheld until the end of the year the difference, as described in the previous section.
After 183 days of stay and in subsequent years, you need to keep personal income tax at a rate of 30%.
3.
Determine the procedure for calculating insurance premiums.
The procedure depends on the nationality of the employee.
If the employee has retained the citizenship of the Russian Federation or has issued dual citizenship, it is necessary to charge all contributions provided for by Russian legislation, depending on the type of contract: labor or state farm.
If the employee after moving has become a citizen of a foreign state, from the date of change of citizenship, only “unfortunate ” insurance premiums should be accrued for payments in his favor: under the employment contract in any case, and under the state farm - if this is provided for by the contract.
Example:
Two employees of the Russian IT company SuperSoft have moved to Armenia since April 1, 2022.
Petrov A. V. left Russian citizenship, and Petrosyan T. S. from June 1, 2022 changed citizenship to Armenian.
Employment contracts continued with both employees, and addresses in the territory of Armenia are indicated as a place of work from April 1, 2022.
If Petrov and Petrosyan remain in Armenia or other foreign countries until the end of 2022 and beyond, the employer and employees will not be obliged to withhold and pay personal income tax from income received after April 1, 2022.
An employee who permanently lives abroad will pay taxes in accordance with the laws of a foreign state.
From what point he will start doing this and on what terms depends on the country of residence and the legal status of the employee in this country.
For example, an employee can obtain foreign citizenship or a residence permit, register a local equivalent of an individual entrepreneur, etc.
But the Russian employer is not concerned in any way.
The employer will have to recalculate personal income tax from the income paid to these employees in Russia for January-March 2022.
This should be done after Petrov and Petrosyan will be abroad for more than 183 days.
Based on the date of the move, this will happen in October 2022.
Therefore, from payments for October-December 2022, it will be necessary to withhold the difference in personal income tax for January-March 2022, calculated at rates of 13% and 30%.
Insurance contributions for Petrov ’ s salary should continue to be accrued during 2022 and further on the same basis as before the move.
The same applies to Petrosyan ’ s salary for April and May 2022.
And, starting from June 1, 2022, only “unfortunate ” insurance premiums should be charged on Petrosyan ’ s salary.
How to transfer the salary of employees abroad
Due to the sanctions with payments abroad, difficulties arose, so you need to solve two issues: where to transfer money and through which operator.
Today, Visa and Mastercard cards issued in the Russian Federation do not work abroad.
True, in some countries it is possible to use Russian maps of the World.
These are, for example, Belarus, Armenia, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan.
But nowhere, except for Belarus, you can not use the MIR card without restrictions.
As a rule, you can only withdraw cash from it and pay at individual outlets connected to the local payment system.
Therefore, the employee in most cases will be more convenient to issue a card of a foreign bank.
The employer must choose the operator through which the transfer will take place.
It can be a bank or a non-bank payment system.
Some banks, for example, VTB, Promsvyazbank, Sovcombank came under blocking sanctions and cannot transfer money abroad.
If the employer has an account with only one of these banks, you will have to open an additional account with a bank that does not fall under the sanctions.
You can also use non-bank payment services, but here you need to take into account that many of them only carry out transfers between individuals.
Of the large payment systems, Unistream works with organizations, for example.
In any case, it should be borne in mind that the conditions for transfers abroad are constantly changing.
In addition, some foreign banks may impose their own restrictions on accepting payments from Russia.
Therefore, before you open an account in a Russian bank or enter into an agreement with the payment system, specify whether it will be possible to transfer money to a foreign bank through them.

Four days has become a reality.
In the UK conducted an important experiment – details
The length of the work week was significantly reduced.
In the UK, workers are transferred to a four-day working week. / Photo: Collage: Today
In the UK, a large-scale experiment has begun on the introduction of a four-day working week.
About 3.3 thousand employees from 70 companies will take part in the pilot program.
It is expected that the reduction of working days will increase the productivity of workers.
This is reported by Sky News.
Advertisement
The experiment involved companies from different industries: for example, the banking sector and the hotel business.
They must continue to pay workers 100% of their wages, provided that they maintain maximum productivity.
The duration of the experiment is 6 months.
During this time, the organizers of the study – 4 Day Week Global in partnership with the analytical center Autonomy and the campaign 4 Day Week UK – should measure the impact of reducing the number of working days on productivity and well-being of staff.
Ed Siegel, CEO of Charity Bank, said: “The concept of a five-day workweek of the 20th century is no longer appropriate for the business of the 21st century. ”
The organizers of the experiment believe that after the coronavirus pandemic, the approach to the length of the working week should change.
Advertisement
Why we need to reduce the working week
A four-day work week increases worker productivity.
This was proved in 2019 in the Japanese division of Microsoft and transferred employees to a new work schedule.
Friday was an extra weekend.
At the same time, people were not reduced wages and did not calculate days from vacation.
During the experiment, it turned out that the efficiency of workers who rest more increased by as much as 40 percent.
The company also saved money.
Because I started to spend 20 percent less electricity and print half as much paper.

Nihon Keizai: China and India reduce the effectiveness of Western sanctions against Russia
Extraction of oil.

MOSCOW, June 10 – RIA Novosti.
Due to the increase in purchases of Russian energy resources by China and India, the effectiveness of Western sanctions against Moscow is declining, while there are fears that more and more countries will make “bypass maneuvers ” in relation to restrictions, according to an article by Nihon Keizai.
While the United States and the European Union have imposed restrictions on the supply of Russian oil, China and India are increasing its purchases, while Russia ’ s income from increasing the supply of resources to alternative buyers has only increased.
“In particular, it receives increased revenues from the export of its energy resources with the support of Sino-Indian purchases, while the effectiveness of US and European sanctions is significantly reduced, ” writes Nihon Keizai.
Indian Foreign Minister sharply answered the question about Ukraine and relations with the West
According to Refinitiv, the volume of crude oil imported by China from Russia by sea, excluding pipelines, in May amounted to about 800,000 barrels per day, an increase of more than 40% compared to January, and maritime imports of Russian oil to India rose from zero in January to just under 700,000 barrels per day in May.
“These are very impressive numbers, ” emphasizes the publication.
In addition, while purchases of Russian coal from Japan and other countries have declined, its exports to India have increased significantly, China is also working to expand supplies of this resource, the article says.
At the same time, there is a high probability that imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) by China will significantly increase in the summer, and it is also reported that Indian energy companies have significantly expanded spot purchases of LNG from Russia.
“This important point should also be taken into account.
Although the supply of Russian pipeline natural gas to some European countries has been suspended (for example, to Poland and Bulgaria), this has not affected them in terms of overall reduction.
On the contrary, they are even increasing against the background of a significant increase in European prices for imported natural gas, ” Nihon Keizai points out.
The United States and Europe are asking China and India not to buy Russian oil and coal, but with the rapid growth of world energy prices, the economic benefit from the purchase of cheaper Russian products is great.
“There are also concerns that more and more countries and organizations will make circumvention maneuvers towards sanctions, for example, falsifying ship registration and destinations, ” the publication summarizes.
After the start of the Russian military special operation in Ukraine, the West increased sanctions pressure on Moscow.
Brussels is seriously considering the option of abandoning Russian oil and gas.
Last week, EU ambassadors approved the sixth package of sanctions, including an oil embargo, disconnection from SWIFT Sberbank, two more Russian and one Belarusian banks.
Hungary has said that it will agree to new anti-Russian sanctions only if it is provided with guarantees of fuel supplies.
As President Vladimir Putin noted, the policy of containing and weakening Russia is a long-term strategy of unfriendly countries, and the main goal of the United States and Europe is to worsen the lives of millions of people.

In Russia, it is necessary to develop measures to support self-employed bloggers, said Deputy Director of RAEC, Member of the Public Chamber of the Russian Federation Sergey Grebennnikov.
Answering the question of the correspondent of IA REGNUM “Why the departure of foreign sites in the future will benefit Russian bloggers and online sites? ”, he explained:
Blogger
(cc) NeONBRAND
“After the start of the Russian military special operation in Ukraine, many foreign social networks became inaccessible to Russian users – Instagram (an organization whose activities are banned in Russia) and Facebook (an organization whose activities are banned in Russia) were recognized as extremist and banned in Russia, TikTok disabled the ability to post new content, Youtube – monetization.
Of course, this does not affect Russian bloggers.
The positive point is that we have a fairly large number of our own services, including the social network VKontakte, which until February 2022 was the leader in the number of users in Russia.
Already in March 2022, a meeting was held on the site of the Civic Chamber of the Russian Federation under the auspices of the Commission for the Development of the Information Society, Media and Mass Communications of the Civic Chamber of the Russian Federation and the Russian Association of Electronic Communications to discuss the future of the blogger community in Russia.
As part of our meeting with representatives of the blogosphere, we came to the conclusion that the topic of the development of domestic analogues of social networks is very relevant.
It is time to create a special working group to develop support measures for self-employed bloggers who worked through social networks that have left the Russian market and for those who are now actively mastering domestic analogues.
Many of the domestic platforms have a wide functionality, including useful for the development of the blogosphere.
However, the transition of bloggers to Russian sites is not painless.
Reasons: difficulties with moderation; inability to fully transfer subscribers to a new platform; difference in the audience of platforms; interface features; lack of usual metrics.
Despite the fact that many bloggers and businesses are accustomed to foreign sites, Russian social networks are now trying to create services convenient and useful for both entrepreneurs and content creators.
“VKontakte ” in the spring held a large-scale program to support authors, and also offered entrepreneurs tools to start and develop their business on the Internet.
Thus, according to a study by RAEC, 44% of respondents from among SMEs named VK the main channel of Internet communication.
Other Russian online platforms are also attracting new users.
We have social networks for different audiences and content formats.
“Classmates ” appeared long before the appearance of all social networks and, of course, for older audiences they are more familiar.
Yappy - an analogue of TikTok - is more interesting for teenagers and young people.
Well, LiveJournal, where bloggers who began to keep a diary at the peak of their career return again.
"Yandex.
Zen is suitable for content creators.
It does not matter that “Yandex ”.
Zen has recently returned a tape of recommendations and introduced new tools for promoting channels.
There is still an opportunity to create and develop new Russian platforms.
For example, Russian social networks ЯRUS and TenChat were recently launched.
But if someone wants to create an analogue of Facebook or Instagram (recognized as extremist organizations whose activities are banned in Russia), it seems to me that it makes no sense to repeat what has already existed for many years.
You need to create completely new social platforms with some other chips and tools that the user needs.
I am sure that we are waiting for the birth of a new, unique market.
Russian companies are already open to cooperation, and this can not but rejoice. ”
As reported by IA REGNUM, every year on June 14, the Internet community celebrates the International Day of the blogger.
In 2022, one of the “best ” gifts for their holiday, Russian bloggers received from YouTube – the Google-controlled video hosting completely suspended all monetization functions, including Premium subscription, Music Premium, sponsorship, super chat, superstickers and“ merch ”.
Demonstrating its anti-Russian position, Google did not limit itself to video hosting, but announced the suspension of the sale of all online advertising in Russia in the search engine of the same name and from external publishing partners.
“When the strongest player disappears in the market, the weak have the opportunity to compete.
I think that it is for online platforms that this is a great opportunity to improve the product, understand what the audience needs and introduce more and more chips.
Moreover, quality standards have already been set, ” said Anton Petukhov, Chairman of the Influence Marketing Committee (IAB).
According to Vladimir Zykov, Director of the Association of Professional Users of Social Networks and Messengers (APPSIM), unlike Europe, Russia has its own platforms, social networks, mail, clouds for storing information and data, and so on.
And Europe does not have this, it is completely dependent on American sites, and this, of course, is a big trouble for them.

Story:

Society
FIAN researcher Ilya Semerikov poses against the background of his "brainchild" - a universal four-qubit quantum computer / Photo: Natalia Feoktistova / Evening Moscow
We continue our column “Simple questions ”, in which we ask professionals about what we do not know for sure.
What came first: idea or matter?
What is the hadron collider for and why can all points of view exist at the same time?
The answers to all these questions are known by one of the most promising young scientists in Russia, the developer of a quantum computer Ilya Semerikov.
Ilya Semerikov ’ s quantum computer occupies almost half a room in one of the FIAN laboratories.
There is some irony in the fact that a device that works with the smallest particles needs such a huge body.
At the same time, the “heart ” of the aggregate, the quantum traps in which ions are encoded, are small.
The rest of the “skeleton ” is needed to service these traps.
While the computer resembles a watch from "Eralash", which was accompanied by two suitcases with batteries.
By the way, this series was filmed in 1991 - a year before the birth of Ilya.
The young scientist is only 30 years old!
The other day, he was included in the Forbes list “30 to 30 ” for his great services to the industry and the country.
Ilya and I discussed quantum qubits, career culbits and other metaphors of our lives.
— Ilya, why do you need a quantum computer?
Today, a quantum computer is much worse than usual.
A modern quantum computer can do almost nothing useful.
So far, this development is not a practical, but a scientific field.
But potentially a quantum computer can solve some problems that are beyond the control of a conventional computer.
For example, factorization is the decomposition of a number into prime factors.
So, 525 decomposes into 5 * 5 * 3 * 7.
The task of factorization is to bring the object to the “main building blocks ”.
On a classical computer, it is virtually impossible to factor a sufficiently large number - it will take a very long time to calculate.
During such calculations, the sun will die out.
A quantum computer will be able to perform such calculations in a few minutes.
But in order to solve such problems, we need not two qubits (the qubit is the smallest unit of information in a quantum computer, by analogy with a bit - "VM") and not even ten, but hundreds, but preferably thousands of qubits.
Quantum computers all over the world today work in fact with units.
In order to go from tens of qubits to thousands, new physical solutions, fundamental science, research are needed.
In this case, not only the number of qubits is important, but also their quality, since all operations on qubits must be very accurate in order to get the right results.
It is believed that the development of quantum computers will bring the emergence of superartificial intelligence closer.
When do we expect intelligent robots?
— There are studies according to which quantum computers can surpass classical ones in the field of artificial intelligence.
But for them to be useful, you need not ten qubits, but at least a hundred.
Here the requirements are lower than to the decomposition of numbers by factors, but still it is a lot.
I am not in favor of the idea that the results will come soon.
Tomorrow nothing will happen unless, of course, someone from under the floor gets a breakthrough idea.
I am so pessimistic because I stand behind these pens every day, collect bolts and screws, and understand the complexity, painstaking experiments in the field of quantum computing.
According to an optimistic estimate, it takes another ten years to do something really useful for applied tasks.
One step in quantum computing experiments, if done quickly without the constraints of finance and staff, takes three to five years.
New ideas are also needed.
And no one can predict the speed of the generation of new ideas.
This is a moment of creativity.
The more people are engaged in one idea, the more likely it is that someone will guess how and what to do.
Yes, we have our own ideas for research.
But three to five years usually go from idea to implementation.
In the world ’ s leading labs, it ’ s faster — they ’ re easier with equipment and staff, but it ’ s still not a week-long step.
Do sanctions affect developments in the field of quantum computers?
- It's a big influence.
More than 90 percent of the equipment was supplied to us from Germany, the United States and Japan.
These countries imposed sanctions.
I am very skeptical about the idea of import substitution in the field of high technologies.
For example, we need precise lasers for a quantum computer.
We can't order it now.
Where can I get them?
Yes, we can develop these lasers, but then who will deal with the quantum computer?
The number of employees in any industry is limited.
In order to educate a new employee in such knowledge-intensive areas, it will take from three to five years.
And it makes life very difficult.
Yes, even before the last massive sanctions, we bought a new set of equipment with which we can finish our ideas.
But these reserves will be enough for a year or two.
It is impossible to build a sovereign science.
For example, people from dozens of countries are working on an ordinary smartphone.
In the Congo, cobalt is mined, which goes to China.
That's where they clean it, then this cobalt is used in the lithium batteries that are in the phone.
Chips are made in Taiwan, and lithography machines are made in the Netherlands, optics for them are made in the United States.
All countries are woven into a large international cooperation.
No country can do everything by itself.
Photo: Pexels
— What is the Hadron Collider for?
In the collider, small structures are examined.
So, there is an inverse relationship between energy and the scale of distance: the more energy a particle flies, the smaller pieces of matter you can look into.
We must understand that the development of humanity is not only about technologies and things that bring benefits.
When Kepler studied the motion of planets and stars in the 17th century, he did not think about how it would be used later.
But after him came Newton, who generalized knowledge and formulated his laws.
On the basis of these laws, most of the mechanical devices work.
But this does not mean that all the knowledge of mankind is converted into technology.
Some things exist simply to understand how the world works.
The Hadron Collider is an important thing to move forward. Why?
Because we're human.
People are different from animals in their curiosity.
We can generate abstract knowledge.
The benefits of Collider are the same as the benefits of music.
It is an art that allows to see the beauty of the world.
I wish it was more widespread so that people could watch this beauty.
I think we need to look for some form of conveying this information to a large number of people.
Is there a matrix like in the Wachowski films?
It seems to me that there are no matrices in the form of the film, but there is a much more interesting structure.
Life is more exciting than any movie.
We create within ourselves the matrix in which we live.
There is such a thing as an echo chamber.
We get information from sources that are close to us.
And those things that are far away, we try to ignore.
We choose a world in which we feel comfortable.
It looks like a social media feed customized for us.
We build our information bubble, which often does not coincide with what is really happening.
How do I perceive the matrix?
Yes, there is an objective reality, but we live inside our comfortable picture of the world and do not look around.
It turns out that we live in a matrix, but we do not want to get out of it.
And when different worlds collide, sometimes terrible things happen.
When people from one echo chamber begin to communicate with people from another echo chamber, it seems that both are deaf and blind.
Where did the 404 error come from?
I don't know, I guess there was some sort of numbering of these mistakes.
You can open Wikipedia and see it.
This is a thing that I recommend to everyone.
You need to look for answers to questions in the sources, and ask yourself these questions more often.
A scientist is different from a non-scientist in that he asks himself questions.
It happens that people put something of their own in such things, for example, in some kind of joke, but here, I think, there is no subtext.
What comes first: idea or matter?
I think these things are inseparable.
What is an idea or a thought?
When we think, electrochemical reactions occur in the brain, currents flow.
The current creates a weak magnetic field.
The magnetic field has energy.
Energy has mass.
The magnetic field created by thinking has mass.
It is already matter.
What is matter?
Something that has mass.
Thought has mass on the physical level.
Thought is material.
Another example.
What came first: the atom or the idea of the atom?
There was a time in the universe when there were no atoms.
And then the first atom appeared, and at the same moment the idea of the atom appeared.
All these things are inseparable and their description depends on the point of view.
The guys from the idealist and materialist camps existed in their echo chambers, but in fact this separation is not.
Photo: Pexels
One of the popularizers of science compared our world with a superconductor in which we all live.
Is that true?
Metaphors about the structure of the world can be very different.
This is also a story about a point of view.
I have never heard of this metaphor before.
Maybe there are people who look at our world this way.
With metaphors in general, you need to be extremely careful.
In physics, there are limits to the applicability of any theory.
For example, if the speeds we work with are less than the speed of light, then classical mechanics apply.
And if the speed is approaching the speed of light, then we need the theory of relativity.
To work with large objects, classical mechanics is necessary, and with small ones, quantum mechanics.
Everything has its limits of applicability, including metaphors.
And here, on the one hand, you need to try not to go beyond this border, and on the other - to look at the problem from different angles.
There is the principle of “Occama ’ s razor ” in philosophy, which says that it is not necessary to produce entities where they do not exist.
But if Occam's razor had been used indiscriminately, most of the physical theories would have been circumcised.
A lot of them look crazy at first.
It is necessary to protect heretics, but not to accept their ideas as something that is not subject to doubt.
There are people who believe in a flat earth.
This is not without meaning, because in many everyday situations the Earth really seems flat.
But if you look at this issue not from the side of a person who walks in the forest, and connect satellite navigation, we will see the failure of this idea.
It is necessary to treat human thought carefully - on the one hand with tenderness, and on the other - with criticism.
If someone claims that the Earth is flat, do not immediately tell him that he is an idiot.
Let ’ s try to figure out what a person means.
— Do our physicists often offer to move abroad?
The question is what is “offered. ”
No one will come to you and say, “Come work with us. ”
Rather, on the contrary: it is necessary to offer oneself, and after that the discussion begins.
It ’ s a matter of aesthetic perception: what we want from life.
People used to go to America not because they wanted to be on the other side of the world.
They went to specific positions that had prospects for them.
Personally, it is important for me to be able to do what I am interested in.
Quantum computers are interesting to me.
If I have the opportunity here to do them, I will gladly continue to do it, and if not, I will think about what to do next.
Maybe there's something more interesting.
Now I am thinking about education.
For example, how to build such an education so that people can do what is interesting and understand what is interesting to them.
For me, creating such a system of education is no less interesting than quantum computers.
An echo chamber is a concept in media theory, which is a situation in which certain ideas are reinforced or reinforced by the transmission of a message or its repetition within a closed system: a party or a circle of like-minded people.
At the same time, such messages drown out other similar information flows.
So, any statements lead not to discussions, but to the giving and support of like-minded people.
Addressees in such a “closed ” system create messages, listen to themselves and agree with themselves.
There is no alternative information in this closed system.

Microsoft closes access to its AI solutions for face recognition and voice generation
Microsoft has published new rules for the use of its developments related to artificial intelligence.
Access to those that allow you to create “risky ” solutions will be severely limited.
Dangerous AI
Microsoft has decided to limit the use of some tools for the development of projects related to artificial intelligence.
On Tuesday, the company published a document called the “Standard for Responsible Use of AI ”, which indicates that Microsoft will make every effort to minimize the possible harm from machine learning tools.
For this purpose, stricter rules for the use of tools developed by Microsoft are introduced.
“There is a growing need for practical guidance of this type, ” said Natasha Crampton, director of responsible use of AI,“ AI is becoming an increasingly significant part of our lives, while civil law lags behind this process.
Lawmakers do not keep up with the unique threats posed by AI, nor the needs of society.
While we ’ re seeing governments increasingly looking at AI, we ’ re also realizing that a sense of responsibility is driving us to take our own action.
We are convinced that artificial intelligence systems should be implemented responsibly from the project level. ”
In practice, this means that Microsoft restricts access to tools in Azure, which allows you to create solutions for recognizing the gender and age of people from their images based on the Face API.
By means of recognizing people ’ s emotions from their videos or photos, a lock is also hung.
New Azure users will no longer be able to access FaceAPI, and existing users are advised to migrate to other services by June 30, 2023.
After that date, Face API will be officially closed.
Microsoft restricts access to “dangerous ” AI tools, such as facial recognition
However, the functions of this API will remain in other services, in particular Seeing AI, an application for the visually impaired that identifies and describes people and objects in voice.
Use of voice only with written consent
Microsoft also plans to restrict access to other “risky ” tools.
In particular, the restrictions will affect the means of facial recognition in general and the generation of realistic voice sound.
Access to such tools will now be subject to prior request, and the decision whether or not to grant access will depend on whether the project is considered potentially harmful.
Existing users will also need permission to continue using these tools until June 30, 2023.
Imitation of someone ’ s voice using generative AI models using the Custom Neural Voice solution will now be considered permissible only with the unambiguous written permission of the original owner of that voice and, in some cases, a recorded oral statement of consent.
This is done in order to combat deepfakes, which can potentially be used for cyber attacks.
The conditions for the use of facial recognition tools are also becoming stricter: it is forbidden to use them to spy on people in any case.
Back in 2020, amid scandals with the misuse of the ClearView AI system, Microsoft announced that it would stop selling facial recognition tools to law enforcement and even invest in such funds in principle.
Now the company says that the current period is critical for establishing rules for the use of risky AI tools and standards for responsible development.
“Microsoft, like any other company, has the right to limit the use of its developments at its own discretion, in the context of AI or outside it, ” says Alexei Vodiasov, technical director of SEQ. – Initiatives to establish the rules of the game in this field are welcome, the question is only whether other players will go for it.
It is not only Western companies that are developing AI tools, including those that Microsoft considers dangerous.
Of course, everyone would benefit from the emergence of global standards for the safe and responsible development of AI, but it will be a long time before they appear. ”

Four working days?
The Ministry of Economy responded to the initiative
Taking into account the fact that the overall increase in productivity in the economy has its own dynamics, which is difficult to influence with innovative measures in a short time, the introduction of a four-day working week will reduce the total added value in the national economy, the Ministry of Economy informed LETA.
At the same time, the Ministry noted that
employers, in fact, can introduce the initiative for a four - day working week now,
because the labor law provides for flexible working conditions by agreement between employees and employers.

The Ministry of Economy notes that the increase in labor productivity is based not only on technological innovations and improving the production process, but also on the redistribution of available resources for the production of products with higher added value, which for objective reasons is relatively slow.
"Therefore, we can conclude that by significantly reducing the working day at the existing level of labor productivity, the total value added in the economy will decrease, as a result of which enterprises' incomes, wages, tax revenues will decrease, that is, there will also be less opportunities to finance pensions, budget areas, etc.", - the ministry points out.
Negative effects on salaries and budget
A significant reduction in working time in a country with such a level of labor productivity as in Latvia will mean a reduction in the volume of the economy with negative consequences for wages, budget and satisfaction of service recipients.
In Western countries with higher productivity, an employee can afford to work fewer hours a week, as he will still receive a salary higher than in Latvia.
As reported, the portal of public initiatives Manabalss.lv started collecting signatures for the transition to a four-day working week.
The initiative was submitted by Denis Melekhov, who proposes to make appropriate changes to Article 131 of the Labor Law.
According to Melekhov, an increase in free time will contribute to employee satisfaction, and labor efficiency will not decrease.
Also, people will have more time for study and self-development, which will have a positive economic effect.

At the same time, in May alone, Boeing and Airbus delivered 35 and 47 aircraft to customers, respectively, and since the beginning of the year, Boeing and Airbus have delivered 165 and 237 aircraft to commercial customers, respectively.
For comparison, for the same period last year, Boeing shipped 111 aircraft, and Airbus – 220.
Thus, this year, Boeing and Airbus are 54 and 17 aircraft higher than last year ’ s deliveries.
After the failure of 2020 (due to the COVID-19 pandemic, air travel almost stopped), 2021 was a year of industry recovery and increased production for Airbus and, to a greater extent, for Boeing.
However, Boeing and Airbus still have a long way to go before deliveries return to pre-pandemic levels.
For all of 2021, Boeing delivered 340 aircraft – more than in 2020 (157), but less than in 2019 (380).
In general, the last “normal ” year for Boeing was 2018: before the COVID-19 pandemic and the“ landing ” of the Boeing 737 Max, 806 aircraft were delivered to customers.
It is expected that this level of supply will be reached at best in 2024.
The past three years have been extremely challenging for Boeing, but despite problems with the Dreamliner and the delayed release of the 777X, the outlook is bright.
Boeing 737 Max is approved for flights in almost all countries, and since the end of 2020, its fleet has flown more than a million hours.
However, the aircraft has not yet returned to commercial operation in China.
In 2021, Airbus delivered 611 aircraft – it is the third year in a row leading the supply.
For comparison, in 2020, the company shipped 566 aircraft.
But here, too, is far from the record set in 2019, when the company delivered 863 aircraft to the market.
Airbus is expected to maintain its lead in supply for the foreseeable future.
As already mentioned, in May of this year, Boeing delivered 35 aircraft, including 30 Boeing 737 (29 Max and one NG), one 747, one 767 and three 777.
Boeing currently produces 27 737 aircraft per month, which is already well over 19 aircraft per month as of the end of October 2021.
However, the target for the second quarter was set slightly more ambitious – 31 aircraft per month, and it seems unattainable: delays in the supply of parts and components led to a slowdown in production.
Instead of rolling unfinished aircraft through the assembly line and taking them to the field for subsequent installation of missing parts, which is a common approach for similar production problems, Boeing suspended the assembly of aircraft right in the hangars.
Production works at various sites have not yet been fully restored.
There are problems not only with the production of the Boeing 737 – deliveries of the Boeing 787 Dreamliner have been suspended for more than a year, and it is not yet known when they will resume.
Boeing has suspended deliveries of the Dreamliner amid a review by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) of the company ’ s methods of checking and evaluating the company ’ s aircraft for compliance with their federal safety standards.
In February, FAA chief executive Steve Dixon said the agency wanted to see a "systemic" solution to problems with the 787 Dreamliner, and that management would not allow Boeing to certify individual new aircraft on its own.
The FAA wants Boeing to have a comprehensive overhaul plan that will apply to all 787 Dreamliners in storage.
According to Boeing, the company comprehensively checks all links in the production and supply chain of components for the 787 Dreamliner, and regularly discusses the situation with the FAA, suppliers and customers.
The company is also working on the 787 Dreamliner.
In order to understand the “scale of the tragedy ”: at the end of last year, Boeing already had 110 787 Dreamliners in storage (produced, but not yet certified).
The company now produces approximately 2,787 per month, and expects to maintain this volume until the supply of components stabilizes.
Then the company is going to increase production to five, and by the end of 2023 to seven 787 Dreamliners per month.
Boeing ’ s 777 program was expected to receive reinforcements at the end of 2023 with the first delivery of the 777X, but in April, Boeing announced that this would not happen until 2025 – more time is needed to complete a full range of certification tests.
Boeing points out that the expansion of production volumes of the 777-9 is being adjusted to minimize the number of aircraft requiring "implementation changes."
In other words, the company prefers to produce already ready and certified, than then finish something in the previously produced.
Therefore, the company takes a pause in production until 2023.
At the same time, the company announced the expansion of the production range of the Boeing 777: in January this year it was announced the release of the cargo version of the 777X, and, for example, Qatar Airways will become the operator of the cargo 777-8F.
Compared to Boeing, Airbus is much better.
In May, the company delivered 47 aircraft to customers, including four A220, 37 Airbus A320 Neo, three A330 and three A350.
During 2021, Airbus gradually increased production of A320 aircraft from 40 per month to 43 in the third quarter of 2021, and at the end of the year brought production to 45 aircraft per month.
And it will continue to grow until it reaches 65 units per month by the summer of 2023.
But this is not the limit: against the background of greatly increased demand, Airbus is negotiating with component suppliers to increase the production of A320 to 75 aircraft per month in 2025!
If all goes well, then from 2026 the company will produce 900 aircraft per year of the A320 family.
For comparison, in Russia by the end of 2030 they plan to produce about 1000 aircraft of different models – and SSJ New, and MC-21, and Tu-214 and others combined.
On June 15, the Airbus A321XLR successfully completed its first flight.
It is planned that the commercial operation of this model will begin in early 2024, this is not a strong delay in comparison with the previously announced deadline - the end of 2023.
Airbus A220 is produced in the amount of five aircraft per month.
In the coming months, production will increase slightly to six aircraft per month, and by 2025 they plan to collect already 14 A220 per month.
The Airbus A350 is now being produced at five aircraft per month, with a plan to produce six A350s per month by early 2023.

The Ministry of Finance proposed to tax Russians abroad.
What is important to know
The Ministry of Finance drew attention to the problem of taxation of Russians who went abroad, continuing to receive wages from Russia.
The Agency proposed to actually increase their tax burden, obliging the employer to deduct personal income tax for them
Photo by Luke Dray / Getty Images
On July 26, the Ministry of Finance presented a bill containing many amendments to the Tax Code, including in terms of taxation of individuals.
The public consultation procedure will last until August 12, and the new rules are scheduled to enter into force on January 1, 2023.
In particular, it is proposed to establish that remuneration paid by Russian organizations – employers for the performance of labor duties remotely outside the country relate to income from sources in Russia for tax purposes.
Even in the coronavirus pandemic, the practice of moving Russian workers to other countries became active, where they could (in agreement with the employer or without warning him) work remotely and continue to receive wages.
With the beginning of the special military operation in Ukraine, this trend continued.
According to the current norms of the Tax Code, the salary received from a Russian employer remotely at the location of the employee in another country is considered income from a source outside Russia.
Accordingly, if a person remains a tax resident of Russia, then he is obliged to pay personal income tax from this labor remuneration in the amount of 13% (highly paid employees - 15%), and when he ceases to be a tax resident (for this you need to stay abroad for more than 183 days a year), the obligation to pay the Russian personal income tax disappears.
The Ministry of Finance proposed to supplement the list of income from sources in Russia with remuneration and other payments when a remote worker performs a labor function under a contract with an employer, as well as remuneration for work performed (services rendered, transferred rights to use the results of intellectual activity), if such performance is carried out abroad, but using Russian domain names and network addresses or technical means located in Russia (if at least one of the criteria is met: the taxpayer is a tax resident of Russia) income is transferred to an account in a Russian bank, the source of payment is Russian organizations or separate subdivisions of foreign organizations in Russia).
The Ministry of Finance proposed a way to mitigate the blow from the abolition of groups of taxpayers
Business
This means that such remote workers will have to pay personal income tax at a rate of 13% (15% - on the part of income exceeding 5 million rubles during the year) as long as they remain tax residents of Russia, and 30% - after becoming non-residents.
At the same time, as a rule, tax deductions are not applied to income taxed at the rate of 30%.
Who is paying the NFL now and who will be
Now the remuneration of remote workers located outside of Russia are considered foreign income and are subject to personal income tax only as long as the employee is a tax resident of Russia, but this is “not entirely logical, since in fact the payment is made by a Russian company, ” says Ernest Aramyan, lawyer of the practice“ International Law and Taxes ” of the company “Lemchik, Krupsky and Partners ”.
“In view of the increased labor migration from Russia beyond its borders in the near future, the Russian budget would lose a significant amount of income, since the employees of Russian companies who left will soon cease to be tax residents of the Russian Federation and they will not have the obligation to pay personal income tax from these incomes, ” he said.

At the same time, in accordance with current norms, the company is not recognized as a tax agent in respect of payments from sources outside Russia.
“Thus, from the first day of the employee ’ s work abroad, the company may not withhold personal income tax from income directly related to the performance of labor duties, ” said Olga Zamesina, Director of the Department of Tax and Legal Consulting at Kept.
While the employee is a tax resident of Russia, to declare and pay personal income tax he must independently at the end of the tax period, follows from last year's letter of the Ministry of Finance.
“If such an employee loses the status of a tax resident at the end of the year, these incomes were not subject to taxation in Russia, and they did not need to be reported to the tax service by filing a tax return in the form of 3-NDFL.
The tax on the received income was paid according to the norms of the tax legislation of the country of residence of such an employee, ” adds Irina Bychkova, a leading lawyer at Amulex tax practice.
In theory, the company may not know that its employee moved abroad, and continue to withhold personal income tax in the amount of 13% of his salary, transferring the tax to the Russian budget.
Theoretically, the confirmation of stay in a foreign country can be stamps in the passport on the dates of departure, but the labor legislation does not contain the obligation of the employee to provide the employer with documents confirming the place of his actual remote work, the audit and consulting group "Unicon" notes.
Accordingly, the employee may refuse to present a passport.
At the same time, the Labour Code obliges to include information about the place of work in the employment contract.
The bill of the Ministry of Finance proposes to establish the obligation of the authorized bodies to report to the tax authority at the place of residence of the citizen information on the facts of the primary issuance (replacement) of the passport of the Russian citizen.
“Obtaining information about foreign passports is necessary for the automatic determination of tax and currency residence of individuals, ” the explanatory note to the project notes.
What are the risks to the employee of the new order
Income received abroad by Russians who are not tax residents of Russia may be taxed in a foreign state in accordance with its legislation.
Therefore, actual taxation will depend on the existence and terms of a bilateral double taxation agreement (DTA).
“If this income will be subject to taxation in the country of work of the remote worker, in practice, there may be difficulties in obtaining an exemption under the SIDS, which, in turn, can lead to double taxation, ” emphasizes Zamesina.
In addition, when the new regulation comes into force, the employer - a tax agent, if he receives information that his employee has ceased to be a tax resident, will not only have to start withholding tax at a rate of 30%, but also recalculate previously withheld personal income tax from the beginning of the calendar year at an increased rate, says Bychkova.
Those who have moved abroad and become non-residents have another option: register as self-employed and pay tax at a rate of 6% when providing services to legal entities.
Russian legislation does not prohibit this, the status of non-residence does not affect self-employment, said the Vice-President of the Association of lawyers for registration, liquidation, bankruptcy and judicial representation Vladimir Kuznetsov.
It is unlikely, but the amendment on personal income tax for foreign workers can still be excluded, since the project has not even been submitted to the State Duma, he adds.
Similarly, it is supposed to impose personal income tax payments for works and services if they are made via the Internet and are connected with Russia.
“The bill lists several conditions under which the binding to the Russian Federation is confirmed (one of them is the receipt of funds to a Russian bank account).
It is important that for such payments it is proposed to introduce the obligation to register foreign legal entities for withholding and paying personal income tax to the budget.
This procedure is somewhat similar to the procedure for paying VAT from electronic services (the so-called tax on Google), said Anna Zelenska, associate partner of MEF-Audit.

Chinese scientists once again finally debunk the myth of the quantum superiority of the Google Sycamore system
In 2019, Google researchers said they were the first in history to achieve quantum supremacy when the company ’ s Sycamore quantum computer performed calculations in 200 seconds that would take a normal supercomputer 10,000 years to complete.
Scientists from China performed the same calculation in a few hours using conventional GPUs and argue that a supercomputer would do the same in a few tens of seconds.
Google's Sycamore Quantum System.
Image source: Google
Apparently, Google was in a hurry when it announced the achievement of quantum supremacy three years ago — the milestone beyond which classical computers finally surrender to quantum computers in the field of computing or simulations of a certain kind.
Such a loud statement could not go unnoticed in the scientific community, and IBM was the first to respond to it, since Google ’ s statement compared Sycamore to the IBM Summit supercomputer.
IBM questioned Sycamore ’ s quantum supremacy and reported that Summit could perform similar calculations in 2.5 days, rather than 10,000 years, as Google claims.
Then, to debunk the myth of the quantum superiority of Google Sycamore for solving a certain type of problems — the execution of an algorithm for modeling an arbitrary random quantum circuit or sampling the output distribution of random quantum circuits — began Chinese scientists, but not theoretically, as they did at IBM, but solving the problem almost on classical computers.
Last year, optimizing the algorithm, the Chinese on 60 NVIDIA graphics cards solved the problem in 5 days.
Obviously, a supercomputer would have coped with the solution faster.
And indeed, the new Chinese supersystem Oceanlite based on the new generation of Sunway chips (ShenWei) received the prestigious Gordon Bell Award for what?
For refuting Google ’ s claim to achieve quantum supremacy.
Oceanlite solved the problem in 304 seconds, simultaneously becoming the first in the world to break the exascale barrier.
The incredible power of Oceanlite is almost equal to the capabilities of quantum Sycamore.
But the Chinese again optimized the algorithm and could solve Google ’ s quantum problem on 512 NVIDIA graphics cards in 15 hours.
According to scientists, if they had a supercomputer, they would solve the problem in a few tens of seconds, which would leave the result of Google Sycamore far behind.
Details about the algorithm and methods of calculations, Chinese experts told in the journal Physical Review Letters.
To speed up the calculations, they went to some coarsening of the level of permissible errors (accuracy).
So, if Google carried out calculations taking into account the probability of errors 0.2%, the Chinese researchers made the probability of errors at the level of 0.37%, which 256 times accelerated the calculation.
Also, the Chinese used tensor matrices, so that the calculations were reduced to simple multiplication operations, and GPUs cope with this best in parallel data processing.
In detail, but in difficult language, you can read about this in the article, which is available on arXiv.org in PDF format.

So whose dish is this?

Ukraine and Russia have been arguing over borsch for decades.
Whose dish is this?
Every country is sure: the invention of thick beetroot soup belongs to it!

Who else is arguing about food?

Stalin ’ s Trophy and UNESCO Heritage
A timeless classic.
Borsch is one of the most famous and favorite Russian dishes, a symbol of traditional cuisine. ”
Such a post was published in 2019 on the page of the Russian Foreign Ministry on Twitter.
And that's where it started!
The world was swept by a wave of battle for borsch.
The BBC even said that the Russians “stole this dish ”.
“Russia ’ s claim to something so Ukrainian is the embodiment of a much larger trend of Russia ’ s historical oppression of the Ukrainian language, politics and, above all, independence. ”
Air Force columnist Andrew Evans conducted an investigation and found out that borsch is a Ukrainian dish.

By the way, UNESCO in 2020 included borsch in the national list of intangible cultural heritage of Ukraine.

Rostov borsch
So the battle for borscht is lost?
Oh, no, no, no.
The recipe of Rostov brown borsch was shared with us by the author of culinary bestsellers Elena Obukhova.
Rostov borsch must be necessarily on meat broth, with pieces of meat, so it turns out more satisfying and tastier.
Meat for the broth can be any - pork, beef, chicken.
REQUIRED: Recipe for a saucepan 5 l: · meat (beef, pork) or chicken (homemade, broiler) · 1 medium beet · 1 medium carrot · 3 large potatoes · a quarter of a small cabbage head · 1 medium onion · 300 g canned red beans · 2 - 3 tbsp. l tomato paste · 4 tbsp. l vegetable oil · salt, ground black pepper to taste · sour cream and greens for serving.
COOKING:
1.
In a saucepan pour water, put the meat, salt and cook until fully cooked, get and cut into small pieces, send to the broth.
You can not cut meat and not add to borscht, it can be served to borscht sliced, on a plate.
2.
Potatoes cut into small pieces, add to the boiling broth and cook for 10 minutes until half-cooked.
3.
Onions finely chop, carrots and beets grate.
4.
Let's get the roast ready.
In a frying pan pour vegetable oil, put the onions, carrots and beets, fry over medium heat for 5 minutes, add the tomato and another 2 minutes fry all together.
5.
From the beans drain the juice and rinse.
6.
Ready roast and beans send in a saucepan, cook together for 5 minutes.
7.
Cabbage thinly chop, add to the pan.
8.
Try the soup soup to taste and add salt, pepper to taste.
9.
After adding cabbage, cook borscht for 10 minutes.
10.
At the very end, season the borscht with herbs, turn off the fire and let the borscht brew for 30 minutes.
Serve with sour cream and greens.
Ukrainian borsch
With the help of Venus Osepchuk, a culinary blogger and author of gastronomic books published by the Komsomolskaya Pravda publishing house, we learned from her subscribers life hacks of Ukrainian borsch.
In the comments noted the Ukrainian hostesses:
“Ukrainian borsch is primarily fatty meat.
In the south of Ukraine, sweet pepper is added to the main set of vegetables, in the west - beans. "
“You have to put the parsnip!
And instead of tomato paste - pureed tomatoes. "
"At the end of cooking, I add salted lard (preferably old), twisted with garlic - 1 tbsp. l, fatty smoked rib, 4 prunes and beets with vinegar, stewed separately at the very end, only all together boil and turn off."
“It is necessary to serve the dish with thinly sliced lard and dumplings with garlic. ”
“After 30 years in different parts of Ukraine, I realized that there is no single recipe for borsch.
How many hosts, so many options for cooking. ”
NEED: · beef brisket - 1 kg · cabbage - 750 - 800 g · onion - 3 pcs.
· potatoes - 3 pcs.
· tomatoes - 2 pcs.
· beets - 2 pcs.
· carrots - 2 pcs.
· garlic - 3 cloves · fresh parsley 1 bunch · bay leaf - 2 - 3 pcs.
· lemon juice - 1 tbsp. · sugar - 2 tsp. · salt, pepper to taste · water - 4 l.
COOKING:
1.
Put the meat in a saucepan, pour cold water.
Bring the broth to a boil, periodically removing the foam.
Salt (first 1 tbsp. l salt, at the end of cooking still add salt) and lower the whole onion.
Cook the meat over a minimum heat for two hours.
2.
Grate carrots and one beet on a coarse grater.
Cut two onions into half rings.
Cut tomatoes in half, grate on a coarse grater, throw out the peel.
3.
In a saucepan, melt 20 - 30 g of butter, sauté onions, grated carrots and beets, simmer for 5 - 10 minutes, add grated tomatoes, 1 tbsp. l sugar and simmer for 7 - 8 minutes.
4.
Chop cabbage.
In a saucepan, heat 1 tbsp. l vegetable and butter, put the cabbage, simmer over medium heat for 7 - 10 minutes.
5.
When the broth is ready, remove the meat from it, remove the bones, cut the meat into pieces.
Remove the whole onion from the broth.
6.
In the boiling broth put potatoes, cut into large pieces.
As soon as it is cooked, add the cabbage, let it cook for 10 - 15 minutes.
Add stewed vegetables (carrots with beets), bay leaf and chopped boiled meat, cook for another 5 minutes.
If necessary, add salt and pepper the broth.
7.
Remember we still have another raw beet?
Now it's her turn.
Beet grate on a coarse grater, squeeze lemon juice on it, mix.
8.
Chop fresh greens, grate garlic.
Add raw beets, greens, garlic to the pan, mix and immediately turn off the heat.
Close the pan with a lid and let the borsch brew for 15 - 20 minutes.
Serve on the table with sour cream.

Everyone knows that this is a dish of Middle Eastern cuisine.
But Israel and Lebanon insist that chickpea paste, which can be spread on anything from tortillas to baked vegetables, they invented.

Tore grape leaves, wrapped minced meat
- Do you like dolma?
- No!
- Because you don't know how to cook dolma!
This dialogue from the film “Mimino ” about chopped meat with rice wrapped in grape leaves took place between a Georgian Valiko and an Armenian Rubik Jan.
But Georgians do not participate in the most “bloody ” battles for the long haul, disputes occur between Armenians and Azerbaijanis.
Armenians refer to the Oxford University Food Guide, where dolma (tolma) is a dish of Armenian origin, which later migrated to Turkey, and from there to other peoples.
The famous culinary historian William Pokhlebkin is also a supporter of this version: from the 17th to the beginning of the 19th century, Armenia was divided between Turkey and Iran.
During this period, the economy of Armenia, its human and material resources fell into decline, but the spiritual and material culture did not change, and the Armenian cuisine did not die.
On the contrary, the Armenians contributed to the cuisine of the Seljuk Turks, so that many truly Armenian dishes later became known in Europe through the Turks as supposedly dishes of Turkish cuisine (for example, dolma).
But the Azerbaijanis do not give up, they are trying to return the “Azerbaijani nationality ” to Dolma and Khasha.
“As khash is being prepared in Azerbaijan, I think no one will be able to do it anywhere.
It is necessary to strengthen the work in the field of promotion of national cuisine abroad, to familiarize the world community with our dishes, ” the representatives of Azerbaijan write in the network.
The pinnacle of the evidence was the recognition in 2017 by UNESCO of the tradition of dolma cooking in Azerbaijan as part of the cultural heritage.
And while they're arguing, we're gonna enjoy the hangover hash and the melting dolma in our mouths.

With the advent of new technologies and the introduction of digitalization, labor relations should be accompanied by processes of reducing labor time.
Why it is difficult to make predictions about the introduction of the “four-day ” in Russia
Chairman of the State Duma Committee on Labor, Social Policy and Veterans Affairs Yaroslav Nilov said that the transition to a four-day working week is “a matter of the near future. ”
Candidate of Economic Sciences, President of the Association of Managers and Specialists in Human Resources Management of the Sverdlovsk Region, Head of the Department of Labor Economics and Human Resources Management of USUE Svetlana Dolzhenko explained what work schedule is optimal for most people, and why it is difficult to make predictions about the introduction of a “four-day ” in Russia.
In the Labor Code of Russia, the schedule of work is regulated by 91 articles, according to which the normal duration of the working week cannot exceed 40 hours.
This is due, among other things, to numerous scientific studies on the organization of work and the formation of a balance between work and personal life.
The logic is simple: time to rest should be enough to restore strength for subsequent effective activities.
At the same time, there are several options for working hours: for example, two after two, five-day and six-day working weeks or an incomplete one.
The idea of a four-day work week is not new.
Back in the twenties of the last century, Henry Ford, the founder of the automobile company, realized that well-rested workers work more productively.
At the moment, a reduced work schedule is successfully practiced abroad.
For example, Perpetual Guardian insurance company in New Zealand introduced a 32-hour work week a few years ago.
According to the results, workers not only manage to do the same amount of work in four days as in five, but also become more motivated (by 24%), and productivity increases by 20%.
Another example is Microsoft Japan.
There, with the introduction of a four-day work week, productivity increased by 40%.
For enterprises in Japan, this case is especially important, since it is in this country that the term “karoshi ” means death from processing.
Since the 1950s, Japan has become a benchmark for hard work around the world.
Japanese companies offered workers a lifetime job guarantee and high wages in exchange for irregular working hours and loyalty to superiors.
And business leaders got what they wanted — incredible productivity gains.
But over time, these conditions led to the opposite effect, people were too tired and could not perform their work qualitatively.
In Russia, the proposal to switch to a four-day working week was first put forward in 2019 at that time by the Prime Minister of the Russian Federation Dmitry Medvedev.
At the moment, making predictions about the reduction of the working week is quite difficult.
While the deputies did not present the bill, it is not clear how exactly it is proposed to change the regime: an 8-hour working day from Monday to Thursday or a weekly workload of 40 hours will be distributed over four days - a 10-hour working day will be introduced.
And in addition, it is not clear what will happen after the innovations with the salary - will be reduced in proportion to a decrease in the amount of time worked or will remain at the same level?
It is only obvious that with the advent of new technologies and the introduction of digitalization, labor relations should be accompanied, as they were centuries ago, by processes of reducing labor time.
This requires more flexible labor legislation, which in turn will definitely lead to an increase in labor productivity.
