Voice Record
Automatic speech recognition (ASR) has always challenged artificial intelligence and machine learning.
Thanks to the Whisper program, OpenAI has taken another successful step in the development of this direction.
A lot of different options
There are a huge number of different speech recognition systems that are the basis of the software and services of such technology giants as Google, Meta and Amazon.
A distinctive feature of Whisper is that this platform has been trained for 680,000 hours based on data collected from the Internet in multilingual and multitasking mode.
This approach has improved the recognition of unique accents, background noise variations, as well as technical terminology and jargon.
"The main intended users of Whisper models are AI specialists who study the reliability, potential, errors, generalization and limitations of the current model.
However, Whisper can also be potentially useful as a solution for automatic speech recognition among developers, especially for English speech recognition. "said OpenAI representatives in the GitHub repository.
Anyone can download Whisper from GitHub; it ’ s completely free.
Models have demonstrated their capabilities
In a press release, OpenAI said: "The models performed well in ASR in about 10 languages.
Tailored to perform certain tasks, such as detecting voice activity, dictaphone recording, and classifying speakers, they can demonstrate a host of useful benefits.
However, they have not yet been thoroughly tested in these areas. ”
Limitations of technology
In certain areas, such as text forecasting, Whisper has certain disadvantages.
Since the system was trained on a large number of "noisy" data sets, the company warns that Whisper may include in its transcriptions words that were not actually spoken.
This may be due to the need to predict the next word and at the same time try to decipher the audio stream.
In addition, Whisper does not work equally well in different languages.
When working with native speakers of languages that are underrepresented in training data or models, the system allows a higher percentage of errors.
The company says: “Although Whisper models cannot be used for real-time transcription out of the box, their speed and versatility allow specialists to develop products based on them that can recognize and translate speech almost instantly.
The true value of applications built on Whisper models suggests that the disparate performance of these systems can have real economic benefits. "
OpenAI is not limited to Whisper technology.
Currently, the company is also engaged in the creation of commercial projects such as DALL-E 2 and GPT-3.
In addition, OpenAI constantly conducts purely theoretical developments, one of which is artificial intelligence systems, which are trained by studying recorded video materials.

Congo, Iraq, Uganda and Bangladesh show unexpected growth in investments in start-ups
Stories
Elena Likhanova
Senior Editor RB.RU
Elena Likhanova
In the vast majority of cases, funded startups are grouped in countries that are easy to do business.
They are rarely seen in regions where it is difficult to start new businesses.
And that ’ s why it ’ s so interesting to find that in a place like this, startup funding can grow.
The Crunchbase platform studied such locations and shared unexpected conclusions.
Congo, Iraq, Uganda and Bangladesh show unexpected growth in investments in start-ups
It turns out that seed and venture capital investments cover more and more corners of the globe.
For simplicity, four countries were chosen that have never been the centers of attraction for startups, but are seeing a sharp increase in funding.
For this purpose, the World Bank rating of 190 best and worst countries for doing business and Crunchbase data were used.
Democratic Republic of the Congo
It is the largest country in sub-Saharan Africa, home to about 108 million people.
It is a country with a tragic colonial history that has spent several turbulent decades under the leadership of strong leaders.
Despite the fact that this country is huge and rich in natural resources, it has never been easy to make a living or build a business here.

By 2050, Africa ’ s digital economy will grow sixfold – forecast
Why Africa is the most interesting region for Russian entrepreneurs
But Congo is too big a territory for startups to ignore completely.
According to Crunchbase, local startups have received about $10.4 million in investments since 2021.
While these numbers don ’ t look as impressive, it ’ s a leap from previous years.
Thus, according to Crunchbase, for the decade from 2010 to 2020, Congolese companies attracted only $1.2 million of pre-seed investments.
One of the largest recipients of funding in recent years is Altech Group, a supplier of solar energy and eco-friendly cookstoves.
The company raised $1.5 million in equity financing with the support of social investor SIMA Funds, as well as $7.1 million in debt financing.
Another $37.5 million this year went to Jambo, an African Web3 superapp whose founders were born in Congo.
In May, the company closed a $30 million round led by investment company Paradigm, focused on cryptocurrencies.
It is unclear if Jambo is also present in the Congo.
Iraq
Iraq is hardly the center of technological start-ups.
According to Crunchbase, from 2010 to 2020, local projects received about $2 million in venture and seed funding.
Recently, however, the situation has been gaining momentum.
Since 2021, startups from Baghdad have raised at least $13.7 million in equity funding.
There is even a special fund, Iraq Tech Ventures, which says it focuses on “diversifying Iraq ’ s economy from oil to more sustainable sectors such as technology. ”
RB recommends the best digital solution providers for your business
Most recently, the most significant funding went to Bely, an app to call a taxi from Baghdad, closing the $10.5 million round.
Food delivery startup Alsaree3 raised $3.2 million
Uganda
Uganda ’ s population is said to be the youngest in the world, with an estimated 45% of its inhabitants under the age of 15.
Only 2% of people in this country are over 65 years old.
Apparently, part of this youthful energy is being translated into startups.
Crunchbase notes that since 2021, at least 20 startups from Uganda have raised seed, venture or debt financing and collectively raised more than $40 million.
For comparison, over the entire decade from 2010 to 2020, Ugandan startups received less than half of that amount.
The most famous of the local projects is Tugende, a startup from Kampala that offers financing and services for small businesses and sole proprietors who want to own income-generating assets such as motorcycles and cars.
According to Crunchbase, Tugende has raised $22 million in equity financing and $27 million in debt financing to date.
In June, the company also announced an undisclosed size round.
And in March, telemedicine solution provider Rocket Health Africa closed a $5 million Series A round.
The company, based in Kampala, offers medical consultations on a smartphone, collection of laboratory samples and delivery of medicines.
Bangladesh
With a population of 170 million people, Bangladesh is the eighth most populous country on Earth.
However, in terms of land area, Bangladesh ranks 94th, which means that it is also one of the most densely populated countries in the world.
Despite geographical difficulties, the natives of the country are industrious, which over the past decade has allowed it to become one of the fastest growing economies in the world.
This has led to a sharp rise in investment in start-ups, many of which create goods and services for consumers and businesses in the domestic market, as well as export-oriented businesses.
Crunchbase has data on nearly 100 rounds of different stages involving startups from Bangladesh that have closed since last year, collectively raising more than $230 million.
Most of that money went to one company: Dhaka based ShopUp, a small business B2B trading platform that raised more than $200 million in venture capital investments.
Other major rounds are dominated by e-commerce, logistics and delivery.

Taras Krishtanovich: “In Thailand, general relaxation is both good and bad ”
Former Surgut businessman about the experience of life in Thailand
Known in Surgut businessman Taras Krishtanovich not so long ago first left our city, moving to Moscow, and now 10 months living in Phuket.
Our editors contacted him to find out what it is like to become not a tourist, but a more or less permanent resident of Thailand.
– How did you leave Russia and why did you go to Thailand?
- The last two years I lived in Moscow, where I had a child, and last autumn we, walking around the city, realized that we do not want to spend the next six months in the cold.
I managed to get cold enough after living in Surgut for almost 40 years.
So I decided to go to Thailand for the winter.
They planned to return in March, and when all these events had already begun, they thought it would make sense to stay here.
In general, I have never considered Thailand as a place of permanent residence for a number of reasons - yet a developing country, Phuket compared to the center of Moscow - is not the most equal exchange in terms of service, capabilities, architecture and other parameters.
But after living here for six months, we realized that there are other interesting and important things, and in the current situation their role has only increased.
So I think the decision to stay here is the right one.
– What is the situation with such parameters as education and medicine?
- The child is now two years old, he goes to kindergarten, where he learns Russian and English.
In principle, kindergartens are for any budget - there are municipal, there is a more expensive one, there is a British School, in which the cost of a month is the equivalent of 150-200 thousand rubles.
That is, for every taste and purse.
Schools and universities are the same.
There are good ones, but they cost money.
But we must admit that if we talk about conditionally free education, it is on average lower than in free education in Russia.
Medicine is not very expensive, again, with clinics of different levels, but if you have insurance, then it covers the bulk of the needs.
In general, Thailand is a place for middle-income and high-income foreigners.
Having some wealth, you can find everything – kindergartens, schools / universities, and restaurants to your taste and budget.
– Are there any problems with legalization of stay?
Visas, residence permits?
– It is almost impossible to obtain a residence permit here, Thailand is reluctant to meet foreigners in this matter.
The only option is to marry someone from the local community.
Getting a different visa is no problem.
Visa-free stay is now 30 days, there is an option to make a student visa, but it is only so called, in fact - it can be language courses for a year.
There is a business visa if you open a company.
There are even “pension ” visas – for people aged 50 + with a certain amount of money in the account.
Of course, there are special visas for “digital nomads ” – IT specialists who come to the country.
In general, there are no problems with legal residence here.
- Many of those Russians who came to other countries after February, faced the problem of opening bank accounts and obtaining plastic cards, as ours one day stopped working.
How did you manage to do that?
- There was a certain moment of panic, but in principle everything is simple.
If there is a registration for three months or more, and it is given automatically when renting housing, then you can go to the bank and open an account with a card.
That's what I did.
– Was there such a thing as “you are Russians, we will not give you anything ”?
- No.
There is a bank that is loyal to all foreigners, it opens accounts even on short-term visas.
The rest of the banks require long-term – the same student or business visas.
And so everything is in order, money is transferred through SWIFT, there are other ways of transactions with Russia, too.
– How are things with the Russian-speaking community?
- It is, and very different.
Many people have moved in the last 10-15 years, they have formed a kind of "Brighton Beach" - they live by the rules and concepts of the same Russia, which they left quite a long time ago.
And in the last six months, a lot of new guys have come, and they're completely different.
Young people, IT specialists, representatives of creative professions, remote workers.
I was at the stand-up the other day, there was a hall for 200 people, mostly aged 20-35, and 90 percent of them arrived in recent months.
And this is a cool community, where there is no division into Russians, Belarusians and Ukrainians, and no one shouts nasty things in your back.
In general, Thailand is a country where people respect and appreciate each other.
Here you forget about aggression in principle, it is not customary to raise your voice, swear, be angry.
Everything is smooth, calm.
And the local community is also positive, there are a lot of cool people who are moving, opening startups and businesses, which is great.
By the way, if any of our countrymen are thinking about moving to Thailand - I am ready to share all the information that I have.
I can write to [banned in Russia and recognized extremist social network, which is not about pictures].
– In conclusion: what do you like the most in Thailand, and what is the most annoying?
I like a quiet life.
There is positivity and absolute security.
You can leave an open wound car, and nothing will happen to it, you can forget somewhere a thing, and you will definitely return it.
This feeling of security is relaxing.
The child goes for a walk, ten meters away, ten people will hug him, something will be given, they are very positive about children.
It ’ s great to feel safe in every way.
What you like is partly annoying.
People are relaxed.
They can promise something, forget it and not do it.
At first, it ’ s just a disaster – you make plans, and they don ’ t work because people just don ’ t fulfill their obligations.
And when you express dissatisfaction - sincerely surprised, they say, "Well, I did not or did not come - what is the problem?"
They don ’ t really understand where your frustration or anger comes from.
I was starting a company here.
It's actually pretty simple and takes two weeks.
But it took me two months.
Just because the locals with whom he worked on this issue, constantly forgot something.
“Do I need anything else? ”“ No, it ’ s okay. ”
Then I go, “Oh, you know, I had to do this, ”“ Okay, let ’ s do this.
Exactly everything? ” – “Exactly! ”
And then, “Oh, that ’ s what I ’ ve been asking. ”
It was really pissed off.
Perhaps the main negative point.
But the funniest and perhaps most terrible thing is that after a while you yourself become so.
Slowly, relaxed, you already say, “Yes, yes, well, ” and you can forget.
You fit into the local rhythm.

Robots in the future will serve as a dog for the elderly or lonely people – scientists
Robots that in the future will support the elderly or lonely, should build relationships with the owner not as people, but as dogs.
In the future, this concept will be applied by developers.
Scientists from the University of Glasgow have made relevant conclusions based on new research.
This is reported on September 29 in the magazine PLOS ONE.
Scottish researchers surveyed more than 150 dog breeders and found that there are seven of the most commonly cited factors most closely related to animals.
These include the ability to communicate, the predictability of reactions, the physical signs of attachment, a positive, sometimes even enthusiastic approach, a propensity for joint activities, a sense of intimacy and, finally, the ability to adapt to each other.
Perhaps robots that behave this way will be approved.
The researchers suggest that embedding this type of behavior into robot software will allow them to provide their owners with the same experience and health benefits as friendship with a real animal, without the attendant responsibilities.
This will allow the technique to be used effectively.
"Our approach has allowed us to gain knowledge about the factors that make people so enjoy the company of dogs.
Although it will not be easy to recreate such behavior in robots, it can help in creating friendships for wards, ” the authors said.
In the next phase of the study, a team led by Katie Riddock intends to conduct tests involving humans and robots behaving like dogs.
An additional topic of study may also be the dependence of preferences of different types of dog behavior depending on the age, origin and environment of specific people.

What can the friendship with India give to Ukraine
India, currently the world ’ s sixth economy, manages to maintain friendly relations with Russia, which is at the same time friendly with China, and with the US, which is at war with Russia, which opposes China.
What is New Delhi interested in Ukraine?
Related video
In early October, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had a telephone conversation with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
They talked, of course, about the war that Russia unleashed against Ukraine, about nuclear blackmail and global food security, as well as about the strengthening of the partnership between the two countries.
The latter is especially interesting, because even after gaining independence, Ukraine for a long time continued to be in the wake of Russian politics.
This was facilitated by the provinciality of our post-imperial elite or by more objective factors – the question of historiosophy.
The fact is that now Ukraine, winning the war "the second army of the world", if it does not break into the center of international relations, it is significantly moving in this direction.
For Kiev, a previously closed door opens - and this must be used.
From Mowgli to the Nuclear Club
One such “door ” is India.
A country that has experienced British supremacy for centuries.
The well-known fairy tale about Mowgli was written by Rudyard Kipling, who was the same British colonizer.
The book became part of the cultural heritage of the British stay in India.
The world political and philosophical heritage was the non-violent struggle of Mahatma Gandhi against the foreign enslavement of his fatherland.
And India is known to everyone as the birthplace of Buddhism and Hinduism, and in the post-Soviet space the country became famous for its films.
But that ’ s all lyric.
What really lives a nuclear state with a billion people and an area larger than Western Europe?
What are its geopolitical goals and challenges?
In all these matters, Focus tried to understand.
In 1947, India gained independence from Britain.
This was a consequence of the non-violent struggle of Mahatma Gandhi, which we have already mentioned.
The young state immediately fell into the maelstrom of a ruthless geopolitical struggle not for life, but for death.
Conflicts with neighbors over the British heritage (the Muslim part of the historical subcontinent was separated into a separate state - Pakistan, but the borders drawn by Europeans did not satisfy either side).
The territories of Indochina (note the first part of the word in the name of this subcontinent), too, according to New Delhi, were torn away from the “mother land ”.
China began to encroach on them as a sphere of influence, and over time these trends only intensified.
Such a tense situation could not but lead to war.
In our case, a whole series of wars broke out, from which India emerged not just "on the shield", but also firmly holding a "nuclear shield" in its hands.
In 1974, after a successful test of atomic weapons, India joined the "nuclear club".
New Delhi ’ s new status has significantly curbed the ambitions of its wayward neighbors, Pakistan and China.
It is important to note that all three currently possess nuclear weapons.
Why India was so close to the Soviet Union
In the middle of the last century, India became one of the initiators of the Non-Aligned Movement.
Its cornerstone was the unification of the former colonies of world empires in order to obtain de facto independence from the former metropolises.
The participants of the movement pledged not to join any of the blocs – participants of the Cold War.
Despite this, India actively cooperated with the USSR, which declared the values of anti-colonialism and the protection of enslaved peoples.
Interestingly, New Delhi and Moscow were friends not only against the United States, as one might think, but not to a lesser extent against communist China.
Senior Research Fellow at the Carnegie Foundation, Asia and the Sub-Indian continent expert Ashley J.
Tellis believes that India still has not forgotten about Moscow ’ s support in conflicts with its neighbors a few decades ago.
Remember in New Delhi and who was supported by the United States at that time.
The USSR blocked UN Security Council resolutions that were unfavorable to India, and New Delhi refrained from condemning the aggressive acts of the Soviet Union.
Dr. Garrett Price, Senior Researcher of the Asia-Pacific Program of Chatham House, notes that this tradition was continued in the cooperation of India with the Russian Federation, in particular, New Delhi chose to remain silent about Moscow ’ s crimes in Chechnya and Abkhazia.
Arab columnist Mihir Sharma notes that in circles close to the Indian establishment, Moscow is considered a reliable partner who can always block a decision that is unprofitable for India in the UN Security Council, which cannot be said about the United States, which can not always go contrary to the declared values.
China: A Dangerous Neighbor
All these factors together form the proximity of India and Russia, but there are other powerful players on the map that influence the coexistence of this tandem.
Thus, China is only intensifying its expansion in the states of Southeast Asia.

By controlling the sources of major Indian rivers, Beijing can threaten the population of the state without the use of weapons of mass destruction.
India cannot stand up to it on its own.
Therefore, in New Delhi, looking for an ally against a powerful neighbor, they became closer to the United States, including by entering into a strategic security dialogue - Quad, which also includes the United States, Japan and Australia.
That is, India manages to maintain friendly relations with Russia, while at the same time being friendly with China, and with the United States, which is at odds with Russia and China.
Garrett Price notes that India has been pursuing such a policy for decades, which led it to significant success – from the former poor starving colony, which the country was in the mid-twentieth century, India became the 6th economy in the world and a nuclear power.
So why should New Delhi change anything?
The answer to this question must be found by Ukraine if Kiev wants to get the support of India.
In particular, as an argument can serve as the statement that it is impossible to sit on two chairs forever.
Despite the objective success of this policy, the world and the situation in it is changing.
The USSR is already in the past, and the times of the “potential end of history ” predicted after the end of the Cold War are becoming the past.
The risk of being in the orbit of the losing side is quite high.
Fighting with the United States and losing the sea
Important
India and Pakistan, all against all: why in the 21st century it is important to be upstream
Now India on land is squeezed by hostile and not too friendly states.
Its only outlet to the world is the Indian Ocean.
Through it, India conducts active trade with Arab countries.
He is trying to establish political and economic ties with Africa.
These two areas represent a competitive space with the “old familiar ” – the People ’ s Republic of China.
The security of the sea routes vital for the state of the Indian subcontinent is the preservation of the current global world order and friendship with the United States.
Also, the United States is the main importer of Indian goods (interestingly, India imports most of the goods from China).
Therefore, cooperation with the United States is important for India both geopolitically and economically.
India ’ s third largest foreign trade partner is the EU.
Foreign Policy columnist Michael Kugelman notes that India ’ s cooperation with a united Europe is only growing.
In addition to trade, cooperation in the areas of climate, modern technologies and migration is an important aspect.
Indian migrants are sending large sums of money back to their home countries, thus investing in their economy.
Therefore, breaking off for the sake of ephemeral support of the Russian Federation with its key partners, India can remain face to face with China and Pakistan (the latter in this case can count on US support in this confrontation) with closed sea routes that can be taken under the control of the enemies, with the tacit consent of Washington.
Moscow and New Delhi: Friendship Involved in Oil
What, in addition to sentimental memories, does Moscow give India?
First of all, it is oil (the last 20 years in the Indian subcontinent there has been almost relentless frenzied GDP growth, and energy resources are needed for production) and weapons.
Russia remains India ’ s largest arms supplier, although its share has fallen from 70% to 49% in recent years.
Russia is popular among the Indian right, which, in particular, relies on the current Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
This is something that a democratically elected government should take into account.
Director of the Institute of Management and Mass Communication Jagrana Nalin Ranjan Mohanty also noted that Russia smoothes the corners in relations between India and China.
However, in the context of intensifying competition with Beijing, which is growing from a border into a global one, relations between India and China will become more and more aggravated.
In such a situation, New Delhi will need not a mediator, but a powerful ally.
And Russia is more likely to choose a more powerful in all respects China than India.
In recent years, Washington has increasingly put New Delhi before a choice in the issue of weapons.
It will not be possible to combine the American and Russian assortment.
It is interesting that the weapons of the Soviet model can fully serve only Ukraine and the Russian Federation, so in the event of a military catastrophe in Moscow, the Indian defense can experience a tangible blow.
Of course, provided that New Delhi stays with the Kremlin to the last.
What might India be interested in?
A significant factor in India ’ s foreign policy is its ambition to become a permanent member of the UN Security Council.
The United States is the shadow instigator of UN reform, and Ukraine is the main mouthpiece of this idea.
A good basis for increasing cooperation.
In general, within the framework of the war, the key point of contact between Kiev and New Delhi was the issue of the evacuation from Ukraine of about 20,000 Indian students who were hostages of hostilities.
This aspect is mentioned by the Indian media in the context of the last conversation between the leaders of the states.
In general, the background of relations between our countries is not the best.
New Delhi remembers Ukraine ’ s criticism of India ’ s nuclear tests back in 1998.
Kiev remembers New Delhi ’ s neutrality over the annexation of Crimea.
These are the main positions where India and Ukraine intersected in world diplomacy – in general, relations are sluggish (Ukraine has never even been visited by the country ’ s prime minister, in whose hands all political power is concentrated).
Now India is in favor of preserving the world order (a thesis that benefits India itself in the context of free navigation in the world's oceans).
After all, this is a system in which India has succeeded.
At the same time, New Delhi is interested in its reformatting in order to become one of the “chosen ones ”.
This walking on the rope is called "strategic ambivalence."
A significant factor in the rapprochement of Kiev with New Delhi may be the economy.
Now India is the second importer of Ukrainian goods in Asia (the state receives 4% of all Ukrainian exports).
Basically, we are talking about agricultural and food products and military-technical cooperation.
Ukraine imports Indian pharmaceutical products.
Education is a major area of cooperation.
As already mentioned, there were 18095 Indian students studying in Ukraine before the war.
And what about the famous Indian cinema?
Bollywood has become a significant component of the Indian economy in recent decades.
Its producers liked the Ukrainian locations, and the scenes of some films in recent years were shot in Ukraine.
In particular, the key scenes of the blockbuster RRR were shot in Kiev.
The film is called the best blockbuster of 2022 - it became the most expensive film in the history of Indian filmmaking.
The main thing is not to stop
All these areas of cooperation can be expanded.
The key for our state remains to win the war - this will significantly change the attitude towards Kiev around the world and open previously unpromising doors.
The conversation itself with Narendra Modi became possible after the Ukrainian successes in the counter-offensive.
It ’ s time for India to finally choose a chair.
What was possible in the past is not always optimal in the present and in the future.

Kokshetau resident Elvira Mukasheva cooks more than 20 types of cheese, some - according to the original author's recipe
A woman raising four children has already won a grant for the Bastau Business project.
With this money, the mother of many children plans to open the first cheese factory in Kokshetau, which she plans to turn into a cult place with a unique color, BaigeNews.kz correspondent reports.
"Customs and sewing, it turned out, not mine"
Elvira is 36 years old, she is the mother of four children, the eldest of whom is 15, the youngest daughter is one and a half years old.
The road to the cheese was not too far away.
The heroine comes from the Kordai district of Zhambyl region.
The place of residence – on the border with Kyrgyzstan – played a role.
The girl learned to be a customs broker: she planned to get a job at the local customs.
But there was not a day to work in the specialty.
But very much helped the second education - tailor-universal.
Years later, becoming a mother and sitting on maternity leave, Elvira not only sheathed the family, but also regularly took orders.
Five years ago, a mother of many children moved to Kokshetau.
"Interrupted orders, I always sewed a lot.
But my soul was asking for something else.
Or something else...
I was always looking on the Internet for an idea that would respond to me, ” admits the interlocutor.
The most important incentive for a woman was her children.
“They were often sick.
I felt like we were eating wrong.
Then I decided.
Completely excluded from the diet sweet, carbonated drinks.
We stopped buying cookies and gingerbread in stores, which only take away energy.
I wanted more protein, but where can I get it?
Natural cheese in expensive shops, in Kokshetau, I am sure that most can only afford a cheese product.
And 100 grams of 25 to 60 percent protein is contained.
Proteins from cheese are faster and better absorbed by the human body than those in milk.
They have a good effect on metabolism, supply energy.
So I started making cheese at home for my children, ” Elvira says.
Cheese also contains vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, C, which are responsible for the functioning of the nervous and cardiovascular systems and immunity.
“I grew up in an aul and, of course, met cows, milked.
And then my mom made sour cream out of it, I washed the separator.
This process fascinated me.
But on sour cream it did not end, further, more - cottage cheese, cheese.
It seems to me that thanks to these products, including today, our generation is still more or less healthy, ” says the mother of many children.
“The internet taught me cheese. ”
Gradually, Elvira realized that cheese is something she wants to do seriously.
In the Akmola region, this niche is free, especially if we talk about soft varieties.
She explained that the solid is prepared at the enterprise in the Zhaksyn district.
In Burabaysky - in the village of Katarkol - lives a virtuoso master, he was trained by Italian mentors, who on a professional cheese factory produces semi-hard and hard varieties.
The village is far from the city, so to take and sell, for example, the same burrat will not be easy.
Information about cheeses and recipes Elvira Mukasheva collected on the Internet on grains.
And then I learned to cook.
Today, in the arsenal of a novice entrepreneur more than 20 types of cheeses: from fresh or soft it is Imereti, brynza, Adygei, halumi, buratta, mozzarella, strachatella in cream, ricotta, suluguni, philadelphia, mascarpone, milk pigtail.
From semi-solid - cachotta, gouda, poshekhonsky, farm, caciocavallo, belper knolle, kurt, primo salé, canestrato.
Two types with mold - camembert and brie.
Let us explain, fresh include types of cheeses that are not pressed and do not ripen.
Some experts even call them curds.
Soft varieties are prepared from cream, they have a delicate taste and consistency.
“For their preparation do not need special equipment, this is a plus.
And it is difficult that you need to eat them immediately, fresh.
Boiled and ate.
That is, you will not prepare it in advance for the assortment.
Well, how not to note that it is soft varieties that lead in the content of protein and amino acids, ” Elvira said.
For solid varieties, a novice businesswoman is not yet ready, you need to unwind, for example, buy cameras for aging.
Semi-hard and hard varieties withstand much longer, because they are dense.
Sales are more comfortable.
“Just as seven notes create billions of melodies, so a pinch of ingredients – thousands of types of cheese. ”
Elvira can talk about cheese for hours.
A mother of many children compares cheese making with music.
As composers of seven notes create different melodies, so cheesemakers - more than three thousand types of product from the classic "handful" of ingredients.
Milk, sugar salt, spices...
"Adygeysky.
Its taste is difficult to distinguish from cottage cheese, the same soft and granular in texture.
Mascarpone - it is made from fatty cream.
Great for desserts such as tiramisu.
Belper Knolle is from Switzerland.
It is prepared like our Kazakh traditional kurt, but spices are used here - saffron, paprika, black pepper, turmeric, garlic...
If the belper knolle is a hundred years old, our kurt is much older, they just patented it.
Or take mozzarella - Kazakhs cook as "uyz" (colostrum), they taste similar.
In general, cheese is a non-waste production.
One kind of "smoothly" goes into the other, remember the music?
Here we cook mozzarella, and from whey, what remains, ricotta with a delicate creamy taste and consistency like cottage cheese.
Or tofu - the so-called soy cottage cheese... ", - enthusiastically lists the woman.
"People clearly don't care about Roquefort."
Elvira Mukasheva cooks in her kitchen, while without special equipment.
Milk is purchased from the local farm of the Rothermel spouses.
The milk of their cows is famous for its luxurious taste: farmers feed animals exclusively with herbs, in winter silage and high-quality modern feed.
"The farm is located in the area of ​ ​ Galochya Sopka, where a chic variety of herbs.
Kokshetau has a wonderful nature, milk is delicious, cheese is a pleasure to cook.
I would also like to use the milk of goats and sheep.
But the first one is expensive for me, it is only to keep my goats.
I dream, when I "spin", I can afford it.
Our ancestors kept mostly sheep and goats, not cattle.
And the cheese was mostly sheep, very useful, ” says the novice entrepreneur.
Today Elvira has formed a circle of its regular customers.
However, housewives rarely buy her cheese: it is expensive.
Restaurants and hotels are booked regularly.
Mozzarella, buratta, halumi.
“The food has also gone up a lot lately.
People, as they say, clearly not up to Roquefort, ” complains the woman.
"I dream that my cheese factory will go beyond gastronomy"
Elvira ’ s dream is to open her own cheese factory / restaurant, cheese shop.
She proudly shows a sign that has been in her head for a long time.
Soon we will see her in Kokshetau: the other day it became known that the mother of many children won a grant of 1 million 225 thousand tenge under the project "Bastau Business".
The woman studied at the courses, she did all the calculations, thought over the strategy and wrote a business plan.
“I plan to spend this money on renting and buying the necessary equipment and inventory.
I have already found a cheese factory for 30 liters in Karaganda, induction cooker and hood, special stainless pots, ” the startup shared.
Elvira foresees possible problems with renting the premises:
“I think to rent a dining room in the building, preferably in the center of Kokshetau.
But, as I learned in the sanitary service, permission to cook cheeses in the dining room is difficult to get.
And all because some norms in the food industry are outdated, they have not changed since Soviet times.
According to the current rules, cheese factories must be opened at a distance of at least 50 meters from a residential building.
At the same time, there are no such restrictions for canteens and cafes.
That is, I have to buy or rent a separate room, and this is unprofitable. "
She plans to get a certificate and hopes to sell through stores.
But there is another, not so obvious, task.
As a mother, Elvira worries about the health of children, as a citizen - for the health of the nation.
“Today, people like to say,“ very tasty food, ” a riot of taste – with synthetic additives – shrugs their shoulders.
- After this, of course, you do not want to eat healthy cereals, cheese, greens.
Zero vitamins, often excess weight and constant loss of strength.
We adults should strive to eat consciously and teach this to children.
A few years ago, I started a new order in my family.
My products are just a tiny piece in a big machine called food culture.
And even if the "wow effect" and big sales do not happen, I at least try. "

Scientists have found that the Fibonacci sequence allows you to stabilize the work of qubits of a quantum computer
The Fibonacci sequence is a series of numbers, each of which is the sum of the two previous numbers (1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, and so on).
The history of this series goes back more than 2 thousand years, it is inextricably linked with the concept of the “golden ratio ” and is invisibly present in many areas of our daily life.
And recently, physicists have found that the Fibonacci sequence can also be very useful in the case of its use in quantum computing and communications.
Our regular readers are well aware that the main problem faced by the developers of quantum computers is the task of long-term maintenance of qubits, quantum bits, in a certain quantum state.
The longer the qubits are in the quantum state, the longer they can store and process the information contained in them, but any influence from the outside, any portion of heat, mechanical vibrations or electromagnetic radiation can destroy the quantum state of the qubits and break the bonds of quantum entanglement induced between them.
Researchers at Quantinum in Colorado are working to increase the stability of qubits.
They are experimenting with a 10-qubit computing system based on the ytterbium ion, which uses electric fields and laser light pulse sequences to control and maintain quantum entanglement.
Previously, these researchers managed to achieve stable operation of qubits for 1.5 seconds, but later one of them came up with the idea to use Fibonacci sequence numbers to encode a sequence of laser pulses.
Surprisingly, there was no limit when most of the qubits became able to stay in a stable state for 5.5 seconds.
Moreover, qubits could have remained stable for a longer time, but the high-precision timekeeping equipment used by scientists did not allow measuring time intervals longer than the 5.5 seconds mentioned.
Laser light pulses encoded by Fibonacci sequence numbers represent a new state of matter, a quantum time quasicrystal having an ordered structure (sequence) but no periodicity.
The sequence was encoded using light with two different frequencies and looked like this: A, AB, ABA, ABAAB, and so on.
But the effect that this new form of matter had on the quantum system turned out to be very unusual and unique.
"A system that has been affected by this has acquired a property of symmetry, which we call the symmetry of time translation.
This means that the same experiment or calculations will give the same result regardless of whether it happens today, tomorrow or 100 years from now, ” says Philipp Dumitrescu, a quantum physicist, “We also realized that such quasi-periodic sequences based on the Fibonacci series lead to the fact that in a quantum system, as it were, two different directions of time flow arise. ”.
Of course, everything that was said just above is quite capable of “blowing the brain ” of an inexperienced person.
But if the Fibonacci sequence in the form of laser pulses is able to ensure the preservation of quantum state and entanglement for a long time, then the developers of quantum computing and communication systems will certainly adopt this technology.

Quantum, Computer, Quantinum, Qubit, Ion, Ytterbium, Laser, Light, Pulse, Sequence, Fibonacci

Six books to read with children
On weekends, employees of Moscow libraries tell mos.ru about books that can captivate not only children of different ages, but also their parents.
You can read them together, and then discuss what you read.
Polina Vinnik chose six books, checked by readers of the library No 114, where she works, and by herself.
Photo: Mos.ruMos.ru
For the little ones
Video of the day
“When Your Dad is a Tiger ” by Irina Zartayskaya
Be sure to introduce your child to a cute tiger cub who talks about his dad, comparing him to the fathers of cubs of other animals.
Especially this book will appeal to curious kids: it is interesting to set out many facts about animals.
And bright illustrations made by the artist Elizaveta Tretyakova will please everyone without exception.
You just need to have this book in your home library.
For example, I have already prepared one copy as a New Year ’ s gift.
I'll tell you a secret: my nephew will get it.
“Once upon a time there were pencils ” by Tamara Mikheeva
Wonderful author Tamara Mikheeva has written many books for children of different ages.
All of them are very popular.
If your family is not familiar with any, I advise you to start with this easy educational book.
Firstly, it is a great option for reading before going to bed, and secondly, the book will help to develop creative thinking and imagination.
Many parents noticed that after reading their children became more interested in drawing.
For some children, Tamara Mikheeva ’ s book even became an incentive for entering an art school.
Older kids
“Asino Summer ” by Tamara Mikheeva
Again, this is Tamara Mikheeva ’ s book.
The story "Asino summer" leaves after reading the warmest and most tender feelings.
And don ’ t let it bother you that November is on the calendar: it ’ s always nice to think about summer when the weather is cloudy outside.
Adults will also be interested: you will remember your childhood, games that were once carried away.
The main character is a girl named Praskovya (or Asya, as her parents call her).
Arriving at the summer camp, she could not imagine that the local forest would be magical, and she herself - a brave heroine capable of saving a friend.
Asyu is waiting for incredible adventures, faithful companions in which will be gnomes and magical creatures.
She'll even learn to fly!
And most importantly, the girl will be able to overcome her fears.
"Astrovityanka" by Nikolai Gorkavy
For all lovers of science fiction I recommend the trilogy of Nikolai Gorkavy "Astrovityanka" (yes, yes, exactly, through the "a"!).
As a result of a space accident, the main character Nikki lost her parents and was left alone on the asteroid.
Ten years later, it is found and returned to Earth.
There, Nikki, who is called Space Mowgli, learns that that accident was not an accident.
The heroine will not only adapt to society, but also find those responsible for the death of her family.
The author of the book about Nikki is an astrophysicist, doctor of physical and mathematical sciences, laureate of the State Prize of the USSR.
Children will learn a lot of interesting facts from the world of physics, biology, chemistry, mathematics - you can not only have fun watching the plot, but also enrich their knowledge, which will be useful in the future.
Interesting fact: Bitter was born in Chelyabinsk and with pleasure mentioned about this city and nearby places in the pages of the trilogy.
You will meet the South Ural national park "Taganai", the city of Korkino, Kopeysk.
If you come from these places, then nostalgia is guaranteed for you.
And one more fact - for fans of "": in "Astrovityanka" you can see an analogue of the game Quidditch.
For Teenagers
The Time of the Bibliomants by Kai Mayer
The main character, Fury Salamandra Ferfax, always knew about the magic of books, because her family is hereditary bibliomants.
They believe that each book has its own soul, hides in itself a huge space inhabited by different mysterious creatures.
But not all books are like that.
There are also empty books that can absorb everything that humanity has written in its history.
Such are Furia and her father destroying.
When I opened the first book of the Time of the Bibliomants series, The Beginning of the Path, I was struck by the scale of the world created by the German writer Kai Meyer, but read it in two days.
Then there were the second and third parts, “Confrontation ” and“ The Book of Blood ”, but the story did not let me go for a long time, and I often returned to it with my thoughts.
The Warehouse of Terrible Words by Elia Barcelo
Once I took this book from the shelf out of pure curiosity, I could not imagine that it could leave such a deep mark.
History will force you to rethink the importance and correctness of words that are uttered under the influence of emotions.
Even one word can inflict a terrible wound that can bleed for many years - this is what the main character Taglieu will have to think about.
In her heart she cried out to her mother that she no longer loved her, and she left.
To rectify the situation, the girl must go to a place where not everyone is destined to get - in the Warehouse of Terrible Words.
There she met Pablo, who suffered a similar misfortune.
Together, the heroes will learn to weigh every word and say only what you really want to say.
The end of the story will make even the most persistent person cry.
Perhaps, after turning the last page, you will want to apologize to loved ones who you may have inadvertently offended.

Down with five days?
24.11.2022 17: 30
The transition to a four-day working week is widely discussed around the world.
There are several reasons: the impact of the pandemic, economic problems, shortage of personnel, supply disruptions, etc.
There is another difficulty: the “culture of vanity ” that has developed in recent years, when work dominates other aspects of human life, which leads to the“ burnout ” of workers.
All of the above has led to the fact that many business owners today believe that a four-day working week is an effective solution in order to cope with problems.
So, in 2021, 27% of American businessmen (owners of companies) out of 1,300 respondents said that they had already transferred their employees to such a schedule, and 35% were going to do so in the near future.
Assuming that such statistics are representative of business in the US as a whole, it means that at least a quarter of all companies are already operating under the new scheme: four days a week instead of five.
However, the phrase “four-day work week ” does not necessarily mean that the company actually works only four out of five working days, and on the other days its employees do not go on calls and do not answer phone calls.
It can mean that the employee of the company works, for example, 30 hours instead of the standard 40.
In any case, judging by the results of the survey, most business owners believe that this approach has huge advantages.
Mainly because it increases employee satisfaction.
Those stop thinking that they live only for the sake of work, become more motivated, increase the productivity of their work, reduce the turnover of personnel.
Of the 35% of business owners who are considering switching to a shorter work week, 84% believe that such a schedule will give them some (48%) or a significant (36%) advantage over competitors.
And half of those who have already switched to four days of work instead of five, say that they have already received this advantage.
Experts believe that this approach is applicable to any type of activity, including installation companies.
However, there is no official data that at least one integrator firm in the United States really adheres to this practice.

Employee went abroad: what to do for the employer
If the employee went abroad, but continues to work in a Russian company, there are some features of its registration, payment of personal income tax and insurance premiums.
We will tell you how to act the employer in order to keep the employee and not cause questions from the Ministry of Labor.
How to continue to cooperate
There are several ways to maintain an employment relationship with an employee who has gone abroad:
• to give leave if it is a temporary departure;
• arrange a foreign business trip;
• Transfer the employee to a remote location.
Vacation: Pros and Cons
The duration of leave without pay is not limited by anything and is determined by an agreement between the employee and the employer (Article 128 of the Labor Code).
The same applies to annual paid leave: its maximum duration, taking into account additional days from the employer, is also not limited (Article 120 of the Labor Code).
The only nuance is that such a vacation can not be given “in advance ”.
Therefore, during the stay of an employee abroad, you can arrange a vacation for him, and pay for the work actually performed by bonuses or financial assistance.
But this contradicts one of the main principles of labor legislation: ensuring the right of every employee to timely and full payment of fair wages (Article 2 of the Labor Code).
If this is found during the inspection, the employer faces a fine for violation of labor legislation in the amount of up to 50,000 rubles (Article 5.27 of the Administrative Code).
Foreign business trip: pros and cons
The employer can arrange a long-term foreign business trip for the employee until he decides to return to a permanent place of work.
But he has to be prepared for big expenses.
According to the Regulation on the peculiarities of sending employees on official business trips of 13.10.2008 No. 749 (items 12, 23), an employee on a foreign business trip shall be reimbursed:
• travel and accommodation expenses;
• the cost of issuing a passport, visa and other travel documents;
• Consular and airfield fees;
• fees for the right of entry and transit of road transport;
• medical insurance for visa;
• Daily subsistence allowance;
• other mandatory payments and fees.
It should also be remembered that during a business trip, the employee retains his place of work and average earnings (Article 167 of the Labor Code).
Remoteness: pros and cons
In order for this option to be legal, the employee must maintain permanent registration in Russia, and the employment contract should not indicate that the work is performed from another country.
Why is it important?
The Ministry of Labor believes that it is impossible to hire a candidate living abroad (letter of the Ministry of Labor dated 09.09.2022 No 14-2 / OOG-5755).
The norms of the LC are valid only on the territory of Russia, unless otherwise stipulated in the law itself or an international agreement (Articles 10, 13 of the LC).
And non-compliance with jurisdiction is also a violation of labor legislation, for which the employer can receive a fine of up to 50,000 rubles (Article 5.27 of the Administrative Code).
At the same time, the Ministry of Finance does not consider the “remote control ” from another country a violation, paying attention only to the peculiarities of taxation (letter of the Ministry of Finance dated 18.07.2019 No. 03-04-06 / 53227).

How to Pay Salaries to Workers Living Abroad
The method of payment of wages must be spelled out in the employment contract or in the employee ’ s application:
• To the account of an employee in a Russian bank to which the card of the MIR or UnionPay system is attached, or the cobadging card of these two systems.
But it should be remembered that not all countries have these payment systems, so there is a possibility that an employee will not be able to pay in another country with such a card.
You can transfer the salary to an account to which the card is not tied, for example, to a deposit.
In this case, the withdrawal of money to foreign banks will be handled by the employee himself.
• To the account of another person (relative or friend) in a Russian bank.
The main thing is that the details of the recipient were indicated in the application from the employee.
• To the employee ’ s electronic wallet.
• To the account of an employee in a foreign bank.
Such a transfer is possible if your bank is not subject to sanctions.
Find out the size of the commission in advance.
Be prepared that the bank may request supporting documents.
For example, the employment contract.
• Through the money transfer system.
The disadvantages of such services are that there are restrictions on the amount of translation and geography of countries, as well as large commissions are charged.
How to pay personal income tax from payments to an employee who is abroad
When calculating personal income tax, you need to take into account two points: the place of work specified in the contract, and the status of a tax resident of the Russian Federation.
A tax resident is a person who has spent more than 183 days in the territory of the Russian Federation for 12 months in a row (paragraph 2 of Article 207 of the Tax Code), while his citizenship does not matter.
Tax residents of the Russian Federation pay personal income tax on all their income, and non-residents - only on income received in the territory of the Russian Federation (Article 209 of the Tax Code).
A tax resident of the Russian Federation must independently calculate and pay tax received outside the Russian Federation (subpara. 3 para.
1 of Art. 228 of the Tax Code).

You can find out the tax status of an employee by requesting one of the following documents from the employee:
• A document from the Federal Tax Service confirming the status of a tax resident of the Russian Federation.
• Migration documents.
Suitable copies of the passport with marks on crossing the border, documents on registration at the place of residence, data of migration cards, documents on accommodation in a hotel.
A document confirming the status of a tax resident of a foreign state does not give grounds to consider an employee a non-resident in the Russian Federation, since the grounds for residence and non-residence in different countries are different and may not coincide.
If the employee does not provide documents that confirm the tax status, the Ministry of Finance allows you to retain personal income tax to the maximum, as with a non-resident - at an increased rate of 30% from the beginning of the year.
In this case, the employer does not exactly underestimate the agency ’ s personal income tax in the budget.
How to calculate personal income tax if the employee has changed his tax status
How to pay insurance premiums
Insurance premiums from payments to Russian citizens are accrued regardless of where they live.
Therefore, if the employee left, but remained a citizen of Russia, nothing changes for him in terms of contributions.
If he became a citizen of another state, the employer pays only mandatory contributions for accident insurance under the employment contract.
It is most convenient to submit reports on taxes and contributions for employees in electronic form.

Checklist: what to do if the employee went abroad
1.
Reissue the contract.
In this case, the employer has two options: to leave the current employment contract, adding to it the provisions on remote work, or to issue a new contract of the state farm.
2.
Determine the procedure for payment of NDFL.
The procedure depends on what place of work is specified in the contract, as well as on the tax status of the employee.
Therefore, it is necessary to request documents from him that determine for how long the employee is already abroad, and to understand whether he is a tax resident or not.
3.
Determine the procedure for calculating insurance premiums.
The procedure depends on the nationality of the employee.
If the employee has retained the citizenship of the Russian Federation or has issued dual citizenship, it is necessary to charge all contributions provided for by Russian legislation, depending on the type of contract: labor or state farm.
If the employee after moving has become a citizen of a foreign state, from the date of change of citizenship, only “unfortunate ” insurance premiums should be accrued for payments in his favor: under the labor contract in any case, and under the state farm - if this is provided for by the contract.

How to find your first job abroad?
Step-by-step plan with expert advice
Finding a job or your first internship abroad is, of course, not rocket science, but it can be a real test.
A clear plan and a well-written summary greatly facilitate this task.
BaigeNews.kz correspondent interviewed Lena Lvova, EP Advisory ’ s career specialist in Eastern Europe and the Baltics, and Yerkezhan Zholdasova, founder of Hired Valley ’ s internship search platform.
Let ’ s break down the job search step by step.
Step 1.
Choose country and type of company
Learn about culture and mentality
There are no bad or good cultures – there is something that will be closer to you.
Study the local mentality in advance to make an informed choice.
After moving "anywhere", the initial euphoria will quickly subside, and without a sincere interest in culture it will be difficult to adapt to life.
For example, in France it is customary to stay in the office a little longer than a working day and communicate a lot with colleagues.
In Denmark, on the contrary, it is completely normal to leave earlier than expected, but it is important not to stand out from society and not so much show your individuality.
In the Netherlands, colleagues or superiors can very straightforwardly surprise you that some task is not done well enough, but immediately offer their help.
And from the British, on the contrary, it is difficult to wait for an open feedback.
Beneath a benevolent response with a brief remark at the end, there may be discontent with the entire project.
“If you ’ re terrified of a mental leap, Eastern Europe is a great place.
Here and a little like us, and a little like in Europe, ” says Lena Lvova, career consultant EP Advisory.
Learn about language requirements
You can find a job in most European countries with knowledge of English, not speaking the local language.
English is the main language of communication in many corporations and fast-growing start-ups that unite employees from various countries.
Most often, for "office" work, you need a confident B2-C1 (Upper-Intermediate or Advanced).
The local language will be useful if your profession is directly related to it.
For example, Communications Manager in Germany or HR specialist in the Netherlands.
Analyze the labor market
Which industries are growing rapidly?
What specialists are needed?
For example, in Germany, IT specialists, engineers, scientists, medical workers, architects are in high demand.
Such specialists will be easier to obtain a visa.
In Denmark, as many as two lists of scarce professions, one with higher education and the other without.
In the second there are even cooks and hairdressers!
Look at LinkedIn – there periodically publish statistics on industries.
“Even just a careful reading of LinkedIn jobs will be helpful.
You will be able to determine what skills are required in the labor market, but so far you have not been pumped enough.
And to undergo additional training or gain project experience to become an even stronger candidate, ” says Lena Lvova, career consultant for EP Advisory.
Choose the type of company
Startup or corporation – where to go?
Both are invaluable experiences.
Startups are about a chamber team, freedom in decision-making and a wide range of responsibilities.
To get into a small developing company, it is better to go directly to hiring managers – for example, through LinkedIn.
The selection takes place relatively quickly: one or two interviews – and you will get the answer.
“In startups, be prepared for the fact that, perhaps, you will be doing absolutely everything, and the range of responsibilities can constantly expand.
In a startup there is no problem of one person, it is always a problem of the whole team!
As a big family, you can't leave anyone in trouble.
Still there are definitely more opportunities to be noticed and experiment, and growth is much faster.
You have a chance to be heard and influence business development, ” Yerkezhan Zholdasova, founder of Hired Valley internship search platform.
In a large company, all tasks are clearly distributed, and in order to make a decision, you often need to go through coordination circles with a large team.
Selection in large companies is more multistage.
It may include a telephone interview, tests, case studies, several in-person interviews.
It is better to submit through a recommendation from the current employee of the company (referrals) - so there are much more chances that your resume will be considered than if you submit through the company's website.
Step 2.
Studying visa issues
Types of visas
For moving to work, in addition to a simple work visa, there are other ways.
For example, in Germany there are such types of visas:
• Blue card.
It is issued to qualified specialists with higher education for four years.
The minimum salary is 56,400 €per year (representatives of popular professions – 43,992 €per year).
There is a blue card in other European countries, but the minimum wage requirements may vary slightly.
• Visa for IT-specialists without specialized higher education.
You need to earn from 50,760 €per year and have a confirmed experience of three years.
• Visa for self-employment.
This is a work visa for those who cannot apply for a Blue Card.
You will need a diploma of higher or secondary vocational education and an employment contract with a German employer.
• ICT card.
For those who move on a relocation program.
You can get a maximum of three years.
You need an employment contract for the entire period of the transfer, issued directly in Germany.
• Visa to confirm qualifications.
We need doctors, teachers, lawyers.
The applicant must come to Germany and undergo the procedure in person.
• Visa for job search is already in place.
You need a diploma, knowledge of the B1 language, money for a month of housing (from 947 €), confirmation of booking accommodation and a motivation letter.
• Scientific visa.
For scientists, researchers, researchers.
• Visa for entrepreneurs.
The package of documents is standard, but in addition, you need to provide a business plan in German.
• Visa for artists and artists.
• Visa for nannies and housekeepers.
There are similar visa opportunities in the Netherlands.
In addition, until 2025, there is a new program to attract employees to start-ups (Essential start-up personal visa).
In England, in addition to the most famous visa Skilled Migrant (formerly Tier 2), you can get a High Potential Individual Visa if you graduated from a high school anywhere in the world, or a Global Talent visa if you are engaged in innovation in the field of technology, art or science.
Digital Nomad visa is gaining great popularity in the world - it gives the right to live in the country for a year, but at the same time work remotely for the company anywhere in the world.
Step 3.
Preparing for selection: resume, LinkedIn and interviews
Make a resume in English
So, we begin to write a competent resume in English.
Resume structure:
• Name
• Profile – description of your experience in 3 – 5 sentences.
• Key competences – key personal qualities or technical skills.
Optional, but it is better to fill.
• Experience – work experience from the most recent to earlier.
• Education.
Usually stands after Experience, the exception is if you have just graduated from the university and can list cool projects.
• Certificates – additional training, retraining.
• Skills & other – here you can make the section Volunteering, if you have relevant experience in volunteer positions.
Resumes should be minimalist.
Without a photo (with the exception of Switzerland and a couple of European countries, where they still prefer to see a photo), date of birth, marital status, bright colors and stars or other symbols.
The task of the resume is to clearly reflect your experience in the resume so that the recruiter does not waste time searching for the necessary information on the file.
Use key phrases from vacancies – this is what the recruiter looks at in the first place.
Emphasize them in the description and try to show as much as possible in your resume that you have such skills.
Example of keywords in the vacancy of a novice project manager in Manchester:
In this description, attention to detail, organization and communication are mentioned twice, and building relationships with customers – more than five times.
Conclusion: the very first paragraph of your resume (Profile) should contain a mention that you have already worked with clients somewhere and / or possess these qualities.
Example Profile 1:
A diligent and resourceful BSc Business Management graduate with over 2 years of experience of addressing students ’ queries and relationship building at Student Union.
High attention to detail proved by a distinction-level final year paper and 3 articles published in media platforms.
Example Profile 2:
A meticulous project management specialist with excellent communication skills.
Successfully resolved 300 + customer issues as an intern at Company A. Overseas delivery timescales and project costs while volunteering at the Student Union.
The last place of work or volunteer position should also name relevant achievements, that is, some results of your work.
In this example, it can be: the number of satisfied customers, how many projects you were running at the same time, how you helped save a budget or how you fully planned the project from communication with the customer to the budget.
How well you adjust the resume for the vacancy depends on the effectiveness and timing of your job search.
Fill out your LinkedIn profile
LinkedIn is one of the most popular social networks for business communication.
It is useful in all European countries, in Germany you can also use Xing.
On LinkedIn, you can follow people and companies you are interested in, communicate, share experiences, and apply for jobs.
Make sure that your profile is correctly packaged – the recruiter can look into your social networks.
Here are some tips on how to fill out a LinkedIn profile:
• Place your photo (in the resume is not worth it).
It should be business-style – no need to hire a professional photographer, but do not cut yourself out of photos of friends or on vacation.
• The name must be identical to your name on the resume.
In the URL (profile link), if possible, it is also better to use the name and surname and not overload the link with numbers and letters.
• Be sure to fill in Headline – this is the very first line under the photo that appears in the search results.
Name your field of activity, key competencies, brands and certificates.
Examples of LinkedIn filling with career EP Advisory consultants in Switzerland and France
• For the About section, you can use the text from your Profile in the resume and add important skills.
There you can also add contact details in the spirit: Feel free to message me + mail name.
“On LinkedIn, don ’ t neglect keywords either – it ’ s like what you emphasized for your resume.
It is by keywords that recruiters are looking for candidates.
This can be a position: Analyst, HR specialist, Executive Assistant.
Skills: performance management, financial analysis, reporting.
Certificates or high level of education: PhD, MSc, ACCA for financiers, ICF for coaching.
Knowledge of programs: Google Analytics for marketers, Salesforce for sales specialists.
Additional languages: Be sure to specify if you have strong German, Czech or other languages.
Big brands and companies – for example, if you have internships or solved cases in the Big Four, you can tell about it in Headline or About, ” says Lena Lvova, career consultant for EP Advisory.
• Check that all information is in English: cities, universities, languages studied, etc.
• LinkedIn has a great opportunity to leave and receive recommendations.
If you have them, do not neglect this section.
Make sure that your profile is filled to the maximum – so there is a better chance that it will rank more in the search.
Develop networking
Write on LinkedIn interesting people in your specialty, ask questions and find new communities.
If you are already studying abroad, stock up on a short elevator pitch and go to specialized events.
Networking in Europe is one of the coolest and most effective channels for job search.
By the way, if there is someone from friends who can write a recommendation to the company, do not hesitate to ask for it.
There's nothing shameful about that.
And if you take, the employee will also receive a material bonus.
Start responding to vacancies
We recommend to write cover letters (cover letters) - they are really often read.
Do not repeat word for word what you wrote on your resume.
Try to give examples of the skills that are most useful to the company.
Cover letter structure: an introduction that immediately shows you as a great candidate for the role, then two or three important skills with examples and a call to action (write to you, call or invite for an interview).
It is also important to show your interest in the company in at least a few offers.
Example of Cover Letter Structure
Try to send applications every day, communicate with people from your field on LinkedIn.
If you ’ ve sent hundreds of responses but haven ’ t gotten through to the next stage, start working on the bugs.
Most importantly, be patient.
From idea to implementation can take several months – and this is a normal period.
“I knew English and German, so I applied for jobs in Switzerland, the Netherlands, Austria.
I had to send 220 resumes to get me anywhere.
Out of 220 responses, two job offers!
When searching, I mainly used LinkedIn, Xing and Indeed ” – Anya Kazarina, the heroine of the project “Moving Stories ”
Prepare for an interview
The next stage is the interview.
Before the interview, make a list of the most common questions and prepare answers to them.
It should not take more than a minute.
Learn a common pool of English vocabulary that pertains to your vacancy.
In stress, you can forget anything.
If you are applying to a corporation, be prepared for several interviews.
For example, in the competency-based interview, you are expected to give specific examples of what task you solved, what was the difficulty and how you achieved the result.
Prepare 10-12 examples of working situations in advance so that you do not get confused in the moment and immediately clearly answer the question.
It will also be useful to conduct additional research about the company and think through 2-3 interesting questions to the recruiter to show your enthusiasm.
Recruiters and managers are also people, and they can simply remember the candidate who named a special reason for the application to this company or a unique fact from the history of business.

INTERFAX.RU - Last week, on November 23, a meeting of the founders and a meeting of the Supervisory Board of ANO "Digital Economy" with the participation of the head of the Ministry of Digital Economy Maksut Shadaev and Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Chernyshenko, where the organization outlined new goals and objectives.
