In recent months, the organization has replaced the general director - he became the head of the Russian Association of Electronic Communications (RAEC) Sergei Plugotarenko.
In an interview with Interfax, Plugotarenko spoke about the “platform ” approach of ANO, interaction with the industry and the increasing status of artificial intelligence.
- Following the meeting of the founders of the Supervisory Board, you wrote about the new goals and objectives of the organization, in particular, it mentioned the creation of a single platform for digital transformation of key sectors of the economy.
What does that mean?
- We see our task as a single platform and ecosystem not only for the digital transformation of key sectors of the economy, but also for the interaction of industries with each other.
Now on the agenda came completely digital businesses and elements of the economy: industry, energy, social sphere, public administration.
All this is connected with industrial competence centers (ICCs), which should become anchors of import substitution.
We presented the idea of becoming a platform for communication at the council and received confirmation.
In December, we still have many meetings with the founders and stakeholders to complement this agenda.
Now we have formulated a principle that we want to put into the basis of interaction with the industry.
This is such a motherboard on which chips stand - this is our economy, its filling with competencies, departments, employees with areas of work.
And around as a link, such aggregates as industry associations, alliances, unions can be connected.
Through them, the state, founders, business representatives, SMEs are connected.
Already in 2023, such an ecosystem should turn out.
- Will RAEC be more closely integrated into this work?
As long as we put RAEC in the same conditions as everyone else.
Despite the fact that I know RAEC from the inside very well, and our employees have already become friends, I want to make RAEC, along with the rest, compete for the right to become part of our platform.
I would like to talk about the ICC, since you mentioned them.
Now this is the main activity of the state on import substitution of software products.
How will AI work in this direction?
We have good experience with oil and gas.
We start working with medicine.
If we have experience working with CCIs, we will understand how these industries breathe, how they develop, what regulatory barriers they have, including, not only software, not only technological ones.
- You mentioned that a number of "breakthrough projects" will be launched next year.
What are these projects?
- Almost all the seven new directions that we approved at the Supervisory Board, in my opinion, are a breakthrough.
One of these areas is the launch of a full-fledged analytical direction within the Digital Economy ANO.
Part of the founders, stakeholders and the state say: "Become a Russian" Gartner ".
We understand that this is a difficult task, we joke that we would be one-third Gartner.
On the other hand, we understand that the ability to aggregate numbers within oneself, draw conclusions, forecasts and further advise on the basis of numbers is the most important feature that can advance us.
The second direction is a kind of superevent, which we want to make in 2023 and which will bring together experts and leaders of various industries.
Then the international.
I hope that we will be able to study the features of working with new markets and recommend the industry to look at these markets.
We are already starting such work in parts of the Asian countries.
Another such breakthrough area is the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) solutions.
It is unlikely that Russia can become the number one country in the development of solutions in the field of artificial intelligence.
Unfortunately, the sanctions pressure leads to the fact that such plans could have been discussed two years ago.
That's a little hard right now.
But it is obvious that Russia should become a leader in the implementation of AI solutions created both in our country and abroad.
- What is happening now with the EPR (experimental legal regimes)?
This was one of the key projects of ANO "Digital Economy" and with its help the regulatory framework in this area was adopted.
But EPR "Yandex" on drones in Moscow and did not work.
Only four EPRs have been launched so far.
Ten are in development at different stages of readiness.
All of them are planned for launch in 2023.
These are completely different areas: from the usual transport and medicine to data processing, simplifying the lease of municipal property and so on.
As for the EPR already launched, the Yandex project on drones is now at the first stage of testing.
At the moment, EPR is actively used as part of the open unmanned taxi service in Innopolis, and in the future we plan to expand the operation areas.
In addition, Yandex is preparing to launch an unmanned taxi in Moscow.
At the moment, it is being tested in the Yasenevo area by employees of the company to work out the service part.
- And the restructuring of Yandex will not affect the testing of drones and the implementation of EPR?
The direction on drones will be given to international business.
“Yandex has already stated that it will continue to develop unmanned vehicles in the Russian market, so there should be no impact of the company ’ s restructuring on the project.
- What could be the support of IT specialists, both those who remained and those who left Russia?
- We believe that it is necessary to create an absolutely adequate business climate, primarily for small and medium-sized businesses in the digital environment, because small and medium-sized businesses do wonders here.
An even bigger story with startup support.
One study done by RAEC a few years ago showed that there are not many technology startups in Russia that are making significant investments - only about 700, with 84% of them concentrated in Moscow and St. Petersburg.
This suggests that our technological entrepreneurship is in its infancy.
If we talk about support measures, then the most unexpected things aimed at the people themselves can work here.
First of all, it is the support of families of IT specialists.
And everything that has been done, it is necessary not to throw, but to revise - the same preferential mortgage to expand on a larger number of employees.
Another of the measures: maintaining contact with all IT specialists - both those who left and those who remained.
We at ANO CE want to make a project in 2023, which we conditionally call the "IT community", to work with 3 million specialists from this field and offer them to feel protected in a certain community, to feel support from business and the state that are interested in them.
But in any case, even if someone has left, do not draw the border between us and them and treat them as Russian citizens.
Not for nothing the other day, the Ministry of Finance explained that it plans to keep the rate for personal income tax at 13% for those who continue to work for Russian companies from abroad, instead of 30% for non-residents.
These positive signals are constantly being sent.
In addition, the industry needs not only "digital goodies", but also offline things.
For example, the same open coworking spaces, preferences for the study of new products, their boarding house on the Black Sea coast for IT specialists and their children - why not?
If we recall the experience of the Soviet Union, when breakthrough areas of the economy were opened and stimulated, when certain preferences were created for specific specialists.
This gave a result at once: people understood that the country was interested in them, they were comfortable here, they launched satellites very quickly, created nuclear energy.
- And three million is just developers?
- No, there are far fewer developers - according to the Russoft Association, there are several hundred thousand of them.
Three million is the total number of people who have a digital profession: developers, designers, content creators, product managers, etc.
This is very little, it is a gold reserve, and everyone is important for the Russian economy.
- Do you think the national program "Digital Economy" requires changes?
If so, what adjustments are needed?
- In general, the goals laid down in the national programs a few years ago are still relevant.
The goals remain, just become more dramatic.
For example, to continue work on eliminating the digital divide between regions, to continue the policy of import substitution, to increase digital personnel.
But it is clear that now we live in a different reality, everything has turned upside down.
In December, at the Russian Internet Week, we will show for the first time negative forecasts for the fall of a number of markets on the Internet.
We have been watching the Internet for 11 years and all the time postulated growth and always said that the crisis for the Runet is if somewhere the growth slowed down.
And now we say that a number of markets, such as advertising and content, can fall by 50-70%.
Let's see if that happens.
But the economy can have an impact on the implementation of directions in the national program.
The government understands this.
Dmitry Chernyshenko has already said that somewhere it will be necessary to adjust the terms, to make them tougher, for example, on import substitution of software, and this is already happening.
But it is necessary not only to adjust, but also to create new milestones.
For example, in AI.
We always say that if Russia does not become number one on the invention of AI, then let ’ s strive to become a leader in the implementation and impact of AI on the economy.
I believe that the status of AI should be increased in the national program, as it is a direct lifesaver for many sectors of the economy.
There is room for achievement and potential.
On the subject of AI, by the way.
Putin recently instructed to remove barriers to its implementation.
What obstacles do you see here?
The main obstacle is the lack of staff.
Yes, we have a lot of smart heads, but in addition to brilliant developers, we need "locksmiths" and "turners" for digital technologies that will be engaged in more routine tasks than writing code - this is support, implementation, revision, additional packaging, consulting.
If in all digital professions we have three million specialists, then in the field of AI - only tens of thousands across the country.
Chernyshenko said that the staffing deficit for AI specialists is estimated at 5 thousand: with the increase in the introduction of technology, it will only increase.
Another problem is the lack of trust.
A lot of horror stories about AI that robots will enslave us, AI will make a decision for us: put you on a plane or not, give you a loan, and also take your workplace.
These are all horror stories that need to be answered that everything is wrong, that AI leads to the release of a person from the routine, AI helps make decisions, and not replaces a person.
But there are many gaps left, if businesses articulate the benefits of using AI, they will quickly sweep away distrust.
Another barrier is money.
The cost of an AI solution is significantly higher than the cost of an employee ’ s working hour.
In a sense, this is an investment in some future, and not every company can afford it.
With the fall in income levels and the economic situation in Russia and the world, not every company will have this priority.
The state should help here.
In addition, the development of AI requires access to large amounts of data.
At the moment, in the Russian Federation, access of developers and users of technology to data is often difficult, because there are serious regulations, prohibitions.
And the EPR is here to help us, but there's still a barrier.

Guide to Cyprus from a former Wargaming employee: legalization, taxes, expenses Editorial articles
Useful information and tips for the publication dev.by prepared by Alexey Gerasimovich.
Alexey Gerasimovich moved with his family to Cyprus in 2014 as Deputy Head of Global Development at Wargaming.
He now lives in the center of the island and works as Chief Production Officer for Eschatology Entertainment.
For 8 + years in Cyprus, Alexey has accumulated a decent expertise on the island and shares it in the blog "Notes of the Hamster Gluck" (in fact, there are mainly about books and music, but about life in Cyprus, too, a lot of useful).
Alexey also wrote a guide to relocating to Cyprus.
The publication dev.by published a slightly shortened version with the permission of the author.
How to come to Cyprus for citizens of Belarus
Now you can enter Cyprus by any flight if you have:
• Double or multiple entry Schengen visa (single entry is not suitable)
• Double or multiple entry visa for Croatia, Romania or Bulgaria
• Residence permit / permanent residence of the EU
• Receipt of Cyprus with a stamp (a document from the migration department stating that you have applied for a residence permit or other legal status: the fact of filing is already sufficient grounds for staying on the island)
• National visa of Cyprus.
More information about all types of entry can be found on the website of the Embassy of Cyprus in Minsk.
Since Cyprus is an island, the easiest way to get to it is by plane (another option is by water: this year the ferry service with Greece resumed).
The main hubs from which usually fly to Cyprus are London, Athens, Dubai, Cairo, Tel Aviv, Yerevan, Beirut, Frankfurt, Paris, etc.
Restrictions in connection with COVID-19
Since June 1, 2022, Cyprus has lifted all entry restrictions in connection with Covid-19.
As well as the mask mode.
On the island itself, masks and a certificate of vaccination (or test) may be required in certain institutions (for example, hospitals).
Details about the old rules and their cancellation - on the official website.
Legal ways to live in Cyprus
In this section, I do not undertake to describe all the possibilities, but only those that are available to almost any specialist.
Individual cases with investments, purchase of real estate and opening of a company, I do not consider yet, since it requires investments that are far from every person who wants to come to Cyprus now.
Tourist
You can come to the island as a tourist, the rules of entry are described above, the time of stay also depends on the country:
• Citizens of Belarus – depends on the issued visa.
• Citizens of Ukraine – up to 90 days.
However, after this period, you must leave the island.
Also, you are not allowed to work on the island as a tourist.
Work visa
A work visa is the right to live in Cyprus while working as an employee of a particular Cypriot company.
That is, you can not just come and apply for such a visa yourself, it is done by the hiring company only after obtaining a visa permit from the Migration Office, and the request goes to a specific person in a particular company.
When obtaining a work visa, family members get the opportunity to obtain visitor visas - this is a type of non-work visas.
Family members include the spouse and minor children.
Since 2022, the spouses have also been able to work, obtaining a Spouse Employee visa.
If you stop working in this company (at your own request or on the initiative of the company), then you have only one month, during which you must either leave Cyprus, find another job on the island, or make yourself and your family a visitor visa.
To obtain a visa, the requirements are imposed on the company rather than on the applicant, but they are also useful to know:
• The company must have a work permit for third-country nationals.
• The salary of the employee must be at least 2500 euros before tax.
• A certificate of no criminal record is required.
Spouses of the holder of a work visa can work in Cyprus.
• For family members, it will be necessary to issue a letter of guarantee in the bank (insurance premium of 550 euros per person + the cost of the letter of guarantee).
Visitor visa
This type of visa allows you to live in Cyprus, but you do not have the right to work on the island.
The latter is important, since it is quite possible to work for a company outside Cyprus.
Or receive income from some of their business abroad.
The visa is issued to the applicant and his family members (spouse and minor children).
It is issued for a year and requires annual renewal.
To obtain a visa, you must:
• Own housing or lease agreement for at least 1 year.
• Submit documents to the Migration Office.
• Open a bank account and put a security deposit of 550 euros for each family member.
• Apply for annual health insurance.
• Transfer to a Cypriot bank account the amount of 10 thousand euros per applicant and 4.5 thousand euros for each family member (dependent).
In the future, this money can be used for life in Cyprus.
• Certificate of no criminal record.
Important: spouses of the visitor visa holder are not allowed to work in Cyprus.
Consideration of the application for a visitor visa takes from 6 to 12 months, but immediately after submitting the documents, you already have the legal right to live on the island and even leave it and return on the basis of the received coupon from the migration service (about obtaining documents for a visitor visa).
However, it is impossible to leave the island for a period exceeding three months.
Even if you have not yet been issued a permit, and it has already been 11 months, you need to apply again - the next year.
IT Nomad visa (digital nomad visa)
This type of visa in Cyprus appeared in the spring of 2022.
They can be obtained by IT specialists who wish to work remotely, living in Cyprus.
But the number of such visas is limited: from March 3, 2022, a limit of 500 per year is set.
To obtain such a visa, you must:
• Work for the company / client outside of Cyprus, performing their duties through telecommunication technologies (read - remotely on the Internet).
• Confirm that you will have a stable and sufficient monthly income of at least 3500 euros net (that is, after paying all taxes).
• Certificate of no criminal record.
• For family members, it will be necessary to issue a letter of guarantee in the bank (insurance premium of 550 euros per person + the cost of the letter of guarantee).
What is this visa:
• 1 year of official stay in Cyprus with the possibility of extension for the next 2 years.
• The right of residence for the spouse and minor children.
• Spouses cannot work in Cyprus.
• If you reside in Cyprus for more than 183 days per year, you become a Cyprus tax resident in that year and are required to pay local income tax (see section below), unless you confirm your status as a tax resident in another country.
The time for obtaining such a visa is now estimated at 5-7 weeks.
In this case, you can officially stay in Cyprus from the moment of applying for such a visa.
Salaries and expenses in Cyprus
There is not a single source that would give reliable salaries for all possible professions.
For the IT industry, more or less relevant data is here.
But you need to understand that this is also a “hospital average ”, and each company can have its own rates.
Some giants pay much more than the average.
Also often, the level of salary may depend on where the main office of the company is located on the island - for example, the cost of living in Limassol is higher than in Paphos or Larnaca.
In terms of cost of living and spending, there is also no single universal answer.
The most expensive city to live in is Limassol, where most Russian-speaking IT companies are concentrated.
Nicosia is cheaper, Larnaca and Paphos are even cheaper.
Plus, a young couple can spend less on life than a couple with two children (schools, circles, etc.).
A very average estimate can be obtained on this resource.
The information there is approximate, but by comparing it with estimates and real spending in your current city, you can calculate the coefficient and based on it estimate future costs.
There is also such a site - the largest "flea market" in Cyprus, where in fact you can find housing for rent and buy a car.
For a starting understanding of the price level is quite a good resource.
Taxation in Cyprus
If a person lives on the island for at least 183 days a year, he automatically becomes a tax resident of Cyprus, that is, he is obliged to pay income tax on his profits.
A detailed and up-to-date instruction on taxation in Cyprus is available on the PwC website, here it is in Russian.
But the most important thing is the tax on individuals.
He is progressive in Cyprus:
In addition, there are deductions from taxable income, of which the most significant are:
• If you are employed in a Cyprus company (work visa) not earlier than 2012 and this is your first job in Cyprus, then you receive a 20% deduction (but not more than 8550 euros) for the first 5 years, starting from the next year from which the work began.
Valid until 2030.
• If you are employed in a Cyprus company (work visa) not earlier than 2012 and this is your first place of work in Cyprus, with your annual income of at least 55 thousand euros, then you receive a 50% deduction for the first 17 years, starting from the next year from which the work began.
• You can also deduct contributions for life insurance, pension funds (figures on the link).
I also wrote about the benefits in more detail on my blog.
There are some good online tax calculators:
• Income Tax Calculator – calculation of income tax.
But it does not take into account the above deductions of 20% and 50%.
• Payroll Cost Calculator is more for companies to understand how much the company will cost an employee with a certain gross salary
• Dividend Tax Calculator - if you open your company and want to pay dividends to yourself, here you can calculate how much you will get on hand, and how much more you will pay taxes
Features of registration in connection with the “special operation ” in Ukraine
• By order of the ECB from March 9, 2022, citizens of Belarus can not have more than 100 thousand euros in their accounts in total.
Anything above this amount will either be frozen by the bank or rejected when trying to replenish the account.
• For Russians, such a restriction was introduced earlier – February 28, 2022.
• Officially, there is no ban on opening accounts for citizens of Belarus and Russia, but any bank can be safe.
However, if you have an official residence status in Cyprus, banks are unlikely to refuse to open an account.
Useful links
In compiling the document, I used materials prepared by the community Cyprus _ IT and personally its creator Oleg Reshetnikov, other chat rooms, as well as my own knowledge and personal recommendations from Cypriot lawyers.
I also recommend watching:
• This article by Oleg Reshetnikov.
Some data is outdated, not with all points I agree 100%, nevertheless it is quite good material;

We live in a quantum world.
Alexander Kholevo about his victory in the Scientific Prize "Sbera"
The winner of the Sbera Scientific Award in the Digital Universe nomination was Academician Alexander Kholevo, Chief Researcher of the Steklov Mathematical Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences, “for his fundamental contribution to quantum informatics and works that open the way to fundamentally new communication and computing systems. ”
What is this work and what is it important, we asked the academician himself.
— Alexander Semenovich, how was the quantum theory of information born and what preceded it?
The key and one of the most important words in information theory is noise.
This theory itself is the fight against noise in communication channels.
In conventional, classical information theory, thermal noise is combated, in quantum there is a specific quantum noise, and it requires a separate mathematical description.
Now in the development of quantum technologies, the fight against noise and interference in quantum communication channels and in computing devices has become the most important issue.
In 1948, Claude Shannon published his seminal work on classical information theory, and very soon, in the 1950s, Nobel laureate Denis Gabor posed the question of what additional interference is caused by the quantum nature of the information carrier, the electromagnetic field.
Then began to appear works of a physical, engineering nature.
Some of them were published in our journal “Problems of Information Transfer ”.
At that moment I came to the subject.
Who are your teachers?
— For me, the two main scientific institutions are the Moscow Phyztech, where I received my scientific education, and the Steklov Mathematical Institute, where I have been working for more than half a century.
A well-known enthusiast of mathematical education, A. P. Savin, worked in Phystech, he drew me into mathematics, and with his submission I wrote my first scientific work under the leadership of Professor M. A. Naimark, who read a course of functional analysis at MIPT.
And Mian is a whole mathematical universe and a separate story.
I was lucky enough to get into the department of probability theory, where I worked in the field of mathematical statistics under the tutelage of direct students of A. N. Kolmogorov - Yu. A. Rozanov, Yu. V. Prokhorov, A. N. Shiryaev, and L. N. Bolshev.
There I defended my PhD and almost immediately went to the library (there was no Internet yet): what to do next?
And I came across a topic called quantum communications.
I saw that a huge field of activity opens here, which allows you to combine the methods of mathematical statistics and the acquired knowledge from functional analysis.
This combination turned out to be very fruitful, and I began to work in this area and get the first results.
- What is Cholevo's theorem?
Can it be explained to non-mathematicians?
— Let me clarify that of my results, this one is the most well-known to the general public.
To explain the essence of the theorem, or Cholevo boundary, one can imagine a secret quantum communication channel with two participants.
In the context of this model, the classical amount of information that an eavesdropper can receive, whatever measurements he makes over this communication channel, cannot exceed a specific amount, which is called Cholevo information.
Knowing the upper quantum limit of what the eavesdropper can extract makes it possible to speed up the transmission and processing of information over the quantum channel.
Initially, this theorem had no cryptographic sound — it ’ s just some mathematical inequality that turned out to be a hard nut.
It was discussed for a long time, but it was not possible to prove it.
I managed to do it.
I was happy, although I had no idea at the time what practical consequences it might have.
Another theorem that follows this one is the quantum analogue of Shannon's coding theorem for a channel with noise.
Shannon's theorem states that if there is a noisy channel, then there is a way to transmit information at a certain maximum speed almost without error.
In other words, there is bandwidth that gives this upper bound of the speed of error-free transmission of information over a noisy channel.
To do this, you need to code the input signal in a special way, then decode it - there are codes that correct errors.
Here I must say about another scientific institution that played a big role in my fate.
This is the Institute for Information Transfer Problems, where Professor R. L. Dobrushin, also a student of Kolmogorov, worked, and he constantly pushed me towards the quantum analogue of Shannon ’ s theorem.
This was proved, and a theorem was obtained that shows that inequality is achievable, there is a way to reach the quantum boundary, and thereby it gives the throughput of the quantum channel.
— We have already said about some of the applied capabilities of quantum information theory.
What else is promising in this area?
— My research has developed mainly in the direction of quantum communications, where perhaps the greatest technological advances have now been achieved.
Optical communication systems have appeared, physicists have learned to distribute secret quantum keys all over the world, and we have communication lines that use the principles of quantum cryptography.
Here, too, there are problems that are being studied, in particular, the problems of repeaters, the sources of single photons.
If we talk about quantum computing, we are now in the so-called era of noisy quantum devices of intermediate size (NISQ).
- The noise again?
- That's exactly right.
This means that those devices that can be implemented in practice are imperfect in terms of accuracy, highly susceptible to interference and errors.
However, if these devices are used in combination with classical computers and supercomputers, it is possible to achieve accelerations in computing in the field of solving problems of multidimensional optimization, quantum chemistry, modeling molecules.
This raises the question of “price – quality ”: how much more expensive is such a quantum device than a classical one that can do the same work, even if for a longer time?
While there is no technology for mass production of quantum chips, there is not even a physical platform on which this should happen.
If we compare the situation with 1948, then a miracle happened: simultaneously with the creation of the theory of information, a transistor was invented, which formed the technological basis for the stunning progress of information technologies of the twentieth century.
Here the situation is different: there is no publicly available cheap technology for the production of quantum elements.
This task is on the agenda today, as is the fight against noise.
When will a new miracle happen?
When will a quantum computer finally arrive?
— Now the emphasis is not on miracles in such matters as, for example, the emergence of a full-scale quantum computer, which has been talked about a lot, but on the study and overcoming of quantum noise.
The author of the famous algorithm Peter Shore, speaking three years ago at the BBVA award for his progress at the forefront of science, said that it would be five to ten years before a quantum computer could do anything close to useful.
However, over time, these devices will provide revolutionary applications — for example, in biomedicine.
At the moment, it takes a huge amount of computer time to mimic the behavior of molecules, but quantum computers can achieve this and help develop new drugs and new materials.
On my own behalf, I would add that the significance of the second quantum revolution now taking place is also, and this should not be underestimated, that a wide mass of researchers are involved – not only physicists, but also IT specialists who did not know quantum physics, but learned it.
Quantum literacy has increased immeasurably over the past couple of decades, and this is very important because the quantum world is radically different from the classical world that surrounds us.
This is a world with completely different laws, and research on a broad front, which is now unfolding, including in Russia, is also very important for creating a favorable environment for the emergence of breakthrough discoveries and new solutions.
“This year ’ s Nobel Prize in Physics, as you know, was awarded for entangled quantum states – this is what you ’ ve been doing all your scientific life.
What can you say about this?
The current Nobel Prize in Physics has been awarded to three researchers for testing the violation of Bell ’ s inequalities for so-called entangled states, but I prefer the term “entangled states. ”
It better reflects the substance of the case.
These are states with properties completely unusual for the classical world.
Coupling means such a strong correlation between particles that interacted, and then flew apart at a macroscopic distance (conditionally speaking, one to Moscow, the other to St. Petersburg) that even use the term “quantum pseudotelepathy ”.
This correlation is so strong that it cannot be modeled by any classical mechanism, and this state is a new information resource.
— What are the fundamental differences from the already known resources?
First, although it is so strong, it does not contradict the theory of relativity and the fact that it is impossible to transmit signals instantly, because it is limited by the speed of light.
But the information from one linked photon to another is transmitted instantly, that is, faster than the speed of light, and this is a paradox.
Ain't he?
- No, it's not transmitted instantly.
The trick is that it is not transmitted at all: coupled states do not allow this to be done.
Nevertheless, it is a kind of correlation that can be considered as a catalyst that enhances or improves the transfer of information.
If we have a receiver and a transmitter connected by an ideal communication channel, and the coupling is distributed between them, then the throughput of such a channel doubles.
This is called the “super-dense coding protocol. ”
This means that although cohesion itself does not allow information to be transmitted, when combined with a communication channel, it allows for an increase in the amount of information transmitted.
And there is also the quantum state teleportation protocol, which also allows for the use of coupling between input and output.
Quantum states cannot be transmitted over a conventional communication channel — say, over a radio channel, because quantum information is much richer, it contains statistics of a set of non-commuting observed, but nevertheless, if there is a catalyst in the form of a coupled state, then the transfer of the quantum state can occur through the classical channel.
You said teleportation.
And will it be possible to teleport material objects as in science fiction films?
— No, we are talking about the transfer of a special type of information, or quantum states, nothing is transferred materially.
We can't teleport Captain Kirk.
But these states exist, it must be taken into account and used.
— Does your scientific group have any original developments in this area?
— In our group, work was carried out in the direction of studying the throughput associated with cohesion.
If we take not an ideal channel, but a channel with strong noise, it turns out that the gain in using the coupling between the input and output is much more than twice.
Another direction is multiparticle cohesion, when there are not two participants, but several; a network arises.
Enthusiasts are talking about the quantum internet, though it may be too early.
But if this can be done, it will be possible to talk about networks with a sufficiently large number of participants, and they will be quantum-protected.
- For all these studies, you received the Scientific Award "Sbera".
How did you feel about it?
I was deeply touched.
This is an extremely high appreciation of my contribution to the creation of a new field, quantum computer science, and a confirmation that I once chose the right path.
In those years, it was completely unobvious.
I am still interested, and the prospects here are huge.
I have no doubt that the initiative of Sberbank, which established its own Scientific Award, will have far-reaching positive consequences for the development of science and technology.
Will she be able to become a Russian Nobel?
- Why not?
Such an award is a very attractive incentive for many young, and not only young scientists, and I hope that this initiative of Sberbank will become an example for other representatives of the business community in terms of supporting scientific research.
Interviewed by Natalia Leskova

What can harm misinterpreted principles of healthy eating
The fashion for proper nutrition has a flip side.
20% of those who experience digestive problems are fans of a healthy lifestyle, writes The Telegraph.
Often during the reception, the doctor finds out: patients are on a diet that they prescribed themselves.
Only their diets have little to do with the scientific principles of proper nutrition.
The most common mistakes: rejection of foods with gluten and lactose, increased fiber intake and veganism.
Why do these misconceptions arise and why are they dangerous?
How much fiber do bacteria need
Long gone are the days when fiber, or dietary fiber, was considered a ballast substance: digestive enzymes do not digest it, so it seems that it is not needed.
Then it turned out that bacteria living in the gastrointestinal tract are able to break it down, receiving energy for their own reproduction and for human life.
However, fiber and in addition to this many useful properties: it regulates peristalsis, reduces the level of cholesterol in the blood, helps to remove toxins and other harmful substances from the body.
Thanks to all these advantages, fiber received good PR, and adherents of a “healthy lifestyle ” began to absorb it in huge quantities.
In fact, attention to fiber is not meaningless.
A study by the British Association of Nutritionists found that 60% of Britons consume on average half of its daily value.
In Britain, the norm is 25-30 g per day.
In Russia, according to the head of the consultative and diagnostic center "Healthy and Sports Nutrition" of the Federal Research Center for Nutrition, Biotechnology and Food Safety (FGBUN "FRC Nutrition and Biotechnology"), Candidate of Medical Sciences Ekaterina Burlyaeva, the rate of fiber consumption is 20 g per day, or 10 g per thousand kilocalories, although some diseases of the gastrointestinal tract can be increased to 35 g.
“Those who want to lose weight, first of all refuse bread, cereals, potatoes, pasta, thereby removing fiber from their diet, ” she says. – Of course, this is obviously wrong, because fiber gives a feeling of saturation, helps to normalize the level of glucose and cholesterol in the blood. ”
If you switch exclusively to foods rich in fiber, eating only smoothies from spinach with cabbage and absorbing tons of prunes, you can achieve an upset stomach, doctors explain.
The most typical disease in these cases is irritable bowel syndrome, which is accompanied by pain and spasms in the abdomen, bloating, diarrhea or constipation.
"If you consume only foods rich in dietary fiber, reducing the number of animal proteins, you can bring yourself to anemia, - warns Ekaterina Burlyaeva. - Possible bloating, increased gas formation."
To avoid this, do not lash out at the fiber, and gradually bring its content in the diet to normal.
And, of course, do not forget that there are other important food components, such as proteins, fats and carbohydrates.
“The body needs fiber, ” explains the scientific director of the FGBUN“ FRC of Nutrition and Biotechnology ”, Academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Doctor of Medical Sciences Viktor Tutelyan. – It is a lot in vegetables and fruits.
Well, if they are presented in the diet, but it is necessary to get substances that are not in these products, that is, the necessary amount of proteins, fats, including omega-3, omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids.
And if you limit yourself, you will not get them. ”
"Like any other science, the science of nutrition is based on laws that can not be violated, - continues the academician. - One of them is the law of compliance of the chemical composition of the diet with our physiological needs in food, biologically active substances.
Of about 200 such substances, 50 are essential or essential.
The more diverse the diet, the greater the guarantee that we will get all these substances.
They are all in the diet - we are healthy, not in the diet - sick. "
The Difficult Childhood of Vegans
This is especially true for strict vegetarians - vegans who refuse any products of animal origin, including honey.
It is a fashion trend now.
“Today, we often see a bias towards plant foods, raw products, ” says Ekaterina Burlyaeva. – And such a diet is often adhered to not only by convinced vegans – this is rather a general trend.
For example, people do not cook porridge, but brew cereal with boiling water or soak in the evening, and eat in the morning.
They believe that since the product has not undergone heat treatment, it means that all vitamins and minerals are preserved in it, therefore, the body will receive more of them.
Actually, it's not.
For example, phytic acid, which is in all cereals, with this method of preparation is destroyed to a lesser extent and, accordingly, prevents the absorption of vitamins and minerals.
A person expects that he will receive more nutrients, but receives less.
Such distortions should not be: in the diet should also be products that have undergone heat treatment. "
Doctors are puzzled: how can you give up meat at the expense of your own health?
“I understand when people become vegetarians for ethical reasons, but to do it for the sake of hypothetical health benefits is at least strange, ” British nutritionist Elaine McGowan told The Telegraph.
It is especially dangerous when parents put children on a vegan diet, says Academician Tutelyan.
“Restrictions harm the physical and mental development of the child, ” he says. – The child needs to get all the vitamins and nutrients in the necessary amount – sometimes he needs even more than an adult.
If the mother by stupidity or ignorance limits it, health is lost for life.
Failure to provide optimal nutrition can even be fatal for a child.
This should not be allowed under any circumstances. ”
And it is difficult for adults to get all the nutrients and trace elements from plant foods.
For the sake of the daily norm of iron and calcium vegan will have to eat 3 bowls of cabbage, 18 tablespoons of lentils and 75 almonds, writes The Telegraph.
At the same time, the main source of protein for vegans legumes have a bad effect on the health of people with stomach diseases, because they have to be consumed in large quantities.
For the stomach, of course, the most useful animal proteins, especially those contained in cheese, doctors believe.
“The diet must be full, that is, animals, proteins: milk and dairy products, fish, meat, eggs, – emphasizes Academician Tutelyan. – We must consume 12 vitamins, 20 amino acids.
Vegetarians and vegans can get proteins from legumes, soy products - they are closest in amino acid composition to a full-fledged protein.
If you do not eat legumes, protein deficiency will develop, followed by a decrease in immunity, infectious diseases, etc.
Gastritis, gastric ulcer, that is, disorders of the digestive system, and then - the destruction of the body.
To get enough vegetable proteins, see your doctor and calculate how much soy and other legumes you need to consume. ”
Glued by a single gluten
In Russian, gluten is called gluten.
This is the protein of cereals: wheat, rye, barley.
Protein is like protein.
But not everyone gets it right.
According to various estimates, from 0.5% to 1% of the population suffers from celiac disease - gluten intolerance associated with a lack of enzymes that break it down in the body.
These people have to avoid gluten products all their lives.
But why the rest?
The prejudice against the unfortunate protein arose due to the work of the American doctor Alessio Fasano, who suggested the existence of a link between gluten and diseases such as schizophrenia and autism.
It was in the early 2000s, and already in the 2010s began an explosive fascination with gluten-free products.
According to research by Mintel Group, from 2013 to 2015, the production of gluten-free products in the United States grew by 136%, and sales in 2015 reached $11.6 billion, significantly exceeding real demand.
And if in 2013 sales of gluten-free products accounted for 2.8% of all food products, then in 2015 it was already 6.5%.
Interestingly, the number of Americans who consider gluten-free food a fashion tribute is also growing: from 31% in 2013 to 47% in 2015.
A study conducted by Nielsen in 60 countries found that 21% of participants consider gluten free to be a very important factor in their food choices.
Most people who do not approve of gluten live in Latin America (32%), the Middle East and Africa (28%).
In the United States, it is about 15-21%.
The University of Sheffield (UK) found that in 2012, 13% of Britons avoided gluten, and in 2015 – already 33%.
The UK market for gluten-free products is estimated at £835 million.
How is it that gluten-free products are needed by only 1% of people, and almost half of them consume them?
“This is an example of global marketing, — explains the medical director of the project“ Allergotop ”, allergist and psychotherapist, candidate of medical Sciences Elena Shuvatova. — Fashion for gluten-free products in the world is colossal.
They are associated with a good complexion, excellent digestion, preservation of youth, etc. For some reason, many believe that they are allergic to gluten and they need gluten-free products, although gluten allergies are isolated cases. ”
It is important that the production of gluten-free products is more expensive than usual.
How to make them profitable?
Organize mass production.
But how can it be organized for the 1% of the population?
Declare a gluten-free diet as part of a healthy lifestyle.
Which was done.
But the question is: how much more useful are gluten-free products?
Scientists at the University of Hertfordshire, for example, studied 1,724 items from 5 British retailers, found that gluten-free products, except for crackers, contain more fat, salt and sugar than those with gluten.
The fact is that people are still learning to extract gluten from wheat and other cereals, and gluten-free products are produced “on the basis of natural gluten-free raw materials, primarily of plant origin. ”
What kind of raw material is that?
Mainly corn and rice flour - simply because these components are the cheapest, because the production of gluten-free products, as we know, is technologically complex and very expensive, and such "cheap" ingredients allow somehow to keep prices at an acceptable level.
To make a gluten-free dough similar to the usual, a lot of sugar and starch are added to it, as well as thickeners, baking powder, etc.
“All the letters“ E ”, from which lovers of proper nutrition are trying to run, are presented here in much greater concentrations, ” emphasizes Elena Shuvatova.
It turns out that gluten-free products are simply dangerous for healthy people.
As scientists from Harvard University (USA) found out, it is because of the high content of sugar and fats that they increase the risk of developing type II diabetes by 13%.
But that's not all.
Scientists at the University of Illinois in Chicago (USA) found that in the body of people sitting on a gluten-free diet, the content of arsenic is twice as high as those who eat normally, mercury is more than 60%.
The intake of these substances with food may increase the risk of cancer and other chronic diseases, the researchers said.
They suggest that rice is the main substitute for wheat in gluten-free food: it is able to accumulate toxic substances coming from soil and water, including those contained in chemical fertilizers.
Another fashionable myth about healthy eating is the harm of lactose, milk sugar contained in dairy products.
Again, a misconception: a lactose-free diet is needed only for those who do not have lactase - an enzyme that processes lactose - and a disease associated with excess lactose intake can develop, explains Victor Tutelian.
"A special diet should be adhered to only by those who have a genetic deficiency of enzymes that metabolize gluten or destroy lactose, - the academician is sure. - Gluten is a very necessary full-fledged protein.
Why look for something if there is regular bread?
Of course, if a person receives other proteins, it does not affect health - just the diet should be varied. "
How dangerous is a healthy diet
Whether a person prescribes a strict diet or parents put on it, the consequences of food restrictions can be catastrophic, doctors warn.
One lady, about whom writes The Telegraph, in 20 years made a home test for food intolerance and stopped eating dairy products.
As a result, by the age of 38, she came up with osteoporosis.
“In Russia, such tests are a common story, ” says Elena Shuvatova. – All of them are very accessible, but people do not know how to handle them.
They are tested for food allergies, they detect an increased level of immunoglobulin E (IgE) for a certain product and, in the complete absence of symptoms, they go on a diet, although it is necessary only for clinical manifestations of allergy. ”
“The saddest thing is when the victims of the diet are children.
Sometimes, the overprotective mother makes "just in case analysis" to "check", there are some indicators, and the child from the diet is removed important products, although there is no reason for this.
Or mom and dad are allergic, and the child is preventive put on a diet, removing products that are not suitable for parents to reduce the likelihood of developing allergies.
Such a diet, especially if it is lifelong, does not correspond to the standard of good nutrition.
Diet should be implemented justifiably and not for life, but for certain therapeutic purposes. ”
All this has implications not only for physical but also for mental health.
“Children, from the diet of which certain products are unjustifiably excluded, grow up with the idea that they are sick, and all their lives live in fear, although this fear is not justified, ” says Elena Shuvatova. – A person should live with the idea that he is strong and healthy – this is a normal attitude.
And the one who considers himself sick, every day experiences stress, increased anxiety, horror before contact with the outside world.
The daily focus on danger significantly reduces the quality of life. ”
The need to adhere to a diet affects interpersonal relationships.
“Among my patients was a girl who did not allow herself to communicate with friends, although she really wanted it, because she was on a strict diet, – continues Ms. Shutova. – They were going to cafes and restaurants, and she was ashamed that she came with her container, because she was afraid to eat in public catering.
In fact, there was no reason for it - so my mother tried. "
“As a doctor, I am often approached by people who are sure that they have allergies.
I have met people with pustular rashes, fungal skin lesions, psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis who have been treated for years with antihistamine pills and a diet.
Someone removed from the diet red apples, chocolate, citrus fruits, someone ate only three or four products, and this lasted for years, affecting the condition of the body.
Suffered teeth, bones, hair, often there were acute respiratory infections and acute respiratory infections, asthenic conditions. "
Fashionable trends in nutrition, misinterpreted analyzes, anxious mothers who care so much about their children that they turn them into patients when there are no diseases - these are the reasons for harmful "useful" diets, Elena Shuvatova is sure.
"It is not always necessary to torment yourself with a diet, - the doctor concludes. - If you think that you are sick, consult a doctor, treat diseases, if any.
Often it allows you to return to a normal diet. ”

The Economist: A New Era in Geopolitics.
The American “world order ” is on the verge of collapse.
04: 06 12 / 31 / 2022
The Economist
United Kingdom
December 31, 2022
A New Era in Geopolitics
Russia ’ s special operation in Ukraine and China ’ s military buildup herald a new era of rivalry between major powers.
This transformation comes at a time when America ’ s weight and influence in the global economy is declining.
President Joe Biden calls this decade “crucial. ”
But this characterization only partially reflects the current moment, which is the beginning of a new era.
In this era, Russia and China will strive to destroy the world order formed by America.
“Great power rivalry ” is too soft a characterization against the background of Russia ’ s destruction of Ukraine.
And the “new cold war ” is too simplistic, given the complex economic interdependence of the West and China.
The Russian-Ukrainian armed conflict has destroyed the norms that emerged after World War II, according to which borders cannot be changed by force.
It has awakened the ghosts of nuclear confrontation for the first time since the end of the Cold War, but with one distinctive feature: Russian President Vladimir Putin threatens to use nuclear weapons not as a last resort, but as an initial gambit in his military campaign.
But Russia is only an “acute problem ”, as America sees it.
A more serious threat to the world order comes from China, the only country in the world that is capable of toppling America from the pedestal of the world ’ s dominant power.
The Pentagon calls this a “defining threat. ”
The Chinese military is growing rapidly.
China already has the world ’ s largest navy, the world ’ s third-largest air force, and a huge arsenal of missiles and weapons of war in space and cyberspace.
What if the “limitless ” friendship between Russia and China turns into a real alliance?
Now there is little evidence that China is helping Russia in the conduct of military operations.
But these Eurasian autocracies regularly conduct military exercises, and senior U.S. officials believe the two countries will inevitably converge.
By 2035, China will increase its nuclear arsenal to about 1,500 warheads, approaching the number of American and Russian arsenals.
In this situation, the United States will have to develop a new concept of trilateral nuclear deterrence.
This, in turn, could lead to a new arms race, especially if START III, which expires in early 2026, is not renewed.
This transformation comes at a time when America ’ s weight and influence in the global economy is declining.
In the past century, U.S. GDP has significantly exceeded the gross domestic product of U.S. rivals Germany and Japan in World War II and the Soviet Union and China during the Cold War.
But now China ’ s GDP is not far behind the US (and already exceeds it, if you count in terms of purchasing power parity).
U.S. military spending is colossal in absolute terms, but close to a historical minimum as a share of GDP.
The situation is beginning to change as Congress on December 23 approved a volume of military spending that is significantly larger than what Biden asked for.
Heartland v. Rimland
Old geopolitical theories are being revised.
In 1904, British geographer and strategist Halford Mackinder declared that whoever controls the core of Eurasia, that is, the geographical space from the Arctic Ocean to the Himalayas, would dominate the world.
Based on this analysis, the alliance between Russia and China poses a terrible threat.
The American contemporary of Mackinder, Alfred Thayer Mahan, on the contrary, believed that the key to world domination was control of the sea trade routes.
Somewhere in between was another American, Nicholas Spickman, who declared in 1942 that the most important thing was not the core of Eurasia, but its periphery.
He argued that the continent's coastal belt, stretching from the Atlantic through the Mediterranean and South Asia to Japan, was a vital territory.
“He who controls Rimland rules Eurasia, ” he wrote,“ and he who rules Eurasia rules the fate of the world. ”
In seeking to strengthen its alliances that create a counterbalance to Eurasian adversaries, America is most supportive of Spickman ’ s thesis.
At the western end of Eurasia, NATO is reviving, strengthening Europe and confronting Russia.
Along the border with Russia, the grouping of American troops and allied forces is growing.
Finland and Sweden, abandoning the last vestiges of their neutrality, have applied to join NATO.
Assuming that it is possible to overcome the last barriers to ratification that Turkey and Hungary are creating, new members will appear in the alliance in 2023.
First of all, Western allies are actively arming and supporting Ukraine so that it can repel the Russian onslaught and launch a counteroffensive.
Although the devoted supporters of former President Trump and the slogan “America First ” were grumbling, Congress agreed in the fiscal year ending in September 2023 to provide Ukraine with seven billion dollars more aid than Biden asked (he asked for 37.7 billion dollars).
Putin did not weaken the Western alliance, but instead gave it new vitality.
Aaron David Miller of the Carnegie Endowment listed two more unintended consequences: “He created a moment of cross-party cooperation in America.
And he gave Biden an opportunity to atone for his chaotic withdrawal from Afghanistan. "
At the eastern tip of Rimland, there is growing talk of a future war with China over Taiwan.
They were especially intensified after the scandalous August visit to Taiwan of the speaker of the house of representatives Nancy Pelosi.
Biden hopes that during the upcoming personal meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping (it will be his first as president), he will be able to stop the deterioration of bilateral relations.
Xi is engulfed in domestic problems and difficulties, not least the economic slowdown and social upheaval caused by his anti-COVID policies.
However, the US military command claims that Xi wants to strengthen the country ’ s military capabilities in order to capture Taiwan by 2027.
In Asia, America does not have a NATO like alliance to deter China.
But it has a system of bilateral military agreements with Japan, South Korea, Australia, the Philippines and Thailand, operating on the principle of spokes on the sleeve.
However, these countries have no obligations to each other.
To bring them closer together and create a unified whole, America is working to expand situational schemes created with a specific purpose.
The Five Eyes Association (USA, Australia, Britain, Canada and New Zealand) is engaged in the exchange of intelligence information.
AUKUS, formed by Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States, was created for the construction of nuclear submarines and the development of other weapons.
The QUAD Quadripartite Safety Dialogue between Australia, India, the United States and Japan is designed to discuss issues ranging from vaccines to maritime safety.
South Korea and Japan put aside old grievances for the sake of conducting joint exercises, seeing how intensely North Korea conducts missile launches (it is also expected to conduct nuclear tests).
Japan has announced its intention to double its defense spending over the next five years, but it has a tradition of pacifism.
The self-governing island of Taiwan does not have diplomatic relations with most countries in the world, and it does not participate in the numerous military exercises conducted by America.
Biden has repeatedly stated that he will defend Taiwan from a Chinese invasion, but much is unclear.
Acting within the framework of the doctrine of strategic duality, America does not say exactly in what circumstances it can intervene, and what it will do, especially in the case of non-military methods of aggression, such as blockade.
Therefore, it is difficult for the island to heed the calls of America and fully switch to the defensive strategy of the "porcupine", which in case of danger curls into a tangle and bristles with needles.
When Congress considered the budget, it largely ignored a bipartisan bill to provide Taiwan with multibillion-dollar grants for the purchase of military equipment, which is akin to aid provided to Ukraine and Israel.
The middle of Spickman's Rimland is unreliable.
The Biden administration is courting members of the ASEAN regional association from Southeast Asia.
But they do not really want to make a choice between their main trading partner China and the main guarantor of regional security America.
Advertisement
India remains a big prize for American strategists.
It has a long tradition of non-alignment and pro-Soviet sentiments.
But as U.S.-China relations deteriorate, it is getting closer to America.
The annual naval exercise "Malabar", conducted by America and India, has expanded its scope to include all members of the Quadripartite Security Dialogue.
But disagreements persist.
India refrains from directly criticizing Putin for his operation in Ukraine.
But as Kurt Campbell, senior adviser to the White House on Asia, puts it, “The relationship with India is the most important bilateral relationship for the United States in the 21st century. ”
As far as the Middle East and Central Asia is concerned, American presidents have been trying one by one to reduce America ’ s military commitments after years of fruitless wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.
It is to be expected that the new Republican-dominated House of Representatives will incessantly condemn the Biden administration for its chaotic withdrawal from Afghanistan.
But in July, the United States launched a drone strike on Kabul, killing al-Qaeda leader Ayman al-Zawahiri.
This indicates Biden ’ s firm intention to continue the remote fight against terrorism.
Rising oil and gas prices this year, exacerbated by the armed conflict in Ukraine, have reaffirmed the geopolitical importance of the Persian Gulf.
Biden once declared Saudi Arabia a “pariah, ” but in July he visited the country and greeted its crown prince and de facto ruler, Mohammed bin Salman.
"We will not leave a vacuum that China, Russia or Iran can fill," Biden told Arab leaders in Jeddah.
In return, he received almost nothing.
There has been neither a drop in oil prices nor a normalization of relations between Saudi Arabia and Israel.
In December, the leaders of the Gulf countries gave Xi Jinping a much warmer welcome.
America ’ s relationship with Israel could also be tested by Benjamin Netanyahu ’ s return to lead a coalition of far-right ministers.
Biden had hoped to contain Iran ’ s nuclear program by reviving the nuclear deal, but his efforts failed.
An agreement to lift sanctions is now simply unthinkable, because large-scale protests against the ruling regime continue in Iran.
However, Iran continues to enrich uranium at a steady pace, and challenges Biden, who has promised to prevent the mullahs from developing nuclear weapons.
As for the world as a whole, America and its allies managed to hold a series of votes at the UN General Assembly condemning Russia.
But the support shown to the West by the global south is very fragile.
Many countries believe that they were victims of a distant conflict in Europe, because of which fuel and food prices have risen, and the world community has been distracted from other crises.
Moreover, they do not want to fall into the trap of the Cold War between America and China.
The West responds differently to such concerns.
It requires the creation of a mechanism that allows Ukraine to export grain from the Black Sea ports.
He is trying to introduce a ceiling on the price of Russian oil.
It promotes global health initiatives.
It is creating a Western system of financing infrastructure projects in an attempt to challenge China ’ s Belt and Road Initiative.
In general, Biden has somewhat weakened his efforts to divide the world into democracy and autocracy.
He has held several major regional summits, including with the participation of government leaders from Asia, the Pacific Islands, Latin America and Africa.
A big drawback to his strategy is the lack of an attractive economic and trade policy that would make it possible to bind allies and friends more firmly.
The US-EU Trade and Technology Council is a useful advisory body for discussing new technologies.
The 14-nation Indo-Pacific Economic Structure promises new initiatives in the digital economy, supply chain strengthening, clean energy and equity (tax rules, anti-money laundering and bribery).
But all these measures in essence do not reach meaningful trade agreements.
For example, America does not want to listen to the wishes of its Asian allies and refuses to join the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement on the Trans-Pacific Partnership, which includes 11 countries.
In fact, Biden ’ s “foreign policy for the middle class ” has a lot of protectionism and industrial policy.
Recent measures include subsidies for green technologies and semiconductor manufacturing, as well as restrictions preventing China from obtaining the most advanced chips.
Such policies increase tensions with European and Asian allies by limiting their access to the US market, restricting exports to China and robbing them of investment.
The European Union may, in response, begin to subsidize its own green technologies and semiconductor production.
Biden ’ s national security adviser, Jake Sullivan, doesn ’ t seem to see anything wrong with a possible war of subsidies.
He told the Carnegie Endowment that America is helping the middle class in other countries by “encouraging a virtuous cycle of investment in other parts of the world. ”
Democracy in the West, especially in America, where a crowd of Trump supporters stormed the Capitol two years ago, is also a major concern.
It seems that America is moving away from Trump and his supporters, who deny the results of the election, but its policy still causes a powerful polarization.
A healthy American democracy is essential because it enables the United States to win over friends and assert America ’ s leadership.
Sullivan said that in November, when Biden arrived in Phnom Penh for the Asian summit, other leaders were interested in the details of midterm elections in places like Nevada.
According to Sullivan, "it reminds us that the rest of the world is looking at the state of American democracy... and questioning America's resilience on the international stage."
