A moment between past and future.
Dear readers!
Not so long ago, on the pages of this blog, there was a material dedicated to the absence of a coherent ideology in Russia, that is, a system of goals, tasks, managerial decisions of a nationwide scale, in the amount of creating social positive, hope, attracting masses with images of a beautiful future - well, or not so pathos, a future with obvious evolution, long-term stable development.
Hope is our earthly compass, this is said remarkably correctly, it is better not to say, society in principle cannot fully exist without a great goal.
There is no doubt that we have such a problem in Russia, but it is only part of a much more global problem – which I will discuss below.
In fact, as I ’ ve said more than once in the “Collective Intelligence Experience, ” regular readers of the blog probably remember these philosophical passages and the discussions around them.
And now I would like to concentrate all that, add something else and again present for public review and discussion.
I ’ m almost sure that some of my conclusions will seem crazy – and okay, this is the privilege of science fiction writers, we can safely say what an ordinary person may, and would like to say, but is afraid to be called crazy.
And we are fine, we have the help to pulsate ideas.
Here I want to share them, hoping to cause an explosion of thoughts, emotions, comments; a sinful deed in advance I grin, anticipating someone ’ s brutally scorched exhaust pipes (in the dialect of the inhabitants of the current wild field, this situation is called “vibuh and pozhezha dupi ”)... - I think readers appreciated my refined humor of a hereditary intellectual...
They were joking and will be.
Let's start a serious conversation.
In my essays mentioned above, the pillar thought was the following: modern humanity – at least what I call “Europogenic ”, and to which we certainly belong, formed by the ancient Christian cultural paradigm – so, this humanity is in a total crisis, generated by the lack of a guiding perspective idea.
In other words, society as a whole does not know where to go.
And here, having collected the previous postulates, I intend to develop this thesis as concentrated as possible with the formation of clear conclusions.
I will start with the position of the most general: a normal self-developing system (hereinafter referred to as SRS) physically grows, occupies an increasing amount of space - this is its natural vector or even tensor, so to speak.
Any healthy human society: a tribe, a people, a state, a superpower is just such a SRS and it increases exactly as, materially, in volume, in mass, determined by two main parameters: territory and population size.
What we habitually call “world history ” is essentially a history of politics, or rather, of geopolitics, of the actions of the largest and most influential states and empires.
Yes, of course, any state is an entity that is born, grows, seeks its place in the world, falls into crises, it happens that it dies, it happens that it is reborn...
But in empires all these processes occur so powerfully, pictorially, that whether, especially instructive, and therefore it is their descriptions that make up the lion's share of the corpus of historical sources: the empire of Alexander the Great, the Romans, Charlemagne, Genghis Khan, Napoleon... and so on.
It is understandable, because, first of all, the actions of superpowers contribute to the unification of different human communities, in other words, they contribute to globalization.
And the united humanity formed in the course of this process, of course, also grows, captures the physical space.
What are the obvious markers on the way to the formation of global humanity?
Probably, it is possible to note quite a lot of such points, but for us the greatest interest is the middle of the XIX century: when the physical surface of the globe with the peoples inhabiting it was actually revealed, and technical progress, after a rather long formation of methods of scientific knowledge, was designated as the most important social factor.
Of course, technological progress in our usual understanding has always existed, since primitive times, but historically it turned out that purely scientific algorithms and models of thinking (differential, integral calculus, Cartesian coordinate system, etc.), led to discoveries made “without leaving the office ”, with the help of the head, goose feather and sheet of paper, and these discoveries, in turn, became a springboard for progress. given before.
It took about one and a half centuries for knowledge in the field of mechanics, thermodynamics, hydraulics, electromagnetism to be embodied in machines that concentrate and transform arrays of energy, many times surpassing the previous ones.
And it is natural that the machines of the middle of the XIX century in terms of the sum of simultaneously operating subsystems became inconceivably more complex, sophisticated and, naturally, more valuable than anything that was created before, and these complexity and high cost are an adequate fee for the ability to concentrate and direct huge energy flows in the channel needed by the operator, to put it simply – to give gigantic forces into the hands of a person.
In some articles here, I gave an example of an image that is extremely sympathetic to my writer's gut: every technical construct is nothing more than a "magical technocostume", wearing which, a person turns himself into a completely fabulous creature, becoming a participant in the "technocarnival":
a) chauffeur + car = centaur;
b) pilot + combat aircraft = dragon … etc.
In short, techno-suit, even the most primitive, like a protective shell, helmet and spear is a fundamental strengthening of the operational capabilities of a person, and even steam locomotives, steamships, electric motors (already in 1839 an experimental electric ship was built, a little Pushkin did not live to see him - this is for understanding the era)!..
- It was clear to any sensible politician what colossal advantages technical progress brings first of all in the military plan, and it is more fair to say, of course, scientific and technical, STP, because the evolution of technology has no basis other than scientific research, including fundamental ones.
My next thesis, I suppose, will cause some controversy, but I am convinced of it: since then and until recently, about 150 years, with all the obvious costs (terrible wars, environmental problems...)
NTP was the main inspiring idea of humanity, it was perceived as the main and elixir of growth, and the hope of humanity, its Eldorado, Belovodye, the magical shore of hope.
Let ’ s not forget: humanity is a normal SRS, it is growing physically, and the NTP gave it both unprecedented losses and a gigantic increase in the population – I will not prove this, everyone will easily find figures and graphs.
Well, where the population growth, there is the growth of the territory, a growing society needs new lands and skies, but with them in the last few decades, the situation is purely ambiguous.
Last year, exactly half a century was marked by the highly acclaimed report of a group of researchers led by the American Dennis Meadows “Limits to Growth ”, developed under the auspices of the no less famous Club of Rome.
The report became a sensation, causing an explosion of polar opinions and fierce controversy.
Let me remind you that back then, in 1972, the Meadows team predicted the exhaustion of the resources of our entire planet within thirty years, that is, by 2002 - with such consumption of these resources by collective humanity as then, in those years.
But it has been 20 years since the supposed deadline.
Thank God, there is no universal catastrophe, resources have not dried up, they are still being drawn to this day, but Meadows and his comrades, I must admit, were right in something.
Maybe even in the main.
Today we see various social measures aimed at inhibiting global consumption (whether these measures are spontaneous or conscious is a special topic): a protracted economic recession, a pandemic, managed local wars – in other words, we see a total crisis in something similar to the Great Catastrophe of 1914-1945, however, which has completely different causes and significant differences, in particular, it proceeds incomparably softer than a century. back.
But I have no doubt that this is a deep, existential crisis of Europogenic society.
This society, in fact, has nowhere to grow, here I fundamentally agree with the statement of the problem, and I undertake to confirm it.
Thus, normal society grows spatially.
The original primitive tribe fed from the surrounding ecosystem (forest, field, river, lake...) within a radius of several kilometers, and with the emergence of cattle breeding, agriculture, the area of ​ ​ cultural development grew significantly for two main reasons:
(a) The technologies required territories, pastures, arable land and steam land;
b) the constant supply of food has led to a demographic, if not an explosion, then a strong rise, and more people, of course, just need more place to live.
And so on - the Russians rushed to Siberia because these expanses carried precious furs, the Spaniards to America, a source of gold and silver, the British to India, the French to Africa... somewhat conditionally, but essentially so.
All this was before the outbreak of the STP, and the rapid breakthrough of technology in the late XIX-early XX centuries absolutely logically led to the idea of ​ ​ the development of extraterrestrial space.
Frenzied progressing humanity urgently needs more and more expanses, and it is quite natural that the eyes turned to distant planets, nebulae, stars and other romance, and it is good that such a romance was, because it provoked quite sober calculations.
I am ready to assert that the idea of space exploration was the main stimulus of Europogenic mankind in the twentieth century, its blissful dream.
It began to take hold of minds at the beginning of the century (“Aelita ” was written in 1923, exactly a hundred years ago), but the Great Disaster, of course, cut down the topic for a long time, everyone was not up to space, would have lived.
But after World War II, people returned to it at an incomparably different technological level, and after the first space flights, people really felt the exciting proximity of huge mysterious spaces, and the dream that we are about to rush there, into unknown distances, joyfully seized many minds.
In the social dimension, society saw before itself the space of great achievements, was inspired by the idea of unlimited exploration of the Universe, which created a generally healthy mood, the expectation of a promising future, that is, the basis of a social positive deeply desired by the authorities.
We are now forced to admit that those hopes have not been realized, having sunk into two intractable problems, or rather, it is the same problem in two guises:
(a) The extreme complexity, hence the riskiness and accident rate of space technology;
b) its ruinous cost.
In other words, over time, it turned out that the practical development of extraterrestrial space is unrealistic: technical systems here are so complex, so many subsystems must work in them at the same time that their impeccable joint work is extremely unlikely, at least somewhere, but some kind of failure will happen.
And spending on this is very burdensome for budgets, of course, only superpowers can afford to play in space, and even then only limited.
And after the first turbulent years of progress, cosmonautics trampled on the spot, there is no question of any settlement of mankind on distant planets, with great efforts, several people only visited the Moon, which ended.
More than half a century has passed since then, the matter has not progressed one step, even the superpowers did not play in such expensive toys.
So the dream of millions gradually melted away.
But the masses cannot live without a guiding idea, this puppeteers know very well, even if they say about a “society without ideology ”.
“No ideology ” is already an ideology, and what else, namely: after the collapse of the USSR, Europogenic society tried to infect with a moral virus such as“ buy and have fun ”; we recognize that it is extremely easy for us by our human nature to get on this needle.
When you can actually buy more goods and services today than yesterday, and tomorrow more than today - not because it is vital for you, but because it is cool and fun, and in general, life is a game of shopping and a demonstration of prestigious junk.
Well, in fact, it kindles well, gives a vector of life to an individual, thereby stabilizing society.
This unspoken ideology of “status consumption ” worked quite effectively – but, of course, smart puppeteers were well aware that this could invigorate and structure society temporarily, that this is only a respite, during which it would be good to find a real, spiritualizing idea.
And if it does not work, then you will have to invent something that moderates consumer appetites.
This, of course, is unpleasant, you can cause an explosion in a society accustomed to contentment and comfort - therefore, here, too, you need a sensible socio-psychological treatment of the population, which is carried out today, not without squeaking, not without noticeable turbulence, which affected you and us - the era of satiety has curled up, and the new time is alarmingly looming pandemics and local armed conflicts.
And still, no flammable idea is not visible: people live because it is necessary to live, home, life, family, again echoes of status consumption - we can no longer imagine how you can live without a car, a smartphone, the Internet, while it is desirable that it was not worse than others, so as not to experience mental discomfort...
This is life today, not the future.
The future, by and large, is not.
Not yet.
I fundamentally believe that society cannot exist without a goal-setting idea, even if it is deceptive, like a carrot before a donkey.
And I would be a bad philosopher and writer if I didn ’ t think about it and make predictions.
Philosophy is the “forward-looking ” of humanity, I said it and will say it, well, I will not forget to repeat that a science fiction writer can and even should produce hypotheses that look good“ crazy ”.
Life will show what will be justified, what will not be justified, but one of the tasks of the forerunner is to stir up society, make it think, worry, argue, and, you see, in the dispute the truth will be born.
First of all, I want to draw attention to the fact that the exhaustion of progress, in particular, the exploration of space, concerns large powerful machines designed to enhance the physical power of man (as a rule, these are so-called heat machines, but I prefer the term “fire machines ”, it is brighter and even more correct, if you think about it).
In fact, the classic STP of the XIX-XX centuries was dedicated to this: to merge a person with a mechanism the more powerful, the better.
A person behind the wheel of a car, the steering wheel of an aircraft, submarines, the remote control of a nuclear power plant - all these are biotechnological complexes, characters of technocarnival.
And it reached its maximum, to the maximum power around 1975 – about, of course – and then either stood up or the pace of progress fell, because the bio-operator of such a complex, Homo sapiens (hereinafter – HS), due to biological limitations, simply does not cope with the greater volume and unpredictability of physico-chemical processes than those that managed to conclude in fire machines half a century ago, so that attempts to create something even more complex (controlled thermonuclear reaction, space aeroplane...) became like a fuss with a herd of mustangs: catch seems to have been caught, but tame is not very good.
Therefore, a dead end.
What is not a dead end in the last forty or fifty years - it is quite obvious that these are the means of informatics and communication, the machines are small, weak, not so much serving the transformation of a person into a powerful biomech, but improving his information and analytical capabilities, that is, the focus of progress is noticeably shifted from the executive to the coginitive-staff, so to speak, the weakest place of the technocarnival figure is being modernized - the bio-operator.
And the more obvious trend for me in recent years is the shift of the epicenter of scientific research in the field of biology, especially genetics, which hints at the possibility of a fundamentally new modernization of man, not by attaching an external technocostume to him, but from within, genetic modification, up to the formation of a new species whose genome is quite different from CS, and we can assume that this genome is more perfect, its owner, let ’ s call it Homo gene mutatio, HGM, is able to perceive a larger volume of the universe.
Some fairly convincing data (referring those interested in the works of the famous neurophysiologist N.P. Bekhtereva) indicate that our sensory system is very limited, we simply do not catch much of the existing.
What we habitually call reality, perceived through the filter of our five senses, is only a part of being, and it does not seem to be very large.
Well, what can I say, Plato with his “cave ” described this picture two and a half thousand years ago: a huge shining world is visible to us in fragments from the twilight cave of sensory communicates (“ idols of the genus ” according to F. Bacon), and gene modification can be considered as an opportunity to reveal access to the completely real reserves of space-time hidden from the CS, only vaguely guessed behind the visible surface of events.
Once I was deeply touched by the ingenious simplicity of the thought of V.I. Vernadsky, and the impression was that the academician himself reacted to it somehow in passing: he said it, but then he did not develop it.
Maybe he just did not have time, I do not know; but in general he was very interested in the problem of finding a fundamental criterion that distinguishes living matter from non-living.
It is clear that the living and the inanimate are radically different forms of the organization of matter, and it is extremely important for the natural scientist to build a system of signs that clearly separate one from the other.
Now, of course, a well-established ensemble of these criteria has been formulated, but Vernadsky ’ s thought seems to cover them with a parachute: in his opinion, the difference between the living and the inanimate is in the structure of space-time; what we call the living is a multidimensional space-time continuum, much more highly organized than the inanimate.
Well, this prompted me to think this: an indirect indicator of the perfection of a particular system is what we somewhat vaguely call “beauty. ”
I undertake to assert that the more beautiful the object, the more highly organized the system it is, the greater the energy and labor invested in it, if it is artificial.
Well, the most beautiful, I would even say beautiful, I will undoubtedly declare the Earth ’ s biosphere (remember Shishkin ’ s picture “Forest Dali ”!) - with the uniqueness of all this in space inexplicable from well-established positions (Fermi paradox).
It is Vernadsky ’ s idea that allows us to explain this uniqueness: the fact that we see how living forests, fields-skies are in fact the surface of yet unknown hyperspace-time, the sensory system and the brain of the CS is able to perceive this continuum only in the image of the extraordinary beauty of the earth ’ s expanses, which are very different from other world space.
I would say that the planet Earth in space is a “white hole ”, the antonym of a black hole, failure to nowhere.
This, on the contrary, is the road upwards, from small space-time into the expanses of light living space.
And all of this leads us to the hypothesis that genetic modification of a person in the foreseeable future will lead to the fact that the HGM will be able to see what is simply not able to see the HS, only vaguely seeing it in the charm of landscapes, horizons in a light haze, sunrises, reflections of clouds in the lake blue...
Here I will decide to express what used to break through the same Vernadsky, Chardin, Lem in Solaris, but what is the twentieth century! - they will tell me, this is all good old Tengrianism!..
I don ’ t mind that comparison either.
And the essence is this: planet Earth, including the invisible part, the noosphere, is a sentient substance, a thinking being whose intelligence is obviously superior to human.
In principle, we can assume that the Earth in one person and the researcher and the laboratory, where it deduces in the course of evolution different bi-realties – like any researcher by trial and error, creating dead-end variants such as invertebrates, dinosaurs, abandoning them, and finally, finding a promising project in the face of the family of hominids, creatures that must evolve before reprogramming themselves, open up “rolled ” dimensions of biospatial space and biotime and make full contact with the soul of the planet.
At Lem Solaris easily communicated with HS, catching human images and turning them into some biogens, well, with the planet Earth in such a hyperproductive contact, suppose, is able to enter HGM, for which the inhabited continuum will be an immanent complement to himself, that is, the person and the personality of the planet will become if not a single whole, then something close to it.
The brain of HGM and the noosphere are in a positive resonance, making up an integral operational capacity, and in other words, modified humanity and the Big Earth will make up a living space.
I call this concept neo-geocentrism, predicting that the space-time reserves of our beautiful planet, when opened to our HGM descendants, will be much more spacious, comfortable, rich than the inhospitable dead spaces of the current universe.
What will it look like? … Well, here even my writer ’ s imagination gives back.
Until I made the painting.
I don ’ t know if I ’ m right to make these hypotheses.
Perhaps our coming century will be very different.
But in the fact that we live at the crossroads of ages, I am sure.
The old one is exhausted, the new one is not yet to be seen, except that its ghosts vaguely roar somewhere beyond the horizon of existence.
But this new must come, must illuminate the world, without a grandiose goal, society will sour and decompose, in general, the entire history of mankind, and the evolution of the biosphere indicate that the goal is an absolutely necessary component of the CCS.
In any case, neo-geocentrism as part of the worldview complex of HGM can become the basis on which further development will unfold.
As far as it is justified, it will not be justified – let ’ s wait, we will see.
And I would highly advise everyone interested in prognostic, futurological problems to closely monitor the achievements of genetics.
The ghosts of the future world are here somewhere.

Latin America is one of the most obscure, but nevertheless popular destinations for Russians who disagree with the war with Ukraine.
In the 10 months since the invasion began, hundreds of Russian-speaking people have arrived on the continent.
Meduza spoke to immigrants in Ecuador, Argentina, Uruguay and Costa Rica about how they decided to fly to the other end of the world, what difficulties they faced in the new environment and how they felt freedom, which they did not feel before.
SOUTH AMERICA
Ecuador
Anton N. Product Manager
I decided to leave on September 21, when the mobilization was announced.
A friend and former colleague of mine wrote to me, “Don ’ t you want to go to Latin America? ”
The offer was not accidental, because his acquaintances offered us a job there.
It took me a minute to respond positively.
So I decided that I was moving to Ecuador, which I knew nothing about.
The road turned out to be saturated - I was afraid that the borders of Russia will be closed, so on the same day I bought tickets to Vladikavkaz and decided to cross the border with Georgia on foot.
Over time, it became clear that there were a lot of such people – the famous traffic jams began.
But I am an optimist, so I was inspired by the walking route to the border.
I was having fun.
In Georgia, I was sheltered by friends: at that time in Tbilisi it was difficult to find housing, even temporary.
A week later, I flew to Turkey, where I met a friend who called to Latin America, and from there to the capital of Ecuador Quito with a long transfer at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, where we slept for 10 hours on benches.
Most of all in Ecuador, I am surprised by the weather - all year round it is the same: during the day the temperature rises to 19 degrees, and at night it drops to nine.
Ecuadorians say that in a day nature lives a cycle from winter to winter.
Life in Ecuador in everyday spending is not very different from Moscow.
For example, a spacious apartment next to the central park, around which all life boils, costs $850 for two (about 53.5 thousand rubles, the currency of Ecuador is US dollars, - approx.
"Medusa").
The cost of the products depends on whether they are imported or local.
For example, a pack of pasta from a local manufacturer costs about $1.8 (about 129 rubles).
“Medusa ”), and imported from Italy Barilla will cost $4.5 (about 322 rubles — approx.
"Medusa").
I work remotely in a Moscow company, so all my salary goes to the Russian account.
It is not yet clear what will happen when I cease to be a resident of the Russian Federation and my taxes will become 30%.
My employer is looking for workarounds, but it's not clear yet.
In addition, the news about the ban on remote work for certain categories of professions is not encouraging.
Time will tell.
Fortunately, I have a card of a Georgian bank, to which it is possible to transfer money with the help of cryptocurrency almost without problems, I use it here.
An account in an Ecuadorian bank can be opened only with a residence permit, while I do not have it.
Some inconveniences in using the Georgian card are still there - for example, payment for renting an apartment or large purchases here prefer to receive exclusively by transfer: the largest bills in the course - $20, in addition, the transfer reduces the risk of stumbling upon fake banknotes.
Because of the time difference, I work from two in the morning to 11 in the morning (Quito time zone minus eight hours from Moscow — approx.
"Medusa").
On the one hand, it is difficult, on the other - at night time flies quickly.
My Russian friends help me with the residence permit, they took me into their local business as an external expert in the local market.
I help them with the implementation of projects in the banking sector, there is a lot of room for growth with my experience in banking in Russia.
At the moment, this employment is more of a formality, because without Spanish it will not work fully, but it helps me to legalize in Ecuador.
Recently, I received a certificate of no criminal record in the Russian Embassy, necessary for obtaining a residence permit.
I have to wait for my turn at the immigration office and become its owner.
I am gay, and it gives me an advantage in making new acquaintances and immersing myself in the local culture.
In my experience, the LGBT + community is always more open.
In addition, the notorious image of homophobic Russia immediately evokes sympathy.
It is unusual for me to be in a country where there is no political pressure on the LGBT + community.
My friends joke that I am very shy and cluttered, I try not to talk about the community outside the four walls - for example, in a taxi; dancing in a bar causes a feeling of excessive attention, it is difficult to feel free.
But friends add that emancipation is a matter of time.
I love how this freedom of expression affects people.
All my new Ecuadorian acquaintances are open, welcoming and always eager to immerse me in local life: they invite me to parties, show sights and tell me where to taste local food.
In Ecuador, no one is interested in the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Many people are surprised that there is a war going on at all.
But those who know about her regret that I had to leave and support my decision.
The only problem - I do not know Spanish, and in everyday life, English is rarely found here.
Such challenges inspire me, so I am glad to be able to learn the language in an environment with native speakers and study with a teacher.
Progress is there, so basic things like going to the store, ordering food in a cafe or traveling in a taxi are given to me without much difficulty.
But a deep understanding of language and culture is far from over.
I have already encountered street crime, and in a tough, even by Ecuadorian standards, form.
We would come back from a party with local buddies and, sitting in the car, decide what the next plan was.
Three criminals opened the doors of the car and, threatening with a screwdriver, took our phones, watches and car keys so that we could not catch up with them.
The police didn't help us.
Then, through Find My Phone, our devices were found in a shopping center that sells everything stolen, in a “criminal ” area.
But none of us took the risk of going there.
I cannot say that I am in complete euphoria from moving, - despite the fact that there are a lot of unusual things happening around me, and I am surrounded by open and ready to help people, the subconscious still reminds me that I had to leave a lot of familiar things in Russia and greatly adapt life to new realities.
But I try to focus on the best and tell myself that it takes time to adapt.
SOUTH AMERICA
Argentina
Mark Boyarsky, photographer
My wife Victoria and I had been thinking about moving for years, but we didn ’ t know where.
Since 2011, we went to rallies and protests - and every year there was less and less hope.
After the “annexation ” of Crimea and the amendment of the Constitution, it became clear that there was no hope.
Life goes on, nothing good happens, and we already have children.
When the war began, we hesitated for a week: to stay or to leave.
By February 2022, we had a mortgage, a third of the renovation, a rented apartment, and my work as a photographer that doesn ’ t correlate with the idea of remote living.
Vika was in a long decree and wrote a blog about housekeeping.
But how to write about the comfort of the house, if something terrible happens around?
No comfort will not allow you not to see what is outside the window.
We bought tickets to Nepal, where our friends called us.
Decided already there to understand where we want to finally.
The experience of six months of living in Nepal changed our whole family and made it stronger: it turned out that we can adapt to a bunch of things that we never knew existed before.
But the most important thing was the opportunity to reboot.
We met with representatives of one of the organizations that help families to relocate.
We were advised to consider the UK: you can apply for tourist visas there remotely.
But we got a waiver.
By this time we had wildly expired Nepalese visas, we had paid a fine of three thousand dollars and were in a fog.
After hesitating, they bought tickets to Buenos Aires and flew here on September 10.
We have been thinking about Argentina for a long time: we were subscribed to the blog of a woman who has a wife and two daughters.
They have a nice queer family.
The blogger told a lot about life in Argentina, according to her photos and posts Buenos Aires looked absolutely perfect and perfectly suitable for us.
The first temporary apartment — the day before the departure from the capital of Nepal, Kathmandu — we found on Airbnb, in an area that we liked from the descriptions on the Internet.
We rent housing for 800 US dollars per month (about 50.4 thousand rubles, - approx.
“Medusa ”), for other expenses our family needs about the same.
My wife works as an editor, receives a salary in rubles on a Russian card.
We withdraw it with the help of cryptocurrency.
I work as a photographer.
In Moscow, the work found me on my own – orders for photo shoots were pouring in, even there was an opportunity to refuse.
And in Argentina, nobody knows me, at first it was psychologically difficult.
In Moscow, I mostly filmed food.
Here in Buenos Aires, I did a few different free shootings, so that there was some kind of base, posted photos in the communities, sent orders.
It would seem that there are not so many, but quite normal.
I take less money than in Moscow.
There - seven thousand rubles per hour, here - $100 for the entire shooting (about 6300 rubles, - approx.
"Medusa").
But it is important to note that for Argentines even $50 for the entire shooting is quite expensive: there is no tradition to order shooting, as in Russia.
A separate quest was to find a school and a kindergarten.
My wife and I have two children: the eldest daughter Hannah, who is seven years old, and a four-year-old son Joseph.
We arrived in September with a feeling of the beginning of the school year and did not take into account that here it begins in March and ends in December, then the summer holidays begin.
At the end of the year, it is almost impossible to get into public school, so we signed up for a private school.
It is more expensive than all the other private ones that we watched, but compared to Moscow prices it is still super cheap: in rubles 10-12 thousand per month per child.
Our new school immediately has a kindergarten, primary school, and middle school, so I take the children together.
For enrollment, we required minimum certificates: confirmation that the daughter graduated from the first grade in Moscow (in the first grade in Argentina, schoolchildren go to six years, - approx.
“Medusa ”) and medical documents from a paid pediatrician (about a thousand rubles per child).
Hannah successfully remotely graduated from the first class started in Moscow, so now she is again in the first, but at the end of the year it is an ideal opportunity to adapt, and from the next school year, in early March, the daughter will go to the second.
Without a residence permit in Argentina, you can stay for 90 days, then it is possible to extend the stay, but only up to 180 days, so a residence permit, of course, is needed.
We are in the process of getting the document.
I spent the last two years learning Spanish at Duolingo because my wife and I were thinking about moving to Spain — but it didn ’ t work out.
My basic knowledge, of course, is not quite enough, so I continue to teach with my family.
In school, a daughter without a language is hard, but surprisingly not impossible.
The teacher uses a Google translator to send us important messages.
When I wrote in the school ’ s parent chat “Hi, my name is Mark, here we are ”, almost all the parents responded to me in private messages with pleasant greetings and offers of help.
This attitude in Argentina we have encountered literally everywhere – all people want to help.
Argentina seems to be good for everyone: both LGBT + and hetero families.
Here, children can not be afraid to express themselves, whatever these manifestations may be.
Here among our friends for the first time there were LGBT families, on the example of which children see that this is normal.
In Moscow, we just talked to them about it, but we did not have a single example.
In Nepal in March, we were embarrassed to say that we were from Russia, afraid that we could be condemned.
Time passed — we were able to rework our own feelings about the war and the fact that we are Russians, and to understand the difference between collective responsibility and guilt.
We let it go, and if we are now being asked about the war in Argentina, we are already finding the strength to answer these questions.
Uruguay
Polina Vinogradova, musician, translator
I moved to the Uruguayan capital of Montevideo with one suitcase in August 2022.
I only said goodbye to my mom.
I have long dreamed of living in a more liberal country.
The war, of course, spurred me not to wait any longer.
It was morally difficult and lonely for me, the usual way of life disappeared, I often cried: here you can not go home for a week and back when you get bored.
This is not my first emigration, so I know that the most difficult thing is the first six months or a year.
This is the time when you get used to a new country and struggle with the desire to return.
You need to survive it, and then it will be easier and more pleasant.
Things are done, breathing easily, the sun shines.
The main problem in the move was a long flight from Georgia to Brazil, which lasted more than a day.
At all the borders (Russia – Georgia – Brazil – Uruguay) there were no special questions for me, no one asked me why I was going and where, all the controls went calmly.
My husband and I are engaged in business together, and he himself is also engaged in programming.
I work at my favorite job remotely and do not want to change it.
The only thing is that you need to carefully calculate the hours of going online due to the time difference with Russia, so as not to accidentally come to the meeting at night (the time difference between Montevideo and Moscow is six hours, - approx.
"Medusa").
I usually start working pretty early, around seven in the morning in Montevideo, and finish around three in the afternoon.
But the evenings are often free and there is time to rest.
It is not difficult to obtain migration documents here: you need to provide the required certificates through an online entry to the National Directorate of Migration and wait from three to six months.
However, some of these documents can only be done on site - for example, a health card.
So it is impossible to register for a residence permit remotely.
First, a residence permit is requested, then a permanent residence permit is requested.
After three years of permanent residence in the country, you can apply for a passport: legalization in Uruguay is not difficult, compared, for example, with the EU.
The main thing is to show the means of subsistence and the absence of a criminal record.
This approach seems reasonable to me.
It is also necessary to vaccinate on the spot, including from the covid, or to show certificates of vaccination in Russia.
So Uruguay is not suitable for anti-vaccinators.
For a quiet life in Uruguay, on average, you need about two thousand dollars per person.
Renting a comfortable two-room apartment costs me 1.2 thousand dollars a month.
If you buy food in the supermarket and in the markets, you can meet $600 per person.
There are a lot of hipster cafes with delicious food here, you can go once or twice a week.
I am pleasantly surprised that my socialization in Uruguay is going well.
For 10 years of living in Russia, I could not find musicians in my band.
And through social networks in Uruguay, I immediately found Russians in the project: we regularly rehearse, prepare for recording in the studio.
I already have a lot of friends: both Uruguayans and Russians who came, like me.
We constantly communicate on Instagram, sometimes we meet live.
While in Uruguay, I faced one difficulty – a new language.
My Spanish on arrival was very basic.
But after three months of living in Montevideo, I mastered the local dialect of Spanish at the household level, and I do not need any more: there are people here who speak English, and I have it free.
I have not encountered street crime, but I know that it exists, rather at night and in poor neighborhoods.
I know that in the area of ​ ​ the Old Town (the oldest part of Montevideo - approx.
“Medusa ”) homeless people can aggressively beg and try to talk to you, but to physical aggression or robbery on the street in broad daylight does not reach.
Yet, unfortunately, domestic murders of women (femicide) are common here, they are talked about on the radio.
Feminists often hold marches in support of victims of domestic violence.
For any sexual orientation other than hetero, Uruguay is completely tolerant (since 2013, same-sex marriage has been legalized in Uruguay – approx.
"Medusa").
On the streets you can often see symbols with a rainbow flag, souvenirs are sold.
September was LGBT + month, and it was my first time on the pride parade: thousands of people participated, including “traditional ” families with children.
What surprised me most was the lack of judgment from people.
In Russia it was too much.
There is no excessive attention to someone else ’ s life: no one tells how to live, where to work and how to dress.
This is an indescribable high, and in Russia I missed it very much.
CENTRAL AMERICA
Costa Rica
Olga Bastron, Sustainable Development Project Manager
My family and I moved to Costa Rica at the end of July, and it was not a planned move at all.
In February, we realized that it was not safe to stay in Russia, and in March, I began to look for where we could move.
Initially, the country of destination was Israel: we had ready documents for repatriation.
But after a few weeks of deliberation, they decided to move to Costa Rica: it is relatively far from the current events, armed conflicts, and it has not had a regular army since 1949.
It seemed to us that in an environment where there is no aggression and conflicts associated with the division of territory, children will be relatively safe.
In addition, this country is in high positions in the ranking of happiness and for the most part consists of natural parks and reserves: people are very sensitive to animals and the environment, including at the state level.
We found accommodation right away: there were no difficulties.
But I suspect it's just a lucky coincidence.
The housing market here is divided into two categories: for Costa Ricans and those who come from other countries for a long time.
The difference in cost is huge.
In the first case, the options will be more modest and without furniture, from about $300 per month.
The second will be with everything necessary and in condominiums with a refined and protected area - already from 900 dollars.
If you move, you will either have rather modest conditions, to which, perhaps, people who lived in large cities in Russia are not quite accustomed, or cool housing with a price several times higher than in Russia.
On average, rent, if the house is not on the ocean, will cost at least $600 per month or $900 if the apartment is on the coast, plus electricity.
We are still looking for something to do in this country.
I actively create a LinkedIn profile and work with a teacher who prepares me for interviews in English.
We faced the issue of self-actualization: we need to understand what the context is, how we can integrate into it and help society.
For example, in the school of children, I took up volunteering: to help with the conduct of Instagram school and photos.
In general, I believe that the chances of adaptation and integration into the local community are high.
We spent more than three years in a settlement in the Tula region, where we also built horizontal ties and non-violent communication, studied international experience of how relationships and education are built in similar places.
I am interested in everything related to the development of the territory.
Suddenly, at the school where our eldest daughter goes, they placed an ad that they needed help in designing a small park in the village where we live.
I went to this meeting and was the only one who didn ’ t speak Spanish — they spoke to me with reverence in English.
For four days, we were immersed in the project: identifying the needs of residents and identifying such functional areas of the park that will help the community to unite and become stronger.
Our goal was to create a place where everyone could cross paths.
For me, it was a turning point: I realized that if this is possible here, then I will not be lost.
There was never a time when someone heard where we came from, and did not show tact and sympathy for what was happening.
Of the mentality traits I ’ ve noticed: every time someone from foreign children or adults reacts expressively or even aggressively, I see a calm and tactful misunderstanding of the locals.
They do not support aggression, do not begin to behave aggressively in response, but simply wait for people to return to an adequate state in order to continue communicating.
We, of course, faced with a difference in mentalities and features of business approaches.
Everything related to the service sector here is slower, more cumbersome and more bureaucratic than in recent years in Moscow.
We tried four times to open accounts in local banks, for various reasons we were refused.
In general, I understand that everything can not be identical and that we are so used to the noisy service in Russia that immediately begin to experience negative emotions and put pressure on people when something goes wrong.
But that's not how it works here.
If you compare with the standard of living that we had in Russia, then life in a new country is more expensive for us.
What saves us is that we have savings and a small passive income, and my job allows me to earn remotely.
Working calls I have from eight in the morning to 12 noon local time (from 18: 00 to 21: 00 Moscow time, — approx.
"Medusa"), the first half of the day - working.
Such a schedule is not difficult, and the work is now more.
We have not yet issued a residence permit, as this is a rather serious issue that requires a large number of papers, and is expensive.
Applicants for residency must pay an expensive health insurance – $400 per month for a family of four.
The easiest way to get a residence permit is to invest in real estate here, it is also not cheap.
We are still at the stage of considering various options for legalization.
Everything that is written about crime in Latin America, we did not notice from personal experience.
There are basic safety rules - for example, do not leave keys, phones and valuables in the cabin of the car in a visible place, close the windows, the car itself and the house.
We comply with these security measures.
In general, everything turned out to be much safer than we were described in various telegram chats.
But we also did not expect how open, friendly and cheerful people are here.
Maybe five months is not the time when you can take off your rose-colored glasses.
Costa Rica has a basic sense of security, tranquility, and inner confidence that the world is good.
And we still need time to understand that this is not a fairy tale: it really is.
My husband and I try not to compare life here with life in Moscow, because it is a completely different experience.
It has its own nuances and features, which we try to approach without any negativity.
I think that this emigration is a chance to rethink everything that was, and take the best, the most valuable, the most interesting in your life.
"Medusa"

As stated in the publication Ars Technica, Enhance Speech spun off from the larger research project ProjectShasta, later renamed Adobe Podcast.
The best browser version of Enhance Speech.

The process of cleaning and improvement takes a few minutes.
Adobe has released a free AI tool for radical cleaning of voice recordings from noise
When tested by Ars Technica journalists, it turned out that Enhance Speech works best with recordings where only one voice is heard, and the noise level remains more or less moderate.
Recording on the built-in microphone of the Apple laptop from a distance of about three meters and with a noisy fan next to it in the end looked like it was done on a professional tape recorder in a completely muffled studio.
How it works
Adobe does not disclose details of how their system works.
ArsTechnica suggests that the AI was trained on a multi-hour array of data, including both clean and noisy records.
The resulting model allows the system to isolate the frequencies of the human voice and synthesize an exact copy of everything that was said.

Enhance Speech is not the first tool that offers the ability to remove noise using AI models.

Enhance Speech is just one element of Adobe ’ s entire group of AI tools aimed at podcasters.

The advantages and disadvantages of remote work were told in the social network ЯRUS
Developer, programmer, tester, UX copywriter, interface and landing page designer.
This is just a small list of IT professions that are suitable for remote work.
About 250 large companies in the field of information technology and related areas in 2022 switched to the “off-the-office ” format.
The team of the social network ЯRUS shared their opinion on whether the “remote ” is really good.
First, let ’ s talk about the benefits of remote work.
The first and, perhaps, the main thing is that you do not need to spend time and money on the road, look for parking for a car, if the office is in a busy place.
This point is especially relevant for megalopolis.
So, residents of the capital spend on average 200 hours in traffic jams annually.
That ’ s more than eight full days.
Another important plus - flexible schedule makes it possible to find the optimal balance between work and other areas of life, pay more attention to family and loved ones.
Only 75% of employees are more productive from home.
In the silence of your own apartment, it is easier to concentrate, there are no distractions, which increases the efficiency of work.
The remote worker can organize his workplace as he likes, with maximum comfort.
For the employer, the remote format can significantly reduce the costs associated with renting office space, utility bills, the purchase of professional equipment and furniture.
Savings are especially important for IT startups, when every ruble is worth its weight in gold.
Instead of an office employee in the office, the employer can invite a specialist from any region of the country and even from abroad on the terms of “remote ”.
In this way, everyone wins.
However, the disadvantages of the remote format of work can outweigh all the advantages and be critical for IT companies.
Owners and business leaders call the main disadvantage of working outside the office – the lack of internal communications.
“It ’ s easier to solve most of the issues at all stages of work.
There are a number of tasks for which you can work alone at home and communicate only through a special program Jira.
And there are projects that do not allow you to solve problems without team participation.
This is especially true for startups, which are still our social network.
Therefore, it is faster and better to form a team in an office format, ” says Ivan Dobrovolsky, head of the social network ЯRUS.
As studies show, only in the first three months remote employees work more efficiently, and then their efficiency drops - the lack of motivation and self-discipline for high-quality remote work affects.
For the IT team, the opportunity to consult and exchange experience with colleagues is extremely important.
In addition, it is not advisable to hire interns and staff with little experience.
For remote employees, the boundaries between work and personal time are blurred.
This leads not only to professional burnout, but also to problems in personal life.
The risks associated with violation of the rules of confidentiality and network security are increasing, the internal information of companies is poorly protected.
In general, remote employees feel lonely if the organization does not properly develop a culture of virtual communication and support.
In addition, the number of fresh ideas is reduced, the quality of “brainstorming ” is deteriorating, loyalty and corporate spirit are disappearing.
Faced with the drawbacks of remote work, even tech giants like Google have curtailed experimental programs that allowed employees to work from home.
In the social network ЯRUS in a remote or hybrid format, less than 10% of employees work, which allows them to develop at a much faster pace.
Last year alone, the number of users of the Russian app reached 9 million.

Economist Andrianov spoke about the formation of Russia and India new contours of energy security
Starting from February 5, another sanctions instrument came into force, with the help of which the collective West has been trying to “tear the Russian economy to shreds ” for several years.
We are talking about the notorious ceiling on prices for petroleum products supplied from the Russian Federation.
However, this is another blow not to our country, but to the system of global energy security.
Perhaps Western politicians in the heat of anti-Russian hysteria do not understand this (but rather, they simply deftly hide their “knowledge ” from ordinary voters).
But such consequences are clearly visible from the side.
The states that refused to participate in the rabid anti-Russian campaign are well aware of what a “curve path ” the United States and its European satellites have become.
One of these sober-minded states is India, which has many years, and even centuries, experience of economic partnership with Russia.
Therefore, the topic of sustainable development of global energy and the role of the Russian Federation in this process became one of the central topics during the Indian Energy Week (India Energy Week 2023), which takes place from 6 to 8 February at the Bangalore International Exhibition Center.
New Leaders and Old Hegemon
Over the past year, India has become one of the main partners of Russia in the field of energy: Russia came out on the first place among oil exporters to this country, there are prospects for increasing supplies of Russian LNG.
Therefore, it is not surprising that the further contours of such interaction are actively discussed during India Energy Week 2023.
In this context, a speech by Rosneft Chief Executive Officer Igor Sechin set the tone for the most important discussion on the future of global energy in general.
What do two countries like India and Russia have in common today?
First of all, the focus on stable long-term development.
As Igor Sechin noted, India, having become the most populated country in the world, is becoming the leader of the world economic dynamics.
“A big country with a huge young ambitious population, where the most important thing is the dynamics.
It is no coincidence that analysts and experts predict for India the growth rate of up to 7% per year, ” the head of Rosneft said.
In turn, he added, Russia was able “in the conditions of unprecedented sanctions, pressure and confrontation with almost the entire Western world to provide a result more significant than that of many leading economies of the world. ”
Of course, this cannot be liked by the guardian of neocolonial traditions – the United States of America, which today uses the full range of political, economic and military tools in order to prevent the emergence of new leading countries on the world stage.
The victims of such steps are not only individual states, but also global markets, primarily energy.
“The actions of the world hegemon, trying by any means to maintain its hegemony, destroyed the single energy market.
There is no single global energy market.
Energy security has ceased to be global, ” says the head of Rosneft.
It is not straight.
Indeed, as a result of the actions of the United States and its allies, all principles of market trade were destroyed, market pricing, contract law were abolished, and logistics chains that had been built for decades were broken.
It is noteworthy that this process began long before the current round of anti-Russian sanctions — the United States has long sought to cut off Europe from stable and relatively inexpensive energy supplies from the Russian Federation, thereby undermining its economic potential and making it completely dependent on its own will.
Over the past year, this process has only accelerated.
As a result, Europe has completely lost its main advantage - energy security - access to cheap and reliable Russian energy and is now forced to pay three to five times more for gas.
According to Bloomberg, the rejection of Russian gas has already cost Europe about 1 trillion euros, ” said Igor Sechin.
Of course, the leading energy-consuming countries in the face of India and China cannot remain indifferent to these destructive processes.
In response to the destruction of the global market, to the rupture of logistics chains, the regionalization of energy will occur, new safe logistics schemes will be built.
Accordingly, the formation of regional payment systems with their settlement and reserve currencies will begin.
In this context, the next attempts to restrict trade in Russian energy resources, in the form of the same ceiling on oil prices, look absolutely powerless.
As Igor Sechin notes, the reference price for our oil cannot be formed where it does not exist.
“If there is no supply to Europe, then reference prices will be formed where it actually goes.
As it is written in Ecclesiastes: “The crooked cannot become straight, and what is not, it cannot be considered, ” the head of the Russian company said.
Green Barrels for Friends
In addition to purely logistical and organizational-financial issues, the question of the “physical availability ” of energy resources also arises.
It is not difficult to notice that the leaders in terms of reserves of the same hydrocarbon raw materials are the countries that were under the influence of Western sanctions: Russia, Venezuela, Iran.
And in the course of this regionalization of energy markets, these countries will become the main suppliers of energy for the rapidly growing economies of India, China and other countries.
One of the guarantors of energy security for Russia-friendly countries will be the Vostok Oil project, implemented by Rosneft and having a resource base of 6.5 billion tons of oil.
It is important to emphasize that the carbon footprint of this project is only a quarter of the global average of new mining projects.
The oil of the Vostok Oil project is actually “green barrels ”, which are extracted using advanced technologies.
And is there a raw material alternative in the same collective West?
Of course not.
So-called majors under the influence of the “green agenda ” in recent years have reduced their investments in exploration and development of deposits.
And even those record profits that they recorded in 2022 will be directed mainly not to the development of production, but to the payment of dividends to shareholders and repurchase of shares.
* * *
Thus, before our eyes there is a reformatting of the global energy market.
The losers and beneficiaries of this process are already obvious.
The collective West, which has embarked on the crooked path of sanctions, is stumbling towards an economic impasse.
And Russia, India and other countries, aimed at constructive and equal dialogue, are clearing a direct path for an active multifaceted partnership.
And only such a direct road leads to energy security.
Ecclesiastes was right.
The author is an expert of the InfoTEK Analytical Center, Associate Professor of the Financial University under the Government of the Russian Federation Valery Andrianov.

Sociologists from Cambridge proved the effectiveness of a four-day work week
2
This change did not affect the company ’ s revenue.
A team of Cambridge University sociologists, together with the British non-profit human rights group 4 Day Week Global, evaluated the effectiveness of the four-day work week.
The results of the study were published on the website 4 Day Week Global.
For six months, several companies have switched to a new format of the working week without reducing the salaries of employees.
In total, about 3 thousand employees switched to the new format.
At the beginning, middle, and end of the study, participants were asked about their performance at work, stress, burnout, and overall well-being.
Staff estimates indicate that anxiety and fatigue levels have decreased, while mental and physical health have improved.
71% of employees reported a lower level of burnout, and 39% said they experienced less stress compared to the beginning of the study.
The number of sick days decreased by 65%, and the number of employees who resigned at their own request decreased by 57%.
The company ’ s revenue has hardly changed during the trial period.
Many respondents also said that it has become easier for them to combine work with family and social obligations.

In Britain, completed the world ’ s largest experiment of four days of work
Wednesday, 22 February 2023, 09: 25 -
In Britain, the world ’ s largest experiment has come to an end, in which employers have tested a four-day work week, and mostly participating companies have decided to stick to it in the future.
This is reported by Reuters.
Workers at 61 companies across the UK worked an average of 34 hours over four days between June and December 2022, earning a steady salary.
Of these, 56 companies, or 92%, decided to continue this practice, 18 of them - on a permanent basis.
According to the British research organization Autonomy, which published the report together with a group of scientists and with the support of the New Zealand group 4 Day Week Global, this study is the largest in the world.
Despite the positive results of the study, other surveys indicate that most British employers are not ready for a four-day working week in the near future.
The Autonomy study involved 2,900 employees in various sectors.
Most agreed that productivity remained at the same level.
Employees noted that their well-being and work-life balance had improved, and data showed that workers were much less likely to leave their jobs as a result of the introduction of a four-day work week.
For some workers, an extra day off was more important than a paycheck: 15% said no money would make them return by the five-day week.
Employers from marketing and advertising, professional services and philanthropy were the most represented in the study.
About 66% of participants had 25 or fewer employees, while 22% had 50 or more.
11% were not engaged in commercial activities.
Last year, a study by the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development (CIPD) found that very few employers expect to switch to a four-day working week in the next three years, and two-thirds do not expect any change in the next decade.
However, evidence that it helped retain staff could prove to be a powerful argument for companies trying to hire workers after the pandemic.

Vitamin K2 (menaquinone) plays a major role in bone and heart health.

Menaquinone-7 (MK-7) has a longer chain and is found in fermented foods.

Vitamin K2 plays a preventive role in heart disease

Google confirms quantum computing breakthrough – more computing power with fewer errors
On the pages of our site you can find a lot of information about quantum computers, so regular readers know that quantum bits, qubits, are very sensitive to external interference.
Light, heat and electromagnetic waves cause errors during calculations, which makes the results of these calculations less reliable.
And, the more qubits are included in the quantum computing system, the higher, naturally, the error rate becomes.
However, representatives of the group of developers of quantum systems Google announced that they managed to “see the light at the end of the tunnel ”.
In their latest work, they used new algorithms for quantum error correction, which allowed them to increase the dimension of the qubit array, while even lowering the error rate.
Previously, Google specialists combined qubits into logical groups of 17 qubits, but the new design of a logical qubit with 49 qubits allowed to implement a more effective mechanism for correcting errors.
According to the available data, this case is the first in the history of quantum informatics, when the size of an array of qubits was increased while reducing the error rate.
And this is a very big and important step towards the creation of a real universal quantum computer.
However, the creation of a large logical qubit with a small error rate in itself entails the need to modify the hardware and software of a quantum computing system.
At present, Google specialists are already working towards the creation of a new system of cryogenics and electronic control.
When all this is ready, it will be embodied in the form of a new processor for the next generation quantum computer Sycamore 2, which will replace the previous computer and will be used as a cloud service for the development of new drugs, battery technologies, new materials, etc.

Decision, artificial intelligence or truth: the media found out the details of the conversation Prigozhin and Akhmedov
Joseph Prigozhin
Recently, the media drew attention to an audio recording in which, probably, producer Joseph Prigozhin and billionaire Farhad Akhmedov criticize Vladimir Putin and his entourage.
Prigogine immediately called audio fake generated by a neural network, which causes a lot of controversy.
Medusa writes about it.
What is known
In recent days, the media and telegram channels widely distributed audio recording of a conversation between the likely Russian music producer Joseph Prigozhin and billionaire Farhad Akhmedov, who are in a foul form criticizing the Russian leadership.
The authenticity of the votes on the tape has not been confirmed.
Prigozhin 's reaction
Later, Prigozhin gave an interview to Fontanka, in which he stated that “people in private conversation can talk about anything ”, and“ neural networks today allow you to do any miracles. ”
At the same time, Prigozhin claimed that he did not exactly remember such a conversation with Akhmedov, but periodically communicates with him.
According to the second version of the producer, the recording is still not solely the result of the work of neural networks, but "is a symbiosis of spoken phrases and generated, but never uttered":
“Of course, some moments are real in the conversation.
The voice is like mine.
But it is unclear what and how they glued.
We need to understand, ” he said.
The conversation completely generated the neural network
This position Prigozhin adhered to when he first commented on the publication of the audio recording.
However, technical experts stressed that neural networks can not yet so qualitatively mimic the voice of a real person, especially do it within 35 minutes.
A person has small parasitic words, he picks up phrases when he forms a sentence.
The algorithm can copy sound and voice, but cannot reproduce unique language features.
According to the IT specialist, the products that are available on the market today and allow realistic voice copying (for example, Prime Voice AI), are sharpened mainly for the English language, and they have no Russian analogues of comparable quality.
“When you try to copy the Russian language, you can always hear the characteristic metal ringing in the voice very noticeably that it is not a real sound.
In English it is already indistinct, but in Russian it is also not dictated.
So from the point of view of AI, this conversation is definitely not deepfake, I am 100% sure of it, ” he said.
The conversation was glued together from the real replicas of Prigozhin and Akhmedov
According to the analysis of journalists, there is some evidence that the conversation is not glued together.
• Background noise and other voices are heard throughout the recording, the background is always different.
On the soundtrack, which probably refers to Prigozhin, a voice sounds very similar to the voice of his wife Valeria (at these moments Prigozhin refers to this voice "Ler").
• Since the voices of the interlocutors are recorded in two channels - left and right - it is easy to hear what is happening on each track separately.
Faking such a different background noise is incredibly difficult (this is the illegible voices of people to whom Prigozhin turns in English, and sounds similar to the sounds of the elevator or pressing buttons).
There is less noise on Akhmedov ’ s track, but at one point someone ’ s female voice in the background tells him to “steal, ” and then he repeats the word.
• The very nature of the conversation and how the interlocutors interact with each other looks natural: repetition of words and cues, when picking up words, reasking "do you hear?" (to make sure that the interlocutor hears), giving in and shouting as a sign of consent.
Such reactions are very difficult to mount on purpose - this is a titanic and very difficult work.
• The quality of communication throughout the conversation is uneven: somewhere Prigozhin can be heard better, and somewhere worse.
Sometimes individual sounds seem to be eaten a little (especially at the end of phrases, which is natural for our language).
It is unlikely that at first a good sound could be deliberately so worsen.
• In some moments, you can hear Prigozhin hiding his voice and trying to speak not very loudly: this is what people do who do not want strangers in the room to hear them.
• Joseph Prigozhin ’ s key remarks about the attitude to power, the war and his opinion about what is happening in the country sound as natural as possible (and these are fragments of a dialogue in which the interlocutors interact absolutely plausibly).
The actors speak on the audio.
"Such an explanation indirectly contradicts the words of Joseph Prigozhin himself - he claimed that in the conversation" there are real moments ", while the audio recording there are no signs of a sharp change in the language of the interlocutors, and it is unlikely that even the most talented actors are capable of such a parody," the newspaper writes.
However, there is another way to fake someone ’ s voice: an attacker can record himself, withstanding all the characteristic pauses and intonations of the victim, and use the voice conversion technology – with its help, the neural network edits the sound, imitating the voice of another person (examples of such neural networks).
An expert on generative neural networks said that such a scenario is theoretically possible, and poor sound quality on the recording could help hide the changes.
In order to teach the neural network, a minute recording of the voice that needs to be simulated is enough.
At the same time, the most difficult task for the alleged creators of fake audio is not changing the sound, but creating a plausible scenario in which fake Prigozhin and Akhmedov discussed many details related to their private lives.
This is noted by journalist Andrei Zakharov:
In 90% of fake conversations, Mike and Nick come out (writing truthful dialogues is a special skill), in the remaining 10% they blind a maximum of two minutes for the same reason - a truthful, live dialogue is very difficult to write.
Recall, the founder of the Russian PMC "Wagner" Yevgeny Prigozhin commented on the scandal with a combined telephone conversation of music producer Joseph Prigozhin with oligarch Farhad Akhmedov.
According to the founder of the PMC, it is possible to speak critically in a private conversation about the so-called "SVO", but there is no one to refuse their words.
