Drop everything and sail around the world
In recent years, the global media began to vigorously promote "travel living", translated from English - travel-life.
Its supporters are called digital nomads, or digital nomads.
They are not attached to the place of residence and work and are ready to trade comfort, stability and career prospects for life in continuous motion.
In the US alone, this philosophy is shared by 22 million people, or one in 15 Americans, in the world – 35 million, and by 2030, the number of digital nomads on the planet is projected to grow to one billion people.
Experts believe that this is the way to form a “seamless ” world with a“ connected person ” without roots.
Photo: Parliamentary GazetteParliamentary Newspaper
Down with office stress
Video of the day
The first digital nomad was an American writer and programmer.
In 1983, he set off on a computerized bike and completed it on a yacht in 2021.
The revival of the ancient nomadic way of life in the 21st century has become possible thanks to the Internet and IT technologies, and the pandemic of the covid with a remote format of work has spurred it.
By 2030, the number of digital nomads could reach a billion people.
What kind of people are these?
The first group is digital.
Programmers, project managers, graphic designers, journalists, writers, lawyers, translators, analysts, testers, copywriters, video editors, product managers.
Six months in the Maldives, three months in Barbados or the United Arab Emirates, where the world ’ s fastest mobile Internet.
The second is adventurers and wanderers.
The third is mortgages, for which loan payments are more expensive than permanent tourism and being in cheap areas of the world.
The philosophy of digital nomads is to untie themselves from their place of birth and one job.
Choose countries where the best climate, cheaper food, where there are no toxic offices, civil duties, but only the right to live in pleasure.
Digital nomads consider themselves the chosen ones of fate, because, in their opinion, they make the free choice of a free person.
Life in motion, they argue, is not bliss, but the norm.
Their favorite slogan is “The values of minimalism make us happy. ”
Nature, freedom, unprocessed food, physical activity...
A lot is said about this on their profile sites.
Anxiety and desire to change places
Hunting for a change of places is a problem of motives, and they are different, correspondent member, philosopher, chief researcher of the Institute of Sociology of the Russian Academy of Sciences Jean Toshchenko told the “Parliamentary newspaper ”.
Someone just has the opportunity to choose the best conditions of life and work.
Others have the pressure of economic circumstances.
This is facilitated by the growing class of precariat (people working in low-paid and unstable jobs without social guarantees - sick leave, vacation, with a reduced salary).
The transition from permanent to part-time, temporary, part-time employment makes it easier for such people to get out of place and go wherever they look.
Another category is those who, in principle, do not care about the content of the work, says the scientist.
They expect to find something to do everywhere.
From here the ease of lifting.
Finally, there are those who choose a way of life where civil obligations do not prevail over them.
An expert from the United States John Peters in a sensational article “Exile, Nomadism and the Diaspora ” called the opposition of nomad and state as the key idea of the movement.
Many travelers begin with the term “climate emigration ”, but constant mobility erases the boundaries of cultural and national identity.
As a result, the concept of homeland is also being rethought, and this is already marginality, he concludes.
A typical portrait of a digital nomad, according to the Nomad List survey, is a minimalist with a laptop, a backpack, a bachelor ’ s degree, a passport and a cup of coffee.
Lives in one place for an average of 70 days.
At the heart of the mentality is anti-materialism and contentment with small things.
The most attractive side of travel is cheapness, according to one of the profile sites.
Nomadism saves a lot of money because the costs of maintaining the property, maintaining the car, parking, winter clothes disappear.
It is fascinating and good for health.
The main cost item is renting a roof over your head and food.
Geo-arbitrage helps to live better and cheaper – the use of price differences between countries.
Peace in your pocket and nothing of your own
Some researchers call traveling a new socio-economic model.
It echoes the program slogans of the “great reset ” of the world proclaimed at the Davos Economic Forum.
According to it, the preservation of the planet in the interests of future generations requires tightening the belts of the living, limiting economic growth and reducing consumption.
The projected image of the future assumes that a person will be available to the whole world, a lot of services, but at the same time he will not have anything of his own.
Globalizers argue that property and binding to a permanent place of residence burden and encroach on the personal freedoms of citizens.
Why buy a house when you can rent it?
Why a personal car when there is carsharing?
Why save money when you can have a basic guaranteed income?
Why spend money on heating an apartment, if you can go to the warm lands for the winter?
When a person has no stake or yard, it is especially easy.
Modern nomads often call themselves citizens of the world.
The nomad is always online, and it is more convenient for him to communicate even with friends online, rather than offline.
Therefore, some experts have given it the definition of “connected person ”.
The unwritten motto of digital nomads: movement is everything, goal is nothing.
There are 300 people in the world who have visited all 196 countries of the world (including unrecognized territories).
Among them are Australian Rach and Slovak Marty.
The women described the adventures of the 15-year-old circumnavigation in the blog “Very Hungry Nomads ”.
They set out to inspire the women of the world to live without office stress, work on the beach, expand horizons and embrace new thinking.
Travelers sold out all the property and lived with luggage from two backpacks of hand luggage.
The focus of their project was food.
Odyssey cost 274 thousand dollars.
Her conclusion: the most delicious food is in Ethiopia, Afghanistan and Uzbek farmers.
The number of nomadism activists in Russia is also increasing.
For example, ethnologist Mikhail Zarubin traveled to 193 countries for 10 years and wrote a book for children “Tales of Young Travelers ”.
Four years more spent on the circumnavigation of his friend, the photographer.
150 hotels annually - the norm for Lisa and Vitalik, whose journey lasts 12 years.
Many other travel bloggers share their impressions on the website travcave.ru.
Traffic infrastructure
The digital nomad relies on infrastructure.
A digital nomad visa allows individuals who earn an income of at least $2,000 from a foreign jurisdiction to legally stay in the country longer than tourists.
Its price in Brazil is 72 dollars, in Greece - 75, Costa Rica - 100, Argentina - from 120 to 240, in Bermuda - 260, in the Bahamas and in the UAE - a thousand dollars.
Validity from 180 days to 10 years.
In countries where there is no such visa, nomads often live on tourist and even student, and the authorities turn a blind eye to this.
The elements of infrastructure are also coworking and coliving (common spaces where you can live and work with like-minded people).
The number of the first, according to forecasts, by 2025 will reach 26 thousand, and the second annually grows by a third.
In Russia, too, there is a coliving - "Station Smena".
It provides, according to the presentation, a unique opportunity to combine work and party.
Remotely you can work from home, public libraries, cafes - if only there was an Internet and a laptop.
The wealthier ones move around in offices on wheels.
However, the vans at home with a table, a lot of sockets, chargers and a background for conferences are like a luxury German crossover.
The system of hubs for nomads is characterized by a favorable climate, high-speed Internet, an easy visa regime and a low cost of living.
The most attractive locations are Chiang Mai (Thailand) and Bali (Indonesia), in Europe - Lisbon, Gran Canaria and the island of Madeira, in America - Medellin, Mexico City and Buenos Aires.
If the money runs out, nomads can spend the night in churches for free, in extreme cases - in a tent, especially since they do not tend to cold lands.
Someone on occasion earns remote trade, hand-made, bartenders, guides, DJs and VJs, nurses, teachers and what God will send.
As befits a philosopher, Jean Toshchenko is not surprised:
“The world is entering an era of great migration of peoples, similar to the one that took place 15 centuries ago.

Russian scientists have figured out how to dramatically increase the performance of a quantum computer
Scientists from Russia have found a way to increase the performance of a quantum computer.
To do this, they used qudits, which allow you to significantly reduce not only the number, but also the time of calculations.
And this, in turn, will allow you to run more complex and complex quantum algorithms.
A new approach
Russian scientists have figured out how to increase the performance of a quantum processor.
This CNews told representatives of the National Research Technological University MISIS.
Scientists from MISIS and the Russian Quantum Center (RCC) have proposed a new approach for launching quantum algorithms using additional levels of the quantum system.
The method improved the final quality of quantum algorithms.
This article was published in the scientific journal Entropy.
Qubits and Qudits
Now most of the research on quantum operations is focused on qubits - all operations that apply to a quantum system are represented in the form of one- and two-qubit quantum gates that convert the input states of qubits at the weekend according to a certain law, the representatives of MISIS note.
Photo: MISIS
Head of the Laboratory of Quantum Information Technologies MISIS Alexey Fedorov
The main way to improve the performance of quantum processors is to increase the number of their qubits (the smallest unit of information in a quantum computer).
At the same time, ions or atoms, which often act as qubits, have more than two levels and can work not only as qubits, but also as qubits (an expanded version of a qubit).
There are three (three), four (four), five (five), and four (four).
These states allow for denser encoding of data in physical media.
And allow you to run more complex and complex quantum algorithms.
Thus, the power of the quantum processor increases and operations can be performed much faster.
What is the novelty
Scientists of MISIS and RCC considered one of the ways of using kukvintov (five-level kudites) and presented an effective model of decomposition of the generalized Toffoli valve.
As an example, Grover's quantum algorithm for searching through a disordered database is considered.
Using only this valve, you can build any reversible classical logic scheme, for example, an arithmetic device or a classical processor.
The advantage of qubits is that their space can be considered as the space of two qubits with a common additional level, explained the head of the laboratory of quantum information technologies MISIS Alexei Fedorov.
This helps to simultaneously reduce the number of physical media, and use the additional layer as an auxiliary state to simplify the decomposition of multi-qubit valves (complex logical operations with qubits) or reduce their number.
This improves the quality of the algorithms.
The results obtained by the scientists apply to quantum processors based on various physical platforms, such as ions, neutral atoms, superconducting circuits and others.
Quantum computers in Russia
In December 2021, Russia created a prototype of a quantum ion computer of four qubits.
The prototype was created within the framework of the “road map ” on quantum computing, carried out by Rosatom.
On its basis, by the end of 2024, they are going to build a universal quantum computer with cloud access.
In 2021, the state corporation allocated more than 6 billion rubles for the development of quantum technologies and the creation of the necessary research infrastructure.
By 2024, more than 23 billion rubles will be allocated for the creation of a quantum computer.
In 2022, physicists increased the power of a quantum computer to five qubits.
On April 5, 2023, remote access to an ion computer was opened in Russia for the first time.

Small changes bring great benefits to cognitive function
In just six months, Duke University researchers found cognitive improvements in the adults involved in their study.
Dr. James Blumenthal, a clinical psychologist at Duke University, led the research published in Neurology.
He believes this was the first study to look at the separate and combined effects of diet and exercise on cognitive decline in those who are more vulnerable to developing dementia in old age.
The study involved 160 adult patients with a prior history of high blood pressure or other cardiovascular risks who had never exercised and had cognitive problems in executive functioning.
Those who were diagnosed with dementia were excluded.
The median age was 65 and two thirds of the participants were women.
At the beginning of the study, the participants' average cognitive skills were the same as those of 93 years old - an average of 28 years older than their actual age.
The volunteers were divided into four groups.
The former participated in a structured aerobic exercise program for the first three months, and in the following three months they were given exercises to do at home.
The second group was asked to follow a low-sodium DASH diet and was taught this program.
The third group was asked to exercise and change their diet at the same time.
A fourth group served as a control group and received a 30-minute training session over the phone on how to improve brain health, but they were asked not to change their training program or eating habits.
Results showed a decrease in brain age by nine years
Before starting the study, each participant underwent a set of cognitive tests, a treadmill stress test, and a nutrient intake analysis.
In addition, blood sugar and lipids were noted.
At the end of the study, the researchers found that those who followed the DASH diet without exercise had no significant improvement in their thinking skills.
The group that only trained had a greater improvement in executive functioning than the group that did not train.
But in the group that changed diet and exercised, the age of the brain decreased by nine years, bringing the average age of the brain to 84 years.
The executive function of the control group decreased by six months, which was expected as they were not subjected to intervention, and this was the total duration of the study.
Leg strength improves the health of the nervous system
Participants in the study were asked to walk for 35 minutes continuously or to cycle regularly just three times a week.
This study confirms other recent findings published in Frontiers in Neuroscience, showing that neurological health depends on both signals from the large leg muscles and signals from the brain to the muscles.
In other words, it is a double-edged sword, and both are equally important.

The government submitted to the State Duma a bill, in the case of adoption of which Russian companies will be required to levy a 30% tax on income of individuals (PIT) from payments to employees who have lost tax residency in the Russian Federation.

Farmer ’ s products store as an idea of agribusiness
A store with its own products and a cafe where these products and dishes from them can be tasted is a great idea for additional earnings for the farmer.
But not everyone decides to implement it: many are afraid that the extra hassle will be empty, and the time and money spent on the launch will go away like water in the sand.
In fact, it's not that difficult.
Farm shops are healthy products without pesticides, antibiotics and unnecessary additives, fresh vegetables and greens, fragrant buns from their own flour and much more.
And it is fashionable - the trend for a healthy lifestyle has been developing for more than 10 years, attracting more and more supporters and at the same time buyers to stores with eco-products.
A classic example is the chain of stores VkusVill, which appeared in Moscow in 2009, which is positioned as a brand of natural products with an honest composition.
Today, more than 1.4 thousand stores of the network in 72 cities choose 6.6 million customers.
The results of a survey conducted by Rosselkhozbank in 2022 showed that almost half of Russians believe that in the modern world, the use of farm products is part of a healthy lifestyle.
At the same time, 29% of survey participants admitted that they prefer variety in the daily diet and are ready to allocate time to buy fresh products.
The example of VkusVila shows that farm products have become so popular that many are willing to drive an extra metro station to the farmer ’ s market to buy them, or try delicious food without GMOs and preservatives from “clean ” foods in public catering.
Further, more.
Citizens are ready to come for shopping and to the farm, where the freshness and organic products can be obtained without intermediaries.
For example, in the Istrinsky cheese factory of Oleg Sirota, where a thousand cows, a bakery, a cafe, a shop, and a guest house are perfectly combined.
But the first one here was a cheese factory, which opened almost 8 years ago.
On their land: relief for farmers
Until 2022, farmers could sell their own products only in markets and fairs, trade on their plots was prohibited.
Farmers' lands are agricultural lands, using them for trade meant misuse of the site.
But there was a request from the farmers.
In addition, local products get to the consumer faster, so they do not need to add preservatives, which means they are healthier than imported ones.
However, if you allow to build commercial real estate on agricultural lands, the fields around the cities will quickly be built up with hypermarkets.
Therefore, the government decided to give the go-ahead to trade “in the field ”, and on its land, only to farms and agricultural cooperatives.
The opportunity to sell the grown crop directly on their land for farmers appeared after the introduction of amendments to the Federal Law No. 407-FZ “On Amendments to Article 19 of the Federal Law“ On Peasant (Farm) Economy ” and certain legislative acts of the Russian Federation ”.
Trading according to general rules
But the relaxation applies only to the location of the outlet or store.
To open a store near your home, the farmer needs to meet several conditions:
• Have the status of a farmer.
• The trading space should be located in a special non-capital structure: in a pavilion, a kiosk, a building fenced off from the house or even in a van.
• Trade should not disrupt the integrity of the soil layer, so trading premises should not be located on arable land, reclaimed land or particularly valuable productive agricultural land.
For example, you can not build a store in the middle of the field, but you can place a trading tent next to the arable land and sell fresh farm products to everyone.
In addition, you will have to follow all the basic rules of the retail trade.
First, the products must have the necessary certificates and be sold through the cashier.
Secondly, the requirements for commercial premises on farm land, as well as for any other retail outlets, are determined by legislation in the field of ensuring the sanitary and epidemiological well-being of the population.
Legal norms in this area and in the field of consumer protection already contain exhaustive requirements for objects of trade both in non-residential premises of residential buildings and in non-stationary objects of trade.
New ones will not be introduced specifically for farmers.
As for the current requirements for retail trade, we are primarily talking about SanPiNakh, relating to the sale of food.
So, in order to sell products on the street without violations, you need to equip a canopy.
It will protect the goods from rain and sun.
Perishable products should be stored in refrigerators.
If the farmer opens a store, he must provide a packing area for the products, a warehouse and a restroom for the sellers.
Just like in a regular store.
What you can sell in a farmer ’ s shop
Everything that farms produce.
These are carcasses of chickens, geese, ducks, rabbits, quails, pork, beef, chicken and quail eggs, mushrooms, butter and sunflower, cheese, milk, cottage cheese, sausages, seasonal fruits, vegetables and greens.
Beekeeping products, fruit drinks and juices, mashed berries and vegetables.
In short, at least foie gras, if the farmer himself grew the ducks.
Control and control again
If the store sells food, you need to be prepared for control.
Moreover, the assortment is mainly a speed port.
Before opening your own store, you need to inform the regulatory authorities that you are starting a business.
Retail and catering will need to notify Rospotrebnadzor.
It is most convenient to do this through the portal of public services.
It's an important moment.
If everything is not ready for the start, it is better not to hurry.
The notification means that the business is already operating in compliance with all sanitary and epidemiological regulations.
For example, if your store has not completed the repair, wait for its completion - and only then contact the department.
Then, in the case of verification, you will not have any problems.
By the way, the store will need permits from the SES - for compliance of the store and products in it with the standards and the fire service - for the safety of the outlet.
It is necessary to conclude a contract for the removal of household waste.
If you sell food, you will need to register with FGIS "Mercury".
This is a system of control of meat, milk, honey and other goods that are subject to veterinary certification.
If you plan to sell wine from berries grown in your own vineyard or garden, you will have to obtain a permit for the sale of alcohol in addition to the license for the production of wine.
How much does it cost to build
The amount can vary greatly depending on the location, area and other factors.
For example, whether you need to build a room for a store, or you plan to convert the existing building - or prefer to put a tent for the sale of watermelons right next to your melons.
Of course, the cost of opening a store will be higher.
You will need commercial equipment:
• racks, counters, slides;
• refrigerated cabinets for meat, dairy products and vegetables;
• refrigerating and freezing lari;
• baskets;
• inventory – cutting boards, knives, basins, boxes;
• cash register;
• cash scales;
• cash box.
In addition to commercial equipment, you may need other equipment - air conditioning, video surveillance system, as well as a scanner.
It is connected to the checkout to add goods to the check by barcode.
The scanner is required for the sale of labeled goods and strong alcohol.
Another item of expenditure is staff salaries and taxes on payroll.
This is at least two salespeople, a cleaner to maintain cleanliness in the store and an accountant.
However, the farmer himself can stand behind the counter, especially at the beginning of the project, when it is important to attract a buyer.
Who better to tell the farmer about their products?
Of course, in any case, the new business will require additional costs.
Rosselkhozbank offers agricultural producers several types of loans for development.
For example, the "Investment Standard" loan, loans for the creation of family farms and / or workshops for the processing of livestock products and loans for investment purposes.
A little about taxes
An old English proverb says that only death and taxes are inevitable.
Of course, the new type of activity will also have to allocate funds to the budget.
What taxes will have to be paid and how much depends on the taxation system chosen by the farm.
The list of tax payments depends on the chosen tax regime and on who should pay them: the CFC-organization or the head of the CFH, registered as an individual entrepreneur.
According to the Tax Code, the peasant farm (legal entity) can choose one of the existing tax systems.
Depending on this, the CFC pays certain taxes.
The first five years after the registration of the KFH do not need to charge and pay personal income tax from the income of its participants from the production, processing and sale of agricultural products, except for those for whom such exemption has already been applied before.
The head of a peasant (farm) economy registered as an individual entrepreneur can apply the patent system (PSN).
The base rate is 6% of the potential annual income established by the constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
If he additionally conducts other entrepreneurial or professional activities, then from the amount of income from this activity, exceeding 300 000 rubles. for the billing period, he pays 1% (but up to a certain limit) for his pension insurance.
In addition, when carrying out business activities without the formation of a legal entity, the head of the KFH will have to independently calculate and pay personal income tax (PIT), as well as submit a tax return on PIT.
But the income received in this economy from the production and sale of agricultural products, its processing and the sale of other members of the KFH are not subject to personal income tax for five years, counting from the year of registration of the economy.
If the farm employs workers, then the head of the KFH or a legal entity will act as tax agents.
They have to calculate and keep the NFL.
In addition, KFH and individual entrepreneurs are obliged to pay land and transport tax regardless of the taxation system.
Let's summarize.
With the opening of the store, the land tax will not change, but the property tax and personal income tax may increase.
The first - with the advent of equipment for the store, the second - with payments to employees.
The remaining taxes are paid according to the previous scheme, but the amounts may also increase.
For example, on the general tax system, with the advent of profit from trade, the amount of tax will increase.
Farmer 's cafe
Where there is a store, there is a cafe: buyers will be able to try various dishes, pastries and drinks from those products that came from the city.
But opening a catering point will require additional permits and approvals.
The legislation does not give any preferences for farmers' cafes.
Approximate package of documents:
• coordination with fire inspection;
• sanitary-epidemiological conclusion from Rospotrebnadzor for compliance with the requirements of the cafe;
• permission to open a cafe from the local administration;
• a license to sell alcohol, if you sell it;
Practice shows that it is most difficult to get permission from Rospotrebnadzor to open a cafe: for this you need to comply with the requirements of several SanPiN.
The Agency will request contracts for disinfection, garbage removal, laundry services, technological project of binding the equipment to electricity, water, sewerage and other documents.
Next, a program of sanitary production control will be approved, according to the plan of which the further activities will be checked.
A farm cafe can increase store sales by 50% due to the fact that visitors who come to eat will definitely come to the store - and if they liked it, they will come again or order the delivery of products home.

Manager of an Estonian company about a four-day work week: experience shows that it is doable
Over time, more innovative ways of working begin to penetrate the Estonian work culture.
Today, the most attention is paid to the shortened working week: for example, a four-day working week or a six-hour working day.
These approaches seem exciting to many, but the fear that they will negatively affect the organization of work, often becomes an obstacle in their implementation in practice.
Elisa manager Joosep Põllumäe noted that while the fear of innovative working methods is understandable, with the right organizational culture, proper pre-planning and strong support systems, confusion resulting from overtraining can be avoided in most cases.
For example, a four-week workweek has been successfully tested twice in Elisa ’ s technology department, which has more than 200 employees.
From now on, it will become a permanent summer mode for IT teams.
“If in recent decades everyone has known that there are forty hours a week to do work, and you can ask for help from colleagues every day from nine to five, then one day off can be a real shock, ” he said.
You just need to know which problem areas to focus on. ”
According to Põllumäe, in order for the introduction of new ways of working to go as smoothly as possible, it is first of all important to focus on establishing clear rules of the game, clear communication and the most accurate measurements.
Expectations should converge
Working four days a week, one weekday is free for the employee.
However, the details associated with this basic thesis may vary from company to company.
Therefore, according to Põllumäe, it is important that all parties involved in the organization of work understand these details equally.
For example, you should establish whether the day off is completely free, or it will be a day of study, a day of concentration or something else.
It is also important to determine who can be disturbed on the fifth day and on what issues, what changes will be made to the organization of work in the remaining four days, so that the work continues to be carried out.
“Employees need to clearly understand what is expected of them and what means are at their disposal to achieve their goals – whether they can cancel meetings, refuse additional tasks, work more from home.
Similarly, employers need to understand what employees expect.
For example, if a four-day work week includes one completely free day, you need to understand that employees do not want to be covered with working letters on this day, ” Põllumäe said.
Work must be measurable
Since expectations of attainable results do not decrease when working hours are shortened, one of the secrets to the success of the new organization of work is clear measurements and a concrete understanding of when the work is done.
According to Põllumäe, the more abstract someone ’ s role or the wider the range of tasks, the more likely it is that some important topics will go unnoticed, or people will always feel that they have to do more, and therefore will not dare to take a day off.
“Employees usually want to exceed expectations.
Try to do as much as possible in five working days.
However, if the employer suddenly allows an employee to take a day off in the case of work performed, then without clear measurements, it is difficult for some employees to understand whether they have completed their tasks or not, - he explained. - That is why very clear measurements are important - thing X should be developed within a month, analysis Y should be completed within a quarter, no "ticket" should "hang" longer than Z days. "
The better people understand their expectations, the better they can plan their work and deliver results in less time.
Communication is important
Since no team or branch of a company operates in a vacuum, clear communication and listening to feedback are also critical to implementing innovative work practices.
For example, departments ordering work from the development department should understand that one day a week from the development department should not wait for answers.
The sales team should know that marketing will not launch new ads on a certain day, and management should understand that one day a week should not expect quick reports from employees.
“If everyone knows how others work, they adjust their work accordingly.
Knowing that the data sphere teams are not working on Friday, the necessary data will be requested on Thursday, he explained. – It is also important to ask for constant feedback – if it begins to seem that the absence of someone from the team is causing real damage to the business, or customers begin to feel their absence, something needs to be adjusted, for example, to change the day when they are absent, or alternate absent employees to always provide some cover. ”

Deliveries of Russian oil to India in April reached a historic high, for the first time exceeding the combined imports from Saudi Arabia and Iraq, Bloomberg reported.
India ’ s refusal to join Western sanctions is accompanied by a stubborn reluctance to support the US and its allies in Ukraine.

In turn, as reported by Reuters, India for the second month in a row accounts for more than 60% of Russian Urals oil exports.

Having failed to convince India, the G20 chair, to join the ceiling on Russian oil prices imposed as part of Western sanctions, the United States and its allies have also failed to secure political support for the “world ’ s largest democracy ” in Ukraine.
“Although key US allies in Europe and East Asia have supported Biden ’ s campaign on Ukraine and are providing it with more and more weapons, abandoning Russian energy sources, elsewhere Washington has faced resistance, ” the Washington Post reports.

“Peter Pan and Wendy ”: a master class on Disney remakes from the author of“ The Legend of the Green Knight ”
Review of Peter Pan and Wendy with Jude Law
On Disney + came the film "Peter Pan and Wendy" - a game remake of the "Disney" cartoon in 1953, filmed by the director of "Legends of the Green Knight" David Lowry.
Film critic "Gazeta.Ru" Pavel Voronkov looked at the tape and tells what a new reading of the fairy tale of James Barry about children who do not want to grow up, Lowry offers.
Wendy Moira Angela Darling (Ever Anderson, daughter of Milla Jovovich and Paul Anderson) starts a new life tomorrow.
But not what her parents had planned for her.
Instead of a boarding school for girls, she and her younger brothers go to Neverland, a magical country where the flying tomboy Peter Pan (debutant of the big screen Alexander Moloney), who refuses to grow up, lives with other Lost Boys (including not only boys) and fights evil pirates under the leadership of Captain Hook (Jude Law).
Game remakes of Disney cartoons - like global warming: bad, but it seems that there is nothing to do.
Unlike global warming, however, Disney remakes have positive aspects, or rather, individual glimpses of something intelligible in the flow of nonsense of varying degrees of monstrosity.
Peter Pan and Wendy, directed by The Legend of the Green Knight director David Lowry, is just one such glimpse.
A few years ago, Lowry already re-shot (quite successfully) for Disney another not the most obvious classic – the fantasy “Pete and his dragon ”.
“Peter Pan ” is a thing, of course, more famous, but still as if not included in the collection of priority hits of the studio: it is not“ The Lion King ”, not “The Little Mermaid ”, not“ Beauty and the Beast ”, not “Aladdin ” and not even“ Mulan ” with “Dumbo ”.
Hence, presumably, some not quite typical for such projects freedom, which Lowry seems to have given when working on the adaptation of the 1953 cartoon (in fact, this is not a remake, but simply a new adaptation of the story by James Barry, starting from the visual images of the “Disney ” tape).
Justifying a return to the original title of the story (as the book was published in 1911 under the title “Peter and Wendy ”), Lowry expands the role of Wendy, endows her with greater subjectivity, and at some point with some power (literal empowerment).
The same order of metamorphosis happens with Princess Tiger Lily (Alice Vapanatank), who ceases to be a racist stereotype and a misogynistic path, and with the Ting-Ding fairy (Yara Shahidi from “The grown-up ”), turned into a witty illustration of deaf male self-admiration, and with the Lost Boys (now it is not only boys, as already mentioned above, they are not only white, plus among them there is a child with Down syndrome, in general, the opportunity to see yourself on the screen appeared in the widest possible range of small viewers).
The main changes here, however, relate to the key male characters (that is, Pan and Hook), so that as a fem-manifesto, "Peter Pan and Wendy" are quite untenable, but in the sense of fairy tales about childhood - with quite unexpected theses - are quite amazing and touching.
Pan is not so great, Hook is not so nightmarish (or at least nightmarish not in the right place), childhood grievances are a terrible thing, and in fact all these questions should be brought to the psychotherapist, but in Neverland with specialists, obviously, it is not enough, you have to squeeze each other out of the light.
What is worth a separate praise - in the end it is a children's fairy tale, that is, no longer faceless and safe in all respects "Disney" hack, but not yet "The Legend of the Green Knight" on the "Disney" cheeks.
Familiar psychedelia Lowry still sometimes includes (quite miraculous movement from London to Neverland, well, and in principle regularly pulls to take a screenshot and press the print button), but "Peter Pan and Wendy" is not replete with meanings and subtexts, digging and deciphering here is especially nothing (at least, not in those quantities), but to be touched and moistened eyes - it easily.
More, perhaps, is not required.

On May 11, MEPs adopted the draft of the first international law on artificial intelligence.
The document was developed for two years, including taking into account the risks posed by neural networks.
The new rules, for example, oblige European developers to specify the materials on the basis of which they train AI.
Now neurons are used in almost all areas of the economy, but most of them require special knowledge and training.
However, there are several categories of AI that will facilitate the work of many professionals and without training.
More details in the material "News".
What Neural Networks Can Do
Neural networks are increasingly used in industries that are not related to IT technologies: for example, medicine, marketing, business, law, and so on.
They are designed for a specific and, as a rule, narrow task.
For example, it is possible to train AI on various signs to notice the symptoms of oncology even at the stage of contacting therapists and paramedics.
Such programs can be used exclusively by doctors, having previously been trained.
On the other hand, some categories of neural networks can be put into operation now and without preparation - all of them are associated with the processing of big data, the generation of content and the execution of the same type of actions, which people take a lot of time.
The neural network faster than a person finds dependencies and solutions for previously defined algorithms, and therefore, its use is justified for monotonous, template operations and can be convenient for automating routine tasks.
But any work departing from the previously set limits leads to errors.
Yes, of course, you can try to make a neural network for everything, but then you will need enormous computing resources, — explained “Izvestia ” software engineer, an AI specialist Sergey Smyslov.
Photo: Global Look Press / dpa / Sven Hoppe
According to Kirill Pshinnik, CEO of Zerocoder, neural networks show good results in the tasks of natural language processing: automatic translation, text generation, chatbots and text tonality analysis.
In this case, they can achieve accuracy in the tasks of classifying texts more than 90% – for example, when classifying reviews in online stores.
In addition, neural networks show progress in the generation of content - images, texts, music and video.
At the same time, the quality of visual content created by the neural network has changed dramatically in recent months.
Such content can already compete with the created person, as confirmation of this – the victory of the image created with the help of DALL-E in the prestigious international photo competition Sony World Photography Awards, ” he noted.
Who will benefit from text generation
According to experts, now two types of generative neural networks are most adapted to a wide range of tasks - text and "picture".
As Nikita Dubinkin, the head of the Prex Internet service, told Izvestia, such text generative models as ChatGPT, Google Bard, Microsoft Bing search engine or GigaChat are trained to understand natural language and are available to a wide range of users.
Some of them have an open architecture, so enthusiasts and private companies create applications and services to solve narrow application problems.
For example, the official browser extension for YouTube from ChatGPT creates a text summary of the video and highlights key points.
Write Release helps PR writers write press releases, WriteSonic — create content for social networks, Audioread will translate any text into audio.
The service of the Russian startup Optic AI or Not quickly recognizes whether the picture is drawn by a person or a neural network.
KickResume is sharpened to create a good resume.
And so on — services of all kinds and purposes with simple functionality appear more and more every day, — said the expert.
Photo: Global Look Press / dpa / Karl-Josef Hildenbrand
At the same time, the text neural network ChatGPT writes more competently, more interesting and faster than a person who is prone to fatigue and, perhaps, little interested in conveyor work, notes Alexander Zhukov, director of development of the software development company Format Code.
Usually these are moments associated with writing a lot of unique descriptions: products for online stores, simple articles for sites, publications on forums, as well as filling commercial blogs and many other tasks about sales, marketing and digital content.
For example, the tasks of SEO-optimization, when the network writes meaningful fragments of text referring to the promoted site, he told the publication.
Such generative models are suitable for other specialists working with the same type of texts, for example, copywriters.
In addition, AI is able to write letters and respond to them, which has already been evaluated by employees of the HR sphere.
How to process media using neural networks
Services that create a picture from a text description are also easy to use.
But experts emphasize: for their application you need to have minimal skills of promting, that is, writing a request.
The more accurately it is formed, the better the result will be.
The most common “drawing ” neural networks are Midjourney, Stable Diffusion or DALL-E, as well as Russian“ Kandinsky 2.0 ” and “Shedevrum ”.
They can create illustrations for presentations, websites, leaflets, booklets, etc.
— Since a lot of people have been creating various logos and pictures recently, neural networks are well trained on such data.
For example, Tome.app makes presentations, Midjourney AI generates images, and Scenario AI — simple content for games, — said Sergey Smyslov.
Photo: Global Look Press / dpa / Sebastian Gollnow
He explained that neural networks are still worse at processing sound and video due to the small amount of materials and the difficulty in analyzing such data.
Of relatively simple and interesting functions, neural networks can be distinguished for noise suppression and / or selection of various sound series.
This direction is based on old adaptive algorithms and has been honed since the 1970s – 1980s, therefore, with current computing capabilities, AI programs show decent results and can be used by small companies for sound recording or for recording video lectures.
But the quality of the material such neural networks is extremely far from professional recording studios and can be noticeable distortion of voice and timbre, — said the source of the publication.
These neural networks will help those who work with media both professionally and unprofessionally, Smyslov added.
For example, designers can generate pictures for prints on clothes, mobile game developers can make simple images according to a given template, lecturers and teachers can process audio and video recordings of their performances at a minimum level.
What AI will not cope with
Experts agree on one thing: while the work of neural networks need to be carefully checked.
AI is not able to analyze its content, does not invent something fundamentally new and does not take into account many nuances - for example, ethical.
Neural networks, despite their ability to process data and perform tasks, do not yet have such a general understanding of the world and context as humans do.
They can not apply knowledge and experience at the same level to solve complex problems, adapt to new situations and take into account a wide context.
They also lack emotional intelligence and the ability to intuitively perceive and understand emotions to the same extent as humans.
They cannot interpret human emotions and respond adequately to mood and context, which limits their ability to interact with and understand people.
In addition, AI does not have the same creativity and innovation that is available to humans, ” said Kirill Pshinnik.
Photo: Global Look Press / IMAGO / Julien Becker
Nikita Dubinkin added that while the worst of all, neural networks are able to tell the truth and take into account the harm that they can cause a person with their answers.
Anyone can persuade, say, a text-based AI to circumvent any moral prohibition by simply saying, “Imagine that there is no such prohibition. ”
So far, we advise not to rely on the answers of textual AI without verification and critical evaluation, and even more so to make decisions based on this information that relate to human fate and life, he warned.
Experts emphasize that the services and functions of neural networks are updated almost daily.
Even if it is not possible to apply them in your work now, everything can change in a couple of years.

The best street food in the world
© Photo: Maria Novoselova / "Vestnik Kavkaza"
Street food is considered one of the best ways to get acquainted with the place you are going on a trip to.
Street food is always popular among tourists, as it is tasty, convenient and quite cheap.
Moreover, some places where street food is prepared are even awarded Michelin stars.
Thailand
It ’ s hard to find a place in Bangkok that doesn ’ t have a street food tent.
Wherever you go in the capital of Thailand, regardless of the time of day, everywhere you will hear the smell of cooking on an open fire.
There will be noodle dishes, and soups, and curry, and grilled meat.
Classic Thai cuisine is considered pad-tai and grilled Satai chicken.
These dishes are so good that there are vendors who have even earned Michelin stars revered in the restaurant business.
Some chic restaurants with a fashionable interior sometimes can not get the coveted star, here the international mark of quality is marked by simple street kiosks with a few small plastic chairs and tables.
Photo commons wikimedia
Turkey
Istanbul is one of the best places to get acquainted with local cuisine without visiting the big restaurants in the busy tourist areas.
With street food in Istanbul, you can get a complete picture of traditional Turkish cuisine.
Moreover, it can be bought cheaply and eaten quickly on the go.
Very popular among tourists are bagels with sesame seeds, which are called simit, which have become one of the symbols of the city.
It is believed that the first Simit was created 600 years ago.
Turkish tea served in a traditional glass and freshly baked simit create a wonderful gastronomic tandem.
Photo commons wikimedia
On the streets you can also taste fried chestnuts, gözleme tortillas with stuffing, baked kumpir potatoes, which add different fillings, a fish sandwich with vegetables and greens - balyk ekmek, as well as Turkish sweets.
Viet Nam
The history of Vietnam can be studied not only in local museums, but also to taste.
Through Vietnamese cuisine, you can trace the influence of various peoples on this country.
For example, the Chinese influence can be felt in baking, French - in sandwiches, Malaysian - in sauces.
Different regions of the country have special taste characteristics, so the food you meet in different cities will be significantly different.
In the north of the country, thinner spices are used, the central part is not indifferent to chili peppers, and in the southern regions prefer sweet products.
Different taste preferences are noticeable in the preparation of the national dish of fo soup with noodles and beef.
Photo commons wikimedia
Very popular here are mini-baguettes - bath mi, rice pancakes, as well as such extremely exotic national dishes as balut - duck egg, in which the embryo has already formed.
India
India produces 75% of the world ’ s spices, which are added to dishes around the world.
The origins of street food in India can be traced back to the time when Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan moved his capital from Agra to Delhi.
Chaat appetizer, the most popular type of Indian street food, first appeared in Old Delhi at that time.
Chaat became popular as a snack after officials of the Mughal dynasty invited cooks from Varanasi to open a shop in Delhi.
Photo commons wikimedia
In India, you can also taste many other interesting dishes.
For example, pani puri - fried in oil hollow balls of dough, the filling of which can vary.
Also popular are dahi wada - lentil pancakes soaked in yogurt.
They can be seasoned with various spices.
This dish is considered popular during the holidays, but it is also often sold at street food stalls.
If you want to be sure that eating local food will not affect your health, many advise you to go to special gastronomic tours with a professional guide.

The majority (81%) of Russian companies support the idea of reducing the working week to four days, while only 4% consider this possibility in the coming years, according to a study by hh.ru (Izvestia).
The main advantage of the four-day plan is the reduction of burnout among employees, the main drawback is the need to cut wages.
Today, business in Russia is not ready for such changes due to the insufficiently stable economy, experts say.
Nothing interferes
The reduction of the working week, advocated by 81% of employers, mainly supports large business.
However, the transition to such a schedule in the next three years is considered by only 4% of companies.
Even fewer are already working in a reduced week - this was told by 1% of companies with less than 50 and more than 3 thousand employees.
Such results were shown by a survey of the HeadHunter service, conducted in May among almost 700 enterprises at the request of Izvestia.
Economically, a shortened working week means a more flexible approach to the formation of a wage fund and increasing employee loyalty.
In the operational business, as well as the entire economy, continues to be under the influence of deep transformational processes caused by external circumstances.
Companies are not yet ready for another factor of possible tension in unstable current conditions, - explained the main expert on the labor market hh.ru Natalia Danina.
Photo: Getty Images / Matthias Kulka
The main advantages in the transition to a four-day period were the reduction of burnout of employees and more efficient use of working time.
In turn, the main disadvantage is the need to reduce wages for employees.
Among the risks, they also noted a reduction in productivity and bureaucratic difficulties.
Reducing the working week can favorably contribute to the development of the company, said the Director of personnel and organizational development of the service "Rabota.ru" Julia Sanina.
For example, the productivity of employees can increase by increasing their free time.
However, it is possible that the business will need additional staff to ensure continuous operation, and this, in turn, additional costs, the expert noted.
According to Article 91 of the Labor Code of the Russian Federation, normal working hours cannot exceed 40 hours per week.
That is, now nothing in the regulatory field does not prevent to switch to a four-day, having organized a shift schedule, said the head of the expert center for labor relations and labor protection of Business Russia, co-founder of the SRG group of companies Vitaly Fedin.
It is worth noting that in recent years there has been a trend of actual increase in working hours.
The corporate culture of Russian business often suggests that employees in offices significantly recycle and the schedule is stretched to 45-50 hours per week, the expert added.
Photo: Getty Images / Thomas Barwick
The four-day work week is something to strive for in the near future, Dmitry Medvedev, deputy chairman of the Security Council, told reporters in January 2022.
He added that it is necessary to make such a decision as the economic prerequisites mature, for individual industries and industries, and based on the general economic situation in the country.
Earlier it was reported that Kazakhstan is going to introduce a four-day period from July 1 of this year.
Amendments to the Labor Code have already been approved by the President of the country.
A similar experiment was also conducted in the UK, Belgium and other EU countries.
“Izvestia ” sent a request to the Ministry of Labor.
Transition to three years
As a rule, the shortened week was previously introduced in developed countries to manage the unemployment rate or against the background of the formation of a structural shortage of personnel, said Natalia Danina from hh.ru.
This was also done to “cool ” production cycles in the absence of demand or transfer the creation of products to other countries.
Recent examples of the introduction of four-day experiments are typical mainly for large technology giants, she stressed.
The desire to balance work and personal life intensified during the pandemic, when a huge number of people had the opportunity to work remotely, said Aghvan Mikaelyan, a member of the Board of Directors of the audit and consulting network FinExpertiza.
— Today, the global transition to a four-day period would be difficult to implement.
This requires either a significant increase in productivity, or a reduction in wages, or an increase in the cost of production.
So, to reduce the working week to four days, that is, by 20%, provided that wages are maintained at the same level, a proportional increase in the productivity of all employees would be required, the expert explained.
Photo: Izvestia / Konstantin Kokoshkin
It is not difficult to switch to a four-day period, it is enough to fix it by law, says Alexander Isaevich, CEO of the SME Corporation.
According to him, it is important that this was an additional option, not an obligation, since Russian citizens are accustomed to a certain level of service and want to receive services all seven days a week, and sometimes even at night.
The expert added that in the matter of reducing the working week, everything depends on the business sector.
For example, there are areas with continuous work, such as security activities, production and others.
Russia today is not ready for the introduction of the four-day plan.
There are serious problems with the structure of the workforce.
Despite the low unemployment rates, a significant part of the employed work at fractional rates for low salaries, and the shortage of personnel is combined with the lack of vacancies in depressed territories and in a number of sectors, ” said Aghvan Mikaelyan.
At the beginning of the adaptation to the new schedule, productivity may temporarily subside, so the transition to a four-day in Russia should be gradual and consistent, taking into account the specifics of business sectors, said Dmitry Puchkov, Director for Development of the Avito Work Platform.
According to the expert, the process of transition to a four-day period in the country can take from one to three years.

According to the non-profit organization Center for AI Safety (CAIS), artificial intelligence can lead to the disappearance of humanity.
This is not the first warning of this kind.
In a relatively short time, several reputable scientists and entrepreneurs have claimed the destructive potential of artificial intelligence.

What to be afraid of?
The American “AI Security Center ” published an official statement.
It details a number of negative effects of the use of AI, which could eventually lead to the disappearance of humanity.
“A more advanced AI could pose catastrophic and existential risks, ” reads the text published on the organization ’ s website.
Eight threats have been identified.
The first is related to the military application of artificial intelligence technologies: “Unlike other types of weapons, AI systems capable of causing harm can be easily distributed digitally. ”
The second is disinformation: “… all this can undermine the collective decision-making system, radicalize individuals … ”.
The third risk is the distortion of the work of recommendation algorithms.
These systems, for example, offer us additional products on online marketplaces.
The fear is that more advanced models will focus on simplifying the process of predicting the desires of the buyer, which can cause people to develop bad habits and so on.
The fourth threat is associated with a sharp increase in the dependence of people on advanced systems, up to the delegation of the most ordinary tasks to them.
The fifth is an even greater concentration of wealth and influence in the hands of a limited number of people who can use it to monopolize power in society.
The sixth threat is the emergence of goals and abilities.
In other words, models can set new goals and develop skills that are not foreseen during their training.
The seventh is related to the deception by AI.
The statement cites an example where Volkswagen programmed engines to show low emissions only during inspections.
In the same way, according to experts, artificial intelligence can do.
The eighth and, perhaps, the biggest threat is the desire for power.
According to CAIS, the risks of artificial intelligence becoming more independent cannot be ruled out: “By inventing more advanced machines, we are playing with fire. ”
CAIS experts conclude: “Reducing the risk of extinction due to AI should be a global priority along with risks such as pandemics and nuclear war. ”
We warned
The company ’ s arguments resonated in many areas.
Signatures under the statement put not only scientists and programmers, but also journalists and businessmen.
The most significant are the autographs of the “godfather ” of AI Jeffrey Hinton and OpenAI ’ s CEO Sam Altman.
Earlier, they had already talked about the dangers of AI.
“I ’ m pretty concerned about the possible existential risks that might arise when these things get smarter than us … I ’ ve come to the conclusion that [artificial] intelligence is different from ours.
It is as if one person learned something, and with him 10 thousand people learned the same thing.
That ’ s how these chatbots know more than anyone. ”
Moderate AI pessimists were also recorded by representatives of BigTech, Elon Musk, as well as Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak.
In their March open letter, they demanded that the development of better language models be suspended.
Should we automate all jobs?
Should we develop non-human brains that could later become smarter … and replace us? ”
According to experts, a pause in the development of AI will provide an opportunity to understand the ethical and social risks that the technology presents.
In turn, this should contribute to the development of safer systems.
However, some companies oppose such steps, as it can harm their immediate interests.
According to Forbes, the majority of surveyed owners are confident in the positive impact of AI on their business.
This applies to improving the quality of service (64%), increasing sales (60%), as well as improving the process of corporate decision-making (44%).
Especially can be outraged by companies that have reached new heights due to the association with AI.
For example, Nvidia broke through the $1 trillion market cap thanks to the AI boom.
The counter-argument of the proponents of a pause in the development of advanced AI is that it will cause only short-term losses.
In their opinion, in the long term, a break and additional research can make the use of technology safer and, thereby, more effectively reduce business costs.
However, these arguments do not convince everyone.
Opponents of the suspension of the development of AI argue that the “bad actors ”, despite all the agreements, will still continue to adapt the technology to their needs.
GeopolIItica
Hence the calls to create a system of its legal regulation of AI.
In the United States, for example, the first rudiments of such legislation appeared under Trump (2020), and in November 2022, the Biden administration published the plan of the Bill of Rights in the field of artificial intelligence.
Even more so, so far these are only sketches that have no force under them.
The situation is quite different in China.
By May 2023

For 6 years, since 2017, the PRC has been studying the legal aspects of the introduction of technology in most areas of life.
One of the goals of this activity is to increase public confidence in AI.
In addition, the presence of rules, according to Chinese experts, will allow entrepreneurs with greater confidence to use AI solutions in the activities of their companies.
A more global and longer-term goal could be to spread Chinese practices to other countries, giving Beijing an edge in technological competition with the United States.
On this account, there are many different considerations: some researchers are confident in the success of the Celestial Empire, another clarifies that the presence of a set of rules does not cancel the lag of China from the United States in some areas of AI (for example, large language models) - but all this only confirms the formation of artificial intelligence technologies as a subject of geopolitical struggle.
RESULTS
The potential risks of AI have been discussed for a long time.
For many years, they were treated superficially, as the beginning of the introduction of technology in everyday life seemed distant.
Nevertheless, the emergence of large language models, the gradual integration of AI solutions in the field of medicine, finance and even art forced experts to think.
Too fast the introduction of artificial intelligence, in their opinion, minimizes the chances of detecting problems in the work of the same language models.
And it seems that there will be more and more such voices.

The search for a usable quantum computer continues, but it could take decades before we have a powerful and reliable device that uses qubits for computing.
Meanwhile, classical calculations with zeros and ones are also evolving, and Nvidia ’ s hardware helps.
The GPU maker, in collaboration with Israeli startup Classiq and Rolls-Royce, has tested quantum algorithms to simulate extremely complex physics inside a jet engine.
It is reported that Rolls-Royce is now conducting a simulation of computational hydrodynamics in the design of a new jet engine.
If in simple terms, the modern jet engine is a rotating monster with blades, drawing in air at a speed of hundreds of kilometers per hour.
Understanding how air passes through an engine when the turbine rotates thousands of times per second is not an easy task for even the most powerful classical computers.
Rolls-Royce engineers have to scale down CFD models or accept a lower level of detail.
But the company believes that quantum computing could pave the way for more powerful and accurate simulations.
Unfortunately, the quantum computers at our disposal in 2023 do not cope with this task.
The most powerful quantum computers used in research have only a few dozen qubits (quantum bits), and their results are not particularly reliable.
However, quantum computing promises a leap forward several generations.
A fully realized quantum computer could use quantum mechanical properties such as spontaneity, superposition, and interference to speed up computations much faster than is possible with bits limited to 0 or 1.
Rolls-Royce used Nvidia A100 graphics cards to replace quantum computers.
The HHL-based algorithm that Rolls-Royce is developing could significantly accelerate the development of a new jet engine, but they don ’ t yet have a quantum computer to run it.
Nvidia doesn ’ t make chips for quantum computing, but it does have the A100 ’ s heavy-duty GPUs.
In collaboration with Nvidia, Rolls-Royce and Classiq have launched the latest quantum simulation scheme with 39 qubits on the A100 cards.
The company did not say how many graphics cards it used, but we can assume that there are a lot.
recommendations
Simulating quantum algorithms on classical hardware involves many challenges, but Rolls-Royce seems pleased with the result.
Lee Lapworth of Rolls-Royce told IEEE Spectrum that this is the first time the company has been able to model its HHL algorithm on a large enough scale to collect useful data.
The greatest interest in quantum computing has focused on applications such as integer factoring and database search, but simulations like the one being tested at Rolls-Royce show just how flexible the technology can be.

The advent of ChatGPT has sparked widespread debate about artificial general intelligence (AGI), in which machines outperform human intelligence.
This question was raised by Jeffrey Hinton, who is an influential figure in the field of artificial intelligence.
After leaving Google earlier this year, he gave several interviews in which he outlined his concerns about the technology.
Consequently, the number of research papers devoted to large language models (LLMs) — the type of artificial intelligence technology on which ChatGPT is based — has increased dramatically.
Other areas of AI research, such as conversational systems and information search, may lose out.
Against the backdrop of this rapid technological breakthrough, it seems that Google is afraid of losing its technological superiority and market dominance.
This concern is not unreasonable.
Created by a direct competitor, ChatGPT used Google ’ s pioneering internet search techniques to generate significant profits.
In addition, the flow of talent from Google to OpenAI — along with the rapid growth of the latter — has become an alarming trend for the search giant.

MOSCOW, July 4 — PRIME.
Fraudsters have learned to use artificial intelligence to deceive citizens in telephone conversations.
What schemes are used by cyber scammers, told the Agency "Prime" head of information security Center digital experts Roskachestvo Sergey Kuzmenko.
Cloning of voice
According to the expert, in this case we are talking not so much about artificial intelligence, but about a neural network with machine learning based on artificial intelligence.
“Thanks to the available technology, hackers only need a 20-second snippet of a conversation taken from a social network to create a clone of any person ’ s voice.
The identity is so striking that even a mother will not be able to distinguish her child ’ s voice from a robot, ” the expert said.
The scheme of deception is the same: the AI calls and asks to transfer money.
Criminals make victims think that they are talking to a relative who suddenly needed money, for example, to compensate for damage as a result of an accident.
Kuzmenko advised immediately to call back his family and friends, from whom the request was received.
It is even better to come up with a code word for your own, so that you can understand: relatives call, not fraudsters.
Imitation of the image
You can fake not only the voice, but also the image.
Using a technique for synthesizing media content based on artificial intelligence, it is possible to impose fake images or videos on real ones.
The technology is called "deepfake" (from the English deepfake - "fake". - Approx. ed.).
Abroad, the attackers tried deepfakes when applying for remote work in the field of IT to gain access to databases.
However, the created video clips give their artificial pace of speech, asynchronous and unnatural emotions.
New technologies are used not only by advanced IT companies, but also by groups of fraudsters.
A wave of deepfakes has already engulfed Southeast Asia and Africa.
It will also certainly reach Russia in the near future and will work according to the scheme of calls from “relatives ”, for example, elderly people, the expert of Roskachestvo warned.
Thus, the moment is not far off when deceptions with calls from law enforcement agencies and bank employees will be fully implemented by software algorithms based on neural networks.
How to recognize deepfake:
• Unnatural facial expressions – the movements of the lips do not fall in time with the spoken words, the same expression of the eyes, no change of emotions is visible.
• Low resolution, pixelation or fuzziness of the image, especially in areas with active facial expressions - eyebrows, corners of the mouth.
• The sound is ahead of the picture or does not keep up with the movements of the character.
The neural networks themselves also help to recognize fakes.
Technologies for creating and detecting deepfakes will be intensively developed in the future.
According to Kuzmenko, for the average user, the best way to protect yourself from deepfakes is to be vigilant, turn to reliable sources of information and follow the development of information technologies.

How to use AI when creating educational courses?
Columns
Tatyana Galkina
Director of iSpring Academy
Alina Aleshchenko
In various industry communities, there is an active discussion about whether AI and machine learning technologies should be applied in the field of education.
It is believed that soon neural networks will completely replace the developers of courses and other educational products.
But that's not true.
AI is a tool that helps and works only in experienced hands, without a “guide ” it is of little use.
How technologies will affect the quality of training, how they are used today by developers of EdTech solutions and what are the obstacles for the widespread introduction of AI in education, says Tatyana Galkina, director of the iSpring Academy.
How to use AI when creating educational courses?
Make artificial intelligence self-learn and improve – choose online courses in the catalog of courses on machine learning.
There are two important points that neural networks will help improve in the learning process.
• First, neural networks will save the sphere from excessive conservatism and clumsiness – AI becomes a good incentive for the study and use of new technologies.
Second, AI can accelerate the process of creating educational products for too long.
Often, courses become obsolete even in the development process, so speed is of great importance.
Reducing the time of content preparation will make training more relevant and timely.
We expect that in the near future, neural networks will allow corporate universities, online schools and universities to accelerate the development of courses - they will take over the function of packaging content.
Now they can be assigned part of the preparatory tasks.
Task number one – generation of images and texts
Developing courses, we use AI to search for interesting ideas, packaging content, generating selling, engaging titles for the course, images.
Experts, experienced designers, methodologists work with neural networks.
Usually it is quite difficult to find a finished image on the stocks that meets all the requests.
For example, a developer is looking for an illustration for the cover of a course about leadership competencies.
He needs the image of a strong, strong-willed pilot at the helm of the aircraft.
AI can offer its own options or adjust the finished picture: change the angle, colors, some details, and thus generate a unique illustration that can be further used in the work.
The main thing is not to forget that artificial intelligence is still not an expert, and the reliability of the content it creates always needs to be checked.
After all, the neural network, as an artist, can depict anything, even the jungle on Mars, in its own way interpret the elements of the clothes of the same aircraft pilot, draw non-existent in reality details.
Therefore, when developing training courses with the help of neural networks, you need to be extremely careful.
With images work:
Artificial intelligence is able to help with the generation of ideas, topics, structures, metaphors of the course, can write a dialogue between the manager and the client or come up with a test question with answers.
You can compare this with brainstorming an entire team, only it will take several times less time and effort.
But in this case, the work of the expert should be even more painstaking and thoughtful than with images.
Neural networks cannot be trusted implicitly — they may well come up with non-existent facts.

For example, we needed to create a course for retail employees about merchandising rules.
For the developer, this topic was new.
Going the standard way, he would have spent hours, if not days, to find sources of information, dive in, delve into and structure the course, or take the expert ’ s time to find out what needs to be included in the course.
AI helped to generate the structure in 5 minutes, it took another 15 minutes to check its adequacy and adjust it to the task of the course and send it to the expert for approval.
Further, for each item of the structure, the developer selected materials, including with the help of colleagues.
In this part of the work on the course, we no longer rely on AI.
In addition to ChatGPT, the generation of texts can be assigned to:
• CopyMonkey (analogues: ruGPT-3, Smodin) — 10 text formats are available.
• TurboText (analogues: Webcanape, WebX) — will come up with a title for a longread, course or text.
Task number two – work with sound and video
Virtual assistants help create unusual video effects to engage in the learning process.
In addition, there are tools for creating talking characters.
Neural networks are able to improve the quality and resolution of videos, process audio tracks and generate unique background music suitable for the course.
One of the frequent cases of using a neural network in training courses is voice acting by a robot.
No need to waste time searching for a speaker, recording in the studio.
You can just write a text, and the neural network will voice it.
It makes it a natural voice.
AI quite well understands the Russian text, accents, nuances of pronunciation.
Our course designer already has such functionality, and we actively use it ourselves.
In this segment will be useful:
• Gen-2 — changes the background of the video, removes unnecessary objects from the picture, adds the desired stylization.
• Synthesia Create — turns a script into a video course.
• iSpring Suite Max (analogues: Freetts, Text to Speech Online, VoxWorker) - one of the constructor tools turns text into voiceover for an online course or video.
• Boomy (analogue – MuseNet) – will generate a melody on request.
In addition, neural networks are used for:
• search for new ideas for the promotion of educational products;
• optimization and automation of the learning process;
• processing and ranking of reviews;
• writing macros to translate PDF files into pictures;
• development of standard TK.
For example, a developer sends a feedback questionnaire to Google Forms to those who have completed an online course in order to receive feedback.
Respondents write what they liked or did not like, the results are collected in the table.
How to process them?
You can unload all ready-made detailed answers and ask the neural network to rank them from the most negative to the most positive.
Or analyze and write down the 5 most positive points.
Task number three — specification of issues and language practice
In addition to generating and processing content, AI as an assistant can clarify user training questions and direct them to experts.
Such mechanics can now be traced in various chatbots - according to standard algorithms, they help to correctly formulate requests.
This also applies to training.
The second scenario is independent language practice.
With the same ChatGPT you can talk in any foreign language – check yourself after the lessons of the expert, consolidate the acquired knowledge.
To talk with the help of chatbots to learn is unrealistic, but they allow you to practice.
See also: Creating a website with the help of neural networks - from the logo to the final layout
What to entrust to AI is definitely not worth it
Especially carefully you need to approach the automation of assessments and verification of homework.
Artificial intelligence can invent any answer and then rely on it.
Therefore, the system of control over it should be very clearly thought out.
It is also better to form the educational trajectory and individual training programs personally, because the neural network does not take responsibility for the result of training.
It is not recommended to trust the AI to compile lists of literature, as they may appear non-existent books, sites and other sources.
It is also not necessary to instruct the neural network to write a script for working with some unique equipment or software, since it can take information not only from available documentation, but also come up with it.
Difficulties in implementation
The mass introduction of neural networks in educational processes is hampered by a number of serious factors:
• lack of control and verification of the created content;
• the risk of leakage of personal data and information constituting a trade secret.
In addition, the use of AI in education is expected to generate a large number of untested courses.
In the pursuit of profit, they will generate everything in a row, but only serious providers and large sites will monitor the reliability.
And this can have a negative impact on the quality of the training itself.
Market participants need a thoughtful and conscious approach, an understanding of what tasks need to be solved with the help of AI and content verification with an expert.
And consumers need to check vendors and choose reliable sites that are ready to be responsible for the created content.
Feedback from curators, experts, teachers, organization of the process is important.
The finished course is still only one part of the educational experience that the user receives during the course of training.
EdTech is more likely to use AI correctly than other areas, as developers understand the value of learning and have a lot of experience in correctly presenting and verifying information.
Therefore, neural networks for them will become an assistant and a friend, not an enemy and a competitor.
