He shouted "Long live freedom!" to the heated crowd and called his own cloned dogs his closest advisers.
These antics, however, overshadowed the most radical point in Miley ’ s platform — a foreign policy aimed at alienating Argentina from its main trading partner, China.
Focus translated Benjamin Gedan ’ s article on the importance of Argentina joining the United States in confronting China.
Throughout his winning campaign, the country ’ s new far-right president, a libertarian economist, made it clear that he would not be a friend of Xi Jinping.
“We don ’ t make deals with the Communists, ” Miley said in an August interview with Bloomberg Television, putting China on a par with Cuba, Nicaragua, Venezuela and North Korea.
Now that Miley is in power, this policy promises to fundamentally change Argentina ’ s international relations, raises the possibility of an economy-catastrophic diplomatic clash between Buenos Aires and Beijing, and provides the United States with an unexpected opportunity to offer an alternative to Chinese trade and investment.
The stakes in a region where China ’ s influence has soared in recent decades and local elites have no incentive to take sides in the U.S.-China rivalry are higher than ever.
Washington should make the most of this opportunity and demonstrate the benefits of cooperation with America.
A brief reference
Miley ’ s remarks surprised many in a region where not joining the growing rivalry between the United States and China has become a tenet of faith.
Trade between Latin America and China has grown rapidly since 2000, reaching $450 billion a year.
Beijing is also investing heavily in the region, both public and private.
The China Development Bank and the China Export-Import Bank have provided $136 billion in loans to Latin America over the past two decades.
It is therefore not surprising that the United States has found few supporters of its idea of secession from China.
President Donald Trump ’ s first secretary of state, Rex Tillerson, has warned U.S. neighbors about China ’ s “imperial ” ambitions.
His successor, Mike Pompeo, followed a similar tone, going to Panama to highlight China ’ s “predatory economic activity. ”
In November, at a meeting of Latin American leaders at the White House, President Joe Biden expressed alarm about China ’ s “debt trap diplomacy. ”
Latin American leaders clearly hold a different view.
Last year, Honduras severed diplomatic relations with Taiwan in favor of official ties with China.
This followed similar decisions by Costa Rica in 2007, Panama in 2017, El Salvador and the Dominican Republic in 2018 and Nicaragua in 2021.
Today, Latin America and the Caribbean accounts for seven of Taiwan ’ s 12 remaining diplomatic partners.
In October, the presidents of Chile and Colombia met with Xi in Beijing, where Colombia and China upgraded their relationship to a “strategic partnership. ”
Both presidents are leftist, but conservatives in the region have also sought to favor China.
These include then Ecuadorian President Guillermo Lasso, a former banker who signed a free trade agreement with China in May.
A total of 21 countries in the region have joined the Chinese Belt and Road Initiative.
So far, this has been particularly true for Argentina, which is the fourth-largest recipient of loans from Chinese banks — a total of $17 billion.
China is the country ’ s second largest export market after Brazil, filling cargo ships on the Paraná River with huge consignments of Argentine corn, soybeans and wheat.
The multi-billion dollar credit line of the People ’ s Bank of China has become a major source of hard currency, helping to pay off imports and repay debts to the International Monetary Fund.
For Argentina, which has no access to international capital markets and where inflation topped 200% last year, China remains indispensable.
In return, Argentina agreed to host a space station in Patagonia run by the People's Liberation Army; offered to use Chinese technology for its next nuclear reactor; expressed interest in buying fighters developed by China and Pakistan; and explored the possibility of building a Chinese port in Tierra del Fuego in the strategic Beagle Strait.
China is a major investor in Argentina ’ s booming lithium industry.
Surprisingly, in 2016, the Argentine Coast Guard sank a Chinese fishing vessel illegally working at sea.
However, Argentina usually pays homage to Beijing.
In 2021, Miley ’ s predecessor, center-left Alberto Fernandez, celebrated the centenary of the Chinese Communist Party, recalling the friendship of Juan Peron and Mao Zedong.
New turn
However, Miley seems ready to put these relations in jeopardy.
While in power, he is not so straightforward in expressing his rejection of China, reluctantly accepting trade and investment relations with that country.
During his inauguration, he amicably exchanged greetings with a senior Chinese diplomat and responded amicably to Xi ’ s congratulatory letter.
However, Miley does not hide his real preferences.
After a meeting at the White House in November, he said Argentina ’ s foreign policy would prioritize “countries that respect freedom. ”
Given Miley ’ s conservatism and his combative and improvisational leadership style, a diplomatic crisis seems increasingly likely.
In just two months in office, he rejected an invitation to join the Chinese-led BRICS bloc in favor of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, called the Colombian president a “communist killer ” and promised to move Argentina ’ s embassy in Israel from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem.
Even among Western friends, he looks like an elephant in a china shop.
At the World Economic Forum in Davos, Miley criticized his colleagues for betraying capitalist principles.
China's Dilemma
For China, the Miley represents a diplomatic challenge.
China has a big appetite for Argentinian exports of agricultural products and minerals, but Xi is known for not turning the other cheek.
China imposed infamous economic sanctions on Australia for criticizing China ’ s mistreatment of the COVID-19 pandemic, and then did the same with Lithuania over Taiwan.
When Brazil ’ s former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro thought about excluding Chinese company Huawei from its 5G wireless network, China threatened to refuse to supply vaccines against COVID.
(He carried out this threat in Paraguay, Taiwan ’ s only diplomatic partner in South America.)
In recent years, Xi has sought to soften the image of China, which has suffered as a result of the pandemic and aggressive “wolf-warrior diplomacy. ”
In Latin America, Xi does not seem to pay attention to the ideologies of presidents and is friends with both conservatives and leftist leaders.
Betting on charm has yielded mixed results.
According to the Pew Research Center, almost half of Brazilians have a negative attitude towards China, the same can be said about a third of Argentines.
In addition, Chinese investment in the region has evaporated in recent years, even as the maturity of previous loans is coming to an end.
However, Xi does not show much tolerance for Miley.
A few days before his inauguration, the Global Times, the newspaper of the Communist Party of China, published an interview with an Argentine economist entitled “The best approach for Argentina is never to take sides. ”
China later expressed disapproval of a meeting (subsequently denied) between Argentina ’ s new foreign minister and Taiwan ’ s senior diplomat in Buenos Aires, leading to fears of a possible freeze on China ’ s credit line.
The experience of the last conservative president of Argentina, Mauricio Macri, is instructive.
Although Macri was more courteous than Miley, at the beginning of his presidency he stirred up Beijing by promising to strengthen ties with Washington, to unveil secret agreements between China and Argentina, and to revisit priority Chinese projects, including two controversial dams in the remote province of Santa Cruz.
In response, China reportedly threatened to suspend other infrastructure investments, including an unrelated railway project, which exemplified the use of unusual cross default and cross cancellation clauses in its overseas contracts.
Macri eventually gave in, and it ’ s entirely possible that Miley would also avoid discord with China.
At the same time, Miley is reputedly much less disciplined and much more ideological than the former businessman and center-right Macri.
Tensions with China could have significant repercussions for Argentina.
In response to Argentina ’ s western pivot, China could restrict access to its market for Argentine food exports, suspend the credit line, stop negotiating a free trade agreement with the Mercosur bloc, cut investment in infrastructure and minerals, and impose other economic sanctions.
Examples of such economic coercion are numerous.
Just this month, Ecuador postponed plans to hand over Russian-made military equipment to Ukraine after Russia threatened to boycott Ecuadorian bananas, one of its main industries.
What about America?
Paradoxically, Miley is a test for the United States as well.
His undisguised admiration led to inflated expectations of support for the ailing Argentine economy.
Argentina's needs are manifold and not easy to meet.
The United States, for example, is unlikely to lend to Argentina, which is a serial defaulter.
Nor is it expected that they will equal the multibillion-dollar mega-projects that China is implementing under the Belt and Road Initiative, such as the construction of railways and dams.
American farmers and pastoralists compete with their counterparts in Argentina, so the United States will not replace China as a major export market.
Finally, Biden does not have as much influence as Xi does in private sector decision-making, and American companies are understandably wary of investing in Argentina.
Disagreements in politics could be another stumbling block, at least for Biden.
Miley calls climate change a “socialist lie, ” opposes abortion rights and gun control, and is loved by far-right figures including Trump, Tucker Carlson and Viktor Orban.
On February 24, he spoke at the Conference of Conservative Policy Initiatives and enthusiastically embraced Trump behind the scenes.
Miley has already tested the Biden administration by trying to control protests in a country accustomed to protesters obstructing traffic and flooding public squares across the capital.
The new government already had several opportunities to demonstrate its approach, including during a nationwide strike in January.
His harsh reaction drew criticism from the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights.
Miley also showed contempt for his opponents in Congress, calling lawmakers who voted against his proposed reforms "traitors" and suggesting that he would be able to rule the country through executive orders.
Such behavior could lead to attempts to impose conditions for supporting Argentina to avoid a repetition of the US Cold War policy in the region, where the logic of “the enemy of my enemy is my friend ” led to blind support for repressive anti-communist regimes.
This was also true in Argentina, where the United States supported a military regime of “dirty war ” that killed an estimated 30,000 people between 1976 and 1983.
During his encouraging visit to Buenos Aires on February 23, US Secretary of State Anthony Blinken rightly hinted at possible disagreements.
Standing next to Argentina ’ s foreign minister at a press conference, he highlighted Argentina ’ s “strong and long history in the field of labor rights, women ’ s and girls ’ rights, and human rights more broadly. ”
If Argentina fails to meet these challenges, or if its democratic institutions are threatened by an authoritarian president, the White House should reconsider its approach.
Violent treatment of peaceful demonstrators or intimidation of legislators, judges or journalists should be considered triggers.
Influence of USA
For now, however, the United States is trying to act in the old way.
That's the right idea.
After all, such love for the US in Buenos Aires has not been felt since the early 1990s, when the administration of President Carlos Menem sought “carnal relations. ”
Biden seconded his energy secretary to Miley's inauguration and later sent his deputy national security adviser for international economic affairs to Argentina.
For his part, Blinken promised that “the people of Argentina can count on us as long as you work to stabilize their economy. ”
The United States has reportedly given the go-ahead for the sale of F-16 aircraft to Argentina, a long-standing request previously rejected by Britain over fears of a new invasion of the Falkland Islands.
Under Menem, the United States included Argentina on its list of “major non-NATO allies, ” and there is now talk of including that country among NATO ’ s official partners (Colombia is the only country in the region that currently holds this title).
The White House is also looking for ways to incentivize purchases of Argentine lithium for electric vehicle batteries, although the inflation reduction law favors minerals for batteries produced and processed domestically or in countries that have signed a free trade agreement with the United States.
NASA has expressed interest in training an Argentine astronaut to fly to the International Space Station.
But the United States must go further and faster.
While Argentina is curbing excessive public spending, the U.S. government must take steps to build infrastructure to significantly expand food and energy production and include Argentina in U.S. clean energy supply chains.
A lot depends on the US strategy towards Argentina.
Even the active support of Argentina from the United States will not be able to compensate for the deterioration of Argentina ’ s relations with Beijing – China will remain an influential player in this country.
However, if the United States helps stabilize Argentina ’ s economy, it will present it as a trusted friend heading South America ’ s second-largest economy.
It will also demonstrate the value of partnering with the US for presidents willing to resist the temptations of China ’ s huge market and pocket-stuffing.
On the other hand, the refusal to support Miley during this difficult period, when deep budget cuts and rampant inflation are undermining his popularity, will serve as a negative signal, reinforcing the desire for non-alignment throughout the Western Hemisphere.

Samaritan women are increasingly developing their business and providing services in business areas that have traditionally been considered “male ”
8 March 2024 12: 08
399
Women are increasingly developing their businesses and providing services in business areas that have traditionally been considered predominantly “male ” – for example, in transportation, IT and telecom, as well as in repair and construction, a study of the Avito Services platform showed.
Ahead of International Women ’ s Day, Avito Services analyzed the gender ratio of performers in various service sectors.
According to the platform, gender inequality in most areas is coming to naught.
So, over the past four years (from January 2020 to January 2024), the share of women among entrepreneurs and private craftsmen has increased significantly in those niches that have traditionally been called “male ” – for example, construction, transport services and IT.
At the same time, men are also beginning to master segments where the share of female entrepreneurs and craftsmen is greater.
According to market research from Avito Services [1], over the past year, the share of women who provide services in the category of “IT, Telecom and the Internet ” has increased from 18% to 23%, that is, today every fourth specialist in the field of IT (software installation and configuration, creation and promotion of sites, programming for technical specifications and other IT and Internet services) is a woman.
At the same time, analysts [2] note that the niches of construction and transport services are also occupied by women by 18% and 25%, respectively.
In 3 years, women overtook men in business services
According to Avito Services, until 2023, more than half of the performers (54%) on the Avito platform in the Business Services category were men, and over the past year the ratio has changed in favor of women.
Today, 53% of the offerings (compared to 46% in 2021) on the Avito Services platform are made by women.
Georgy Hakobyan, Director of Vertical Avito Services:
“The service market is a segment that attracts an increasing number of entrepreneurs in various categories every year.
A developed system of platforms for finding private performers in Russia helps both novice entrepreneurs and large companies to attract orders, build up the customer base and effectively develop their business in the service sector.
The number of performers on Avito Services is growing: ads are placed by both private masters and large enterprises - today it is more than 3 million ads about services across the country.
And the role of Avito as a socially responsible business is to provide a platform for the development of entrepreneurship in any segment of services: from construction and transportation to the beauty industry or home services. ”
The largest share of women entrepreneurs remains in the field of beauty and health, domestic services and training, but these segments are gradually coming to men
Analysts also found that the share of beauty masters among women across the country as of 2023 is almost 90% (and over the past three years, the share of male masters did not exceed 11%).
According to the market research from Avito Services, in the country as a whole, men are increasingly developing their business in this area: the share of men in the category increased by 9 percentage points in 2 years (from 14% in the second half of 2021 to 23% in the second half of 2023).
Analysts also note that among the masters who carry out household services and minor household repairs (repair and tailoring of clothes and shoes, minor household repairs, laundry, dry cleaning, etc.), women also dominate (67%).
Among the performers of services of domestic staff, women - 89%.
Another area in which women are more likely to develop their business is animal care services (80%).
On Avito, the share of ads in the category “Training and courses ” (tutors, specialists in vocational training) from women throughout Russia is 77%.
At the same time, in the whole market, male tutors across the country increased by 11 p.p. (from 25% to 36%) in 2 years [4]

Researchers conducted a new experiment with fasting volunteers.
The result was very surprising.
Why People Are Hungry
In the distant past, our ancestors had to go for a long time without food.
The ability to store and conserve nutrients is our evolutionary advantage.
No one is threatened by hunger.
People give up food voluntarily.
There are many types of fasting, from short one-day religious fasts to long periods of strict abstinence from eating.
In the middle of the last century, interval fasting was invented, when a person does not eat anything for 12-18 hours in a row.
Refusal of food for health purposes is very popular.
It does not require any expenses, nor does it require a doctor.
According to Benjamin Horne of Stanford University School of Medicine, short fasting is usually harmless.
Even with some chronic diseases.
This is usually done in order to lose weight.
With malnutrition, the body consumes internal sources of energy.
First - glucose, then it is taken for lipids stored in various organs and tissues, as well as muscle fibers.
Weight decreases.
It is believed that this has a beneficial effect on the heart and metabolism, in particular, insulin resistance, glucose and cholesterol levels in the blood, pressure are reduced.
There is evidence that fasting improves mental activity, mood, reduces inflammation, chronic pain.

Now you can comprehensively examine the blood at once by thousands of indicators to understand how the body reacts to this or that effect.

They didn ’ t eat anything for a week, they just drank water.

1044 molecules have noticed changes.
Even three days after the hunger strike, 66 indicators did not return to normal.
Scientists have identified proteins associated with weight loss.
The turning point is the switching of the energy source from glucose to fats.
This happens on the third or fourth day of the hunger strike.
On average, the volunteers lost 5.7 kilograms.
The decrease in muscle mass stopped three days after the completion of the experiment.
"This is the first time we've seen what happens at the molecular level in the body when fasting," said lead author Claudia Langenberg of Queen Mary University in London.
Scientists hope that their work will help evidence-based study of fasting.
But they also recognize the shortcomings of the experiment.
In particular, the small number of participants, the lack of a control group for comparison.
These and other factors may influence the results and their interpretation.

Composer, singer Yuri Loza: “The authority of intellectual work has ceased to flourish in society ”
Denis BOCHAROV
25.03.2024
The material was published in No. 2 of the printed version of the newspaper Kultura on February 29, 2024.
In early February, the author and performer of the songs “I Can Dream ”,“ Reserved Places ”, “One Hundred Hours ”,“ Sing, My Guitar ” and, of course, “Raft ” turned seventy.
The artist, famous for his sincerity and straightforwardness of his judgments, was frank in an interview with the correspondent of Kultura.
You recently celebrated an anniversary.
Do round dates have any special significance for you?
Time is a relative concept.
I suppose a man is as old as he feels.
I know a lot of people who do things with their bodies in their nineties that I can ’ t do at my age.
How can you give a man ninety if he likes to jump, run, squeeze, pull up and so on?
On the other hand, it was much less different than I was, but they passed away as decrepit old men.
Everyone chooses a way of life for himself, which ultimately determines how much a person should live and in what state he should approach a particular calendar date.
I don ’ t take the numbers seriously.
Another thing is that I can plan something.
For example, until the next “big figure ”, that is, until the 75th anniversary, I have as many as five years.
To paraphrase a well-known saying, I will generalize: as you meet a five-year plan, so you will spend it.
And I decided to meet the five-year concerts: in early February, I performed in Moscow and St. Petersburg.
Thus, involuntarily — or perhaps just the opposite, quite consciously — he set himself the task: according to the assumption to spend the entire five-year period in labor.
- In the work, which, as I understand, will be associated mainly with concert activities?
After all, it is known that you approach studio work carefully and selectively: you prefer to share new songs on the Web, and release full-fledged albums extremely rarely.
Let ’ s find out where the concept of “album ” came from.
If we begin to study this process, we will find out: the music album appeared and blossomed in violent colors in the sixties of the last century.
It was then that the LP became ubiquitous – a vinyl record that allowed you to put a certain amount of information on its audio tracks: about twenty minutes on each side.
It was called an album.
Later, in the nineties, there were CDs that contained much more information.
And the concept of the album began to gradually dissolve, blur.
After all, the album in its canonical form was a kind of picture in the literal sense of the word: the people who created the album covers (artists, designers, graphics) were indicated on the envelopes as full co-authors of the final product along with musicians and sound engineers.
The record was a real thing, with a self-valuable design, beautiful detailed tabs, with which many music lovers decorated the walls of their rooms.
Now everything has been reduced to the level of a flash drive, on which you can download not only all your creativity, but also the works of your friends, as well as put all the work of Bach.
So what album can we talk about now?
I recently released a new album called The Scream of the Soul.
In addition, two collections were released, the content of which was compiled by representatives of the record label.
These releases, in my opinion, have the right to be called albums.
Because, again, I am convinced that the real album is a vinyl record.
But the publications I mentioned are rather an exception to the rule, since they are designed for amateurs, collectors.
For the bulk of both creators and consumers of musical information today do not understand why to think albums, if they are in any form, by and large, not realized?
Many of your songs can often be heard in the performance of other artists.
How do you feel about cover versions of your own hits?
For example, one of the best things that came out from under your pen, "Reserved places", the vast majority of compatriots is known in the performance of VIA "Ariel".
It is possible that very few people know that the authorship of this composition belongs to Yuri Loza...
— Some of the works I personally gave, in particular, the song you mentioned “Reserved places ”.
By the way, the authorship of this thing is not entirely mine: the text we wrote together with Sasha Zhigarev.
I met the guys from Ariel in 1980, at a festival in Tbilisi.
At that time, I was still working at Integral and did not have big plans for a solo career and major tours.
Although the songs have already written in full.
And once, after the Tbilisi festival, we met with the musicians of “Ariel ” in Moscow, I sang a few things to them, the guys liked it, in the end they took five of my compositions, written on the poems of other poets, into work.
And the song “Protected places ” was called a separate program.
As for the whole question of the performance of my works by other artists...
If I sometimes object, that ’ s my right.
I believe that if someone wants to hear the song “Raft ”, he should invite Yuri Loza to perform it, and not someone else.
Understand it correctly: I do not forbid to sing my songs - I forbid to make money on them.
— In conversation with you the theme of the song “Raft ” really can not be bypassed.
After all, for many, the concepts of Yuri Loza and the composition "Raft" are inextricably linked.
How do you explain its huge, ever-fading popularity over time and do you consider this work your main creative success?
This song has a strange and long story.
She wrote for a long time, about a year.
Then, starting in 1982, for seven or eight years, I tried to put her somewhere, to speak with her on television, but invariably received a refusal.
It was crossed out with a red pencil and, with the words “you ’ re not going there ”, returned back.
That is, the way to a mass audience and wide recognition of this song was very thorny.
In the mid-eighties, I began to implement my tape albums: from 1983 to 1986, I had four of them.
About fifty songs were recorded on these phonograms, but "The Raft" did not make it into any of these releases.
The song continued to stand on the sidelines: I knew it was a separate, special topic.
And I was not mistaken: her turn came only at the end of the decade, and in 1990 I performed with her at the festival “Song of the Year ”.
A lot of work was invested in the creation of the composition, perhaps that is why it still lives, and lives its own life, not always dependent on me.
It has been translated into several languages, and the story goes on: in particular, last year I posted it on the Web in French — quite interesting sounds.
And recently I was sent the text "Raft" in Udmurt...
I sometimes hear the opinion that “The Raft ” just turned out to be a topical piece at the turn of the 1980s and 1990s.
But it seems to me that the really good thing is not tied to a specific time.
There are such works that, if they appeared at any time, would become popular.
I think if I had written “The Raft ” today, it would have made its way too.
Yes, the historical context in which a work is born undoubtedly matters, but the artistic level of the latter is still much more important.
For example, if the Rolling Stones had released the same album today that made them famous in the mid-1960s, nobody would have wanted it, nobody would have noticed it.
Because the work itself, in terms of quality and internal content, does not deserve the glory that it received when it came out at the right time.
And vice versa: if we take, say, the Chicago album, which is called Night & Day: Big Band, then it, released in 1995, even today would have taken all the Grammys — and would have done the same in the sixties, had it been recorded then.
Because it's a job done very well, very well, very hard.
A lot of work, skill and talent are invested in it.
- You are known as a person who does not get a word in his pocket and from whom other people get "nuts".
In particular, you do not deny yourself the pleasure of “driving ” the Rolling Stones and have just done it once again.
What exactly did they not like?
- Yes, the yard team - as it was, and remained so.
If we take the Rolling Stones of 1963 and today, we will see the same group, which in its development has not advanced even a centimeter.
The technique of mastering the instruments is the same, the guitar sound has not changed, everything is still crooked, oblique, past the notes.
You see, in society sometimes there is a blatant discrepancy between the level of universal adoration and worship to the performance level of the artists themselves.
Some musicians do not progress over the years and even decades, while others grow and develop – this is required by their healthy creative ambitions.
Take, for example, the Beatles of 1962, when they were denied a recording contract (they were then preferred by The Tremeloes, which today few people remember), and the Beatles of 1967, when they recorded the record Sgt. Pepper ’ s Lonely Hearts Club Band, which many still tend to consider the pinnacle of musical pop culture as such.
Put on Pink Floyd ’ s 1968 album A Saucerful Of Secrets and immediately after it start The Dark Side Of The Moon, released in 1973, and you will feel the difference.
Richie Blackmore of the late 1960s and mid-1970s are two different musicians.
Do you know where I'm going?
Artists, whether singers, instrumentalists or arrangers, must constantly improve their creative and performing level.
And then it turns out that the records of some musicians, made in different years, are the earth and the sky, and listen to others, so just carry the saints out.
— Let ’ s return to the very gloomy, in terms of popular music, modern realities.
Why today on our, and the world stage of songs comparable in artistic level with the same "Raft", the day with fire can not find?
- Because the authors are pushed below the baseboard.
Many people even quit writing because they don ’ t see much sense in it.
The authority of intellectual work has ceased to flourish in society — that is the problem.
By itself, decent content will not appear, it must be created by someone.
Writing a good song is hard work.
But if the authors are deprived of attention in relation to themselves, if they do not receive their legitimate moment of glory, they gradually lose interest and cease to do all this.
Therefore, songs today are written not by worthy composers and poets, but hastily concocted teams of producers, costumers, ticket holders and God knows who else.
Forgive me for the tautology, professionals have left the profession.
Now the young artists have a rather strange manner: to sing as if their teeth are knocked out, but not yet spit out.
This happens, in particular, because they simply have nothing to sing - they do not even try to convey the essence of the text, since this very text is devoid of meaning completely.
Here they go, chewing some words.
I ask myself: why should I listen to them if I do not understand what exactly they want to convey with their opuses?
For the sake of pure experiment, I tried to get acquainted with the texts from the last “Song of the Year ” and realized that many of them must be translated from Russian into Russian: some random set of words.
I don't know, maybe some computer program writes texts for them...
You have a blog where you share ideas on a variety of topics from time to time.
Have you ever thought of writing a complete autobiography or publishing a book?
- I have that idea.
But there are two points: first, it is necessary to sit down and write, and as usual, there is always not enough time.
And secondly, few people buy books in printed form now.
Everyone is busy reading short notes on the Internet.
The culture of reading is lost.
A hundred and fifty or two hundred years ago, a young lady took a thick book, went out into the gazebo into the garden, and for a few hours immersed herself in reading.
Can you imagine the same girl today?
And let ’ s not even dive so deep into history: 50 years ago, everyone read books.
Now the picture is different: they read smartphones on the go in the subway, on the bus, and not novels, but tiny texts.
A friend advised me: “Yura, if you do decide to take up the pen, do not write a novel.
It is better to give out small plots that can be mastered at the stop while waiting for transport. ”
I do not know if I will use this advice, but if I do decide to write an autobiography, it will probably be designed for people who think out of fashion, for those who are divorced from general trends and live an independent life.
By the way, such people, as I think, understand that the songs of Vine are not fashionable, not old, they are just songs.
I, by the way, many tend to refer to the category of artists who were, and not who are.
Like, I was popular, my songs sounded, and so on.
They talk about me as a person in the past (smiles).
— Now in the West it is fashionable to ban and cancel all Russian.
How long, in your opinion, will this state of affairs last and how much do we lose in the current situation?
Every medal has two sides.
The good thing is that all these prohibitions make us more actively engage in import substitution, develop our own business, awaken to life dormant in us for the time unknown internal resources, and so on.
But it is bad when, say, an athlete who has devoted his whole life to training in the hope and desire to win the title is deprived of the opportunity to go somewhere and take part in major competitions...
It is important to understand the main thing, and I always say this: guys, they hate us.
They hate us just for what we are.
As in the fable of Krylov: “It ’ s your fault that I want to eat. ”
It is our “fault ” that we exist.
And this hatred is based on the fact that we are big, we have a lot of natural resources, and we refuse to give them to others.
And the stronger we are, the more they will hate us.
But it's not just about the economy.
Alas, hatred is not selective, so they try not only to influence the notorious sanctions, but also to cancel everyone in the cultural sphere - from Dostoevsky to Tchaikovsky.
If they are given the go-ahead to hate Russian, it means that they will hate everything related to us.
And so, as to how long it will last, I am not so much a pessimist as a realist.
For this state of affairs has always existed, it is just that it may not have been so pronounced before.
In one of your songs, written about forty years ago, there are these lines: “It is already difficult for me, a lot not to experience.
It is impossible to return the years, but I know how to dream. ”
What else would you like to experience and do you still know how to dream?
Dreams are transformed over time.
If in youth dreams have some global connotation (to travel with world tours, achieve fame, delight everyone, surprise and so on), now they have become more simple, mundane and, rather, similar to ordinary desires: something concrete to get, to do, a good song to write, to keep working capacity, in the end.
I ’ m not doing a major tour right now, I ’ m not starting large-scale projects that could turn the world upside down — all this is in the past.
When a person is seventy, he can not even theoretically look to the future with great optimism.
Venerable age and an optimistic view of things are mutually exclusive.
I am aware that I have much less ahead of me than I have already lived.
The next seventy years I have not intended for myself, so every new day and year not only matter, but also, alas, take away a piece of the remaining life.
And even if I now begin to make titanic efforts, against nature is still not reproach: a certain wear and tear of the body has already occurred...
On a more global scale, I have no illusions here either.
Just because heaven on Earth is impossible.
Nature has not created a single perfect creature, and therefore a perfect society, as well as a flawless form of government, is excluded.
Perhaps this is why people tend to think about paradise, that they hope: somewhere there everything is built so well and harmoniously that there is nothing better to wish for.
Yuri Eduardovich Loza was born on February 1, 1954 in Sverdlovsk.
After serving in the army in 1974, he got a job as a milling apprentice at the factory.
He also became a self-employed member.
He graduated from the Alma-Ata Music School named after P.I. Tchaikovsky.
He worked in the groups “Integral ” and“ Architects ”, in 1987 he began his official solo career.
In 1988, the company "Melodiya" released the debut solo album "What is said, is said", which included the song "Raft", which became the hallmark of the artist.
Yuri Loza is known as a supporter of conspiracy theories - the flat Earth and the Flood in the XVIII century, which, in particular, destroyed the forests of Siberia and flooded all the cities of the world.

It turned out that the warming of the oceans spoils the vision of octopuses
University of Adelaide: Octopus eyes blurred due to heat stress
Australian biologists from the University of Adelaide found that the heating of the water of the oceans due to climate change negatively affects the vision of octopuses.
The study was published on the official website of the scientific institution.
"We found several proteins important for vision that are affected by heat stress.
One of them is a structural protein, which is found in large quantities in the lenses of the eyes of animals and retains the transparency and optical clarity of the lens, and the other is responsible for the regeneration of visual pigments in the photoreceptors of the eyes.
"Levels of both of these proteins have been significantly reduced in the face of projected ocean warming, suggesting that octopus vision is likely to deteriorate even further," explained Dr Kiaz Hua.
The eyes remain the main sense organ for octopuses.
In these animals, 70% of the brain is responsible for vision, which is 20% than in humans.
Scientists have also found that higher water temperatures accelerate the metabolism of octopuses, make them smaller and change the distribution area of some species of these mollusks.
In addition, the warm ocean has a negative effect on the reproduction of the octopus, reducing the number of eggs that spawn.
In some cases, entire broods remained unhatched, the researchers noted.
Earlier it became known that octopuses are the oldest animals with sex chromosomes.

Mahatma Gandhi
Despite the close attention of all the world media to the problems of Syria, refugees and plane crashes, events continue to occur on other continents.
And even if today they do not seem to be events of the first row, they will have a huge contribution to history.
The situation is reminiscent of Houdini ’ s tricks: once a magician took an elephant into a large box, and in a moment the animal disappeared.
According to Houdini ’ s sign, the white veil was pulled off, and the elephant covered with a black veil was invisible against a black background.
So the whole continent turned out to be “invisible ” to the world media against the background of terrorists, explosions, endless elections.
Building on the experience of the summits in New Delhi (2008) and Addis Ababa (2011), the Third Africa-India Forum Summit was recently held with the participation of 54 African countries.
On October 29, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with African leaders.
Given the range of issues discussed, the meeting was a huge step forward in the growing engagement of India and Africa.
At the global level, Indian and African leaders are pushing for governance reforms and advocating the inclusion of India and at least two African states as permanent members of the UN Security Council.
The issue of global warming was touched upon, and a call was made to convene a meeting of “sun-rich ” countries ahead of the climate summit in Paris, which begins at the end of this month.
Political and energy security, the fight against terrorism, cooperation in the field of trade, investment, education and health were discussed.
India has announced a five-year loan of $10 billion.
In addition, India will offer $600 million in aid grants to the India-Africa Development Fund and $10 million to the India-Africa Health Fund.
India has also announced 50,000 scholarships for African students to continue their studies in India.
Some 137 projects were also created in 41 countries.
But let ’ s go a little deeper into the story.
As a result of the Cold War, many African countries joined the non-alignment movement initiated by Egypt, India and Yugoslavia.
Since the beginning of decolonization, India has exerted considerable political and ideological influence in Africa — as a model to follow.
But India ’ s ability to play a broader strategic role in Africa in the twentieth century was fraught with a number of challenges.
India ’ s influence was limited by the fiscal weakness of its domestic economic policies.
Adherence to the methods of non-violent resistance also did not contribute to the provision of military or any assistance in general to the national liberation movements of African countries.
However, despite all this, the leaders of the towering India, Gandhi and Nehru, their ideas of liberation and Afro-Asian unity influenced African independence fighters such as Albert Lutuli (South Africa), Nelson Mandela (South Africa), Julius Nyerere (Tanzania), Kenneth Kaunda (Zambia) and Kwame Nkrumah (Ghana).
After the won political battles for the liberation of Africa, the current predominance of economic factors in India-Africa relations has become logical.
As of 2011, India has become Africa ’ s fourth-largest trading partner after China, the EU and the US, while Africa has become India ’ s sixth-largest trading partner after the EU, China, the UAE, the US and ASEAN.
Former Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh said: “Africa has all the prerequisites to become one of the main growth poles in the world in the twentieth century.
We will work with Africa to realize this potential. ”
At the India-Africa Forum Summit, held in New Delhi in April 2008, India offered for the first time a framework for South-South cooperation.
Since 1991, India ’ s economy has experienced significant growth of more than 6%.
And strategic resources, especially oil, have become an urgent necessity.
This has prompted India to actively forge relations with oil-rich countries such as South Africa, Morocco, Egypt, Sudan, Nigeria and Angola.
The main minerals of Africa, such as uranium, gas, copper, iron ore, phosphates, platinum, are also of great interest to India.
In turn, Indian technology is suitable for tropical conditions and investment and is vital to Africa ’ s development.
Indian capital, both private and public, has long entered Africa.
India-Africa trade has grown 20-fold since 2000 and has doubled in the past five years, and now stands at $70 billion.
Of course, this is not an impressive figure compared to China, whose trade turnover with Africa is approximately $200 billion.
Even if India becomes a major trading nation with growing investment, it must contend for a place under the African sun with other formidable rivals such as China, Japan and South Korea.
Nevertheless, the moment is very opportune – a slowdown in the Chinese economy may open a window to Africa for India wider.
As trading peoples of the sea, India and African countries are seeking to strengthen their security.
India has been successful in confronting Somali pirates along the east coast, Mauritius, Seychelles, Djibouti and the western Indian Ocean.
In addition, the emergence of non-state transnational terrorist organizations, such as Al-Shabaab in East Africa and Boko Haram in Nigeria, as well as a variety of terrorist groups operating in India, is pushing both countries to join forces.
A number of countries, including Cameroon, Nigeria, Niger, Chad and Benin, have appealed to India for help in the fight against Islamic extremism.

In turn, India hopes for the support of African states in order to raise its status as a world power.
It also wants to make sure that it is not in the shadow of its neighbor and rival China.

The main items of Indian imports from Africa are resources and minerals, including crude oil, coal, precious stones and gold.
African countries are a market for Indian pharmaceuticals, vehicles and refined petroleum products.
India and many African countries “are the fastest growing emerging economies in the world, ” said Indian Foreign Minister Sushma Swaraj.

South Sudan appealed to India for assistance in the development of livestock and livestock.
India, the world ’ s largest milk producer, agreed to provide experts.
In Mozambique, a solar power plant built by Indians will not only help the country use environmentally friendly solar energy, but is also expected to ensure the export of solar panels to neighboring countries.

China in the Indian Ocean.

From electric planes to taxi-drones.
What to expect from the future of aviation
Photo by Shutterstock, DELFI
Text: Baiba Krastina, Raivis Viluns, Delfi Bizness
The journey of one passenger from Riga to Paris and back by plane brings an average of 684 kilograms of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions.
The same emissions are emitted by a medium-sized car that travels 80 kilometers per week for a year.
Over the past half century, air travel has developed very quickly.
In 1960, traveling by plane was expensive - only a few could afford it.
During the year, 100 million passengers went on the flight.
In less than 60 years, in 2019, the world already had 4.56 billion air passengers.
Cargo transportation, tourism, business, geopolitics, and more are all closely related to the availability of air travel.
But in addition, it is one of the industries for which it is quite difficult to become "green": electric passenger and cargo aircraft are not yet an option, and sustainable energy sources cannot replace aviation fuel.
The pandemic stopped air traffic for a while.
In 2022, when the recovery from the pandemic began and the aviation industry returned to its usual rhythm, air travel accounted for about 2% of global CO2 emissions (80% of pre-pandemic levels).
As the world struggles to reduce CO2 emissions to slow down climate change, aviation will not escape the new reality.
In 2023, at the UN Climate Conference, representatives of more than 100 countries decided to reduce global carbon dioxide emissions from aviation by 5% by 2030.
However, the previous project provided for a reduction of 5-8%.
The goal was decided to lower because of China and other developing countries, who feared it would harm their economies.
As with other green targets, Europe is leading the movement to reduce aviation emissions.
However, according to experts, it is not so simple.
Green fuel
In 2023, the European Parliament approved a green air transport plan.
Airports and fuel suppliers in the EU are required to ensure that by 2025 at least 2% of aviation fuel is produced on an environmentally friendly basis.
This figure will increase every five years.
As a result, by 2050, 70% of aviation fuel should be environmentally friendly.
Part of this fuel should become synthetic - that is, it must be produced from renewable energy sources of non-biological origin.
The main speaker on this issue, Spanish MEP Jose Ramon Bausa Diez, noted that this decision will not only reduce emissions, but also make Europe a leader in the field of environmentally friendly aviation fuel.
The European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) explains that hydrogen, for example, can be used as an environmentally friendly aviation fuel.
Theoretically, it can also be obtained from solid household waste, oil and other sources.
However, the scale of production of environmentally friendly aviation fuel raises concerns.
Speaking to Euractiv, Stephen Duly, an assistant professor at Trinity College Dublin and aviation fuel expert who heads the Ryanair Research Center at the university, said Europe has set itself very specific goals.
But it is not clear how they will be achieved.
In addition to the 69 traditional biofuel processing plants, 300 more biorefining plants are needed to achieve the EU ’ s goals.
Currently, there are plans to build about 30 such plants in Europe.
In 2022, 127 million liters of environmentally friendly aviation fuel were produced, and in 2023, about 434 million liters were already produced.
Despite a threefold increase, this is still less than 1% of global aviation fuel use.
Slow innovation
Vladimir Petrov, head of the Innovation Center of the Transport and Communications Institute (TSI), told Delfi Bizness that the introduction of green innovations in aviation will be more difficult than the same process in the field of motor transport.
“In large aviation, everything has long been standardized.
If you need to implement a new technology, a new fuel, it ’ s hard to do all the tests. ”
Vladimir Petrov
Head of the Innovation Center of the Transport and Communications Institute (TSI)
The next step is to integrate all of this into production processes.
Compared to the automotive industry, where many jobs are done by robots and innovation can be implemented fairly quickly, aviation standards are higher, and all processes are much slower.
Another problem is what to do with planes when they are on the ground.
Maintenance and refueling will require changes from airports: for example, there will have to create infrastructure to charge electricity.
However, it is unlikely that you will have to build new airports or completely rebuild the old ones, said Petrov.
“In the case of aircraft, there is also a question of safety, so that there is no fire in any case.
We heard about the fire Tesla, ” — said Petrov.
Now all over the world there are research and projects in various areas: electric aircraft, renewable fuels, hybrid models (aircraft partially use hydrogen engines, partially - electric).
In the future, we will see more differences in the aircraft used for short flights - for example, between European countries, said Petrov.
Technologies that reduce short-haul emissions by powering aircraft engines with electricity or hybrid systems are already being tested.
The aviation of the future can develop in the direction of micro-flights - for example, from Purvciems to Zolitude (air urban mobility).
Autonomous drones can be used for this.
However, even in this case, there are security issues, as well as other potential problems.
“The main thing is infrastructure, ” says Petrov.
We will have to create a network, command centers that will control the movement of these drones.
When will we be able to fly from Riga to Brussels by electric plane?
Petrov believes that even with the active support of the EU, this is a matter of the next 20 years.
Efficient aircraft and green fuel
Latvian national airline airBaltic has repeatedly called itself "green" and focused on the environment.
For example, it uses 47 Airbus A220-300 aircraft - these are some of the most efficient passenger aircraft in the world.
Zita Baranova, head of sustainability at airBaltic, told Delfi Bizness that the aircraft exceeded the airline ’ s expectations.
They consume significantly less fuel than expected.
According to her, the Airbus A220-300 is the first aircraft with transparent environmental impact indicators, and it reduces CO2 emissions by 25% and nitrogen oxide by 50%.
According to Baranova, sustainable development of aviation is based on four main directions: the use of environmentally friendly types of aviation fuel, improving the efficiency of airlines, new technological solutions and compensation for emissions that cannot be completely avoided.
"In the case of Latvia, the aviation industry should be able to provide several aspects of sustainability at the same time: to reduce the impact of flights on the environment and to ensure stable communication of the Baltic region with European economic centers," Baranova said.
The main problems are related to the availability and price of environmentally friendly aviation fuel.
Now it is two to four times more expensive than the old aviation fuel.
Alternative technological solutions are at an early stage.
“Therefore, airBaltic pays special attention to the most efficient use of aircraft, reducing fuel consumption and gradually switching to environmentally friendly aviation fuel, ” adds the representative of the company.
airBaltic already in 2020 added a small share of "green" fuel.
From May 2023, airBaltic passengers can add 1-1.5 kilograms of green fuel when buying a ticket for an additional fee.
By the end of the year, more than 9,300 passengers had taken advantage of this option.
What airBaltic is doing to become greener
In 2023, the airline saved more than 6.7 thousand tons of CO2, reducing emissions by an average of 184 kilograms per flight.
This has been achieved:
• through the introduction of high-precision arrival procedures;
• reduction of aerodynamic drag during takeoff and landing;
• Reduction of flight range and other efficiency measures.
Can the EU make “green ” those who actually pollute?
Not all EU decisions seem acceptable to European environmental organizations.
For example, earlier this year, five non-governmental organizations (NGOs) appealed to politicians about the rules adopted in 2020.
These regulations clarify which activities, including in the field of aviation and road traffic, are considered sustainable and environmentally friendly and can be supported by various funds.
Hiske Arts, a spokesman for the Dutch NGO, says that for most, these rules have gone unnoticed.
However, if they are not challenged, they will allow fossil-fueled aircraft and ships to be labeled "environmentally friendly."
“This means that money dedicated to addressing climate issues will actually contribute to climate catastrophe because it enables these industries to continue their previous growth. ”
According to EU criteria, European low-cost carriers Ryanair, easyJet and WizzAir can be considered “best in class ”.
Moritz Nahshat of Austrian organization Protect Our Winters argues that the aid, allowing European airlines to buy new planes to be more environmentally friendly and resell old ones, contributes to the global increase in the number of aircraft and flights.
This, in turn, will lead to an increase in both the total number of aircraft and air pollution.
Carly Hicks of Opportunity Green, an aviation and shipping NGO, believes that the EU should create a system to exchange old aircraft for newer ones by recycling and recycling old ones.

Catastrophe under water: how climate change turned into a tragedy for marine life
Deadly sea “cooling ” may become more frequent
3: 42
In March 2021, a terrible phenomenon occurred on the coast of South Africa.
Giant manta rays, resembling bats with their wings, were found on the shore, lying on their backs on rocks.
Huge bull sharks lay dead in the sand, and puffer fish occupied the beach, looking like soccer balls.
This mass death of fish is usually associated with hot water, lack of oxygen, or the flowering of toxic algae.
But this time it was something unusual.
According to a new article, the dead fish were victims of an unexpected cold snap that appears to be linked to climate change.
With global warming leading to record-high ocean temperatures and sea heatwaves attacking our planet, it seems paradoxical that climate change could lead to a sharp cooling under water.
But researchers believe that in some parts of the world, phenomena such as the 2021 cold snap are becoming more common as a result of changing ocean currents, which could have disastrous consequences for marine life.
The mass extinction of sharks in South Africa attracted the attention of Nicholas Lubitz, an Australian shark researcher and then a doctoral student at James Cook University.
He collaborated with a group of ecologists and oceanographers to analyze what happened and its relationship to broader ocean trends.
Particular attention was paid to the Agulhas Current, a rapid flow of ocean water near the western edge of the Indian Ocean that heads south along the coasts of Mozambique and South Africa.
Usually this current brings warm subtropical water further south, but when in contact with the continental shelf, it can cause whirlpools similar to the rotating puddles formed behind the boulders in the river.
These vortices divert water from the shore, attracting colder water from a depth of up to three kilometers.
Eastern winds can also shift warm surface waters into the open sea, leading to a rise in cold water.
At the end of February 2021, weather and ocean conditions off the coast of South Africa coincided, and a cooling began.
Data from satellites and buoys showed that a large vortex passes through the region, which moves south with a strong easterly wind, contributing to upwelling - raising deep waters to the surface.
Ocean surface temperatures dropped by more than 7 ° C in 48 hours, reaching 10 ° C.
Near Port Alfred on the southeast coast, the temperature dropped by more than 9 ° C in one day.
Upwelling covered 230 kilometers and lasted a week.
According to Lubitz, for fish that prefer warm waters, such as bull sharks, the cold has become deadly, especially due to its rapid onset.
Scientists warn that climate change could change upwelling zones in areas where ocean currents meet continents, in particular by amplifying winds that help lift colder water.
Researchers have noted an increase in cold upwellings elsewhere, such as the East Australian Current, bordering the eastern edge of Australia.
While the threat of cooling adds another potential way that climate change could reduce shark habitats, scientists stress that further study is needed to fully understand the process.

Specialists from the Scientific and Educational Center (REC) “Functional Micro / Nanosystems ”, created on the basis of the Bauman Moscow State Technical University (MSTU) and the All-Russian Research Institute of Automation (VNIIA) named after N.L. Dukhov, launched the first domestic high-precision superconductor quantum processor.
It is called Snowdrop 4Q.
This is a system that includes a chip based on four qubits, modules for reading their signals with parametric cryo-amplifiers and control electronics units.
The accuracy of simple single-qubit algorithms on the new processor was 99.76%, and more complex two-qubit operations – 99.11%.
These characteristics are record-breaking for Russian science and are comparable to the world ’ s leading achievements.
The obtained parameters made it possible for the first time in Russia to perform complex algorithms that consist of more than a hundred quantum logic operations.
In particular, the magnetization of the material was modeled (Ising model), the equation of thermal conductivity was solved and a sequence of calculations was implemented to solve the systems of equations.
“The best test for a processor is to run a complex algorithm on it using all the available qubits, which we did.
Directly calibrating and fully characterizing a quantum system is a complex process, and we have been working on it for the last three months.
The accuracy of the logical operations achieved by our chip allowed us to conduct a whole series of operations aimed at solving practical problems, "Nikita Smirnov, a leading developer of quantum processors at the scientific and educational center, told Izvestia.
The scientist also said that in the process of development, experts have tried their own method of error mitigation, which is based on neural network learning.
As specified by the scientific director of VNIIA Alexander Andriyash, the presented device acts as a coprocessor for a classical computer.
With its help, specialists will be able to solve the most difficult subtasks for traditional microelectronics.

MOSCOW, June 27 – PRIME.
Russia began supplying Kuzbass coal to India via a new North-South transport corridor, which could revolutionize international trade, writes The Economic Times.
The North-South Corridor (INSTC) stretches for 7,200 kilometers from St. Petersburg to the Indian port of Mumbai.
It includes a network of railways, highways and seaports.
Part of the route passes through Iran.
The creation of this route was facilitated by Western sanctions - Russia sought and found opportunities to smuggle trade supplies to the Middle East and Asia.
So far, we are talking about two trains with coal, launched from the Kemerovo region, then through Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan to the port of Bandar Abbas in Iran.
The development of this corridor is significant for Russian-Indian trade, especially in the light of sanctions.
The country considers it an alternative to the ambitious Chinese project “One Belt, One Road ”.
In May, India took control of the port of Chabahar in southeastern Iran for 10 years.
This should be an incentive for the development of the North-South corridor, since the port will become a key hub in it.
As a result, trade with Central Asia, Afghanistan, and then - through Russia - and with Europe will receive a new impetus.
The INSTC corridor is considered an alternative to the logistics route through the Suez Canal, which remains vulnerable to attacks and emergencies similar to the container ship that ran aground in 2021.
It will reduce travel time from 45 days to 25 and save up to a third of transportation costs.
It is most advantageous to use it for the pharmaceutical industry, health care, agriculture, textile and jewelry industries.
In addition, India is ramping up purchases of coal and renewable energy from Russia, and this dependence will grow.
The North-South corridor will allow the country to save currency and increase the profitability of production.

Disproved the popular hypothesis about the extinction of mammoths: the “mysterious event ” was the real cause of the disappearance
Scientists have refuted the popular hypothesis about the cause of the extinction of mammoths
1: 09 AM
Woolly mammoths survived on Wrangel Island for 6,000 years after the extinction of their mainland counterparts.
A new genomic study has revealed that their last population disappeared not due to genetic inbreeding, as previously thought, but as a result of a sudden and mysterious event.
The study, published in the journal Cell, found that the population of Wrangel Island, which grew from eight to 300 individuals, died 4,000 years ago not for genetic reasons.
DNA analysis of 21 mammoths showed signs of inbreeding and low genetic diversity, but the mutations were only moderately harmful and gradually disappeared.
The exact cause of the mammoths' disappearance remains unknown, but it is assumed that it was a sudden event.
Scientists are planning further studies to unravel this mystery, and believe their findings are important for modern biodiversity conservation programs.
Earlier it was reported that scientists discovered that there was an ocean in Mongolia.
Author Oleg Loginov
Oleg Loginov — HSE student, Pravda.Ru freelance correspondent

A new study has refuted the mystery of the extinction of the last mammoths

A new study by an international team of scientists has found that the extinction of mammoths in the Wrangel Islands, which were the last on Earth, has more questions than answers.
The last population of woolly mammoths living on Wrangel Island died out 4,000 years ago.
The reason was closely related crossing - to this conclusion came the Russian scientist Sergei Vartanyan.
A group of Russian and European scientists analyzed the genomes of mammoths from Wrangel Island and their relatives from the mainland and found that the animals died not from incest, but from something else.
The herd, which turned out to be cut off on Wrangel Island, grew from eight heads to a number of 200-300 individuals in 20 generations.
Analysis of mutations in island mammoths did show that they had closely related interbreeding, resulting in low genetic diversity.
But the most dangerous mutations have disappeared from the genome.
"We can now confidently reject the idea that the population was simply too small and that they were doomed to extinction for genetic reasons.
This means that there was probably some random event that killed them, and if this random event had not happened, the mammoths would have survived to this day, ” said the author of the work, Love Dalen from the Center for Paleogenetics in Sweden.

Bloomberg: India will prevent Putin from getting closer to China
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has launched the plan.
Russia ’ s active rapprochement with China worries India, which is countering its growing influence in the region.
Concerned about the expansion of the “limitless partnership ”, Prime Minister Narendra Modi next week will go to Moscow for talks with Vladimir Putin, writes Bloomberg.
It will be his first visit to Russia since the start of Putin ’ s war in Ukraine and his first trip abroad since Modi took office as prime minister for the third time.
While Moscow will try to present the meeting as proof that Russia has not been isolated since Western sanctions were imposed, Modi ’ s trip is more motivated by a desire to reaffirm the status quo in bilateral relations and limit China ’ s influence, experts and experts close to the Indian government say.
India is wary of Moscow ’ s growing dependence on Beijing, says Swasti Rao, a research fellow at the Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defense Studies and Analysis at the Indian Ministry of Defense:
The deepening of strategic interaction between Russia and China makes New Delhi uncomfortable, as it is like a best friend sleeping with the enemy.
Given our concerns, it makes sense for the prime minister to go there and talk to Putin at the highest level.
Like China, India has taken advantage of the difficult situation that Russia has found itself in because of the sanctions.
It has more than 20 times increased purchases of Russian oil compared to 2021, saving 13 billion thanks to discounts on it, according to the April report of the rating agency ICRA.
It continues to purchase services and components from Russia to service previously purchased weapons, although major deals do not seem to be going any more.
In 2019-2023, according to the Stockholm Peace Research Institute, India for the first time since the early 1960s purchased less than half of the weapons from Russia / the USSR: the share of imports was only 36% compared to 76% in 2009-2013.
Russia has lost the Indian arms market, which has dominated for more than half a century
Russia has lost the Indian arms market, which has dominated for more than half a century
The meeting between Modi and Putin is expected to discuss the supply of logistics to India to strengthen cooperation between the armed forces of the two countries and resume discussions on joint development of a fifth-generation fighter, but breakthrough agreements in either this or other areas are likely not, informed Indian officials told Bloomberg.
Also, according to them, cooperation in nuclear energy will be discussed.
Payments in rupees for Russian oil for a long time hung on accounts in Indian banks, all of them accumulated by $8 billion.
Although the countries agreed to continue to pay for oil in UAE dirhams and increase purchases of Indian goods, their annual exports to Russia still do not exceed $5 billion.
Fearing sanctions and difficulties with calculations, Indian business is not eager to increase turnover.
Modi ’ s visit is “maintaining the status quo, ” Alexei Zakharov, an expert on India at HSE, told Bloomberg:“ Relations are not deteriorating, but there is no particular desire to improve them. ”
This is the second time that Putin ’ s turn to the East has caused concern among the leading countries in the region.
Thus, Chinese leaders may believe that Putin ’ s rapprochement with North Korea and the conclusion of a military alliance with it during a recent visit to Pyongyang may reduce the dependence of Russia and North Korea on Beijing and provoke unnecessary tension in the region.

Why India is walking the tightrope between the US and Russia
05.07.2024
After the Cold War, which began in the 1950s, split the world into two camps, the newly independent India became the founder of the Non-Aligned Movement, a group of countries that did not side with either Washington or Moscow.
Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India retained some elements of this policy unchanged, while abandoning others.
In particular, Modi has strengthened ties with the United States, in which he sees a partner in the confrontation with a more assertive China.
At the same time, he continued to develop his country ’ s long-standing ties with Russia.
As a sign of Russia ’ s important role for India, Modi will meet with President Vladimir Putin on July 8 during his first foreign visit to a fellow leader after being elected for a third term.
But these relations are becoming increasingly complex as Russia strengthens ties with China, seeking its broader support.
China and India are not allies.
1.
Is India an ally of the United States?
India and the United States have been strategic partners for at least two decades, which means they can build relationships and cooperate militarily, but are not official treaty bound allies.
Although they have much in common – both countries are large and diverse democracies – New Delhi pursues its own interests in ways that sometimes conflict with US interests.
For example, India has refused to condemn Russia in the conflict with Ukraine, while an alleged plot of assassins in the United States has triggered a criminal investigation in which senior Indian officials are implicated, according to prosecutors.
The basis of relations remains the transformation of China into an assertive regional power.
China and India are long-time rivals with a bitter border dispute, and the US is seeking to draw India as a counterweight to Beijing ’ s rise.
India is part of the Quartet, a regional security dialogue with the United States, Japan and Australia.
A group of senior U.S. officials recently visited India to discuss cooperation in technology, security and foreign investment.
2.
What is India ’ s relationship with Russia?
Although India openly declared its non-alignment during the Cold War, it maintained warm relations with Moscow and was wary of the United States, which was closer to India ’ s main rival, Pakistan.
India and Russia maintain strong ties to this day.
The basis of this relationship is India ’ s status as a reliable buyer of Russian arms and crude oil.
Today, Russia remains India ’ s largest arms supplier, although, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, shipments have declined from about two-thirds of India ’ s arms imports more than a decade ago to just over one-third today as India seeks to diversify its sources of arms supplies.
Russia also remains India ’ s largest oil supplier, although sanctions imposed on Russian oil exports have affected Russian oil imports to India.
India also stands out among the leading democracies for its unwillingness to criticize Russia and abstained from voting at the United Nations, which condemned Russia for the conflict in Ukraine.
3.
What is India ’ s relationship with China?
Relations have been tense for years.
The source of tension was a territorial dispute along their common border that lasted decades and over which the two countries fought a war in 1962.
The dispute flared up again in 2020, culminating in a series of deadly skirmishes and prompting New Delhi to ban Chinese smartphone apps and limit Chinese investment in India.
Recently, there have been rumors of a relaxation of tension.
In May, Beijing appointed its first ambassador to India in 18 months.
After his arrival, he expressed a desire to improve relations between the two countries.
China also congratulated Modi on winning the election in June, and a Chinese official said the countries were on a "healthy and stable path."
The two countries agreed on further negotiations to resolve the border dispute.
4.
How are relations between Russia and China changing?
Russia and China have been rivals since the Sino-Soviet split during the Cold War (a rivalry that also brought Russia and India closer together).
But relations have noticeably warmed as both countries united in their opposition to the US-led international order.
The Russian president made his first foreign trip to Beijing after he was re-elected for a third presidential term in March.
At the July summit on security in Kazakhstan, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin said that relations between them are “the best in history, ” and both sides vowed to jointly defend“ calm and stability in the region. ”
China has become another major buyer of Russian oil, gas and coal, helping Russia counter Western sanctions.
5.
How does the United States view relations between India and Russia?
Washington still views India as a bulwark preventing China from spreading its influence in the Indo-Pacific region.
While he has occasionally criticized India for alleged human rights abuses and the treatment of minorities, India ’ s ties with Moscow have come at minimal political cost.
Following a recent visit by senior US officials, Deputy Secretary of State Kurt Campbell said the US side had raised the issue of India ’ s ties with Russia, as well as accusations of India ’ s involvement in a plot to murder for hire.
But he also said that the United States is confident in its relations with India and wants to expand cooperation between the two countries.
According to some analysts, the US sees India as an important ally in its quest to contain China, so it does not want to risk antagonizing officials in New Delhi.

Western sanctions do not greatly harm the Indian fleet, and problems with mutual settlements are gradually solved through one-day laying firms, which in India are almost more than the Indians themselves.
This is usually explained by two reasons: India ’ s capacious market critically needs stable energy supplies.

Oil, food and cooperation.
Indian leader Narendra Modi, the leader of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (Indian People ’ s Party), who was recently elected to the post of Prime Minister of India for the third time, is going to visit Moscow.

After all, they are playing a major political game with Delhi, in the hope of unleashing the huge human resources of the Indians on China.

It does not seem to bother him, because in his third term, Modi hopes to significantly improve the lives of his own citizens.
And this cannot be done without Russian resources and the trust of the Russian authorities.

According to officials, during the meeting, Modi and Putin will discuss regional and global security, trade, and other topics on the agenda, ” writes the Times of India.
It is understood that India also claims its share of Russian fertilizers – because over the past year, the Russians (along with the Belarusians) confidently lead this cluster in the world market.
It is believed that this is important for Modi – to eliminate the threat of hunger in the poorest states of his country.

We (Russia and India) are jointly involved in integration processes, so regional affairs, regional security and global security are always in the spotlight.
In addition, of course, our bilateral trade and economic cooperation is always in the spotlight, "the Indian press warns, citing a Kremlin spokesman.
Thus, Moscow actively and on equal terms interacts with all influential countries of the world.
The West may not like this, but its parties lost the election to the Modi bloc, which constrains the influence of Americans.
Elections in India: the Russian factor.
As Delhi took from London a hundred tons of goldenIn India, the general parliamentary elections, which began on April 19, ended.
Washington could try another strategy by flooding Delhi with printed money in the form of loans.
But in the face of the huge deficit of the US budget, which even financial gurus talked about, this is clearly not the best option.
Not to mention the fact that external borrowing will still have to be repaid someday.
As for China, the development of Russian-Indian cooperation serves as a security buffer for it.
Despite all the provocations of the West, Delhi will continue to refrain from conflict with Beijing – because any such actions will seriously affect its economy, and especially the oil industry.
However, it is important to remember that interaction with Delhi is not only gasoline, and even not only fertilizers.
India has become famous for breakthroughs in the field of cinema, which Russia probably needs today – although initially in this business did not invest much money.
Well, Indian IT workers are generally ahead of the whole planet, and are often able to get the professionalism of Americans from California.
Local information companies, together with American and Arab investment funds, are lining up to invest in the Indian information sector and develop cooperation with Indian IT corporations such as Jio Platforms.
Three of the four IT professionals in the world market are Indians.
The city of Bangalore, which accounts for 38% of India ’ s IT exports, may overtake San Francisco with its Silicon Valley as the world ’ s most important information technology hub in the coming years.
In short, on the eve of Narenda Modi ’ s visit, it is important to remember that his country is not reduced to pioneering bhai-bhai.
And that the current India is one of those states that quite justifiably claim to participate in global projects.
Cooperation with him is the future, and it should be discussed in Moscow.
