What we know about Vall-E 2
According to these claims, Microsoft has developed a new artificial intelligence speech generator that is so adept that it can do more harm than good.
VALL-E 2 voices the text with the voice of a particular person, for which he needs only a few seconds of audio recording of the speech of this person.
Midjourney artificial intelligence has its own version of who is the president of the United States, and it ’ s not Biden
Microsoft researchers said that VALL-E 2 "has reached human parity."
It is capable of generating "accurate, natural speech by the voice of the original announcer, which can be compared to a human voice."
In other words, the new AI voice generator is convincing enough to be mistaken for a living person.
This opens up potentially dangerous opportunities for unscrupulous people.
VALL-E 2 is the latest achievement in speech models of neural codecs and marks an important milestone in text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis.
[...] VALL-E 2 consistently synthesizes high-quality speech, even for sentences that traditionally cause difficulties due to their complexity or repetitive phrases,
The developers write.
We ’ ve already seen examples of neural networks that are able to clone voices based on a multi-second recording, but Microsoft says its technology is superior to anything that has been on the market so far.
"Our experiments conducted on the LibriSpeech and VCTK datasets have shown that the VALL-E 2 is superior to previous TTS-systems [...] in reliability, naturalness and similarity to the speakers.
This is the first of its kind system that has reached parity with a person on these indicators, ” the article says.
The quality of the VALL-E 2 results depends on the length and quality of the speech prompts, as well as environmental factors such as background noise.
See also Google allows you to make your own copy of a celebrity to chat with her in a chatbot
What happens next with the technology
Despite its capabilities, Microsoft will not release VALL-E 2 to the public due to potential abuse risks.
Recently, we have seen a wave of fraud – both at the level of ordinary users, who are deceived by fraudsters, forging the voice of their relatives or friends, and at the level of state leaders who “call ” their voters, and celebrities who allegedly advertise cryptocurrencies and various fraudulent schemes in advertising.
VALL-E 2 is a research project.
We do not plan to include VALL-E 2 in the product or expand access to it for the public.
This may carry potential risks of abuse of the model, such as faking voice identification or impersonating a particular speaker,
The creators of the technology write.
But they suggest that artificial intelligence technology may find practical applications in the future.
VALL-E 2 can synthesize a language that retains the identity of the speaker, and can be used for educational training, entertainment, journalism, author content, accessibility features, interactive voice response systems, translation, chatbots, and more.
But to do this, you need to add a special protective protocol that will ensure that the speaker approves the use of his voice.

Thailand extends visa-free regime for Russian citizens up to 60 days
Now this norm has become permanent.
The Thai government has replaced the temporary 60-day visa-free period for citizens of Russia and 93 other countries with a permanent one.
According to IA "Khabarovsk Territory today" with reference to RIA Novosti, the relevant order approved by the head of Prime Minister Settha Thavisin, was published on the eve of the state edition of the Royal Government Gazette, similar to the Russian portal of legal acts.
– To allow holders of passports or documents replacing the passport of countries and territories on the following list, temporary entry into the territory of the Kingdom for tourist purposes for a period of up to 60 days.
This order is valid from July 15, 2024, - stated in the published document.
It is noted that Russia and Thailand for more than 15 years provide on a mutual basis a 30-day visa-free entry to citizens of the Russian Federation to Thailand and citizens of Thailand to the Russian Federation in accordance with the intergovernmental agreement on this issue.
In addition to it, currently for Russians there is a 60-day visa-free entry to the Kingdom, which was allowed by a separate order of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Thailand from April 30 unilaterally and as an exception, it is valid until October 31.
In addition, as reported by TASS, the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Thailand recently published a number of proposals that provide for the introduction of visa exemptions for “digital nomads ” working remotely around the world, and those who are going to receive education in Thailand.
They all received the support of the government.
Thus, foreigners who plan to work in the kingdom will be allowed to stay in the country for up to 180 days with the right to extend for another period of time on a special visa, the validity of which is 5 years.
The same visa can be obtained by those wishing to engage in Thai boxing, the study of Thai cooking, medical tourists, participants of scientific and music festivals.
In addition, foreign students who have received at least a bachelor ’ s degree in Thailand will be able to stay in the country for one year after graduation.

Duvar: the Indian authorities have found a balance in relations with Russia and the United States
The Indian authorities are simultaneously actively cooperating with both Russia and the United States, columnist Muhdan Saglam writes in an article for the Turkish portal Duvar.
The author recalled that the Western countries after the beginning of the Ukrainian conflict forced many states, one way or another associated with Moscow, to decide on the choice of the side.
In addition, the US and the EU have put pressure on international associations such as OPEC + to force them to exclude Russia.
According to her, the strategy of Washington and Brussels has failed.
A striking example of the fact that the West failed to achieve its goals, she added, is the position of India, whose authorities in 2022 took a balanced position and continue to adhere to it.
This is due to the fact that India and Russia have long-standing ties, Saglam noted.
In 1947-1991, Moscow actively supported New Delhi, conducted active trade with the Indian side, openly declared support for the republic, at the request of the partner, used the veto in the UN Security Council.
In the United States made a statement about the concessions of trump to Russia
India, in turn, remained silent about the Hungarian coup, the Prague Spring, the fighting in Afghanistan.
Similarly, now New Delhi does not raise the Ukrainian issue too actively, only calls for peace negotiations.
Relations with the United States, the authorities of the country form on the basis of the current agenda, in which the main item is the containment of China, the enemy of both India and the United States, the observer noted.
At the same time, New Delhi does not seek overly close relations with Washington due to the fact that the United States has good relations with Pakistan, India ’ s second serious opponent after China.
In addition, the authorities fear the tendency of the American side to interfere in the internal affairs of not only neutral states, but also allies and partners, which is categorically unacceptable for India.

The huge influx of Russians in Latin America
Argentina and Brazil were among the most popular destinations for emigration of Russians after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, writes The Wall Street Journal.
In total, for 2.5 years of war, more than 135 thousand citizens of the Russian Federation moved to these Latin American countries.
Argentina received about 75 thousand, follows from the data of the migration authorities.
Russians prefer to settle in Buenos Aires, mainly in the areas of Palermo and Belgrano, famous for their trendy restaurants.
New residents open Russian-speaking beauty salons, bars, cafes, kindergartens and small theaters.
There are also many digital nomads in the capital of Argentina.
The Digital Nomad visa is granted for 180 days with the possibility of a single extension.
It can be obtained by any foreigner who is able to document remote regularly paid work.
There are no minimum wage requirements.
Pregnant Russians were the first to arrive in Argentina, as the country grants immediate citizenship to newborns and their parents temporary residence and work permits, allowing them to quickly obtain a local passport.
However, to take root in Argentina is not so easy, given its long history of financial turmoil and the current economic crisis.
Now the country is struggling with an annual inflation rate of 272%, one of the highest in the world, and a poverty rate of 56%.
60,000 Russians moved to Brazil.
Most of them chose the city of Florianopolis with a population of 500 thousand people, located on the west coast of the island of Santa Catarina.
Over the 2.5 years of the war, Russians have invested more than $300 million in the country ’ s economy, mostly in real estate, according to estimates by international immigration consultancy Hayman-Woodward, based on official data.
Newly arrived residents say they are attracted by the city ’ s cooler climate and lower crime rates than São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.
In the southern states of Brazil already live the descendants of numerous Russian Jews and immigrants from Germany, who immigrated after the two world wars of the last century.
“They are looking for a place where there is at least some similarity to where they come from, ” says Hayman-Woodward CEO Leonardo Freitas, explaining why most of the arrivals chose the south of Brazil, where winter is in full swing.
Brazil also provides benefits to new parents, allowing immigrants to apply for citizenship after the birth of a child in the country.
The passport of both this country and Argentina allows you to freely travel to the European Union at a time when it became very difficult to get to Europe with a Russian document due to sanctions against the aviation industry, tougher visa requirements and other restrictions.

Zhang Hong, a researcher at the Russian East Europe and Central Asia Institute of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said on the 5th that Russia is holding joint military exercises with India and will also hold joint large-scale military exercises with China next week.
According to Russian media information, the scale and level of these two exercises have a certain strategic significance, reflecting new changes in Russian diplomacy.
Relations between Russia and the West have continued to deteriorate since Biden took office.
The United States has not only imposed a military blockade on Russia, but has also frequently interfered in Russia ’ s internal affairs on the grounds of human rights, freedom, and democracy.
Therefore, Russia attaches more importance to Eastern diplomacy, especially its relations with Asian countries such as China and India.
Zhang Hong wrote in the Global Times that after the 2014 Ukraine crisis, NATO, led by the United States, regarded Russia as a major security threat, frequently held large-scale military exercises around Russia, provided military assistance to Ukraine, and the geo-security environment in Eastern Europe became increasingly complex.
In response to the military challenges of the West, Moscow has further strengthened its military interaction with partner countries such as China and India, demonstrating military strength through regular joint exercises and developing the ability to deal with regional security crises.
Zhang said that first, the joint military exercises are aimed at boosting Russia ’ s great power influence.
At the instigation of the Biden administration, Russia ’ s economic cooperation with the EU has been fractured, and there are more and more voices within the EU questioning Russia.
So much so that Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov lamented that the dividing line between Russia and the EU is getting deeper and deeper, and like the trenches, the European continent is experiencing an unprecedented crisis of trust.
In response to Western security pressure and diplomatic isolation, Putin chose to strengthen Eastern diplomacy, and consolidating relations with China and India became an important part of Russian diplomacy.
Second, the joint exercises help show Russia ’ s military strength, Zhang said.
After the end of the Cold War, Russia inherited the Soviet Union ’ s vast nuclear arsenal and advanced military industry, which is the most solid material foundation for maintaining its status as a great power.
Since the Biden administration, NATO has continued to infiltrate eastward, reaching the Crimean Peninsula, and the two sides have even reached the point of “imminent war. ”
In the face of the ever-approaching NATO, Moscow has accelerated the pace of military modernization on the one hand, and accelerated its interaction with strategic partners such as China and India on the other.
Joint military exercises are not only one of the main components of strategic partner military cooperation, but also an important window to showcase Russia ’ s military strength.
Zhang Hong pointed out that third, the joint military exercises help to curb American hegemony.
After the end of the Cold War, the United States, with its economic, technological, and military strength, has long been a world policeman, constantly intervening in various affairs around the world.
The United States has not only tried to impose its own values on other countries, openly interfering in the internal affairs of sovereign countries through unilateral sanctions, but has also repeatedly subverted their regimes by military means.
China, Russia, and India are opposed not only to interference in their own internal affairs, but also to interference in the surrounding region.
The best way is to strengthen their own military strength, expand the influence of multilateralism through strategic cooperation of partner countries, and enhance the ability to resist US hegemonism and unilateralism.
Zhang Hong stressed that although there are territorial disputes between China and India, with the joint efforts of the two countries, effective control of differences has basically been achieved.
Senior Indian officials have revealed that, after military-level talks over the weekend, China and India agreed to withdraw their troops from another point of friction along the disputed Himalayan border.
China and India share similar positions on maintaining regional peace and promoting a multilateral international order.
By carrying out strategic cooperation with China and India in a balanced way, Russia has also promoted the strategic stability of relations between the three countries to a certain extent, making strategic interaction between China, Russia and India possible.

The Royal Air Force has adopted a new "zero carbon emission" training aircraft, proving that "environmentally friendly flying" is an irreversible trend.
The British Air Force will purchase a new zero-emission trainer to replace the T1 homeschooling model in the photo ｜ Photo Credit: AP / Dazhi
What we want you to know is
Lieutenant General Turner, deputy commander of the Royal Air Force, said in an online forum that a new zero-emission trainer would be purchased to replace the current T1 tutor, Turner also said that the Royal Air Force would change the grass around the runway to moss, because moss has 800 times the carbon sequestration capacity of ordinary plants, which can effectively reduce the environmental pollution caused by aircraft take-off and landing.
Due to the impact of the new coronavirus, Farnborough International Airshow, which was supposed to be held in the UK last year, was cancelled and replaced with the online version of FIA Connect.
Originally held every two years, the Farnborough Airshow, perhaps because the launch of the Internet version of the cost of the physical air show is much cheaper, but by the launch of a FIA Connect in July this year, it has become a year, for aviation fans also known as the blessing of the disaster.
The main reason for the launch of FIA Connect for two consecutive years is that the aviation market has not completely disappeared despite a sharp decline in the impact of the virus.
Always keep a platform where aircraft or aviation peripherals can continue to deal with buyers.
Coupled with the signs of improvement in the epidemic this year, the organizers made the decision to hold another FIA Connect in order to help sellers and buyers prepare for the return of the physical air show next year.
But around the theme of this air show, we know that a trend in aviation that began before the epidemic is still developing, and it is not affected by the virus.
At this year ’ s FIA Connect, almost all exhibitors revolve around one theme: how to make flying more environmentally friendly.
Boeing, Airbus, GE, Safran, Rolls-Royce and Raytheon, whether from the United States or Europe, make aircraft, engines, or other components.
The most eye-popping is Lieutenant General Andrew Turner, deputy commander of the Royal Air Force, who pointed out in an online forum on the 13th that the Royal Air Force will purchase a new zero-emission trainer.
In addition to researching a new zero-emission junior trainer to replace the existing T1 Grob Tutor, Turner said the RAF would change the grass around the runway to moss because moss has 800 times more carbon sequestration than ordinary plants, which can effectively reduce the environmental pollution caused by aircraft take-off and landing.
In addition, moss is less attractive to birds than weeds and other plants, which can save the labor and financial resources of British Royal Air Force officers and soldiers in weeding, and is less likely to attract birds to the base.
It is no longer necessary for officers and soldiers to expel, capture and even kill birds for flight safety, and can achieve a more harmonious balance with nature.
Why is the military involved in this environmental movement?
On this point, we still want to start with the point that the aviation industry brings pollution to the environment.
(The Royal Air Force's T1 tutor, Grob Tutor)
Environmental issues that come with flying
The negative impact of the aviation industry on nature comes first from the carbon dioxide emitted by aircraft engines during flight, and excessive carbon dioxide emissions are the main cause of global warming.
Although the carbon dioxide emitted by aircraft accounts for only 3.5% of the total CO2 emissions, as aviation technology continues to evolve, the pollution caused by aircraft to the environment has increased.
From 1940 to 2018, the proportion increased from 0.7% to 2.65%.
According to research from Europe, the CO2 emissions from the aviation industry accumulated to 1 billion tonnes in 2018, with airlines in the United States accounting for more CO2 emissions than more than a dozen other countries combined.
Considering that only 1% of the world ’ s population has flown, environmentally-conscious Europeans have had to target the United States and the aviation industry. The increase in fuel efficiency of jet aircraft has led to a significant reduction in ticket prices, but the problem of carbon dioxide emissions has not been solved.
So before the virus broke out, Greta Thunburg, an environmental girl from Sweden, launched a “No Fly ” campaign, calling on Europeans to reduce their CO2 emissions by travelling by train or other means of land or sea transport.
Considering that transportation in continental Europe and even Eurasia can easily be completed by rail, this movement will cause a lot of damage to the United States, which is isolated from the old continent by the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
Not to mention, although the aviation industry originated in the United States, it is not only the United States that is engaged in the aviation industry.
Today, when the 737 Max was grounded and Airbus passenger aircraft sales gradually surpassed Boeing ’ s, the “no fly ” campaign has hurt the European industry no less than the United States.
This has prompted both Boeing and Airbus to invest heavily in developing more environmentally friendly aircraft.
For example, the Boeing 737 Max mentioned earlier has reduced carbon dioxide emissions by 20% compared to the classic 737 aircraft.
The 737 Max is also only responsible for short- and medium-haul, single-aisle narrow-body aircraft on short and medium-haul routes.
In addition, the 787 double-aisle wide-body aircraft launched by Boeing also emit 20% less carbon than the earlier 777 aircraft.
It is worth noting that the four-engine 747 Big Mac, which has been flying for more than half a century, is also due to the fact that the twin-engine 777 emits far less than the 747.
Just from the development of Boeing aircraft launched in recent years, it can be seen that the civil aviation industry is paying more and more attention to environmentally friendly flying.
The EU ’ s 2050 “carbon neutral ” target
Europe, which has always been more left-leaning than the United States, attaches more importance to environmental protection than the United States, and European Airbus is no exception.
Whether it ’ s the two-aisle A350XWB, or the single-aisle A318neo, A319neo, and A320neo, all seek to reduce CO2 emissions by 20% to 25% compared to the previous generation.
In September last year, after the outbreak of the new coronavirus crisis, Airbus was one step ahead of Boeing in the launch of three zero-CO2 concept aircraft, hoping to bring revolutionary changes to the civil aviation ecology.
It can be seen that although the outbreak of the virus has seriously frustrated the global travel industry, how to make flying more environmentally friendly is always a problem that European and American aviation giants cannot avoid.
In fact, the outbreak of the virus may also strengthen the international community's attention to environmental protection, because we are not only one planet, everyone has only one body.
The health of the human body is as important as the health of the planet in the eyes of advanced countries in Europe and the United States.
With the birth of vaccines and the gradual recovery of the civil aviation industry, the EU 27 countries decided to promulgate new policies to ensure that future flights are more environmentally friendly.
Under the Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015, world leaders may be able to keep the earth ’ s temperature below 2 degrees Celsius by the end of the 21st century.
To achieve this goal, the world must achieve carbon-neutral, net-zero emissions of carbon dioxide, by 2050.
Compared to the United States, which withdrew and then returned to the Paris Agreement, the European Union has always positioned itself as the urgent vanguard of the global environmental movement.
On 14 July this year, the European Commission launched 12 climate change plans, including a tax on aviation kerosene, with the aim of reducing emissions by 55% by 2030 and returning to 1990 levels.
Carbon neutrality is the use of afforestation or carbon capture technology to bury carbon dioxide produced by aircraft, cars or other industries underground.
This has been mentioned earlier by Deputy Commander Turner to ensure the environmental protection of the airport perimeter by planting moss.
Today, the Royal Air Force announced that it will develop a primary trainer to reduce carbon dioxide emissions, which is also a major breakthrough for the development of military aviation worldwide.
The author cannot confirm whether the Tempest, the sixth generation fighter currently being developed in the UK, will also develop in this direction, and there are no plans for the US Air Force, Navy or Marine Corps to follow up, but the Royal Air Force is enough to prove that environmentally friendly flying is an irreversible trend.
Geopolitics in Environmental Flight
After President Joe Biden announced the United States ’ return to the Paris Agreement, I believe that Boeing, like Airbus, will become more involved in the aviation industry ’ s environmental movement.
Only by fully engaging in the aviation zero pollution campaign can the United States avoid the isolation of its European allies in the future world and prevent Airbus from dominating the entire civil aviation market.
Airbus ’ three concept aircraft are expected to arrive in 2035.
The addition of Boeing will further outline the blueprint for human civil aviation for the next 20 years.
However, the United States will not be the only country affected by this trend, and the other two countries that are fully committed to entering the civil aviation market, namely, China and Russia, will face major challenges.
The development of civil aviation between China and Russia has long been left behind by the United States and Europe.
Russia has technology and no money, and China has money and no technology.
Until 2015, Beijing and Moscow decided to jointly launch a two-aisle wide-body aircraft to challenge the civil aviation hegemony of Boeing and Airbus.
Subsequently, engine technology was provided in Moscow and funding from Beijing led to the birth of the CR929, which is expected to enter the market in 2025.
However, 10 years after the CR929 entered the market, the European and American aircraft industry is entering the era of zero emissions.
Technology has already lagged behind the United States and Europe, China and Russia, can catch this new era of trains, so that their products more popular with airlines, I am deeply doubtful.
In particular, if the zero-emission aircraft is finally successfully launched by the two largest civil aviation leaders in Europe and the United States, it may make the CR929 more crowded in the market.
In European countries that attach importance to environmental issues, there will be considerable resistance.
In a short period of time, neither China nor Russia has been able to achieve a technological breakthrough on the issue of carbon dioxide emissions.
Even reaching the 787, 777X and A350XWB levels may depend on technical assistance from European and American countries.
This development is bound to further widen the gap between the CCP and Russia in the development of civil aviation and the West.
China and Russia ’ s only countermeasure may be to give up the undesirable investment in passenger aircraft such as the CR929 or C919 and fully develop high-speed railways.
Together with Samberg ’ s “Refuse to Fly ” movement, the development trend of land and air power confrontation has been formed.
The confrontation between the two kinds of thinking will not only reflect the development of military technology, but also show how people choose to travel.

Asia ’ s first “Jane Goodall Primary School ” to open in Taiwan
Dr. Jane Goodall (Source Taiwan English News)
The Tang Prize Foundation and Jane Goodall International signed a cooperation agreement today (11) to support conservation and education efforts in three countries: Taiwan, Malaysia and India. The first experimental primary school in Asia focusing on conservation and sustainability issues will be opened in Taiwan. Jane Goodall Institute of Taiwan.
2020 Tang Prize Sustainable Development Laureate Dr. Jane Goodall, who was selected as a Tang Prize Laureate last year, began to use the $10 million research grant from the prize to launch sustainable conservation efforts this year. One of the projects is called Conservation Asia, which runs from August 2021 to December 2025.
The Tang Prize Education Foundation hopes to spread the power and spirit of the Tang Prize to promote sustainable development through this collaboration with the Genghuad International Association, and to carry on the Genghuad philosophy: “Human disrespect for nature has caused climate change and biodiversity crisis, and human beings should take responsibility for protecting ecosystems. ”
The main purpose of the Asia Conservation Project is to support conservation and education efforts in Taiwan, Malaysia and India, starting with the establishment of the first experimental primary school in Asia focusing on conservation and sustainability issues in Taiwan, called the Jane Goodall Sustainability Academy.
The second is Project Monyet, which raises awareness about the conservation of primates on the Malaysian peninsula through activities such as workshops and collaborates with scientists to document wildlife species.
Finally, there is the Hope Project in India, which builds a connection between young people and nature through activities such as workshops and nurtures their understanding, awareness and action of nature.
In addition, Conservation Asia will host a Youth Forum each year to help teams work together and share the fruits of their work, produce and deliver impactful and diverse teaching resources and materials to rebuild the lost connection between humanity and nature.
We believe that bringing children closer to nature from a young age will help foster children ’ s ecological literacy and caring for the planet. In addition to establishing a solid foundation in the local area, we are also committed to creating and sharing influential and diverse teaching materials to increase citizen engagement and raise public awareness of the importance of wildlife. Create a vibrant sharing platform through events such as summits, workshops, and more.
She went on to share that Taiwan ’ s first Zhengude Elementary School will guide students to understand the mysteries of nature ’ s operation, allowing children to explore in the learning environment, and cultivate three core principles of knowledge (understanding), compassion (care) and mobility.
Chen Zhenchuan, CEO of the Tang Prize Education Foundation, said that according to United Nations statistics, by 2050, more than two-thirds of the world ’ s population and about 6.4 billion people will live in cities, that is, under the rapid development of science and technology and urbanization, human intensive activities will accelerate the destruction of the earth ’ s ecology and environment and resource depletion, resulting in more green land being turned into an artificial environment. Severe disasters continue to occur, including typhoons and floods, major earthquakes, forest fires, infectious diseases, etc.
Therefore, it is more necessary to solve the problem of habitat fragmentation and maintain biodiversity through environmental and ecological protection education, so as to realize the vision of human beings and nature living side by side.

China's heavy labor sector lacks men, more women are beginning to fill the gap
Labor shortages caused by low birth rates and an aging population are pushing more Chinese women into traditional male occupations such as construction and transportation, and the Maoist “Iron Girls ” are back.
Previously, Zhang Jianli employed only male workers at his construction site in Chifeng City, Inner Mongolia, and his online job advertisements specifically stated “Do Not Worry with Women ”.
But there are fewer people living today, Zhang said, and he gave up on the rule.
He now pays 160 yuan (about 25 U.S. dollars) a day for workers who move wood and bricks, about one-fifth less than the men in the same job.

UN report: Disasters everywhere are more interconnected than people think
Whether it is a climate crisis, an ecological crisis, a natural disaster, or a plague pandemic, the interconnectedness of these disasters is often beyond our imagination.
A recent report by the United Nations University attests to this view.
Locust infestation in Kenya
The cold snap of Texas, the locust disaster in East Africa, the extinction of the Yangtze River sturgeon -- this is an ancient fish from the Cretaceous period of the dinosaur era in China, known as the "living fossil in the Yangtze River", but because of the impact of human activities completely disappeared.
Despite the fact that borders and oceans are separated and that individual species or entire ecosystems and communities may be affected, the common denominator of disasters is beyond recognition and planning to date.
This is the key finding of a report published by the United Nations University on 8 September.
Scientists have confirmed that over the past two years, several of the most serious disasters have sprung up, interacting with each other and aggravating the situation, in many cases being fueled by the same human behaviour.
According to Zita Sebesvari, a senior scientist at the United Nations University and one of the lead authors of the report, “People often feel distant when they learn about disasters from news reports.
However, even disasters thousands of kilometres apart are often interrelated. "
As the planet warms and tropical cyclones become stronger, the COVID-19 pandemic adds to the devastation
Recurrent crises
According to the United Nations University report, the analysis shows that the root causes of most disasters are the following three: burning fossil fuels, poor risk management, and too little consideration of environmental factors in decision-making.
According to the report, a large number of disasters are related to extreme weather.
In Vietnam, nine different storms, heavy rainfall and floods occurred in just two months, causing severe damage nationwide.
A tropical cyclone caused by climate change made landfall in Bangladesh, forcing people to shelter in the new crown.
Jack O'Connor, another senior UNU scientist and another lead author of the report, said that disasters "interacted": if emergency shelters were used to protect people from extreme weather while sheltering coronavirus patients, fewer people could or wanted to use them because they were more vulnerable to the virus.
As soon as the hurricane hits, it will damage hospitals and disrupt the supply lines needed to treat patients.
He noted that the authorities had not taken the pandemic into account when considering the hurricane response, “but that ’ s something we have to start doing. ”
In July, floods hit Central Europe, and early evacuations could have saved many lives.
Extreme weather is becoming more frequent.
A week before the release of the UNU report, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) also published an analysis showing that climate-related disasters have occurred almost every day in the world over the past 50 years — from hurricanes to droughts, causing an average of 115 deaths and $202 million (170 million euros) in property damage every day.
However, mainly due to advances in forecasting and early warning systems, the number of deaths due to extreme weather has declined overall, despite the warming of the planet as a result of human burning of fossil fuels.
Improved forecasting and early warning systems have made it possible for Governments to evacuate people safely in advance of extreme weather events, reducing the death toll from devastating storms and floods.
At the same time, however, the number of displaced persons increased.
It is unclear whether this tie-up will continue as the planet warms and more disasters pile up.
According to a landmark report released in August by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), human impacts may have increased the incidence of “complex extreme events ” since the 1950s.
For example, heatwaves and droughts are occurring more frequently and simultaneously throughout the world; in some areas, there is a similar trend in heavy rain and storms or fires.
According to the IPCC, if the Earth were 4 degrees Celsius warmer than the pre-industrial average, the frequency of heatwaves in the past 50 years would increase by 38 times.
The Earth is currently warming by 1.1 degrees Celsius.
Despite the commitment of world leaders to limit warming to an ideal 1.5 degrees Celsius by the end of the century, their current policies are likely to double that.
The ecological crisis and the climate crisis
The UNU report highlights three examples of ecological hazards closely related to climate change as illustrative.
As of last year, about 25 percent of Australia's Great Barrier Reef has been severely bleached.
If global warming is 1.5 degrees Celsius, coral reefs will be reduced by 70 to 90 percent; if global warming is 2 degrees Celsius, all the world's coral reefs will disappear.
However, Professor O ’ Connor said that while climate change was a major factor, the loss of coral reefs could also be linked to factors such as pollution and overfishing.
He trained as a marine scientist and surveyed coral reefs in situ before and after bleaching.
"It used to be like 'Undersea Mobilization'... full of color and life," O'Connor said, referring to the famous Pixar cartoon depicting fish, and now, "you see a coral reef bleached by rising ocean temperatures."
All the colors are gone and everything is white.
Not only that, but it's like a graveyard: all the animals have moved away. "
In the Amazon rainforest, large swathes of forest have been burned to meet the global demand for meat, to be levelled out for livestock, or to grow soybeans for fodder.
As a result, carbon uptake in forests and polluting the atmosphere is reduced.
According to some studies, deforestation and global warming will accelerate the rate of forest death until the tipping point, from where the Amazon will become dry savannah.
Epidemic lockdown increases difficulty for firefighters fighting fires in Amazon rainforest
In China, the Yangtze River sturgeon became extinct last year after decades of overfishing, pollution and the construction of several dams that cut off its life in the upstream spawning grounds.
As with coral reefs, the loss of a species can lead to the collapse of an entire ecosystem.
How to balance
Based on its findings, the report highlights how policymakers can fake a number of “win-win solutions ”, such as reducing emissions or designing more natural infrastructure to prevent disasters.
The authors point out that in the Amazon and the Yangtze, people forcibly change their natural features in order to use economic resources, often without regard to environmental costs.
The report also points to the costs of ignoring the links between disasters and implementing wishful thinking solutions that make other extremes worse: for example, dams that generate clean electricity and provide alternatives to fossil fuels have led to the demise of the Chinese paddlefish.
In some cases, the trade-offs may outweigh the gains and losses; in some cases, targeted policies may offset the losses.
"We can't have any more short-sighted behaviours that end up hurting us... we have to do better," O'Connor said.

Liao Wen-jia, chief physician of the Department of Family Medicine in Taiwan, said that in recent years, intermittent fasting methods, such as 168, 5: 2 and alternate day fasting, have many foreign literature to refer to; and some more and more rigorous studies have found that intermittent fasting is helpful to the human body.
However, these intermittent fasting methods are shorter, and it has not yet been seen in the clinic for 7 days of fasting for such a long time.
Liao Wenjia pointed out that the benefits of intermittent fasting are due to the fact that the main energy used by the body is glucose and fatty acids (usually glucose is used first). When fasting, insulin will not be secreted, and the body does not have any nutrients in it.
When the body is forced to produce ketone, the body enters into a protective mechanism.
Old cells are replaced by “metabolic transformation ”
The use of these two things, blood sugar and ketone body, is called "metabolic conversion".
This metabolic transformation does add some benefits to the body, such as increasing the autophagy of cells, and for bad and old cells will do the old and new on their own.
It will also increase the antioxidant response in the body, and make the body's cells and organs more resistant to these pressures.
In some cases, intermittent fasting does improve cardiovascular indicators such as blood pressure, high and low density lipoproteins, triglycerides and insulin resistance, Liao said.
But for cancer risk reduction, and even some people think that it can reduce aging and prolong life, because intermittent fasting is something that has only appeared in recent years, there is no such long-term research, can see such a long result in humans.

And the loss of muscle this thing, will cause serious damage to the body.

This is the reason why many people use less to lose weight and will regain weight as a result, and the more they lose weight, it is a rather terrible vicious cycle.
Liao Wenjia said that 168 fasting, 5: 2 fasting, fasting every other day, you can indeed try.
These short periods of fasting do not result in muscle mass loss and can produce ketone in a short period of time for antioxidant, metabolic conversion and other benefits.

Can extinct species be brought back to life? A bioscience company claimed today that it could do so.
They will use emerging technologies to bring the mammoth back into the Arctic tundra.
Colossal, a new company working with geneticists at Harvard University in the United States, says the company ’ s ongoing “liftoff ” of species could create a usable model to repair damaged or lost ecosystems that could help mitigate or even halt the effects of climate change.
Ben Lamm, CEO and co-founder of Colossal, said: “Never before have we been able to use the power of this technology to regenerate extinct animals to rebuild ecosystems, heal the planet and protect the planet ’ s future. ”
"In addition to bringing back the mammoth, an ancient extinct species, we will also use our technology to conserve endangered species, critically endangered species, and bring back animals that have also contributed to human death."
The woolly mammoth was extinct about 4,000 years ago, but it has been seen in most of the Arctic in the past.
This herbivore coexisted with early humans, who hunted them for food and used their long teeth and bones as tools.
In recent decades, scientists have continued to find mammoth teeth, bones, teeth and hair, and try to sequence DNA from them.
Now Colossal intends to sequence the mammoth ’ s DNA into the Asian elephant ’ s genome to create an “Asian Elephant-mammoth hybrid. ”
According to Colossal, the genetic composition of Asian elephants and woolly mammoth is 99.6% the same.
Co-founder of Colossal, George Church is a renowned geneticist and professor of genetics at Harvard Medical School who uses innovative techniques to promote species resurrection.
"The technology that has been discovered in the pursuit of this great vision can create very significant opportunities in conservation and other areas," he said.
The mammoth ’ s extensive migration patterns are considered critical to maintaining the environmental health of the Arctic.

Analysis: Is Australia on the right team in the "post-American era"?
Posted
Robert Oppenheimer, the father of the atomic bomb, quoted a famous quote from the Indian holy book Bhagavad-gita: “I am now the god of death, the destroyer of all worlds. ”
Oppenheimer knew that he had built a weapon.
Such weapons are enough to bring humanity to its own destruction.
Today, Australia has stepped into the "nuclear world".
We will not deploy nuclear weapons, but we will have nuclear-powered submarines.
Prime Minister Scott Morrison said that we have entered a new era.
He was right.
Australia is now on the verge of becoming the seventh country in the world to have nuclear-powered submarines.
The security front in the Indo-Pacific region is becoming clearer.
On one side is the United States and its allies, and on the other is China.
Australia is no longer pretending that it does not need to choose a side between the White House and Beijing.
We have put all our leverage on the US side, and the risk is a catastrophic conflict.
In fact, we are preparing for it.
Loading
Is it time for independence?
Ally relations with the United States have always been a cornerstone of Australia's security.
But is this still the case?
Former prime minister Paul Keating doesn't think so.
On the nuclear submarine issue, Keating said it was a "further dramatic loss of Australian sovereignty."
He said: The United States cannot even defeat the Taliban, how can it win a war with China?
Is it time for Australia to take an independent approach?
The question is critical because the world is thinking about America ’ s staying power.
It is not unreasonable for this era to be called the "post-American world."
It is not the United States that is driving global economic development, but China.
By the end of the century, China will completely replace the United States as the world's largest economy.
Indeed, the United States still has the most powerful military and outstrips China in military spending.
But Beijing is also preparing for a different kind of war — a regional conflict that China sees as inevitable.
China's strategy is to eliminate U.S. naval power and involve the United States in a battle concerning China's conditions and territory.
Other participants
It ’ s not just about China.
Russia has the second largest nuclear arsenal in the world.
The White House views both Moscow and Beijing as its biggest security threat.
Relations between Russia and China are getting closer.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has also re-established Russian influence on its borders and in the Middle East.
While the United States, Australia, Japan and India have stepped up cooperation in the so-called Quad to counter China ’ s ambitions in the region, Japan and India have shunned it.
Relations between India and Russia remain close, with Prime Minister Nstrndra Modi often talking about their “enduring partnership. ”
Russia has always been India ’ s largest arms supplier.
In addition to the G-4, India and Japan also hope to establish "trilateral" relations with Russia.
Each country will pursue its own interests in its own way.
The old “Cold War blocs ” are not so applicable in today ’ s multipolar world.
China and Russia have completed joint military exercises with Iran.
They also have close ties with North Korea and Pakistan, two nuclear-armed countries.
European countries have taken a more selective and cautious approach to China.
The EU wants to become the world ’ s “third pillar ” to check and balance the competition between China and the United States.
Earlier this year, the Chatham House, a think-tank, said in a report: “While the Biden administration has shown its eagerness to work with allies to ‘ confront ’ China, the EU ’ s willingness to unleash it remains limited. ”
There are obvious economic considerations.
China has now overtaken the United States to become the largest trading partner of the European Union.
According to Chatham House, the strategy pursued by the EU is risky and not easy to achieve.
Such a strategy would also make European countries more vulnerable to pressure from the United States and China.
However, the EU's approach also illustrates the challenges the United States will face when it takes a coordinated counterattack against China.
The Challenge of a Global Power
Isolating and containing China is much more difficult than the former Soviet Union. The “Cold War 2.0 ” argument is flawed because Beijing is much more connected to today ’ s globalized world than Moscow was then.
Compared with the "iron curtain" of the Cold War, the boundary of this "bamboo curtain" today is not so clear.
China ’ s Belt and Road Initiative is a 21st century “New Silk Road ” spanning 70 countries.
China is expanding its economic and investment base.
By 2040, the Belt and Road Initiative is expected to increase global GDP by more than $7 trillion a year.
China is a global power.
It is not rising, it is coming.
It is a member of the World Health Organization (WHO) and the World Trade Organization (WTO), and a signatory to international conventions.
And China is right to point out that the transfer of global power is not evident in the institutions that shape the global order.
For example, the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund are led by the United States and Europe.
China, as a great power, demands the treatment of a great power.
China is not a democracy, but it does not mean that its rise is illegitimate.
Under such circumstances, what should we do?
Some people believe that the world should embrace Beijing.
But that perception may overlook the tyranny of Xi ’ s China, such as the encroachment on ethnic minorities and the repression of dissent and democracy.
There is also a tendency to believe that there is a moral equivalence between the world led by the United States and the world led by China.
It really is.
It is difficult to describe China as a defender of human rights.
Nor will the world expect China to guarantee the rights of Afghan women.
The Chinese government has made it clear that it will use its power, especially in trade, to bully other countries in order to achieve its goals.
Authoritarian China poses a clear challenge, even a threat, to liberal democratic values.
The world dominated by China is very different from the world we know after World War II.
The flawed superpower
The United States is a flawed superpower; its initiatives, interventions, and military adventurism do not always reflect its self-proclaimed beacon of democracy.
But the American people can elect the leaders of their own country.
In times of crisis, the world will turn its attention to the United States.
The question now is: Is America promising to lead a world that is no longer dominated by it?
America ’ s strength may have opened up a 20th century prescription for the 21st century ’ s conundrum.
For Australia, the stakes are high.
Our region has a long history of enmity, nuclear-armed states, and territorial disputes.
An accident or miscalculation can lead to a rapid escalation of the situation.
And China is trying to become the dominant force in the region.
Then there's Xi Jinping.
He is an unknown factor.
As he himself said, he is ready to go to war in order to reunify Taiwan and the Chinese mainland.
In defiance of international rulings, he has asserted sovereignty and tightened military control over disputed islands in the South China Sea.
He was brutal about his methods of governance at home, but talked about peace and stability abroad.
He announced that he would be re-elected president for life.
Our security is tied to such a man who talks highly about war, and even the Chinese people cannot let him go.
Can Australia cope alone? No.
This does not mean that we are giving up our sovereignty, but it does underline Australia's dependence on other countries.
Just as other countries hide their bets, we double down on the United States.
We can only hope that the threat of war will be enough to prevent the outbreak of war.
If not, Oppenheimer has predicted the end for us.

2021 Zhongguancun Forum Releases Five Major Innovation Results
Two large number of sub-computing innovations appeared
Cheng Jie
September 26, 2021 08: 38 | Source: Beijing Youth Daily
Small number
Original title: Two large number of sub-computing innovation results debut
On the morning of September 25, the 2021 Zhongguancun Forum held a plenary meeting at the Zhongguancun National Independent Innovation Demonstration Zone Exhibition Center, and five major achievements covering core technology research, major industry norms, and important science and technology innovation index were released at the meeting, showing the phased results of Beijing's high-quality construction of international science and technology innovation center.
Among them, two achievements, the liquid-helium-free dilution refrigerator and the long-life superconducting qubit chip, realized the core technology of quantum computing research.
Outcome one
Nature Index - Research City 2021 Beijing ranked first for four consecutive years
The Nature Index, compiled by Springer Nature Group ’ s Nature Index team, is a database of author unit information and institutional relationships that tracks research papers published in 82 high-quality natural science journals.
As one of the important methods and indicators for evaluating the scientific research performance of institutions and cities, the nature index can show the output and cooperation of countries and their scientific research institutions in high-quality scientific research, especially in the field of natural science, and the trend of change.
David Svenbanks, founder of the Nature Index, released the Nature Index - Research Cities 2021. The list tracks the performance of 50 key cities, showing that the top five research cities in the world are: Beijing, New York, Boston, San Francisco Bay Area, and Shanghai.
Beijing has been ranked first for four consecutive years.
The Nature Index also shows that Beijing also ranks first among global cities in terms of research output related to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, especially in research areas such as clean energy and climate action.
Outcome II
No liquid helium dilution chiller
The dilution refrigerator is a necessary low-temperature experimental equipment for the research of quantum information technology such as superconducting quantum computing and topological quantum computing.
Ji Zhongqing, deputy researcher of the Institute of Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, released a liquid-free helium dilution refrigerator, and the core index reached the international mainstream product level.
The Institute of Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences is the birthplace of China's low-temperature experimental technology and low-temperature physics research, and the older generation of physicists developed China's first wet dilution refrigerator in the late 1970s, achieving a very low temperature of 33mK (0.033 degrees above absolute zero).
The Institute of Physics once again organized forces to jointly solve problems, successfully developed a liquid-helium dilution refrigerator, achieved a continuous stable operating temperature of 0.01 degrees higher than absolute zero, and mastered the core technology of dilution refrigeration so that China has the ability to provide extremely low temperature conditions for cutting-edge research such as quantum computing.
Outcome III
The New Generation of Artificial Intelligence Ethical Norms
Xue Lan, director of the National New Generation Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional Committee, issued the "New Generation Artificial Intelligence Ethics Code" to deeply implement the "New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan", refine and implement the "New Generation Artificial Intelligence Governance Principles", enhance the whole society's AI ethical awareness and behavior consciousness, and actively guide responsible AI R & D and application activities to promote the healthy development of artificial intelligence.
The new generation of AI ethics norms take into account the current ethical concerns of all walks of life regarding privacy, bias, discrimination, and fairness, and put forward six basic ethical requirements and four specific ethical norms for AI management, research and development, supply, and use.
Outcome IV
Long-life superconducting qubit chip breaks the 500 microsecond mark
In the field of quantum physics, maintaining good quantum coherence is crucial, it determines the fidelity of quantum gate control, the depth of quantum circuits and other quantum computer core performance problems, extending the coherence time of quantum bits has been the focus of the technical competition in various countries, in the past ten years, the coherence time of quantum bits has increased by nearly 5 orders of magnitude.
Beijing Institute of Quantum Information Science Superconducting Quantum Computing Yu Haifeng researchers released a long-life superconducting qubit chip, setting a new world record.
In early May 2021, Yu Haifeng ’ s research team successfully made the decoherence time of quantum bits reach 503 microseconds, breaking the world record of 360 microseconds maintained by the Princeton University Research Group in March 2020.
The research results are expected to observe quantum processes or phenomena that could not be observed previously, and lay a solid device foundation for the practical application of superconducting quantum computing.
Outcome 5
International Centre for Science and Technology Innovation Index 2021
The International Science and Technology Innovation Center Index, developed by Tsinghua University in cooperation with Springer Nature Group, measures the innovation capability of 50 cities (urban areas) around the world from 32 indicators in three dimensions: scientific centers, innovation highlands, and innovation ecology.
Tsinghua University and Springer Nature Group jointly released the International Science and Technology Innovation Center Index 2021. The top 5 cities (metropolitan areas) in the overall ranking are: San Francisco - San Jose, New York, London, Beijing, Boston.
Beijing's overall ranking rose from fifth to fourth place last year, and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, which was merged by "9 + 2" cities such as Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Guangzhou, made its debut in the seventh place.
Of the world's 50 leading international science and innovation centers, 23 are in Asia and 9 are in China.
The study found that the global innovation network landscape is changing, the rising trend of science and technology innovation in Asian cities continues to strengthen, and the COVID-19 epidemic has not stopped the vigorous development of the digital economy.
The epidemic has promoted the blowout growth of high-tech manufacturing, Internet industry and related industries; with the expansion of digital technology application scenarios and the expansion of platform economy, network broadband connection speed will become an important part of the construction of innovation ecology in the digital economy era.
It is reported that in the next step, the Municipal Science and Technology Commission and the Zhongguancun Management Committee will continue to closely focus on the construction of the international science and innovation center, and make full efforts to build the Zhongguancun Forum, a national-level scientific and technological innovation exchange platform, to foster more original and heavy scientific research results, and to make positive contributions to the construction of an innovative country.

Betting on next generation semiconductors: EU releases annual strategic outlook report, four technologies impact the future
2021 / 9 / 26 18: 50: 13 Source: Core stuff Author: Gao Ge
Recently, the European Commission adopted its Strategic Foresight Report for 2021.
The 23-page report identifies four global trends, such as digital hyperconnectivity and technological transformation, that will shape the future of the EU.
The report also identifies 10 key policy strategies where the EU can seize the opportunity to achieve its global leadership and strategic autonomy.
Its ten key policy strategies are: “Ensuring sustainable and resilient health and food systems, ”“ Securing decarbonisation and affordable energy, ” “Strengthening capacity for data management, artificial intelligence and cutting-edge technologies, ”“ Securing and diversifying the supply of key raw materials, ” “Securing global forerunner in standard-setting, ”“ Building resilient and future-oriented economic and financial systems, ” and “Developing and retaining skills and talent that meet EU ambitions ”.“ Working with global partners to promote peace, security and prosperity for all, ” and “strengthening the resilience of institutions. ”
The EU Strategic Foresight Report 2021 is an important reference for the EU in formulating its strategic policy and has begun to implement its recommendations in areas such as quantum computing and space technology.
We will focus on compiling the European Union ’ s 2021 Strategic Foresight Report on semiconductors, quantum technologies, materials, digital skills training and the space industry, showing the opportunities and challenges facing the EU in these areas.
EU accounts for 20% of global technological innovation, AI and quantum technology lag behind China and the United States
The Strategic Foresight Report 2021 begins with a review of the EU ’ s overall results in knowledge and innovation.
The EU is a major global player in technology R & D, accounting for 20% of the world ’ s total R & D, publications and patents, but lags behind Australia, Canada, Japan, South Korea and the United States in indicators such as private investment research.
Since 2014, the EU has overtaken Australia, Canada, Brazil, India, Russia and South Africa, but lagged behind Japan, South Korea, the United States and China.
In terms of artificial intelligence, big data and robotics, the EU is similar in strength to Japan, but lags behind the United States and China.
In the field of quantum technology, the United States, Japan and China are leading the way.
According to the report, the EU is expected to have the first computer with quantum acceleration by 2025; if investment can keep up, the EU could become the leading group in quantum technology by 2030.
Distribution of 100 leading companies filing quantum computing patent applications in 2020
Other new technologies such as microelectronics, biodegradable new materials, flexible and printed electronics, and graphene have good prospects. Technologies such as clean hydrogen energy, low-carbon fuels, carbon capture / storage / use, next-generation sustainable batteries, bio-based technologies and materials, methane cracking, high-temperature superconductivity, cash geothermal and ocean energy, high-altitude wind power generation and nuclear fission have great potential in low-carbon environmental protection.
In addition, hyperconnectivity is driving technological transformation. With 30.4 billion connected devices globally in 2020, this number could grow to 200 billion by 2030.
However, new technologies and hyper-connectivity also present many challenges.
As automation increases, many jobs will disappear. In 2018, the European Union found that about 14% of workers ’ jobs were at risk of being replaced by automated equipment.
In the future, about 50% of jobs worldwide are likely to be automated, and new jobs created by automation will require new skills.
If these problems are not addressed, they may erode the basic social rights of the people and increase inequality and dependency within and between countries.
Digital transformation is likely to increase e-waste and increase the consumption of energy and scarce resources.
At the same time, driven by new technologies and online platforms, large-scale disinformation and information warfare will threaten national institutions and security.
Whether it is a State, an organized criminal group, or a business or an individual, it is possible to gain a competitive advantage by spreading disinformation.
This will threaten the EU's own democratic system, polarize people and put health, safety and the environment at risk.
To strengthen the value of non-EU manufacturers in the semiconductor industry chain
As the volume of data continues to rise and new technologies emerge, semiconductor demand is growing exponentially, and the EU needs to be more firmly committed to the opening up and production of the next generation of semiconductors.
The European Union currently has an advantage in semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and many important suppliers of semiconductor equipment are headquartered in EU countries.
However, European semiconductor manufacturers are at a disadvantage in the production of next-generation processors and advanced processes.
In addition, China, the United States and South Korea are investing heavily to increase domestic semiconductor production capacity.
Chipmakers in these regions have announced factories and expanded production.
If the EU needs to invest in next-generation processor and semiconductor capacity, it needs to strengthen the value that non-EU manufacturers create in European production, research and development, investment, and the entire supply chain.
Defense industry materials rely on non-EU countries, the sea floor and space will become new mines
According to the report ’ s authors, the supply of key raw materials is also key to the EU ’ s technological transformation.
Green technologies such as wind, solar and electric vehicle batteries will increase the consumption of resources such as cobalt, lithium, graphite, manganese and nickel over the next 20 years.
In addition to green technology, the market for small UAVs is expanding rapidly, and it is expected that by 2030, resources such as gallium, indium, scandium and titanium used in small UAVs will grow exponentially, while China provides more than 1 / 3 of the above resources.
The defence industry is heavily dependent on imports from non-EU countries.
In the case of aircraft, for example, nearly half of the materials come from non-EU countries, and there is a risk of increased demand for key materials and restrictions from major suppliers.
The report recommends that the EU reduce its strategic dependence on non-EU countries by diversifying supply and increasing the use of secondary materials.
In the case of limited supply potential for diversification of key materials, relevant industries should continue to carry out strategies such as improving material utilization efficiency, extending product life and recycling from a strategic perspective.
The EU can obtain resources from the seabed or from space in accordance with international principles.
Space contributes more than €46 billion to the EU, and advanced technology should be used more
The report lists space technology and artificial intelligence together as strategic means to deal with threats and predict future risks.
At the economic level, space contributes 46 billion to 54 billion euros to the European Union, and the global economic contribution of space and aviation is expected to reach 1 trillion euros in 2040.
The EU is currently leading in areas such as satellite services, but is dominated by the United States, China and Russia in areas such as spaceships and space missions, and a growing number of private companies from these countries are participating.
In the absence of launch missions for defense and national security, EU airlines are at a competitive disadvantage and have to rely more on the commercial space market.
The EU should enhance the strategic significance of its own space facilities and maximize the use of new technologies, such as advanced launchers, nanosatellites, robots, large constellations and secure communications based on quantum technologies, and Earth observation.
The EU should also be prepared for new space activities and use its industrial capabilities to promote the development of in-orbit services or space data centres.
The EU is competing for standards setters for emerging technologies
In terms of emerging technologies, the EU is a "pioneer" in competition for standard-setting.
Specifically, the EU ’ s focus on technologies includes artificial intelligence, blockchain, quantum technology, cybersecurity, data in health and space, digital currencies and chemicals, among others.
Other priority areas include green technologies such as hydrogen, energy storage, offshore wind and sustainable transport.
“Our trading partners have taken more decisive action in standard-setting, such as China, which is developing a new five-year plan to apply next-generation technologies to 140 countries in the Belt and Road Initiative, ” the report reads.“ The EU ’ s trade position is a key driver of regulation and standard-setting. ”
The EU is the largest participant in world trade and the largest trading partner of 74 countries, surpassing China (66) and the United States (31).
The report concludes that EU standards are critical to their impact on the global order and leadership on climate change, sustainability and consumer protection, personal data and the right to work.
The EU will further actively carry out regulatory cooperation to ensure that it plays a leading role in international norm-setting organizations such as the International Organization for Standardization (ISO).
Youth employment faces challenges in digital skills demand
With the development of emerging technologies, the employment of young people has become a major focus of the report.
The report said that the EU needs to help youth employment through targeted support programs, promoting the transition from education to employment, creating quality entry-level jobs and engaging youth in policy dialogue are key to young people entering the labor market.
But the EU still faces challenges in digital skills training and getting young women to study subjects such as S.T.E.A.M. (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics).
The report predicts that by 2050, 54% of job market participants will have post-secondary education.
The EU should encourage more talent (at universities, research institutions or businesses) to stay in Europe and reduce the brain drain between member states and regions.
The EU should build data storage capacity to avoid being constrained by non-EU countries
The EU ’ s digital sovereignty will depend on its ability to store, extract and process data, as well as on its ability to gain people ’ s trust, security and protection of their fundamental rights.
The implementation of the digital economy is likely to have a positive impact on the EU ’ s economy and competitiveness, especially with technologies such as data technology, high-performance cloud and edge computing playing a more positive role.
EU companies and governments will increasingly adopt user and physical data for data analytics, IoT and artificial intelligence.
In order to facilitate the development and deployment of the next generation of disruptive cloud and edge technologies, the EU has introduced important investment targets and financing tools.
As data is increasingly adopted in industrial and commercial applications, the development and deployment of industrial IoT systems, 5G / 6G and edge computing applications are critical to achieving the goal of dual transitions.
In today ’ s big data and advanced analytics, the United States and China are leading the way.
These technologies help detect possible crises, detect diseases and monitor military activities remotely.
From the EU ’ s perspective, the development of these technologies requires respect for their fundamental rights and EU values, especially in cases where these technologies rely on large amounts of data containing individual privacy.
At present, a large amount of EU data is mainly stored and processed in the cloud by non-EU operators, which makes its large amount of data subject to third country jurisdictions, which may cause EU dependence and risk.
The report recommends that the EU should build capacity to store data and ensure that data access is open, secure and transparent, as well as the connectivity availability of large volumes of data.
The EU also needs to develop and deploy AI worthy of new arrivals, and work with partners around the world to promote the implementation of standards and values.
Maintain its leading edge in developing and deploying trusted human intelligence.
It should work with trusted partners around the world to promote standards and values.
Conclusion: Preemptively formulating emerging technology standards will help the development and standardization of the industry
The report not only presents the current challenges and opportunities facing the EU in a wide range of areas, but also presents a clear picture of global developments in semiconductors, quantum computing, aerospace and digitalization, as well as the EU ’ s views on current trends.
For China, the challenges and opportunities in many of these areas are also facing China.
Among them, the positive actions of the EU in various emerging technology standards will help the development and standardization of the local industry, which has a certain reference value.

Fans regardless of gender, age, personality "star-chasing" self-adversity heart needle
Post Date: September 27, 2021
[Ming Pao News] MIRROR ’ s popularity is soaring, and fans are willing to spend huge amounts of money on advertising to celebrate their idol ’ s birthday.
No matter what age, there are always crazy fans.
For star-chasing people, we have a lot of criticism: star-chasing poisons the minds of young people; introverted people are not confident enough, only one-way fans of the star to have a more "sense of security"......
Experts stress that star chasing is not a bad thing, and from it you can find identity and enhance positive emotions.
Liao Chia-min, a registered clinical psychologist, says that there is no significant relationship between sex, age, personality, and so on.
One-way relationships are considered intimate.
According to Liao, there are a number of psychological theories that can be used to analyze star-chasing behavior, one of which dates back to 1956, when psychologists Donald Horton and Richard Wohl proposed "parasocial relationship", and with the popularity of mass media such as television, the two observed that people began to interact with characters on television.
This concept is used to describe a one-way relationship between people and a crush (such as a star).
People feel that they have established a real social relationship with each other and treat them as their true friends, and any action or emotion on the other side will touch them: "He just looked at me, smiled at me! I am so happy!" Even if there is no real or limited interaction with each other, they will put a lot of time, energy, and resources on each other, so that they feel like they have a kind of intimate contact with the popular culture. More and more diverse, the objects that people are obsessed with today are no longer limited to celebrities, but also athletes, YouTubers, KOLs, and so on.
Idol is close to your ideal self.
We know stars from the media. The other person doesn ’ t know who we are. Why do we still fall in love with each other? In recent years, the age of star chasing is quite extensive, no longer the monopoly of young people, why is the age of mature, even mothers are addicted to it?
Liao explained that from the concept of "pseudo-social relations", it can be understood that we are fascinated by some characteristics of the star, such as appearance, personality, experience, life attitude, etc., and hope that through the one-way "link" with the other party, get resonance, so that they have the corresponding good value, but also closer to the ideal of their own.
"Young fans find the ideal life characteristics they aspire to in idols, such as attractive appearance, brilliant talent, passion for dreams, modesty, etc.; following idols is like connecting with these ideal characteristics, drawing the distance between themselves and good value, and people become full of positive emotions."
The more mature fans may be "convinced" by other factors, such as the idol's passionate dream chasing experience, so that they can remember the beautiful moments of their youth and feel empathy. "
"Warm hearth" recognized
In addition, it can also be explained from the "social identity theory" in psychology.
Psychologist Henri Tajfel proposed in the 1970s that by forming a relationship with someone or a group (usually with common characteristics, preferences, and behaviors), an individual feels that he belongs to that group, and thus feels that the group brings him important emotions, self-esteem, and valuable meaning.
According to Liao, identity is important for growth, especially in adolescence.
When we are young, the awareness of life is overwhelmingly instilled by parents. At this time, we will feel that parents are the best in the world and naturally become their own life goals.
As we enter the adolescence stage, our psychological development changes, coupled with the increasing social reading experience, we aspire to establish our own identity, independence and self-determination, and look outward for life goals, such as stars.
Fans who like the same star and gather together, even if there is no real or limited interaction with each other, but there is an identity (belonging to a certain group), and work together for the beauty of the idol.
In addition to identity, Liao believes that star tracking also plays a positive role in enhancing self-worth and regulating emotions.
Life is never smooth, when you feel pressure, when you encounter adversity, listen to an idol song, think about the story of the idol ’ s struggle, etc. Even though the difficulties in front of you may not immediately appear to be the solution, but the heart seems to add a strong needle.
Liao Chia-min points out that some groups derived from the phenomenon of star chasing, such as "My wife married Zuo than Mirror led to the breakdown of marriage care group", members shared experiences (that is, the other half fell in love with MIRROR) around the stove to warm up, and then slowly share other life points.
