Global aviation industry to move to carbon neutral trench oil by 2050 is the savior? ｜ TECH
Author: Sze Heng
Published: Updated:
Are traditional cars energy-intensive and carbon-intensive?
Switching to electric vehicles can greatly reduce emissions, and major cities and regions such as Seoul and Singapore have begun to gradually electrify.
As one of the key industries facing the task of reducing emissions, how to achieve carbon neutrality in the long term is uncertain.
But with the recent agreement by the International Air Transport Association on carbon neutrality goals, the path to reducing emissions for an industry that accounts for 2% to 3% of the world ’ s carbon emissions seems to be starting to clear, but there are still multiple breakthroughs to be made in aviation fuel.
On Monday (October 4), the International Air Transport Association (IATA), the world ’ s largest aviation industry association, announced an ambitious plan to become carbon neutral by 2050.
More than 50 airlines and energy companies, including Boeing, BP and Shell, have announced that they will replace 10% of aviation fuel with sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) by 2030.
This fuel is mainly made of recycled food oil, various types of animal and plant waste oil (commonly known as gutter oil), in addition, waste wood chips and some common solid waste are also the source of waste oil production.
According to IATA data, this fuel can be 80% lower than the carbon emissions of ordinary aviation kerosene, but still ensure sufficient power during the flight.
This puts the future of SAF in the aviation industry on track, but there is debate in the industry as to whether SAF is the best solution to the aviation industry ’ s emissions reduction.
Aviation industry cut emissions without "golden oil"
According to a report released by the World Economic Forum in November last year, in 2019, the world's SAF production was less than 220,000 tons, and commercial routes used more than 300 million tons of aviation kerosene, SAF probably only supply less than 0.1% of aviation kerosene.
According to the same report, even if all known SAF development projects are implemented, their supply will only reach about 1% of projected global aviation coal demand by 2030.
Meanwhile, hydrogen aircraft start-ups ZeroAvia, Boeing and Airbus, which are pushing for zero-carbon emissions, have included hydrogen or electric aircraft in their emissions reduction plans – both popular alternatives to SAF that could reduce emissions for the aviation industry, but their prospects are even more muted.
In the case of hydrogen energy, because of its high energy density (that is, the energy produced at the same weight is extremely high), it is called "energy for aviation".
However, due to the low density of hydrogen per unit volume, it is only possible to be loaded on aircraft after cooling and liquefaction. Even so, hydrogen storage tanks are still three times larger than fossil fuel tanks that provide the same energy, aircraft passenger load is reduced, and storage conditions as low as minus 253 degrees are required.
Airbus, which is betting on hydrogen-powered aircraft, is also working on a metal hydrogen storage tank and hopes to make its first test flight using the technology in 2025.
At present, the successful test flight of hydrogen or electric aircraft - such as the start-up MagniX, ZeroAvia, etc., are basically small short-range aircraft, the real commercial long-distance flight of the aircraft, but also need to make a revolutionary breakthrough in the above technical difficulties can be achieved.
Gutter oil expansion or can it be expected?
Compared to the technical difficulties that have not been solved for many years, biofuels are a more realistic and feasible solution.
In fact, many airlines have already started using biofuels, but most of them are mixed with standard aviation kerosene.
The main obstacles to the large-scale promotion of bio-aviation fuel are the production and cost issues.
Airbus has established R & D bases in France and Germany to develop metal hydrogen storage tanks. (Airbus)
According to McKinsey ’ s “Sustainable Aviation Fuels as a Pathway to Net-Zero Aviation ” report, SAF is 2.5 times more expensive than conventional aviation coal through current most affordable production methods (HEFA).
However, the UK government ’ s advisory body, the Climate Change Commission, estimates that in the long run, once these fuels are deployed on a large scale, the cost of a round-trip ticket from London to New York will increase by around £80 (about HK $850) – an acceptable price increase.
In addition, in recent years, governments have many supportive policies for SAF, and even forced coal suppliers to set a minimum SAF supply ratio to promote its growth.
In particular, the Norwegian government requires all suppliers to participate in at least 0.5% of SAF in all aviation coal starting in 2020, and aims to achieve an overall share of 30% by 2030.
In addition, the European Union has proposed to achieve the 2% target by 2025 and increase it to 5% by 2030, and the United Kingdom and the United States are also studying related measures or launching them in the near future.
IATA official Chris Goater said that in 2016, only two countries in the world implemented SAF-related policies, but now it has grown to 36 countries.
Although both hydrogen, electric and SAF are facing practical or technical difficulties, which makes aviation one of the most difficult industries to reduce emissions, IATA's carbon neutrality blueprint has to be multi-pronged, but in this, SAF is responsible for nearly 70% of the emission reduction tasks, the industry's confidence in SAF can be seen.

African bond markets are an attractive way for global investors to participate in Africa ’ s economic transformation.
The relatively high growth rate is supported by favorable demographic trends, rapid urbanization, technological breakthroughs, abundant natural resources, and deepening financial markets.
Second, the ultra-low interest rate environment that has continued over the past decade has accelerated the long-term pursuit of yield and portfolio diversification by global investors, in part because of ample liquidity provided by central banks; these conditions have created a favorable environment for low- and middle-income countries to borrow foreign currencies from international financial markets and promote market consolidation.
Eurobond makes it easier for investors to expand their investment footprint to Africa without incurring additional currency risk or administrative costs.
There is considerable diversity in the African European bond market.
As of March 2021, the outstanding major debt of 20 African countries in European bonds exceeded US $110 billion.
Most European bonds are denominated in US dollars, but there are also some denominated in euros, especially from countries with close ties to the Eurozone, such as Morocco, Benin, Ivory Coast and Tunisia.
Both Egypt and Ghana are candidates for the JPMorgan Emerging Market Government Bond Index, so this should be a boost to increased foreign participation in the future.
Due to the lack of development in African countries, governments need foreign sources of financing to reduce infrastructure gaps and realize their full growth potential.
We believe that European bonds can be one of the sources of funding if they are part of a sustainable and responsible public financial management programme.
European debt remains an important tool for investors to reach Africa.
The coronavirus crisis has worsened balance sheet and affordability weaknesses in many countries, including border markets. Spreads on European bonds issued by African governments surged in March, helped by a slide in investment risk appetite and a lack of liquidity.
But immediate policy responses from mature and emerging countries, as well as unprecedented support from institutions such as the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, have helped stabilize markets.
While debt restructuring processes are often opaque, China, as one of the continent ’ s most important lenders, is critical to addressing liquidity pressures. In November 2020, the G20 unveiled its “Common Framework for Debt Treatment beyond DSSI (the World Bank ’ s Debt Relief Initiative) ” to coordinate debt treatment among creditors in low-income countries.
Overall, this set of policies represents a suspension or maturity extension of debt repayment, not a cancellation of debt.
To date, only Zambia and Ethiopia have applied for the scheme, and progress to date has been limited.
The framework calls for private sector participation, but it is unclear how it will work.
We believe that it is best to involve the private sector on a case-by-case basis in order to find the best outcome from the perspective of issuers and creditors.
The latest potential form of policy is the new SDR, which could be used to increase countries ’ international reserves by $650 billion.
The IMF Board approved the funds in August this year. Special Drawing Rights are not subject to any specific conditions, and countries can decide how to use them.
As mature countries continue to discuss the redistribution of special drawing rights in the form of donations, more room for survival is in the pipeline.
Overall, African bond markets remain an attractive investment opportunity for active emerging market investors in the medium to long term.

As the saying goes, "prevention is better than cure", if you want to be able to protect yourself and reduce the risk of injury when you fall, you must learn a safe landing method.
There may be differences between different martial arts methods, but this article will be explained from the judo way of receiving the body, judo can be divided into four kinds of receiving: rear receiving, cross receiving, front receiving, and front rolling receiving.
Back to the ground (back to the ground)
Falling backwards is the most common occurrence of falls on a daily basis, and it is also the most risky.
Because when falling backwards, the person who falls cannot observe the environment behind him, it is difficult to grasp the opportunity of falling down, so it is very easy to get injured.
The rear body is the way to hold the body when you fall directly behind, and both hands are patting the mat at the same time, such as when you fall by a large mow.

It is used to hold hands when a person falls down, such as when the person falls down.

When you fall down, gently bend your knees and lower your waist. At this point, your hands extend forward and get ready to pat the mat. When you land on your hips, bend your back and press your chin as close to the locking bone as possible.
At the beginning of the practice, you can fall back from the squat position, and then ask your partner to gently push, and then fall back from the upright position, or even fall.
Cross over (down to the side)
Cross body, also known as side body, is the way to receive the body when landing on the side. This method is used when most of the moves fall. (Image taken from: https: / / bit.ly / 3lTYy3x)
The horizontal body is also the lateral body, which is the way to receive the body when landing on the side. The one-handed mat is used when most of the moves fall.
This method is divided into left and right hand patting mat, the following example of using the right hand patting mat.
Image taken from Youtube: http: / / bit.ly / sideukemi
When you fall, your right foot is inclined to the front of the left side. Your right hand extends forward with the body swing. Your left foot is bent to the center of gravity and ready to fall back.
The practice method is similar to the posterior body. It can be practiced from the squat position and gradually.
Practicing the horizontal body is helpful to the forward body. In addition, the horizontal body is often used, and everyone should practice more.
Front to the ground (forward to the ground)
(Image taken from: https: / / bit.ly / 3vudJU3)
The method of receiving the front body when the front body falls forward, landing on the ground with both hands.
This method is less useful, but it is better to protect yourself if you fall forward.

This method flexes the arms to the ground, and the hands are in the shape of "eight". At the same time, the hands are stressed with the palm and upper arm. Do not extend the elbows, otherwise it may cause sprain.
You should practice in a kneeling position before using a squat or standing position.
Get your feet off the ground.
In addition to being used when being cast by a person, it can also be used as a landing method after jumping. However, this is more difficult and requires more practice.

This idea is to leave the final salvation to the humanistic spirit, and the literary pursuit of the "ultimate good."
From the examples of Ray Bradbury and Liu Cixin, it can be seen that the intellectual challenge caused by the intersection of literature and science is the highest intellectual thinking in the human world today, and it is also a new topic facing literature.
The emergence of outstanding science fiction, such as The Three Bodies, is challenging many traditional literary theories and definitions.
Looking at the history of literature, especially the history of modern literature, we will find that many new literary categories and literary patterns are the result of the intersection and grafting of literature with other disciplines, and over the past 100 years, we have also seen that the intersection of literature and psychology has produced the giant flow of consciousness novels such as Proust's "Remembering the Year of the Passing Water" and Joyce's "Ulysses.
Since then, we have seen Orwell ’ s Animal Farm, a new type of novel that has hit the world, which is actually the intersection of literature and politics.
We do not support literature as a tool of politics (including the idea that literature serves politics), but we do not deny that political life is also a part of real life, and political activities can also become a part of literature.
Orwell is familiar with literature, but also familiar with politics, he did not put politics above literature, but turned politics into the material and tool of literature, the art of politics refining and upgrading, so that politics is fully literalized.

China achieves "quantum computing superiority" in two physical systems
Xu Jing
October 27, 2021 08: 26 | Source: People's Daily - People's Daily
Small number
Original title: Quantum computing prototype "Zuchongzhi II" and "Jiuchang II" came out - China in two physical systems to achieve "quantum computing superiority"
Recently, the research team of China University of Science and Technology has made important progress in the quantum computing of superconducting quantum and light quantum systems, and successfully developed the "Zu Chongzhi II" and "Jiuchang II", making China the only country in the world to achieve the "quantum computing superiority" milestone in the two physical systems.
The research team composed of Pan Jianwei, Zhu Xiaobo and Peng Chengzhi, and the Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, recently successfully built the 66-bit programmable superconducting quantum computing prototype "Zuchongzhi II", which solved the "quantum random line sampling" task more than 10 million times faster than the fastest supercomputer in the world.
The research team composed of Pan Jianwei, Lu Chaoyang, Liu Naile and other researchers, in cooperation with the Shanghai Institute of Microsystems and Information Technology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the National Parallel Computer Engineering Technology Research Center, recently successfully built 113 photon 144 mode of quantum computing prototype "Nine Chapter 2", solving Gaussian Bose sampling mathematical problems 10 times faster than the world's fastest supercomputer.
In 1981, Nobel Prize winner Richard Feynman proposed the idea of a quantum computer.
Quantum computing is thought to be a key technology for the next generation of the information revolution.
"'Quantum computing superiority' refers to a specific task, or a special track, that surpasses the current supercomputer," said Lu Chaoyang, a professor at the China University of Science and Technology.
The physical realization of large-scale quantum computers is one of the major challenges at the forefront of world science and technology.
Therefore, to achieve the physical realization of quantum computing, the international academic community takes a three-step road map.
Among them, the first milestone, is known academically as the “superiority of quantum computing. ”
At present, random line sampling based on superconducting bits and Bose sampling based on photons are two important schemes to demonstrate the superiority of quantum computing experimentally.
The latest achievements of these two programs are "Zuchongzhi II" and "Jiuchang II" respectively.
"In terms of volume, you can think of the two as a large special computing device that can be installed in a room," Lu said.
As for the difference between the two, Lu Chaoyang said, mainly the media is different, "superconducting quantum computing mainly depends on the medium is superconducting material, light quantum computing mainly depends on the medium is photon."
According to the existing theory, the speed of the quantum-random line sampling problem handled by "Zuchongzhi II" is 7 orders of magnitude faster than the fastest supercomputer at present, and this achievement is the first time that China has reached the "quantum computing superiority" milestone after the "nine chapters" of the optical quantum computing prototype in the superconducting quantum bit system.
According to the existing theory, Nine Chapters Two can process Gaussian Bose samples 10 times faster than the current fastest supercomputer 24 times faster.
This achievement has once again refreshed the international technical level of light quantum manipulation, and further provided experimental evidence of quantum computing acceleration.
According to reports, the successful demonstration of the superiority of quantum computing marks the second stage of the development of quantum computing research, and begins the exploration of quantum error correction and recent applications.
"At present, the development of quantum computing is still in a very early stage, it is difficult to predict how broad the application prospects in the end, but now, it can improve our computing capabilities, in many scientific research areas are very helpful, such as drug design, molecular simulation, code deciphering, etc." Lu Chaoyang said.

Travel / Istanbul preserves the imperial glory
Istanbul, formerly known as Constantinople, is one of the bustling international metropolises. It is the economic, cultural and transportation center of Turkey, as well as a world-famous tourist destination. It was also the capital of the ancient Three Great Powers – the Roman Empire, the Byzantine Empire and the Ottoman Empire.
Ten years ago, I stood on the black coast of Batumi, a famous city in Georgia ’ s Black Sea. The azure sea showed before me, the sea breeze gently blowing in my face, and I looked fondly at the other side of the sea, the misty Istanbul, dreaming about when I could go to the other side.
Finally, on the Golden Week of the Spring Festival the year before last, I took a flight north to Turkey after a trip to Egypt with my wife and daughter.
Before the plane landed, I saw the earth in the air, the green Mamoras Sea and the curved Bosphorus Strait, three Eurasian land bridges on the strait clearly visible.
The plane flew north over the Black Sea, fluttered a beautiful arc, turned around and landed at Ataturk Airport, and I finally set foot in Istanbul, which has been my dream for 10 years.
Snow White Cotton Fort is a hot spring.
The next morning we flew to a cotton fort in the interior of Turkey.
The Bosphorus, Mamorah and Dardanelles straits are the dividing lines of Eurasia, dividing not only Turkey into two, but also the Istanbul metropolitan area. The Cotton Fortress is located in Asia, which is why we came to Asia from Europe.
When the plane landed at the airport south of Denizli, the sun was just rising on the Anatolian mountains, and the earth was painted with pale gold. The Cotton Castle is the site of the ancient Roman city of Hilápolis, a snow-white limestone formed by volcanic eruptions, and the rock formation of numerous hot springs.
Because of the rich hot spring resources in the area, the ancient Roman and Greek nobles used this as a healing place, and built the prosperous city of Hierapolis here in 190 BC.
At 9: 00 a.m., we entered the Cotton Fort, and in front of us was the snow-white limestone of the entire ring-shaped hillside, layered and crystal-clear, like cotton.
At this moment, the light sun is shining on the snow-white limestone, and the pale blue hot spring is rippling, and the water surface is reflected.
We took off our shoes and walked on the rocks wearing socks, some hurt feet and cool, the hot spring through the gully rushing down, the little girl soaked her feet in the hot spring, and was very happy.
2000 Old Town Theatre intact
Walking uphill through the Cotton-Fort area is the ruins of the city of Hirápolis, including the ancient cemetery, large baths, markets, arches, amphitheatres, the Temple of Apollo and ancient hot springs, which are scattered on the hillside from north to south.
When I sit in the amphitheater, I am not shocked by the majesty in front of me! The theater more than 2000 years ago is basically intact, and the entire theater is divided into 18 areas, which is easy for the audience to enter and exit; it is said that the theater can accommodate 15,000 people, looking up from the bottom, and the highest row of people seems to be in the sky.
As I sat in the top row, I could look beyond the stage and see countless sites such as the Temple of Apollo, which stands at the bottom of the hillside. Through the years, it has become more and more quaint, elegant and fragmentary in the sunlight.
Further up, we walked into the ruins of the ancient Roman market.
There is a large circular square in the middle of the market, and the tall Romanesque door tower is like an eight-petal lotus flower around the square.
I wandered through the market, shuttling between the doors, imagining the happy bustle of the crowd and the hustle and bustle of shopping in those years, and now all this prosperity is gone, leaving only the lonely ruins in front of me, abandoned on the desolate slope.
The whole afternoon lingered in the ruins, not by the sigh of a thousand years, white clouds and pale dogs.
We flew back to Istanbul that night, and when the plane landed at Ataturk, we were back in Europe from Asia.
Istanbul has a Mediterranean climate, and we are greeted by an endless, all-day rain.
We took the bus past the ancient city wall for miles and got off to Sultan Ahmed Square.
Looking up, you can see the towering square pillars, 32 meters high, which were built by the ancient Roman emperor Constantine VII in the 10th century in memory of his grandfather.
The column was originally filled with gold-plated bronze reliefs, but was later ransacked by the Crusaders and only the core pillars remain.
In front of the square pillars stands an ancient Egyptian obelisk, reflecting on the wet square floor.
This monument was originally built by the ancient Egyptian Pharaoh Thutmose III. It was erected in the temple of Luxor Kanak, which was purchased by Theodosius the Great from Egypt in 390 AD.
There is also a famous monument between the two pillars, the bronze snake pillar.
These three relics are like an open-air museum, adding to the splendor of the square, showing a sense of ancient history and glory.
The square itself is also an ancient Roman site, originally a huge arena that was expanded after the relocation of the Roman Empire; according to historical records, the arena is next to the palace to the east, completely modeled after the Roman Colosseum, but 40 meters longer.
The racetrack is paved with sand and can accommodate eight horse-drawn carriages, and the surrounding stands can accommodate tens of thousands of people to watch the race, and the Roman emperor can see the scene in the arena from the palace.
In 330 AD, the Roman emperor Constantine I moved the capital to this place and named it New Rome, which was soon renamed Constantinople.
The walls of Constantinople, built by Constantine I, extend westward from the north to the south.
Both north and south of the city are facing the sea, so the height of the two walls is only 12 to 15 meters, and the entire city is located on the hills behind the wall. From the sea, the merchant ships from afar can see the majestic buildings such as the palace, the arena and the Hagia Sophia.
The western end of the city was later rebuilt with a third wall, the 4.3 km long wall of Constantine.
Saint Sophia Cathedral Inclusion 2 Religions
In 395 AD, the Roman Empire split into Eastern and Western Rome, and Constantinople became the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire (Byzantine Empire).
In the 5th century AD, the Byzantine emperor Theodosius II added the Theodosian wall to the west of the city wall built by Constantine, which doubled the area of the city. The enlarged wall of Constantinople was 21.5 kilometers long, of which the wall facing the Sea of Mamorah was 8 kilometers long, the side of the Golden Horn was 7 kilometers long, and the side of the land was 6.5 kilometers long.
This land wall design is incomparably complex, from the outside to the inside and in turn for the outer wall, the moat, the moat inner wall, the steep slope wall, the outer wall, the inner wall, the inner wall; the outer wall and the inner wall stand more than 300 towers, corner buildings and bunkers, forming a strong support system.
Constantinople faces the sea on three sides, plus the western land city defense system, bronze walls and iron walls, so that the city became a "barbarian" city.
The old city wall that we saw along the way is a remnant of the Byzantine Empire.
In the 6th century AD, a great generation of monarchs emerged in the empire, Justinian I.
He went on to conquer the West, and recovered a large part of the western lands lost by the Roman Empire. The weather of the revival of the Roman Empire was very good, and the Byzantine Empire entered its peak.
The city of Constantinople also entered the glorious period, most of the buildings are in the ancient Roman style, the main buildings include the above-mentioned walls, gates, palaces, squares, arches, public baths, cisterns and churches.
To the north of Augustus Square is the majestic Hagia Sophia.
This is the most glorious legacy Justinian has left in the history of architecture. Built between 532 and 537, this church became the center of Byzantine religion and Eastern Orthodoxy and became a symbol of the empire.
The Cathedral of St. Sophia uses the shape of a Greek cross on the plane, creating a huge dome in the space, but no pillars support the interior; the dome is 55 meters above the ground, and it was the largest church in the world until the completion of St. Peter ’ s Cathedral in the 17th century.
In 1453, the Ottoman Empire captured Constantinople, and the Eastern Roman Empire fell, and the Empire moved its capital there and renamed it Istanbul.
Sultan Mehmed II converted the cathedral into a mosque and added an Islamic minaret, and over the next 500 years it became one of the most important places of worship for Muslims.
After World War I, Turkey ’ s founding father, Kemal, converted it into a museum in 1934 and gradually became a famous tourist attraction.
Last year, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announced the conversion of the Cathedral of St. Sophia into a mosque. On July 24 of the same year, he attended a Muslim service at the Cathedral of St. Sophia, the first religious event held in the church after nearly 90 years.
Entering the Cathedral of St. Sophia, visitors are amazed by the tall, domed dome and the exquisite Byzantine frescoes on the dome, especially the statue of the Virgin and Child on the top of the altar.
We walk through the spiral passage paved with medieval stone blocks to the second floor of the church gallery, which can be closer to and carefully admire the various corners of the church. In particular, we can see the wall of the gallery with many murals of Christian stories.
Overlooking the entire hall, you can feel the grand space design of the hall.
100,000 tons of underground water
Another architectural gem left behind by Justinian is the "Groundwater Palace".
Constantinople was built solid, but the rulers of the empire were still worried, and built a secret underground reservoir and brought water from the forests near the Black Sea, which could store up to 100,000 tons.
If the city is besieged during the war, it serves as a strategic reserve for the entire city to drink for a month; during the Song and Dance Period, it provides water storage for the palace and other palaces.
The reservoir is 140 meters long and 70 meters wide, with 336 Corinthian stone columns 9 meters high, supporting a huge brick vault with exquisite relief, and it is also called an underground palace.
There are two places in the park that are worth looking at.
One place is a weeping column, the underground humidity is large, specially designed a column, and the water drops flow down the column, as if someone is crying.
The other is a column supported by two inverted Medusa heads, decorated with figures from Greek mythology.
This revealed that the Byzantine Empire was passionate about Greek civilization, and its influence was everywhere.
Blue Mosque 6 Minaret Tower Rare
The next day we took the subway to Istanbul University Station, then took the light rail to Sultan Ahmet Square, passing through the square to visit the Blue Mosque.
The original name of the mosque is Sultan Ahmet Mosque, because the walls are all decorated with Iznik blue and white tiles, so it is also known as the Blue Mosque, which is a landmark of Istanbul.
The first thing we see is the mosque ’ s six long and towering minarets, full of lightness and spirit, and looking far away like the city in the sky.
The Blue Mosque is the largest domed building in Istanbul, with more than 30 domes rising up to the 41-meter diameter central dome.
Take off your shoes and enter the mosque, look up at a huge dome, and the sun shines through the stained glass of 260 small windows.
The four columns supporting the large dome are clearly chiseled, and the blue gold word Arabic on the column head and the black gold word Arabic on the column body are as beautiful as the pattern.
The shrine is an important part of the interior of the Blue Mosque, made of carved marble. Beside the shrine, there is a beautiful mission altar, and scholars stand on the altar to preach on Fridays at noon and religious festivals.
The Blue Mosque, an artistic masterpiece of the Ottoman Empire, took seven years to build and became an icon of the empire ’ s heyday.
It is said that the Ottoman Sultan asked the architects to build the minaret into gold, and the Turkish pronunciation of "gold" and "six" is very similar, so it became the only mosque in the world with six tall towers, and thus one of the ten wonders of the world.
Out of the Blue Mosque, gaze across the square, and you can see the minaret towering above the clouds, which is the “Mosque ” of St. Sophia, which we visited yesterday and features both Christian and Islamic architecture.
The two mosques are opposite each other and form a beautiful landscape in Istanbul.
We walked through the square and walked to Topkapi Palace.
The palace is the first officially built palace after the Ottoman Empire entered Istanbul. It has a strong Ottoman style royal architecture characteristics, mysterious and elegant.
The Old Palace is a former place of national ceremonies and royal entertainment, from the construction of the Topkapi Palace by the Conqueror Mehmed II in 1465 until 1853, nearly 400 years ago, it was the place where Sultans worked and lived.
There is a main entrance in the middle of a tall wall, which only the sultan could enter and exit, and it was called the "Gate of the Emperor". Through the main entrance, you enter the first courtyard and follow the courtyard path, and you can see a sacred peace church built in the Byzantine period on your left hand.
Continue forward to the welcome gate, which is a city gate with an octagonal tower on the left and right, like a castle gate.
When you look up at the door, you can see the Qur ’ an engraved on the door.
Pass security and walk into the second courtyard, looking at a large area of grass and flower beds.
Passing through the Gate of Happiness is the Venerable Room in the Third Courtyard, where the sultans and the Grand Vizier (equivalent to the Prime Minister) and generals met four days a week. Passing through the Third Courtyard and entering the Fourth Courtyard, it is the Baghdatin, with its interior walls decorated with Iznik tiles and shells.
At the edge of the platform is a small gold-topped pavilion, Ifthaya, from which you can see the Golden Horn Bay and the new urban area across from it.
We visited the four courtyards in turn, then turned back to the entrance to the harem of the second courtyard, and then visited the residence of the four wives of the sultan, the queen ’ s room, and the sultan ’ s bathroom.
We were dazzled by the golden splendour of the harem, the many rooms covered with fine tiles and the beautifully decorated scenes of life.
In front of the harem there is a quadrangular column building called the "Tower of Justice", which has been used to monitor the city and defend against external enemies, and is also a large landscape.
There is also an open-air restaurant with great views inside the palace. Here you can see the Bosphorus Strait, Eurasia Bridge, Istanbul ’ s new city district and the world ’ s smallest sea, the Mamora Sea.
At noon, the sun is still hiding behind the clouds, the light is not strong, the sea is full of green waves, and the silver bridge across the Eurasian continent in the distance, it is really pleasing to see.
Once out of the palace, we took the light rail through the bustling business district to the Galata Bridge, where we boarded a boat from the Golden Horn pier to explore the Bosphorus Strait.
The sky was clear, the sky was blue and white, the waves were flowing, and the boats were weaving.
Thousands of seagulls soar around the cruise ship, and the moving pictures of historical buildings, mosques, Galata Towers, and villas built on the mountains are displayed in turn, forming an absolutely beautiful exhibition of sea-view paintings.
When we crossed the first Eurasia land bridge, we came to the second Eurasia land bridge, and saw a fortified castle on the left bank, which attracted my attention, and regretted that we could not abandon the boat to go ashore to visit.
After an hour and a half of excursion, we disembarked and boarded the bridge, and looked at the city area on the north shore of the Golden Horn from the Galata Bridge.
Darkness falls on the ground, night falls, looking back at the old area on the right bank, by the mountains and the water, stars point, experience in the eyes, the lights of Suleiman Mosque live on the top of the mountain, suspended above thousands of households.
The New Palace witnesses the Westernization of Osman
On the third day, the weather changed.
My wife and daughter were tired and stayed at the hotel to rest. I went out alone. Take the subway to Taksim Square station, walk around Taksim Gezi Park, walk up or down the steep road, and after more than ten minutes to the sea, you can see the Dolmabach Mosque with a blue dome and a milky white wall. The road, facing the Dolmabachet clock tower.
Through the bell tower is the Dolmabache Palace.
Built in the middle of the 19th century, it is the last palace of the Ottoman Empire. Also known as the "New Palace", it is built in the style of the Baroque and neoclassical European palace. It is located on the coast of the European part of the Bosphorus. The building stretches 600 meters along the Strait, and the interior wall is covered with gold leaf, and the main body is made of white marble and Egyptian alabaster. And...
The palace has two main parts, namely the ceremonial palace, the harem and the concubine court, with 285 rooms, 43 halls and 6 Turkish baths.
Both inside and outside the palace are extremely luxurious and luxurious.
Among the most noteworthy attractions are the crystal staircase pillars in the ceremonial palace, as well as the large and spacious Imperial Hall, which has 56 columns and 4.5 tons of giant crystal chandeliers, and the golden throne of Sudan.
Compared with the old palace, the new palace is more elegant and luxurious, but less of the mysterious elegance of the Oriental palace, extremely European and modern, the degree of luxury is far more than the Meichun Palace in Vienna and most of the European palaces, and Versailles in France.
The courtyard of the new palace is larger than the four courtyards of the old palace, and the layout is also European style. There are fountains, statues, lawns, etc., especially the grand doors facing the Bosphorus Strait, which are beautifully decorated.
During World War I, the Ottoman Empire joined the Allies, and with the defeat of the Allies, the Ottoman Empire split, and the Sultanate was abolished two years later.
In this crisis, Kemal defeated the invaders and the military intervention of the European powers, saved Turkey, became the founder of the Turkish Republic, and the Ottoman Empire was destroyed. Kemal ruled for more than ten years, achieving great success, making Turkey secularized, Westernized, and modernized, becoming the model and standard of secularization of the Islamic state.
From the New Palace Tea House, I walked back to Taksim Square from the original road.
The square is the main transportation hub of Istanbul and the meeting place of the Turkish people for major meetings and processions.
In the center of the square stands a circular monument of independence to commemorate Kemal. Bronze reliefs show the father of the country ’ s glory.
Every year, thousands of Turks offer flowers to their Father of the Nation to express their admiration and gratitude.
Go southwest from Taksim Square to the north entrance of Independence Avenue.
This 4-kilometer pedestrian street, with many boutiques, music shops, cinemas, libraries, cafes, bars and restaurants, is a leisure avenue for Turks to shop and play, and is therefore known as Istanbul ’ s “Champs Elysees ”.
I wandered south from the north entrance to fully appreciate the Turkish way of life.
Local women have deep eyes and high noses, elegant temperament, and rarely have a headscarf, let alone a veil, revealing the inclusiveness and openness of the city.
The Turkish look is not very different from the Uighurs in Xinjiang, and it feels very friendly to deal with them.
There are many small streets on both sides of the street.
Look at the small streets on both sides, are downhill paths or stairs, leading to highways or community buildings, I found that Independence Street was originally built on a ridge.
As I walked, I looked at the buildings on both sides of the street, many of which were old buildings with long history or mottled ruins. There were government departments, consulates, various churches, etc. It can be said that this area occupied an important position in the political, economic and cultural life of the Ottoman Empire, and now it has become a paradise for ordinary people to relax, shop and entertain.
St. Anthony ’ s Church, Istanbul ’ s largest Roman Catholic church, is hidden behind an ordinary old neighborhood.
The entrance is not very eye-catching, easy to miss, I also accidentally saw the two red brick towers are different, with curiosity only to find that there is no hole in the sky.
As I walked along the street, there were art shows and begging, and on this street, foreign tourists could experience the secular life of the local Turks and fully experience the freedom, openness, romance and vitality of modern Istanbul.
Fort Rumeli World Military Miracle
The Bosphorus Strait, also known as the Istanbul Strait, is also known as the "Turkish Strait" (also known as the Black Sea Strait), along with the Mamora Sea and the Dardanelles Strait.
On the fourth day, my friend, Mr. Chung, accompanied us on a tour of the Black Sea Scenic Area, which allowed us to see both the Black Sea exit of the Bosphorus Strait and the entire Strait as we headed north along the coastal highway.
The weather is sunny, driving up the mountain road, and the scenery is spectacular when it comes to the sea canyon.
About half an hour later we drove to the cliffs of the sea and we finally saw the Black Sea.
When we got out of the car, we stood on a cliff, and the wind was fierce, stirring the waves.
In front is an endless sea, on the left is the jagged coastline, and on the right is the Bosphorus Strait exit, narrow like a stream, a rainbow bridge across both sides of the strait, is the third Eurasian land bridge just built in recent years.

Fractures and osteoporosis are related to osteoporosis: "Women have four times more osteoporosis than men."
Casual Spending 14: 15 2021 / 11 / 01

The orthopedic surgeon said the fracture was related to osteoporosis.
Chief Executive Carrie Lam was hospitalized with a fractured elbow, attracting concern.
Orthopedic specialist Huang Huabang said that fracture and bone density are closely related, "bone regeneration and loss to maintain a balance, regardless of whether men and women have passed a certain age, if the bone is loose, the bones are fragile, and the support is insufficient, even if the impact is not too large, it will lead to fracture."
How to avoid osteoporosis, it is better to listen to what Dr. Huang said.
Orthopaedic specialist Dr Wong Wah-pong said that early menstruation in women and smoking and drinking in men can cause osteoporosis, which can lead to fracture problems.
(Photo by.. istock)
The martial arts novels often describe martial arts practitioners as "marvelous skeletons," but the orthopedic specialist Huang Wah-pang says:
Bones are actually like wallets, children and puberty development, is "more money than money laundering", the body bone building function is strong.
By age, bone loss is greater than bone preparation, and osteoporosis is serious under the imbalance.
Huang Hua-pang says that women who are smaller and have early menstruation, those who have thyroid or adrenal gland secretion disorders, or who have problems with the absorption of nutrients after surgery in the intestine, are more likely to develop osteoporosis.
Orthopaedic specialist Dr Wong Wah-pong explains the relationship between fractures and osteoporosis. (Photographer: Fung Pak-wai)
Does osteoporosis make you shorter?
Whether osteoporosis is a disease or not, says Huang Hua-pang, there are many things that can be done.
In many cases, there are no signs.
But as an orthopedic surgeon, careful observation is not without signs.
For example, women ’ s early menstruation, and men ’ s smoking and drinking will increase the alertness of diagnosis.
In addition, if you have osteoporosis, the body will slowly become short, like the kitchen cabinet in the home is high enough to open, and start to play stool.
This is because osteoporosis causes several sections of the spine to be flattened, and when walking, the gravity drops, people will become short or cold back.
Sometimes I see the elderly people with paper skin bent back, which is precisely the effect of osteoporosis.
The image shows the normal bone density (above), compared with the osteoporosis of the bone (below). (Photographer: Fung Pak-wai)
Fractures are most common in 4 locations
Dr. Wong said that osteoporosis, women are about four times higher than men, and white and Asian people have higher rates than black people.
For fractures caused by osteoporosis, Dr. Wong said there are four most common locations.
Including the proximal part of the femur (thigh bone) of the neck and between the bulge, followed by the lumbar vertebrae, the distal part of the bone (wrist) and the proximal part of the humerus (shoulder), of course, elbows can also occur.
In several cases, the fracture of the femur and lumbar vertebrae is the most serious. "The elderly must not rise from this position, and they must call an ambulance to be sent to the hospital, and at least they can walk after the fracture of the upper limb."
After the fracture of the femur, surgery should be done after X-ray.
But the problem is that after surgery, the ability to move will also decrease, such as walking with a cane, using a wheelchair and so on.
Milk products and wheat skin are rich in calcium to prevent osteoporosis.
(Photo source..
Economic Daily Photo Gallery)
Preventing osteoporosis, food and exercise
Dr Wong said there was also a osteoporosis test, known as a Dual Energy X-ray Absorber (DEXA), which measured bone density by T-score. The bone density classified by osteoporosis degree was compared with young people of the same race who were at the peak of bone density to show the extent of bone loss.
To prevent osteoporosis, one of the components is supplementing calcium and vitamin D, such as milk products, salmon, sardines, tofu, wheat skin, etc. It is not necessary to eat calcium tablets. Vitamin D helps bones absorb calcium from the blood.
Of course, doing 30 minutes of exercise a day can also be beneficial. “Exercise can stimulate bone cells to make new bones, such as dancing and running slowly, ” Dr. Wong said.
In addition, you can also learn tai chi to strengthen the stability of the body, learning horse steps is not easy to fall, but also can slow down the pace of life, mood can slow down. 」
The elderly can do tai chi, strengthen the stability of the body, it is not easy to fall and cause fractures. (Photo source.. Economic Daily Photo Library)
For those with low bone density, Dr. Wong recommends doing less yoga and tennis, which require torsion. "Skiing and bouncing beds may not be suitable, and if bone density is not high, it is more likely to fall."

"Superfood" avocado has become one of the most popular fruits in the world due to its dense taste and wide use, but environmental awareness has risen in recent years, and due to the need for water and high carbon footprint during cultivation, some restaurants around the world have resisted avocado, replacing the ingredients used in dishes with other fruits and vegetables.
According to the Guardian and The Hill, growing avocados requires a lot of water. According to DanWatch, an independent Danish investigative media, it takes an average of 320 litres of water to grow one avocados.
In addition, thanks to the popularity of avocados around the world, the international transportation of avocados after harvest has further boosted the carbon footprint, which is estimated by Carbon Footprint Ltd to be nearly 850 grams for two avocados commonly found on supermarket shelves.
The main production area of avocado is in Central and South America, but because it is popular with North American and European consumers, the avocado has to be transported across continents when it grows.
Because the journey is too long, farmers often pick the avocado before it is ripe, and it is necessary to use temperature-controlled containers to transport the avocado, all of which push up the avocado ’ s carbon footprint.
In addition, the price of avocado has been soaring in recent years, according to Business Insider, by 2019, the Hass avocado produced in California has risen to $2.1 (about NT $58).
In recent years, the price of avocado has risen, and the cost of its cultivation and transportation has been inextricably linked, and California's casepear production has been severely affected by drought and wildfires in recent years.
Growing and distributing avocados also requires a lot of labor, and the avocados need to be transported to the ripening center first after picking them first, and then to the sales sites after adding ethylene.
Thomasina Miers, founder of the British Mexican restaurant chain, pointed out that today's strong demand for avocado around the world has caused the price of avocado to soar to the point that indigenous people in the region cannot afford it.
Realizing the environmental impact of avocados, restaurants around the world are beginning to resist them. Myers says his restaurant has replaced the cornflake sauce “avocados ” with beans, green peppers, lime, parsley, etc.
Canadian Mexican chef Aldo Camarena also introduced dipping sauces made with pumpkin seeds and tomatoes, while Irish restaurant owner JP McMahon removed the avocado from the menu, calling it “Mexico ’ s blood diamond. ”

Can Saudi Arabia break through its natural limitations? ｜ Geography of the World
Author: Zhou Xuan
Published: Updated:
“By 2030, Saudi Arabia will grow 450 million trees to supply 50% of the country ’ s electricity through renewable energy.
By 2060, Saudi Arabia will be carbon neutral … ” As early as a week before the United Nations climate summit, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman made such an ambitious pledge at the country ’ s first Green Initiative Forum, reversing the past Saudi Arabia ’ s barring of climate commitments.
Since his father became king in 2015, Mohammed has been aggressively diversifying and greening the Saudi economy, trying to break through the country ’ s path of development shaped by oil and desert.
However, the gap between ideal and reality is as wide as the sky, can Saudi Arabia get what it wants?
Geography has been an important factor dominating the trajectory of modern Saudi Arabia.
The natural environment of the country is quite harsh, subtropical high pressure and subtropical cyclone lock up hot air from the equator, forming a tropical desert climate, 95% of the country is desert, the maximum daily temperature for five months in the summer reaches an average of 45 degrees Celsius, the annual rainfall is less than 100mm, and there are even no regular rivers on the surface.
Saudi Arabia is a barren land compared to Syria and Iraq, which feed on the two river plains to the northeast, Egypt, which feeds on the Nile River to the west, and fertile land with abundant rainfall on the Yemeni plateau to the south.
However, the country has become the world ’ s largest oil exporter by relying on its rich oil reserves, thus breaking through the harsh environment and easily becoming a high-income country.
But in the context of the country ’ s race to develop renewable energy, there is uncertainty about the oil wealth that Saudi Arabia has relied on in the past.
The country has formed a fairly single economic structure, oil revenue accounts for about 70% of the state's fiscal revenue, 90% of the total exports, and the industrial system and service industries other than oil are quite weak.
When most major powers are determined to become carbon neutral by 2050 or 2060, it can be said to pose an existential crisis for Saudi Arabia, which urgently needs to embark on an economic transformation.
A future limited by drought and heat
However, Saudi Arabia ’ s poor natural conditions have created strong resistance.
The country ’ s water resources are extremely scarce, hindering the prospects for industrial development.
Although it has been very dry, it has at least been rich in groundwater resources, that is, the Arabian aquifer with reserves of up to 500 billion cubic meters.
However, since the 1980s, Saudi Arabia has overexploited these non-renewable fossil water resources, and the government subsidized the development of agriculture and livestock at high prices, which made the country create a desert agricultural miracle, and even became the world's sixth largest wheat exporter.
Saudi Arabia only woke up in 2008, cutting subsidies for wheat every year until 2016 to zero, and further adding desalination plants to increase the use of desalinated seawater, which has so far reached 50% of the country ’ s water, but this can no longer make up for the fact that four-fifths of the country ’ s groundwater has been depleted.
Considering that desalination is expensive and consumes electricity, the country will face the restrictions of expensive water prices if it wants to develop its industrial system, especially the photovoltaic and hydrogen production industries that are currently under consideration in Saudi Arabia, and the electronics industry that is standing in the wind outlet of the future are large water consumers.
Saudi Arabia once created a desert agricultural miracle as a wheat growing area in Saudi Arabia, but paid the price of over-extravagant groundwater and land salinization. (Wiki Commons)
In addition, warming will also be a serious constraint.
While some would argue that the Saudis are used to high temperatures and that rising temperatures have little impact, it ’ s not that simple.
Temperatures in Saudi Arabia have risen three times faster than the global average over the past four decades, with daily maximum temperatures likely to reach an average of 50 degrees Celsius by the end of the century, and humidity is also rising rapidly. Dewpoint, a measure of humidity, has risen by 6 degrees in the past four decades, especially on the east and west coasts.
Such a combination of high humidity and high temperature can make it difficult for sweat to evaporate, making it difficult to regulate body surface temperature, raising the risk of heat stroke and dehydration, and even life-threatening.
Saudis accustomed to dry heatwaves will find it hard to withstand the changes, and the country ’ s highly dependent foreign workers will find it even more intolerable.
In particular, Saudi Arabia has planned a large number of infrastructure options for its future development, and the open-air construction industry will bear the brunt of the extreme hot and humid climate.
In addition, such a deadly heat wave will also reduce the attractiveness of foreign talent and tourists.
To make matters worse, Mecca, Saudi Arabia ’ s first holy city, and Jeddah, the second largest port city, are both on the west coast, while Dhahran, the city of Saudi Aramco, where Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco is headquartered, is on the east coast of the Persian Gulf, suffering more from rising humidity than Riyadh, deep in the heart of the desert.
These cities have now occasionally exceeded the “extremely dangerous ” threshold of“ Wet bulb Temperature, ” a comprehensive measure of humidity and heat, and scientists warn that they will become increasingly uninhabitable by the middle of the century.
Not only will this have a serious impact on Saudi economic activity, it will also affect the summer Hajj in Mecca, dealing a blow to its religious supremacy.
Saudi Arabia ’ s “Wet bulb temperature ” map on September 8 shows that the East and West coasts have exceeded the“ extremely dangerous ” threshold of 29 degrees Celsius. As temperatures and humidity continue to rise, the Saudi coast will become more uninhabitable. (Meteologix.com)
Off-site transformation and greening planning
The Crown Prince Mohammed is well aware of the unpromising prospects for the future.
Since 2016, he has proposed a “Vision 2030 ” aimed at attracting foreign investment and tourists and developing a diversified economic structure. In October last year, he proposed the“ Let ’ s Make it Green ” project for afforestation in Saudi Arabia, and recently proposed the goal of planting 450 million trees by 2030, generating electricity from 50% renewable energy, and achieving carbon neutrality by 2060.
However ambitious, these grand blueprints are underpinned by a lack of actionable action.
For example, the pillar project of Vision 2030, Neom Techno City, is full of Mohammed ’ s whims, including a taxi flying in the air, a Jurassic Park-like robotic dinosaur island, a sandy beach glowing in the dark, and a giant artificial moon.
The latest idea also includes a 170-kilometer stretch of The Line, connected by high-speed rail, with no roads and no vehicles, and an entire city powered by clean energy.
The whole idea is far beyond Saudi Arabia ’ s scientific and technological level and management capabilities, if not impossible.
The 170 km long line city (The Line) envisioned by the King of Saudi Arabia. (Neom official website)
At present, Saudi Arabia has invested US $1 billion in this project, but the project is still largely in the conceptual stage, and many foreign experts have resigned because they are not adapted to the management methods and the current situation of the project, so it is impossible to talk about the development of advanced technology and industry under the project.
As for attracting foreign investment, the influx of Saudi foreign investment has been greatly reduced since Mohammed seized royals and businessmen in the name of anti-corruption in 2017 and the dismemberment of dissident journalist Jamal Khashoggi in 2018, and the epidemic has worsened. Foreign direct investment (FDI) in the four years from 2017 to 2020 totaled only $15 billion, which is only 40% of the peak of foreign investment in Saudi Arabia in 2008. Desperate to step.
Similar to the loft-like Neom in the air, the Saudi carbon-neutral plan is also lacking in feasibility.
Muhammad, for example, has pledged to plant 450 million trees by 2030.
Not to mention that this rate is six times faster than the rate of tree planting in Saudi Arabia in the past year and a half, and it is doubtful whether it is feasible, and the specific tree planting options, planting areas and irrigation methods are unknown.
Planting trees in the desert is not easy. Although some traditional desert trees such as date trees and pea trees can survive on groundwater, the land may not be able to withstand large amounts of such trees in the case of excessive groundwater extraction and rapid decline in water levels in Saudi Arabia, which may require sophisticated irrigation technology, which is quite demanding in terms of technology and water resources. The cultivation of exotic trees can lead to an ecological crisis.
As for increasing renewable energy generation, this commitment is more feasible, after all, Saudi Arabia has sufficient light, large desert open space can be set up solar panels, and the strong wind brought by the northeast wind in the summer is also conducive to the development of wind energy.
However, given that the country ’ s renewable energy accounted for less than 0.05% of the country ’ s electricity supply in 2018, it is far from the target of 50% by 2030.
Coupled with the country's planning of a large number of infrastructure projects, the rapid increase in population, and the demand for desalinated seawater with the further depletion of groundwater, it is expected that electricity consumption will also rise, and the number of renewable energy installations and grid speed can catch up with electricity consumption is unknown.
For Saudi Arabia, the gift of oil allows the country to break through environmental constraints and easily become rich, but it also prevents it from developing industries, technologies and management experience other than the petrochemical system.
But as the share of oil wealth shrinks in the future and the country seeks to transform, harsh natural conditions begin to constrain the country ’ s development, and deadly climate change adds to the challenge. At the same time, the young king is too ambitious and avant-garde project planning, it is difficult to say whether it can transform the Saudi economy as it intended, rather than a waste of public money. And...
However, there is still time and money to transform the country in Saudi Arabia, which may be able to truly escape the blessings and curses of black gold and the restrictions of the sand and create a diversified green economy.

Recently, scholars from the Chinese Academy of Sciences announced the results of quantum computing research, announced that superconducting quantum computing and optical quantum computer Zuchongzhi No. 2 achieved a record computing performance, and German experts said that China has at least matched the Western level in this basic research field.
However, the current global quantum computer is still in the prototype stage, and the actual application is far from.
"German Voice" pointed out that Chinese scholars recently published a paper claiming that its newly developed 66 qubits (Qubits) programmable superconducting quantum computer Zuchunzhi No. 2, achieved record computing performance, 10 million times faster than the fastest supercomputer currently, and the computational complexity is 1 million times higher than Google's superconducting quantum computer prototype Sycamore.
In 2019, Google ’ s 54-qubit Suzuki became the world ’ s first quantum computer to achieve “quantum supremacy ” (Quantum Supremacy), significantly surpassing the performance of traditional supercomputers.
However, Suzuki can only handle some very abstract specific tasks, and there is still a lot of distance from the daily application scenarios.
According to the research and development team, the difficulty of handling the task is 2-3 orders higher than that of Suzuki.
Pan Jianwei, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences who led this research, said that the next step will be to solve quantum error correction, so as to explore the use of quantum computing to solve some scientific problems of great application value.
The report said that Pan's team also launched the optical quantum computing prototype 9 Chapter 2, which has the computing power per millisecond equivalent to 300 billion years of traditional supercomputers.
However, for the time being, Chapter 2 can only deal with specific tasks and is not yet suitable for practical application.
German experts said that in the past, the Trump administration's sanctions against Chinese technology can only be temporary measures, and they must strengthen their competitiveness in the long run.
In recent years, China has achieved a global leading position in the field of quantum technology. In 2020, Pan Jianwei ’ s team and scholars from international scientific research institutions such as Oxford University achieved unrelenting quantum secret communication based on quantum entanglement between two ground stations separated by thousands of kilometers.
These scientists also used the Mozi quantum communication experiment satellite as a quantum entanglement source, for the first time to achieve the distribution of quantum keys between two places thousands of kilometers apart.
The latest research results of quantum computing have been rated by Kristel Michielsen, a professor of physics at Aachen University and an expert in quantum communication at the Ulrich Research Center for Supercomputing in Germany, as “at least up to the level of quantum computing in the West. ”
However, Pan stressed that his team ’ s Zuchong II has 66 qubits, so its performance is four times that of a 54 qubit Google Suspension.
Neither of the two prototypes used their maximum computing power when handling the experimental task.
Pan Jianwei pointed out that the current quantum computing prototype error rate is still too high, so it can not be put into the actual application scenario.
The stability of qubits remains a major challenge for researchers around the world.
Michelson said that first to try to make high-quality qubits and quantum logic gates, but to keep them stable, it can only last 30 to 95 milliseconds, and scientists are fighting for the moment to let quantum computers handle experimental tasks.

Because no matter the content and the way of appreciation, they are so closely related to life, so cartoons are always the creation of ordinary people or people.
Therefore, the promotion, collection or research of manga, whether it is the analysis of the industry, the preservation and display of museums, or the discussion of the aesthetic or external significance of the manga, must eventually return to the level of life.
Only by restoring the link between "people" and "manga" can we show the unique nature of manga as the "ninth art".
Return to the content level of the comic, as mentioned earlier, the use of living materials, not necessarily with the contemporary reality as the background, but more broadly, direct or indirect reference to the reality of human beings.
Even the most fantastical sci-fi, there is a reflection and criticism of the current human situation; even if it seems to be a bloodthirsty royal drama, it also contains some encouragement or comfort for people's emotional shortcomings.
In short, the theme of the comic is inclusive of all things, but it must resonate with the hearts of the people and create a connection with life, so that the reader can forget and become intoxicated.
In recent years, with the cooperation of the government and the private sector, Taiwan's comics can be said to be full of flowers and vitality, which is quite a new trend in the new century.
Since 2010, the 12th consecutive Golden Manga Awards events have outlined the long-term trend of continuous vertical improvement and horizontal expansion of Taiwanese comics. Looking at these works, among different types and themes, Taiwanese comics are gradually forming their own graphic grammar and content narration, forming their own characteristics, and trying to intersect with the modern, past and future of this land to attract readers.
Taking the history of Taiwan as a creative idea is a very eye-catching category among the many themes of Taiwanese comics in recent years. This may be a natural phenomenon, because there is no more intuitive connection with life than history.
However, the reasons for this can be traced back to the rediscovery and understanding of Taiwan's history in the overall environment.
The history of Taiwan has never been taken for granted, and for many of today's middle-aged and older readers, most of Taiwan's history education in the course of study is lacking, often just as a glimpse of the vassals, do not talk about historical events or historical views, and often even do not even ask questions.
Growing up in that era, I would not know what the Silaya people were, nor would I know the prosperity of the Dadaocheng, let alone the political taboos such as the February 28 Incident or the White Terror.
It was not until after the lifting of martial law, political pressure gradually eased, and the academic community invested heavily in the investigation and study of Taiwan history, and began a series of educational reforms in 1990, that Taiwan history was "discovered".
First, there is knowledge, then there is knowledge, then there is knowledge of all creation.
In recent years, the creation of Taiwan history as a theme has sprung up like a spring. Whether it is a novel or a movie or a drama, you can clearly feel this strong trend. It can be regarded as the seed planted by many of the predecessors of the 1990s, and it has finally blossomed after decades of accumulation and brewing.
And not just a single flower, but a whole garden with strong roots and strong stems.
Comics with the theme of Taiwan history are a part of this wave, and the creations of other different media reflect each other.
For example, Kinono ’ s “Orchid Story II: South of a Stream, North of a Mountain ” is a sequel that has readers looking forward to five years. From the perspective of the Silaya people, outline the history of Taiwan under the power of all parties.
Unlike the first episode, which focuses on a single event, the second episode focuses on the daily life of the Silaya people, intertwining the tension between different ethnic groups and different nationalities on the island, which seems to suddenly explode and disintegrate at any time due to interests.
Kinono ’ s style of painting has also changed from the brightness of the previous work, to a certain melancholy atmosphere, with “people ” as the core, supplemented by detailed evidence, leading the reader into this hidden and uneasy historical world.
That feeling, outlined by the pen of fiction, seems to be restrained and fierce, is the god envied by historians.
Han Bao ’ s “Beast of the Clouds: Guardians from the Ancient World ” also has a similar effect to“ Orchid II ”, which is also based on fiction, reflecting the changes in Taiwan ’ s history with the passing of the clouded leopard from generation to generation.
In this fantasy story, the clouded leopard, who was accidentally blessed by a witch, appears in the National Taiwan Museum as a soul across time and space.
As the story progresses, readers suddenly realize that the author does not just want to describe the past, but more importantly, to point out the purpose and meaning of historical writing or heritage collections, which are efforts to retain the past in time, in other words, what the mission of the museum is.
When finally, through the mouth of the librarian, he said the joy of seeing the visitor say "Ah! That is...!", indicating that the museum collection became a part of him, but also represents the past, and a new life in the heart of another time and space. "Nothing, really will disappear!" VRE: Sense and Sensibility.
Unlike the fictional intersections of The Orchid II and The Beast of the Clouds, which are based on the story of Tsai Lin-kun, the victim of the White Terror and winner of the Golden Manga Special Contribution Award, Chou Mei-hsin and Yu Pei-yun ’ s Children from Clear Water are adapted in a non-fictional way to present history.
This unique presentation also reflects the new wave of “Graphic Novel ” that has emerged in Taiwan ’ s comics industry in recent years, breaking away from the established conventions and routines of Japanese and American commercial comics, and using images to tell stories in a freer way.
Using images to describe non-fiction may be more difficult than text, and the author conducts a large number of tests, with evidence for each frame.
At the same time, unlike the fixed form of text, the book also tries to use different image techniques, such as light and shade, to convey the various ups and downs of Cai's life.
If the writer's writing is passive in the hope that the reader will use emotion and imagination to enter, then the use of images of non-fictional comic books, with lines and pictures, to create a world of abstract and figurative co-construction, and actively invite the reader to join.
This effect also appears in Qiu Xianxun's "Hand Painting Taiwan Keywords: Painting 1940-2020", he once took Shi Ming's "400 Years of Taiwanese History" as the object of creation, and always took the "ignorant" as the premise of self-vigilance and creation, and left a record of Taiwan's history with images.
That is what his generation will understand, some kind of debt and atonement to this land.
We must continue to dig, constantly talk, so that more people understand the weight and importance of this knowledge.
This book also challenges existing people's established impression of class textbooks or comics, showing that Taiwan in recent years in the creative form of the unfettered, no longer limited to commercial comics.
In addition to these cartoons, which directly focus on Taiwan's historical events, historical elements have also infiltrated other works, and Chien Chia-cheng's "The Man Who Painted the Movie: The Good Times of Hand Painted Posters" has collaborated with the National Film Center to tell the forgotten fragments of Taiwan's film history.
Yang Shuangzi and Monday Recycling Day's "Qi Tan Hua Story" uses a delicate pen to describe the pursuit of freedom of Taiwanese women during the Japanese era. This book can of course be regarded as a type of comic, but it is full of historical evidence and tone, reflecting Yang Shuangzi's continuous self-breakthrough and challenge in the past few years between genre literature and historical novels.
The success of the story illustrates the possibilities of all kinds of crossover, between genres and genres, between novels and comics... Tell us about your past, and there are endless combinations.
As an example, if you go back to the previous Golden Manga Awards, the Inhuman Tea Traces series, The Night Long Dream, The Shou Niang, The Hundred Paintings of the North City, and The Invasion of the Last Name of 1661 can all be discussed in the same context.
Through the link between the past and the modern, history is the most direct link to life, but history is not the only way to link life. The different types of works accumulated over the 12 years of the Golden Comic Awards have captured and entered people's lives in various ways.
These works are waiting for people to read and find the joy, anger and sadness that echo their own.

Recently, the situation between the two sides of the Taiwan Strait was tense, and some experts compared the mainland's most equipped J-10 and Taiwan's main fighter aircraft F16, and found that the missile loading points of the two fighters were different.
Zhou Ziding said on his Youtube channel "Discovery Time" that the fourth-generation aircraft most equipped in mainland China is the J-10, while Taiwan's main fighter is the F16.
Both of these aircraft are four-generation aircraft, and both are light aircraft.
He compared the carrying capacity of the J-10 and F16 to see which fighter can carry more missiles.
Zhou Ziding pointed out that the J-10 has a total of 11 hanging points, and the F16 has 9 hanging points.
Although the J-10 has 11 hanging points, it can only carry four missiles.
In other words, the J-10 wing has three hanging points, and the belly has five hanging points, but the center axis hanging point of the belly and the two hanging points of the wing against the fuselage can only be hung with the auxiliary fuel tank, not the missile.
He analyzed two reasons, one is that the internal oil load of the J-10 is small, only 2.9 tons, if only rely on internal fuel, the combat radius and range are too short.
The second reason, the J-10 structure design, the two hanging points below the wing near the belly can not carry the missile.
As for the four hanging points below the belly, due to the design problems of the aircraft landing gear, missiles can not be carried, only bombs can be carried.
In this case, only the two outmost hangers on the wing can mount the missile, adding up to four hangers, and because of weight restrictions, the outermost can only carry light air-to-air missiles, usually the Thunderbolt 10, and the other two can carry the Thunderbolt 15.
In short, the J-10 has 11 pylons on the outside, but can only carry four missiles, including two short-range and two medium-range missiles.
In addition, as for the F-16's mounting capacity, Zhou Ziding said that because of the wing design and engine thrust, it can carry 8 tons of weapons, a total of 9 hanging points, each can be loaded with missiles, including the wingtips can be mounted weapons, two wings below each of the three hanging points, there is a hanging point below the belly.
Under the wing can also be replaced with a composite hanger, and in "beast mode", the F-16 can carry up to 15 missiles. The J-10 can carry a composite hanger only between the abdomen, so the J-10 can carry up to 6 missiles into the air.
