The ketogenic diet limits carbohydrate intake to less than 10% of total calories, while protein accounts for 20% and fat for 70%.
This method claims that meat can be eaten to lose weight. Compared to limiting calories and limiting eating time, Cheng Xinyi, Gin Lee, and Le Pont James are all supporters.
Ketogenic diet, "ketones" is the most important part.
Carbohydrates are normally converted into glucose to provide calories; when carbohydrates are reduced, glucose is insufficient, and the body is in a state of hunger, it is necessary to burn fat as fuel, and ketones are produced in the process.
Originally used to treat children with epilepsy, this method stabilizes brain cells by producing ketones to relieve seizures.
Later, it was discovered that the body produces ketone, which means that it burns fat, and has become a popular weight loss method in recent years.
The actual operation is as follows:
:: Limit carbohydrates to 20 to 50 grams per day
• Unlimited meat, egg and milk products, even fat, chicken skin, fried food
• Unrestricted fat, more butter, olive oil, coconut oil, etc.
• 2 cups of salad or 1 bowl of cooked vegetables daily, avoid high-carb vegetables such as taro and sweet potatoes
Some people take more than one vitamin.
Drink at least 8 to 10 glasses of water a day.
• Exercise for at least 30 minutes 3 days a week
■ Principle and effectiveness
One year later, the rebound was clearly causing cholesterol damage.
Very low carbon heat reduction
Many people eat carbohydrates in their daily diet, eliminating one type of food and reducing their calorie intake.
Inhibiting appetite
The ketogenic diet is dominated by high protein or high fat foods, which are easy to be satiated.
A normal meal, with rice, meat and vegetables, usually will be hungry after 4 hours; but if you add two steaks and a piece of butter, the feeling of fullness will be longer and you can avoid extra eating.
Consumes more calories
The stomach needs more calories to digest protein and fat and consumes more calories than other foods.
How effective is weight loss?
According to the study, people with very low carbohydrates lost more weight after 24 weeks, but also had higher levels of bad cholesterol, compared with people with low-fat diets.
Another study found that people who practice low-carbon weight loss rebounded significantly after 1 year.
■ Nutritionist 's opinion
It's against healthy eating.
The ketogenic diet violates the rules of healthy eating, and Lin Siwei disapproves of its use.
If you insist on trying, Lin Siwei means that you should choose good fats, such as avocado, salmon, olive oil, etc., and reduce the consumption of processed foods.
Ketogenic is a very low carbohydrate diet. It is recommended to slowly reduce the carbohydrate ratio, from 50% to 55%, to 40% to 45%, 30% to 40%, and choose high-quality carbohydrates, such as low glycemic index red rice, brown rice, whole wheat pasta, etc.
Short-term side effects:
• Headaches, fatigue, and other flu-like reactions, commonly known as keto flu
:: Irritability
:: Constipation
:: Stop menstruation
Long term impact:
Long term effects unknown.
Lin Siwei noticed that there are health problems in ketogenic diet online, she said: "When there are symptoms such as menopause and hair loss, you should consider whether to stop."
These medical questions should not be asked to online groups, they are not medical personnel; they should be understood by doctors and dietitians. ”
Unsuitable people:
• Pregnant or lactating women
• Children and adolescents
• People at risk of heart disease
Patients with type 1 diabetes (type 2 diabetes should be discussed with a doctor)
Patients with eating disorders
■ Summary
Fasting is more balanced and sustainable
Fasting and ketogenic, which is better? Combination of the two, the effect is better?
Losing weight is a very personal thing, living habits, working hours, etc., all affect the effect of weight loss.
Lin Siwei believes that the first consideration is the scientific basis and safety of each method, and the second is whether it can match their own living habits, such as eating habits, working hours, eating preferences and so on.
In addition, whether the method is easy to continue to be implemented, whether it is necessary to adjust the drug, etc., and then make a decision based on a series of factors.
Compared with ketogenic diet, Lin believes that the diet is more balanced and more sustainable; the ketogenic diet advocates eating a large amount of saturated fat, lacking in nutrients such as fiber, calcium, and antioxidants, or relying on vitamin supplements to supplement nutrients, contrary to the concept of absorbing nutrients from natural foods.
Some scientists have studied the effects of mixing different diets, such as intermittent eating and calorie control, but this has not been confirmed, and Lin Siwei does not recommend trying it on his own.

It was learned from Nvidia that Nvidia has broken a record in the emerging field of quantum computing and is launching software so that anyone can do the job.

The MaxCut algorithm is used to design large computer networks, find the perfect layout of chips with billions of silicon pathways, and explore the field of statistical physics. Nvidia says its solutions reach 96% of the best known answers.
cuQuantum ’ s first library, cuStateVec, is now available for download.

The cuTensorNet library, which helped Nvidia set a world record, will be launched in December.

Older people 's health _ Fall can be big or small! 10 ways to avoid home accidents
Filed to: Health 2.0
Published: Updated:
According to the Taiwan National Health Administration's 2020 cause of death analysis, the second cause of accident injury and death in elderly people aged 65 and above is "fall".
The elderly fall easily causes head injuries, fractures and other injuries, which in turn lead to the main cause of death.
The common indoor falls are in the bedroom, living room and bathroom.
In order to prevent the elderly from falling down and maintain safety at home, the public may wish to improve their home environment by "taking steps with peace of mind."
10 Tips to Save Your Home (by Graphic Design)
+ 8
1.
Adequate home lighting
Keep the room bright and set up small night lights or contactless lighting to prevent the elderly from tripping over obstacles.
2.
Spatial planning
The more simple the space planning, the better, remove more than 3 cm threshold, less debris, reduce the elderly fall risk.
3.
Positioning sign
Objects or pictures of distinctive colours for the elderly logo, such as clocks and calendars.
4.
Bathroom needs to be non-slip
The bathroom floor is equipped with anti-slip strips and armrests, which can make the anti-slip chair convenient for the elderly to use.
5. Stairs safety
Stairs should have solid handrails, the edges should be clear, and the stair surface should be coated with different color anti-slip strips, and there should be sufficient light.
6. Appropriate furniture
Too low, too soft chairs are not suitable for the elderly, choose furniture suitable for the elderly to provide home safety.
7. Fit clothes
The elderly should not dress too long or too wide, and choose shoes that fit their feet.
8. Appropriate room temperature
The elderly have lower body temperature and are more sensitive to low temperature. It is recommended that the room temperature should not be less than 24 degrees Celsius.
9. Safety Medicine
Some drugs can cause dizziness side effects in the elderly, such as blood pressure lowering drugs, sedatives, sleeping pills, muscle relaxants, diuretics, cold drugs, antihistamine, etc.
If you cannot avoid taking it, you should remind your elders to rest more after taking the medicine and slow down.
10.
Nutritional intake and regular exercise need to be balanced
To prevent weakness and build muscle strength, it is recommended to consume enough calories and protein daily to meet the body needs. Regular exercise can enhance muscle strength and maintain daily independent activity, which can help reduce the risk of falls in the elderly.

Is there a way out for Argentine politics to turn left and right again?
Author: Zhou Xuan
Published: Updated:
Argentine politics is like a pendulum, swinging violently from left to right, and the frequency is accelerating.
Two years ago, Alberto Fernández, a leftist, defeated a neoliberal to win the presidency, chanting “We ’ re back, ” but he suffered a setback in the parliamentary election, making the Peronists lose their Senate majority for the first time in nearly four decades and the ruling party a lame duck in legislation. But the resulting potential policy wobbles have further deepened the predicament.
Can Argentina find a way out of its crippling foreign debt and inflation crisis?
Since Argentina left the military government in 1983, it has experienced 20 years of neoliberalism (mostly right-wing conservative and right-wing Belonism), followed by 12 years of leftist Belonism, four years of right-wing rule, followed by the election of Fernández two years ago.
But he was only halfway through his term, and the right wing quickly shot back.
According to the results of the mid-term parliamentary election on November 14, the ruling coalition lagged behind the right-wing coalition by 8 percentage points in the House of Representatives election, and 11 fewer than the other party in the half of the elected seats.
The outcome of the Senate election was even more decisive. The overall vote of the Belonists lagged by nearly 20 percentage points, the first time they had lost a majority in the Senate since the return to democracy in 1983.
Inferno and Epidemic
These results are not surprising.
Fernández inherited a rotten mess from his predecessor, Mauricio Macri: annual inflation of more than 40%, a raging exchange rate (80% devaluation of the peso over four years), and a new $44 billion in foreign debt to the International Monetary Fund (due in 2022 and 2023).
Such a bad start, coupled with natural disasters such as the COVID-19 pandemic, has devastated global markets, and Argentina, whose lives depend on commodity exports, has taken the brunt of the financial crisis further, becoming the first country in the epidemic to default on its debt in April 2020, its ninth default.
Subsequent developments follow the Beronists ’ inertia, with their emphasis on government intervention and welfare initiatives that run counter to the IMF ’ s principles of free and open markets and fiscal austerity, and their national sentiments often see agreeing to IMF conditions as yielding to foreign powers.
Argentina ’ s $44 billion debt with the IMF has yet to be negotiated despite a successful $66 billion debt restructuring with private bondholders last year. This stalemate not only cuts off the country ’ s access to more loans during the pandemic, but also threatens another sovereign default on its first major repayment day in March.
Argentines took to the streets in September to protest against Fernandez ’ s government. (Reuters)
At the same time, Fernández also had to fulfill the Beronists ’ welfare obligations to the working masses, and foreign debt was not enough to print money, but this was no different from quenching his thirst, and the annual inflation rate rose further to more than 50%.
And the welfare measures of a cup of water can not withstand the longest blockade he has imposed in Latin America, 4 million people have returned to poverty in the past two years, and the number of new coronavirus victims has reached 110,000. Adjusted by population size and close to the neighboring country of Brazil, which has caused public anger. And punishing the ruling party with votes.
Sadly, despite the public ’ s anger, the fate of the lame duck in Congress will only make it more difficult for the ruling party to move forward and lead Argentina out of its predicament.
At the same time, it also raises the possibility that the right will return to the Rose Palace after two years, bringing about a new round of policy changes, but in the light of history, such a rapid swing will often only further deepen the predicament.
Argentina, which has mandatory voting rules, will struggle to cast a bright future no matter how it votes.
Difficult to solve on both sides of the road.
At the end of the day, the dilemma facing Argentina is not a simple left or right line can solve, the country's vulnerability is like a porcelain man walking a wire rope, accidentally will fall to pieces, and the left and right line leaders every open policy turn, so that the wire shakes even more.
At the same time, the international environment may blow a headwind at any time, and no matter what route the porcelain people can not avoid the fate of being blown down.
From the perspective of the domestic economic structure, the most prominent problem in Argentina is the excessive dependence on agricultural exports, which accounted for 57% of the value of total export goods in 2019.
This is the product of the country ’ s centuries-old dependence on the Pampas steppe, a land of agro-pasture, and the failed “import substitution industry ” of the last century. Although Argentina was clearly aware of the need to develop industry, Juan Perón, who ruled in the 1940s and 1950s, drew up his first five-year plan focused on industry, his sweeping nationalization plan, universal trade unions, welfare populist policies and opposition. Foreign capital inflows stifled market dynamism.
The ensuing three decades of military rule and bloody repression of the Beronists also saw the country miss a golden period of development.
When the literati returned to power in the 1980s, the priorities for restructuring the economy gave way to two major debt crises – the first due to the military government ’ s excessive borrowing of petrodollars in the 1970s, and the second due to the collapse of the 1979 oil crisis, the second due to the right-wing Bayonne government ’ s excessive borrowing from the IMF in the late 1990s, and the Asian financial crisis.
However, in the context of China's rise as the world's factory, Argentina's development of industry at this time has no comparative advantage and lack of foreign investors, and can only be tied to the position of an agricultural power.
At the same time, the specter of Belonism continues to haunt the land and gain a supreme aura as a result of the military government ’ s repression.
Since then, the ruling Beronists have also made it easy to use welfare populism to attract votes, but this has often resulted in excessive financial burdens and short-sighted characteristics of “giving people fish ”, such as Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner ’ s government, which held power from 2007 to 2015, whose direct cash transfers to the poor reduced extreme poverty by 30%, but inflated currency. Inflation has engulfed the broad middle class, and its successors have since planted the root of high public spending, leaving them with little fiscal space to reform.
For the Argentines, the core of Peronism is actually the passion for the poor, and today ’ s Peronism has mostly left the spirit of welfare populism, as shown in the exhibition of the 100th anniversary of the birth of Mrs. Peronism at the Argentine Museum in 2019. (AP)
In the absence of the ability to adjust the economic structure and the wind of welfare populism to limit the space for fiscal policy, the country is like a boat in the international environment, and it is difficult to withstand the headwinds that are blowing at any time.
Both the 2008 financial crisis, the end of the commodities boom in 2014, the 2018 US-China trade war, and the 2020 epidemic have had a huge impact on the country, triggering a sharp decline in current project revenue and fiscal revenue.
In these circumstances, it is difficult for any government to resist the shortcut of printing money to make up for the fiscal hole, triggering a devaluation of the currency to boost its export advantage, but also drowning in inflation caused by the high import of industrial and consumer goods.
Worse still, in each of these downturns, the sword of Damocles is shaken by the huge extra debt, which is exacerbated by the fact that keen investors are withdrawing their capital when the situation is not good.
To this end, left-wing governments usually adopt capital controls, but such a restrictive environment has deterred investors from the beginning, and right-wing governments, while opening up markets, are more vulnerable in headwinds.
For example, although the Macri government traded the principle of free and open access to the IMF in exchange for historic high aid, it was intended to give Argentina a strong shot in the economy, but in 2018 due to the great environmental headwinds of the Sino-US trade war, and the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates and sucked US dollar capital back to the United States, which caused international investors to withdraw, causing the peso to devalue. This fragmentation only deepened the heavy debt burden.
From this, it can be seen that simple left and right lines are difficult to solve Argentina ’ s plight, and the fierce left-right line conversion will only make investors and the public more uncertain, tend to short-term speculation, and politicians often only take advantage of the short-term period of power to make a big profit, or short-sighted welfare policies to attract people.
Only by the rational policy design of depoliticization, the long-term stability of the domestic political atmosphere, and the blessing of the beneficial international market, can Argentina have a chance to gain a piece of life and jump out of the continuous cycle of crisis.
But how easy is it to talk about?

Written by Yi-ching Kuai
The report on the state of the Thames, led by the Zoological Society of London, points to changes since the “biological death ” of the River Thames in 1957: the range of birds, marine mammals and natural habitats has increased since the 1990s.
However, experts in the Thames tidal zone have found a slight reduction in some fish species.
Conservation scientists say further research is needed to determine the cause.
Climate change has increased the temperature of London's waterways by 0.2 degrees Celsius per year.
The Zoological Society of London said rising temperatures meant that the tide levels of the Thames had risen since 1911.
According to the report, the sea level in Silvertown, on the north bank of the Thames, has risen by 4.26 mm per year since 1990.
The Thames is home to sharks including the tope, starry smooth-hound and spurdog, and hundreds of species of fish are found in the 215-mile river, the report said.
In addition, short-term trends show an improvement in water quality and an increase in dissolved oxygen from 2007 to 2020.
Top predator seals as an ecological indicator
Conservationists pointed out two months ago that changes in seal numbers showed that the River Thames was healthier than everyone thought.
Marine biologists see seal numbers as an indicator of the health of the river, which is alive and well despite the decline.
To monitor the seal population, the researchers compared the total number of seals taken by light aircraft over three days at different haul-out spots at the Thames Estuary, taking into account that some of the seals did not come ashore.
Researchers from the Zoological Society of London found that after the breeding season, a total of 2,866 grey seals and 797 spotted seals were home to the River Tamworth.
Seal numbers have been counted every year since 2013. In 2019, there were 932 spotted seals and 3,243 grey seals – grey seals have longer noses.
Marine biologists say a relatively stable seal population indicates good water quality and stable fish resources.
Conservation biologist Thea Cox said: "Seals, as top predators, are an important indicator of ecological health and can tell us about the Thames."
“People think of the Thames as a dead river because the water is brown, but the Thames is full of life – the water quality has improved a lot, ” Ms. Cox said.
Although seals are a protected species, they face many threats, such as disease, marine litter, entanglement in abandoned fishing nets or being hit by boats.
In addition, seals are also vulnerable to interference when raising young animals, especially in water activities such as human sighting, dog wandering and canoeing.
£4.2 billion ‘ super sewer ’ to be opened in 2025 to save water quality
Alison Debney, of the Zoological Society of London, said: “Estuaries are threatened but often overlooked ecosystems.
The estuary provides us with clean water to prevent flooding and is an important nursery for fish and other wildlife.
“The Thames Estuary and associated ‘ blue carbon ’ habitats, which use marine activity and marine life to absorb and fix carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, are critical to our efforts to mitigate climate change, build a resilient future for nature and humanity. ”
"This report allows us to truly understand how far the Thames has come on the road to recovery since the announcement of the biological death and, in some cases, set the stage for future development."
The River Thames is an important part of what makes London unique, and plays an important role in the lives of many Londoners. Tom Edwards, BBC London ’ s transport and environment correspondent, analysed the first major report on the state of the River Thames in 60 years.
The good news is that since the announcement of biological death in 1957, the ecological environment of the River Thames has improved dramatically, and there are now 115 species of fish and 92 species of birds, including seahorses, eels, seals, and even sharks.
Hopefully, things will improve when the Super Sewer opens in 2025.
Officially known as the Thames Tideway Tunnel, the report highlights the need for the Thames Tideway Tunnel.
The £4.2 billion sewer is 15 miles (24 km) long and 200 feet (6,100 m) deep and is estimated to collect 39 million tons of untreated sewage now flowing directly into the Thames each year.
Liz Wood-Griffiths, of the Tidal Road Project, said: "This sewer will have a great impact on the water quality of the River Thames and will provide a healthy environment for wildlife to survive and thrive."
The concern is the effects of climate change: sea levels are increasing by 4 millimetres a year, and the temperature of the Thames is increasing by 0.2 degrees a year.
These changes can seriously affect wildlife at the mouth of the river.
The Zoological Society of London says it is currently working closely with partners to create new estuarine habitats, including seagrass habitats and saline marsh habitats.
“This not only helps to restore the river to life, but also acts as a natural flood defence and helps mitigate the effects of extreme climates such as storms and floods, ” said the Zoological Society of London.

Breaking the Quantum Hegemony: The National Supercomputing Wuxi Center Team Won the ACM Gordon Bell Award in 2021
2021 / 11 / 21 17: 23: 16 Source: IT House Author: Muquan
According to the official news of Jiangsu Science and Technology, in the early morning of November 19, at the Global Supercomputing Conference (SC21), the Shenwei Quantum Simulator (SWQSIM) jointly developed by the National Supercomputing Wuxi Center, Zhijiang Laboratory, Tsinghua University and Shanghai Quantum Scientific Research Center won the ACM Gordon Bell Award in 2021.
The winning project is: “Bridging the ‘ Quantum Hegemony ’: Real-time Simulation of Random Quantum Circuits Using the New Shenwei Supercomputer ”.
Liu Xin, the head of the team, revealed that SWQSIM can get a million higher fidelity association samples within 304 seconds, and the same number of unrelated samples within a week, breaking its claim of “quantum supremacy. ”
And the software can also complete more than 1000 times more complex quantum circuit simulation than "Suzuki" in 60 hours, and realize the single amplitude and multi-amplitude simulation of 100-400 bit quantum circuit algorithm, providing a solid simulation support for the development of quantum computing in the future.
Although Google has previously said that the quantum computer it developed successfully completed the problem that traditional computers need 10,000 years to deal with in 3 minutes and 20 seconds to achieve "quantum hegemony".
But this year's "Gordon Bell" award winning results, a powerful response to Google's statement, breaking the quantum hegemony.
IT House learned that the team of the National Supercomputing Wuxi Center has won the Gordon Bell Award many times before. In 2016, the whole-machine application based on the "Shenwei Taihu Light" system won the "Ten Thousand Approval Extended Global Atmospheric Dynamics Full Implicit Simulation", and in 2017, the whole-machine application based on the "Shenwei Taihu Light" system won the "Nonlinear Large Earthquake Simulation".
The official said that in the future, the National Supercomputing Wuxi Center will continue to carry out research and development of domestic independent systems (including chips, servers, supercomputing (intelligent computing) systems, system software, etc.), focusing on the existing foundation of the supercomputing center, building a full-stack domestic high-performance computing application ecosystem, and actively carrying out supercomputing ecological construction based on the autonomous supercomputing system.
The center will also develop large-scale parallel application software, research to solve the problem of parallel application software neck, to achieve the localization of large-scale parallel application software replacement, has now supported climate meteorology, life science, marine science, materials science, advanced manufacturing and many other important areas, for China's basic research and local industrial development to provide strong support.

What we want you to know is
According to the book "Sakyamuni's Medicine Box," written by the Japanese preacher Tao Dong-tsung, who has studied Buddhism and medicine, ginger is a "life-long medicine" approved by Sakyamuni, and traditional Indian medicine Ayurveda is also used to treat ear diseases, nasal diseases, and vocal problems.
Text: Lotus Seed Water Community
Ginger plants are mainly grown in the tropics, so if there are temperate gardeners who want to grow Ginger plants, one of the most important points is to protect against the cold.
However, Ginger flowers are very attractive to temperate gardeners. If you can plant one or two plants in your own greenhouse garden, it will not only bring warm aroma to the greenhouse, but also bring bold vitality to the temperate garden.
Of course, for East Asians, the main value of Ginger plants is still in the edible value, so although there are many Ginger plants, if you want to choose a representative Ginger plant, everyone's daily consumption of ginger (Latin name Zingiber officinale) should still be the main seat.
Ginger, as we call it in our daily lives, is also the only species of Ginger family that offers edible stalks, and the ginger that Europeans eat should also be passed down from Asia.
And who, exactly, domesticated Ginger?
The most plausible corollary is probably the people who lived in what is now India or southern China in ancient times, because not only is this region likely to be the earliest place of origin of ginger, but Buddha Siddhartha also recognized the benefits of ginger for self-cultivation.
According to the book "Sakyamuni's Medicine Box", written by the Japanese preacher Tsung-tsung, who has a certain knowledge of Buddhism and medicine, ginger is a "life-long medicine" approved by Sakyamuni, and traditional Indian medicine, Ayurveda (meaning "everlasting life"), is also used for some ears. Treatment of diseases, nasal diseases and vocal problems.
Therefore, it is very likely that the doctors and the people of East Asia gradually came to understand the "various therapeutic effects of ginger" during the Eastern Buddhist period.
Of course, ginger is also very effective for many diseases, but according to the current laws in Taiwan and many East Asian countries, only medical personnel can talk about or comment on the efficacy.
Therefore, although many Chinese books regard "ginger" as a kind of herbal medicine, the general public may still want to see ginger as a kind of "food".
Otherwise, if a very controlling medical director appears, in the future, even the "ginger" harvested by farmers may not be able to buy in the general market.
And what is the difference between "Ginger" and "Dried Ginger"?
Basically, "ginger" can be divided into "old ginger" and "tender ginger" according to the growing period.
Of course, some people call ginger with a shorter growth period "ginger", and "old ginger" to be distinguished, so in some cases, some people say "ginger" is actually "tender ginger". As for, "Why is ginger old spicy"? This should be because "old ginger" has more "ginger" (ginger) than "tender ginger".
As for dried ginger, it is the food obtained after some special cooking process (or "cooking") of old ginger, because in this process some "ginger" will form a new polymer, so that the effect of the medicine becomes a little different from that of old ginger.
So, what about "ginger" or "dried ginger"?
It depends on what you want to improve.
For example, when Japanese eat sushi, it must be "pickled ginger slices". In addition to removing the fishy smell and killing bacteria, it is also an appetizing effect of "tender ginger".
As for, if you want to "drive out the cold", to alleviate some cold caused by the chilling condition, it is natural to use "old ginger" or "Chen ginger".
Of course, in addition to consulting relevant professionals, you can also study some Chinese herbal medicine books by yourself, and after learning more about the various possibilities of ginger, you will naturally have less misunderstandings when taking it.
In short, herbal enthusiasts in East and South Asia are quite familiar with “Ginger ”, and some observations are quite subtle, which is worth your reference.
In contrast, Western Europeans' knowledge of ginger is relatively stuck in the stage of "telling stories", the most famous of which is the story of the "gingerbread man".
(The following video introduces the adventures of the Gingerbread Man. The story is very short, but it is quite childlike. It is a story that many European children know.)
Basically, the protagonist of this story, the “Gingerbread Man ”, is a cute and arrogant character who escapes from the table and tries to chase him back, but he can escape safely until he finally meets the clever fox.
In addition to its popularity in Europe, the story may have inspired many new creative ideas, including the world-famous Pinocchio.
For lovers of world history, whether it is the era behind the story of "Gingerbread Man" or "Puppet Story", it is a historical topic worth knowing.

U.S. President Joe Biden on Wednesday placed Chinese technology companies involved in quantum computing on a trade blacklist for national security reasons.
What is quantum computing? Why are the United States and China working hard to develop this black technology? Are they even more defensive? If China succeeds in developing it, it will completely disintegrate the US military advantage?
Quantum computers have their roots in quantum physics, which emerged in 1920, and are very different from classical mechanics, which even Einstein could not accept.
In 2012, physicist and bestselling author Brian Engelin used a popular science approach to explain what “quantum physics ” and“ quantum computers ” mean on National Geographic Channel.
First, he explained by the "double slit experiment" that the world is not composed of "particles", but "probability waves", and the size of the fluctuations represents the probability that electrons may appear here.
The large fluctuation does not mean that most of the electrons are gathered here, but that the electrons are most likely to exist.
Electrons are just a collection of possibilities, not electrons there.
In addition, quantum physics has a so-called "entanglement phenomenon", two particles can be entangled with each other when they are close, and then a cascade relationship will occur. Even if these particles are separated and moved to the opposite position, they are still entangled and inseparable.
And the electron has a spin phenomenon, not clockwise, or counterclockwise.
If you use a wheel as a metaphor, there is a "entangled phenomenon" of a wheel, a finger red.
The other must point to the blue, even if it is placed on the moon without a power connection, it is called the "telephantom effect", that is, when measuring one particle, it will affect the other particle.
Applications of quantum physics include quantum computers. The bits of a quantum computer are not traditional bits, and can have 0 and 1 at the same time, called qubits, or Q-bits.
Just as an electron can be a mixture of clockwise or counterclockwise rotation, a qubit can also be a mixture of 0 and 1, so the Q-bit can be multitasking, and the computing power grows exponentially.
According to the political commentary program "Critical Moment", according to the existing data, if China successfully develops a quantum computer, not only can it detect the US stealth fighter, but the US military advantage may completely collapse.

China-Africa Cooperation Forum Summit
China's African Disillusionment
The China-Africa Forum opened in Dakar on Sunday, and the French newspaper Le Monde published a series of analyses and reports under the headline "Africa and China: A Moment of Disillusionment."
The China-Africa Cooperation Forum, held every three years, opened on November 28 in Dakar, Senegal, at a much lower level than previous summits, with more African heads of state attending the Forum than attending the United Nations General Assembly.
Advertisement
The “downgrade ” of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation is, of course, related to the COVID-19 pandemic, with Chinese President Xi Jinping preferring to stay in China, but it also highlights the contraction of the once-thriving“ Central Africa ”, which is lower than their respective hopes when compared to the once lavish scale of nearly two decades.
The limited effectiveness of industrial programs, uneven trade exchanges, debt traps, corruption by elite groups, and lack of respect for workers ’ rights by Chinese enterprises have increased Africa ’ s discontent.
As a result, although the level of satisfaction of the African people with China is still relatively high, a retrogressive trend has begun.
Congo, the country that once signed the “Pact of the Century ” with Beijing, big contracts for“ mineral infrastructure ” remain a mirage: none of the 31 hospitals have been built, and the two announced universities have yet to be seen.
According to the Pew Center ’ s long-term survey for 2013-2019, South Africa ’ s satisfaction with China decreased from 48% to 46%, Kenya from 78% to 58%, and Nigeria from 76% to 70%.
Everyone realizes that spending money is not enough to spur development.
Africans, in particular, are aware that the vast amounts of money released by the Chinese are ultimately quite expensive in terms of interest rates and that repayment periods are too short to spur the desired development.
From 2002 to 2020, trade exchanges between China and the African continent increased 20-fold, from $10 billion to $200 billion, enabling China to replace the United States as the continent ’ s largest trading partner.
According to McKinsey & Company, in 2017, there were about 10,000 Chinese companies operating in Africa, but the actual number registered in China was about 3,000-4,000, and the rest were Chinese-led African companies, adding up to about 1 million Chinese working, investing, and doing business in Africa.
Beijing's political interests
China is also selling soft power to Africa, setting up 62 Confucius Institutes in Africa, while Chinese universities enroll 60 million African students, a way to train future pro-Beijing elites for Africa.
Beijing has also continued to strengthen its cooperation with “African brothers ” in the historical trend of decolonisation in Africa, and in 2017, Beijing opened its first military base in Djibouti, expanding another strategic dimension for China and Africa into the framework of the Belt and Road, a country in the Horn of Africa that is very important in the eyes of the Chinese as a major strategic link between the Indian Ocean and the European continent.
China has also gained huge political benefits in Africa. Thierry Pairault analyzes that every time China makes a small investment, buy or sell, it can retain a customer, it can receive a “dividend ” from the United Nations – a vote of support from African countries.
This is the mystery of how China got the leaders of the four UN agencies.
These are the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the Industrial Development Organization (Onudi) and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).
Neither Europeans nor Americans have ever led so many United Nations bodies at the same time.
China can conquer these positions only with the support of Africa, and the cost is quite low.
The Congo Dream.
After all, the number of China's expansion in Africa cannot hide the growing discontent and even the increasing friction.
Contrary to popular belief, the reality is that China is a service provider, not an investor, in Africa.
By contrast, Chinese investment in Laos, a small country of 7 million people, has in recent years accounted for 30-40% of China ’ s investment in the entire continent of 1.2 billion people.
The Chinese actually invest less in Africa than in services, such as infrastructure contracts, which are ultimately passed on to Africans through debt, with Beijing investing $2.7 billion in Africa in 2019, but providing services as much as $44.4 billion.
Moreover, Chinese investment tends to be concentrated in areas where there is little technological value added, such as mining.
A compelling example is Congo ’ s relationship with China. In 2008, Joseph Kabila confirmed a huge barter deal with Beijing that would be a “contract of the century, ” the perfect embodiment of this“ win-win ” partnership that China has promised Africa.
China buys cobalt and copper from his country for infrastructure: roads, railways, hospitals, schools, universities...
More recently, relations between the Republic of Congo and China have been strained, and the incoming president has reassessed contracts with China for copper and other mining investments and found that the large “mineral infrastructure ” contracts signed under Kabila in 2008 remain a mirage: none of Beijing ’ s planned 31 hospitals have been built, nor are the two announced universities.
In Kenya, amid ongoing construction plans for the Nairobia-Mombasa railway, a court ruled in 2020 that Chinese companies awarded contracts had not complied with competition rules, and the country ’ s judiciary questioned the legality of some past contracts with the Chinese.
In this context, the Dakar China-Africa Forum may mark a tortuous shift in China-Africa relations, in contrast to the ambitions of the last two decades, when experts say that the Chinese face a much more complex situation in Africa than they did two decades ago, when relations between the two sides were only a matter of elites, and now the Chinese must face an increasingly demanding civil society.
African leaders have had to contend with increasing questions about opaque contracts, debt traps, and limited access for African products to the Chinese market.
For China, how to accurately grasp the changes in Africa and adjust its own plans.
Otherwise, she would see her satisfaction curve continue to decline.

In 2014, when U.S. shale oil was being pumped, it was thought that the international energy map had flipped, that the United States was becoming less reliant on the Middle East, and that the focus of diplomacy would shift to Asia.
However, when the epidemic raged and countries tried to revive their economies, everyone found that they still relied heavily on oil in the Middle East.
Even the United States has released 50 million barrels of war oil and hopes to persuade Saudi Arabia to increase production to lower oil prices and slow inflation.
When the United Nations Climate Change Conference was held in the United Kingdom, everyone stressed the need to develop green energy and reduce dependence on oil, but when the price of energy soared, people only found that they could not quit oil in a moment or two.
The international situation is full of paradoxes and unexpected turns.
Rising oil prices have given Saudi Arabia political and economic leverage.
The United States hopes that Saudi Arabia can cooperate with the increase in production to ease oil prices, but Saudi Arabia has not easily waited until the epidemic has slowed down and oil prices have rebounded. Why should it cooperate with the United States to increase production to pull oil prices down?
Biden spoke only to King Salman, the prince ’ s father.
Biden also said last month that there are a lot of people in the Middle East who want to talk to him on the phone, but he has not decided whether to talk to them.
One of the things he hasn ’ t decided on yet is MBS.
The relationship between the Trump administration and Saudi Arabia is very close.
Therefore, in October 2018, Saudi dissident journalist and Washington Post columnist Khashoggi was killed at the Saudi consulate in Turkey, and Trump only raised his head and put it down lightly.
After Bai boarded the stage, he said that it was necessary to investigate the incident, and it is likely that the incident will follow up to MBS.
In addition, the 9 / 11 investigation report, Biden is also preparing to declassify and release, which may also involve the Al-Qaeda organization and the Saudi royal family's countless funds.
This makes the relationship between Biden and Saudi Arabia tense.
What ’ s more, Biden ’ s desire to restart relations with Iran is more likely to change the balance of power in the Middle East.
As a result, Saudi Arabia quickly adjusted its policies, resumed diplomatic relations with the United States, began contact with Iran, and began to prepare to end the civil war in Yemen, hoping to use these gestures to rebuild relations with the United States.
However, oil prices have risen, and this situation has changed.
MBS snatched the throne from his cousin in a bloodless coup d'état in 2017.
At that time, oil prices continued to fall, from $115 per barrel in June 2014 to $45 in January 2015, and even lower than $30 in early 2016. MBS put forward its Vision 2030 plan to attract international investment and help Saudi Arabia transform its economy, instead of relying solely on oil.
However, the fundraising effect was not good, the Khashoggi incident seriously damaged the image of Saudi Arabia, and encountered the economic contraction caused by the epidemic, and the collapse of oil prices, forcing Saudi Arabia to increase taxes, reduce expenditures, and borrow money.
MBS support in the country also began to falter.
Who knows now that oil prices are starting to rise, the shale oil industry in the United States, which has been hit hard by the epidemic, cannot make up for the gap in oil supply, and international funds are beginning to pour into the Middle East to steal oil.
Saudi oil production increased to 10 million barrels per day, exceeding even pre-pandemic production.
Instead of using oil to cut taxes or increase public spending, Saudi Arabia has used the money to pay off its debts and enter sovereign funds, giving it more leverage to invest abroad or map out its economy.
Of course, if the epidemic heats up and the economy shrinks, it will affect oil prices.
Whether Saudi Arabia and non-OPEC Russia can coordinate production also affects oil prices.
Therefore, the most important thing for MBS now is to grasp the current prosperity, hurry to attract foreign investment, jointly push forward the economic transformation plan of Vision 2030, and consolidate its power base.
Therefore, unless the Biden administration can provide sufficient incentives, MBS really has no reason to cooperate with the United States to increase production in order to lower oil prices.

The Extra Complexity of Quantum Mechanics: How Quantum Computers Will Correct Errors in the Future
2021 / 11 / 29 10: 31: 12 Source: Sina Technology Author: Ren Tianren Editor: Gucheng
Beijing time November 29 news, according to foreign media reports, the topic of quantum error correction is far less than "quantum hegemony", for the application of quantum computers, quantum error correction is far more important than quantum hegemony.
So, what kind of error correction will a practical quantum computer take? Recently, researchers demonstrated on a real machine.
The state of a single qubit needs to be changed to 9 qubits for error correction.
In 1994, Peter Shore, a mathematician at Bell Labs in New Jersey, proved that quantum computers could solve some problems much faster than classical machines, even exponentially.
The question is, can we build a quantum computer?
Skeptics argue that the quantum state is so fragile that the environment will inevitably confuse the information in a quantum computer so that it is not a quantum state at all.
A year later, Peter Shore responded.
The classic error correction scheme is to correct errors by measuring a single bit, but this method is not suitable for qubits, because any measurement will destroy the quantum state and thus interfere with quantum computing.
Shure found a way to detect if an error occurred without measuring the state of the qubit itself.
This approach marks the beginning of the field of quantum error correction.
As the field flourished, most physicists began to see Shur ’ s algorithm as the only way to build practical quantum computers.
Without this approach, there is no way to improve the performance of quantum computers so that they can solve really difficult problems.
As with normal quantum computing, developing error correction code is one thing, and implementing it in a working machine is another.
However, in early October 2021, a research team led by University of Maryland physicist Chris Monroe reported that they successfully demonstrated multiple elements necessary for Shur ’ s error correction circuit to operate.
So, how did Peter Shore solve this problem?
In short, he took advantage of the extra complexity of quantum mechanics.
Repeated comparison
Peter Shore modeled the code for classical repeaters when designing error correction codes, which involved copying each bit of information and then periodically checking those copies.
If one of these bits is different from the other, the computer can correct the error and proceed with the calculation.
In the quantum error-correcting coding designed by Shure, he used three separate “physical ” qubits to encode a single qubit of information, namely“ logical ” qubits.
Of course, his quantum relay encoding cannot be exactly the same as the classical version.
The advantage of quantum computing essentially comes from the fact that qubits can exist in a “superposition ” of 0 and 1 at the same time.
Since measuring the quantum state disrupts this superposition, there is no direct way to check if an error has occurred.
The classic error correction scheme is to correct errors by measuring a single bit, but this method is not suitable for qubits, because any measurement will destroy the quantum state and thus interfere with quantum computing.
In order to solve this problem, quantum error correction coding needs to find another way to detect the state of the qubit.
Instead, Shure found a way to tell if the three physical qubits were in the same state.
If one of the qubits is different, it indicates that an error has occurred.
Checking whether a qubit has gone wrong is not much different from solving a simple logic puzzle.
If you were given three balls that looked exactly the same, but one of them might have different weights; and if you were given a simple balance, what measure would you use to determine if there were balls of different quality? If so, which ball?
The answer is, first pick out the two balls and compare their weights, then replace one of them with the remaining balls, and check again.
If the balance is balanced twice, then all the balls are the same weight; if the balance is balanced only once, then the ball being replaced or the ball being replaced is of different weight; if the balance is not balanced twice, then the ball that is still is of different quality.
The Shur code replaces the balance with two additional "auxiliary" qubits.
First, compare the first auxiliary qubit with the first and second physical qubits; then, compare the other auxiliary qubit with the second and third physical qubits.
By measuring the state of these auxiliary qubits, it is possible to know whether they are in the same state without interfering with the three physical qubits containing information.
This code prevents what ’ s called a “bit flip ” — the only error that can occur in classical computing.
However, qubits have another potential source of error.
Superposition is the key to quantum computing, but what matters is not just the value of the qubits, but the relative “phases ” between the qubits are also important.
You can imagine the phase as a wave, which describes the position of the crest and trough of the wave.
When two waves are in phase, their ripples are synchronized.
If two waves collide, they will produce constructively interfere, merging into a wave twice as large; but if two waves are inverse, then when one wave is at its peak and the other at its lowest, they will cancel each other out, that is, destructive interference.
The quantum algorithm uses the phase relationship between qubits to set a situation in which the correct result of the calculation is interfered for a long time, thereby being amplified, and the wrong result is eliminated by the cancellation interference.
However, if an error causes a phase reversal, the cancelling interference becomes a phase long interference, and the quantum computer begins to amplify the wrong result.
Peter Shure discovered that he could correct phase errors using a principle similar to that of bit-flipping.
Each logical qubit is encoded into three qubits, and the auxiliary qubit checks if one of the phases is flipped.
Shure then combined the two codes to obtain a code that could convert a logical qubit into nine physical qubits, correcting bit flips and phase errors.
fault-tolerant
Shur's coding can, in principle, protect a single logical qubit from error.
But what if the error measurement itself is wrong?
In this case, when you try to correct an error that doesn ’ t exist, there may be a bit flip that unknowingly introduces a real error.
In some cases, this can cause an error cascade to propagate into the code.
Shur ’ s coding also didn ’ t consider how to operate a quantum computer built from logical qubits.
In 1996, after three years of pioneering research, Peter Shore proposed the concept of fault tolerance.
Fault-tolerant coding can handle errors introduced by the environment, errors introduced by imperfect manipulation of these qubits, and even errors introduced by the error correction step itself – provided that these errors occur less frequently than a certain threshold.
Just in October 2021, a team of researchers announced that they had successfully used the Bacon-Shor code — a fail-safe version of the Shor code — to demonstrate almost all the tools needed for a fully fault-tolerant quantum computer.
They encoded a logical qubit into a quantum state of nine ions and then used four auxiliary qubits to demonstrate that all the single-qubit operations required for quantum computing can be performed under fault-tolerant conditions.
The results show that fault-tolerant quantum computers are feasible.
However, this is still a long way off, and we will only see the advantages of error correction when the quantum computer reaches about 100 logical qubits.
Such a machine requires about 1,300 physical qubits, because each logical qubit requires nine physical qubits plus four auxiliary qubits (the largest quantum processor at the moment is IBM ’ s newly released Eagle, which has 127 physical qubits), and only then can we start building a qubit factory and then introduce error correction coding.

The European Union launched a "global portal" to compete with the "Belt and Road"
The European Commission on Wednesday unveiled a €300 billion global infrastructure investment plan in Brussels.
The EU wants to be a more attractive investment partner with the ability to compete with China ’ s Belt and Road Initiative.
The European Commission (EC) plans to invest 300 billion euros in infrastructure projects around the world, especially in Africa, Asia and Latin America, over the next five years.
The initiative, called Global Gateway, is a bit more expensive than it was when it was first proposed in September.
The European Commission (EC) has announced plans to build transport links, transmission lines and fiber optic cables in Africa and Latin America.
Some projects are already being planned or implemented.
Transparent, equitable and sustainable
The Commission stressed that the Global Gateway is based on the principles of sustainability, climate protection and digitalisation.
Relations between the EU and the beneficiary countries would be on an equal footing and would be committed to ensuring transparency in procedures and adherence to democratic values.
Local communities should also benefit from infrastructure investment.
For example, investing in the production of hydrogen fuel in Africa.
The EU will provide a guarantee of 3.5 billion euros to private investors, and as a condition, the beneficiary countries will promise that locally produced hydrogen fuel will be free from trade barriers when exported.
Another planned project is the laying of Internet broadband cables on the seabed of the Black Sea.
In addition, in Jordan, the European Union is interested in financing the construction of a bridge between the country and the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
European Commission President von der Leyen
The EU also plans to provide export subsidies to European firms to enable them to compete with local firms or foreign firms with state-funded backgrounds, such as Chinese firms.
At the same time, the EU is committed to implementing its universal standards in certain industrial sectors, as China has done with 5G and mobile network communications.
Investments under the Global Gateway framework focus on digitalization, climate protection and alternative energy sources.
European Commission President von der Leyen said several months ago that the purpose of the plan was “not to build roads for ports built by the Chinese. ”
The EU said that the Global Gateway investment plan does not exclude countries that have joined the Belt and Road Initiative, and interested countries can participate at the same time.
The United States and Japan launched their own global infrastructure investment plans several years ago to counter China ’ s “New Silk Road. ”
“China will not be scared. ”
Michael Clauß, a former German ambassador to China and now ambassador to the European Union, believes that the “global gateway ” is a good idea and“ has the potential to make the EU a more efficient geopolitical player. ”
For many countries, equal opportunities for cooperation based on rules and values are an attractive option outside of China ’ s Belt and Road. ”
Markus Ferber of the CSU, an expert on fiscal affairs in the European Parliament ’ s People ’ s Party group, is less optimistic about the huge plan.
He criticized the EU for its excessive market norms and excessive demands on the approval of funds.
Phil Bell believes that despite the increase in the total amount, this will not change the cumbersome procedural system of the EU, "most of the money comes from existing program projects, which is not a big deal."
China will not be afraid of this. "
The Global Gateway programme needs to be approved by the Council of the European Union (EU Member States' representative bodies) and the European Parliament before the first funds are scheduled to be disbursed in January next year.

How did Frank Herbert ’ s Dune, based on his journalistic experience, revolutionize science fiction?
Photo credit: Warner Bros.
What we want you to know is
When readers first came into contact with Dunes World in the 1960s, it quickly became apparent that it was unlike any fictional world they had ever read before.
A few decades before George Lucas ’ first draft of Star Wars, science fiction was still in its infancy.
Compiled by: Alice
The film “Dune ” has swept the world, and at the top of the box office, the studio has also announced the official launch of the sequel, which is expected to be released in 2023.
The Dune was originally written by Frank.
Written and published by Frank Herbert in 1965, the series consists of six songs, including the first, Dune, Dune Messiah, Children of Dune, The God Emperor of Dune, Heretics of Dune, and The End of Dune. "Chapter House: Dune", which won the Nebula Award in 1965 and the Hugo Award in 1966.
In fact, before becoming a science fiction writer, Frank Herbert did odd jobs. In 1957, while working as a journalist, Herbert traveled to Oregon to write an interview about how the state government was using jungle weeds to stabilize sand dunes along the coast line.
Herbert was impressed by the vast area and extent of the Pacific Northwest, where the natural landscape seemed to dwarf the large cities that Herbert had visited.
The interview, which Herbert never finished, was replaced by the experience that inspired him to work on the most influential science fiction series in history, The Dune.
Set in a fictional, extremely distant future, the story of humanity ’ s successful colonization of the most remote corners of the Milky Way.
The protagonist, Paul Atreides, is a young heir to the aristocratic family, which in the past was granted the management of the desert planet Arrakis, responsible for overseeing the extraction and export of spices, a drug that only exists in Arrakis and can distort time and space and prolong life.
When readers first came into contact with Dunes World in the 1960s, it quickly became apparent that it was unlike any fictional world they had ever read before.
A few decades before the first draft of George Lucas ’ Star Wars, science fiction was still in its infancy, often dominated by short stories and published in inexpensive magazines such as Amazing Stories.
In general, these stories are more concerned with creating suspense plots and exploring interesting ideas about human nature than with creating a lifelike, paper-based fictional time and space — Herbert ’ s Dune is both.
Rethinking science fiction
Of course, Herbert wasn ’ t the first to try.
More than a decade before Herbert published Dune, the English linguist and fantasy writer J.R.R. Tolkien ’ s classic The Lord of the Rings trilogy expanded the Middle-earth border, as he depicted in his earlier work The Hobbit.
The book contains an appendix to the history of the kingdom and royal blood to make the story more believable. Tolkien ’ s story is inspired by English and Gaelic folklore. In contrast, Herbert ’ s transformation into the original material of the sand dunes is not in myth, but drawn from history.
Readers familiar with "Dune" can find many connections between Herbert's imagination and the real world that inspired it.
Since the story takes place in the future of our real world, it makes sense to think that the society depicted in "The Dune" should carry traces of today's society.
In Dune, the planet colonized by humans is organized into a feudal system called Landsraad — a word taken from Danish that means “Land Commission ”.
Herbert chose to use foreign rather than English terms, suggesting that the Galactic Empire in the story may have originated in Scandinavia or was based on European feudalism.
Similarly, many of the characters in the story — despite living in very different time and space — have modern surnames.
For example, the main villain in the novel, Vladimir Harkonnen, a long-time rival of the Atreides family, is named De Vries, a surname derived from the province of Friesland in the north of the Netherlands.
In Dune, spices are the rarest and most valuable commodities in the known universe, such as today ’ s natural resources such as oil and natural gas – all of which exist only in specific locations around the world, and their existence has a major impact on human development and international relations.
History in the Dune
In The Dune, Herbert not only tries to make his writing acceptable to a large number of readers, but also satisfies his academic interests.
In order to make his fictional universe as real as possible, he made the history of the dune-world as complex and similar as that of our real world.
For example, it is no coincidence that the planets mentioned in the story came together under the rule of the emperor and were organized in a system of fiefdoms.
Centuries before the beginning of the Dunes story, when humans were pushed to the brink of extinction by robots and finally managed to turn things around, the survivors of the war (later known as the Bartland Jihad) decided to ban the development of artificial intelligence.
This resolution — “Thou shalt not build machines to impersonate the human mind ” — became the central precept of civilization ’ s progress, and explains why the society in Dune is not as advanced as one might think.
Culturally, the Battle of Bartland also seems to have brought society back to its half-century state.
For example, the reader may be surprised to find that religion is still active in the distant future and plays an even more important role than in our time — humanity unites all of the “old world ” religions into a single humanitarian text.
Known as the Orange Catholic Bible, this text is one of the most influential works in the entire dune-world.
Its spiritual teachings are a combination of monotheistic, polytheistic religions that serve as guidelines for how the citizens of the empire should behave and progress.
The highest commandment, “Thou shalt not destroy the soul, ” is a variation of the lessons learned from the Battle of Bartland.
Many of the above details did not appear in Danny.
In the film adaptation directed by Denis Villeneuve, it is not even emphasized in the original novel, but it can be seen in the appendix and index at the end of each book – Herbert ’ s genius and revolutionary influence on science fiction are hidden in these often overlooked title pages.

China 's heavy industry spawns new super rare earth group
According to the Wall Street Journal, China is expected to announce this month the approval of a new large-scale rare earth company, becoming one of the largest rare earth companies in the world.
Beijing hopes to maintain its dominant position in the global rare earth supply chain at a time of deepening tensions between the United States and China.
The report quoted people familiar with the matter as saying that the new company will be called China Rare Earth Group, and will be set up in Jiangxi Province, where the industry is developed, as soon as this month.
The new group was formed by the merger of several state-owned enterprises, including China Minmetals, China Aluminum, and Ganzhou Rare Earth Mining.
People familiar with the matter also said the new group aims to further strengthen the Chinese government ’ s pricing power, avoid conflicts between Chinese companies, and use that influence to undercut Western efforts to catch up in the rare earth sector.
Some analysts believe that China mines more than 70% of the world's rare earths and accounts for 90% of the complex rare earth refining process; but a White House report estimates that China controls only 55% of the world's rare earth mining and 85% of the refining.
In September this year, Minmetals Rare Earth Company issued an announcement that they received a notice from the parent company China Minmetals Group that they would plan a strategic reorganization of related rare earth resources with China Aluminum Group and the People's Government of Ganzhou City.
Minmetals Rare Earth Company said at the time that the relevant plan has not yet been finalized and has yet to be approved by the competent department.
At that time, Chinese media quoted data from the United States Geological Survey (USGS) as saying that in 2020, the global rare earth reserves were 120 million tons, and China's reserves were 44 million tons, accounting for 36.67% of the world's largest.
In view of the chaotic layout of China's rare earth industry and rampant underground rare earth trading, prices have been pulled down for a long time, and the "13th Five-Year Plan" in October 2016 is clear, to complete the integration of all rare earth mining, smelting and separation, and comprehensive resource utilization enterprises in the country.
Minmetals and China Aluminum Group are one of the six rare earth groups in China's rare earth industry, and the other four rare earth groups are Northern Rare Earth, Xiamen Tungsten Industry, Southern Rare Earth and Guangdong Rare Earth.
Today, Minmetals and China Aluminum for rare earth assets reorganization, China's domestic rare earth industry pattern will be reshaped.
The Wall Street Journal pointed out that rare earths containing 17 elements are highly valued for their magnetic and conductive properties, ranging from electric vehicles, smart phone touch panels, missile defense systems and even the components of stealth fighters.
Its dominance in the rare earth sector has allowed Beijing to influence the current fast-growing technology manufacturers.
At a time when relations between the West and China are increasingly sensitive, the West is worried that Beijing will use rare earths as a tool for geopolitical gaming.
In February, the Pentagon signed a technology investment agreement with Australia ’ s Lynas Rare Earths Ltd, which the U.S. military says is the largest rare earth mining and refining company outside of China.
According to the agreement, Linus will open a light rare earth refining facility in Texas.
Also around February, U.S. President Joe Biden issued an executive order listing rare earths as one of four key areas where stronger policies are needed to reduce supply chain risks.

Experience and Potential of China-Africa Cooperation in the New Era (Text: Zhou Yuyuan) (09: 00)
"Developing solidarity and cooperation with African countries is an important cornerstone of China's foreign policy and China's long-term and firm strategic choice." On November 26, the Information Office of the State Council issued a white paper entitled "China-Africa Cooperation in the New Era", which comprehensively summarized the new concepts, new practices and new achievements of China-Africa cooperation in the new era.
Through the white paper, we can find that Africa's importance in China's international strategy is on the rise, and China-Africa cooperation is at its best in history.
China-Africa cooperation is at its best in history
The White Paper outlines a brilliant transcript of China-Africa cooperation.
From political mutual trust, economic and trade cooperation, to social, humanities, peace and security cooperation, from agriculture, infrastructure, trade, investment, finance to digital economy, green development, from China-Africa cooperation to tripartite cooperation and international cooperation, China and Africa are forming an all-round, broad and three-dimensional cooperation pattern.
The "Ten Major Cooperative Plans" and "Eight Major Actions" have transformed China-Africa cooperation into visible and accessible projects, figures and results.
China has been Africa ’ s largest trading partner for 12 consecutive years since 2009, and is Africa ’ s largest international engineering contractor, infrastructure financier, important source of investment and development partner.
China and Africa have made important progress in important areas of cooperation such as infrastructure, energy and power, information and communication, and industrialization.
More than half of Africa ’ s wireless stations and high-speed mobile broadband networks are built by Chinese enterprises, with a total of more than 200,000 kilometers of optical fiber serving more than 900 million African people.
The achievements of China-Africa cooperation are the result of many factors.
It is easier for China and African countries to achieve understanding and consensus on the concept of development. According to a study by Africa Barometer, a well-known African polling organization, China ’ s development model is highly recognized in Africa.
China's cooperation with Africa pays more attention to Africa's needs and local realities, and often promotes the implementation of cooperation projects, and the actual projects increase the visibility of China-Africa cooperation.
In addition, China-Africa cooperation is mainly concentrated in infrastructure, power, information and communication, finance, public health, poverty reduction and other areas, these cooperation projects can often produce major economic effects, development effects and even political impact.
Rome was not built in a day.
As stated in the White Paper, China-Africa cooperation is carried out by the two sides step by step.
China-Africa cooperation is not only driven by the government.
In fact, in recent years, the rapid development of China-Africa relations has been inseparable from the participation of more and more Chinese private enterprises and social organizations.
China has more than 3,500 enterprises in Africa, employing more than 80% of the African workforce and creating millions of jobs.
Private enterprises are becoming the main force of non-investment, and private forces are also profoundly affecting China-Africa relations in the new era.
China-Africa Cooperation Faces "Growing Trouble"
Of course, China-Africa cooperation is not a smooth sailing, but also faces "growth troubles."
The process of deepening China-Africa relations is a process of continuous collision, interaction and integration between China and African societies, and a process of continuous adjustment of relations between China and other countries involved in Africa.
This process is often accompanied by a variety of issues, such as the impact of Chinese goods on local vulnerable industries and small businesses, the impact of Chinese projects on the local environment, the relationship between Chinese companies and local employees, and the legal awareness and cultural integration of citizens.
Although these problems are only cases, they often have a large negative impact.
The emergence of problems is not terrible, because the process of solving problems is also a process of continuous development of China-Africa relations.
In recent years, as the main platform for China-Africa cooperation, the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation has stepped up its response to problems arising in the process of cooperation, and formulated a series of measures and regulations in regard to considering the concerns of local society, supporting inclusive development, and enhancing China's corporate social responsibility.
The Chinese government has expressed zero tolerance for Chinese companies that have caused environmental damage and adverse impacts in Africa.
China-Africa cooperation is accompanied by conspiracy theories
The process of China-Africa cooperation is also accompanied by various rumors, conspiracy theories and stigmatization. After the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation in 2006, the smear of China-Africa cooperation began to increase rapidly, and it continues to expand and evolve.
From “neo-colonialism, ”“ resource predation, ” “opacity, ” to the current“ debt trap, ” China-Africa cooperation has been labeled negatively by some speculative politicians and the media.
This has caused interference in the international community's correct understanding of China-Africa cooperation, and has also affected the normal development of China-Africa cooperation and international cooperation with Africa.
These absurd arguments against common sense have been refuted by various professional and rigorous investigations.
Some wise people in the United States and the West have also clearly called on their governments to review China-Africa relations on the basis of facts.
To properly handle relations with Africa and the international community
Although these problems are only superficial, they reflect a deep-seated problem: the socialization and internationalization of China-Africa cooperation.
In short, it is a question of how China communicates, interacts and cooperates with African and international communities.
A good African society and international social environment can create conditions for the rapid development of China-Africa cooperation, and the rapid development of China-Africa relations needs to properly handle the relationship with African society and the international community.
There has never been a lack of cooperative initiatives and projects between China and Africa, but there may be a lack of institutional, public opinion and public opinion environment to ensure the smooth development of China-Africa cooperation.
Especially in the new era of the century-old changes and the century-old epidemic, the need to build a more open and inclusive China-Africa cooperation is stronger than ever.
In May this year, China and Africa jointly launched the "Support for Africa's Development Partners Initiative"; in September, President Xi Jinping proposed the "Global Development Initiative" at the United Nations General Assembly.
The main purpose of these two initiatives is to call for greater international solidarity and greater support for developing countries in Africa and elsewhere.
"Africa is the big stage of international cooperation, not the arena of the game of big countries", Africa's development potential and needs are very large, the development tasks and challenges are difficult, and Africa's fight against the epidemic and recovery and reconstruction need international solidarity and cooperation.
For China, giving play to the driving effect of China-Africa cooperation and leveraging more international resources to support Africa's development will be of great significance.
The new era of China-Africa cooperation should not be a one-off, but should fully release the potential of the China-Africa Cooperation Forum as a platform for international cooperation with Africa through sincere communication, integration of rules and action orientation, and promote the establishment of benign, complementary and higher-level international cooperation with Africa.
The author is a researcher at the West Asia Africa Research Center of the Shanghai Institute of International Studies
