Putin's visit to India focuses on military and energy cooperation
Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in New Delhi on Monday to seek to strengthen military and energy cooperation with his traditional ally.
The trip is Putin's second foreign visit since the outbreak of the coronavirus pandemic.
India has also been "courted" by Washington.
On November 13, 2019, Modi and Putin met at the BRICS Summit in Brazil.
In response to a rising China, Washington has recently established a quadrilateral security dialogue with India, Japan and Australia, raising concerns in Beijing and Moscow.
During the Cold War, India had close ties with the Soviet Union.
The relationship has always existed, and New Delhi calls it a “special and privileged strategic partnership ”.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Putin at a video summit in September that "India-Russia friendship has stood the test of time... You have always been a great friend of India."
The visit is Putin's second overseas visit since the outbreak of the pandemic.
In June, after a summit in Geneva with US President Joe Biden, he did not attend the G20 and COP26 summits.
Nandan Unnikrishnan of the Observer Research Foundation, a think-tank in New Delhi, called the trip “symbolic. ”
"There has been a lot of speculation about the nature of India-Russia relations and whether this relationship has been fractured by the close relations between Russia and China and between India and the United States, and this visit has put an end to all these speculations," he said.
However, Putin still has to deal with the complex regional situation.
Relations between New Delhi and Beijing, a traditional ally of Moscow, have been strained following bloodshed in the disputed Himalayan region.
Tatiana Belousova, of Om Prakash Jindal Global University in Haryana, said, “Russia ’ s influence in the region is very limited.
This is mainly because it has close ties with China and is unwilling to act contrary to China's regional interests. "
September 2021 BRICS Video Summit
Defence and energy
The Kremlin said last week that the Russia-India summit would focus on defense and energy issues.
As the negotiations involved "several important energy agreements", Russian energy giant Rosneft boss Igor Sechin also attended the summit.
Russia has long been a major arms supplier to India.
India is committed to modernizing its armed forces, and one of the most high-profile India-Russia military contracts is the S-400 long-range surface-to-air missile defense system.
The deal, worth more than $5 billion, was signed in 2018.
The delivery of the weapon system is reported to have begun.
However, the arms deal has the potential to upend bilateral relations between New Delhi and Washington, which have grown rapidly in recent years.
The United States has threatened to impose sanctions under the Sanctions Against American Adversaries Act (CAATSA), which aims to deter Russia.
The State Department said last week that no decision had been made on granting India an exemption.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Monday that Indian friends had made it clear to the Russian side that India is a sovereign state and that it is up to itself to decide whose weapons to buy and who can become India's partner.
New Delhi has long sought to diversify its military imports.
However, analysts pointed out that it will take some time to get rid of Russia.
Unok Richenan said that given the "unabated" tension with Pakistan, military equipment is of "vital importance" to India and "to ensure this, it will do its best to get what it needs."
India is also focusing on expanding its own arms manufacturing capabilities.
Recently, the country has established a joint venture with Russia to produce AK-203 assault rifles.
The annual bilateral summit has been the practice of India and Russia.
However, the last time the two leaders met was during the BRICS summit in Brazil in 2019.
In a statement last month, India's Foreign Ministry said that at this week's summit, the two countries "leaders will assess the current status and prospects of bilateral relations and discuss ways to further strengthen the strategic partnership between the two countries."
Prior to Putin's arrival on Monday, the foreign and defense ministers of the two countries had held preliminary talks.
Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh tweeted that the two sides had signed a number of agreements and contracts on small arms and military cooperation.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Moscow and New Delhi held "consistent or almost identical positions" on the most important global issues and security issues.

Modi Meets Putin, Putin Praises India as ‘ Strong and Reliable Ally ’
Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is visiting India, praised India as Moscow's "strong and reliable ally", Putin's visit focused on "energy" and "national defense", and the foreign ministers and defense ministers of the two sides held their first 2 + 2 meeting and signed a number of military cooperation agreements.
In a joint statement, the two sides reiterated their intention to strengthen defense cooperation and achieve the goal of 30 billion US dollars in bilateral trade by 2025.

Indian diplomatic officials said on Monday that Russia had begun supplying India with S-400 long-range air defense systems.
During Putin's meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the two sides also signed a 10-year military cooperation agreement and an oil cooperation agreement.
In a joint statement issued after the meeting, the two sides reiterated their intention to strengthen defense cooperation, including joint research and development and production of military equipment.
The two sides also stressed the need to achieve the goal of 30 billion U.S. dollars in bilateral trade by 2025, and to strengthen cooperation in energy and satellite navigation.
The two sides pointed out that it is necessary for the Eurasian Economic Union and India to start negotiations on a free trade agreement on goods.
Speaking to the media before his meeting with Modi, Putin said: "We consider India to be a big country, a friendly country and a security ally."
Putin ’ s visit to India is aimed at strengthening ties with India ’ s traditional allies, which are being eroded by the United States.
To counter China ’ s rise, the Quadripartite Security Dialogue (Quad), established by the United States with India, Japan and Australia, has drawn the attention of Beijing and Moscow.
During the Cold War, India had close ties with the Soviet Union, a relationship that continues to this day, described by New Delhi as a “special and privileged strategic partnership. ”
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with visiting Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday to discuss defense and trade relations between the two countries in an effort to strike a balance with the United States.
"There have been many fundamental changes and geopolitical elements in the world over the past few decades, but India's friendship with Russia remains the same," Modi said before meeting Putin.
India ’ s foreign ministry said the annual bilateral summit covered political and defense issues.
The two leaders also discussed the humanitarian crisis in Afghanistan caused by the takeover of the Afghan government by the Taliban earlier this year.
India and Russia have long had close ties, and both sides have set a goal of reaching $30 billion in bilateral trade by 2025.
Recently, however, India has drawn closer to the United States, believing that the United States is a key force against China.
India is also trying to manage its defense relations with Russia while strengthening its military ties with the United States, the sources said.
India, a major arms importer, relied heavily on the former Soviet Union for armaments during the Cold War, but now it is diversifying its procurement of arms, as well as buying US-made weapons.
During the period of former US President Trump, India signed more than $3 billion of arms purchase contracts with the United States, and the arms trade between the two countries has increased from zero in 2008 to $15 billion in 2019.
On the other hand, India's purchase of the Russian-made S-400 missile system to counter China has become a major problem in relations with the United States.
This sophisticated anti-missile system, once available, is expected to enable India to gain strategic deterrence power against China and Pakistan.
However, the United States has asked its partners not to purchase Russian-made armaments, or it may impose sanctions.
In addition, India and Russia held their first 2 + 2 meeting in New Delhi on Monday, where the two sides signed a number of cooperation agreements on "military and small arms".
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu arrived in New Delhi on Monday for a 2 + 2 meeting with Indian Foreign Minister Sujson and Defense Minister Manmohan Singh.
The 2 + 2 ministerial meeting was the first between India and Russia.
Singh tweeted after the meeting that discussions on defense cooperation between the two sides had been fruitful and that India cherished the "special strategic partnership" with Russia.
He added that the two sides have signed several agreements, contracts and protocols on small arms and military cooperation.
However, Singh and India ’ s Ministry of Defence have not issued a formal statement or press release disclosing details of the various agreements signed with Russia.
Indian media reported that one of the major agreements was the transfer of technology and local production of the Russian-made AK-203 assault rifle.
Under the agreement, India will produce more than 600,000 AK-203 assault rifles in India over the next 10 years through an Indian-Russian joint venture.
The report also said that another agreement is to extend the 10-year India-Russia military-technical cooperation agreement until 2031.

During the Cold War, India had close relations with the Soviet Union, a relationship that continues to this day, described by New Delhi as a “special and privileged strategic partnership. ”
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with visiting Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday to discuss defense and trade relations between the two countries to strike a balance with the United States.
"Over the past few decades, there have been many fundamental changes in the world, as well as various geopolitical elements, but India's friendship with Russia has always been the same," Modi said before the meeting with Putin.
India ’ s foreign ministry said the annual bilateral summit covered political and defence issues.
The two leaders also discussed the takeover of the Afghan regime by the Taliban earlier this year, which has led to a humanitarian crisis in Afghanistan.
India and Russia have long had close ties, and both sides have set a goal of reaching US $30 billion in bilateral trade by 2025.
But recently, India and the United States have drawn closer, seeing the United States as a key force in the fight against China.
India, while strengthening its military ties with the United States, is also trying to manage its defense relations with Russia.
India, a major arms importer, relied heavily on the former Soviet Union for its military supplies during the Cold War, and now buys weapons from the United States in a decentralized manner.
Under former US President Donald Trump, India signed more than US $3 billion in arms purchase contracts with the United States, and the two countries ’ armaments trade has increased from zero in 2008 to US $15 billion in 2019.
On the other hand, India ’ s purchase of the Russian-made S-400 missile system to counter China has become a major problem in relations with the United States.
This sophisticated anti-aircraft missile defense system, once available, is expected to give India the strategic deterrent power against China and Pakistan.
However, the United States has asked partners not to purchase Russian-made military equipment, or it may impose sanctions.
In addition, India and Russia held their first 2 + 2 meeting in New Delhi on Monday, where they signed a number of cooperation agreements on "military and small arms".
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu arrived in New Delhi on Monday night and held a 2 + 2 meeting with Indian Foreign Minister Igor Sujason and Defense Minister Manmohan Singh.
The Ministerial 2 + 2 meeting was the first between India and Russia.
Singh tweeted after the meeting that discussions on defence cooperation between the two sides had been fruitful and that India valued the "special strategic partnership" with Russia.
He added that the two sides had signed several agreements, contracts and protocols on small arms and military cooperation.
However, Singh and India ’ s Ministry of Defence have yet to release a formal statement or press release disclosing details of the various agreements signed with Russia.
Indian media reported that one of the major agreements was the technology transfer and local production of the Russian-made AK-203 assault rifle.
Under the agreement, India will produce more than 600,000 AK-203 assault rifles in India over the next 10 years through an Indo-Russian joint venture.
Another deal is to extend the 10-year India-Russia military-technical cooperation agreement until 2031.

An estimated 45,000 aircraft worth U.S. $2.9 trillion to be delivered by 2040.
Revealed in Cirium's new Fleet Forecast.
LONDON -- The newly released 2021 Cirium Fleet Forecast shows that around 45,000 new, more fuel-efficient aircraft will be purchased globally over the next 20 years, with an estimated $2.9 trillion in aircraft purchases.
According to the Cirium Fleet Forecast released by Ascend by Cirium, a consulting firm of aviation analytics firm Cirium, global cumulative aircraft deliveries for the next 20 years will be 4% higher than predicted a year ago by 2040.
The report outlines the positive outlook for the aviation industry and its recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic.
The COVID-19 pandemic has severely affected air travel, as well as aircraft deliveries.
Global aircraft deliveries fell by 43% - or 600 aircraft - in 2020.
Aircraft deliveries recovered somewhat in 2021, but are still 25% below 2019 levels.
Air travel is reopening as global vaccination programs become more widespread, leading to an increase of 300 aircraft deliveries in 2021 — a feat achieved when Boeing 787 was found to be problematic.
Rob Morris, Global Advisory Director, Ascend by Cirium, said: “The Cirium Fleet Forecast 2021 presents an optimistic long-term outlook for the aviation industry, which will return to a more traditional growth trajectory after 2024, although structurally different from before.
Air passenger traffic is expected to grow at an annual rate of 3.7%, so the global passenger fleet will need to increase by almost 22,000 aircraft.
“If the above projections are realized, the global passenger fleet will reach the size of about 47,200 aircraft by the end of 2040. ”
The projected delivery of new aircraft will not only meet the growing demand for air transport, but will also replace older aircraft that are less fuel efficient. "
China leads in aircraft deliveries
The number of aircraft deliveries will vary depending on the region where the airline is located, and the Asian market is expected to be the growth engine.
China is expected to lead the world with more than 6% growth in air passenger traffic – also topping the list in aircraft deliveries, accounting for 20% of the world ’ s total.
China ’ s delivery figures are significantly ahead of all other Asia-Pacific countries, which together account for 22% of the total.
North American carriers are expected to account for 20 percent, while European carriers will account for 17 percent.
The Middle East is estimated to account for 7% of the share, but because the region will deliver a large number of twin-aisle aircraft, it will account for 11% in terms of aircraft value.
Latin America, which is similar to the Middle East, will also account for 7%.
Russia and the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) accounted for 4%, and Africa accounted for 3%.
Most of the new deliveries will be single-aisle jets
The fleet forecast report shows that over the next 20 years, single-aisle jets will account for 70% of total aircraft deliveries and 55% of total delivery value.
The total value of newly delivered single-aisle jets is $1.6 trillion.
The mainstream model will still be the 150-seat aircraft, represented by the Airbus A320neo and Boeing 737 Max 8, which will account for 50% of deliveries.
Popular models with more than 180 seats include the A321 neo and the B737 Max 10, which will have an increasing share each year and will account for 40% of deliveries over the next 20 years.
Airbus and Boeing are expected to develop a new generation of single-aisle aircraft in the early to mid-2030s.
The $1.1 trillion dual-aisle aircraft market will be dominated by the B787 and A350 models, with 250-300-seat “medium ” aircraft accounting for about 65% of the total value delivered.
The large passenger aircraft market will be contested by the A350-1000 and the B777-9.
Aircraft deliveries in regional markets are expected to reach a scale of $150 billion.
About a third of them will be turboprop aircraft, based on 70-seat models.
Starting in 2030, a larger 90-seat model will enter the market.
Future new aircraft projects in the market include the MA700 from China and an expected new line of aircraft from Embraer.
Older models will be replaced by a new generation of aircraft.
It is predicted that about 80% of current passenger aircraft will be out of passenger service between 2021 and 2040.
As the airline industry begins to focus on driving down carbon emissions and focusing on sustainability, it will become increasingly important to replace these older, more fuel-efficient aircraft with new models.
Overall, in addition to several relatively new aircraft that are being phased out earlier, around 19,000 aircraft in the global passenger fleet will be phased out by the end of 2020.
According to analysis by Ascend by Cirium, the average economic life expectancy for single-aisle aircraft is 22 years and for twin-aisle aircraft is 20 years.
The number of freighters is growing: including new freighters and refitted freighters
As the global freight industry continues to perform strongly, freighter capacity (based on available tonnage kilometres) is expected to grow by 3.3% over 2019, with a projected supply of around 3,500 freighters over the next 20 years.
Of this total, it is expected that 30 per cent will be new freighters and 70 per cent will be converted from passenger aircraft.
About 1,050 new freighters are expected to be shipped, valued at $121 billion.
More online shopping during the epidemic period has promoted the development of e-commerce, and the growth of e-commerce has promoted the conversion of airliners to freighters.

A system engineer who is fluent in English and Spanish lost his call center job because of a non-standard accent.
That ’ s why three of his friends at Stanford University set up a startup and developed an app, hoping to solve the communication problems caused by accents.
According to CNN, startup Sanas is testing a self-developed AI driver that can instantly change the accent of people to solve the problem of communication.
For example, a call center worker in the Philippines can normally speak to a microphone, but a U.S. customer on the other end of the phone sounds like they ’ re from Kansas.
Sanas ’ s founders say the call center is just the beginning; according to the company ’ s website, their campaign slogan is “Speech, Reimagined. ”
Ultimately, the founders want their app to be used in a wide range of industries as well as personal communication.
They point out that the app can help doctors understand patients better, help grandkids understand what their grandparents are saying, improve movie dubbing accuracy, and help smart appliances and voice assistants understand different accents.
Sanas CEO Maxim Serebryakov is from Russia, where he met two other co-founders, Andrés Pérez Soderi and Shawn Zhang, at Stanford University.
The chief financial officer is a Venezuelan who graduated from Stanford with Seri Bureakov, and the chief technology officer, Shaun Zhang, who is from China, dropped out of school to focus on setting up Sanas.
Seriabreakov points out that people from different countries have been treated differently because of their accents. "It can be quite sad at times."
English is still the most spoken language in the world, with about 1.5 billion people speaking it, but most of them are not native speakers.
In the United States alone, millions of people speak English as their second language.
This has allowed the market for English pronunciation apps to grow, but Sanas has taken a different approach, arguing that instead of spending a lot of money or time learning to change accents, technology can help users effectively communicate what they want to say.
Sabriakov stressed that Sanas did not try to eliminate any accents or imply that one way of speaking is better than the other. “We want to make sure people don ’ t have to change their way of speaking for the sake of a position or a job. ”
We also understand that self-identity and accent are essential, and that they are inseparable. ”
Currently, Sanas ’ algorithm can be used to convert English accents in the United States, Australia, the United Kingdom, the Philippines, India and Spain, and the team plans to add more accents.
While the American accent still sounds blunt in the sample audio files provided to CNN by the Sanas team, the call center that tried the app has given positive initial feedback.
The Sanas team said they had received $5.5 million in seed funding from investors earlier this year and will continue to develop improved accent conversion technology in the future.

Russia-India coordination, balance, US-India approach?

Source: Global Times
Author: Wang Shida
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke by telephone with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the 20th to further develop the "special and privileged strategic partnership" between the two countries.
At the beginning of this month, Russia and India held an annual leaders' summit, launched the first "2 + 2" dialogue between foreign ministers and defense ministers, and agreed to strengthen cooperation and coordination on bilateral and multilateral issues, and signed up to 28 cooperation agreements.
In just two weeks, the summit had two interactions, which sent a signal that Russian-Indian relations were more special than before.
From the interaction on the 6th, Putin led a strong delegation to visit India and held the annual Russian-Indian leaders' summit.
This is Putin's second overseas visit since the outbreak of the COVID-19 epidemic, highlighting the importance he attaches to the "special and privileged strategic partnership" between the two countries.
During the visit, Russia and India held their first "2 + 2" meeting, which will help deepen mutual understanding and strengthen the special and privileged strategic partnership between the two countries.
The most important of the 28 cooperation agreements signed by Russia and India is the Agreement on Military Technical Cooperation 2021-2031.
The document will provide guidance for Russian-Indian military cooperation in the next 10 years, especially to promote joint development and production of weapons and equipment.
It can be said that the foundation for the next stage of military interaction between Russia and India has been laid.
In addition, Russia and India are also actively discussing the signing of a military logistics agreement similar to the memorandum of understanding on logistics exchange between the two countries to facilitate the use of each other's military bases.
Once signed in the future, the Russian-Indian military relations will take another step forward.
The two leaders discussed how to implement the agreement reached at the December 6 meeting, agreed to maintain regular contact on all aspects covered by the Russian-Indian “special and privileged strategic partnership ”, continue to deepen bilateral cooperation and consultation and coordination in multilateral forums, and exchange views on international stability and security issues, including the situation in the Asia-Pacific region.
Since taking office as US president at the beginning of the year, Biden has inherited and strengthened the Indo-Pacific strategy of his predecessor, Trump, and has courted India as the key to its success.
To this end, Biden has made efforts to promote the upgrading and implementation of the four-nation mechanism.
In March this year, the four-nation mechanism held its first video summit, issued a joint declaration, and established three working groups to implement the summit consensus.
In September, the four-nation mechanism held its first offline summit, reiterating the implementation of cooperation in the fields of vaccines and high-quality infrastructure, and proposing to jointly train scientific and technological talents to create a "closed loop of scientific and technological talents of the four countries".
For example, the United States has continued to deepen the "comprehensive global strategic cooperative partnership" between the United States and India.
On March 19, U.S. Defense Secretary William Austin visited India, calling the U.S.-India relationship "a key pillar of a free and open Indo-Pacific."
Under the continued cozying up of the Biden administration, India's attitude of strategic autonomy has become blurred, and it has clearly moved closer to and tilted toward the United States in implementing its foreign policy of "multi-faceted alliance."
During his visit to the United States in September, Modi said that "the relationship between the United States and India has entered a critical transition period".
In the face of the continuous promotion of the "Indo-Pacific Strategy" by the United States and the drift and deviation of India in the two strategic directions of the Indo-Pacific Ocean and the Eurasian continent, Russia is certainly alert.
As early as the Cold War, Russia and India established a relatively special strategic cooperative partnership, even reaching the level of quasi-allies.
At the end of the Cold War, Russia pushed India to join strategic designs such as the "trilateral dialogue between China, Russia and India" in an attempt to promote the establishment of a fair and multipolar world order.
Russia also sees India as an important partner in the Indian Ocean region and an important contributor to the effects of radiation in the Indian Ocean region.
To this end, Russia has taken a series of actions, Foreign Minister Lavrov and other high-level leaders directly expressed opposition to the United States using the "Indo-Pacific strategy" as a tool to contain China and Russia and create regional division.
This round of Russian-Indian strategic coordination is also the proper meaning of Russia's anti-Indo-Pacific strategy.
In particular, Russia and India signed a major defense cooperation order, began the delivery of S-400 air defense system, and will soon sign a military logistics agreement, which is conducive to consolidating defense and military cooperation between the two countries, hedging the penetration and erosion of the traditional Russian arms market by the United States in the past 10 years, and preventing India from falling into the "Indo-Pacific camp" because of increased dependence on weapons and equipment.
Therefore, Russian-Indian interaction is conducive to maintaining the relative balance between the two camps of the Eurasian continent and the Indo-Pacific Ocean, as well as to global strategic stability and peace.
(The writer is deputy director of the South Asia Institute of the Chinese Institute of Modern International Relations)

Here, there is a stage for thousands of miles (to accelerate the construction of the world's important talent center and innovation highland ③)

University of Science and Technology of China
Some members of the "Chapter 9" research team pose for photos in the laboratory.
The fourth left is Deng Yuhao, and the fifth left is Zhong Hansen.
University of Science and Technology of China
At the end of 2020, the "nine chapters" of the quantum computing prototype appeared, shocking the world.
This is the first time that Chinese scientists have realized the "superiority of quantum computing", which is regarded as a milestone breakthrough in quantum computing.
A team of scientists from the Chinese University of Science and Technology (hereinafter referred to as the Chinese University of Science and Technology), with the "post-90s" as the main body, has completed this major achievement.
The "post-90s" research on quantum computers is the epitome of the rapid growth of young talents at the Chinese University of Science and Technology.
As of November 2021, the University of Science and Technology has 533 high-level talents of various types at the national level. Among the more than 1,400 teachers, the proportion of 45 years old and below reached 74%.
Why is the "Millima" competing here?
Adhere to the "use is the best training", give young people a burden, promote growth.
Deng Yuhao, 24, is one of the first authors of the "Nine Chapters" results. In 2017, when he was in his third year of undergraduate, he accidentally read a classic paper on quantum information, and was attracted by the research prospects in this field.
"Although I am studying physics, I have not yet established a systematic knowledge of quantum information, and I have no experimental experience in related systems. I did not think that the teacher let me do such an important task." Deng Yuhao recalled, just entered his senior year, Professor Lu Chaoyang gave himself "astronomical scale quantum interference" experimental work.
This is a work based on a new concept. Deng Yuhao was originally a novice, and when he asked his brothers to teach, he also said that “there is a challenge ” and“ it is not good to say ”. “But Teacher Lu seems to be very sure, and encouraged me to study and give guidance when I encounter problems. ”
Deng Yuhao 's efforts paid off. In 2019, his paper was published in the Physical Review Letters.
At this time, Deng Yuhao, a first-year master's student, completed enough results to earn a doctorate.
Zhong Hansen, another first author of “Nine Chapters ” work, has a similar experience. In 2016, shortly after joining Lu Chaoyang ’ s research group in his third year of undergraduate, he began to do research on 12 photon entanglement.
At the time, the best result in academia was 10 photon entanglement, which was a job no one had ever dabbled in.
"Some things are not taught, to master in practice." Zhong Hansen remembers the teacher's teaching.
At the beginning of 2017, he completed the research idea, made the best comprehensive quality entanglement source at that time, and realized 12 photon entanglement on this basis. Zhong Hansen continued to explore and explore the experimental path of “Gaussian Bose Sampling ”, which is the method of“ Nine Chapters ” to achieve “the superiority of quantum computing ”.
For the 20-year-old Zhong Hansen and Deng Yuhao, building the "Nine Chapters" is an unprecedented challenge.
Although theoretically, the solution with "Gaussian Bose sampling" is expected to achieve "quantum computing superiority", but the scientific engineering faces too many unknown, they were once lost.
"This is a rare opportunity for researchers to make heavyweight research." Lu Chaoyang gave them encouragement, and drew elite soldiers from the whole group, and research resources were given priority.
As it turns out, the work of "nine chapters" is indeed a big deal: in the past year, the paper has been cited about 500 times, making it one of the highest international citations in the field of quantum information.
In October this year, the CAS team built the "Nine Chapter Two", once again refreshing the international technical level of light quantum manipulation. Zhong Hansen, 26, is an important backbone of this work.
At present, the research and development work of "Nine Chapter Three" is being carried out intensively, and Deng Yuhao took over Zhong Hansen and became an important backbone of this project.
At this time, in the field of research and development, there have been "00 after". "I will teach them good experience and continue the good tradition of the research group." Deng Yuhao told reporters.
It ’ s not just the Sun Research Group.
The Chinese University of Science and Technology adheres to the concept of "using is the best training", and promotes the growth of young people, including students.
Ten years ago, many students from the Chinese University of Science and Technology went to European and American universities for further study. Today, more and more people are staying in the school to continue their research.
The support received, the work done, is no worse than the top research groups abroad.
Build public scientific research conditions and build a good platform for young teachers to start
In 2013, Fu Binqing was hired as a special associate researcher of the School of Life Sciences of the Chinese University of Science and Technology.
Although working in a large scientific research team, but in the initial stage of research, young teachers' scientific research resources are relatively limited, facing the pressure of promotion and retention within the six-year employment period, Fu Binqing felt the pressure at first.
However, she soon settled down, including the "reassurance pill" scientific research public experimental platform.
"The scientific research public platform has rich, cutting-edge scientific instruments, and open to the whole school, everyone can queue up to apply, hourly billing." Fu Binqing told reporters, benefiting from this, his own project quickly ran up, the progress of the research was not delayed at all.
In 2018, with excellent results, in the fifth year of the assessment period, Fu Binqing successfully turned into an associate professor in the School of Life Sciences.
The young teacher grew rapidly after crossing the first kaner.
Now, Fu Binqing has set up his own laboratory, with doctoral students to do research, not only in the field of reproductive immunity, but also participated in the clinical research of the fight against COVID-19, and the relevant research results have been adopted into the treatment plan of severe COVID-19 patients.
Concentrating resources to build an open and shared "big platform" is the tradition of the Chinese University of Science and Technology.
As early as 2000, the school spent 80 million yuan to build four public experimental centers.
The school's consideration is: rather than "pepper", it is better to build a public scientific research platform.
The Chinese University of Science and Technology is mainly based on basic research in science and technology, and the demand for some cutting-edge experimental equipment and software platforms is common.
Constructing a centralized and shared public experimental platform can give full play to the utility of national resources than keeping instruments and equipment in a few task groups.
In recent years, to meet the growing demand for scientific research, the public experimental platform of the Chinese University of Science and Technology has become increasingly perfect.
At present, the school has built six public experimental centers, including physical and chemical science, life science, engineering and materials science.
At the Chinese University of Science and Technology, young teachers do not have to worry about doing research without scientific research conditions.
Each public experimental platform every year to purchase equipment, will collect the views of scientists, and then the platform expert committee to plan.
In order to run the public platform well, the school has set up professional management talents and developed a transparent and perfect management system.
Because of the convenience of sharing, professional technical services, the frequency of use of the instruments of the public experimental platform is very high, and some popular equipment is even operating 24 hours a day throughout the year, and the resources are used to the maximum extent.
Xue Tian, minister of human resources of the Chinese University of Science and Technology, told reporters that while strict requirements are put forward for young people, it is more necessary to provide sufficient guarantees so that they have a stage to fully display their talents.
Xue said that in recent years, the Chinese University of Science and Technology has explored targeted support measures according to the needs of talents at different levels and at different stages.
For example, in order to strengthen the training and support of outstanding young talents and create a new generation of academic leading talents, since 2017, the school has implemented the academic leading talents training plan, key financial support for outstanding young talents with development potential, and funded its strengthening of laboratories and team building.
"Talent first" service concept, let scientists feel at ease to do scientific research
In 2018, before returning to the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Wang Bing received a tenured teaching position at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and is a well-known young scholar in the field of geometric flow.
To create a scientific research team and settle the family, Wang Bing often needed to deal with the administrative department in the early days of his return.
Wang Bing told reporters that he was not good at communication, and that he had misunderstood the staff of the human resources department because of a certain job. But every time he went to work, the staff here were very enthusiastic and solved many real problems. "I felt their enthusiasm for serving scientific research."
In recent years, there are more and more outstanding overseas talents returning to China Science and Technology University. Xue Tian told reporters that overseas scientific researchers return to China, usually there is a period of adaptation, and the responsibility of the administrative department is to do a good job of service, to help them adapt to and fully carry out teaching and research work as soon as possible.
"Talent first" is the service concept of China Science and Technology University.
According to the tradition of the Chinese University of Science and Technology, the heads of some major administrative services departments are academic and administrative shoulders.
"These cadres work in the front line of teaching and research, understand the needs of talents at different stages, and are easy to push themselves and others when dealing with talents," Xue said.
In addition to serving as the Minister of Human Resources, Xue Tian is also the Executive Director of the Department of Life Sciences and Medicine, and has achieved outstanding research results in light signal transduction, neural circuits and visual regeneration and repair of photoreceptive neurobiology.
"The policy of personnel work is very strong, and on the premise of strictly abiding by the personnel system and principles, we strive to do our work in a practical and detailed manner, and to be more humane."
For example, if the system does not allow a certain demand, while trying to explain and gain understanding, but also actively solve specific problems for talents within the scope of the principles of the system, instead of simply holding the provisions and coldly saying 'no'. "Xue Tian said.
How to set up a team as soon as possible is a matter of great concern for overseas talents to return home.
In response to this concern, in 2012, the Chinese University of Science and Technology implemented a system of appointment of scientific researchers, encouraging the introduction of talents to recruit members on their own.
To set up a high-level scientific research team and make a weighty voice on behalf of Chinese researchers in his own field of work is the original intention of Wang Bing's return to China.
After three years of returning home, his idea is becoming a reality.
He worked with his former mentors, Chen Xiuxiong and Chen Qing, to establish the Geometry and Physics Center gradually on the right track.
After the adjustment period, Wang Bing felt more and more that returning home was the right choice: there is a strong academic atmosphere, there is a vigorous vitality, there are top smart students, and there are dedicated colleagues.
In November 2020, Wang Bing and Chen Xiuxiong made a major breakthrough in the field of differential geometry, successfully proving the two core conjectures that have been pending in the international mathematical community for more than 20 years.
“We have excellent students, the right research and communication environment, strong support from the school, and I am confident in the future of the team. ”
King told reporters.
Jiang Yi, executive deputy secretary of the Party Committee of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said that the talent work of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has a fine tradition.
In recent years, in order to help talents grow and develop in an all-round way, the school has built an academic honor system, and the talent team, including young talents, has endogenous motivation throughout the academic life cycle.
As long as it is a thousand miles, you can find the stage here.

What we want you to know is
Russia is actively engaged in the world's two largest countries with the largest population, and it can be said that it is very serious business, as well as leading Russia's foreign policy, so as not to allow the United States to be ahead of the United States, but also to hinder the rise of China.
And India, in the big countries still have strategic autonomy, is also a winner.
Putin visits India for first time in six months, "Putin meeting" strengthens Russian-Indian relations
On December 6, the New York Times reported that Russian President Vladimir Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi held their 21st summit in India, reaffirming the “special and privileged strategic partnership ” between India and Russia and witnessing the signing of 28 agreements and memorandums of understanding.
The defence agreement was signed by Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, Defence Minister Sergey Shoigu, and Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh after a "2 + 2" meeting.
According to the report, the new defense agreement, which includes the potential US sanctions risk S-400 surface-to-air missile defense system, amounted to $5.4 billion. In 2020, the Trump administration imposed sanctions on Turkey for purchasing the weapon from Russia.
Indian Deputy Foreign Minister Harsh Shringla said at a press conference after the summit: "The delivery of the S-400 missile defense system has started and will continue."
It is important to note that both we and Russia have an independent foreign policy. ”
The 28 agreements and MOUs mentioned above cover trade, energy, technology, intellectual property, space, geological exploration, cultural exchanges and education.
According to the list released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, nine of the agreements and memorandums signed are of an official nature, including: the 2021-2031 Military Technology Cooperation Agreement, the roadmap for cooperation in science, technology and innovation, and the space technology protection agreement; the rest are memorandums between industries, companies or academic institutions.
India and Russia have set a goal of raising bilateral trade to $30 billion by 2025, as well as broader inter-regional cooperation between the Russian Far East and Indian provinces.
This time Russia and India deepen relations, it is important to counter the United States' active deployment in the Indo-Pacific region.
Among them is Joe Biden, a member of the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue at the heart of Indo-Pacific foreign policy: India.
Not only can Russia pull India ’ s important partner, but it also proves that Russia has other “good friends ” in the international community in addition to China at a time of tension with most Western countries and international isolation.
In addition, India is still under pressure from the United States to buy arms from Russia, on the one hand, to show its foreign policy autonomy and diversification, India in the procurement of weapons options, but also to try to achieve a balance in the United States, India, Russia triangle relations.
After all, since the outbreak of the border conflict between India and India in mid-2020, there has been a trend for India and the United States to get closer and closer.
It also includes the gradual deepening of the "quartet security dialogue."
Russia has a greater influence than the United States in coordinating border conflicts between China and India.
For example, in September 2021, the foreign ministers of China and India discussed border issues in Moscow, Russia, and issued a joint statement.
In addition, according to a report by the Russian News Agency on December 15, Russian presidential assistant Yuri Ushakov said: "Putin and Xi agreed to continue to exchange views on the 'Russia-India-China cooperation model' in order to try to hold the next trilateral summit within the framework of this model in the future."
US-Russia Video Summit: Biden, Putin Discuss "Ukraine Issue"
On December 7, US President Joe Biden and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a video summit, which was also the second time the two met in Geneva, Switzerland, in June this year.
According to a White House press release, the two sides discussed a number of US-Russian issues in the video.
During the meeting, Biden told Russia that the United States and its European allies have expressed strong concern about its actions in Ukraine.
He made it clear to Putin that the United States and its allies would respond economically or otherwise to an increase in military activity.
He also reiterated U.S. support for Ukraine ’ s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and called for a return to foreign interaction to reduce tensions.
The two sides also discussed the U.S.-Russia Dialogue on Strategic Stability, cyber-ransomware attacks, and cooperation on regional issues, such as Iran.
The Kremlin said in a statement after the meeting that Putin stressed that responsibility should not be transferred to Russia, all stemming from NATO ’ s dangerous intentions to conquer Ukrainian territory and establish military potential sites on the Russian-Ukrainian border.
Putin asked Biden to provide legally binding security guarantees against NATO ’ s eastward expansion and the deployment of offensive weapons systems in Russia ’ s neighbors.
But White House national security adviser Jake Sullivan told reporters that Biden made no promises or concessions to Putin ’ s demands, including not allowing Ukraine to join NATO and reducing U.S. forces in the region.
Speaking at a Council on Foreign Relations event on December 17, Sullivan said in response to Putin ’ s request: “The United States is ready to start a dialogue with Russia, and we will raise and discuss issues of concern to us. ”
In addition, according to the "Mist Valley Crystal Policy", a recent CNN "Wall Street Journal report, the Biden administration, in addition to maneuvering with Russia at the negotiating table, on the other hand, is also considering increasing military support for Ukraine.
Military support projects under consideration include Mi-17 helicopters and Stinger surface-to-air missiles.
However, a White House spokesman declined to discuss details of military support for Ukraine.
Putin, Xi Jinping Video Summit to Strengthen Bilateral Relations Against the West
Following the US-Russia Video Summit on December 7, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin held an hour-long video summit on December 15 to discuss a wide range of issues between China and Russia.
According to the BBC, the video summit is the 37th meeting of the leaders of China and Russia since 2013, and the frequent meeting reflects the unusual relationship between China and Russia.

Last year, the UAE set up a "remote work visa" to allow people who work online for overseas companies and earn more than 3,500 US dollars a month to live for one year.
This means that even if they do not work in the UAE, as long as they are “profitable talents ”, they can also settle in the UAE.
TOKYO -- The aging of young children, including the young population of developing countries, is expected to gradually decline in the near future, which will make the world's competition for talent even more fierce.
But if immigrants stop coming, how will the world compete for talent?
The United Arab Emirates announced in March last year the creation of a "remote work visa" for people working for foreign businesses online.
The scheme allows people employed by overseas companies with a monthly salary of more than US $3,500 (about S $4,720) to live in the UAE for one year.
This means that even if they do not work in the UAE, as long as they are “profitable talents ”, they can also settle in the UAE.
Countries like Estonia have similar visas.
According to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), “a succession of countries are trying to make themselves a centre of technological innovation through ‘ digital nomad ’ visas. ”
High-income immigrants will become good consumers in the country, thus promoting economic development.
In the future, it may also be rooted in local society and contribute to the country of residence.
There ’ s no such thing as “immigration = cheap labor. ”
The fight for immigration is not a temporary phenomenon under the coronavirus epidemic.
The global phenomenon of childlessness is accelerating, and the demographic explosion that quadrupled the world ’ s population in the 20th century will soon end.
It is expected that the global population will begin to decline after the middle of this century at the earliest.
India ’ s population aged 15 to 29 will peak in 2025.
China's population will also decline by about 20% in the next 30 years, and the world's labor resources will be exhausted.
By 2020, the number of people living outside their home country will reach 280 million.
Many people migrate to rich countries in order to make a living.
It is predicted that the UK population will increase by 9% by 2050, but without immigration, the population will be reduced by 0.3%.
The outbreak has led to border closures, giving a sense of the future of reduced immigration.
Border closures caused by the epidemic give a preview of the future of reduced migration.
Prior to the outbreak, Australia had a net inflow of 240,000 migrants per year.
As a result of restrictions on entry, the population growth rate fell to 0.1 per cent, down sharply from 1.3 per cent in the previous year.
Some countries are trying to get rid of their dependence on immigrants.
Immigrants in New Zealand make up less than 30% of the country ’ s population.
Kiwifruit, a specialty of the country, needs to be harvested one by one according to its maturity, but Wilson of the New Zealand Institute of Economic Research pointed out that "such jobs have always relied on cheap labor, causing mechanization to stagnate."
In May last year, the New Zealand government issued a "new immigration policy" to adjust immigration policy from scratch, proposing a policy of restricting the entry of low-wage workers and valuing high-skilled workers.
However, in the digital age, there are ways of working across borders, even if migrants are reluctant to come.
Every weekday, Jodari (22), who lives in India, opens his computer at home and logs into the company ’ s system.
She has just graduated from the prestigious Indian Institute of Technology, working for Diverta, a Japanese technology company.
The company's president, Kenta Kato, said that it will not be able to acquire talented people in the future if the barriers to national borders are not removed.
"As long as you have the skills, you can choose which country to work in," said Kanner, an international political scholar.
"In countries with declining populations, the market will shrink," he said.
Countries that have access to young talent can stay innovative and dynamic. ”

(Ming Pao News) Pakistan's military confirmed on Wednesday (5) that it is buying multi-purpose J-10C fighters from China in response to the introduction of French Rafale fighters by the Indian Air Force. The J-10C is the main equipment of the People's Liberation Army Air Force, and once a deal is reached, it will be the most advanced fighter aircraft exported by China in history and will also be the Pakistan Air Force's strongest fighter.
It has been rumored that the number of J-10Cs exported to Pakistan is 35 to 40, and the price is about 1.5 billion US dollars (about 11.7 billion Hong Kong dollars).
Speaking at a press conference, Maj. Gen. Babar Iftikhar, a spokesman for Pakistan ’ s army, said: “This is a step to upgrade our air force and get the best possible technology because we know what the other side (India) is getting. ”
"Our opponents are using one excuse after another to keep buying the latest equipment," Iftihal warned.
Any conventional imbalance in the region is dangerous, "and" it will lead us into a race to buy more equipment. "
It is expected to purchase more than 30 aircraft, each about $390 million.
This is the first time the Pakistani military has made it clear that it is buying Chinese J-10s, but Iftihar did not say how many will be purchased.
China has not commented on this.
According to the military self-media "white wolf view of the world" on December 23 last year, since the service in 2006, the Chinese Air Force has been equipped with nearly 500 J-10C, becoming the Chinese Air Force's largest number of fighter aircraft.
Its foreign trade version of the J-10CE is also of interest to many countries, including Ukraine and "Pakistan Railway" (the nickname of the mainland people for Pakistan), Pakistan is ready to sign with China 35 to 40 aircraft, worth about 1.5 billion US dollars, each less than 50 million US dollars (about 390 million Hong Kong dollars).
"China Times" reported that this arms case is China's long-awaited defense deal, from the beginning of the J-10A until the J-10C deal, in addition to the Indian purchase of wind, J-10C successfully replaced the turbofan -10 vector thrust engine and decided to match the PL-15 long-range air-to-air missile, is Pakistan willing to finalize the deal two key factors.
Low-price export of Huamou real war inspection J-10C
Another eye-catching item is the price, which was first reported at the 2018 Zhuhai Airshow at $70 million per aircraft, and is now about $50 million.
China is willing to sell to Pakistan at such a low price, in addition to friendly relations, but also considering that the India-Pakistan border may be the only battlefield that can allow the J-10C to have a combat test.
The report also said that last year, China and Pakistan agreed to the export of the Perila-15 (PL-15) long-range air-to-air missile, in addition to the use of the Pakistan Dragon Block 3, can also be equipped with the newly purchased J-10C.
It is believed that after importing the J-10C, its active phased array radar plus the long-range air-to-air missile, as long as it grasps the opportunity and uses it properly, it has the opportunity to defeat the fighter jet.
In 2015, India announced the purchase of 36 French fighter aircraft, worth US $8 billion (about HK $62.4 billion), with a unit price of nearly US $300 million (about HK $2.3 billion).
Pakistan: March National Day parade will see J-10 formation

The 25 J-10Cs are believed to be the first aircraft to be delivered to Pakistan.

San Francisco Startup Permanently Implemented Employees: Increased Efficiency
San Francisco unicorn startup Bolt announces new employee benefits: a permanent four-day workweek.
The e-commerce development company trialed the system last fall, and the results were very positive.
“I can ’ t think of a better way to run this company, ” said Ryan Breslow, founder and CEO.
Breslow said that with the implementation of the program, the company has increased productivity, streamlined workflows, and employees are happy.
At the end of the three-month pilot program, Bolt conducted an opinion survey and 94% of employees and 91% of management wanted the program to continue.
In addition, 84% of employees reported increased productivity, 86% reported increased productivity, and 84% found a better work-life balance.
Breslow noted that the idea is not to increase the number of hours employees work, but to increase their productivity.
After the implementation of the plan, the concentration of employees during working hours has increased significantly.
“Many companies are like ‘ theater ’ where people care more about appearances than the work itself, so there are endless meetings and endless reports, ” Breslow added.
In this case, it is impossible to exclude noise from the core of the problem. "
With 550 full-time employees, Bolt is one of the few companies in the United States to implement a four-day workweek.
Supporters of the system hope that this approach will be adopted by more businesses, especially at a time when the focus is on attracting and retaining employees.
Millions of people in the United States have quit their jobs in the Great Resignation over the past few months, a record 4.5 million last November alone.
Joe O ’ Connor, Global Experiment Program Manager at 4 Day Week Global, said: “The companies we ’ ve helped transition to a four-day week say it ’ s significantly broadened the pool of potential candidates. ”
In fact, in July last year, Members of the United States introduced a bill to reduce the working week from the standard 40 hours to 32 hours, but no progress has been made.
The four-day work week is not applicable to all businesses, because the business model of each company is different.
“It should be seen as a starting point for how companies can work smarter and more efficiently, ” O ’ Connor said.

KFC "blind box" in the mainland, some people throw 10,000 yuan to buy food, and the Consumer Association strongly criticized: when boycotting

Recently, KFC and POP MART, a blind box seller, launched the “DIMOO co-branded blind box package ”, which immediately set off a rush to buy.
In order to collect a full set of blind box dolls, some consumers are willing to spend tens of thousands of yuan to buy a set meal, and there is also a "food substitute" service on the Internet.
In this regard, the China Consumer Association criticized KFC for using limited edition blind box sales methods to induce and connive consumers to irrationally purchase food packages, which should be resisted.
Comprehensive mainland media reported that DIMOO, a character jointly named with KFC, is one of the most popular IP (Intellectual Property) of POP MART.
Starting from the 4th of this month, you can get a random “KFC × DIMOO ” limited series doll by purchasing a designated package of 99 yuan (RMB, the same below).
This series of blind box set of 6, plus 1 hidden doll.
A total of 263,880 copies were sold in mainland stores.
The probability of hidden money is 1: 72, which is very rare.
The price of the hidden doll has risen 12 times.
Consumers want to collect a whole set of dolls, at least 594 yuan.
Online photos show that there is a blind box "player" in order to draw the hidden money, a single breath throw 10,494 yuan, buy 106 sets of packages.
Another person admitted that the 99 yuan package seems to be expensive, but the blind box of a DIMOO on the market is at least 69 yuan.
Today's joint activities, in addition to getting dolls and eating fried chicken, are very cost-effective.

In view of the blind box fever in recent years, and the famous IP blessing, the series of blind box packages were coaxed and robbed once launched, and a box is hard to find.
On the second-hand platform, the regular doll is also the cheapest selling 70 yuan, and the price of a full set of 6 sold is between 600 yuan and 800 yuan.
As for the most scarce hidden funds, the maximum has been fired to 800 yuan, which is 8 times higher than the "original price"; compared with the general DIMOO doll on the market, the asking price of 69 yuan has soared nearly 12 times.
Blind box dolls are hot in the second-hand platform, and the "professional food" service has also come with it.
On the Internet, "professional food, never waste", "blind box for you, fat for me" and other messages are endless, and even some netizens began to take orders across provinces.
Inducing irrational shopping is contrary to public order, morality and the spirit of the law.
On Wednesday (12), the Chinese Consumer Association issued an article "Using the" blind box "to induce excessive consumption of food, when boycotting!", saying that normal profit promotion not only enables merchants to increase sales, but also allows consumers to get affordable, which is understandable.
However, KFC as a catering company, the use of limited edition blind box sales is to stimulate consumption by means of "hunger marketing", which is easy to lead consumers to impulsively consume in order to obtain limited edition blind boxes, and cause unnecessary food waste due to excessive purchases.

In April last year, the "Anti-Food Waste Law" was officially implemented, which clearly requires catering service operators to consciously resist food waste, prompt consumers to consume moderately, and take measures to prevent consumer waste if necessary; and must not induce or mislead consumers to overspend, resulting in food waste.
The Consumer Association believes that KFC, as a food operator, uses limited edition blind box sales methods to induce and condone consumers to irrationally purchase food packages, which is contrary to public order and morality and the spirit of the law.
In addition, we advocate consumers to take a prudent view of their own consumption needs, carry out scientific and rational consumption activities, and jointly resist blind, impulsive, excessive consumption and other bad consumption behaviors.

Smart Living
Smart care products are widely available in various markets, such as screening the risk of 28 diseases of the elderly through AI artificial intelligence technology, including various eye diseases, diabetes, high blood pressure, coronary heart disease, Parkinson ’ s disease and other diseases.
At present, this solution is used in more than 30 triple-A hospitals in China.
In Hong Kong, Healfie is a mobile app that monitors and manages macular lesions. The aim is to help users and their families pay attention to and face up to this type of eye disease.
In addition, the research team of the Department of Biomedical Engineering of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University has developed a simple and easy-to-use “Artificial Intelligence Assessment System for Knee Arthritis ” to identify high-risk patients, so that they can reverse their condition in golden time, reduce joint degeneration, and relieve the pain of surgery, thereby relieving the pressure on the public health care system.
The term "Gerontechnology" has also been translated into "Elderly Technology" or "Elderly Technology".
The International Society of Gerontechnology (ISG) defines the fields of gerontology as health, housing, mobility, communication, leisure and work. Every industry should find room for development and innovation in the field of gerontology.
Intelligent Home Rehabilitation System, the application of computer graphics and image processing technology, rehabilitation treatment can be integrated with the remote home care system, tele-rehabilitation software or platform allows the elderly to carry out rehabilitation at home, and real-time online communication, to achieve the effect of consultation and rehabilitation, reducing the need for elderly to travel to and from home. With the time, cost and manpower of the hospital, we also provide a variety of rehabilitation projects to choose from.
Ambient Assisted Living (AAL), the development of smart home, smart living technology and products, allowing the elderly to spend their later years at home in a familiar environment. In recent years, Europe has further expanded to the development of environmentally assisted living technology. In a reactive environment, it is possible to analyze data, make decisions, take action, and so on.
Intelligent Mobility Assisted Devices (Mobility) is one of the basic conditions for the elderly to enjoy a high-quality, independent and autonomous elderly life.
It refers not only to the physical mobility of the elderly, but also to the ability to travel on their own to the place they want to reach.
Senior-Friendly Communication Devices And Online Social Network is a communication platform and social network developed for the elderly to provide learning, social, activities, travel and other services to enhance participation in the community, as well as life support assistance.
Companion Robot For Older Adults (Companion Robot For Older Adults), various service robots integrate into human life with different roles.
The development of many robot pets and robot dolls can interact with the elderly, which really helps to alleviate the psychological loneliness of the elderly and feel the value of being needed again.
Interactive Fun Technology for Older Adults is an interactive entertainment technology for the elderly. It is designed for the elderly 's past experience, physiology and cognitive ability. It enables the elderly to continue their mental activity and provide appropriate sensory stimulation from interactive entertainment to reduce the risk of dementia.
The application of smart technology to the life and care of the elderly is an important opportunity in the industry. From the upstream technology industry, to the midstream life industry, to the downstream service providers, it can also enhance the image of professional caregivers and relieve the pressure of family caregivers.
With the maturity of AI (artificial intelligence) technology, coupled with big data and machine deep learning, AI has been widely used in the financial and medical fields.
In the retirement market, smart robot banking can now be used to assist in retirement planning, and AI and the Internet of Things can be used to improve health management and long-term care needs.
In addition, there are currently insufficient health care personnel and uneven distribution of medical resources around the world, and users ’ health risks are predicted through the Internet of Things and mobile devices.
It can help doctors make more accurate diagnosis and treatment from a large number of medical records; help the elderly to live independently through automated means of transportation, such as preparing meals, assisting in changing clothes, and maintaining their social participation; and track the physical condition and activity of the elderly through mobile devices to ensure the physical condition of the elderly and provide immediate emergency medical assistance.

Dr. Kuo Fu-xuan, chief physician of the Senior Medical Center of Taichung Veterans General Hospital, said that the main cause of Parkinson ’ s disease is the brain ’ s “meso-melanin ” and“ basal nucleus ” related to the degeneration of the neurons that produce dopamine.
The common age of onset is 50-60 years old, and the average age of diagnosis is about 60 years old; the incidence rate of over 65 years old is about 1-2%.
Dr. Guo Fuxuan pointed out that in the case of primary Parkinson ’ s disease, the most important symptom will occur in the movement performance, the patient will experience “static tremor ”, and the hand will involuntarily tremble, trembling about 3-5 times per second.
In addition, there will be walking, slow movement and other symptoms, as well as expressionless, talking quietly and so on.
Many people can not distinguish between Parkinson's disease and stroke caused by neurological symptoms, Dr. Guo Fuxuan said that the stroke will have a very clear time, such as the night before sleep when the state is normal, the next morning but found that half of the body is paralyzed and powerless, and Parkinson's disease mainly by action signs are not the same.
Stiffness in the body is also a possible symptom of Parkinson ’ s disease. How to distinguish it from the 50 shoulder? Dr. Guo said that the 50 shoulder is usually accompanied by shoulder pain and limited movement of the shoulder joints.
The stiffness symptoms of Parkinson ’ s disease are not limited to the shoulders, but are systemic stiffness or shaking of the hands.
Dr. Kuo recommends that if you do not know what kind of medical assistance you should seek, you should first go to the family medicine, neurology, and senior medicine departments to get a preliminary diagnosis and clarify the problem.
How long does Parkinson ’ s disease last?
Could there be a combination of "dementia"?
Dr. Guo Fuxuan explained that the course of Parkinson ’ s disease is very slow, from the onset of the disease to the bed, the interval may be 10-20 years.
In general, the progression of Parkinson ’ s disease can be divided into the following 5 stages (Hoehn and Yahr Stage):
Stage 1: Symptoms mainly affect one side of the body (such as tremor, stiffness) and can walk.
Stage 2: Symptoms affect both sides of the body without affecting balance.
Stage 3: The “middle axis ” of the body is affected and the balance system begins to have problems.
Patients may have difficulty walking and fall easily.
Stage 4: The disability becomes serious, although you can still walk or stand, but you need to help with your daily life.
Stage 5: Patients need to stay in bed or in a wheelchair for a long time, unable to walk on their own.
Dr. Guo said that late Parkinson ’ s disease is indeed easy to combine dementia with other mental illnesses.
However, if you have cognitive impairment such as memory decline and mistaken recognition in the first 1-2 years before the occurrence of static tremor, mask face and other symptoms, you should consider whether it is caused by other diseases.
Can Parkinson ’ s only take medication? What about switching phenomenon and ADHD?
Dr. Guo Fu Xuan explained that the general primary Parkinson ’ s disease, controlled by drugs, has a good treatment effect, and most patients ’ symptoms such as shaking hands and walking slowly can be significantly improved.
However, after more than 5-7 years of treatment, the effect may gradually shorten, causing the "switch phenomenon" of the patient to become obvious, and further adjustment of the drug is required.
Dr. Guo Fuxuan pointed out that one of the main treatments for Parkinson ’ s disease is supplementing the brain with “left dopamine ”, which is used in younger patients and is prone to“ ADHD ” problems, that is, involuntary movements caused by fluctuations in drug concentration.
Therefore, the treatment of Parkinson ’ s disease must evaluate conditions such as age and give appropriate medication in order to achieve good symptom control.
Other effective treatments include dopamine receptors, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and anti-acetylcholine.
Dr. Guo Fuxuan said that with the growth of Parkinson's disease, the "switch phenomenon" may increase with it. On the other hand, if the drug concentration fluctuates too much, it is easy to have side effects such as ADHD.
In addition to the adjustment of medication, some patients have been evaluated for the surgical treatment of "deep brain stimulation".
However, if there have been cognitive dysfunction, depression and dementia and other diseases, it is not recommended to hastily open the knife, so as not to worsen the related symptoms.
Is there a way to prevent Parkinson ’ s disease?
Is Tai Chi the most effective?
Dr. Kuo emphasizes that there is no clear way to prevent primary Parkinson's disease, but "secondary" causes of Parkinson's disease, such as basal nuclei caused by stroke, melanoid damage to the brain, the use of specific drugs to destroy the brain neurons, and frequent exposure to pesticides to metals such as manganese and copper, are possible risk factors for secondary Parkinson's disease.
In the event of Parkinson ’ s disease, in addition to regular medication, you can also improve your movement through exercise and activity. Dr. Guo suggested that patients with Parkinson ’ s disease can perform aerobic exercise, combined with rehabilitation to train their sense of balance, which can improve static tremor, hand shake and other problems.
There is also research evidence that "tai chi" can effectively improve the movement symptoms of Parkinson's disease, is one of the methods of exercise that can be considered.
People with Parkinson ’ s disease often have trouble starting. Dr. Guo said that in addition to exercise and rehabilitation, you can also use a laser walking machine, walking stick or walking stick to help improve the starting and movement of patients.
Consult a senior medical or neurologist before using an assistive device.

To build a man who will always love me, from Frankenstein to Science Lovers.
2022 / 1 / 22 10: 34 (Updated on 1 / 22 11: 20)
