British author Jeanette Winterson pays tribute to the science fiction classic "Frankenstein" 200 years ago with "Science Lovers".
The new classic culture invites two domestic science fiction writers Gao Yifeng (author of "2069") and Lin Xinhui (author of "Flawed Man") to talk, and the Central News Agency is authorized to publish the wonderful content of the talk, and share with you the common desire behind the strange man and his lover.
Gao Yifeng:
The year before last, I opened a science fiction reading and commentary course at the Institute of Interdisciplinary Literature at Beijing Arts University. The first book was “Frankenstein ” in 1818.
Before I was ready to read Science Lovers, all I had in mind was Mary Shelley ’ s Frankenstein, and the discussions I had with my fellow students at the Institute at that time.
As far as I ’ m concerned, Science Lovers started with the name.
When you look at the cover, you can see that the kiss in the middle is changed from the ken in the middle of Frankenstein to the kiss, and FranKISSstein becomes the new novel name.
Janet Winterson, a modern, powerful female thinker, uses this kiss to deconstruct Mary Shelley ’ s Frankenstein 200 years ago.
Frankenstein is not the name of the monster, but the name of the scientist who invented the weirdo.
The first time I read this novel, I found it very challenging - if you haven't read Frankenstein, you may not know why the author wrote an 1816 story first, and then through the story of Mary, to create a near-future science fiction story.
In this near-future story, frame another story where Mary Shelley meets her own character.
It has 3 very deep levels, which started with Frankenstein.
Because The Frankenstein of 1818 is the way to write a “framing novel ” — it uses a story with a narrator in it, and then tells you that the narrator has the next story.
In "Frankenstein" there is a nautical adventurer, in the snow and ice to see the scientist chasing the weirdo, rescued him, and began to tell the whole story.
"Science Lovers" has been paying tribute to Mary Shelley from the frame structure!
Science fiction writer Gao Yifeng said that "Science Lovers" changed the ken in Frankenstein to kiss, and used the kiss to deconstruct "Frankenstein" 200 years ago. (New Classic Culture provided)
The 19th century is a very patriarchal era, Mary this important writer experienced a complicated and hard life, eloped with Shelley, miscarried several times, but she and Shelley two people have always loved, very close to the theme of this: to build a person who loves me.
Why do we want to create a strange person out? It is actually as a human lust.
Why create a weirdo ’ s lover after creating a weirdo? It ’ s because the weirdo has an selfish desire.
The author is debating this.
As a woman, Janet Winterson pays homage to Mary Shelley's Frankenstein as she contemplates the Old Testament descending from the Bible.
What was Adam ’ s function in the Garden of Eden in Genesis?
The first work of “he ” is to name creatures and even take out a rib to create women. Why do men create women?
The whole novel starts with the name, and she ’ s making fun of it all — I think it ’ s a very beautiful gesture.
There are many naming attempts in the novel: First, the scientist / creator Victor Frankenstein (Victor Frankenstein) becomes Victor Stein (Victor Stein), and he and a transgender man named Ry Shelley (Ry Shelley) have developed a love that seems desegregated.
The author also uses a lot of naming skills for many people around him, such as Ron Lord (Ron Lord) is the reverse of the name Lord Byron.
Lord is the Lord of the Christian faith. This self-proclaimed character of the same name is the maker of sex robots in the near-future world.
This new creator, Longen, has created a female sex robot that can meet men - it is really possible to build a person who only loves me? Such a modern, sci-fi scientific lover, in the novel the author pushed farther - Longen Lord even thought: Is there a way for me to build sex robots for priests and priests?
This can also solve the problem of pedophilia in all priests.
In "Mythical Tales", Prometheus molded the clay man in the form of a god, and Athena injected the soul (wisdom) into man.
The male Creator created the human form, but the female God gave it to the inside.
This is in contrast to the “story of faith, ” in which Jehovah created Adam, who, as the Creator, split up another man, Eve.
This is the story of an "artificial man" and a "human being".
There are subtle differences and reflections between the two.
This process of creation has become something that the author has to resist and confront as a female thinker.
So when I read it, there will always be a strange, as a heterosexual, male perspective, the back will suddenly cool, not sure if she is accusing me?
Lin Xinhui:
I found that creating science fiction and gender attention, the two things seem inseparable.
When I started writing science fiction, I wrote a short story, "Hotel California," which, as everyone knows, refers to the Eagles' classic song.
I appropriated the lyrics to create, in the story reverse write "Eve was born from a rib of Adam" myth: the heroine in the novel is unknown, do not know whether she is human or biotic, she uses the length of the ribs to measure the human male protagonist, the male protagonist is instead deconstructed as a component of the rib.
The woman turned and used the rib to disassemble the man around her.
This is what I wanted to do when I first wrote science fiction.
Intentionally or not, I felt from the beginning that science fiction should be gender, it must be related to gender, why do I have this inexplicable intuition?
Many science fiction works, both ancient and modern, put women in non-human roles.
For example, Rachel in "Blade Runner" is a biotic, and the operating system for falling in love with the human male protagonist in "Cloud Lover" is also set to be female.
The robot, Sophia, who is considered a citizen in the real world, is also a girl.
Non-human beings are always assigned a female position, and in these stories, the protagonists are always men, and they are all humans.
Why isn ’ t there a sci-fi story to break this structure? Sci-fi is preset to be a male story from the start?
But in retrospect, today ’ s Science Lovers pays homage to Mary Shelley ’ s Frankenstein, which is considered the first science fiction novel ever written by a woman.
Echoing the deconstruction that Teacher Yifeng just talked about, the role of transgender doctor Rui brought out a lot of gender thinking, and a lot of female thinking is concentrated in the story line of Mary Shelley's history in 1816, the women's movement has just begun to flourish, not to mention Mary Wollstonecraft, the mother of the first wave of feminism advocates.
Is “knowledge ” male or female?
There is a dialogue that women seem to bring disaster to the world, which Byron said: women are red face evil water.
If Pandora hadn ’ t opened that box, many of our things would have been less painful.
And Mary Shelley replied to him that if we didn ’ t hurt, it wouldn ’ t be human, because machines don ’ t hurt.
She said, “Does knowledge cause pain? ”
Or is the knowledge that women bring to make us human?
In this near-future storyline, Janet Winterson uses the role of Rui to bring out a problem of mind-matter dualism that we are still debating.
Our understanding of transgender may be that his body and his soul want to reach another state of harmony, not that he was not reconciled, but that he wanted to change.
For example, she was originally a biological woman and wanted to become a so-called "complete male".
The transgender doctor in the book, he did not become a so-called complete boy, his upper half is male, the lower half is female, but he likes the state: a soul lives in two bodies, he is both male and female, and then he is very comfortable in this state.
(New Classical Culture Provided)
Rui ’ s relationship with Vito thus has an undefinable ambiguity, which challenges the state of men and women in the era of 1816.
The love story of Ray and Victor is difficult to define as gay or heterosexual, which can be said to be a state of desegregation.
And the state of sexualization also echoes the world that Vito wants to create — the human consciousness is uploaded to the cloud, without the bondage of the body.
Without the body, there is no label: there is no label for skin color, and there is no label for gender.
In fact, Victor also wants to create a new human, just as Frankenstein in Frankenstein wants to create a creature.
There is a scene in the novel that is super scary: Ray opens the door and sees a lot of hands crawling around on the ground, which is very creepy.
This section reflects that Victor wants to create a new human body, and this human body can have its own will and drive itself? This part corresponds to "Frankenstein", whether the creature can drive its own will and body.
"Creation" is "life", and the back of "life" is actually talking about "death".
You want to bring the dead body back to life, you want to use technology to create eternal life, you want to upload consciousness to the brain, anyway, as long as you are conscious, you will live forever.
Vito said that at this stage, we are very comfortable with all kinds of life technology, such as when we are only pregnant, the mother's body will be subjected to various invasive tests: to see if your fetal position is correct, the sex of the fetus, whether it is so-called "normal health", and to preserve embryos, frozen eggs and other technologies... And...
In contrast, we have been vocal about technology ’ s desire to end death, perpetuate death, or immortality as a major moral issue.
Why are we optimistic about "life" and so afraid of "death"? Don't want to talk about it, don't want to imagine technology intervening in its world.
Gao Yifeng:
In the novel, page 174, a very simple sentence is mentioned: "So, Vidor, non-living forms of life, because their forms are purer, closer to the essence of love than we are?"
The story of the transgender doctor Rui, his body is neither a man nor a woman, such a body is more aware of love?
Absolutely fully tested Janet, with a classical, Gothic romance, to talk about the love story of Mary and Shelley. Mary's love is completely gender-neutral, she really loves Shelley the poet.
She loved that no matter how many children she had and how many times she lost, even if I was crazy, even if I did not know whether I could still have the next life in the future, whether the function of a woman given to me by the Bible or mythology could be achieved, I was willing to love you.
In "Science Lovers", Janet constantly probed this point through many characters, constantly asking: Is it possible in the world to create a person who loves me that way through a way like "Frankenstein"?
Want to create a person like this, even if it is not a living body, even if it does not have any gender to test, even if it is a kind of sex robot we can not predict, can it really have love?
Claire is a very old-fashioned sex robot.
Does such love exist?
At the heart of the book is its subtitle: a love story.
Beyond the gender we have to face, or the various discussions of organic and inorganic life, Janet Winterson is asking the same question she wanted to ask two hundred years ago under such complicated and highly literary writing.
I love Frankenstein so much that when someone challenges me, I think, "Okay, I see what you can write."
"Science Lovers" actually carried "Frankenstein".
Not only did he write about the monsters created by Frankenstein, but he also wrote about the love of Mary Shelley.
I think this is a great place.
Lin Xinhui:
When it comes to “love ”, I think a lot of discussion is about what“ reality ” is.
We all know that love is between two people, and the most basic consensus is "what is the reality we all recognize."
When both parties have a common understanding of "where the reality is going", there is the beginning of the "relationship".
Science fiction writer Lin Xinhui (middle) says that every chapter of Science Lovers begins with "What is reality?" (courtesy of New Classic Culture)
Every chapter of Science Lovers begins with “what is reality ” — reality is soluble in water, reality is the present, reality cannot withstand excessive human beings.
These inquiries about reality, on the one hand, are similar in the form of the novel and the "trans" of the transgender, which constantly appears in different chapters, a bit like the role of the past and the soul, or the reunion of the afterlife, or the feeling of the same soul into different bodies.
On the other hand, it is rooted in its sub-label: the love story.
But in the end, Rui and Victor are not together in Science Lovers.
Why can't they be together? Because their perception of "reality" is different - Rui's perception is "reality is the body", our love is based on the body; but Victor told him that sex does not have to be achieved by the body, he said that the perception of receptors in the brain everywhere, even a "brain in a vat" (brain in a vat), can still have sexual love. Feeling.
Even Victor would say that reality is an emergent: it is because your brain thinks that it exists, and there is no direct causal relationship between this reality and your nervous system (such as what structure creates what reality).
So that reality cannot be proved as a reality.
This inference, even Vito said, has entered a state of Buddhism.
All in all, Vito and Ri think differently about reality, so although they love each other very much, they can ’ t be together in the end.
This also leaves a lot of suspense, because we don ’ t know what happened to Vito.
There are no quotation marks in this book – many foreign readers are scolding it.
But the fact that there are no quotes is still functional in the end, because it will make the reader uncertain whether the person who is speaking now is Mary Shelley or Ray? The last person they call together is Victor or Frankenstein? Because Mary Shelley and Frankenstein later meet in a fictional way.
Rui calls his beloved Vito until the end, but we no longer know if he is alive or dead.
In a way, the old Vito is still alive, and the Vito at this point in time seems to be missing.
Their last common call was, “Vidor, is that you? ” and it ended.
This is the end of a beautiful love story. (Editors: Huang Shufang, Wang Jingyi) 1110122

Economic stratification
Airbus, Boeing duopoly's eastern competitors
The attack on the two Western manufacturers ’ duopolies in the international aircraft market has begun: Russian rival MC-21 has been approved; China is also committed to entering the market.
How dangerous is this for Boeing and Airbus?
China ’ s C919 successfully tested for first time in 2017
For Airbus and Boeing, which have dominated the international aviation market for decades, the challengers are Russia ’ s MC-21 and China ’ s C919.
Both are double-engine narrow-body airliners.
They have been developed for quite a long time, with some delays, and have not been able to worry Western aviation overlords.
However, after several delays, the day finally came: in December 2021, the MC-21 received passenger certification and plans to enter regular routes in Russia for the first time this year.
The Chinese want to deliver their C919 to the first customer airline in the same period, but because of the temporary "shutdown" of the Xi'an test base, the date has been postponed, and it is uncertain whether it can be put into operation in 2022.
An inflection point?
However, one thing is clear: the era of new aircraft in key segments of the lucrative international aviation market has begun, and Airbus and Boeing will have to wait.
That ’ s especially true, experts say, because at least the MC-21 may still be superior to Airbus and Boeing ’ s current models in some areas.
Incidentally, this is not surprising given that the two giants from the United States and Europe have been on their own for decades: the Boeing 737 prototype dates back to 1967; and the Airbus A320 from 1987.
Unlike China, Russia has long had its own civil aviation manufacturing industry.
Since its farewell to communism, however, it had been in the shadow it had shrouded in the post-Soviet era.
Although almost all of the country ’ s manufacturing bases still exist, Russia produced only 14 civil aircraft in 2020.
This number can be reached by Airbus factories in a matter of days.
Some of the traditional Russian aircraft design bureaus, such as Polev or Ilyushin, have not produced any civilian designs for 30 years.
The long and painful process ended when the Irkut MC-21-300 was approved as a basic model by the Russian aviation authorities on December 28, 2021.
The aircraft first flew on May 28, 2017, and so far, four prototypes have been completed.
More economical?
The standard version of the MC-21 has two class cabins, with a total of 163 seats.
According to the current industry assessment, it is absolutely competitive in terms of passenger capacity and range.
Nico Buchholz, senior fleet procurement specialist at Deutsche Lufthansa for many years, pointed out that "in theory, the flight performance of the MC-21 is better than that of the latest Airbus A320neo."
He is familiar with the concept of a new aircraft.
He believes that the MC-21 is likely to be more economical than its Western competitors.
Of course, whether this also applies to performance such as efficiency, reliability, and carrying capacity is yet to be seen when the normal operation of Aeroflot ’ s subsidiary Rossiya begins this summer.
The passenger comfort of the advantages of Russian commercial aircraft should not be overlooked.
In the cabin, MC-21 passengers can also expect a more spacious sense of space: the cabin space is 11 cm wider than the A320, and the cabin diameter is 27 cm larger than the Boeing 737.
For airlines with six seats in each row, this space is not enough, but it provides passengers with more elbow space and a wider aisle.
A recent visit to the MC-21 at the Dubai Airshow demonstrates this.
The manufacturer is also proud to point out that the windows of the MC-21 are significantly larger than those of its Western competitors.
Therefore, it is known as "the world's widest narrow-body aircraft", by no means groundless.
Russia ’ s MC-21 unveiled at Dubai Air Show 2021
Possible sanctions risk
Russian commercial aircraft are in trouble right now.
Because, especially when it comes to engines and composites, they cannot be separated from the supply of various parts in the West.
The MC-21, which uses 40 percent composite material, set a record for such an aircraft, but was purchased from the United States and Japan, and the now licensed MC-21-300 is powered by a Hyundai Pratt & Whitney PW1400G gear-driven turbofan engine.
At present, the political situation is tense and Russia cannot rely on Western suppliers.
At the same time, Moscow has found important sales markets in countries such as Iran, but could not supply these countries with Western-equipped aircraft.
The aircraft on display in Dubai, MC-21-310, has not yet been certified because it is powered by a new large-aisle PD-14 turbofan engine developed by Russian company Awiadwigatel.
On December 25, 2021, another MC-21-300 prototype flew for the first time, with a new wing made from a patented Russian-made polymer composite.
MC-21 at the Dubai Air Show
Better quality than Airbus?
According to the manufacturer, there are currently 175 confirmed orders and “hundreds of intended orders ” for MC-21s from Aeroflot alone.
Juri Slyusar, managing director of Irkut ’ s parent company, United Aircraft Corporation (UAC), pointed out that Russia itself is a huge market.
"The forecast shows that in the next 20 years, Russia alone will need 800 aircraft of this size.... Once we prove the effectiveness of the aircraft domestically, we will move to the international market," he said.
MC-21 Internal Display
Self-use is also the most important perspective of China's development of the C919 with a passenger capacity of 156 to 168 passengers.
"Regardless of how many Airbus and Boeing flights there will be in China, the Chinese aircraft market itself will be able to accommodate a large number of which can be sold (C919)," Buchholz said.
In addition, China is striding ahead of Russia in manufacturing capacity, which is critical to the future success of the C919 in the market.
The former Lufthansa procurement expert pointed out that "the biggest challenge is to industrialize aircraft manufacturing and produce hundreds or thousands of aircraft of the same quality."
Since the Chinese have more experience in industrial mass production of aircraft than the Russians, they may become competitors to Airbus and Boeing.
Western manufacturers, like Airbus, have their own assembly lines in China, contributing to this.
Aircraft made in China are sometimes of better quality than Airbus made in Hamburg. "

The US aircraft carrier USS Lincoln and the Japanese Maritime Self-Defense Force held a joint exercise recently, and the two sides sent a total of five aircraft carriers / amphibious attack ships for a "group photo", the scene is very spectacular.
At the same time, 39 Chinese warplanes entered Taiwan's southwest airspace, not only setting a new high this year, but also the second highest in history after Taiwan's release of Chinese military aircraft dynamics on October 4 last year.
The Chinese Communists have obviously been confident that they can fight against the US-Japan alliance, so from millet with rifles, to today no longer fear the US-Japan alliance, how did the Chinese military development come about?
On June 4, 1985, Deng Xiaoping proposed "the army should be patient" at the enlarged meeting of the Military Commission. After the "863 Plan" which began in March of the following year and the "973 Plan" in March 1997, the PLA's investment in the development of military equipment was finally rewarded. Project 63, as well as other special projects, focuses on major scientific and technological research such as agriculture, energy, ecological environment, health, industry core competitiveness, overall independent innovation capability, and national security strategy.
At present, the overall combat strength of the PLA has been able to catch up with the level of the Western military, and some areas have even surpassed the Western military, which is the result of many years of touching the stone across the river and taking small steps.
On this basis, the Chinese military industrial system has gained a lot of technology accumulation, not only to produce new weapons, but also to develop and explore the next generation of military equipment.
Touch the stone across the river.
"Touch the stone across the river" is to want to pass an unfamiliar river, in the absence of previous experience, no boat and no bridge under the situation, to test the water to explore the river stone, in a more conservative or even primitive way to gradually understand the situation and find a way to safely wade.
Touching the stone across the river has a clear strategic goal, in practice is to take a positive attitude to try and firmly touch the stone forward.
In terms of military development, China's position in the world is not much better than that of Iran, especially since the Tiananmen Incident and the imposition of arms embargo on China by the Western world, China has been unable to obtain advanced military technology from the West.
Relatively speaking, during the construction of China's submarine, it is inevitable that the problem of hasty regulations will be committed.
The more stable and conservative approach is to start with the transformation of the Jianlong class submarine, and then build yourself after getting the technical accumulation of the construction of the submarine.
Otherwise, manufacturing a submarine is a highly integrated project, and it is easy to have problems if the technology is not accumulated enough.
Before the submarine was built, it was safer to touch the swordon-class stone to cross the river.
Solve the "yes" problem first
More than 10 years ago, the equipment of the PLA's active forces was generally 25 to 30 years behind that of the Western armies, for example, when the Chinese tank forces were not yet mechanized, they were about to change to the digital age, and of course, they were far behind the Western armies.
Another example is the development of four generations of fighter aircraft, the indicator product is the J-10.
The Chinese Air Force has already had a foundation for the development of the three generations of aircraft, such as Narrow Dragon and Leopard are a standard three generations of aircraft, and now want to enter the four generations of aircraft era, several key points are necessary: First, the use of low-detectability composite materials to reach more than 30%.
Second, the RCS (Radar Reflection Section) cannot exceed 0.0001 square meters.
Third, the single engine thrust reaches at least 14,500 to 15,000 kg, while installing a two-dimensional or 360-degree vector engine.
Fourth, use Multi-Function Active Phase Array Radar (AESA).
As the fourth generation of the J-10 series has been developed to the J-10C, the engine has used domestic Taihang engine, which uses stealth coating, infrared suppression and other stealth technology, which can effectively reduce infrared radiation and radar reflection.
Therefore, the importance of the J-10C lies in its role as a verification aircraft for China's fifth-generation J-20.
Before the launch of the four-generation fighter F-35, the US military also conducted a stealth design verification on the F-16E. The successful development of the J-10C indicates that the real four-generation fighter in China has come out.
The same is true for the development of the main tank.
The PLA first modified and upgraded the Type 55, then developed the Type 96, and then launched the Type 99, which solved the problems of the three generations of tanks before gradually upgrading.
The newly launched Type 99 still has many problems, such as the turret is too small and the armor is weak, the operating environment is too poor (no air conditioning, no automatic gear), there is no combat network platform, the digital equipment is too primitive, the display system is too simple, and so on.
The modified Type 99 improved all of the above problems, and became a veritable third-generation tank, with an estimated 1,000 units built.
More than 10 years ago, Western experts believe that the PLA and the Western army have a gap of 5 to 10 years, referring to the weapons and equipment just launched by the PLA, such as J-20, Type 99 tanks, 052C Chinese Aegis, etc., which is not far behind the Western countries, but has not been improved and mass equipped to the first line of troops.
All this points to the fact that the PLA first solved the "yes" problem, which is to develop the latest weapons and equipment, distribute them in small batches, and then gradually improve and upgrade them to keep up with the western standards, and then start mass production.
The Navy's 054A frigates, 052D destroyers, and even the 055,000-ton destroyers, especially the 052C, are the products of this thinking.
Little step, let's go.
The so-called small step fast is not to rush, not to fast, get rid of the rapid psychology, step by step positive efforts, step by step for the camp, and finally achieve the established goal.
The only way to solve the problem is to take a small step!
For example, after setting a big goal, and then setting a number of sub-goals, if you use a small step fast way to achieve a small goal every day, you can complete 30 small goals each month, these 30 small goals add up to become a big goal.
For example, the People's Liberation Army Navy imported modern class destroyers from Russia, ostensibly for the purpose of claiming to be capable of striking aircraft carriers, but in fact for the purpose of developing (cottage) phase array radar technology.
The 051B Shenzhen (167) was built only one, because it was necessary to learn the technology of building a stealth hull.
In order to imitate the domestic GT-25000 gas engine, the 052B Guangzhou and Wuhan imported the DA / DN-80 gas turbine from Ukraine.
For the sake of the vertical launch technology, the SA-N-12 missile equipped on the modern stage (later known as the Sea Red Flag -16) was developed in reverse.
Taken together, these piecemeal technologies become a complete destroyer. This is how the 052D and 0550,000 tons of large destroyers were born.
China's construction of submarine technology from "nothing" has been a huge gap, in the process of building submarines, we will not go, even touch the stone process is also saved, will start to run, the future is really worrying.
For example, submarine hull welding technology, even if the welding quality of ordinary surface warships is not qualified, it is not easy to show, as long as there is no large-scale leakage, it can also be used at ordinary times, but for submarines it is not.
Because hundreds of meters deep underwater, the hull of the submarine is subjected to huge water pressure, and the water pressure of the submarine is 30 atmospheric pressure, whether it is the ribs and pipes and valves that determine the pressure of the hull, as long as the welding is not qualified will lead to the collapse of the whole ship system.
In particular, the pipe welding is extremely delicate, requiring a large number of skilled workers, but also wearing oxygen supply special work clothes, how many skilled welders are there on the Taiwan ship?
Production generation, trial generation, pre-research generation, exploration generation
China's military development has a saying: production generation, trial production generation, pre-research generation, exploration generation.
The so-called production generation, is the use of mature technology, technology, raw materials, equipment for production, industrial production of a generation of weapons equipment.
The so-called trial generation refers to the development of new processes, new technologies, new raw materials, new equipment, ready for industrial mass production, and patented next-generation weapons equipment.
The so-called pre-research generation refers to the use of the existing basic theory to support the development of new weapons and equipment that can be equipped with the army and have a patent, and prepare to produce the next generation of new products.
The so-called exploration generation is to explore new basic theories, develop new processes, new technologies, new raw materials, new equipment and other new products with market prospects and patents.
By this logic, the PLA has at least three generations of active and developing weapons and equipment at the same time.
For example, J-20 is an active five-generation aircraft, which can be made public to the world, and the six-generation aircraft must have been put on the agenda, which is confidential and cannot be disclosed.
We began to explore the seventh generation machine, and began to research new basic theories, develop new processes, new technologies, new raw materials and new equipment.
In this way, the PLA can ensure the sustainable development of weapons and equipment, weapons and equipment research and development often take many years, an aircraft from research and development to service, may take 10 or 20 years, only to develop a sustainable military policy, is a stable and long-term approach.
Although the Chinese army does not have to copy the PLA's armaments policy, it is always possible to use enemy divisions if it seems that the opposite shore policy is more reasonable and stable.

"Wow! It 's Gender and Technology!?": Viewing the "Public" Cheng Shi Culture in the Information Technology Industry from a Gender Perspective
Photo Credit: Shutterstock
What we want you to know is
Under the influence of masculine organizational culture, based on the traditional gender expectations of “men outside the home ”, the IT workplace has less consideration of the needs of family care, which makes the work mode of long-term overtime and high pressure become the norm.
The interview analysis showed that respondents, both men and women, found it difficult to take care of their families in this workplace, and the struggle was particularly pronounced among female programmers who were mothers.
(Associate Professor, Department of Health Care Management, Kangning University)
Viewing the "public" brogrammer culture in the IT industry from a gender perspective
Taiwan is known as the computer kingdom and the island of technology. As an important producer of information technology products, Taiwan has witnessed and participated in the rapid development of information technology around the world.
When information technology has become an important part of modern people ’ s daily life, have you ever wondered who is responsible for the production of hardware, software development, and even the design of mobile phones and web user interfaces?
The Gender Imbalanced Information Technology Industry: Women Who "Missed" the Homeless World?
Compared with traditional industries, the information technology industry, as a relatively new industry, often gives people an open, modern, and out-of-touch image.
However, a number of previous studies have pointed out that the ratio of men to women in the information technology industry is even greater than in some traditional industries.
The reality that women are a minority in this workplace often leads to women being “invisible. ”
Take the popular American drama “Silicon Valley Wind ” as an example, in this 53-episode series featuring Silicon Valley IT engineers, only one female engineer appeared briefly on the screen.
Women in the information technology industry have also long been regarded as a special group.
The concept of "male equivalent to male and female equivalent to computer idiot" often appears in daily life, and is also a common theme of ridicule in film and television works.
For example, in the first episode of the British series IT crowd, Jane, who doesn ’ t know anything about computers, accidentally becomes the head of two IT geeks in the company ’ s basement.
This computer idiot to become an IT director of the ridiculous drama, ostensibly in line with the stereotype of gender to lay the comedy, but in fact in the satirical public view of women into IT as "abnormal" habit of reaction, and with this obviously absurd, surreal drama challenge the viewer to think: Are women entering the IT industry really "wrong"?
The answer, of course not.
But such gender stereotypes are still visible today.
How did this gender stereotype come about?
How can we improve?
The author ’ s Ministry of Science and Technology plans to explore this issue.
This study focuses on programmers, given the wide range of occupations within the IT industry itself and the complexity of the division of labor as the industry develops rapidly.
The author first uses the data from the Executive Yuan's Human Resources Survey and payroll productivity survey to outline the current structure of the industry, and then uses the interview method to explore the personal workplace experience of the programmer.
There's a big difference between men and women in the IT industry.
In terms of quantitative data, the ratio of men to women in Taiwan ’ s IT industry is about 4: 1, and women ’ s wages have been lower than men ’ s for many years (Figure 1 below).
When comparing the proportion of single and married people in employment, the proportion of married women in employment is significantly lower than that of men.
On the surface of quantitative data alone, overall, the incentive for women in this workplace is low (low salary), and the resistance is high (marriage and divorce).
However, in view of the complex ecology in the workplace is often not fully reflected in the data, the author further excavated through the interview and found that in addition to the differences in salary and marriage, the position and situation of female programmers in the workplace is often very different from that of men.
According to tokenism, as a minority, women naturally "attract attention" in this field.
But in addition to the influence of this “critical minority ”, the organizational culture and gender relations of the workplace itself are more important.
Studies have pointed out that there are strong masculine ideologies and interaction patterns in the IT workplace.
When the gender structure of society has long regarded a certain workplace as a male field, the culture in it will reflect a male-dominated view.
When the author collated the interview content, she found that when male and female colleagues interact in the workplace, the female normal posture is lower; when the supervisor is assigned to work, women are often assigned to tasks that are more transactional and repetitive; when promoting in the organization, most of the managers are men.
All of these are indicative of the visible gender constructions in the IT workplace.
In addition, under the influence of masculine organizational culture, based on the traditional gender expectations of "men outside the home", the information technology workplace less considers the needs of family care, which makes the need for long-term overtime and high-pressure work mode become the norm.
The interview analysis showed that respondents, both men and women, found it difficult to take care of their families in this workplace, and the struggle was particularly pronounced among female programmers who were mothers.
Strategies for Women's Survival in the IT Workplace
Research has also found that female programmers develop a variety of coping methods to integrate into the workplace.
One of the most common strategies is the "assimilation imitation strategy".
Female engineers integrate into the masculine workplace culture by imitating men, that is, deliberately displaying masculine temperament, aggression and strong work style.
But this strategy not only easily puts women in a double bind dilemma, but also contributes to the masculine organizational culture.
Another strategy is to make good use of women ’ s characteristics, that is, to gain the help of male colleagues by being pretentious and deliberately lowering their posture.
Although this strategy is ostensibly different from the previous one, its essence is still to match the mainstream masculine workplace culture.
Even if women gain temporary benefits from doing so, it won ’ t help improve a male-dominated workplace culture in the long run.
Even if female programmers do not lose to men in terms of academic qualifications and professional abilities, they will still face the reality that the workplace culture is often male-oriented and it is difficult to give women a fair evaluation.
In this dilemma, can female programmers only survive by imitating men, or deliberately changing themselves?
There are many female programmers in the interview who are trying to go another way.
They will hold community events, such as Girls in Tech Taiwan, WoFOSS, LaraGirls, and establish a network of female programmers in this field by meeting regularly to discuss the programming profession, enhance professional energy, and bring more women together to improve the situation of women at the edge of the IT workplace.
Reversing the "public" Cheng Shi culture begins with the overthrow of gender stereotypes!
A few years ago, there was a recruitment advertisement for e-commerce giant Alibaba in the news.
The title of the advertisement is: Recruitment of "Programmer (Programmer) Encourager", with a picture of a man sitting in front of a computer screen surrounded by many "hot girls".
Although some people then said that this was nothing more than a fool ’ s joke, the implicit gender stereotypes are really cruel.
In order to promote gender equality in the IT workplace, not only the masculine culture in the workplace needs to be challenged, but the gender stereotypes in the overall environment need to be changed.
In short, it is only by reversing the “public ” Cheng culture of“ computers are equal to men and housewives are equal to professionals ” that more women are willing to enter this field and stay.
In this way, it is also possible to further let everyone regardless of gender have the opportunity to cross the fence and play their talents and abilities!
About this article: This article introduces the research results of the Ministry of Science and Technology ’ s 105th Annual Gender and Technology Research Program, “Gender Segregation in Taiwan ’ s Information Technology Industry and Male Preference for Women, ” conducted by Associate Professor Zhang Yonghan of the Department of Health Care Management at Kangning University.
Some of the results of this article were published in December 2018, Feng Chia Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences, No. 37, The Working Situation of Women in Information Technology Workplace: Taking Female Programmers as an Example.

How Warming Affects Growing and Supply of Popular Crops
Matt McGrath (Matt McGrath)
• BBC environment correspondent
Have you ever thought that many of the agricultural products consumed on the market today may come from completely different regions in the near future?
Warming climate will change the regions of the world that are suitable for growing coffee, cashew nuts and avocados (also known as avocados).
This is the conclusion of a recent study.
What important information can consumers and growers learn from this research?
Coffee growing
Coffee is one of the most important crops in the world, not only because it is sought after by hundreds of millions of consumers around the world as a daily staple drink, but also because coffee cultivation is the livelihood of millions of small-scale farmers.
On the other hand, due to changes in tastes and perceptions among consumers in wealthier countries, the demand for avocado and cashew nuts in rich countries has also increased significantly in recent decades.
But a reality that must be faced is that by 2050, Brazil, Indonesia, and Vietnam, the world ’ s most important coffee growing regions, will “drastically reduce ” by about 50%.
However, the areas suitable for cashew and avocado cultivation will increase, but most will be far removed from current production sites.
The authors of the report, published in the Public Science Library, an international non-profit information-sharing organization, call for greater efforts to help farmers adapt to the changing conditions of production brought about by climate change.
Fascinating food
While there has been well-documented research in recent years on the threat of climate change to coffee growing, there is little information on how climate change will affect avocados and cashews.
In this study, the authors looked at how rising temperatures and changing precipitation rates will affect these three crops over the next 30 years.
The researchers also included information on land and soil features for the first time.
Coffee is the most vulnerable crop to high temperatures.
According to the report, in those countries where small fruit coffee is mainly grown (also known as Arabica, Arabica), the adaptability of the conditions under which this crop is grown will change “dramatically ” by about 50% by 2050.
Some major production areas will be more severely affected.
Considering the minimum temperature limit for coffee growing, the best coffee growing areas in Brazil will be reduced by 76%.
In Colombia, coffee plantations will also be reduced by 63%.
However, some areas in the northern and southern ends of the world ’ s coffee growing regions will now become more suitable for growing coffee, including Argentina, South Africa, China and New Zealand.
But the authors of the study say this does not mean that new regions will easily replace existing ones.
Roman Grüter of the Zurich University of Applied Sciences is one of the authors of the study.
“The most critical message for those who are in major production areas today is that farming systems have to adapt to changing natural conditions, ” he said.
“If coffee cultivation has already started in those new areas that are more suitable for growing coffee, it may be easier to produce, or it may be possible to expand the production operation, just by adjusting the management. ”
But that ’ s not to say that these areas will become unique coffee growing areas in 10 years or so. ”
In addition, the cultivation of cashew nuts will also change.
Overall, there will be a 17% increase in the number of regions in the world that are very suitable for growing cashew nuts.
However, the regions that have increased are also not those that currently rely on cashew nuts as a major cash crop.
For example, India will lose a large number of areas suitable for cashew cultivation, while Benin, the main cashew producer in Africa, is predicted to lose half of those areas suitable for cultivation.
Avocado cultivation will also become complicated, especially for the largest producers.
Mexico, now the world ’ s largest producer of avocados, will see a significant increase in the amount of land suitable for cultivation by more than 80%.
However, another major growing country, Peru, has predicted it could lose about half of its suitable growing areas.
While rising temperatures and changing rainfall patterns may make some areas more suitable for cultivation, the authors are concerned that these crops, once planted in new areas, will have a significant environmental impact on those areas: more deforestation and erosion of more native species.
“In areas that may become more suitable for growing these crops, the most important thing is to ensure that there are no negative environmental impacts such as deforestation. ”
In his view, to avoid this situation, the stakeholders involved in the local planting industry and the local community must be involved in the process of responding to the change, "must be involved in all aspects."
While climate change may be bad news for current crop growers, there are some positive steps producers can take to mitigate the effects of climate change.
Dr. Joaquin Guillermo Ramirez Gil of National University of Colombia, who did not participate in the study, said, “Utilizing the genetic variability of avocados may help in some areas where avocados are currently grown. ”
According to him, avocados have three different “races ” with different geographical origins, which makes avocados quite“ malleable ” and able to adapt to different climatic conditions.
"Local adaptation and new management methods, such as the use of biostimulants and nanotechnology-based products, can serve as a basis for reducing stress caused by extreme weather conditions," he said.

Third, the use of blind boxes to sell sick live animals;
Fourth, some merchants refuse to bear the after-sale responsibility of blind box products;
Fifth, to induce minors to impulsively consume in the name of treasures, rarity, and limited quantities;
Sixth, most of the blind boxes are opaque, and there are fraudulent situations such as selling them after they are opened.

2022 / 1 / 31 17: 24: 50 Source: ijiwei Author: JZ
According to surging news reports, recently, Europe's first quantum computer with more than 5,000 qubits was launched at the Forschungszentrum Jülich Research Center in Germany.
The center said it was an important milestone in the development of quantum computers in Europe.
Built by D-Wave, a Canadian supplier of quantum computing systems, the supercomputer is the company ’ s most computationally capable machine to date and is deployed outside of the company ’ s headquarters for the first time.
This quantum annealing computer is essentially the same idea as adiabatic quantum computing, and the machine is designed to deal with optimization and sampling problems.
The advantage of quantum annealing is that the stability of the system is much higher than that of the quantum gate.
With this super quantum computer and the establishment of the remote cloud-access D-Wave quantum system at the Leahy Research Center, the center is able to participate in the practical application of quantum computing at an early stage.
Quantum computers are expected to revolutionize drug development, cybersecurity, financial modeling, weather forecasting and many other fields, dealing with problems that classical computers cannot solve.
In order to realize the commercial application of quantum computing as soon as possible, the center established the JUNIQ quantum computing user infrastructure (JUNIQ) to provide friendly access to quantum computing systems for different user groups in Europe.
In the future, JUNIQ will provide facilities for German and other EU researchers and companies to use JUNIQ to help them use quantum computers, from experimental systems and machine prototypes to first-of-its-kind production systems, and develop algorithms and applications.

Hugo ’ s Soul – Hugo Award, the highest honor in contemporary science fiction
A crazy idea from a science fiction novel has come true.
How can they give up this feeling of being in heaven? Of course they want to go on to heaven.
Heaven appeared in Chicago for the second time in 1940 and Denver for the third time in 1941.
However, the Second World War broke out and their annual extravaganza was interrupted.
After the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, the vast majority of science fiction fans enlisted in the military, and only a few stayed home.
Those who stay will send science fiction magazines to their comrades on the front lines, because the comrades who hide in the trenches must rely on them to protect their souls.
In 1945, a crazy idea in science fiction came true, two atomic bombs exploded in Nagasaki, Hiroshima, Japan, ending the war, bringing peace back, and, of course, heaven. In 1946, the Fourth World Science Fiction Conference reopened in Los Angeles.
At science fiction conventions, sometimes science fiction fans vote for their best novel or short story.
At the Eleventh Congress in 1953, a rocket-shaped trophy was presented to the winner, but it was only a temporary initiative that did not continue the following year.
It was not until the Thirteenth Congress in 1955 that the people decided to make the award a permanent ceremony, and the award was named The Science Fiction Achievement Award, but it was still called the Hugo Award in private in honor of Gensbach ’ s contributions.
In 1958, the Hugo Award became the official name.
And so the Hugo Award was born.
Nearly 70% of the awards were awarded.
Canadian author Jo Walton is the winner of the 2012 Hugo Award for fiction.
Starting in 2010, she spent three years reading the novels that won awards and were shortlisted in the 42-year period from 1959 to 2000, and published them on the science fiction website, and in-depth discussions with the science fiction community, which caused widespread response.
In 2018, she published An Informal History of the Hugos.
She said she expanded her reading range to include the finalists because she was curious to see if the winning entries were actually the best ones of the year.
She concluded that twenty-five of those forty-two years were indeed well chosen, equivalent to 69% of the winning entries.
In addition, why stop at the year 2000? She gives two reasons.
First, she has published her own work since 2000 and was shortlisted for the John Campbell Memorial Award in 2001, so she cannot include her work in the evaluation in order to remain detached and objective.
The second and most important reason is that the work must stand the test of time.
Since she started writing the column in 2010, a ten-year interval is a reasonable time frame.
For example, if a novel published in 2000 is not out of print by 2010, it can barely stand the test of time.
It takes time to see the works from the depth of history.
Finally, she said that because she also won the Hugo Award in 2012, deeply shocked, coupled with reading 250 novels and writing a column for three years, she is more convinced that the Hugo Award is indeed of extraordinary significance, indeed the most important literary award in science fiction.
The Ideal Science Fiction Reading Guide
So, for readers in Taiwan, what does the Hugo Award mean?
Compared to English-speaking countries, Taiwan's science fiction publishing is much cooler, however, with the efforts of many publishers, Taiwanese readers can still get access to some classic works in the history of science fiction.
Therefore, the Hugo Award can still be an ideal reading guide.
For example, the 1966 award-winning Dune is a classic in the history of science fiction.
The film based on this novel has been popular around the world since its recent release, which has sparked a rush to read the original novel.
Successful film and television adaptations do help drive readers ’ interest in science fiction reading.
Similarly, the 2016 Oscar-nominated film “Arrival ” is also based on classic science fiction.
The success of the film has made Chiang Feng-nan, one of the most prominent Taiwanese-American writers of the time, a household name.
His two collections of novels, The Story of Your Life and The Breath, won four Hugo Awards in 2002, 2008, 2009 and 2011.
And the 1966 Hugo Award "Best Science Fiction Series" of the "Base" series (Chinese translation fantasy base publication) is the history of science fiction super classic, the impact on the future generations is unparalleled.
A television series based on the novel is also popular.
The 1970 award winning "Left Hand of Darkness" and the 1976 award winning "Nothing" are representative works of the life of the female writer Esula Le Guen, who is familiar to Taiwanese readers.
The 2002 award for American Gods is the work of Neil Gaiman, a leading contemporary fantasy writer, and his award is the most successful example of a Hugo Award-compatible fantasy genre.
The publication of classic science fiction novels in Taiwan still has a long way to go. (Part II)

EU plans to raise $150 billion in infrastructure funding for Africa
With the newly launched Global Gateway initiative, the EU hopes to inject $150 billion into the continent.
The aim of the plan is to expand the EU's international influence and compete with China.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen introduced the EU's 150 billion euro investment plan during his visit to Senegal.
In Dakar, Senegal, she said the EU is the largest and most credible partner of the African continent.
Von der Leyen said that the Africa-Europe project is the first regional initiative of the European Union (EU) since the launch of the Global Gateway initiative in December last year.
The European Union (EU) hopes to use the Global Gateway to expand Europe's international influence. Von der Leyen stressed that although the project is funded by the EU, it will be implemented in partnership.
Von der Leyen at the Global Gateway Initiative press conference on December 1, 2021.
Global portals for the world
Through the “Global Gateway ” initiative, the EU plans to provide a total of 300 billion euros in infrastructure to emerging and developing countries around the world over the next few years.
For this purpose, the EU will receive funding from a range of EU institutions and projects, including the European Investment Bank (EIB).
The proposed investment plans include the construction of climate-neutral liquid hydrogen energy facilities in Africa and a submarine data cable linking the European Union and South America.
In addition, the funds will be used to build roads, railways, Internet networks, health, education and scientific research.
For several years, China has been promoting the “Belt and Road ” project in Africa.
The picture shows the Zambian international airport built by China.
More details of Africa ’ s investment plans will be unveiled during the EU-Africa summit in Brussels next week. The Global Gateway will compete with China ’ s Belt and Road initiative.
In the past few years, China has launched related projects in many countries.
Critics pointed out that investors from China and Russia on the African continent often do not pay attention to issues such as environmental protection and human rights.
China has also been accused of dragging some African countries into debt traps with unrepayable loans.
(Reuters, DPA, Agence France-Presse)

Chinese company Sheng He Resources has announced plans to acquire an equity interest in Peak Rare Earths Limited (PEK), an Australian-listed rare earth company.
Australian media reported on Monday (14) that if the acquisition is successful, China will further grasp the lifeline of the global supply of rare earths.
Sheng Ho Resources (Singapore) Limited said on Friday (11) that it plans to purchase a 19.9% stake in the Australian rare earth company held by private equity fund Appian Capital, which was unanimously approved by the company's board of directors, for a total purchase of about A $39.25 million (about HK $218 million).
According to the report, if traded according to Sheng and Resources ’ bid, PEK ’ s market value will be close to A $196 million (about HK $1.09 billion), more than 24% higher than the company ’ s market value at Friday ’ s close.
Headquartered in Perth, Western Australia, PEK ’ s current business scope includes rare earth mining plans at the Ngualla mine in Tanzania, and plans to build a rare earth refinery in Middlesbrough, North Yorkshire, to handle rare earth in the Enla mine.
According to Australian media, 80% of the world ’ s 17 rare earth elements are produced in China, and the Chinese government has imposed a production ceiling on rare earth mining and refining companies in China, which has a huge influence on rare earth prices.

Two days before French President Emmanuel Macron ’ s talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday, the CDRC announced on Monday that it had “recently ” reached an agreement with the French Ministry of Economy and Finance on cooperation in third countries.
France has not yet made an announcement on the deal.
The commentary said that in the context of the economic downturn, China may use its cooperation with France to continue to advance its pawn in Africa.

According to the Chinese newspaper, the cooperation agreement with France covers seven projects worth more than 1.7 billion US dollars (1.5 billion euros) and "covers infrastructure, environmental protection and new energy."
Investments to be made in "regions such as Africa and Central and Eastern Europe."
According to the French newspaper Le Monde, six of the seven projects are in Africa.

Three other hydropower projects involve Gabon.

The origins of the agreement date back to June 2015, during an official visit to France by Chinese Premier Li Keqiang.
At that meeting, the two countries issued a joint statement on cooperation in third-party markets.
Since then, however, French diplomats have complained that no progress has been made and Beijing has continued to work alone, particularly in Africa, as part of its vast Belt and Road Initiative (BRI).
Why is France low?
Analysis of Le Monde reports, public reports in China and official silence in France suggest that Paris does not necessarily want to emphasize this cooperation on the eve of the EU-African Union summit on February 17 and 18, which "aims to launch an ambitious Africa-Europe investment plan."
At a time when the EU wants to compete with China ’ s Belt and Road project by launching the Global Gateway initiative, China ’ s public approach is designed to alert France, one of the major European countries involved in African affairs, to its role.
As early as January 13 of this year, only Beijing mentioned the visit of the President of the Republic's diplomatic adviser, Bonnet, to China on the occasion of the "strategic dialogue", and the French government also remained silent.
In the context of the economic downturn, China is using France to continue to advance its pawn in Africa?
"Under the innovative model of third market cooperation, Chinese companies and their partners can participate in joint development projects in third countries under the Belt and Road Initiative," said Liu, a researcher at the China Institute of International Trade and Economic Cooperation, in an interesting comment, as the West criticized China for reserving contracts it co-financed within the framework of these partnerships to its own companies.
In the article, Mr. Liu also suggested that “in order for Chinese companies to better understand local rules, the government should establish an effective investment dispute settlement mechanism. ”
The expert acknowledged that disputes are arising and that China has yet to find a satisfactory solution.
As its economic growth begins to slow, China certainly cannot afford to let the debt trap end up on its own.
Thus, its cooperation with France has enabled it to push its pawn further to Africa.
Advantages of Sino-French Cooperation
According to Reuters, France is the first country to establish a third-party market intergovernmental cooperation mechanism with China.
The third party market cooperation between China and France is enterprise-oriented and market-oriented, abides by the laws and policies of the host country, conforms to the development priorities of relevant national plans, and adheres to mutual benefit, consensus, market rules and fair competition based on economic feasibility, social and environmental sustainability.
From the comparative advantages of the two sides, French enterprises have unique advantages in advanced manufacturing, environmental protection and engineering construction, and Chinese enterprises have accumulated rich experience in infrastructure construction, energy, equipment manufacturing and the Internet.
Enterprises of the two sides have their own advantages and strong complementarity, and there is great potential for third-party market cooperation.

Belgium will push for labour market reforms in just four days a week
Belgium ’ s prime minister said it would include “giving workers more flexibility ” as the first element of labour market reforms, allowing full-time workers to work four days a week if they had to complete the required hours.
In addition to the reform blueprint proposed by Belgium this time, some European countries, even Japan and New Zealand on the other side of the world, have developed or are working on reducing the working day.
Many countries have developed or are developing experimental programs to shorten working hours.
According to Belgian Prime Minister Alexander De Croo, the first point of labor market reform is to give workers more flexibility and more freedom.
He said that after the reform, full-time employees can flexibly extend their working hours and complete the required hours within four days of the week, which will benefit the compatibility of work and personal life.
A sustainable, innovative and digital economy
The prime minister also said that another key element of the reform is that workers have statutory training opportunities.
In addition, the rules for night work will be more flexible to facilitate online transactions.
He said it would also improve protections for freelancers on internet platforms such as Uber, which includes mandatory work injury insurance.
"We are committed to a sustainable, innovative and digital economy," he said.
The Belga news agency reported that the aim of the reform is to reach 80% employment by 2030.
At present, the employment rate in Belgium is 71%, and there are wide regional differences.
For comparison: According to the figures provided by the Federal Statistical Office, the current employment rate in Germany is 75.5%
What other countries and companies have considered similar working models?
Deutsche Welle has compiled some examples:
Iceland
Iceland tested a similar provision between 2015 and 2019 - reducing working hours from 40 to 35 or 36 hours, but the pay remained the same.
At the time, 2,500 workers took part in the study ’ s tests, which showed significant improvements in employee wellbeing, optimized workflow and closer collaboration with colleagues.
Productivity has largely remained the same; it has even increased, as Icelandic Prime Minister Katrin Jakobsdottir once said: In her country, most people can now shorten their working week.
Icelandic Prime Minister Jacobus Stottir: Most people in Iceland can shorten their working week
Scotland and Wales
Scotland is currently testing the four-day workweek, with participating companies receiving around £10 million in funding from the state.
A four-day working week has also been discussed in Wales, with officials calling for shorter working days in the public sector.
Sweden and Finland
Sweden had already tested the four-day full pay system in 2015, but even Sweden ’ s leftists found it too costly to implement.
However, there are also individual companies that insist on reducing the working day.
In addition, Finland has made international headlines in a short time for reducing working hours.
The Nordic country is said to want to introduce a system of four days a week and six hours a day at the same time.
But this was a false report, which was later clarified by the Finnish government.
Spain and Germany
At the request of the left-wing party Más País, some 6,000 employees of 200 small businesses in Spain will be able to extend their weekends by one day — and be paid in full.
The pilot phase will last at least a year and it is unclear when it will begin.
In Germany, mainly smaller startups are trying to shorten the weekday.
New Zealand and Japan
Multinational consumer goods company Unilever is currently testing a four-day workweek in New Zealand for about a year and maintaining the same pay, and if the model proves successful, Unilever plans to roll it out to other countries.
Large Japanese companies, such as Microsoft, are experimenting with similar ideas.

Airbus plans to test hydrogen engines for 2026 A380 wide-body aircraft
European aircraft giant Airbus plans to test hydrogen-powered engines on an improved A380 by 2026 in an attempt to bring low-emission fuel to commercial air travel.
Kumba said on Tuesday it was working with engine manufacturer r CFM International to test the aircraft, including an improved version of the engine in use, which will have to deal with higher temperatures from hydrogen burning and will begin testing in 2026.
Aircraft manufacturers and airlines are scrambling to cut carbon emissions, which account for more than 2% of the world ’ s total.
Airbus has been actively promoting hydrogen power and is developing a passenger aircraft powered by hydrogen, which is scheduled to enter service in 2035.
Competitor Boeing (BA-US) is focused on more sustainable aviation fuels, which currently account for less than 1% of aviation fuel supply and are more expensive than conventional aviation fuels.
Boeing CEO Dave Calhoun said at an investor conference in June last year, “Hydrogen-powered aircraft will not be able to reach the size we ’ re talking about before 2050, and will only be able to carry some very small packages. ”
Richard Aboulafia, director of Aerodynamic Advisory, an aviation consultancy, said that one of the challenges of using hydrogen fuel is the need for additional storage, which increases the weight of the aircraft and reduces the number of people or cargo that the aircraft can carry.
"If engineers and economists don't communicate with each other, hydrogen power will advance," he said.
Kumba said the A380, the world's largest aircraft, was chosen because of its wide space to store liquid hydrogen tanks and other equipment.

The Ministry of Labor stated that China's Equal Pay Day is based on the "Employee Wage Survey" of the General Accounting Office of the Executive Yuan, which calculates the average hourly wage gap between the sexes in the current year from January 1 of the following year, and the number of working days that women need to increase.

To have a good weekend, you have to have some key elements.
It ’ s hard to be 100% perfect on every weekend, but even with just a few of these elements of relaxation, you can completely change how you feel from the inside out.
You might also be inspired to take a different kind of casual approach next weekend, or better yet, experience it directly during the week.

Seneca is well aware of the importance of time: “No one can recover the lost time; no one can bring you back to yourself. ” In short, the weekend is a shelter and a laboratory where we can experiment with what we want to live.

Top 10 Declarations for a Great Weekend
• Build a connection with people.

Second, pay attention.

Do not make a plan, leave more blank.
8: Walk around.
9) Be curious.
10, live in the moment.

Felicitas Betzl is Managing Director of Serps Invaders, an online boutique marketing company based in Edinburgh, Scotland, with clients around the world.
In order to compete with other larger companies and attract top talent in the industry, she decided to give her employees (five full-time employees, plus about 20 consultants and freelancers) what she called a “gift ”: a four-day work week.

At the end of the day, you no longer waste your time at work, leading to a calmer, more relaxed environment.
People can use their weekend time to do more interesting things and thus create more interesting people.
It ’ s hard to quantify its value, but you feel it ’ s the right thing to do.
For example, how do you measure the value of giving thanks to humanity? How do you measure the value of a smile? You can ’ t measure these things, you just know it ’ s the right thing to do.
Failure to complete or delay does not affect our company, and since it does not affect us, why not do it?
Don ’ t you want everyone to have a better work-life balance, spend more time with their families, or do what they want? A four-day week feels like the right thing to do. ”

Many people have the habit of supplementing vitamins, and for convenience, often along with other drugs, but the Ministry of Health and Welfare Food and Drug Administration said that many people do not know that vitamins and drugs will also interact, can not be mixed to eat, especially some high levels of vitamins already belong to the category of drugs, improper use will cause side effects and other adverse reactions.
The Food and Drug Administration of the Ministry of Health and Welfare has listed the following five common vitamin and drug interactions:
1.
Vitamin C and Acid Containing Aluminum:
Aluminum acid is one of the common gastric medicine ingredients, if combined with vitamin C, may lead to increased absorption of aluminum, resulting in increased side effects, people with poor kidney function, should try to avoid combined use.
2.
Vitamin K, Vitamin E and Anticoagulants:
Vitamin K, commonly found in dark green vegetables, may reduce the efficacy of the anticoagulant warfarin; conversely, vitamin E enhances the efficacy of the anticoagulant warfarin. If you are taking an anticoagulant, check with your doctor and pharmacist.
3.
Folic acid and chemotherapy drugs:
Some chemotherapy drugs interact with folic acid, and use may lead to increased drug activity, leading to serious side effects.
4.
Vitamin B6 and Parkinson ’ s Disease Medications:
Vitamin B6 inhibits levodopa, the drug dopamine precursor for Parkinson's disease, and prevents levodopa from entering the central nervous system, resulting in decreased efficacy.
The Food and Drug Administration reminds that in addition to the above five types of vitamins, there are many other vitamins that may interact with each other.

China has added an average of 18,562 new jobs to Africa each year over the past decade.

In addition, the rise in commodity prices has also provided some support for the growth of African trade.

China invested 280 million US dollars in South Africa, including 130 million US dollars in non-financial investment and 150 million US dollars in financial investment.

Chinese Ambassador to Tanzania Chen Mingjian said: "At present, countries in the world are still facing the two arduous tasks of epidemic prevention and control and economic recovery. Science and Technology Daily, Beijing, March 1 (Reporter Zhang Mengran) According to the latest issue of "Paleontology" magazine, by analyzing how now-extinct sea creatures once lived, a team of geoscientists at the University of Hamburg in Germany directly linked their extinction to the following climate change: declining oxygen content in water, rising water temperatures and ocean acidification.
The late Permian is characterized by the largest mass extinction event in Earth ’ s history. 252 million years ago, a series of volcanic eruptions in Siberia led to the release of large amounts of greenhouse gases.
Over the next few thousand years, the climate eventually warmed by 10 ° C.
As a result, on land, about 75% of all living things went extinct; in the ocean, the figure was about 90%.
These changes are similar to current trends.
Researchers say the Permian findings cannot be applied one-on-one to modern climate change.
The two climatic systems differ too much, yet they do show which features are essential for survival or extinction under similar conditions.
The team analyzed more than 25,000 records of 1,283 marine fossils from southern China, such as bivalves, snails, sponges, algae and crustaceans, all of which have mineral skeletons or shells.
Their fossil remains can be dated using a special method that provides insight into marine ecosystems millions of years ago.
The team also leveraged a vast database that provided a variety of ecologically relevant information about how these creatures lived.
For each genus, the researchers analyzed 12 of these criteria to identify certain survival-related traits.
With the help of machine learning, all of these factors were analyzed simultaneously, and the team compared the results to determine which organisms existed before, during, and after the mass extinction.
The team ’ s new findings shed light on the four most important factors that make it possible for organisms to survive the end of the Permian: where they live in water, how mineralized their shells are, the diversity of species within their genus, and their sensitivity to acidification.
Using the new game theory approach, the team succeeded in revealing the survival of a variety of organisms: some live in deeper water, where worsening hypoxia poses a risk.
By contrast, animals that live near the surface have to cope with rising water temperatures.
Also, if a creature has only one limited habitat, it has nowhere to go when that particular habitat becomes uninhabitable.
The findings identify which biometrics are "potentially lethal."
The team ultimately confirmed that mass extinctions can be directly attributed — suggesting that these could also be the three main causes of long-term extinctions in future climate crises.
Editor-in-Chief Circle
Declining oxygen levels in the water, rising water temperatures, ocean acidification — scientists have identified the culprits responsible for the extinction of marine life hundreds of millions of years ago.
These three reasons, which are not surprising, are also entirely logical deductions.
Only, it clearly reveals the catastrophic consequences of climate warming.
These three phenomena seem to be unremarkable, and because of this, it is actually very easy to appear.
As the article says, we cannot directly correspond to today ’ s climate in the Permian, nor can we directly regard the Permian mass extinction as today ’ s pessimistic assertion.
However, no matter what geological period, life is equally fragile, and they do not have enough time to adapt to a sudden climate crisis.
