The importance of semiconductors, solar power, batteries and drones to the national economy is undeniable.
At the beginning of the related technology, Japanese companies play an important role in R & D, production, and market development compared to other countries in the world.
However, after entering the 21st century, as Japan's economic policy changed from industry-focused to financial-led, financial omnipotence occupied the political and economic center, people saw that companies began to show slow product updates and serious deficiencies in subsequent research and development.
While the international market continues to expand, the domestic market in Japan is gradually shrinking.
Politically, Junichiro Koizumi's visit to the Yasukuni Shrine showed a beggar-thy-neighbor attitude; in the era of the Democratic Party, it provoked territorial disputes and serious confrontation with neighboring countries; in the period of Shinzo Abe's administration, Japan's relations with South Korea and North Korea became strained; and after the reign of Manio Kishida, Japan-Russian relations reached the bottom of the post-war.
Economically, Japan entered the "lost decade" in the 1990s, and after entering the 21st century, Japan ushered in the "lost twenty years" and then extended this economic phenomenon to the "lost thirty years" through the Abe administration after 2010.
During this period, Japanese semiconductor from more than 50% of the world market, reduced to less than 10%; photovoltaic (solar) industry promotion policy has been rushed away; lithium ion batteries and other technologies are invented by Japanese companies, Panasonic Electric was once the world's largest battery manufacturers, but now in the world's most influential 5 battery companies, has not seen the shadow of Panasonic Electric; as early as the 1950s Japan has begun to develop the use of unmanned But drones have been lukewarm in Japan and so on, so far they have not been able to occupy a place in the international market.
Today, Japan still has a considerable influence in the world economy is the robot.
However, in the loss of three consecutive decades, Japan's artificial intelligence, industrial Internet, quantum computing capabilities, etc., can not occupy the mainstream position in the world, and politically began to implement the economic security law from 2022, cutting off the links between Japan and the major economic powers.
Will the Japanese robot industry be affected, like the semiconductor, battery and other industries, from the protagonist to the supporting role, and then enter the stage of the dragon suit? Is Japan more willing to enjoy the role of the dragon suit?
It can be said that the future of the robot industry is actually a microcosm of the development of Japan's industrial economy.
Robot adoption rates are starting to fall sharply.
In the Industrial Machinery Division of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, there is an organization responsible for robots, the Robotics Policy Office.
The Robot Policy Office is responsible for relevant industrial policy research, the introduction of robot policies, and the regular production of industry reports.
The latest version of the report to date was published in July 2019.
From the report of July 2019, the following characteristics have emerged in the Japanese robot industry;
First, from the election of Shinzo Abe as Prime Minister of Japan in 2012 to the statistics of the Ministry of Economy and Trade in 2017, the introduction of Japanese robots has gradually retreated from the number one position in the world, and has opened a huge distance with China in terms of growth rate.
In 2012 alone, Japan imported 28,680 robots, ranking first in the world, while China imported 22,987 robots, ranking third in the world.
In 2017, Japan imported 45,566 robots a year, an increase of 58.9% compared to 2012; while China imported 137,920 robots a year, nearly six times the number in 2012.
Regardless of volume or growth rate, China has completely crushed Japan.
In terms of robot introduction, Japan is not only inferior to China, but also lags behind other countries.
In terms of growth rate, Japan lags behind North America and South Korea, only slightly higher than Germany, and the world average (139.3%), which is also far behind.
Second, Japan's dominant position in the field of robotics has been declining year by year.
From the perspective of the Chinese market, the robots produced in Japan are no longer the mainstream, and the pursuit of enterprises from various countries has made Japanese robots more and more common.
Or look at the relevant figures issued by the Ministry of Agriculture:
In 2012, China ’ s own products accounted for only 13% of the robots needed in the Chinese market, Japan accounted for 65%, and imported from other countries accounted for 22%.
However, by 2017, the proportion of robots made in China has doubled to 27%, and the number has increased from 3,000 in 2012 to 37,800, and the proportion of Japan has dropped to 44%. Although it is still the most important country to introduce robots in China, the importance has decreased;
More importantly, the share of robots exported to China from other countries increased to 29% from 22% in 2012, indicating that not only has China ’ s robot industry changed dramatically in the past five years, but other countries are also trying to catch up with Japan.
Third, in terms of the use of robots, Japan lags behind South Korea and Germany, and although it is still higher than other countries and regions, there is little room to continue to introduce robots in the future.
Still from the data released by the Ministry of Economic Affairs: the density of robots per 10,000 people is 710 in South Korea, 658 in Germany, and less than half that in Japan, only 308.
Of course, Japan is much higher than the United States (230) and China (97), but China is catching up very fast.
Home and self-help.
After losing the advantages of semiconductors, batteries, photovoltaics, drones and other finished products, Japanese companies have temporarily retained the world's leading position in semiconductor packaging, battery positive pole and diaphragm, monocrystalline and polysilicon production capacity, and unmanned aerial vehicle motors.
Therefore, Japan is now more willing to retreat from the finished product into the key raw materials, key parts of the field, so that only make no loss - Japanese finished products in the price, market development does not have an advantage; but in the key products to maintain uniqueness, enterprises can enjoy the benefits of market development, and do not need to bear the risks arising from the mutual competition of finished products, new product development failure and so on.
In the robotics industry, there are two ends of the smile curve, one is the material and the other is the system integration.
Japanese companies in the composite materials, resin, intelligent materials, control, communication, sensors and other sub-areas have certain advantages; in the system integration, Japanese companies in processing machines, robot systems, information processing machines and other aspects have more accumulation, which ensure the profitability of Japanese robot companies.
In addition, Japanese companies have ample capital, but little investment in robot research and development, and the introduction of robots is limited, so Japanese companies are trying to expand the scope of use of robots – only if they succeed in new fields can the Japanese robot industry continue to develop.
In other words, robots began to enter various fields of Japanese society, and the path of development was constantly broadening.
If you see a beautiful woman or handsome man on the street, staring at people with straight eyes, reaching out a pig's hand to touch each other's face or hand, what is the immediate result, not self-evident.
But on the streets of Shibuya, Tokyo, there is a beautiful woman standing there 24 hours a day, a group of red men and green women looking around three levels, from time to time, a salty pig hand extended, but not slapped, only heard a polite warning from a nearby speaker: "Please don't touch!" - this "beautiful woman" is a robot.
This kind of robot, which can talk and communicate with people with affectionate eyes, is not many in Japanese society, and there are many robot animals.
For example, the robot dog AIBO developed by Sony was sold very well in Japan.
This kind of dog can walk, can make the same as the real dog but some like comic, some exaggerated actions, very loved by the elderly in the apartment who can not have a dog. Take such a robot dog to walk at home, talk to the dog, and listen to the dog in a language that people can understand and talk to themselves, for the lonely elderly, can alleviate the feeling of loneliness to a considerable extent.
In Japanese nursing homes, in addition to robot pets like AIBO, you can also see robots that can help the elderly defecate or help the elderly in bed to bathe.
Due to the low income of nursing workers and the lack of hands, the desire to introduce robots in Japanese nursing homes is very large, but the extent to which the current robot can meet the needs of nursing homes, and whether it can be low-cost in manufacturing is still a big problem.
The big change seen in Japan in recent years is that there are quite a lot of places at the front desk of government agencies that have been replaced with robots, which can answer questions from visitors in Japanese, Chinese, and English, and guide visitors to relevant departments or conference rooms.
Some office buildings also began to use robots to patrol, in the event of an emergency, although the robot can not directly control the relevant personnel, but take video, to provide backstage personnel with preparation time, etc. These functions can play a great role in solving the problem.
In fact, more of the robots made in Japan are used in the production process.
In addition to the robots we see in the car welding process in daily life, many fixed operations, the use of robots than the use of workers to ensure the stability of quality.
For example, after the Fukushima nuclear power accident, Hitachi, Toshiba and other nuclear power companies are developing corresponding robots, trying to investigate the accident situation of the nuclear power station through robots, and to a certain extent to deal with the accident.
However, how to deal with the situation, there is still very little information that can be learned, and the related work is being promoted, and it is estimated that there are many problems.
When talking to Japanese diplomatic and military personnel about robots, they are more concerned about military robots, such as unmanned submarines, drones equipped with explosive devices, etc., which will greatly increase in the use of war in the future.
In addition to long-range weapons such as missiles, the use of these robots will greatly change the course of war, making war more destructive and able to reverse human history at a very rapid rate.
Ending language
Affected by China and other countries and regions in terms of robot finished products, Japan's share of the international finished robot market will further decline in the future, but the research and development and production of robots over the past few decades, so that Japanese companies will not necessarily be squeezed into the corner, it is impossible to fight back.
What really makes the Japanese robot industry finally go bankrupt is still Japan's industrial policy.
After the adoption of the Economic Security Law in 2022, even with advanced materials and system integration capabilities, it is not possible to cooperate with the most important countries in the world (such as China), or can only cooperate with other countries with relatively backward technologies.
This seems to be able to provide protection for the robot industry in Japan to a certain extent, but the Japanese market is narrow, not enough to make the company become a giant of the robot industry; the external market is not to fight for, but not to fight for, and ultimately the robot industry can only take the old road of semiconductor, battery and other industries, and gradually decline in Japan.
The Kishida regime is also fighting for the revival of semiconductor, battery and other industries, such as taking out huge capital to introduce TSMC and other companies' semiconductor technology, encouraging investment in battery companies, and trying to build a complete industrial supply chain.
However, in the world economy, once industries are lost, there are very few precedents for recovery through economic policies.

Japan ’ s Fujitsu Corporation, together with the Institute of Physical and Chemical Sciences, is expected to start making quantum computers available to enterprises in 2023 (April 2023-March 2024) in order to promote the practical use of quantum computers.
The ground-breaking product is expected to be used in financial market forecasting, new materials and drug development, an achievement that will solidify Japan ’ s position as the world ’ s No. 3 in quantum computing and lead to new technologies for Japan ’ s economic industry and defense security.
According to the Nikkei Chinese website, Fujitsu has been developing quantum computers since April 2021 when it set up a cooperation center with the Institute of Physical and Chemical Sciences in Saitama Prefecture and Hikari City, with about 20 researchers participating.
It is planned that the machine will be manufactured, disclosed to enterprises and used for technical research by 2023.
This will be the first time that a domestic company will launch a general-purpose quantum computer that can complete a wide range of calculations, or become a catalyst for a new generation of technologies that affect industrial competitiveness and defense security.
The report pointed out that compared to supercomputers, quantum computers are extremely fast in computing, and have the potential to bring technological innovation to the development of materials and other aspects, affecting the competitiveness of various industries including chemistry, pharmaceuticals, automotive and finance.
Since April this year, Fujitsu and Fujitsu have started joint research on material design in cooperation with Fujitsu Film Co., Ltd., and will increase partners in the future to accumulate knowledge for future applications.
Compared with overseas companies, in Japan, IBM set up a self-developed quantum computer in Kawasaki in 2021, and the development speed is relatively slow.
Fujitsu gained technology and experience from the Institute of Physics and Chemistry as the first real opportunity for a Japanese company.
Like Google and IBM, quantum computing will be performed using “superconducting ” circuits that are cooled at extremely low temperatures to eliminate resistance.
The report said that the manufacturing of quantum computers has been dominated by American technology companies.
Google achieved what it calls “quantum transcendence ” in 2019, and it can solve the 10,000 year problem of a supercomputer in about three minutes.
In recent years, China's technology has also been improving, and emerging companies have also clearly risen.
Japan currently ranks third in the world in patent distribution in the field of quantum computers, behind only the United States and China.
The report pointed out that the computer developed by Fujitsu in 2023 reached 64 qubits, more than the 53 qubits that Google achieved when it achieved quantum transcendence.
This is second only to the 127 qubits developed by IBM in 2021, which are also considered to achieve highly competitive performance in the world.
Fujitsu is expected to achieve more than 1,000 qubits after 2026.
Quantum computers have the potential to perform supercomputer calculations in minutes and hours that take hundreds of millions of years.
The Boston Consulting Group predicts that economic benefits of up to $850 billion will be realized around 2040 through the development of new materials and more.

Chasing the waves, sniffing the business opportunities, two Israeli veterans create a hotel designed for remote workers, targeting millennials and Gen Z, while catching the subscription trend, even hotels can "let you stay full."
Text: Crystal (Innovative Latte)
When it comes to travel, different groups have different needs.
Therefore, from tour groups to hotels, attractions, there are specific segments of the audience.
There are honeymooners, relatives, silver-haired people, medical and beauty people, etc. Today, tourism companies are targeting a group of newcomers: remote workers.
Remote workers, also known as “Digital Nomads ”, are a group of people who can work remotely from anywhere in the world.
They can travel all over the world while working online.
The number of people working remotely has increased dramatically since COVID-19 swept the world, and many of these companies allow employees to travel internationally while working.
Tourism operators have sensed this opportunity and have begun to provide exclusive accommodation and travel services for remote workers.
But as early as 2014, when remote work was not so popular, two retired Israeli soldiers, Rafael Museri and Danielle Rudasevski, had already observed this niche demand.
They crossed the ocean and opened Selina, the first hotel for remote workers in the Central American country of Panama. Ten years later, Selina not only survived COVID-19, which hit the tourism industry hard, but also has 163 hotels in 23 countries around the world, making it a “travel subscription ”.
How did they go from military to a new generation of tourism stars?
The story begins in 2004 when two young Israelis met.
Innovation: A subscription-based hotel integrated into a co-working space that allows travelers to travel and work
Chasing the waves, sniffing the business opportunities
In 2004, Daniel Rudasevski, who retired from the Israeli army, came to Costa Rica, also a Central American country, because of his love of surfing.
Through the introduction of friends, he met Rafael Museri, also an Israeli, who also retired from the Israeli army.
They saw Costa Rica ’ s development opportunities and returned to Israel to raise investment from friends and family, develop real estate and earn their first pot of gold.
But Costa Rica ’ s saturated market allows them to look for their next potential market.
From other surfers, Daniel and Rafael hear about Panama, the Central American nation, and its beautiful coastline along the Caribbean Sea.
Based on the passion of surfers, or the precision of business intuition, after visiting Panama several times, they fell in love with the beautiful beach and the simple town of Pedasi, a four-hour drive from the capital, Panama City.
With just a few thousand inhabitants, this town has become a must-see for many who love surfing, beaches and staying away from tourists.
But in 2008, the town didn ’ t have many foreign investors or tourists, and the roads were bumpy.
Taking advantage of the global financial turmoil in 2008 and the housing market being at a low point, two young people in their 30s decided to develop a series of seaside homes and storefronts here.
They returned to Israel to raise funds from family and friends, and even to recruit their own friends, opening coffee shops, restaurants and hostels in Pedasi.
By 2013, they had 12 properties in Pedasi: a shopping mall, a resort, a bakery, a coffee shop, and a bar.
The opportunity comes from their own experience: after staying in more than 120 hotels, they believe that the market still lacks a high-quality, interactive experience between the main passengers, and affordable accommodation service.
They want to create a space where travelers can feel a sense of belonging, leave unforgettable memories, and have a place to work and build relationships with others.
A hotel designed for remote workers, targeting millennials and Gen Z
Whether out of intuition or from years of experience in property development, Daniel and Rafael have caught a rising wave of travel like surfing.
Since building the first Selina hotel, they have targeted Millennials (people born between 1981 and 1996) and Gen Z (people born between 1995 and 2010).
They believe that millennials prefer to work remotely and will increasingly prefer to travel while working.
So, in this beachfront hotel, they introduced the coworking space, which was gradually popular at the time.
This allows visitors, whether they are freelancers, corporate employees, digital nomads (people who work digitally, can do their jobs via computers and the Internet, and do not need to enter the office), to complete a high volume of work while traveling.
Daniel and Rafael observe that millennials are finding it increasingly difficult to separate their lives from their work: even while traveling, they are constantly checking their phones, their company mailboxes, and keeping up with their work.
Whether they are remote workers or not, a co-working space can help them with their work.
On the other hand, co-working spaces not only help millennials get work done, but also help them reduce their inner loneliness.
Daniel and Rafael also observed that despite growing up on the Internet and in 3C products, millennials often feel lonely.
So they gave Selina Hotel an alternative KPI: how many friends can a traveler make at Selina Hotel.
At Selina Hotel, people from different industries can meet and communicate through co-working spaces.
In addition, Selina Hotel also arranges local artists to visit the hotel from time to time to interact with guests.
Selina will also invite musicians, artists, and yoga teachers to travel for free without selling beds, which will increase the variety of activities at the hotel without increasing operating costs. In 2021, 66% of travelers said they made at least one friend in Selina.
Subscription: All-you-can-travel
Selina Hotel is also unique in that it adopts a subscription system.
Most hotels use a single transaction, accumulate membership points, and exchange for room upgrades or free accommodation in the future.
This is mainly due to the fact that most travelers (especially non-business travelers) spend less frequently on hotel accommodations.

Blind box, for what?
Font Size:
Source: Economic Daily
Author: She Ying
Blind box, which at first sounds like something for children to play with, what can you handle?
It really is.
Recently, the Shanghai Municipal Market Supervision Bureau issued China's first blind box business compliance guidelines, put forward some compliance standards, such as a single blind box should not exceed 200 yuan (RMB, the same below, 40 Singapore dollars), live animals, special food and other blind box sales, and prohibit blind box disguised gambling, lottery business, etc.
Compliance guidelines are generally found in financial, pharmaceutical and other industries, or in key areas such as antitrust.
The marketing innovation of the toy industry has led the regulatory authorities to formulate compliance guidelines, on the one hand, indicating that the pre-regulatory threshold has moved forward, and the supervision is more refined, on the other hand, it also shows that the blind box chaos has a tendency to expand to other areas and needs timely guidance.
Blind box is not new, nor is it unique to China.
Japanese stores have always had a "lucky bag" business method, putting several kinds of goods together, selling at preferential prices, consumers buy hands, open to know what is inside.
This "lucky bag" can be regarded as the predecessor of the blind box.
But it is essentially a promotional means, consumers a picture cheap, two pictures of the actual use of goods function.
In recent years, the "lucky bag" gradually transparent, let consumers clearly choose the preferential; at the same time, the blind box appeared, but also with the tide play, in the United States, Japan and other countries in full bloom.
Although it has become an "experience school" that only needs to be owned, its ecology is still relatively benign, and the tide of fans can support themselves.
But with more and more speculators eyeing the blind box circle, the blind box gradually "blind", and repeatedly speculated the sky-high price, shocking.
Industry linkage is another push for the blind box out of the circle, ticket blind box, food blind box, hotel blind box so that consumers who do not care about the tide are also familiar with the word.
Some cross-border blind boxes maintain the "lucky bag" attribute, still focus on promotion, such as in the ticket blind box, the blind box is only an interesting carrier, consumers want preferential tickets.
This kind of stimulus plus concessions has effectively stimulated consumption, which is a relatively successful innovation.
On the contrary, the sales of blind box as the main business, blind box itself is the object of purchase, the stimulation is still in, but the concessions are gone; plus some enterprises engage in "hunger marketing", let the cattle hype, if long-term, it is likely that the cattle are still there, but the fans are gone.
There are also some industries that improperly introduce blind boxes, such as pet blind boxes that cause the death of small animals, and fast food blind boxes that have been criticized by the Chinese Consumer Association for wasting food, which have caused negative effects.
These are the main reasons why regulators cannot sit idly by.
Shanghai issued compliance guidelines, first limited blind box business is limited to life consumption, arts and entertainment and other fields, not "everything can be blind box", guide blind box to play the advantages of driving consumption, to avoid disorder cross-border, resulting in adverse effects.
Second, the emphasis on the risk of speculation, such as not to induce non-player users to join the speculation speculation, deliberately causing sharp fluctuations in the price of the second-hand market.
At the same time, merchants are also required to publish the rules for drawing boxes, the probability of hidden money extraction, and so on.
It should be said that these measures pinpoint the risk point of disorder in the blind box market and reflect the purpose of promoting development by standardization.
China has always taken an inclusive and prudent approach to the regulation of new formats, and this blind box compliance guide is no exception: it is only a guiding document, not a mandatory standard.
Scarce commodities naturally have investment properties, it is difficult to avoid speculation. The nature of the hype blind box is not much different from the hype of Dutch tulips and high-priced Pu'er tea.
A paper file may be difficult to make the abnormal hype of the blind box dumb fire, more to play a role in expressing attitudes and prompting risks, but as the first blind box industry standard in the country, from scratch is a kind of progress in itself.
At present, the head company Bubble Mart has stated that it will gradually explore specific solutions that can be landed in accordance with the compliance guidelines.
Enterprises themselves also said that a healthy and orderly tide play market is not only conducive to protecting the rights and interests of consumers, but also can create a good development space for enterprises. Blind box is already a large industry of 100 billion yuan, and will also be linked with many industries, and it is necessary to adhere to the rules of transparency and openness to avoid blind development.

In Belgium, on the other hand, employees are entitled to work four days a week, but the working hours are extended each day, and the total number of hours worked per week remains the same, and so far the results appear to be mixed.

While there are examples of productivity gains, it depends on the field and type of work.
In other cases, reduced working hours mean employers need to hire more people.
At the same time, there are also concerns that wages may be reduced, and some people may face greater pressure by working longer hours per day.

Preventing falls in the elderly, strengthening muscles and joints
September is Fall Prevention Month.
Elderly people fall is very common and the impact is very large, causing severe fractures, stroke and even death, said Wu An An, a physical therapist at On House.
Tips to prevent falls, such as enhancing muscle joint flexibility, sitting down or getting up slowly, shoes suitable for non-slip.
Wu Anan said that falls are common among the elderly and have a great impact.
According to the data, each year 3 million elderly people fall emergency department, one fifth of them are seriously injured, need to be admitted to hospital or even surgery, if there is a fracture, head injury, it is difficult to restore the previous mobility, and even to receive long-term care or go to a nursing home for long-term care.
Many elderly people suffer from osteoporosis and fall resulting in fractures.
If the elderly take drugs to reduce blood pressure, the head will be injured, there will be cerebral hemorrhage, internal bleeding, serious stroke and even death.
Wu said that there are two reasons for elderly people to fall, either physical condition or environmental reasons.
If the elderly have osteoporosis, arthritis, bones and muscles are not solid, inconvenient to move; or walk with balance problems, dizziness due to side effects of taking drugs; or have vision problems; or because they have fallen, afraid of falling, but prone to falling.
"After the old man falls once, his family or doctor may blame him, 'Why are you so careless?'"
Injuries after a fall cause inconvenience to movement, loss of self-care, affect the mood of the elderly, and produce depression.
Because of the fear of falling, the elderly simply do not move, resulting in rapid decline in physical function and rapid muscle atrophy.
When it is necessary to walk, it is easy to fall. ”
In addition, environmental reasons can also lead to falls.
For example, there is not enough light in the home of the elderly, and there are no handrails in the toilets and stairs, and the staircase design is too curved and the stairs are too narrow.
Many wires are laid on the ground, the bathroom is very wet, and the shoes in the home or the auxiliary tools used are not suitable, which can also lead to falls.
Wu Anan said that there are many ways to prevent falls.
For example, strengthen muscle and joint flexibility to help balance.
Elderly people are also encouraged to check their eyes and ears regularly to understand the side effects of the drug.
Family can help explain.
Seniors need to make sure they get enough sleep.
Usually, waking up in the morning is not awake and prone to fall.
It is recommended that the elderly sit down or get up slowly to avoid dizziness.
"When walking, the elderly should be careful that the road is wet and the ground is uneven.
In addition, shoes should be non-slip.
There are many people like to wear slippers, but it is not necessarily suitable, it is best to find shoes that cover the front and back of the foot, so it is the safest.
The elderly should also pay attention to the situation at home, check the power lines on the ground, whether there are handrails in the bathroom, whether there is anything blocking the stairs, and whether the things they want to take can be reached at once, so as to avoid the possibility of falling down when they climb high and low. "
Wu said that if an elderly person falls and has an injury, he must notify the doctor.
“Sometimes, the elderly have fractures and don ’ t feel the pain immediately.
Or head injury bleeding, because of taking medicine and other reasons, they do not know.
It is important to inform the doctor about the fall and treat it as soon as possible.
It can also help doctors or therapists understand the cause of falls and prevent the next fall. ”
She reminded that the elderly can do exercise or balance ability at home.
Such as holding a stool or a fixed object, with the help of family members to exercise.
If an elderly person needs assistance tools, such as walking aids or crutches, do not use them on the grounds that they are independent.
When the elderly stand up firmly, get up slowly.
It ’ s all about staying active, participating in social activities, and getting in a better mood.
"Family members can encourage them to exercise."
Wu An-an said that the role of a physical therapist is to help the elderly to have a safety check every six months to ensure that their physical functions have not changed significantly.
And according to the interests of the elderly to develop sports, maintain independence.
When they fall, they go to the door to see if the situation has changed.
Timely education for the elderly to help them exercise, relieve arthritis, osteoporosis and low back pain.

Population question: How many people can our planet feed?
• Zalia Gerwitt
(by Zaria Gorvett)
At this moment, the valley, which is a swampy valley at the bottom, is still calm and peaceful, with green grass and palm trees casting faint shadows on the water, and fish quietly hiding under the mangroves, where orangutans are searching for fruit with their tenacious fingers.
Then, with a bang of thunder, a sleeping giant suddenly wakes up from his sleep.
It was around 72000 BC in Sumatra, Indonesia.
This is the moment when the Toba supervolcano suddenly erupted.
It is believed to be the largest volcanic eruption on Earth in the past 100,000 years.
A series of thunderous explosions produced 9.5 trillion kilograms of volcanic ash, which rolled into the sky, forming a dark cloud that quickly spread to the atmosphere about 47 kilometers above the ground.
After the eruption of the Toba Supervolcano, a huge area of Asia was covered by a layer of 3 to 10 cm thick volcanic dust, which blocked the water source and stuck to the vegetation like cement, and even deposits from the eruption were found in East Africa, 7,300 km west of the volcano.
And most importantly, some scientists believe that this supervolcano eruption has plunged the world into a volcanic winter that has lasted for decades, almost killing us all.
As early as 1993, a team of researchers in the United States studied the human genome in order to find clues to the long history of mankind, and found a major sign left by the "population bottleneck" era in the human genome, indicating that at some point, the number of humans has shrunk sharply, and since then, all human descendants outside Africa are significantly more closely related than before.
Later research revealed that this dramatic decline in human numbers may have occurred 50,000 to 100,000 years ago, when our total human population may have been as low as 10,000, equivalent to the population of Elkhorn, a quiet small county town in Wisconsin, USA, or the number of people attending a car-free wedding in Malaysia during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
At the time, the region least affected by the bottleneck was Africa, where genetic diversity is still high to this day, and on the African continent, genetic differences between certain groups are greater than those between Africans and Europeans.
Some people think that this timing is not by chance, they think that the culprit of the rapid decline in the global population is the eruption of the Toba volcano.
This view has been hotly debated, but there can be no doubt that humanity in all regions of the world suffered a great existential catastrophe, and today most of our human species evolved from a small but hyper-tenacious group of human ancestors.
Today, 74000 years later, our species of hairless apes, once endangered by a volcanic eruption, is experiencing another big explosion, a big explosion in our human numbers.
Now we humans have climbed mountains into the sea, occupying every habitat on the planet, and we have our footprints even in the most remote corners. In 2018, scientists discovered a human plastic bag at the bottom of the Mariana Trench, a seabed 10,898 meters below sea level, and another scientific team recently discovered man-made “perpetuating chemicals ” on Mount Everest.".
Today, no part of the world is pristine, and every lake, every forest, and every gorge is more or less disturbed by human activity.
At the same time, the sheer size and intelligence of the human race have enabled us to accomplish great things beyond the reach of other animals, such as splitting the atom, sending complex equipment into space nearly 1.6 million kilometers away to observe the forming planets in distant galaxies, and creating extremely colorful art and culture, the sheer size and diversity of which is difficult to measure.
For example, we take a total of 4.1 billion photos every day, and the number of words used to communicate with each other is as high as 80 to 127 trillion.
The United Nations predicts that on November 15, 2022, there will be 8 billion people living on Earth, 800,000 times the number of survivors of the Toba disaster 74000 years ago.
Today, humans have such a large population but so little genetic diversity (outside Africa) that one researcher recently observed that it would not be surprising to find someone who looks strikingly similar to a stranger without blood ties, given that the human limited gene pool is constantly circulating and that there are about 370,000 new babies born every day.
The explosion in human numbers also led to a huge divergence of opinion.
In fact, there is an emerging school of thought that the number of humans is not enough and that the population needs to grow further. In 2018, tech billionaire Jeff Bezos predicted that in the future, the human population will reach a new decimal milestone, with 1 trillion people migrating to the solar system. Bezos announced that he is making this a reality. Targets and plans.
But others, including the BBC and the natural historian Sir David Attenborough, have called the massive expansion of our planet the “plague of the earth. ”
In this way, almost every environmental problem we face today, from climate change to biodiversity loss, from water stress to land conflicts, can be traced back to the explosion of our population over the centuries.
Back in 1994, when the global population was only 5.5 billion, a team from Stanford University in California calculated that the ideal human population size should be between 1.5 billion and 2 billion.
So far, the debate about the ideal size of the planet ’ s population has been as varied and emotional as ever, but in any case, there is not much time left for us humans to decide which is the best trend in population size.
The ancient humans began to worry about the population.
In the late 1980s, a group of archaeologists at the University of Baghdad unearthed an abandoned library in the ancient city of Sippar in central Iraq.
In the sand, dust and ancient walls, 400 pieces of clay were found, buried in this academic tomb, forgotten for more than 3,500 years, but still on the shelves that the Babylonian added to the library.
Four of the clay tablets are special and contain fragments of a mythical story from Mesopotamia.
This myth is found throughout Mesopotamia in the four clay tablets found in documents, and the account of these four tablets is the missing part of the myth, which continues to fascinate historians today.
On the clay slab is an epic poem, “Atra-hasis, ” written by an unnamed scribe in the 17th century BC, which says,“ Before 1200 years [since God created man], man has expanded the land and multiplied … ”
The legend of the Great Flood, in which civilizations were destroyed by gods and resurrected after death, has been found in cultures around the world with similar themes and different forms of ancient flood mythology. These four clay tablets record the Mesopotamian version, which may be the earliest mention of overpopulation in human history.
In Mesopotamia ’ s Flood mythology, the gods were annoyed by all the “noise ” and“ commotion ” made by humans, as well as by the “roaring of the earth like a bull ”, as they were pressured by the insatiable need for human greed.
Enlil, the god of the earth and air, decided to release some calamities to constantly reduce the number of humans, so designed pestilence, famine and drought to be triggered every 1200 years.
Fortunately, on the day of this cycle disaster, another god saved humanity.
So Enlil plans a great flood... followed by the classic story of a human hero who built a ship to save humanity and life.
At the time of writing, the world's population was estimated to be between 27 and 50 million, equivalent to the number of people currently living in Cameroon or South Korea, or between 0.3 and 0.6 percent of the world's population today.
In the following millennium, scholars seemed to have had little say on population issues.
It was only in the ancient Greek era that humanity was once again thinking about population.
The philosopher Plato had some drastic views.
After the population of Athens, the Greek city-state state, doubled in size, Plato lamented, “What is left is like a skeleton that is consumed by disease; the fertile soil is washed away, leaving only the whole desolate earth. ”
Plato not only argued that the state should strictly control the population, he also concluded that the ideal urban population should not exceed 5,040, and that the establishment of colonies was a good way to reduce the overpopulation of the city-states, and he also believed that it was important to curb consumption.

Plato ’ s masterpiece The Republic, written around 375 BC, describes two hypothetical city-states (city-states are administrative areas that resemble small states), one healthy, one “extravagant ” and one“ fanatical. ”
In the second city-state, the population was swollen and greedy, and consumption was unrestrained until its consumption “exceeded the limits of its necessities. ”
Alas, this morally depraved city-state went so far as to seize the land of its neighbors in order to satisfy its needs, which naturally turned into a war between city-states, because it could not feed its surplus and greedy population without taking additional resources from outside.
Plato here raises a question that is still hotly debated throughout the ages: Is population a problem, or is the resource consumed by the population a problem?
More than 500 years after Plato, the scale of the global population explosion became clear.
Tertullian, a theologian who lived in the Roman city of Carthage, looked like modern human observation across millennia and prophesied that the earth ’ s population had increased and that the natural environment had been destroyed.
By 200 A.D., when Tertullian made this judgment, the world's population had reached between 190 million and 256 million, roughly equivalent to the number of people currently living in Nigeria or Indonesia.
The Prophet believed that "the whole world has been on the hunt, and so many people have become a burden on the earth... because nature has been unable to sustain our human existence."
In the following 1500 years, the global population more than doubled.
Eventually, the theologian ’ s detached concern for the population turned into a real panic.
Then came Thomas Malthus.
He was an English pastor with a pessimistic bent.
In his famous book An Essay on the Principle of Population, published in 1798, he first presupposes two important observations: that one needs to eat to survive, and that one loves to make love to reproduce.
He explained that it is logical to conclude that these two simple facts will eventually lead to human needs exceeding the Earth ’ s supply.
In his book, Marsas states that "the population, if left unchecked, will multiply in geometric series, and the food that sustains human existence will only grow at arithmetic rates."
One needs only a little knowledge of the numbers to know that the power of the first rate of increase is infinitely greater than that of the second. "In other words, in a positive feedback cycle, a large population leads to a larger number of offspring, but our ability to produce food does not increase in the same accelerated way.
Such a concise statement immediately had an immediate effect, provoking intense fear in some people, and anger in others, an emotion of fear and anger that has persisted throughout society for decades.
The former believes that something must be done to stop the human population from getting out of control.
The latter argues that limiting the population is both absurd and immoral, and that every effort should be made to increase food production.
There are also a few who are particularly dissatisfied with the English Poor Laws, which came into force in Britain hundreds of years ago, because the Poor Law provides subsidies to people living in poverty to help them raise children, such as in the case of the Malthusian population, which encourages the poor to have more children and is detrimental to population control.
At the time of Malthus's publication, there were 800 million people on Earth.
Then came 1968, when Stanford University professor Paul Ehrlich and his wife, Anne Ehrlich, published The Population Bomb.
The book was inspired by an experience of the academic couple in the Indian city of Delhi.
One night, as they returned to their hotel by taxi, they passed a slum and were horrified by the crowded crowd on the street.
Their account of the experience was criticized, especially when London was more than twice as populous as Delhi.
The scholarly couple wrote this book out of fear of mass starvation.
They believe that famine is coming, especially in developing countries, and even places like the United States, where people are beginning to notice the impact of population growth on the environment.
It is widely believed that much of the current anxiety about overpopulation is due to the Ellich couple ’ s book, but there are also accusations that Population Bomb is provoking unfounded panic.
Whether this book is positive or critical depends on your point of view.
Of course, there has never been a purely academic discussion about how many people the planet should have.
Demography is sometimes used to legitimize crimes such as persecution, ethnic cleansing, and genocide.
In each particular case, the perpetrators are not trying to reduce the number of people as a whole, but are trying to reduce the population of a particular group, such as people of a particular social class, religion or race, but these human crimes are sometimes seen as examples of similar dangers arising from overpopulation.
The UK Poverty Act was repealed and replaced with stricter laws.
Partly this was because Marsas feared that the social class (he called it the “peasants ”) would have more orphans locked up in squalid squalid penitentiaries because they had too many children, as depicted in Charles Dickens ’ novel Oliver Twist.
Over the next century or two, eugenics continued to be disguised as a population control theory or supported by population control movements, such as the forced sterilization of ethnic minorities in the United States in the 1970s.
Population control is also used to restrict individual freedom. In the 1980s, China introduced the controversial one-child policy, which is widely seen as a violation of human sexual and reproductive rights.
The future of population will continue to be contentious.
The population control plan has been controversial in the past, and now the support and opposition are even more divided.
Today, any policy to increase or reduce population quotas or targets is almost universally condemned, with the exception of a few extremist groups.
These measures to encourage population control are considered to lead to coercion or other atrocities and are at high risk.
But beyond that, there is little consensus on other aspects of population issues.
At the other end of the population debate, some see low fertility in some areas as a crisis.
A demographer who is so worried about a drop in the UK ’ s local birth rate has suggested a tax on childless adults.
As of 2019, the UK has an average of 1.65 children per woman, which is below the generational replacement level, i.e. the average fertility rate of 2.075 needed to maintain the same population size, but the UK population is still growing due to the addition of immigrants from other countries.
The opposite view is that reducing and ultimately halting global population growth is not only very controllable and desirable, but can be achieved by completely voluntary means, such as providing contraceptives and contraceptives to those who are willing to use them, and educating women.
Proponents of this view argue that slowing population growth in this way not only benefits the planet, but also improves the quality of life of people in the poorest countries around the world.
Population Matters, a UK-based charity, is one NGO that believes in such a solution.
The organization is committed to achieving sustainable growth in the global population.
They argue for addressing the pressures of consumerism, especially in developed countries, on the planet, while emphasizing the role that population size must play in this regard.
To this end, they urge people to take personal responsibility for the environmental crisis while eliminating global poverty and inequality through debt relief and overseas aid.
Robin Maynard, director of Population Matters, said: “We are saddened by any form of population control or coercion, and restrictions on reproductive choice.
Therefore, our job is to focus on the population, give people the right to choose, and act in accordance with human rights. Let people choose for themselves and make decisions that are good for the planet, and this is the most effective way to deal with the population.
""
On the other hand, some argue that shifting the focus of attention away from adjusting the size of the world ’ s population to human behavior, no matter how moderate or indirect this adjustment may be, will help improve the planet ’ s environment.
Supporters of this view argue that the amount of resources consumed by each individual has more or less an impact on our collective human influence.
They also point out that resource consumption is significantly high in rich countries with low birth rates.
Reducing our personal need for the planet can reduce our carbon footprint without stifling economic growth in poor countries
The West's intention to reduce population growth in the underdeveloped parts of the world has been criticized as racist, as the overall population density in Europe and North America is actually higher than in the underdeveloped parts of the world.
Finally, for this long-standing demographic problem, there is a fatalistic “solution ”, listen to it and do nothing to control it.
This view is based on the fact that the global population has been in a highly unstable dynamic, with a significant increase in population, but then a decline.
People from every point of view are likely to get the results they want, though not forever.
Estimates of future global population growth trends vary, but are expected to reach a “population peak ” around 2070 or 2080, when the global population will be between 9.4 billion and 10.4 billion.
This is likely to be a slow growth process, and if it reaches 10.4 billion, the United Nations is expected to maintain this level for up to 20 years, with the final population expected to decline.
A recent book, “Empty Planet: The Shock of Global Population Decline, ” offers us a picture of the world ’ s future that is quite different from what we usually expect.
The authors of this book anticipate that humanity will face new challenges and opportunities brought about by the global population decline.
Population issues are too controversial and uncertain, and we may find it difficult to start thinking about how to deal with them.
Here are a few key aspects of how the size of the planet ’ s population could affect our future lives: the environment, the economy, and our collective well-being.
Environmental challenges
The BBC documentary “Indian Ocean with Simon Reeve ” has a scene like this: we see the camera with a shaking hand-held lens, shuttling through the dense forests of Madagascar.
All of a sudden, a blurry white thing popped out and disappeared across the lens into the distance.
This is a lemur, a shy and haunted monkey with long limbs, pale fur and dark complexion, like a lanky teddy bear.
After this scene, Simon Riff quickly gives the audience a surprising hint about the expedition ’ s lucky discovery: it ’ s not a wilderness forest at all, but the Berenty Reserve in southern Madagascar, a small forest surrounded by commercial plantations on all sides and one of the few remaining homes for the rare animal lemurs.
Speaking at the reserve visitor centre, Simon Rieff said that according to credible information he had obtained, almost all photographers photographing wildlife in the reserve went deep into the forest and set their equipment where the lemurs were most numerous, trying to avoid shooting any buildings.
Viewers may think they peek into an uncharted wilderness world, but you can argue that what the audience actually sees is through a carefully curated illusion of pristine nature.
The BBC documentary highlights the "wilderness myth" deliberately created by humans.
If the spectacular beauty of the natural world presented in the lens completely excludes humans and their footprints from the lens, or downplays the ubiquitous nature of humans, suggesting that there are still large unexplored virgin lands on Earth outside of human activities, this misconception is the “wilderness myth ”.
Satellite imagery is a particularly powerful tool for crushing wilderness myths, because from a bird ’ s eye view from high above, it can be found that the lands of many countries have been completely occupied by humans.
For example, the land that lemurs live in, when you look at it, you can see that the farmland is connected to the sky, and there are roads and rows of buildings between them.
Due to large-scale engineering or forest development, in just a few decades, the landscape of some areas has become completely unrecognizable.
The dramatic changes in Earth's ecology due to human behavior are supported by some startling data.
According to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization, 38% of the earth ’ s land is developed for human and livestock production of food and other crops, such as fuel crops, with a total area of up to 5 billion hectares.
Although our modern ancestors lived in the world of raptor beasts, living alongside mammoths, giant wombats and 450-kilogram elephant birds, today only humans are the dominant species in the entire vast land vertebrate population, from geckos to lemurs.
By weight, humans now make up 32% of terrestrial vertebrates, while wild terrestrial vertebrates make up only 1% of the total.
The rest are livestock raised by humans.
The World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), an NGO that protects wildlife, found that between 1970 and 2020, wildlife numbers fell by two-thirds, while the global human population more than doubled during that period.
In fact, as our dominance of the planet has increased, so have many changes in the planet ’ s ecology. From primatologist Jane Goodall, known for chimpanzee research, to naturalist and television presenter Chris Packham, many prominent environmentalists have expressed their concerns. In 2013, Sir David Attenborough was interviewed by Radio Times "The smaller the population, the easier it will be to solve all the environmental problems we face, and the larger the population, the more difficult it will be to solve, and ultimately impossible to solve."
Some have decided to have fewer or no children because of concerns about the human environmental footprint, including Britain ’ s Prince Harry and wife Meghan, who announced in 2019 that they would not have more than two children for the sake of the planet.
In the same year, American singer Miley Cyrus also announced that she would not have children because the earth was “angry ”.
More and more women are joining the anti-fertility movement, calling for a “birth-strike ” unless the current climate emergency and species extinction crisis are resolved.
This anti-fertility trend was supported in 2017 by a study that calculated that in developed countries, just one fewer child would reduce one person ’ s annual carbon emissions by 58.6 tons of “carbon dioxide emissions, ” about 24 times the emissions of a car.
In 2019, a study led by Jennifer Sciubba, associate professor of international studies at Rhodes College in Tennessee, analyzed population growth levels in more than 1,000 areas across 22 European countries between 1990 and 2006 and compared these data to changes in urban land use patterns and CO2 emissions over the same period.
The research team concluded that the absolute number of people in Western Europe had a "considerable influence" on these environmental parameters, but in Eastern Europe it was not the most important factor.
While there are many other studies that support the idea that environmental degradation is caused by population growth, there are also many that argue that environmental degradation is not caused by population growth but by an increasing demand for natural resources, especially in rich countries.
In fact, many environmentalists now believe that the current problems facing humanity are mainly due to consumption, not overpopulation. From this perspective, the worry about overpopulation is unfairly shifting the blame for the deterioration of the bad situation to poorer countries.
A 2021 study found that both population growth and the use of non-renewable energy in the United States are contributing to environmental degradation.
Another study found that China ’ s economic growth and use of natural resources from 1980 to 2017 led to higher CO2 emissions.
Interestingly, other studies have found that while China ’ s use of natural resources and urbanization have increased the rate of environmental destruction, some of the damage has been offset by “human capital, ” or human knowledge and skills.
Today, it is widely believed that humans are putting unsustainable pressure on the world's limited resources, which is known as the "Earth's Ecological Overload Day" phenomenon.
The so-called Earth Ecological Overload Day refers to the fact that humans have used up all the biological resources that the earth can sustainably regenerate throughout the year, and the rest of the year is a load. The Earth Overload Day in 2010 is August 8, and the year 2022 is July 28.
Sciubba, author of “8 Billion and Counting: How Sex, Death, and Migration Shape our World, ” says that“ I can ’ t understand why an increase in population is beneficial to the environment, whether it ’ s because there are too many people, or because people consume too many resources, or both. ”
Perhaps one solution, she suggested, would be to see people and the environment as one, “but children, that ’ s a hard argument to make. ”
However, Shuba is keen to point out that the idea of a “population bomb ” in Ellich ’ s book that is about to destroy the planet is outdated.
“I think at that time (the time of writing this book), women in 127 countries in the world had an average of five or more children in their lifetime, ” she said.
In those times, demographic trends did seem to be growing exponentially, but Schuber argues that the demographic panic created by the book has continued into the minds of certain generations that are still alive today.
“But today there are only eight countries (with a fertility rate of more than five children), so I think it ’ s important for us to recognize that these trends have changed, ” says Shuba.
Increasing population is conducive to economic development
In 2012, the Singapore government devised an unusual way for people to celebrate national independence, spreading the important message of multiple births through a new rap song.
This short film showcases Singapore ’ s cultural and scenic attractions with colourful images, as well as encouraging young couples to have more children.
The song ’ s lyrics read: “… Let ’ s make a little man like you and me, explore your body like a night safari, I ’ m a patriotic husband, you ’ re a patriotic wife, let me come into your camp and create life … ”
Singapore released this song to encourage fertility because the government is worried about the low fertility rate.
By 2020, Singapore ’ s fertility rate will be only 1.1 children per woman.
This is an extreme example of a general downward trend in fertility in rich countries.
People in rich countries marry later and choose to have fewer children.
In Singapore, this phenomenon has led to fears that the population decline may be detrimental to the country ’ s economic development, so the Singapore government has urged citizens to have more children if they love the country.
It is a central concept in economics that the more people a country has, the more goods or services it produces and the more its citizens consume, so population growth is the best catalyst for economic growth.
This is one of the reasons why concerns about population growth in developing countries are sometimes seen as a problem.
Many developed countries already have quite high population densities, which is partly why these countries have become rich.
But now denying other countries the opportunity to become rich would be considered unfair, even racist.
However, a slowdown in population growth is not necessarily accompanied by a recession.
Take Japan, for example, whose fertility rate has fallen below replacement level in other rich countries as early as 1966, when Japan ’ s fertility rate suddenly dropped from around 2 to 1.6.
Andrew Mason, an emeritus professor in the Department of Economics at the University of Hawaii, said, “If you look at the standard of living in Japan, I don ’ t think Japan ’ s recession has reached the level that some have described. ”
They invest a lot of money in human capital, so they have fewer children, but they value education and have a very good healthcare system. ”
Mason also notes that savings and investment are also common in Japan, “so [money] capital has increased and productivity has improved. ”
If these factors are combined … I think Japan is a good case study for why Japan is not panicking [about declining birth rates]. ”
In addition to fertility factors, there are other ways for a country to develop its economy.
Often, Mason notes, the introduction of immigrants provides a new source of labor that contributes to economic development and does not add to the total human population.
But in some countries, immigration is still a controversial and highly politicized topic, so it is impossible to choose this method to slow population decline if the nationals of these countries do not have a cultural shift towards immigration.
"Especially countries like Japan and South Korea, which have been very resistant to immigration, will gradually find that it will be more and more good for them," Mason said.
Similarly, the benefits of immigration to countries of introduction are highly uneven in nature, with one country bringing in immigrants for economic growth but another suffering from the loss of workers.
There is a growing realization that the global obsession with economic growth at all costs is outdated and should be abandoned altogether. “One thing that frustrates me about the overpopulation debate is that a lot of the comments are coming from the same people who say we don ’ t want too many people, but we also want to make sure that the economy keeps growing. ”
“In a world of declining populations, we really need to completely change our mindset and stop thinking that economic growth equals progress, ” she said.
A happy future.
However, demographics affect not only the earth ’ s environment and the economy of human society, but also a powerful hidden force that affects the quality of life of people around the world.
According to Alex Ezeh, a professor of global health at Drexel University in Pennsylvania, the absolute size of a country ’ s population is not the most important factor.
On the contrary, the rate of population growth or decline is the key to a country ’ s future development prospects, because it determines how quickly things change.
Ize explained that in Africa, for example, the current rate of population growth varies greatly among African countries, and whether it is good or bad depends on which region of Africa you are talking about.
"In some countries, particularly in southern Africa (one of the five major regions of Africa as defined by the United Nations), contraceptive use has increased, fertility has indeed declined, and population growth has declined, which is partly good news," he said.
In some Central African countries, population growth remains high due to high fertility rates and high life expectancy.
In some places, population growth rates are much higher than 2.5% per year, “which is quite high, ” he said.
In some countries in Central Africa, the population doubles every 20 years or so.
Even in the same region of Africa, different countries will choose different paths, with East Africa ’ s two neighbors, Burundi and Rwanda, as examples. While the former still has a higher level of growth, 5.3 children per woman, the latter growth is slowing, with Rwanda having 3.9 children per woman in 2020, compared to 4.5 in 2010.
“I think the discussion about population size and economic numbers is wrong.
If you think about a city whose population doubles every 10 years, and this is a city in Africa, which African government has the resources to improve every existing infrastructure every 10 years to keep the coverage of existing services at a normal level? ”
The explanation for this is that it is difficult to maintain the development of human capital, especially in conditions of extreme population growth, because research has found that human capital plays an important role in the well-being of urban residents, even more important than how much they earn.
Human capital is also considered to be another important predictor of a country ’ s economic growth in addition to population size.
“When economists think about it, large populations have a big impact on many different outcomes, but do you get to this huge population size in 10, 100 years, or 1,000 years later? ”
The excessive length of time that has been achieved makes it possible to create the right structures in the social infrastructure system to support such a large population size. ”
There are reliable data showing that one of the factors that reduce population growth is women ’ s access to education, as the average age of childbearing for educated women is delayed.
“Over time, the more women have access to education, the more they move out of the home, gain a foothold in society, and get a job, all of which conflict with their traditional role of having children, ” says Ize.
However, he strongly emphasized that the value of education is not based on its impact on population size.
Education is one of the 17 sustainable development programs of the United Nations.
This relates to the central idea of a modern conception about population engineering that policies should be implemented for the benefit of society, which can only be considered an additional benefit if beneficial demographic changes happen to occur.
“My view is that we don ’ t want to instrumentalize women ’ s education, we can ’ t let women go to school because we want them to have fewer children … We can ’ t minimize a lot of positive things just because we want to reduce the fertility rate, ” he says.
In fact, the combined effect on the population of policies implemented for other purposes underscores the alarming reality of population science, which is that population science ’ s predictions are often far from accurate.
Globally, the decisions made by governments in the coming decades will have a huge impact on the future population size of the planet, with the power to push humanity from a future of 10 billion to a future of 15 billion people, but it may also be the opposite trend.
“I think one thing we can be sure of is that when people say that the population of Africa will be x by year y, it ’ s not doomed. ”
If you look at the southern African region, by 2100 the population could be three to four times what it is today, but it could also be less than 50% larger than it is today.
We now have a wide range of options for making the necessary investments to achieve the rate of population growth that each country hopes to achieve.
This is the great opportunity that exists. "
The reality of continued global population growth
However, while the scale of humanity ’ s continued expansion on Earth remains to be determined by human behavior, some trajectories of population development are clear.
One of them is that the population will continue to grow over time, regardless of any possible measures taken to reduce the population.
The future of human expansion depends on a phenomenon known as “population growth inertia ”, whereby the number of young people will continue to grow as long as the population ’ s mortality and migration levels remain the same, although the fertility rate is below replacement level.
This is because demographic changes are related not only to the birth rate but also to the demographic structure, especially the total number of women of childbearing age.
All of this means that in countries with high fertility rates, the full impact of this growth will not be seen until women born in high fertility years reach reproductive age decades later.
A 2014 study found that even if major global tragedies such as deadly epidemics or catastrophic world wars occur, or every country on the planet implements a draconian one-child policy (of course, no one wants that), we humans will still grow to 10 billion people by 2100.
That is, two billion people will die in five years in the middle of this century, and the population will still grow to 8.5 billion by 2100.
The authors of the study conclude that no matter what happens, it is highly likely that there will be many, many people living on Earth, at least until the next century.
Humanity will be more important to the planet in the coming years, so finding a way to live together and protect the environment may be the greatest challenge facing our species today.

For example, Iceland requires a monthly income of 7,100 euros (about HK $54,000), while Portugal only requires 700 euros (about HK $5,292), and Spain is reported to require a monthly income of about 2,000 euros (about HK $15,000).
Some countries may require a certain amount of cash to be deposited in a bank account, such as the Czech Republic, which requires a deposit of 5,500 euros (about HK $41,000), and some countries may require that applicants have medical insurance.
According to a report published this year, the average monthly salary in Spain is 1,751 euros (about HK $13,000), which is 20% lower than the EU average of 2,194 euros (about HK $16,000).
