Chinese Medicine in the World, Part II: Alternative Therapies to the West?
Author: Law Baoxi
Published: Updated:
Many countries now have what is known as alternative medicine. Traditional Chinese medicine and a wide range of other traditional medicine belong to this category, in order to distinguish it from mainstream Western medicine.
In recent years, TCM has gained popularity due to its increased visibility, including being referred by Western medicine in some countries, endorsed by the World Health Organization, and being seen at major international sporting events.
This is Part 2 of the "Chinese Medicine in the World" Series
At the Beijing Winter Olympics in February this year, Chinese medicine clinic attracted many famous athletes from all over the world. Among them, acupuncture and massage are the most popular. They said that "Chinese medicine is a magical means of relieving pain and calming the body and mind", which allows them to relax their minds and meet the competition in a better state.
Today, Chinese medicine is not difficult to find around the world, among which acupuncture, massage and so on not only attract many foreigners to try it, the former is a first-line treatment for pain in many countries.
German TCM teacher Tim Vukan pointed out to the Hong Kong 01 reporter that local acupuncture is also very popular, and many people have tried it, especially for the treatment of shoulder pain, back pain, knee pain and other pain.
"Many Germans have these experiences and have achieved good results, and the cost of these treatments can be covered by medical insurance," he said. Many local Western doctors now offer acupuncture, massage and other treatments.
Acupuncture is already a first-line treatment for pain in many European and American countries. (Getty)
Apart from this kind of external therapy, there is still no foundation for internal medicine. Germans generally know very little about Chinese herbs. Although some Chinese herbs can be bought in local pharmacies, but few people know about them.
However, Germans are more open about alternative medicine. Tim Vukan points out that locals already have a lot of knowledge about alternative medicine, and they don ’ t necessarily have to go to a Western doctor if they are sick.
In Europe, we are mainly Western medicine, and there is also a natural medicine system based on European herbs, which is still believed and adopted by many people today, as well as homeopathy and flower therapy.
According to Tim Vukan, Europeans like natural treatments. “They don ’ t feel good about taking antibiotics because they know the side effects, so we also ‘ walk on two legs ’, go to a doctor and buy herbal tea from Europe. ”
He added that there are also schools in Germany that specialize in such alternative therapies, and products can be purchased at local pharmacies, which are still common today.
Although most Germans still go to Western medicine, some people may not fully recover and will start looking for alternatives, so when people fail to make progress in Western medicine, they will also seek treatment from Chinese medicine and other alternative medicine.
According to Giles Sadler, the majority of Australians who come to see Chinese medicine are well-educated middle class women. (Interviewee provided)
In the West, there are herbs, traditional medicine, and natural medicine.
Giles Sadler, a Chinese medicine practitioner in Australia, told reporters that many Western countries actually have herbal traditions, which were dominant before the Western medicine epidemic. Today, people still take Western herbs and often use them in combination with vitamin and mineral supplements.
“In Europe and the United States, these Western natural medicine practitioners are more numerous than Chinese medicine practitioners, and they are often the first choice for alternative treatment for patients, ” he said.
He also shared that Australians who come to see Chinese medicine are dominated by well-educated middle-class women, most of whom want to take care of their health more effectively.
Is it easier to promote in traditional medicine countries?
Some people believe that the development of TCM in the world will have an advantage in countries with a traditional medical background and history. To some extent, Tim Vukan agrees with this statement, stating: “For example, Indians grew up in Ayurveda culture, Thailand, Vietnam, and Korea also have their own medicine.
Because these countries have a traditional medical system that is different from Western medicine and has proven to be helpful to patients, people in these countries will generally be more receptive to these alternative treatments and medications.
However, Tim Vukan added that this does not mean that only countries with these backgrounds are more willing to accept Chinese medicine.
Currently engaged in online Chinese medicine teaching work, he pointed out that the students he teaches are from the United States, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, all from very modern Western countries.
Tim Vukan told reporters that alternative therapies such as Chinese medicine are very common in Germany. (Interview screenshot)
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), people in Western countries are suffering from anxiety, depression, and many other problems, and there is a possibility of a greater global epidemic crisis in the future.
He believes that the general public wants to find prevention and treatment methods that are suitable for them, and this is not limited to traditional Chinese medicine, but also other alternative medicine.
It can also be seen from his sharing that Germany is exactly such a country, and some Chinese medicine practitioners believe that apart from places with a traditional medical background, the more acceptable a country is to alternative medicine, the easier it is to promote Chinese medicine.
The forecast for the growth of the Chinese medicine market in the Mainland to 2023 shows that the outside world is optimistic about the development of the industry under the epidemic.
(Statista)
Unpretentious, combined with modern life
Tim Vukan, who has studied Chinese medicine in the Mainland for 10 years, told reporters: “It is very difficult for foreigners to study Chinese medicine because it is not part of our culture. I learned it because I am interested. I have to work hard to learn the language and understand the relevant ancient books. ”
Later, he found that it had to be connected with modern life to better understand Chinese medicine, but inevitably it still took a lot of time and effort.
The four classics of Chinese medicine, "Huang Di Inner Classics", "Typhoid Theory", "Jin Zi Guan" and "Warm and Sick Sections" are all important learning contents.
Tim Vukan believes that the promotion of TCM can only be effective by using simple language and not using myths. (Getty)
In order to better understand Chinese medicine, Tim Vukan has collected and translated many instructional books and made his own Chinese medicine learning card to facilitate studying while on the bus.
He also sometimes questioned whether the content of ancient books still applies to today's society and modern diseases, and spent a lot of time understanding the concepts of "qi", "blood", "yin and yang" and so on.
Fortunately, he also has a good understanding of Chinese kung fu since childhood, and has practiced Wing Chun, Tai Chi and Qigong, so he has a certain understanding of Chinese humanities.
"For example, what is qi, because I can feel the qi in my body during practice, so I know more about the operation of qi."
“I try to avoid using Chinese medical terminology during my treatment, otherwise I would spend hours explaining things, ” says Giles Sadler, an Australian Chinese medicine practitioner. For example,“ improve the digestive system ” rather than “replenish the spleen and stomach ” or“ improve metabolism ” rather than “replenish qi. ”
He bluntly stated that although these statements are not equal, they are sufficient to tell the patient what treatment he is doing.
Tim Vukan believes there is no speed or shortcut to treating patients. (Getty)
Tim Vukan stressed that he believes that Chinese and Western medicine are completely different medical systems. Although the two can be well combined, he tries not to confuse the two.
"There is no need to believe in Chinese medicine from the bottom of your heart, because it is not a religion, and it is important to maintain an open mind."
After 17 years of contact with Chinese medicine, Tim Vukan believes that the most important thing for the future development of Chinese medicine is: “When we teach Chinese medicine, we should make it easy to understand, use simple language, don ’ t make it mysterious, don ’ t make people think it is a small circle of knowledge. ” The effect of Chinese medicine may not be rapid enough, but it also causes fewer physical problems, convinced that" there is no shortcut to the process of treating the disease. Rising average temperature, melting sea ice Arctic waters acidify faster than other oceans
Scientists warn that this acidification could worsen in the coming decades if sea ice continues to melt.
The rapid melting of Arctic sea ice caused by global warming makes it easier to absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, which accelerates the rate of ocean acidification.
(Photo / Associated Press)
Most people agree that the increase in carbon dioxide in the atmosphere caused by human activities is not only absorbed by forests, but also nearly a third of the world ’ s oceans. However, it is precisely because of the large increase in carbon dioxide needed to be absorbed that ocean acidification is rapidly worsening, especially in the polar regions.
Researchers from the Institute of Polar and Ocean Studies at Jimei University in Xiamen and the School of Marine Science and Policy at Dalawi University have found that rapid melting of Arctic sea ice due to global warming is exposing the lower sea water to the air, making it easier to absorb atmospheric carbon dioxide, thereby accelerating the rate of acidification.
Scientists have long believed that the rate of ocean acidification is related to the rate of increase in carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, but the team looked at data from 1994 to 2020 and found that the Arctic Ocean acidified about three to four times faster than the Atlantic Ocean, the Pacific Ocean and even the Antarctic Ocean.
Scientists warn that this acidification could worsen in the coming decades if sea ice continues to melt.
Because of the Arctic amplification effect, the Arctic Circle has warmed up to four times the global average in the past 43 years, and as sea ice melts, the sea water will continue to be diluted and the pH will decrease, which will also reduce the ability of the sea to resist acidification.
In addition to the coral reefs that are most directly impacted, ocean acidification affects a wide range of areas and may even make some metals more toxic, although more detailed results may be needed for further analysis.

[Ming Pao News] After 15 years of research and development, the C919, which has independent intellectual property rights, was certified to take off before the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC), and will deliver its first aircraft within the year.
C919 is regarded as the "heavy weapon" of China's technological innovation, and the state media said that its localization rate is about 60%; its research and development achievements have been affirmed by President Xi Jinping, and the evaluation carries the national will, the national dream and the people's expectations.
At present, the pre-purchase of commercial orders for C919 has exceeded 500 billion yuan (RMB, the same below).
As the "pearl of modern manufacturing", C919 is expected to drive the upgrading of the entire industry upstream and downstream in the future, and promote the economic growth of multiple cities.
Ming Pao reporter Wang Shengchen
The C919 is a narrow-body trunk civil transport aircraft ranging from 158 (basic mixed-class layout) to 168 seats (all-economic layout). It is also the first self-developed jet trunk passenger aircraft with independent intellectual property rights in accordance with the international standard of airworthiness.
With a range of 4075 to 5555 kilometers, the C919 is designed to meet the market needs of large and medium volumes at home and abroad.
In September, the civil aviation qualification certificate can be put into commercial operation.
It has been 15 years since the C919 was first introduced in 2007. In 2010, its manufacturer, China Commercial Aviation (COMAC), submitted an application for a Model Conformity Certificate to the Civil Aviation Administration of China and accepted it.
After five years of research and development, the first C919 aircraft was put on the line in 2015. In 2017, after the successful first flight of the C919, a comprehensive test flight began, including six test aircraft participating in power, performance, control and other subjects, and two in static test, fatigue test and other subjects.
In September this year, the C919 completed all airworthiness certification and obtained the model qualification certificate issued by the Civil Aviation Administration of China, which means that China Commercial Aviation can start delivery and enter commercial operations.
Official media: C919 localization rate 60%
The commercial operation of the C919 is now countdown. This progress marks China ’ s ability to independently develop world-class large passenger aircraft and is a milestone in the development of China ’ s large aircraft industry.
Previously, according to Zhou Guirong, deputy chief designer of C919 model large passenger aircraft, the overall domestic production rate of C919 model aircraft can reach more than 50%, including domestic enterprises and domestic and foreign joint ventures in the domestic production.
The Economic Daily pointed out that the domestic production rate of the C919 is about 60%.
Bulk delivery with production license only
Xinhua News Agency reported that Xi Jinping met with representatives of the C919 project team in Beijing on September 30 and visited the project achievements exhibition, during which he fully affirmed the stage achievements of the C919 large-scale passenger aircraft development task.
Xi Jinping said that allowing China's large aircraft to soar in the blue sky carries the national will, national dream, and people's expectations, and stressed that it is necessary to give full play to the advantages of the new national system and make greater breakthroughs in key core technologies.
Next, the C919 only needs to get a production license, and it can be delivered in bulk and officially go to market.
According to China Commercial Aviation, the first C919 aircraft will be delivered by the end of this year.
Order 815 more than 500 billion
34 overseas Nigerians, 30
According to China Commercial Aviation official website and "data treasure" statistics, there are currently 28 C919 customers, a total of 815 confirmed or intended orders, the total order amount of more than 500 billion yuan.
Among them, China Eastern Airlines is the first customer of C919 in the world.
According to China Eastern ’ s 2022 semi-annual report, China Eastern will introduce a C919 in the second half of this year.
According to the previous announcement of China Eastern Airlines, the unit price of the C919 catalog is 653 million yuan.
With a row of 6 seats (3 seats on each side of the single aisle), the C919 is in high demand in the global aircraft procurement market.
China Airlines orders account for about 25% of the market demand, and the first customers of C919 are expected to be mainly China Airlines.
It is worth noting that out of the current 815 orders, overseas orders account for 34.
Nigeria ’ s aviation minister, Hadi Sirika, said on the 1st that because of “cordial, friendly and mutually beneficial relations ” with China, the country will consider purchasing the C919, which is currently in its infancy, and plans to increase the number of aircraft to 30 by 2025.
US research claims that aircraft development has a driving effect of 1: 15
The continuous growth of Chinese and foreign orders is a positive trend for C919. The C919 project has the characteristics of capital-intensive, technology-intensive and resource-intensive high-end equipment industry, and is known as the “pearl of modern manufacturing ”.
The aviation industry itself has always been known for its long industrial chain and high value-added.
According to the analysis of the think tank of "Beijing News", the successful operation of C919 will lead to the comprehensive upgrading of the entire related upstream and downstream manufacturing industry and promote economic growth.
The design and development, advanced manufacturing, operation and maintenance of the large aircraft industry chain involve many subsystems such as system research and development, new materials, parts, aircraft manufacturing, etc., and the upstream and downstream have become a huge industrial chain.
The research and development of the C919 has directly promoted the establishment of 16 joint ventures in avionics, flight control, power supply, fuel, landing gear and other aircraft systems.
RAND research indicates that the development of large aircraft and its core technology diffraction into related industries can achieve a 1: 15 driving effect, so it is beneficial to the industrial chain.
Nearly 200,000 people in 22 provinces and cities participated in R & D and production
Some mainland cities also enjoy the "cake" of the big aircraft industry.
At present, Shanghai, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Liaoning, Jiangsu and other 22 provinces and cities, as many as 200 enterprises, nearly 200,000 people have participated in the research and development of the C919 project, and the mainland has formed a number of industrial clusters such as Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Pearl River Delta, Southwest, Northeast and Northwest.
"Outlook Oriental Weekly" statistics pointed out that in terms of the number of listed enterprises in the aerospace industry chain, Jiangsu ranked first in the mainland, followed by Beijing, Guangdong, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Zhejiang and other places, all have more than 10 listed companies and developed equipment manufacturing base.
New strategic industries around Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Shanghai
Taken off by the big plane "Dongfeng"

Since 2008, COMAC has been following up on the layout and construction of related industrial parks in Suzhou, Wuxi, Changzhou, Nantong, Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Shaoxing, Taizhou, Wuhu, Anhui, and other surrounding cities.
Last year, Shanghai planned to continue to promote the aviation industry, and by 2035, it will develop into a civil aviation industry base with global influence, and at the same time, cooperate with the Yangtze River Delta to form a world-class civil aviation industry cluster.

Here is our interview with the author:
• Q: In Greenhouse at the End of the Earth, which character do you most love and sympathize with? Why? Which character would you like to be? Why?
A: My favorite character is Zhixiu.

I don ’ t really want to be a character, after all, the characters in the novel are too hard.
• Q: In the process of thinking about “Greenhouse at the End of the Earth ”, what factors led you to eliminate bacteria, insects and other organisms, and ultimately choose plants to save the novel? What are your favorite and feared plants? Why?
A: I have looked for many books on bacteria, insects, mold, and so on.
I have always been more interested in small creatures than big creatures, so I find these books very interesting.
But in The Greenhouse at the End of the Earth, I hope that the appearance of these creatures can give a more intense sense of closeness visually.
After all, it ’ s not easy for microbes to visually impact. Although I can also make the appearance of insects very impactful, it ’ s a bit contrary to the atmosphere I want to create.
The idea that humans and non-humans are changing the landscape of the planet is more in line with the story I want to write.
It ’ s not just leaves, trunks and flowers that can grow, but can be spread around the world by relying on seeds.
The more I learned about plants, the more I felt that plants, a creature that grows slowly, have the power to change the world.
My favorite plant is cactus.
I like the sharpness with which they refuse to be touched, and the coldness with which they can sustain even without watering the water.
There is nothing to be afraid of, but every time you see the back of the fern, you get goosebumps.
Q: In Greenhouse at the End of the Earth, why did you choose to cast most of the characters, especially in Prim Village, as women?
A: I often want to create a story: in times of disaster or crisis, witnessing violence against women and the weak, and creating a safe community for women.
The village of Prim is, in a way, a space that reflects this desire of mine.
However, on the other hand, it is not a safe place in a female-only community environment; moreover, the utopia that is isolated will be disintegrated if it does not face the pain of the outside, which is the story I want to tell.
• Q: In “The Greenhouse at the End of the Earth ”, the Dust Ecology Research Center is slightly disappointed with the sour taste of the raspberry. Do you think that in the future, human taste and aesthetic standards will move toward perfection?
What is your opinion on this? What are your favorite fruits in real life that you would like to see disappear? Why? Are there any fruits that you have only read and heard about in books that you would like to revive or actually taste? Why?
The problem is profound.
In Korea, there is a very high and expensive watermelon, called the "mountain watermelon", which is usually used as a gift.
However, according to the food notes of people who have actually eaten this watermelon, the taste of this watermelon is more flat and not sweet compared to the watermelon that has been improved in recent years, so it is surprising.
When I heard this story, it seemed to me that the human sense of taste was becoming more and more extreme, and that there was a tendency to pursue more and more intense tastes.
I don ’ t want to judge which taste is better, but it makes me think that over time, people ’ s preferences and aesthetics have not improved.
I like mangoes and peaches.
There is no fruit that you want to eliminate.
As a child, there is a fruit "figs" that I often see in novels or religious books, and I am very curious about it.
But when you grow up, you eat figs and find that the taste is even more bland than you think. (Note: Human taste is becoming more and more dull, so you need a more exciting taste.)
• Q: Have you ever read a website such as the book “Strange Tales ”? Have you heard of some wonderful stories, mysterious events, and how did these affect your creation?
A: I ’ m not going to go to a website that specializes in curiosities, but stories like curiosities are always very popular material in the online community.
In fact, I don ’ t really believe in weird talk, and I don ’ t believe in supernatural phenomena, so I don ’ t feel too afraid to see weird talk. It ’ s the complete opposite of the character “Arjun ”, which is why I intentionally did it.
But I also often think: Why do people like strange talk and go looking for it?
• Q: How did you choose “Greenhouse at the End of the Earth ” storylines like Kuala Lumpur, Malacca, Ethiopia, etc.? Have you visited any of these places? What are your impressions of these places?
A: I went to Ethiopia when I was a college student.
It was also my first trip abroad, where the streets were full of life and the roadways were very complicated, and I loved the streets there.
Coffee celebrations can be seen everywhere.
There is a strong argument that the origin of human beings is in Ethiopia.
It would be a good story if the possibility of a new life began to emerge in Ethiopia on a planet that was rebuilt after the destruction.
(Note: Ethiopia is home to coffee, and coffee festivals are a local tradition of making coffee every day for family members, friends or visitors.)
It is also said that local coffee farmers hold coffee festivals after the harvest in order to increase the price of coffee.)
As for Malaysia, it is because there is a place called the Malaysian Mountain Forest Institute, so I want to set the background in Malaysia.
In the forests of the rainforest region, the concept of finding a place where research institutes and villages exist at the same time is very close to FRIM, the Malaysian Institute of Mountain Forests. It is said that there are also residential and school nearby. FRIM is located near Kuala Lumpur.
Although I wanted to go to Malaysia in person, I was unable to do so because of COVID-19.
However, I made this novel by referring to the amazing plants in tropical countries I ’ ve seen so far, as well as related films and books.
I wanted to write a story about people from different countries coming together and dispersing around the world, so I liked the idea of bringing people of different nationalities together in Kuala Lumpur.
Q: If we rewrite the history of the earth with plants as the center, what kind of history would you imagine it to be? What might be the biggest difference from existing history?
A: I think it would have been a much longer, much bigger, much bigger history.
In the plant-related books that I read in preparation for a long novel, I am very interested in the process of the reconstruction and formation of ecosystems in wasteland or volcanic eruptions and other ecologically extinct terrain.
In South Korea, this process is called “Succession. ”
In the naked land, moss and weeds begin to grow, and gradually, large plants such as annuals, perennials, trees, etc. begin to spread on the land. Insects and animals need plants to survive, so I think we can call them “pioneers. ”
• Q: How did you arrange the order of chapters in Planetary Bookstore? Why did you choose to name the book after Planetary Bookstore?
A: The order of the story is determined by the editor of the publishing house.
The first part is a little different from the second part.
In the first part, there are many stories of people with different feelings or different worlds communicating with each other face to face. In the second part, there are more stories of invasion and complicated entanglement.

Economically based on agricultural and animal husbandry processing products, the military has long been supported by the former Soviet Union and Russia, and the existing weapons are mostly Russian-Chinese systems, and there are a small number of US-French weapons.

On Wednesday, Canada ordered three Chinese companies to withdraw their stakes in Canadian rare earth companies, citing "national security."
Five days ago, the Canadian government introduced new rules, except in special circumstances, foreign state-owned enterprises are not allowed to participate in Canadian rare earth companies.
According to the relevant statement, the three companies that were ordered to withdraw their capital are China Mineral (Hong Kong) Rare Metal Resources Co., Ltd., Chengze Lithium International Co., Ltd., and Zangge Mining Investment (Chengdu) Co., Ltd.
Francois-Philippe Champagne, Canada ’ s minister of innovation, science and industry, said Canada ’ s national security and intelligence agencies had conducted a “rigorous review and evaluation ” of the Chinese companies before making the decision.
"Canada continues to welcome foreign direct investment, but we will act decisively when investment threatens our national security and our key mineral supply chains," Mr. Sabini said.
Rare earth minerals are considered key to the green technologies of the future and are already widely used in the electronics, aerospace, automotive and defense industries.
China is a global leader in rare earth mining and exports.
Pictured is a rare earth mine in Baotou.
Five days before the announcement of the decision, Canada tightened the rules for foreign state-owned enterprises in the rare earth sector, and only a few exceptions will be approved in the future.
In response to Canada's request to divest its assets in lithium ore, the relevant person in charge of Zangger Mining told the Chinese media that the company is actively communicating with relevant Canadian companies about the next steps to deal with and deal with them.
"The company invested little, only about 4 million Canadian dollars, about 20 million yuan, and the risk is controllable."
Another Chinese company involved in the mine (Hong Kong) rare metals resources Limited also said that the decision of the Canadian side will only affect some of the company's enterprises.
Ottawa has drawn up a list of 31 so-called "critical minerals" that it believes are vital to the country's economic prosperity, including cobalt, lithium and manganese used in solar panels, wind turbines and electric car batteries.
Over the past 20 years, China, the world ’ s largest producer of rare earths, has invested billions of dollars in Canada to secure its supply of rare earths.
China dominates the global market in terms of mining, refining and exporting rare earths, but as geopolitical and trade disputes intensify, many countries are struggling to shake off their unilateral dependence on Chinese rare earths.

“The war in Ukraine is putting climate action on hold, while our planet itself is burning, ” UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said recently.
Pro-Putin leaders come from some of the most influential and polluting countries.
In the wake of Russia ’ s invasion of Ukraine, China ’ s Xi Jinping and India ’ s Modi accelerated the pace of massive purchases of Russian coal and oil at low prices, buffering both economies from the global energy crisis while allowing Putin to continue profiting from energy exports despite Western sanctions.
Brazilian President Bolsonaro, who destroyed vast swathes of the Amazon rainforest for gold mining and beef production, flew to the Kremlin just days before Russia ’ s invasion of Ukraine to sit alongside Putin and show “solidarity with Russia. ”
After that, he announced that Russia would provide Brazil with a new batch of much-needed fertilizer and diesel.

Even Saudi Arabia, the world ’ s largest oil exporter, has taken advantage of extremely low prices to buy more Russian fuel oil this year.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has also joined forces with Putin to reduce output from the oil-producing cartel OPEC +, pushing up global oil prices and thus replenishing Putin ’ s coffers.
General Min Aung Lay, the leader of Myanmar's military junta, met with Putin nine months after the Russian-Ukrainian war and reached an agreement to buy oil.
Creating the conditions to undermine global climate cooperation is one of Putin ’ s biggest admirers: former US President Donald Trump.
He pulled the United States, the largest polluter in history, out of the 2015 Paris climate agreement.
The agreement, signed under the auspices of the United States and China, represents a moment of global solidarity for countries willing to work together to mitigate climate change.
However, since then, Sino-US relations have begun to deteriorate.
The two countries are so nervous about everything from trade to Taiwan that the two biggest emitters of greenhouse gases are now barely talking.
As the increasingly authoritarian Mr. Xi finds more places to work with the Kremlin, Mr. Putin is benefiting from strained U.S.-China relations.
With Xi under pressure to boost economic growth and ensure energy security, China has softened its stance on participating in addressing global climate change.
"In terms of our climate agenda, we are entering a more difficult period," said Li Shuo, head of Greenpeace East Asia in Beijing.
Over the past decade, the world has made considerable progress in reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
Moreover, the global failure to mitigate further warming cannot be blamed solely on authoritarian leaders.
After Russia ’ s war on Ukraine, to avoid an energy crisis that would lead to political instability at home, even many liberal democracies have regressed in their efforts to reduce their dependence on fossil fuels.

There are many reasons for the failure to further slow warming.
But the rise of authoritarian and nationalist leaders complicates the situation.
“Nationalist authoritarian leaders undoubtedly pose a threat to solving global problems because they may be willing to blatantly defy a system that relies on each country to shoulder its due responsibilities, ” said Carrie Sims Gallagher, a professor at Tufts University ’ s Fletcher School and a former U.S. climate diplomat.
But she noted that the extent to which authoritarian leaders try to address climate change or undermine solutions depends on how good it is for them to do so. “Much depends on whether authoritarian leaders see climate action as in their own interest. ”
While their actions have helped Putin, their record on climate has been mixed.
As Russia ’ s president, Vladimir Putin, who leads an oil nation, has never welcomed a transition to reduced fossil fuel use.
Trump and Bolsonaro have deliberately avoided international cooperation.
While both Xi and Modi are pushing for the use of renewable energy, their cooperation with Putin, coupled with the expansion of coal use in the name of energy security, has allowed carbon emissions to continue to grow in both countries.
As for Putin, his invasion of Ukraine may eventually unravel his grand strategy.
The war could inspire countries to get rid of oil and gas more quickly.
The International Energy Agency last week predicted that global demand for natural gas will peak by the end of this decade, coal demand will peak before then, and oil demand will decline in the next decade.
Putin has denied claims that he is using energy resources to gain geopolitical power and has accused the energy-consuming West of hypocrisy.
He instead blamed the reduction in investment in oil and gas on what he called a “massive green agenda push. ”
"Other countries are always trying to blame their own mistakes on other countries, specifically Russia," he said.

The Russian embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.
Igor Sechin, a close Putin confidant and head of state oil giant Rosneft, told an energy conference that a new drilling project in the Arctic would ease the problem of rising global energy prices.
"This is the only project in the world that can bring stability to the oil market," Sechin said.
He went on to compare the project to Noah's Ark.
Oil will save the world.
Oil and Empire
As Putin takes control of Russia on the first day of the new millennium, the former KGB intelligence officer embarks on a path to restoring the glory of the Soviet empire, which was built on Russia ’ s abundant oil and gas resources.
He quickly took control of Russia ’ s energy companies, putting his trusted allies in charge of them. In October 2003, he ordered the arrest of Russia ’ s richest man, oil tycoon Mikhail Khodorkovsky, split up his Yukos company and handed over most of the company ’ s assets to the state-owned Rosneft.

By 2007, Putin had reached an agreement with Germany to build a gas pipeline.
A few years later, he came to Vyborg, the starting point of the pipeline, and pressed the button to start the gas delivery.
By this simple act, he gained a powerful economic lever that allowed him to influence the daily lives of Europeans and their elected politicians.
In less than a decade, 40% of the gas that Europeans use for heating and power generation has come from Russia.
After Putin ’ s invasion of Ukraine, Europe ’ s eagerness to shed its dependence on Russian energy has instead encouraged new gas projects elsewhere in the world.
Putin mocked the commitment of continental European governments to reduce or end their energy dependence on Russia.
"There is no reasonable alternative in Europe right now," he said.
Pipeline to China.

That year, in violation of international law, Putin classified Ukraine's Crimea as Russian territory.
Soon, Russian energy companies faced sanctions aimed at cutting revenues in the country.
Xi Jinping came out at this time.
He received the Russian leader in Shanghai.
They announced a 30-year, $400 billion deal to build a 3,000-kilometer gas pipeline from Russia ’ s Arctic to China.
For Putin, this expands ties with the world ’ s largest energy consumer.
For Xi, this reduces his country ’ s dependence on coal, which is polluting the air and provoking public discontent.
Mr. Xi pursued the relationship even when he met with President Obama, and later that year, China and the United States announced a landmark climate cooperation agreement that laid the groundwork for the Paris agreement.
He also set China on a path to becoming the world ’ s most developed country for wind and solar energy.
He secured the global supply of cobalt and lithium, the key minerals in the renewable energy economy.
He turned China into a major exporter of everything from solar photovoltaic cells to electric buses.
His call for an "ecological civilization" was hailed by Chinese officials as part of the "Xi Jinping Thought."
"He sees climate as an area that has laid China's global leadership," said Cecilia Han Springer, who tracks China's energy and climate policy at Boston University.
China's foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment.
This is in stark contrast to Putin.
Nevertheless, the two men carefully cultivated a relationship of mutual need.
They met nearly 40 times and sometimes celebrated birthdays together. In 2018, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, Xi put a gold medal around Putin ’ s neck, China ’ s first ever medal of friendship.
Xi Jinping called Putin his "best confidant friend."
He was paying tribute to a year ago, when Putin hosted Xi at the Grand Kremlin and awarded him one of Russia ’ s highest medals for foreign dignitaries.
The personal and political trajectories of the two men are very similar.
Both have consolidated their power at home, and both harbor deep-rooted distrust of the West.
Today, Xi ’ s green economy goals face significant challenges, many of them of his own making.
Xi's "zeroing" policy has hit the economy.
Last fall, coal shortages triggered widespread power outages.
Few things can call into question the competence of a leader like a power outage.
Therefore, economic growth and energy security take precedence over the green development of China's economy.
Over the past year, China, which accounts for just over half of global coal consumption, has increased its investment in coal, adding 33 million kilowatts of new coal-fired power capacity in 2021, three times more than the rest of the world combined. Coal emissions have risen significantly
The deepening tensions between the United States and China now pose a serious risk to the world's ability to reduce global greenhouse gas emissions.
This widening fault line will only benefit Putin.
“The goal of Russian-Chinese cooperation is to exclude the United States, which is bad for climate action, ” said David Sandro, a former White House aide who has written a book on China ’ s climate policy.
Buy low, sell high
Without India, Putin ’ s bet on Asia would not have been possible.
India's energy demand is expected to grow faster than all other countries over the next 20 years
Modi took full advantage of that role.
India needs cheap energy.
India also has some very large oil refineries.
The war in Ukraine has given India a new opportunity.
There is what Modi calls a “special chemistry ” between Modi and Putin.
Modi said he believes Putin is trustworthy and enjoys wildlife and fitness just as much as he does.
"I know he is a strong man, he has an active lifestyle and keeps in good shape.
I like that, "Modi said in an interview with Russia's TASS news agency.
"He is also interested in the environment, wildlife, the underwater world, especially the protection of tigers," he said.
And so is my nature, "he said.
Modi can be said to be a contradictory figure.
He is a charismatic pro-business Hindu nationalist politician who won landslide elections in 2014 and 2019.
At home, his critics point to his government's crackdown on dissent, entrenching his power to make religious minorities second-class citizens, and in 2021, the government charged young climate activist Disha Ravi with sedition.
The Modi government did not respond to comment.
In the past, the government ’ s response to criticism was that the country was a “vibrant democracy ” where the law applied equally to all citizens.
On the world stage, Modi has cast himself as a climate politician.
He set an ambitious target for India to generate half of the country ’ s electricity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030.
He made regulations requiring utilities to get a large portion of their electricity from renewable sources.
At the same time, his government approved the mining of coal, including in an ecologically sensitive ancient forest.
A government agency estimates that India may need 28 GW of coal-fired power capacity over the next decade.
During Modi ’ s tenure as prime minister, coal tycoon Gautam Adani, with whom he had a long and close relationship, became Asia ’ s richest man.
Modi ’ s “special chemistry ” with Putin has benefited both countries.
Refineries in India are bringing in significantly more low-cost Russian crude than ever before and converting it into diesel, which is now sold at a high price due to the war.
According to data from commodity analysis firm Kpler, India's imports of Russian crude oil increased to 1 million barrels per day in April from 30,000 barrels last year and are now hovering around 800,000 barrels per day.
At present, most of the crude oil appears to be sold in India.
But analysts expect exports to grow as Europe tightens sanctions on Russian oil imports in December and diesel demand will soar.
“This is purely a refinery economy, ” Kpler analyst Homayong Farakshahi said.
Once refined into diesel, it is no longer considered Russian oil. "In theory, it will be Indian diesel," he said.
In addition, India will double its coal imports from Russia this year compared to 2021, according to Kpler.
India's oil ministry did not respond to a request for comment.
Modi ’ s oil minister, Hardeep Singh Puri, said there was no “moral conflict ” in India ’ s purchase of Russian oil.“ The Modi government is not feeling the pressure.
We are the fifth largest economy in the world, "he said in a recent interview with CNN." India will respond in its supreme national interest. "
Destroyed heritage
On the other side of the planet, Brazil elected a right-wing nationalist president, Jar Bolsonaro, in 2018.
He is dismissive of the need to address climate change.
He set out to transform large areas of the Amazon forest into farmland in an effort to elevate Brazil's position as an agricultural powerhouse.
One of Bolsonaro ’ s top priorities when he takes office in 2019 is to dismantle the $1.2 billion Amazon Fund, backed by Norway and Germany, which aims to combat environmental crime.
He cut down environmental agencies and stripped them of their budgets, leaving little to no way to impose fines on illegal deforestation.
Bolsonaro's office did not respond to a request for comment.
He has often denied before that his policies have taken a toll on the Amazon forest.
Bolsonaro made his first trip to Moscow on February 14, just as Russian troops were massing on the Ukrainian border.
At a news conference with Putin, Bolsonaro thanked the "good friend", saying that it was Putin who gave him support when his Amazon policy was criticized by other world leaders. "I want to thank you for your mediation, always on our side, to defend our sovereignty."
Putin said Brazil is his most important partner in Latin America.
He gave Bolsonaro what he desperately needed, promising to supply Brazil with unlimited quantities of Russian fertilizer at low prices, at a time when global fertilizer prices were soaring, placing a huge burden on Brazilian farmers.
In the five months since then, Russian fertilizer imports, which had fallen sharply, have increased by more than 20 percent over the same period last year.
Brazil also started importing Russian diesel for the first time since 2018.
That didn ’ t save Bolsonaro ’ s political future.
He lost the election last week.
But the damage he left behind could take decades to repair, perhaps in vain.
In the first three years of his presidency alone, more than 33,000 square kilometers of Brazil ’ s Amazon forest were deforested.
Like Bolsonaro, the impact of Trump ’ s actions will extend far beyond his presidency.
One of his first decisions in office was to pull the United States out of the Paris agreement that his predecessor had just negotiated.
This perfectly caters to Putin ’ s plans for the future. In 2015, when the world agreed in Paris to tackle climate change together, Putin did not object.
But he didn ’ t need to object, because just the following year, the newly elected Trump broke the ice, not only withdrawing from the Paris Agreement, but also starting to roll back environmental regulations altogether.
Trump's behavior is still changing the world.
His repeal is expected to add at least 1.8 billion tons of extra carbon dioxide emissions to the atmosphere by 2035 and result in a significant increase in the number of excess deaths caused by poor air quality each year.
On Friday, Trump spokesman Tyler Budovich said, “Climate activists want to destroy not only the U.S. energy industry, but the pursuit of the American dream. ”
President Trump has led the nation ’ s energy renaissance, ensuring safe and reliable energy production and providing affordable prices for every American. ”
Changing the War of the Future
Earlier this year, on February 4, Xi and Putin met during the Beijing Winter Olympics.
They signed an oil deal worth $117 billion.
Twenty days later, Putin invaded Ukraine.
In October, Xi won a third term as president.
He has almost absolute power.
In his speech at this historic moment, he made it clear that he would not rush to get rid of coal. "We will stick to the principle of first, then second, and have a plan to implement the carbon peak step by step," he said.
It has always been difficult for the world to ignore Putin ’ s fossil-fuel wealth.
Since the war, the value of his exports has been increasing.
China's oil imports from Russia doubled, Turkey more than tripled and India quadrupled.
Last month, at an energy forum in Moscow, he said that while developing renewable energy is a good thing, giving up oil and gas in the short term would be futile.
"Hasty for political reasons, especially populist domestic policies - come on, who would do that?"

China 's largest aircraft C919 orders 300 civil aviation industry reviewer: this is just the beginning
Author: External Submission
Published: Updated:
On the first day of the Zhuhai Air Show on November 8, with the C919 vacated for flight performance, COMAC signed a confirmed order for C919 with a number of domestic leasing companies, with a total of 300 aircraft.
Civil aviation industry worker, civil aviation commentator Zhang Zhonglin in the "Observer Network" article pointed out that the C919 aircraft project is based on a large enough domestic market for C919 growth, for C919 aircraft on the air show 300 orders is only the beginning.
This article is authorized by the "Observer Network" reprint, the author is civil aviation industry worker, civil aviation commentator Zhang Zhonglin
When China's three airlines signed an order with Airbus for 292 Airbus aircraft, I once predicted that "maybe in the near future, we will see the three airlines once again brush up on the underground C919 super order, and then we may have forgotten today's Airbus super order."
+ 8
The super order of 300 C919 and 30 ARJ21 signed by a number of financial leasing companies at the Zhuhai Air Show today undoubtedly exceeded the number of Airbus orders in July, and also exceeded the 105 ARJ21 orders of the three major airlines in 2019, becoming the largest order ever in China's aviation manufacturing industry.
Although I expected a new confirmed order for the C919 at the Zhuhai Airshow, such a large number still exceeded my expectations.
This unprecedented order is undoubtedly the best adult gift for the C919.
When Shangfei C919 received the model qualification certificate issued by the Civil Aviation Administration of China on September 29 this year, although there were more than 800 intended orders, it was only an intended order, not a definitive order, and the firm order that had been finalized before the Zhuhai Air Show was only five Eastern Airlines.
Xi Jinping met with representatives of the C919 project team and visited the project achievements exhibition. (Xinhua News Agency)
For the C919 that has already received the model certificate, the number of confirmed orders for five is indeed small. If the first C919 will be delivered within this year, the remaining four C919 orders will be completed and delivered in 2023.
Although the initial production capacity of the C919 is very low, the confirmed order for four C919 aircraft is indeed too small for the production line of the aircraft, and the signing of the new confirmed order can be said to be a nail in the plate.
If you refer to ARJ21 ’ s production capacity climbing path, it will take at least 5 years for COMAC to climb the production capacity of the existing production line and slow down the production growth rate to a certain extent after rapidly increasing the production capacity to reach a stable production capacity.
Given that the number of production lines and the planned capacity of the C919 is larger than the ARJ21, its production capacity is destined to be higher than that of the ARJ21 at the same stage. The order size of 300 aircraft is estimated to be sufficient for commercial production until 2030 to protect the C919.
The difference between this order signing and the past is that the main party signing the purchase is not the usual airline, but the main domestic leasing company.
The domestic leasing companies that signed the contract to buy C919 are: BOC gold rent, ICBC gold rent, CCB gold rent, CMB gold rent, CMB gold rent, Pohang gold rent and Su Yin gold rent, from the name of the leasing companies that signed the contract can be seen, these very low exposure leasing companies are behind the major state-owned banks and financial institutions, is the real "national team".
The C919 aircraft model qualification certificate ceremony was held in Beijing. (Xinhua)
It should be noted that it is very common for leasing companies to buy aircraft and then rent them out to customers in the civil aviation industry, which is determined by the high price of aircraft and the operation of heavy assets in the civil aviation industry.
The domestic aircraft leasing companies rely on the huge funds of the trust bank to carry out aircraft leasing business, which undoubtedly alleviates the huge financial pressure brought by the airlines to purchase aircraft on their own.
Moreover, compared to purchasing on their own, leasing will undoubtedly allow airlines to make more flexible operational adjustments, and if they feel that the aircraft does not meet their operational needs, they will be refunded when they expire.
It can be said that the aircraft leasing business of the major banks has played a very good role in financial services to the real economy.
The stable rental income generated by aircraft leasing is also an investment target with extremely healthy returns and low risk.
Therefore, in the epidemic has lasted for three years, the major domestic airlines continue to suffer huge losses and capital constraints, it is undoubtedly the most appropriate arrangement for the leasing companies of the major banks to buy aircraft and lease them to the domestic airlines.
By the strong financial leasing company to carry out the bottom of the order, and then rent out to each airline on demand, can reduce the financial pressure and worry of domestic airlines to use the C919.
POSCO Leasing, which contracted to purchase C919, is a company with a shareholder background in the civil aviation manufacturing and aviation services industries (photo provided by the author)
It is worth noting that the leasing companies involved in the signing of the confirmed order also include the overseas subsidiary of Bank of Communications Aviation Ireland.
CBC Ireland is noteworthy, on the one hand, because it is the first overseas platform to sign a contract with COMAC, and on the other hand, because its aviation leasing business is aimed at the Irish region.
Ryanair, Europe ’ s largest low-cost carrier, is headquartered in Ireland, and Ryanair signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) for 200 C919s with COMAC back in 2011. “We are still committed to the C919 project, ” Ryanair ’ s President said in a press interview in 2020, even though it has been more than a decade since Ryanair signed the MOU for 200 C919.
Therefore, the order for 50 C919s and 10 ARJ21s signed by Bank of Communications in Ireland makes people think about it.
After the C919 is granted an EASA airworthiness license, it is highly likely that Ryanair will acquire the C919 and put it into operation on a less-risky model such as leasing.
Moreover, unlike users in some developing countries, Ryanair, as the largest low-cost airline in Europe, has sufficient experience in aircraft operation and maintenance, and can be said to be an ideal overseas user.
China Commercial Aviation signed a contract with Bank of China Airlines Ireland. (Photo provided by the author)
Although the firm order of 300 aircraft is a "big order of the century" in terms of a single contract, for an aircraft model, the order of 300 aircraft is far from being a meal, even if it can only be plugged in the teeth, it is not enough for COMAC to formulate a long-term production plan and arrange production capacity.
In order to achieve long-term stable production and allow supporting suppliers to confidently expand production capacity, more orders are required, at least thousands of confirmed orders and production time is extended to more than ten years to achieve the passing line.
Ryanair painted C919 by foreign aviation enthusiasts (Photo by the author)
The C919 ’ s single-aisle trunk aircraft is the most competitive in the international market, and Airbus and Boeing compete fiercely on this track. Even though the Boeing 737MAX has suffered a setback due to the Boeing scandal, the C919 still has insufficient strength in the international market for the 737MAX, let alone the buoyant Airbus A320NEO. It's over.
Therefore, C919 is bound to rely heavily on the domestic market in the first and medium term, and under the policy support, it will first establish a stable domestic environment and obtain stable development, and then consider going to the sea to the world.
Is the domestic market enough to support the C919?
In the 2020 China Aviation Market Forecast Report, AVIC believes that the fleet size of China's aviation market will reach nearly 9,000 by 2039, which is similar to the forecasts of Boeing and Airbus.
In the 20-year period from 2019 to 2039, China needs a total of 7,576 new aircraft, and the demand for narrow-body passenger aircraft belonging to the category of C919 is about 5,000. Even if the C919 completes its production capacity in 2030 and achieves stable mass production, it still cannot fill the huge demand of the Chinese civil aviation market. A sizeable proportion of foreign aircraft purchases – the 472 aircraft ordered by Airbus over the past six months – is a clear signal.
China's procurement of Boeing will remain low in the future
Due to factors such as tensions between China and the United States and the Boeing scandal, the procurement of Boeing aircraft is bound to remain at a lower level in the foreseeable future if Sino-US relations do not undergo a violent turn of 180 degrees.
The long-term advantages of Airbus aircraft in the domestic stock and use inertia doomed Airbus to occupy half of China's future fleet.
With the fleet composition shuffle brought by the C919, when this shuffle stabilizes, China's fleet composition is likely to be about 50% -60% of Airbus, about 30% -40% of Commercial Aviation, and about 10% -20% of Boeing's structure, which means that the C919 has at least 1,500 domestic orders, enough to provide a long-term healthy environment for the C919 project.
This is precisely the basis for China ’ s initial decision to build a large C919 aircraft project: there is a large enough domestic market for the C919 to grow.
On October 30, 2021, China Commercial Airlines C919 passenger aircraft made a static display at the Nanchang Flight Conference 2021.
Photo by Li Tong / Visual China
Of course, it is not enough to have a large enough market, support from the national will and a clear national strategy is the key.
Of course, from the establishment of commercial aviation in 2008 to now, China's national will to engage in large aircraft has been very clear, this time several major leasing companies brush down the order is also from the action on the substantial support of the large aircraft project.
However, for the C919, this does not mean that the US government's threat to the C919 project and COMAC has always been a hanging sword of Damocles. Although the C919 has raised the C919's domestic production rate to about 60% through the mode of Sino-foreign cooperation, the leap1C engine of public concern still needs to be supplied by the United States.
Although the C919 project has the CJ1000A large channel ratio engine developed by AVIC as a power backup, the official certification time node of the CJ1000A engine has been quietly postponed from 2025 to 2027.
And even if the CJ1000A engine is certified and put into production, there are still a considerable number of parts (such as bearings, etc.) inside the engine depends on foreign supply - after all, the complexity of the engine is no less than that of the aircraft.
But there is no need to be pessimistic about this, which is the stage that later pursuers must go through.
From only buying imported aircraft to buying imported devices to buying imported parts, the field of dependence on foreign countries is getting smaller and more microscopic, and we can produce more and more things on our own, and the level is getting higher and higher.
The basis for the development of the relevant industrial chain driven by the large aircraft project is the huge order and demand, and for the C919 large aircraft, the order of 300 aircraft at the air show is just the beginning.

"We're looking at hydrogen to actually achieve net zero emissions," said Alan Newby, director of aerospace technology at Rolls-Royce. "The advantage of hydrogen is that it doesn't contain carbon, so it doesn't produce carbon dioxide when burned."
easyJet chief operating officer David Morgan said hydrogen fuel was an "exciting" idea.
Morgan said: “We started thinking about the future of aviation fuel a few years ago.
We have considered battery technology, but it is clear that battery technology may not be able to support the large commercial aircraft we operate. "
Compared to battery technology, the advantage of using hydrogen energy in aircraft is that it can provide more energy per kilometer range.
For large aircraft, batteries are too heavy.
However, the use of hydrogen in the aviation industry still faces bottlenecks.
These tests have so far shown that the aircraft engine can only be started with hydrogen energy and travel at low speeds.
In addition, hydrogen energy storage is more complex and requires more space than ordinary aviation fuel.

Women in Japanese Colonization: Did the sacrifice of female workers create male members of the family, or did it help change family roles or status?
Photo Credit: Shutterstock
What we want you to know is
In addition to official records, related publications, photographs, advertisements, reports, etc., Professor YU Chan-ming has a direct dialogue with women pioneers in the workplace.
The author interviewed nearly 100 professional women who walked through the Japanese era, and presented in plain words how they were torn between tradition and modernity, race and gender; the achievements and bitterness of the school, training, job search, and employment process; the evolution of interpersonal relations, and the impact on the family and society.
Through their workplace stories, see the most authentic history of Japanese women in Taiwan.
Text: YU Kam-ming
Chapter 6: Women Workers Who Help Others
Fourth, the role of women workers and their impact
The Role of Women Workers in the Home and the Factory
A survey found that only one of the eight or 90 women workers in the Tainan and Chun Weaving Fabric Factory had to work because of difficulties in household finances. The Jidong Tuocheng Tea Club also said that most of the women workers in the factory came from families with a decent environment.
Therefore, this article believes that although there are female workers from ordinary families, but the poor still account for the majority, many female workers into the factory work is forced by the environment.
And once they have an income, it is not used as a household, or to help other siblings to study, such as Qiu Li Aye, who I visited, who is Qiu's child daughter-in-law and has not been educated, but her income supports the sister-in-law and uncle to complete public school education.
This situation in which female workers earn money for their younger siblings to study, in order to subsidize the male majority, under the influence of the concept of male preference, many poor families do not hesitate to sacrifice female workers to create male members of the family, so they sacrifice their childhood, give up their studies and even marry late or not.
As for whether the sacrifice of female workers helps to change the role or status of the family?
I've been working in a liquor store.
Soon, I married my adoptive father ’ s eldest son and went on to produce. Due to the fixed working hours in the factory, the work of cooking or caring for the children had to be left to my mother-in-law.
In order to sympathize with me, the holiday mother-in-law does not force me to do housework, and sometimes even my own clothes are also taken care of by my mother-in-law.
As can be seen from the example of Qiu Li Aye, she not only became a full-time professional woman, but also gained a more respected family status, which is very difficult for women as child brides.
In addition, as mentioned above, the sacrifices made to improve family life are also respected by the family.
However, there are also many women workers who have never changed their family status. Many women workers need help with household chores before they go to work in factories. Women in rural areas are also given farm work, so when they become factory workers, rural work is certainly reduced and not completely exempted.
Chen Cheng Si-mei, who once worked at the Pineapple Club in Nantou, said that because her husband is a farmer, she also wants to help on the farm.
Although it is impossible to see her family status from the example of Chen Cheng Si-mei, it is clear that her role in both work and housework has not changed, although this is common to most working women, but it is particularly common among women workers.
Other female workers leave the factory after marriage, they take the factory work home to carry out, and become OEM women, continue to play a dual role.
In the face of this role, the attitude of female workers is not very consistent, some are regarded as labor, and some are as sweet.
Compared with the family status of female workers, the status of female workers in the factory is even lower.
In addition to the fact that the wages are not comparable to other workers, the nature of the work requires them to rely on the nose and listen to the command of the factory supervision, coupled with the lack of family background and academic qualifications, female workers are not easy to obtain a higher social status.
In fact, women workers work in factories for the purpose of making money, and most women workers do not care about the status of the factory.
However, sexual harassment due to low status has plagued women workers, and newspapers have exposed such incidents and railed against them.
In 1929, the Taiwan People's Daily published a scandal in which Japanese supervisors forced female workers to take up positions, and it was reported that the supervisor often used his power to harass beautiful female workers and ordered them to leave their jobs if they disobeyed. In places such as Hsinchu and Tainan, it is reported that many of these women workers are in oppressed positions.
In view of the low status of women workers, people with knowledge have made appeals on behalf of women workers, and they have reported on the situation of women workers in newspapers and magazines, such as the author of "Red", who pointed out in an article entitled "International Day of Proletarian Women":
At this time, ordinary workers, farmers, small urban women,... now have no leisure to consider what is the "male and female unmarried", "male and female" Mr. Kong's high education, leaping out of the factory for female workers, or for low-grade monthly living.
In the workshop of capitalist society, they are subjected to the same abuse and abuse by capitalists as male workers.
Despite the fact that many of these statements are propagandists of the labour movement, there is no doubt that the unequal status of women workers is a cause for concern.
In fact, not all women workers are living in miserable conditions, there are still women workers are highly valued, such as promotion from female workers to chief workers and technical guidance and other positions, and senior or full-time women workers have the opportunity to be rewarded, which is an affirmation of the role of women workers.
However, most of this situation comes from large factories, and ordinary small factories are rare.
Second, the impact of a female worker ’ s job on the individual, family and society
And regardless of the status of female workers, what impact does a female worker ’ s job have on her personal, family, or Taiwan ’ s economy? As far as female workers are concerned, workers are divided into educated and uneducated.
Take the Shulin distillery as an example, because most of the factory ’ s women workers are educated in public schools, the factory ’ s women will read magazines in groups every time they take breaks. Although they read the magazine of a retired woman, they can get some new knowledge of women from the magazine.
In addition, the factory had sent a special person to teach women to knit sweaters in the early days, although it will no longer be held in the future, but under the mutual teaching, every break time, the factory women almost have a line of hands, and the women's family or friends also have the opportunity to wear warm sweaters, which was quite fashionable at that time.
With the transfer of knowledge, various ideas were introduced, including the idea of anti-factory unreasonable system, which caused some factories to tremble in the 1920s and 1930s. As mentioned above, some women workers joined the strike, although the majority of the strike movement was defeated, many women workers returned to their families, and under the forced repression of the colonial government, these ideas only affected workers in the late 1920s and early 1930s. Undeniably, the strike movement has changed the minds of some women workers.
However, on the whole, what had a greater impact on the thinking of women workers was the Japanese policy of assimilation, especially since the 1930s, which had been reinforced by the colonial government.
As part of the policy of the colonial government, in addition to requiring female workers to accept Japanese language instruction, the factory also adopted a half-coercive and half-encouraging method to allow employees to participate in social education groups or related activities that foster the Japanese national spirit. For example, in November 1928, the Taiwan Anesthesia Club asked more than 40 men and women workers to dress up as indigenous people to participate in the celebration and procession on Fengyuan Street. He fell ill because of the cold rain.
In other words, remember:
Before I joined the factory, I was a member of the Young Women ’ s League. After I joined the factory, I still took part in the activities of the group on holidays.
Sometimes the time of the event and the working hours conflict, the factory not only did not prohibit me, but allowed me to take time off to participate in the event.
This situation was not allowed until the activities of the Youth League were too frequent, and the factory itself began to strengthen the national spirit training, so I was not allowed to take a leave of absence.
At the same time, the factory also rewards female workers for participating in Japanese language seminars or seminars. For example, in 1934, Lin Hao, a female worker at the Chinese Language Seminar, participated in the lecture on the topic "Help from the Workshop", and in 1931, Chen Po-yu, a female worker at the Hsu Te-ding Socks Factory, wrote "Our Work". Question, with members of the stone maiden club to participate in the radio recording performance.
Understandably, regardless of whether the female workers undergo indoctrination activities are autonomous or passive, these activities have enabled many uneducated female workers to gain new knowledge and broaden their knowledge; some female workers have been molded into the mother of the kingdom or the daughter of the kingdom.
As is shown, this factory-led thought transformation activity has an unnegligible impact.

North Korean Women Challenging Male Domination
# Focus on Korean Peninsula l 2022-11-30
Focus on Korean Peninsula
About YONHAP News
North Korea has always stressed that women should sacrifice for their families and be loyal to the country, and is committed to shaping this image of women.
But after the young women born in the 1990s, known as the "market generation", entered society, the image of women in North Korea gradually changed, and many women took control of the family.
In 2021, Kim Jong Un, chairman of the North Korean State Council, sent a letter to the Socialist Women ’ s League Congress calling on society to respect women and stressing that party organizations at all levels should make precise efforts to help society form a culture of caring, helping and respecting women.
In fact, after Chairman Kim Jong Un took office, the North Korean media often introduced women who challenged male-dominated fields and were recognized for their strength.
In fact, North Korea has long enacted the Gender Equality Law to protect women's rights and interests.
The DPRK promulgated the Gender Equality Law in 1946, and passed the Socialist Constitution, the Law on the Protection of Women's Rights, the Family Law, the Law on Civil Procedure, and the Law on Labor Protection.
However, in daily life, the gender concept of male and female owners is still deeply rooted, and North Korean women are still unable to shake off the fetters of the patriarchal culture. In the middle and late 1990s, the North Korean "suffering march" to overcome the food shortage and economic crisis, many women went to the market to earn their livelihood and take control of the family.
For example, women must dress in accordance with the standards of socialist beauty, and women must not engage in dangerous work.
In modern society, the dress of women should not be the object of restrictions and harsh criticism, and not allowing women to engage in dangerous work can be seen as restricting the right of women to freely choose their profession and work.
After Kim Jong Un, chairman of the North Korean Council of State, took office, the women depicted in North Korean novels were not only women who worked in light industry production sites, such as spinners, but also scientists, defense science researchers, and other women who worked in professional jobs.
The reason for this is that they are recognized for their strength in challenging male-dominated fields. One of them is the novel “First Step ”, published in the North Korean literary journal Korean Literature in 2017.
En Shu's grandfather, father and uncle are truck drivers working in the reclaimed land, and his father is very proud of being a truck driver.
But the retiring father, who has no son, is dismayed that his family is unable to continue the life of a truck driver.
Because his father firmly said that "truck driver is not a woman's occupation", En Shu had to give up being a truck driver.
The same has been true of the social climate in South Korea in the past, and North Korea has recently seen truck drivers as an undesirable occupation for women.
Under the North Korean Labor Protection Law, female workers are not allowed to engage in work that is harmful to their health.
Although the law does not prohibit women from driving, in the case of transportation and fuel shortages, drivers are also responsible for vehicle maintenance, so driving is characterized as a male-dominated field.
In addition, North Korea has passed a law prohibiting women from working as furnace workers in labor-intensive and dangerous occupations and dealing with heavy chemical substances that are harmful to their health.
Eun Shu-ben gave up working as a truck driver because of her parents' objections, but one day she changed her mind after seeing a TV show about a female driver.
She ignored her parents' objections to the truck driver's license, first drove a 5-ton truck, and persuaded her father to teach her how to repair the car, so that she could self-diagnose and repair it in the event of a failure, and then drive a 25-ton heavy truck on the spot in three years.
But the reality is more difficult than Enshu thought.
The heroine, En Shu, was insulted and accused by the equipment manager and went to the secretary of the Youth League to complain.
At this time, what the Secretary of the Youth League said to En Shu can be said to be the core of this novel.
The secretary of the Youth League told En Shu that because Chairman Kim Jong Un encouraged the youth, you have the opportunity to drive a truck, which is not that you are special.
You have to thank the leader, not be ungrateful.
In other words, En Sook became a truck driver and drove a truck in the besieged area not because she drove well, but because Chairman Kim Jong Un attached importance to youth and cared for the welfare of youth, so we must thank and repay Chairman Kim Jong Un for his care and dedication to make due contributions to society.
The North Korean Central Television (KCNA) also broadcast a programme of women challenging male-dominated fields, which, like the novel "First Step", breaks down patriarchal attitudes.
The show introducing Kim Eun-hsin, a 20-year-old female driver, is one of them.
Kim Eun-hsin was a truck driver driving heavy logs on unpaved or cemented mountain dirt roads in a truck full of wood.
Kim ’ s father said he has four daughters, and his kindness is no less than his son ’ s daughter.
Like Eun Suk, the situation of North Korean women in other media is similar.
It tells the story of a daughter growing up in a family without a son who challenges the male dominance of the field, inherits the father ’ s profession or job strength to gain recognition.
But this is not what you want, but when you have to make the choice, so the story itself is problematic.
North Korean media reported that Chairman Kim Jong Un also spoke highly of Kim ’ s efforts and contributions.
Challenges, successes, and self-achievement can be said to be the process by which women realize their personal ideals and ambitions, but North Korean novels and media portray women challenging male-dominated fields as the blessing of Chairman Kim Jong Un ’ s emphasis on youth policy, and glorify the personal challenges and efforts of women as the performance of Chairman Kim Jong Un.
In addition to Kim, North Korean television recently introduced female drivers who drive bulldozers, women who work in mechanical plastering, women who directly manufacture tractors, and other women who are active in male-dominated fields.
Women who appear in the North Korean media or through literature have challenged male dominance and succeeded in social production, so the North Korean authorities have tried to use the female labor force and their accumulated wealth in the 1990s, when many North Korean women went to markets to earn their living, some through business, etc., so the North Korean authorities have tried to use the female labor force and their accumulated wealth to promote male dominance in the country. The area is engaged in social production.
In addition, the rate of women's participation in social activities is an important indicator of gender equality in society, so North Korea has also encouraged women to participate actively in social activities in order to increase the rate of women's participation in social activities.
After Kim Jong Un, chairman of the North Korean State Council, took office, he stressed that women should exert their abilities through social life and create a social atmosphere for this purpose.
In particular, North Korea has also trained female supersonic fighter pilots. In 2014, North Korean media reported that Chairman Kim Jong Un visited the flight training of the first female fighter pilots, Zhao Jinxiang and Lin Xue, and took commemorative photos with them. In 2015, North Korean media reported that Chairman Kim Jong Un visited the flight training and praised the female pilots as “flowers in the air. ”
According to reports, the aircraft they flew during the training was a MiG-21 fighter with a maximum speed of Mach 2.2.
It is very difficult for women to become fighter pilots.
In today's world, the number of female fighter pilots is small, and the number of female fighter pilots in various countries is even more limited, so North Korea's training of young female fighter pilots is something to show off to the world.
At the same time, North Korea has shown off its defense capabilities with elite female fighter pilots.
As a result, the number of North Korean women challenging male-dominated fields and gaining recognition is increasing, and it is interesting to see how this change in North Korean women will affect North Korean society as a whole.
