Site workers reveal a shocking truth about their industry, where they are often deprived of workplace-like infrastructure.
There are construction workers who reveal a shocking truth about their industry.
Source: AAP / Andy Brownbill / AP
Access to a functioning toilet should be a basic human right in any workplace, but it is a luxury for many construction workers.
A survey of thousands of electricians across Australia found that one in five women did not have a toilet to use at work.
The Electrical Trades Union survey of health facilities nationwide received 2,656 responses, and women were 10% less likely than men to use standing toilets.
Nearly half of the female respondents said they had raised the issue of inadequate facilities, while less than 30% of the male respondents had raised the issue.
Shockingly, toilet paper, soap and clean water are often considered luxuries.
According to the survey, about one in four workers said they did not always have access to toilet paper, and one in five did not often flush toilets with water.
Carlin, a 22-year-old electrician apprentice, told NCA NewsWire that the harsh working environment that electricians face every day is a problem for all electricians, especially women.
The problem seems to have become a cultural phenomenon, she says, but it shouldn ’ t be, “because they [toilets and water] are basic human necessities. ”
“If you ’ re called to a remote rural area, or even in the suburbs, you don ’ t have a toilet for hours … ”
Sometimes she avoids drinking water to reduce the number of trips to the toilet, but she says it makes her feel tired and dehydrated.
Carlin says it ’ s not a matter of public discussion, especially among older men.
She said this caused a lot of problems, especially in trying to increase the number of female electricians.
Toilets are actually a real problem, she said, especially when women are not able to use reliable toilets and related facilities during menstruation.
She revealed that she knew of several girls who had been infected by germs because they could not change sanitary towels or other items for 16 hours.
According to the Electrical Technicians Union, only 2% of electrical workers in Australia are women, and the union says more needs to be done to recruit women.
As Australia shifts towards electrification and more renewable energy, the electricity shortage is only expected to get worse.
The union called for a review of minimum health and safety standards in the workplace.
Michael Wright, acting national secretary of the Electrical Industry Union, said access to a hygienic, adequate number of toilets at work should be the basic expectation in 2022.
White collar workers expect these basic standards, he said, but for women on construction sites, there is still no guarantee of available toilets.
He questioned "how can we expect to increase the number of people if we discriminate against the other half of the potential workforce?" and "if we are to build Australia's future, we cannot exclude workers of all genders."

The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has updated its Red List of Threatened Species to include marine species such as dugongs, abalone and columnar corals.
According to the new list, nearly 10 per cent of the marine species assessed are at risk of extinction.
The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) announced Friday in Montreal, Canada, that of the 17,900 marine species assessed, more than 1,550 are at risk of extinction.
At least 41 per cent of these threatened marine species are affected by climate change.
One of the focuses is the marine herbivorous mammal dugong, which is a "vulnerable" species worldwide, but the dugong, which lives in the waters near East Africa and the waters near New Caledonia in the South Pacific, has been upgraded to "critically endangered" and "endangered" respectively.
New research has found that the number of adult dugongs in the waters near East Africa has dropped to less than 250, while the number of adult dugongs in the waters near New Caledonia has dropped to less than 900.
The major threats to them include accidental injury by fishing boats, poaching and destruction of their food seagrass by oil and gas exploration and exploitation activities.
The IUCN also assessed the survival of abalone for the first time, finding that 20 of the world's 54 species of abalone are at risk of extinction. The main problem facing abalone is unsustainable harvesting and illegal fishing, exacerbated by climate change, disease and pollution.
For example, the increasing frequency and severity of marine heatwaves caused the death of 99 per cent of Roche ’ s abalone in Western Australia ’ s northernmost region in 2011.
In addition, the number of columnar corals in the Caribbean Sea has dropped by more than 80% since 1990, and the threat level has jumped from "vulnerable" to "endangered" and directly increased to "critically endangered".
In recent years, a highly contagious "stony coral tissue loss disease" has emerged, infecting large areas of columnar coral and posing the most urgent threat to it.
IUCN Director General David Oberle said that human activities have created a "perfect storm" that is destroying the survival of marine life around the world.
He expressed the hope that the United Nations Conference on Biological Diversity, which is being held here, will be a success and set the direction for natural recovery in the coming period, and help solve the twin crises of climate change and biodiversity.
The IUCN Red List is the most authoritative list of species extinction risk assessments.
The latest Red List includes more than 150,000 species, of which 42,000 are threatened.

The present and future of quantum computing
New Research 2022 / 12 / 13 19: 16: 07 Edited by: Yuansheng
The limitations of contemporary supercomputers, as well as their implications for academia and institutions around the world, are drawing the attention of the scientific community.
For example, researchers can use current techniques to perform more complex simulations, such as those that focus on chemistry and the reactive properties of each element.
However, as the complexity of these interactions increases, they become more challenging for current supercomputers.
Due to the limited processing power of these devices, it is nearly impossible to complete these types of calculations, forcing scientists to choose between speed and precision when conducting these studies.
To provide some context for the breadth of these experiments, let ’ s start with the example of hydrogen atom modeling.
With only one proton and one electron in hydrogen, researchers can easily perform chemical reactions manually or rely on computers to complete calculations.
However, depending on the number of atoms and whether the electrons are entangled, the process becomes more difficult.
To write out every conceivable result of an element like thulium, which contains a staggering 69 electrons, all twisted together, would take more than 20 trillion years.
Obviously, this time is too long for us, and we need a new way out.
Quantum computers open the door to a whole new world of possibilities.
The equations needed to simulate chemistry have been known to the scientific community since the 1930s, but it has only recently begun to build computers with the ability and reliability to perform these calculations.
Today ’ s quantum computers provide the speed researchers need to mimic all aspects of chemistry, making them significantly predictive and reducing the need for laboratory testing.
Colleges and universities may be able to use quantum computers to augment existing knowledge of chemistry.
Consider the potential time and cost savings that could be achieved if quantum computers were able to eliminate the need for laboratory testing during research.
Moreover, since the computational power to master chemical properties did not exist previously, this step could lead to a major step forward in chemistry previously unknown to the world
01. Quantum computing in practice
Many companies are already using quantum computing.
For example, IBM is working with Mercedes-Benz, ExxonMobil, CERN, and Mitsubishi Chemical to implement quantum computing into their products and services:
Mercedes-Benz
Mercedes-Benz is exploring quantum computing to create better batteries for its electric vehicles.
The company hopes to shape the future of modern electric vehicles by implementing quantum computing in its products and making an impact on the environment by implementing quantum computing in its products in an effort to be carbon neutral by 2039.
Simulating what ’ s going on inside a battery is incredibly difficult, even with today ’ s most advanced computers.
However, using quantum computing technology, Mercedes-Benz can more accurately simulate chemical reactions in car batteries.
Exxon Mobil
ExxonMobil is using quantum algorithms to more easily discover the most efficient routes for transporting clean combustion fuels around the world.
Without quantum computing, it would be almost impossible to compute all routing combinations and find the most efficient routing combinations.
European Centre for Nuclear Research
The European Centre for Nuclear Research (CERN) is trying to discover the secrets of the universe.
Using quantum computing, CERN can find algorithms to pinpoint complex events in the universe in a more efficient way.
For example, quantum computing could help CERN figure out patterns in the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) data.
Mitsubishi Chemical
A team from Mitsubishi Chemical and Keio University is working on a key chemical step for lithium-oxygen batteries: lithium superoxide rearrangement.
They are using quantum computers to "perform accurate simulations of what happens inside a chemical reaction at the molecular level".
Advantages and disadvantages of quantum computing
Quantum computing has the potential to revolutionize industries such as finance, pharmaceuticals, artificial intelligence, and automotive in the coming years, fundamentally changing the world around us.
The value of quantum computers comes from the probabilistic way in which they operate.
By using the probabilistic computing style directly instead of simulating it, computer scientists have shown potential applications for fast search engines, more accurate weather forecasts, and precise medical applications.
In addition, quantum computers represent the original motivation for the development of quantum computing and are very useful in directly simulating quantum mechanics.
Perhaps the main appeal of quantum computing is that it can solve problems faster, making it ideal for applications that need to handle large amounts of data (for example, aerospace logistics, drug manufacturing, molecular research, or other fields that use canonical processes at the atomic level).
However, creating a powerful quantum computer is not an easy task and involves many drawbacks.
The sensitivity of quantum computing systems to extreme temperatures is one of the main drawbacks.
In order for the system to function properly, it must be near absolute zero temperature, which poses a major engineering challenge.
Moreover, quantum bit quality is not where it needs to be.
After a given number of instructions, qubits can produce inaccurate results, and quantum computers lack error correction to solve this problem.
Because of the number of wires or lasers required to make each qubit, keeping control is difficult, especially if the goal is to create a chip with a million qubits.
And quantum computing is very expensive: the cost of a single qubit can be as high as $10,000 or so.
Finally, if standard information systems and encryption methods are used for malicious purposes, they will be overwhelmed by the processing power of quantum computers.
These computers ’ reliance on the principles of quantum physics allows them to decrypt the most secure data (e.g., bank records, government secrets, and internet / email passwords).
Cryptography experts around the world will need to develop encryption techniques that can withstand possible attacks from quantum computers.
Impact of Quantum Computing on Higher Education
The education community is always looking for new opportunities for growth and prosperity.
Many higher education institutions have begun extensive research into quantum computing, using the unique properties of quantum physics to usher in a new era of technology, including computers capable of performing currently impossible computations, ultra-secure quantum networks, and exotic new quantum materials.
Oxford University
Researchers at the University of Oxford are interested in quantum research because of its huge potential in areas such as healthcare, finance and security.
The university is recognized worldwide as a pioneer in the field of quantum science.
Oxford and York universities demonstrate first working pure state NMR quantum computer
Harvard University
Researchers at Harvard University have established a community group, the Harvard Quantum Initiative for Science and Engineering, with the goal of making significant progress in science and engineering related to quantum computers and their applications.
According to research conducted by the group, the “second quantum revolution ” will build on the first quantum revolution, which is responsible for the development of global communications, technologies such as GPS flight, and medical breakthroughs such as magnetic resonance imaging.
University of Maryland
Researchers from the University of Maryland's Department of Physics, the National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the Physical Sciences Laboratory are part of the Joint Quantum Institute "dedicated to the goal of controlling and utilizing quantum systems."
Institute of Technology
MIT researchers have built a quantum computer and are working on areas such as quantum algorithms and complexity, quantum information theory, measurement and control, and applications and connectivity.
University of California, Berkeley
Researchers at the Center for Quantum Computing and Information at the University of California, Berkeley are working on basic quantum algorithms, cryptography, information theory, quantum control, and experiments with quantum computers and quantum devices.
University of Chicago Quantum Exchange
Researchers at the University of Chicago Quantum Exchange are focusing on developing new ways to understand and utilize the laws of quantum mechanics. CQE encourages collaboration, joint projects and information exchange between research groups and collaborating institutions.
China University of Science and Technology
Researchers at the University of Science and Technology of China are exploring quantum optics and quantum information.
Areas of major interest include quantum foundations, free space and fiber-based quantum communication, superconducting quantum computing, supercooled atomic quantum simulations, and quantum metrology theory and theory-related concepts.
One broad impact on higher education is that quantum computing will open up new careers for tomorrow ’ s students.
In addition, this technology will allow for accurate forecasting of the overall growth of the job market and the demand for skilled and knowledgeable workers in all fields.
In the near future, the power of quantum computing will be unleashed on machine learning.
In the field of education, quantum-driven algorithms will make informed decisions about student learning and deficiencies, just as quantum computing promises to revolutionize medical classification and diagnosis.
In addition, quantum computing will power a new era of individual learning, knowledge and achievement.
This will be achieved by processing large amounts of student data in a timely manner, and quantum computers may eventually have the ability to control programs designed to accommodate students ’ unique achievements and abilities, as well as backfilling specific areas where students may need help.
These aspects of quantum computing are critical to achieving the goal of truly personalized learning.
Through the cloud, you can access any of the relatively small number of physical quantum subcomputers in the world.
These computers include the 20 + IBM Quantum System One, which is currently installed more in the United States, Germany and Japan, and more are planned in the United States, South Korea and Canada.
Anyone with an internet connection can log on to a quantum computer and be educated on the basics of quantum programming.
For example, IBM offers a variety of quantum-centric education programs, including access to quantum computers, teaching support, summer schools, and hackathons.
The IBM Quantum Educator and Investigator Program and Qubit ’ s “Introduction to Quantum Computing ” are just two examples of quantum computing resources that are accessible to educators and students alike.
Such initiatives are absolutely necessary.
Colleges and universities around the world need to collaborate to bridge the current knowledge gap in quantum education and prepare the next generation of scientists and engineers.
04 、 Conclusion
The quantum computing revolution is happening.
We have just entered a new era of computing.
Next generation computing is not the next generation of hardware, but the next generation of algorithms and computing
Quantum computers use quantum mechanics principles to solve problems.
Compared to classical computers, the state of a quantum system is inherently probabilistic.
This means that quantum computers can handle many times more computations than conventional computers.
05, extended reading
The main players in quantum computing can be divided into four categories: the first category is international technology giants, such as IBM, Google, Honeywell, etc.; the second category is quantum computing startups, such as Rigetti, IonQ, etc.; the third category is national scientific research institutes, such as Fermilab, Argonne National Laboratory, and the Institute of Quantum Information and Quantum Technology Innovation. University of Cambridge, University of Science and Technology of China, Harvard University, etc.
Today's quantum computers can only deal with one or a few aspects of the problem, and they have not yet reached the level of generality.
Quantum technology companies not only need to invest heavily in developing quantum computers, but also need to have many researchers designing and manufacturing quantum hardware and software to support these machines.
In the future, general quantum computers need to work on the underlying quantum physics equipment, quantum computer architecture, quantum resource scheduling, upper quantum programming language, quantum algorithms and quantum application software.

In the fall of 2013, Ian Goodfellow and his university lab partner held a farewell party at the bar.
Everyone took their seats and started pouring beer.
After three rounds of drinking, Goodfellow was already slightly intoxicated, and the group of researchers began to debate what was the best way to create a machine that could create a realistic picture of itself.
They knew they could train a set of neural networks to recognize images and then reverse them to produce them.
But it can only produce some fine, photo-like images, and the results are unconvincing.
But Goodfellows have an idea.
They can perform statistical analysis of images generated by neural networks — identifying the frequency, brightness, and relationship of specific pixels to other pixels.
The results of these analyses are then compared with real photos, which shows where the neural network went wrong.
The problem is that they don ’ t know how to encode this data into their systems — which can take billions of counts.
Goodfellow offers a completely different solution.
What they should do, he explained, is build a set of neural networks that can learn from another set of neural networks.
The first neural network creates an image that tries to trick the second neural network into thinking it ’ s real.
The second set points out the first set of errors, and the first set continues to try deception, and it starts again and again.
He said that if the two sets of opposing neural networks had been facing each other long enough, they would have been able to make realistic images.
But Goodfellow's friends do not agree.
They say the idea is worse than theirs.
At the same time, if he hadn ’ t been a little drunk, Goodfellow might have felt the same way.
“It ’ s hard enough to train one neural network, ” a sober Goodfellow might say.“ You can ’ t train another neural network in a neural network that ’ s learning algorithms. ”
At the time, however, he was fully convinced that it could be done.
When he returned to his apartment that night, he sat at his bedside table in the dark, still slightly intoxicated, with the light of his laptop screen reflected on his face.
“My friend is wrong! ” he kept telling himself, while piecing together what he called two sets of adversarial neural networks with old code from other projects, and began training the new device with hundreds of photos.
After a few hours, it began to show the performance he expected.
The resulting image is small, like a nail, and there is some blur.
But they look just like the photos.
He later said he was totally lucky.
“If it doesn ’ t work, I might give up, ” he later called it“ generative adversarial networks ” (GANs) in a paper that published the concept.
Since then, he has become the “father of GAN ” in the global AI research community.
He officially joined Google in the summer of 2014, when he was already actively promoting GAN, emphasizing that it would help accelerate AI research and development.
When he explains the concept, he often uses Richard.
Feynman for example.
Feynman once wrote on a classroom blackboard: “What I can ’ t create, I don ’ t understand. ”
Goodfellow believes that Feynman ’ s dictum applies to machines in addition to humans: what artificial intelligence cannot create, it does not understand.
They point out that creation can help machines understand the world around them.
“If AI can imagine the world in realistic detail — being able to learn how to imagine realistic images and realistic sounds — it can encourage AI to learn about the structure of the real world, ” says Goodfellow.“ It can help AI understand the images it sees and the sounds it hears. ”
Like speech, image recognition, and machine translation, GAN represents a big step forward in deep learning.
Or at least that ’ s what deep learning researchers think.
Yann LeCun, director of Facebook ’ s Artificial Intelligence Research Center, praised GAN in 2016 as “the coolest concept in deep learning in nearly two decades. ”
Goodfellow ’ s achievements inspired many projects around his concept, either to improve it, to build on it, or to challenge it. Researchers at the University of Wyoming built a system that produced small but perfect images of insects, churches, volcanoes, restaurants, canyons, and banquet halls.
A research team at NVIDIA is building a neural network that can transform a photographic image of a hot summer day into a dead winter day.
A team at the University of California, Berkeley, has designed a system that transforms images of horses into zebras, turning Monet ’ s paintings into Van Gogh ’ s.
These are the most popular and interesting R & D projects in science and technology and academia.
But at that moment, the world changed dramatically.
In November 2016, Donald Trump won the US presidential election.
American life and international politics have changed dramatically, and artificial intelligence is hard to escape.
Almost immediately, the government began to crack down on concerns about the flow of talent caused by immigration.
The number of international students studying in the United States has been declining, and now it has fallen sharply, and the American science and mathematics community, which relies heavily on foreign talent, is beginning to suffer.
“We ’ re shooting ourselves in the head, ” said the CEO of Seattle ’ s renowned Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence.“ We ’ re not shooting in the foot, we ’ re shooting in the head. ”
Some big companies are already expanding their overseas R & D operations. Facebook has set up laboratories in Montreal and in his hometown of Paris.
The threat posed by the Trump administration ’ s immigration policies became apparent in April 2017, just three months after he took office.
Meanwhile, Geoffrey Hinton, the “father of the deep learning movement, ” helped found the Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence.
It is a research and development incubator in Toronto with $130 million in funding, including contributions from U.S. tech giants such as Google and Vinda.
In addition, Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau has pledged $93 million to support AI R & D centers in Toronto, Montreal and Edmonton.
Sara Sabour, a young researcher, is a key partner in Hinton, and her career illustrates just how politically sensitive international aspects of AI can be. In 2013, after completing computer science at the Sharif University of Technology in Iran, Sabour applied to the University of Washington to study computer vision and other aspects of artificial intelligence. Wisdom, the school accepted her application.
But the U.S. government refused to grant her a visa, apparently because she grew up and studied in Iran, and her field of study, computer vision, is also potential military and security technology.
The following year, she successfully enrolled at the University of Toronto and followed Hinton to Google.
Meanwhile, the Trump administration continues to block immigrants from entering the United States.
“It looks like American companies are benefiting now, ” Adam.
Adam Segal, an expert on emerging technologies and national security at the Council on Foreign Relations, said, “But in the long run, neither technology nor jobs will be realized in the United States. ”
But the relocation of talent is not yet the biggest change Trump has made in the White House.
Since the end of the election, the domestic media has begun to question the impact of online fake information on the election results, causing the public to worry about "fake news".
In an initial attempt to allay such concerns, Zuckerberg, in a public appearance in Silicon Valley a few days after the election, downplayed the idea that voters were being influenced by fake news as a “pretty crazy idea. ”
But many journalists, lawmakers, celebrities and citizens disagree.
In fact, this problem was rampant during the election, especially on Facebook ’ s social network, where tens of thousands, if not millions, of netizens shared fake stories with titles such as “FBI agent suspected of Hillary Clinton ’ s email leak was found dead and apparently committed suicide after murder ” or“ Pope Francis supports Trump ’ s presidential campaign to shock the world. ” A Russian company with close ties to the Kremlin paid more than $100,000 to buy online ads on 470 fake accounts and pages, spreading false information about race, gun control, gay rights and immigration.
At the same time, public concerns are projected onto GAN and other related technologies, bringing them into the spotlight with a completely different look from the past: these technologies appear to be conduits for generating fake news.
However, research by artificial intelligence scientists at the time was entirely fueling this view.
A team at the University of Washington used the neural network to create a video of Obama speaking.
Engineers at a Chinese startup used the same technology to make Trump speak Chinese.
The fake images are not new.
Since the invention of photography, people have used technology to fake photos.
But because modern deep learning can self-learn these jobs — or at least part of them — they make such edits easier.
Politicians and activists, nation-states, social activists, and dissidents don ’ t need to hire large numbers of people to create and distribute fake images and videos. They can do this automatically by building a neural network.
AI ’ s image manipulation potential is still months away from being fully realized during the US presidential election.
At the time, GANs could only produce images the size of a nail, and putting words into the mouths of politicians still required rare expertise, not to mention other hard work.
But a year after Trump ’ s victory, a team at the Finnish lab developed a new GAN, called a “progressive GAN, ” that uses a network of antagonistic neurons to create realistic-sized images of plants, horses, buses, and bicycles that can be virtually unreal.
But the most important thing about this technology is that it can create a human face.
After analyzing thousands of celebrity photos, the system can create an image of a person who looks like a celebrity but isn ’ t — a face that looks like Jennifer Aniston or Selena Gomez, but isn ’ t actually a real person.
These created faces look like real people, with their own wrinkles, pores, shadows, and even personalities.
“The technology is moving so fast, ” says Phillip Isola, a professor at MIT who helped develop it.“ It started out like, ‘ Well, this is an interesting academic question, you can ’ t use it to make fake news, it can only produce something that ’ s slightly ambiguous.
And it turns out, “Oh, you can really make a face that ’ s as real as a photo. ”
""
A few days after the announcement of the new technology, Goodfellow spoke in a small conference room in Boston, minutes before a reporter asked him what the technology meant.
He noted that he knew that anyone could already use Photoshop to create fake images, but stressed that the point was to make the job easier.
“We are accelerating what is already possible.
"He said.
He explained that with the improvement of these methods, the era of “drawing and truth ” will also come to an end.
“Historically, it ’ s a bit of a fluke that we can rely on video as evidence that something has happened, ” he said.“ We used to look at a thing based on who said it, who had the motivation to say it, who had the credibility, who didn ’ t.
Now it looks like we ’ re going back to that era. ” But there ’ s going to be a difficult transition in the middle.
“Unfortunately, people today don ’ t think critically.
At the same time, people tend to think from ethnic consciousness about who has credibility and who does not.
It also means that there will be at least a period of adjustment.
“Artificial intelligence has opened many doors for us that we haven ’ t opened.
We don ’ t know what ’ s on the other side of the door, ” he says. “But in this technology, it ’ s more like artificial intelligence closing doors that our generation is used to opening. ”
The adjustment period began almost immediately when someone, calling themselves Deepfakes, began to clip images of celebrities into pornographic videos and then upload them online.
The anonymous prankster later made available the apps that worked out the tricks, and the videos immediately popped up on discussion boards, social networks, and video sites like YouTube.
Platforms such as Pornhub, Reddit and Twitter rushed to ban this behavior, but this operation and related concepts have infiltrated into mainstream media.
“Deep Forgery ” has also become a term that refers to any artificially created video that is distributed online.

Liu Yangwei, chairman of Honghai (2317), pointed out that if semiconductor technology is the automotive industry, quantum technology is like the aircraft industry, and will do cars does not mean that it will definitely do airplanes, so Taiwan's development of quantum technology must screen out the myth of semiconductor advantages.
In addition to continuing to promote software and hardware technology, and international integration and exchanges are also very important, and we call on industry, government and academic circles to join together to make more contributions.
Speaking at the "Annual Conference on Quantum Computing and Information Technology and TAQCIT" on the 25th, Liu Yangwei said that Taiwan has some myths about quantum technology and believes that due to its advantages in semiconductor manufacturing, it will definitely lead the way.
But in fact, it is not so simple. The core of quantum computing is quantum superposition and entanglement, which can not be achieved by relying on advanced semiconductor processes alone.
Liu Yangwei reminded that Taiwan cannot follow the past mentality and thinking to face the rise of quantum technology, and must find a clear development direction and goal to catch up.
He pointed out that if we think of semiconductors as the automotive industry and quantum as the aircraft industry, this relationship is clear.
An airplane will not replace a car, but being able to do a car does not necessarily mean being able to do an airplane.
Liu Yangwei believes that in the future, the entire computing system will be a mixture of quantum and classical computing systems, just like the current transportation system is a diverse system composed of cars, ships and airplanes.
Semiconductor technology does not automatically extend to quantum technology, just as a car running on the road does not automatically become an airplane.
Liu Yangwei said that the core of quantum computers is based on hardware and quantum bit chips.
Taiwan is good at chip manufacturing, packaging, peripheral materials and control bits. It should first be based on the advanced process of semiconductors to develop high-end components of quantum computers, cutting in from the perspective of design and peripheral systems, rather than thinking of it as an advantage.
At the same time, Taiwan needs to cultivate software talents, focus on the error correction and programming language of quantum bits, and master the overall technology of quantum computers. Liu believes that the development of quantum technology in Taiwan is not only a continuous advancement of software and hardware technology, but also a very important part of international integration and communication.
Liu hopes that the government can organize project research teams from a macro perspective of industry, government, and academia to exchange and learn from foreign research institutions, introduce relevant research equipment and machines, and help local research teams develop relevant applications, and continue to expand the regulatory flexibility of talent introduction.
Liu Yangwei pointed out that since the establishment of the Institute of Quantum Computing of Honghai Research Institute in 2020, there are currently 14 members, a total of 19 papers have been published, and quantum research talents have been discovered through the holding of the “Honghai Science and Technology Award ”, which has awarded more than 9 million yuan in scholarships as of this year.
In addition to discovering talents, Honghai Education Foundation has also cooperated with Professor Zhang Qingrui to organize a summer high school quantum computing learning camp and teacher training camp, which has so far been attended by more than 1200 teachers and students.
Quantum comics and high school quantum textbooks will be launched at the end of this year, allowing quantum education to take root and accumulate Taiwan ’ s quantum talent pool.

Functional and physical therapy division and collaboration in the rehabilitation of Parkinson ’ s disease
Health Care Network
Wu is 82 years old. She was diagnosed with atypical Parkinson ’ s disease five years ago. Her daily life or work needs to rely on a walking aid to walk. significantly improved.

Grandpa Liu is 75 years old and has been suffering from Parkinson ’ s disease for 10 years. He was able to walk without assistive devices. He suddenly became severely degraded and fell all the time. Even with the help of a single crutch, he still fell many times.
Fall prevention and recovery, the sooner you start, the better.
The incidence of Parkinson ’ s disease falls is 50%. Although early rehabilitation can reduce the incidence of falls, most people still like Grandma Wu and Grandpa Liu, wait until the fall will go to the rehabilitation department, but in fact, the sooner the rehabilitation is carried out, the better.
Regarding fall prevention, Dr. Yang Yunlin and Dr. Cheng Zhiyan, who work in the same clinic, said that occupational therapy and physical therapy can provide promotion strategies to improve both typical and atypical Barkinsonian disease, and they can choose health insurance or pay for it according to their conditions and needs.
But what is the difference between functional and physical therapy in recovery from Parkinson ’ s disease?
Figure 2: In response to Pai Yo ’ s stiffness, the occupational therapist focuses on daily practice, while the physiotherapist focuses on the improvement of ability.
Functional Therapy Exercises Focusing on Daily Life
Occupational therapists will choose appropriate aids and adjust the environment according to the ability of the case to successfully complete a task, set stage goals, and plan step-by-step training strategies to help patients recover the most daily activities, such as waking up, standing or turning in a small space, going to the bathroom, lighting and darkness in the space, and walking space.
Dr. Yang said that people with Parkinson ’ s disease often fall because they are distracted by not focusing or doing two things at the same time. Therefore, functional therapy will disassemble the original automated movements into simpler steps, allowing patients to reconnect, practice and remember them, giving “inner prompts ” to reconstruct the automated path, or designing action-awareness dual task training.
Take Grandma Wu as an example, the promotion strategies he offers are:
1. Focus on movement and steps
2. Practice stride and turn techniques
3. Practice life tasks such as taking things while walking
4. Turn around and squat down to check things
Physiotherapy is the promotion of eyesight.
Physiotherapy will assess the overall state of the patient ’ s posture, muscle strength, balance, mobility, ability to shift, and continuous movement performance, and then prevent and improve the patient ’ s movement through exercise, equipment, hand therapy, functional training and technical aids, and improve the injury by correcting posture or reducing pain.
LSVT BIG ® (Lee Silvermann Voice Treatment - BIG therapy) is a movement training therapy designed specifically for Parkinson ’ s disease that emphasizes the principle of “big movement ” to increase the quality of movement.
Therefore, when Zheng therapists guide the case to balance, joint activity, muscle strength, and gait training, they will always ask the case to remind themselves that the action strategy should be large, the center of gravity should be shifted, and the center of gravity should be in place when standing up, so that the risk of falling can be reduced.
Grandpa Liu also thought of seeking physical therapy because of a fall. The strategies of Dr. Cheng ’ s physiotherapist are:
1. Movement Enlargement Training
2. Core stability training
3. Dynamic Balance Training
4. Gait training
Whether it is functional or physical therapy, people with Parkinson ’ s disease can significantly improve their walking ability in one to three months as long as they have professional guidance and practice, and gradually reduce the incidence of falls.
The step-by-step walking training strategy is short for stride skills, flat ground walking, big turns, and road walking. Each practice time is 2-4 times a week, one hour each time, plus 15-20 minutes of daily self-training at home.
Fig. 3: Occupational therapists use assistive devices in combination with training for Pau ’ s hand stiffness. Physiotherapists assess the main cause of the overall condition before planning a training program.
Hand stiffness and physical treatment of Parkinson ’ s disease
For example, in patients with Parkinson ’ s disease, when their hands are weak, trembling or stiff, they will use meal aids combined with training to improve their ability to eat autonomously, for example, by increasing the handle of a spoon so that they can hold it better, so that their fingers can be less laborious.
Physiotherapy will focus more on the patient ’ s respiratory, nervous, skeletal, muscular endurance and other physical conditions to assess why it is impossible to eat autonomously.
Is it possible that the problem is due to insufficient support for the shoulder blades, or is it because his muscles are too stiff to get to his mouth?
Or is the movement too small to scoop for a long time? The tremor is too severe, affecting the smoothness of the movement.
Once the problem has been identified, the physiotherapist will plan the training according to the individual situation.
Dr. Cheng added that although Dr. Yang and I are usually responsible for different cases, because we work together, we can often communicate with each other quickly on the situation of the case, learn from each other's professional perspectives, and propose strategies to promote the integration of functions and physical therapy, which is also one of the advantages of self-funded rehabilitation.
It's best to do a rehabilitation assessment for people with Parkinson's disease with or without drugs.
In particular, Yang Qineng therapists pointed out that the patients with Parkinson ’ s disease have a large difference in drug effectiveness. The ideal state of rehabilitation is that they can also do training or evaluation when there is no drug effect. If the patient ’ s condition assessment can also have drug effect and no drug effect, it can provide more complete information, and the therapist can provide more assistance.
If it is really difficult to go out in a drug-free state, the family can at least help to photograph the patient ’ s difficult movements at home.
Exercise is better than one.
Exercise has been shown to improve mobility and walking balance in patients with Parkinson ’ s disease.
Which exercise is most effective for people with Parkinson ’ s disease?
The two therapists said that diversity is better than a single, and patients are encouraged to do a variety of sports. It is best to include muscle strength, balance, coordination, softness, aerobic and double work situations for training to promote balance, muscle endurance, movement control, cognition and other different functions. Tai Chi, walking, dancing, and cycling are all good ways.

The official domestic production rate is 60%, but most of the core components are imported from Europe and the United States, or are manufactured by foreign companies authorized by joint ventures in the mainland, especially the aircraft engines that are considered the most important.
The C919 is powered by a LEAP-X1C turbofan engine developed by General Motors of the United States in cooperation with Safran of France, and is the same series as the Boeing 737 and Airbus A320.
The Trump administration has tried to ban the sale of Chinese LEAP engines, but it has not succeeded. However, the current export license period is only until 2025.
If the C919 is not sold well, the license may be extended, and if the C919 is sold well, the supply may be severed under the current Sino-US relationship.
The Chinese alternative is to step up research and development of the domestically produced "Yangtze" CJ-1000A engine, which was also officially unveiled at the Zhuhai Air Show in September 2022.
Some analysts predict that domestic engines can be replaced as soon as 2025, but the relevant airworthiness certification will have to go all the way, which may take years.
According to a research report published by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) in 2020, C919 has 82 major suppliers, of which 48 are US companies or joint ventures with the United States, 26 are European or European companies, and only 7 are Chinese companies.
The report also ridiculed the C919, saying that it was not a Chinese-made aircraft at all, because most of the components were imported, so the C919 did not pose a commercial threat to Boeing or Airbus.
The ARJ21, which is also made by China Commercial Aviation, has only delivered less than 100 aircraft in the past seven years, and the C919 will probably encounter the same problem in the future.
Although the C919 technology is not enough to compete with the competitiveness of Boeing and Airbus, the mainland still expects it to introduce more key technologies for the development of China's civil aviation industry.
At present, in addition to the possible replacement of the Yangtze CJ-1000 engine, 16 Chinese and foreign joint venture companies participate in the C919 supply chain, providing important systems such as avionics, flight control and communications navigation for the C919.
The consideration of international airworthiness standards is also an important factor in the low production rate of C919. European and American countries take flight safety as the reason to lead the development of airworthiness standards, which are exclusive in many systems and components, and cannot obtain airworthiness certificates without using systems and parts that meet international airworthiness standards.
The industry estimates that it will take at least 20 years for all domestically produced parts and systems to meet international airworthiness standards.
In this view, the current expectation of C919 to open up the international market or greatly improve the domestic production rate is too high and unrealistic.
China's main purpose is to develop the civil aviation market, C919 is only the first aircraft of its own production, from the determination of the case so far only more than 10 years, if compared to Airbus spent 40 years to stand firm in the international market and Boeing Chamber of resistance, China Commercial Aviation this experience can only be regarded as just entering the door, now do not worry that China can become a rival.
Since China has decided to develop civil aviation, it needs to give civil aviation manufacturers and suppliers a chance to test and improve, and it needs to use the vast market in China to train and build aircraft manufacturers.
However, the worry is that state-owned enterprises like private enterprises to produce highly competitive goods, from past experience it is almost impossible.
Perhaps under the requirements of the policy, there will be a considerable part of China's civil aviation to buy domestic civil aviation aircraft, but state-owned civil aviation aircraft manufacturers can not produce internationally competitive products because of this, inefficient, wasteful, corruption problems will still be the nightmare of the operation of the state-owned enterprise system, these are the biggest obstacles to the future difficult to compete with Boeing and Airbus.

Xinhua News Agency, Beijing, January 19, (International observation) Sweden found large rare earth mines may be difficult to alleviate the "rare earth shortage" in the European Union.
Xinhua News Agency reporter Xie Binbin
Sweden's state-owned mining company Luosa-Kiruna Mountain has announced that it has discovered a rare earth deposit in the Kiruna region of northern Sweden, containing more than 1 million tons of rare earth oxides.
It is the largest known rare earth deposit in Europe.
Analysts believe that although this discovery will help the EU to ease the situation of highly dependent on imports of rare earths, the EU's "rare earth shortage" is unlikely to have significant changes in the short term.
“A long way from discovery to development. ”
Jan Mostrom, chief executive of Luosa-Kiruna Mountain, said recently that the scale of rare earths in Kiruna has yet to be determined.
The company plans to submit a mining concession application this year, and it is expected to take several years to explore the deposits and the conditions for sustainable mining.
Rare earth is known as "industrial vitamins" and is widely used in metallurgy, military, petrochemical, glass ceramics, agriculture and new materials.
But the EU relies almost entirely on imports for rare earths.
"There is a long way to go from discovery to real mining," Mostrom said.
"It will take at least 10 to 15 years to start mining the deposit and supply it to the market," he said.
Several rare earth deposits have previously been found in Europe, such as in Kwane Bay in Greenland and Norrachel in Sweden.
However, because these sites are located near the Arctic, the need for local environmental protection has led to the development of the project is not smooth.
Ross Embleton, a researcher at Wood Mackenzie Consulting in the United Kingdom, believes that unless the approval process is shortened, the newly discovered deposit will not have an impact on the global supply of rare earths in the short term.
New opportunities for the Swedish industry
European Commission President von der Leyen said that the EU ’ s demand for rare earths is expected to increase fivefold by 2030, and that rare earths and lithium will “soon be more important than oil and gas. ”
For Sweden, the discovery of rare earth minerals will help reshape its image as an EU mining powerhouse, giving it a bigger role in the EU ’ s green transition.
The website of the French newspaper Le Monde pointed out that in the past decade, metal prices have been depressed, and mining exploration activities in Sweden have decreased sharply, but there are signs of recovery in the recent past.
It is also reported that this spring, the European Commission will introduce measures to strengthen its own supply of key raw materials, which means that Sweden's rare earth project may receive EU support.
Short-term changes to the pattern.
The European Union has been trying to diversify the rare earth supply chain for several years.
After the escalation of the crisis in Ukraine, the EU is more eager to push forward the process, especially to seek to strengthen its own supply within the EU.
However, the rare earth industry chain involves a series of procedures such as mining and separation, and the rare earth mineral reserves alone are not enough, which is also an important reason for the EU to get rid of its import dependence.
Geologists from the Swedish Geological Survey pointed out that Europe currently lacks the comprehensive capacity to process rare earth metals and manufacture intermediate products. “We also need to focus on the entire industry chain of rare earth metals, such as rare earth permanent magnets for wind turbines or electric vehicle engines. ”
Analysts stressed that the European rare earth industry chain is incomplete, the lack of advanced technology, talent and other supporting resources required, which will lead to the production of rare earth products cost too high, lack of competitiveness, and thus lead to the lack of incentives for enterprises to invest in this industry.
Experts pointed out that because China has the advantages of technology patents and industrial scale in processing links such as refining, many European companies choose to cooperate with China to process and extract raw materials, which is more economical.
Argus Media, an international independent pricing agency involved in energy and commodity markets, believes that some companies are pushing for a supply chain for rare earth products in Europe, "but the road to production of rare earth products is very difficult and requires huge investment and political will."

This is an anecdote, but it reflects China ’ s influence in Africa today.
Chinese foreign minister visits Africa for first time in 33 years
In January, Chinese Foreign Minister Qin Gang visited Ethiopia, Gabon, Angola, Benin and Egypt for the first time in 33 consecutive years.
These five countries are located in the east and south of Africa, including English, French, Portuguese and Arabic-speaking countries, while the capitals of Ethiopia and Egypt are the headquarters of the African Union and the League of Arab States respectively.
A simple look at these points shows that China ’ s diplomacy with Africa is by no means simple.
The United States is shouting that it wants to compete with China, and the Biden administration has refocused its attention on Africa, no longer treating African countries as “muck pits ” as in the Trump years.
US Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen visited Senegal, Zambia and South Africa last month; UN Ambassador Linda Thomas-Greenfield also visited Ghana, Mozambique and Kenya.
Before that, President Joe Biden hosted the second U.S.-Africa Summit in Washington in December, after eight years, and announced his intention to visit sub-Saharan African countries this year.
Africa is becoming a territory that cannot be ignored by both sides of the Great Game, and there are multiple logics behind it.
Economically, China is the world ’ s factory, and the United States intends to reindustrialize, which requires Africa ’ s abundant natural resources to drive it.
Africa has 30% of the world ’ s mineral deposits (including 40% gold, 90% platinum), 12% oil, and 8% natural gas.
50% of the world ’ s production and 70% of the world ’ s production of cobalt are from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Africa is also one of the most promising markets in the future.
With a population of 1.4 billion, or about 17% of the world ’ s population, Africa is on par with China and India, but with an economy of only $3 trillion, or only 3% of the world ’ s population, and the equivalent of less than 70 million people, the United Kingdom is still behind India.
Africa ’ s population is expected to grow to 2.5 billion by 2050, a quarter of the world ’ s population and a relatively young population overall.
Politically, Africa today has 54 countries, more than Asia, accounting for more than a quarter of the 193 member states of the United Nations.
In the voting of the United Nations General Assembly, all countries, big or small, have an equal vote, which is why it is called “Africa ’ s Got the World ”.
In 1971, the United Nations proposed to restore the People ’ s Republic of China to the United Nations, with 11 of the 23 countries in the United Nations; the General Assembly voted in favor of the 76 countries, and Africa accounted for 26 of the 26 countries. The Biden administration is convinced to realize that it would be a big loss without African help.
Geographically, Africa is located between the Indian Ocean and the Atlantic Ocean, and it is the offensive and defensive pass of the great chess game between China and the United States outside the Pacific Ocean.
Maritime security in the Horn of Africa is related to China ’ s energy and raw material supply lines, which has led to the establishment of a Chinese naval supply base in Djibouti.
The US Indo-Pacific Strategy would also be a short-sighted mistake if it did not include Africa.
Some in the US have even speculated that Chinese investment in West African ports “threatens the east coast of the United States. ”
The United States mends African relations to ease racial tensions at home
In addition, for the United States, repairing relations with Africa may also have the hope of alleviating racial contradictions at home, which is also in line with the characteristics of the current Democratic Party.
So the Biden administration is re-energizing the U.S. diplomatic offensive on Africa, and to be fair, at least by American standards, the card is quite sincere.
Although Biden repeated the joke at the US-Africa summit, he said that the plan to invest in Africa's digital economy was $350 billion, but only $350 million in fact, but the entire US initiative covers trade, investment, health, climate and other aspects, with a total value of $55 billion.
Compared to Biden ’ s $150 million for ASEAN and $810 million for South Pacific island nations, he clearly attaches much more importance to Africa, in his words, “all in. ”
But the United States has a lot to do to counter China ’ s influence in Africa.
“The United States always feels that Africans need help and need to be told what to do, ” Arikana Chihombori-Quao, the African Union ambassador to the United States from 2010 to 2019, told Al Jazeera last year.“ Unless the United States treats them as equals, it will fail. ”
She explained that the United States and African countries have not set an agenda in advance of the meeting, such as "Come to Washington, let me tell you what to do", "Biden will not do this to other heads of state." She criticized the US practice of insulting, disrespecting Africa, and there is some racism in Washington.
In contrast, he pointed out that before the meeting between China and African countries, the African heads of state will discuss and clarify what issues will be discussed, such as trade, aid and investment, to “provide a way forward and follow up ”; China has such a mechanism with individual African countries on both sides or with Africa as a whole.
She admitted that the Chinese side was not like this at first, but quickly changed its strategy.
“They understand that Africa has what they want.
“You are important, our relationship is important.
""
Indeed, during the U.S.-Africa summit, Biden singled out six African countries that will vote this year to meet their leaders and “urge them to ensure that elections are free and fair. ”
In the United States election result is questioned by many voices in the United States (whether it is reasonable) today, this is not very humorous?
Fighting for people ’ s hearts takes a long, sustained effort, and Biden ’ s $55 billion initiative is only the beginning, if it does eventually come to fruition.
China ’ s total trade with Africa in 2021 amounted to $254 billion, almost four times the $64 billion that the United States and Africa have.
China ’ s stock of overseas direct investment in Africa increased from US $490 million in 2003 to US $43.4 billion in 2020, and has surpassed that of the US since 2014.
The Awakening Age of Pan-Africanism Is Expected to Come True
To be honest, the United States should also downplay the message that it sees them as pawns in the game of big powers.
Now the United States does not mention the opponent, any investment seems to be unable to rationalize internally, can not get on the horse.
The United States invited African countries to be guests, but they were all "infiltrated" by China and Russia; and when Yellen went to Zambia, he had to mention China to be comfortable.
Southeast Asian countries have repeatedly stated that they will not stand for the side between China and the United States, and African countries believe that they are equally sober, because no normal person wants to be the next Ukraine.
Now that the US military aid to Ukraine is almost $100 billion, what is the non-US $55 billion initiative?
The US attitude of putting war and military-industrial interests before construction and development will never change, and it will never be able to counter China ’ s influence in developing China.
In addition, the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA) came into force in 2019, and although there is still a long way to go, this still reflects that Africa is beginning to have sufficient conditions to promote pan-Africanism.
Africans realize that the borders that the West carved up over Africa in the past have evolved into today ’ s borders, which are the shackles of Africa ’ s development, and that Africa must be integrated and self-strengthening in order to have a way out.
This is the awakening of Africa, is the United States and other Western countries ready?

Many countries expressed disappointment with India's stance on the Russian-Ukrainian conflict.
However, some observers believe that India has shown signs of considering a rupture with Russia, and India may change its previous neutral course. In September 2022, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said in a conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin that “today ’ s era is not an era of war ”, a phrase that seemed to warn Russia, as U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken called Modi ’ s stance“ significant. ”
American political scientist Happymon Jacob also wrote that the Indian government is weakening its “long-term partnership ” with Russia and is committed to closer cooperation with the United States.
Based on the interpretation of these events, India needs to strengthen its cooperation with the West and is alienating Russia.
However, the view that "India and Russia will part ways" is too "taken for granted" and does not reflect realistic possibilities.
It is true that in the context of Russia ’ s growing economic dependence on China and its provision of unreliable weapons to India, India should theoretically move away from Russia and promote diversification of partnerships, but this is not realistic or feasible.
The United States, the first Western country to win over India on a number of issues, turned a blind eye to the human rights dispute.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Joe Biden at last year ’ s G20 summit. (Reuters)
In fact, India is not ready to give up the India-Russia partnership, and in November 2022, Indian Foreign Minister Sujishin visited Russia, stressing that the relationship between the two countries is “strong and stable. ”
For this reason, US policymakers still need to make policy plans around the reality of a lasting India-Russia relationship, but they should also make India realize that Russia is a burden; the United States cannot punish and sanction India because of the close India-Russia relationship.
Because for the United States, India can play a more prominent and more active role in the Indo-Pacific region.
The False Dawn
Analysts have concluded that India is trying to distance itself from Russia based on what Indian officials say, including Modi ’ s verbal confrontation with Putin in September 2022, a vote against Russia at the United Nations, and the cancellation of a multi-billion dollar Russian weapons procurement program (fighters and helicopters).
However, these developments do not mean that India has explicitly chosen to stay away from Russia.
The Washington Post called Modi ’ s September 2022 statement to Putin a “rebuke. ”
But in fact, Modi ’ s statement was not intended primarily to address the Russian-Ukrainian conflict, but to express concern about rising food and energy prices.
Several assessment reports issued in India have warned against over-reading Modi ’ s remarks, which are no different from the official position of India in the past that the war has inflicted great trauma on developing countries.
It is undeniable that India has indeed sided with the West in some of the UN ’ s procedural votes, such as allowing Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky to speak at the UN General Assembly in September 2022.
But in more substantive votes, such as the October 2022 vote on four regions of Russia ’ s military campaign in Ukraine, India abstained.
In addition, in early 2022, India cancelled several agreements to purchase Russian weapons (such as the MiG-29 fighter).
But the decision has little to do with the Russia-Ukraine conflict, and is more about promoting domestic arms production and supporting India ’ s “self-reliance ” program.
A few months before the Russian-Ukrainian conflict erupted, the Indian government had planned to cancel these deals, including the purchase of Boeing P-8I aircraft from the United States, in favor of domestically produced weapons.
But India will still buy major weapons such as S-400 air defense systems, stealth frigates and nuclear submarines from Russia, which means India will be tied to Russia for decades to come.
In fact, India cannot really break with Russia, because Russian-made weapons account for a large share of India ’ s arsenal, and Russia still plays a significant role in India ’ s geopolitical considerations, so most of India ’ s political elite still prefer friendly Indian-Russian relations.
India can ’ t really break with Russia because Russian-made weapons make up the bulk of India ’ s arsenal and most of India ’ s political elite still prefer friendly India-Russia relations.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

(2) Patience and persistence
India has long regarded Russia as a valued partner in its “multidirectional alliance ” strategy.
Within the framework of this strategy, India wants to maintain a constructive strategic partnership with several major powers at the same time, but refuses to form an exclusive alliance with any major powers.
India ’ s leaders believe that the “multidirectional alliance ” strategy is still valid today because Western analysts have misjudged Russia in several important ways.
The authors ’ study found that despite strong Western sanctions against Russia, Indian national security officials still believe in Russia ’ s endurance and durability.
They expect Europe to struggle under pressure from inflation and energy shortages, while Russia ’ s economy will be boosted by rising commodity prices.
After all, Indian companies are investing in Russian energy projects, such as oil and gas extraction projects in Sakhalin, Russia ’ s Far East.
In addition, India has doubled its investment in future India-Russia cooperation in defense technology research and development (including the development of the Brahmos cruise missile).
The leaders also believe that the Russian-Ukrainian conflict is likely to turn into a military stalemate that will culminate in a negotiated cease-fire and that Russia will eventually be allowed to reintegrate into the international community.
Indian policymakers also believe that Russia will remain an important geopolitical force that will help India.
India relies on Russia for missile technology, submarine nuclear reactors, and hypersonic weapons, and Russia can still provide diplomatic support to India in the United Nations Security Council, which can exert influence on India ’ s other continental neighbors.
In addition, with the Russian regime in turmoil, Indian officials want to be able to extract more benefits from their dealings with the Russian government, just as India did at the beginning of the collapse of the Soviet Union, when the two countries established the Brahmos Aerospace Joint Venture.
As India continues to maintain friendly relations with its old partner Russia, the West is hesitant to punish India.
Some observers believe that India will downplay the India-Russia relationship as Russia becomes closer to China and even more dependent on China.
But unlike Western officials, Indian officials do not believe that tough sanctions will force Russia into China ’ s arms, because there is no shortage of friction between China and Russia over Central Asia and the Arctic.
In the eyes of Indian policymakers, India can become a "wedge" between Russia and China, helping Russia retain some autonomy in Sino-Russian relations, and avoiding Russia becoming a "small follower" of China.

Third, get on with it.
Much of the Indian military ’ s combat and strike equipment is dependent on Russia.
The Russian-Ukrainian conflict has limited and delayed India ’ s process of acquiring spare parts and equipment upgrades, thus creating a “supply shock ” to India ’ s main Russian-made weapons arsenal.
While India remains concerned about the performance of Russian-made weapons and Russia ’ s ability to provide spare parts, it has not taken any hard measures to curtail the use of Russian materials or to purchase substitutes to accelerate the diversification of military equipment imports.
All in all, India has no plans to achieve a rapid and comprehensive transformation of its Russian-made weapons systems by bringing in other foreign suppliers. After the border crises of 2019 and 2020, there has been some peace and stability in the border area, and Indian strategists believe that India should maintain a low level of operational readiness for the next few years, even if that means increased vulnerability.
In the short to medium term, India plans to keep up with its existing inventory, while at the same time sourcing from the secondary market for Russian components and relying more on domestic military equipment.
India will continue to work with Russia to meet outstanding delivery commitments and selectively sign contracts with the West to support the development of India ’ s indigenous defence industry.
In the long run, India wants to be largely self-sufficient in terms of defense needs and no longer rely on external suppliers.
While India aims to diversify its arsenal and become self-sufficient within the next 20 years, it still needs some key technical support from Russia.
Su-30 fighters will remain the backbone of the IAF for decades, but they cannot be maintained or upgraded without Russian technical support.
India ’ s most important defense export, the BrahMos anti-ship cruise missile, currently sold mainly to Southeast Asian countries to deter China, uses Russian propulsion technology.
As long as Russia is in control of key elements of India ’ s advanced weapons systems, especially fighter jets, cruise missiles and submarines, Russia has considerable influence over India.

The First Friend of India
In addition to the above material considerations, the common ideological orientation has also driven India and Russia to maintain friendly relations.
Both Indian and Russian officials support the “polycentric ” vision of a global order in which there is no single dominant hegemony and each major power maintains its own sphere of influence.
Both India and Russia believe that a “multicentre ” is more stable than an international order governed by one or two superpowers.
India ’ s political elite also maintains a “sense of closeness ” to Russia, which stems from India ’ s decades-long tradition of cooperation with the former Soviet Union.
Two months after the conflict broke out, Yoga Jyotsna, an Indian scholar, said that “Russia is India ’ s number one friend in the eyes of the military and people of insight. ”

[Retain talent] Enterprise test 4 days a week production efficiency improvement
Do you want to work four days a week?
According to the Wall Street Journal, most of the British companies participating in the four-day work week test said that after six months of testing, the staff turnover rate and absenteeism rate fell sharply, which is the largest four-day work week test to date. 61 companies, including banks, fast food restaurants, marketing consultants, etc., involved 2900 employees. Eighteen companies said they would permanently implement the four-day workweek.
For decades, the market has been exploring the idea of working less than five days a week, or 40 hours a week, which has become a new opportunity under the pandemic, as home-based and mixed-work arrangements have become more widely accepted, and employers have also taken the opportunity to explore whether shortening work hours can improve employee happiness and loyalty.
Working days have become a retention and recruitment issue
Juliet Schor, an economist and sociologist at Boston College, said that it was initially due to the mental fatigue of wage earners during the epidemic, but it has now become a retention and recruitment problem.
Her team has helped conduct research around the world on a four-day workweek, including researchers from the UK think tank Autonomy and the University of Cambridge.
The research is being conducted around the world. Small tests in the United States and Canada are being led by research institutes in the United Kingdom, and similar tests are being conducted in Australia and Brazil. Unilever, an internationally renowned consumer goods company, is also participating in the tests.
Testing in Iceland, involving more than 2,500 employees in various industries, researchers found that most employees maintained or increased productivity, as well as reduced work stress.
Most companies that try 4-day work are small employers
Since most of the companies experimenting with four-day work are small employers, many large companies have yet to embrace the concept.
In the test, some employees reported that it was difficult to complete all the work during this time.
In a study conducted in the UK from June to November, most employees did not increase their work intensity, but bosses held fewer meetings to give employees more time to get their work done.
Finally, employers rated employee productivity and performance on an average of 7.5 on a scale from 0 (very negative) to 10 (very positive), and at half of the test, 46% of companies said their business productivity remained unchanged, while 34% reported a slight improvement and 15% reported a significant improvement.
20% of your time is wasted on unnecessary meetings
On the other hand, 39% of employees reported less stress at work, but half of employees reported no change in their index.
Nearly half of employees reported improved mental health and 37% reported improved physical health.
Claire Daniels, CEO of Trio Media, a digital marketing company with 13 employees in the UK, said she took part in the trial to see if she could improve productivity.
Before the test began, she analyzed with employees that 20% of their time was wasted on unnecessary meetings, business trips, and other inefficiencies.
"Very soon, we will know that we do not have to do any extra work in these four days," she said.
The productivity of the 4-day work was flat or slightly improved from the same period last year
Daniels pointed out that she would have employees work from Monday to Thursday, and Tuesday to Friday, and have employees take extra places to follow up on their colleagues ’ work during the holidays.
No longer do marathon daily team meetings with employees, in longer meetings involving customers and multiple presentations, employees will only attend part of the meeting based on necessity and then leave.
The hardest part, she says, is for employees to make sure they don ’ t go back to their old work mindset or habits. Overall, productivity was flat or slightly higher compared to the same period last year, with revenue up 47%.
She wants to continue experimenting for another six months before making a permanent change, “but I don ’ t think we ’ re going to go back to the typical five-day week. ”
If the four-day work week can improve production efficiency and the employees are happy, the bosses think that they can give it a try, or they think that the workload of five days can be completed in four days, so that the employees can continue to overcomplete their work on the fifth day.
