Experts from the German Institute of Ecology: The biggest problem in the development of electric vehicles is not the shortage of raw materials.
An electric car recharges at a public charging station in Berlin, Germany on October 29, 2021 ｜ Photo Credit: GettyImages
What we want you to know is
Lithium, cobalt, rare earth and other resources are very rich, which is the problem that restricts the development of the electric vehicle industry?
Matthias Buchert, an expert at the German Ecological Institute, said in an interview with Deutsche Welle that the biggest bottleneck in the development of electric vehicles is how quickly the automotive industry is transforming.
Text: Voice of Germany Chinese Network
Interviewee: Bucht (Head of Resources and Mobility at the German Institute of Ecology)
• Voice of Germany: The popularity of electric vehicles seems to be growing faster than predicted.
Previously, experts predicted that by 2030, the world will produce about 130 million pure electric vehicles.
That estimate has now been raised to more than 200 million.
Mr. Bucht, is there enough raw material to put so many new electric cars on the road?
Bucht: There are enough raw material reserves around the world, and resource constraints are not the problem.
Of course, there may be problems such as temporary shortages in the industrial chain.
Whether in the actual mining process of raw materials or in the process of processing raw materials into finished products, if demand suddenly and sharply rises, there may be short-term problems.
But this does not mean that the whole market will collapse, but rising demand will bring a bumpy market.
We experienced semiconductor shortages during the COVID-19 (Severe Special Infectious Pneumonia, COVID-19, Wuhan Pneumonia) pandemic.
At that time, there were temporary bottlenecks in chips for cars and electronics, and delivery of some vehicles was delayed for more than a year.
For electric vehicles, people will of course ask whether there will be a shortage of important raw materials for a longer period of time.
In this regard, experts from the German Mineral Resources Agency believe that the biggest problem is lithium, which is a key element of lithium-ion batteries.
I would think this situation is a reminder that the supply side needs to pick up the pace to keep up with the rapidly growing demand.
Germany: Do you think it will work?
Bucht: Let ’ s keep talking about lithium.
At present, lithium is mainly mined in Australia and Chile, and a smaller amount is mined in China.
In the two main mining countries (Australia and Chile), geopolitical unrest is unlikely.
In fact, there are many lithium mines in the United States, Latin America, Asia, Africa and Europe, but so far only a small amount of mining has taken place in Portugal.
There are also potential mining possibilities in Finland, Austria, Serbia, Spain, Portugal and France.
In Italy and Germany, high temperature deep groundwater rich in lithium is ideal for exploitation.
• Deutsche Welle: You mean that you think the raw materials sector is mainly a relatively manageable risk and problem? So what is the situation in terms of energy supply? More electric vehicles will also consume more electricity.
Bucht: Electric cars are very efficient.
If the entire sedan industry and many commercial vehicles are powered by electricity, it is predicted that the total electricity consumption will not be ten times what it is today, but will only increase by about a third compared to the current total electricity demand in Germany.
Moreover, there is still a great potential for energy savings in terms of electricity consumption, for example in the field of lighting or by replacing old appliances (using a new generation of more energy-efficient appliances).
This also applies to the industrial sector.
• Deutsche Welle: In terms of heating, more and more electricity will be consumed in the future due to the installation of a heating system with a heat pump.
Bucht: This is the second important area, and it will certainly be involved.
In the industrial sector, the demand for electricity is also rising due to the increasing use of green hydrogen energy and the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions, which requires a large amount of clean electricity.
That ’ s why the European Union and German governments want to expand photovoltaic and wind power plants on a large scale.
These are major challenges, and there is not much time left for us, not 50 years.
(Germany) The federal government ’ s goal to expand renewable energy has been tightened and tightened a lot recently.
I think in the last 10, 15 years, a lot of time has been wasted.
That ’ s why everything moves faster in the future.
• Voice of Germany: Electric cars also need more charging stations and larger grid capacity.
Consider the arguments over whether electricity supply should be limited at certain peak times, such as charging electric vehicles or heating with heat pumps, because the grid may not have enough capacity at certain peak times.
Bucht: It really is.
Conversely, at other times, our power grid tends to have excess power.
We just need a better balanced system, that is, an intelligent system.
Then, the (electric) car may not start charging at 7 p.m., because it is the peak of power consumption and only starts charging at midnight.
As for the additional charging stations (electric vehicles) needed, research has shown that there is less need for fast charging devices in public places, as many electric vehicles are charged in parking lots at home or at work.
Of course, this does not mean ignoring the expansion of public charging infrastructure.
But we must also be careful not to overplay the problems we could have dealt with.
Voice of Germany: But if people don ’ t know if there are enough charging stations, will they still buy electric cars?
Bucht: Of course, the charging infrastructure needs to be expanded as soon as possible, and there needs to be more charging stations.
This requires cooperation between public authorities and private investors in the energy sector.
In addition, the energy industry recently said that the utilization rate of existing charging stations has been greatly improved, which of course can increase the profit margin.
• Voice of Germany: If you are an expert, draw up a league table.
From today ’ s perspective, what factors are the biggest obstacles to the spread of electric vehicles?
What is the biggest problem at the moment?
Bucht: The biggest problem is probably that supply in the industrial chain lags behind demand.
In addition, some politicians have said that there are other options besides electric vehicles, such as using synthetic fuels for internal combustion engines.
But it ’ s already technically obsolete.
In the car field, the use of synthetic fuels (E-Fuels), even if the production is enough for one day, is too low in efficiency.
The real challenge is the huge transformation of the automotive industry.
Billions of euros will have to be redistributed.
Look at the production of batteries, which so far have mostly been done in Asia.
Europe wants to build more than 30 large factories for the production of electric vehicle batteries, more than half a dozen in Germany alone.
It requires a huge investment.
We also need battery cell components, namely cathode materials, anode materials, etc.
In order to do so, Europe ’ s capacity must also increase faster.
We have to go further back to raw materials through intermediate materials that come from hard rock, salt lakes or deep geothermal energy, like lithium.
In my opinion, there is too little discussion about the motor.
The production of electric motors requires so-called permanent magnets, which in turn require rare earths.
So far, China has a strong position in the production of magnets.
There is plenty of room for improvement in the United States, Europe and Australia, which is why there needs to be a huge strategic change here, and the term “turnaround ” fits well here.
• Deutsche Welle: You believe that there are still many problems to be solved in the development of electric vehicles.
This may be only a small consolation, but the fact is that the internal combustion engine cars we know today also took quite a long time to develop.
Bucht: It is so.
The difference is that in the current situation, the time pressure is very large.
According to EU regulations, from 2035, only new cars with zero emissions can be sold, that is, they are actually fully electric vehicles.
Germany wants to be climate neutral by 2045, so it ’ s best to have no internal combustion locomotives on the road.
Therefore, we have at most 10 to 15 years to achieve these goals, which is not easy.

IQM to deliver first quantum processing unit in Q2 2023
Quantum computer to be installed at Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC) and integrated into MareNostrum 5 supercomputer
IQM Quantum Computer opened (Photo: Business Wire)
BARCELONA, Spain -- (BUSINESS WIRE) -- IQM Quantum Computers (IQM), a leader in quantum computers in Europe, announced today that it has been selected to supply quantum processing units for the first Spanish quantum computer.
The computer will be installed at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC) and integrated into Spain ’ s extremely powerful MareNostrum 5 supercomputer.
IQM is a member of a consortium led by Spanish companies Qilimanjaro Quantum Tech and GMV, selected by Quantum Spain. Quantum Spain is an initiative promoted by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation through the Secretary of State for Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence (SEDIA) in December 2022 to build the first quantum computer for public use in Southern Europe.
Dr. Jan Goetz, co-founder and CEO of IQM Quantum Computers, said: “This is a major announcement from IQM.
We have the right background and experience in developing quantum processors, computers, and national quantum ecosystems.
We look forward to working with Qilimanjaro Quantum Tech and are excited to be part of such a strong consortium and play an important role by providing quantum processing units for this prestigious project. ”
The integration of quantum computers into MareNostrum 5 enables solutions that complement the capabilities of existing supercomputers for use by research institutions, companies and public organizations, as well as the development of technology and industry in Spain and the creation of high-quality jobs, thereby significantly increasing the impact of research and innovation.
Victor Canivell, co-founder and CEO of Qilimanjaro, said: “We are delighted to be able to leverage the expertise of an excellent company like IQM to support the development of this innovative system, which will be based entirely on Spanish and European technologies.
We believe this will be a productive collaboration and we look forward to working with IQM to roll out the system. ”
Jani Heikkinen, Head of Business Development and Regional Manager, Spain, said: “This is yet another example of our European leadership and it demonstrates our commitment to working with public and private institutions to advance the Spanish quantum ecosystem.
We can also provide the necessary support for the project through our office in Madrid, "he said.
About IQM Quantum Computers
IQM is a pan-European leader in building quantum computers.
IQM provides internal quantum computers for supercomputing centers and research labs and provides full access to their hardware.
For industrial customers, IQM leverages its quantum advantage through a unique, application-specific joint design approach.
IQM is currently working with VTT to build Finland ’ s first commercial 54-qubit quantum computer.
In addition, a consortium led by IQM (Q-Exa) is building quantum computers in Germany that will be integrated into HPC supercomputers to create quantum accelerators for future scientific research.
IQM has offices in Singapore, Paris, Madrid, Munich and Espoo and employs more than 240 people.
For industrial IQMs, quantum advantages are provided through a unique, application-specific, co-design approach.
About Qilimanjaro
Qilimanjaro Quantum Tech is a high-tech startup that uses analog models, a different but complementary model of quantum computing, to bring practical applications of quantum computing to market in less time than digital quantum computers.
Qilimanjaro has created a coherent quantum retreater that runs real-world applications through our cloud, such as optimization tasks in areas such as logistics, finance and energy sectors, as well as quantum simulations of chemical and physical processes that are prevalent in the materials and pharmaceutical research industries.
Qilimanjaro aims to provide customers with faster, more accurate and sustainable solutions to computing problems.
Since its first year of operation, the company has signed a number of customer contracts and is a major contributor to the European Commission ’ s AVaQus H2020 coherent quantum annealing project.
Qilimanjaro is a spin-off of the Barcelona Supercomputer Centre (BSC), the University of Barcelona (UB) and the Spanish Institute of High Energy Physics (IFAE).
About GMV
GMV is a privately held technology conglomerate founded in 1984 that trades globally in the following industries: aerospace, aviation, defense and security, cybersecurity, intelligent transportation systems, automotive, healthcare, telecommunications and IT, serving government agencies and large corporations.
With more than 3,000 employees, the company currently has subsidiaries in Spain, the United States, Germany, France, Poland, Portugal, Romania, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Belgium, Malaysia and Colombia, with 2021 revenue approaching 260 million euros.
75% of its turnover comes from international projects on five continents.
The company adopts a growth strategy based on continuous innovation and invests 5% of its turnover in internal research and development. GMV has been certified by CMMI Level 5, the world ’ s most authoritative model for organizational process capability enhancement, and holds several international patents.

AI phone scam, gangster AI "copied" son's voice to ask for help, Canadian couple lose 120,000 yuan
Author: Zhang Yuejing
Published: Updated:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology is developing rapidly, and now there are free software online for users to upload short recordings, after which AI can “copy ” the extremely real sound line.
US media reported on March 5, a fraudster phoned a Canadian couple, using AI to imitate their son ’ s voice, and swindled $21,000 (about HK $120,000) from them.
The Washington Post said on the 5th that the fraudsters used AI to synthesize their son Benjamin Perkin ’ s “voice ” to call the couple on the phone, saying that“ he ” drove to kill an American diplomat and was in prison, and urgently needed money to pay for his lawyer.
A few hours later, the fraudster said that Perkin's lawyer called, saying that Perkin needed $21,000 before the trial.
Although the two feel that there is something wrong, but because the sound is very similar to the truth, they still withdraw cash and exchange it for Bitcoin, and give it to the scammers.
Later that night, they received a call from Perkin himself, and the two were shocked to be deceived.
They later said that when the gangster called, they felt like they were really talking to their son.
Perkin said the family had made a report to the local police but could not get the money back due to lack of insurance.
It ’ s not clear how the fraudster got Perkin ’ s voice, but he has a YouTube channel where he introduces his favorite snowmobile sports.

Russia ranks among India ’ s top five trading partners for the first time
Author: Zhang Yuejing
Published: Updated:
Russian media reported on March 11 that Russia became India ’ s top five trading partners for the first time, and in the first 10 months of the 2022-2023 financial year, the two countries ’ trade volume has reached a record of about US $39.8 billion (about HK $310.4 billion).
According to data from India ’ s Ministry of Commerce and Industry, between April 2022 and January 2023, Russia ranked 5th in the list of India ’ s major trading partners.
This is the first time this has happened in India since such statistics began in the late 1990s.
In the previous financial year (April 2021 to March 2022), Russia was ranked 25th, while the best ranking appeared in the financial year 1997-1998, ranking 16th.
Russia ’ s rise in the ranking is due to a sharp increase in trade between the two countries: the trade volume between the two countries was only $13.1 billion in the last fiscal year, but reached $39.8 billion in the first 10 months of the current fiscal year.
India exported about $2.5 billion worth of goods to Russia during this period and imported about $37.3 billion worth of goods, with a trade deficit of about $34.8 billion.
India ’ s top four trading partners for the fiscal year were the United States (trade volume of about US $108.4 billion), China (about US $95.9 billion), the United Arab Emirates (about US $70.2 billion) and Saudi Arabia (about US $44.3 billion).
India has a trade deficit with all of its major partners outside the United States.

The boss, the staff, come back and try?
Three weeks after the British try "two working nine days a week"
Journalist Ni Haoxuan / Comprehensive Report
The UK has previously held the world ’ s largest “3 Days a Week Off ” experiment, and the final results seem to be very successful. The companies involved in the experiment have not only achieved high revenue, but also significantly reduced employee turnover and absenteeism, and significantly improved employee health and satisfaction.
However, there are still a small number of companies willing to implement the "3 days a week", and now the UK has launched the next wave of experiments, this time the "9 days a week", hoping to find a new model that is acceptable to more people.
This is an advertisement, please continue reading.
According to CNBC, although the "3 Days a Week" experimental project jointly organized by the British non-profit organization 4 Day Week Global, the British think tank Autonomy, Boston College, Cambridge and the University of Oxford has received positive feedback, but many companies still cannot accept it, after all, from 2 days a week to 3 days a week, which is equivalent to a 20% reduction in the working day.
So now there is a new way of working, that is, "two working nine days a week."
The “9-day work week ” method is usually the employee takes regular leave every other Friday of the week, taking two days off a week and three days off a week.
Some companies have adopted a "9-day 2-week" with conditions, such as requiring employees to work overtime on the working day; others have implemented a "9-day 2-week" without any conditions, but require employees to commit to maintaining the same output as in the past.
Basically, the concept is similar to the three days off, which is to reduce the working day of employees, so as to achieve a better balance between life and work; while improving employee mood and satisfaction, improve work efficiency, and thus maintain the same work output in less working hours.
One company CEO, who is implementing a “9-day two-week ” plan, told CNBC that switching between two and three days off creates a magical balance that prompts employees to guarantee that they can do the same amount of work as they do on the 3-day weekend.
However, there are also additional troubles, that is, every Friday there will be someone to work, someone on vacation, and sometimes it will bring some problems.
In any case, the focus is on finding flexible models that work for the company that are acceptable to both bosses and employees, rather than being constrained by the way society is currently accustomed to working.

China and Africa have been closely linked by similar historical experiences and common historical missions, and China and Africa have always been a community of destiny. Over the past 10 years, under the joint leadership and promotion of leaders of the two countries, China and Africa have worked hand in hand and mutually beneficial cooperation to promote economic and social development and benefit the people of both countries.

Belt and Road investment drops to low, US and Europe challenge China ’ s influence in Africa
Journalist Ni Haoxuan / Comprehensive Report
China ’ s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) will last for 10 years this year, and China ’ s influence on the African continent has been important even before the BRI.
However, as the United States and the European Union increase their investment power in Africa, China is under threat in Africa. According to a study by the Center for Green Finance and Development at Fudan University in Shanghai, Chinese investment in sub-Saharan Africa last year fell to 7.5 billion yuan from 16.5 billion yuan in 2021, a decline of about 55%, which is also the lowest level of Chinese investment in sub-Saharan Africa since the implementation of the Belt and Road Initiative.
This is an advertisement, please continue reading.
According to the Africa Report, in addition to the research report of Fudan University in Shanghai, research by the Center for Global Development Policy at Boston University has also found that China ’ s financing activities in Africa have continued to slow down since the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic.
But even so, China remains the largest foreign financier of infrastructure projects in sub-Saharan Africa, with investments totaling $155 billion over the past 20 years, giving it an important position in African countries.
After the Belt and Road Initiative was proposed, the United States saw it as a tool for China to expand its geopolitical influence, and the U.S. Congress hoped to counteract it by passing the Anti-China Malicious Impact Fund Authorization Act in December 2019, which aims to counter China ’ s influence in Africa and beyond by expanding foreign investment.
Just recently, the U.S. House of Representatives agreed to authorize the Anti-China Malicious Impact Fund to allocate $325 million per year for the next five years as anti-China bullion ammunition.
America ’ s positioning of the Belt and Road Initiative as a fraud is a debt trap for China to exploit African national interests.
However, for African countries, despite concerns about China ’ s opacity, not all countries have fully embraced the American narrative, and Africa still hopes that Chinese investment will help, especially in infrastructure construction.
According to Nikkei, Alicia Garcia-Herrero, chief economist for Asia Pacific at French investment bank Natixis, “The increased interest of the United States and the European Union in Africa reflects a shift in the global economic order. ”
As China slows its investment in Africa, both the United States and the European Union want to use this opportunity to expand their influence in Africa.
However, Nigerian economist Uche Igwe warned that “China is leading in Africa ” and that China ’ s long-term investment in infrastructure projects makes it easy for all Chinese companies in Africa to gain a huge advantage.
Some experts familiar with African issues believe that if the competition between the United States, the European Union and China is benign, such as competing for better loan terms for African countries to finance, then such competition can promote African prosperity and is welcomed by African countries.
But if the competition is vicious, such as the goal of eliminating each other ’ s power, and does not provide more tangible benefits to African countries, then this unhealthy struggle may have many negative effects on Africa.
In any case, the EU claims to be neutral and does not exclude some degree of cooperation with China, compared to the obvious hostility of the United States to China.
Although China ’ s investment in Africa has slowed down, it is still Africa ’ s main trading partner and has no intention of giving up its key influence in Africa.

Prehistoric meatballs made from woolly mammoth DNA, scientists fear death and dare not eat them.
Share:
How dare you eat woolly mammoth meatballs? Scientists from a meat company in Australia have created “prehistoric meatballs ” from muscle proteins from extinct woolly mammoth remains about 10,000 years ago. Scientists are afraid to eat“ prehistoric meatballs ” because they don ’ t know how the human immune system will react to the proteins of the woolly mammoth. Life.
How to make prehistoric meatballs
After sequencing the mammoth muscle protein, scientists took DNA from the African elephant (the closest relative of the mammoth) to fill in the missing genetic code.
The genes were then sequenced into stem cells from the muscle mother cells of the sheep, from which 20 billion cells were replicated to grow the mammoth meat, which was eventually used to make meatballs.
However, mammoth meatballs are not even available to researchers. Ernst Wolvetang, a professor of bioengineering at the University of Queensland who participated in the study, said, “We haven ’ t seen mammoth muscle protein for thousands of years, and if we eat it, we don ’ t know how our immune system will react ”, or further research can meet regulatory requirements.
He added that the research process for prehistoric meatballs was surprisingly simple and quick, and was completed in a matter of weeks.
Mammoth _ Cultivated Meat Company: Want to show the potential of cell culture meat
Cultivation meat company Vow said the mammoth study was chosen because it symbolizes the loss of biodiversity and the effects of climate change.
The extinction of the woolly mammoth is believed to be due to human hunts and the increase in the temperature of the Earth after the Ice Age.
The company hopes the research will show that cell-grown meat can replace meat from slaughtered animals, and that carbon dioxide emissions from large-scale livestock farming are also linked to global warming.

More than 1,000 tech leaders and researchers, including Elon Musk, have urged AI labs to pause development of state-of-the-art systems, warning in an open letter that AI tools "pose profound risks to society and humanity."
The letter, published Wednesday by the nonprofit Future of Life Institute, says AI developers are “locked in a race out of control to develop and deploy increasingly powerful digital minds that no one — even their creators — can understand, predict, or reliably control. ”
Other signatories include Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak, 2020 presidential candidate and entrepreneur Andrew Yang, and Rachel Bronson, head of the Bulletin of Atomic Scientists, which sets the world's "Doomsday Clock."
“These things are shaping our world, ” Gary Marcus, an entrepreneur and scholar who has long criticized AI system flaws, said in an interview.“ We face a perfect storm of irresponsible businesses, widespread adoption, lack of regulation, and a host of unknowns. ”
Advertisement
ChatGPT, Microsoft Bing, and Google ’ s Bard all have AI behind them, which can talk like humans, write articles on a variety of topics, and perform more complex tasks such as computer programming.
The push to develop more powerful chatbots has sparked a race that has the potential to determine the next leaders in the tech industry.
But these tools have been criticized for making mistakes in detail and for spreading false information.
The open letter calls for a moratorium on the development of AI systems more powerful than GPT-4, the chatbot launched this month by OpenAI, where Musk is co-founder of the research lab.
The letter said the suspension would provide time for AI systems to introduce a “shared security protocol. ”
"If such a moratorium cannot be implemented quickly, the government should step in and establish a moratorium," the letter said.
The letter states that development should be advanced “only when we are confident that robust AI systems will have a positive impact and that the risks will be manageable. ”
“Humanity can enjoy a prosperous future brought about by AI, ” the letter said.“ After successfully creating strong AI systems, we can now enjoy a ‘ summer of AI ’ in which we reap rewards, design regulatory systems for the benefit of all, and give society a chance to adapt. ”
OpenAI's chief executive, Sam Altman, did not sign the letter.
Advertisement
Marcus and others argue that persuading the broader tech community to agree to a pause is difficult.
But the likelihood of governments acting quickly is also slim, as lawmakers have done little to regulate AI.
Representative Jay Obernoldt, Republican of California, recently told The New York Times that the technology is not well understood in American politics. In 2021, EU policymakers proposed a law aimed at regulating AI technologies that could cause harm, including facial recognition systems.
The measure, expected to be passed as early as this year, requires companies to conduct risk assessments of AI technologies to determine how their applications will affect health, safety and individual rights.
GPT-4 is what AI researchers call neural networks, a mathematical system that learns skills by analyzing data.
Neural networks are the technology used by digital assistants such as Siri and Alexa to recognize voice commands, as well as the technology used by self-driving cars to identify pedestrians.
Around 2018, companies such as Google and OpenAI began building neural networks that learned from large amounts of digital text, including books, Wikipedia articles, chat logs, and other information picked from the Internet.
These networks are called Large Language Models (LLMs).
By finding hundreds of millions of patterns across all texts, LLM learns to generate texts on its own, including tweets, term papers, and computer programs.
They can even have a dialogue.
Over the years, LLMs built by OpenAI and other companies have learned from an increasing amount of data.
Advertisement
This improves their capabilities, but these systems still make mistakes.
They often mistake facts and make up information without warning, a phenomenon researchers call “hallucination. ”
Since the system seems to be completely confident in all the information it provides, it is often difficult to tell what is right and what is wrong.
Experts fear that these systems could be misused to spread disinformation faster and more efficiently than in the past.
They believe that these systems can even be used by people online to influence people ’ s behavior.
Prior to the release of GPT-4, OpenAI asked outside researchers to test the system for dangerous uses.
Researchers have shown that it can be coaxed into suggesting how to buy illegal guns online, describing how to make dangerous substances with household items, and writing Facebook posts to convince women that abortion is unsafe.
They also found that the system was able to employ a person on the internet using TaskRabbit and defraud the captcha test, which is widely used to identify robots online.
When people ask if the system is a “robot, ” the system calls itself a visually impaired person.
After changes to OpenAI, GPT-4 no longer does these things.
For years, many AI researchers, academics, and technology executives, including Musk, have worried that AI systems could cause even greater harm.
Some of them belong to a vast network of so-called “effective altruists ” who believe that AI will eventually destroy humanity.
Advertisement
The letter was led by the Future of Life Institute, an organization dedicated to studying the existential risks to humans that has long warned of the dangers of AI.
But the signatories came from all walks of life and academia.
While some of those who signed the letter are known for repeatedly voicing concerns that AI could destroy humanity, others, including Marcus, are more concerned about the immediate dangers, including the spread of disinformation and the risks caused by people relying on these systems for medical and emotional counseling.
The letter "indicates that many people are deeply concerned about what is happening," said Marcus, who signed the letter.
He believes the letter will be a turning point. "I think this is a very important moment in the history of AI, and perhaps in the history of humanity," he said.
However, he acknowledged that those who signed the letter may find it difficult to persuade companies and researchers in the broader AI industry to pause.
"This letter is not perfect," he said.
"But the spirit of the message is exactly right."

If the J-20 is China ’ s top and most popular fighter, then the J-10C should be given the most expectations, because the CCP believes it is a more competitive fighter in the international arms market in recent years. Although the J-10 was designed in the 1980s, after many improvements and upgrades, it has spawned at least 11 models, and its export model, the J-10C, has gradually opened up the international market. There was a lot of praise in the beginning.
Foreign military analysts believe that after continuous upgrading, the J-10 fighter will be able to use by the 2040s, becoming the United States F-15's most powerful competitor.
The initial design was a 3rd generation fighter architecture, but the constantly upgraded J-10 series has been included in the 4th generation fighter by many experts, it has more than 11 mounting points under the fuselage and wing, and can carry an astonishing number of weapons, including laser-guided missiles, GPS-guided and glide bombs, as well as general air-to-air and ground attack ammunition.
The J-10 was designed by Chengdu Aircraft Design Institute (611) and manufactured by Chengdu Aircraft Company. It was designed in the 1990s, when the PLA developed its own fighter aircraft with a program called the "Destroying Project Plan". It was the No. 10 project, hence the name J-10.
The original concept was to extensively use the technology of the 1980s US F-15 and F-16 fighter aircraft and new fighter manufacturing concepts. The chief designer was Song Wenchong, which first flew in 1998 and entered service in 2003.
With a range of 2,500 kilometers and a payload of 1.9 tons, the J-10 has appeared in at least 11 types of aircraft after years of modification on this basis, making it the largest number of derivative aircraft in China.
According to the British Institute for International Strategic Studies (IISS) estimates, the Chinese air force currently has at least 540 J-10s, which can be assembled on a large scale to deal with super large battles.
The "Global Defense" website has carefully analyzed the latest J-10 upgrade to a phased array radar, which can control multiple modes of fire control radar and track 10 targets at the same time. If it is a semi-active radar, it can attack 2 targets at the same time, and if it is an active radar, it can attack 4 targets at the same time.
Analysis pointed out that the ability to track and attack multiple targets at the same time is very important for modern aircraft, and this ability can also be matched to the AN / APG-63 (V1) radar on the F-15.
Later, Boeing again updated the active phased array radar version of the F-15, allowing the F-15 to follow 14 targets simultaneously and attack six of them simultaneously.
This upgrade is said to maintain a nominal advantage over the J-10 fighter that has replaced the active phased array radar.
The upgrade of the J-10 is also the most noteworthy, including the replacement of its domestic engine WS-10B, and the 2018 Zhuhai Air Show was also the first time that the J-10B was equipped with a thrust vector jet engine for a difficult flight performance, which won the attention of many international media and heated discussion on the Internet.
Since then, the WS-10 engine has gradually replaced the Russian AL-31 engine, and some of the J-20 fighters have been switched to the WS-10.
In addition, military experts also noted that the new version of the J-10 also uses a water drop type cockpit cover, allowing the pilot to have a wider and nearly 360-degree all-round view.
Analysts believe that after the radar, fire control, avionics, cockpit covers and engines have been upgraded, the J-10 has the ability to fly into the 2040s, and in recent years began to complete transactions in the international market, proving that nearly 20 years of continuous upgrading and improvement has achieved considerable results, and will also become a very strong international competitor for the United States F-15 fighter.
However, to compare the F-15 with the J-10, some people may think that it is not fair.
Because the F-15 architecture was determined in the late 1960s, it first flew in the early 1970s; in contrast, the J-10 was determined in the early 1980s, and it first flew in the late 1990s.
The theoretical basis of the original design is more than 10 years apart, and the final design is more than 20 years apart.
From the design background difference analysis, the F-15 is a high thrust ratio, low wing load, low resistance high-speed air superiority fighter designed by the US military according to the experience of the Vietnam War and the failure of the F-4 Phantom fighter. Air and ground attack aircraft.
Therefore, some analysts believe that if we want to compare, J-10 may be more suitable to take the F-16 as the target.
Coupled with the tense situation in the Taiwan Strait in recent years, there are more and more people are more concerned about the comparison of the J-10 and Taiwan's main air force fighter F-16.

After artificial intelligence company OpenAI launched its newly upgraded ChatGPT last week, AI industry executives, including U.S. electric car maker Tesla CEO Elon Musk, recently signed a letter calling for the development of all more advanced artificial intelligence developer systems than ChatGPT-4 to be suspended for at least six months until an artificial intelligence security agreement has been reviewed by outside experts.
The letter was signed by more than 1,700 people, including Yoshua Bengio, a scholar often referred to as the “godfather of artificial intelligence, ” and Stuart Russell, an artificial intelligence scientist and industry pioneer.
This open letter points to the potential risks to society and humanity of having human-competitive intelligence, and outlines the potential risks of misinformation, a new wave of automation taking away jobs, and even eliminating humans.
“All key players in the industry should publicly suspend R & D and be subject to supervision. If R & D cannot be suspended immediately, the government should step in and implement a suspension order. ”
Will a "complete" exam result be a substitute for a job?
Since the first publicly tested ChatGPT program was made available to users late last year, many users, experts, and national legislative and regulatory authorities have raised concerns about ChatGPT.
For example, after the launch of ChatGPT-4 last week, OpenAI released a series of test results for the program ’ s intelligence, showing that GPT-4 can pass most SAT tests (US University Entrance Test), GRE (Graduate Entrance Test), and score more than 90% on the US Attorney ’ s exam.
In the US university preparatory course exam, GPT-4 also passed the test from art history, biology, environmental science, macroeconomics, psychology, American history and many other subjects.
OpenAI specifically states that all results are obtained without specific training of the program on individual exam items.
This ability to cut across disciplines and professions means that employees in all walks of life can be impacted.
According to the latest study by researchers from OpenAI and the University of Pennsylvania, as many as 80% of the U.S. workforce, at least 10% of the work area will be affected by ChatGPT, and about 20% of the labor force and even up to half of the work force will be affected.
The researchers also found that higher income occupations may be more exposed to GPT, but it covers almost all industries.
Is ChatGPT4 easier to spread error messages?
On the other hand, according to NewsGuard, a platform of journalists who check various information sites, the new version of ChatGPT has become more prone to generating false information, and even more persuasive.
Through a collection of common fallacies, conspiracy theories, etc., the website selected 100 of them to conduct inductive tests on the old and new versions of ChatGPT, and found that GPT4 responded to all 100 tests with false information, while GPT3.5 managed to avoid 20 of them, and inspectors found that the new version was better at imitating the propaganda of vaccine conspirators and Russian authorities. Taitung ’ s first ever International Slow Food Forum will be held on April 28!
International slow food representatives from Italy, the Philippines, India and Malaysia gathered at the Taitung County Government Hall to share the experience of slow food promotion around the world, and exchange and learn with local slow food practitioners in Taitung, making Taitung a new base for dialogue with the international slow food movement and linking up the southern island culture.
The slow food movement originated in Italy, has been popular around the world for more than 30 years, and has been promoted in Taitung for 10 years.
The slow food spirit of “Good quality, clean and fair ” comes from Italy, but it has grown up in Taitung with a rich variety of local features.
The Taitung County government specially invited seven international slow food activists and local slow food practitioners from Taitung County to exchange ideas on the eve of the first slow food festival this year, “from the festival to the day, from the traditional to the contemporary. ” The theme is to explore how traditional food culture can be practiced in contemporary society through the Slow Food Movement, and how the international Slow Food Movement can blossom in all corners of the world through the diverse participation of citizens and community power.
On the agenda, Andrea Amato and Daniel Cruse, from the International Slow Food Headquarters in Italy, first introduced the expansion of Slow Food from Italy to the world, and shared the classic Ark of Taste and Slow Food Presidia projects of the Slow Food movement.
In response to the International Year of Xiaomi 2023, Indian representative Aruna Tirkey will introduce the Xiaomi Kitchen in Jharkhand, India.
Nazlina Spice Station in Malaysia is an introduction to the local cuisine, starting from Laksa, to the preservation of Penang ’ s food culture.

ChatGPT designs Hong Kong-style content for Chinese and English learning difficulties Yu Chun-keung Memorial Secondary School trial plug-in

The education community is discussing how to introduce ChatGPT to assist in teaching and administrative work. In an interview with Education 01, Yang Xuehai, the principal of Ho Man Tin Yu Chun Keung Memorial Secondary School, described ChatGPT as able to transcend Moodle ’ s limitations on student practice and improve teaching efficiency.
He also mentioned that schools are now purchasing Plug-in for ChatGPT, which allows ChatGPT to directly access the school database and enable ChatGPT to generate information for the education sector in Hong Kong, including DSE examinations, school administration and related regulations.
Yu Chun Keung Memorial Secondary School Principal Yang Hue Hoi mentioned that ChatGPT can go beyond Moodle ’ s limitations in student practice and improve teaching efficiency by targeting students ’ learning difficulties. (photo by Yu Chun Leung)
Moodle Limited Features ChatGPT to Learn Advanced Concepts
In 1994 and 1999, Principal Yang was seconded to the then Education Department to assist in the development of school and administrative management systems and to support schools in the development of information technology education.
After he became president in 2015, he gradually upgraded the school ’ s information technology facilities and introduced the Moodle system, which is commonly used in universities.
After students have completed their practice in the system, teachers can analyze the performance of students according to the data, understand the students' weaknesses, adjust the curriculum in a timely manner and make good use of the class time.
"ChatGPT came out and found it so interesting, it seemed to satisfy my shortcomings, it was like adding wings to the tiger," and "it satisfied the whole idea of education, and every subject was satisfied."
The school has introduced ChatGPT to help teach in a variety of subjects, such as senior high school history to develop students ’ appreciation and understanding of the DSE scoring criteria, and to help produce teaching materials for Chinese and English subjects.
For example, some teachers have used ChatGPT to prepare teaching materials, and the time required has been reduced from 45 minutes to 5 minutes. The extra time can be spent chatting with students or professional exchanges with colleagues.
The principal of Yu Chun Keung Memorial Secondary School, Yeung Hue Hoi, said the school is planning to trial the “Retrieval ” plugin so that ChatGPT can directly read the school ’ s content stored in the cloud to generate content suitable for the Hong Kong curriculum.
(photo by Yu Chun-liang)
Buy Plugin Enhance ChatGPT Function to Read School Data Generated Content Directly
YU Chun-keung Memorial Secondary School ’ s efforts to optimize ChatGPT teaching did not stop there. Yang pointed out that the content generated by ChatGPT is limited by the database, and the data source is only foreign as of 2021. Therefore, ChatGPT plans to try the “Retrieval ” plugin to enable ChatGPT to read the content stored in the cloud directly by the school to generate content suitable for Hong Kong curriculum.
As an example, teachers often need to look through various kinds of documents when dealing with administrative matters, which takes a lot of time.
In the future, schools only need to store the relevant documents in the database and have ChatGPT read the data. Teachers can ask ChatGPT to find out the articles that need to be cited and provide administrative steps, and then the teachers can check and confirm them, so as to improve efficiency.
Individual teachers first try IT teachers one-on-one technical assistance
ChatGPT has been under discussion for only a few months, and many teachers are still holding a wait-and-see attitude. For example, President Yang will invite individual teachers to try ChatGPT first, and arrange IT teachers to provide 1: 1 guidance to help solve technical problems, so that teachers are more willing to try.
Once they understand the new technology, they can also help other teachers learn the new technology. It is believed that 60% to 80% of teachers in schools can master the new technology in only about two years and consider extending it to the whole school level.
The Principal of Yu Chun Keung Memorial Secondary School, Mr Yeung Hok-hoi (pictured), also has a set of initiatives to promote new technologies in schools to encourage teachers to adopt them.
On the left is Cai Tsung-hsi, a Chinese teacher, and on the right is Li Kun Wai, a history teacher. (photo by Yu Chun-liang)
As one of the first batch of trainees, the Chinese teacher of the school, Tsai Tsung-hsi, believes that if teachers are to use new technologies, they must first have relevant demonstrations, and their teaching examples will be able to lead the way, and other teachers will be willing to try them out when they see that their colleagues who have tried first can help students learn.
Using ChatGPT to generate listening volume recordings with AI for students ’ difficulties
ChatGPT has been introduced to help teachers in both Chinese and English subjects of Yu Chun Keung Memorial Secondary School. Mr Choi noted that it is difficult for teachers to carefully understand what students do not know. For example, the weakness of students may be due to lack of vocabulary and writing skills.
For example, he pointed out that one of the most common problems of students is that they cannot distinguish which data provided by the topic is suitable, so he used ChatGPT to generate the topic, and specified that there must be a certain amount of useless data in the data, so as to strengthen the ability of students to filter information.
As for English, teachers use ChatGPT to integrate teaching content, so that "listening, reading and writing" exercises can be closely linked to each other.
For example, through instructions, ChatGPT helps generate the "Listening, Reading and Writing" test papers with the same content and words, so that students can continue to use the same content to deepen their memory.
In the past, teachers would need to invest a lot of time to produce a similar result.
In addition, the English section also uses AI ’ s Text to Speech function to record the audio of the listening volume, eliminating the difficulty and time of the teacher recording, adjusting the speed of speech, setting different accents, and even adding the classic song “Green Sleeve ” to the HKDSE listening volume.

The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, after the 1980s, challenged traditional forces, and the Middle East is rapidly changing.
Author: Lu I
Published: Updated:
After the 1980s, Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) led a comprehensive Saudi offensive and vigorously pushed for a readjustment of the situation in the Middle East.
With the mediation of Beijing, Saudi Arabia restored relations with Iran.
The foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Iran have just signed a joint declaration in Beijing announcing the official resumption of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
Earlier, in early April, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi visited Saudi Arabia and the two countries intend to strengthen cooperation in “all areas. ”
Recently, a Saudi government delegation visited the Yemeni capital of Sana'a and held direct talks with the Houthis, making substantial progress.
The two sides discussed renewing the ceasefire agreement, which expires in October 2022.
On April 3, 2023, Saudi Arabia ’ s Crown Prince Mohammed personally greeted Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi on the tarmac. (Reuters)
In a joint statement on 13 April, Saudi and Syrian foreign ministers welcomed the start of the process to resume consular services and flights.
Saudi Arabia is reportedly planning to invite Syrian President Bashar al-Assad to the Arab League summit hosted by Riyadh in May.
This will officially end Syria ’ s isolation in the region.
There's no way Biden can get rid of Mohammed.
One of the two sides of the Saudi initiative on regional affairs is the change in US-Saudi relations.
In October last year, the United States wanted Saudi Arabia to maintain or increase crude oil production to avoid stimulating international oil prices to continue to rise, increase domestic inflation, and affect the US Democratic Party's midterm elections, but the request of the Biden administration was rejected by Saudi Arabia.
In April this year, OPEC and OPEC + (the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies) led by Saudi Arabia announced a further reduction of production of about 1.16 million barrels per day, drawing opposition from the United States.
In the context of the high inflation in the United States and the Russian-Ukrainian war, Saudi Arabia and Russia have "one nose out", which obviously did not put the Biden administration in perspective.
Saudi Arabia is the most important partner of the United States in the Arab world, and this relationship is based on the post-World War II international pattern and the strategic needs of Saudi Arabia and the United States.
However, this "need" is changing, which has directly led to the continuous twists and turns of the two countries in recent years.
Mahdi al-Mashat, Chairman of the Supreme Political Council of the Houthi Armed Forces, meets with the Saudi and Omani delegations in Sana'a, Yemen, on April 9, 2023. (Saba News Agency / REUTERS)
For example, the Houthi armed forces, as an offshoot of the Shi'ites of Islam, pose a great real threat to Saudi Arabia, but after Bahai came to power, he became involved with the Houthi armed forces and was no longer on the list of terrorist organizations, opening the door for the organization to obtain funds and buy weapons internationally.
The US actions have caused strong discontent in Saudi Arabia.
In addition, although the Saudi side investigated the murder of Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi in January 2018 at the Saudi Consulate in Istanbul, Turkey, and severely punished the people involved, the United States seized the Saudi royal family and refused to forgive, which also made Saudi Arabia very angry.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman visited Al Ula on January 5 to attend the 41st Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit.
(Reuters)
And to touch the fundamental interests of the matter, since 2014, the United States has vigorously developed shale oil mining, a leap from an oil importer to an exporter.
As the new big seller in the world oil market, the United States has effectively taken market share from major OPEC members such as Saudi Arabia, which makes Saudi Arabia very unhappy.
In order to deal with the new seller of the oil market in the United States, Saudi Arabia, together with Russia, announced a significant increase in crude oil production in 2020, leading to a collapse in oil prices, which has dealt a heavy blow to the shale oil mining industry in the United States, and many American companies have been forced to stop production.
Moreover, Muhammad, after all, was young and arrogant, and it was unacceptable for the United States to be rude and arrogant.
In October last year, the US government expressed "anger" through multiple channels, and some of its words were even threatening.
As National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan threatened, President Biden would “methodically ” reassess relations with Saudi Arabia and said Biden had no intention of meeting Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed at the G20 summit in November.
Sullivan also said the United States may consider halting security assistance and arms sales to Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed arrives on the steps of 10 Downing Street to meet Prime Minister Theresa May in London, UK, on March 7, 2018. (Getty)
Muhammad's choice.
Mohammed has a clear understanding of the hegemony of the United States, a deep insight into the world situation, and a grand vision for Saudi Arabia ’ s development, he is committed to opening up new development space in Saudi Arabia, away from dependence on oil, and launched a grand development plan in renewable energy, high-tech manufacturing and financial services sectors – focusing on implementing the Saudi Vision 2030.
In recent years, the Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed, who is actually in charge, has launched a series of strategic initiatives involving the long-term development of Saudi Arabia.
In order to achieve his “great cause ”, Muhammad knew that relying on the United States alone would not be possible and that new diplomatic horizons must be opened up.
Xi Jinping and Saudi Crown Prince: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed shakes hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the China-Saudi Arabia Summit on December 9, 2022. (Reuters)
On the one hand, defense security is the biggest concern for Saudi Arabia, which has relied entirely on U.S. military equipment in the past.
The United States also uses security as the main tool to control Saudi Arabia, but Saudi Arabia has sought to diversify its military equipment in recent years, and China and Russia have become new sources of Saudi weapons and equipment.
At the same time, as mentioned earlier, Saudi Arabia is beginning to actively cooperate in the region, and the countries that once posed a major threat to Saudi Arabia are adjusting their policies towards Saudi Arabia, which is no longer a real threat to Saudi Arabia.
The “landmark ” settlement agreement between Saudi Arabia and Iran has created the conditions for regional security and reduced the risk of conflict.
Ending the Yemeni war will open a new stage in regional relations, which also proves that the parties can resolve conflict differences through negotiations and dialogue, eliminate interference from external forces, and have the opportunity to achieve lasting peace and stability in the region.
On the other hand, the approach of Saudi Arabia and China is also worthy of attention.
China is clearly the target country for Muhammad ’ s key relationship development.
Saudi Arabia regards China as the best partner in many aspects such as manufacturing development, new energy development, and the introduction of advanced weapons. In 2022, the Chinese government and the Saudi government signed the “Implementation Plan of the Government of the People ’ s Republic of China and the Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on Jointly Building the Belt and Road Initiative and Vision 2030 ”.
In addition, Saudi Arabia also made a clear application to join the SCO, which is an important signal of Saudi diplomatic strategy to “look east. ”
As the world ’ s most influential oil exporter and the strongest economic power of the Middle East, Saudi Arabia ’ s diplomatic moves have important significance for the international situation.
In terms of magnification, the evolution of US-Saudi relations and China-Saudi relations reflects the microcosm of the great changes of the century.
Although wars and conflicts still pervade the world, peace and development will always be the primary pursuit of all countries.
Inciting wars and creating crises are the means by which superpowers maintain their hegemony.
In the face of Saudi Arabia ’ s increased diplomatic self-awareness, the United States does not have a hard card to play.
Seeking peaceful development and independence is the general trend of world development.
As a big country, only by adhering to the principle of equality, mutual benefit and win-win can we win the recognition and goodwill of other countries.
National relations based on the pursuit of unilateral interests and hegemony cannot be sustained.

In recent years, the popular "very low calorie diet", daily calorie intake is controlled at 400 to 800 kcal, a week can reduce 1 to 2.5 kg; but experts warn that using this method to lose weight may appear tired, weak or even hair loss, long-term prone to obesity.
The “Practical Guidelines for Adult Obesity Prevention and Control ” published by the National Health Administration of the Ministry of Health and Welfare in 2023 lists three common weight loss methods, including the ketogenic diet, the 168 fasting method, and the very low calorie weight loss method.
Huang Bao-Ying, a nutritionist at Keelung, points out that the ketogenic diet is mainly to limit the intake of carbohydrates. When the body is unable to produce enough glucose to provide energy, it will use the “ketones ” produced by the breakdown of fat as an alternative energy source.
The ketogenic diet almost does not eat rice, bread, bread, etc., and even fruits can not be eaten. Instead, high-fat meat, cheese, cream, nuts and other high-fat and protein foods are mainly used.
Wong cautions that you need to consider your physical state when carrying out a ketogenic diet, because a large number of ketone bodies need the kidneys to metabolize, and it is not suitable if the kidneys are not functional or have cardiovascular disease.
The 168 fasting method is to fast for 16 hours and eat for 8 hours within 24 hours of a day, press the time you can eat for 8 hours, and the other 16 hours do not eat calorific food, you can drink water, sugar-free tea or low-calorie black coffee.
The very low calorie diet, which is controlled at 400 to 800 calories per day for rapid weight loss, can reduce obesity patients by 1 to 2.5 kg per week; some studies have suggested that the use of the very low calorie diet may increase insulin sensitivity in patients with type 2 diabetes, but this must be done under the guidance of a professional doctor.
Huang Baoyun reminds that ultra-low calorie diet has a significant effect on short-term weight loss, but it may be tired, weak and even have hair loss, and it is easy to gain weight in the long term.
Finally, Wong said that no matter which diet method to choose to lose weight, as long as you reduce your calorie intake, you can achieve weight loss, but to maintain your posture, you should avoid sugary drinks and high-oil foods, and mix with adequate sleep and moderate exercise.

Why is Northern China once again a place of bitterness?
Author: External Submission
Published: Updated:
The northern part of China was once again hit by severe sandstorm weather.
The dust has affected eastern Xinjiang and southern Xinjiang Basin, Inner Mongolia, western Gansu, northern Ningxia, northwestern Shanxi, central Jilin, northern Liaoning, northern China, northeastern China and the Huanghuai.
Due to this, as of 6: 00 a.m. on April 11, Beijing Real-time air quality index is 500, is critical pollution level, and the primary pollutant is PM10.
The Beijing Meteorological Station issued a yellow sandstorm warning. It is expected that there will be obvious sandy weather in Beijing from 21: 00 to 17: 00 on April 10, and the lowest visibility in most areas is less than 1000 meters.
As previously reported in the Anbang briefing, the frequency of dust storms in northern China has increased significantly this year, and it has entered the stage of dust and sand weather.
This article is licensed by Anbang Think Tank.
This large area of sand and dust weather is not limited to northern China, but also all the way south "crazy" across the Yangtze River.
According to the China Meteorological Bureau's meteorological detection center monitoring shows that at 16: 00 on April 11, the dust and dust cluster moved south, and the dust frontier has been to Hubei, Anhui and Jiangsu, and the concentration of PM10 in many places exceeds 1000ug / m3.
The frequent sandy weather in the northern region has made northern China once again a "bittersweet place", and the livability has greatly deteriorated.
If similar sandy weather continues, it will drive more people from the north to the south, and continue to widen the economic development and population distribution differences between the north and the south, which is undoubtedly very detrimental to the development of the north.
+ 8
Why is it that after sticking to the "green water and green mountains" strategy for many years, the northern region is still experiencing large-scale dust storms so frequently? The relevant departments said that "dust and dust weather is generally decreasing", but this argument is difficult to convince, and can not explain the weather changes this year.
From a public policy perspective, researchers at ANBOUND believe that there is a need to objectively look at the formation and effects of sand and dust weather, and then find countermeasures within the limits of human ability.
First, the dust source area is very wide and belongs to large-scale weather phenomena, which goes beyond the protection of the existing ecological environment.
Since this year, there have been eight sandy weather processes in the Mainland.
It is worth noting that this year, the sandy weather in the northern part of the mainland has a wide range of sources, both domestic and foreign.
For example, the sandy weather from April 10 to 11, the sand source is Mongolia and central Inner Mongolia; on March 22, the sand source is central Mongolia and northwest China; from March 14 to 15, the southern part of Mongolia, the border of Central Mongolia and the eastern part of Inner Mongolia continued to sand source; on March 10, the central and southern part of Mongolia and the border areas of China appeared systematic sandy weather; On January 17, dust broke out on the border of China and Mongolia, and the dust gradually moved to the east.
+ 3
From a spatial point of view, dust weather is a large-scale weather phenomenon, small scale local area vegetation improvement and ecosystem restoration, do not play a big role in suppressing dust weather.
Especially when the sand source comes from other regions (such as Mongolia), many parts of the country are basically passive acceptance.
The impact range of the sandy weather, from north to south, spans 2000-3000 km, passing through the relatively dry, less vegetated warm temperate zone and relatively moist, more vegetated subtropical areas.
This means that the efforts of the Mainland to improve the ecological environment and improve the vegetation in local areas are not enough to reduce large-scale dust and dust weather.
Second, frequent sand and dust weather may be related to global warming, which is the result of a combination of short-term and long-term factors.
Some experts said that this year, the dust and dust weather is mainly related to the recent atmospheric circulation. March to April is the northern high wind season.
Under certain windy conditions, the dust from the sand source is transported to China many times, which is the most direct reason for the severe dust weather many times this year.
It is important to note that warming also has an important impact on the production of sandy weather.
According to the China Meteorological Bureau on March 25 this year, it is expected that this spring (April to May), the precipitation from the southern part of Mongolia to the central and western parts of Inner Mongolia is less, the temperature is higher than the same period of the year, and there is a southward influence of the Mongolian cyclone stage, which is conducive to the formation of sandy weather.
Statistics from the National Climate Center show that since late February 2021, the temperature in western Inner Mongolia and Mongolia has been unusually high of 2 ° C to 6 ° C, causing the snow to melt ahead of time and the sand source to be exposed.
The exposed surface of the large area provides sand source conditions for the production of sand and dust weather. In the 2022 vegetation growth season, Mongolia has less precipitation than the same period in the past 20 years, the vegetation cover of the sand source is poor, and the exposed surface lacks vegetation protection.

It is worth noting that global warming is a long-term trend, and the resulting global abnormal climate change is becoming increasingly obvious.
In the past two years, the Northern Hemisphere has experienced unusually high temperatures and dry weather in summer, which has accelerated the melting of glaciers.
According to Swiss research, the size of the Alps Glacier has shrunk by about 60% since 1850.
According to German glaciologists, 2022 is a record year for glaciers to melt.
Due to factors such as rainfall, reduced snowfall and drought, hot weather, the amount of glacier melt in the entire Alps in 2022 is estimated to have increased by about 50% compared to previous years.
In China, in recent years, there has also been an abnormal phenomenon of "drought and waterlogging" in the north and south.
Global warming constitutes the macro background of global climate change, and if there is widespread warming and drought in the northern region, it will lead to frequent sandy weather in the spring.
Third, human activities are still increasing overall, and the impact on the undersurface of the atmosphere is constantly increasing, which is one of the important reasons for catastrophic dust and dust weather.
Although the world and China have increasingly attached importance to ecological protection and climate change issues, on the whole, human activities - industrial activities (such as industrial production, large-scale mining, etc.), urbanization, life consumption activities, war and other man-made factors, the changes and impact on the atmospheric surface are constantly increasing, resulting in the artificial intervention of the atmospheric surface is constantly strengthening, and the ecological destruction and soil desertification in local areas are constantly increasing.
These changes can be an important reason for the increase in catastrophic dust weather.
Objectively speaking, in recent years, the vegetation in northern China has increased significantly, and the ecological environment has improved significantly, which is generally conducive to the gradual reduction of the number of sand and dust in China.
However, ecological destruction in other countries (such as Mongolia) and surface features such as the Gobi Desert are also important sources of dust affecting China.
The final analysis conclusion:
This year ’ s significant increase in sand and dust weather constitutes a force majeure in China ’ s environmental problems.
As a large-scale weather phenomenon, the generation and impact of sand and dust weather are beyond the ecological environment improvement efforts of small scale and local areas.
In order to reduce the occurrence of sandy weather through human efforts, this is more difficult and complex system engineering than ecological governance at the national or regional level, and requires global or regional countries to strengthen cooperation to continue to curb the trend of climate warming, or cooperate to change the regional ecological environment.
For China, which is more affected by the continental climate and monsoon climate, it is feared that it will suffer the effects of catastrophic weather similar to sand and dust for a long time, which will have a greater negative impact on economic activity and livability in northern China, and may continue to widen the economic and social development gap between the north and the south.
