Finally, his father, Richard, took part of his blood, made room, and received Johnson ’ s plasma.
Three generations complete "blood transfusions" in a matter of hours.
Anti-aging method ｜ Eat 100 capsules a day after noon do not eat experts oppose
This is not Johnson ’ s first “blood exchange ”. He has already entered the plasma of an anonymous young donor in the past few months, emphasizing that he has made sure that the person is free of disease, healthy lifestyle and ideal BMI.

US domestic industry law will hurt African economies
Author: External Submission
Published: Updated:
The Biden administration has stepped up protectionist and industrial policies amid heightened economic tensions with China. Legislation passed in 2022, releasing hundreds of billions of dollars in subsidies to spur domestic production of renewable energy and electric vehicles and support other carbon reduction targets.
The legislation also aims to support domestic strategic industries, such as high-end semiconductors, while limiting China ’ s access to such technologies.
Jonathan Munemo, Professor of Economics at Salisbury University
Having observed the pattern of global trade since World War II, I fear that we are now entering a new and more dangerous period.
Washington ’ s protectionist industrial policy began with the U.S.-China trade war under the Trump administration, and it is intensifying the fragmentation of the global economy, driven by the war in Ukraine and economic sanctions imposed on Russia.
It is doing this by intervening in trade and investment flows based on geopolitical considerations.
As a result, global economic integration is being reversed.
Over the past 30 years, global economic integration has increased productivity growth, raised living standards, and reduced extreme poverty.
We can see this happening as America ’ s allies respond with their own inward-looking protections and align themselves with the United States to create a global supply chain that is less dependent on China.
The European Union, Japan and South Korea are examples of this.
This could have a profound negative impact on African countries.
Some countries will be hit harder than others.
For example, 19 African countries facing debt distress have minimal financial resources to manage the costs of these adverse effects.
However, almost all countries will feel the effects of higher inflation as global output declines in a less productive world.
Many countries will also feel the impact of blocked regionalization efforts, as importers lose access to the price-competitive sources needed to add value; and diversification of investment flows may also limit access to investment.
This will have a negative impact on the continent ’ s growth and plans to promote green investment.
The United States and its allies are using their own inward-looking protective measures to create a global supply chain that is less dependent on China, pictured at the Hiroshima G7 summit in the middle of this month (Getty)
U.S. initiatives on protection and industrial policy
Last year, Congress approved the Chips and Science Act and the Inflation Reduction Act.
They provide hundreds of billions of dollars to encourage domestic production of chips and clean energy technologies.
They also aim to ban the export of high-end semiconductors and equipment to China and push allies to do the same.
These actions, along with the infrastructure bill Biden signed into law in 2021 to boost U.S.-made steel with more federal spending, together form America ’ s current protectionist industrial strategy.
This has unnerved policymakers in Europe and Asia, who argue that these laws unfairly benefit American companies and distance themselves from free trade.
It also raises concerns that companies and investments in its region will be drawn to the United States.
The concerns foreshadow that Germany-based Volkswagen will build a $2 billion car factory in South Carolina for a new electric brand in March.
In addition, Swedish battery manufacturer Northvolt AB said its expansion into the US market is now one of its top priorities.
For its part, Samsung intends to use chip subsidies for an advanced plant it is building in Texas.
The EU has responded to these initiatives with its own massive subsidy scheme to support businesses in paving the way for a low-carbon economy.
It also passed the Chip Act in April to support semiconductor manufacturing in the region with billions of dollars in subsidies.
Other U.S. allies are following suit.
The Japanese government has negotiated a deal with Washington to allow key minerals shipped by its companies to qualify for U.S. subsidies.
The European Union is also supporting semiconductor manufacturing in the region with billions of dollars in subsidies. (Getty)
The EU is also interested in a similar agreement.
South Korea plans to spend hundreds of billions of dollars on chips, batteries, electric cars and other green technologies.
The US-led subsidy push and export controls are fragmenting supply chains by shifting them from China to the global economy.
They are also alienating non-EU and Asian allies who cannot support their companies with similar subsidies.
African countries will be hit hard.
These changes will ultimately reduce the gains made in the consolidation of international commodity and investment markets.
These results include higher global output growth, opportunities to take advantage of new technologies, and lower costs for businesses and consumers.
This means that countries with larger economies, such as Nigeria, South Africa, Ethiopia and Kenya, which need more imports, are likely to be hit harder by rising domestic costs and rising international prices of imported goods.
These will lead to higher inflation rates, which will be bad for businesses and households.
Another blow is that regional trade integration efforts, including expanding the digital economy, improving infrastructure, strengthening regional trade logistics and providing financial services, will be affected by higher intermediate inputs costs and a lack of new technologies.
Both are critical for building regional value chains and diversifying production.
In addition, companies in most African countries will miss out on opportunities because they lack big-money government support to provide huge subsidies and other incentives to take advantage of green investment opportunities on a scale close to that of the United States and its wealthy allies.
African countries do not have sufficient financial resources to respond to changes in global trade patterns.
(Getty)
According to the International Monetary Fund, the African continent has suffered the most from the fragmentation of the global economy.
In a recent assessment, the Fund said the cost to African countries could be as high as 4% of GDP.
Measures to Mitigate Impacts
The U.S. strategy for sub-Saharan Africa, unveiled last year by the Biden administration, appears to be the ideal platform to address concerns about U.S. protectionist industrial policy.
This is because of its primary goals, including helping Africa navigate the energy transition and strengthening U.S. trade and investment with the continent.
Building on this strategy, policymakers in Washington and Africa should prioritize the following:
Establish public-private partnerships for the production and domestic processing of minerals that are key components of the green energy transition, including nickel in Tanzania, palladium and manganese in South Africa, copper in Zambia, cobalt in the Congo and lithium in Zimbabwe.
Promoting investment to build strong regional supply chains should include enabling Africa to leverage technologies such as digitalization to facilitate trade through e-commerce.
Under the African Growth and Opportunity Act, use any positive impact to drive the growth and diversification of trade with Africa.

"AI Sun Yanzi" explodes network copyright issue caused controversy
First of all, "AI Sun Yanzi" is definitely the hottest Chinese singer in the first half of this year, followed by "AI Zhou Jielun", "AI Lin Junjie" and "AI Wang Xinling".
Before I heard that AI can arrange music and paint, now you will find that the role of big stars on the stage, AI is equally competent.
It doesn ’ t even need to be in person, the singers ’ “new album ” is already flying around.
What the hell is going on here?
It is understood that some people use the existing human voice samples of Sun Yanzi, through AI training timbre, tone quality and pronunciation characteristics, establish its sound model, and then use the generated timbre to cover other songs, there is "AI Sun Yanzi".
This uses an open source AI speech conversion software, the original author has stopped updating and maintaining this year, but there are still many netizens independently developing new features on the current version.
The enthusiasm of netizens for the creation of virtual singers implies the recognition and pursuit of emerging technologies.
As early as ten years ago, the virtual idols represented by "Hatsune Future" and "Luo Tianyi" have gradually entered the public eye, and their voices are made from real human sound source data.
With the iterative development of technology, the "real person double" virtual singer represented by "AI Sun Yan Zi" made a shining debut, "invading" is not only everyone's "childhood memories", but also some legal ambiguity.
The new songs produced by AI sound cloning technology are very similar in sound and style to the singer himself, which has led many netizens to believe that they are true.
Is this impersonation infringing?
The scope of works protected by the Copyright Law includes written works, oral works, music and fine arts, and sound is not listed.
Therefore, the mere imitation of performers' timbre, singing skills and other characteristics, does not belong to the protection of the Copyright Law.
In addition, only on a video platform, the "AI Sun Yanzi" cover works have exceeded a thousand, among which the works of the singer Zhou Jielun's "Hair as Snow" and other works have even won more than two million views.
A number of lawyers said that the works of the virtual singer's cover show the specific song name and singer's name, which is suspected of infringing on the singer's right to name, personality, and the copyright of the song.
Even if some publishers mark the disclaimer of "entertainment only and not for commercial use" in the video, the huge traffic and economic benefits behind it are difficult to be clear, and there is no way to completely discard the infringement issue.
"AI face change" fraud attack someone 10 minutes to be cheated 4.3 million
At present, Sun Yanzi himself has responded to his own "AI version" of music.
However, the concern of netizens about the application of artificial intelligence technology has not stopped.
In May, Apple announced that it plans to embed a new feature in the new version of the software: mobile phone users who have gradually lost their ability to speak for various reasons can create a unique "personal customized voice" by recording 15 minutes of audio, and can still use the phone's call and video functions normally after losing their ability to speak.
In this regard, many users expressed concern that the technology is more likely to be used by criminals, such as through the production of fake videos and audio recordings, for the implementation of telecommunications fraud.
Such fears are not unfounded.
According to the police, not long ago a Fujian boss fell into the "high-end" fraud bureau, because of the credulous use of "AI for face" fraudsters, just 10 minutes lost 4.3 million yuan.
The rapid development of AI has brought not only "unemployment anxiety", but also a new challenge to "true and false discrimination". At present.
A number of EU countries have already begun to review the issue of artificial intelligence feeding data.
In March, foreign publishers protested against the copyrighted content used by ChatGPT in data training, demanding compensation from its company OpenAI.
In China, the regulatory system of the artificial intelligence industry is also being actively improved.
At the end of last year, the State Internet Information Office issued a document requiring that when providing in-depth synthesis services such as synthetic voices, imitation voices, face substitution, and gesture manipulation, users should be prompted to inform the edited individuals according to law and obtain their individual consent; and if the synthetic content may lead to confusion or mistaken recognition, it must be marked in a reasonable position and explain the specific information of the synthetic work.
In April this year, the State Internet Information Office drafted the "Generative Artificial Intelligence Service Management Measures (Draft for Solicitation of Comments)" to clarify the data of pre-training and optimization training, and must not contain content that infringes intellectual property rights.

Lai Shi Baoti 3 Suggestions: Accelerate the implementation of relevant laws
▲ Lai Shih-pao attended the press conference on “Intellectual Property Challenge in the Wave of Generative AI ”. (Photo / Courtesy of Facebook / Lai Shih-pao)
Journalist Chan Yi-ting / reporting from Taipei
With the advancement of AI artificial intelligence technology, there are a large number of "AI singers" on the Internet, which can simulate the singer's voice to sing various songs.
In this regard, KMT legislator Lai Shibao suggested on the 26th that the government should formulate norms for the rational use of generative AI, require clear identification and disclosure of material copyright sources, accelerate the promotion of AI-related laws, and promote the vigorous development of reasonable supervision.
At the press conference today, Lai Shibao said that AI technology has caused many considerations about intellectual property rights, such as the recently discussed "AI Sun Yanzi incident", AI technology has opened up new possibilities for the future of mankind, but the market development is still at an early stage, and there is no consensus on the treatment of related legal issues.
Therefore, in order to balance the development of AI technology with the related legal disputes, he put forward three propositions.
First, the government should formulate norms for the rational use of generative AI, and require AI works to be clearly identified. Lai Shibao revealed that AI technology is developing rapidly, and individuals or enterprises that will not use AI tools in the future will face great competitive pressure.
However, unclear legal regulations may hinder the further adoption of AI technology by the public due to infringement concerns.
Therefore, I advocate that the government should establish fair use regulations for generative AI to ensure the rights of creators and inform the public about how to use AI tools safely and legally.
In addition, all AI-generated works should be required to be clearly labeled “AI-generated ”, which will help raise public awareness and provide important references when clarifying relevant liability issues.
Second, generative AI model developers should be required to disclose the source of material copyright, as the European Union has done. Because generative AI tools may use creators ’ work to train and reap benefits, creators may not be aware of this, Lai said.
To this end, the European Union has begun to amend regulations to require generative AI model developers to disclose the source of copyrighted material used, which will become an important basis for creators to compete with AI companies in the future.
Therefore, Lai Shibao argued that the government should follow the practice of the European Union and enact relevant laws to protect the rights of creators.
Third, accelerate the promotion of AI-related laws, so that AI technology can flourish under reasonable supervision. Lai Shibao pointed out that with the introduction of AI technology, the European Union and the United States have already begun to propose various AI-related laws, and even the recently concluded G7 summit emphasized the need to immediately address the opportunities and challenges brought by “generative AI ”.
Our country has always been a big country in information and communication technology, but the advancement of AI-related laws has been relatively slow.
To this end, Lai Shibao will accelerate the implementation of AI-related laws (such as the AI Basic Law), so that AI technology can continue to develop healthily under appropriate supervision, so as to ensure that we can fully grasp the development opportunities brought by AI technology.

After the evolution of quantum computing, people will have more certain answers to various difficult problems such as weather and earthquakes.
Talking about the future development of quantum computing, Guo Guoping believes that it must be around the various needs of human production and life.
He said that human beings develop various cutting-edge technologies, one is to expand human cognition, and the other is to optimize and improve production and life.
He hopes that through the improvement of computing power, more new drugs will be born and disease treatment plans will be more diversified.

Turkey election: Erdogan re-elected, country continues to divide
Paul Kirby and Ece Goksedef
• BBC reporter from Ankara
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who has been in power for years, won another five-year term, and his supporters celebrated all night.
“All 85 million people in the country have won, ” he told cheering crowds at his huge residence on the edge of Ankara.
But his call for unity appears hollow as he mocks his opponent, Kemal Kilicdaroglu, and targets jailed Kurdish leaders and LGBT (gay, bisexual and transgender) support policies.
The opposition leader did not publicly concede defeat.
Kirida Oru called it "the most unfair election in recent years" and said the president's party had used all the power of the government against him.
According to unofficial statistics close to the count, Erdoğan won just over 52% of the vote — nearly half of voters in a deeply polarized country who did not support his authoritarian vision for Turkey.
In the end, Krida Oru could not match the well-trained Erdogan campaign, even though he has pulled the current president into the runoff stage for the second round – the first since the Turkish president adopted direct elections in 2014.
But he failed to reverse his opponent's lead in the first round, with a gap of more than two million votes.
The Turkish president, for his part, proclaimed his victory to the greatest extent possible.
He spoke to crowds on a bus in Istanbul, the largest city, and then on the balcony of his official residence after dark, where some 320,000 people gathered in support of him.
“It ’ s not just us who won, it ’ s Turkey as a whole, ” he said, calling it one of the most important elections in Turkey ’ s history.
He taunted his defeated opponent: "Bye, Kemal." — a phrase echoed by supporters in Ankara.
He also denounced his rival allies for supporting LGBT policies, saying that he was at odds with his own family-centered principles.
Although the final result of the election was not confirmed, the Supreme Electoral Council said that the victory was no longer in doubt.
Erdoğan supporters everywhere in Ankara took to the streets to celebrate the victory, with some calling out the slogans of Islam and some laying the Turkish flag on the lawn to pray.
While some supporters say they believe Erdoğan will do better in the next five years, the president himself has acknowledged that Turkey ’ s high inflation rate is the most pressing problem at the moment – the country ’ s annual inflation rate is already close to 44%, affecting the lives of every citizen.
And the economy is not the biggest concern of Erdoğan ’ s supporters at the moment, who say they are proud of Erdoğan ’ s strong position in the world and his toughness in fighting “terrorists, ” by which they mean the Kurdish armed forces.
Despite the euphoria of supporters, the idea of unity in this torn country seems to be as far away as ever.
After the failed coup in 2016, Erdoğan had abolished the post of prime minister, with a high concentration of power, which opponents described as a step backwards.
Turkey ’ s opposition now has to regroup in order to prepare for the 2024 local elections.
A strong leader for 20 years.
From humble beginnings, Erdoğan is a giant in Turkish politics and has led the country for 20 years and is the most influential figure in the country since Mustafa Kemal Ataturk, the founding father of the modern republic.
Despite a series of crises, he won the 2023 election and remained in power.
It was his most precarious position in years, and his opponents believed he could defeat him.
Critics have accused his unruly economic policies of exacerbating the cost of living crisis in Turkey.
Moreover, as a combative leader who set a record in Turkey ’ s modernization, he seemed to be slow to respond to the earthquake that claimed 50,000 lives in February.
After escaping a coup d'état in 2016, he transformed the presidency into an executive role of supreme power and suppressed opponents and dissidents.
Beginning in 2003, first as prime minister and then as president by direct election since 2014, Turkey under Erdoğan ’ s leadership has been “flexing its muscles ” as a regional power, pursuing the Islamist cause and quickly overpowering its political rivals.
Although the head of a NATO member state, he placed himself in the position of mediator in the Russo-Ukrainian War, and made Sweden wait a bit longer to join the Western defense alliance.
His hard-line diplomacy angered Europe and beyond.
Erdoğan polarized his country, but he was a victorious general in the election.
His supporters refer to him as a "leader."
He accused opponents of contempt for Turkish voters and unpopular: "85 million people, we will protect our votes, our will and our future."
On the throne of power.
Recep Tayyip Erdoğan was born in February 1954 on the Black Sea coast of Turkey, the son of a member of the Coast Guard. At the age of 13, his father decided to move to Istanbul, hoping for a better environment for his five children.
Young Erdoğan used to make extra money selling lemonade and sesame packets.
He attended an Islamic school and later earned a degree in management from Marmara University in Istanbul – and was a professional footballer.
In the 1970s and 1980s, he was active in Islamic circles, joining the pro-Islamic Welfare Party of Necmettin Erbakan. As the party gained popularity in the 1990s, Erdoğan was elected mayor of Istanbul in 1994, leading Turkey ’ s largest city for the next four years.
But his tenure came to an abrupt end when he was accused of openly reading nationalist poetry inciting hatred, which included phrases such as: “Mosques are our barracks, domes are our helmets, minarets are our bayonets, believers are our soldiers. ”
After a few months in prison, he returned to politics.
But his party has been banned for violating the strict secular rules of the modern Turkish government.
In 2001, he formed a new party with his ally Abdullah Gul. In 2002, the Justice and Development Party (AKP) won a parliamentary majority, and Erdoğan was appointed prime minister the following year.
To this day, he is the chairman of the AKP.
First 10 years in power
Since 2003, he has been Prime Minister for three terms, leading a period of steady economic growth and earning international recognition as a reformer.
At a time when Erdoğan prioritized modernizing Turkey with large infrastructure projects, the middle class expanded and millions lifted out of poverty.
But critics also warn that he is becoming more authoritarian.
Protesters took to the streets in 2013, partly because of his government ’ s plan to transform a popular park in central Istanbul, but also because the population was challenging increasingly authoritarian rule.
The Prime Minister accused the protesters of being a nuisance, and people in the streets would beat pots every night at 9 o'clock to show resistance.
The sons of three cabinet allies have also been indicted on corruption charges.
The Gezi Park protests became a black and white spot for his rule.
To his critics, he acted more like an Ottoman monarch than a democratic leader.
Erdoğan also had a feud with Fethullah Gulen, an Islamic scholar based in the United States whose social and cultural movements helped Erdoğan win three consecutive elections and contributed to the military ’ s secession from politics.
The incident has caused a fierce reaction in Turkish society.
Muslim Revival
After a decade in power, Erdoğan ’ s party also worked to lift the ban on women wearing headscarves from public service imposed after the 1980 military coup.
The ban was eventually lifted, allowing women to join the police, the military and the judiciary.
Critics say he dug the walls of the secular state in Ataturk. Although Erdogan himself is a believer, he has always denied that he wants to impose Islamic values on viewers, insisting that he supports the right of Turks to express their religious beliefs openly.
However, he has repeatedly supported the criminalization of adultery.
As the father of four, he said that “no Muslim family ” should consider birth control or family planning.
“We will expand our descendants, ” he said in May 2016.
He extolled motherhood, denounced feminists, and argued that men and women could not be treated equally.
Erdoğan has long championed the cause of Islam — he is known to raise four fingers in a salute gesture to Egypt ’ s oppressed Muslim Brotherhood.
In July 2020, under his auspices, Istanbul ’ s historic Hagia Sophia was converted into a mosque, infuriating many Christians.
Built 1500 years ago, the cathedral was turned into a mosque by the Ottoman Turks, but Ataturk turned it into a museum – a symbol of the new secular state.
It is not a coincidence that, just hours after the start of the 2023 elections, the president spoke to supporters during an evening prayer.
Enhanced control
After being barred from running for prime minister, he ran for president in his first direct election in 2014, when it was a symbolic office.
He has a plan to reform this office, to create a new constitution that benefits all Turks and places their country among the top 10 economies in the world.
But in the early days of his presidency, he twice faced a shake-up in his position of power.
His party lost its parliamentary majority in a vote in 2015, and a few months later in 2016, Turkey witnessed its first violent coup attempt in decades.
The rebels almost captured the president, who was vacationing at the seaside resort, but he was safely rescued by plane. In the early hours of 16 July, he appeared victorious at Ataturk Airport in Istanbul, greeted by cheers from supporters.
They blocked the advance of the conspirators, and nearly 300 civilians were killed.
The president appeared on national television and met with supporters in Istanbul, declaring himself "commander in chief".
But the situation was also clearly tense, and he openly wept as he spoke at the funeral of a close friend who was shot dead by the rebels.
Some 150,000 civil servants were fired and more than 50,000 detained, including soldiers, journalists, lawyers, police officers, academics and Kurdish politicians.
The crackdown on critics has raised alarm abroad and soured Turkey ’ s relationship with the EU: Turkey ’ s attempts to join the EU have gone years without progress.
The controversy over the influx of migrants into Greece has also fuelled hostility.
But in his 1,000-room gleaming palace overlooking Ankara from Aksalai, President Erdoğan ’ s position seems more secure than ever.
His victory in a 2017 referendum gave the president sweeping powers, including the ability to impose a state of emergency, appoint top officials and interfere with the legal system.
A year later, he won the first presidential election.
His core votes came from small towns and rural conservative districts in Anatolia. In 2019, his party lost in three of the largest cities – Istanbul, the capital Ankara and Izmir.
In the Istanbul mayoral election, the party narrowly lost to the main opposition Republican People's Party (CHP) Ekrem Imamoglu, a bitter defeat for Erdoğan, who was mayor of the city in the 1990s.
He never accepted the result.
Before Imamoglu was barred from the May elections, he was ahead of the president in opinion polls.
The president and his allies have been accused of using the courts to disqualify the popular mayor.
Turkey ’ s third-largest party, the People ’ s Democratic Party of New Kurdistan (HDP), was similarly fearful of being barred from voting in parliament because of alleged links to Kurdish forces, but instead decided to run under a different name.
Like Turkish leaders in the past, Erdoğan has imposed a strong crackdown on the outlawed Kurdish Workers ’ Party (PKK).
While Turkey has accepted more than 3.5 million refugees fleeing the Syrian civil war, Ankara has also launched several operations against Kurdish forces on the other side of the border, crowding out Kurds in Turkey.
Erdogan has long had close ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who has also tried to play an important mediator role in the Russian-Ukrainian conflict.
Although a NATO member, he bought Russia ’ s anti-missile defense system and chose Russia to build Turkey ’ s first nuclear reactor.
Before the 2023 election, he tried to win the trust of nationalists and conservative voters by accusing the West of targeting him.
“My country is going to smash this conspiracy, ” he asserted, describing it as a flashpoint.
He ended his 2023 campaign by visiting the tomb of Adnan Menderes, Turkey ’ s first democratically elected prime minister, who was executed after a military coup in 1961.
He wanted people to know: "The era of coups and warlords is over."

WFH to Japan? Government proposes digital nomad visa to attract remote office workers
Author: United Morning Post
Published: Updated:
The Japanese government is considering issuing digital nomad visas to attract “digital nomads ” who travel around the world while working remotely to Japan.
As more and more countries introduce digital nomad visas, the Japanese government also hopes to boost spending by foreign visitors by creating a convenient environment for highly skilled digital workers.
The visa programme is expected to be completed this month.
According to the data, there are an estimated 35 million digital nomads worldwide, who spend about US $787 billion (about HK $6.16 billion) annually.
According to an overseas survey, about 66% of digital nomads stay in the same place for three to six months.
In order to attract this group of highly skilled, high-income digital nomads to stay in Japan for more than 90 days, the Japanese government is considering issuing long-term visas.
According to the current regulations, individuals must work in Japan for more than 90 days to apply for a work visa.
However, individuals who receive salaries from overseas companies are not eligible to apply for this visa; applicants must receive salaries from companies with branches in Japan in order to obtain the visa.
Pictured is a collection of traditional Japanese bungalow buildings in front of the Hilton Hotel Niseko, Hokkaido, Japan, on January 28, 2021. (Getty)
Countries such as Europe, Central and South America, in order to attract more digital travelers, in addition to providing long-term work visas, some countries even offer tax concessions.
According to the data, 15 European countries have introduced similar digital nomadic visas, but the application criteria vary, such as Croatia requires applicants to earn no less than 2,300 euros (about HK $19,000) a month, Iceland requires 7,100 euros (about HK $59,000), Portugal requires no less than 700 euros (about HK $5,860), and Spain sets the income threshold at around 2,000 euros (about HK $17,000).

(ii) AI Assistant

Earthquakes and rampant inflation: Why did Erdogan win again?
Font Size:
Source: Hong Kong 01
Author: Liu Yanting
On May 28, Turkey held the second round of the presidential election.
Although Turkey's Supreme Electoral Council is not expected to announce the official results until June 1, according to preliminary election statistics, with 99.59% of the votes cast, the incumbent President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan has 51.91% of the votes, defeating his opponent Kemal Kılçdaroğlu with 48.09% of the votes. Determine the rate of re-election.
This election has caused global concern.
First, people are curious about whether there will be a regime change in Turkey, changing its fierce cross-border diplomatic style.
Looking back over the past two years, since the outbreak of the Russian-Ukrainian war in 2022, Turkey has repeatedly played a fierce swing beyond the size of medium-sized countries, including facilitating the Russian-Ukrainian foreign ministers' talks in March 2022, blocking Finland and Sweden's accession to NATO in May, and announcing the "green light" in June, leading Russia to sign the Black Sea Food Agreement in July, and negotiating energy cooperation with Russia at the CICA summit in October. For the first time since the start of the war, senior officials have talked about launching a new round of military action in Syria, implying that it may threaten Russia ’ s and Iran ’ s geopolitical interests.
In between, the outside world is surprised by Erdoğan ’ s active actions, and also uncertain about Turkey ’ s opportunistic diplomatic style.
Second, Erdogan suffered two major shocks before the election, causing the outside world to generally not optimistic about his re-election, one is in 2022 for months to break through 80% of the serious inflation, the second is the earthquake disaster.
Among them, Turkey ’ s high inflation is the sequela of the 2018 economic crisis. The deep reason is that Turkey ’ s long-term economic overheating and political interest rate cuts have caused a linked financial storm after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates in Turkey. He lost power in big cities such as Istanbul and Ankara.
And the earthquake will also affect voters' support for Erdogan.
On February 6, 2023, a 7.8-magnitude earthquake occurred in southeastern Turkey, killing nearly 50,000 people, and economic losses are even more incalculable.
After the disaster Erdoğan once faced criticism, public opinion criticized its failure to improve the phenomenon of uneven development and urban poverty, resulting in old buildings with low earthquake resistance being vulnerable to a strong earthquake, and fragile buildings are often difficult to get away from the collusion of officials and businessmen, cutting corners, the ruling Erdoğan and the positive development party are to blame.
However, from the results of this election, although the gap between the two people is less than 5%, but Krechidaloğlu is finally a step away from the door, showing that whether it is high inflation or an earthquake, can not prevent Erdogan from being re-elected.
In addition to the lack of integration of Turkish opposition forces, Erdogan ’ s success in mobilizing the new situation of “Turkey ’ s rise ” is also key.
The opposition is not well integrated.
First of all, although the polls of the Republican People's Party (CHP) party leader Krechidar Oulu once exceeded Erdoğan ’ s, making many foreign media boldly predict that Turkey will soon change, but focusing on the current state of Turkish politics, Erdoğan ’ s positive party is the strongest force, and the opposition ’ s long-term mountainous and independent government has not only offset the integration efforts to challenge Erdoğan, but also to some extent.
Looking at the interaction of Turkish opposition parties in recent years, there have been obvious signs of integration until the 2017 constitutional referendum.
At that time, Erdoğan greatly expanded the presidential power and removed the obstacles to re-election in the system, causing a collective panic among the opposition forces. The four major opposition parties, the Republican People's Party (İYü), the Good Party (İYü), the Happiness Party (SP) and the Democratic Party (DP), jointly formed the "State Union" (Millet İttifakı), advocating the restoration of the parliamentary system and abolition of the executive presidential system, hoping to curb the positive party and Erdoğan. Together with the Democratic and Progressive Party (DEVA), they formed the "Six Party Round Table" (Altılı Masa), which is seeking to jointly launch a presidential candidate representing the opposition forces and compete with Erdogan in 2023.
After all, Erdogan was the president at the time, with political resources such as the media and the judiciary, enough to crack down on various opposition forces, such as Ekrem İmamoğlu, the mayor of Istanbul from the Republican People ’ s Party, who was originally highly polled and regarded as a star of tomorrow enough to end Erdoğan ’ s 20 years in power, was sentenced to more than two years in prison in December 2022 for “suspected insult to the Supreme Electoral Council. ” He lost the right to run for president.
After Imam Oulu was forced out, the "six-party round table" did not immediately integrate new candidates, but entangled in ideological scuffles, political spoils distribution, until March 2023, it was determined to nominate CHP party leader Krechidar Oulu, but this nomination was initially not supported by the good party, the latter also threatened to withdraw from the "six-party round table".
After many days of consultations and political exchanges, Krechdarolu agreed to have Ankara Mayor Mansur Yavaş and Imam Oulu as vice presidents, and the good party agreed to stay at the "six-party round table" and support the nomination of Krechdarolu for election.
In fact, from the point of view of the composition of the structure, the only ideology that can unite the "six-party round table" is against Erdogan.
Because the Republican People's Party with the most seats is the centre-left pro-European secularism party, the Happiness Party is a Eurosceptic conservative party with Islamism, the Democratic Party is a centre-right nationalist party, the Democratic and Progressive Party is a centre-right pro-European party, the Future Party is a right-wing pro-European party, and the Good Party is a centre-right nationalist party.
In short, the parties have a combination of ideologies that straddle Islamism and secularism, and basically if Erdoğan and the AKP had not been in power for too long, the parties would have no incentive to integrate.
However, even if it is reluctantly integrated, the "six-party round table" is still divided, otherwise it will not be until two months before the election to determine the nomination of candidates; and after the confirmation of the presidential candidate, the "six-party round table" broke out in a new civil war on the list of parliamentary candidates, all parties want to strive for more security seats distribution, resulting in the continued difficulty of the list.
All these things are quite chilling in the eyes of Turkish voters: Erdoğan may have a monopoly on power and love the position of power, but the opposition forces are also only interested in the division of territory and political division of spoils, and have no intention of changing Turkey's development predicament.
Under the balance of the two, or some voters who are tired of Erdoğan, after going through a thousand turns of heart, they chose to continue to vote for the positive party and Erdoğan, instead of supporting the opposition forces whose governing ability is unknown and whose positions are mixed, resulting in the eventual defeat of Krechdar Olu by a small margin.
How Erdoğan mobilised the "rise of Turkey"
In addition to the weak integration of opposition forces and the failure to gather enough political energy, Erdoğan and the Positive Development Party are still able to gather support and call for votes under the impact of high inflation and earthquake disasters, which is also the key to the defeat of Krechdar Olu.
According to the results of the poll, voters in large cities whose wealth has been severely eroded by high inflation supported Krechdarolu in the election, including the top three cities of Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir and Adana, the fifth largest city; however, Bursa, the sixth largest city of Gaziantep, and the seventh largest city of Konya. (Konya) is still supporting Erdoğan, and Gaziantep is still the hardest hit area of the 2023 earthquake, but voters still vote for the current president who has been denounced by public opinion, and it is clear that Erdoğan still has a certain degree of political energy.
Looking at this source of energy, it is obvious that it is not all the economic achievements that have been downhill.
Looking back at Erdoğan ’ s path to power, he experienced high economic growth in Turkey during his term of office, which can escort him to power.
From 2008 to 2013, developed markets such as the United States, Europe and Japan adopted a number of rounds of quantitative easing policies, international "hot money" poured into emerging markets including Turkey, stimulating the latter's economic growth. Erdogan took advantage of the momentum to promote easy credit, ask the central bank to continue to cut interest rates, and promote large-scale infrastructure projects. On the altar alone, no one can resist.
However, after the US Federal Reserve released a possible interest rate hike in 2013, foreign investment was greatly withdrawn, and emerging market currencies, including the lira, began to depreciate, and Turkey ’ s economic growth continued to slow down. And...
In the process of coping with the crisis, Erdoğan obviously wants to sacrifice prices and preserve economic growth, so he used extreme economic means and insisted on cutting interest rates in the face of high inflation.
The result, while maintaining economic growth to a certain extent, has led to a sharp depreciation of the lira, soaring prices, a near collapse of the bond market, and widespread protests in major cities such as Istanbul.
But looking at Erdoğan ’ s political actions in the past 10 years, it can be seen that he has begun to actively mobilize public support in the military, historical traditions, and diplomatic fields of major powers to fill the “Turkish rise ” narrative under the slowdown in economic growth and make up for his political loss.
As far as the diplomatic tradition after the Cold War is concerned, Turkey is an intermediate power anchored in the Western world and, with its strategic position across Eurasia, moves among different groups of countries.
However, after the outbreak of the Arab Spring in 2010, the outside world saw a more "eastern" and "military power" Turkey: on the Egyptian issue, its support for the Muslim Brotherhood, its involvement in the local political situation; on the battlefield of Syria and Libya, it has successively sent troops to intervene in the civil war there since 2016, and successfully achieved certain results. In the Gulf field, Turkey and Iran have maintained close interaction with Qatar, to a certain extent, prompting the 2017 Qatar severance storm, but because Turkey and Iran insisted on not retreating, the final storm ended with Saudi concessions in 2021, and Turkey successfully maintained its political achievements in the Gulf.
Of course, Turkey's foreign military operations are not all fruitful results.
Taking the Syrian battlefield as an example, Turkey launched four military operations against Syria: the Euphrates Shield from 2016 to 2017, the Olive Branch in 2018, the Peace Spring in 2019 and the Spring Shield in 2020.
Since the "olive branch" operation, the Turkish army has not only attacked the Kurdish forces, but also exchanged fire with the Syrian government forces supported by the Russian side, causing strong dissatisfaction in Moscow.
After many unsuccessful coordination, the Russian army was brazenly engaged with Turkey in 2020, resulting in the scribbled end of the "spring shield", and Turkey can only be forced to obey the Russian-led order in northern Syria.
However, under the propaganda of the Erdogan government, Turkey is not clearly aware that Turkey lost to Russia, but to see the Turkish army fighting in northern Syria in order to fight terrorism, which is very encouraging for nationalists and patriotic people.
In addition, in the historical tradition, Erdogan ’ s most classic action is to announce in July 2020 the abolition of the 1934 cabinet decree, the end of the 86 years of Hagia Sophia ’ s museum years, and the restoration of its mosque status.
Although this has caused many Western countries to criticize, but Erdoğan is not without the basis of public opinion, because in the 2015 capture of Junstenburg memorial ceremony, many Turks have held morning prayers in the museum square, in 2018, the Turkish Islamic Association is publicly applied to hold worship in the museum, although it was finally rejected, but has attracted a lot of public support.
Therefore, Erdogan's decision to "liberate St. Sophia" is aimed at the Islamic resurgence in Turkey in recent years, hoping to draw the support of anti-Kemalist voters.
And in the great power diplomatic field, Turkey's action is not to be said, in addition to the neighboring Central Asia and the Middle East, the Russian-Ukrainian war under various violent swings across Eurasia, are Erdogan's excellent election materials.
Taking the March 2022 Russian-Ukrainian Foreign Minister ’ s talks in Turkey and the landing of the Black Sea Food Agreement in July as an example, Turkish state media vigorously promoted Erdogan ’ s “peacemaker ” role; as for blocking Finland and Sweden from joining NATO, Turkish state media used Erdogan ’ s“ defense of national interests ”, “no fear of offending the West ” and“ combating Kurdish terrorism ”.
Of course, under the burden of economic decline and governance for many years, the narrative situation of mobilizing military, historical traditions and great power diplomacy can play a role in Erdoğan ’ s election, which can only be determined by the election results.
Judging from the results of 51.91% to 48.09%, although the above actions did not create a brilliant victory, they were enough to defeat the opposition forces and guarantee Erdogan another five-year term, which obviously still has some effect.
However, Turkey ’ s high economic growth has ended, and how to buffer Turkey ’ s economic storm and find new solutions outside of “Erdoğan ’ s economics ” are difficult issues that cannot be solved in the short term.
After the election, Erdoğan ’ s challenge continued.

Saudi women ’ s rights activists ’ use of hashtags is also a crime.
Manaher was arrested for her support of reform.
(Photo / Instagram @ manahelal _ otibi, same below.)
Journalist Wu Mei-yi / Comprehensive Report
Manahel al-Otaibi, a 29-year-old Saudi woman who championed and promoted reforms on Twitter and Snapchat calling for more basic rights for women in the country, was arrested last November and has been jailed since then on charges including using the hashtag # societyisready to call for the abolition of male guardianship.
Manaher, a licensed fitness instructor who loves art, yoga and travel, often shares and promotes female empowerment content, and is accused of not wearing “proper ” clothing in addition to using social media.
She is currently in detention and has not been convicted or sentenced, but previous similar cases have shown that public demands for women ’ s fundamental rights can be seen as inflammatory.
In fact, Manaher ’ s sister, Fouz al-Otaibi, was also accused of not wearing proper clothing, but managed to escape from Saudi Arabia before being arrested.
Another sister, Maryam, a prominent women ’ s rights advocate, was released in 2017 after serving time in prison for protesting against the male guardianship system.
Saudi Arabia has relaxed strict rules for women, including the ability to dress and work outside the country, to help shape the image of the new country, promote the kingdom and tourism, but the authorities continue to clamp down on women demanding more reforms.
Manaher is just the latest example of a Saudi arrest for using social media to challenge authorities.
Previously, Salma al-Shehab, a PhD student at Reed University in the United Kingdom, was arrested and sentenced to 34 years in prison by a special terrorist court after returning home for using Twitter, tracking and forwarding posts from dissidents and activists.
Lina al-Hathloul, head of ALQST, a Saudi human rights group living abroad, said the case highlighted the authorities ’ empty promises of reform: “Saudi women will still be imprisoned or face false trials for claiming their rights or simply believing they are free to wear what they want. ”
Saad bin Khalid Al Jabri, a former Saudi minister of state who has been in exile in Canada since May 2017, also said the case was an example of the Saudi government ’ s hypocrisy and selective application of strict laws, “in order to promote tourism to foreign Instagram models and even publish swimsuit photos, the authorities have locked up Saudi women without burqas. ”
Saudi Arabia ’ s government, led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, routinely suppresses dissidents, allegedly indirectly holding a large stake in Twitter through the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund (PIF), and planting spies inside the company to obtain personal data from users seen as threats to the kingdom.

Gender gap in science and technology
While the tech industry has made significant progress and pioneering innovation, it is sadly tarnished by a glaring, substantial gender gap.
This gap is not a single, stand-alone issue, but rather a multifaceted issue that permeates all aspects of the industry, such as the apparent underrepresentation of women in influential leadership roles, unequal access to opportunities and resources, and the glaring wage gap between the sexes.
The statistical evidence supporting the reality of this gender gap is undeniable and worthy of attention.
In a recent study, only 27% of female students said they would consider a career in technology.
This statistic contrasts sharply with that of boys, 62 per cent of whom said they would consider such a career path.
Globally, the situation is no different, with women making up only 25% of all computer positions.
These figures show that women in technical jobs face persistent barriers on a daily basis.
These challenges include, but are not limited to, pervasive gender bias, the lack of female role models in the field, and the pervasive shadow of workplace discrimination.
The impact of this pervasive gender gap extends beyond the personal struggles faced by women in tech.
It has wide-ranging consequences, affecting entire industries and stifling innovation and economic growth.
The lack of gender equality in science and technology positions limits the scope of intellectual diversity and the scope of talent, a shortcoming that is detrimental to a science and technology industry that relies on diverse ideas and unique perspectives.
Therefore, the gender gap in the tech world is not only an issue of equality and social justice, but also a major obstacle to the continued development and prosperity of the industry.
No-Code as a platform for balancing tools
Code-less platforms have become powerful tools that help level the playing field for women in tech.
By providing accessible and easy-to-use tools, these platforms remove barriers to programming knowledge and enable more women to enter the field without traditional software development expertise.
This provides an opportunity for women from diverse backgrounds to find their place in the tech industry, whether as front-end developers, UX / UI designers, or software product managers.
The rise of no-code platforms has also led to the creation of supportive communities where women can connect, learn and grow with their peers.
These communities include online forums, networking events, mentorship programs, and dedicated online resources tailored for women in tech.
This support system enables women to overcome challenges and barriers to entry, help them advance their careers and contribute to a fairer tech industry.
Challenges still facing women in tech
While the no-code platform has greatly improved the situation of women in tech, many challenges remain.
Despite the progress made so far, the tech industry still has unresolved systemic issues that hinder gender equality and inclusion.
Some of the key areas where women continue to struggle include:
1.
Gender bias: Women in science and technology still face gender stereotypes and biases that question their ability to pursue or excel in technical roles.
This can lead to women being overlooked in promotions, receiving less recognition for their work and encountering the assumption that their skills, knowledge or commitment to a career are inferior to those of their male counterparts.
2.
Discrimination and harassment: Many women in skilled jobs report gender-based discrimination and harassment in the workplace, both overt and subtle.
This hostility can lead to emotional tension, hinder productivity and affect their confidence and career development.
3.
Lack of visibility and representation: the absence of women in leadership positions and the underrepresentation of women in the workforce can hamper support networks for female talent.
Women may find challenges in identifying role models and mentors, limiting access to mentoring, knowledge-sharing and networking opportunities for career advancement.
4.
Work-life balance: Traditionally, women have assumed the primary responsibility for caring for the family, which can conflict with demanding technical occupations.
This challenge forces many women to leave the workforce or to choose positions that offer greater flexibility but fewer opportunities for advancement.
5.
Channel issues: There are gaps in women ’ s representation in STEM fields, starting with primary and secondary education, to higher education and the workforce.
Ensuring equal access to education and opportunities for girls and women plays a key role in addressing these issues.
There is no doubt that efforts must continue to narrow the gender gap in science and technology.
The industry must work collectively to eliminate prejudice, promote diversity and inclusion, provide equal opportunities, and develop support networks for women. The No-code platform has made a huge contribution to this cause, but much remains to be done to achieve true gender equality.
AppMaster: A powerful No-Code platform for women in tech
AppMaster is an excellent example of a powerful no-code platform that empowers women in tech.
By providing an easy-to-use yet effective tool for creating back-end, web, and mobile apps, AppMaster reduces barriers to app development and helps women succeed in the tech industry, even without coding knowledge.
The AppMaster platform features features such as visual data model creation, a business process designer for back-end applications, a REST API, and a WSS endpoint that facilitates the application development process.
Women can create networks and mobile applications without programming knowledge, enabling them to engage in entrepreneurial activities or promote their existing businesses.
As a no-code solution, AppMaster democratizes the tech industry by making it easier for women from diverse backgrounds to reach out.
The platform offers different subscription plans to meet the needs of different types of customers, from small businesses and startups to businesses with large projects.
In addition, AppMaster is committed to helping its users succeed.
The platform offers a wealth of documentation, online tutorials, expert guides and dedicated customer support for women looking to enter the tech industry or improve their existing skills.
Using these resources, women can learn platforms, develop applications, and establish themselves as leaders in the industry.
In short, platforms like AppMaster are advancing gender equality in the tech industry by breaking down barriers and providing accessible tools to empower women.
While challenges remain, platforms like AppMaster help women enter tech, grow their careers, and strive for a more inclusive future.

Behind the C919 is the cultivation of national capabilities ｜ Experts have something to say
Author: External Submission
Published: Updated:
The first commercial flight of China ’ s domestic aircraft, the C919, has undoubtedly attracted global attention.
According to the Wall Street Journal, the success of the C919 ’ s commercial debut means that the “duopoly ” of Boeing and Airbus for decades has been challenged in the Chinese market.
The challenge is small but symbolic.
At present, the C919 order has exceeded a thousand.
According to the “China Commercial Aviation Company Market Forecast Annual Report (2021-2040) ” released by China Commercial Aviation, China ’ s fleet is expected to reach 9,957 aircraft by 2040, accounting for 22% of the global passenger fleet, making it the largest single aviation market in the world.
More importantly, with the advancement of the domestic aircraft industry, a large number of industrial chains will be driven to develop.
This driving effect has made the large civil aircraft industry regarded as a pearl in the crown of modern industry, and it is also an important reason why China insists on independent research and development.
At that time, when the news of China's decision to build a large aircraft was made public, the Western world responded for the first time.
Some of them are cynical, such as the American "Aviation Week" published an article, the author of which said, "At Beijing Capital International Airport to board the C919 to fly to Chengdu or Shanghai, I do not believe that I can live to that day."
At the same time, there are many people in the Western industry who are aware of the objective trend.
“I don ’ t think China has insurmountable technical hurdles, they ’ ve sent astronauts into space twice, and some of the best aerodynamics in the world are Chinese, ” the former Boeing CEO said.
Europe and the United States are at the forefront of the world's civil aviation industry, and their political and business circles are well aware that for high-technology systems industries such as aerospace, national capabilities are an important support, which is the successful experience of Europe and the United States.
On December 9, 2022, the world ’ s first C919 was delivered to China Eastern Airlines, and on December 26, the flight verification mission began, with an estimated total of 100 flight hours.
It is reported that the verification flight will simulate the entire operation process of the flight, including the signing and release, passenger boarding, pilot operation, aircraft maintenance, etc., to comprehensively test the reliability of all aspects of the commercial operation of China Eastern Airlines C919, and lay a solid foundation for the successful launch of commercial passenger flight.
(Xinhua News Agency)
Chinese aircraft have carried the dreams of generations of Chinese people.
Professor Lu Feng of Peking University mentioned in an interview that China's high-level rediscussion of the big plane was in 2003, and there were two important events in the background: First, the 1995-1996 Taiwan Strait crisis, and second, in 1999, the United States-led NATO missile attack on the Chinese Embassy in the Southern Alliance.
After these two events, the Chinese government leadership began to increase investment in the defense industry, so today's series of achievements, such as the J-20, J-10 fighter aircraft and so on.
However, what is less known is that as early as 1980, China ’ s first large-scale long-range jet passenger aircraft-10, independently developed and with full intellectual property rights, had its maiden flight at Shanghai Dachau Airport.
Zhao Yining ’ s book “Great Country Project ” mentioned that the successful development of the Yun-10 marked that China had stepped onto the stage necessary for the development of large civil aircraft, and its development was only three years later than that of Airbus.
Unfortunately, by 1983, the Yun-10 had no financial support, and it was gradually shelved. Although this was a regret in the era of transition, it was a great proof of China's independent industrial system and capabilities, and also laid the foundation for the subsequent development of China's civil aviation industry.
Today, the C919 was born, which can be said to fill the regret of the year.
Whether it is the current level of economic development in China, or a strong manufacturing industry and foundation, or the cultivation of high-end scientific and technological talents, it has laid the foundation for the development of the civil aviation industry.
Coupled with clear strategic support at the national level and the recognition of the public opinion as a whole, the big aircraft business has clearly entered a thick and thin era.
Those who question the lack of innovation in the C919, or the so-called "assembly", obviously do not understand the basic situation of the civil aviation industry.
Today, the mainstream of aircraft manufacturing is the "master manufacturer-supply model" (referred to as the "master supply model"), which is represented by Boeing aircraft, and about 65% of its parts are purchased outside of Boeing's home location.
The core competitiveness of Boeing aircraft is reflected in its supplier-led integration capabilities.
COMAC is learning from Boeing ’ s “main supplier model ” and innovating on core designs such as“ the soul of the airplane ” wing components, while integrating domestic and foreign suppliers.
Of course, it should also be acknowledged that there is still a gap between China COMAC and Boeing in terms of the dominant integration capabilities of suppliers.
However, as long as the stage is set up, the subsequent drills will naturally deepen their strength.
Photo of the C919 aircraft on the tarmac at Shanghai Hongqiao Airport (May 28).
On the same day, C919 ’ s first commercial flight, Eastern Airlines MU9191, will depart from Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport and arrive at Beijing Capital International Airport. (Xinhua)
In fact, there has been an argument in the mainland economic sector for several years that the market economy can spontaneously realize industrial upgrading without government intervention.
In recent years, China's automobile industry, new energy industry, high-speed rail, large aircraft and a series of industrial achievements, precisely prove the simplicity of this argument.
Looking at the history and reality of the world, the prosperity of the high-tech industry cannot be separated from the endorsement of the government and national capabilities.
In the United States, for example, the initial market for almost all of its core technological innovations, such as computers, jet engines, and semiconductors, was provided by the U.S. government through government procurement, including defense orders.
Typical of them, such as basic research on many common technologies for Apple ’ s smartphone applications, are funded by the Defense Department ’ s Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA).
The Chip and Science Act and the regulations on subsidies for new energy vehicles issued by the United States in recent years directly highlight the influence of the government on industrial policy.
Europe and the United States, what is the exception to China?

How does China ’ s development of AI demand “socialist core values ” differ from country to country?
Author: United Morning Post
Published: Updated:
China ’ s artificial intelligence (AI) boom continues.
Three first-tier cities, Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen, released policy documents to encourage AI development in the last two days of May, once again demonstrating official support for the hottest track in the technology war.
According to the Securities Times, Shanghai issued a document on Tuesday (May 30) to strengthen support for the development of private investment, and proposed to give full play to the guiding role of artificial intelligence innovation and development, and support private enterprises to participate widely in the construction of artificial intelligence infrastructure such as data and computing power.
The two documents released by Beijing on the same day put forward specific goals such as the scale of the core industry of artificial intelligence to reach 300 billion yuan (RMB, the same below) by 2025, the continuous growth of more than 10%, and the scale of the radiation industry to exceed 1 trillion yuan.
At the same time, it also proposed specific measures in five aspects, such as improving the ability to coordinate and supply computing resources, and general AI technology systems such as system construction models, to promote breakthroughs in domestically produced AI chips, and deployed AI technology innovation and application related work around six fields, such as finance, medical care, and autonomous driving.
The global artificial intelligence (AI) boom continues. (Reuters)
The plan to promote the development and application of artificial intelligence released by Shenzhen on Wednesday (May 31) also proposed that the city should build a new generation of national artificial intelligence innovation and development pilot area and national artificial intelligence innovation and application pilot area, and strive to create a global artificial intelligence pioneer city.
The plan is clear, to build a city-level computing power coordination and scheduling platform, promote "thousands of industries + AI", and encourage enterprises in the financial, business, industrial, transportation and other fields to upgrade existing production, service and management methods through artificial intelligence.
It can be seen that the recent exposure of AI fake news and AI fraud has not shaken China's official support for the development of AI.
Internationally, when foreign dignitaries and experts are debating how to manage the threat of artificial intelligence, China ’ s optimism and enthusiasm for AI, and its rapid development in this field, are particularly unique.
China ’ s AI ambitions
China is so keen on AI development that cities are scrambling to launch support initiatives that are closely related to the approaching milestones for the country ’ s ambitious goals set a few years ago.
Baidu held a press conference in Beijing headquarters on the afternoon of March 16, officially launched the big language model "Wenxin One Word":
In 2017, the State Council issued the "New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan", which proposed that China's overall artificial intelligence technology and application should be synchronized with the world's advanced level in 2020; in 2025, it will achieve a major breakthrough in artificial intelligence basic theory, so that AI will become the main driving force for industrial upgrading and economic transformation; in 2030, AI theory, technology and application will reach the world's leading level.
To lead the world in AI for more than a decade is a challenging goal for China.
Perhaps due to multiple factors such as the Sino-US trade and technology war, the epidemic, and the rectification of technology companies, Chinese officials have not announced that they have reached the 2020 goal, but at the same time, there is no sign of abandoning or adjusting the next two goals.
This means that the time left for scientific research institutions and technology enterprises to complete major breakthroughs in basic theory and achieve a leading position in some fields will be two and a half years.
And from the end of last year chatbot ChatGPT phenomenal explosion, Chinese technology companies launched the performance of the target products, at least in the field of generative AI, China has not much advantage.
On the other hand, a 2021 Harvard Business Review article pointed out that although the number of Chinese research papers in the field of AI has jumped from 1,086 in 1997 to 30,343 in 2017, more than the number of US research papers in the same period, academic research does not necessarily translate into innovation in AI and the advantage of global leadership.
Harvard Business Review points out that although China (Deep Blue Line) has surpassed the United States (Yellow Line) in the number of research papers in the field of AI, academic research does not necessarily translate into the advantages of innovation and global leadership in the field of AI. (Internet)
The article also summarizes the advantages of China ’ s rapid development in the field of AI, including the large amount of learning data available in a large market, as well as strong support for AI development and relatively weak privacy protection regulations.
As an example, China ’ s ubiquitous surveillance cameras have created excellent conditions for AI companies specializing in facial recognition – a field that will be much more difficult to develop in countries and regions with stricter regulations on privacy.
Different countries have different regulatory focus.
China does not have laws and regulations on the protection of privacy information, but neither the "Personal Information Protection Law" passed in 2021, nor the draft "Management Measures for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services" proposed in April this year, does not prohibit or restrict the access of relevant enterprises to personal information, but emphasizes that the collection and processing of personal information should have a clear and reasonable purpose, and the data should contain personal information and obtain the consent of the subject of personal information.
On the other hand, the focus of the management method of generative AI services is not on the protection of personal information and privacy, but rather on the content generated should reflect the core values of socialism, and must not contain content that subverts state power, overthrows the socialist system, incites division or undermines national unity, promotes terrorist extremism, ethnic hatred, and may disrupt economic and social order.
Merchants use AI face changing technology to let the anchor pretend to be a star with goods. (Network resource map)
At the same time, it is also clear that China supports independent innovation, application and international cooperation in basic technologies such as artificial intelligence algorithms and frameworks.
Today, when artificial intelligence has become a mainstream development, China is not the only country that has expressed support for development while also giving regulatory opinions on AI.
Tech experts warn AI threat equates to pandemic and nuclear war
According to the official website of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) AI Policy Observation Platform (Oecd.AI), 69 countries and the European Union have proposed strategic plans for AI development.
Many of these countries have launched or are studying guidance and regulatory measures for AI, but their strength and direction are not small differences.
According to the official website of Oecd.AI, 69 countries and the European Union have put forward strategic plans for the development of AI, and many of them have launched or are studying guidance and regulatory measures for AI.
For example, India, like China, a developing country in Asia, has also strongly encouraged the development of AI, but has yet to introduce regulations or regulations that specifically target AI.
Japan, as a developed country in Asia, although there are no prohibitive regulations for AI, is cautious about AI risks and has issued guiding regulations; South Korea, which is also a developed country, is expected to introduce regulations to classify risk levels and put forward different regulatory requirements for AI applications within the year on the premise of allowing AI development.
In the developed countries of Europe and America, the United States as a leader in the field of AI, although there are no regulations restricting AI at the federal government level, many officials have recently expressed a stronger regulatory will; at the same time, there are different levels of regulatory measures in different states and organizations in the United States.
Canada, a neighbor of the United States, is pushing the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act to clarify the threat of AI to individuals and monitor their development.
The European Union, which has the most stringent attitude towards AI regulation, introduced the Artificial Intelligence Act in 2021, emphasizing the need to control risks through the establishment of a regulatory system to ensure that AI development is safe, ethical and trustworthy.
The bill assesses the risks of using AI in different areas and prohibits the use of AI in areas of “unacceptable risk. ”
However, not all EU countries agree with the risk classification of the bill, such as France ’ s AI video surveillance program, which is contrary to the EU law.
In 2017, Tesla founder Musk and 116 other AI experts from around the world signed a letter asking the United Nations to ban countries from developing killer robots to avoid World War III. (Reuters)
On the other hand, while member states have different attitudes towards AI regulation, the Group of Seven (G7) Digital and Technology Ministers, after concluding their meeting in Japan at the end of April, agreed to introduce a regulatory bill on AI based on risks while maintaining an open and enabling environment.
In addition, according to a joint statement released on the White House website on Wednesday, the United States-EU Trade and Technology Commission meeting held in Sweden at the end of May also discussed the potential regulation of AI and reached cooperation on monitoring and measuring existing and future AI risks.
Overall, calls for AI regulation are higher in developed countries; compared to Asian countries, European and American countries are generally more worried about AI development.
Pray for wealth?
In addition to differences in attitude at the government level, AI threat theory is also the focus of attention of the industry and the general public. With the rapid development of AI technology, many people are worried that AI will replace millions of white-collar jobs and even threaten human survival.
For example, more than 350 AI technology leaders and experts jointly warned on Tuesday (May 30) that the extinction risks posed by AI are on a par with other social-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.
In March, more than a thousand industry figures called for a moratorium on the development of AI systems more powerful than GPT-4 for at least six months, citing potential risks to society and humanity.
On the other hand, an Ipsos survey released in 2022 showed that the American people are the most pessimistic about the future of AI technology, with only 35% of Americans believing that the benefits of AI outweigh the risks, while China is the most optimistic country in the world, with nearly 80% of Chinese believing that the benefits of AI outweigh the risks.
Robots are developing rapidly, and many people in the outside world worry that robots will get out of control and do harm to human beings.
However, it seems that before the episode of "Transgression", the harm caused by robots to people is due to the network security problems of robots and hackers, not the AI itself. (online picture)
From strongly encouraging development to implementing stronger regulation, it seems that every emerging sector has to go through the process, and AI, a large and opportunistic market, is no exception.
According to International Data Corporation (IDC), global AI revenue will exceed the US $500 billion mark in 2023 (the same below, about S $675.5 billion).
IDC also predicts that China ’ s AI market spending will increase to $14.75 billion in 2023, accounting for about one-tenth of the global total.
ChatGPT, a chatbot, believes that the arguments against regulating AI, including over-regulation, could make it downhill when it comes to technology competition with other countries. (Reuters)
If ChatGPT is asked whether it should regulate AI, it gives reasons for opposition, including that regulation will not keep pace, that regulation will limit industry innovation and economic growth, that regulation will place an undue burden on relevant companies, and that over-regulation may discourage competition in technology with other countries.
Perhaps this is the last reason why both China and the United States, which are engaged in a technology war, are reluctant to introduce tougher regulatory measures against AI.
Although experts have analyzed that even China ’ s best big language modeling technology is still 18 months to two years behind the United States, such a gap will not take the United States lightly – especially when China looks like it is ready to overtake the curve with AI.

Published: Updated:
U.S. President Joe Biden fell again while attending an Air Force Academy graduation ceremony on June 1, and health issues continued to receive attention.
White House communications director Ben LaBolt said on Twitter that Biden was not in a big way right now, adding that there was a sandbag on the podium.
Biden, now 80, is not the first time he has fallen in public, most recently when he landed on Air Force One at the end of a trip to Poland in February.
During the Group of Seven (G7) summit last month, Biden nearly fell down the stairs while visiting the shrine.
