The elderly are more likely to fall than the average person. In daily life, we can often see the news of the elderly being injured by falling. Why are the elderly prone to falling?
What can I do to prevent falls?
5 Major Causes of Falling
According to the 2017 statistics of the Department of Health Elderly Health Centre for the Elderly, more than 10% of the more than 45,000 community elders aged 65 or above have fallen at least once in half a year, and 10.2% of the elderly who have fallen have suffered a fracture.
There are many causes of falls in the elderly. Here are five common causes of falls in the elderly:
1.
Physiological factors
As we age, the body ’ s various physiological functions decrease, including balance, responsiveness, muscle strength, and bone health, all of which increase the risk of falls.
2.
Environmental factors
The elderly often face various environmental factors in their daily lives, such as uneven ground, accumulation of miscellaneous objects in the home, narrow corridors and staircases, etc. These environmental factors may cause the elderly to fall.
3.
Medication factor
Elderly people often need to use a variety of drugs, such as blood pressure reduction drugs, sedatives, sleeping pills, etc. These drugs may affect the elderly ’ s sense of balance and responsiveness, increasing the risk of falls.
4. Disease factors
The elderly often suffer from a variety of chronic diseases, such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes, osteoporosis, etc., which affect the physical health and function of the elderly and increase the risk of falls.
5. Psychological factors
Older people often experience negative emotions such as loneliness, loss, and depression, which may affect their cognitive and mobility and increase the risk of falls.
What can we do to prevent the elderly from falling?
+ 6
Osteoporosis Calcium Tablets Really Useful?
Osteoporosis has long been considered one of the leading causes of fractures and falls in the elderly.
This can lead to a reduction in the strength and stability of the bones, which makes the body of the elderly more fragile and more prone to fractures and falls.
Especially in the daily life of the elderly, such as walking, going up and down stairs, bending and other activities, if there is not enough bone density and bone mass support, it is easy to fall.
In order to prevent osteoporosis, many elderly people will choose to take calcium tablets, but there have been studies showing that calcium alone can not completely prevent or treat osteoporosis.
In fact, osteoporosis is caused by a variety of factors, including genetics, lifestyle, nutritional intake, hormones, etc. All of the above factors need to be taken into account in prevention and treatment.
In addition, taking into account the absorption capacity of the body, taking too many calcium tablets will not only not replenish calcium, but may also cause side effects such as constipation and bloating.
Therefore, for the elderly and other people prone to osteoporosis, supplementing calcium through a normal diet is healthier and more beneficial than relying on calcium tablets.
4 Tips to Prevent Osteoporosis!
To prevent osteoporosis, in addition to the loss of calcium supplements, you should also pay attention to the following five points:
1.
A balanced diet
Eat enough calcium and vitamin D in your diet to promote bone health. Calcium-rich foods include dairy products, soy products, fish, shellfish, leafy greens, and more.
Vitamin D rich foods include fish, egg yolks, liver, dairy products and so on.
2.
Adequate exercise
Moderate exercise helps increase bone density and muscle strength, preventing osteoporosis.
Recommended exercises include aerobic exercise, strength training, and balance training.
3.
Improving lifestyle
Avoid smoking and alcohol, reduce caffeine intake, and help maintain bone health.
4.
Check bone density regularly
For high-risk groups such as women with family genetic history, menopause and the elderly, it is recommended to check bone density regularly, and to detect and treat osteoporosis early.

Taiwan's Minister of Digital Development, Tang Feng, is also among the signatories.
“Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI, as well as other society-scale risks such as global infectious diseases and nuclear war, should be a global priority, ” the San Francisco nonprofit Center for AI Security said in a brief statement.
More than 350 AI executives, researchers, and engineers signed the statement, in addition to Altman, Hassabis, and Anthropic CEO Yoshua Bengio, who won the Turing Award for neural network research and is known as the “Godfather of AI ” by Geoffrey Hinton.
Other signatories include Feng Tang, Microsoft Chief Technology Officer Scott and Chief Science Officer Robert Horvitz, OpenAI co-founder John Schulman, Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn, and professors from Harvard University, MIT, and Tsinghua University.
However, Yann LeCun, a third AI godfather at Meta, did not sign up.
European lawmakers are pushing for the European Artificial Intelligence Act, and the United States is exploring legislative regulations. Altman called for regulations in the form of licenses when he attended a U.S. congressional hearing in May.
EU officials revealed that EU industrial policy executive Bladon will discuss with Altman in June how to enforce AI regulations.
In March, billionaire Musk and more than 1,000 other researchers and technology executives called for a six-month moratorium on the development of advanced AI systems to halt the arms race.
However, the letter ’ s approach has been criticized, and other researchers have disagreed with the recommendation.
The Center for AI Security told The New York Times that the statement was made in a short statement to avoid disagreement.
Hendrix, executive director, said the center did not want to push for a massive proposal that included 30 potential interventions, “which would be a dilution of the message. ”

Shi Wanqing
Cairo, the capital of Egypt, suffered a huge dust storm on the afternoon of the 2nd, the blue sky instantly turned turquoise, the huge advertising signs on the land bridge hit the car, causing one death and five injuries, the accident made the weekday traffic on the land bridge is even worse, completely unable to move.

The 20-kilometer-long viaduct is the "October 6th Bridge", which connects the main artery on the east and west bank of the Nile River and winds through downtown Cairo, home to more than 22 million people, to Tahrir Square and the Egyptian Museum in the city center, and to Cairo Airport in the west.
The dust storm killed three people and forced the closure of two ports in the Suez Canal Economic Zone and the Red Sea, suspending all maritime navigation and activities.
According to the Egyptian authorities, the sea-surface wind at the port was as strong as Category 6, with waves ranging from 3 to 4 meters high.
In addition, the Cairo – Suez desert road is also covered by a large yellow sand wall, drivers panicked, turned around and retrograde to prevent being caught in the dust storm.
The dust storm caused a total loss of sight in some areas.
The worst affected areas are Cairo, Suez, Ismailia and the Sinai Peninsula.
Environment Minister Yasmine Fouad warned that the environment ministry predicted strong winds and more sandstorms in some areas of Cairo, the north coast and Upper Egypt on Wednesday.
The Egyptian Meteorological Agency (EMA) has advised people to avoid going out for the next two days, wear masks outdoors and avoid direct sunlight to avoid danger from strong winds, sandstorms and heat waves exceeding 40 degrees Celsius in some areas.
According to the Egyptian Ministry of Health, dust storms often cause respiratory problems and allergies in Cairo residents, and people with thin nasal membranes are also prone to nosebleeds.
The annual dust storm season in Egypt is called Khamsin. The name originally means 50 in Arabic, meaning that the annual wind period is about 50 days, which occurs intermittently in late winter and early summer, but generally starts in early April and ends in mid-May.
Consin, also known as the Levant, is a very dry, hot wind with large amounts of dust and sand that blows from the south (the Sahara Desert) to the southeast at extremely high speeds (up to 140 km / h), affecting Egypt and the eastern Mediterranean countries.
When the air over the desert is strongly heated, causing the lower atmosphere to become unstable, this instability mixes strong winds in the mid-troposphere and begins to blow down to the surface, creating stronger winds at the surface.
A dust storm can usually last three to four days.
When the wind stops, a layer of fine sand is deposited on the surfaces of buildings, cars, and objects.
This phenomenon also indirectly affects the appearance of traditional Egyptian buildings and ornaments, often based on the gray earth color system, similar to the concept of insect camouflage protection color.
When the wind blows, the humidity in the area drops below 5%, resulting in extremely dry weather and even affecting the performance of electrical equipment.
According to the Egyptian Meteorological Agency, the worst dust storm in 30 years occurred on May 2, 1997.
At that time, the storm was 97 km / h (97 km / h), and several road trees and advertising signs were toppled, and the airport was temporarily closed.
The dust storm changed the sky from gray to red and then to creepy white, reducing visibility to zero in many places, killing at least eight people and injuring dozens.

From generative AI to responsible AI, we talk about AI ’ s self-discipline and other laws from a legal perspective.
【 Text / Photo courtesy of Feng Zhenyu / Tachih Images / Gettyimages 】
As the ChatGPT craze swept the world with a thunder, it also created a serious issue.
That is, who should be responsible and how should be regulated for all kinds of illegal, infringing, or improper behavior that accompany the use of AI.
One of the key questions is whether it is still handled by the operators through the self-regulatory approach of Responsible AI (RAI), or whether it should be handled by the legal aspects of other laws, which is an important issue to be solved under this wave of AI.
Since the birth of the concept of AI, people have been full of illusions about AI and worried about the possible threat of AI development.
Generative AI advances beyond the past, led by ChatGPT, and even with the help of a new generation of large language models such as GPT-4 and Google PaLM 2, it is moving toward the goal of General Artificial Intelligence (AGI).
As the technology of generative AI advances, people from the initial worry about ChatGPT (used to write reports or papers) gradually become concerned about whether these emerging AI tools will mislead people, spread false information, violate privacy or intellectual property rights, replace some human work, and even be used to influence election results. This has raised the responsibility of responsible AI, which originally existed only at the level of the enterprise industry and is a self-regulatory function, to the level of the national and even the international level, and has transformed into the responsibility of the AI required by law.
Self-discipline for responsible AI
The so-called responsible AI, is a deep thinking on machine learning services, believes that various organizations in the development of machine learning services, should pay attention to the individuality and particularity of the service object.
According to Microsoft, responsible AI is a way to develop, evaluate, and deploy AI systems in a safe, reliable, and ethical manner, respecting enduring values such as fairness, reliability, and transparency.
Although Google did not initially use the term, its Recommended best practices for AI believe that software development best practices should be followed when designing AI systems, and a “human-centric ” approach to machine learning, taking into account basic principles such as fairness, interpretability, privacy, and security. And...
After Google launched this AI principle in 2018, teams such as TensorFlow have developed products according to this principle, and have also launched tools and techniques for responsible AI, which has become an important driver of responsible AI.
However, this principle of responsible AI self-discipline at the enterprise level, under the impetus of generative AI, has been unable to cope with the various problems caused by the development of AI, resulting in the continuous expansion of the voice of supervision of AI from all walks of life, and countries have gradually begun to intervene in a legal manner, which also makes the principle of responsible AI self-discipline face a major challenge.
The sound of slowing the development of AI is emerging
First, in March 2023, the Center for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Policy (CAIDP), through an open letter and a complaint to the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC), called on the FTC to adopt measures to suspend advanced AI experimentation and use.
More eye-catching is the open letter on the suspension of AI development proposed by the Future Life Research Institute (FLI).
The letter, citing the potential risks AI poses to society and humanity, calls for a six-month moratorium on the development of AI technologies more advanced than GPT-4 until independent experts develop common safety guidelines and implement them.
This open letter attracted thousands of signatures from Tesla founder Musk and Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak, and more and more people have signed the open letter. As of May 18, 2023, more than 27,500 people have signed the open letter.
Even academics and experts who develop AI are concerned about the development of unregulated AI.
Artificial intelligence expert Geoffrey Hinton, known as the “godfather of AI, ” believes that generative AI is more likely to be difficult to control in advance.
Enterprises in order to achieve a leading position in technology, I am afraid that the corresponding regulations and restrictions will be relaxed. If government agencies, management units and technology companies themselves are not ready to provide corresponding regulations and effective control measures, I am afraid that it will make AI more uncontrollable, and even affect ethics.
Unexpectedly, even OpenAI CEO Altman, who developed ChatGPT and set off this wave of AI craze, said in testimony to the U.S. Senate in mid-May, “With the advancement of AI technology, we understand that the world is anxious about how AI will change the way we live. ”
We feel the same way, ” he added. “If something goes wrong with this technology, it could be very bad. ”
To that end, he suggested creating a U.S. or global regulatory body to issue licenses for powerful AI systems to stop AI models from “hubris of self-replication and self-infiltration ” and have the power to“ revoke licenses and ensure compliance with safety standards. ”
However, just as all parties expressed concern about AI, Microsoft threw a shock bomb.
According to a report in the New York Times on May 17, the Microsoft AI research team demonstrated in a 155-page paper, "Spark of Artificial General Intelligence", that GPT-4 demonstrated the ability to understand human concepts and skills, which is an important step towards general artificial intelligence (AGI).
This shows that despite all the calls, there is still no obstacle to the rapid development of AI technology.
Why is the voice of AI monitoring increasing?
Despite the international call, there are still limited countries to regulate AI, and many people believe that AI has not reached AGI (or strong AI), and does not have the ability to perceive and act, so there is no need to regulate the developing AI technology.
However, this does not mean that AI will not pose a threat to human society and civilization. The main reason is that the rapid development of generative AI has self-learning and self-correction capabilities, which even exceed the expectations of AI system developers.
In addition, the new AI has been able to control the language, and through continuous dialogue and interaction with humans, so that humans have a relationship of trust in AI, which affects human opinions and ideas.
Because language is the most important communication and creative tool for human beings, through the mastery of language, AI is equivalent to obtaining a key to open the human spiritual world. Through the use of language and gain human trust, it may have an impact on human economy, society, culture, technology, religion, and even politics, and its influence will even surpass the existing social media platforms.
Another reason why AI needs to be properly regulated is the difference between AI and traditional media or communication tools.
Traditional media or tools can only transmit and distribute information or creations created by humans, and cannot create new information to spread, but AI has the ability to create its own creation, and even has the possibility of creating a new culture.
Since AI has such a powerful influence and function, it can continuously introduce new products and even go public on its own without being audited and regulated by any government agency, which also highlights the problems that have arisen in the regulation of AI in various countries.
The emergence of these problems, so that the principle of responsible AI, which originally existed only at the level of corporate self-regulation, has begun to be concerned by various countries, and even some countries have tried to elevate this principle to other legal aspects of the law, the most active of which is the European Union, which has specially planned a complete regulatory framework for AI, and also gave responsible AI a new meaning.
From self-discipline to AI regulation
As the competition in the AI industry continues to expand, in addition to the rapid development of AI technology, and even the red line of general AI, it also highlights the shortcomings of self-discipline and responsible AI, which have led to calls from all walks of life to freeze the development of stronger AI and strengthen supervision.
According to an AI Index survey released by Stanford University in 2023, 37 AI-related laws have been passed into law worldwide in 2022.
The federal government did not act aggressively, but the states took the lead, passing nine laws, followed by five in Spain and four in the Philippines.
International efforts to regulate AI seem to be picking up steam after the potential problems with AI have been revealed.
Looking at the world, the most complete and active plan for the AI regulatory framework is the European Union.
After the breakthrough of AI machine learning and deep learning technology, the European Union began to conduct research on the regulation of AI. In addition to the publication of the AI white paper, the most important thing is to promote the overall legislative framework.
The European Commission first proposed the AI Act (AIA) in 2021, which classifies AI tools according to the level of risk into four categories: Minimal, Limited, High, and Unacceptable.
Two supporting bills were then introduced in September 2022.
The first is to amend the Revised Product Liability Directive (PLD) to allow compensation for damage caused by software updates, AI or digital services, and network security vulnerabilities in robots, drones or smart home system products; and the second is to establish the AI Liability Directive (ALD), which aims to establish uniform rules for information acquisition and mitigation of damage caused by AI systems. The burden of proof is regulated.
On May 11, 2023, AIA, the most critical AI regulation, was approved by the Internal Market and Equity Committee of the European Parliament, which is also an important step towards the birth of the first AI regulation bill.
The newly revised draft expands the scope of high risk to include, in addition to health, safety, fundamental rights or environmental hazards to people, voters and social media platforms that will affect political campaigns (more than 45 million users), and requires companies that provide large-scale AI-based models to establish risk assessment processes, describe copyrighted content used to train AI, ensure that users understand whether they are interacting with AI, and prohibit the public from using AI. Face recognition in real time.
The European Parliament will hold a final vote on the law in June.
In addition to the above-mentioned bills, the European Commission also proposed three European regulatory drafts at the end of 2020, including the Digital Governance Act (DGA), the Digital Market Act (DMA), and the Digital Services Act (DSA). A leader in technology.
In addition, in April 2023, the European privacy regulator, the European Data Protection Board (EDPB), announced the formation of a working group on ChatGPT, a significant step towards developing a common policy for AI privacy rules.
Reflections on regulation
Principles and Guidelines Not of a Legal Nature
In contrast, the United States, because of the leading position in the development of AI technology, so far, the United States has not considered the development of federal regulations similar to the European Union to regulate AI, only California, Colorado, Connecticut, Virginia and New York City, unless the user consent to prohibit AI "personal data analysis"; in addition, California and six other states are legislating to prohibit companies from using AI to discriminate or deceive. Consumers and job seekers.
On the federal side, although some policy documents are issued by various ministries, the more specific action so far is the "AI Bill of Rights Blueprint" issued by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy in October 2022, which lists five principles aimed at minimizing the potential harm of AI systems, but unlike the EU's AI bill, the Blueprint is not binding; and the Federal Trade Commission issued in May 2023. A guide on how to build AI and machine learning systems responsibly, which identifies biases and discriminatory outcomes through lifecycle monitoring, is also non-legal.
In 2023, after calls from all walks of life, the White House finally convened a meeting of the CEOs of AI companies such as Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI in early May to discuss the prospects and risks of AI.
While the White House said the meeting was a “frank and constructive discussion ” on how to make AI systems more transparent to policymakers, how to assess the safety of such products, and protect AI systems from malicious attacks, it did not address the goal of legislative regulation, and the White House announced only that it would allocate $140 million to expand AI research and work with the tech community to build an assessment system to“ solve the problem. ”
His laws and regulations are a long way off.
As countries are at different stages of the development of AI regulation and have different views on how to achieve it, it seems unlikely that at the international level there will be a consensus on any measures to regulate AI and limit the potential illegal use of AI in the near future.

Hong Kong ’ s water is contaminated with antibiotics by animals, and children may be overweight and harmful to their health.
• Add Favorite Column
• Collection of articles
In order to reduce animal disease and speed up reproduction and growth, the agricultural and fisheries sector may use antibiotics in the breeding process, but residual antibiotics may pose risks to human health, such as damaging the intestinal flora, making bacteria resistant, and even delaying the growth and development of brain cells.
Research by the Education University of Hong Kong has found that the use of animal antibiotics will not only lead to pollution of the water in Hong Kong, such as the ingestion of animal antibiotics from food by children, but also lead to overweight.
Tang Wenjing (Teaching University picture)
Professor Tang Wenjing of the Department of Science and Environment at the University of Hong Kong, said that excessive antibiotic intake may change the intestinal environment and even cause drug resistance problems. Since 2015, the research team has investigated the impact of animal antibiotics on environmental ecology, food safety and children ’ s health, including 13 river water samples and 15 sea water samples collected in various regions of Hong Kong in 2021.
The results showed that the samples contained 3 kinds of tetracycline, 10 kinds of sulfonamides, 9 kinds of quinolones, erythromycin, and neomycin, and other antibiotics.
A variety of antibiotics have been detected in organic egg drinking water
According to district statistics, the concentration and variety of antibiotics detected in Yuen Long, where there are more farms, were higher, and the level of antibiotics in Kam Tin Ho samples was as high as 114.26 ng / L. Although the concentration of antibiotics detected was lower than the findings obtained by the team in 2015, the number of antibiotics detected increased.
In addition, the team collected urine samples from 31 Hong Kong children aged 4 to 6 years who had not taken antibiotics within one month in 2016. The results showed that 77.4% of the samples contained antibiotics with a maximum concentration of 0.36 ng / mL, which was much higher than that of Shanghai and Korea.
The team said that although the concentration of antibiotics does not exceed WHO standards, the use of antibiotics in animals is closely related to the overweight of children, and parents should not take it lightly.
In the same year, the team also purchased chicken and aquatic products in the markets near the children ’ s homes, and processed them in traditional cooking methods such as water boiling, slow stewing and stir-frying.
It was found that high temperature cooking also failed to effectively remove antibiotics from food. “Organic eggs ” and drinking water, which claimed to be free of antibiotics, were also found to contain a variety of antibiotics, reflecting that antibiotics used by animals have unconsciously invaded human daily life, and even flowed into the body, or affected the health of the next generation.

24 year old girl working in 20 countries in 5 years sharing 4 financial management tips for being a “digital nomad ”
Personal Value Added 21: 30 2023 / 06 / 10

Remote work during the pandemic made home-based work or digital nomad popular, and Canadian schoolgirl Daniella Pashuk became a digital nomad five years ago.
At that time, the new crown had not yet broken out, and only at the age of 19, she entered an online university and began working full-time while traveling.
The term “digital nomads ” refers to people who travel freely while working remotely on the Internet.
They usually have the least material possessions. They work online using computers or smartphones in temporary homes, hotels, cafes, public libraries, shared offices or motorhomes. They often move between different countries and regions, and work as programmers, designers, writers, translators, etc.
“I can go where I want to go and do what I want in different countries.
It changed the trajectory of my life, "she told CNBC.
Pashuk, 24, has traveled to more than 20 countries in five years and is a freelance writer whose monthly income fluctuates.
“My monthly income ranges from $2,500 to $3,500 … Some months I travel as a family nanny, so I don ’ t have to pay any accommodation fees. ”
It also means that she has to plan her finances with extra care, although she can travel and work whenever she wants.
“You have to accept a little bit of unpredictability … each month looks different because you ’ re often in different regions, in different currencies, with different spending, so forecasting is a challenge, ” she says.
Extremes like “spending 600 euros last month and 3,000 euros the next month, ” Pashuk recalls.
To be a digital nomad, she says, it ’ s important to keep your finances in good shape because you have to fund the lifestyle you really want.
She shared four financial tips for being a digital hobbyist with CNBC.
Decide what kind of digital nomad you want to be
Pashuk says that what type of digital nomad you want to be will determine your situation.
The first type is people who change places frequently, going to a new place every one to two weeks.
She was in this state for almost two years at one time, but then stopped doing it because she found it was too stressful for her.
This can quickly become expensive, she said, as there is a big chance of problems with each move, such as high ticket prices, train cancellations and other extra costs.
Now she ’ s a “Slow Digital Nomad ” who stays in one place for at least a month or as long as her visa allows.
Pashuk says this helps the budget because the budget is fixed for months, and you stay in the same place and still spend the same things.
In addition, building an affordable “base camp ” can go a long way, providing some stability.
Currently, Pashuk has a “headquarters ” in Montenegro, but also works in different places:“ I still travel every month, but I have a place to come back. ”
She has to spend at least a certain amount each month, such as paying rent in Montenegro, but it has little impact on the total expenditure.
2. Use the correct debit card
When Pashuk started out as a digital nomad, having a stable and reliable cash flow was a huge challenge.
Her Canadian bank account has been locked because she is constantly changing locations, which the bank thinks is a bit suspicious.
So she was forced to call the bank all the time.
In addition, when you use a Canadian card to withdraw money from a local ATM, the offshore transaction fee is also considerable.
“Sometimes I lose $30 to $40 every time I withdraw cash, and if you have to withdraw it multiple times, you lose a lot of money. ”
Two years ago, she switched to a multi-currency debit card, which allowed her to top up and withdraw cash in the currency she wanted. Pashuk said she saved her freelance earnings into the card and took it to more than 20 countries without any problems.
29-year-old nurse earns 1.5 million a year travelling the world: seizing the opportunity of high pay and working only nine months a year
3.
Do full research.
She said that as a digital traveller, in the process of moving to a workplace, it is really important to do adequate research.
To figure out the average local prices, determine if they fit your budget, and find the average prices for Airbnb apartments, food, and other essentials.
Before going somewhere, Pashuk always makes a small table of the items needed for life.
“You never know what unknowns might creep up and steal your money. ”
For example, public transport can be prohibitively expensive in some countries. People often don ’ t think of this, Pashuk shares, because public transport is always cheap where you ’ re staying. “But I went to London and it cost a lot more than I thought, up to $20 a day. ”
Pay close attention to tax requirements
Pashuk also regularly keeps an eye on the latest tax requirements of different countries to ensure that a stay in one country is not long enough to be considered a tax resident.
"I just don't want to deal with it," she said. "Canada's taxes are enough for me."
If you ’ re considering becoming a “slow-moving digital traveller, ” Pashuk suggests studying digital traveller visas, as they typically offer tax relief — and some even complete exemption.
The more you travel, the more accurate you can predict how much you will spend, she says.
“Where you can cut costs, you have to be a little smart.
Being financially proficient is definitely a good thing in the long run and can keep you moving forward. ”

AI becomes a hotbed of crime Scammers use voice synthesis to cheat

Some criminals recently used artificial intelligence (AI) technology to deceive, pretending to be the voice of the victim to ask for help from the other party's family, and falsely claiming that they were kidnapped for ransom.
A quarter of the 7,000 people interviewed by a multinational computer software security company in nine countries, including the United States, have experienced AI voice scams, and 70% of the respondents admitted that they have no confidence in distinguishing between AI voices and real voices.
Arizona woman Jennifer DeStefano (Jennifer DeStefano) recently received a kidnapping call, the fraudster claimed to have kidnapped her 15-year-old daughter, demanding to hand over $1 million (about HK $7.84 million) in ransom, otherwise the consequences are self-defeating.
As a result of the phone call from her daughter's screams and cries for help, DeStefano was at a loss.
Fortunately, she immediately called her husband and finally confirmed that her daughter was safe and well.
The daughter's voice in the phone was only synthesized by an AI, and the police have now intervened in the investigation.
Using AI to synthesize other people ’ s voices is not difficult. Scammers can obtain a small recording and then use AI to synthesize them. It is difficult to distinguish between true and false. AI startup ElevenLabs has admitted that its voice synthesis tool can be used for “malicious purposes ” and previously used it to impersonate British actress Emma Watson to read Hitra ’ s autobiography“ My Struggle ” ".

Driven by deep learning, data processing capabilities, and improved computing resources, AI language models have made rapid progress.
The first generation of AI language models was characterized by simplistic rules-based systems that lacked the ability to understand and generate contextual information.
The development of statistical models has pushed AI language processing into the realm of generating more coherent text, but still lacks the ability to mimic human responses.
The introduction of converters, especially attention mechanisms, marks a major leap in the ability of AI language models. Vaswani et al., first proposed in their paper “Attention Is All You Need ”, the convertor model makes it possible to understand different parts of a sentence and establish better context in the text generation task.
This achievement laid the groundwork for the development of OpenAI ’ s GPT (Generative Pre-Training Translator) family of models. The GPT family has learned augmentation models, as well as considerable ability to generate human-like text, culminating in the latest version of GPT-4.
With each iteration, the GPT model was improved, lessons were learned from previous versions, datasets were expanded, and structures were strengthened.
GPT-3: Review
GPT-3, Generative Pre-trained Transformer 3, is a very advanced AI language model developed by OpenAI.
As the third iteration of the GPT series, it combines deep learning and NLP techniques to perform a wide range of tasks, including but not limited to text generation, translation, summarizing, content analysis, and answering questions. With 175 billion parameters, GPT-3 is far larger and more capable than its predecessors, making it one of the most complex AI language models available today.
The model has an autoregressive structure, which means it generates text sequentially by predicting the next word based on the previous word.
Due to its large number of parameters and extensive training data, GPT-3 can generate highly credible, contextual responses that are difficult to distinguish from text written by humans.
While GPT-3 opens up many potential use cases, from chatbot development to AI-driven content generation, it also raises concerns about possible biases in its training data, ethical considerations, and the level of computing resources required to train and deploy models.
Introduction of GPT-4
Building on the success of GPT-3, OpenAI introduced GPT-4, bringing further progress in the field of artificial intelligence language models. GPT-4 has more parameters than its predecessors, enabling it to generate more complex human-like text and excel in more NLP tasks.
Increasing the number of parameters is not the only improvement of GPT-4. OpenAI has made significant architectural improvements, including adjustments to attention mechanisms and optimization techniques, resulting in higher quality language generation and more accurate task performance.
GPT-4 can also handle more complex tasks such as code completion and demonstrate better reasoning and problem-solving capabilities.
Compared to GPT-3, GPT-4 ’ s training data has been expanded and refined to address a number of issues related to bias and data quality.
However, it must be noted that these improvements do not completely eliminate bias, and developers must be vigilant to address any bias that may be caused by the training data.
In summary, GPT-4 represents a major leap forward in AI language modeling capabilities compared to GPT-3, which improves its architecture, increases its scale and training data, and advances its contextual understanding and language generation capabilities.
GPT-3 and GPT-4: Major Differences
As AI language models continue to evolve rapidly, the differences between the previous generation ’ s GPT-3 and its successor, GPT-4, become more pronounced.
Here are the main differences between these two powerful language models:
Model Size: One of the most significant differences between GPT-3 and GPT-4 is their respective model sizes.
Compared to GPT-3, GPT-4 has more parameters, making it more capable of understanding complex contexts and generating better quality text.
• Training data: GPT-4 is trained on a larger and more diverse dataset than GPT-3.
The increase in training data enables GPT-4 to learn from a wider range of topics and styles, resulting in better generalizations and a more comprehensive understanding of the language.
• Architectural enhancements: GPT-4 benefits from improvements in its underlying architecture, such as attention mechanisms and advances in optimization techniques.
These improvements enable the model to process information more efficiently, thereby improving language generation and task performance.
• Fine-tuning capability: GPT-4 provides more advanced fine-tuning options than GPT-3, giving developers the ability to customize models for specific use cases and applications.
This leads to higher accuracy and better performance, tailored to the task at hand.
Use case: GPT-4 vs. GPT-3
GPT-3 and GPT-4 are both designed for a range of natural language processing (NLP) tasks.
Although their capabilities are similar, their performance tends to be better due to GPT-4 ’ s advanced architecture and more training data.
Here are some use cases where GPT-4 is superior to GPT-3:
• Content Generation: GPT-4 ’ s improved language generation capabilities lead to higher quality content and a better understanding of context and tone.
This makes the model more suitable for generating copies of articles, blog posts, and ads that require human-like creativity and relevance.
• Translation: GPT-4 ’ s larger training dataset means it has been exposed to more languages, giving it an advantage in translation tasks.
The model can effectively deal with complex idiom expressions and nuances of multiple languages and provide more accurate translation.
• Inductive summarization: GPT-4 ’ s advancements make it better suited to summarizing text because it has a more thorough understanding of context and can extract the most relevant information while maintaining coherence.
• Chatbot development: GPT-4 is very effective in creating natural, conversational chatbots that engage users in a more human-like interaction.
The model can accurately understand the user ’ s input and generate contextual responses, resulting in a more satisfying user experience.
Code generation: GPT-4 ’ s ability to understand context is enhanced, making it more suitable for generating source code by understanding human-readable queries and translating them into well-structured programming language syntax

This approach enables businesses to innovate faster and create better solutions to adapt to the changing industry landscape.
Challenges and considerations
While both GPT-4 and GPT-3 bring many benefits, they also bring a variety of challenges and considerations that users should take note of.
These include ethical considerations, computational resource requirements, and bias in training data.
Ethical considerations
As AI language models become more advanced, they raise ethical questions such as how to use these technologies responsibly and the possibility of malicious use.
Both GPT-3 and GPT-4 can produce very convincing text, which can be used for false information, fraud, or any number of nefarious purposes.
Developing guidelines and mechanisms to ensure that these robust AI models are used responsibly and ethically is critical.
Calculated resources

The Future of Artificial Intelligence Language Models

Drug lord avocado rises in Mexico, superfood wreaks ecological havoc
(Photo by Pixabay _ tookapic)
As a superfood, avocado has gained a lot of attention in recent years, and many cafes and restaurants have taken advantage of this trend, launching avocado meals and beverages. However, as the demand for avocado has increased, the cultivation of agricultural land has also expanded, which has caused ecological havoc in Mexico, the country of origin, and the rise of "avocado criminal organizations."
Avocado is native to Central America, Mexico and Peru, with Mexico ’ s largest producing region located in the southern state of Michoacán, producing 70% of the country ’ s avocado, and the neighboring state of Jalisco, producing about 11% of the country ’ s avocado. As demand for avocado grows, the cultivation of avocado spreads to other states, including Colima. and Chiapas.
However, this wave of expansion of the avocado garden has not been carefully evaluated, but under the guidance of local criminal organizations, with almost brutal methods of deforestation, the local preservation of the original forest has been completely destroyed.
According to the conservation news website Mongabay, one tree in Jalisco is illegally cut down every 75 seconds to be converted into a casserole garden, with around 1,100 trees disappearing every day.
The study found that in 2010, Jalisco ’ s avocado garden was about 0.84 million hectares, but by 2021, it has reached 27.8 million hectares, more than tripled, and nearly half of the state ’ s 56,000 hectares of agricultural land has been used to grow avocado; and correspondingly, deforestation has accelerated since 2019, at least 0.51 million hectares of woodland has become avocado, resulting in pristine acorn. A large number of forests and evergreen forests have disappeared.
Under the avocado craze, criminal organizations also sniffed business opportunities, and the notorious Mexican drug lord Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes extended his reach into the field, and his Jalisco New Generation Cartel acquired the land of local residents and transplanted the avocado to obtain huge amounts. Profit.
Locals point out that not only private land, but also protected woodlands that require official permission to convert to other crops, and that even if people report to the government that these organizations have substantial control over these areas, they end up sinking into the sea, with the result of course more virgin forest areas being destroyed.
In addition, compared to the original forest, planting avocado requires a lot of water, so after the new avocado garden is planted, it is necessary to build a large water storage tank to reserve irrigation water, which reduces the function of rainwater infiltration and local water collection.
Mexico is not a country with abundant water resources. As the number of avocado trees continues to increase, it will undoubtedly worsen the local water shortage and exacerbate political tensions.
On the other hand, there are also locals who try to coexist with the original ecology and introduce more eco-friendly avocados.
Javier Magaña Cárdenas, a avocado farmer who has long maintained the forest and helped restore the trees, said the authorities should establish a system to help identify and verify the provenance of avocados and ensure that illegal avocados are eliminated by consumers.
Already, many smallholder farmers have partnered with the Rainforest Alliance, a non-governmental organization, and around 1,500 hectares of avocado gardens in Jalisco have been certified for sustainable agriculture.
Sergio Graf Montero, head of the Jalisco Ministry of Environment and Territorial Development (SEMADET), said that as long as the demand for non-destructive avocados in the market rises, farmers will naturally choose such methods, and it is still consumers who determine the future of the ecology.

Modi ’ s visit to the United States: Is the fighter engine technology a “stepping over ” gift from Biden to Modi?
Author: MIAO Yongqi
Published: Updated:
In an interview with the Wall Street Journal ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’ s first state visit to the United States in nine years, he described the level of mutual trust between the leaders of the United States and India as “an important pillar of the partnership ”.
Indian media also described the United States as India ’ s most important military and economic partner, and India-US relations have officially ushered in a new stage.
Deepening India-US defense industry cooperation and sharing high technology are the focus of Modi ’ s visit.
Modi ’ s visit comes at a time when, in addition to the honeymoon period of India-US relations, defense cooperation, including arms deals, is the focus of his visit.
Modi is expected to sign a historic defense agreement with the White House in Washington this week. National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan is said to be the driving force behind the U.S.-India defense cooperation, and Indian Defense Secretary Rajnath Singh and U.S. Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin discussed the cooperation plan before the beginning of this month.
Defense cooperation is expected to have three major outcomes:
First, the two sides will facilitate a $3 billion order for India to purchase 31 MQ-9B drones from the United States, which are expected to be used for aerial reconnaissance over the Indian Ocean and the India-China border in the Himalayas, and India will become the first non-US treaty ally to purchase this type of armed attack drone, but it has been reported that the purchase will be reduced to 18 to 24.;
Second, General Electric (GE) and Hindustan Airlines (HAL) produce the GE-F414 light fighter engine in India, which is used by the Indian light fighter "Tejas" Mk2.
Third, the United States will sell 26 F-16s to the Indian Navy.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to finalize a $300 million purchase deal with Biden for the MQ-9B Predator drone.
Although the defense cooperation plan between the United States and India has been talked about for many years, it has not been meaningful until recently.
As early as 2005, the two countries have signed a framework for defense cooperation; in June 2010, when US President Barack Obama stressed the "return to Asia", he opened the US-India strategic dialogue, saying that US-India relations are "indispensable in the process of building the 21st century."
In July 2018, the United States relaxed export restrictions on the sale of high-tech products to India and designated New Delhi as a Strategic Trade Authorization Level 1 (SDA1) country, which also makes India the only South Asian country among the most important U.S. allies. In September 2018, India and the United States signed the Communications Compatibility and Security Agreement (COMCASA), which allows India to acquire cutting-edge and advanced technology from the United States while buying high-end U.S. defense equipment.
As of 2019, India is eligible for funding from the U.S. Department of Defense ’ s Maritime Security Initiative.
In the past decade, the strategic cooperation between the two countries has been considered more symbolic than practical, but the new US-India defense cooperation roadmap is considered significant, and the production of high-tech fighter engines in India and increased technical cooperation are a major focus of Indian military production.
While the United States wants India to counterbalance China in the region, it also wants New Delhi to reduce its dependence on imported Russian-made weapons.
India, the world ’ s largest arms importer, relies on Russia for nearly half of its military supplies, including tanks, jet fighters, S-400 air defense systems and ammunition, but procurement has become increasingly diversified in recent years, including the United States, Israel and France.
Perhaps the outbreak of the war in Ukraine has made Washington even more urgent, taking the opportunity to coax India into changing its long-standing military cooperation with Russia.
An Indian version of the F414-GE-100 engine used to power the Boeing F / A-18E / F Super Hornet.
High-quality technology transfer
The U.S. Embassy in New Delhi said in a statement that the agreement aims to change the “paradigm ” of defense cooperation between the two countries and will“ rapidly advance technical cooperation and joint production in the areas of air combat and land mobile systems, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, ammunition and seabed. ”
Therefore, of the three cooperation agreements mentioned above, the one related to fighter engine manufacturing has received the most attention in India, as it involves the sharing of key technologies between US companies and Indian state-owned enterprises.
These technologies are protected by intellectual property rights and the production process is the highest state secret, and the United States has never shared such a degree of core technology with other countries.
This would make India one of the few countries in the world to localize aircraft engine production.
“It ’ s not just India ’ s manufacturing sector, it ’ s a real technology transfer, ” said Rudra Chaudhuri, head of Carnegie India, a think-tank based in New Delhi.
The GE-F414, produced by General Electric, is currently supplied to light aircraft in eight countries.
This includes India ’ s Tejas Mark 2 single-engine supersonic multirole fighter, which is expected to enter service in 2026.
(GE Aerospace)
This is undoubtedly a great gift to the Modi government and a testament to the sincerity of the Biden administration towards India.
According to official sources in India, 80% of the technology of fighter engine manufacturing will be transferred to HAL, and India will have access to at least 11 major production technologies, including special coating for melting and heating, processing and coating of single-crystal turbine blades, processing and coating of nozzle blades and end parts, and overall blade processing.
With these technologies, it will be possible for India to achieve the production of high-thrust engines and eliminate some key technical barriers, and the transfer of these technologies will occur in the next two to three years, the sources said.
Aparna Pande, director of advocacy at the Hudson Institute in India, said: “It is the India-Russia partnership that has traditionally kept the United States on the lookout for a closer defence relationship with India. ”
“If India approaches because of a lack of supply of spare parts, problem equipment, or Russia ’ s relationship with China, then (you can) convince India to buy more from the United States and its allies, it ’ s an opportunity. ”

El Niño could drive up food prices
A new El Niño weather phenomenon has arrived, which will bring floods to some parts of the world and drought to others.
Such destructive weather phenomena in the past have caused trillions of dollars in damage to the global economy and triggered inflation.
Tropical Storm in Mumbai, India (June 2023)
The El Niño phenomenon is a natural phenomenon that changes global weather patterns.
A comeback after four years could exacerbate already high food inflation.
Last week, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) Climate Prediction Center said El Niño is already present and is expected to "gradually strengthen" over the next six to nine months, bringing new periods of extreme weather to much of the world.
"The likelihood of a strong El Niño happening again is quite high."
Harald Kunstmann, a professor at the Institute of Meteorology and Climate Research (IMK-IFU) at Karlsruhe University of Technology in Germany, said: "If this happens, it can be expected that there will be extremes and anomalies that are usually associated with this phenomenon."
El Niño, named after the Spanish El Niño (boy), is a phenomenon in which the waters of the eastern Pacific Ocean warms abnormally every few years.
It has contributed to flooding in the Americas, tropical storms in the Pacific and drought in many parts of the world, including southern Africa.
These natural disasters wreak havoc on fisheries, agriculture and other sectors of the economy, and also exacerbate the effects of climate change.In 2016, El Niño caused the hottest year on record, and scientists fear it could cause global temperatures to hit new highs
El Niño brings flooding to some areas
Earlier this month, researchers at the European Union ’ s Copernicus Climate Change Service Center found that global surface temperatures rose 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels for the first time, the limit for future warming agreed by countries at the 2015 Paris climate summit.
"The 1.5 ° C warming in June is no small feat."
"We may soon cross that threshold, not only for a few weeks, but for a longer period of time," Kunstmann told Deutsche Welle.
El Niño has caused huge economic losses.
Even after the most extreme weather has passed, the economic impact of the El Niño season tends to persist.
According to research by Dartmouth College in the United States, the economic impact lasted for five years following the 1982-83 El Niño event, with total losses amounting to about $4.1 trillion (3.7 trillion euros).
In a paper published in the US journal Science, researchers said that the loss of global economic growth after the 1997-98 El Niño season amounted to $5.7 trillion.
Christopher Callahan, a doctoral student in the Ecosystem and Society Program at Dartmouth College, said: "We can say with certainty that there will never be a quick recovery after a social and economic hit," adding that growth could be affected for as long as 14 years after El Niño, and possibly even longer.
Researchers at Dartmouth College found that El Niño events in 1982-83 and 1997-98 caused the U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) to fall by about 3 percent in 1988 and 2003.
In countries such as Peru and Indonesia, where agriculture accounts for 15 per cent of GDP, GDP fell by more than 10 per cent in 2003.
Dartmouth researchers estimate that the negative economic impact of the latest El Niño season could reach $3 trillion between now and 2029.
"The economic impact is first and foremost the fishing industry, which has suffered greatly as a result of rising ocean temperatures."
Künstmann told Deutsche Welle, "Then it will hit large agricultural areas in Africa, South America and even several parts of North America."
Next, if the harvest is not good and the infrastructure is damaged by the storm, the insurance industry will also be affected. "
Food and energy prices could rise sharply
Models released this week by Bloomberg Economic Research found that previous El Niño events led to nearly 4 percentage points higher prices for non-energy commodities and 3.5 percentage points higher prices for oil, weakening global food security.
As a result, inflation in Argentina and Brazil was about 0.75 percentage points higher, and in the Philippines and India it was half a percentage point higher, Bloomberg found.
Fearing that this El Niño could be the warmest and costliest on record, analysts believe it also has the potential to prolong food inflation.
The post-Covid-19 peak may be over, but it could take years to return to the 2% inflation target set by the United States and the European Central Bank.
Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest private lender, said in a research note last week that growing warnings about El Niño had led to steep increases in coffee, sugar and cocoa prices in recent weeks.
Other food prices are expected to follow as the harvest is affected by bad weather.
"(Price increases) could have a particularly negative impact on emerging markets."
In emerging markets, food typically accounts for at least a third of consumer spending.
They are also geographically more vulnerable to climate change, such as floods, and El Niño increases that possibility, "Deutsche Bank analysts wrote.
In India, agriculture is the cornerstone of the economy and the annual monsoon is critical to food production.
Reserve Bank of India governor Shaktikanta Das recently said: "Close and sustained attention... is absolutely necessary, especially as the monsoon expectations and the impact of El Niño remain uncertain."

Xu Jiansheng: Quantum technology is the future of the digital economy is the present
[Ming Pao News] Five or six years ago, a senior invited the author to participate in the event to introduce the development of quantum technology in Hong Kong by the university. It was indeed an eye-opener and a lot of learning, and then I realized that Hong Kong also has the ability to develop quantum technology.
However, after many years, quantum technology is still in development and has not been officially commercialized.
So what are quantum technology and quantum computers?
Quantum technology uses the principles of quantum mechanics to link matter and energy levels to create some very strange, very powerful phenomena and applications.
One of the most common is the quantum computer.
A quantum computer is a computer that uses qubits to perform calculations.
Unlike traditional binary (0 to 1) bits, qubits can be in multiple states at the same time, and operations such as quantum interference and quantum cascade can be performed during the calculation process, enabling quantum computers to deal with more complex problems than traditional computers in an instant.
In specific computing models, the computing power of quantum computers is millions or even billions of times faster than current supercomputers.
Quantum computers have a wide range of applications, such as in the fields of chemistry, materials science, financial risk assessment, artificial intelligence, etc.
The impact of quantum computing on the development of artificial intelligence will be exciting, but it can also be risky.
Quantum computing can accelerate the training of AI models to improve the efficiency of algorithms such as natural language processing, image recognition, and more.
In addition, quantum computing is able to handle more complex tasks, better understand context, and provide more accurate and reliable responses.
Applications of this capability are very wide, such as deep learning and natural language generation that can be used for chatbots.
Quantum computing can be used for data verification and accuracy checking.
Its exponential computing speed can filter large amounts of data to confirm and verify the accuracy of information, a level that AI chatbots cannot achieve.
Quantum Computing and Artificial Intelligence Potential Data Risk
There are also potential risks associated with the combination of quantum computing and artificial intelligence, especially threats to data security.
In theory, quantum computers are capable of cracking current encryption methods, which could endanger the security of encrypted data, communication and transactions in various industries, which poses a risk parameter for its future development.
In addition, the emergence of quantum computing may also accelerate the rapid development of artificial intelligence chatbots, because the raw computing power of quantum computers can make the new generation of artificial intelligence systems superior in terms of speed, efficiency and the ability to verify information, which will mark the beginning of a new era of artificial intelligence.
Examples of the combination of quantum computing and artificial intelligence:
Case 1: Quantum computing in artificial intelligence chatbots.
Quantum computing can improve the experience of human-machine conversations by improving the efficiency and accuracy of chatbots.
For example, Microsoft ’ s Q # language could be used to develop a quantum chatbot that can understand natural language for intelligent conversations.
In addition, the UK quantum computing company Cambridge Quantum Computing (CQC) has also developed a chatbot based on quantum computing that can be learned through dialogue and provide a better experience.
Case 2: The application of quantum computing in the medical field.
Quantum computing can process large amounts of data and provide more accurate and reliable analysis results.
For example, D-Wave Systems in Canada partnered with quantum computing company 1QBit to develop a cancer diagnostic tool based on quantum computing.
This tool can analyze large amounts of medical imaging and medical data to provide more accurate diagnostic results and help doctors develop better treatment options.
There must be sufficient resources to cultivate the Web 3.0 industry
Quantum technology is still in its infancy, and experts estimate it will take 10 to 20 years for it to reach commercialization.
In this year ’ s Budget, “Treasurer ” Chen Maobo has earmarked $3 billion for the development of quantum technology and artificial intelligence. The author is of course pleased that the Government has given sufficient resources to support the development of cutting-edge technology.
However, compared with only $50 million for the Cyberport to promote one of the most promising Web3.0 industries to drive the development of the local economy, it is slightly inferior.
In order to cultivate a healthy Web 3.0 industry development soil, we must have sufficient resources to do a good job of user education, lay a good market foundation, in order to more effectively achieve commercialization and popularization.

A major breakthrough in the development of reliable quantum computers
June 26, 2023 09: 24 | Source: Science and Technology Daily
Small number
BEIJING, June 25 (Xinhua) -- A team of researchers from the quantum division of Microsoft Corporation in the United States has made the first milestone breakthrough in creating a reliable and practical quantum computer.
In a recent paper published in the journal Physical Review B, the team describes this milestone breakthrough and their plan to build a reliable quantum computer over the next 25 years.
For a quantum supercomputer to be able to solve not only problems that classical computers cannot solve, but also to scale to solve the most complex problems facing the world today, it must be both high performance and reliable.
The research team has devised a new way to represent logical qubits with hardware stability.
It is reported that the device can induce the type of fermions, a phase of matter characterized by the zero mode of Majorana.
The research team also reports that these devices have shown low enough disorder to demonstrate that the technique is feasible through topological gap protocols.
Microsoft said in its announcement that it has created a new metric to measure the performance of quantum supercomputers — reliable quantum operands per second (rQOPS).
This number describes how many reliable operations a computer can perform in a second, and it takes into account the performance of the entire system, not just the performance of the qubits, so it ensures the correct operation of the algorithm.
Research shows that the first quantum supercomputer requires at least 1 million rQOPS and will scale to more than 1 billion to solve impactful chemical and material science problems.
Christa Wall, Microsoft ’ s vice president of advanced quantum technology development, said that within 10 years, the final part of the company ’ s quantum computing roadmap, which is to build a quantum supercomputer, will be reached.

Central News Agency
(Central News Agency reporter Zhang Shuling Shanghai 3) Chinese state media disclosed that there have been a number of AI (artificial intelligence) fraud incidents, using "face change" and sound technology to impersonate government personnel to deceive, should be highly vigilant.
This is an advertisement, please continue reading.
Xinhua News Agency's Watchful News Weekly WeChat public number issued today, saying that the police in the northern province recently released a case of "political fraud" using "AI to change faces".
The impersonation of the culprit was made by a leading cadre known to the victim.
The swindler after the "face change" suggested in the WeChat video call that his friend had a project deposit that needed to be borrowed from the public account of the victim's company.
In just over 10 minutes of communication, the victim transferred millions of yuan.
This video screen through the "face change" of the AI deceiver facial expression is natural, the voice is realistic, so the victim relaxed their vigilance, and then called to confirm after the transfer, only to know that they were cheated.
The report pointed out that some leading cadres have a relatively high probability of going to television for work reasons, which provides a wealth of facial recognition material for illegal people; in TV and radio news, many sound data of some leading cadres can also be found, which makes the "fake cost" lower.
"You only need to extract at least 10 words and at most 32 words to synthesize the sound," said Zhao Mingming, an expert in security research at the National Internet Information and Communication Industry Group.
The Tianjin Daily reported today that Zhang Xiankun, deputy dean of the School of Artificial Intelligence at Tianjin University of Science and Technology, said that "AI face changing mimicry" is not a new technology, but with the continuous development and improvement of artificial intelligence technology, especially the improvement of computer computing power, the "face changing" effect is more realistic and has been widely used in the fields of film, television, advertising and games.
The report pointed out that China's "Civil Code" and "Personal Information Protection Law" promulgated in 2020 and 2021 respectively provide for biometric information.
The “Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Applicable Law for the Trial of Civil Cases Related to the Use of Facial Recognition Technology for Handling Personal Information ” issued by the Supreme People ’ s Court in 2021, and the“ Provisions on Deep Synthesis Management of Internet Information Services ” jointly issued by various departments in December 2022 have also been further regulated.
However, Professor Jiao Yanling of the School of Law of Tianjin Normal University believes that there are so many legal provisions that the use of AI to change faces to illegal situations is still repeated, "reflecting that the core problem is not at the legislative level, but in the implementation of the law and the awareness of citizens", and it is necessary to increase the prevention and supervision of illegal acts.
Zhang Xiankun believes that although AI face modification can now be done with fake real, but "fake is fake", through the computer can still be identified, the future should soon appear a variety of "AI face" pictures or video applications.

The leaders of the three powers convened a virtual summit via video on Tuesday in an attempt to reshape the U.S.-led global order.
But apart from the unity implied by their common appearance, each seemed to focus on their own different goals.
For Russian President Vladimir Putin, that meant showing strength after the Wagner mercenary mutiny and claiming international support for his war in Ukraine.
For China's top leader, Xi Jinping, the summit is another opportunity to attack the United States by calling for an end to "hegemonism" and "power politics."
For Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the host of the meeting, it was a sign of India ’ s growing stature – and an insinuating attack on its main rival, Pakistan, by calling on other countries to unite to “fight terrorism. ”
Advertisement
In the speeches of the leaders prepared in advance of the annual meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, no significant statements were made about the changes in the alliance.
But this forum – established in 2001 by China and Russia, with Pakistan and the Central Asian countries of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan – does allow us to see how a regional club set up to counter Western influence deals with conflicting priorities.
There is no mention of the growing friction between Beijing and New Delhi that has pushed historically non-aligned India closer to the United States.
If Putin wants other leaders to deliver loud statements of support to ease his weakened position at home and justify his war in Ukraine, he can only be content with conventional rhetoric and a wintry tone.
What ’ s more, under the watchful eye of the Biden administration and many other countries around the world, the forum essentially seems to be stating that the three leaders have taken control of their own domestic issues and are ready to embrace what Putin calls a new “multipolar ” world.
“They all have a motive to downplay things and make everything seem normal, ” said Chong Ka-ying, an associate professor of political science at the National University of Singapore.“ They show that things are under control, there are no cracks, and India wants to explore relations with the United States despite Russia ’ s problems. ”
On Tuesday, no leader needed to reshape his image more than Putin.
Last month, Wagner mercenaries tried to overthrow Russia ’ s military leadership, and Putin ’ s more than two decades of rule faced the biggest challenge.
Advertisement
While Putin defused the crisis by agreeing with mercenary leader Prigozhin to travel to Belarus, the brief rebellion raised questions about his authority and future.
It was Putin ’ s first appearance at an international forum since the rebellion, and he thanked member states for their support after the mutiny, which he claimed did not have popular support in Russia.
"A profound responsibility for the fate of the motherland unites Russian politics and society as a whole, showing a united front against armed mutiny," Putin said, also seeking to use the summit as a sign of international support for his invasion of Ukraine.
Support from China is most important, and it is the only major power to provide diplomatic and economic cover for Russia.
China has done so because it has made a long-term bet on Putin as a necessary partner to challenge the United States.
The bet comes at a cost, however, as Beijing struggles to repair relations with Europe ’ s main economic partners.
China ’ s refusal to condemn the war in Ukraine has also drawn growing global attention to Beijing ’ s aggressive stance on Taiwan.
The virtual meeting provided Xi with an opportunity to advance China ’ s goal of wresting influence from the United States.
He hailed the SCO as a way to “improve global governance ” and promote“ Chinese-style modernization ” — a veiled expression of a world vision in which Beijing and its partners have a greater say in international rules and norms.
In this vision, India ’ s positioning remains to be seen.
India, China ’ s biggest emerging strategic rival, joined the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in 2017 and sees the forum as a way to balance its own relations with the West as well as with China and Russia.
India has maintained stable relations with Russia, mainly economic, after refusing to condemn the invasion of Ukraine.
But its relationship with China has deteriorated due to border disputes and its participation in the quadripartite security dialogue mechanism, including the United States, which focuses on security and which Beijing views as a tool to contain China.
Modi's high-profile visit to Washington last month heightened suspicions in China that India is pulling closer to the United States to contain China's rise.
Advertisement
Despite these tensions, India has a sweet spot in the forum.
Its dependence on the Central Asian countries for energy and maintaining its influence in Afghanistan could have spillover effects on Pakistan.
Modi praised the forum as an "important platform" for peace and prosperity, but urged the group to condemn countries that "use terrorism as a tool of their policies."
The remarks were directed at Pakistan, which India accuses of funding militants in the disputed Kashmir region.
“India will not abandon or withdraw from the SCO because it will lose its foothold in Central Asia and cede the Eurasian region to India ’ s main rival, China, ” said Sriram Chorya, dean of the School of International Affairs at Jindal Global University near New Delhi.

The news of China's control of gallium and germanium exports has caused widespread concern in the German media.
The move was seen as retaliation against Washington.
The Berlin Daily said that the West could use this opportunity to further reduce its dependence on Chinese raw materials.
The new Zurich newspaper pointed out that it may be difficult to find suppliers to replace China in the short term.
China's move to regulate gallium germanium exports is seen as retaliation against Washington, which imposed a ban on chip exports.
"The next round of the US-China trade dispute has begun.
Beijing announced export restrictions on the rare metals gallium and germanium on Monday evening, "an article in the Berliner Zeitung newspaper began Tuesday (July 4).
The move is seen as retaliation against Washington, which has imposed a ban on chip exports.
China's Ministry of Commerce announced export controls on gallium and germanium related items needed to manufacture high-performance chips.
The purpose is to protect national security.
The controls will be in place from August 1.
The article pointed out that these two metal minerals are widely used in semiconductor materials, electric vehicles and other fields, and can also be used for military purposes.
Author Simon Zeise wrote: “At present, many electronic devices, such as mobile phones, are produced in China: do the Chinese want to further expand their dominance here? ” The article argues that the West can use this opportunity to further reduce its dependence on Chinese raw materials:“ If Beijing uses these new regulations to limit supply to other countries, prices may rise, then it will be more economical to mine rare metals elsewhere. ”
For example, China ’ s previous restrictions on rare earth exports have reduced the country ’ s market share.
Many countries around the world, including Germany, are trying to diversify their raw material supplies to reduce dependence on China.
According to the Confederation of German Industry (BDI), Beijing ’ s export controls highlight the urgency of Europe and Germany to “rapidly reduce ” their dependence on key raw materials.
Therefore, intra-European exploitation must be developed.
Beijing ’ s latest export rules for rare metals are not the first time China has imposed an export ban: “China imposed export restrictions on rare earths for the first time in the 1990s. ”
This has put pressure on Japanese companies that are highly dependent on Chinese supplies.
Things changed in 2010, when China suspended exports of rare earths to Japan in response to a collision between a Chinese fishing boat and the Japanese Coast Guard near islands claimed by both sides.
The incident sparked a race to find an alternative to Chinese supply.
Subsequent increases in production in Australia and the United States have resulted in China ’ s share of global mineral production falling from a peak of 98 per cent in 2010 to 70 per cent in 2022. ”
"Bloomberg notes that China currently accounts for about 94 per cent of global gallium production," the article entitled "German Economic Alert: Why China Restricts Exports of Rare Metals?" reads: "Bloomberg notes that China currently accounts for about 94 per cent of global gallium production.
Nevertheless, these metals are not particularly rare or difficult to obtain.
But so far, the Chinese government has made production costs cheaper than other countries through subsidies.
Interview: It is time for the United States to show its willingness to engage in dialogue
An article published on Tuesday in Switzerland ’ s New Zurich newspaper pointed out that for years, China has threatened that it could use certain materials as leverage.
Now, that moment may have arrived.
The article titled “Don ’ t say we didn ’ t warn you! ”: China fights back against chip sanctions with rare earth export controls (« Sagen Sie nicht, wir hätten Sie nicht gewarnt! »: China kontert Chip-Sanktionen mit Exportkontrollen für seltene Erden) reads:“ China ’ s gallium, germanium Material ’ s biggest customers include three countries that have imposed chip sanctions on Beijing, the United States, the Netherlands and Japan.

Matthias Sander, the paper ’ s China correspondent, wrote: “The United States imposed export controls on chips using gallium oxide in 2022.

Russia and Ukraine may be able to replace Chinese suppliers, however: "Gallium and germanium are not really scarce, but China is almost the only country in recent years to continue to use subsidies to strategically expand production and exports."
Therefore, it may be difficult to replace suppliers in the short term, especially in view of factors such as the Russian-Ukrainian war.
