More than 300 people change their name to eat enough … your favorite salmon is abused and pollutes the sea? Netflix "Ocean Conspiracy" exposed to the black screen
In the past, more than 300 people in Taiwan changed their name after turning around the famous sushi restaurant “Sushi Lang ” to launch the“ Free Salmon to Eat ” campaign, setting off a “salmon chaos ” in society, showing the people ’ s love for salmon.
With Netflix ’ s new ecological crisis documentary “Seaspiracy ”, which exposes the problems of antibiotics released by“ sea captive salmon ” and fears of pollution, as well as millions of salmon crammed in underwater cages, mercilessly attacked by fish lice, and violating the nature of wild migration, people can ’ t help but look at the issue of animal persecution. It has been proven to sense pain.
What are the cruelties hidden in the world-famous seafood “farmed salmon ”?
How can fish welfare be improved?
More than 300 people changed their name to "salmon" to eat! The salmon that Taiwanese love to eat is not wild at all.
As with many livestock farms on the land, salmon is of high economic value, so many aquaculture operators around the world use sea box nets to trap and breed salmon in captivity, and regularly feed them to pipelines in order to obtain huge "salmon gold" business opportunities.
If you look at Taiwan from a perspective, according to the statistics of customs imports and exports in 2020, the weight of locally imported “captive salmon ” alone is as high as 18,000 tons, with a total value of about NT $5.15 billion.
On the other hand, even if the world is hit by the epidemic in 2020, Norway, the world ’ s largest exporter of salmon, not only will the production of salmon still reach 1.1 million tons, but the export volume will also reach a record second high.
But with the release of Netflix ’ s new marine crisis documentary “Seaspiracy ” in 2023, the blood-soaked disclosure of the sea farming salmon behind the following three unknown dark sides, finally let the terrible“ salmon hell ” shake the world.
1.
High-density farmed salmon have nowhere to escape! Scales and fins are mercilessly devoured by sea lice parasites
Compared to free wild salmon, captive salmon are likely to be crowded together by the fish, constantly colliding, friction, conflict, and nowhere to hide, resulting in scales, kisses, and fins are broken, infectious anemia, spinal deformities and other symptoms, and are more likely to be parasitized by sea lice.
For example, a survey by the global animal lobby welfare organization Compassion in World Farming found that floating dead fish can be found everywhere in crowded salmon farms, and such a harsh living environment is simply a hotbed for the spread of disease.
What is even more frightening is that once the salmon is entangled in sea lice, the scales, skin tissue, surface mucus and blood on the body will soon become food for the parasites.
As the scales of the salmon gradually disappear, in addition to the pain of the body beginning to erode, the pain of infection in the wound or loss of immunity can also plunge them into the abyss of death.
For example, in the clip of "The Ocean Conspiracy", it directly captures the horror of the salmon being eaten alive by a parasite to the eyes, the limbs, and the body.
2.
Marine farmed salmon put into chemicals, antibiotics! Marine pollution affects ecological food chain
In order to solve the salmon nightmare, farmers have to put a lot of irritating chemicals and antibiotics into the box to remove sea lice and reduce the risk of disease in high-density breeding, or to increase the water temperature and try to kill sea lice.
But the pumps and containers used by the former to transport chemicals have undoubtedly made the salmon's sea cages smaller and tighter, while the temperature of the latter has already exceeded the range that the salmon can adapt to, and each of them has brought great pain to the salmon.
At the same time, antibiotics and pesticides flowing into the sea will of course lead to pollution of the surrounding environment, and the organic waste generated by captive salmon will also seriously affect the entire bottom ecology.
In April 2023, the environmental group Greenpeace accused Chile ’ s salmon farming industry of dumping sewage into the ocean, killing more than 5,000 tons of salmon from oxidation.
3.
Undersea cages violate the migratory nature of wild salmon! Millions of animals are ignored
Not only that, Scotland, the world ’ s third largest Atlantic salmon farming exporter, which supplies about 10% of Taiwan ’ s salmon imports each year, has also been raised by the farm animal protection group Compassion in World Farming (CIWF) at the end of 2020, pointing directly to the 22 farms of the local five largest salmon farming companies, and raising millions of salmon in the sea bottom in one breath, completely depriving them of their migratory nature.
Because the migratory nature of salmon has always been a mystery in the animal world, some studies have suggested that salmon can always find the "origin" by remembering the special smell of their birthplace, or by being guided by the magnetic fields of the Sun and Earth.
Regardless of the truth, the physiological structure of salmon is obviously sensitive to sensing the environment, judging the location, and even evading electric shocks in real time.
Therefore, allowing them to roam aimlessly in the box for many years is a kind of cruelty to the body and spirit, depriving the fish instinct of long-distance migration.
All the unhealthy salmon raised in captivity are eaten by humans!
Food chain security in jeopardy
In other words, the three major concerns of captive salmon at sea have caused more than 25% of Scotland ’ s fish populations to suffer and die before they are slaughtered, resulting in a huge waste of food and a complete disregard for animal welfare.
In addition, countless dead fish have been dumped directly in open barrels by Scottish farmers, allowing wild birds and other wildlife to come into contact for food, potentially endangering the safety of other ecological chains.
Salmon farming on land is more humane to the earth! Salmon business opportunities and marine conservation to create food sustainability
Fortunately, this traditional salmon farming method is expected to gradually come to an end.
Because the international company Atlantic Sapphire has been developing "land salmon farm" for 10 years, and in 2022, it invested nearly 4 billion US dollars (about 112 billion US dollars) to build the world's largest land salmon farm Bluehouse in Florida, the United States.
The biggest feature of the land salmon farm is the use of the Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS) to effectively control the temperature, salinity, pH and oxygen content of the water body, and effectively eliminate carbon dioxide and filter waste, to ensure that the salmon are free from parasites and diseases, while reducing the possibility of marine pollution.
Johan Andreassen, CEO of Atlantic Sapphire: “Ten years ago no one believed that farming salmon on land was financially viable; now Atlantic Sapphire is finally proving that it works, so the question now is how much competition there will be and how much scale there will be in this industry. ”
In order to prove that land-based salmon farming will eventually become a trend in the marine industry, Atlantic Sapphire CEO Johan Andreassen is also looking further into the future, with an estimated 372,000 square meters of fish tanks on about 650,000 square meters of land by 2031, allowing land-based salmon to meet 41% of the annual salmon consumption in the United States.
Also thanks to Atlantic Sapphire, one of the world ’ s largest salmon producers, Norwegian company Grieg Seafood has entered into a joint venture with Årdal Aqua to build a 5,000-tonne annual land farm there.
Salmon Evolution, also from Norway, joined forces with Dongwon Industries, South Korea ’ s largest seafood company, in 2023 to expand its “salmon footprint ” to South Korea.
At the same time, Benchmark Genetics, an aquaculture company that has always strictly controlled the quality of salmon eggs, now sells up to 10% of its salmon eggs to the land-based farming industry to improve the yield and quality of “land-based captive salmon. ”
People from all walks of life, through their own efforts, hope to work for the welfare of salmon, no longer be poisoned by the lust of human words, even if they reproduce artificially, they can also maintain their physical and mental health, and achieve the true meaning of "sustainable food" on earth.

Save coral debris repair by 3D printing citizens to book a visit to Ocean Park

Climate warming, marine pollution, severe coral bleaching.
Ocean Park and others launched “Coral Rejuvenation Action ” to save coral fragments in Hong Kong waters and then use the world ’ s first 3D printed terracotta coral reef plate technology to repair. The first batch of 7.5 square meters of coral reef plates has been transplanted to Ironing Bo Chau, and more than 120 pieces of coral debris are being raised in the“ Activated Coral Center ” in the park.
The "Activating Coral Centre" was officially opened to promote community participation in coral conservation and learning about coral ecology.
In September last year, Sino Group and the Hong Kong Innovation Fund, together with Archireef, Ocean Park Hong Kong and The Fullerton Ocean Park Hotel, launched a coral conservation programme aimed at reconstructing 20 square metres of coral reefs in the southern waters of Hong Kong in the next three years.
The operation first collected debris from the larger coral population from the Eastern Sea area and transferred it to the University of Hong Kong to split and breed more corals. It was then sent to the Ocean Park Activated Coral Centre for culture and rehabilitation of branched corals, including rose corals, coastal corals, flatbrain corals and antler corals.
After cultivation and restoration, the coral fragments are placed on a 3D-printed coral reef plate for attachment growth and then moved to the seafloor of Ironing Island.
The first 7.5-square-meter reef was moved into the sea in May. David M. Baker, co-founder of Archireef, said that within the first year after the transplant, he hopes to achieve a 95% survival rate and a 50% growth rate.
Sino Group ’ s Assistant General Manager of Sustainable Development, Ms KK Kwok, said she hoped to promote the importance of coral conservation through the programme.
The Activating Coral Centre, which helps aquaculture, is also open to the public this month and will provide guided tours, interactive STEAM experiences and other educational activities, such as understanding coral food with a microscope, understanding the impact of microplastics and the threats to coral growth.
Fullerton Ocean Park Hotel Hong Kong provides in-centre snorkeling experience and conservation workshops for guests to participate in.
Guided tours are offered on Saturdays and Sundays for public participation. Visitors can pick up tickets for the activities at the “Ocean Wonders ” registration counter, with 20 seats per session, on a first-come, first-served basis, while stocks last.

At the same time, in the current international situation, the key materials, core devices and high-end instruments required in the field of quantum science and technology in China face an increasingly serious embargo risk.

Innovate the science and technology financial system, guide and encourage enterprises and social capital to participate in the research and development of quantum technology, especially frontier research, and realize the continuous development of the innovation chain and industrial chain.
Give full play to the research advantages of scientific research institutions, the industrial advantages of enterprises, the financial advantages of financial institutions and social capital, and carry out independent research and development of relevant key materials, core devices, high-end instruments and equipment, and basic software to ensure that the key links of the industrial chain and supply chain are independent and controllable.

"Controlling" means having asymmetric advantages in some links, and it is difficult for other countries to "jam the neck" in other links. "Open source" means sharing each other's needs and drawing on others' strengths on this basis.
Based on China's existing advantages, it has taken the lead in organizing international scientific plans, participating in the development of international standards and technical specifications, and improving China's influence and voice in global quantum science and technology innovation.
Time is like a stream, time is like a stream.
Over the past ten years, we have always kept in mind General Secretary Xi Jinping's important exposition on the development of quantum science and technology, worked hard and tackled difficult problems, and contributed a small amount to the leap of national quantum science and technology.
In the new journey, we will continue to persist in tackling key problems and innovation, and make new and greater contributions with practical actions to promote China to play its core leading role in the second quantum revolution and accelerate the realization of high-level scientific and technological self-reliance.

Sunday Literature: "The Fearful Imagination": Ideas, Novels, and the World: An Interview with Wang Dewei
Post Date: July 23, 2023
[Ming Pao News] After a lapse of 20 years, following the "Trans-century Flair: 20 Contemporary Novels" (2002), Professor Wang Dewei once again launched the preface collection of contemporary Chinese novels, "The Fearful Imagination: 31 Contemporary Novels", which can be regarded as an indicator of novel research.
The 31 writers in the book are in different historical time and space, but form a common dialogue in the book.
Professor Wang uses the concept of “awesome imagination ” to guide the way, allowing us to rethink the incredible power of contemporary fiction.
Yau Ting Kit (Lecturer, Department of Chinese Language and Literature, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Wang: Dewei Wang (Edward C. Henderson Chair Professor, Department of East Asian and Comparative Literature, Harvard University; Academician, Academia Sinica; Academician, American Academy of Arts and Sciences)
First of all, congratulations to Mr. Wang on the publication of his new book.
The title of the book, “The Fearful Imagination, ” comes from the concept of Hannah Oran, who explores the relationship between contemporary fiction and politics.
Can you explain that the current world of viruses, nuclear pollution, war, political chaos... is not reality "scary"? Why is it necessary to find "scary imagination" in the novel, and how can it lead us to face future crises and challenges?
Wang: Thank you, I ’ m happy to explain the concept of “the fearful imagination ”, inspired by Hannah Arendt ’ s argument.
First of all, the interaction between Chinese literature and politics has its own tradition, especially in the late Qing Dynasty, when the novel appeared on the horizon of modern literature, bringing about "incredible" or what I call "awesome" imagination, enough to arouse the uneasiness and thinking of society, the reader group, or the possibility of expecting great change.
In the current turmoil, why do we need to exercise the “awesome imagination ”? We can return to Oran ’ s thought system and its ultimate care.
Her historical roots in The Origins of Totalitarianism are, of course, rooted in the millennial history of the Jewish people, especially the Holocaust in Nazi Germany in the 1930s and 1940s, and the ravages of modern-day totalitarianism.
However, she elevated this experience to a metaphysical, philosophical level.
Her “awesome imagination ” is not just those terrible or incredible experiences that are within our power and are exposed to by modern experience, such as viruses, nuclear pollution, etc., but she urges us to imagine all kinds of“ evil ” possibilities that we can ’ t imagine.
In the face of immediate problems such as viruses and nuclear pollution, we can deal with them with drug treatment, preventive measures and even protests, but from Oran ’ s point of view, this is not enough.
If we cannot be one step ahead of the monsters of history, if we cannot imagine the incredible evils of history, politics, or power struggles, then how can we be able to judge and respond to real catastrophes when they erupt? The unthinkable, the unspeakable, in order to explore the various forms of ignorance and impermanence of life, and to think about the options that human beings can and cannot do.
For scholars in Oran, or the late Qing dynasty, who promoted fiction as a literary genre, this “formidable imagination ” has its ethical and political commitment.
We understand that many things in the world happen when they happen, that is, the so-called "historical contingency" problem, people are likely to be unable to resist.
But if we can use the power of narrative, which is the power of “storytelling ” in Oran ’ s words, and connect with each other, perhaps we can prevent it from happening in the future.
"Dark Consciousness" and "Dark Consciousness"
Yau: In addition to the "awesome imagination", the book also uses the term "dark consciousness", in recent years, Mr. Wang has been sharp in different occasions.
What is the relationship between “Dark Consciousness ” and Mr. Cheung ’ s“ Dark Consciousness ”? How does it relate to the novel?
Wang: I was deeply influenced by Mr. Cheung Ho. The term “dark consciousness ” is obviously a tribute to Mr. Cheung Ho, but the concept is slightly different, so I deliberately used the word“ dark ” or “dark ” to distinguish it.
According to Mr. Zhang ’ s definition of “dark consciousness ”, it is“ a reflection of the original dark forces in human nature or in the universe ”, “because these dark forces are deeply rooted, the world is flawed, can not be complete, and human life has all kinds of ugliness, all kinds of regret. ”
The theoretical roots underlying Mr. Zhang ’ s introduction of “dark consciousness ” in the 1980s and his contemplation of China ’ s democratic process are, I believe, a broad tradition of classical liberalism, including the influence of Max Weber ’ s school, which is basically based on humanism.
For the theoretical background of this concept in the context of Chinese and Spanish, I have a more detailed analysis and discussion in the fourth chapter of the English monograph Why Fiction Matters in Contemporary China (2020).
In addition, I was also influenced by the neo-Confucianism, as Mr. Mou Zongsan said, "the self-encroachment of conscience", which is a kind of democratic vision that first sets limits on the self, and then thinks about the more likely realization.
However, in my use, I would prefer to see “dark consciousness ” not only as a starting point for ethics, morality, or self-reflection — that is of course important, but I would prefer to see it as a technique, knowledge, or method that is necessary for a rationalist to argue his thoughts.
What I say is "quiet" is less focused on the definition of the moral potential of good and evil, which does not have to be immediately connected with ethics and morality, but is more a way of thinking about reality and rational dialectics.
It means that beyond the reach of our reason, there are infinite possibilities, including the operation of knowledge, emotional impulses, so-called unconscious or subconscious dynamics, and, of course, the contingency of historical and objective circumstances.
We have to look at such a larger, unattainable realm or space, and I think that fiction can help us to understand this aspect.
Therefore, in the literary space, or in the genre of fiction, the so-called "imagination" is "terrible", but at the same time "feasible".
In fiction or literature, we can have all kinds of earthly imagination, which in other professions such as history, economics, etc., may be intolerable, just reflect the uniqueness of literature and fiction.
Therefore, the usage of Mr. Zhang and I are not the same, but the same is that we will all think that in the superficial era full of light, in fact, on the other side of the dark, whether it is in epistemology or perception theory, there is potential (self) criticism and even deconstruction power, which is an unblemished and infinite field.
From the perspective of different knowledge systems, we can also refer to the traditional Chinese Taoist philosophy of "knowing white and keeping black", and people need to maintain a relatively awe attitude in the world of "disdain" and "dizzy and silent".
In the field of modern contemporary literature, the most important spokesperson for the dark consciousness should be Lu Xun.
"Contemporary" as Critical Time Consciousness
Qiu: Teacher Wang specifically mentioned the definition of the term “contemporary ” in the preface, holding that it is not limited to“ the present moment ” or “after 1949 ”, but refers to a sensitive and critical sense of time.
Why emphasize such timing?
Wang: Let me first explain a few different definitions of "contemporary".
The first is "the present moment", which is the 2023 contemporary, a time and space in which you and I live, and the second is the so-called "after 1949", which is the naming of the historical stage after the founding of New China by the Chinese Communist discourse.
Here it actually produced a kind of self-contradiction: "contemporary" originally refers to the new and new present, but it is after 1949, until today as long as 74 years of space and time, the so-called "contemporary" time seems to be fixed, or thousands of years.
The third definition I want to point out, it must be admitted, was influenced by Walter Benjamin.
Benjamin taught us that when we look at the modernity of things, we are not only concerned with the present moment, the moment of change, but we also need to have a sense of history to go back to history. Today ’ s “now ” burst out, giving us a fresh, shocking,“ revolutionary ” feeling.
I am also inspired by Giorgio Agamben ’ s thesis: the so-called contemporary sense is the “untimely ” phenomenon that occurs in the fold of time; it is the energy of the beam of light that can ’ t be looked at from facing reality and seeing darkness in the light.
Thus, The Fearful Imagination uses 31 writers to demonstrate the “contemporary ” of the third definition, from the various“ anachronisms ” that writers face in the face of historical trends or the mainstream.
Specifically, in the layout of this book, I especially connect a certain story with a certain point of time, so that it has a new meaning that was never seen before.
For example, Taijingnong's "A History of the Dead Ming" and Shi Mingzheng's "Love and Death on the Island", the former was in the mid-1940s during the Anti-Japanese War, and the latter in the 1960s and 1970s, all of which were delayed to this century for various reasons, but they are not out of date.
This "anachronism" also creates a structural reversal of the "contemporary" and generates new forces.
The tension of story and history
Qiu: The book discusses the history of Taiping Jingnong ’ s “The History of the Dead Ming ”. This novel seems to be insufficient in Chen Duxiu ’ s eyes, and“ hopes to become a history rather than a novel ”, revealing the tension between narrative — saying (good) stories — and history.
Tsing Nong regarded history as a novel, writing heavy subjects as frivolous and funny.
Is this way of deliberately keeping a distance from the big narrative, or deliberately competing, or even finding a way to escape, a characteristic of contemporary writers?
Wang: There are thousands of ways of contemporary writers to create, and this is one of them. Tsing Nong was deeply influenced by Lu Xun ’ s “New Story ”, which is precisely the best example of Benjamin ’ s so-called“ contemporary ” meaning that I have just explained.
So at this point, you can see the absolute gap between Tsing Nong and Chen Duxiu in the aesthetics of the novel or in the political science of the novel. Chen Duxiu's literary stance is conservative, he hopes that "The History of the Dead Ming" is like a historical narrative, medium and square, but Tsing Nong is deeply aware of the past kind of conservative realism as a benchmark in the novel writing style, has been unable to answer to his "contemporary" The War (War).
Especially under the pressure of the political narrative and ideology at that time, it must be explained in a different way.
He chose to write in a playful, flirtatious way.
You can call it the “escape route ”, which is of course the more fashionable Gilles Deleuze term.
But on the other hand, it can be said that history is so complicated that he adopted a narrative that, from his own perspective, can best expose the dark side of the era.
Therefore, I think that Taishinong shows absolute modernity, writing a most strange story in the narrative of the War of Resistance and Patriotism.
So whether or not this escapes, escapes the hidden explosive until it bursts out, I have no standard answer.
This is equivalent to a novel, hidden in the drawer 80 years later, we suddenly understand that with hindsight, and fall in different geographical space, will produce their own feelings.
"Light" and "Heavy" Chinese Literature
Yau: Witness the evolution of Chinese novels, from “Transcendental Flags: 20 Contemporary Fiction ” (2002) to“ The Fearful Imagination: 31 Contemporary Fiction ” (2023).
In general, does Mr. Wang think Chinese literature is “light ” or“ heavy ”?
Wang: Since the 20th century, the great turbulence and disintegration of history faced by China has definitely manifested itself in the creation of different periods and literary categories.
In my reading experience, I deeply understand the influence of politics on the novels of the past hundred years, whether slight or heavy.
Political interference itself brings light and weight, which may affect the ecology between the novelist and the reader.
For example, about 30 years between 1949 and 1978, it was an unbearable amount of weight and how difficult it became to create.
By the 1980s, Chinese novels, whether in mainland China, Taiwan, or Hong Kong, had a sense of liberation, and all of a sudden there was a variety of exchanges, which promoted the interaction between different genres and styles.
I think there has been such an era of very repeated interactions between the two sides of the Taiwan Strait, three places or four places. Looking back, it was really an era of loud voices. After the 1990s, after the ups and downs of various political historical experiences, I think these experiences have left a lot of traces in literature.
These traces are not only the theme or style, but also confirm the phenomenon of the entire literary production, including the problems and pressures encountered in the publishing process, and the online literature ecology we face today, which affects our definition of literature and the way literature is consumed.
This is the literary ecology that I have been observing and witnessing for the past 30 years.
The interplay between literature and history is part of something we have been unable to evade for thousands of years.
Now the challenge, no less than we in any period in the history of literature, seems to be an era of literary liberation, and at the same time, between the various shades and taboos, say and not say the choice, once again to think about the meaning of "literature". (Qiu: I agree, like Yan Lianke, Chen Guanzhong's novels, the publishing ecology is very complicated.) The complex phenomenon should not be simplified.
Each era has its own laws of survival, and literary and artistic creators have their — in the words of Zhang Ailing, the Shanghainese — “strange wisdom. ”
These literary ecology, I don't think need to be overly pessimistic.
Hong Kong's new story, how to tell it?
Qiu: Of the 31 writers, it is said that the one who made Teacher Wang “awesome ” is Chen Guanzhong.
Chen Guanzhong recently shared his less pessimistic views on Hong Kong and Hong Kong literature in an interview (“How to Write a New Story in Hong Kong? – Interview with Hong Kong Writer Chen Guanzhong ”, Ming Pao, July 2).
What is Mr. Wang ’ s view on Hong Kong ’ s literary development and urban prospects?
On the new story of Hong Kong, which writers are worthy of our attention?
Wang: To me, the most “awesome ” writer must be Chen Guanzhong. Reading every book of Chen Guanzhong ’ s novels makes me feel interesting on the one hand, and shocking on the other: he can actually make them write like this.
I guess I ’ m a professional novelist, but I get excited every time I read his novel, and I can ’ t guess how he ’ ll write his next novel.
He also reminded me of the era when Liang Qichao invented the genre of “New Novels ” in 1902.
Returning to the less pessimistic view of Chen Guanzhong, I agree.
You and I live in the present moment of the contemporary, do so many people, there is no way to continue to tell a different story? Back to the most basic definition of Oran, the so-called "storytelling" is in a public field, people communicate with each other, meaningful narrative behavior.
A story is not a story of the past, a story of the present, but a story of the future.
So when you ask about the literary prospects of Hong Kong, in theory, there are still many stories to tell in Hong Kong.
Of course, not everyone has the courage and wisdom to tell the story of Chen Guanzhong, but at the same time there are many other young writers telling various stories.
In my speech at HKUST this year, I introduced several young writers in Hong Kong: Wang Zhen-heng (author of "The Southern Return Truck"), a young left-wing writer who inherits the Chen Ying-chen tradition; Li Wei-yi (author of "The Road Is Difficult"), a community-based work full of public awareness; Huang Kewei's "Fake Two Cities" depicts the past and present life of Frog City, hiding a faint depression.
These writers are still trying to tell stories.
In Oran's words, when a society has the energy and willingness to tell stories, it is a civil society; if there is only one kind of story to tell, it is not a civil society.
I am happy to believe that there is more than one way to tell the new story in Hong Kong. We still have many ways to tell the story, and the most worthy of telling is the “awesome ” story.

Leaving the “Chinese capital ” of the West in search of resources, turning to Southeast Asia, South America and the Middle East Beijing = Resident Journalist
Posted July.
25, 2023 07: 57
Updated July.
25, 2023 07: 57
한국어
“Chinese money, ” which has invested aggressively in the United States and Europe for more than a decade, is turning its back.
The “global money ” that has been pouring into China, which sees high development possibilities, is also leaving.
Some analysts believe that due to the all-around intensification of the contradictions between the United States and China, both sides are unwilling to invest, and both countries are caught in the loss of the "subtraction" game.
"China will not increase investment in developed countries"
The US “Wall Street Journal ” reported on the 23rd, citing data from the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development, that China ’ s overseas direct investment last year was $147 billion (about 189.3360 trillion won), down 18% from the previous year.
25% decrease compared to the most in 2016 ($1961 billion).
In particular, Chinese capital outflows from Western developed countries such as the United States and Europe.
According to the American Enterprise Institute, a think tank, and the Heritage Foundation, there were 120 acquisitions made by Chinese companies in the seven major industrial countries (G7) in the West in 2016, but only 13 last year.
In the same year, US $84 billion (107.6712 trillion won) of all overseas investment by Chinese companies was concentrated in the seven Western countries, but last year it was only US $7.4 billion (9.4779 trillion won), accounting for 18%.
In addition, in 2017, China Hainan Airlines Group purchased the Landmark Park Avenue Building in Manhattan, New York, United States. A few years ago, Chinese capital was still buying large real estate in major developed countries, but it is difficult to see such an investment in the future.
In other words, amid the growing U.S.-China conflict, U.S. real estate and corporations are no longer attractive places to invest in Chinese capital.
"(Chinese President) Xi Jinping will not return to 2016, when China's overseas investment peaked," predicts Derek Sezer, a senior researcher at the Enterprise Research Institute.
China is turning its attention to emerging markets such as Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa.
In order to take the lead in future industries such as renewable energy and electric vehicle batteries, the large consumer markets and resource-rich resources in these regions are mainly considered.
The Wall Street Journal explained: “China spends a lot of money setting up factories in Southeast Asia or buying South American mines.
This is to strengthen ties with emerging countries and ensure access to key resources (rare metals, etc.). ”
Last year, Chinese companies invested $24.5 billion (31.5241 trillion won) in these emerging markets, up 13% from 2021.
In Indonesia, which has the world ’ s largest reserves of nickel, the core raw material for electric vehicle batteries, the proportion of investment is 17%, which is invested in Chinese funds flowing out of the West.
China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC), a state-owned oil company, has invested US $1.9 billion (KRW 2444.7 billion) in Brazil, and electric vehicle company BYD has invested in Thailand.
Western capital has also set off a “fever ” to break away from China.
Western capital is turning its back on China.
According to the Ministry of Commerce, foreign direct investment in China in the first quarter of this year (January-March) was US $20 billion (25.61 trillion won), down to only one-fifth of US $100 billion (128.500 trillion won) in the same period last year.
Despite efforts to attract overseas capital, the Chinese government, which has designated this year as the “Year of China Investment ”, also saw a 2.7% decrease in foreign direct investment in the second quarter (April-June) compared with the same period last year.
The Financial Times pointed out that the Chinese authorities ’ high pressure social controls, including the anti-espionage law, and the Biden administration ’ s measures to restrict investment in China by cutting-edge industries have made foreigners hesitant about Chinese investment.
According to the Financial Times, Bain, a global consulting firm, informed new employees in China that “work will not begin until 2025. ” That is, there are no jobs in China.
It is reported that about half of the staff of another consulting company, Mackenzie China, also gave up their business because they did not have a job, and the Boston Consulting Group China Branch recently held a strategic meeting for the job.

Greenland to mine rare earths in 2024
According to the German "Economic Weekly" reported that a mining company has obtained permission from the Greenland government to mine rare earths on the island.
The company said production could begin next year.
Tanbreez Mining, a mining company, plans to mine rare earths in Greenland next year, according to the Economic Weekly.
“We can start production next year, ” said Greg Barnes, a geologist and owner of the company. Greenland ’ s deputy minister for minerals confirmed to the journal that a mining licence had been issued.
Barnes said the Tanbreez mine "contains more than half of the world's rare earth resources" and has 19 million tons of rare earth oxides.
Of these, 30% are highly favored heavy rare earth elements.
Rare earth contains a total of 17 kinds of metal elements, the properties of each metal are different.
Each metal has a unique industrial value.
Some of them are irreplaceable.
They are used, for example, in the manufacture of electric vehicles or wind turbines.
Last year, about two-thirds of Germany ’ s rare earths came from China. Mining such as rare earths is difficult and often harmful to the environment, as rare earths are often associated with iron ore, and the chemical process of refining often requires the use of acidic substances.
What is Rare Earth?
Barnes, owner of Tanbreez Mining, told Economic Weekly that to start mining for rare earths in Greenland, a factory would be needed to separate rare earths from heterosexual rocks.
Currently there are only such factories in Russia and China.
But one such plant will be built in the United States in the coming months.
There are also plans to build a factory in Europe.
Thanks to technological advances, the equipment that separates rare earths currently costs only $40 million.
According to Barnes, China paid 1.7 billion U.S. dollars for the equipment 13 years ago.
In January, Swedish state-owned mining company LKAB announced the discovery of Europe ’ s largest rare earth deposit to date.
But the company said it would take 10-15 years for the rare earth mine, located in Kiruna in northern Sweden, to be available to the market.

Gediminas Ziemelis, Chairman of Avia Solutions Group: Challenges for new freighters compared to P2F passenger freighters
DUBLIN, Ireland, July 31, 2023 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Air cargo revenue hit a record high during the pandemic.
Shipping prices per kilogram of cargo soared as passenger aircraft grounded down capacity and booming e-commerce led to increased demand.
According to TAC Yields data from Trade and Transport Group, in 2019, the air freight price from Hong Kong to North America was $3.80 / kg, while the price from Europe to North America was $2.10 / kg.
By 2022, the above service charges are $9.00 / kg and $4.50 / kg, respectively.
Naturally, this changed the status of air cargo suppliers.
According to IATA, freight revenue more than doubled: from $100 billion in 2019 to $210 billion in 2021, while passenger revenue plummeted from $607 billion a year to $239 billion.
During the pandemic, Cargolux ’ s annual revenue grew from $2.2 billion to $5.1 billion, while Silkway ’ s revenue more than doubled and its profit margin changed from -10% to + 30%.
These huge gains, combined with the long-term potential of e-commerce (which is why Airbus and Boeing are optimistic about the growth prospects of air cargo), have led many airlines to focus more on cargo.
However, the increase in passenger capacity led to another sharp drop in freight prices.
IATA forecasts that freight yields will fall 28.6% this year.
This means that air freight, the notoriously cyclical industry, is once again entering turbulent times.
Based on this background, the airline is considering whether to purchase a new freighter.
Comparison of new freighter and passenger freighter
Airlines and air cargo providers adopt different strategies when building their freighter fleets.
According to KPMG ’ s latest report, last year, 35 new orders for the 777-200F, 33 new orders for the 777-8F, and 20 suppliers purchased the A350F.
Purchasers of these orders include specialized air cargo suppliers (Cargolux, Silkway West, DHL, FedEx) and airlines (Lufthansa Cargo, Qatar, Air Canada, China Airlines, EVA, Air France, Etihad, SIA and Western Global).
At the same time, annual passenger to freighter (P-to-F) refitting has reached an all-time high, and is expected to reach a peak of 180 aircraft per year by 2025, and then maintain a stable level of around 160 aircraft per year.
By comparison, before the COVID-19 pandemic, production of such aircraft was only 70 per year.
The decision to purchase a new freighter or a P-F refitted freighter is influenced by many factors.
Of course, cost is a major factor, but variables such as total order number, fuel consumption, maintenance costs and prepaid production costs are also taken into account.
In addition, production lead time, load capacity and flexibility are key factors.
Factor 1: Rental costs
There is a huge difference between the benchmark cost of a new freighter and a modified freighter.
The upfront purchase cost of the new 777-200F or A350F is approximately $170-185 million, while the monthly rent is between $1.2 and $1.3 million.
Judging from last year's purchase orders, most airlines have a large number of these models in their fleets, especially hybrid airlines.
In this case, the actual purchase cost is likely to be well below the $170-185 million range.
Economies of scale are also a factor that helps these airlines reduce costs.
Still, even with those savings, airlines would still be cautious about $1 million in monthly rentals.
By comparison, a P-to-F modification of the 777-300 model costs $600,000 a month and the purchase cost is about $65 million.
Compared with the new aircraft of the same manufacturer, the performance of this modified aircraft is likely to be comparable, but the cost is significantly reduced.
Factor 2: MRO and operating costs
In terms of MRO, airlines can save money by choosing P-to-F passenger freighters.
Through the second-hand parts market, it is much cheaper to maintain these aircraft than to keep new ones running.
Of course, for airlines, in addition to cost savings, the use of second-hand parts can also speed up and simplify the aircraft maintenance process.
Fuel consumption is another consideration.
Historically, when new aircraft come into service, we ’ ve always seen significant improvements in fuel consumption metrics.
When the 777F was introduced as a new generation of the 747-400F, the energy consumption was significantly reduced: the fuel consumption of the latter was 10,230 kg / h, while the former was only 6,800 kg / h.
Fuel consumption has been reduced by 30% from the 747-400F to the 777F, but the new 777X and A350 aircraft are unlikely to achieve the same level of improvement.
The maximum range of changes we can actually expect is 10% to 15%.
All in all, while the new aircraft ’ s fuel consumption performance has improved and (in some cases) economies of scale may help reduce the cost of purchasing new freighters, the P-F passenger freighter is clearly more attractive in terms of cost.
Factor 3: Capacity and flexibility
New freighters may have the upper hand in terms of cargo volume and flexibility.
The nose load function in particular has a huge advantage.
Aircraft are able to carry very large cargo, such as large generators, engines, trucks and specialized technical items.
On top of that, this oversized cargo is lucrative, bringing more profit than ordinary pallet transportation.
However, new freighters such as the 777X and A350F currently in production do not have a nose load function.
Therefore, this advantage of a dedicated freighter over a modified freighter does not play a role in reality - both are now limited to transporting goods that can be loaded through the side door and can be "fair competition".
What is the performance of the modified freighter in terms of volume, storage density and total payload?
Let ’ s take a look at Aircraft Commerce ’ s comparison data for 2022, comparing the 777-300ERCF to the 777F, which currently accounts for half of the world ’ s large freighter fleet.
While the 777F has a total payload of up to 106.6 metric tons, the 777-300ERCF is significantly superior to the 777F in terms of volume.
The total volume of the 777-300ERCF is nearly 6,000 cubic feet more than the 777F (28,739 cubic feet for the former and 22,971 cubic feet for the latter).
Revenue per unit payload is also quite high.
At a storage density of 6.5 pounds, it corresponds to 186,804 cubic feet; at a storage density of 7.5 pounds, it corresponds to 190,900 cubic feet; and the corresponding figures for the 777F are 149,312 cubic feet and 172,283 cubic feet, respectively.
The point about this comparison is that the most important thing in the e-commerce express business is quantity, not total payload, and e-commerce may be an important growth driver in the future.
In this area, the 777-300ERCF has clear advantages.
Avoid the risk of buying new freighters
Airbus estimates that the global cargo fleet will need an additional 1,040 freighters by 2041, with Boeing forecasting more.
If this demand is met by the purchase of new freighters, airlines are at great risk.
Due to the sharp drop in freight prices, capital expenditure investments on the new A350 or 777F have meant huge financial costs.
In 2021, when air cargo prices hit record levels, it may make sense to invest heavily in new freighters worth $185 million.
However, by 2023, this is certainly not a prudent strategy.
In addition, the purchase of new freighters offers little benefit in terms of performance and capacity.
The P-F passenger freighter can match the volume of the newly produced freighter and has significant advantages in maintenance and production.
By contrast, airlines choosing to retrofit their freighters can help reduce financial risk and thereby sustainably improve their air cargo capabilities.
As a result, the P-to-F passenger freighter business grew significantly, while the delivery of new cargo aircraft stalled.
This is arguably the right choice: With freight prices plummeting, many airlines are reluctant to take on the financial risks posed by new aircraft, and there is little room for added value compared to retrofitting airliners.

How to invest while living?

For our new generation, the value of freedom is becoming more and more important.
We want to have greater autonomy over what and how we work, and even the ability to decide when and where we work.
As a result, a digital nomadic lifestyle has emerged around the world in recent years.
The digital nomadic lifestyle allows us to make money through the Internet and achieve a more free life, regardless of geography and time.
But behind freedom, we need strength and money.
Therefore, for those who want to become digital nomads and travel the world, mastering investment skills and learning to create passive income will undoubtedly give us a great foundation.
Since digital nomads pay for everything on the road, we prefer investments with passive income, such as money funds, stocks, ETFs, real estate and dividend funds.
The most friendly way to invest for beginners is to invest in a money fund.
Money funds mainly invest in the money market, such as short-term government bonds, bank deposits, commercial paper and other high-quality, low-risk investment instruments to ensure the stability and security of the fund.
As a result, the value of the money fund fluctuates less, there is basically no loss of principal, and the risk of default and loss is very low.
At the same time, money funds are highly liquid, investors can buy or sell at any time, and usually do not have to pay a handling fee.
So, like a high-interest current savings account, all the money we spend while traveling is put into the money fund ’ s daily interest rate.
At the same time, we can invest in stocks and ETFs with higher dividend payouts, or even use them to build a portfolio that pays monthly or quarterly dividends to support our lives on the move.
In terms of Hong Kong stocks, domestic banks are a good choice to collect interest, but mainly pay interest once a year.
In terms of US stocks, there are more choices, various high-interest stocks and ETFs, such as ABBV (Abbvie Inc) and SCHD.
However, it should be noted that there is a 30% dividend tax on US stocks.
In addition, real estate is also a method that more people choose, which is relatively stable.
Many European and American friends will use the rent to support their daily consumption in places with lower living standards, implement geographical arbitrage, and live a higher quality of life.
Even if the original unit does not sign a long-term contract, you can rent short-term through Airbnb and collect rent.
However, the initial investment in real estate rental is larger.
If you want to be lazy, you can also consider a dividend fund.
Many funds can achieve a stable monthly dividend payout according to market demand. We can invest through banks, insurance companies and securities companies.
However, you should pay special attention to the past performance and risks of the fund when investing, such as whether there is excessive concentration of a certain industry.
In the past, some high-dividend funds were particularly concentrated in the real estate industry in the Mainland. If there is a headwind in the industry, the fund returns will also fall sharply.
Even if the monthly interest rate is paid, the return will not fully cover the capital loss.
In addition to working remotely or receiving cases, digital nomads can also choose the above investment methods according to their own risks and circumstances to increase passive income.
But passive income also needs some management to play better.
Therefore, we need to continuously learn and improve our investment and financial knowledge in order to better manage passive income and better live a digital nomadic living.

China ’ s control of gallium and germanium exports threatens South Korea ’ s semiconductor base
As a countermeasure to the US sanctions, the Chinese government announced that since August 1, the export control of gallium and germanium related items will be implemented, and the export of gallium and germanium will not be allowed without permission.
On the day the regulation came into effect, the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Resources of South Korea convened a gallium and germanium supply chain inspection meeting.
There are reports that South Korea has begun to prepare for the possibility of long-term or category expansion of relevant Chinese measures.
Korean media said that China 's export controls on gallium and germanium threaten to shake the foundation of South Korea' s semiconductor industry, which is an important material for semiconductor research and development and OLED display, while germanium is used in the production of key gases in the semiconductor industry.
The report said that although South Korean companies can find alternative sources of imports from Australia and other places, because China's production of gallium and germanium accounts for a high proportion of the global market (94% of gallium and 83% of germanium), the market has also begun to worry that the related regulatory measures will be long-term, and even expand to rare earths and other items.
The South Korean Industrial Research Institute report believes that China's restriction of these two metals is not just to cope with the pressure of the United States, China's ultimate goal is likely to be to develop a new generation of semiconductor industry based on gallium nitride, and ultimately win this fierce semiconductor competition.
China's Ministry of Commerce issued a ban on the export of gallium nitride, gallium oxide, gallium phosphide, gallium arsenide, gallium indium arsenide, gallium selenide, gallium antimonide, gallium oxide, gallium antimonide, and other related items without permission.
The industry admits that gallium and germanium are not particularly rare, but processing costs are higher. China has long exported relatively cheap raw materials to other countries at low cost, so other European countries that can produce production capacity has also decreased.
However, as long as other suppliers enter production, it will be expected to meet market demand.

What is the healthiest meal?
Research expert dissects: intermittent fasting vs dieting
A growing body of research shows that our health is influenced not only by what and how much we eat, but also by the time we eat.
So what does it mean to schedule a meal?
Does intermittent eating help?
A growing body of research shows that eating time can affect health.
Credit: Mr Lin
The former hunter gatherers faced a long fasting.
Their access to food depended on successful hunting, fishing and the supply of wild plants.
Over time, the development of modern agriculture and industrial societies have changed our daily eating patterns, pushing back our dinner times to a later part of the day to accommodate work schedules.
Nowadays, with our access to abundant food, it is rare to experience long periods of fasting, except for weight loss or religious activities.
It is now common to eat four or more meals a day, with the most calories eaten later.
Snacking frequently is also common, with a duration of about 15 hours.
Biological clocks don't just control sleep.
The biological clock in our bodies regulates many aspects, including physiology and behavior.
It tells us to stay awake and active during the day, rest and sleep at night, and can also tell us the best time to eat.
Our bodies are biologically ready to eat during the day.
When we should be active and eating, the body is most efficient at food digestion, nutrient absorption, and energy metabolism.
Eating regularly when we should be sleeping and fasting violates this default stage, which can damage these processes and affect our health.
Unstable eating patterns, including late-night meals, have been linked to weight gain and a greater risk of developing metabolic diseases.
People who work shifts, such as night work, night shifts or shifts, have a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and diabetes.
But adopting a diet that matches our circadian clock can reduce these risks.
Does intermittent eating help?
Nutritional intervention programs focus not only on what we eat, but increasingly on when.
Intermittent fasting is a way to limit the amount of time we eat instead of the amount of food we eat.
There are several types of intermittent eating, one of which is limited time eating.
This means eating all of your calories in 8-12 hours or less per day.
But is there any evidence to back it up?
Much of what is known about intermittent and time-limited diets today comes from studies in small mice that have shown that these types of dietary interventions can lead to significant weight loss and overall health benefits.
However, some aspects of a mouse ’ s physiological clock may differ from that of a human.
Mice need to eat more frequently than humans, and even a short period of fasting can have a significant impact on their physiology.
Fasting for a day in mice resulted in a 10% weight loss, while in humans it was required to fast for 14 days to achieve similar results.
This makes it difficult for mouse studies to be applied directly to humans.
Intermittent and time-limited diets have less significant results in weight loss than calorie-restricted diets.
Credit: Chris Radburn / PA / Alamy
Although intermittent and time-limited diets have health benefits, results in weight loss are less clear.
Current data suggest that people who receive these dietary regimens have limited success in weight loss, if any, compared to calorie restriction diets.
Due to small sample sizes, individual metabolic differences, changes in study design (such as the use of different regimens, different food restriction times and durations), and participants ’ failure to follow instructions, it may be more difficult to draw definitive conclusions in humans.
Eating fewer calories is healthy.
Most studies that show the health benefits of limiting time eating or intermittent fasting also find that these diets are accompanied by calorie restriction: reducing the amount of time it takes to get food will undoubtedly lead to people eating less.
Studies that control calorie intake have not found that intermittent eating is more beneficial than restricting calories alone.
The observed weight loss and health benefits of intermittent eating can be attributed to these practices resulting in reduced calorie intake.
A similar discovery was made for limited time eating.
Benefits of following a biological clock
However, a limited time diet brings additional health benefits to humans, such as improved glucose metabolism and blood pressure, even if there is no difference in calorie intake, especially when restricted to eating earlier in the day (i.e. there are six hours of eating before 3pm and dinner is the last meal).
For people who work shifts, limiting food intake during the day can alleviate metabolic differences caused by shift work, and this effect is not obvious when food intake is limited to the night.
Eating early is another idea that aligns with our circadian rhythms helps to synchronize with our biological clocks.
This can restore the rhythm of our autonomic nervous system, which regulates basic functions such as breathing and heartbeat, and keeps our physiological functions “tuned, ” as shown in mice.
While there is still much to study in this area, the evidence suggests that in order to maintain a healthy weight and overall health, we should regularly eat nutrient-rich foods during the day, while avoiding late-night meals and frequent snacks.
The authors are: Frederic Gachon, Associate Professor of Circadian Rhythm Physiology, Institute of Molecular Biological Sciences, University of Queensland; Meltem Weger, Postdoctoral Fellow, Institute of Molecular Biological Sciences, University of Queensland

Parkinson ’ s disease is a neurodegenerative disease, and patients want to regain their autonomy in life.
Exercise is considered a good medicine for Parkinson ’ s disease, how to do it most effectively?
Dr. Xie Yixi shared that it is best to maintain exercise for at least 30 minutes a day, five times a week.
If you are just starting your exercise program, divide 30 minutes into three times for 10 minutes each, and the results will be better than 30 minutes at a time.
More importantly, learning to improve the quality of movement, the “conscious movement ” can be used as a starting point for change, such as the Feldenkrais method of active awareness, tai chi, yoga.

Conscious Action: Moving Awareness
Dr. Xie has long studied mindfulness stress reduction and Feldenkrais methods and is licensed as a lecturer. He tries to apply what he has learned to rehabilitation.
Based on foreign research experience and patient feedback, conscious movement is important for people with Parkinson ’ s disease.
General exercise training focuses on repetition and muscle endurance training, using willpower or more effort to force yourself to achieve the goal; but "in-motion awareness" is concerned with the individual's awareness of themselves, by starting from a gentle and slow start (it is easier to be aware of what they are doing), aware of their original use of the body's habitual pattern, and then exploring different ways to use the body. Quality first, then increment gradually.
When you are aware of the practice in action, do not force yourself or over-stretch, remind yourself that the range of action is within the comfort zone.
If you feel pain, it is necessary to slow down the speed or amplitude of the action, or stop the rest first, and simulate it in the brain (visualization) in an imaginary way, and wait until the body is ready to start again.
Dr. Xie said that often practice moving with awareness, over time, you will know more about how you use your body, and the more you understand your body and mind, you can find a more relaxed and effective way to get along with it.
When you can call up more parts of the body to work together and participate in the movement wholeheartedly, it will be easier and labor-saving, and reduce the risk of injury due to improper activities.
Can housework be a sport?
According to the American Parkinson ’ s Association (APDA), any form of activity or exercise training can be beneficial for Parkinson ’ s disease, even for gardening and housework.
Dr. Xie said that the same activities, with different attitudes, different ways to do, the effect is different.
If you do the work mechanically, it is good to do it, it is only to strengthen the old habits, and even aggravate the old injuries.
Work consciously, find uncomfortable or unsmooth, or hold your breath while doing, know the appropriate adjustment, find a better way to do it, that activity is exercise, that is rehabilitation.
The core of in-action awareness is not the size or amount of the action you are performing, but the quality of attention and awareness when you are doing it.
In the process of movement, be curious, pay attention to and be aware of the physical and mental sensations and changes during the practice. Be aware of the body ’ s sensations, breathing, movements, emotions and thoughts, and accept the feelings of the moment, avoiding evaluation or judgment.
The important thing is that there is no awareness to carry out every action, labor, movement, activity may look similar in appearance, but the mentality and the quality of the movement may be very different.

Parkinson ’ s disease exercise mode selection reference
In addition to being aware of movement during exercise, Dr. Xie quotes from the book “Parkinson ’ s disease – a multidisciplinary guide to management ”, where people with Parkinson ’ s disease can choose the right type of exercise according to their symptoms.
For example, for problems with slow movement and rigid limbs, you can take a balance training course, tai chi, or game machine exercise.
For quivering, stretching activities and activities that require both hands to bear weight (such as cycling) can be helpful.
In addition, resistance training, balance training, and fall prevention exercise courses can also help improve posture instability and reduce the risk of falls.
In addition to movement disorders, people with Parkinson ’ s disease often have problems such as fatigue, apathy, depression, insomnia and constipation.
It is recommended to choose aerobic and social exercises to increase flexibility and strength of muscles and promote relaxation and balance of mind and body, such as walking, jogging, dancing, tai chi and yoga.
Crossing the barriers that hinder movement makes it easy.

Through this people-centered approach, patients can be helped to practice continuously every day, improve mobility and improve quality of life.
The right mindset is also crucial for the body ’ s flexibility and mobility.

Respond again.
Break complex things into simple steps, reconnect, practice, remember...
Focus on one thing at a time.

What kind of beliefs, what kind of body and life, Parkinson ’ s disease people can be aware of the way of exercise to delay the course of the disease, improve physical and mental health.

SYDNEY (AFP) – Australia ’ s Great Barrier Reef could deteriorate again if warmer ocean temperatures trigger another massive coral bleaching event later this year, the Australian Academy of Marine Sciences said today.
Advertisement
Parts of the Great Barrier Reef were originally showing good signs of recovery before a bleaching event in 2022 turned large swathes of vibrant coral to a pathological pallor.
The Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) said that while conditions on the Great Barrier Reef had stabilised after a "relatively mild" summer in 2023, the reef was still in danger.
Australian Academy of Marine Sciences president David Wachenfeld said there was an increased risk to the Great Barrier Reef "due to more frequent and severe bleaching due to climate change".
The Australian Bureau of Meteorology said the El Nino weather pattern "may" occur in Australia in the coming weeks, which will bring higher temperatures to the Pacific Ocean and once again increase the risk of coral bleaching.
Average global ocean temperatures have been breaking seasonal high temperature records since April.
Earlier this year, Australia was given a brief respite after a group of UNESCO experts failed to list the Great Barrier Reef as “endangered. ”
The Great Barrier Reef is one of Australia ’ s most important tourist attractions, and its inclusion on the endangered list could seriously affect its attractiveness to international visitors.
UNESCO considered listing the Great Barrier Reef on the List of World Heritage in Danger after a scathing report issued in 2021, but the decision was put on hold after strong lobbying by Australia ’ s former conservative government.
Instead, UNESCO has set up a monitoring mission in Australia to assess the impact of pollution, fishing, climate change and coral bleaching.
Researcher Mike Emslie said even the slightest bleaching event could "put the brakes" on the Great Barrier Reef's recovery, noting: "This means the reef could still decline due to frequent disturbances."

Is there another “Trump ” in Argentina?
Libertarian maniacs will shake up Latin America ’ s geopolitics
Author: Ye Dehao
Published: Updated:
On August 13, Argentina held preliminary presidential elections, which were considered the country ’ s “most accurate polls ” due to the fact that the people had to vote.
The pre-election “general poll ” showed that libertarians, economists, television personalities, rock singer and former coach Javier Milei, who had only 20% support, actually led the traditional right and left candidates with 30% of the vote.
The political junkie, who idolized Donald Trump and was endorsed by Brazil ’ s former president Jair Bolsonaro (known as “Tropical Trump ”), has a clear chance of winning the October 22 official election.
Like the rise of Trump in 2016, Millet is a very personal political savant.
Known for his thick and loose hair, he said he has never combed his hair since he was 13, often talking about his love of three people, and has raised five British Mastiff dogs, four of which are named after famous economists including Milton Friedman.
Mirai, who has a thick and loose hairstyle, claims to have never combed her hair since she was 13 years old. (Reuters)
After earning two master ’ s degrees in economics as a young man at the age of 52, he spent many years working as an economist at different institutions, advocating small government and big markets. He publicly criticized the economics school of the University of Buenos Aires as a “Marxist brainwashing center. ”
It was only in 2021 that he entered politics for the first time, winning elections in Buenos Aires to join Congress.
Millet is a total "anti-establishment".
He advocated the outright abolition of Argentina ’ s central bank, a nationwide shift to the US dollar, a drastic reduction in government spending, the abolition of currency and price controls, a ban on abortion (with no exception for rape pregnancies), full liberalization of gun rights, and the creation of a market for human organs.
He also questioned the scientific consensus on global warming, calling it a “socialist lie. ”
After the primary, Millet told supporters: "We are the real opposition, we are the people who want real change, because you have to remember that as long as the same old people, the same old people who have failed, the same old people who have failed for the last 100 years, a different Argentina will not be possible!"
The newspaper headlines the day after the primary election were full of news of Millai's stunning lead.
(Reuters)
Argentina ’ s inflation rate is now 115%, foreign exchange is in dire straits, the Argentine peso has depreciated more than half its value against the US dollar in the past 12 months, and burning the Argentine peso has become a common trick for foreign fans to mock Atingan fans (the country has recently criminalized this).
Today, Argentina is also the largest lender to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), with four adults living in poverty.
Argentina ’ s long history of habitual high inflation and low economic development is seen as an economic “miracle ” – Simon Kuznets, Nobel laureate in economics in 1971, once said:“ There are four economies in the world: developed, developing, and Japan and Argentina. ”
Millet ’ s talk of “100 years of failure ” is also not a hollow wind.
More than 100 years ago, Argentina ’ s per capita GDP was 80% of that of the United States, similar to that of European powers such as Britain, France and Germany, but now it is less than 20% of that of the United States.
And neither traditional left nor right parties have been able to tackle Argentina ’ s perennial economic problems: the right-wing Juntos por el Cambio (Juntos por el Cambio) President Mauricio Macri, who ruled from 2015 to 2019, nor the left-wing Beronist President Alberto Fernández and Vice President Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner, who are in power today.
The Rose Palace, the presidential palace of Argentina. (Reuters)
Under the haze of "100 years of failure", voters of course have the heart to seek fundamental political change, no matter what the specific content of such change is.
This is the core reason why Mile has attracted voter support. (Although the market is worried about the possibility of Mile ’ s coming to power, after the election results were announced, the Central Bank of Argentina immediately lowered the official exchange rate of the peso by 18%, raising interest rates by 21 percentage points to 118%, and the price of Argentina ’ s dollar bonds fell by nearly 10%.)
Compared to Milai's lead, the traditional left and right sides did not perform well.
Sergio Massa, the current economy minister in the Unión por la Patria, won only 21.4% of the vote, defeating his rival in the other party, with 27% of the vote.
The leading party in the pre-election polls, the Together for Change party, received 28% of the vote, but its winner, Patricia Bullrich, with 17% of the vote, was a representative of the party ’ s more right-wing stance – a result that seems to indicate that Millet has room for expansion.
At the same time, Mirai leads in 16 of Argentina ’ s 24 provinces.
It was expected that the traditional right-wing party “Together for Change ” would come to power after the failure of the Beronist government to manage the economy again. Although this possibility is still not low, Millet ’ s momentum has been overwhelming after the primary election, and October ’ s presidential election coincided with Millet ’ s 53rd birthday.
In May 2022, Miley said, “I ’ m not going to apologize for having a penis, I ’ m not going to be ashamed of being a man, a white man, a man with blond hair and light blue eyes. ” (Reuters)
In the general election, if Millet is to win on the first ballot, he must receive at least 45% of the vote, or be more than 10 percentage points ahead of his second opponent and receive more than 40% of the vote at the same time.
In the context of the three-party contest (and several small party candidates), this threshold is very high, but it is not entirely impossible, and even if Milai is to enter the second round of elections, it is not without a chance of winning.
As a politician, Millet has no allies in parliament, and not all seats are vacant in the October election, so if elected, he will face considerable political resistance to implementing his extreme policies.
At this time, however, Latin America is experiencing a “left-wing trend ”, with many countries in the region represented by Brazil being run by left-wing politicians.
Under the leadership of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the Union of South American Nations (UNASUR), excluding the United States, has been revived, and Lula and the Argentine authorities reached a consensus earlier this year to study a common currency.
If the Argentinian version of “Trump ” succeeds in overthrowing the country ’ s traditional political forces, the Latin American story seems to return to its historical cycle of left-right political opposition, and once again take its place in geopolitical positioning.
