Taiwan will launch a post-quantum cryptography Academia Sinica Yang Peiyin calls on the government to invest heavily to recruit the best talent
Yang: If the public sector is willing to provide the right cryptographic utilities, then the cost of adopting post-quantum cryptography will be lower.
Yang Pei-yin, a research fellow at Academia Sinica's Institute of Research, believes that post-quantum cryptography, whether it is theoretical or practical, should be studied on various topics.
(Source: Taiwan English News)
(Taiwan English News / Lin Ching-yi, Taipei Interview) Countries in Europe, the United States and Asia have noticed the need to switch to post-quantum cryptography, and Taiwan, which has been hit by a recent surge in attacks, is clearly no exception.
Professor Yang Boyin, a researcher at the Institute of Information Science at the Academia Sinica, reminded that the entire society should have a consensus on the matter of post-quantum cryptography, and the public sector should smash the capital and recruit good talents to help migrate to a cryptographic system that can resist the threat of quantum computers.
As for the future development of post-quantum cryptography, Yang Po-yin, a research fellow at Academia Sinica's Institute of Information Technology, says that 30 years later, when post-quantum cryptography, also known as anti-quantum computational cryptography, replaced all cryptography systems that are now unable to resist quantum computer attacks, there was no need to add the word "post-quantum" when talking about cryptography.
As for when quantum computers will develop to crack the current public-key cryptography, Yang said that this part is still worth debating, maybe five, 10 years or more.
He also reminded that, in fact, everyone has information that they want to hide for 30 years, from highly sensitive information of government agencies, financial information, medical records, to other high-value information, which must be kept secret for a long time.
So, when we are determined to transition from the current public key cryptography system to the post-quantum public key cryptography system, it will take another 5 to 10 years, and this period is a dangerous period.
"Cryptography" is unfamiliar to the public, but when it comes to terms such as information security, such as solid-state drive encryption in mobile phones or hard disk encryption in computers, chip cards in ATMs, and end-to-end encryption in conversation software, everyone knows that cryptography has been integrated into daily life.
Yang proposed that some national powers are now collecting all the encrypted transmission information they think is worth collecting, and at some point, when they have a quantum computer, they can break the encryption and read all the information.
For the sake of information security, the U.S. government signed National Security Memorandum No. 10 (NSM) in 2022, requiring all federal governments and their agencies to use post-quantum cryptography by 2035.
The first post-quantum cryptography system was developed in 1978 by Robert McEliece, an asymmetric encryption algorithm developed by Robert McEliece, and it was not until 1994 that Shor discovered that quantum computers could crack traditional public-key cryptography.
In 2003, in order to distinguish whether the public-key cryptography system studied was quantum-resistant, someone gave this research a new name called Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), so he is not a completely new cryptography system, not a completely new learning, only the last seven or eight years have been emphasized.
In 2006, a group of post-quantum cryptography researchers held the "First Post-Quantum Crypto International Conference (PQCrypto)", which has been nearly 20 years, although not the top or most highly regarded information security conference, but it has also received wide academic and industry attention.
Yang Boin talks about the 1989 IBM experiment, the company used a large molecule of hydrogen atoms to simulate seven qubits, through the Shor factorization algorithm to successfully break the whole number of 15 into three times five, which is Proof of Concept (proof of concept), said "it is possible".
Over the years, IBM ’ s quantum computer has only grown to a hundred bits.
Although it feels that there is little progress in terms of quantity, because the qubits are now all kinds of scalable qubits such as atoms in superconductors or traps, there is actually a big push in terms of quality.
Yang has been involved in various aspects of quantum cryptography for 20 years, and for him, the study itself is very beautiful, of course, for this reason to study it is more like a religious belief, just like the mountain is there so climbers to climb the mountain.
He believes that post-quantum cryptography, whether theoretical or practical, should be studied on various topics.
Moreover, Taiwan's chip manufacturing technology is a major advantage, he believes that Taiwan's industry will therefore have a good space for development in post-quantum, and in post-quantum cryptography, Taiwan must not be absent.
Yang Boyan suggested that, first, we need the entire society to have a consensus on the matter of post-quantum migration.
Second, all programs related to cryptography should be led by the public sector to provide fast, secure, efficient and free programs, and eliminate legal issues such as patents and copyrights.
Third, the public sector should re-establish itself and recruit good talents to work in Taiwan.
Yang Boyin explained that today, a person who understands quantum cryptography can get a very high salary in the industry, and the public sector can keep him in Taiwan as long as it can pay not too much difference with the industry.
But if not, then the migration effect of quantum cryptography is not very good.
Take Google, IBM or Amazon as an example, their slightly seniority researchers, his salary is many times that of our researchers, if it is to provide sufficient incentives and relatively good salaries, it can attract our foreign doctoral students or foreign senior professionals to Taiwan to work.
However, this matter is difficult to rationalize the expenditure in the private sector, so he believes that it is best for the public sector to take the lead, otherwise it is basically difficult to continue for a long time, which is not only a problem of information security or post-quantum cryptography, but also in other areas of technology.
Yang has just retired a 14-year advanced computing server, which he purchased in 2009 for about $1 million.
He wants to tell everyone that after the research, quantum cryptography is much cheaper than biomedicine, biochemistry, and pharmaceuticals. "We will not go down with a reagent on tens of thousands of pieces, so the sunk cost of quantum cryptography will not be so high, of course, there is no way to immediately see recovery, but this is a necessary investment."
Yang Bo pointed out another blind spot, we all regard "security" as a "cost" to look at. Although, security is to spend money and time, but we must let everyone know that investment in security is cheap and necessary.
If you don ’ t provide a secure password environment, your costs will go up in the future.
For example, if a contractor wants to bid on a government case, and he does not use a known secure post-quantum cryptography, the government can predict that in seven to ten years, as in the future, the United States will not be able to bid.
This allows everyone to use the new password system.
On the contrary, if the contractor can bid without post-quantum cryptography, he will not want to use it – there are fewer post-quantum cryptography talents today, and there must not be many people who can write this program, so it is more expensive.
We should use different methods to make post-quantum cryptography more beneficial than non-post-quantum cryptography, because if one day, you are hacked because you did not switch to post-quantum, you will be much more expensive than not investing, which is why the public sector should take the lead and provide fast, safe, efficient and free programs.
Yang Boyan encouraged the government and enterprises, should have professional security personnel to do after the migration of quantum cryptography.
Before the migration, they need to inventory the hardware and software equipment, those still using the old password system, need to gradually change to the new encryption system according to the level of risk and process.
In order to ensure that everyone can implement, the public sector should provide a considerable amount of resources to provide efficient and formally verified utilities. If the government is willing to provide a post-quantum cryptography utility library and can allow everyone to be exempted from legal liability when adopting it, the cost will be lower, and everyone will be more willing to switch to post-quantum cryptography.
For the future of Taiwan can refer to the post-quantum cryptography implemented by those countries, Yang Pei-yin admits that countries in the Asian region are passive, and no one really wants to create a post-quantum ecosystem (PQC Ecosystem).
If you ask which country is more diligent, South Korea is running its own post-quantum race and turning them into its own national standard.
Although there are such competitions in China, they do not seem to have the intention of standardizing the winners, even if in the future they will have official (not academic or industry) national standards.
Yang noted that the “Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) ” competition held by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) will be used to determine their national standards.
And their standards, in fact, will eventually become the standard of most people in the world, so NIST PQC is actually quite important.
In recent years, almost all public key cryptographers have devoted most of their time to this competition.
Sharing the story of the Rainbow cipher system he and other scholars developed, and his team ’ s experience of entering the NIST PQC final, he pointed out that Rainbow was an enhanced version of the UOV (Unbalanced Vinegar Signing) and was selected as the finalist (equivalent to reaching the final), but has now been eliminated.
That ’ s because a young Belgian, Ward Beullens, discovered a very beautiful attack, so Rainbow ’ s system is not safe.
Yang believes that the research team spent on Rainbow ’ s research, whether theoretical or practical, has not really been wasted.
Basically, the cryptographic system will look for parameters that are both secure and suitable for implementation, and then implement them, and then convince enough people to embed it into a practical system, as is Rainbow, and so is UOV. Most of the properties of UOV and Rainbow are the same, so why not propose UOV in the first place?
This decision was conclusively proven wrong by Beullens because of changes made in Rainbow for higher performance.
However, UOV is still the loudest algorithm in this round.
Yang doesn ’ t like to use “advanced deployment ” to describe post-quantum cryptography, but it ’ s a job that has to be done.
When the European and American countries are about to embark on the migration of post-quantum cryptography, he believes that immediately knowing that every bet now placed may go directly to the water, but we still have to bet, the bet is always risky, but even if the bet is not necessarily right, but you do not bet, you will lose.
In addition to Elliptic Curve Cryptography and RSA Cryptography, SHA-1 (Secure Hash Algorithm 1), MD5 (Message-Digest Algorithm) Wait for the algorithm should also be eliminated, these algorithms, there are still many places in Taiwan are still used.
Taiwan is currently moving slower than others, and needs to keep up with the international pace in the migration of post-quantum cryptography by virtue of its hardware advantages.

【 Viral Marketing 】 Experts warn enterprises to shake sound, small red book brand promotion must be cautious
Business 11: 00 2023 / 08 / 18
Share:
Share:
Recently, a short video of mainland influencers and “Raw Coke ” in Japan became the topic of discussion, and Japanese department stores in Hong Kong were immediately introduced to the shelves, once again proving the influence of social media on the creation of trends.
Consumer trend research organization WGSN experts said that TikTok, small red book and other social media become a platform to drive trends, Gen Z in these platforms are not only followers of the trend, but also creators, if the brand wants to have the ability to create trends, it can not ignore the efforts in these platforms.
Taihe McDonald becomes LEED Zero Carbon Certified Restaurant to save 987,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity
In recent months, the media has frequently reported on the trends created by social media such as TikTok and Little Red Book. From “Carrying a McDonald ’ s Bags to Punching at McDonald ’ s Road ”,“ Carrying a Card in Fai Fu Street Soon ”, to “Taking a Photo in Hong Kong School Uniform ” and“ Drinking a Student Coke to Get a Bright Sense of Light ”, all kinds of trends brought by TikTok and Little Red Book. TikTok and Little Red Books are both popular among Gen Z, and they can quickly create trends and topics, which can be both a channel for marketing and a crisis, and must be used carefully, according to WGSN trendsetter Huang Jiajing.
According to Little Red Book data, as of April 2023, the number of Little Red Book users in Hong Kong has reached 1.13 million, with daily active users increasing by 50% year-on-year.
Since the customs clearance began in February and March this year, a large number of mainland tourists have used small red books and trembling to punch in Hong Kong, and even created special punching methods, which have caused many people to imitate.
Some merchants also smell the business opportunities behind, and more and more merchants are using Little Red Book to promote "Hong Kong Letter", even allowing bottled oolong tea to be almost bought out of the market.
Huang Jiajing believes that this phenomenon not only appears in mainland China, but also through TikTok is popular in foreign countries. TikTok ’ s characteristics make its influence “come and go quickly ”, which can viral create trendy topics, but also shorten the cycle of the trend. The heat will soon be overshadowed by new trends.
Huang Jiajing believes that with the emergence of TikTok and Little Red Book, it is not traditional brands or celebrities that create trends, but ordinary people.
Trendsetter fragmentation
She believes that these social platforms are “windows ” to the world, and cites Google data that 40% of Gen Z have listed TikTok and Instagram as the preferred search methods. Younger generations use these platforms to observe the world, and if brands are absent from these windows, it is difficult to promote brands to younger generations.
She also refers to the creation of popular is not the brand, but as the user of the Z generation itself, each user can shine hot, niche culture may also create a trend, and its influence is always better than the brand spend big money to sell advertising publicity.
Huang Jiajing pointed out that in the past, commercial promotion could not be separated from brands, trademarks, celebrity effects, etc., but today's trends often come from "ordinary people".
Many of the creators of TikTok or Little Red Books are not celebrity stars, and the taste and personality of these small users through social platforms can infect other small people who feel the same way.
These potential consumers are more willing to show their personality and taste and pay more premium, of which Nothing Phone is an example, their information on TikTok has received 182 million views, which is recognized by many small consumers who do not want to use traditional big brand phones.
Forty percent of Gen Z have identified TikTok and Instagram as their top search options, and younger generations use these platforms to see the world.
Brands should first understand their “brand DNA ”
However, if the brand is not careful enough to handle the promotion on TikTok or Little Red Book, it can easily be counterproductive.
Since the leading trend comes from the minority, if the brand uses the traditional, lack of tolerance for multiculturalism to promote, it is easy to provoke consumer antipathy, so Huang Jiajing believes that the brand must seriously think about the "DNA of the brand".
She cites the recent hot Barbie as an example, which is not emphasizing pink, but emphasizing the need to choose between femininity and seeking power, which makes Barbie resonate with female audiences who are struggling to find a balance between femininity and the pursuit of power.
Many people are attracted to certain lifestyles, not the product itself. For example, Apple products promote lifestyle, not the performance or value of the product itself.
Huang Jiajing said that brands should understand whether their positioning is niche or mainstream, whether it is to face consumers in a cultural or tangible way, and through the appropriate way to hype topics on social platforms.

Nonprofit organization 4 Day Week Global and Brazilian think tank Reconnect _ Happiness at Work today announced at a press conference in Sao Paulo that 15 Brazilian companies will pilot a four-day week starting in September.
Generally speaking, the working day in Brazil is Monday to Friday, and only special industries work on Saturdays and Sundays, and the maximum working hours can not exceed 44 hours per week, 8 hours per day, and overtime can not exceed 2 hours.
The four-day workweek initiative, launched in New Zealand in 2019 and gaining more traction during the COVID-19 pandemic, has been tested so far in the United Kingdom, the United States, Spain, Australia and other countries, and the model will be carried out in Brazil by Global Four Days a Week in partnership with Reconnect _ Happiness at Work.
According to Global 4 Days a Week, nearly 500 companies around the world test the possibility of working four days a week, and employees must commit to using 80% of the time and 100% of the time under the same salary conditions to improve their quality of life.

The 15 participating companies will decide for themselves how to implement the plan and how many departments will enter the pilot phase, and with the help of the Global 4 Days a Week, they will meet from September 5 to learn the basic concepts and steps of the project.
Renata Rivetti, founder of Reconnect and a specialist in corporate happiness, points out that it takes three months to redesign the workflow, and everything has to be done with great care, not only to propose a reduction in workload, but also to propose a new business model with results.
The pilot program began in December, and data on project performance was collected after 3 months.

MIT researchers have made significant progress in extending the coherence time of qubits, a key step in the development of quantum devices such as quantum sensors and gyroscopes.
The team, led by Ju Li and Paola Cappellaro, used concepts inspired by noise-cancelling headphones to enhance the coherence of nuclear spin qubits.
By characterizing the noise caused by heat, the researchers were able to implement an “unbalanced echo ” technique that increased the coherence time from 150 microseconds to up to 3 milliseconds.
The method the team used involved understanding and eliminating specific noise sources, similar to the way noise-cancelling headphones eliminate unwanted sounds.
This method has the potential to greatly improve the coherence time of quantum systems.
Wang Guoqing, the first author of the study, believes that a longer coherence time can be achieved by further exploring and mitigating other noise sources.
The results of the study are expected to have a significant impact on the development of quantum devices.
Dmitry Budker, head of the material-antimatter department at the Heinz Helmholtz Institute, praised the team ’ s innovative approach and thought it could be easily implemented in practical applications.
Cornell University professor Gregory Fox also highlighted the usefulness of the study in achieving long-life nuclear spin synthesis for a variety of applications.
The experiments conducted by the researchers focused on the large number of nitrogen vacancy centers (NV centers) in the diamond, which are ideal candidates for quantum sensors and other quantum technologies.
The challenge was finding a way to synchronize the clocks of billions of NV centers for enhanced consistency.
The goal is to take advantage of multiple clocks while maintaining phase coherence to retain quantum information for longer.
This groundbreaking research opens up new possibilities in the field of quantum computing and paves the way for the development of more efficient and reliable quantum devices.

Five areas will become the forefront of future industrial innovation
September 10, 2023 08: 28 | Source: Guangming Daily
Small number
Original title: Five major areas will become the forefront of future industrial innovation
A new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation have accelerated development, and new disruptive technologies have emerged. On September 9, the results conference of the Pujiang Innovation Forum was held in Shanghai.
At the meeting, the report "Frontier Areas of Future Industrial Innovation" jointly compiled by the China Institute of Science and Technology Information and the Shanghai Institute of Science and Technology was officially released.
Based on multi-dimensional analysis of scientific and technological information such as national and regional science and technology policy and R & D investment, papers and patents, expert opinions and academic conference materials, the report selects five frontier areas of future industrial innovation - brain chips, quantum information, synthetic biology, green hydrogen production and blockchain.
Brain chips: rapid development in the past 10 years
The brain-like chip is a new type of computing chip developed by drawing on the information processing mechanism of the human brain, which has developed rapidly in the past 10 years.
The report pointed out that brain-like chips entered a period of rapid growth from 2013 to 2016, and entered a period of rapid growth after 2016. Before 2013, the number of global papers on brain-like chips was less than 500, rising to 1,000 in 2016, and nearly 4,000 in 2022.
The number of patent applications for brain-like chips also rose sharply after 2015, from less than 300 in 2015 to more than 2,600 in 2021.
From a national point of view, the United States is the leading country in the research and application of brain chips in the world; Switzerland is the initiator of neuromorphic chips, and its academic influence is large; China's brain chip research started late, but in 2016, it entered a period of rapid growth with the United States.
At present, China ranks first in the world in the number of basic research and technological research and development achievements in this field, but there are still problems such as low academic influence, and gaps between research quality and top institutions.
Liu Qiyan, deputy director of the China Institute of Science and Technology Information, said at the press conference that brain-like chips are the foundation and pioneer of the development of artificial intelligence industry, and are still in the stage of laboratory exploration, and there are still many technical bottlenecks such as theoretical modeling, power consumption reduction, integration of sensing and calculation, and efficient sensing.
Brain chips integrate knowledge of brain science, computational neuroscience, cognitive science, statistical physics and other disciplines, and it is necessary to fully mobilize experts in relevant fields to participate and strengthen interdisciplinary.
Quantum information: fierce competition among innovation powers
Quantum information is a subject formed by the intersection of quantum mechanics and informatics.
The report shows that in the field of quantum information, the competition of innovative countries is fierce, and the number of basic research and technological research and development achievements continues to increase.
The United States has a clear advantage in quantum computing and quantum measurement.
China's current number of quantum information patents ranks first in the world, the number of papers is second only to the United States, and the scale of quantum communication applications and industrial development are in the leading position in the world, but the level of research and application in the field of quantum computing and quantum measurement is still a certain gap compared with the United States.
In the field of subdivision, quantum computing has the largest industrial influence and is the focus of attention in the field of quantum information.
The future direction of quantum communication is to build quantum information networks based on key technologies such as quantum teleportation, storage relay and conversion.
The report pointed out that the cutting-edge scientific and technological achievements of quantum information are still in the period of exploration and research, and need to carry out in-depth proof of concept, the technology maturity is not high, and there are many difficulties in transferring and transforming.
Therefore, it is necessary to strengthen the communication and collaborative innovation of all parties in the field of quantum information, and organically combine academic forces with industrial resources.
Synthetic biology: the need for continued policy support
Synthetic biology, a new branch of biological science, is an artificial biological system research based on genetic engineering and engineering methods of systems biology.
The report pointed out that in the field of synthetic biology, the United States belongs to the first echelon, and China, Japan and the United Kingdom belong to the second echelon.
From a global point of view, the research of synthetic biology has formed a relatively fixed academic cooperation circle, and the geographical relationship has a greater impact in the cooperation of scientific and technological innovation.
Liu Qiyan said that the development of synthetic biology is still at an early stage and requires continued policy support.
At present, the development of the entire industry still lacks a medium- and long-term clear development plan.
In terms of subdivision, the upstream tool layer is the foundation and key of the synthetic biology technology system, and the competition barriers are high, and the digitalization and artificial intelligence of the midstream are crucial for the rational design of life systems, and technological innovation is difficult.
Solving the problem of large-scale production is the only way to realize the commercialization of synthetic biology products.
In addition, synthetic biology research requires a convergence of disciplines such as life sciences, engineering, informatics, physics and chemistry.
Ethical controversies, biosafety and effective regulation also need to be explored.
Green hydrogen production: renewable energy electrolytic water hydrogen production is the focus
In the field of new energy, green hydrogen production has received much attention in recent years.
According to the report, the use of solar energy, wind energy, ocean energy, water energy and other power generation and then electrolytic water to produce hydrogen, resulting in hydrogen energy, is the focus of green hydrogen production, in the commercial will be able to compete with coal, oil and other fossil energy, but there are still material costs, catalyst activity, gas diffusion layer and other technical challenges.
On the research and development route, China, the United States, Germany, Canada, India and the United Kingdom focus on proton exchange membrane electrolytic water technology; South Korea, Italy and Japan focus on alkaline electrolytic water technology; France focuses on solid oxide electrolytic water.
From the perspective of international competition, in the green hydrogen production, Japan's technology research and development patents ranked first in the world, with an absolute advantage.
China ’ s patent application volume is second only to Japan, but it lacks a global layout.
Among the top 20 R & D institutions in the world, Japan has 15, and all are enterprises.
China has three institutions, but only one company is Huaneng Group.
China's research and development force is still dominated by universities and research institutes, which is easy to cause industrial demand and R & D direction disconnect, and R & D results are not easily converted into products.
Blockchain: China 's R & D level is leading the world
Blockchain is essentially a decentralized distributed database, which is an innovative application model of distributed data storage, multi-center peer-to-peer transmission, consensus mechanism and encryption algorithm in the Internet era.
Blockchain has been used in many industries such as global finance, logistics and transportation, and healthcare.
In the future, with the maturity of technology and the improvement of cognition, it is expected that more industries will begin to explore and adopt blockchain technology.
As blockchain applications increase, personal privacy and authentication issues become more important.
In terms of scientific and technological innovation, global innovation powers cooperate closely in basic research in the field of blockchain, and nearly half of the papers are completed by cooperation between multiple countries or regions.
Among them, the frequent cooperation between China and the United States is the first.
At present, the research and development of blockchain technology is mainly concentrated in the upstream data layer, the contract layer, and the downstream financial field.
China has an absolute advantage in the number of papers and patents at the upper, middle and lower levels, which is especially reflected in the alliance chain, consensus layer in basic research, and the alliance chain in technology research and development, logistics and transportation.
It can be seen that China is leading the world in basic research and technology research and development in the field of blockchain.

Rare earth minerals have been heavily influenced by geopolitics in recent years, and Western countries are trying to bypass China at all stages of the supply chain, with the United States joining Europe, Australia and Japan to launch cross-border cooperation in the field of rare earth.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming more and more advanced, but it also raises related intellectual property issues.
The voice actor (voice actor) of Conan, the protagonist of the Japanese animation "Detective Conan", has been "stolen" by AI, and the songs she covers on the social network are in fact masterpieces of AI. Although the agency is angry and troubled, it can not manage.
According to Yomiuri News, these voice actors are being used without consent, and after being learned by artificial intelligence, they are imitating them to cover songs or read articles aloud.
In order to protect intellectual property rights and prevent abuse, the use of AI must be regulated, experts say.
In July of this year, TikTok appeared "Conan covered the song for me", the video is Conan's "voice", but the singing is completely unrelated to the anime popular song, in fact, it is a work produced by the author using AI.
Conan's character is voiced by the voice of the voice Yo Ko Shannan, and someone in the comments section said, "It seems that Takayama himself is singing."
Takayama's agency 81 Produce said it was not authorized to use Takayama's voice.
"We are very troubled by our inability to do anything about it," said Yoshida, managing director of the brokerage company.
He also said, "I am worried that in the future, AI voice will be used in film and animation dubbing without consent."
The industry must set rules for the use of AI. ”
There are also a number of Kenproduction voices that have been used by artists without permission.
Representative director Kentaro Uchikai said, "There are no regulations on the use of AI sound at present, and it would be really annoying if it developed into something like swearing."
Generative AI takes only a short time to learn the voice of a specific person and imitate it perfectly.
There is also an "AI voice changing system" that can change the sound line to become the voice of others, and it is difficult to distinguish whether it is true or not.
The change in AI ’ s voice has also sparked controversy overseas.
Earlier this year, AI startup ElevenLabs admitted that its speech synthesis tool could be used for “malicious purposes ” and users posted a speech synthesized through“ deepfake ” technology to impersonate British actress Emma Watson to read Hitler ’ s autobiography “Mein Kampf ”.
In Japan, which has a huge voice industry, the sense of crisis brought by artificial intelligence is even stronger.
Article 30-4 of the Japanese Copyright Law stipulates that AI can learn copyrighted works without authorization, and can also learn the lines of animations or movies, which is not illegal.
The revision of the law was originally intended to promote the development of the artificial intelligence industry, but it brought side effects.
In June this year, Japan ’ s Peugeot Union (actors ’ union) said that “AI is easy to encourage imitation and embezzlement, and it is feared that it will infringe on the workplace ”, and called for a revision of Article 30-4 of the Copyright Law, requiring that AI must obtain the consent of the copyright owner before learning.

Women win Nobel Prize in Economics for the first time
The Nobel Prize in economics was awarded to American economist Claudia Goldin for her research on understanding the role of women in the labor market.
Claudia Goldin, a 77-year-old Harvard professor, is the third woman to win the Nobel Prize in economics.
The jury said she “deepened our understanding of the female labor market. ”
In an interview with AFP, Golding said the prize was "important" but there were still "huge" gender inequalities in the labour market.
By studying the history of women in the U.S. labor market, Golding shows some of the factors that historically influenced the supply and demand of female labor, the jury explained.
"She demonstrated that the causes of the gender gap change over time," Nobel committee member Randi Hjalmarsson said in a news release.
Halmason added that while Golding does not research policy, her work provides "the foundational theory" for different policies around the world.
Around 50% of women globally are involved in the labour market, compared to 80% of men, but women earn less and are less likely to reach the peak of their careers, the Nobel Committee noted.
The Nobel Prize in Economics has the fewest number of women laureates.
In addition to Golding, there have been only two other female winners since it was first awarded in 1969: Elinor Ostrom in 2009 and Esther Duflo in 2019.
Claudia Goldin, a 77-year-old Harvard professor, is the third woman to win the Nobel Prize in economics
Golding's Special Contribution
The jury said Golding had "combed through the archives and collected data from the United States for more than 200 years."
Halmsson called Golding a "detective" in the interview and said: "She studied things that many people, like many historians, had previously decided not to study because they thought the data didn't exist."
Golding ’ s research also shows that the trend of women ’ s participation in labor is not always on the rise, but rather a “U-shaped curve ” as the transition from an agrarian to an industrial society takes place.
As the service industry grew in the early 20th century, women ’ s participation began to increase, and Golding explained this trend as a result of “structural changes and evolving social norms. ”
The jury also noted that despite modernisation, such as economic growth and a rise in the share of women in the labour market, the income gap between men and women has barely narrowed over a long period of time.
"According to Golding, part of the explanation is that educational decisions affecting career opportunities for life were made at a relatively young age," the jury said.
Although the historical income gap can be largely attributed to differences in education and career choices, Golding has shown that "this income gap now exists mainly between men and women in the same occupation, and most of it comes with the birth of the first child."
The Nobel committee said Golding ’ s research also demonstrated that the spread of the pill accelerated educational attainment in the 20th century because it “provided new opportunities for career planning. ”

It is reported that the results once again refresh the world record of light quantum information technology, solve the Gaussian Bose sampling mathematical problem than the world's fastest supercomputer 100 million times faster, in the development of a quantum computer is an important step.
Quantum computing is a new computing paradigm in the post-Moore era, with ultra-fast parallel computing capabilities in principle, and is expected to achieve exponential level acceleration compared to classical computers in some problems of great social and economic value through specific quantum algorithms.
Therefore, the development of quantum computers is one of the biggest challenges at the forefront of world science and technology.
The internationally renowned journal Physical Review Letters published the results.
According to the best algorithm published in the public, the speed of Gaussian Bose sampling is 1 million times faster than the previous generation of "Nine Chapters 2". The most complex sample can be calculated by "Nine Chapters 3" in 1 microsecond, and the current world's fastest supercomputer "Frontier" (Frontier) takes about 20 billion years.
China has successfully developed the prototype of the "Nine Chapter Three" quantum computing machine. (CCTV News)
In 2020, a team from China University of Science and Technology successfully built a 76-photon "Nine Chapter" optical quantum computing prototype, achieving the "quantum computing superiority" of the optical system internationally for the first time, and overcoming the loophole that quantum superiority in Google's experiments depends on the number of samples.
In 2021, a team from China National University of Science and Technology successfully developed a 113-photon phase-programmable “Jiuchang No. 2 ” and a 56-bit“ Zuchong No. 2 ” quantum computing prototype, making China the only country to achieve “quantum computing superiority ” in both optical and superconducting technology routes.
The international competitive situation of optical quantum computing. (CCTV News)

Text: Liu Xinxiang
On August 23, US time, a research team from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) and the University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley) used brain-computer interface (BCI) combined with artificial intelligence (AI) technology to convert brain signals into synthetic speech and facial expression animation for the first time. It ’ s faster with any similar technology.
The results were published in the leading scientific journal Nature.
The research was led by Edward Chang, a well-known Taiwanese-born neuroscientist and director of neurosurgery at UCSF Medical School, who has been involved in brain-computer interface research for more than a decade.
Published in NEJM in July 2021, the team translated the brain activity signals of paraplegic people trying to speak into words and sentences and displayed them on a screen for the first time, at a rate of 15 words per minute.
“In this new study, we accelerated the rate of translation of brain activity signals into words while trying to speak to about 78 words per minute. Not only that, we can also directly convert this brain signal into a synthetic speech that can be heard, and present accurate facial movements in a digitized body, ” Zhang said.
The study involved a 48-year-old woman, Ann, who suffered a stroke in her brainstem 18 years ago that left her severely paralyzed, and after years of physical therapy was able to turn her head and control facial muscles like laughing or crying, but the muscles that kept her talking remained motionless.
The team implanted a paper-thin rectangular electrode tablet with 253 electrodes into the cortical surface of Ann ’ s brain ’ s language region and set up a port in her head to connect to the computer via a cable.
This technique, called electrocorticography (ECoG), records the combined activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously.
If Ann had not had a stroke, the nerve signals received by these electrodes could have been transmitted to her tongue, jaw, throat, and face muscles.
Ann trained the system ’ s AI algorithms with the research team for several weeks, and she repeatedly tried to say different phrases from a vocabulary of 1024 words until the computer could recognize her unique neural activity patterns for each phoneme.
Phonemes are the smallest unit of sound in a speech. For example, "Hello" contains four phonemes: HH, AH, L, and OW.
Using this method, a computer can interpret any word in English with just 39 phonemes, which not only improves the accuracy of the system, but also makes it 3x faster.
In order to create a digital double, the research team developed a synthetic speech algorithm, trained on Ann's pre-stroke, wedding speech video files, to create a personalized synthetic speech that sounds like her.
The research team also used a facial animation software developed by Speech Graphics, and used machine learning to transform Ann's brain signals into the muscle movement of the virtual character's face, including the movement of the jaw, lips, tongue, and facial expressions expressing emotions such as happiness, sadness and surprise.
“It felt fun, it was like hearing the voice of an old friend, ” Ann said of hearing the digital duo succeed in speaking in her place.“ Being involved in this research gave me a sense of purpose, I felt like I was contributing to society, and it felt like I was getting a job again. ”
This research makes me feel real! ”
Our goal is to restore a complete and authentic way of communication for the paralyzed, which is the most natural way for people to talk to others.
According to the team, the key to the next phase is to create brain-computer interfaces that do not require electrical wiring.

Science fiction: the rise of Chinese women writers
While the space for feminist expression in China has shrunk further over the past decade, there ’ s good news from this week ’ s World Science Fiction Conference in Chengdu: Chinese female writers are thriving in the science fiction world, making them one of the most striking trends in the genre.
The rise of Chinese female writers in science fiction has become one of the most striking trends in the genre, according to participants at this week's World Science Fiction Conference in Chengdu.
The World Science Fiction Conference, the world ’ s oldest and most influential science fiction event, was held in China for the first time this year and attracted a large number of local fans, both male and female.
China remains a relatively socially conservative country, and under President Xi Jinping, the space for feminist expression has narrowed further over the past decade.
But author and editor Regina Kanyu Wang, who was nominated for two prestigious Hugo Awards at the World Science Fiction Conference this year, said the number of women writers in science fiction has soared in recent years.
She said more and more women are now realizing that "it's not just nerdy, nerdy science-fiction novels like Liu Cixin [author of the three-body series] that can be published, or can be considered science fiction." Liu Cixin is great, and we all like him.
But there's a lot more to it than Liu Cixin's style. "
The good news, says Wang, is that once women start to become writers, they don ’ t feel they ’ re being treated unequally.
The market and readers need a new perspective, she said.
The 81st World Science Fiction Conference will be held in Chengdu from October 18 to 22.
"Now, many Chinese female science fiction writers focus on issues that women face that men may not feel," Zhou Danxue, a literary scholar at XJCC Liverpool University, told AFP. "These writers can reflect unique female experiences in their own way."
Wang said that in the past two years, four anthologies of Chinese fantasy novels written only by female or non-binary authors have been published, which is a major breakthrough.
There wasn ’ t even an all-female science fiction writer ’ s portfolio before that.
Before the 1990s, there were very few female science fiction writers.
An article in the collection "The Way Spring Comes", which Wang Kanyu participated in compiling, pointed out that the Internet is a training base for women and queer talents.
Author Ni Xueting explained that the widespread use of the Internet “not only brought a new sense of community to people, but also … removed many barriers to writing based on industry and social stereotypes, especially for non-male writers. ”
Chen Qiufan, one of China ’ s leading science fiction writers, told AFP that the genre had traditionally not received special attention and was seen as “written and read by boys. ”
He said there was now a "wider and more diverse audience", estimating that his readers were split equally between men and women.
Chinese women writers begin to make their mark in science fiction
Monet, a 21-year-old woman who visited the science fiction convention on Friday, said she sometimes felt isolated among her own fan base.
“It ’ s hard to share my interests with people who don ’ t understand me.
They ask, "Why does a girl like science fiction?"
She is optimistic about these changes in attitude, pointing out that there are a lot of interested primary and secondary school students at the conference site.
“I think interest in Chinese science fiction has to be nurtured from an early age, ” she says.“ We didn ’ t have that opportunity when we were young … I really envy them, to be honest. ”

Recent research by marine biologists at the University of Sydney has revealed the resilience of juvenile crown-of-thorns starfish to heat waves, raising fears that climate change could exacerbate coral reef destruction.
Native to the Great Barrier Reef, it is considered one of the most important coral predators.
In terms of coral mortality, the damage they cause is second only to cyclones and bleaching events.
The study, led by Professor Maria Byrne and published in the journal Global Change Biology, shows that young crown-of-thorns starfish can tolerate high temperatures that are deadly to corals.
This ability to recover allows them to survive heat waves and continue their life cycle as carnivorous predators feeding on newborn corals.
The findings suggest that even if adult crown-of-thorns starfish populations are reduced by warming oceans due to climate change, herbivorous young starfish can wait patiently for the right conditions to grow into coral-eating predators.
This could lead to a resurgence of predator numbers and further destruction of coral reefs.
When water temperatures rise by 1-3 degrees Celsius, climate change already causes coral bleaching and death.
Research has found that juvenile crown-of-thorns starfish can withstand three times the heat that causes coral bleaching.
This ability, coupled with their preference for coral bleaching and death-producing gravel habitats, has allowed their numbers to gradually increase over time.
The researchers also identified factors that help young crown-of-thorns starfish survive warming conditions.
Their smaller size reduces their physiological needs, and their ability to feed on a variety of food sources, including coral algae, enhances their resilience.
The study ’ s co-author, Matt Clements, said the findings highlight the potential role of bleaching caused coral deaths in causing outbreaks of crown-of-thorns starfish.
The loss of natural enemies and the accumulation of nutrients in the water have also exacerbated the effects of climate change on coral reefs.
Further research is needed to understand the impact of these findings on marine ecosystems and coral reef protection.

The United Nations reports that the amount of sand and dust in the global air will increase in 2022.
The increase was attributed to increased emissions in several regions, including central and western Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, the Iranian plateau and northwestern China.
The United Nations World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has called for more research on how climate change is exacerbating dust storm hotspots.
According to the World Meteorological Organization ’ s Airborne Sand and Dust Bulletin, dust storms are caused by human activities such as rising temperatures, drought, increased evaporation and poor land management.
These activities reduce soil moisture and create favorable conditions for the formation of dust storms.
The annual report of the World Meteorological Organization examines the incidence and hazards of dust storms and their impact on society.
According to the report, the average annual concentration of dust on the global dust surface in 2022 is slightly higher than in 2021.
Last year the figure was 13.8 micrograms per cubic meter, compared to 13.5 micrograms per cubic meter in 2021.
The report highlights that about 200 billion tons of dust enters the atmosphere each year, affecting air quality and darkening the skies over thousands of kilometers of outlying areas.
These dust storms have significant impacts on the economy, ecosystems, weather and climate.
Although some dust is a natural phenomenon, a large part of it is caused by poor water and land management.
Notably, the bulletin details three major events in 2022. In 3,500 months, unusual dust storms occurred over Spain and Portugal in North Africa, with peak concentrations exceeding 50 micrograms per cubic meter per hour, well above the EU daily limit.
In October, the Middle East and the eastern United States experienced severe dust storms, affecting visibility and farmland.
World Meteorological Organization President Petrie Taras highlighted the adverse effects of dust storms on health, transport and agriculture, and stressed the need for further research into the relationship between dust storms and climate change, which is relatively unexplored.
The World Meteorological Organization has called for the global implementation of early warning systems for weather hazards, combining sandstorm forecasting skills and early warning services to mitigate the effects of worsening climate change.

Technology continues to innovate, investment opportunities surge
Technological innovation drives the world ’ s progress and provides explosive value addition opportunities for investment.
For example, when the social networking platform Facebook (now Meta) went public in 2012, it was reported to have made 5.4 times as much for some initial investors; the plant meat company Beyond Meat also rose 1.63 times on its first day of listing in May 2019.
With artificial intelligence (AI) in the ascendant, it ’ s time to discover the treasure of the next generation of high-tech investment.
Quantum Computers Solve Complex Computing
The next generation of commercial computers is likely to be the first.
The so-called quantum computer is built on the basis of very complex and difficult for ordinary people to understand quantum mechanics, and its computing power can greatly exceed the "0" and "1" as the base unit of traditional computers.
In particular, in recent years, the progress of computing power in traditional computers has slowed down, but the demand for computing power growth has become increasingly important, making the research and development of quantum computers more urgent.
It takes 5 to 10 years to reach the general purpose
However, on the hardware, the operation of quantum computers to avoid vibration, without interference from electromagnetic fields or even thermal disturbances, so they need to operate at ultra-low temperatures close to absolute zero, involving the use of "superconductors", "helium-3" and other supermaterials, which are difficult for general enterprises to manufacture or assemble.
Therefore, in recent years, technological progress has been made, such as the United States large technology companies such as IBM, Microsoft, Intel and so on.
Among them, IBM was the first to introduce the Quantum System One quantum computer in 2019.
The mainland side, in cooperation with the Chinese Academy of Sciences, recently announced the successful construction of a quantum computing prototype, "Jianchang No. 3".
The computer can process samples of the highest complexity in a millionth of a second, allegedly hundreds of millions of times faster than the most powerful supercomputers available today.
The international mainstream believes that the market will have a universal quantum computer in 5 to 10 years.
With software, algorithms, and application scenarios in place, you can predict the weather more accurately, develop new drugs faster, design materials, and more.
BIOCOMPUTER ENVIRONMENTAL
Biocomputers are not new concepts, but they have recently received renewed attention because the training and use of AI requires powerful computing power and considerable energy consumption.
It is estimated that the energy used to train the AI model is enough to power the average American home for 41 years!
Organ cultivation or ethical issues
The hardware of biological computers is to use human stem cells to grow a large number of brain "organoids". The advantage is that the organoids have a three-dimensional neural structure, which is expected to be better than the planar and process limitations of the chip manufacturing process.
It works by connecting these “brains ” to sensors and output devices and training them with machine learning, big data, and other techniques.
According to Johns Hopkins University scientist Thomas Hartung, although supercomputers can process large amounts of computation faster than humans, the advantages of the human brain are more energy efficient, better at learning and making complex logical decisions.
If you distinguish between cats and dogs, the human brain is easy to complete, and the computer often makes mistakes.
Using cultivated organs to drive computers may have ethical implications, but Hartung said earlier this year that he had gathered 40 scientists to develop a technology called Organoid Intelligence and signed a declaration calling for more research to explore the potential of organoid cell culture to advance understanding of the brain and develop new types of biocomputers, while recognizing and addressing ethical issues.
However, it may be decades before biological computers can become commercially available.
Artificial pollination to save bees
There is a famous saying in the world: "If the bees disappear from the surface, humans will not live for four years", because humans will lose all the plants that transmit pollen by the bees, which will lead to food shortages and human extinction.
This kind of outcome is unthinkable, but in fact, more than 80% of crops are pollinated by insects.
However, climate change affects the number of naturally and artificially bred bees, and studies have suggested that migrating bees to farms to help pollinate crops may lead to a significant decline in native bee populations, which involve competition for food between bee colonies and the introduction of new germs.
China 's first pollinator to assist agriculture
In order to solve the problem of unstable bee numbers and competition among insects, Israeli startup BloomX invented a machine for artificial pollination.
At present, the company's two machines can be applied to two types of fruit trees, namely blueberries and avocados. In the future, the new machines may be designed according to the shape of different plants.
In addition, transporting bees from bee farmers to different agricultural areas for pollination will also involve other problems. First, a long drive will easily kill the bee colony; second, allowing the bee colony to eat unaccustomed nectar in a new environment is not ideal, and the pollination efficiency is not high, which directly affects the number of crops harvested.
So another Israeli startup, Edete, invented a way to collect, store and keep pollen fresh.
The advantage is that when plant pollen is most vigorous, it can be collected and collected manually, and then removed and pollinated when needed, reducing reliance on bees, and greatly improving the efficiency of plant pollination and improving the harvest.

This year ’ s Nobel Prize in Economics was awarded to Claudia Goldin, a scholar of women ’ s employment, who collected more than 200 years of U.S. employment statistics to explore the reasons why women earn less than men.
In fact, Golding mentioned this problem, has always existed since ancient times, think of the great literary heroes we are familiar with, whether at home or abroad, there are several women, as far as our country is concerned, the Tang and Song eight, the great calendar ten talents are all men, and the Song Dynasty lyricist only Li Qingzhao is female.

Taiwan's labor statistics can not be traced back 200 years, but can be traced back 70 years, according to this data, you can find that since the end of World War II, women in employment, labor participation, wages have changed greatly, and let this change occur for two reasons, one is the industrial structure change, one is the increasing popularity of women's college.
45% of the female workforce
Talking about the changes in the industrial structure, in 1951, only 28% of Taiwan's employed population was female, in 1980 this rate rose to 33%, in 2000 broke 40%, and now it has reached 45%, and in a few years, it will probably catch up with men.
Why? This is because the service sector needs a lot of manpower, especially women. The service sector accounted for 70% of GDP in 2001, which brought considerable employment opportunities. Today, there are 450,000 more women than men in the service sector.
Looking at the changes in education, in 1951, only 6,000 students in the campus of the national university, girls accounted for only 15%, with the popularization of education, in 1980 this ratio has risen to 39%, since 2000, boys and girls have been evenly divided, girls get better education, for the future employment of natural help, which not only reflected in the growth of female employment, but also in the increase of wages, to 42 years. From 1980 to 2022, women ’ s wages increased 6.2 times, while men ’ s wages increased 5.3 times, and the pay gap between the two gradually narrowed.
Perhaps some people will think that this is still unfair, why men's total monthly salary of 63,000, is still far higher than women's 52,000? This looks like unfair, but this is the result of different inputs into the industry, women into the service industry, most of the wages are not as good as the manufacturing industry, and the number of men in the manufacturing industry is 40% more than women.
In fact, this is not because of discrimination, but because of the weight of statistics, it is very easy to fall into Simpson's paradox and make a wrong judgment by looking at the final average without delving into the original series.
The role of women in the family does not change.
However, if the problem goes further, it will be found that women are now highly educated, so why do they still have to work in the service industry and engage in some low-paid jobs such as working hours?
The reason is that the family, although the industrial structure has changed in the past 70 years, the academic qualifications have also changed, but the role of women in the family is still not easy to change, from the perspective of family education, mothers take care of the home, is naturally good for children, but for personal achievements is also a loss, but is a loss?
In 1951, Simpson found that in some cases, when groups of data are combined into a group of data, the opposite conclusion is reached, such as the male and female acceptance rates of colleges were originally evenly divided, but the female acceptance rate was low, and the male enrollment rate was higher, and the male enrollment rate was high. But this view is clearly wrong, which is Simpson ’ s paradox.
In the 1950s, the male labor participation rate in the United States and Taiwan was more than 80%, and the female labor participation rate was less than 40% (Taiwan 1951-1952 for a short period of 40%), which was caused by the agricultural society. The participation rate is still much lower than that of men.

Original title: Enhancing people-to-people communication: an effective way to deepen cooperation between Chinese and African universities
The recently held third "Belt and Road" international cooperation summit forum people-to-people thematic forum released the "Silk Road" common initiative, and stressed that further exchanges and cooperation in education and other fields will be carried out to enhance people-to-people communication.
The Belt and Road Initiative is one of the main contents of the Belt and Road Initiative and an important guarantee for the smooth implementation of the Initiative. After the Belt and Road Initiative was proposed in 2013, the Chinese government set up a special scholarship for the Silk Road, which opened a new era of Belt and Road higher education exchanges.
Africa is an important part of the Belt and Road international cooperation. Fifty-two of the 54 African countries have signed the Belt and Road cooperation documents with China. China ’ s education cooperation with Africa began in 1956, and large-scale university cooperation began in 2009 with the “China-Africa Cooperation Forum – Sharm el-Sheikh Action Plan ”.
In the plan, China "proposes the implementation of the '20 + 20 Cooperation Plan for Chinese and African Universities', selecting 20 Chinese universities (or vocational education colleges) and 20 African universities (or vocational education colleges) to establish a new model of 'one-to-one' inter-university cooperation."
This plan was further emphasized in the 2015 FOCAC Johannesburg Plan of Action and the 2018 FOCAC Beijing Plan of Action. In July 2023, the Chinese Society of Higher Education and the Association of African Universities (AAU) jointly established the China-Africa University Alliance Exchange Mechanism, and its secretariat and research institute were also established in Beijing Foreign Studies University and Zhejiang Normal University respectively.
Based on interviews with most of the participating institutions and Confucius Institutes in Africa in the “20 + 20 Cooperation Program between Chinese and African Universities ” and the sorting of relevant documents, this paper puts forward some suggestions for further deepening cooperation between Chinese and African universities from the perspective of ensuring project effectiveness and sustainable development.
The program needs to be aligned with the university ’ s own development mission.
University cooperation is a bilateral international activity, and cooperation with non-universities cannot be regarded as a unilateral aid, but needs to be considered in the light of the unique attributes of the university itself and the mission of the university itself.
From the perspective of the existing project implementation, the significance of the implementation effect is closely related to the position of discipline in the discipline system of the university.
If the content of cooperation happens to be a key subject of the university, then cooperation will be highly valued and implemented more smoothly.
For example, the cooperation between Nanjing Agricultural University and Egerton University in Kenya has not only promoted the development of the two sides, but also strengthened the social impact of Egerton University, which enjoys a high reputation in the agricultural field in East Africa.
If the university itself already has a teaching and research strategy for Africa, it will also help the development of the China-Africa university partnership.
For example, Zhejiang Normal University has set up an African Studies Center since 2003, and its comparative education discipline also focuses on African education research, which plays an important role in the overall development of the school.
For example, the Middle East Institute of Peking University has long established the Arabic Department, and has a long history of cooperation with Cairo University, and many teachers and students have gone to Cairo University to study, which has played a positive role in its growth and development.
Setting up collaborative projects that can “grow in African soil ”
“Studying Africa and understanding Africa ” is the key to the success of China-Africa university cooperation.
On the one hand, it is necessary to understand the development stage and development needs of different countries on the continent at a macro level, so that cooperation projects can be adapted to the country's development strategy.
Africa is a diverse continent, encompassing different economic, social and political patterns, and therefore has different development needs and priorities.
Some countries already have relatively developed economies and high levels of per capita income, such as Morocco, Tunisia and Mauritius.
Other countries are becoming centres of information technology and innovation, such as the S & T ecosystem in Kenya, e-government in Rwanda and the S & T Innovation Centre in Egypt, but others face serious challenges in poverty reduction, food crisis, disease treatment and peace maintenance.
On the other hand, there is a need for an in-depth understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of higher education and the development needs of different African countries in order to embed cooperation projects in their development plans and become priorities.
Higher education on the African continent shows diversity and diversity, and its stages of development are also very different.
Some countries have world-renowned universities or disciplines, such as archaeology at Cairo University in Egypt, medicine, engineering, computer science at the University of Cape Town in South Africa, economics and law at the University of Ghana, and medicine and engineering at the University of Nairobi.
Many universities are actively developing and implementing development plans to meet the development needs of the country and society, such as Cape Coast University in Ghana, Lagos University in Nigeria and Dar es Salaam University in Tanzania.
Countries in conflict and turmoil, such as Niger, Burkina Faso, Somalia, South Sudan and Libya, have struggled to develop higher education.
As a result, in the Union of Central African Universities, some universities have remained largely in aid relations, others in cooperation that can benefit from each other, and some disciplines are learning from Africa.
In short, only on the basis of understanding Africa and African higher education, can scientific cooperation projects be set up to "grow in the soil of Africa".
Strengthening cooperation in agriculture, forestry, water, medicine and humanities and social sciences
African countries, confined to their own stage of development, have given priority to agricultural modernization and industrialization.
In terms of cooperation in higher education, Confucius Institutes, the "20 + 20 Cooperation Plan for China-Africa Universities", the Luban Workshop, and the "Future Africa-Africa Vocational Education Cooperation Plan" have contributed to the cultivation of talents for improving people's livelihood and modernizing governance in Africa.
The main areas that have taken root and achieved remarkable results are agriculture, forestry, water science and engineering, medicine, language and teacher education.
Future cooperation should encourage more agricultural and forestry universities, high-level comprehensive universities with water science and engineering, normal universities, and higher vocational colleges to participate in the current scale of cooperation.
In the field of medicine, the Chinese government has made remarkable contributions in providing medical supplies, building medical facilities, providing vaccine assistance, and sending medical experts and medical teams to Africa to provide medical services and technical training.
Cooperation between universities in the future can explore new ways, such as establishing medical education centers in Africa, or making full use of modern distance learning resources and artificial intelligence to create new types of joint medical education programs. Livestock is also an important industry in Africa, while animal medicine is a discipline lacking in Africa, and relevant fields can be incorporated into university cooperation.
He said that Sino-African cooperation in the fields of humanities and social sciences has a long history and has made great contributions to the people-to-people
From the successful experience of existing projects, language education, teacher education and modern governance are still key areas of cooperation.
In addition, Chinese universities can jointly set up research centers on local history, languages, cultural heritage and social dynamics in African universities on the basis of full research, thus jumping out of the one-way aid mindset and training Chinese talents who understand Africa and understand Africa.
Optimize project operation mechanism
A good working mechanism is the key to the success of the project.
Operational mechanisms include project rules and procedures, resource allocation and management, communication and collaboration, feedback and adjustment, monitoring and evaluation.
Only when both parties participate in the development and implementation of the operational mechanism can the project be successful.
The Confucius Institute has become a successful model of cooperation between Chinese and foreign universities after 20 years of development.
However, there are also some cooperation projects that need more financial and resource support from Chinese and African universities, so as to enhance the importance of cooperation, participation and support of the management and staff of the two sides.
Another important factor affecting the success of the cooperation is the cultural and linguistic background, and in the course of the cooperation, both sides have had difficulties in continuing the project due to poor communication.
Therefore, the establishment of clear and efficient communication and cooperation mechanisms is the key to the success of cooperation.
At the same time, it should also be noted that barriers to communication and difficulties of understanding caused by different cultural and linguistic backgrounds require both sides to actively strengthen cultural exchanges and promote mutual understanding and adaptation.
In addition, supervision and feedback are the key to project optimization and entering the virtuous circle, which is a relatively weak link in the mechanism construction.
In the future, in the process of policy entering a new cycle, the actual participants, stakeholders, researchers, etc. of the project should participate in policy formulation, actively listen to the existing problems and suggestions for improvement, so that the project setting is more in line with the logic of scientific development, which is the key to the project not being a formality.
(Author: Tian Xiaohong, Associate Research Fellow, School of Education, Zhejiang Normal University)

"Myosclerosis" has become a very concerned health issue in recent years, especially for the elderly, myosclerosis not only brings reduced muscle mass and insufficient strength, but also accompanied by decreased mobility, weakened physical function, and even greatly increased the risk of falls, if the elderly themselves have osteoporosis plus myosclerosis, there will be a higher risk of fracture.
In order to help the elderly fight against sarcopenia, it is important to conduct an integrated assessment through professional doctors, physiotherapists and coaches!
Chen Chung-wen, a coach at Muscle Wellness Physiotherapy and Exercise Science Center, points out that cross-professional integrated assessment of the elderly with muscular dystrophy can be used to design exercise programs more safely and effectively to stimulate the bones and muscles of the body, and improve the body ’ s function and mobility.
Chen says that the so-called "load type resistance training" is the use of different load levels and methods, such as their own weight, elastic band and free weight, to stimulate muscle growth.
For the elderly, load-based resistance training should follow the concept of “gradual ”, starting with a“ light ” load, such as using your own body weight or using a low-weight load method, and assisting the elderly through movement design similar to the function of daily life.
The Center for Physiotherapy and Exercise Science also offers a few simple, easy-to-learn ways to help the elderly fight against muscular dystrophy together.
Coach Fang Jen-chun teaches you the first move is to "squat against the wall". The movement setting first needs to stand about half a step away from the wall, and the back is flat against the wall; then, keep your toes facing forward and your heels full of the floor; and finally, squat to an acceptable position, at most level with the ground.
Fang said that each time you perform a "deep squat against the wall" should stay for 10 seconds - 1 minute, rest for 1 minute between groups, and repeat 3-4 groups.
Pay attention to the soles of the practitioner's feet on the ground, knees to the second toe, the core force, neck, waist should be flat against the wall.
This exercise can train the muscles of the hips and legs, as well as the core muscles, strengthen the muscle strength of the trunk and lower limbs, increase the muscle endurance, and increase the body control ability. It has been proved that this exercise can effectively control blood pressure.
The second move is "core power", the movement setting first let the practitioner lie flat on the ground, then extend the hand directly above the shoulders, pointing to the ceiling; then bend the feet 90 degrees above the hip, can roll the hand to the cheek, knee straight.
Repeat 6-8 times on both sides of the movement group, rest for 1 minute between groups, and repeat 2-3 groups.
Fang Renjun pointed out that the second action should pay attention to the core force, the neck and waist should be flat on the ground, and at the end of each execution, it should return to the center of the starting position.
In this way, the core muscles of the trunk are trained, and the core strength and muscle endurance are strengthened to increase the body control and the stability of the lumbar spine.
As for the third move is the "four-legged kneeling posture", the action settings first let the hands and shoulder width, shoulder, elbow, wrist straight line; then let the feet and pelvis width, knees under the hip; then let the stomach slightly retract, head, neck, waist straight line, and finally lift the knee slightly off the ground.
This action group lasts 30 seconds – 1 minute, interval 1 minute, repeat 3-4 groups.
Fang Jen-chun stressed that the shoulder should be directly above the wrist and the knee under the hip, and the back and the ground should be kept level. This is the correct action.
Training arm, trunk core and lower limb muscle groups helps strengthen arm, trunk core and leg muscle strength and muscle endurance. Through contact training with the floor, the elderly can understand how to react even if they accidentally fall, so that the injury is minimized.
Finally, Fang Jen-chun also reminded that appropriate sportswear should be worn for “load-bearing resistance training ”. The sports venue should be kept open and free of obstacles. In addition, pay attention to physical conditions during exercise, keep normal breathing, and rest and replenish water in a timely manner.
The above group number is the recommended amount of exercise, each exercise should be based on personal circumstances and increase or decrease; depending on the situation of each person, if there is any discomfort, please take a rest and seek professional assistance.

In the wake of the pandemic, digital nomad has become the latest form of work, and many people who can “work remotely ” have begun to travel to other countries around the world, taking vacations and working with their computers.
In a survey of digital nomads, three cities in Vietnam are among the top 10 most visited places in the world for digital nomads: Da Nang, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.

According to Nomad List, the world ’ s largest database of remote workers, Da Nang, a coastal city in central Vietnam, ranks second behind Tokyo, Japan, with a 109% increase in the digital nomadic population in 2023; Hanoi ranks seventh with a 58% growth rate; and Ho Chi Minh City ranks ninth with a 55% growth rate.
Most Vietnamese cities have excellent wireless access, low cost of living, and beautiful scenery, making them the latest darling of digital nomadic workers around the world.
Of these three cities in Vietnam, Da Nang is considered the third largest city in Vietnam after Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, with free Wi-Fi in the city center, fast internet speeds and beautiful coastline.
An important factor for digital nomads considering a temporary city is the living environment, as well as the cost of living to meet the convenient and comfortable working environment, while the cost of living in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City is quite low.
The average cost of living for a number of nomads in Hanoi is US $1,289 per month (about NT $38,000) and in Ho Chi Minh City US $1,157 per month (about NT $34,000).
Other places on the list are Seoul, South Korea, in third place; Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in fourth place; Penang, Malaysia, in fifth place; Montevideo, Uruguay, in sixth place; Manila, Philippines, in eighth place; and Lubjana, Slovenia, in tenth place.
To compile the list, experts at Nomad List ranked the fastest-growing cities for remote workers by analyzing nearly 300,000 registrations in the database over the past two years.
Vietnam, with three cities on the list, does not offer a “digital nomad visa ”, but it offers global travelers from nearly 200 countries the ability to easily apply online for e-visas for up to 90 days, and in Southeast Asia only Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia offer special digital nomad visa programs for foreigners to work remotely if they meet certain requirements.
