The doctor ’ s words / people ’ s old heart is not old to solve the aging myth
In recent years, the average life expectancy of humans around the world has been increasing.
According to WHO estimates, by 2030, one in six people worldwide will be over the age of 60.
By 2050, the number of people over 60 will double to 2.1 billion.
By that time, the number of people over the age of 80 will have doubled to 426 million.
While older populations are now more common in high-income countries (for example, 30% of Japan ’ s population is now over 60), low- and middle-income countries are also experiencing the biggest changes.
In the face of the increasing number of elderly people, the first thing to do is to eliminate the many paradoxical myths associated with aging.
1 Is it normal to be depressed?
The image of the older people today is completely different from that of the old days, and they are still full of vitality even at the age of 70.
From the point of view of clothing and lifestyle, in addition to the pursuit of fashion, but also accustomed to consumption.
Unless there is a specific illness, it is common for the elderly to travel and enjoy life.
If you suddenly feel depressed, feel annoyed about everything, lack of interest in activities and going out, or suddenly feel uneasy about life, it is necessary to consider whether depression is the cause of the phenomenon rather than naturally occurring due to aging.
In addition, the elderly who live alone for a long time will obviously feel lonely, and even cause depression and anxiety, which are not normal phenomena of aging.
What the family should imagine is that these elderly people want to be cared for and cared for by their family and friends.
2 Don ’ t you need to learn new things?
This is a big misunderstanding, older people still have the ability to learn new knowledge, new technologies, and according to the research of neuroscience experts, in the learning process, neurons are stimulated to increase activity, and the connection between each other is increased, which relatively delays the aging of brain cells.
For example, learning a new language, photography or practicing the piano can improve the quality of life of the elderly, increase physical and mental pleasure, and slow down the aging of brain cells.
3 Don ’ t you need to sleep too much?
Many people believe that older people need less sleep, and it is likely that this idea is based on stereotypes of older people getting up early.
In fact, according to a study by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), people aged 61 to 64 need seven to nine hours of sleep per night. People over 65 need seven to eight hours of sleep per night.
It is also believed that older people need more sleep than younger people.
This statement is sometimes due to changes in hormone levels, affecting the rules of the circadian rhythm, so if the quality of sleep is not good, daytime naps are also natural.
4. No need for exercise?
The source of this theory is likely to be the fear that the elderly will fall and hurt, so they will not dare to go out to exercise or exercise.
In fact, regular exercise can increase blood circulation, improve cardiopulmonary function, and reduce the risk of high blood pressure, blood sugar, and lipid disease.
Generally speaking, gentle exercises such as tai chi, eight danjin, and five birds can improve balance and reduce the risk of falling.
In addition, many people think that exercise does not have any benefits when they are older.
In fact, a study in the Journal of Aging reported 42 weeks of weightlifting training for adults aged 60 to 80.
Participants were found to have increased dynamic muscle strength and muscle size and motor function after training.
And the vast majority of the elderly can engage in moderate sports activities.
5 Responses to Looking for an Elderly Woman?
This is most likely due to a report by the International Osteoporosis Foundation that around a third of women over the age of 50 worldwide suffer from osteoporosis.
At the same time, one in five men will have a fracture associated with osteoporosis.
Only according to the latest reports, the rate of bone loss in men and women is almost the same after the age of 65.
Another related myth is that osteoporosis in women is inevitable with age.
In fact, two-thirds of women over the age of 50 do not have osteoporosis.
If you improve the level of hormonal disorders early, taking foods containing calcium and vitamin D, combined with regular exercise, can prevent osteoporosis.
6 Is Quitting Smoking Meaningless?
This is not true, according to the National Institute of Health Research, no matter how old you are, how long you smoke, or how many cigarettes you smoke every day, once you quit smoking, your health will begin to improve. While some health benefits can be noticed immediately, others will be effective over time.
No matter what, it ’ s never too late to quit smoking.
7 Responses to Unwanted Sex?
Some people think that they gradually lose the ability to enjoy sex.
According to a report in the International Journal of Clinical Practice, 0.4% of men aged 18 to 29 have erectile dysfunction, and 11.5% of men aged 60 to 69.
But turning this statistic upside down is not so scary, because nearly 90% of men over the age of 60 do not have erectile dysfunction.
According to the HSIN Scientific Research Society, this idea is a big misunderstanding, because aging does not necessarily end a healthy sex life.
In the West, it is particularly emphasized that both men and women of old age may exhibit very active sexual life until very old age.
Therefore, the American Psychological Association recommends that you do not deliberately endure and force yourself.
The brain nerve that controls desire is not in the frontal lobe of the brain.
If the body's organ skills are not used, it will degenerate, deliberately suppress desire, reduce or suppress the chance of frontal nerve activity, and also accelerate the decline of the brain.
In fact, desire is an innate instinct that motivates us to generate motivation and desire.
Whether it is appetite or sexual desire, it should not be too suppressed to delay the brain nerve aging in the frontal lobe area.
8 Is dementia inevitable?
According to WHO research, the risk of dementia increases with age, but it does not include all older people.
Around the world, it is estimated that 5-8% of people over the age of 60 suffer from dementia.
This means that 92% to 95% of people over the age of 60 do not suffer from dementia.
In the United States, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 13.9% of people over the age of 71 suffer from dementia.
In other words, 86.1% of the elderly over the age of 71 do not suffer from dementia.
Do you see if your cognitive abilities decrease as you age?
Contrary to popular belief, a decline in cognitive ability does not necessarily mean that dementia is about to begin. Although people with dementia often experience a decline in cognitive ability, not all people with dementia will experience dementia.
According to research estimates, 22.2% of Americans over the age of 71 have problems with cognitive decline, and only 11.7% to 20% of them have dementia.
Thankfully, in 2015, the Alzheimer ’ s Association assessed the relationship between cognitive decline and dementia.
Maintaining regular physical activity and strict control of cardiovascular diseases such as diabetes, obesity, smoking and high blood pressure significantly reduce the risk of cognitive decline, according to a report submitted to the World Council on Dementia.
Healthy eating, constant learning, and cognitive training can also reduce the risk of cognitive decline.
Age is just a symbol of life, in the current society should look at old age from a positive point of view, no matter how old, should re-understand old age, good planning of life, remember that people should not be old.
(The author is a practicing physician in the Greater Washington area)

Singapore-based quantum software startup Entropica Labs has recently secured a $4.7 million Series A funding round.
It is understood that the financing was jointly led by Italian deep technology investment institution Liftt and its existing investor Wavemaker Partners, with participation from SEEDS Capital (the investment arm of Singapore Enterprise Development Authority), CerraCap Ventures, SUTD Venture Holdings, Elev8 and others.
According to the statement, the funds will be used to expand Entropica Labs ’ team building in the areas of quantum error correction, software engineering and computational architecture.
Entropica Labs was founded in 2018 to provide developers and users with software development tools that enable quantum computers to recognize and correct errors during computation, helping them improve accuracy and efficiency in quantum computing.
Entropica Labs says that as hardware companies continue to roll out larger and more advanced quantum computing systems, some of which have crossed computational thresholds, the demand for complex error correction schemes in the field has become more intense, so Entropica Labs hopes to enhance the space for quantum computers with scalable software tools.
According to the official website, Entropica Labs has now launched two products, OpenQAOA and JEPOS, the former is a multi-end and open source Python software development kit for quantum computer optimization, and the latter can be used for benchmarking quantum performance.
It is worth mentioning that earlier this year, another Singapore-based quantum computing startup called Horizon Quantum Computing also received a Series A funding round.
It is understood that the size of the financing is 18.1 million US dollars, and the investors include Tencent.

Sea and air transport low carbon fuel popularity slow 2050 net zero carbon emissions stumbling block
More than 130 countries have declared net zero carbon emissions by 2050.
However, the world ’ s carbon-emitting maritime and aviation industries are still in the embryonic stage of low-carbon sustainable fuel use, mainly because traditional fuels are still difficult to replace when dealing with high energy density and long-distance navigation.
Under the 2015 Paris Agreement, nearly 200 countries around the world agreed to work to reduce warming to less than 2 degrees Celsius by the end of the century compared to pre-industrial levels, and to try to keep it below 1.5 degrees Celsius.
The 28th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP28) will be held in Dubai from November 30 to December 12 in the United Arab Emirates, where the phasing out of fossil fuels will be the focus of the agenda.
According to The National, aviation accounts for 2% of global carbon dioxide emissions, and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), made from waste cooking oil, agroforestry biomass waste and other raw materials, is seen as an important option to curb aviation ’ s carbon footprint because net CO2 emissions are much lower than fossil fuels.
According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the amount of sustainable aviation fuel contracted between fuel suppliers and airlines increased from 2.38 billion gallons in 2021 to 5.8 billion gallons in 2022.
However, the International Energy Agency believes that by 2027, low-carbon fuel production will only meet a small proportion of aviation fuel demand.
Mark Martin, chief executive of aviation consultancy Martin Consulting, told The Nation that the cost of producing sustainable jet fuel is 20 to 40 times higher than the average jet fuel.
The current oil infrastructure is used to convert crude oil into refined products such as diesel and petroleum, but producing sustainable aviation fuels requires a “whole new level ” of technology.
Air France-KLM Group, a French-Dutch consortium, has invested $4.7 million in the sustainable aviation fuel industry ’ s DG Fuels plant in Louisiana, US, on track to achieve a 10% share of sustainable aviation fuel use by 2030.
“The company has been given the option to purchase up to 25 million gallons or 75,000 tons of sustainable aviation fuel per year for a period of several years starting in 2029, ” the Air France Group said in a press release today.
The European Union reached an agreement earlier this year to set binding targets for European airlines to increase the use of clean fuels.
The agreement stipulates that by the end of 2025, suppliers must guarantee that 2% of the fuel supplied to EU airports will be clean fuel, then increase to 6% by the end of 2030, 20% by the end of 2035, and 70% by the end of 2050.
In the United States, the world ’ s largest aviation market, Washington aims to work with the aviation industry to achieve an annual production of 3 billion gallons of sustainable aviation fuel by 2030, and plans to achieve the goal of all aviation fuel as sustainable aviation fuel by 2050.
The US inflation reduction bill, which came into effect last year, provides fuel producers with a tax cut of $1.25 per gallon.
International shipping, which accounts for more than 80% of world trade and about 3% of global anthropogenic carbon dioxide emissions, has made little progress in decarbonization. The aging of ships is also a factor in the negative net zero carbon emissions of the maritime industry.
At the beginning of 2023, the average ship age of the world ’ s ocean shipping is 22.2 years, and more than half of the ships are more than 15 years old. These ships are old enough to be refurbished, but they are not yet obsolete, and they are at an awkward time.
In addition, the adoption of alternative fuels in the maritime industry is still in its infancy.
According to the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), 98.8% of ships are still on fossil fuels.
According to UNCTAD ’ s Review of Maritime Transport 2023 in September, only 21% of new ship orders use clean energy.
UNCTAD estimates that the annual cost of decarbonization of the global maritime fleet could be as high as US $28 billion by the end of 2050, not including up to US $90 billion per year for infrastructure that uses 100% carbon neutral fuels.
On the other hand, the International Maritime Organisation raised its decarbonisation targets for the maritime industry this year and confirmed the development of new fuel standards and greenhouse gas emission pricing mechanisms.

Silver hair health _ How to deal with the elderly in the face of degenerative disability? Expert Tutor 4 Training
Author: Heho Health
Published: Updated:
Your body is old, not by ID card, but by vitality!
Active energy means that you are free to do what you want without physical limitations or physical disturbances, such as being able to walk, climb stairs, take things, dress, climb mountains, etc.
If the activity is good, anything can be done alone, indicating that the body is young, on the contrary, life can not take care of itself, low activity, is old!
With age, many elderly people are at risk of degeneration and disability of physical function, which affects not only their daily lives, but also their mental health and social activities.
Therefore, exercise training for the elderly is an indispensable health care measure that can help them to enhance muscle strength, muscle endurance, joint mobility, balance and coordination, thereby improving quality of life and delaying the effects of aging.
Sports Training for the Elderly (see below)
+ 23
However, exercise training for the elderly is not an easy task, and suitable plans and methods need to be developed according to the physical condition, exercise experience and goals of the individual. The training principles and techniques adopted by the elderly vary greatly from age to age.
Coach Will pointed out that the exercise training for the elderly can be divided into two categories according to the purpose: one is to improve bone density and balance, prevent falls and fractures; the second is to enhance cardiopulmonary capacity, prevent and improve metabolic fitness and chronic diseases.
This type of exercise training is designed to address the common physical problems of the elderly.
Anti-fall, anti-bone loosening, anti-muscle less muscle training
Mainly muscle training and movement control, Coach Will explained that bone density changes with age, hormones, diet, exercise and other factors.
If bone density is insufficient, it can lead to bone loosening, increasing the risk of fracture after a fall.
An important factor affecting bone density is body load, that is, the weight or pressure the body is subjected to.
If the body is not loaded enough, it will reduce the stimulation to the bones, which will prevent the bones from being renewed and strengthened.
Muscle strength training can boost bone density by increasing muscle mass and strength and increasing body load.
Balance refers to the ability of the body to maintain stability in different postures and movements.
Balance is affected by vision, hearing, vestibular system, muscles and joints.
If the balance is not good, it is easy to lose the center of gravity and fall.
An important factor affecting balance is muscle strength.
Coach Will, for example, some elderly people actually have a good sense of balance, they know that they are going to fall, and they know how to restore balance, but they do not have enough muscle strength and control to pull themselves back, so they have not been able to prevent the fall from happening at the moment of losing balance.
Therefore, the use of muscle training to help the elderly to enhance balance and body control is also the key to preventing falls.

+ 5
Three high looking for the door?
Cardiopulmonary endurance training promotes metabolic fitness
Controlling the three highs mainly depends on cardiopulmonary endurance training. Coach Will said that cardiopulmonary ability can affect metabolism, blood circulation and so on.
If the ability is not good, it is prone to poor metabolism, fatigue, easy asthma and other symptoms, and reduced daily activities will also increase the chance of chronic diseases.
Cardiopulmonary endurance training can improve cardiopulmonary function and metabolic fitness to prevent chronic diseases by increasing the intensity and time of exercise.
Elderly training principle: be able to cope with daily needs
When training the elderly, the main goal is to enable them to cope with the daily needs of daily life, such as shopping, walking, and traveling abroad.
These activities not only increase the physical activity of the elderly, but also increase their social interaction and psychological satisfaction.
Therefore, we will design suitable sports according to the needs and preferences of the elderly.
Sports coaches will also take care to control the amount of training, so that the elderly do not exercise too much or become too tired.
If the amount of training is too large, it may cause physical injury or counter-effect.
Trainers will adjust the intensity, frequency and duration of training based on the physical response and recovery of the elderly. They will also use testing tools or questionnaires to assess the physical function and health risks of the elderly.
Coach Will recommends that exercise training for the elderly should be done in the form of a small number of meals, that is, do some moderate exercise every day, instead of doing a lot at a time or only a few times a week.
This can make it easier for the elderly to digest and adapt to the load of exercise, and also allow their bodies to maintain a certain level of activity.

+ 2
Adjust training orientation according to age group
1.
50 ~ 60 years old
The elderly in this stage usually have certain work or family responsibilities, and there are also some high level of leisure activities, such as mountaineering, golf, tennis, etc.
They are trained to reduce the risk of these activities, such as joint wear, muscle strain, and so on.
At the same time, they also have a forward-looking concept, that is, to lay the foundation for the future of aging to prepare.
Therefore, they will pay more attention to movement control, muscle strength and muscle endurance training, and will also prefer sports performance or specific training.
2.
70 ~ 80 years old
The elderly at this stage usually have retired or reduced their workload. There are also some chronic diseases or sub-health conditions, such as three highs and joint discomfort.
Their training orientation is to delay disability and maintain self-care in daily life.
Therefore, they will pay more attention to balance, coordination and flexibility training, and will also prefer functional and leisure training.
3.
Over 90 years old
The elderly at this stage usually already have some degree of disability or cognitive impairment and need help or care from others.
Their training orientation is to maintain a quality of life and reduce physical and psychological discomfort.
Therefore, they will pay more attention to social interaction, emotional management, and cognitive stimulation training, and will also be more relaxed and fun training.
Remind everyone that exercise training for the elderly should be based on the physical condition and goals of the individual to make plans, not blindly follow others or mess with themselves.
It is recommended that the elderly before starting sports training, first find a professional coach and doctor to do an assessment to understand their physical strengths and weaknesses, and then according to the recommendations of the coach or doctor, choose the appropriate sports items, intensity, frequency and time, so as to ensure that the exercise training of the elderly is both safe and effective.
Sports training for the elderly is not only beneficial to the body, but also beneficial to the mind. Sports can make the elderly feel happy, confident and fulfilled. It also allows them to make more friends, increase social activities and enrich life.

As competition in the workplace intensifies, young Chinese are moving into Africa to pay for gold, escape and rebel.
Photo Credit: Getty Images / BBC News
What we want you to know is
In the past, in addition to French majors, working in Africa was basically not a consideration for Chinese fresh graduates. Language barriers, safety issues, cultural differences and other factors deterred them.
But slowly, with increasing competition in the workplace, Africa has entered the vision of more and more young Chinese.
Chen Zhuo, 20, was born into a rural family in central China with a younger brother.
In order to reduce the burden on his family, he chose to work immediately after graduation, instead of continuing his studies.
He began looking for a job when he was recruited on the campus in the autumn of 2022, and over 1,000 resumes were sent to domestic enterprises in the past six months, but he did not realize a suitable job when he graduated.
Despite his family ’ s concerns, after weighing up, he eventually accepted a job as far away as Africa.
In the face of China's economic downturn and high youth unemployment, there is fierce competition in the workplace, especially for young people like Chen Zhuo who graduated from ordinary colleges and universities.
He studied international trade at an ordinary university in Chongqing, and by the time he graduated, only a dozen of the more than 50 students in his class had landed their jobs.
With the increasing frequency of China-Africa economic and trade exchanges, a large number of Chinese enterprises have entered many African countries, and more and more young people who have graduated from universities have turned their eyes to Africa and tried to find a way out there.
In June, Mr. Chen arrived in the western African country of Ghana with trepidation, but later found out that it wasn ’ t as bad as he thought.
“Before I came to Africa, I was worried about eating badly, getting sick often, and having a lot of mosquitoes, but then I realized that these things didn ’ t exist, ” Chen told the BBC.
In the past, in addition to French majors, working in Africa was basically not a consideration for Chinese fresh graduates. Language barriers, safety issues, cultural differences and other factors deterred them.
But slowly, with increasing competition in the workplace, Africa has entered the vision of more and more young Chinese. Some people value the opportunities brought by China ’ s growing investment in Africa, and the local thriving Chinese community, thinking about the future of entrepreneurship; and some young people want to experience multi-culture and improve their foreign language skills in Africa.
Growing interest and demand
There are no reliable statistics on the number and geographical distribution of young Chinese working in Africa.
But on Chinese social media, interest in sending jobs to Africa is growing.
On Weibo, the topic “Will you consider sending to Africa with an annual salary of 200,000? ” soared to the top of the hot search list at the end of July this year, with a reading of 200 million articles and nearly 300,000 people participating in the interaction.
On the social platforms where young people gather, Little Red Book and BiLi BiLi, some of the writers filmed work experiences in Africa that attracted millions of people. In the comments section, many people asked how to go to Africa, how to choose a company, whether it is safe there, and so on.
“More and more young Chinese are working in Africa, not only in large state-owned enterprises, but also in smaller groups and even individuals looking for entrepreneurial opportunities in Africa, ” said Maria Repnikova, an associate professor of international communication at Georgia State University in the United States.
She studied Chinese in the African context.
“This demand comes in large part from large projects in China, especially in the infrastructure and technology sectors. ”
“This trend is not balanced development, but depends on the security and economic conditions of specific African countries, ” Professor Repnikova noted.
Based on her research experience in Ethiopia in northeastern Africa, the Chinese community there has shrunk over the past four years due to the COVID-19 (Severe Special Infectious Pneumonia, COVID-19, Wuhan Pneumonia) pandemic and war.
Interestingly, some Chinese did not choose to return home after leaving, but moved to other countries in Africa.
China has been Africa ’ s largest trading partner for the past decade.
According to official statistics, China-Africa trade reached US $282 billion in 2022, an increase of about 11% year-on-year; at the same time, the number of Chinese enterprises in Africa has almost doubled to about 3,500.
After arriving in Accra, the capital of Ghana, Chen said, it was a constant surprise.
In a downtown shopping mall, there are quite a lot of Chinese retail brands in the vicinity, and there are also Chinese-owned hot pot shops, KTV, milk tea shops, hotels and so on.
He even ate northern Chinese pork with green onion buns and Henan snacks with horseradish soup.
“If I hadn ’ t seen the black-skinned locals, I would have thought I was in China, ” he says.
In the past, Chinese companies in Africa mostly recruited contract workers in the form of labor exports and tended to hire experienced people for management positions, but now some Chinese companies in Africa seem to be starting to favor young people with technical and managerial potential.
A recent graduate, Chen is already a sales manager for a Chinese-owned heavy construction equipment company in Ghana.
High salary attraction
Many young Chinese say that one of the main reasons for attracting them to work in Africa is the high salaries.
First of all, most young people have a small studio of their own. The company will provide meals suitable for Chinese tastes, and pay for round-trip air tickets, visa fees and so on.
Second, in addition to the basic salary, many companies will also pay employees high distribution subsidies and hardship subsidies, as well as bonuses, commissions and so on.
At Chen Zhuo ’ s company, as a freshman at his university, all expenses add up to earn at least 200,000 RMB a year.
The general assignment contract is signed every year or three years, then three years down, deduct the expenditure, "at least can save 500,000".
Chen Zhuo comes from a rural family, and this level of wages has greatly reduced the burden on the family.
He took out his first month's wages and bought a necklace for his mother to send back to his hometown, bringing much comfort to her mother who was afraid.
By contrast, with his qualifications as a freshman at an ordinary university, he earns at most about NT $10,000 a month from working in a big city, and almost nothing is left after deducting expenses such as rent and transportation.
However, there is endless solitude behind the high salary.
Even though there are many entertainment venues open by Chinese people, the comfort and technical content cannot match the domestic level.
In the past few months, Chen Zhuo has not yet figured out how to use his spare time to fight loneliness.
Occasionally, when he is criticized by his boss at work, he will write a diary at night to express his inner loneliness.
But beyond that, he is generally satisfied with his life and work here.
For him, a good income is more important, after the end of the contract period, he will still consider staying to continue working.
“Young after all, ” he said.
Joshua Eisenman, an associate professor of political science at the University of Notre Dame, said it was “surprising ” that China, which for years had hoped for an economic rise to attract overseas youth back to China, was willing to work so far away, or that it had to go so far to find opportunities.

"We will analyze how employees respond to an extra day of rest, including stress and burnout, job and life satisfaction, health, sleep, energy use, travel and life," she said.
The government-backed four-day work week trial will also begin in Spain and elsewhere later this year.

Record breaking for four key climate change indicators in 2021
KATHAN / NOURSAN / 18 May – Four key climate change indicators – greenhouse gas concentrations, sea level rise, ocean heat and ocean acidification – set new records in 2021, according to the United Nations Information Service.
According to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), this is another clear sign that human activities are causing changes in the interior, oceans and atmosphere around the world, with lasting and harmful impacts on sustainable development and ecosystems.
The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) is the United Nations system's authority on weather, climate and water.
The agency ’ s State of the Global Climate Report 2021 confirms that the past seven years have been the warmest on record. 2021 was “just ” one of those seven warmest years because of the La Niña events at the beginning and end of the year.
The La Niña event produced a temporary cooling effect, but did not reverse the overall trend of rising temperatures. The global average temperature in 2021 was about 1.11 (± 0.13) ° C above pre-industrial levels.
Getting out of the “dead end ” of fossil fuels
On the occasion of the launch of the flagship report, UN Secretary-General António Guterres criticized "humanity's dismal record in tackling the problem of climate degradation".
He called for urgent action to seize the "low-hanging fruit" of the energy system transformation and get out of the "dead end" of fossil fuels.
In his video message, Guterres identified five key actions to kick-start the renewable energy transition.
These include acquiring more renewable energy technologies and supplies, tripling private and public investment in renewable energy, and ending subsidies for fossil fuels, which currently amount to around $11 million per minute globally.
Guterres said:
- Renewable energy is the only way to real energy security, stable electricity prices and sustainable employment opportunities.
If we act together, the renewable energy transition can be a peace project for the 21st century.
He stressed that we must take global action within this decade to prevent worsening climate impacts and keep warming below 1.5 ° C above pre-industrial levels.
The heavy cost of inaction
U.N. General Assembly President Shahid said the report was yet another reminder of how costly inaction can be.
The report ’ s conclusion is clear: we are losing the battle to control climate change, and we cannot stop environmental degradation.
We have the resources, the skills and the technology, we have the science that tells us the need to fight climate change: what we lack is political will.
As a small island resident who is very aware of the risks of sea-level rise, I am well aware of that.
As President of the General Assembly, I remain hopeful that this urgency will translate into increased political will and collective action. - He said.
Early warning is key.
Professor Talas, Secretary-General of the World Meteorological Organization, said:
- It's only a matter of time before we see the next warmest year on record.
Climate change is happening before our eyes.
The heat captured by human-caused greenhouse gases will warm the planet and affect generations.
Unless technologies to remove carbon from the atmosphere are invented, sea level rise, ocean heat and acidification will continue for hundreds of years.
Some glaciers have become irreversible, and this will have long-term implications for a world where more than 2 billion people are already suffering from water stress.
Taras further stated:
Extreme weather has the most direct impact on our daily lives.
Years of investment in disaster preparedness mean that we are better able to save lives, even as economic losses continue to soar.
But we have a long way to go.
The drought emergency that the Horn of Africa is experiencing, the recent deadly floods in South Africa, and the extreme heat in India and Pakistan are right before our eyes.
He stressed that "early warning systems" are key to adaptation to climate change, but less than half of WMO member states have them.
As requested by Secretary-General António Guterres, we are committed to making early warning accessible to everyone over the next five years. »
The World Meteorological Organization ’ s report on the state of the global climate, released on the eve of the World Economic Forum ’ s 2022 annual meeting in Davos, Switzerland, on May 22, will also become an official document of the United Nations climate change negotiations (the 27th Conference of the Parties) in Egypt later this year.
Key Message
Greenhouse gas concentrations
In 2020, the greenhouse gas concentration reached a new high in the world, and in 2021, the greenhouse gas concentration continued to increase.
Temperature
The global average annual temperature in 2021 was about 1.11 ± 0.13 ° C above the pre-industrial average in 1850-1900. The last seven years (2015-2021) were the warmest on record.
Ocean heat
Ocean heat reached a record high. In 2021, the upper 2,000 meters of the ocean continued to warm up, and it is expected to continue in the future – a change that is irreversible on a timescale of 100 to 1000 years.
This warming is continuing to penetrate deeper. In 2021, most of the seas experienced at least one “strong ” ocean heat wave at some point in time.
Ocean acidification
The oceans absorb about 23% of the carbon dioxide that humans emit into the atmosphere each year.
This reacts with seawater and leads to ocean acidification, threatening biological and ecosystem services and, in turn, food security, tourism and coastal protection.
As ocean pH declines, so does the ocean ’ s ability to absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
Sea level rise
The global average sea level rose by an average of 4.5 millimetres per year between 2013 and 2021 before reaching a record high in 2021.
This rate is more than double the rate between 1993 and 2002, mainly due to the accelerated loss of ice in the ice sheet.
This has had a significant impact on hundreds of millions of coastal residents, increasing their vulnerability to tropical cyclones.
Cryosphere
Although the glacier year 2020-2021 is less melting than in recent years, there is a clear acceleration in ice loss over a decades-long timescale.
Since 1950, the world's benchmark glaciers have thinned by an average of 33.5 metres (ice equivalent), 76 per cent of which occurred after 1980.
2021 was a particularly bad year for glaciers in Canada and the northwestern United States.
Due to heat waves and fires in June and July, ice loss was record.
In mid-August, Greenland experienced a special melting event and recorded its first ever precipitation at the summit station, the highest point of the ice sheet at 3,216 meters above sea level.
heatwave
An unusual heatwave in 2021 broke records in western North America and the Mediterranean. On July 9, high temperatures reached 54.4 ° C in Death Valley, California, and 48.8 ° C in Syracuse, Sicily. On June 29, the temperature reached 49.6 ° C in British Columbia, Canada.
Floods
The floods in China's Henan Province caused economic losses of 17.7 billion U.S. dollars. In mid-July, western Europe experienced the worst floods on record, and the economic losses in Germany exceeded 20 billion U.S. dollars.
The loss of life was heavy.
Drought
The drought affected many parts of the world, including the Horn of Africa, Canada, the western United States, Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan and Turkey.
In the subtropical region of South America, drought has caused enormous agricultural losses, disrupting energy production and river transport.
The drought in the Horn of Africa has intensified so far in 2022.
East Africa is facing a very real prospect: a fourth consecutive quarter of no rain, which has plunged Ethiopia, Kenya and Somalia into a 40-year drought.
Hurricanes
Hurricane Ida, the largest hurricane of the season in the North Atlantic, made landfall in Louisiana on August 29, causing an estimated $75 billion in economic damage to the United States.
The ozone hole
The ozone hole over Antarctica is very large and deep.
Under the influence of strong and stable polar vortices and below-average temperatures in the lower stratosphere, the maximum area reached 24.8 million square kilometers (equivalent to the area of Africa).
Food security
The combined effects of conflict, extreme weather events and economic shocks, exacerbated by COVID-19, have undermined decades of progress in improving global food security. The worsening humanitarian crisis in 2021 has also put an increasing number of countries at risk of famine. More than half of the total undernourished people in 2020 live in Asia (418 million) and a third in Africa (282 million).
Displacement
Hydrometeorological hazards continue to lead to internal displacement.
As of October 2021, the countries with the highest number of documented displaced persons are China (more than 1.4 million), the Philippines (nearly 390,000) and Vietnam (more than 660,000).
Ecosystem
Some ecosystems are being degraded at an unprecedented rate.
For example, mountain ecosystems – the world ’ s water towers – have been severely affected.
Warming increases the risk of irreversible loss of marine and coastal ecosystems, including seagrass meadows and kelp forests. Coral reefs are particularly vulnerable to climate change.
They are expected to lose 70 to 90 per cent of their original cover area at 1.5 ° C and more than 99 per cent at 2 ° C.
Depending on the rate of sea-level rise, 20-90% of the current coastal wetlands are likely to disappear by the end of the century.
This will further damage ecosystem services such as food supply, tourism and coastal protection.

Marine Ecology and Healthy Coral Reefs
Corals can provide a sound marine ecosystem, including habitats, food and nutrient sources, tourism and educational resources, and maintain the marine food chain and ecological, species and genetic diversity. Corals have an annual production value of about US $11 trillion.
The rich coral colonies in the world ’ s oceans make a huge contribution to marine ecology, especially in East Asia, which accounts for 30.1% of the world ’ s coral reefs.
For example, corals can protect land from typhoons and waves, which are better than human-made jetties.
Many of the new drugs are also sourced from the ocean, such as postagladin (PG), which has anti-cancer effects, from the sea fan extract, and moschicidin, which has viral suppression and anti-cancer effects, from the coral root.

Warming, overfishing impacts fishing
However, due to human activities and global warming sea temperature anomalies, coral reef coverage in various ocean regions around the world has decreased since 2011, and algae cover has increased, affecting marine biodiversity, which in turn affects fisheries, food supply and tourism in coastal areas.
For example, in Kenting and Penghu in Taiwan, the disruption of urban development and tourism activities has also led to changes in coral reef species.
The documentary “Chasing Coral Reef ” presents the bleaching phenomenon of undersea coral reefs, exposing the ecological crisis under global warming, and trying to awaken people ’ s awareness of protecting the environment and protecting the marine ecology.
About 25% of fish depend on coral for their entire lives, but at least 500 million people around the world rely on “reef fish ” as a staple food. Without these proteins, these 500 million people would be starved of nutrients.
The series "Ocean Conspiracy" mentions that most of the current offshore fishing industry uses trawling nets to catch fish, especially giant trawls can net the entire church, 13 Boeing 747 aircraft, resulting in serious catches of sharks, whales and dolphins, and the use of bottom trawls to cause overfishing and destroy the coral and bottom marine ecological foundation.
Since 1950, the Endangered Species Index (Endangered Species Index) of the upper marine life chain (e.g. tuna, swordfish) has deteriorated by about 27%, while the shark Endangered Species Index (Endangered Species Index) has continued to deteriorate.
Calcium, Iron, Protein Supply Slide
Dr. Xu said that marine aquatic food provides a wealth of important nutrients, and seafood intake is conducive to nerve development and function, prevent coronary heart disease, and reduce the risk of diabetes.
In addition, fish provides more than 20% of the animal protein for 3 billion people worldwide, and small fisheries in developing countries such as Bangladesh, Ghana and Indonesia supply more than 50% of animal protein.
A study conducted a 10-year assessment of marine nutrition in temperate and tropical regions. It is estimated that a 4 ° C increase in global warming by 2100 will cause a 30% decrease in the nutrient supply of developing countries. If the increase is controlled at 1.5 to 2 ° C, the nutrient supply will also decrease by about 10%. Global Warming Is Like Chronic Disease Marine Ecology Conservation Focuses on Three Major Aspects
Professor Chen Xiuxi explained that the three major aspects of marine ecological conservation include biodiversity, marine food supply, and ocean carbon sequestration.
It was assessed that maintaining 45% of marine protected areas would increase biodiversity by 71%, carbon sequestration by 29%, and food supply by 92%.
Coral reefs and benthic flora are important elements that provide carbon sequestration and reduce ocean acidification, but under the influence of industrialization, the ocean ecology changes.
Global warming, like chronic diseases, reduces the number of fish and plants and algae when certain organisms begin to degenerate and increase, and reduces overall biodiversity, thus affecting the human environment and the more extreme climate.
In the face of climate change and climate warming, as well as human activities, the impact of overexploitation on the entire environment and ecological diversity has attracted global attention.
Sustainable biodiversity and social development pursue three main goals.
Reduce carbon emissions
Mitigate climate change and maintain global warming trends in order to maintain a livable ecological environment.
Rehabilitation and care
Maintaining sustainable ecological habitats and biodiversity.
Maintaining natural ecosystems
Support the symbiosis of human society.
Land, freshwater ecology and marine settlement biodiversity are interconnected.
Humans are part of these three ecosystems on Earth, and the impact of human activities on the environment can be divided into three levels, including extensive pristine natural habitats, support for biodiversity, and nature-social symbiosis.
Australia is committed to biodiversity conservation through a combination of native colonies and modern scientific capabilities to achieve coral conservation; the EU is also focused on restoring biodiversity and has set many goals to be achieved by 2030, such as reaching 30% of land and marine protected areas, reducing pesticide use by 50%, and restoring the free flow of 25,000 km of EU rivers.
In addition, “digital twin ” has become an important technology for international ecological sustainability. Compared to traditional methods, digital twin can consider more factors and respond to various potential situations in real time, and can also help people understand the overall ecological and evolutionary trends to achieve sustainable biodiversity.

Time-restricted feeding (TRE)
For example, the early hours and the late hours.
Intermittent fasting (IF)
For example: 168 fasting method, the daily calorie intake is concentrated in 8 hours, and the remaining 16 hours can only consume zero calories of things such as water, salt, black coffee, tea, and eat by counting the time instead of counting calories.
Intermittent Time-Restricted Feeding (iTRE)
Combine the above two characteristics.
Overweight – Limited-Time Diet and Intermittent Diet Affect Health
The long-term effects and safety of a limited time diet (TRE) for weight loss are unclear. One study divided 139 obese patients into a limited time diet group, eating only from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. with calorie restriction; another group had daily calorie restriction.
The results showed that at the 12th month of the experiment, the diet group lost an average of 8.0 kg and the daily calorie restriction group lost an average of 6.3 kg. There was no significant difference in weight change between the two groups.
In addition, the analysis of waist circumference, BMI, body fat, blood pressure, and metabolic risk factors was consistent with the main results, while there was no substantial difference in adverse event occurrence between the two groups.
Overall, for obese patients, a limited time diet was not more beneficial than daily calorie restriction in terms of weight loss, fat loss, or improved metabolic risk factors.
(Liu D, et al.

2022)
Another study of overweight and obese young adults, divided into morning intermittent eating (eTRE), evening intermittent eating (lTRE), control group (no dietary restrictions), 8 weeks later found that eTRE and lTRE achieved weight loss; eTRE reduced systolic pressure, mean blood sugar, fasting insulin, insulin resistance, leptin and leptin. In the case of glandular axis activity, lTRE can reduce leptin, indicating that intermittent eating in the morning or at night can achieve certain health effects (Zhang LM, et al. iScience., 2022).
High Blood Glucose – Intermittent Limited-Time Diet Improves Blood Glucose
An Australian trial studied people with type 2 diabetes in three groups: iTRE (eating from 8am to 12am three days a week with calorie restriction, fasting for 20 hours, and unrestricted for the remaining four days), calorie restriction group, and standard care group.
Glucose changes in the iTRE group showed greater improvement after half a year, however, these differences disappeared at the 18th month.
Another study found that the fatigue rate was higher in the iTRE group compared to the calorie restriction group and the standard care group, while the constipation and headache rates were higher in the iTRE and calorie restriction group compared to the standard care group.
Overall, iTRE can significantly improve post-meal glucose metabolism in people with type 2 diabetes (Teong, X.T., et al.
Nat Med, 2023).

Look at the sleepless tricks of the world.
December 09, 2023 08: 41 Source: Beijing Youth Daily
Have you ever been depressed because you have difficulty falling asleep, or have you finally fallen asleep, but you have not slept soundly and wake up repeatedly? The sleep problem has always been a global health problem, and while there is no one-size-fits-all solution, people around the world have found the best sleep aid for themselves.
Let ’ s take a look at this and it may be helpful to improve your sleep quality.
China
Soak your feet with hot water.
If you like to do hydrotherapy or pedicure, you may want to try this method.
This practice before going to sleep stems from traditional Chinese medicine, which is a great way to relax, it can soothe tired body and mind and get the benefits of hot water immersion therapy.
All you need is a bath or foot basin, and different soothing ingredients can be added to the hot water, such as bath salts, lavender or rose oil, peel and certain herbs (such as wormwood).
According to traditional Chinese medicine, these ingredients can reduce the amount of "qi" in the brain.
A slightly higher temperature can pull the "gas" from the head and play a sedative role.
Using hot blisters to relax the limbic system and send signals to the brain and body to “relax ” in preparation for sleep.
Eat jujube seed products
Chinese medicine uses jujube seeds to soothe the brain and mood, promote relaxation and deep sleep.
Jujube seeds contain saponins and flavonoids, two chemicals that both suppress stress and promote relaxation.
These two chemicals also help to prolong sleep.
Specifically, flavonoids can extend the duration of slow-wave sleep.
Slow-wave sleep is the most rejuvenating part of sleep.
It is related to memory and learning, and the lack of this sleep can lead to a decrease in function and alertness during the day, and a feeling of not being awake when you wake up.
A randomized clinical trial conducted by nursing scientists at the Medical University of Ahwaz Judi Shapur in Iran required 106 postmenopausal women to take 250 mg of jujube seed capsules twice a day for 21 consecutive days.
The results showed that compared with the control group, taking jujube seeds significantly improved their sleep quality.
India
Herbal remedies
In the traditional medicine of India (Ayurveda), Indian ginseng (also known as Afrikaner) has been used for thousands of years as an important sleep aid herb.
It is used to reduce stress and anxiety and to support the treatment of symptoms associated with mental health.
A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study by sleep physicians at the International Institute of Sleep Sciences in India asked 150 healthy adults to take 120 mg of Indian ginseng daily for six weeks.
The results showed that the therapy shortened the time to fall asleep, improved the quality of sleep, reduced the time of non-restorative sleep, and improved the quality of life.
A systematic review and meta-analysis conducted by family physicians at the University of Science Malaysia found that Indian ginseng has a significant role in improving sleep quality, especially for insomnia patients.
It can also reduce anxiety and improve mental alertness.
However, more safety data is needed to determine its potential side effects.
Health scientists at Murdoch University in Australia have found that taking Indian ginseng reduces anxiety and lowers morning cortisol levels compared to placebo.
Cortisol is a stress hormone produced by the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis (HPA), which causes sleep disruption.
Sweden
Eat elk meat.
According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, 100 grams of elk meat contains 30.2 grams of protein and 0.545 grams of tryptophan.
In contrast, 100 grams of turkey chicken contains only 19.5 grams of protein and 0.219 grams of tryptophan.
Food scientists at the National University of Singapore have found that taking nutritional supplements containing tryptophan helps with sleep.
Drink cereal milk powder
One sleep aid for adults and children in Sweden is to drink cereal milk, a hot drink containing milk and cereal, before going to bed.
Hot milk guides sleep and contains sleep-promoting compounds such as tryptophan, magnesium, melatonin and serotonin.
Guatemala
Owns a worry-free doll
Worry-free dolls are handicrafts of the indigenous people of the highlands of Guatemala.
It was made of wood, wire and colored fabric and then put on a traditional Mayan costume.
The doll is usually given to anxious children, who are encouraged to put the worry-free doll under the pillow before speaking out about their worries and fears.
Locals believe that this symbolic act helps cope with difficult emotions and smooth sleep, which is a healthy form of diversion.
Psychologists at St. Luke's Hospice in Plymouth, England, have found that worry-free dolls can provide psychological support to bereaved children to prevent them from feeling too sad and helpless.
South and Central America
Use of hammocks
If you like to swing in an outdoor hammock, consider hanging one indoors. Hammocks are a popular sleep tool in South and Central America because they are both safe and comfortable.
While most of the sleep benefits of hammocks are based on infants, neuroscientists at the University of Geneva in Switzerland examined how hammocking movements promote deep sleep. Twelve men took naps for 45 minutes on different days, one on a fixed bed and another on a swinging hammock.
Using data from multiple sleep maps and electroencephalograms, the researchers found that napping in a swinging bed shortens the time to fall asleep and extends the sleep duration of the second stage (light sleep, the stage before deep sleep).
Russia, UK and other countries
Drink chamomile tea
As a global sleep aid method, especially in countries such as Russia and Britain, people have the custom of drinking chamomile tea to help them fall asleep.
This tea has a soothing and calming effect.
Chamomile tea contains celery that binds to receptors in the brain, causing drowsiness and relaxation, making it a natural way to fight insomnia and other sleep disorders.
Nursing scientists at Islamic Azad University in Iran have found that oral chamomile extract has a sedative effect on hospitalized elderly patients and improves their sleep quality.
Japan
Sleeping Tatami
Tatami is a traditional Japanese bed that is often used for sleep or rest. A mattress can also be added to the tatami to increase the comfort of sleep.
It not only saves space, but also helps to promote sleep.
Mattresses are usually made from environmentally friendly and natural materials such as cotton and wool.
Using this mattress helps relieve back pain and provides support for the spine.
Finland
Sauna
Finnish people use a sauna at night as a traditional sleep aid.
The process of using steam to treat the human body in a closed room can raise body temperature, relax muscles and induce sleep.
Biomedical scientists from the Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology in Australia have found that sauna has benefits for a variety of physical and mental diseases, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, congestive heart failure, peripheral artery disease, rheumatoid arthritis and anxiety and depression.
In a survey of 482 respondents, 83.5% of people were able to get a good night ’ s sleep after a sauna session, and those who had a sauna session five to 15 times a month had higher levels of psychological well-being.
During the sauna, make sure to drink plenty of water.
As long as there is enough water in the body during the sauna, you can sleep as sweet as a baby.

A recent study by scientists at Incheon National University has revealed the effects of climate change on marine microbes and subsequent changes in greenhouse gases in the ocean.
The results of this study contribute to a better understanding of the severity of climate change and the importance of marine resources.
Climate change drivers such as ocean warming, acidification, deoxygenation and nitrogen deposition have harmful effects on vulnerable microbial populations in the oceans.
These changes disrupt the marine microbial community, which plays a vital role in the production of greenhouse gases such as nitrous oxide (N2O) and methane (CH4).
The research team, led by Professor Il-Nam Kim, studied the simultaneous effects of climate change factors on marine microbes in the western North Pacific.
By assessing prokaryotic population changes and metabolic changes, scientists have gained insight into how climate change affects marine ecosystems.
The study highlights the close link between prokaryotes and drivers of climate change in different layers of the ocean.
The findings suggest that long-term exposure to identified climate change factors may lead to increased N2O production, altered pH, and ultimately increased CH4 emissions.
These results challenge previous assumptions about the potential of prokaryotic and biogeochemical processes associated with climate change, underscoring the need to reassess the impact of climate change on open ocean ecosystems.
Understanding the complex relationship between climate change and marine microbes is critical to developing effective strategies to mitigate the impacts of climate change on marine ecosystems.
By implementing policies aimed at reducing ocean acidification and warming, microbial communities and the greenhouse gas cycle in the oceans can be stabilized.
This groundbreaking research has the potential to influence future research into marine ecosystems.
It highlights the importance of considering the role of microbes in understanding the impacts of climate change and highlights the urgent need to prioritize the conservation of marine resources.

Possession of huge lithium mines is more like a curse for African countries.
Photo Credit: GettyImages
What we want you to know is
Africa is rich in lithium, but the report released by the NGO Global Witness points out that lithium mining may cause damage to local communities and the environment.
According to the report, “Africa ’ s mining industry has been linked to corruption for decades, and the public has not been able to truly share in the profits, a trend that continues in the lithium sector. ”
Written by Kate Hairsine
Local workers working at a lithium mine in Namibia complain of poor living conditions and unsafe working methods.
The Namibian Miners Union conducted an investigation into the Uyse mine operated by the Chinese mining company Xinfeng Investment and found that the accommodation conditions of the employees were not good, not only the space was narrow, the indoor was hot, and there was not enough ventilation equipment.
The union also criticized the lack of privacy in health facilities and the substandard of safety measures such as protective clothing, compared with the better treatment of working and living conditions of Chinese workers.
However, this is not the only controversy surrounding Xinfeng.
Worrying corruption trends
Global Witness, a non-governmental organization, has filed new charges against Sunfung.
Global Witness pointed out in a report that the use of small-scale mining licenses to develop lithium mines meant that the company paid “ridiculously low ” fees to mine and circumvented some environmental regulations.
The group also added that the lithium mines in the Congo and Zimbabwe violate human rights, corruption and unsafe working conditions.
Colin Robertson, one of the authors of the report, said: “Africa ’ s mining industry has been linked to corruption for decades and the public has not been able to really share in the profits, a trend that continues in the lithium sector, which is very worrying. ”
The Battle of Lithium
Lithium, which has a wide range of important applications in the field of new energy, is known as "platinum".
It is a key component of lithium-ion batteries, from mobile phones to electric vehicles, and it is inseparable from its existence.
At present, the world ’ s lithium suppliers are mainly concentrated in Australia, Chile and China, and 90% of the total lithium raw material mined worldwide in 2022 will come from these three countries. Although Africa ’ s lithium reserves account for only about 5% of the world ’ s total, its huge development potential cannot be underestimated.
Zimbabwe and Namibia currently export lithium ore, and Congo, Mali, Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Ethiopia are developing mining.
The International Energy Agency predicts that demand for lithium ore will grow 40-fold by 2040, and some big countries, as well as commercial giants, are working to mine lithium in Africa, and many African countries are hoping to seize the opportunity.
Zimbabwe has the largest lithium reserves in Africa and ranks sixth in global lithium exports, with lithium exports reaching US $209 million as of September 2023, almost three times as much as last year.
Zimbabwe, like the governments of Namibia and Tanzania, has banned the export of unprocessed lithium ore.
However, the ban is often ignored: the Global Witness survey found that large quantities of lithium ore are still being transported out of the country by truck.
In addition, Zimbabwe Defence Industries, a military-linked company sanctioned by the United States and the European Union, has a special license to export lithium ore to China.
"Lithium is a curse."
Farai Maguwu, director of the Zimbabwe Natural Resources Governance Center, is not optimistic about the benefits of lithium mining to Zimbabwe.
He believes that under the current system, the abundance of lithium deposits is more of a curse for Zimbabwe.
In an interview with Deutsche Welle, he said: "Lithium mining may lead to the collapse of the country."
The communities involved have had to pay for the cost of mines, land loss, biodiversity loss, etc., because there is no guarantee that the state can prioritize income over local systems. ”
The Sandawana mine, known for producing emeralds and other gems, is an example.
In early 2023, the mine was reportedly taken over by companies linked to Zimbabwe ’ s ruling party and the military. Magouu believes there is “no magic cure ” for corruption in Africa ’ s mining industry.
More Western mining companies should invest in lithium mining in Africa, and such companies are often more stringent in environmental management and other standards.
Concerns about Chinese monopolies
China has almost a monopoly on lithium mining in Africa.
According to estimates by consulting firm Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, about 83% of Africa ’ s supply of lithium in 10 years involves China.
In 2022, three Chinese mining giants acquired $678 million worth of lithium mines and projects in Zimbabwe.
According to a recent report published by the Zimbabwe Environmental Law Association, “Single-country leadership in lithium mining can lead to adverse consequences, such as underestimating the value of mineral resources, tax avoidance and human rights violations. ”
Robertson, of Global Witness, called on the European Union and the United States to ensure greater transparency in the mining industry and greater oversight by local activists to combat corruption.
Maguu stressed that the benefits of mining projects should be given back to communities in the form of roads, medical facilities and schools: “We see untapped mineral resources as our natural capital, and local people, as well as children, should benefit from them. ”

C919 Visit Hong Kong _ How strong are Chinese aircraft? Compete against Boeing 737 and Airbus A320
Author: Au Jingluo
Published: Updated:
China ’ s C919 visited Hong Kong and gave a flight demonstration over Victoria Harbour on 16 December. What is the difference between the C919 and the C919, which is the first large domestic aircraft and is regarded as a rival to similar models of Boeing and Airbus?
Cut-off and flight distance
The C919, Boeing 737-MAX and Airbus A320neo are all narrow-body aircraft, three of the same size, designed for short and medium routes.
The first comparison is the passenger capacity and flight distance:
C919: Standard passenger capacity 168 people, range about 4600 km
737-MAX 8: Standard passenger capacity of 178 people, range of about 6,500 km
A320neo: Standard capacity of 194 passengers, range of about 6,500 km
In terms of passenger capacity, the C919 has a passenger capacity of 168 to 190, which is not comparable to the 737-MAX 8 and the A320neo, but it is not far apart.
The C919 and the other two use CFM LEAP engines (-1A, -1B and -1C respectively), both of which are of the latest generation.
Theoretically, the distance between the three should be similar, but this is not the case.
Due to the design and use of different components, the C919's fuel capacity and efficiency are low, so the range of the 737 MAX and the A320neo is not comparable, which has an impact on the flight distance.
China Southern Airlines' first Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft (registration number B-1206) landed at Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport. (Weibo @ China Southern Airlines)
Cost and production
Then there ’ s the build price, which is $99 million for the C919, down from $121 million for the 737-MAX 8 and $111 million for the A320neo.
However, it is not surprising that aircraft manufacturers will slash prices to attract orders, even at a 50% discount, and the C919 needs the same discount to attract airlines to buy.
Because the C919 is currently almost exclusively ordered by Chinese airlines, it is difficult to compare with the international sales of Boeing and Airbus aircraft.
However, since this is a domestic aircraft, it is believed that it will be cheaper to attract domestic airlines to buy it under state subsidies, and may be cheaper than the 737-MAX 8 and A320neo.
COMAC claims that nearly 1,200 orders have been placed for the C919, but only a few have been delivered on the production line.
China Commercial Aviation has indicated that it will reach a production rate of 150 aircraft per year within five years, which is still a long way from Boeing and Airbus producing about 60 aircraft per month.
Pictured is an A320neo from ITA Airways on April 28. (Reuters)
Three Days in the Future
As COMAC increases its production, it can be expected that Chinese airlines will prefer to opt for the C919 over other aircraft.
Airbus CEO Guillaume Faury has said that the C919 will make the narrow-body market a "three-point world" in the next decade, at least in China.
At present, the biggest resistance to the C919 is the international market. It is difficult to expand overseas because it is not certified by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) or the European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA).
However, as China Commercial Aviation continues to improve its aircraft, it is almost certain to increase its passenger capacity and range to the equivalent of the 737-MAX 8 and the A320neo.
When the C919 or future model gets international certification and exports, it will change the situation of the two-headed monopoly of Boeing and Airbus for decades.

Argentine Economy Minister Luis Caputo announced a series of economic measures on December 12 to launch “shock therapy ”.
Argentina ’ s 11 provinces declared a state of economic emergency on Wednesday in response to the central government ’ s sharp cuts in spending.
Eleven provinces, including San Diego del Estero and San Luis, have declared a state of economic emergency.
The St. Louis provincial government said it was severely short of funds to operate and couldn ’ t even pay its employees ’ December salaries.
Some provincial governments said they would not follow the central government in adopting austerity measures.
Argentina ’ s new government announced the launch of “shock therapy ” on the 12th to try to solve the economic crisis, including devaluing the currency peso by 54% and slashing government spending.
These include reducing the number of government departments from 18 to 9, reducing government subsidies for energy and transportation, and stopping tenders for new public works.
The government says economic reforms will help lift the country out of the economic crisis, but Argentines will have to endure months of pain, with prices expected to rise 20% to 40% in the coming months.
Argentine Economy Minister Roberto Caputo said on Wednesday that the goals of the dollarization plan promised by President Javier Milei during his campaign remain unchanged, stressing that the idea is still valid even if the future is painful.

Travel + work, is it possible?
Remote work has become a new normal in the workplace, so long as you have a laptop and a stable network, you can move the “office ” to any corner of the world.
Whether it ’ s surfing season in the Philippines or winter in Chiang Mai, the “digital nomad ” lifestyle is no longer just an imagination.
After 90 years, Kristie and Kate quit their jobs during the epidemic to join the digital nomad, living and living in a different place, and returning to the rhythm of life. Kristie said, “Nomad ’ s gift to me is to help me clean up my life and start again. ”
While the reporter was writing in the newspaper, Kristie, who had returned from Xinjiang for less than a month, flew to Chiang Mai, Thailand. Browse her sharing on social media platforms, she enjoyed the sunshine while leisurely working with her laptop in the open coffee shop, so that the reporter “grape ”“ bathed ” in the white light tube was very good. Kristie began her digital nomad career early last year. Bali, northern Thailand Chiang Mai, and then to Switzerland, a full year did not return to Hong Kong, "began the journey about 1 month, I have decided to live such a life in the future."
Get up at 8 and 9 a.m. every day, go to the beach, meditate, and work efficiently for 4 hours. After dusk, learn new things, read books, and live the creative life that many wage earners dream of.
He made $50,000 a month at the peak of his career.
Before the pasture, she worked in the advertising industry, and her body and mind were eroded by the pressure of work, and she suffered from chronic gastritis, "(sometimes) pain so that she could not eat all day, and she would vomit after eating."
Finally, the doctor said that even if the prescription of many drugs is useless, because my life pressure is too big, let her decide to change the environment, for their own life to a big clean.
At that time, she took the initiative to propose a 30% pay cut to her superiors, and switched from full-time employees to freelance workers.
There is no regular income, employee welfare, she confessed that "initially very scared, suddenly lost the sense of security", so she had saved six months of living reserve before leaving to prevent zero income during the period; and for themselves to open up a new source of income, operating from the media, doing small business.
She also became an oblique person, relying on writing advertising copy, public relations and marketing planning to maintain the nomadic living expenses, peak monthly income can reach 50,000 yuan, the off-season income is only more than 10,000 yuan, but stretched to make up for the short, life is still good.
In particular, she is mostly nomadic in Southeast Asia, where the consumption is low and the quality of life is good. Taking the island of Phangan in Thailand as an example, she lives in an independent holiday home, with a monthly expenditure of about 12,000 Hong Kong dollars, such as clothing, food, housing and travel.
Low prices, good living, Indonesia, Thailand, a hot spot
In addition to freelancers like Kristie, there are also people engaged in online teaching, design, e-commerce, programming and other remote work, as well as enterprises due to industry characteristics, full-time employees can also work remotely, such as Kate working in the web3.0 industry. Web3.0 is a decentralized Internet based on blockchain technology, NFT, cryptocurrency, metaverse and other popular technology concepts in recent years. It is based on Web 3.0 technology.
Kate, 24, who worked as an occupational therapist for a year after graduating from college, found that she did not like working in fixed locations and hours, and wanted the freedom to travel while working as a digital nomad.
She is interested in cryptocurrency, so she turned to web3.0, engaged in marketing, operation of blockchain projects and other work, usually through online communication with colleagues.
"Web 3.0 is a more international company, with employees from all over the world, most of them do not have a physical office, and many times employees can only choose to work remotely."
It ’ s like living three or four different lives.
Every time she goes to different places to participate in seminars, and after completing her work, she will stay there for 1-2 weeks, traveling all over Japan, Thailand, Australia, Singapore, France, etc. Although she is a full-time employee, she has no fixed office hours, sometimes she does not need to turn on the computer all day, she can go sightseeing, sometimes she needs to meet and meet constantly. Bring a computer, wired headphones and plenty of mobile data.
When I tried to watch animals in the Australian zoo, I suddenly had a meeting; I suddenly had to deal with work on the way to shopping in Korea, and the store has been closed for seven or eight years, which is completely different from the excellent nomadic life I imagined.
Kate, who often hangs "work first" and "have self-discipline to have freedom", admits that even the beauty of the current can not be completely relaxed and appreciated, "I think you can not because your work location is not in a fixed place, and people feel unprofessional; it should make people believe that you can complete the work wherever you are, and there is quality, and no need for others to adapt, so as to maintain this way of life for a long."
Digital nomads have bitterness and sweetness, but both say they can ’ t go back after they set foot on this road.
Read this year Kristie published in the book fair, from the nomad, to find the heart of the sea ", she met on the road only two seasons of American couples, with children wandering the world of nomadic families, Lin Lin's total lifestyle has brought her a shock," I know in Hong Kong, many of them are a life to the end, but in the nomad meet them, I ’ ve lived three or four different lives, ” and there are fascinating stories in each life.
Embark on a nomadic journey to open Second Life, their book of life, and add a few unforgettable experiences.

Bubble Mart Blind Box Store opens in San Jose Valley Fair
In recent years, Asian pop culture has become popular among young people in the Bay Area, ranging from K-pop to Japanese manga to Chinese fantasy novels, which have influenced clothing, hairstyles and more.
And it is no longer limited to East Asian ethnic groups, and its influence is gradually expanding among young people of all races.
Pop IP Blind Box Company Bubble Mart ’ s first store in North Carolina recently opened in San Jose Valley Fair, the largest mall in North Carolina, attracting many players to visit.
Blind box culture was born in Japan, originated in the early 20th century Department Store's Fukushima bag and egg twist toys.
Early content was limited to the fields of anime and video games, and later even expanded to books, fresh produce, etc. Blind Box players collected dolls, shared, discussed, exchanged, and formed a unique community culture.
