The Stagnation Gender Revolution: Images and Changes of Gender Division in Taiwan
Photo Credit: Shutterstock
What we want you to know is
Taiwan is in the first stage of what scholars call the gender revolution, that is, women are increasing paid market hours, and progress is relatively faster than Japan and South Korea, but in the second stage of the gender revolution is relatively slow compared to Western welfare countries (except Southern Europe), such as the formulation and promotion of family-friendly policies, resulting in a relatively high total labor hours in Taiwan, especially for women.
Text: Chiu Si-yi (Researcher, Institute of Sociology, Academia Sinica)
Author's Note: This article is excerpted from the speech at the opening of the Academia Sinica campus on October 21, 2023. For the purpose of preliminary descriptive statistical analysis using cross-sectional data, the average number of the whole society, not the individual, can not be used as a causal inference.
【 Note 1 】
Movies staged in recent years, such as "Da-Fa" (2016 Taiwanese drama), "The Wife of the Moon" (2016, 2021 drama), "The 82-year-old Kim Zhiying" (2019 Korean drama), have seen the invisible domestic labor and difficulties in East Asian society.
Why these domestic labor will be ignored for a long time? When time and labor have become goods that can be measured in the market with prices, it is divided into paid and unpaid, which distinguishes between "valuable" market labor and "worthless" family labor, and family labor without market value is often ignored.
This division of labor is also associated with gender roles, with men engaged in paid market labor as breadwinners, and women responsible for unpaid domestic labor as the dominant gender division of labor (with few social exceptions).
The inequality of power and opportunity inherent in this way of operation is also deeply linked to gender.
If the operation of the capital society is based on the extraction of the labor production of the employee, then the regenerative labor (such as washing, cooking, cleaning) that allows the employee to engage in daily labor production is the second layer of hidden labor that is exploited.
Neglect affects the rights and well-being of domestic service providers, including labor security, retirement income, etc., and the value of providing domestic services and care services in the market is often devalued and underestimated.
Due to changes in labor conditions, education and many social initiatives and movements, a large number of women enter the labor market, and men engage in paid work, obtain social status and recognition, but the labor within the family is still not challenged, deeply tied to the gender line, resulting in women in full-time paid work, still responsible for the second shift, or even the third or fourth shift of family labor. [Note 2]
Therefore, some scholars believe that women engaged in paid market labor, just walked the first half of the gender revolution, in order to break through the imbalance in the division of labor caused by women entering the labor market, to continue the second half of the reform, is to allow more men to share the domestic labor.
However, the study found that although the difference between men and women in family work time has become smaller, women are still responsible for most of the housework, mainly because women reduce housework time, and men have a limited increase.
The imbalance in the gender division of labor caused by only half of the reforms is closely related to many phenomena, such as: the quality of family relations, gender inequality in the workplace, workplace conflicts, reproductive intentions, and so on.
These discussions in Europe and the United States provide a perspective on Taiwan, which is undergoing rapid change, especially as the number of children in Taiwan is declining and the proportion of dual-income families reaches more than 60% (Research Center of Academia Sinica 2023).
This article through the "basic survey plan of social change in Taiwan" data [Note 1] supplemented with the research of foreign scholars, to the generation and life stage as the latitude, try to answer three questions, preliminary explore the changes in the gender division of labor in Taiwan.
The difference is: First, do men and women's work and household time have changed?
Second, do women have a second shift? Third, is there a difference between the gender division of labor in Taiwan and other international society?
The generation of this article is expressed by birth year, divided into: ≤ 1950s, 1960s, 1970s, 1980s, ≥ 1990s, and the life stage is divided into: "single, no 0-17 years old children", "have a partner, no 0-17 years old children", "have 0-6 years old children", "have 7-17 years old children".
Note that a partner refers to a cohabiting / married partner living with the same family; the category of children aged 0-6 or 7-17 includes a single or two-parent family; and life history and age are not linear, for example, when the child reaches adulthood, it is possible to return to “single, no children aged 0-17 ” or“ with a partner, no children aged 0-17 ”.
Q1: Has there been a change in men ’ s and women ’ s work and household time?
First of all, Figure 1 on the left shows that both men ’ s and women ’ s working hours are related to life stages.
However, the trend of change is opposite for men and women, and the change is greater for women than for men.
Men ’ s working hours gradually increased with partners and children, peaking when they had young children (an average of 46.8 hours per week) and then slowing down; women ’ s working hours continued to decline after entering a partnership, reaching the lowest point with preschool children (an average of 25.9 hours per week) and then slowing down.
In terms of domestic work (excluding care) time (Figure 1 right), men do not change much at different life stages, almost all maintain 5 hours per week, and women increase from nearly 7 hours per week to about 15 hours per week after entering a partnership or having children.
The difference in domestic work time between men and women has remained roughly 10 hours per week since entering into a partnership.
Take a closer look at the changes in the number of hours worked by men and women across generations (Figure 2).
The relationship between the number of working hours and life stages of men has not changed much in different generations, except for the younger generation, where the curve is slightly flat, and the number of hours is maintained at a higher level at different stages.
However, there is a marked change in women, and although the number of hours women work continues to fluctuate with their life stages, the younger generations work longer hours.
It is worth noting that entering a partnership (with a partner, no 0-17 children) is gradually unrelated to the increase and decrease in the number of working hours of women, and it can be seen from the graph that the number of working hours of young women is not as reduced as before because of entering a partnership.
Figure 3 shows the time of housework for different generations of men and women (the dotted line indicates the deviation that may occur due to the small sample size). There is no significant difference in the time of housework for men across generations, which is about 5 hours per week.
Although the number of domestic work hours of women is still closely related to the life stage, it is clearly showing a sharp decline in the generational trend.
Younger generations of women, in the single, no children 0-17 years old stage, the number of domestic work hours has been similar to that of men at the same stage.

Intermittent fasting is not useful for weight loss? First, distinguish between calorie restriction and limited time eating.
Photo Credit: Shutterstock
What we want you to know is
Compared with other dietary strategies such as ketogenic diets, plant-based diets, and low-calorie diets, intermittent fasting has the adaptive advantage of being more in line with the daily and nightly routine.
Some studies have also pointed out that intermittent fasting can not only reduce the risk of lifestyle related lifestyle diseases (such as metabolic diseases), but also improve the quality of life. However, it is important to remind that the most common side effects of intermittent fasting include low blood sugar, dizziness, weakness, etc., and excessive blood sugar fluctuations in the elderly can increase the risk of falls and fractures.
Consult a specialist and dietitian before making any dietary adjustment strategy to ensure that your health is in line with your individual ’ s health and safety.
What is intermittent fasting?
Can controlling the daily eating time and total eating time really help to lose weight and even improve metabolic syndrome?
Metabolic syndrome is considered to be a major risk factor for increased prevalence of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.
The latest issue of the Journal of Internal Medicine pointed out that diet control is an important part of the prevention of metabolic syndrome, and the "intermittent fasting" that has emerged in recent years has become a new choice for many people because of its simple implementation and is believed to have the benefits of helping to lose weight, prevent high blood sugar and cardiovascular disease.
The idea that fasting is good for health is not unique to contemporary society. It has been documented since ancient Greece that fasting was used to treat diseases and improve brain cognition.
Generally speaking, intermittent fasting refers to limiting eating to a specific time, which can be roughly divided into four ways: First, periodic fasting, taking less than 25% of the calories required for several days of the week, and cycling every other week; Second, fasting every other day, completely without calories in one day, and eating normally on the other day; Third, eating for a limited time, the complete fasting time is greater than 12 hours, as usual 16 / Fasting refers to complete fasting for 16 hours a day; Fourth, religious fasting, in particular religious fasting or fasting areas, the intake of food and water is prohibited.
However, when discussing “intermittent fasting ”, it is important to understand that“ calorie restriction ” and “limited eating ” are not exactly equal.
Calorie restriction refers to the reduction of total caloric intake, but not to the extent of malnutrition, and calorie restriction has been shown to have an effect on weight loss and longevity for various species.
Limited-time eating in intermittent fasting usually refers to continuous fasting for a specific period of time and is used as an alternative to calorie restriction.
The physiological mechanism of intermittent fasting?
Avoiding increased blood sugar and fat metabolism?
The main motivation for modern people to adopt intermittent fasting is to lose weight and health, and the reason why the diet control strategy of "limited eating" may be effective is thought to be related to the physiological clock, intestinal microbiota, lifestyle changes, and the effects of carbohydrate and lipid metabolism.
The center of the human body's physiological clock is located in the upper crossover nucleus of the "hypothalamus" of the brain, which is also known as the "satiety center", which controls the urge to eat and the feeling of satiety.
The operation of the hypothalamus shows a certain rhythm by the degree of light, and eating is an important factor in stimulating the rhythm.
Small studies have found that as long as the daily routine of life deviates from the circadian rhythm for 12 hours, the leptin concentration in the body is significantly reduced, and the glucose and insulin concentration is increased after meals, and the insulin resistance is increased.
In addition, the increase in blood sugar and insulin during night eating was larger, which showed that eating less after dinner was more in line with the physiological clock and reduced the risk of blood sugar rise.
In mammals, it has been found that when fasting, the cellular energy of the organism is converted from glucose to fatty acids and "ketones", which have a role in regulating proteins and have a great impact on the metabolism of the body.
In animal experiments, intermittent fasting has been found to increase AMP and ADP, prompting AMPK activation to inhibit various synthetic metabolisms and stimulate autophagy responses in cells, thereby eliminating damaged proteins.
Through prolonged fasting, it helps to improve fat metabolism, reduce abdominal fat, and reduce inflammation.
Can intermittent fasting effectively reduce weight?
Total heat intake is the key factor.
Whether intermittent fasting is more likely to lead to successful weight loss is not entirely certain.
A 2020 systematic review found that by fasting for 12-20 hours, obese people can lose weight and fat, and do not affect lean tissue, but in healthy people only the effect of reducing fat, there is no significant difference in weight and lean tissue.
It is worth noting that in 2022, a longer, more tightly planned randomized distribution trial in China compared obese people who performed calorie control and calorie control “plus ” diet restriction (8: 00 a.m. to 4: 00 p.m.) showed no significant difference in weight loss between the two groups, indirectly proving that the weight loss effect of time-limited diet or intermittent fasting is more likely to be self-feeding. The reduction in total calorie intake due to reduced eating time is the benefit of the“ calorie deficit ”.
A prospective study of sexual generation in the United States in 2023, based on the analysis of participants' records of eating a small amount (less than 500 calories), a medium amount (500-1000 calories), and a large amount (more than 1000 calories) per meal, found that the length of time from the first meal to the last meal per day is "unrelated" to weight.
In terms of current research, the main reason why intermittent fasting can reduce body weight may be that limiting the eating time and indirectly reducing the total calorie intake, so as to achieve weight loss benefits.
What are the side effects of intermittent fasting?
Consult a specialist before making a dietary adjustment
Although intermittent fasting may not directly lead to effective weight loss, other disease-related studies have found that intermittent fasting can help reduce blood sugar drug use and weight loss in people with diabetes.
A randomized HER2-negative study of 2-3 breast cancer patients also showed better treatment in the fasting group.
In addition, animal experiments have found that fasting contributes to the neurogenesis of strong nerve stem cells and the activation of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), which induces the brain into a neuroprotective state, which may be beneficial for the prevention of Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease.
In general, intermittent fasting has the adaptive advantages of being more in line with the daily and night rules, and is easier to implement than other dietary strategies such as ketogenic diets, plant-based diets, and low-calorie diets.
Some studies have also pointed out that intermittent fasting can not only reduce the risk of lifestyle related lifestyle diseases (such as metabolic diseases), but also improve the quality of life. However, it is important to remind that the most common side effects of intermittent fasting include low blood sugar, dizziness, weakness, etc., and excessive blood sugar fluctuations in the elderly can increase the risk of falls and fractures.
Consult a specialist and dietitian before making any dietary adjustment strategy to ensure that your health is in line with your individual ’ s health and safety.

New Algorithm Transforms Physical Problems into Quantum Language
December 28, 2023 09: 07 | Source: Science and Technology Daily
Small number
New Algorithm Transforms Physical Problems into Quantum Language
Scientists at Google have devised an algorithm that can translate complex physical problems into the language of quantum physics, which could make quantum computers more useful.
The paper was published recently in the journal Physical Review X.
Once quantum computers become powerful enough, they may be useful for specific tasks such as encryption and drug discovery, but whether they can solve many scientific problems that traditional computers cannot handle is still unknown.
Lead researcher Ryan Barbush and colleagues have developed an algorithm that can translate a large number of traditional physics problems to run on a quantum computer.
Moreover, when simulating an important traditional system on a quantum computer, the operation speed will be exponentially increased.
The team explained that any stabilization system that is disturbed by an external force, such as a Kevlar vest suddenly hit by a bullet, can be described in the mathematical language of systems such as balls and springs.
Objects in these systems obey Hooke ’ s law and bounce back and forth.
The study found that, no matter how complex, the mathematical description of these traditional spring systems can be represented as a version of the Schrödinger equation, which describes how any quantum system changes over time.
By observing the similarity between the two equations and using symmetry, the researchers wrote an algorithm that translates the distance and speed of the spring ’ s movement into the language of the Schrödinger equation as well as the qubits used by the quantum computer.
This ball and spring system can describe many physical problems, including most wave-like systems, such as neuronal activity maps or light reflected from the surface.
Babush ’ s team has yet to figure out how many qubits it would take to run an algorithm, possibly beyond the number of qubits available in today ’ s quantum computers, to solve these physical problems or one of the first applications for error-correcting quantum computers.

Why did Argentina give up on joining the BRICS?
You don't have to be too serious about the new president, Millet.
Author: Ye Dehao
Published: Updated:
December 29 is the last government working day in 2023.
The Argentine government issued a letter to the BRICS countries as early as the 22nd, indicating that Argentina is not suitable for joining the BRICS at present, saying that its foreign policy is very different from the previous government.
Argentina ’ s new president, Javier Milei, a far-right liberal who was sworn into office on December 10, has been highly pro-American and pro-Israel, and his formal decision to forgo joining the Golden Brick, which is seen as close to China, comes as no surprise.
Negotiations are fruitless?
After Millet ’ s victory in the second round of voting at the end of November, Chinese Ambassador to Argentina Wang Wei quickly met with then-Foreign Minister Diana Mondino, and Millet himself released a Spanish translation of a personal letter sent to him by Chinese President Xi Jinping, thanking Xi Jinping for holding up a letter of “common interest ” between China and Argentina.
Although Millet, who had indicated during the election that he would not talk to communist countries (for Millet during the election campaign, this included China and Brazil), expressed goodwill, the foreign minister said publicly on social media in early December that he would not join the BRICS.
Subsequently, at the invitation of Argentina, China sent special envoy of President Xi Jinping and Vice Chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People ’ s Congress Wu Weihua to Buenos Aires to attend the inauguration ceremony of Milai on December 10, and met with Milai with Wang Wei the following day.
Mirai later wrote back to China, which Argentine media said contained references to a currency swap agreement between China and Argentina, when one of Argentina ’ s loans to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) was due to be repaid.
Later, Chinese officials also met with Milay ’ s nominee for governor of Argentina ’ s central bank (although Milay had stated during his campaign that the central bank would be abolished and fully dollarized), as well as his economy minister, Luis Caputo.
Ukrainian President Leonid Zelensky also attended the inauguration ceremony of Millet.
(Reuters)
In the end, there seems to be no progress on the currency swap agreement and the related issues of joining the BRICS.
By December 14, Reuters had reported that Milay had reached a loan agreement with the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean (CAF), allowing Argentina to repay the IMF as scheduled on December 21.
On December 19, Argentine media revealed that China had suspended the currency swap agreement with Argentina, saying that Beijing had recalled Wang Wei to Beijing the previous day.
The letter from Argentina renouncing its accession to the BRICS came on the 22nd.
Argentina ’ s renunciation of BRICS membership has been widely interpreted as a setback for China ’ s efforts to “expand ” solidarity with the global South at the BRICS summit in South Africa in August 2023.
At that time, the BRICS decided to invite the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Argentina, Egypt, and Ethiopia to join the BRICS.
However, to put it another way, Millet ’ s renunciation of joining the Golden Brick was just an act of symbolic significance greater than practical significance, and his attitude toward China and even his right-wing libertarian stance have weakened significantly since his election.
Foreign Minister Guido Mondino has made it clear that he will not abandon diplomacy with China and Brazil (Argentina ’ s first and second largest trading partners, respectively).
Millet has quickly appointed a new ambassador to China, and his letter to the BRICS states that he hopes to deepen bilateral relations and increase trade and investment contacts with other countries, and hopes to meet with the leaders of the BRICS countries.
On December 10, Millet addressed supporters after he was sworn in as president. (Reuters)
During the campaign, there were fears that Millet would behave badly when he came to power.
However, the majority of those who were elected were on the right wing.
For example, Economy Minister Caputo is a member of former President Mauricio Macri ’ s Juntos por el Cambio party, and Central Bank governor Santiago Bausili was Finance Minister from 2015 to 2019.
The Adventures of Shock Therapy
Of course, after coming to power, Millet quickly pushed for “shock therapy ” economic reforms, immediately devalued the Argentine peso by half (but its exchange rate remained below the black market), and declared a two-year economic emergency, proposing more than 300 measures in the form of presidential decrees, from loosening controls on food retailers to loosening the use of foreign exchange, from privatization of state-owned enterprises to deregulation of proprietary medicines, from labor protection to employee restrictions. All strikes are complete.
Unions in Argentina have mobilized a revolt, but the scale of the demonstrations has not reached enough to worry Millet.
Security officials from the Milai authorities also issued a stern warning against the demonstrations, which seemed to have a degree of deterrent effect.
On December 29, the economic emergency in Milai came into effect, with demonstrators gathering in the streets of Buenos Aires to protest against economic reforms.
(Reuters)
At the end of the year, Millet also sent more than 600 reform bills to Congress, asking Congress to initiate a special session from December 26 to January 31 to help Argentina move forward quickly with reforms.
The bill includes legalizing Millet ’ s previously declared economic emergency, abolishing the primary election system, increasing penalties for various protest-related crimes, protecting the right to self-defense and strengthening the police, listing state-owned enterprises that can be privatized, allowing the legalization of undeclared property, modifying policies related to the oil industry (such as the government will not impose price limits), and temporarily handing the president more legislative powers on taxes, pensions, security, and other items.
Millay ’ s government says it wants to reduce the government deficit to zero by 2024 (which would have been about 5% of GDP), thereby drastically reducing the size of the government, cutting subsidies for electricity and transportation, cutting funding to local governments, and temporarily raising import taxes and increasing benefits such as the value of food cards to help those most in need.
With only 40 of the 257 seats in the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies and 7 of the 72 seats in the Senate, Millet ’ s party, even with less than half of the traditional right-wing “working together to change ” support, is hoping to use popular opinion to put pressure on Congress to show that if Congress is unwilling to pass his reform bill, it will resort to the law (no law). Binding) referendum.
[Here: Chainsaws are a symbol of Millet ’ s reformist economy, and he often picks them up to campaign events.]
Millet ’ s “crazy ” economic reforms, and the voters ’ support for him, are understandable. After all, Argentina ’ s economy has been a tragedy for more than a century, and its per capita GDP was higher than that of Germany and France 100 years ago, but it is now several times behind them, from advanced countries to developing countries.
According to statistics, its ratio of negative growth to positive growth has been worse than that of war-torn Iraq and Sudan since 1950, and it is now the largest recipient of IMF assistance since its inception.
Not to mention that Argentina has an inflation rate of more than 100%.
Millet has long shown that his shock therapy will bring economic pain, but voters have limited tolerance for the pain, and the pain is likely to grow.
The street demonstrations are not threatening Millet at this point, but if Millet ’ s new deal doesn ’ t work, the situation will be very different in a few months.
In the midst of a crisis-ridden march of economic reform, Millet ’ s foreign policy will remain at the symbolic level, and will never dare to do anything that will really negatively affect the Argentine economy.
Giving up on joining the Brick is just one example.
We don ’ t have to read this diplomatically too seriously — it ’ s just the political norm in Latin America, where the ideologies of the right and the left are fiercely opposed.

RTHK will open its Cantonese database for the Centre to develop multilingual voice AI technology, and the Centre will provide the AI technology developed accordingly.
Meng Mei-ling, director of the center, said that with the use of AI technology, "there may be fewer people (for verbatim production), but it can speed up the production time, and the organization can deploy manpower to produce more programs."
At present, the multi-language voice AI technology developed by the Centre can be split into three functions, namely “Text Generation Robot ”,“ Automatic Subtitle Summary Generation Technology ” and “Controlled Cantonese Text Imitation Technology ”, which can be used to process and analyze text data and audio in Cantonese, English and Putonghua.
Meng Mei-ling said that there are many changes in Hong Kong people ’ s speech, “speaking and speaking can be used in combination with three languages, or even more ”, and the data of three-language mixing is very small, so it is not a challenge in research and development.
She added that the team has been working on the technology since 2021. The technology is mature enough to broadcast weather news and news bulletins, and the automatic generation of subtitles can also save time in producing verbatim manuscripts. However, it is still difficult to identify more unique Cantonese words such as “rising ” and requires manual error correction.
Meng Mei-ling also mentioned that the team encountered a lack of computing power during the development of AI technology. "GPUs (graphics processors) are difficult to buy and expensive, and they can only design some algorithms without using so much computing power."
She described the dilemma of insufficient computing power in the academic and research fields is quite common, waiting for the government to complete the supercomputing center to solve, "if we have 100 times the computing power, we can all use it, but also use it. (1000 times?) can also be used up."

"Aida Mordu" officially opened the first commercial cruise ship to sea travel dream come true
On January 1, the "Aida Mordu" docked at Shanghai Wusongkou International Cruise Port (drone photo).
Photo by Xinhua reporter Ding Ting
On January 1, the first domestic large-scale cruise ship "Aida Mordu" officially opened its first commercial voyage at the Wusongkou International Cruise Port in Shanghai.
The dream of the Chinese to travel to sea on their own big cruise ship has come true.
"Aida Mordu" is a "modern city on the sea", the ship has 2125 rooms, can accommodate 5,246 passengers, equipped with up to 16 floors, an area of 40,000 square meters of public living and entertainment area, after 8 years of research, 5 years of design and construction, after the completion of the test flight verification officially put into operation.
By building domestic large-scale cruise ships, the overall strength of China's shipbuilding industry has further leapt.
From hull design and space construction to special catering and entertainment projects, "Aida Mordu" combines multiple ingenuity and innovative ideas to create a "boat show" through the cross-border integration of East and West cultural and tourism elements.
In the future, "Aida Mordu" will also open the cruise line from China to Southeast Asian countries, provide guests with a variety of travel vacation options combining long, medium and short, and launch the Maritime Silk Road cruise line in a timely manner.
AG60E electric aircraft successfully flew for the first time to adapt to low-altitude economy and green and low-carbon development
Adapt to the requirements of low-altitude economy and green and low-carbon development, improve the energy saving, emission reduction, noise reduction performance of domestic general aircraft, and comprehensively improve the green manufacturing level of aviation … On January 3, the AG60E electric aircraft independently developed by China Aviation Industry Group General Aircraft Co., Ltd. successfully completed its first flight at Qiandao Lake General Airport in Jiande, Zhejiang.
AG60E is a single-engine single-wing light sports aircraft, side-by-side two-seat, all-metal structure, mainly for aviation clubs, aviation companies, private users, etc., for flight experience, basic flight training and private entertainment flight.
The aircraft has a length of 6.9 meters, a height of 2.6 meters, a wingspan of 8.6 meters, a maximum takeoff weight of 600 kg, a maximum flat flight speed of 220 km / h, and a maximum cruise speed of 185 km / h.
The picture shows AG60E electric aircraft. (Photo courtesy of Aviation Industry Group)
It is reported that the development team uses the existing mature general aviation equipment platform to carry out electric modification on the finalized aircraft and verify the key technologies of the electric aircraft.
Since the start of the project in August 2022, the development team has carried out a number of tasks such as motor, electric control, power battery selection, electric propulsion system integration test verification, electric aircraft safety and airworthiness compliance design technology research, and completed the electric conversion of AG60 light sports aircraft, breaking through a number of key technologies such as pure electric power device design and system integration.
The rated output power of the modified AG60E electric aircraft power system is equivalent to that of the prototype, and all performance indicators except the flight time reach or exceed the level of the prototype.
The electric aircraft torque output linearity is better, and the acceleration response is faster, which is conducive to improving the take-off performance of the aircraft.
Compared with the traditional fuel engine aircraft due to the increase of altitude and the attenuation of the output power, the motor is basically not affected by such factors, which can provide continuous climbing power for the aircraft and shorten the climbing time.
In addition, the motor noise is smaller, more environmentally friendly and comfortable, its structure is simpler, and the use and maintenance are convenient.
The AG60E electric aircraft technology demonstrator successfully flew for the first time, accumulated valuable experience for the development of electric aircraft products and the electric modification of active fixed-wing aircraft, and laid a solid foundation for seizing strategic opportunities for the transformation of aviation power, promoting the layout of strategic emerging industries and promoting the development of low-altitude economic industries.
China's first launch in 2024 was a complete success, and the future space mission is very interesting.
At 19: 20 on January 5, China successfully launched the Tianyi No. 1 meteorological constellation 15-18 in Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center using the Kuaizhou No. 1 carrier rocket, and the satellite smoothly entered the predetermined orbit and the launch mission was a complete success, which is the first launch of China Aerospace in 2024.
The Kuaizhou 1A carrier rocket successfully launched the meteorological constellation 15-18 of Tianmu I into the sky.
Xinhua News Agency (photo by Wang Jiangbo)
Looking forward to 2024, a series of major space missions are very interesting.
In the Chinese space station, the Shenzhou-17 crew has successfully completed the first extravehicular activities, and a large number of scientific experiments and technical experiments will be carried out in the future, as well as a number of astronaut extravehicular activities and application load extravehicular tasks.
In addition, the Long March 7 and Yao-8 carrier rocket, which is carrying out the Tianzhou-7 launch mission, has completed all the research and development work before leaving the factory and arrived safely at the Wenchang space launch site.
At present, all the participating systems in the launch site area are making steady preparations for the mission as planned.
The space station complex will be docked after the launch of the Tianzhou VII, an improved cargo spacecraft of China.
This time, Tianzhou-7 will send to our space home which "baby", let us sit and wait for the "unpacking time".
In the field of deep space exploration, the lunar exploration project Chang'e 6 mission is carrying out research and development work as planned, and is scheduled to launch in 2024.
According to the arrangement, the Chang'e 6 mission will carry out the lunar far side sampling return. So far, the 10 lunar samples returned by humans have been located on the lunar front, and the far side of the moon is more ancient than the front of the moon, and the Aitken Basin, one of the three terrestrial bodies on the moon, has important scientific research value.
In order to successfully complete the communication between the spacecraft on the far side of the moon and the earth, China's newly developed Queqiao II relay communication satellite is scheduled to be launched in the first half of 2024.

China 's third-generation autonomous superconducting quantum computer online

01 / 07 / 2024 09: 09 | Source: Xinhua Network
Small number
Original title: China's third-generation autonomous superconducting quantum computer online
The reporter learned from the Anhui Quantum Computing Engineering Research Center and the Anhui Key Laboratory of Quantum Computing Chip on the 6th that China's third-generation autonomous superconducting quantum computer "The Source Wukong" was launched at 9: 00 on the same day in the Source Quantum Computing Technology (Hefei) Co., Ltd.
It is understood that the quantum computer is equipped with 72 independent superconducting quantum chips "Wukong core", which is currently an advanced programmable, deliverable superconducting quantum computer.
The superconducting quantum computer is a quantum computer based on a superconducting circuit quantum chip.
Internationally, IBM and Google quantum computers are using superconducting technology routes.
According to Dr. Kong Weicheng, deputy director of Anhui Quantum Computing Engineering Research Center, “Benyuan Wukong ” matches Benyuan ’ s third-generation quantum computing measurement and control system“ Benyuan Sky Machine ”, which truly landed the batch automated test of quantum chips, and the overall operation efficiency of quantum computers has been greatly improved.
According to Dr. Jia Zhilong, deputy director of the Anhui Provincial Key Laboratory, "Wukong" is equipped with a 72-bit superconducting quantum chip "Wukong Core", with a total of 198 qubits, including 72 working qubits and 126 coupler qubits.
It is understood that the superconducting quantum computer released this time is named "Wukong", derived from the mythological figure in Chinese traditional culture, Sun Wukong, which means "72 changes" like Sun Wukong.

Boeing to Airbus deal: Aerial competition
January 15, 2024 22: 18
Just a few days ago, an Alaska Airlines Boeing 737 Max 9 plane had an accident, which fortunately did not have a significant impact on the health of passengers.
Boeing and Airbus are the biggest competitors in the aviation industry.
The incident triggered a discussion of Boeing products, forcing Boeing's share price to plunge for two days in a row.
In this article, novice traders will have the opportunity to learn more about Boeing and Airbus, which can help them form their views on airline company trading.
Alaska Airlines 737 Max 9 cabin panel causes Boeing shares to fall
Before we review Boeing ’ s performance, let ’ s take a look at what happened to Alaska Airlines ’ flights.
According to media reports, a cabin panel built into the plane to fill the emergency exit (not required by Alaska Airlines) exploded during the flight, resulting in the lives of passengers.
The pilot managed to fly the plane back to the airport without causing any injuries or serious injuries to the passengers.
Flight safety issues hurt Boeing
The crash is not the first to be linked to the 737 Max. Two accidents involving the 737 Max 8 in 2018 and 2019 caused heavy casualties and raised concerns about aircraft safety as FAA investigators highlighted problems with how the autopilot system worked. In 2019, the 737 Max fleet was grounded for 20 months at a cost of about $21 billion.
Airlines such as United Airlines, Aeromexico and Turkish Airlines have been forced to suspend their fleets and work with Boeing experts to resolve any problems.
The Alaska Airlines incident has prompted companies to re-examine the state of their fleets.
Boeing shares fell 8 percent on Jan. 8 after U.S. aviation regulators temporarily grounded some 737 MAX jets.
Boeing CEO Dave Calhoun told CNBC on Jan. 10 that the blowout at Alaska Airlines was caused by "quality escapes."
Asked how to explain the meaning of the word, Calhoun pointed out that it was "a description of the problems that people find in the inspection... anything that has the potential to lead to an accident."
In a speech to Boeing employees, the Boeing CEO said: "We will acknowledge our mistakes.
We will approach every step in a 100% and completely transparent manner. "
Some analysts see the new 737 Max 9 incident as a temporary setback for U.S. companies.
But some analysts said "quality escapes" were unacceptable in an industry where failure could have serious consequences, adding that authorities had grounded 171 aircraft.
Boeing loses battle with Airbus
Boeing has maintained strong sales through 2019, claiming more than $100 billion in revenue.
Boeing, backed by U.S. diplomacy, won a contract with Airbus in the Gulf countries, but the next few years were not easy for the American manufacturer. Technical problems with the 737 Max and a commercial war between China and the United States pushed Boeing out of one of the world's largest markets.
Stakeholders in airlines that use the 737 Max, such as Ryanair, are not happy with the grounding of its fleet, as there is growing evidence of quality control issues.
Reuters reports that Boeing delivered 528 aircraft in 2023 and booked 1,314 net new orders, up from 480 deliveries and 774 net new orders in 2022, the third-best year.
Last year, the company delivered 396 narrow-body 737 jets, achieving a revised target of at least 375 single-aisle aircraft, but falling short of the original target of 400 to 450 jets.
Airbus grows and ascends to the throne
Airbus, the European response to Boeing, was founded in 1970 by several European aerospace companies to compete with their American counterparts.
Airbus' first product was the 1972 A300, the world's first wide-body twin-jet aircraft.
Since then, Airbus has produced a wide variety of commercial airliners, including the A340 and A320neo, as well as the jumbo A380, which competes directly with Boeing ’ s 747 in the long-haul passenger market.
Airbus has been the world ’ s largest aircraft manufacturer for the past five years. On January 11, Airbus announced its pre-orders and deliveries for 2023.
The report shows that Airbus received 2,094 aircraft orders in 2023, the highest number in the company ’ s history, after the previous figure of 1,503.
Despite supply chain problems, Airbus delivered 735 jets to customers last year, exceeding its own delivery target of 720.
“We initially expected the aviation industry to recover in some time period from 2023 to 2025, but what we saw in 2023 was the return of widebody airliners much earlier than expected and vibrant, except for the single-aisle market, ” said Christian Scherer, Airbus Commercial Chief Officer. Schered added:“ We have never sold so many A320 or A350 aircraft in any year …
Tourism is back, and it's going strong. "

BEIJING, Jan. 17 (Xinhua) -- In the more than a month since he took office, Argentine President Emile Millet has introduced a series of “shock therapy ” reforms aimed at saving the economy, with a view to reducing the fiscal deficit and controlling inflation.
Since the introduction of the new policy, prices in Argentina have soared and the quality of life of the population has declined, and opposition parties and trade unions have raised doubts.
In his inauguration speech last December, Millet said Argentina faced a “critical ” economic situation, with high inflation, rising poverty and difficulties in obtaining external credit support.
Argentina needs “shock therapy ” to save the economy.
In the early days of his administration, Argentina will face a period of "stagnation", during which economic data will be worse than before.
The Millet government introduced a series of policies to reduce the deficit, including reducing the number of government departments from 18 to 9, reducing government subsidies for energy and transportation, and halting tenders for new public works.
The new government also devalued the official exchange rate of the Argentine peso from about 400 pesos to about 800 pesos to the US dollar and eased import controls.
In addition to direct fiscal and economic measures, the Milai government is also promoting the repeal and amendment of more than 200 laws to ease government and legal controls on domestic economic sectors and to facilitate import and export trade.
In addition, Millet and his team have said that "dollarization" is the medium-term goal of his administration, but so far has not released a "dollarization" roadmap.
After a series of new policies, prices in Argentina have risen sharply.
Argentina ’ s National Institute of Statistics and Census released a report on the 11th, saying that the country ’ s inflation rate reached 25.5% in December 2023 and the cumulative inflation rate in 2023 reached 211.4%, both setting records since 1990.
Food prices in Argentina have almost doubled since December 2023.
For example, in early December, the supermarket price of a kilogram of beef in Argentina was about 4,000 Argentine pesos (about RMB 35), and in early January, it has risen to about 8,000 Argentine pesos (about RMB 70).
Many families have had to switch to cheaper pork and chicken because of the soaring price of beef.
In an interview with local media, an executive at a food company in Argentina said the retail price of its products rose by an average of 40% to 50% after the new policy was announced.

Avoid “fatal ” fractures and keep in mind“ fall prevention + bone pine ”
Li Ning, Wu Xinbao
January 19, 2024 07: 48 Source: People 's Daily Overseas Edition
Gou Jianshan (Xinhua News Agency)
Since the beginning of winter, many people have ushered in the cooling weather, the road surface is easy to freeze, and the number of patients who slip and fall has increased significantly.
Among them, the risk of fracture caused by osteoporosis in the elderly is greatly increased, which not only affects the quality of life of the elderly, but also may bring fatal consequences.
Avoiding “fatal ” fractures, preventing falls and treating osteoporosis are key.
Beware of early warning signs for osteoporosis
Osteoporosis is a common bone disease, mainly manifested as bone mass reduction and bone tissue structure destruction, resulting in increased bone brittleness and prone to fracture.
It is a lack of typical symptoms of the disease, most patients do not have obvious clinical symptoms, some patients may have waist and back pain, spine deformation, systemic multi-joint pain and other symptoms, many patients are in the occurrence of fractures before understanding its existence.
In fact, the risk of osteoporosis is higher in the elderly, especially in women.
Risk factors for osteoporosis include advanced age, female menopause, family history of brittle fractures, low physical activity, insufficient sun exposure, smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, calcium and / or vitamin D deficiency, excessive consumption of caffeinated beverages, nutritional imbalance, low weight.
Osteoporosis can lead to multiple fractures throughout the body, with hip, spine and wrist fractures the most common.
These fractures can lead to long-term bedridden, disability and even death, placing a heavy burden on the family and society.
Some diseases can also cause or worsen osteoporosis, including hyperthyroidism, diabetes, rheumatic immune diseases, gastrointestinal diseases, and so on.
At the same time, long-term use of drugs that affect bone metabolism, such as glucocorticoids, aromatase inhibitors (breast cancer treatment drugs), will also lead to osteoporosis.
Bone density screening is the most effective method of osteoporosis screening.
If the elderly have a fracture due to a slight external force or fall on the ground, it is likely to be "osteoporotic fracture", which means that the patient has osteoporosis and needs to be paid attention.
Focus on post-operative rehabilitation to prevent recurrence of fractures
After the elderly fall, if they feel hip pain and cannot sit, stand or walk hard, they should be highly vigilant about whether a hip fracture has occurred.
The general doctor can get a clear and intuitive diagnosis through the X-ray made by the patient.
But there are also a few cases where X-rays do not show significant fractures.
At this time, it is necessary to carry out further CT scanning or nuclear magnetic resonance examination, of which the accuracy of nuclear magnetic resonance examination is higher.
Patients with hip fractures should undergo surgery as soon as possible if their physical condition permits.
The purpose of the operation is to relieve the pain as soon as possible, to get the patient out of bed as soon as possible, to avoid the complications caused by long-term bed rest (such as pressure sores, lung infection, deep vein thrombosis of lower limbs, etc.), and to restore the function of the patient to the level of function before the injury.
Postoperative fracture pain is usually reduced to varying degrees.
Under the condition of conscious awareness and cooperation, patients can sit up and practice the contraction of lower limb muscles early after surgery.
If the patient's whole body condition allows, it can be moved from the bed under the assistance of the walker as soon as possible.
Under the guidance of professional rehabilitation doctors, the patient's recovery effect will be better.
For elderly patients, only the above rehabilitation treatment is not enough, because the risk of recurrence of fractures in the elderly who have experienced hip fractures is very high, so prevention of recurrence of fractures is just as important for elderly patients as surgical treatment, including prevention of falls and treatment of osteoporosis.
Osteoporosis is a chronic systemic disease, similar to high blood pressure and diabetes, which requires long-term standardized treatment to reduce the risk of repeated fractures.
Improve bone health pay attention to balanced diet
Prevention of fractures is more important than treatment, especially for the elderly.
Regardless of whether a fracture has occurred before, the elderly can improve the health of the bones through some simple measures in their daily life.
In the lifestyle, the elderly can pay attention to the following points: strengthen nutrition, balanced diet, increase the intake of calcium-rich foods, such as dairy products, soy products, seafood, nuts, green leafy vegetables, etc. Pads, handrails, etc.
In addition, daily supplementation of calcium and vitamin D is also an effective means of maintaining bone health.
In general, daily calcium supplement 500-600 mg, vitamin D31000-2000 international units (IU), can meet the needs of most elderly people.
It should be noted that patients who have been clearly diagnosed with osteoporosis or have suffered brittle fractures are not enough to achieve the purpose of treatment, and they need to receive long-term standardized treatment under the guidance of professional doctors.

Traditional computers process data in the form of bits, each of which switches between two states, labeled 0 and 1, while quantum computers use qubits, which can be stacked in linear combinations of 0 and 1.
In the superposition, Zhang said that if the position of the bit is marked by a sphere, the position of the south and north poles represents 0 and 1 respectively, the bits of a traditional computer can only be switched between the poles, but if the quantum bit is superimposed, it can be anywhere on the two-dimensional sphere, not limited to the north and south poles.

Physical quantity subbits with built-in error correction function
Zhang Mengran
February 5, 2024 09: 23 | Source: Science and Technology Daily
Small number
Original title: The physical quantity subbit with built-in error correction function came out
A team of researchers from the University of Tokyo in Japan, Johannes Gutenberg University in Germany and the University of Paratsky in the Czech Republic recently demonstrated a new way to build photonic quantum computers.
Instead of using a single photon, the team used a laser generated pulse of light that can be made up of multiple photons.
The findings were published in a new issue of the journal Science.
Qubits are highly susceptible to external influences, which means that the information they store is easily lost.
In order for a quantum computer to provide reliable results, it is necessary to produce a real entanglement that connects several physical qubits together to form a logical qubit.
If one of the physical qubits fails, the other qubits will retain the information.
However, one of the main difficulties hindering the development of functional quantum computers is the need for large quantities of physical qubits.
A single photon is usually used as a physical qubit.
In a sense, these photons are tiny particles of light that essentially run faster than solid-state qubits, but are also easier to lose.
This time, the research team converted the laser pulse into a quantum optical state, providing an inherent ability to correct errors.
Although the system consists only of laser pulses, in principle it eliminates errors immediately.
Therefore, there is no need to generate individual photons into qubits through a large number of light pulses, and then let them interact as logical qubits.
The researchers say they only need one pulse of light to get a powerful logical qubit.
In other words, in this system, physical qubits are already equivalent to logical qubits.
It is an extraordinary and unique concept.
Although the quality of the logical qubits produced by the University of Tokyo experiment is not enough to provide the necessary level of fault tolerance.
But the new research clearly shows that it is possible to convert non-universally corrected qubits into correctable qubits using the most innovative quantum optics methods.
The physical qubits are the basic units of the physical system, they are real, and there is no doubt that they will "make mistakes".
A logical qubit is an ideal, abstract concept that preserves the stability of the result no matter how many errors are made in the calculation.
People can regard the latter as the former's "protective shell", such as encoding logic qubits, so that its information is retained in the physical qubits, so as to achieve the protection and fault tolerance of the physical qubits.
In this study, scientists have made physical qubits almost identical to logical qubits, which can indeed be called a remarkable advance.

Work while playing! Japan will open up digital nomad visa application conditions at a time
Japan is about to implement the Digital Nomad Visa Program at the end of March, which will open to applications from 49 countries, including Taiwan.
What exactly is Digital Nomad? What are the application requirements?
The concept of “digital nomad ” was first proposed by Japanese semiconductor expert Shigeru Shigeru in 1997, meaning that both travel and work can be taken care of at the same time.
This is because their work can be done only by computers and the Internet, which means that the world can be an office.
A report by market research firm Qualtrics also found that nearly 80% of job seekers would consider whether a job offer could work remotely, indicating that the trend of digital nomads is sweeping the world.
In order to welcome the digital nomads, various countries have also strengthened their soft and hard facilities, including comfortable co-working space, tourism consultation, and a job search website for the digital nomads.
According to Bloomberg, the most popular full-time location for remote work in 2023 has been replaced by a city: Tokyo, Japan, has replaced Lisbon, Portugal, as the city with the largest growth in the number of digital nomads.
The rise of digital nomads is related to the tendency of millennials to value “experiences ” over“ possessions. ”
Research shows that more than three-quarters of millennials prefer to spend their hard-earned money on exciting experiences or activities rather than buying products.
Want to go digital nomad in Japan? Check your pockets aren ’ t deep enough first!
However, people who are interested in traveling to a digital nomad abroad may want to check their wallets first; especially in Japan, where the application threshold is not cheap.
Japan will implement a digital nomad visa program at the end of March, allowing spouses and children to stay in Japan for up to six months if they are granted visas.
However, the applicant must provide proof of income of at least 10 million yen (about NT $2.09 million) per year, and must have private health insurance.
In addition, the visa cannot be renewed immediately and can be reapplied after six months of departure from Japan.
“To be honest, Asian countries don ’ t seem to have a ‘ simple ’ digital nomad visa, ” Brittany Loeffler, head of the digital nomad website Nomad Embassies, told the BBC.
The BBC reported that in addition to Japan, Thailand also has strict conditions for digital nomads, and applicants need to submit a minimum income proof of at least US $80,000 (about NT $2.52 million) per year, and a proof of assets of US $1 million (about NT $31.6 million).
In contrast, the conditions in European countries are relatively relaxed, most of the income proof requires between 2000 and 3000 euros (about NT $68,000 to 102,000), and Finland only needs 1200 euros (about NT $41,000) of income proof to apply.
Digital nomadic potential is limitless, the Japanese government hopes to inject innovation and vitality into society
According to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation, Japanese society has a conservative attitude towards immigration, and the effectiveness of digital nomads has yet to be seen.
The Japanese government also hopes that the digital nomadic trend can promote digital transformation in the country and bring innovation and vitality to society.
However, digital nomads may also cause social problems in the region.
According to the BBC, when local landlords realized that several nomads could pay higher rents each month, they raised prices, causing property prices to soar, making it more difficult for locals to rent or buy homes.
Even now, the Japanese digital nomad visa has not been implemented at all, and Tokyo house prices have soared due to the depreciation of the yen and the influx of investors.
Therefore, whether Tokyo can maintain its reputation as the city with the largest growth in the number of digital nomads will depend on the wisdom of the Japanese government.

Freedom Square (Beishe Review) Policy response strategy for artificial intelligence deep counterfeiting and voice copying technology
◎ Cai Yue Ting
Deep hypocrisy and voice copying are technologies that use artificial intelligence to generate fake or manipulative media that can be used for a variety of purposes, including entertainment, education, and journalism.
If it is abused for fraud and the dissemination of false information, it will damage the reputation and rights of the individual, and it will affect social order and national security.
Because there are major potential hazards, it is necessary to formulate relevant regulations and effective management, and it can promote the healthy development of this innovative industry.
Consolidating practice cases to standardize policy measures to manage deep counterfeiting and voice copying can go hand in hand with the following aspects:
I. Regulations:
The content of the bill should include: (1) clearly stipulate the legal and illegal use of deep counterfeiting and voice copying to protect personal and national security and rights; (2) establish effective enforcement mechanisms and regular amendments to ensure the effective implementation of the law and adapt to the rapid development of technology; (3) use ethics education and advocacy; and (4) specify appropriate punitive measures.
2. Technical supervision:
(1) Establish an effective enforcement mechanism, consisting of experts with professional knowledge and technical ability, to (1) supervise the development and application of deep counterfeiting and voice reproduction technology to ensure that the use of the technology complies with laws, regulations and ethical standards; (2) adhere to the principle of minimum intervention, and strike a balance between protecting personal privacy and preventing abuse; and (3) promote the sound development of the industry.
Restrictions on use: Restrictions on the use of deep counterfeiting and voice copying technologies, especially in sensitive areas such as finance, politics, law, and medicine, and where they may have a serious impact on personal privacy.
Transparency and Authentication: (1) Require developers and users of deep counterfeiting and voice copying technologies to provide transparency to ensure that users are informed and consent to the use of their data.
(2) Establish a certification mechanism to ensure that only accredited institutions and individuals can use these technologies.
(4) Technical research: Encourage research on deep counterfeiting and voice copying technologies, especially research on detecting and preventing abuse, and research on how to protect personal privacy.
Participation, use of ethics education and public awareness: to strengthen the education of the public and related industries, and to raise awareness of the potential risks of deep counterfeiting and voice copying technology.
Authorities should provide corresponding preventive measures and education and training.
The development of deep counterfeiting and voice reproduction technology has brought many potential risks, but it is also an integral part of the country ’ s sustainable development.
This industry requires the participation of multiple stakeholders, how to ensure that these technologies are used responsibly and ethically through legal, technical and educational means, and to minimize their potential hazards, to the rapid and vigorous development of the industry is a matter of urgency.

Germany relies heavily on China in rare earths and other fields
Germany ’ s position as Europe ’ s largest economy is not optimistic – it is currently stagnant.
At the same time, another sword of Damocles hanging overhead cannot be ignored: Germany is increasingly dependent on imports of important raw materials, especially rare earths.
Volkswagen ’ s battery production workshop for electric vehicles in Salzgitter, Germany
Rare earths are also known as rare earth elements (SEE) or rare earth metals, including scandium, cerium, promethium, terbium, thulium and 12 other elements.
They are not as rare as the name suggests (the rarest thulium is actually more common than gold), yet they are distributed in a way that is barely rich enough to be economically mined.
Last week, consulting firm IW Consult and Fraunhofer ISI, commissioned by Germany ’ s KfW Research, published a report on import research that explores its impact on value chains and employment.
The report analyses copper, lithium and rare earths, raw materials that are critical to future key technologies.
Copper for manufacturing processing needs to be imported (pictured, copper rods from the Hamburg warehouse of metal supplier Aurubis AG)
According to the study, nearly a third of the gross value added in German manufacturing comes from the production of copper products. 10% of the value-added income comes from the production of lithium products and 22% from products containing rare earth.
Among them, automobile manufacturers and their parts suppliers, electrical, electronic and optical products manufacturers are particularly dependent on imports.
The raw materials market is dominated by a handful of suppliers with large market shares – a fact that exacerbates the dependence on imports.
The largest rare earth deposits are located in China.
Mineral deposits in Greenland, Canada and Sweden have not been sufficiently explored to quantify their reserves.
Almost a third of Germany ’ s lithium, 19% of copper and rare earth imports are considered at risk. The three major suppliers of lithium and rare earth metals have a market share of more than 80%.
Of particular importance to the German market are copper from Russia and lithium carbonate from Chile, which accounts for 72% of Germany ’ s total lithium carbonate imports.
Germany will remain highly dependent on China for rare earth imports for a long time – 84% of Germany ’ s rare earth imports come from China.
Background reading: How important are rare earths and why is China's dominance difficult to shake?
It is more dependent on Russian natural gas.
Matthias Wachter, head of the division of the Confederation of German Industry (BDI), also noted this dependence.
"Germany is more dependent on China for non-energy raw materials than Russian gas," he told Deutsche Welle, adding that imports of mining, refining and trading products are already at "the highest risk level."
The danger lies not in the availability of these raw materials, but in the concentration of exploration, especially subsequent processing, in China.
This high level of dependence is vulnerable to threats and extortion.
By imposing export controls on some rare earths, China has shown that it can regulate these key areas.
Cornelius Bähr, a senior consultant at the German Economic Research Institute in Cologne (whose subsidiary IW Consult is one of the authors of the study), told Deutsche Welle that the future demand for raw materials may increase: “For example, lithium for battery production. ” He also confirmed Wacht ’ s concern:“ Another risk factor is the high dependence on a single country, such as gallium, germanium or graphite. Imports from China.
This risk is particularly worrisome if these countries start to threaten to impose strategic trade restrictions, "he said.
How can Europe break China ’ s monopoly on rare earths? Start with recycling!
Vaht said the current delivery disruptions "have not reached critical levels."
But a reliable supply chain is “totally out of the question. ”
The Houthi rebels in the Arabian Peninsula are now showing the world the “fragility of global trade. ”
Bell also points to political risks in the supply chain.
For example, the China-US trade dispute and the China-EU trade dispute.
This could lead to mutual restrictions on exports, or at least threaten to impose such restrictions. "
What's the way out?
“Ensuring the safety of raw materials requires consideration of the entire value chain from extraction to the import of semi-finished products. ”
Fritzi Köhler-Geib, chief economist at KfW, came to this conclusion.
“Resilient, stable and anti-jamming raw material supplies may come with costs at first, but in the end it is a prerequisite for green and digital transformation, ” she said.
“We shouldn ’ t be fooling ourselves: reducing dependency and building more resilience isn ’ t something that can be done overnight. ”
The key is “diversification of supply countries and the development of new capacity. ”
Strengthening domestic resource extraction or production is also part of the solution.
Contrary to popular belief, Germany is actually rich in many raw materials.
Lithium mining in Chile ’ s Atacama Desert – where 72% of Germany ’ s lithium imports come from
Bell urged Germany to take action to “diversify suppliers, find alternatives to key raw materials, expand its own resources, and increase recycling. ”
This will be achieved on the basis of appropriate location conditions (such as energy costs) and public acceptance, "he said.
Supply of raw materials has been disrupted.
Wachter called for a broader layout of the German economy: “The lack of diversification in the supply chain endangers Germany ’ s supply security. ”
Even without assessing the economic consequences of the worst-case scenario, it is entirely conceivable that Germany's geographical advantages and prosperity as an industrial nation would be seriously threatened: without raw materials, industrial enterprises would not be able to function and climate targets would not be met.
"If the supply of raw materials is not available, there is a risk that the corresponding industrial production can not be carried out," Bell said, for example: "Without lithium supply, it is impossible to produce batteries, batteries must be imported, but if the batteries can not be imported, it is impossible to produce electric vehicles."
With that comes the fall in the value of German industry and the loss of jobs, "he said.

Xinhua News Agency, BUENOS AIRES, March 19 (Xinhua) -- Argentine President Gloria Macapagal-Millet has been in power for 100 days
Xinhua News Agency, Wang Zhongyi
Argentine President Gloria Macapagal-Millet has launched a series of "shock therapy" reforms aimed at reducing the fiscal deficit and controlling inflation since he took office last December.
The two main reform measures proposed by the Millet government are still pending due to parliamentary procedures.
Argentina has achieved a fiscal surplus for two consecutive months, and inflation has eased, but unemployment has increased, industrial production has fallen and prices have risen.
Analysts believe that whether the reform can get parliamentary support, whether inflation can be controlled, and whether public anxiety can be relieved are still challenges facing the government.
Prospects for reform uncertain
In his first month in office, Millet introduced two major reforms, a necessary emergency decree called "The Basis of Argentina's Economic Reconstruction" and a comprehensive bill called "The Basis and Starting Point of Liberties for Argentines", aimed at loosening government and legal control over the economy, reducing the fiscal deficit and facilitating import and export trade.
Mile also devalued the peso, Argentina's currency.
On March 14, the Argentine Senate voted to reject the necessary emergency decree signed by Millet, which will then be submitted to the Chamber of Deputies for consideration and vote.
According to Argentine law, even if the decree is rejected by the Senate, the decree may enter into force if it is passed by a vote of the Chamber of Deputies; if it is rejected by the Chamber of Deputies, the decree will be null and void.
The bill, which has not yet been passed by the parliament, is currently scheduled to be amended to be submitted to the parliament for consideration.
Analysts believe that the resistance to the reform mainly comes from the left and the trade unions, and because the ruling party and the left-wing opposition parties do not have a majority in both houses, Millet still needs to win the support of the central parties to push for the reform.
Sun Hongbo, deputy researcher of the Latin American Institute of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, believes that the Milai government intends to carry out a systematic and radical reform, but the relevant reform measures are facing various political checks and balances.
On the whole, Millet's government is facing constraints from various forces, such as the ruling coalition, left-wing parties, local governments and trade unions, and there are many uncertainties in its prospects for radical reform.
People's plight to be alleviated
Recently, many news is regarded as good by the Argentine government: Argentina's central bank cut its benchmark interest rate to 80%, two consecutive months of fiscal surplus, inflation pressure has eased, the International Monetary Fund approved another 4.7 billion US dollars of loans to Argentina, Argentina completed more than 50 billion US dollars of debt replacement.
Despite this, the population of Argentina is still plagued by rising unemployment and rising prices.
In March, the Argentine people ushered in the day of resumption of work and school, but many people received calls to be dismissed.
Argentine media reported that companies said sales had fallen sharply and could not afford to hire so many employees.
Unemployment, poverty and rising prices loom over the Argentine population.
Argentine sociologist Marcelo Rodríguez said that more than 50,000 jobs have been lost due to government cuts, layoffs and the withdrawal of funds from public programs, and unemployment in Argentina is expected to rise in the future.
According to the latest report of the Argentine Industrial Union, Argentina's industrial production index fell to 29.9% in January this year, the lowest level in recorded history, and for the seventh consecutive month it was in the contraction range of less than 50%.
The report said that more than half of the small and medium-sized enterprises in the survey declined in output, and multiple sets of data showed that the plight of industrial production in Afghanistan has intensified, with small and medium-sized enterprises bearing the brunt
According to UNICEF, poverty among children and adolescents in Argentina will reach about 70% and extreme poverty 34% in the first quarter of 2024.
On March 18, a number of labor unions in Argentina launched marches in Buenos Aires and other cities across the country. In January, a number of national trade unions and leftist organizations also held a national strike to protest that the reform measures of the Mile government ignored the rights of labor and social vulnerable groups, resulting in the suspension of services in banks, gas stations, airports, airlines, sanitation and other industries in Argentina.
Economy faces stagflation challenge
Argentine economist Gustavo Nefa believes that the Mile government has reversed the decline in Argentina's dollar reserves in the past 100 days, but the country's economy still faces the challenge of stagflation.
Argentina's National Institute of Statistics and Census data show that Argentina's inflation rate in February this year was 13.2%, down from 20.6% in January and 25.5% in December last year; the cumulative inflation rate in the past 12 months reached 276.2%.
Rosendo Fraga, a researcher at the National Institute of Ethics and Political Science in Argentina, said that although the monthly inflation rate has decreased, inflation is still at a high level.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) released a report on January 30, predicting that Argentina will face recession and rising inflation in the context of a sharp economic policy adjustment.
The report predicts that the Argentine economy will shrink by 2.8% in 2024.
Argentina's TN news television recently quoted a report by the international rating agency Moody's Investors Service saying that the Argentine economy is expected to shrink by 5% in 2024, a decline far beyond the 2.5% forecast in November 2023.
In terms of inflation, Argentina ’ s inflation rate is expected to exceed 280% in 2024 and will still exceed 220% in 2025.
