Aircraft development aimed at high energy, intelligent
The "double carbon" goal requires civil aviation to develop in the direction of green and low-carbon, and civil aviation will be more environmentally friendly, safer and more economical.
The general trend of the development of aviation science and technology is the compound development of high energy and intelligence, high energy for "body" and intelligence for "soul".
High energy is more control of energy and matter, which determines the physical boundary that aviation equipment can achieve, and has a direct impact on performance indicators such as flight height, range, speed and mobility.
Intelligence is the control of the information domain and the cognitive domain, which determines the ability of aviation equipment to use, and can achieve higher efficiency and more accurate decision-making.
Aviation high energy mainly includes high kinetic energy, high energy supply, efficient energy use and so on.
The high kinetic energy mainly corresponds to the technical innovation direction of the aviation platform.
High-speed flight, ultra-maneuverability, long-time stagnation and so on are the core demands of its development, speed from subsonic, supersonic to hypersonic, altitude from low altitude, hollow to high altitude, near space, time from hours, tens of hours to days and so on.
High kinetic energy can play an important role in the field of aviation, such as the application of low-noise supersonic civil aircraft.
High energy supply mainly corresponds to the technical innovation direction of aviation power.
Large push weight ratio, high fuel efficiency, high power extraction and new energy system are becoming the main development trend of aviation power system, including the active flow control of intake and exhaust, high pressure ratio gas pressure system, new concept power system and other related technologies are currently the hot direction of aviation power research.
In addition, electric aircraft and hydrogen-powered technology will also become the cutting edge of low-carbon, creating greater environmental and economic potential for the future civil aviation industry.
The efficient use of energy mainly corresponds to the technical innovation direction of aviation electromechanical.
Among them, multi-electric / all-electric technology, whole-machine energy optimization, and transformative energy transmission and storage will play a key role in the aviation power electrical system, thereby greatly improving the performance level of the aircraft.
The core of aviation intelligence is to make the aircraft have the ability of autonomous perception, autonomous decision-making, autonomous execution and autonomous evolution.
The autonomous sensing enables the aircraft to classify and identify complex environments and targets through the fusion of various sensors and data, and generates information that can be used for decision-making. Based on the "autonomous genetic evolution" algorithm, the autonomous evolution can make the intelligent aircraft have the characteristics of a living body, and the cognitive decision-making level can evolve in real time through continuous learning, and the ability can be independently improved to cope with a new environment.
It should be said that intelligence will greatly improve the perception, decision-making, execution, and learning capabilities of aircraft in different environments, and will open up greater imagination for future aviation.
2. Metamaterials, intelligent structures or will bring about disruptive changes
In the field of aviation, there is a saying that "one generation of materials and one generation of equipment", it can be seen that material properties are crucial to aircraft performance.
In addition, the aviation industry is essentially a high-end equipment manufacturing industry, and manufacturing technology is important for achieving stable large-scale batch production.
With the development of technology, the aviation industry is entering the era of material and manufacturing integration, and it has also made the field of material manufacturing an important source of disruptive technologies.
Metamaterials are man-made materials that achieve supernormal physical properties by artificially designing internal structures, and their basic structural unit scale is smaller than its wavelength, which can control the propagation of light waves, radio waves and mechanical waves. Typical metamaterials include left-handed materials, photonic crystals and phonon crystals.
Left-hand material is an electromagnetic metamaterial that can regulate and control electromagnetic waves. Its dielectric constant and permeability are both negative values. It has the characteristics of negative refraction, inverse Doppler effect, inverse Cherenkov radiation and subwavelength diffraction. Acoustic metamaterial, its band gap can inhibit elastic waves in a certain frequency range can not propagate, can achieve shock absorption and noise reduction.
Metamaterials enable reverse design from function to structure, which can have a number of potentially disruptive effects in the aviation sector:
— — Construct a metamaterial “invisibility cloak ” and a metamaterial wave-absorbing body that can achieve perfect invisibility, greatly improving the invisibility of the aircraft;
- Manufacturing small RF antennas and super-resolution imaging systems to effectively enhance detection and tracking capabilities;
The coupling design of the planar transmission antenna and the metamaterial can improve the antenna radiation efficiency and reduce the size, and promote the miniaturization and integration of the microwave radio frequency components of aviation equipment.
Intelligent structure technology integrates sensors, drivers and control elements into matrix materials to achieve self-diagnosis, self-adaptation and self-repair functions, which is one of the development directions of advanced aircraft in the future, and the main research directions are intelligent skin and self-adaptive variant structures.
The intelligent skin implanted thousands of micro-computing systems with sensing, processing and communication capabilities only the size of rice grains into the material, cooperatively sensing the surrounding environment, thereby regulating the overheating and overstrain areas, or adjusting the internal electromagnetic parameters, reducing electromagnetic scattering signals to achieve stealth functions.
The intelligent skin integrates functional components with the structure, and has functions such as radio detection and energy storage, which has great potential in reducing weight, saving space and improving the stealth performance of the aircraft.
The adaptive variant structure is characterized in that the adaptive variant structure is composed of a processor and a controller, and the processor is connected with the processor.
The intelligent structure is characterized in that the intelligent structure is composed of a wing self-adaptive structure and a wing self-adaptive structure, wherein the wing self-adaptive structure is arranged on the wing self-adaptive structure; the wing self-adaptive structure is arranged on the wing self-adaptive structure; and the intelligent structure is arranged on the wing self-adaptive structure.
Changes in engines and fuels, or will profoundly change the future of aviation
The engine and fuel can be seen as the heart and blood of the aircraft, and disruptive developments in this field will profoundly change the future of aviation.
The application of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is considered to be the most promising technology.
SAF refers to renewable, the use of the process of environmental impact of small aviation fuel, with less carbon emissions, reduce dependence on oil and other non-renewable energy, promote economic development and other advantages, mainly divided into biomass fuel, synthetic fuel, electric energy and hydrogen fuel four.
Due to the problems of high production cost, small production scale, storage and transportation difficulties, sustainable aviation fuel has not been widely used at present.
Sustainable aviation fuel technology has an irreplaceable role in helping to achieve carbon peak carbon neutrality goals and enhance energy security, and can achieve major changes in aviation power systems.
In the future, civil aviation power systems will significantly reduce aviation carbon emissions by using sustainable fuels as turbine engine fuel or directly using fuel cells to power aircraft.
Adaptive variable cycle engine is a next-generation turbofan engine that automatically switches between high thrust and high fuel efficiency modes by adjusting the thermal cycle parameters such as engine duct ratio and total pressure ratio.
The self-adaptive variable cycle engine has good economic performance and wide working range, and can meet various performance requirements, so that the future aircraft presents a multi-mission and multi-purpose development trend.
At the same time, engine technology can be shared on a variety of aircraft, and a series of engines can be derived from the benchmark engine, which can expand the scope of application of the engine and reduce the research and development cost
A rotary detonation engine (RDE) booster combustion in the form of detonation.
The coupling of shock wave and combustion wave is realized in the propagation process of detonation wave. The combustion speed is fast, and the pressure and density after wave are obviously increased.
The utility model has the advantages of simple structure, high specific punching efficiency, wide working area, etc.
Some studies believe that the thermal efficiency of the rotary detonation engine can theoretically increase by 15% compared with the current turbine engine.
In addition to being used as a power device alone, the rotary detonation engine can also be combined with a turbine engine, a ramjet engine and a rocket engine to improve the performance of the original power device.
The rotary detonation engine has become one of the most potential innovators in the field of aeronautical power in the future, and the application prospect is broad.
4. Quantum information, 5G, big data, enabling aviation technology
In recent years, as the research of artificial intelligence technology has entered the third wave, breakthroughs have been made in quantum information, 5G, big data, etc., which has quickly become a hot research direction and an important source of aviation enabling technology.
Brain-computer interaction, also known as brain-computer interface (BCI) technology in the field of aviation has great application value, the world is actively studying. In 2013, the University of Minnesota achieved the first human brain wave control four-axis remote control aircraft; in May 2014, the German "brain flight" program realized the pilot with the brain precision control flight.
Brain-computer interface technology can create a new type of aircraft control.
Perhaps, in the future, the aviation field can directly control the aircraft by the brain, reduce or completely replace the limb operation, and greatly change the traditional man-machine interface.
Perhaps, in the future, the aviation field can learn from the structure and operation of the human brain, develop a new information processing system, and give the avionics system a new function and form.
Perhaps, the future can be combined with virtual reality technology, applied to flight simulation training, can effectively reduce training costs and improve training safety.
In recent years, quantum information technology has made great progress in theory and experiment.
In theory, more advanced theories such as quantum error correction codes have been mastered, which has greatly improved the fault tolerance rate of quantum computing; in experiments, countries have invested a lot of resources in research and development.
Quantum information technology will change the traditional avionics form in an all-round way.
For example, quantum computing superconventional computing power can not only achieve the optimization of aircraft research and development, but also accelerate the training and implementation of artificial intelligence algorithms, and improve the efficiency of system command and decision-making; for example, quantum communication can provide high-speed confidential communication guarantee, and inertial navigation based on quantum gyroscopes can greatly improve the autonomous navigation accuracy of aviation vehicles.
Multidisciplinary cross-field is an important source of disruptive technologies, and interdisciplinary, cross-field integration innovation is also a feature of the aviation field, which makes a number of aviation disruptive technologies reflect the characteristics of cross-integration innovation.
After decades of development, China's aviation industry has made brilliant achievements.
Entering the new era, the exploration and research and industrialization of disruptive technologies is an important support for the realization of aviation power, and it is also an extremely complex system engineering, which requires strategic planning and layout and strategic focus to promote development.
Strengthening the original innovation is the only way to achieve a high level of development in the aviation field in the new era, and taking disruptive technology as the traction is an important grasp of the new era of aviation to achieve lane change and overtaking, and it is necessary to take the initiative to carry out scanning, identification and prediction of aviation disruptive technology, and firmly grasp the pulse of future aviation development.

Science fiction "Three Bodies" adapted into a new drama on the Internet to impact the Chinese scale
Created by Chinese writers, the “Three Bodies ” was adapted by Western producers as a series performed by a number of foreign actors, which not only greatly reduced the Chinese elements, but also opened with scenes of the Cultural Revolution fighting dead.
Like the story of the alien invasion of Earth, it is also impacting the “beliefs ” of many Chinese and the“ yardstick ” of the Beijing authorities.
“Three Bodies ” is a bestselling novel by renowned Chinese science fiction writer Liu Cixin, who has won one of the world ’ s most influential awards in science fiction literature. In China,“ Three Bodies ” has been considered “difficult to adapt ” for its puzzling time jumps, philosophical dilemmas and intensive exploration of scientific theory.
Today, the “Three Bodies ” are on the international screen through Netflix, a rare breakthrough in foreign media observation, in contrast to the suppression of science fiction in Chinese history.
★ A rare breakthrough under Beijing ’ s repression
Produced by Game of Thrones producers, Netflix ’ s new series “3 Body Problem ” is based on China ’ s best-selling science-fiction novel of the same name, according to the BBC. The novel is still popular in China despite China ’ s ongoing censorship of the genre.
The story structure of the “Three Bodies ” is roughly the same: one day in 1967, Ye Wenjie, an astrophysics student in Beijing, witnessed her father being beaten to death by the Red Guards during the Cultural Revolution.
She joined a military project in Inner Mongolia to avoid being punished by a series of sit-ins, but on the condition that she never leave the base.
At this cold outpost, under a huge parabolic antenna, Ye Wenjie lost all confidence in humanity.
She devoted her life to research and made scientific breakthroughs, broadcasting high-power radio signals into outer space.
This action will have serious consequences, and it all stems from that disastrous day in Beijing.
In addition to the trans-cosmic plot, the Three Bodies also involve secret scientific projects; an alien species in the solar system beyond the stars; and a strange video game depicting the rise and fall of great civilizations over the millennia.
“The Three Bodies ” is the first of a trilogy of“ Past Events on Earth ” written by Beijing-born Liu Cixin. A Chinese adaptation of the film was shelved in 2017.
But now it ’ s on the international screen via Netflix, the belated return of Game of Thrones creators David Benioff and DB Weiss.
Early reviews were divided over whether they could be successfully adapted.
What ’ s more, the original novel has been an incredible success. It was first serialized in China ’ s Science Fiction World magazine in 2006 and translated to Western readers by Liu Yukun in 2014.
Its fans include former US President Barack Obama and "Game of Thrones" author George RR Martin.
He is the author of the Qur ’ an.
Liu Cixin won the most prestigious Hugo Award for Best Novel in 2015, and the book and its two sequels have sold nearly 9 million copies worldwide.
Today, Liu Cixin is credited with bringing Chinese science fiction to the world.
This is an incredible feat considering China ’ s historical suppression of science fiction.
The English translation begins with the words: “In more than 40 days, in Beijing alone, more than 1,700 victims were beaten to death at a protest meeting ” and“ many others have chosen an easier path to avoid this madness. ”
Set in 1967, the novel kills as many as 2 million people in the Cultural Revolution over the next decade as the student-led radical Red Guards gradually turned violent in support of the Communist policies of then-Communist leader Mao Zedong.
Many of the victims committed suicide to “end their suffering. ”
The report believes that, in the modern episode of the “Three Bodies, ” the unexplained suicides that have occurred in the scientific community hint at this fact.
But what ’ s more striking than how this real history shapes events in Liu ’ s work is how the Mao regime shaped the course of science fiction in the real world.
It was dormant in the 1960s.
Liu Cixin was born in 1963, three years before the Cultural Revolution.
Li Hua, a professor of Chinese at Montana State University, said that in that era, scientists, writers and other intellectuals were branded “counter-revolutionaries ” and sent to labor camps for“ ideological transformation, ” with few literary works published, “Chinese science fiction remained dormant from the early 1860s to 1967, ” and it was especially difficult to survive the turbulent political situation, with many common themes being taboo, such as Mao ’ s. Marxist-Leninism makes no provision for the existence of aliens in the universe.
But as the “three bodies ” postscript reveals, after witnessing China ’ s first artificial satellite painting the sky in April 1970, six-year-old Liu Cixin will still be moved by“ unspeakable curiosity and longing. ”
A few years later, he found a box of books under his father ’ s bed, including Jules Verne ’ s “Journey to the Heart of the Earth. ” Liu found that he had a determination, like the character in his book, Ye Wenjie, that would ultimately have a profound impact.
Mao Zedong died in 1976, and Ye Wenjie described that year in “The Three Bodies ” as“ the horrors experienced during the Cultural Revolution gradually subsided ”. After Deng Xiaoping came to power in 1977, science fiction flourished for a short time. Deng Xiaoping said that “science and technology are the first productive force. ” Creation.
Fearing a greater spread of Western ideas to China, the CCP launched a campaign in 1983 to “clean up mental pollution. ”
Li said: “It aims to eradicate the Western-inspired trend of ‘ bourgeois liberalization ’.
The Propaganda Department singled out specific literary genres to attack and suppress, including sci-fi works of ghost stories, violence, sex, anti-scientific assumptions, and veiled criticisms of socialism, and classified them as “spiritual pollution. ”
Leading writers such as Ye Yonglie, who wrote stories about space travel when China launched its first satellite into orbit, were condemned, and Science Literary magazine was forced to publish non-fiction works, and in the process renamed the more unobtrusive “Strange Tales. ”
Li said that after a few months, Deng Xiaoping ended the event, but "many science fiction writers, disappointed and emotionally hurt, left the field."
Even if science fiction is revived again, political sensitivities are holding back its development.
Liu Cixin ’ s first full-length novel, China 2185, in 1989, describes cyberpunk fantasies about Mao ’ s resurrection in virtual reality.
This suggests that sci-fi narratives “were prevented from appearing in print due to sensitive sociopolitical topics, but were later published online, ” Li said, but many such works would soon be removed.
Most writers are self-censoring.
With its rapid economic growth in the 1990s, China is now a modern and prosperous country, and science fiction has flourished in China. In the 1990s, with films such as Jurassic Park and The Hacking Empire, Western works by Hugo Award winners Philip K Dick and Arthur C Clarke hit bookshelves.
By the turn of the century, “Science Fiction World ” had reached 400,000 copies, the largest of its kind. In 2019, another film,“ Wandering Earth ”, directed by Liu Cixin, became a hit in China, marking a watershed moment for Chinese science fiction films.
Li Hua believes that the change during this period is that the Chinese government's censorship system is relatively strict on social and political issues, but relatively lax on technical issues, so most writers will self-censor their works and avoid mentioning sensitive topics.
But the report believes that sociopolitical criticism is not impossible for Chinese writers.
Liu Yukun, a translator, said at the Reddit “Geek ” conference in 2015 that“ criticism of the Cultural Revolution is not a forbidden topic in China. ”
Liu Tsz Hin became the first Asian to win a Hugo Award, but his book nonetheless exposes the sensitive nature of his ideas. After all, chapters with a Cultural Revolution background were moved to the middle part of the original Chinese version for fear that government censors might find them too politicized, which is the beginning of the English version of the “Three Body ”.
Netflix ’ s new series “Three Bodies ” starts in the same way as the English version of the book, and they don ’ t worry about censorship.
But the new series is based on Liu Cixin ’ s original novel, and unlike the original novel, they will face the critical judgment of the audience.

San Francisco-based OpenAI said, “We acknowledge the significant risks involved in generating speech that resembles someone ’ s voice, especially given the election year … We work with U.S. and international partners in government, media, entertainment, education, civil society, and other areas to ensure that we incorporate their input into the build process. ”
Fake information researchers are concerned that AI-powered applications are being abused in a critical election year, as voice copying tools become more and more affordable, easy to use, and difficult to track.
OpenAI, which recognises these issues, said it would be cautious and kept abreast of wider releases "based on the potential for synthetic speech abuse."
A few months ago, a political adviser to a Democratic presidential primary candidate in the United States admitted to impersonating President Joe Biden ’ s voice by calling AI-generated automated voice calls that sounded like Biden ’ s call to voters not to vote in January ’ s New Hampshire primary.
The incident alarmed experts who feared a flood of AI-generated fake information ahead of the US presidential election in November and other important elections around the world.
OpenAI said that partners testing the Voice Engine have agreed to a number of specifications, including requiring that all voices copied by the tool be given explicit and informed consent.
OpenAI also said that it is also necessary to clearly inform the audience that the sound they hear is generated by AI.
“We have implemented a range of security measures, including digital watermarking to track the source of all audio generated by the Voice Engine and proactively monitor how the tool is used, ” OpenAI said.

Hong Kong Guide Dogs Raising Difficult AI Guide Dogs as a New Choice?
The Visually Impaired: Heart Comfort Is Hard to Replace
Author ： BU 《新報》

“When young blind people apply for a guide dog in their 20s, they will need to retire by the time they are in their 30s. There is always a demand for more than one guide dog in their lives, ” said Mr Lam Wai-pong, former Chairman of the Hong Kong Guide Dogs Association.
The process of training a "qualified" guide dog is not easy. Volunteer Zandee said that the selection of a potential dog into the "school" is based on the dog's eight generations of family history.
In the era of artificial intelligence, guide dogs are also "intelligent", but for the visually impaired Dick, guide dogs are not only "working dogs", but also "spiritual comfort", and AI guide dogs are difficult to replace the status of living guide dogs in his heart.
This article is licensed by the New Yorker.
The number of guide dogs to middle age and retirement training is difficult to catch up with the speed of loss.
When Wing and the guide dog Doctor cross the road, Doctor will actively slow down, quietly stop and wait for further instructions from Wing, Wing said that such companionship increases the sense of security of going out.
But it turned out that Doctor ’ s arrival was not easy, she waited five years to meet Doctor.
In the process, she once gave up the idea of queuing, and sighed: "Wait so long, it is better not to raise."
According to government statistics in 2021, there are about 200,000 visually impaired people in Hong Kong, but there are only two guide dog training institutions in Hong Kong. Among them, the Hong Kong Guide Dogs Association has 60 active and training dogs.
The average waiting time for a guide dog for a visually impaired person is three years. “Not every guide dog works until the age of 10 and retires early if he is sick or has other problems.
If 10 blind people apply for a guide dog, the association will need to train at least 16 guide dogs, ” he said. He added that the average number of guide dogs successfully trained by the association in a year is only 2 to 3, so it is difficult for applicants to find a suitable guide dog in a short period of time.
Wing, now 30, has been living with Doctor for four years, and will retire in six years, when she will have to wait in line for another guide dog.
According to the International Guide Dogs Federation (IGDF), the ideal ratio of visually impaired people to guide dogs is 100: 1.
Wing and his mother, who are visually impaired, are very fond of the guide dog Doctor, saying that if Doctor retires, they will not be willing to apply for a new guide dog. (photo by Cheung Hsiao-lin)
Application guide dog strict conditions expert: personality fit is the most important
Dick, a visually impaired man who used two guide dogs, has now been on the waiting list for two years.
He said that people with visual disabilities often face a variety of objective conditions when applying for a guide dog. Among them, environmental factors are the biggest consideration, such as the crowded environment of some people with visual disabilities, opposition from their families, or financial pressure to abandon the application.
In addition, there are many conditions for matching a suitable guide dog, such as whether the pace and personality of the visually impaired person and the guide dog are suitable.
A guide dog can be paired with a visually impaired person for up to eight years. The guide dog needs to spend more than half of its service time with the owner. Therefore, Lin Wei-pang pointed out that the dog ’ s lifestyle and personality are important considerations when applying. If the applicant is more active, the association will pair the dog with a more active guide dog. A quieter guide dog will be assigned.
Passengers are very concerned about the guide dog Wang Wang, who accompanied his owner on the train. (photo by Zhang Xiaolin)
Insufficient breeding resources to train dogs to retire at least 500,000
Unlike pet dogs, guide dogs are bred not by natural mating, but by artificial insemination.
"She (guide dog Ivy) has been a guide dog for eight generations, so that she can inherit stable temperament, wisdom, cooperation with others (genes). People who may not understand will think that it is OK to have two dogs on the dog farm, but it is not so." 」
Zandee, who is also a volunteer with the Guide Dogs Association and a foster family, will often bring retired guide dog star "Little Q" Ivy to the streets, hoping that more people will know the guide dogs. (photo by Zhang Xiaolin)
As a dog mother, she is only allowed to have a maximum of three children in her lifetime, and the sperm of the dog needs to be exchanged with other countries from time to time to avoid inbreeding and genetic diseases.
Lin Wei-bang said that the process of artificial insemination of guide dogs is more complicated, "the largest and most active sperm should be selected with a microscope for artificial insemination". Breeding guide dogs requires a lot of technical support, and the process will also increase the difficulty and cost of breeding a guide dog.
For example, Ivy, mother of a guide dog breed, and her children, a dog must have at least three generations of guide dog blood and have a reproductive success rate of 80% before it can be selected as a breeding dog to inherit good genes.
(courtesy of Zandee)
In addition to the complicated breeding process, the shortage of local professionals has also become a problem in breeding guide dogs.
For example, the Guide Dogs Association of Hong Kong has only one Guide Dog Instructor (GDMI) who is responsible for matching guide dog applicants with guide dogs, and only three Guide Dog Trainers.
"Many people are interested, but because we are a non-profit organization, the salary is not significant." In addition, the government does not provide subsidies, the organization matches guide dogs to the visually impaired, and there is no extra charge, resulting in huge expenditure; "he bluntly:" If there is not enough financial support, we will be very difficult to expand the guide dog service. "」
Lin Wei-bang says that to become a trainer, you must first become a staff member of the association, and then conduct on-the-job training according to the course provided by the International Guide Dog Federation. The training course is about 2 to 3 years. (photo by Zhang Xiaolin)

Dick believes that Hong Kong ’ s crowded urban environment is not suitable for smart guide dogs, especially when there are more people. Street," I guess these (AI guide dogs), you try to walk in the women's street, (AI guide dogs) do not know where to be kicked! "

Sarah, trainer of the Hong Kong Guide Dogs Association, and Cookie, a guide dog in training. (photo by Liu San-yi)

Dick said that he prefers to travel with animal guide dogs. For him, the guide dog Wangwang is not only a travel aid, but also a comfort and companion. (photo by Zhang Xiaolin)
Visually impaired people call for more government support

Lin Weibang believes that the development of science and technology may solve some of the problems, but the investment of social resources is the key.
He hoped that the Government would support the development of a guide dog service, improve the relevant policies and resources, provide more long-term protection for the guide dog service, and share the medical costs of dogs with the Association. "Although the Government has been encouraging the use of guide dogs by the visually impaired, it has not provided any substantial subsidy."

Intermittent fasting is one of many popular practices for weight loss or maintenance, also known as time-limited eating, which limits eating to a period of time, usually 8 hours in a 24-hour period, with only clear fluid for the remaining 16 hours.
Previous studies have shown the benefits of limited time eating, and a December 2019 review of human and animal studies found benefits of intermittent fasting, including promoting longevity, lowering blood pressure and weight loss.
However, a preliminary study reported at the American Heart Association meeting on March 18 showed that eating for eight hours or less was significantly associated with a 91% increased risk of cardiovascular disease compared to eating for 12 to 16 hours; the study immediately drew skepticism and comment from experts who have not yet been peer-reviewed and published.
"We were surprised to find that people who followed the eight-hour limit were more likely to die of cardiovascular disease," said study senior author Zhong Wenze, head of the Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics at the School of Medicine at Shanghai Jiaotong University.
"Our findings encourage a more cautious and personalized approach to dietary recommendations, ensuring they are consistent with an individual's state of health and the latest scientific evidence," Chung said in a statement.
The new study analyzed data from 20,000 people who answered their 24-hour eating habits within two days of their first year of registration, a long-term analysis of the health of American adults, and then looked back at deaths in subsequent years.
The analysis showed an association between eight-hour restricted eating and death from cardiovascular disease, but the study was unable to determine whether this dietary pattern was responsible for death.
Many experts question the results of the new study.
“There ’ s a lot of content in the study summary that raises questions about whether this study can show the results that it claims to show, ” said Kevin McConway, an expert in applied statistics in the UK.
“The researchers classified people into different eating patterns based on what and when they reported their diets in just two days, compared to an average of eight years over the study period, ” said McConway.

Rossum, the inventor of the play, originally means "intelligent" (rozum) in Czech, and robota, the robot he created to replace human labor, means "hard work".
The robots that were originally slaves eventually wiped out humanity, becoming the rulers of the earth and launching a new wave of creation.
Since the establishment of the modern chemical industry society in the 20th century, there have been a large number of "human agency" propositions in art and culture in the past 100 years.
As the films Metropolis (1927) or Modern Times (1936) show, the advent of the age of automation has shown a strong distrust of machines as a modern product.
As a narrative setting of text propositions, the "robot against humanity" not only embodies the absence of subjectivity of the human spirit, but also expresses the existentialist crisis of the existence of "I".
American science fiction writer Walter Michael Miller Jr. ’ s 1955 novel “The Darfsteller ” tells the story of the 21st century theater in which there are no more real actors, but perfect and flawless robots performing on stage.
The protagonist, Tony, is an old-school actor who believes in the value of human body performance. He uses every means to interfere with and destroy the robot, in order to allow himself to stand on the stage once again to complete the final performance, in order to make the ultimate sacrifice to the theater art.
Interestingly, the author did not intend the reader to sympathize with Tony, but instead created an image of a preachy, old-fashioned old man, to justify and reflect on the sense of crisis brought about by the so-called “technological progress ”, based on what kind of ideological and value judgment.
The collaboration between AI and generative technologies and humans in the performing arts over the past half century has largely provided a new level of creativity.
However, as human beings as machine users, how can we more specifically imagine the narrative and problem consciousness of human agency in the performing arts?
Science Fiction Imagination and Ethics of Human Organ Relations
Although the famous "three laws of robots" (Note 1) in the novel "I, Robot" seems to have a major shift in the current AI era, but we are often exposed to many films and TV works, the general understanding of the "human agency relationship" is the first ethical problem, but also from the hidden concern of the three laws: robots will not develop human emotions, and then the opposite. Replacing and replacing humans?
The use of machines and data to reconstruct avatars of the dead has been a common theme in science fiction texts.
The ethical issues involved are also based on physical values and spiritual levels.
Tainan Opera Company "Solo Date" (2016) and the singing collective "Love (AI) Wife" (2022) also use AI as a substitute for the deceased lover. Is the intimacy of digital virtual enough to make up for the unfinished regret?
Xu Jiafui ’ s “Dark Dark ” (2018) uses digital technology combined with supernatural imagination to try to demonstrate the performance collaboration between real people and ghosts / non-humans by summoning the soul of the late dance master Tu Fangxun.
From “human-machine coexistence ” to“ being replaced by robots ” in the sense of civilization crisis, Louis Woggart Theatre ’ s “Fairy Tales and Legends ” (2019), or the“ Future Prescription ” (2019) of Qiqiao Theatre and Yu Theatre Taiwan (2019) explore what human values have been preserved and lost under the exchange of principal-subordinate relations after the change of technology.
Playwright Lin Meng-huan ’ s “Ark Trilogy ” (2017-2019) series (Note 2), on the basis of this, continues to investigate the regeneration of civilization, what should post-human and post-civilization do?
This foreboding of the collective human existential crisis, operated by Rimini Protokoll ’ s “Valley of Terror ” (2018), while providing the audience with a centralized robotic rationale as a starting point to reflect on themselves, also potentially ignites our political reflections on the human otherness.
The fear of dissent involved in the "Valley of Terror" theory, compared to the "human agency relationship", the ethical problems it brings to the future are probably more related to the exclusive problem of human beings.
At this point, we can not help but ask is that the common theater text in dealing with the AI and human agency narrative, is prone to our cognitive misunderstanding of the concept of "robot"?
Will the long-term focus on the “robot ” anthropomorphic crisis limit the physical life we imagine in the future, resulting in the misbridging of science fiction propositions?
"Human Organs" as Theatrical Methods and Aesthetic Experiments
“Science fiction ” and“ future ” have never been the same in literature.
As a science fiction text, there are already types of disasters, viruses, or plagues that are common in the narrative tradition. What are the differences and points of emphasis between "human agency" and these propositions?
So, how do we avoid making it easy on imagining AI propositions?
New media artist Wang Liansheng ’ s theatrical creation “Living Room ” (2022) combines AI, experimental sound, motion capture, interactive devices, and real-time generated images to simulate the daily lifestyle of future people.
However, behind the narrative of human agency relations, Wang Liansheng has not only applied AI and generative digital tools as a creative means for a long time, but also continued his creative method of thinking about media or organizational systems to combat the current mechanism.
In addition, the three main aspects of his past creative work: installation, audiovisual performance, and cross-field performance, are integrated in the Living Room.
Japanese director Hirata Oriza ’ s “Robot Five Parts ” (Note 3) is the result of his collaboration with robotics scholar Hiroshi Ishiguro at Osaka University to develop the“ Robot Theater Project ” in the form of robots as AI.
However, Hirata has been exploring the relationship between scientific activities and near-future society since the 1990s with the “Science Trilogy ” (Note 4), in which the relationship between humans and apes is also based on the core of“ human and non-human ”.
In addition, Hirata also put into practice the scientific method of directing “modern colloquial drama ” that he has always advocated, and consciously made a dialogue with Brecht ’ s“ alienated theater ” to make a viewing relationship, which in the macro view is more related to the dialectical return of Japanese realistic drama.
In other words, from the "science trilogy" to the "robot five", Hirata since the 1990s, the Asian concern and mass consciousness has a clear context, so that his later robot theater series is not only a simple "human machine relationship", but also a theater method set into practice.
In addition to focusing on propositions of AI and human-machine narratives, testing the boundaries of human agency relationships in aesthetic experiments has become particularly critical.
If it is said that the digital era has brought about any major changes, the trend of perceptual forms and sensory patterns should not be underestimated.
Lin Yihua ’ s “One by One ” (2021) was premiered in the era of the epidemic, and the creative results promoted by the limitations of reality have made the narrative effectiveness canceled by the virus, and they can only be forced to return to the real physical and technical problems – media conversion, instrumental application, and the validity of the physical body.
The fragmented and fluid performance structure and character actions in the play can be used to verify the perfect metaphor for the existence of the human subject as opposed to contemporary technology.
“City of Sin ” (2013), a collaboration between artist Wang Junjie and“ Luxurious Mechanic ”, is Taiwan ’ s first tech-media unmanned theater, using power installations, robotic arms, images and sound and light effects to replace live performances.
Later, Sodom Nights (2015) at the North American Pavilion used a fully automatic robotic unmanned theater to complete the creation experiment of high-density narrative but abstract aesthetic output.
In addition, due to the relationship of cross-disciplinary teamwork, it is possible to overcome the simple imagination of human agency relations on paper, and the straight-ball responds to the relationship of human cooperation, and also faces the future of contemporary technology theater.
In fact, AI artificial intelligence is a highly technical and logical computing digital tool, strictly speaking, the type of science fiction with AI as the subject should be more inclined to refer to the technical details and logic of the "hard SF" (hard SF).
However, most of the existing human-computer narratives in theater still use "science and technology narratives" as the sociological code of "soft SF", perhaps also related to the human-computer narratives we have received from popular culture for a long time. Although the soft and hard parts of the sci-fi genre may be fake issues, we may wish to ask: How can we continue to advance the premise of "theater art" The radical idea of human agency?
Perhaps, we can separate from "the practice of human organs exploring as a theater method" and "the practice of aesthetic experiments of human organs" as the first step forward.

Promote the application of artificial intelligence to good (new language)
Yu Si-nan
April 09, 2024 09: 01 | Source: People's Daily Online - People's Daily
Small number
To better promote the development of artificial intelligence technology, it is necessary to look ahead and judge the relevant risks, and protect the legal and ethical bottom line.
Find a balance between development and norms, and guide the development of AI applications in the upward direction of goodness
Recently, the phenomenon of using artificial intelligence technology to generate virtual characters has attracted attention.
By collecting photos, voice and other information, the technology can generate images of deceased loved ones, providing emotional support for some families, but also causing some controversy.
Artificial intelligence can restore the image of people more realistically, and it can not be separated from the application of large models.
With high-quality data for training "nourishment", supported by high-performance computing power, artificial intelligence technology has excellent content understanding and generation capabilities.
Organize documents, write code, detect parts and components defects … Artificial intelligence technology has gradually become an important auxiliary for people ’ s production and life.
With the updated iteration of technology, more efficient AI applications will accelerate in the future to empower thousands of industries.
It should also be noted that artificial intelligence technology has brought risks and challenges to social governance and ethics.
Taking the generation of human images as an example, artificial intelligence technology may violate personal privacy and portrait rights when collecting and generating data.
There are also some ethical controversies about breaking the real and virtual boundaries and allowing loved ones to "meet again".
Further, if the relevant technology is used maliciously, it may also lead to illegal activities such as the creation of false information and fraud.
In addition, the use of artificial intelligence technology for creative activities, whether it will infringe intellectual property rights, etc., need to be explored and prevented in continuous practice.
To better promote the development of artificial intelligence technology, it is necessary to look ahead and judge the relevant risks, and protect the legal and ethical bottom line.
Find a balance between development and specifications, and guide AI applications in the direction of upward good.
In this regard, China has made a lot of useful explorations: in order to prevent the abuse and infringement of generative artificial intelligence technology, the Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services were issued in 2023, which clearly proposed the provision and use of generative artificial intelligence services, which should abide by laws and regulations and respect public order and good customs.
How to "get along" with artificial intelligence, the key is the people who use the tools.
From a larger time span, throughout the history of human civilization, from the Stone Age, the Bronze Age, the Iron Age, to the steam age, the electric age, and then to the current information age, the intelligent age, every time the transformation of production tools, have impacted people's inherent experience and thinking, each time we have moved to a new stage in the challenge.
We believe that through forward-looking examination of risks and challenges, sound safeguards ethical norms and legal systems, and strengthened global cooperation and dialogue, we can promote AI technology to better enhance social welfare.
Embracing a better era of intelligence, we need to clarify the boundaries of technology.
In the future, perhaps artificial intelligence will reduce the production of general knowledge, but we should not lose creativity; perhaps the influence of the virtual world is increasing, but it should not let the meaning of the real world dissipate.
No matter how powerful artificial intelligence is only an auxiliary tool, in addition to computing and logic, there is a better world, which is worth our unremitting efforts to achieve.

As the development of the J-10 series failed to meet the challenges of the border environment last week, the Chinese Air Force urgently needed to introduce the third-generation fighter, but due to technical and economic problems, it was unable to import it from the West.
The road to Su-27 is full of thorns.
In 1989, the Soviet Union faced a serious internal crisis and the quagmire of Afghanistan. In May, the leader of the Soviet Union, Gorbachev visited China and sent a generous gift to restart Sino-Soviet military cooperation. On May 31, 1990, General Liu Huaqing, a former army commander, and General Lin Hu, a deputy commander of the Air Force, led a large military representative. It was the first time in more than 30 years that China and the Soviet Union had exchanged views on the possibility of introducing three generations of Soviet aircraft.
In fact, the first thing the Soviet Union wanted to sell to China was not the Su-27, but the MiG-29.
But the MiG-29 is just a “swallow that can ’ t fly over the Dnieper ”, far less capable than the Sukhoi Design Bureau ’ s all-weather heavy air superiority fighter Su-27, which has a combat radius of up to 1,700 kilometers.
In addition to performing aerial missions, the Su-27 and its improved variants are capable of both land and sea attack functions.
It can be seen that the Chinese military leadership has formed the concept of establishing offensive air power as early as the early 1990s, and this concept has had a profound impact on the flight of China's air force.
Therefore, even though the Soviet Union strongly recommended the MiG-29, China was determined to purchase the Su-27.
The NATO nickname given to the Su-27 and its derivative series of fighters is Flanker.
This led to extremely difficult negotiations between China and the Soviet Union, but in the Chinese effort to fight, also used the Soviet military industry, because the system reform caused many enterprises to pay wages, resulting in internal conflicts between the enterprises, the value of $1.4 billion Su-27 military purchase project was finalized in less than a month.
In December 1990, before the collapse of the Soviet Empire, the Politburo of the Communist Party of China agreed to sell the Su-27 fighter to China, the first time in Soviet military history that it was allowed to export the fighter, and the first time since 1962 that China had imported a major fighter jet from abroad.
On March 4, 1991, the personnel of China and the Soviet Union signed a commercial contract in Moscow, completing the contract negotiation and signing tasks of the Su-27 project ahead of schedule.
It determined the specific content of the future transfer of military technology from the Soviet Union to China and the development of military cooperation between the two militaries.
According to the contract, the Soviet Union will deliver 72 Su-27s to the Chinese Air Force within three years, of which 48 are intended.
On December 25, 1991, the Soviet Union was officially declared extinct, and Yeltsin became the first President of the independent Russian Federation, serving as Prime Minister.
Whether or not the agreements signed with the former Soviet Union can be implemented will have to be renegotiated with the Russian Federation.
In order to save the economic crisis, Yeltsin appointed extremely pro-American "boy gang" officials with First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Geidar and Foreign Minister Kozilev as the core to practice "shock therapy".
The world view and attitude of these people to China is: 1.
The new world order after the Cold War will be centered on the G-7, led by the United States, and Russia ’ s foreign policy must be designed around this core, so it must be integrated into the ranks of democratic countries as soon as possible in order to gain a more reasonable historical and social status. 2.
Russia must strengthen ties with the West, especially the United States, and even with Japan and South Korea to minimize the damage to Russia after China collapses.
Russia has resolutely assumed the great responsibility of guarding China and protecting the vested interests of the West.
Therefore, Gaidar and Kozyrev were strongly opposed to inheriting the Su-27 agreement.
Yeltsin himself attaches great importance to developing friendly and cooperative relations with China, but it is precisely through the strength of the two men that he will promote economic reform and deal with the West to obtain assistance.
Therefore, in order to avoid direct dissatisfaction with him by the "boy gang", General Halchenko, the director of the Aviation Technology Administration of the Military Industry Council, who secretly authorized a visit to China, signed an agreement with China on March 2, 1992, confirming that the Russian Federation will honor the military cooperation agreement and related contracts between the former Soviet Union and China, thus ensuring the smooth operation of the Su-27 aircraft.
On June 27, 1992, the first batch of 12 Su-27 fighters, including 8 SK single-seater and 4 UBK two-seater trainers, took off from Jeddah Airport in Russia's rear Baikal Military District and arrived safely at Wuhu Air Base in Anhui, China at 10: 15 a.m. on the same day. The airport is directly connected to the Wuhu Air Force Base.
From the end of last century to the beginning of this century, the Chinese Air Force imported a total of 78 original Su-27SK series fighters from Russia in three batches.
From the introduction to the innovative J-11 series
In April 1993, China's Central Military Commission approved the introduction of the entire Su-27 production line of the "934 project", began the process of the Su-27 nationalization, the two sides through the negotiations, until December 1996, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Poreenakov visited China, and officially signed an agreement with the Chinese side to introduce the Su-27 production line.
According to the contract, Shenfei built 200 Su-27s over a period of 15 years. The first batch of aircraft was all provided by the Komsomolsk-on-Amor Aircraft Production Complex. Later batches of aircraft were gradually transferred to Chinese production, but Russia still provided all 200 aircraft with engines, radar and electronic equipment, and airborne weapons.
At the end of November 1997, Shenfei received all the drawing materials that met the requirements of domestic production.
In December 2001, Shen Fei completed the task of opening the production line, and since then has the ability to start the production of J-11 from the parts (in addition to the engine and radar are also imported from the original Russian factory).
However, after China and Russia signed an agreement to produce 200 Su-27 fighters, Shenyang Aircraft Company only assembled 105 J-11s in five batches from 1998 to 2006.
During its use, the Chinese Air Force discovered some problems with the Su-27SK fighter.
Since 2001, Shen Fei has started to develop the domestically produced J-11B fighter. Compared with the previously licensed J-11A, the biggest feature of the J-11B is the replacement of domestically produced subsystems with better performance, including a new inertial combined navigation system, fuel system, flight control system, environmental control system and domestically produced 1474 radar.
The head-on detection distance of this type of radar to air targets can reach at least 180 kilometers, and with the use of the fourth-generation PL10 infrared air missile and PL12 missile, the overall performance of the J-11B fighter is at least 1.5 times that of the Su-27SK.
After entering 2010, the J-11B fighter technology became more and more mature, and finally got rid of the dependence on Russia in terms of engines, which also laid the foundation for the birth of the J-15 carrier-based aircraft and the J-16 fighter.

The J-35 far exceeds the US F-35 in terms of stealth ability, speed, agility and combat radius, and is the world's leading air superiority type, carrier-based fighter, which forms a high and low match with the J-15.
This once again fully demonstrates that the development of the Scout fighter in China has surpassed that of the Russian equivalent.
The Chinese people were lucky to choose the best aircraft platform, combined with China's high-speed progress, derived from the West's avionics technology and composite material technology, to develop a nearly perfect fighter series!

The Third Generation of Autonomous Superconducting Quantum Computers in China
April 28, 2024 08: 28 | Source: Science and Technology Daily
Small number
Original title: "Goku" generates great computing power
"In just three months, 'Benyuan Wukong' has attracted a total of 5.11 million remote visits from 117 countries around the world, and has completed about 169,000 global quantum computing tasks!" Guo Guoping, deputy director of the Key Laboratory of Quantum Information of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and professor of the Chinese University of Science and Technology, said excitedly in an interview with Science and Technology Daily.
On January 6, 2024, China's third-generation autonomous superconducting quantum computer "Origin Wukong" was launched and opened for free to global users for a limited time.
This is the first large-scale and long-term opening of China's quantum computing power to the world, marking China's formal entry into the "usable" era of quantum computing power, which also means that China's independent superconducting quantum computer manufacturing chain has been "chain".
Three generations of scientists.
The beginnings of quantum computers in China date back to 26 years ago.
"In 1998, I was organizing the Xiangshan Scientific Conference on 'Quantum Communication and Quantum Computing'.
Guo Guangcan, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a professor at the University of Science and Technology of China, recalled to reporters that the conference was to be hosted by a "big person" in order to expand the influence of the conference.
This "big man" is "two bombs and one star" founder Qian Xuesen.
In the letter to Qian Xuesen, Guo Guangcan boldly suggested that "we should take out the spirit of" two bombs and one star "to engage in quantum information", and eagerly invited Qian Xuesen to chair the meeting.
Not long after, Guo Guangcan received a reply from Qian Xuesen.
Qian Xuesen highly agreed with his view that "China should mobilize national forces to overcome the technical problems of quantum information systems."
Although Qian Xuesen was unable to attend due to his physical condition, his support, such as the dawn of light, illuminated the future of quantum scientific research in China.
Since then, Guo Guangcan has applied for relevant research projects. In 2001, he received the first national major project grant in the field of quantum information in China.
In 2010, Guo Guoping, a student of Guo Guangcan, took over the baton and became the chief scientist of the major project of “solid-state quantum chip research ”. In 2013, Guo Guoping led the team to achieve 10 picosecond quantum logic gate operation on“ one electron ”, which increased the previous world record by nearly 100 times, laying a solid foundation for quantum computer research based on semiconductor materials.
In 2017, Guo Guoping led the establishment of the first domestic quantum computer industrialization enterprise - Benyuan Quantum Computing Technology (Hefei) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Benyuan Quantum").
Quantum computers are regarded as the super “industrial accelerator ” of the future because of their powerful computing power and wide application prospects. In 2023, Google conducted a comparative test and showed that quantum computers take less than 3 minutes to complete the same computing tasks, while the fastest supercomputers take about 50 years.
At the beginning of this year, Benyuan Quantum launched a quantum computer equipped with 72 autonomous superconducting quantum chips - "Benyuan Wukong".
The name "Wukong" means that it has the powerful computing power of "72 changes".
Every development starts from zero.
"Superconducting quantum computer industry chain has three key points, chip, hardware, software," Guo Guoping said.
In order to build China's own quantum computer, Benyuan Quantum built two laboratories for quantum chip manufacturing and packaging and quantum computer assembly testing, and completed the full-stack development of software and hardware from the chip to the whole machine.
The quantum chip needs to operate at extremely low temperatures of -273.15 ° C.
This requires that the cable connected to the quantum chip not only transmits the signal without distortion, but also insulates the heat.
"In order to solve this problem, we jointly developed a high-density microwave interconnect module suitable for extremely low temperature environment and realized the localization of the module," said Jia Zhilong, deputy director of Anhui Quantum Computing Engineering Research Center and member of the "Origin Wukong" development team. "This provides important support for the industrialization of superconducting quantum computers in China."
Quantum computer assembly test requires the whole machine assembly and testing of quantum chips, quantum measurement and control instruments, quantum operating systems, quantum software, etc. "Every research and development must start from zero, which means a huge challenge." Guo Guofeng said.
"Benyuan Wukong" hardware development team leader Kong Weicheng introduced, the new machine matching Benyuan third generation quantum computing measurement and control system "Benyuan Tianji", to achieve the first batch of automated testing of quantum chips in China, so that the overall operation efficiency of quantum computers increased by tens of times.
In addition to chips and hardware, "Benyuan Wukong" is also equipped with China's first quantum computer operating system - Benyuan Senan 3.0 version.
Dou Junhan, head of the operating system research and development team, told reporters that this system has realized the support for batch processing of quantum computing tasks for the first time in China, which can not only support ultra-collaborative computing, but also efficiently dispatch quantum computing resources and greatly improve the overall operation efficiency of quantum computers.
Moving from laboratory to manufacturing chain
On April 10, "Benyuan Wukong" successfully equipped the first PQC (post-quantum cipher) "anti-quantum attack shield" in China.
From computing power to "attack and defense", it marks that China's quantum computer manufacturing chain is more complete.
"To build a superconducting quantum computer, you need to start from the theoretical research in the laboratory and go through the whole process." Zhang Hui, general manager of Benyuan Quantum, introduced that Benyuan Quantum has also successively developed and manufactured the domestic quantum chip production equipment such as the first non-destructive probe instrument for quantum chip testing and the laser annealing instrument for quantum chip repair.
With the formation and improvement of the manufacturing chain of superconducting quantum computers integrating research and development, design, production and testing, Origin Quantum has become the only company in China with the overall delivery capability of superconducting quantum computers.
At present, "Origin Wukong" has cooperated with a number of national supercomputing centers and departments and units such as finance, communications, power, aviation and aerospace.
The active participation of these industries has provided a better scientific research soil for the manufacturing and application of quantum computers in China.
This year's government work report proposed to actively cultivate emerging industries and future industries, formulate future industrial development plans, open up new tracks such as quantum technology and life sciences, and create a number of future industrial pilot areas.
"We will accelerate the principle verification, technology transformation and application development of quantum computing, and make steady progress towards realizing the goal of large-scale programmable universal quantum computer."
(Editor: Li Yihuan, Li Fang)

Webmaster 's House (ChinaZ.com) April 30 news: Recently, the well-known voice actor Zhao Qianjing authorized his voice to the AI audio drama "The Legend of Mortal Immortals".
The qin language engine developed by TME Tianqin Lab uses Zhao Qianjing ’ s voice to train a multi-tone AI human voice, which achieves a one-person multi-angle dubbing effect.
The innovation, once announced, caused widespread controversy on social platforms.
Some netizens expressed disappointment, they called themselves "clowns", pointed out that they had just supported the action against AI violating the rights of human voice actors, and in an instant, there were dubbing artists who authorized their voices to AI.
These netizens believe that the one-time sale of sound may damage the long-term interests of voice actors, and because of the extremely low cost and high efficiency of AI sampling, this may pose a threat to the livelihood of traditional voice actors.
On the other hand, some netizens from the perspective of the development of dubbing art and industry, emphasized the irreplaceability of human dubbing.
They believe that the artistic and emotional expression contained in traditional dubbing is difficult for AI to fully replicate.
In addition, empowering the voice to AI may also compress the living space of new people, which is not conducive to the fresh blood injection of the industry.
The controversy gained more attention when the Beijing Internet Court handed down the country ’ s first “AI Voice Infringement Case ” on April 23.
The cause of the case was a dubbing artist who discovered that his voice had been AI and sold without authorization, and that his voice had been used for film and video commentary and game commentary.
According to Article 1023 of the Civil Code of the People ’ s Republic of China, the voice of a natural person enjoys similar protection as the right to portrait, provided that the voice is recognizable.
In this case, the defendants denied infringement, arguing that the plaintiff ’ s AI-based voice lost its recognisability with the soundtrack itself.
However, after the court investigation and the parties' statements, the judge held that the plaintiff's AI voice maintained a high degree of recognizability, and connected with the plaintiff, and finally ruled that the defendant violated the plaintiff's rights, requiring the defendant to apologize in writing and compensate 250,000 yuan in economic losses.
In summary, the rapid development of AI technology has brought challenges and opportunities to the dubbing industry.
The industry needs to find a balance, so that AI technology and traditional dubbing art can coexist, complement and progress together.
At the same time, ensuring that the rights and interests of voice actors are properly protected and their voices and labor are reasonably rewarded is an important issue that the entire industry needs to face.

The research team supported by the National Science Council has developed a special "digital annealing" algorithm, and cooperated with Formosa Plastics, Fujitsu and the Institute for Information Technology to select five kinds of inhibitors from 5,000 candidate structures. The time required has been greatly shortened to 1 / 10 of the original. Research.
Digital Annealing is an attempt to solve complex problems that are too time-consuming to deal with before quantum computers mature to be able to operate, and digital annealing is best used to solve various problems of "combination optimization", such as nurse scheduling.
Fujitsu ’ s third-generation digital annealing hardware has achieved remarkable results by developing a digital annealing algorithm for cyclic compound screening, using the fitting parameters of Formosa Plastics ’ complete compound database, Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO).
The NSC pointed out that the molecules selected by the calculation process are being tested in the PVC (polyvinyl chloride resin) process after being confirmed by the Formosa Plastics pilot plant, and the results have been selected as one of the next covers of the International Journal of Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research.
The research team further explained that the petrochemical products in contact with oxygen, natural oxidation phenomenon will occur, the appropriate addition of inhibitors, can effectively slow down the oxidation rate of compounds, this time is selected phenolic inhibitors for research, hoping to quickly screen the structure with good inhibitory effect from a large number of combinations.
According to the research team, through the annealing model, the team selected five of the more than 5,000 candidate structures that were expected to have the best results, and verified them with traditional classical simulation calculations, and found that the annealing model calculation results were quite accurate.
In the comparison of time cost, from 5000 candidate structures, the selection of 5 kinds of good effect, classical simulation requires 7500 hours, annealing model only needs 700 hours, in other words, the screening time is greatly shortened to about 1 / 10 of the original, for the industry in the synthesis of compounds and the search for new compounds, there is a good acceleration effect.
The research team pointed out that before the general purpose quantum computer mature, the actual application value of this annealing technology is very high. In addition to the phenolic inhibitors research, Formosa Plastics will also be extended to the research of environmentally friendly and green energy-related materials. At the same time, the current screening structure has not yet considered the cost, and price screening will be added in the future.
