A listed company must have at least one female director by the end of the year
Author: Huang Jie
Published: Updated:
Hong Kong Stock Exchange (0388) Listing Supervisor Ng Jie wrote about the achievements of women ’ s equality in Hong Kong stocks.
She said that Hong Kong has achieved remarkable results in encouraging enterprises to increase the proportion of women in senior management.
One in three of the senior management team of the HKEx is female.
The HKEx also requires listed issuers to appoint at least one director of another gender by the end of the year, a move that is already bearing fruit.
She noted that as of June this year, the share of Hong Kong listed issuers with female directors in the market had risen to 84% from 70% in 2021.
With the transition period coming to an end at the end of December this year, issuers with only male members on their boards must seize the time to appoint their first female director as soon as possible.
Mr Ng said this year would be an important turning point for Hong Kong ’ s capital market, where a male-only board would no longer exist, but a forward-looking board culture in line with the 21st century, further strengthening Hong Kong ’ s position as a modern and leading international financial centre.
She added that large companies have leadership advantages and can use their resources, network relationships and influence to drive significant change, but smaller companies need to overcome different challenges, but there is still much that companies can do to find the most qualified, competent and visionary directors in addition to introducing more female directors.
Wu Jie added that promoting board diversity is a revolutionary process that not only changes society and breaks down barriers, but also creates a better and more equal future for society.

The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is the largest and most economically developed country in the Middle East and the third largest oil producer in the world.
Thanks to rapid economic growth and a series of government incentives to attract foreign investment, Saudi Arabia provides a broad market space for companies interested in exploring the Middle East market.
About Saudi Arabia
The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (hereinafter referred to as "Saudi") is located at the strategic crossroads of Europe, Asia and Africa, and its unique location provides investors with unparalleled innate advantages to enter many markets such as the Middle East and North Africa.
Saudi Arabia is an absolute monarchy in the Arab Islamic world, where the king and crown prince consult with the cabinet on all political decisions and adopt an authoritarian system.
As the world ’ s largest oil exporter, Saudi Arabia ’ s economy is highly dependent on the oil and energy sectors.
However, in 2016, Saudi Arabia launched Vision 2030, which aims to diversify its economy and attract more foreign investment to reduce its dependence on oil exports.
With the vigorous development of many fields, the Saudi economy has achieved rapid growth and the level of diversification has also increased significantly.
The investment in science and technology, tourism and renewable energy has effectively improved the country's economic structure and laid a solid foundation for future development.
A series of large-scale infrastructure projects, such as the “Saudi New Future City ” (NEOM), the Red Sea Project and Riyadh Metro, have created lucrative investment opportunities for the construction industry.
Saudi Arabia has also invested a lot of money in promoting the tourism industry, introducing a series of convenient measures such as electronic visas for foreign tourists, which have resulted in a double increase in the number of foreign tourists and employment opportunities in the country.
Saudi Arabia is the only member of the Arab Group of 20 (G20, which accounts for about 80% of world GDP) and the largest member of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).
Saudi Arabia is also a member of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and a founding member of international organizations such as the United Nations, the Organization of Islamic Cooperation and the Arab League.

Saudi Arabia has a favorable geographical position, a long history and rich resources, which is of great attraction to investors from all over the world.
However, companies intending to enter the Saudi market should fully understand the local business environment and complex regulatory system to ensure that business activities are carried out smoothly.
Advantages of doing business in Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia ’ s oil and gas reserves are second and sixth in the world, respectively.
The huge profits of the oil industry are undeniable, but in recent years, Saudi Arabia has shifted its focus to tourism, entertainment, manufacturing, health care, education and technology.
According to the World Bank, Saudi Arabia is a high-income economy and ranks 19th in the world in terms of nominal GDP.
The main advantages of the business environment in Saudi Arabia include a business-friendly overall environment, excellent geographical location and excellent infrastructure.
As a result, Saudi Arabia has become an ideal destination for companies to set up regional headquarters (RHQ) in the Middle East, providing great convenience for further opening the Middle East market.
As the largest economy among GCC members, Saudi Arabia is behind more than 60 million consumers, high economic integration among GCC members and free trade agreements, which provide a broad space for business development.
Saudi Arabia has developed infrastructure, has successively invested in a number of large-scale projects in transportation, logistics, communications, public utilities, etc., which is very suitable for serving as a logistics center for related enterprises such as supply chain management, distribution, and warehousing.
All modes of transportation can be seamlessly connected here, which provides great convenience for entering the international market while improving the efficiency of the movement of people and goods.
The Saudi government has launched a series of incentives and projects, which are also a highlight of the local business environment.
In order to promote private sector growth, Vision 2030 has launched a series of projects to promote privatization, regulatory facilitation and economic diversification around four areas: improving the quality of human resources, improving the business environment for foreign investment, improving public management, and creating a competitive and adaptable labour market.
These projects have significantly enhanced Saudi Arabia ’ s international reputation.
Saudi Arabia actively participates in regional and international political affairs, and gives strong support to the alliance and related projects that promote prosperity, development, peace and stability, which has been highly recognized by the international community.
Saudi Arabia has actively carried out various diplomatic activities, hosted many international summits, and worked hard to build its image as an international power.
The Saudi government has introduced many incentives to stimulate foreign investment, including tax exemptions, subsidies, land grants and expedited approvals.
Special Economic Zones (SEZ) such as King Abdullah Economic City and NEOM provide additional incentives and regulatory convenience for businesses operating in the region.
Saudi Arabia offers a lot of facilities for foreign investment, but to operate smoothly, companies must have a thorough understanding of the local culture and regulatory requirements.
Doing Business in Saudi Arabia: Culture
Islam originated in the land where Saudi Arabia is located.
According to the Basic Law of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Islam is its state religion.
Saudi culture is heavily influenced by Islam, and businesses operating here must fully understand and respect local religious customs and traditions.
Saudi business culture is characterized by conservatism, low profile and friendliness.
Proper greetings and excursions play a very important role in creating a good atmosphere of exchange and building a long-term relationship of mutual trust and cooperation.
In the Western world, regulatory compliance and corporate governance are the foundation of all business practices.
However, in Saudi Arabia, business practices incorporate many local cultural elements on the basis of the above.
Building good cooperation with local parties is a top priority.
To be successful in business, companies must invest a lot of time in building good relationships of mutual trust and respect with the parties concerned.
Top executives should establish good personal relationships with potential partners to pave the way for future business contacts and long-term cooperation.
In exchanges and exchanges, compared with pragmatic and direct, Saudi Arabia is more inclined to euphemism and roundabout.
Before entering into substantive business negotiations, locals are more accustomed to familiarizing themselves with potential partners.
The progress of communication and consultation here is relatively slow, leaving enough room for both sides to maneuver, so rushing forward and rushing time may leave the impression of unreasonable offense.
Therefore, in the negotiation or business meeting, the senior management of the enterprise should be patient and courteous.
Saudi regulatory environment
As the Saudi government continues to simplify regulatory requirements and introduce numerous incentives to attract foreign investment, it has become increasingly easy to set up wholly foreign-owned enterprises in the country.
As a result, Saudi Arabia jumped from 92nd to 62nd in the World Bank ’ s Ease of Doing Business report.
In order to achieve the goals of "Vision 2030", Saudi Arabia has taken various measures to attract foreign investors to establish limited liability companies (LLC) in Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi Ministry of Investment (MISA) even issued a decree in 2015 to repeal the previous law, allowing the establishment of wholly foreign-owned enterprises in the retail and wholesale industries.
Despite the relaxation of regulations, companies still need to be fully aware of the complex local regulatory requirements.
1. Type of enterprise and capital requirements of foreign enterprises
The types of entities that foreign investors can set up in Saudi Arabia are as follows:
The most common include LLC, Joint Stock Company (JSC) and branch companies, where branch companies are preferred by multinational companies.
Although local laws and regulations do not set minimum capital requirements for an LLC, in practice, MISA stipulates a minimum capital of 500,000 Saudi riyals for foreign-owned LLC.
Specific areas such as real estate investment, contracting and business have clear minimum capital requirements.
Investors interested in participating in government procurement projects (wholly or partly funded by the government) are required to set up regional headquarters in Saudi Arabia.
2. Labour legislation
A good understanding of local labour laws and regulations is essential to ensure employment compliance.
Saudi Arabia has set strict requirements for the proportion of its citizens employed, which is a key challenge for foreign investment.
Vision 2030 sets out detailed criteria for promoting employment for nationals. The "Saudi Nationalisation" programme, also known as "Nitaqat", aims to increase the proportion of Saudi citizens employed in the private sector.
The proportion of Saudi employees in the company must not be less than 75% unless special permission is obtained from the Saudi Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD).
If the company can prove that it is unable to find a sufficient number of qualified Saudi employees (with relevant skills or qualifications), the MHRSD will grant the corresponding permission.
Saudi employees can enter into fixed-term or non-fixed-term contracts, but foreign employees can only enter into fixed-term contracts.
Foreigners must hold a work visa to work in Saudi Arabia, for which they must obtain a guarantee from a Saudi employer.
The processing time for work visas is approximately two to three months.
Before hiring foreign workers, companies must obtain a "block visa" (or indicator) approval from the MHRSD.
3. Guarantor system (kafala system)
More than half of Saudi Arabia ’ s workforce are foreign workers.
Like many other GCC member states, Saudi Arabia also adopts the Kafala system for foreign workers (i.e., the guarantor system), which defines the relationship between foreign workers and their employers in the form of a law, including employment contracts, remuneration and working conditions.
Under the system, Saudi Arabia will give companies permission to hire foreign workers.
Human rights organizations have long expressed high concern about the system because of its restrictive nature and the absence of employee safeguards.
In recent years, however, the system has undergone several reforms that have strengthened the protection of the interests of employees and eased restrictions on the freedom of movement of personnel.
From 2021, employees can leave Saudi Arabia or change jobs without the employer ’ s consent after their employment contract expires.
An employee may change jobs during the duration of the contract, provided that the employer is informed within the specified time
Employees are also no longer subject to “exit authorization ” and can travel indefinitely without an employer ’ s permission.
4. Tax system
Saudi Arabia adopts a territorial tax system, and the corporate tax rate varies depending on the type of industry and the number of Saudi employees.
In general, non-Saudi investors who invest in Saudi Arabia are obliged to pay corporate income tax, and non-resident enterprises, whether or not they are Saudi enterprises, are also required to pay corporate income tax as long as they carry out business activities in Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia has a number of tax regulations that benefit investors, such as no personal income tax and standard tax year (companies can use their internal fiscal year), and its tax system is easy to operate, companies only need to log in to a single port, and most of the content is in English.
Although the tax work seems relatively simple, there are still some issues that must be taken seriously.
Access to public information and tax requirements is limited, and there are inconsistencies in tax codes and specific operations.
The application of the Double Taxation Treaty (Double Taxation Treaty) has to be submitted in Arabic.
The main taxes that investors should pay attention to when doing business in Saudi Arabia are as follows:
Corporate Income Tax (CIT): A flat rate of 20% for non-Saudi entities or permanent establishments and 2.5% for domestic companies (including GCC member states).
Withholding Tax (WHT): The tax rate varies between 5% and 20% depending on the type of income that non-resident entities receive from Saudi Arabia.
• Value Added Tax (VAT): The standard tax rate has been raised from 5% in 2020 to 15% today to mitigate the economic impact of COVID-19.
Specific goods and services are exempt from VAT, specifically including the international transport of goods and passengers, some medicines and medical equipment, and the supply of investment metals.
• Social Insurance Tax: All companies must pay social insurance tax for each employee, with different rates for Saudi and foreign employees.
• Zakat: Also known as zakat, all Saudi entities are required to pay this tax according to Islamic teachings.
The General Directorate of Taxation and Customs (ZATCA) is the official tax authority of the Kingdom and is responsible for all tax and customs matters in the Kingdom.
Companies intending to operate in Saudi Arabia must ensure that they are kept abreast of the latest local tax regulations to ensure compliance and avoid unexpected tax liabilities.
In February 2024, Saudi Arabia issued new tax incentives for regional headquarters of multinational companies in its territory.
According to the latest regulations, entities that meet the relevant standards can be exempted from the preferential treatment of CIT and WHT for a period of 30 years and renewable.
In addition, some regions also provide additional tax incentives for businesses.
Specific destinations for doing business in Saudi Arabia
Multinational companies intending to operate in Saudi Arabia must carefully choose a specific destination.
In order to determine the most suitable city, enterprises must consider the following factors: whether it is close to the target market, whether it is convenient to recruit high-quality labor, and whether the infrastructure is adequate.
The eyes of businesses are mainly on Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam.
Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia and the center of its economic, financial and commercial activities.
Freight forwarders in Riyadh operate daily, providing great convenience to travel to other parts of the country and to other countries around the world.
With a population of more than 6 million, Riyadh is one of the fastest growing metropolises in the world.
Jeddah is the second most populous city in Saudi Arabia after Riyadh and the largest port to the Red Sea.
In recent times, Jeddah tourism has undergone a rapid development, and the local infrastructure and development level have entered the fast lane, making it an ideal destination for urban-related investors.
The Dammam region is rich in oil resources and is an ideal location for investors in the oil industry.
In addition, it is also very suitable for start-ups, attracting entrepreneurs from many different fields to invest here.
In addition to the above three cities, SEZ and other industrial cities are also good choices for many companies.
In April 2023, the Saudi government announced the establishment of four Special Economic Zones (SEZs) to provide a unique competitive advantage to foreign investors, some of which are fixed in the form of legal provisions.
The four SEZs are: King Abdullah Economic City (KAEC), Jazan Economic City (Jazan), Ras Al Khair and King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology.
They provide incentives for multinational companies operating in the region, such as 5% CIT for up to 20 years, WHT exemption, and tariff relief for goods in the region.
Employee recruitment and human resources management
One of the biggest challenges for doing business in Saudi Arabia is employee recruitment and human resources management.
According to the official Saudi census data for 2022, the total population of the country is 32.3 million, of which 42% are foreigners and 63% of Saudis are under the age of 30 (Saudi Bureau of Statistics, 2022).
Faced with such a large young population, the Saudi government has launched a number of programs to promote education, training and job creation to empower young people, which is particularly noteworthy for companies interested in recruiting employees in the country.
Vision 2030 not only drives economic reform, but also brings about social change on a larger scale.
We should not only realize the core goal of modernization, but also inherit and carry forward traditional culture.
Empowerment programmes for women and young people have had a particularly strong impact.
Under the framework of "Vision 2030", women have gained more jobs, a number of educational reforms and entrepreneurship projects have been successfully implemented, and Saudi Arabia's human resource advantages have been brought into full play.
With more and more Saudi women entering the workforce, Saudi Arabia has seen a rapid growth in the number of highly qualified workers in the fields of finance, engineering, medical care, science and technology.
Since 2019, Saudi Arabia has carried out several employment reforms, and women ’ s right to work has achieved unprecedented progress.
According to the World Bank ’ s Women Business and Law report, some of the reforms include women ’ s right to choose their place of residence, a ban on gender discrimination in the workplace, and a ban on firing pregnant women.
In order to maintain a compliant operation in Saudi Arabia, effective human resources management is indispensable.
It is important and necessary to keep abreast of the latest policies, do a good job of consulting related work, and establish good relations with relevant government agencies.
To improve transparency, implement best practices, and align business strategies with financial and operational objectives, companies need to build their presence in local markets and government systems.
Businesses operating in Saudi Arabia should attach great importance to hiring local Saudi employees.
Investors can attract top talent by partnering with third-party recruitment agencies and conducting skills training.
Saudi Arabia has a series of special regulations for the employment of foreign workers, which also need to be focused on.
If non-Saudi employees with professional skills are required, companies need to recruit talent through international recruitment channels, and support and assist in visa processing, resettlement, cultural integration and other aspects.
Foreign enterprises operating in Saudi Arabia need to pay high attention to cross-cultural training when carrying out human resources management work.
Onboarding training should be provided to non-Saudi employees to help them understand Saudi working culture and social practices to minimize misunderstandings and promote efficient collaboration.

FAQs
1.
What are the benefits of doing business in Saudi Arabia?
Benefits include access to vast markets in and around the Middle East, with up to 60 million consumers, business-friendly infrastructure, tax incentives for foreign investors, and less difficulty in obtaining capital support.
2.
What types of companies can be set up in Saudi Arabia?
Many types of companies can be set up in Saudi Arabia, but the most common are LLC, JSC and branch offices.
Among them, foreign investors usually choose to set up branches.
3.
What are Saudi Arabia's restrictions on foreign companies?
In general, Saudi Arabia allows the establishment of wholly foreign-owned enterprises, provided that the shareholders meet the requirements set out in the MISA.
4.
How long does it take to establish a business
Companies need to obtain an investment license from MISA before they can begin the formalities related to the establishment of an LLC or a branch.
It takes about three to four months for the Ministry of Commerce and Industry to complete a business registration (CR).
5.
What does "Saudization" (Nitaqat) mean?
It refers to the “Saudi Nationalisation Programme ” run by the Ministry of Labour, which makes it mandatory for companies to hire Saudi nationals.
6.
What are the prospects for doing business in Saudi Arabia?
In general, doing business in Saudi Arabia can bring substantial economic benefits with a full understanding of Saudi culture and regulation.
The Saudi economy is developing rapidly, the government has introduced many incentives, capital is abundant, and many industries are in the ascendant period.

Science fiction writer Liu Cixin: Someone must dare to dream like this
June 16, 2024 08: 58 | Source: Xinhua News Agency
Small number
"No one knows what the future holds, but someone must dare to dream like this."
At the recently concluded 8th China Science Fiction Conference in 2024, a science fiction short film adapted from the novel of the same name by science fiction writer Liu Cixin, "Earth Cannon", was unveiled for the first time.
The classic quotes and shocking pictures complement each other, bringing the audience into a futuristic world full of science fiction.
On the wings of imagination, what kind of future will science fiction arrive? Recently, in an interview with Xinhua News Agency reporters, Liu Cixin, who is the president of the Beijing Yuanyu Science Fiction Future Technology Research Institute, further explained the underlying logic of science fiction imagination.
“Everything needs imagination. ”
During this science fiction conference, Liu Cixin, who is over 60 years old, is very busy, and the topics and questions related to science fiction converge to this representative of the Chinese science fiction community.
Liu Cixin, born in 1963, worked as a computer engineer at a power plant in Shanxi Province and began publishing science fiction works in the 1990s.
Its published novella "Wandering Earth", imagines the human race struggling to find a suitable home when the sun is destroyed; the subsequent novel "Three Bodies" leads the reader to explore unknown civilizations outside the world with a more strange and bold imagination.
The latter won the Hugo Award, the highest honor in science fiction, and Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg has recommended the book to his tens of millions of fans.
Many readers are curious about the "underground city" in "Wandering Earth", the refuge of mankind in the face of the sun crisis. Liu Cixin said that the "underground city" that will be built in the future is completely different from what we imagine now.
It doesn't have to be closed, it can be very expansion.Where humans need to build underground cities the most, it may be on the moon or Mars.
There, the underground city can effectively block the strong radiation in space, while creating a breathable and temperature-appropriate environment, "Liu said.
Liu Cixin believes that science fiction is based on the imagination of science and technology, and with the rapid development of science and technology, many scenes in science fiction are gradually becoming reality.
For example, in the sci-fi imagination, humans can achieve "brain networking", connecting the brain to the outside world and even other brains.
In the current reality, brain-computer interface technology has enabled paraplegic patients to use their thoughts to control the cursor to move.
In Liu Cixin's view, when humans use brain-computer interface technology to 100% identify, store information in the brain, and then send it to the computer - this is digital survival.
Science fiction originates from the rational expansion of cutting-edge scientific and technological achievements and scientific discoveries, and constantly "ignites" people's imagination and curiosity, and technological innovation is also changing the connotation and extension of science fiction.

"Tumbler" anti-fall exercises home to play across space
Post Date: June 17, 2024
[Ming Pao News] In Hong Kong, for every 100 elderly people living in the community, an average of about 20 people fall one or more times a year. Each fall, about 75% will suffer various types of injuries, of which about 7% are more serious, including head injuries, wrist or hip fractures, resulting in reduced mobility.
Some elderly people who have fallen have restricted their social activities because they are worried about falling again, resulting in a deterioration in their quality of life and a reduction in their healthy life expectancy.
Therefore, it is especially important to assess your risk of falling and learn how to reduce it.
According to data released by the United Nations, the life expectancy of Hong Kong is 86 years, which is among the highest in the world.
According to the data of the Census and Statistics Department of Hong Kong, the elderly population aged 65 or above accounts for about 20% of the total social population, with the number of people reaching 1.45 million. The data also predicts that the proportion of the elderly population will climb to 36% in 2046.
Thanks to the increasing advances in modern medical technology, a large group of elderly people can rely on various advanced technologies to help them maintain a healthy old age with limited social resources.
Among them, fall prevention is one of the health management issues closely related to the lives of the elderly.
3-step screening to assess fall risk
According to the World Falls Guidelines, the risk of falls in the elderly can be initially screened through the following three questions:
1.
Have you fallen in the last 12 months?
2. Do you feel unstable when walking or standing?
3.
Are you worried that you will fall?
If the elderly answer "yes" to any of the above questions, it means that they are at a certain risk of falling and should be further assessed.
Initial screening shows that elderly people who are at risk of falling may undergo a “walking speed test ” or a“ standing up and walking test ” to further identify the risk of falling.
The Walking Speed Test calculates the daily walking speed of an elderly person by measuring the time it takes to walk 4 meters.
The "sit up and walk test" requires the elderly to sit in a chair first, then stand up and walk forward for 3 meters and then return to the chair to sit down, and calculate the completion time of the whole process.
If the walking speed is greater than or equal to 0.8 meters per second, or if the time to complete the walk is less than 15 seconds, the risk of falling is considered "low".
Conversely, it indicates that the risk of falling is “medium ” and requires“ tailor-made ” fall prevention training.
A more detailed fall risk assessment is required to identify other fall risk factors, such as cognitive ability, vision, environmental factors, etc., if one of the following criteria is met, indicating that the risk of falling is “high. ”
• Has been injured as a result of a fall
• Lie on the ground after falling and “can ’ t get up ”
Fell more than twice in a year.
• Diagnosed with senility
• Sudden fainting and loss of consciousness
Step training to save yourself when you fall
Once you know your risk of falling, how can you reduce your risk and prevent falls?
Exercise training has been shown to be one of the most effective measures to reduce the risk of falls.
The main sports training content includes: balance training, strength training and walking training (see "fall training").
In addition, in recent years, studies have shown that different types of step training can effectively improve the agility and reaction speed at the moment of falling, and train the elderly to step quickly and save themselves at the moment of falling.
This type of training is thought to have a significant fall prevention effect in a shorter period of time.
The Department of Rehabilitation Sciences of The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) is focusing on the development of compound treadmill training to enhance the effectiveness of anti-fall exercise.

He explains: “Synthetic data is data generated by machine learning models that mimic real data.
Its advantage lies in providing a large amount of high-quality data and solving the problem of insufficient existing data.
In addition, synthetic data can solve data privacy and security issues and avoid legal disputes. ”
The application of quantum computing in artificial intelligence | Dr. Yu Longwu
Dr. Yu Longwu is optimistic about the application of quantum computers in the field of artificial intelligence.
Quantum computers have powerful parallel computing capabilities, which can greatly improve the computing power of artificial intelligence.
With the continuous progress of quantum computing technology, quantum computing is expected to become the key to solving the bottleneck of AI computing power.
He pointed out: "The parallel computing power of quantum computers gives them a significant advantage in solving complex computational problems.
For example, in machine learning, many algorithms need to do a lot of matrix operations and optimization problems, and quantum computing can greatly speed up these processes. ”
Interview with Dr. Yu Longwu: Looking forward to the future development of artificial intelligence and quantum computing
Self-supervised learning and multi-modal learning
Dr. Yu also mentioned that technologies such as self-supervised learning, multi-modal learning and edge computing will play an important role in the development of artificial intelligence in the future.
Self-supervised learning can reduce dependence on labeled data by training with unlabeled data; multi-modal learning can process and integrate data from different sources; and edge computing can handle real-time processing where the data is generated, reducing latency and improving efficiency.
He said: "By using unlabeled data for training, self-supervised learning can greatly reduce the dependence on labeled data and improve the training efficiency."
Multi-modal learning, which can process and integrate data from different sources, will greatly expand the scope of AI applications. ”
Future challenges and responses
Despite the bright prospects, Dr. Yu also reminds us to be cautious about the challenges ahead.
He pointed out that the development of artificial intelligence is not without resistance and problems.
The first is technical bottlenecks and resource constraints.
The training and operation of large-scale models requires a lot of computing resources and electricity, which is a huge burden on the environment and the economy.
In addition, data privacy and security issues remain serious.
AI systems need a lot of data to train, which often contains sensitive information and personal privacy, and how to protect this data is a major challenge.
"We must develop and implement effective laws and policies to ensure that the development of AI is ethical and ethical and prevents misuse and malicious use," he said.
Interview with Dr. Yu Longwu: Looking forward to the future development of artificial intelligence and quantum computing
The integration of quantum computing and artificial intelligence
The application prospect of quantum computing in artificial intelligence
When talking about the integration of quantum computing and artificial intelligence, Dr. Yu Longwu showed great enthusiasm.
He pointed out that the application prospect of quantum computing in artificial intelligence is very broad.
First, the parallel computing power of quantum computers gives them a significant advantage in solving complex computational problems, such as in machine learning, where many algorithms need to perform a large number of matrix operations and optimization problems, and quantum computing can greatly speed up these processes.
"Quantum computers are capable of dealing with problems that classical computers cannot solve, such as cracking complex encryption algorithms, simulating the quantum behavior of molecules and materials, and solving complex optimization problems," he said.
Quantum machine learning
Dr. Yu also stressed that the combination of quantum computing and artificial intelligence can improve the training efficiency of AI models.
Quantum machine learning algorithms can run on a quantum computer, speeding up the model training process and improving the training accuracy.
Especially for deep learning, which requires a lot of computational resources, this will bring significant improvements.
He said: "Quantum machine learning algorithms can run on a quantum computer, speeding up the model training process and improving the training accuracy.
This is especially important for deep learning, which requires a lot of computational resources. ”
Challenges Faced
Dr. Yu Longwu also pointed out that at present, quantum computing still faces many challenges in practical applications, such as the limitation of quantum bits, the problem of quantum error correction, the development of quantum algorithms and the limitation of hardware technology.
Nevertheless, he is confident in the future of quantum computing, believing that as technology continues to advance, quantum computing will play an increasingly important role in the development of artificial intelligence.
"Despite these challenges, I believe that with the continuous advancement of technology, quantum computing will certainly play an increasingly important role in promoting the development of artificial intelligence in the future," he said.
Collaboration between quantum computing and traditional computing
Dr. Yu Longwu believes that in the future, quantum computers will not completely replace traditional computers, but the two will develop together and play their respective roles.
Quantum computers have significant advantages when dealing with complex parallel computing tasks, while traditional computers still perform well when performing some simple, linear tasks.
By combining quantum computing with traditional computing, optimal computing efficiency and performance can be achieved.
"Quantum computing and traditional computing have their own strengths, and in the future the two will work together to achieve the best computing efficiency and performance," he said.
Specific Application Scenarios
In terms of specific application scenarios, Dr. Yu Longwu mentioned that quantum computing can play an important role in areas such as drug discovery, materials science, optimization problems, and financial modeling.
For example, in drug discovery, quantum computing can simulate the quantum behavior of molecules and accelerate the drug screening process; in materials science, quantum computing can help design new materials and optimize their performance; in optimization problems, quantum computing can quickly find the optimal solution and improve decision-making efficiency; in financial modeling, quantum computing can improve the accuracy of risk assessment and investment strategies.
"Quantum computing has broad application prospects in areas such as drug discovery, materials science, optimization problems, financial modeling, and can greatly enhance the level of research and application in these fields," he said.
Social Impact of Artificial Intelligence and Future Prospects
Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Society
At the end of the interview, Dr. Yu discussed the far-reaching impact of artificial intelligence on society.
He pointed out that artificial intelligence has great potential in improving productivity and quality of life.
For example, AI can be used in medical diagnostics to help doctors diagnose diseases more accurately and improve treatment effectiveness; it can be used in autonomous driving to improve traffic safety and efficiency; it can be used in smart homes to make our lives more convenient and comfortable.
In addition, artificial intelligence can also be used for scientific research, accelerating scientific discoveries, and solving some of the major challenges facing humanity, such as climate change, energy shortage and so on.
"Artificial intelligence has great potential to boost productivity and improve quality of life, and can dramatically improve efficiency and effectiveness in all areas," he said.
Challenges and Risks Faced
However, Dr. Yu also warned about the challenges posed by artificial intelligence.
He mentioned that the development of artificial intelligence may lead to the disappearance of some traditional jobs, which will lead to employment problems.
Businesses may try to hire fewer people to perform the same tasks, resulting in large numbers of workers losing their jobs.
In addition, data privacy and security issues are also important challenges for AI.
AI requires a lot of data to train and operate, which may contain personal privacy and sensitive information, and how to protect the security of this data is a major challenge.
"The development of artificial intelligence may lead to the disappearance of some traditional jobs, and companies may try to hire fewer people to perform the same tasks, which will have a knock-on effect on the job market," he said.
Ethical and Moral Issues of Artificial Intelligence
The third is the ethical issue of artificial intelligence.
Dr. Yu Longwu pointed out that the development of artificial intelligence may bring some ethical and moral issues, such as whether artificial intelligence decision-making is fair, and whether artificial intelligence will pose a threat to human beings.
How to formulate and implement effective laws and policies to ensure that the development of AI is ethical and ethical is an issue that needs to be studied and explored in depth.
"The development of artificial intelligence raises a number of ethical and ethical issues, and we have to make sure that the development of artificial intelligence is ethical and ethical," he said.
Future outlook
Dr. Yu Longwu is full of expectations for the future development of artificial intelligence.
He hopes that AI can play a role in more fields, solve more practical problems, and make greater breakthroughs in intelligence and autonomy.
At the same time, he stressed that the development of artificial intelligence must be safe and controllable, and a sound artificial intelligence governance system needs to be established to ensure that it does not pose a threat to human society.
"I hope that AI can play a role in more areas, solve more practical problems, and at the same time ensure that the development of AI is safe and controllable," he said.
Advice for young researchers and students
Finally, Dr. Yu Longwu put forward several suggestions for young researchers and students.
He encouraged them to maintain their curiosity and spirit of exploration, focus on basic knowledge learning, develop interdisciplinary thinking skills, focus on teamwork and communication skills, and have a sense of social responsibility.
He believes that the younger generation of researchers will play an important role in the development of artificial intelligence in the future, bringing more benefits to human society.
"I encourage young researchers and students to remain curious and inquisitive, focus on basic learning, develop interdisciplinary thinking skills, focus on teamwork and communication skills, and be socially responsible," he said.
Summing up
In this in-depth interview, Dr. Yu Longwu painted a blueprint for the future of artificial intelligence and quantum computing for us.
His insights not only reveal the current direction of technology, but also provide us with ideas and ways to meet the challenges of the future.
With the continuous advancement of technology, artificial intelligence and quantum computing will continue to drive social progress and bring a better future for mankind.

Can Singapore ’ s 3-Day Weekend Pass Taiwan ’ s Work-Time Revolution?
Singapore ’ s flexible working guidelines are set to hit the road in December 2024, allowing workers to request three days off a week.
(Photo / Dazhi Imaging / Associated Press)
● Document / salary
Singapore ’ s flexible working guidelines are set to hit the road in December 2024, allowing workers to make demands such as three days off a week, which has aroused popular debate in Taiwan about the possibility of taking three days off a week and reducing basic working hours.
Can Taiwan get rid of the name of "island of labor" and keep up with the working hours revolution in various countries?
Why are all countries shortening their working hours?
In consultation with the government, businesses and workers, Singapore has officially adopted the flexible working guidelines, which will be implemented on 1 December 2024.
This guideline encourages workers to apply to enterprises for the following working hours adjustments:
1.
Three days a week, that is, four days a week (four-day workweek).
2.
Remote work, including working from home (WFH).
3.
Special working hours, such as compression and segmented working hours.
Singapore ’ s flexible working hours guidelines are not legally binding, but companies must establish an application mechanism, and when receiving employees ’ flexible working hours applications, they must make a decision based on actual operating needs, costs and other factors, and must not be rejected because of corporate culture or management dissatisfaction.
According to a survey conducted by market research firm milieu in 2022, more than 60% of workers in Singapore, Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines support the three-day weekend, and 76% of workers in Singapore strongly support it.
Directors of recruitment companies in Singapore believe that workers in mature economies are naturally more concerned about quality of life and the meaning of work.
▲ More than 60% of workers in Southeast Asian countries such as Singapore, Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines support a three-day holiday. (Photo / Weekly Wang)
Singapore ’ s labour force is shrinking, with a quarter of the population expected to be aged 65 or over by 2030.
In the context of corporate and labour support, fewer children and an ageing population, the Government hopes to reduce labour market pressures and provide incentives for retention through flexible working hours policies.
So far, no country has fully implemented the three-day weekend, but Iceland, the United States, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, Scotland, Japan and other countries have conducted the three-day weekend experiment, and some countries, such as Singapore, have established relevant guidelines.
For example, Iceland began a three-day week off trial in 2015, which resulted in an increase in staff productivity and a work-life balance. The United Kingdom also received positive reviews for a large-scale experiment in 2022. For example, after Tyler Grange, an environmental consultant, found that employees ’ productivity and service standards increased, the number of job seekers doubled.
However, the director of the Federation of British Industry believes that working four days a week is not the answer, and many industries will not be able to recover costs.
Taiwan has no consensus on the three-day weekend, and the government can encourage flexible working hours for enterprises.
▲ Lucas, a citizen, launched a proposal on the Public Policy Network Engagement Platform on March 7, 2023, hoping that everyone will join the petition to make Taiwan the first country in Asia to take a three-day weekend. (Photo / NDC-Public Policy Network Engagement Platform)
The public in Taiwan proposed on the Public Policy Network Engagement Platform to “make Taiwan the first country in Asia to take a three-day break. ”
After the number of signatures reached the target, the Ministry of Labor responded, saying that the three-day weekend involves legal amendments, national economic and social consensus, and it is difficult to implement at this stage.
According to the Ministry of Labor, the average annual working hours in Taiwan are gradually decreasing, but they are more than 2,000 hours in 2021, so workers have always wanted to reduce their working hours.
Since it is difficult to implement the three-day weekend, some Taiwanese people have proposed a six-hour daily work plan.
However, according to a survey conducted in the community, Taiwanese workers still tend to take three days off a week between “three days off ” and“ six hours a day. ”
In recent years, work-life balance has become more important, and many countries have begun to implement a three-day weekend on a trial basis.
Taiwan is entering an aging society, and the problem of job shortage has yet to be solved.
The government may be able to use Singapore ’ s similar background as a model to encourage companies to adopt flexible working hours to ease a tight labor market.

Interchange station: Let the historical material speak for the red scarf
Font Size:
Recently, a huge street mural has aroused controversy. The "Red Turban at Rest" on Qiaosan Road depicts a red turban smoking during a break.
The woman in the painting has a thin body, delicate skin, clean nails, and a cigarette between two slender fingers.
Critics believe that the woman in this mural is not like a diligent working woman, but like a prostitute; others think that the painting is suspected of advocating smoking and has a negative impact.
Proponents emphasize artistic freedom, arguing that the painting depicts a red turban in between work breaks, and that the image of smoking is unmistakable.
I recognize the freedom of art, but I believe even more that if art reflects history, it must fit with history; if art depicts historical figures, it cannot violate the image of the historical figures painted.
In my opinion, the biggest problem with this painting is that the woman painted is contrary to the true image of the red headscarf in history.
Some time ago, I happened to do a study on red headscarves to discuss the progressiveness of their presentation, and here is a brief introduction.
The red headscarf refers to female workers from the Sanshui area of Guangdong who worked in the construction industry in Singapore in the first half of the 20th century.
They are remembered for their hard work and contributions to Singapore ’ s construction industry; and they are also a symbol of female workers and women ’ s strength.
As early as March 21, 1991, the article "Forget the Red Headscarf" published in the Lianhe Zaobao newspaper, affirmed the progressiveness of the red headscarf.
The description given in the article is as follows: "Sanshui women can be said to be the pioneers of the women's liberation movement.
They left early and went to work in the fields.
In order to survive, and to feed and clothe their families, they, like the male immigrants, bravely followed the watermen south.
From these words, it can be seen that the emergence of the red headscarf group can reflect the traditional gender relationship - the change of the pattern of men who earn money outside the main body and support their families, and women who teach their children inside the main body.
They are the pioneers of women's movement towards society and self-reliance.
What is even more noteworthy is that this group of three water women entered the rather sexist construction industry.
Due to the high physical requirements of the construction industry, men are born with the advantage of gender physical strength, becoming the main force in the construction industry.
However, the red headscarf has once again broken the tradition, carrying the masonry earth with the female body, challenging the imbalance of the gender ratio of construction industry practitioners brought about by physiological characteristics.
On June 9, 1977, the "Xingzhou Daily" article "The escape of several women - tofu out of the chatter" wrote: "In the construction site, the most labor."
They are not afraid of toil, rubbing ash and sand under the hot sun, carrying bricks and stones, carrying mud and carrying wood.
These women are the most devoted to their work, never lazy, never idle, let alone strike. "
Throughout history, it can be seen that the red headscarf has crossed the traditional industries of women, broken into the construction industry, which is monopolized by men, and reduced gender discrimination at work to a certain extent.
It can be seen that the reason why the red headscarves can leave influence in Singapore is that they have made great contributions to the construction industry in Singapore, relying on the spirit of hard work they have left, and their progressiveness in life and work.
I can't help but ask, they obviously have more worthy of attention, why use such a giant mural to paint a picture of a weak woman who is far from the real historical image, like a woman who cannot carry her shoulders and cannot carry her hands?
Finally, I recommend that you go to the National University of Singapore and take a look at the building site (red turban) painted by the painter Liu Kang in the museum, and see the powerful arms and muscular thighs in the painting, which is the image of the red turban as a female group.

Free from manpower constraints, accelerate automation in Malaysia ’ s oil palm farms

KUALA LUMPUR (Reuters) - Malaysia is the world's second-largest palm oil exporter, but its oil palm farms have faced years of uncertainty over the supply of human resources and increasingly stringent human rights regulations in Western countries.
Local oil palm operators have invested heavily in accelerating full automation to meet these challenges.
Although the palm oil production process has been generally mechanized, from the removal of old trees, soil loosening, planting, fertilization and deworming to the harvest, theft and transportation of oil palm fruits after maturity, it is still a dangerous, dirty and exhausting work that is highly dependent on manpower.
Mohamad Helmy, managing director of SD Dental Direct, Malaysia ’ s largest oil palm plantation group, told Bloomberg that continuing to rely on foreign workers for all of these critical tasks puts operators at very high risk.
As a result, Naomi has decided to invest around RM100 million (about S $28.7 million) in automation to reduce its reliance on manpower.
That represents about 50% of its research and development budget this year.
In the next three to four years, it will invest about 30% of its R & D budget in this area each year.
Mohd Hilmi said that the research and development focus of future automation in the plantation industry includes the use of drones, robots, unmanned trucks and artificial intelligence.
Since it often takes years from developing and improving machinery to actually deploying it to commercial applications, companies still have to retrain their employees during this time.
During the coronavirus epidemic, Malaysia imposed an action control order and imposed a total blockade of the country's borders, which severely damaged the cultivation industry, which relied heavily on foreign workers.
At that time, the oil palm plantation was completely empty of labor and no one was harvesting, causing production to plummet, with direct and indirect losses of nearly $1 billion (about S $1.351 billion).
Mohd Hilmi said that in addition to the coronavirus epidemic, SD teeth were also accused of forced labor in the United States, which imposed a two-year import ban on the company's products from 2020.
He said that the company decided to actively promote automation reform and become the first grower in Malaysia to set up a machine research and development institution.
SD-Tooth first uses machines to take over non-harvest tasks, such as spraying pesticides and testing yields.
In addition to SD Dental Direct, growers such as Cotai Agricultural Resources and IOI Group are beginning to adopt the same approach.
Automation allows women to enter the field as well.
Human resources in the oil palm industry have traditionally been dominated by men, but automation has allowed women to enter the field, for example, by using machines to assist women workers in transporting about 30 kilograms of oil palm fruit each.
Female workers can also operate insecticide sprinklers, a job that used to require six male workers.
"These machines have reduced the demand for manual labor and now the work has become easier," said Ms. Nohidayu, 41, a female worker.
It's not like before, only men can do this kind of work. "
Pereira, executive director of the North-South Initiative, a Malagasy rights group, believes that the acceleration of automation in large growers will not affect workers ’ livelihoods, but will help them reduce accusations of forced labor.
"We hope that Federación will take the lead and prove that the industry can eliminate forced labor as soon as possible," Pereira said.
However, fully robot-managed oil palm parks will not become a reality so soon, because oil palm parks are mostly located in hilly areas, and there are still technical challenges for robots to automatically navigate or correctly identify mature oil palm fruits in the hilly areas.
Various automation equipment in the oil palm industry still needs to be operated by skilled workers, such as allowing automatic harvesters to safely harvest fruit from six-storey oil palm trees.
Still, Aditya Tuli, SD Dental ’ s chief digital officer, says the change will continue.
“Once we start mechanizing, we can imagine that the numbers in terms of production will increase or have a positive impact.
That's what we're chasing, "he said.

India ’ s medical facilities speed up the development of intelligent system to help rural remote consultation

For many Hong Kong people, India may look like a relatively backward and populous country, with a population of 1.4 billion, and it is hard to imagine how the local medical system can accommodate such a large population.
The author went to the local area to participate in the large-scale international engineering alliance conference, found that the local medical facilities are developing rapidly, the number of hospital beds in the country has increased by 40% in the past 10 years, and some large hospitals have added intelligent equipment to assist in the diagnosis and daily operation of the hospital.
If you have the ability to increase investment in the future, coupled with the development of local information technology, and gradually trend towards intelligent development, I believe that it is not difficult to see the emergence of comprehensive intelligent hospitals, so that patient services are more efficient and no longer subject to geographical restrictions.
Author: Yuan Pak Leung, Former President of the Institution of Senior Engineers and Engineers
I am the Vice-Chairman of the International Engineering Technologists Agreement and the Chairman of the British delegation chaired a review meeting of the agreement in New Delhi, India.
As the Vice President of the International Engineering Technologists Agreement (IETTA), I went to New Delhi, India, to attend this year ’ s IETTA conference hosted by my host, and also chaired the annual meeting held in India in the same capacity as the chairman of the Seoul Accord.
Over the course of more than 10 days, I have met many people in the engineering industry from all over India, some from the medical industry, so I have the opportunity to learn more about the development of local hospital facilities.
According to the local industry, the number of hospitals and beds in India has increased rapidly over the past decade. For example, from 2010 to 2020, the total number of beds in the country has increased from about 1.2 million to more than 1.7 million, an increase of more than 40%.
As of 2023, the market share of hospital spending across India, including public and private hospitals, is in the hundreds of billions of dollars. However, the number of beds per 1,000 people is still relatively low globally.
On both sides of a highway in New Delhi, I saw 20 medical statues placed by Yatharth Hospital to thank and honor the work of “anti-virus warriors ” during the COVID-19 pandemic.
However, unlike in Hong Kong, Indian hospitals are dominated by private hospitals, accounting for 70% of the total number of beds.
Some people in the local industry admit that this reflects that the investment in public health care is not enough at present, but it is understood that the local public sector is trying to catch up with the demand, but the demand is too large and it is difficult to meet 100%.
Therefore, ensuring equitable access to quality health care is a challenge for local authorities, especially in remote areas such as mountains or rural areas.
It is said that there is a medical culture in India with a long history in Asia that can alleviate some of the medical needs of the general population.
It is a system of traditional medicine called Ayurveda, which is called Ayurveda. It is composed of two Sanskrit words, ayur refers to life and veda means knowledge.
Together, they mean “knowledge of life ” and are considered to be one of the most ancient forms of holistic natural medicine in the world, originating from ancient India, for thousands of years. Ayurveda and Chinese medicine have many things in common, especially the focus of both is on the patient, not on the disease.
Its core concept is to maintain their own spiritual balance and harmony, will make people physically healthy, the theory that life should avoid excessive hyperactivity, because it will lead to too much stomach acid, so that people become irritable, anxiety and other problems.
Excessive hyperactivity can also affect the joints, mucous membranes, and fats that protect our body structure, leading to obesity and depression, and people ’ s physical and mental activities, including breathing, blood circulation, and nervous system if over-regulation, can bring anxiety, constipation, joint pain and so on.
Ayurveda emphasizes the uniqueness of the individual and regulates and prevents diseases according to the physical and psychological characteristics of the individual.
In general, Ayurveda believes that a variety of herbs, spices, minerals, etc. can be used to treat diseases, and diet therapy is used to adjust the diet according to the body, while lifestyle adjustments include yoga, meditation and massage.
In addition to its unique medical concept, India ’ s relatively advanced information technology development, I believe it can also be an opportunity to make up for the lack of medical services.
In fact, many local hospitals have begun to add intelligent systems, such as electronic medical record system, remote medical system and the application of digital technology, which improve the ability of doctors to treat patients, and increase the ability of remote consultation, so that patients in remote rural areas can benefit.
In order to increase the efficiency of consultation and make more accurate diagnosis, local doctors will also use wearable devices to understand the patient ’ s physical condition, and even use intelligent systems to help make clinical decisions.
The conference hotel I stayed at offers authentic Indian Ayurveda healing massages, including the Ayurveda oil drip, which is said to be effective in helping to relieve stress.
The author believes that Hong Kong and India have very different cultural backgrounds, but they are also working hard to promote the development of intelligent hospitals.
However, some local technology industry people pointed out that, regardless of whether the two places or other regions should pay more attention to the convenience and efficiency of intelligent systems, there are opportunities for network security risks or personal data leakage, so there are challenges when using different smart technologies.
With the rapid development of the local medical system with advanced technology, I believe that if the world can introduce more intelligent elements in its medical system, and continue to invest in it, coupled with the policy support of government departments, we can cite each other, exchange learning and practice verification, I believe that it is not difficult to build a fully intelligent hospital in the future, and hope that this efficient service model can meet the increasing medical demand of society.

Yuan Pak Leung has always been committed to promoting the professional development of the engineering profession and is the former President of the Hong Kong Institution of Engineers.
The decades of professional journey are worth remembering, and I am convinced that the latter may understand the key points of the engineering profession.

Analysis of China ’ s Investment in Europe
* If you would like to reprint this article, please contact the North American Intellectual Property Journal
John So / Industry Analyst
According to the survey, Chinese investment in Europe in 2023 fell to the lowest level since 2010: Chinese investment in Europe (EU27 + UK) again fell from 7.1 billion euros in 2022 to 6.8 billion euros in 2023.
M & A activity also continued to decline, with an overall value drop of 58% to just €1.5 billion, as economic difficulties in China and strict capital controls, as well as strict scrutiny of foreign investments in Europe, led to fewer M & A deals.
In 2023, Chinese corporate investors face the challenges and uncertainties of multiple factors such as European and global political and economic factors, and geopolitical tensions such as the protracted war in Ukraine and the Middle East conflict continue to escalate, and the uncertainties of the global economy affect the investment willingness of Chinese companies.
China ’ s sluggish economic growth in the post-pandemic period has weakened the financial base of many Chinese companies. Strict capital controls and the devaluation of the yuan have also dampened foreign investment.
The European Union is seeking to rebalance China-Europe relations and strike a balance between de-risking and cooperation, a shift that adds to the uncertainty facing potential Chinese investors, all in the context of increased regulation of foreign investment at a time when economic security has risen to the agenda of European governments.
Chinese companies remain highly willing to invest in green
The composition of Chinese investment in Europe is undergoing a fundamental transformation, with the share of investment in the green sector rising from just 2% in 2017 and an average of 9% from 2012 to 2021 to 51% in 2022 and 78% in 2023.
Large-scale investments in batteries and electric vehicles have led to dramatic changes in the regional distribution of Chinese investment in Europe, with Hungary being the main beneficiary, which has grown significantly from a very low base in the past two years. Between 2012 and 2021, Hungary increased from an average annual investment of just €89 million to €1.51 billion in 2022 and to €2.99 billion in 2023.
In fact, Central Europe has become the most important destination for Chinese investment, with Hungary alone attracting 44% of Chinese direct investment in Europe, surpassing the “big three ” of France, Germany and the United Kingdom combined, and Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia also receiving Chinese investment in 2023.
Chinese investment in the value chain of electric vehicles in Europe has increased significantly over the past two years.
In 2023, China ’ s investment in electric vehicles amounted to 4.7 billion euros, accounting for about 70% of China ’ s total direct investment in the EU, a significant increase from 2.9 billion euros the previous year (up 61%); as in 2022, most of the investment came from billions of euros in battery plants.
China ’ s leading battery manufacturers CATL, AESC and Svolt contribute 85% of the total investment related to electric vehicles. CATL has established a battery factory in Germany and is currently building a €7.3 billion battery factory in Debrecen, Hungary; AESC is investing €2 billion in a factory in Douai, France, with an investment value of €13 in the UK. The trend is likely to continue: AESC has announced a €2.5 billion project in Spain, expected to start in 2024, and Eve Energy has announced a €1 billion battery investment in Hungary.
China ’ s foreign direct investment is increasingly flowing upstream and downstream along the value chain of electric vehicles, and China ’ s battery feedstock suppliers such as positive and negative poles are trying to expand their market share in Europe ’ s rapidly growing battery ecosystem.
Some agencies predict that Europe may soon see more downstream investment in electric vehicle production.
In Slovakia, Geely ’ s Volvo is already building an electric car factory at a cost of 1.2 billion euros; in December 2023, Chinese electric car maker Biadi announced plans to produce electric cars in Hungary by 2026, and the EU ’ s ongoing investigation into Chinese electric car imports could spur Chinese electric car producers to further expand their investments to avoid potential import tariffs.
From a country perspective, it is safer for Chinese companies to invest in countries with close ties to Beijing, like Hungary, than in other destinations such as Italy, which has recently stepped up regulatory scrutiny of Chinese corporate governance.
But Hungary ’ s leading position in attracting investment in electric vehicles is not limited to Chinese companies, and South Korean companies have also increased their foreign direct investment in Hungary; the main reason may be that the country has several leading car manufacturers, providing cheap and skilled labor, issuing millions of euros in subsidies, and committing to invest in infrastructure and industrial parks.
Of course, from a broader perspective, China ’ s EV investments are not limited to Europe, with battery and EV producers announcing significant investments in Asia, Latin America and North Africa.
Many of these investments are driven by the host country ’ s local content requirements, and most importantly, the U.S. Inflation-Reduction Act requires certain raw materials to be processed in the United States or its free-trade partners to avoid U.S. tariffs.
In the European region, Chinese companies announced major investments related to electric vehicles, including Guoxuan Gaoke and CNGR Morocco New Energy Technology, whose abundant phosphate reserves (a key component of LiFePO4 batteries) make Morocco an attractive destination for Chinese electric vehicle investors.
The country also has free trade agreements (FTA) with the United States and the European Union, and has factories for several French automakers, which aim to ship products to the European market, making Morocco a more attractive manufacturing hub if the EU decides to impose tariffs on Chinese-made electric cars.
Investment status in non-green sectors
Under the European Union ’ s increasingly stringent scrutiny, Chinese investment and mergers and acquisitions in non-green areas continued to decline, although some areas still attracted Chinese companies.
Sectors such as healthcare, consumer-oriented (consumer products, entertainment) and information and communications technology (ICT) continue to attract Chinese investors, attracting an average of €3.1 billion per year in 2021-2023, although this is only half of the average annual investment in the previous decade (€6 billion), but the decline is much smaller compared to other industries such as transportation, real estate or financial and business services. 70% of non-EV related Chinese manufacturers have direct investment in Europe, double the 35% share in 2014. In 2021 and 2022, such major acquisitions include Hillhouse Capital Group ’ s acquisition of the Philips Home Appliances business unit and Tencent ’ s acquisition of gaming studio Sumo Digital.
In fact, unlike the FDI activity associated with electric vehicles over the past three years, most of the investments in these sectors have taken the form of acquisitions and are geographically concentrated in the “big three ” economies of France, the UK and Germany.
The continued interest of Chinese investors in these sectors has to do with the push and pull factors.
The entertainment industry is facing a tighter regulatory environment in the country, as Beijing ’ s tech rectification campaign aims to shift investment toward strategic industries rather than consumer-oriented ones.
For a company like Tencent, which is well-capitalized, competitive and has accumulated extensive knowledge in the gaming industry, it is possible for Chinese companies to look for new, more profitable opportunities overseas.
Unlike sensitive industries, the regulatory environment in Europe is also tolerant of many consumer-oriented investments.
Indeed, China ’ s increasing scrutiny of critical infrastructure or semiconductor investments over the past five years may partly explain why Chinese companies are focusing on consumer goods and services.
In addition, the healthcare industry is also the top destination for Chinese venture capital, and despite the sharp decline in Chinese venture capital in Europe, the healthcare industry remains the second largest beneficiary of Chinese venture capital in the past five years, accounting for an average of 24% of all venture capital. The largest deal in 2023 was Tencent ’ s investment in CMR Surgical, a developer of medical robotics systems in the UK, with an estimated investment of 17 million. Euros.
So far, there are few examples of investments being blocked in the healthcare industry compared to investments such as critical infrastructure or semiconductors.
However, the Covid-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of the industry and Europe ’ s overreliance on China for key goods such as personal protective equipment. Unsurprisingly, the acquisition of Heyer Medical by Chinese ventilator and anesthesia machine manufacturer YiAn Medical was initially blocked by the German government in 2022. In April 2024, the European Union also announced an investigation into the public procurement of medical devices in China, indicating that the healthcare industry is receiving more attention from European policymakers, which could lead to restrictions on Chinese companies ’ participation in EU procurement tenders.
Future Outlook: Stricter Investment Censorship
In recent years, the proportion of transactions related to Chinese companies reviewed by European censors has been declining, roughly related to the decline in Chinese direct investment in Europe.
The share of investment review notifications submitted to the European Commission from China for final shareholders fell from 8% in 2020 to 5% in 2022.
The German data reflects a similar trend, with the proportion of Chinese companies screened by acquirers falling from 17% in 2020 to 12% in 2022 and only 8% in 2023; the main likely reason is that Chinese companies have become more cautious about acquiring certain European countries or certain more sensitive industries due to increased regulation.
Declining FDI levels in China have become the new normal and are likely to continue. This year, the EU and US elections will provide investors with more reasons to wait and see. Long-term factors that reinforce this trend include a greater focus on economic security, trade conflicts, and uncertainty about China ’ s economic strength.
In the future, critical infrastructure; critical technologies and dual-use items are key audit targets, and even trains, solar panels, wind turbines, and port and airport security equipment may face more stringent standards of scrutiny.

Eat healthy food carefully!
Japanese Expert: Interaction with Drugs and Taking Terrorism
2024 / 07 / 31 14: 44
Pharmacology experts remind that some health foods are eaten together with blood pressure and blood-sugar related drugs, which may cause dizziness and other interactions.
People have nothing to do with the news.
(Image from PhotoAC)
Yeh Li-pin / Authentication Editor
[Health Channel / Comprehensive Report] In recent years, various kinds of health food are quite diverse, and many people will buy and eat according to their own needs; but many people think: even if you are taking chronic diseases drugs, you can also eat health food?
Japanese media "Zhongji News" reported that Professor Kiyoshi Kitakyushu of the Laboratory of Pharmaceutical Dynamics at Gifu University of Pharmaceutical Sciences observed that some patients who are taking drugs related to high blood pressure and blood sugar have seen health food advertisements mentioning keywords such as "blood pressure" and "blood sugar", which may misunderstand that these health food can improve high blood pressure, high blood sugar and other problems.
Taipei Qingshin emphasizes that health food is suitable for: blood pressure and blood sugar conditions do not need medication.
Finally, Ching-hsing of Taipei City reminds that if people use blood pressure lowering or blood sugar lowering drugs together with health foods labeled “For people with high blood pressure ” or“ For people with high blood sugar ”, they may cause dizziness or fall.
It is important to be careful before using healthy foods.
According to the Food and Drug Administration, health foods undergo concentration, extraction, processing and other processes, and their concentration and content are different from ordinary foods, and the public should pay attention to the amount of food consumed and the reaction after ingestion.
Photo taken in context. (Photo taken from PhotoAC)
In addition, the Food and Drug Administration of China said that the health food sold on the market and general capsules and tablets are originally food, but health food due to the concentration, extraction, processing and other processes, its concentration and content are different from ordinary food, so please pay attention to the amount of people eat and pay attention to the physical reaction after ingestion.
In particular, people with chronic diseases or long-term drug use may have food and drug interactions that affect the efficacy of the drug or increase the incidence of side effects.
Patients with cardiovascular disease who are taking antiplatelets or anticoagulants may be affected by consumption of health foods such as fish oil, seal oil, ginkgo or vitamin E, which may affect the coagulation function of the human body and increase the risk of bleeding.
At the same time, the composition structure of health foods containing red yeast or natto ingredients is similar to that of Statins blood lipid-lowering drugs, which leads to increased drug efficacy and increases the risk of adverse reactions, causing side effects such as liver or muscle-related diseases, and should be avoided in combination with blood lipid-lowering drugs.
Finally, the Food and Drug Administration reminds the public that if you have unexplained bruising, bleeding gums when brushing your teeth, and resolving dark black feces, please seek medical attention immediately.
